title: rf/route-link raises :rf.error/no-frame-context on first render — every example that renders one fails to boot at tip d1e6a707a3
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, running the operator half of docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md. Tip d1e6a707a3.

SYMPTOM. A browser build that renders `rf/route-link` anywhere in its tree throws on first render and mounts NOTHING — #app innerHTML length 0, blank page. The throw is a CLJS ExceptionInfo carrying [:rf.error/no-frame-context], :operation :route-link, :recovery :supply-frame, :where re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render. React reports it as 'An error occurred in the <re_frame.core_routing.route_link> component'.

The message text is the standard no-frame-context ladder: 'a frame-scoped route-link ran with no frame context — no carried frame stamp and no established scope...'.

MEASURED ACROSS FOUR APPS, all compiled with 'npx shadow-cljs compile <build>' from implementation/ in a clean full clone of this tip (own node_modules, npm install exit 0), then served as static files over a local HTTP server and loaded in headless Chrome via playwright-core. Every serve root carried index.html, main.js, cljs-runtime/ and examples/_shared/, and every run reported ZERO failed requests, so nothing here is an asset or 404 artefact.

  FAILS  :examples/routing            (examples/capabilities/routing/routing/) — the canonical routing example, 10 route-link sites
  FAILS  :examples/realworld          (examples/real-apps/realworld_http/)     — pilot 1's application
  FAILS  linearlite                   (examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/) — pilot 2's application, 1 route-link site
  BOOTS  :examples/login              (examples/core/login/)                   — no route-link; #app 643 chars, renders 'Sign in', 0 errors

The login row is the instrument control: the same harness, the same serving method, the same tip, exit 0. So the harness is sound and the discriminator is the presence of a route-link, not the build or the server.

NOT A WORKSPACE ARTEFACT. The failure reproduces identically in-repo (the repo's own shadow-cljs build, the example's own unmodified index.html, all _shared assets present, 0 failed requests) and in a pilot workspace built from :local/root per workspace.md. Both routes, same error, same :where.

NOT A URL ARTEFACT. Loading '/' and '/index.html' fail identically, so it is not the missing SPA push-state fallback.

STRUCTURE LOOKS CORRECT AT THE CALL SITES. realworld_http/core.cljs mounts [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default ...} [root-view]] and every route-link sits inside a reg-view under root-view; linearlite/core.cljs has the same shape at core.cljs:630. So this is not an obviously mis-wired application — which is what makes three independent applications failing the same way read as a framework regression rather than three app bugs.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE EXAMPLES. It blocks rf2-t4jpz at hour zero: workspace.md step 5 is an OPERATOR boot check that must pass with the app still on Reagent BEFORE a pilot agent is dispatched, and it fails for BOTH ratified pilots. rf2-hic-063's 2026-09-02 ruling makes that check a precondition of dispatch. It also removes outcome 2's baseline — pilot 1's brief tells the agent 'it works today. Run it before you change anything', which is false at this tip.

NOTE THE BEHAVIOURAL SUITES DO NOT CATCH IT. Both pilot baselines are green at this tip (realworld 4 tests / 123 assertions exit 0; linearlite 10 tests / 51 assertions exit 0). They drive events and read subscriptions without rendering, so a render-time route-link failure is invisible to them. Examples are test-free by policy and the browser smoke coverage is one adapter-level smoke per adapter, so nothing currently renders these three apps in CI.

REPRODUCE. From a clean clone at this tip: cd implementation && npm install && npx shadow-cljs compile :examples/routing; then serve out/examples/routing/ together with examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html and examples/_shared/ and open it. Expect a blank page and the ExceptionInfo above. Control: the same procedure on :examples/login renders 'Sign in'.

FILED, NOT FIXED — the rehearsal is a harvest task and re-frame.routing / implementation are held by live workers.
notes:
SHARPENED 2026-09-03 03:10 AUSEST, same rehearsal, and this CORRECTS a reading in the description above.

THE RULE IS EXACT: route-link fails whenever it actually RENDERS. Not 'these apps are broken', not 'dev builds are broken'. Dev and release both fail; the discriminator is solely whether a route-link is on the screen being rendered.

THE DECISIVE PAIR — ONE BUILD, ONE SERVER, TWO URLS. linearlite's release bundle (npx shadow-cljs release app, exit 0, 217 files, 0 warnings), served as static files, loaded twice:

  /             -> matches :linearlite.app/board, board-page renders, NO route-link on screen
                   BOOTS. #app innerHTML 2295 chars, 0 page errors, full board text renders
                   ('Linearlite — optimistic issue board', the three status columns, the
                   armed-failure toggle).

  /index.html   -> matches no route, so root-view falls through to not-found-page, whose
                   single route-link (core.cljs:591, {:to :linearlite.app/board}) renders
                   FAILS. #app innerHTML 0, 1 page error, the same [:rf.error/no-frame-context].

Nothing differs but the URL. That is the cleanest possible isolation and it is why the earlier
'linearlite FAILS' row needs qualifying: the application is fine, the component is not.

THE DEV/RELEASE AXIS IS A RED HERRING — I RAISED IT AND IT IS WRONG. It looked briefly as though
the guard might be a development-only assertion elided by :advanced, because linearlite's release
booted where its dev build had not. That comparison was mine and it was invalid: I had loaded the
dev build at /index.html and the release at /. Corrected, the guard fires under :advanced too —
realworld's release build (exit 0, 332 files, 1.66MB) raises the identical error with the identical
:where. Recording the false trail because it is the natural first hypothesis and the next person
should not spend the same run on it.

FULL MATRIX at tip d1e6a707a3, every row a captured exit code and a headless-Chrome load:

  app                              route-link on loaded screen   build     result
  examples/core/login  /           no (app has none)             dev       BOOTS  (#app 643, 'Sign in')
  examples/capabilities/routing /  yes (10 sites)                dev       FAILS
  examples/capabilities/routing /  yes                           release   FAILS
  realworld_http  / and /index.html yes (navbar, every screen)   dev       FAILS
  realworld_http  /                yes                           release   FAILS
  linearlite  /                    NO                            release   BOOTS  (#app 2295)
  linearlite  /index.html          yes (not-found-page)          release   FAILS

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FIX. The failing path is the render of re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render
itself, not application wiring, not the frame-root, not the build mode, and not the workspace. Any
application that puts a route-link on screen — which is every routed application — cannot render at
this tip.

WHAT IT CHANGES FOR THE PILOTS. Pilot 1 is blocked outright: realworld's navbar carries route-links on
every screen, so no screen renders. Pilot 2's board route happens to avoid the one site, so its board
DOES render and pilot 2 has a usable baseline screen — but its card-detail work (the authoring half,
which the ruling calls the more important of its two jobs) requires routing to and from a new screen,
which is exactly the surface that fails.

NOTE ON PRIORITY. Filed P0 on the strength of 'no example renders'; the sharpened rule does not soften
it — a routed application cannot show a link to another route.
MAYOR TRIAGE 2026-09-03 03:2x AUSEST. THIS IS THE TOP OF THE DISPATCH QUEUE AND THE ONLY P0 ON THE BOARD.

WHY I AM NOT DISPATCHING IT THIS MINUTE, stated so nobody reads the delay as a judgement about severity: the fleet ceiling is 6 (Mike, in his own words) and all six slots are live. I will not displace a running worker to make room — killing live work strands uncommitted changes, which is the one thing the stranded-sweep rule forbids building around. Three of the six have been running over an hour, so a slot frees on its own; this bead takes it, ahead of every P2 already queued.

WHAT MAKES THIS REPORT UNUSUALLY CREDIBLE, and worth saying because a P0 filed by a rehearsal agent deserves scrutiny rather than reflex: it carries an INSTRUMENT CONTROL. :examples/login has no route-link and BOOTS on the same tip, same harness, same serving method, #app 643 chars, 0 errors — while three apps that DO render a route-link mount nothing at all. So the discriminator is isolated to the presence of a route-link rather than to the build, the server, the assets or the clone. It also rules out two artefact classes explicitly: it reproduces both in-repo and in a :local/root pilot workspace, and "/" and "/index.html" fail identically, so it is not the missing SPA push-state fallback. Zero failed requests on every run.

A POINTER, EXPLICITLY NOT A DIAGNOSIS. I ran one cheap history read and stopped there, because a plausible-looking candidate stated confidently is how this project has burned itself before. Commit aa9e90af7f "hicasso: retire hframe; core admits the pure frame doors inside a refusing extent (rf2-6c12m.13, rf2-t32wg)" is the most recent change touching frame-context admission that a -S search over no-frame-context surfaces. That is a place to START a bisect, nothing more. DO NOT TREAT IT AS THE CAUSE. The honest first step is the bisect the bead earns: find the commit at which :examples/routing stops booting, using the login example as the control at every step.

WHAT THE FIXING WORKER MUST NOT DO: do not "fix" this by wrapping the call sites in a frame context. Three independent applications, each already mounting [rf/frame-root {:id :rf/default ...} [root-view]] with every route-link inside a reg-view under root-view, is the shape of a framework regression, not three app bugs. If the applications turn out genuinely wrong, that is a finding and a much bigger one.

IT ALSO BLOCKS rf2-t4jpz AT HOUR ZERO: workspace.md step 5 is an OPERATOR boot check that must pass with the app still on Reagent before a pilot agent is dispatched, and it fails for both pilots. So the pre-pilot rehearsal cannot proceed past its own first gate until this lands.

FIXED 2026-09-03 by PR #9050 (worker routelink-a). Root cause, bisect and the
browser evidence are on the PR; the load-bearing findings are recorded here so a
fresh maintainer needs nothing else.

BOTH BRIEFED MECHANISMS ARE REFUTED, and the reproduction refutes them by itself.
:examples/routing's root-view is a reg-view whose body is an AMBIENT
@(subscribe [:rf.route/id]) with no explicit frame, and it renders BEFORE any
route-link. The raised error names :operation :route-link / :where
re-frame.routing.link/route-link-render, never a subs site — so the ambient
resolution in root-view had already SUCCEEDED through the React-context tier that
frame-root establishes. The scope was present and readable (refuting "frame-root
no longer establishes the scope"), and require-current-frame! admitted it for
every reg-view in the tree (refuting "the admission changed").

THE CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, one level up from both. rf/route-link is a defwrapper
(re-frame.core-routing), so its body is (apply <hook-fn> args) — an ORDINARY
FUNCTION CALL. The :routing/route-link hook carried the registered :route/link
view HEAD, so that head ran INSIDE the component the substrate mounted for
rf/route-link itself, instead of becoming a component of its own. A plain Reagent
fn carries no {:contextType frame-context}, so (.-context cmp) was React's empty
default, views.provider/current-frame resolved nil, and route-link-render's
render-time require-current-frame! raised. This is precisely the failure mode
re-frame.views.provider/current-frame's own docstring already describes for plain
fns; nobody had noticed rf/route-link was one.

FIX: publish an element-emitting shim. The hook now returns
[(views/view-head :route/link) props & children], so the head reaches the
substrate as an element TYPE and is componentized exactly as a reg-view view is —
[rf/route-link ...] and [home-page ...] now take one path. The head is resolved
per render through view-head rather than closed over, because it is a property of
(registration x installed substrate) and the reg-view* seed is taken at ns-load
before rf/init! seats an adapter (rf2-8mkmb). SSR untouched. Confined to
implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc; no call site was wrapped in a
frame context, and none needed to be.

THE BISECT POINTER IN THE TRIAGE NOTE WAS WRONG, and by two and a half months.
aa9e90af7f (2026-08-30) is NOT the cause. The break is fda84bb117 (2026-06-16),
"fix(routing): route-link click carries the render-time frame (rf2-o3nam4)" — the
commit that introduced the render-time require-current-frame! into link.cljc. A
-S pickaxe over that symbol scoped to link.cljc returns EXACTLY ONE commit and the
count goes 0 -> 2 across it. Measured in the browser at both ends with
:examples/login as the control (the example lived at examples/reagent/routing/
before the #4999 reorg):
  1e443dde7a (fda84bb117^)  routing BOOTS  #app 267, 0 page errors ; login 627
  fda84bb117                routing FAILS  #app 0, the identical
                            :rf.error/no-frame-context :where route-link-render ; login 627
Note what that dating means: examples/capabilities/routing/routing/ did not exist
at fda84bb117, and realworld_http / linearlite did not exist at all. The routing
example was born into a tree that already carried the defect — this was never a
recent regression.

BROWSER ACCEPTANCE (headless Chromium, static serve, 0 failed requests every run):
  :examples/routing   before  #app 0    1 page error   / after  #app 268, 0 errors
  :examples/login     before  #app 643  0 errors       / after  #app 643, 0 errors  (control, unmoved)
  :examples/realworld  (pilot 1) after  #app 2350, navbar renders, 0 errors
  :examples/linearlite (pilot 2) after  #app 3535, 0 errors
  linearlite /index.html (the bead's decisive pair, the not-found-page route-link)
                       after  #app 274 "Not found / Back to the board", 0 errors
The link also NAVIGATES: clicking "See the articles" moves / -> /articles and
re-renders, 0 page errors — so rf2-o3nam4's render-time frame capture, which
fda84bb117 existed to add, still works.

THE DURABLE REGRESSION, and why the old coverage could not catch its own case.
EVERY pre-existing route-link suite calls routing/route-link-render directly and
establishes the frame with rf/with-frame — the DYNAMIC-VAR tier, which answers
from anywhere. Not one mounts [rf/route-link ...] through a substrate, so all of
them were green about a component no application could render. New file
implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_frame_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs
adds two rows in the :browser-test lane (unguarded PR-time job in test.yml) that
mount through the Reagent adapter into a real document with :ambient-frame nil,
establishing the frame ONLY through a React-context boundary — frame-provider in
one row, frame-root in the other. Proven to bite: reverting only routing.cljc to
its pre-fix blob and re-running gave exit 1 with exactly 2 failures, both the new
rows, both reporting container innerHTML = "" — the blank-page signature — while
the other 774 tests were unmoved.

GATES (exit codes captured from each runner): test:browser 776 tests / 4211
assertions 0F 0E exit 0; routing clojure -M:test 554 / 3454 0F 0E exit 0;
test:cljs 11193 / 55780 0F 0E exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh exit 0. test-fast-pr
--plan prints "No browser, bundle, adapter, Xray, MCP or tool-JVM gate is in any
tier" for this diff, which is this bead's thesis restated by the tool: the spine
cannot see this class of bug, which is why the regression is in the browser lane.

NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY: rf2-6sqv obstructed the diagnosis exactly as the brief
predicted — the raw ExceptionInfo reaching console.error showed only
{meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), ...}. Worked around locally by pr-str-ing
inside the (uncommitted, out-of-repo) measurement harness. Follow-on filed for the
defwrapper sharp edge underneath this: rf2-nvcp's cause generalises to any
late-bound hook whose value is a COMPONENT but whose wrapper CALLS it.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9050. rf/route-link now renders as a component (the :routing/route-link hook emits [(views/view-head :route/link) props & children]) instead of being called as a function, so the frame-root's React context reaches it. Browser acceptance: :examples/routing #app 0 -> 268 with 0 page errors, :examples/login control unmoved at 643/0 before and after; realworld (2350) and linearlite (3535) both boot, and linearlite /index.html — the bead's decisive pair — renders its not-found route-link at 274. Durable regression added in the browser lane (route_link_frame_context_dom_cljs_test.cljs, 2 rows) and proven red against the pre-fix blob. Bisect: the break is fda84bb117 (2026-06-16, rf2-o3nam4), NOT the triage note's aa9e90af7f. Follow-on rf2-02w1 filed for the defwrapper sharp edge underneath. Note beads close on PR-open in this repo; #9050 is open and green-pending, not yet merged.

title: bug(pair-skill): experiment loop restores the post-dispatch epoch, so compared handlers start from different state
description:
## Scope

Correct the canonical commit-and-compare procedure in `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md` so every handler version is exercised from the same retained frame-state. Reconcile the smallest carrier set that teaches or pins this procedure: the recipe, its prompt regression, and any Pair README/meta wording needed to keep one coherent workflow. Preserve the current `restore-epoch!` contract and the preference for `dispatch-dry-run` when no committed comparison is needed.

## Correctness finding

The recipe says the manual experiment holds the starting `app-db` constant, but it captures the epoch produced BY the baseline dispatch and restores that same epoch before running the edited handler. `restore-epoch!` restores a named record's canonical `:frame-state-after`, not its `:frame-state-before`. The restore therefore reinstalls the baseline event's POST-state. The edited handler runs from an already-mutated frame, so the two epochs do not share a starting state and their difference cannot be attributed solely to the code edit.

This is the canonical live-runtime validation workflow, not a wording nicety: following it can compound non-idempotent state, produce a false patch verdict, and then present that verdict as a controlled experiment.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md:213` promises “same starting app-db, same event, only the code changes.”
- `recipes.md:217` tells the agent to dispatch first and capture the `:epoch-id` from the resulting record. Lines 219-223 then restore “the captured epoch”; lines 230-231 dispatch the edited handler and compare the two results.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md:112` specifies that `(rf/restore-epoch! frame-id epoch-id)` restores the named epoch's whole `:frame-state-after`. `spec/API.md:644` repeats the same contract.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1017-1049` binds `recorded-frame-state` from `(:frame-state-after epoch)` as the only restore source and installs it.
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj:2830-2838` explicitly pins that restoring a record restores its `db-after`, not its `db-before`, and says callers must restore an earlier epoch to rewind past a mutation.
- The Pair README already demonstrates the correct concept at `skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md:130-134`: restore `<pre-click-epoch-id>` before retrying.
- Pair-MCP's rollback guidance likewise names the preceding head: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/dispatch_dry_run_test.cljs:634-650` instructs manual recovery through `:before-epoch-id`.
- Current prompt regression is non-discriminating. `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj:118-123` merely requires `dispatch-and-collect`, `restore-epoch`, and `reg-event`; lines 618-625 require the dedicated restore-tool spelling but never assert which epoch id it receives. The incorrect procedure is green.
- The same procedure has a nearby capture error: `recipes.md:229` says `handler-meta` should differ from “what you captured at step 1”, but step 1 captures only the result epoch, not handler metadata. Separating the state anchor, result epoch, and handler fingerprint resolves this without expanding scope.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Begin at retained epoch E0 with app-db `{:n 0}`.
2. Register a baseline handler that increments `:n` by 1.
3. Follow recipe step 1. Dispatching records E1 with `:db-before {:n 0}` and `:db-after {:n 1}`; capture E1 as instructed.
4. Follow recipe step 3 and restore E1. The frame is still `{:n 1}`, because E1's `:frame-state-after` is the restore source.
5. Replace the handler with one that adds 2 and dispatch again. The result is `{:n 3}`.
6. Under the promised common starting state E0, the edited handler's result would be `{:n 2}`. The observed 3 includes the baseline run's mutation, so the comparison is confounded.

Append, toggle, consume-once, and other non-idempotent handlers exhibit the same problem, and repeated iterations compound it. The existing warning about HTTP/navigation/storage effects is necessary but orthogonal: this defect is in the supposedly rewindable frame-state itself.

## Required invariant

The baseline handler and every edited handler must receive the same whole pre-dispatch frame-state. The epoch containing a run's result is comparison evidence; it is never the rewind anchor for recreating that run's input.

## Recommended minimal fix

- Before the baseline dispatch, read and capture the operating frame's current retained head as `pre-dispatch-epoch-id`. Separately capture the current handler fingerprint if later reload/re-registration verification will compare it.
- Dispatch the baseline and retain its RESULT epoch for outcome/diff evidence only.
- Before every edited comparison run, call the dedicated `restore-epoch` tool with `pre-dispatch-epoch-id`, verify `:restored? true`, then modify/verify and dispatch. Repeat the same restore before subsequent iterations.
- If the frame has no retained pre-dispatch epoch, or the anchor has aged out of the bounded ring, refuse this commit-and-compare procedure or use `dispatch-dry-run` when one consequence answers the question. Never silently substitute the baseline result epoch.
- Correct the handler verification step to reference the separately captured pre-edit fingerprint rather than claiming step 1 captured it.
- Keep the whole-frame restore warning and the escaped-side-effect warning exactly in force.

Use the smallest existing epoch-read form/tool that exposes the current head; no new public framework or MCP API is required merely to correct this recipe.

## Non-goals

- No change to `restore-epoch!` semantics, epoch storage, or ring retention.
- No new restore-before API, transaction/sandbox abstraction, generalized experiment framework, or compatibility layer.
- No claim that external effects can be undone; HTTP, navigation, storage, timers, and other escaped host work remain explicit caveats.
- No replacement of the manual loop when the programmer genuinely needs two committed epochs; `dispatch-dry-run` remains the preferred simpler path for a one-off consequence.
- No broad rewrite of unrelated Pair recipes or tool surfaces.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status `.beads/issues.jsonl` searches over title, description, and notes covered `experiment loop`, `same starting state`, `same starting app-db`, `pre-dispatch epoch`, `pre-event epoch`, `wrong epoch`, `captured epoch`, `commit-and-compare`, `pre-click-epoch-id`, and restore combined with baseline/result. No bead owns this restore-anchor defect.

- Closed `rf2-1f60u` fixes `tail-build` comparing against a post-edit handler probe; it does not address the pre-event frame-state anchor.
- Closed `rf2-k2qus` is a stale-vocabulary hygiene sweep.
- Closed `rf2-tnmuq` reconciles the `eval-cljs` posture.
- Closed `rf2-p1keh` removes cross-process Story composition.

`git blame` shows the capture-result/restore-result sequence has persisted since commit `344754178f` (2026-06-03), while later changes updated the restore wording around it. `git log -S'Rewind to the captured epoch'` shows no repair. The README's older `pre-click-epoch-id` example is an internal contradiction, not an implementation of the correct procedure in the canonical recipe.

## Uncertainty

The exact lowest-friction existing read used to obtain the current epoch head should be selected while implementing against the current tool catalogue. The correctness invariant is not uncertain. A new frame may have no predecessor and a bounded ring may evict it; those cases require an honest refusal/fallback, not invented rewindability.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The canonical experiment procedure captures a `pre-dispatch-epoch-id` before the baseline dispatch and restores that id before every compared dispatch. The baseline RESULT epoch is named separately and used only as outcome/diff evidence.
2. No current Pair instruction states or implies that restoring the epoch produced by an event recreates that event's starting state.
3. A focused worked regression starts from `{:n 0}` and proves baseline `+1 => 1` and edited `+2 => 2`. Reintroducing the current result-epoch restore produces 3 and makes the control fail.
4. A missing, aged-out, or rejected pre-dispatch anchor fails honestly before the edited live dispatch; the workflow does not substitute another epoch or claim a controlled comparison.
5. The handler fingerprint is captured separately before re-registration/source edit, and the verification step references that actual capture.
6. The existing prompt regression for “Experiment loop” requires pre-event/pre-dispatch anchor semantics and distinguishes the restore anchor from the resulting epoch id, while retaining the dedicated `restore-epoch` tool assertion.
7. README, recipes, and relevant prompt/meta carriers agree on the corrected sequence; existing Pair prompt/runtime gates remain green.
8. The fix adds no framework/MCP API, history mechanism, side-effect rollback, or generalized experiment abstraction.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9225 (branch worker/skpair-a).

PREMISE CONFIRMED AT TIP. restore-epoch! binds recorded-frame-state from
(:frame-state-after epoch) as its only restore source
(implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc), matching
spec/Tool-Pair.md:112 and spec/API.md. PR #9205 / commit 4f5993de17 (rf2-f8wu)
changes only WHICH records survive a depth reduction, not which state a restore
installs, so it does not disturb this finding; it adds one live eviction route
for a captured anchor, which the corrected step 4 now names.

WHAT LANDED (2 files, 126+/14-, both under skills/re-frame2-pair/):

- references/recipes.md, section "Experiment loop". The canonical
  commit-and-compare procedure now keeps three roles apart by name:
  pre-dispatch-epoch-id (the rewind anchor), baseline-epoch-id (result evidence
  only), pre-edit-handler-meta (patch-landed proof). Step 1 captures the anchor
  BEFORE any dispatch, from watch-epochs' :head-id; step 4 restores that anchor
  and step 9 restores the SAME anchor on every further iteration. A null
  :head-id and a refused restore each stop the procedure rather than
  substituting another epoch. A worked control carries the numbers ({:n 0} ->
  baseline {:n 1} -> edited {:n 2}, with {:n 3} named as the confounded
  reading), and the mechanism is stated inline (restore reinstalls
  :frame-state-after) so the rule cannot drift back as a style preference.
  Anchored to Redux DevTools, which jumps to the state AFTER a selected action.

- tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj. The :experiment-loop row's
  must-mention now requires the two id names, and a new deftest
  experiment-loop-rewinds-to-the-pre-dispatch-anchor pins the distinct roles,
  the ORDER (anchor introduced before the baseline result), the restore
  invocation carrying <pre-dispatch-epoch-id>, the :frame-state-after
  mechanism, the honest-refusal branch, the worked control's four numbers, and
  the separately-captured handler fingerprint.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 met as written. AC 3 (the worked
{:n 0} regression) is realised as a doc-carried worked control plus a
structural pin on its numbers, NOT a live-frame test: the skill tree's only
test lanes are babashka AST/structural pins over runtime.cljs and a node
pure-fn build (docs/TESTING.md 1a/1b); there is no live-frame lane under
skills/re-frame2-pair/, and adding one would need implementation/ and CI
changes outside this bead's fence. The control is real and was measured in
both directions: the suite exits 1 with 11 failures against the pre-fix
recipes.md and 0 (29 tests / 223 assertions) against the corrected one.

NO API ADDED. watch-epochs already returns :head-id and is already
allow-listed by the skill. dispatch's :before-epoch-id was considered and
rejected: it rides only the queued, not-yet-drained branch, which the recipe's

title: bug(skill-xray): manual init!/mount bypasses the only goog.DEBUG gate despite elision guidance
description:
Surface: skills/re-frame2-xray/** (manual/programmatic launch guidance), checked independently against the current Xray facade, preload, mount path, framework initialization, elision probe, tests/config, and git history.

Problem

The skill makes a universal production-safety promise that is false for the manual path it explicitly teaches. SKILL.md:29-32 says Xray is "elided entirely from production builds." references/launch-programmatic.md:14-25 and 38-45 then tells a host app to require day8.re-frame2-xray.core, call rf/init!, call xray/init! without a guard, and invoke a mount verb. references/launch-lifecycle.md:101-128 says goog.DEBUG=false gates every dev-only branch, including Xray's, and presents npm run test:elision as proof that Xray cannot reach production.

Exact implementation evidence

- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:92-114 contains the only outer interop/debug-enabled? gate. It protects preload boot only.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:159-180 makes the documented manual init! path unconditionally register Xray handlers, trace and epoch collectors, browser globals, and the keybinding before applying options. It does not traverse preload or check goog.DEBUG.
- core.cljs:71-102 directly aliases open!, open-overlay!, toggle!, and popout! to mount operations without a production gate.
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:31-36 says mount needs no elision logic because "The preload's gate means mount never reaches production builds." That premise does not hold for the public manual facade.
- mount.cljs:886-921 mounts when a substrate adapter exists. A normal production SPA has that adapter after implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc rf/init!; adapter presence is not a production discriminator.
- implementation/package.json:38 invokes the framework elision probe. implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs and implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs root/check re-frame framework trace/schema/registrar surfaces, not the Xray namespace, manual Xray sequence, browser globals, keybinding, handlers, DOM root, or Xray bundle sentinels. The cited gate therefore cannot establish the skill's Xray claim.
- Git history is consistent with this split: dbb3c35522 intentionally separated the explicit core facade from preload side effects and described production exclusion as a host/devtools-block responsibility. The later skill language generalized the preload guarantee to the manual path.

Causal reproduction

In an ordinary app namespace, follow the documented sequence: require day8.re-frame2-xray.core, run rf/init!, xray/init!, then xray/open!, and compile an advanced production build with goog.DEBUG=false. The preload gate is irrelevant because this path never enters preload. xray/init! still installs tooling surfaces; the normal production re-frame adapter lets xray/open! proceed to mount. This is a static, direct call path, not an edge-case inference.

Impact and priority

A programmer or AI following the canonical low-friction example can ship state-inspection browser globals/UI, :rf.xray/* handlers, listeners/collectors, and retained Xray code while the skill explicitly assures them production inclusion is impossible. That is a production correctness, exposure, bundle, and performance defect at the API's trust boundary, so P1 is warranted pre-alpha.

Bounded recommendation

Make the canonical manual facade safe by construction: apply one coherent debug/production gate to manual foundation initialization and externally visible mount entry points, not only to preload. Add a real optimized Xray elision probe/control rooted through the exact documented manual sequence. This preserves the elegant one-model promise and avoids making every host remember bespoke build placement.

If maintainers intentionally support production use through the manual facade, the immediate fallback is documentation-only but must be explicit: scope the elision guarantee to preload, require manual consumers to exclude or host-guard the facade, and remove the claim that the framework-only test:elision proves Xray absence.

Non-goals

Do not add a new runtime warning banner, disable setting, compatibility layer, or launch mode. Do not redesign panels, mount lifecycle, Pair, or the framework's general elision system.

Acceptance and tests

1. An optimized goog.DEBUG=false probe rooted through rf/init! + xray/init! + xray/open! cannot register :rf.xray/* handlers, install Xray browser globals or its key listener/collectors, or create #rf-xray-root. A goog.DEBUG=true control exercises those effects so the check cannot pass vacuously.
2. The optimized-bundle gate checks distinctive Xray sentinels or an equivalent reachability/size assertion, with a positive control, rather than reusing only the framework elision probe.
3. Existing preload development launch and manual development launch remain functional, including init/mount tests.
4. SKILL.md, launch-programmatic.md, and launch-lifecycle.md all state the same actual boundary and do not cite a non-Xray probe as proof.
5. Add a skill answer-quality eval asking whether manual init! from a normal app namespace is production-safe; the answer must identify the actual gate and required host responsibility, if any.

Duplicate distinction

Targeted searches of .beads/issues.jsonl and git history found no exact issue. rf2-fguoj and rf2-2oug concern an unshipped production warning banner, not the documented manual facade bypassing the only gate. Open rf2-ar67 enrolls 16 core facade exports in the API manifest/classifier; it does not address production gating or elision. rf2-11hn covers framework elision, whose probe is precisely what fails to cover this Xray path.

Uncertainty

No optimized compile or runtime was executed because this review was constrained to static/read-only analysis. The runtime side-effect path is unambiguous from the calls above; the exact number of retained production bytes is not established and is intentionally delegated to the proposed optimized probe.

title: bug(skill-implementor): minimum ports can skip v1-required flows and report false-green conformance
description:
## Scope

Correct the skills/re-frame2-implementor/** workflow so a minimum port cannot treat Spec 013 Flows as an optional, known-skipped capability and then call itself v1-complete. Reconcile the skill with the current pinned owners (spec/013-Flows.md, spec/Implementor-Checklist.md, and spec/conformance/README.md) and update the focused implementor-order guard that currently certifies the stale three-family model.

Keep the existing two-phase/no-interview ergonomics, host scope, conformance subset mechanism, and narrow EP loop. This is one downstream contract-drift repair, not a redesign of flows or the conformance system.

## Correctness finding

The published skill explicitly defaults flows to no, places EP 013 in the optional table, and defines required completion around only :core/*, :identity/*, and :data-classification/*. The current normative corpus says the opposite: Spec 013 is v1-required, the Implementor Checklist puts Flows in the non-gated Required table, and the conformance README says :flow/* is not optional.

That creates a clean false-green path. On a minimum-port request, the skill records flows as an intentional known skip. Its harness therefore does not trigger the unknown-capability floor; it deliberately excludes the flow fixtures, obtains claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable over the smaller claim, and the Done checklist accepts the result. The port is reported as re-frame2 v1-complete while omitting a runtime surface the contract says every port ships.

## Evidence

- spec/013-Flows.md:3-7 opens with Status: Drafting. v1-required, defines the minimum flow claim, and deliberately restrains flows to a narrow convenience rather than making them optional.
- spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:37 lists Flows under Required (not gated; every implementation ships these). Lines 122-124 say :flow/* cannot be declined; line 138 repeats that Flows is v1-required; line 562 marks :flow/* as nothing — always run.
- spec/conformance/README.md:287 says :flow/* is Not optional because Spec 013 is v1-required.
- The live corpus has 11 fixture files carrying :flow/*, including recomputation, topology, dirty-checking, lifecycle/toggle, frame scope/teardown, hot reload, and error/trace behaviour.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-1-decisions.md:68 calls flows one of three extra optional, skill-local scope decisions and says the minimum-port default is no.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:49-61 declares only three v1-required families and maps :flow/* to that optional skill-local decision.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:74 puts EP 013 in the optional table behind flows claimed; line 81 says the checklist stops at Q7 and calls flows, managed HTTP, and resources three skill-local choices. The current checklist instead has Q1-Q9: Q8 is Managed HTTP and Q9 is Resources; Flows is Required and intentionally has no Q-number.
- The first completion gate at skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:40, skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:76, and references/cardinal-rules.md:21 runs only :core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*.
- skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json id 20 currently grades an answer that defaults flows to no, so the existing behavioural expectation reinforces the defect.
- scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py:50-63,184-194,335-363,422-448 hard-codes exactly three required roots, cross-checks that stale set against the skill rather than the normative spec, and reports green when every skill surface repeats the same omission.

## Failure scenario

1. Ask the skill: Build me a minimum re-frame2 port in TypeScript.
2. Following phase-1-decisions.md, record flows in known-skipped with the other optional capabilities and default it to no.
3. Implement the listed foundation sequence 001 -> 002 -> 006 -> views -> 009 -> 015.
4. Run the skill's gate 1 over :core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*; run gate 2 over the claimed set. The :flow/* fixtures are intentionally out of claim, not unknown, so both gates can be green.
5. Satisfy the current Done checklist and report claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable, despite having no reg-flow, lifecycle effects, flow transform in the drain, or flow conformance.

The invariant is simple: a minimum port may keep the flow API deliberately small, as Spec 013's restraint says, but it may not opt out of the Spec 013 minimum claim or omit :flow/* from its required conformance accounting.

## History / cause

Commit c261b45590 fixed the then-real phantom-Q problem by moving flows, managed HTTP, and resources to three skill-local optional choices because the checklist stopped at Q7. Commit 1b0b87a404 subsequently changed the authoritative checklist: it added Managed HTTP as Q8 and Resources as Q9, and explicitly made Flows a non-gated v1-required row because putting Spec 013 behind yes/no would let a port opt out of required behaviour. Later checklist correction 6fff78e7fc preserved that Flows ruling while sharpening cross-tagged derivation prose. No later implementor-skill commit consumed the new contract, so the formerly correct fallback became stale.

## Recommended minimal fix

1. Remove Flows from the profile's optional/default-no decisions and state it as a fixed required obligation linked to Spec 013.
2. Put EP 013 on the required implementation path after its declared dependencies and before the first completion claim. Preserve the one-EP loop; do not add a special workflow.
3. Always include :flow/* in the minimum claim and in the required gate alongside the existing required roots. Keep fixture subset semantics for genuinely cross-tagged cases.
4. Reconcile optional numbering with the current checklist: Managed HTTP is Q8, Resources is Q9, and Flows has no Q because it is Required.
5. Update the existing eval id 20 so the no-interview default still sets every genuinely optional capability to no but does not opt out of flows.
6. Update scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py and its self-tests so omitting :flow/* from any required-gate statement is red. Derive/cross-check the required roots against the authoritative checklist/conformance owner rather than merely proving that a stale skill agrees with itself.

This is a small documentation-and-guard correction. It requires no new runtime implementation, fixture, generated manifest, interview step, or compatibility path.

## Duplicate distinction

Targeted all-status title/body searches for implementor + flows/013, required/optional flows, required-family gates, and the exact three-family completion phrase found no open bead owning this false-green.

- rf2-ozocz is closed. It correctly removed phantom Q8-Q10 references when the checklist had only Q1-Q7. This issue is the later downstream drift created when the authoritative checklist changed; it reverses only the now-stale Flows part and adopts the real Q8/Q9.
- rf2-yyr6c is closed. Its landed checklist work is the source of truth this skill failed to consume; its final correction concerned cross-tagged :derivation/* fixtures, not the implementor skill's ability to skip Spec 013.
- rf2-3758j is closed and owns the distinct EP-006 live sub-cache observability witness. It does not cover flow capability selection or the omitted :flow/* gate.
- rf2-nuy8x is closed and owns the broader workflow reduction. This is a bounded correctness residual after that reduction, not a request to reopen its rejected eval-platform or ceremony work.

## Uncertainty

The required status and missing family are unambiguous. The precise presentation of EP 013 in the dependency list should be derived from its pinned owners during implementation; acceptance requires that all its prerequisites precede it and that no completion gate precede it, not a new global taxonomy or an invented ordering rule.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Given the existing eval-20 prompt, Build me a minimum re-frame2 port in TypeScript, the produced port profile cannot put Flows or any :flow/* capability in known-skipped. It defaults only genuinely optional capabilities to no and still begins work in the same run with no interview.
2. Every shipped skill surface classifies Spec 013 consistently with spec/013-Flows.md and the Implementor Checklist: Flows is a fixed v1-required obligation, not a profile scope choice. Managed HTTP is Q8 and Resources is Q9; no prose says the current checklist stops at Q7.
3. The Phase-2 path includes the minimum Spec 013 slice after its real dependencies and before any foundation/v1 completion claim. It still uses the existing six-step EP loop and does not add a flow-specific process.
4. Required conformance accounting includes :flow/* alongside :core/*, :identity/*, and :data-classification/*. A port with no flow implementation cannot achieve the skill's required passed / claimed-applicable result or satisfy Done merely by marking flows out of claim.
5. The existing eval id 20's expected output/expectations no longer asks the agent to default flows to no; its no-interview and same-run guarantees remain intact.
6. scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py is updated with focused self-tests: removing :flow/* from a required-gate statement makes the checker exit nonzero, restoring it returns green, and the owner cross-check cannot pass solely because the stale skill and checker agree with each other.
7. Implementor order/partition checker self-tests and CI modes, skill packaging checks, and skill-link checks remain green. The PR reports exact commands and exit codes.
8. No framework API semantics, Spec 013 behaviour, conformance fixture content, host scope, optional-capability policy beyond this stale mapping, generated sync layer, new eval platform, or backward-compatibility shim is introduced.
notes: Surface review performed independently at 4c44c86f206599299f8d0734de717ea33b4c5e2c. Read the full published skill, all four operational references, package/plugin metadata, evals, internal design/inputs/authoring prompt, current Spec 013, Implementor Checklist, conformance README/fixtures, focused guard source, and relevant git history. No repository files were edited.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9229 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9229). Both halves established and repaired. SKIP HALF: phase-1-decisions listed flows among three skill-local optional scope decisions defaulting to no, and phase-2-impl-order carried EP 013 in the optional table behind 'flows claimed' - both resting on the checklist numbering only Q1-Q7, which it no longer does. FALSE-REPORT HALF: conformance.md declared three v1-required families, so the flow fixtures were intentionally out-of-claim rather than unknown, which is exactly the case the harness unknown-capability floor is designed NOT to fail; gate 1 ran three families and gate 2 scored claimed-applicable/claimed-applicable over the smaller claim. Neither half fixes the other: repairing only the skip leaves the accounting certifying a flowless port; repairing only the accounting leaves the document self-contradictory. Every premise verified at source (013-Flows.md:3 v1-required; Implementor-Checklist:37 Required row, :120 always-run families naming :flow/*, :100/:108 Q8/Q9, :558 family table; conformance/README:287 Not optional; 11 fixture files, 20 distinct :flow/* tags). Fix: four v1-required families; EP 013 in the foundation after its real dependencies (001->002->006->views->009->015->013) before any completion claim, on the existing six-step loop; a sixth harness floor refusing a known-skipped entry that names a v1-required capability, which is what makes the reduced path safe by construction; Q1-Q9 reconciled with the bug's own inference named and refused (a missing Q-number is not evidence of optionality - Flows lacks one for the opposite reason); Spec 013 restraint reframed as a budget for how much flow API to build, never whether. eval 20 keeps its no-interview/same-run guarantees and no longer defaults flows to no. Guard updated per criterion 6: requires 013 with 015 in any foundation sequence and :flow/* in any gate-1 statement, and its cross-check is now two-sided - roots derived from Implementor-Checklist Part 3 always-run rows, since the one-sided check was circular (skill and guard agreed on three families throughout). Proven live, not assumed: removing :flow/* from a gate-1 statement gives exit 1; making skill and guard agree on the stale three-family set gives exit 2 citing the spec; check_doc_slugs proven with a planted anchor+target (exit 1), all restores cmp byte-identical. 12 gates run, all exit 0. Scope beyond the item: docs/skills/re-frame2-implementor.md (the published summary) repeated the defect verbatim and is fixed under criterion 2 'every shipped skill surface'; two residual copies in the skill's own re-authoring notes (spec/inputs.md, spec/authoring-prompt.md) also corrected - that is the mechanism by which the next authoring pass would have re-encoded the drift. title: bug(skill-reagent-migration): MIG-04/05 silently turn queued Reagent dispatches into synchronous Hicasso intents
description:
## Scope

Correct the scheduling contract taught by skills/reagent-migration/** for Reagent handler rewrites into Hicasso intents. Keep Hicasso's synchronous runtime semantics and data-first event API unchanged. The target is truthful, low-friction migration guidance: ordinary intents remain the default, while the rare ordering-sensitive handler gets one explicit preservation route.

## Correctness finding

The skill classifies its full M-tier, including MIG-04, MIG-05, MIG-06 and MIG-33 handler lifts, as unambiguous and observably identical. Its canonical rewrite turns a Reagent closure that calls rf/dispatch into a Hicasso intent vector.

Those two forms do not have the same scheduling contract. re-frame2 rf/dispatch appends to the router queue and returns immediately before the handler runs. A Hicasso intent closes over the frame API's dispatch-sync operation, drains the event and its synchronous cascade inside the browser callback's turn, and notifies the store before that turn ends. This is intentional Hicasso behavior, especially for controlled-input convergence, but it is a behavior change in an arbitrary migrated handler and the skill never names it.

## Exact evidence

- skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:107 calls the M-tier rewrites, expressly including dispatch lifting and keystroke maps, unambiguous and observably identical.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:64-84 makes #(dispatch [:go 1]) -> [:go 1] a direct MIG-04 rewrite and performs the same lift for value/checked handlers in MIG-05. The MIG-33 rule at lines 397 onward likewise replaces conditional queued dispatch calls with a key map.
- skills/reagent-migration/evals/evals.json:38 and :51 grade the direct event-vector result. No expectation asks the agent to disclose or preserve queue ordering.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1167-1171 defines rf/dispatch as enqueue-and-return before the handler runs. Lines 1200-1207 distinguish dispatch-sync as an end-to-end fixed-point drain for tests, REPL and bootstrap.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:85-96 mints Hicasso's frame dispatch from the captured :dispatch-sync operation. Lines 513-522 state that the event drains synchronously inside the caller's turn and store notification occurs before the turn ends.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:497-524 routes ordinary intent vectors through that captured dispatch.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/callback_form_dom_cljs_test.cljs:8-17 and :101-108 are an existing real-browser witness: a returned intent reaches the synchronous door and produces its echo in the same turn.

## Concrete impact

A Reagent click handler that only enqueues an event returns before application handlers and effects run. After the prescribed migration, those handlers and their synchronous cascade finish before the Hicasso callback returns. Ordering can therefore reverse relative to later propagation listeners, browser default actions, imperative code outside the component, and observations made immediately after the callback. A coeffect or structural failure that used to occur during the queued drain can also surface on a different stack.

Most application events should still use the concise intent vector. The defect is not that Hicasso is synchronous; it is that the migration promises observational identity and gives an ordering-sensitive application no signal that it crossed this semantic boundary. Shadow comparisons that inspect settled DOM and intent streams can remain green while missing callback-turn ordering.

## Recommended bounded fix

1. State once in the mental model/procedure that Hicasso event intents dispatch synchronously, unlike rf/dispatch, and explain why controlled writes require same-turn convergence.
2. Remove the blanket observably-identical claim for handler-lifting rules. Keep ordinary dispatch-only closures as the idiomatic default rather than turning every handler into a decision ceremony.
3. Add one narrow detection/question for an explicitly ordering-sensitive site: code, tests or comments that require the event to remain queued until after the callback/propagation/default-action phase.
4. For that exceptional site, teach the existing preservation route: call rf/capture-frame during render, close a plain callback over the captured frame API's queued :dispatch function, and return nil. Do not call ambient rf/dispatch after the render extent; that is the separate no-frame-context failure already taught by MIG-26.
5. Add one behavioral eval that distinguishes queued-after-callback semantics from Hicasso's same-turn intent semantics and rejects an answer that calls the two observationally identical.

## Non-goals

- No Hicasso runtime change, async-intent variant, scheduler abstraction or new public API.
- No per-handler prompt, blanket refusal to use data intents, or compatibility mode.
- No weakening of synchronous controlled-input convergence.
- No redesign of event vectors, key maps, h/event, the reporter or the view migration tiers beyond the scheduling distinction.
- No attempt to enumerate every browser ordering edge; one clear invariant and one existing escape are enough.

## Duplicate and history research

Targeted all-status searches over .beads/issues.jsonl for reagent-migration, MIG-04, dispatch-lifting, Hicasso intent and dispatch-sync found no bead owning this async-to-sync migration seam. Closed rf2-90k4a covers three frame-context/refusal diagnostics, rf2-vpdrf covers SSR adapter boot, and rf2-qxca8 covers retired Hicasso read/navigation doors; none addresses event scheduling.

Git history strengthens the mismatch: the exact MIG-04 example originated in 819a2f68a7 for an earlier destination and survived the Hicasso retarget in 6cdc1979da unchanged. Hicasso's captured synchronous dispatch was established separately in 69e160e1d1. No later skill commit reconciled those two contracts.

## Uncertainty

No new runtime was launched in this review-only worker. The semantic mismatch is directly established by current public core docs, current implementation, and an existing real-browser Hicasso witness. What remains unknown is how many consumer handlers rely on callback-turn ordering; that uncertainty is why the repair should preserve the vector as the default and add one bounded exception rather than impose ceremony on every event.
acceptance_criteria:
- SKILL.md and the routed migration references no longer describe rf/dispatch-to-intent handler lifts as observationally identical without qualification.
- The skill states the exact scheduling boundary once: rf/dispatch queues and returns before the handler runs; a Hicasso vector, key-map branch, or vector returned from h/event drains synchronously inside the callback turn.
- MIG-04/05/06/33 remain concise defaults for ordinary application handlers. The guidance does not ask about every handler or introduce a new runtime form.
- The skill identifies only explicit queue-order dependencies as judgment work and gives a valid preservation spelling using a render-time rf/capture-frame and its captured queued :dispatch operation in a plain callback. It clearly distinguishes that captured operation from an ambient rf/dispatch invoked after render.
- Controlled input guidance continues to require same-turn synchronous writes and explains that this is intentional rather than accidental equivalence.
- A focused behavioral eval presents or states an ordering-sensitive Reagent handler and fails an answer that silently emits an intent while claiming equivalent timing; it passes either an informed semantic change accepted by the author or the captured queued-dispatch escape.
- Existing handler-lifting, no-frame-context, key-map and controlled-input eval expectations remain coherent; eval JSON and skill/package structural checks pass.
- No Hicasso/core runtime API or behavior changes.
