title: machines: compatibility reset drops spawned-actor identity and strands the live snapshot
description:
## Finding

The supported handler-entry recovery for an incompatible machine snapshot replaces the entire snapshot with the registered type's fresh initial snapshot. That is correct for authored state/data, but for a spawned actor it also deletes the runtime-owned identity envelope that makes the actor addressable. The event that discovers the incompatibility completes against the fresh definition; the next event to the same still-present actor snapshot resolves no handler and is rejected as `:rf.error/no-such-handler`.

This is a composition bug between snapshot compatibility recovery and runtime-db-derived spawned-actor liveness, not a request for a migration framework.

## Verified current behavior

I exercised the public runtime on the JVM with the machines `:test` classpath:

1. Register child type `:probe/worker` at snapshot version 1 with state `:old` and `{:n 0}`.
2. Register a parent whose transition declaratively `:spawn`s that type; capture actor id `:probe/worker#1`.
3. Re-register `:probe/worker` at snapshot version 2 with initial state `:ready`, `{:n 100}`, and a `:bump` action that increments `:n`.
4. Dispatch `:bump` twice to the actor.

Observed (process exited 0):

```clojure
{:actor :probe/worker#1
 :before-root {:state :old
               :meta #:rf{:snapshot-version 1}
               :rf/machine-type :probe/worker}
 :before-data {:n 0
               :rf/self-id :probe/worker#1
               :rf/parent-id :probe/parent
               :rf/invoke-id [:running]}
 :after-first-root {:state :ready
                    :meta #:rf{:snapshot-version 2}}
 :after-first-data {:n 101}
 :after-second-data {:n 101}
 :version-errors 1
 :no-handler-errors 1}
```

The first dispatch proves version drift is detected and the replacement definition runs. It also drops `:rf/machine-type` plus the actor lineage. The second dispatch cannot lazily resolve a handler, does not increment `:n`, and emits `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, even though the actor snapshot remains physically present in runtime-db.

## Root cause and exact surfaces

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc`, `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot` (around lines 334-358), returns only `(assoc @base-initial :rf/bootstrap-pending? true)`. `prepare-machine-ctx` / `reconcile-snapshot` applies this to every existing snapshot, including spawned actors, for both `:version-mismatch` and `:state-not-in-definition`.
- That `base-initial` is derived from the current type definition. It contains authored initial data and fresh transient counters, but it cannot contain per-instance values stamped only by the spawn runtime.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc`, `machine-type-ref` and `stamp-framework-data` (around lines 252-280), establish the missing envelope: root `:rf/machine-type`; data `:rf/self-id`; optional `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, and `:rf/join-child`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc`, `spec-from-snapshot` (around lines 63-82), intentionally resolves an unregistered actor instance only through root `:rf/machine-type`.
- `registration.cljc`, `resolve-actor-handler-meta` (around lines 1347-1389), returns nil when that slot is gone, handing the next dispatch back to the router's genuine no-handler path.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, Snapshot shape invariants and Reserved snapshot-internal keys (around lines 58-87), calls these keys framework-owned and says `:rf/machine-type` persists and makes spawned liveness a function of runtime-db. The reset currently treats the identity envelope like disposable user data.

## Coverage gap

`implementation/machines/test/re_frame/snapshot_compat_test.clj` proves compatibility recovery for singleton/manual snapshots only. Spawned-actor lifecycle tests (including `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/actor_liveness_cljs_test.cljc`) prove spawn/destroy/restore resolution but do not compose it with handler-entry compatibility recovery. Consequently each feature's local tests pass while their combination strands the actor.

## Impact

Hot reload is an explicit pre-alpha productivity path: an author who correctly bumps `:rf/snapshot-version`, or merely removes a live state, can silently turn every affected spawned instance into an inert snapshot after its first post-reload event. The same lost lineage is also used for declarative ownership/finalization, and `:rf/join-child` carries exact-attempt completion correlation for `:spawn-all`; losing it can break parent cleanup or join completion even during the reset event. The directly reproduced impact is the actor becoming unaddressable on the next dispatch.

## Bounded recommendation

Keep the existing fresh-user-snapshot reset, but preserve or reconstruct a deliberately small, canonical spawned-actor identity envelope from the existing snapshot before bootstrap/transition processing. At minimum this includes root `:rf/machine-type` and data `:rf/self-id`; when present, retain the runtime-stamped ownership/correlation values `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, and `:rf/join-child`. Implement this through one named helper/catalogue so snapshot recovery and spawn agree on which values are durable actor identity.

Do not merge the old `:data` map wholesale: authored data and transient timer/spawn/history counters should continue to reset exactly as the current compatibility contract intends.

## Non-goals

- No general snapshot migration API or user hook.
- No per-instance handler registry or change to runtime-db-derived liveness.
- No broad merge of old user data, timer epochs, spawn counters, or history into the new definition.
- No redesign of actor ids, spawning, hot reload, or epoch restore.

## Posture rationale

This is a narrow fix with high ergonomic leverage. It makes the documented, simple action (bump the snapshot version during a pre-alpha definition change) safe for the ordinary SPA actor model. Preserving the runtime-owned envelope keeps the API minimal and trusts the programmer; it avoids both a migration subsystem and surprising zombie actors.

## Duplicate and history search

I searched the review-time tracker corpus (923 issues) across titles/descriptions/notes/close reasons and repeated `bd search` queries for `machine-type`, `snapshot-version`, `version mismatch`, `state-not-in-definition`, `compatibility`, `hot reload`, `reset-to-initial`, `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot`, `spawned actor`, `inert snapshot`, and `no-such-handler`. No issue described this reset/liveness composition. Spawn-related matches concerned mixed-prefix teardown, naming, tooling branches, cancellation docs, and websocket correlation; hot-reload matches were unrelated examples/templates/Hicasso work.

Relevant landed history shows why the gap is plausible:

- `6b445ca978` (2026-05-14), snapshot-compatibility checks, introduced `rebuild-incompatible-snapshot` with singleton-oriented tests.
- `38b5a25407` (2026-06-03), runtime-db-derived spawned-actor liveness, later made `:rf/machine-type` the dispatch authority.
- `d0ce1cd437` (2026-06-09), spawned-actor version-drift checks on epoch restore, did not exercise a subsequent handler-entry rebuild.

No later commit in the affected files adds a compatibility-reset/spawn composition test or restores the envelope.

## Uncertainty

The live reproduction exercises the version-mismatch branch for a registered `:machine-id` spawn. The state-not-in-definition branch calls the identical replacement helper, so its identity loss is source-proven but was not separately driven. Loss of subsequent handler resolution is directly observed; the additional parent/join lifecycle effects follow from the documented consumers of the erased lineage and should be pinned by focused regression tests rather than assumed beyond those paths.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a regression test in `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/snapshot_compat_test.clj` (or a narrowly named spawned-compatibility test) that declaratively spawns a registered v1 type, re-registers it with a v2 definition, dispatches at least two events to the same actor, and proves: exactly one mismatch recovery occurs, the first event uses the fresh definition, the second event is processed, no `:rf.error/no-such-handler` occurs, and the snapshot remains handler-resolvable.
- Cover `:state-not-in-definition` as the second entry path into the same recovery behavior, either by parameterizing the regression or with one focused sibling assertion.
- Compatibility recovery still replaces authored state/data and resets transient runtime counters per the existing contract; it does not wholesale merge the old snapshot.
- The recovered spawned snapshot preserves/reconstructs the canonical runtime identity envelope: root `:rf/machine-type`, data `:rf/self-id`, and any present `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/invoke-id`, and `:rf/join-child`. Registered keyword and inline-definition type references remain valid.
- Add one lifecycle assertion that an affected declarative child can still complete/tear down through its parent after recovery; if the implementation touches `:rf/join-child`, pin exact-attempt `:spawn-all` completion as well.
- Existing singleton compatibility behavior and trace shapes remain unchanged. Update the implementation/spec prose only where needed to state that reset replaces user state while retaining framework-owned actor identity.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor's backlog reread — CHECK 3, a reverted closure. THIRD instance today of the worker-close-mid-tick race, and the discrimination needed a different instrument this time.

WHY THE USUAL TEST WAS NOT AVAILABLE. For rf2-hic-064 and rf2-2hpxo the tell was a notes field unchanged across the newest snapshots. Here NOTES IS EMPTY — 0 characters in every snapshot — so "unchanged" would have been the null-hash trap: an absent field hashes constant and reports a clean walk in exactly the words a genuinely unchanged one does. Believing it would have been believing nothing.

SO I CONTROLLED AGAINST FIELDS THAT DO VARY ON THIS ITEM. The description holds at 7,847 characters and acceptance_criteria at 1,562 across the newest six snapshots, while 23 snapshots in the history DO carry status=closed — so the item was genuinely closed and the only thing that moved back is the status. Control on a bead that is closed and stayed closed (rf2-4thn) returns 19 closed snapshots by the same query, so the query discriminates.

NO AUDIT OBLIGATION. Greps for AUDIT-REOPEN, "REOPENED THIS EXACT", REOPENED, "residual" and "still owed" all return zero, against a control counting rf2- references that returns 1, so the instrument bites. Contrast rf2-c5w1 and rf2-o8ek, which reverted in the same window and DO carry REOPENED markers with residuals — those are audits and stay open. This one wrote nothing, because nothing reopened it.

THE DELIVERABLE IS ON MAIN, verified in the tree: PR #9192 reads state=MERGED, and `carry-actor-identity` resolves at tip in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc. The fix carried a real red witness — 17 assertion failures with the tests in place and the fix absent, 1244 tests / 4528 assertions green after — plus a 210-line snapshot-compat suite and the two-line spec/005 clarification at invariants 3 and 4. Nothing about this bead's output is missing.

MECHANISM, unchanged from the earlier two: the prescribed checkpoint-then-checkout ordering protects the MAYOR's own tracker mutations, because the checkpoint exports them before the checkout restores that same commit. It does not protect a WORKER's close landing between my checkpoint's export and my checkout. All three instances today fit that shape — a worker closed the bead, I verified CLOSED immediately after merging its PR, and a later tick found it open with its text intact.

STILL NOT PROPOSING A PROCESS CHANGE. Three re-closes across a session is cheaper than reordering a sequence that exists to prevent tracker time-travel, and check 3 catches every instance by design. What this one adds is the lesson that the discrimination must use a field that VARIES on the item in front of you — the notes-length test is not universal.

title: reagent-slim: ordinary after-render callbacks can precede the React 19 DOM commit
description:
## Correctness finding

`reagent2.core/after-render` promises to run after the next React commit, but reagent-slim's ordinary production microtask path can invoke the callback while React 19 still exposes the old DOM. This is a live-path ordering bug, not a request for broader Reagent compatibility.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/batching.cljs`: `RenderQueue.flush-queues` calls `ratom/flush!`, then `flush-render`, then `flush-after-render`. `flush-render` only invokes each dirty class's bare `.forceUpdate`; there is no React commit boundary or commit callback. Therefore "forceUpdate was requested" is treated as "React committed" before callbacks run.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs`: the `flush-render!` implementation and its load-bearing comment document the opposite React-19 fact: under `createRoot`, bare `forceUpdate` outside a React batching boundary is scheduled rather than committed, and the DOM remains OLD when `batching/flush!` returns. That is why `flush-render!` wraps the same drain in `react-dom/flushSync`. Commit `3d89c29c61` records the browser proof: the post-flush assertion read the old value without that boundary.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs`: public `after-render` says "after the next React commit" and routes to `batching/do-after-render`. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs` publishes that function as `:adapter/after-render`, so `re-frame.interop/after-render` reaches this exact queue.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md` §2.3/§2.9/§4 repeats the post-render contract, while `spec/002-Frames.md` names after-render effects as the canonical "show this, then run the heavy block" replacement for queue-pausing. `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs` also treats the adapter hook as post-commit/pre-paint for `:await-render`.
- Existing slim coverage does not exercise this boundary. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/batching_cljs_test.cljs` uses fake JS objects whose `forceUpdate` body runs synchronously, so its `[:render :after]` assertion proves call order only. `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/client_cljs_test.cljs` similarly uses fake components and/or `act`; `reagent_slim_flush_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs` tests the explicit `flushSync` API. `reagent_slim_late_bind_publication_cljs_test.cljs` pins hook publication, not DOM timing. There is no reagent-slim counterpart to the real-DOM post-commit assertion used by the React spine.
- Independent substrate comparison: the repository-pinned Reagent 2.0.1 `reagent.impl.batching/run-queue` wraps dirty component updates in an injected `react-flush`, and `reagent.dom.client/render` installs `react-dom/flushSync`; only after that wrapper returns does stock `flush-after-render` run. Slim copied the queue order but omitted the commit-bearing seam on its ordinary path.

## Concrete failure sequence and impact

A ratom/app-db change queues a slim component, and application or framework code queues an after-render callback. The shared microtask drains dependencies, calls bare `forceUpdate` (React schedules the class update), and immediately invokes the callback. The callback can read stale DOM. Worse, the documented long-running-work pattern can start its heavy block before React paints the requested "working" state, delaying the very feedback the API exists to provide. The Pair `:await-render` path is consequently founded on accidental later-rAF timing rather than the adapter hook's promised post-commit invariant.

## Recommended bounded fix

Make the ordinary scheduled queue defer `flush-after-render` until the dirty updates in that turn have actually committed. Keep `reagent2.impl.batching` host-neutral; a small client-installed commit wrapper (analogous to stock Reagent's `react-flush`) used when a pending after-render queue requires the guarantee is one plausible minimal shape. A reliable class-update commit callback is another. Let the real-DOM regression choose the smallest correct seam.

Preserve the current callback FIFO order, once-only drain, per-callback throw isolation, no-dirty callback behavior, next-turn cascade rule, and explicit `flush-render!`/`flush-views!` semantics. Reconcile the local docstrings/IMPL-SPEC only where they currently equate a bare `forceUpdate` call with a completed render.

## Posture and non-goals

This repair makes a retained minimal API tell the truth and directly supports responsive SPA feedback. Do not add a general scheduler abstraction, copy the React-spine driver-root machinery, expand the public API, emulate transitions/Suspense policy, or litigate arbitrary unmounted/cross-root edge cases. Do not globally force every ratom microtask synchronous merely as an easy workaround if a narrower commit-bearing path for queued after-render work preserves the intended React-19 concurrency.

## Duplicate and history search

Searched every current bead in every state across title, description, acceptance, design, and notes for `after-render`, `after render`, `flush-after-render`, `post-commit`, `commit phase`, `forceUpdate`, `stale DOM`, `React commit`, `microtask`, and reagent-slim/render variants. The only `after-render` matches were closed `rf2-6r9j.33` (stale IMPL-SPEC architecture prose) and closed `rf2-6r9j.44` (an unrelated SSR response parameter); neither owns runtime commit timing. Broader matches were unrelated surfaces. Git history searches for `flush-after-render`, `after-render`, `forceUpdate`, and `flushSync` found: initial scheduler commit `1d621015bd`, callback-throw isolation `a834ab9bbd`, and explicit synchronous `flush-render!` repair `3d89c29c61`; none repairs or tests the ordinary microtask path. The UIx post-commit work (`e616aabbbd` and shared-suite tests) is a different substrate implementation.

## Uncertainty

No new browser bundle was built in this review-only worker because the assigned worktree intentionally has no `node_modules` link and no source/test edits were authorized. The stale-DOM timing is nevertheless independently established by the current control flow, the stock-Reagent implementation, and this repository's prior React-19 browser failure/fix in `3d89c29c61`. The exact narrowest repair seam remains intentionally open; the required real-DOM ordinary-path test below resolves it behaviorally.
design: Favor the smallest commit-aware seam that keeps the queue node-safe and preserves ordinary concurrent behavior when no post-commit callback is pending. A client-installed wrapper around the dirty-component phase is worth testing because stock Reagent already demonstrates that shape; if used, avoid unnecessary `flushSync` on queue turns without after-render work and avoid double-drain/nested-boundary surprises under the existing explicit `flush-render!`. Acceptance is behavioral rather than prescribing that mechanism.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_after_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (or an equivalently named reagent-slim browser test) that installs the slim adapter, mounts a ratom/subscription-backed view through `reagent2.dom.client/create-root` + `render`, commits the initial value, changes the value, and calls `re-frame.interop/after-render`.
- In the callback, read the mounted node's `textContent` and prove it contains the new value; also assert the callback fires exactly once. The test must assert the old DOM before the scheduler turn so a synchronous mutation cannot make it vacuous.
- The regression must exercise the ordinary queued microtask path. It must not use `reagent2.dom.client/flush-views!`, adapter `flush-render!`, `react/act`, a manual `react-dom/flushSync` around the update/drain, or an extra `requestAnimationFrame` before the callback assertion, because each masks the defect.
- On the pre-fix implementation the test fails specifically because the callback observes the old committed DOM while the class update is only scheduled. On the fix it observes the new DOM after the actual commit under the repository's React 19 floor.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/batching.cljs` preserves callback FIFO/once-only/throw isolation, callbacks scheduled with no dirty component still fire asynchronously, and components queued during a drain remain for the next turn.
- `reagent_slim_flush_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, the focused batching tests, the slim node tests, and browser tests remain green. Any changed contract prose in `reagent2.core`, `batching.cljs`, or `IMPL-SPEC.md` agrees that after-render means post-commit, not merely after calling `forceUpdate`.
- The implementation stays private and bounded: no new public symbol and no broad React-spine/scheduler redesign.
notes: Review scope was `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/**`; consumers/spec/history were read only to establish contract and impact. No tracked file was edited, no test artifact was created, and no bead was updated. Evidence is source/history-based with the remaining uncertainty explicitly captured in the description.
close_reason: CONFIRMED and FIXED. The premise held and was measured, not reasoned: on a real React 19 createRoot root, ordinary microtask path with no test primitive driving it, an after-render callback registered after a dispatch taking n=1 to n=2 was handed n=1. RenderQueue.flush-queues called ratom/flush!, then each dirty component's bare .forceUpdate, then the callbacks, with no commit boundary; under React 19 an update issued outside React's batching context is scheduled, not committed. Fix: the dirty-component pass now runs inside a host commit boundary that reagent2.dom.client INJECTS into reagent2.impl.batching/render-commit at ns-load (react-dom/flushSync), the same direction reagent2.ratom/rea-schedule is filled, so batching keeps requiring nothing of react-dom and a Node/SSR consumer without the DOM client keeps the bare drain. Gated on there actually being a callback waiting, so an ordinary reactive re-render is not promoted to discrete priority. Witness: reagent_slim_after_render_dom_cljs_test.cljs reads textContent from INSIDE the callback and asserts the OLD DOM between dispatch and callback so a synchronous commit could not satisfy it vacuously; no flush-views!, flush-render!, act, manual flushSync around the update/drain, or rAF before the read. Fails before (browser lane exit 1, one failure, actual (not (= "n=2" "n=1"))) and passes after (792 tests / 4280 assertions, 0 failures, same totals). FIFO, once-only, throw isolation, fire-with-nothing-dirty and next-turn cascade preserved and pinned. No new public symbol. spec/002-Frames.md and the pair-MCP dispatch.cljs were NOT changed: both already describe the hook as post-commit, which the repair makes true rather than prose needing revision. :advanced release (bundle-isolation) 0 warnings. PR #9209.

title: surface-review(reagent-adapter): rethrow the first teardown failure after draining every reaction and root
description:
## Scope

Correct the stock Reagent adapter-wide teardown path, with the shared ratom-spine helper changed only where needed: `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs` (`spine-fns`, `dispose-once!`, and the adapter map), `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs` (`dispose-frame-sub-caches!`, `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!`, and `make-ratom-spine`'s `dispose-adapter!`), plus focused stock-Reagent lifecycle tests under `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/`. Keep the one shared drain rather than forking a Reagent-only copy.

## Correctness finding

The stock Reagent adapter does the good half of best-effort teardown—attempting sibling cached-Reaction disposals and sibling root unmounts—but silently discards every failure. `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` catches each disposer throw as `_` and returns `nil`; `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!` does the same for every `unmount-op`. Consequently `rf/destroy-adapter!` reports clean success even though adapter-owned cleanup failed. This directly contradicts Spec 006's current lifecycle rule: attempt all remaining cleanup, preserve and rethrow the first failure, and attach or report later failures as secondary evidence.

This is not a request to stop at the first throw. The required invariant is **drain everything, finalize ownership, then surface the original first failure**.

## Verified evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1470-1519` documents and implements the frame sub-cache walk. Lines 1517-1518 are `(try (dispose-reaction! r) (catch :default _ nil))`; the exception is irretrievably dropped before the caller can see it.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1521-1547` is the shared adapter drain. Lines 1542-1544 catch and drop every root-unmount failure, then lines 1545-1546 clear active-root ownership and the emitter and line 1547 returns `nil`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3539-3545,3657-3660` shows the stock Reagent ratom spine owns those exact cells and delegates its entire `dispose-adapter!` to that helper.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:88-113` injects guarded stock `Reaction` construction/disposal and `reagent.dom.client/unmount` into that spine. `dispose-once!` correctly preserves a throw from stock `ratom/dispose!`; the shared outer catch is what erases it.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:230-257` already provides the right process boundary: it invokes the adapter disposer in a `try/finally`, clears the claimed generation even if cleanup throws, and naturally rethrows the adapter's exact failure. The Reagent drain prevents that tested/public mechanism from ever seeing its failures.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2613-2624` publicly promises that `destroy-adapter!` marks the adapter disposed and then rethrows the primary cleanup failure.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:320-337` requires every resource to be attempted, caches/claims to be cleared in a finally-shaped boundary, the first failure to be rethrown, and later failures to be attached or reported.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/dispose_adapter_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs:144-188` already builds the decisive stock-adapter witness: a poison cached entry throws while real reactions in the same and later frame are still disposed and both caches are cleared. Line 179 currently expects `adapter/dispose-adapter!` to return normally, so the test pins only sibling progress and accidentally codifies disappearance of the primary error.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/spine_dispose_cljs_test.cljs:54-76,185-209` likewise proves sibling drains but never asserts the promised post-drain rethrow. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/boot_test.clj:163-187` separately proves the core preserves exact cleanup-error identity and terminal lifecycle state when an adapter actually lets a failure escape.
- The adapter README recommends Form-3 wrappers for imperative libraries and says cleanup is mandatory (`implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:23-42,94-101`). Silent teardown failure makes the shutdown/test-fixture boundary claim success precisely when application or host cleanup has malfunctioned.

## Impact / concrete failure scenario

A test or hot-reload fixture installs the stock Reagent adapter, creates subscriptions in multiple frames, and registers a user/framework on-dispose hook that throws. During `rf/destroy-adapter!`, the throwing Reaction is terminally marked and its error reaches `dispose-frame-sub-caches!`; other cached Reactions and roots are still attempted and ownership cells are cleared, but the original exception is dropped. The caller sees `nil`, so the fixture, reload tool, or programmer cannot distinguish clean shutdown from a failed cleanup and may continue after listeners or an imperative host resource failed to release.

The same masking exists when the injected root unmount operation throws. Whether React has already detached some host state is host-specific; the certain defect is that the adapter reports success despite the observed cleanup failure.

## Recommended bounded change

At the existing shared drain chokepoint, capture cleanup failures by **presence**, continue every Reaction and root attempt, clear each sub-cache plus `active-roots-cell` and `emitter-cell` in finally-shaped cleanup, then rethrow the first captured value unchanged. Reuse the spine's existing private `capture-none` identity sentinel (or an equally explicit sentinel), because CLJS may throw `nil` or `false`; a truthiness accumulator would recreate a silent-failure hole. Retain later failures as secondary diagnostic evidence using the project's existing diagnostic/attachment convention without replacing or wrapping the first failure.

Keep the direct zero-argument test seam compatible if it has a distinct caller contract; an optional accumulator/result between `dispose-frame-sub-caches!` and `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!` is preferable to duplicating the walk. Do not retry a consumed Reaction/root and do not add a supervisor, rollback transaction, or root registry.

## Acceptance criteria

- Update the stock-Reagent poison-entry proof so `rf/destroy-adapter!` throws the identical sentinel error **after** the real cached Reactions in the same and later frames have been disposed and every involved sub-cache is `{}`.
- Add a stock-Reagent root proof with one throwing injected `rdc/unmount` and at least one healthy sibling: every snapshot root is attempted exactly once, active-root ownership and the emitter are cleared, and the identical primary failure reaches the caller only after the drain.
- With more than one cleanup failure, the first encountered value stays the thrown primary and later failures are attached or emitted as secondary evidence; `nil`/`false` thrown values are captured by presence rather than lost.
- After either failure, `adapter/current-adapter-spec` is `nil`, `adapter/adapter-disposed?` is true, public delegation reports `:rf.error/adapter-disposed`, and a fresh `rf/init!` can install a new generation.
- Happy teardown still returns `nil`; empty frames/roots remain no-op-safe; existing stock-Reagent exactly-once Reaction disposal and client-root idempotence tests remain green.
- Non-vacuity: on the pre-fix implementation the new primary-error assertion fails because the call returns `nil`, while counters still prove sibling cleanup ran. Record that red control and then restore/apply the fix.
- Run the focused stock-Reagent CLJS adapter lifecycle lane plus the shared spine/core lifecycle tests that cover the helper and process finalization.

## Non-goals

- No change to callback registration order, the landed exactly-once marker (`rf2-rzeko`), or isolation among multiple callbacks inside one native Reagent `Reaction` disposal.
- No retry/recovery protocol for a root or Reaction whose teardown threw, no async-settlement machinery, and no new public API.
- No Reagent 1.x or React 18 compatibility work.
- No redesign of UIx, reagent-slim, Test-React, frame destruction, or application Form-3 lifecycle policy. The shared helper should remain contract-consistent for its existing callers, but this bead's regression proof and reviewed product surface are stock Reagent.

## Posture rationale

This is a small correction at an existing lifecycle chokepoint, not gold plating. Best-effort cleanup and loud failure complement each other: drain siblings for robustness, then trust the programmer with the original error so tests and tools do not claim success falsely. It preserves the minimal adapter API and removes friction from diagnosing real SPA teardown bugs.

## Duplicate and history research

Searched the complete 913-bead corpus across all statuses (title, description, notes, acceptance, and close reason) and repeated final `bd search` checks for `reagent teardown failure`, `dispose active roots`, `sub-cache cleanup error`, and `rethrow first cleanup`; no bead owns this outcome. Exact symbol/phrase searches for `dispose-active-roots-and-caches!`, `dispose-frame-sub-caches!`, `unmount ... swallow`, `cleanup failure`, `first failure`, and `secondary diagnostic` found no matching adapter-drain task. `rf2-rzeko` is closed and distinct: it made one stock Reaction's callbacks exactly-once and explicitly excluded general callback-exception isolation. `rf2-k5r9t` is closed and distinct: it added the reusable client-root lifecycle/idempotent explicit unmount, not adapter-wide failure propagation.

History confirms the defect is still live rather than already repaired: `df8aad1215` introduced per-entry swallow for the unified sub-cache walk; `1ae9c8846c` consolidated root draining with per-root swallow; `2d51830e37` then ratified terminal adapter destruction and the first-failure rule in Spec 006 while retaining both swallow catches. Later stock-Reagent disposal work (`rf2-rzeko`) changed only exactly-once behavior. Current HEAD `1ad17a77fe123bc233a88b89335dcf48196500c1` still contains both catches and the tests above still expect normal return.

## Uncertainties

- React/Reagent may have performed part or all of a particular host teardown before an unmount error escapes; do not claim rollback or infer host settlement. Surface the observed error after local ownership is finalized.
- Spec 006 intentionally permits later failures to be either attached or reported. Choose the smallest established project mechanism; do not invent a new user-facing error taxonomy solely for this fix.
- The active-root set does not promise semantic insertion order. The primary is the first failure in the actual snapshot traversal; tests should avoid depending on a different ordering contract.
notes:
PR #9201 audit reopened this exact owner: the shared Reaction/active-root drain now captures and rethrows correctly, but make-dispose-adapter! still catches and discards an exception from the separately owned singleton after-render driver root at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1716-1719. That root is a host-specific resource outside active-roots-cell. If its unmount is the only failure, destroy-adapter! still reports clean nil; if the shared drain already failed, the driver-root failure is not attached as secondary evidence. Both violate Spec 006 lines 320-350 and contradict the PR/README claim that every teardown failure is audible. Keep one teardown transaction across the shared drain and layered cleanup, then rethrow only after the driver-root attempt and ownership resets. Add driver-root-only and shared-primary-plus-driver-secondary witnesses; preserve primary identity and continued finalization.


--- 2026-09-05 08:5x AUSEST, reagteardown-a dispatch: REAGENT SURFACE IS DONE; REMNANT IS OUT OF THE REAGENT FENCE ---

Dispatched to implement this on the Reagent adapter. Measured at tip 82c1361993: there is NO
remaining Reagent-surface work, and the live remnant this bead was reopened for is NOT on the
Reagent teardown path at all. No code change made; no PR opened.

1. WHICH HALF WAS WRONG: neither, on Reagent. PR #9201 (MERGED 2026-09-04T14:57:03Z) landed the

   Corroborated three ways: the reagent adapter requires make-ratom-spine; its :after-render is

3. EVERY REAGENT ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS ALREADY MET, and the witness is NOT vacuous. Proven by a

   11220 tests / 56708 assertions, 0 failures. Planted: exit 1, 10 failures + 2 errors, of which

4. THE #9212 FUNNEL HYPOTHESIS DOES NOT APPLY. frame.cljc safe-call-hook! / safe-teardown-step! /

LEAVING THIS BEAD OPEN. Re-dispatch the remnant under a core + UIx fence, not a reagent one:
make-dispose-adapter! should thread the shared accumulator through its finally-shaped layered
teardown so the driver-root unmount failure becomes primary when it is the only failure and

close_reason:
Both halves are now on a PR. The Reagent half was PR #9201 (merged 2026-09-04): the shared drain in dispose-active-roots-and-caches! got make-teardown-failures / record-teardown-failure! / rethrow-teardown-failure!, presence-keyed on capture-none, with later failures attached to the rethrown primary via the rfAdapterTeardownSecondaryErrors string expando. The previous carrier verified that half is complete and its witnesses non-vacuous, and correctly identified that the live remnant was NOT on the Reagent path at all.

This bead's remnant — the swallowed singleton after-render DRIVER ROOT unmount in make-dispose-adapter! — is PR #9254. That is the UIx half: make-dispose-adapter! is built only by make-react-spine, which serves the UIx adapter and Hicasso's substrate; stock Reagent and reagent-slim use make-ratom-spine, whose whole dispose IS the shared drain (no warn-cache, no driver root). The ratom path is untouched by #9254.

What #9254 does: dispose-active-roots-and-caches! gains a five-arg arity that records into the CALLER's accumulator without rethrowing (the four-arg arity is behaviourally unchanged, so the ratom family keeps exactly what #9201 gave it), and make-dispose-adapter! owns one accumulator across the shared drain and its layered warn-cache / driver-root / set-tick teardown, rethrowing once after every ownership reset. Two nested accumulators would not compose: the inner rethrow attaches its secondaries to the primary and an outer one would overwrite the same expando with only its own, dropping the shared drain's evidence.

The primacy rule the note asked for is explicit in code and PR body, and it is asymmetric: a driver-root failure that is the ONLY failure becomes the PRIMARY and surfaces (a clean nil over a React root that never released is the silent hole Spec 006 MUST (2) forbids), while one arriving after the shared drain already failed becomes a SECONDARY on the primary's expando (the earlier failure names the real fault; attachment never wraps or replaces). The old bare catch got the second case right by accident and the first wrong every time.

No spec change was needed or made: Spec 006's existing "attempt every step under its own boundary, keep the first thrown value by PRESENCE, finalize ownership, and only then rethrow" already covers the driver-root unmount as a teardown step. The code was behind the spec.

Witnesses: three tests in implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/spine_dispose_cljs_test.cljs (driver-root-only primary; shared-primary-plus-driver-secondary; falsey throw captured by presence), each separating DRAIN from RETHROW assertions. Proven live by TWO complementary plants: restoring the bare catch gives exit 1 / 5 failures with every DRAIN assertion green and only RETHROW failing; removing the guard so the throw escapes the finally gives exit 1 / 9 failures with test 1's DRAIN failing and its RETHROW green. The halves fail for different reasons in both directions.

Gates: npm run test:cljs exit 0, 11223 tests / 56725 assertions, 0 failures (+3 tests / +17 assertions over the 11220 / 56708 baseline, matching the new deftests exactly), re-run on the final rebased base. npm run build:hicasso-release exit 0, 0 warnings — the :advanced / :infer-externs :auto gate for the .unmount interop, which shadow-cljs.edn records as the only Closure-optimised compile these namespaces get and whose comment names core's spine.cljs. npm run test:hicasso-compile exit 0, 11 namespaces, zero warnings. npm run test:browser does NOT cover these tests and was not claimed: :browser-test binds :ns-regexp ".*-dom-cljs-test$" and this namespace ends -cljs-test; no real React root is needed, since the spine only invokes .unmount on whatever occupies the cell.

title: hic: §13's two canonical tables are written over a native tier that no longer ships — reconcile or re-state the bullets
description:
Filed by the rf2-hic-064 §13 definition-of-done audit (2026-09-04, main@aa0ee76ae4). Measured at source, not inherited.

THE ARTEFACT. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc is 82 lines and defines exactly TWO public names — use-frame and use-sub. Its own ns docstring states the end state: 'The two React hooks that join a React island to the Hicasso frame it is mounted in ... and nothing else. An island is a UIx defui or a raw React function component, mounted through h/defhost or [:>].' That is rf2-6c12m.3's ruling (option A) executed. n/$, n/props, n/defcomponent, n/memo and n/lazy do not exist.

THE DOCUMENTS §13 NAMES. Two §13 bullets cite a canonical table by link, and both tables are still written over the retired grammar:
  * bullet 7 cites lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md#public-surface-ssrhydration-matrix — 4 lines still carry the retired names, including the two matrix ROWS 'Intrinsic n/$ form' and 'n/defcomponent, component-headed n/$, memo/lazy/ref helpers'.
  * bullet 11 cites lanes/hot-path-architecture.md#canonical-native-tier-acceptance-checklist and says 'Every row ... passes; no partial parity result substitutes for that checklist' — 8 lines still carry them, including the Native-form grammar row ('the provisional n/$ grammar handles omitted and literal props, explicit n/props dynamic maps/objects ...') and the Component ABI row ('One raw-JavaScript props/children ABI survives n/defcomponent, memo, lazy loading, ref forwarding').
specification.md itself carries 8 such lines, at :132-134 (the §4 facade table rows for n/$, n/props and n/defcomponent), :139, :180, :203, :209 and :353.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT A TIDY-UP. §13 bullets 7 and 11 cannot be scored as written: their subjects do not exist. A reader of the definition of done is told to check a checklist whose first two rows are about a grammar the package does not have, and told that no partial result substitutes for it. Bullet 6's 'same-root native islands' is in the same position. The rf2-6c12m campaign was explicitly authorised to shrink the runtime; nothing in it was asked to restate the definition of done, and no bead carries that.

WHERE THE TEACHING CORPUS ALREADY IS. docs/core/hicasso/ carries ZERO occurrences of the retired names — the guide was swept. dispositions.md carries zero as well. So the drift is confined to the specification and its two lane tables, which is the small end of the repair and the load-bearing end of the harm.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is not a request to re-adjudicate any verdict. Checkpoint 3's Phase 3 verdict stands as the record of what was measured on 2026-08-14; this is about the tables the CURRENT definition of done points a reader at.
acceptance_criteria: lanes/hot-path-architecture.md's canonical native-tier acceptance checklist and lanes/react-compatibility-notes.md's public-surface SSR/hydration matrix each state, at the top and in their affected rows, which rows describe a surface retired by rf2-6c12m.3 and what is owed of the two-hook tier that replaced it; specification.md §4's facade table no longer publishes n/$, n/props or n/defcomponent as shipped names without saying they are retired; and §13 bullets 6, 7 and 11 are either restated over the surviving surface or annotated with what they now mean. Exact-phrase search of the remote ledger found no separate owner; rf2-aunp already owns these three canonical documents and this retirement reconciliation.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-05 by the mayor's backlog reread — CHECK 3, a reverted closure. FOURTH instance this session, and the SECOND time this particular bead has come back, which is exactly why the discrimination had to be sharpened rather than repeated.

WHY THE MARKER TEST WAS NOT ENOUGH HERE, and this is the refinement worth keeping. This bead carries a REOPENED marker — but that marker is from its FIRST reopen (the audit of PR #9184, which hicnative-a then serviced in PR #9193). A grep for reopen markers therefore returns a hit on a bead whose CURRENT transition wrote nothing. Stale evidence from an earlier round reads exactly like fresh evidence for this one. On a bead that has been through a chain, "does it carry a REOPENED marker" is the wrong question.

THE TEST THAT ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATES: compare the notes length ACROSS THE REOPEN BOUNDARY, not across the newest N snapshots. Walk the history newest-first, find the first snapshot whose status is `closed`, and compare it with its immediate newer neighbour — that pair IS the transition. For this bead: idx39=closed/notes=1045, idx38=open/notes=1045. Identical. The status moved and not one character was written. Compare rf2-r9kf, reverted in the same window, where the same probe reads idx22=closed/notes=4369 → idx21=open/notes=5521: 1152 characters added BY the reopen, which is an audit writing its reason. That one stays open and is real work.

Note also why "notes unchanged across the newest four" was insufficient: both beads read unchanged over that window, because both had settled since their transition. The window has to be anchored to the boundary, not to the head.

NO AUDIT OBLIGATION ON THIS TRANSITION. Nothing was added, so there is nothing owed. The first reopen's residual — Hicasso-native still presented as a third component-authoring route across hot-path-architecture.md, specification.md and react-compatibility-notes.md — was serviced by PR #9193 (merged): 12 files amended, every passage restated with an italic note giving its former wording, the ruling and the date, plus three live checklist rows and two stale witness citations the first pass had left.
