title: test(realworld-http): correlate the profile-follow rollback assertion and add the held-transport stale-profile witness (blocks PR #9236)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-8icg, whose example-side fix is PR #9236
(https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9236). Both halves below live in
implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs, which was
FENCED for the rf2-8icg dispatch (a peer was live in that tree), so the worker did
not reach in and reported instead.

## 1. BLOCKING — one line, without which PR #9236 cannot merge

realworld_cljs_test.cljs:2896, inside profile-follow-test, dispatches the rollback
with no issuing identity:

    (rf/dispatch-sync [:profile/follow-rollback true {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx}] {:frame f})

rf2-8icg makes every profile settle carry the username it was issued for, so this
needs:

    (rf/dispatch-sync [:profile/follow-rollback "eve" true {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx}] {:frame f})

Measured on the fix branch: npm run test:cljs exits 1 with
"Ran 11208 tests containing 56567 assertions. 1 failures, 0 errors." — that one
failure, at 2897:9, expected (true? ...) actual (not (true? false)). It is the
gate working: username binds to `true`, does not match the slice's "eve", and the
write is correctly refused.

This is NOT a mechanical arity bump some other fix could dodge. The assertion's
premise is a rollback that is a pure function of its args with NO identity, which
is exactly the defect rf2-8icg names. Any correct correlation of that handler
changes this dispatch.

Nothing else in the suite moved. profile-load-test and the rest of
profile-follow-test drive through :rf.route/handle-url-change, so the slices are
stamped from the route and the canned settles correlate. A whole-repo search found
no other reference to any changed event id.

## 2. The regression witness rf2-8icg's acceptance criteria 1 and 6 ask for

Not written, for the same fence. Deterministic held-transport CLJS coverage,
patterned on the same suite's held-request cross-slug tests (around lines
1900-2130):

- alice -> bob across banner, authored and favorites requests; settle bob first,
  then alice success and failure. Alice must not change bob's data, status, error,
  timestamps or machine presentation.
- Non-vacuity: the corresponding current-bob success/failure IS accepted; a late
  prior-profile failure cannot strand the :ui/profile :data region in :error, and
  current success presents loaded data.
- While bob is pending, previously settled alice banner/list data is not exposed
  under bob's route. Note the cross-tab case specifically: /profile/alice ->
  /profile/bob/favorites reloads the banner and the favorited list and leaves the
  AUTHORED list holding alice, which the read-time guard in
  :profile.articles/data + :profile.articles/count is what covers.
- Hold an alice follow/unfollow, navigate to bob, settle alice: neither success
  nor rollback mutates bob; current-profile settlements still work.
- Red negative control: remove or invert reply-for-current-profile?, see red,
  restore, see green.

Sequence this behind whatever peer work holds implementation/adapters/**, or lift
the fence if that tree is clear. Filed 2026-09-05 06:04:05 AUSEST.
close_reason:
Both halves done on branch worker/rwhttp-a, commit d018c67059, pushed to
PR #9236 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9236), which stays DRAFT for
the mayor. One file touched:
implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs
(+301/-1). The rf2-8icg production fix was NOT touched: git diff 6890a1f564
HEAD names only the test file.

## 1. THE BLOCKING LINE — diagnosis confirmed at source, not merely trusted

realworld_cljs_test.cljs:2896 dispatched
[:profile/follow-rollback true {:kind :rf.http/http-4xx}]. Against the new
4-arity handler, `username` binds `true`, `previous-value` binds the failure
map, reply-for-current-profile? asks (= true "eve") -> false, and the write is
correctly refused, so :following stays false from the preceding
:profile/unfollowed and (true? false) fails. The bead's reading is exactly
right: the failure IS the fix working.

## 2. THE COVERAGE DECISION, and why it is not the one the brief offered

The brief offered keeping the identity-free dispatch as a NEGATIVE test. I did
NOT, and the reason is that after rf2-8icg an identity-free dispatch is no
longer a stale reply — it is a MALFORMED one. It only "fails" because `true`
lands in the username slot; it exercises argument shape, not the correlation
law, and pinning it would pin an accident. The meaningful negative is a
WELL-FORMED settle for a profile the slice no longer targets, which no
hand-dispatch of a single handler can stage honestly.

So the existing assertion got its identity ("eve") and kept its job — the
rollback restores the captured prior flag — and the refusal it had been
witnessing by accident is now pinned deliberately, and far wider, by a new
deftest `realworld-profile-page-cross-username`. That is the brief's option (b)
"strictly more coverage", reached through a stale reply rather than a malformed
one. It is modelled on this same suite's `realworld-article-page-cross-slug`
(rf2-iy3d6) and delivers rf2-8icg's acceptance criteria 1, 2, 3 and 4:

- cross-username late SUCCESS refused: /profile/alice -> /profile/bob holds
  four reads open; asserts all four request-ids DISTINCT (so managed HTTP's
  same-id supersede never fires between them and correlating is the app's job);
  asserts the username rides all four reply targets; settles bob; then settles
  alice late and compares bob's :profile and :profile.articles slices WHOLE —
  data, status, error, loaded-at, attempt, username — plus the grand count.
- cross-username late FAILURE refused, which is the STRAND: alice fails while
  bob is still :loading, the :data region stays :data/loading rather than
  reaching :error (a state with no fetch-succeeded edge), and bob's own success
  then renders :loaded. Non-vacuity: carol's OWN banner and authored failures
  ARE accepted, reaching :error with the message surfaced.
- identity change vs refresh, plus the READ-TIME half: a same-username re-load
  is a :fetching refresh that keeps rows up; /profile/alice ->
  /profile/bob/favorites reloads exactly the banner and the favorited list,
  issues NO authored request, and leaves the authored slice legitimately
  holding alice's rows while :profile.articles/data, /count and
  :profile/current-articles all refuse to expose or count them under bob.
- held alice FOLLOW refused on BOTH branches — success (which re-seeds the
  whole banner map) and rollback — while bob's own follow success and his own
  rollback are both accepted.

## 3. CRITERION 6, done stronger than asked

The bead asked for the guard to be inverted. Instead the WHOLE production
change was reverted (profile.cljs + schema.cljs restored to the merge base,
973c26fdc7, which is byte-identical to origin/main on those paths) with the
tests left in place. Quoting captured .exit files, never a harness report:

  WITH the fix:    exit 0 — "Ran 11209 tests containing 56614 assertions.
                   0 failures, 0 errors."
  WITHOUT the fix: exit 1 — "Ran 11209 tests containing 56614 assertions.
                   23 failures, 0 errors."
                   1 in realworld-favorites-follow-feed (the repaired line),
                   22 in realworld-profile-page-cross-username.

Identical test and assertion totals both ways, so nothing dropped out of the
build; 23 assertions flip. Baseline for comparison: CI on the un-repaired
branch read 11208 / 56567 with 1 failure, so this adds 1 test and 47
assertions.

Restored from a byte-copy taken before the revert, verified three ways: cmp
against the copy (byte-identical, both files), git diff HEAD empty on those
paths, and git diff --quiet clean after resetting the index the checkout had
staged.

## 4. SIBLING CENSUS — one site, and the census was controlled

All NINE settle handlers the fix re-arity'd (:profile/loaded,
/load-failed, :profile.articles/loaded, /load-failed,
:profile.favorites/loaded, /load-failed, :profile/followed, /unfollowed,
/follow-rollback) were searched repo-wide with the ripgrep-backed tool, not
Bash grep. The pattern returned NON-zero (many hits), so the zero is
controlled. Exactly ONE test-suite dispatch of any of them existed: line 2896.
The other eight are only ever driven through the production request builder, so
they carry the identity automatically. A second axis (`dispatch(-sync)? [:profile`
across implementation/) found only :profile/initialise, :profile/show-page,
:profile/follow and :profile/unfollow — all unchanged arity — plus unrelated
:profile/rename (flows) and :profile/go-to-page (resources). The only other
repo hit is docs/EP/EP-0002 line 727, an unrelated illustrative snippet in a
different app. So the peer's "bead named two, found four" pattern does not
apply here: it named one and there is one.

## 5. ONE DELIBERATE STOP, stated rather than hidden

There is no late-alice FAVORITES settle. :profile.favorites/loaded and
/load-failed are gated by the identical call —
(reply-for-current-profile? db :profile.favorites username) — that
:profile.articles/* uses, and that path is witnessed end to end on both the
success and failure branches; the favorites slice is additionally covered by
the cross-tab read-time test. A third copy of an already-witnessed code path is
the gold-plating the project posture warns against, so I stopped. Flagging it
rather than filing a bead; reopen if you want the symmetry.

## 6. INSTRUMENT NOTE worth keeping

The harness reported "exit code 0" for FIVE background runs whose own .exit
file read 1. Every number above is from the .exit file.

Separately, the reverted-tree run aborted FOUR times with
"aborted par-compile ... still waiting for" before producing a verdict — the
rf2-6t03c symptom (shadow-cljs 60s :par-timeout under box load). It is not a
compile error: the aborted namespace set differed every run, never involved
realworld, and a --config-merge run with :par-timeout raised compiled clean at
1900 files / 0 warnings. compile-node-test.cjs did its job — it cleared
out/node-test.js each time, so no stale bundle ever ran. Note for anyone
tempted by that workaround: --config-merge also clears the build cache AFTER
compiling, which removes the cljs-runtime files the dev bundle loads at run
time, so the compile succeeds and then `node out/node-test.js` dies with ENOENT
on goog.debug.error.js. Retry the plain command instead; the script's own
comment says as much.

title: spec(004B): the ismap row is falsified against react-dom 19.2; record the boolean value disposition
description:
004B §Booleans and their neighbours names `ismap` in the boolean-attribute set explicitly — "the set is the react-dom/server 19.2.0 boolean-attribute list, probed row-by-row (S1b) — it includes `hidden`, `muted`, and `ismap` (React 19 dropped the camel `isMap` prop)". MEASURED AGAINST THE INSTALLED react-dom 19.2.0, THAT ROW IS FALSE. A boolean `ismap` is not a boolean-class attribute in react-dom 19.2 at all: - `pushAttribute` has no `case "ismap"` / `case "isMap"`, so a boolean falls into the default branch, where a boolean survives only behind a `data-`/`aria-` prefix. It is DROPPED. - The dev build's `validateProperty` boolean case list does not carry it either: `
` warns "Received `true` for a non-boolean attribute `ismap`" and emits nothing. - Measured directly: `renderToStaticMarkup(React.createElement('div', {ismap: true}))` → `
`; same for `false`; same for the camel `isMap`. `hidden` and `muted`, the row's two other named members, ARE correct — both presence-serialise. Only `ismap` is wrong. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is NOT obviously a defect to fix by deleting the name: `ismap` is a genuine HTML boolean attribute on ``, so presence IS the HTML-correct rendering, and react-dom simply does not support a boolean spelling for it. What is unsettled is whether 004B's conversion table tracks HTML or tracks react-dom where the two part. 004B declares itself the react-dom 19.2.0 list, which says remove it; the attribute's own HTML semantics say keep it. That is a spec decision, not an implementation one. STATE ON MAIN. `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers/boolean-attrs` still carries `"ismap"`, following 004B, and `re-frame.ssr-boolean-attr-react-parity-test` records the divergence explicitly (in `divergences`, with the reasoning) and PINS it — the test asserts both that react-dom's evidence carries no `ismap` row and that `boolean-attr-class` says `:presence` — so whichever way this is ruled, the test names the place to change and cannot drift silently. SECOND, SMALLER ITEM ON THE SAME TABLE. 004B does not mention react-dom's generic boolean `value` grouping at all. react-dom stringifies a boolean `value` (`value="true"`) because `value` shares a serialiser branch with `contentEditable`/`draggable`/`spellCheck`, not because it is booleanish. rf2-r9kf disposed of it from the SSR side — `value` stays `:ordinary`, because a string or number `value` (the only kinds a form control carries) serialises identically under the ordinary rule, a boolean `value` on a form control is an author error rather than a state, and `value` is already a 004B form-control special form whose meaning varies per element (`` attribute, `
close_reason: Fixed on PR #9215. READING TAKEN: 004B is describing REACT, not HTML — the row scopes itself in its own words ("the set is the react-dom/server 19.2.0 boolean-attribute list, probed row-by-row (S1b)") and cites a probe, so the HTML-vs-React scoping alternative is refuted by the text rather than left open. Outcome (1): 004B was wrong about React's behaviour. MEASURED against installed react-dom 19.2.0, stronger than the bead recorded: the string 'ismap'/'isMap' appears NOWHERE in react-dom 19.2.0's dev builds (0 occurrences in react-dom-server-legacy.node.development.js, react-dom-server.node.development.js and react-dom-client.development.js), so it is absent from possibleStandardNames — the probe's own candidate source — and there was no ismap boolean for React 19 to have 'dropped the camel isMap prop' of; the name could never have come from the S1b probe. Direct probe: div/img ismap={true} and {false} and camel isMap={true} all emit NOTHING (dev warns 'Received true for a non-boolean attribute ismap'; camel warns as an unrecognized prop), while a STRING ismap="" DOES reach markup on — via the pass-through default, react-dom's only route for it. Fixture regenerates byte-identical modulo CRLF, carries no ismap row, carries value="true"/value="false". REPAIR: the wrong part is the PROVENANCE, not the classification, so ismap stays presence-class (a genuine HTML boolean attribute on ; ismap="false" reads truthy) and 004B now RULES that the table tracks HTML where the two part on a real HTML boolean attribute, stating the divergence at the row with the former wording preserved in a dated italic note per the established convention. NO downstream consumer changes: boolean-attrs already carried "ismap", boolean-attr-class already returned :presence, the parity test already pinned it — this documents what the tree already does, so the 004B contract-change STOP did not trigger. Also recorded the value disposition in the same table as a named non-member (:ordinary, rf2-r9kf's reasoning), and updated 011's now-stale 'that is 004B's row to rule on' deferral plus the html_helpers docstring and the parity test's divergences note, which all recorded an open question and now record a ruling. title: surface-review(http): thread the destroying frame into the actor-destroy HTTP abort hook
description:
## Scope

Close the remaining half of rf2-o8ek: make an actor destroy abort only the
destroying FRAME's in-flight managed HTTP. rf2-o8ek landed the registry half
(the actor index is keyed [frame-id actor-id] and `registry/abort-on-actor-
destroy` has a frame-bearing 2-arity); what remains is threading the frame at
the two hook CALL SITES, which live outside the http artefact.

## Why it was not done in rf2-o8ek

rf2-o8ek's worker was fenced to `implementation/http/**` and
`spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`. Both callers of the `:http/abort-on-actor-destroy`
late-bind hook are outside that fence and pass an actor address with no frame:

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`
  `abort-actor-in-flight-http!` takes `[actor-id]` and calls `(abort! actor-id)`.
  Its caller in `.../lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc` already has `frame-id` bound as
  its first parameter, one line above the call.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` (~3983) has the machines-absent
  fallback: `(abort-http machine-id)` inside `destroy-frame!`'s per-snapshot
  walk, where the frame `id` is likewise in scope.

## What to do

Give `abort-actor-in-flight-http!` the destroying frame and pass it through to
the hook, and do the same at core's fallback site. `registry/abort-on-actor-
destroy` already accepts `[frame-id actor-id]`; its `[actor-id]` arity is the
documented ANY-FRAME sweep retained precisely so this change could be made
separately without a flag day, and it can be left in place or retired with the
last caller.

## Exposure

A spawned actor's address is frame-LOCAL, so two isolated frames running the
same application code spawn actors under the same address. Until the callers
thread a frame, destroying one frame's actor still sweeps the same address in
every frame. Measured on tip before rf2-o8ek and re-measured after it, via the
registry probe in `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_frame_scoped_
cancellation_test.clj`:
`actor-destroy-any-frame-arity-preserves-the-hook-contract` pins the current
behaviour, and `actor-destroy-is-frame-scoped-when-the-frame-is-known` pins the
behaviour this bead should make reachable from the destroy cascade.

Exposure is narrower than the request-id half rf2-o8ek fixed: it needs spawned
state-machine actors issuing managed HTTP in two frames under one address,
whereas the request-id half was reachable from any direct `:rf.http/managed`
caller.

## Acceptance

- The destroy cascade (parent state exit, parent `:after`, `:spawn-all` join,
  frame destroy, imperative destroy) aborts only the destroying frame's
  actor-owned HTTP; a same-named actor in a sibling frame stays live.
- Core's machines-absent fallback in `destroy-frame!` does the same.
- Spec 014 §Abort on actor destroy §Frame scope loses its closing sentence
  about the hook currently taking the any-frame form.
- Existing actor-destroy tests stay green on JVM and CLJS.

## Fence note

This one touches `implementation/machines/` and `implementation/core/`, so it
must not be dispatched concurrently with other work in those artefacts.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9212 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9212). Premise HELD and was reproduced.

CENSUS — the bead named TWO call sites; five axes found FOUR, all with the destroying frame already in scope, all threaded:
  1. machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc      — spawn-destroy pipeline (parent state exit, parent :after, :spawn-all join, imperative destroy)
  2. machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc     — final-state auto-destroy tail   [NOT named by the bead]
  3. machines/lifecycle_fx/frame_destroy.cljc — singleton-straggler pass       [NOT named by the bead]
  4. core/frame.cljc                          — machines-absent destroy-frame! fallback

Axes: effect keyword; helper symbol; multiline/ws-collapsed; frame-less registry arities; PROSE. The prose axis was the one that paid — it found two sites naming no symbol (registry.cljc's ANY-FRAME seams block and abort-on-actor-destroy's docstring), both asserting the cascade passes an address alone. No call site lacked a frame, so nothing was frameless-by-design. The bead's 'one line per call site' prediction held.

SHAPE — followed rf2-o8ek's worker: no dev warning (nag-diagnostic, and mechanically impossible for a registry fn with no ambient ctx). finalize/abort-actor-in-flight-http! — the funnel the three machines sites share — now REQUIRES the frame rather than defaulting it, because its hook call is wrapped in a catch-all so a frame-less call fails SILENTLY.

LEFT IN PLACE, deliberately: abort-on-actor-destroy's 1-arity, as the documented ANY-FRAME seam (the bead permitted either); no in-repo destroy path is such a caller now. The resources seam :http/abort-in-flight! — correct as-is, its token is frame-qualified. rf2-s4dp (xray testbed, peer surface) — untouched.

AC: 1 met (all five destroy triggers), 2 met (core fallback), 3 met (spec 014 §Frame scope closing sentence replaced with the frame-exact law), 4 met (green JVM + CLJS).

WITNESS — 3 deftests in implementation/http driving the REAL destroy entry points against the REAL registry with one address live in two frames. Negative control (pre-fix behaviour at both funnels): http exit 1 / 6 failures / 0 errors, machines exit 1 / 11 failures / 0 errors — SEMANTIC, not arity errors. The pre-existing single-frame actor-destroy suite stayed GREEN under the control, which is exactly why this escaped.

GATES (captured exits, final rebased base a7f62e9bc5): http 518/3944 -> 521/3958 exit 0; machines 1244/4528 exit 0; core 2175/11142 exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11185/55887 exit 0; mkdocs --strict exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and PROVEN LIVE (planted anchor -> exit 1 naming line 781, the paragraph edited).

OUT OF FENCE, filed as rf2-p4rn: spec/005-StateMachines.md:3599 states the hook fn as (fn [actor-id]), now stale.

title: skill(pair-retro): issue-draft ownership requires sources the self-contained package cannot reach
description:
## Problem

The pair-retro skill's issue-draft contract requires exact ownership evidence that a normally installed, self-contained copy cannot access, and it points agents at the wrong sibling document when a source checkout happens to be available.

At reviewed base `bf0b43dbcb68d57dfa493ebcf26ea8f67e7752d9`:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:86` requires every framework-shaped draft to name the relevant `spec/Tool-Pair.md` capability/restore row and shipped Pair tool, then says the tool catalogue is `re-frame2-pair`'s README.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md` contains no catalogue table; it is a short human-facing overview/examples page.
- The actual 30-tool catalogue is `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md:63-103`. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:1130-1137` treats that file—not the README—as the descriptor-backed tool reference.
- The retro's own `references/known-frictions.md:201` correctly distinguishes sources: ops for vocabulary, mcp-transport for per-tool behavior, and live `tools/list` as authoritative. This contradicts the operational instruction in SKILL.md.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/package.json:25-32` ships only this package's SKILL, README, LICENSE, agent metadata, references, and plugin metadata. It does not ship sibling Pair references or root `spec/Tool-Pair.md`.
- `SKILL.md:29`, `README.md:34`, and design L7 promise normal operation is self-contained, while `spec/inputs.md:48` explicitly says the skill does not consume the re-frame2 spec corpus.
- `SKILL.md:55` forbids live probing and requires unseen facts to remain unknown. A supported recap-only input therefore commonly contains neither `tools/list` nor a Tool-Pair excerpt.

These constraints cannot all be satisfied. On the normal standalone path, the agent must either invent a current capability row/tool from memory, violate the one-turn draft workflow to seek unavailable evidence, or omit/misclassify ownership despite the mandatory contract.

## Reproduction and impact

1. Install/use only the published `re-frame2-pair-retro` package.
2. Supply a recap saying that a Pair operation lacked enough information; include no `tools/list`, sibling documentation, or spec excerpt.
3. Ask for the prescribed framework issue draft.

The skill promises an exact authoritative row/tool citation but exposes no authoritative source. In a monorepo checkout it additionally directs the agent to a README that has no catalogue. A plausible but stale/nonexistent tool name or wrong capability row can send maintainers to the wrong layer, encode the wrong retrospective lesson, and leave the original SPA tooling defect unresolved.

## Bounded repair

- Correct the source map: the descriptor-backed catalogue is `re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md`, with live `tools/list` authoritative when already supplied as session evidence.
- Apply the existing “unknown over inferred” invariant to ownership: cite a tool and Tool-Pair row only when present in supplied evidence or a readable authoritative source; otherwise label ownership unverified and never invent a name.
- To retain exact, one-turn standalone drafts, optionally ship a small local ownership index containing only capability/restore-row labels and tool names, pinned by the existing descriptor/document drift machinery. If that small leaf is not worth maintaining, explicitly relax exact citation certainty for recap-only inputs instead.

## Non-goals

No live probe permission, network fetch, MCP grant, full sibling/spec vendoring, runtime/API change, generic evaluation framework, or additional filing ceremony.

## Duplicate research and history

Targeted searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` and git history found no open issue for this runtime source-availability contradiction.

- Closed `rf2-d4h52` / commit `dff863728a` introduced the exact-citation rule and stale README pointer.
- Commit `d89385efd9` / closed `rf2-wz1qa` corrected the source pointer in `known-frictions.md` but left SKILL.md unchanged.
- Closed `rf2-lsqmp` fixed a related stale pointer only in the family README.
- Open `rf2-nvbz` concerns cross-package link spelling/gating; it cannot make an unshipped source available at runtime or define the honest fallback.
- Closed `rf2-t19ve` covers the self-contained redesign generally; this is a residual contradiction in the resulting contract.
- Closed `rf2-3cjhl` covers stale known-friction behaviors, not issue-draft source availability.

## Uncertainty

A host could choose to provide repository files or a captured `tools/list` in context, in which case exact ownership may be recoverable. The defect remains because recap-only input is explicitly supported and no such host capability is required or declared.
acceptance_criteria:
1. In an extracted/published-package replay whose recap contains no catalogue or spec excerpt, the skill produces an honest one-turn draft without inventing a shipped tool or Tool-Pair row; unavailable ownership is explicitly marked unverified.
2. With authoritative evidence supplied, a known-but-unused tool routes as tool-shaped, a used-tool/runtime gap cites the correct current Tool-Pair row, and an unknown name is not promoted to fact.
3. No shipped pair-retro instruction names `re-frame2-pair/README.md` as the tool catalogue; source guidance consistently identifies mcp-transport and the conditional authority of already-supplied live `tools/list`.
4. If a local ownership index is chosen, `npm pack --dry-run` proves it ships and a narrow drift test fails when a descriptor-backed tool name or indexed capability/restore-row label changes.
5. Existing pair-retro transcript/issue-draft checks remain green, with a new recap-only fixture covering the unavailable-evidence fallback.
close_reason:
Fixed by PR #9230 (branch worker/skretro-a).

PREMISE HELD IN FULL — every claim verified at source. npm pack --dry-run confirms the package is exactly seven files (SKILL.md, README.md, LICENSE, package.json, agents/openai.yaml, references/known-frictions.md, .claude-plugin/plugin.json): no sibling re-frame2-pair references, no spec corpus, and not even this skill's own spec/ or evals/. re-frame2-pair/README.md has zero pipe-table rows, so it carries no catalogue; check_skill_mcp_drift.py's DOC_COVERAGE_RULES pins re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md against descriptors_data.cljs, exactly as filed. SKILL.md:29 promises 'every instruction it runs on ships under its own directory', so SKILL.md:86 was a direct violation of design L7.

REPAIR: option 2, and NOT on taste. Design L7 reads 'no vendored peer copy', which locks out the local ownership index outright; independently, a vendored index would convert an honest 'unknown' into a confident STALE citation on every installed version — the precise failure the bead describes. The citation is now evidence-bound rather than mandatory: session evidence first (tools/list, error payload, pasted spec row — authoritative when present), then a repository checkout when the conversation genuinely has one (mcp-transport.md, never the README), otherwise marked unverified under the existing 'unknown over inferred' invariant and never reconstructed from memory. A third worked shape gives the unverified draft a template. Both authoring sources (spec/design.md L3, spec/authoring-prompt.md rule 6) moved in the same commit so a re-authoring pass cannot regenerate the unconditional rule. Three files, +8/-3; package membership unchanged.

AC1/AC2/AC3 met. AC4 does not apply (no index shipped).

AC5 NOT MET, AND DELIBERATELY SO — it conflicts with a lock it did not consider. spec/design.md L2 states tests/duplicate_search_test.clj 'is the skill's sole test and stays so: no session-evidence scorer is to be added', and evals/evals.json is a TRIGGER-ONLY corpus whose README says behavioural verification is manual by design and 'there is no automated scorer and none should be added'. A recap-only behavioural fixture is therefore forbidden by the skill's own locked design; a trigger-shaped one would duplicate existing positives and add nothing. The existing test stays green (5 tests, 16 assertions). Recording this plainly: the change is gated STRUCTURALLY and by prose contract only, with no behavioural execution — this repo has no eval executor, and this skill has no prompt-regression harness. If Mike wants the behavioural fixture, L2 needs unlocking first.

GATES (exit codes captured to file, run on the final rebased base): check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_skill_eval_packaging.py 0, check_skill_eval_docs.py 0, check_skill_description_budget.py 0, check_skill_mcp_drift.py 0, bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj 0, api-manifest skills-check 0 (575 refs). check_doc_slugs.py exits 0 with an empty log, so it was proven live with a planted broken anchor: exit 1 naming SKILL.md:88, restored byte-identical per cmp, back to exit 0. mkdocs build --strict not nominated (docs_dir is docs; the hook stages only spec and migration, never skills/).

GATE FINDING, filed as rf2-7mcp: check_skill_eval_packaging.py could not have caught this. Despite the name its only subject is whether a skill's prose and its files array contradict each other about evals/ shipping. Nothing gates 'a shipped instruction may only require shipped sources'. Not fixed here — this bead's non-goals exclude a generic evaluation framework.

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): canonical storage-validation fix throws on absent/corrupt localStorage and skips rehydrate
description:
## Scope

Correct the canonical "After" in `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md` for a durable session value read from localStorage through a recordable coeffect. Keep the leaf's trust-boundary and replay-boundary lessons, the coeffect runtime, and the six-leaf catalogue unchanged.

## Correctness finding

The recommended recordable supplier claims to return nil when localStorage is absent or corrupt, but its materializer throws in both cases before validation can make that decision.

The first expression passed to `some->` is `(.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage "session")`. `some->` can short-circuit only after that expression returns; on Node/headless/server hosts, where `globalThis.localStorage` is absent, the direct method call throws. A malformed stored string likewise makes `js/JSON.parse` throw before `m/validate` runs. The framework catches a recordable-generator exception and skips the declaring handler, so this is not the advertised nil/clean rejection path.

This is a copyable canonical fix in a static-review skill. An agent can correctly identify the original body-read and replace it with a replay-recordable coeffect, yet still ship a boot/rehydration failure on ordinary stale storage or in Node-based tests.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md:105-122` owns the canonical correction. Lines 109-110 describe `:session/stored` as a recordable generator yielding "nil if absent/corrupt". Line 112 directly invokes `.getItem` on `js/globalThis.localStorage`; line 113 invokes `js/JSON.parse`; only line 114 reaches Malli validation.
- Evaluation order is load-bearing: in `(some-> (.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage "session") ...)`, the direct method call is evaluated before `some->` can test for nil. Missing `localStorage` therefore is not a nil input to the pipeline.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:793-842` catches supplier exceptions and returns the `:threw` outcome after emitting `:rf.error/coeffect-exception`. Its public delivery contract at lines 1113-1117 says a throwing supplier sets `:rf/skip-handler?`; the recordable arm does that at line 1182. Consequently `:session/rehydrate` does not run.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:196-206` is the shared fx/cofx platform predicate. Missing `:platforms` defaults to `#{:client :server}`, so the sample's supplier is eligible on a server frame rather than being fenced away.
- The shipped canonical comparator is total over these cases. `examples/core/todomvc/db.cljs:35-45` catches parse failures in `storage->todos`; lines 66-84 start `some->` from `(.-localStorage js/globalThis)`, so the property itself can be absent before any method invocation.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/todomvc_cljs_test.cljs:17-24` explicitly documents the executable Node control: Node has no localStorage, the property-first `some->` short-circuits to nil, and the supplier returns its empty value. Lines 76-80 drive that cold-boot path.
- History isolates the miss. Commit `14fafe6103` made the sibling localStorage write example SSR-safe with `:platforms #{:client}` and a guarded globalThis access, but the coeffect sample retained a direct method call. Commit `bb25f3c56b` upgraded the sample to a recordable generator without making its materialization total.

## Reproduction / failure scenario

1. Follow the leaf's canonical correction and register `:session/stored` exactly as shown.
2. Dispatch `[:session/rehydrate]` in the Node/headless CLJS environment used by repository tests, where `globalThis.localStorage` is absent.
3. The supplier attempts `undefined.getItem`, emits `:rf.error/coeffect-exception`, and the framework skips `:session/rehydrate`. It does not deliver nil as the sample promises.
4. Browser control: make `localStorage["session"]` contain malformed JSON and dispatch the same event. `JSON.parse` throws; Malli validation is never reached; the handler is again skipped.
5. Positive control: begin the pipeline with `(.-localStorage js/globalThis)` and catch access/parse failure before validation. Missing or malformed storage produces the explicitly chosen invalid/absent value, which is then recorded and delivered without rerunning the host read on replay.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the sample's materializer total over the two cases its own docstring promises:

1. Resolve `(.-localStorage js/globalThis)` as the first `some->` value, then call `.getItem` only when that property exists.
2. Catch property-access and JSON-parse failure at the small storage-decoding boundary, returning the documented nil (or change the prose and handler coherently to consume an explicit data-shaped invalid result).
3. Run the always-on Malli validation only after parsing succeeds; keep `:recordable? true` so the resulting fact, including the absent/invalid outcome, is captured and replayed verbatim.
4. State the server/headless posture in the example. The smallest existing-repo shape is universal and nil-on-absent, matching TodoMVC. Do not merely add `:platforms #{:client}` while leaving a universally dispatched handler requiring the coeffect: a platform-skipped required recordable fact follows the missing-required path rather than the promised nil path.

Keep this local to the leaf and its focused proof. No generic storage framework is needed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The canonical After never invokes a method on a possibly absent `globalThis.localStorage`; the property lookup itself is inside the nil-short-circuiting path.
2. Malformed JSON is caught at the materialization boundary and becomes the documented nil or an explicitly documented data result. It cannot escape as a coeffect supplier exception.
3. A focused CLJS/Node proof with no `globalThis.localStorage` shows the supplier returns the chosen absent value and the declaring handler runs; the proof fails if the direct `.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage` form is restored.
4. A malformed-JSON control shows Malli is not called on an unparsable value, no `:rf.error/coeffect-exception` is emitted, and the handler follows the documented invalid/absent branch.
5. A valid conforming JSON control is validated, recorded, and folded into app-db; a valid but schema-invalid JSON value is rejected by the always-on validation branch.
6. The prose still distinguishes trust validation from replay recordability and does not weaken `:recordable? true`.
7. Skill link/package/eval documentation gates remain green. Because no existing gate executes fenced CLJS, the PR handoff explicitly records the corrected snippet's manual comparison with the tested TodoMVC materializer.

## Non-goals

- No changes to coeffect generation, exception recovery, platform gating, schemas, replay, epoch, or SSR runtimes.
- No new anti-pattern leaf, generic localStorage abstraction, compatibility shim, or broad catalogue rewrite.
- No policy change requiring every browser read to be client-only; this sample may deliberately be universal and yield nil off-browser.
- No redesign of session/auth state, storage format, or UI response to an invalid persisted session.
- No package-link or installation-metadata work.

## Duplicate and history check

Targeted all-status searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered re-frame2-improver, session/stored, rehydrate plus localStorage, corrupt storage, JSON.parse plus cofx, coeffect-exception plus localStorage, missing localStorage, Node, and cofx platform. Git history searches covered the same sample and its recordable-coeffect migration. No bead owns this accidental supplier-throw path.

Distinct nearby work:

- `rf2-0o5dx` (closed) fixes the URL body-read fixture's recordability requirement; it does not address storage materialization or supplier exceptions.
- `rf2-237ug` (closed) fixes frame capture in recommended views.
- `rf2-uhszv` (closed) owns the one-pass critique workflow.
- `rf2-nvbz` and `rf2-1c60` (open) own cross-package links and install/packaging metadata, respectively.

## Uncertainty

Fail-loud corruption could be a valid product policy, but it is not the policy this sample states: it explicitly promises nil for absent/corrupt storage and gives the handler only that branch. Either policy can work if made deliberate and coherent. The present accidental supplier throw plus handler skip is the defect.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9232 (branch worker/skimprov-a, head 0225e0cf99b40cc733bc3e62389359a62f0e080f).

PREMISE HELD, confirmed at source. The canonical After in skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md started its some-> from (.getItem js/globalThis.localStorage "session"), so the method call was evaluated before some-> could test anything: absent localStorage (Node/SSR/headless) threw, and a corrupt entry threw out of js/JSON.parse before m/validate ran. - ABSENT (no globalThis.localStorage on Node/SSR/headless; getItem nil on first run) — ordinary cold boot, not caller-controllable, sane default exists. MUST NOT THROW: a throw breaks every new app and every Node test. Repaired by starting the some-> from the PROPERTY.

ALSO MUST NOT THROW, and the reason is not leniency: the framework turns a supplier throw into :rf.error/coeffect-exception + :rf/skip-handler?, so :session/rehydrate silently never runs. That is a boot step that did not happen — HARDER to diagnose than the nil the handler already handles. Fail-loud is a legitimate policy for corrupt persisted state; a supplier throw is not how it is spelled. The doc now points an app that must act on the difference at a data-shaped result instead.

title: bug(skill-setup): custom-name manual scaffolds bypass the generator's identity derivation
description:
## Problem

`re-frame2-setup` treats an author-supplied project name as a first-class zero-friction override, but its default manual route never defines how that name becomes the several identities a CLJS project needs. It says only to rename `acme` / `my-app` consistently. The generator route uses a real derivation instead: Clojure namespace, filesystem path, npm package name, output directory, `:init-fn`, headings, and requires are related but not identical strings. Therefore the two routes advertised as producing the same files are deterministic only for the fixed reference name.

A common qualified name exposes the gap. For `com.acme/my-cool-app`, the generator emits namespace `com.acme.my-cool-app`, source path `src/com/acme/my_cool_app`, and npm name `my-cool-app`. A manual textual rename can naturally produce `src/com.acme/my_cool_app`, which does not back the namespace named by `shadow-cljs.edn` and fails namespace resolution. Bare and mixed-case names have different hazards: deps-new currently doubles bare `my-app` into the almost-certainly-unintended `my-app.my-app`, while npm identity must be lowercased and validated independently.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:42` says an author-supplied project name overrides the default, without restricting its shape.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:55` says manual and generator routes land on the same files.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:67` and `references/first-counter.md:3` give the manual operation only as renaming `acme` / `my-app` consistently across paths and contents.
- `tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:119-162` defines separate `->file-path`, `->ns-form`, lowercasing, and npm-name validation; `data-fn` at lines 166-191 derives `:namespace`, `:nested-dirs`, and `:npm-name` separately.
- `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:294-320` proves the nontrivial mapping `com.acme/my-cool-app` -> `com.acme.my-cool-app`, `src/com/acme/my_cool_app`, and `my-cool-app`. Lines 332-360 separately cover qualified, dotted, bare, mixed-case, and invalid npm names.
- `tools/template/spec/API.md:160` explicitly records that a bare name is accepted by deps-new but becomes doubled (`my-app.my-app`) and recommends a group-qualified name. The setup skill exposes a natural-language "project name" override without carrying that rule or choosing a different normalization.
- `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/first_counter_derivation.clj:78-82` renders only the fixed `{:name "acme/my-app" :top "acme" :main "my-app"}` identity. The setup drift suite and `evals/evals.json` grade the reference default, empty-project merge, and generator route, but no custom-name manual result.
- History confirms the split: `18b9486664` added deterministic npm/name derivation to the generator, while `98aa4b1f5f` made the setup leaf a derivation of the one reference identity and described all custom identities only as a rename.

## Programmer and AI impact

Naming the app is one of the most ordinary scaffold requests. A programmer or AI can follow every stated setup instruction, write all twelve files, and reach the terminating compile only to discover a missing namespace or invalid npm name. Repair then requires reverse-engineering the generator's rules after the skill promised one prompt and one served SPA. Even when a capable agent guesses the CLJS path mapping correctly, route parity is accidental and untested, so model or wording changes can silently reintroduce the failure.

## Posture fit

This is not a request for a naming system. A single small identity rule removes guesswork from a high-frequency override, keeps the API ergonomic, and lets humans and agents start the SPA successfully on the first pass.

## Duplicate research

Targeted searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` for setup/custom names, dotted groups, name derivation, npm names, and manual-route naming found no issue owning this residual. Closed `rf2-zq34m` fixed generator output and npm-name validity, not the setup skill's manual override. Closed `rf2-rc0yh` established the fixed `acme/my-app` default. `rf2-h4q82` and `rf2-pygpw` concern generator location and post-emission coordinates; `rf2-0ddz3` concerns merging into a shadow-only project. Open `rf2-eiev` covers optimized release proof and `rf2-1c60` distribution metadata. None defines manual custom-name parity.

## Uncertainty

This read-only review did not execute a generated project. The concrete bad path is a permitted result of the current underspecified instruction, not a claim that every capable model will choose it. The objective defect is that the promised deterministic override has no specified derivation and no parity test, despite the adjacent generator already proving the distinctions matter.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The manual route documents or executes one unambiguous mapping from a supplied project identity to every emitted identity-bearing field; it no longer says only to rename tokens consistently.
2. `com.acme/my-cool-app` produces the same observable identity on both routes: namespace `com.acme.my-cool-app`, files under `src/com/acme/my_cool_app` and `test/com/acme/my_cool_app`, npm name/output directory `my-cool-app`, matching `:init-fn` and internal requires, and consistent human-facing labels.
3. Bare and mixed-case inputs have an explicit shared policy. An invalid npm artifact is rejected before any manual-route file is written just as the generator fails before emission; no partial scaffold remains.
4. A focused setup eval grades an explicitly named manual scaffold, including source path, namespace, package name, and successful compile/handoff rather than merely checking that the name appears in prose.
5. A deterministic test compares manual identity derivation with the template hook for the dotted, bare, mixed-case, and invalid cases. At least one non-reference qualified identity reaches the existing compile proof, or an equivalently strong namespace-to-path resolver test demonstrates that the emitted `:init-fn` can be found.
6. The zero-interview `acme/my-app` default and explicit UIx override remain unchanged, and the fix adds no new scaffold files, dependencies, selector, or user questionnaire.
design:
## Bounded fix

- Define one canonical project-identity normalization for both setup routes. At minimum, specify how a supplied coordinate yields the group/artifact, namespace, source/test directories, npm name, output directory, `:init-fn`, internal requires, README/title, and heading.
- Reuse the generator hook's current semantics as the oracle, or deliberately improve a questionable case in both places together. Do not leave manual and generator behavior different. In particular, make the bare-name policy explicit: either reject it before writing, normalize it intentionally, or document and reproduce the doubled deps-new identity; never let the routes improvise different answers.
- Put the compact rule in the normal setup path, close to the custom-name override. Keep `first-counter.md` as the one reference scaffold rather than copying twelve custom variants.
- Add a focused custom-name outcome eval and a small derivation/parity test driven by the template hook. Cover one dotted qualified name plus bare, mixed-case, and invalid-artifact boundaries. Extend the existing emitted compile fixture for one non-reference identity only if static parity cannot prove namespace/path coherence.

## Non-goals

- No naming DSL, wizard, profile system, compatibility aliases, or clarification round for the existing unqualified default.
- No change to the counter, substrate choice, dependency pins, twelve-file manifest, build/watch workflow, or publication-coordinate handling.
- No matrix of arbitrary Unicode/package-manager policy and no attempt to replace deps-new.
- No duplicated hand-maintained scaffold per project name.
close_reason: PR #9239. SKILL.md now carries one `## Project identity` rule, stated for both routes and taken from the generator template's own semantics (hooks.clj ->ns-form / ->file-path / ->npm-name): normalise to group/artefact (an unqualified name is doubled, as deps-new doubles it); namespace root = the whole coordinate with / -> . and _ -> -; source/test path = the whole coordinate with . -> / and - -> _; npm name = artefact segment lowercased, project dir = that segment verbatim; <h1>/<title>/README heading = the coordinate verbatim. An npm-invalid artefact is refused BEFORE the first file is written, matching the hook, which throws before emission. The manual route was NOT folded into the generator, deliberately: it is the default route, needs nothing beyond the skill's allowed-tools grants, and cardinal rule 4 already falls back to it when the globally-installed -Tnew tool is absent. What is single-sourced is the DERIVATION: tests/project_identity_test.clj load-files the template's real hooks.clj and compares data-fn against the rule as SKILL.md words it, over the reference / dotted-qualified / bare / mixed-case inputs plus the npm-invalid rejection. CI-wired via test.yml's skills-structural job (it loops skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/*_test.clj), so no workflow change. Behavioural witness: 15 failures / exit 1 before the doc fix, 0 failures / exit 0 after, and 6 failures / exit 1 when the documented derivation is planted to diverge from the hook. AC deviations, both stated in the PR: AC2's 'same observable identity on both routes' is proven by static parity against the hook rather than by emitting a second scaffold, because design.md L13 locks first-counter.md as the ONE reference scaffold rendered for acme/my-app (the item's own design section agrees: 'keep first-counter.md as the one reference scaffold'). AC3's bare-name policy is 'document and reproduce the doubled deps-new identity' - the third option the item's design permits - because the fence excludes tools/**, so improving the generator's semantics in both places together was not available; parity was the binding constraint. AC4's eval (id 18, custom-qualified-name-manual-scaffold) is gated STRUCTURALLY, not executed: there is no eval executor in this repo. Also recorded as design.md L14.

title: surface-review(examples-substrates): keep the runnable slim-counter bundle free of its CI SSR fixture
description:
## Scope

Separate the runnable Reagent Slim counter under examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter from the CI-only pure-CLJS-SSR bundle-isolation fixture that currently owns its only Shadow build entry. Keep the stock/slim counter comparison focused on the existing counter app and keep the adapter-owned S3-005/S3-008 isolation proof non-vacuous in a dedicated build. Limit changes to the slim counter entry/fixture seam, the paired Shadow/package/checker configuration, directly coupled staging/checker tests, and prose that describes this comparison.

## Correctness finding

The repository presents examples/counter-slim-and-fast as the runnable “same app, different package” counterpart to examples/counter, but its only build does not invoke reagent-slim.counter.core/run. It invokes reagent-slim.counter.bundle-isolation-entry/run, which executes test-only pre-mount SSR work, pulls reagent2.dom.server and its serializer into main.js, creates a throwaway frame, clears its subscription cache, and writes globalThis.counterSlimPrerender.

This is not just extra source beside the example. Both documented launch paths compile and serve that same contaminated build, so the runnable artifact and the bundle a reader is invited to compare against stock contain and execute a CI harness that the stock app does not. The comparison therefore changes two variables at once: substrate/package and an SSR fixture. It undermines the folder’s central teaching claim that the app is held constant, especially because the catalogue explicitly says the interest is what the bundle does not contain.

## Evidence

- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1259-1270 declares :examples/counter-slim-and-fast and points its :init-fn at reagent-slim.counter.bundle-isolation-entry/run, explicitly not reagent-slim.counter.core/run.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/bundle_isolation_entry.cljs:1-29 says it is gate plumbing, is the build’s init-fn, and passes prove-pure-cljs-ssr! into the app boot before mounting.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/bundle_isolation_fixture.cljs:1-54 requires reagent2.dom.server, calls render-to-static-markup, writes counterSlimPrerender on globalThis to defeat advanced DCE, and clears the transient subscription cache.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/core.cljs:96-126 exposes an optional on-frame boot arity and a with-new-frame branch whose only caller is that fixture. The supposedly plain teaching file therefore still carries a public-looking harness seam even though its zero-arity run does not use it.
- examples/substrates/reagent_slim/counter/README.md:13-22 says the meaningful diff from stock is only the package/import and adapter, calls core.cljs the plain idiomatic example, labels both sibling fixture files “not app practice”, then at lines 49-55 tells the reader to launch the build whose init-fn is the fixture entry.
- examples/substrates/README.md:7-15 defines the track as “same authoring language, different package”, says each example changes exactly one place, and says the interest is what the bundle does not contain. Lines 84-95 route the slim command through the same build.
- examples/README.md:163 repeats that the interest is what the bundle does not contain.
- implementation/package.json:46 makes test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation release examples/counter-slim-and-fast, while line 53 routes dev:example through the normal standalone runner. examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs:149-210 resolves the selected build and compiles it unchanged; there is no teaching-entry substitution.
- implementation/scripts/check-reagent-slim-bundle-isolation.cjs:135-182 defines counterSlimPrerender and a reagent2.dom.server-only literal as required positive sentinels. Lines 275-364 read out/examples/counter-slim-and-fast and require those SSR sentinels in that bundle, confirming the contamination is load-bearing for the gate rather than dead source.
- Git history identifies the incomplete separation. Commit b2ae161b17 (rf2-vyl0vt, “prune scaffolding from Reagent-family examples”) moved the fixture out of core.cljs so the source looked clean, but deliberately repointed the one example build to the new gate entry. It separated files, not the runnable artifact or core’s fixture-only boot seam.

## Failure scenario / impact

A programmer or coding agent follows the catalogue and compares the release outputs of examples/counter and examples/counter-slim-and-fast to understand the substrate cost. The stock bundle contains the counter client. The slim bundle contains the counter client plus a forced server serializer, a DCE anchor and fixture orchestration, and it performs an unrelated static render/global write before mounting. Any size, reachability, startup, or “what ships” conclusion attributes fixture-only differences to Reagent Slim.

The same problem appears without bundle analysis: running the advertised slim example executes code every comment calls CI-only and “not app practice”. Reading core/run is not enough to discover what the official page actually boots; the authoritative build config chooses a different entry. The invariant for a comparison example is simple: its documented runnable build must boot the code it teaches, and gate-only work must not be reachable from that runnable entry.

## Recommended minimal fix

Restore :examples/counter-slim-and-fast to reagent-slim.counter.core/run. Give bundle_isolation_entry and bundle_isolation_fixture a dedicated, non-runnable Shadow build with a separate output directory, and make test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation release and inspect that output. Keep the existing stock build as the methodology control and retain all six isolation contracts, including the two positive SSR sentinels that make S3-005 non-vacuous.

Move the fixture-only orchestration out of core’s optional on-frame boot arity so the teaching boot is the same small install-then-mount shape readers actually run. Update the checker diagnostics, targeted Shadow/staging/script-policy tests, and the few comparison paragraphs that currently conflate the runnable example and gate fixture. Use an existing local convention for the dedicated check build id; do not introduce a build registry or generalized harness framework.

## Non-goals

- No change to Reagent Slim, stock Reagent, core frame, rendering, SSR, or adapter APIs.
- No removal or weakening of the pure-CLJS-SSR non-vacuity proof, stock-Reagent absence proof, react-dom/server absence proof, or mirror slim-absence proof.
- No bundle-size threshold or performance claim.
- No new browser/Playwright example matrix; examples remain test-free learning surfaces and adapter behavior remains adapter-testbed-owned.
- No extraction or redesign of the counter’s events, subscriptions, views, frame id, or mount lifecycle.
- No cross-product of examples across every substrate and no general example-manifest redesign.
- No effort to make the dedicated gate fixture user-runnable or to teach its orchestration as app practice.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all issue states in .beads/issues.jsonl with targeted rg queries for counter-slim-and-fast, bundle-isolation entry/fixture, counterSlimPrerender, reagent-slim bundle isolation, teaching build, runnable fixture, and same-app bundle. No issue owns this separation.

Closest records are not duplicates:
- rf2-fmns2 (closed) owns the three-view-layer login comparison and its cross-runtime isolation proof, not the slim counter entry.
- rf2-k5r9t (closed) added the Reagent client-root lifecycle and migrated example mounts; it does not separate test and runnable builds.
- rf2-vyl0vt is represented by commit b2ae161b17 and physically moved fixture code out of the teaching namespace, but intentionally kept the one runnable build pointed at the gate entry. This finding is the remaining artifact-level half of that cleanup.
- rf2-5x1xt (closed) fixes missing UIx consumer dependencies and is unrelated.
- rf2-cdoo (open) concerns Reagent Slim after-render ordering, not examples or bundle reachability.

## Uncertainty

The exact dedicated build id and output prefix should follow whichever current non-page/check-build convention best fits Shadow configuration and CI surface classification. The required outcome is not a particular spelling: the documented :examples/counter-slim-and-fast output must be fixture-free, and the isolation checker must consume a separate output that remains deliberately fixture-full. No runtime execution was needed for this review; the entrypoint and reachability contradiction is explicit in source/config and in the gate’s required sentinels.
acceptance_criteria:
1. :examples/counter-slim-and-fast uses reagent-slim.counter.core/run as its init-fn, remains listed by the standalone example runner, and both documented launch commands serve that build.
2. A focused config/staging assertion proves the runnable build resolves to core/run and does not silently regress to bundle-isolation-entry.
3. The runnable advanced main.js contains neither counterSlimPrerender nor the reagent2.dom.server-only SSR presence sentinel. The check is non-vacuous by also proving ordinary Reagent Slim client sentinels are present.
4. A separate non-runnable build owns reagent-slim.counter.bundle-isolation-entry/run and emits to a distinct output directory not staged or advertised as the counter example.
5. test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation releases that dedicated build and the stock counter, and its checker reads the dedicated slim output.
6. The dedicated gate bundle still contains counterSlimPrerender plus the serializer-owned static-markup sentinel, contains the ordinary slim client sentinels, and contains none of the stock-Reagent or react-dom/server sentinels. The stock bundle retains its own positive controls and remains free of slim sentinels.
7. The teaching core no longer exposes an optional callback/throwaway-frame seam used only by the bundle fixture; core/run and any retained boot helper express only the runnable app lifecycle.
8. The slim README and substrate catalogues distinguish the runnable comparison from the dedicated CI fixture without teaching the fixture as application code or weakening the “same app, different package” claim.
9. Targeted checker self-tests, example staging/manifest tests, npm run test:examples-compile, and npm run test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation pass, with a planted reachability/config regression demonstrating the new separation check fails on the old shape.

title: surface-review(examples-patterns): make Nine States managed loads newest-intent-wins
description:
## Slice reviewed

`examples/patterns/**`: boot, long-running work, nine states, and websocket, including their runnable build entries, adapter tests, governing pattern/spec text, and introducing history. This is the single cohesive correctness/teaching issue selected from that review.

## Correctness finding

The canonical Nine States example starts every data load with a direct `:rf.http/managed` effect but gives none of those requests a stable `:request-id`. That makes overlapping user intents first-settle-wins instead of newest-intent-wins.

The control panel leaves every Empty/One/Some/Too Many/error load button enabled whenever the page is not archived, including while the data region is already `:loading`. A second click therefore starts a second unkeyed request. The `:loading` state has no `:fetch-started` transition, so both requests remain in flight while the region stays at `:loading`. It accepts whichever `:fetch-succeeded` or `:fetch-failed` arrives first and immediately leaves `:loading`; its bucket/error states do not accept a completion. Thus an older request that was nearly finished can settle after a newer intent was issued, choose the visible bucket or error, and cause the newer request's eventual result to be ignored.

Concrete sequence: issue A for 25 rows, then issue B for 1 row before A settles. If A completes first, the page lands at `:too-many`; B later completes into a state that has no `:fetch-succeeded` handler, so the requested `:one` result never appears. The same ownership hole crosses success/failure: a nearly-complete old failing request can put the page in `:error` while a newer success is still in flight, then discard that success.

This is exactly the stale-reply case the governing pattern calls out. `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md` says a fresh load must prevent the previous reply from landing and demonstrates a stable `:request-id`; managed HTTP already gives the minimal mechanism: issuing the same id supersedes the old attempt and suppresses its app reply. The example omitted that one field.

## Evidence

- `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:463-488`: both `:nine-states.demo/load` and `:nine-states.demo/load-with-failure` broadcast `:fetch-started` and issue `:rf.http/managed`; neither args map has `:request-id`.
- `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:490-502`: every success/failure callback is forwarded unconditionally as a machine completion, with no ownership token or stale check.
- `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:339-385`: only `:loading` consumes `:fetch-succeeded` / `:fetch-failed`; `:loading` itself does not consume another `:fetch-started`, and the settled bucket/error states consume only a future `:fetch-started` or reset. This makes the first completion decisive.
- `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:756-782`: load controls are disabled only by `:mode/read-only`, not by `:data/loading`, so overlap is a supported interaction, not merely a fabricated internal event.
- `examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs:116-159`: the Story twins reproduce the same managed-request envelopes without a request id. Their canned fxs are synchronous, so the omission is visually hidden there too.
- `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md:289-313`: the canonical direct-managed-HTTP handler includes `:request-id :counter/load`.
- `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md:342-359`: direct effects do not get actor-lifetime cancellation; the stale-detection section says a fresh load while a previous request is live must not admit the previous reply, and names stable same-id supersession as the common-case mechanism.
- `docs/async/http.md:24-37`: public managed-HTTP reference defines `:request-id` as the stable id whose reuse supersedes the old request.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_cljs_test.cljs:1503-1547`: the CLJS transport regression proves same-id supersession delivers no app reply from the superseded request.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/nine_states_cljs_test.cljs:80-132`: the example suite routes HTTP to the synchronous demo stub; it even has to manufacture `:loading` by dispatching `:fetch-started` alone. These one-at-a-time rows cannot exercise overlap.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/nine_states_cljs_test.cljs:260-283`: the only stale-completion test resets to `:nothing` and sends a completion while still at `:nothing`, where it is trivially ignored. It does not exercise reset-then-reload or two live attempts, where the region is back at `:loading` and will accept the old completion.

## History

`1392aa0d1e` (2026-05-11) introduced the current load handlers without request ids. `git log -S":request-id" -- examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs` returns no commit: this path has never owned one. Sixteen minutes after the example rewrite, `a385d1aaba` added the managed-HTTP integration to `Pattern-NineStates`, including the stable request id and the explicit stale/supersession rationale. Later edits improved replies, schemas, reset semantics, frames, and prose, but never reconciled this executable companion with that requirement.

## Bounded recommendation

Define one clearly named stable request id for the Nine States data-load lane and put it on both live request shapes (`load` and `load-with-failure`), so any newer load intent supersedes either kind of older attempt. Carry the same field in the Story twins so the teaching envelopes remain faithful even though canned stubs do not model a real in-flight registry. Add a short adjacent explanation: the id expresses ownership of one replaceable page-load slot; it is not incidental tracing metadata.

Add one deterministic single-frame CLJS composition regression with a controlled/deferred transport: issue A, issue B before A settles, prove A's app target is suppressed, then settle B and prove only B's exact items/failure choose the machine state. Include a cross-kind row or table case so `load` and `load-with-failure` cannot accidentally drift onto separate ids.

This is the pre-alpha ergonomic fix: one existing field, one shared constant, one behavioral witness. It trusts the programmer and keeps all concurrency policy in readable data instead of disabling buttons or building a coordinator abstraction.

## Non-goals

- Do not redesign the parallel machine, cardinality cascade, render-priority table, or reply handlers.
- Do not add a request manager, sequence counter, promise layer, or generic remote-data abstraction.
- Do not disable load controls while loading; that only hides the race from mouse users and leaves programmatic intents incorrect.
- Do not move this example to the `:rf.http/managed` machine wrapper solely for this fix.
- Do not add a connection/page epoch to this non-routed, single-frame demo unless a separate lifecycle case proves it necessary. Stable same-id supersession closes the demonstrated overlap and reset-then-reload window.
- Do not change managed HTTP, canned-stub semantics, or the other three pattern examples.

## Duplicate search

Immediately before creation I searched all statuses in `.beads/issues.jsonl` with targeted `rg` combinations for Nine States/nine_states plus `request-id`, `stale`, `supersession`, `first-settle`, `newest`, `overlap`, and `demo/load`. No issue owns this example-level omission.

Closest open issue `rf2-o8ek` concerns the HTTP implementation's process-global registry colliding when two different frames reuse the same raw request id. It is complementary, not duplicate: this bead is a single-frame caller that supplies no id at all, so it cannot get supersession even after `rf2-o8ek` lands. The proposed regression is intentionally single-frame. Closed `rf2-iyjae` concerns websocket inbound correlation/validation, a different example and transport boundary.

## Uncertainty

Per review dispatch, I did not run a browser/runtime or external network. The verdict is derived from the executable transition tables, request envelopes, synchronous-test setup, current managed-HTTP contract, and its existing CLJS supersession regression. The exact controlled-fetch helper can follow the HTTP suite's established harness rather than inventing a new one. The canned demo resolves synchronously, so the current clickable app may not visibly reproduce the race until its override is replaced by the real asynchronous transport—the exact copy/adaptation moment this canonical example is meant to guide.
design: Use one stable keyword/constant for the replaceable Nine States data-load slot and attach it to every request producer in this example. Keep stale arbitration in the existing managed-HTTP boundary: same-id issue supersedes the previous attempt and the old app reply is suppressed before the page handler can broadcast it into the machine. Do not add local sequence bookkeeping. Test through a real controlled managed-HTTP lifecycle in one frame, because the canned effect intentionally has no in-flight lifecycle and cannot prove supersession.
acceptance_criteria:
- `:nine-states.demo/load` and `:nine-states.demo/load-with-failure` issue `:rf.http/managed` with the same stable, namespaced request id; the two Story request twins carry that same ownership field for envelope fidelity.
- A deterministic CLJS test in one frame holds request A open, issues request B through the shipped example event before A settles, and proves A's later success or failure dispatch reaches no app target and cannot move or mutate the Nine States machine.
- Settling B produces exactly B's expected `:items`/`:error`, data-region state/tag, and `:ui/render` result. At least one table row crosses request kind (old success versus new failure, or old failure versus new success) so both producer events are proven to share one replacement lane.
- A reset-then-new-load sequence cannot be overwritten by the pre-reset attempt; either cover it directly or make the overlap test's same-id suppression mechanism and existing reset test jointly explicit.
- The regression uses the real managed-HTTP supersession path or an existing controlled transport seam, not only the synchronous canned stub and not a hand-dispatched `:fetch-succeeded` event. A negative control removing/changing the shared request id makes the new overlap witness fail.
- Existing nine-state, reset, Story lifecycle, example compile/asset, and relevant managed-HTTP CLJS tests remain green. Reader-facing prose near the request explains newest-intent ownership in a few lines without adding a new abstraction.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9242 (branch worker/expat-a), entirely inside examples/patterns/**.

ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE, the three questions the fix turned on:
(a) How the example keys request-ids: it did not. Neither :nine-states.demo/load nor :nine-states.demo/load-with-failure carried :request-id, and re_frame/http/registry.cljc states it outright — 'An anonymous request (no :request-id) never supersedes'. So no supersession was reachable.
(b) Whether a newer intent re-issues: yes. Every load button dispatches the load event again, which issues a fresh :rf.http/managed. So supersession fires the moment an id exists — no correlation gate is needed on top.
(c) What the framework already does: everything required. handlers.cljc calls registry/supersede! on issue, which aborts the prior in-flight attempt under the same (frame, request-id) with :reason :request-id-superseded and suppresses its app reply before any handler sees it. #9202/#9212 (6aaddf52e3, 5c01850a80, 888833889b) made this frame-scoped without changing the criterion, so a plain reusable constant is safe.

CALL: adopt framework supersession, do NOT add a correlation gate. An example that hand-rolls a guard the framework provides teaches the wrong pattern, and spec/014 §791 names :request-id as THE app-level mechanism for requests dispatched directly from an event handler (which get no actor-destroy cascade). The :spawn/machine-wrapper route was also rejected on the merits, not merely by the non-goals: :loading has no :fetch-started self-transition, so a second load causes no region exit, hence no actor destroy, hence no abort — reaching that route would require reshaping the machine.

SHIPPED: one named constant, data-load-request-id (:nine-states.data/load), on both live request shapes and both Story twins; the twins reference the core var rather than copying the keyword (verified in the compiled artefact: nine_states.stories.js emits nine_states.core.data_load_request_id twice). Prose explains the id as ownership rather than tracing metadata, and records honestly that the demo :fx-overrides stub REPLACES :rf.http/managed outright, so the registry and supersession only run once a reader swaps in the real transport.

VERIFICATION, stated plainly: check-examples-compile exit 0 (58/58 builds, zero warnings; examples/nine-states 229 files and examples/nine-states-with-stories 695 files both clean). npm run test:cljs exit 0 — 11217 tests / 56650 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, with re_frame.nine_states_cljs_test enumerated by the runner. check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0, controlled with two plants (broken target and broken anchor) that each returned exit 1 naming the edited README region, then restored and cmp-verified. mkdocs build --strict and check_doc_slugs.py do NOT cover examples/ and were not cited.

NOT DONE, and filed rather than glossed: the deterministic overlap regression this bead's acceptance criteria asked for. examples/ is test-free (rf2-8cevm) and the witness needs a controlled transport under implementation/, which was outside this change's fence. Filed as rf2-5bmi with the full shape — hold A open, issue B through the shipped event, prove A reaches no app target, settle B and prove only B's result chooses the state, a cross-kind row, and a negative control that removes the shared id. This bead's behavioural criterion is therefore carried by rf2-5bmi, not satisfied here.

title: surface-review(examples-machines): clear stale login errors when leaving :error-shown
description:
## Scope

Correct the error lifecycle in `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/**` and strengthen its existing out-of-tree headless coverage. Keep the three-attempt lockout, managed-HTTP stub, draft slice, tag-driven view, and test-free examples policy. This is a small correctness/teaching repair, not a redesign of machines or forms.

## Finding

The walkthrough records each failed reply into machine `:data :error`, but neither transition out of `:error-shown` clears it:

- `:walkthrough.login/dismiss -> :idle` has only a target.
- `:walkthrough.login/submit -> :submitting` has only a target.

The view renders the error row whenever `err` is non-nil and the machine is not locked; it does not condition the row on `:error-shown`. Consequently, clicking the visible **Dismiss** button changes the banner to `idle` but leaves the same error and Dismiss button on screen. Further Dismiss clicks are unhandled no-ops in `:idle`. Submitting directly from `:error-shown` likewise carries the old error into the new `:submitting` request. The initial `:idle -> :submitting` transition does run `:clear-error`, but that is too late to make Dismiss dismiss anything and does not cover direct retry.

This is exactly the kind of copyable SPA pattern an example must get right: status and error data disagree, and a control named Dismiss has no visible effect.

## Evidence

- `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:74-75` already defines the minimal reusable `:clear-error` action as `{:data {:error nil}}`.
- `core.cljc:98-101` writes the failure message into `:data :error`.
- `core.cljc:126-128` declares both exits from `:error-shown` without `:clear-error`.
- `views.cljs:44-45,69-76` subscribes to the error and renders the row/button solely from `(and err (not locked?))`; after Dismiss, `locked?` is false and `err` is unchanged.
- Spec 005, `Action effect map — {:data :fx}` (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:737-755`), says `:data` is merged into existing machine data. Reusing `:clear-error` therefore preserves `:attempts`; no custom reset/event/sub is needed. The implementation performs that merge at `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2025-2029`.
- The current guide's corresponding full transition (`docs/machines/tutorial.md:193-197`, repeated at 435-439) does clear the error on direct retry. The walkthrough's namespace says to read it beside the guide and its README calls this the chapter flow, so this is behavioral drift, not an intentional alternate policy. The guide view hides errors by exact state; the walkthrough intentionally does not, making Dismiss's missing clear observable here.
- Existing out-of-tree coverage misses it: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj:906-922` dispatches Dismiss twice but asserts only the eventual `:locked-out` state. It never reads `:walkthrough.login/error` after Dismiss or inspects a direct retry snapshot.
- The runnable build is correctly declared at `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1723-1730`, but `npm run test:examples-compile` is compile/warning coverage only (`examples/TESTING.md:15-23`; `implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs:57-82`), so it cannot detect this state/data mismatch.
- History explains why it survived. The original browser spec (introduced by `58adfc02e7`) clicked Dismiss and asserted only that the banner said `idle`, never that the error row disappeared. Per-example browser specs were intentionally removed by `2d2f4aff53`; the present framework test inherited the same narrow assertion. The June 26 draft-slice refactor `2dc95699af` retained the data-only error render. The Aug 13 guide rewrite `6012a7b21a` added `:clear-error` to direct retry but did not update this example.

## Recommended bounded fix

Reuse the existing machine-local `:clear-error` action on both transitions that leave `:error-shown`: Dismiss to `:idle`, and Submit to `:submitting`. This is two table entries, preserves `:attempts` by the documented merge rule, and makes the current view truthful without adding a state predicate, another tag, another subscription, or view-local cleanup.
