- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:260-384, especially 328-337: validate-resource-spec! checks only contains? for :request. reg-resource at 435-535 reconstructs metadata plus the unchecked third value before validation.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_registry.cljc:59-183, especially 78-86: validate-mutation-spec! has the same presence-only check. reg-mutation at 187-296 stores the unchecked third value.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:753-754 invokes (:request spec) unconditionally during ensure.
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1280-1283 invokes (:request spec) unconditionally during execute.
- Existing boundary tests cover missing/mislocated request and malformed metadata but not a non-function third slot: implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs:109-151 and implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc:207-247.

## Verified behavior

Reproduced from implementation/resources at HEAD ac778f089a by registering a resource and mutation with valid metadata and integer request values:

    (r/reg-resource :review/nonfn-resource
      {:scope :rf.scope/global :params-schema [:map]} 42)
    (r/reg-mutation :review/nonfn-mutation
      {:params-schema [:map]} 42)

Both calls returned their IDs and both introspection APIs reported :request 42. Directly exercising ensure-handler and execute-handler then produced:

    :ensure  java.lang.ClassCastException ... Long cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IFn :ex-data nil
    :execute java.lang.ClassCastException ... Long cannot be cast to clojure.lang.IFn :ex-data nil

The reproduction process exited 0 because it caught and printed the exceptions; registration itself did not throw.

## Bounded recommendation

At the shared registration-validation boundary, require the reconstructed :request value to satisfy the library's documented function predicate, matching the existing reg-resource-scope convention. Reject a bad resource with :rf.error/resource-bad-spec and a bad mutation with :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec, include the definition ID and offending value/type in ex-data, use :recovery :fix-registration, and do so before registry mutation. Add focused resource and mutation registration regressions in the existing boundary suites.

Non-goals: do not introspect callback arity; do not invoke request functions during registration; do not validate the managed-HTTP result until normal invocation; do not broaden this bead into auditing every optional callback or redesigning metadata validation.

## Posture rationale

This is a small fail-fast guard on a core public API, not defensive gold-plating. It removes a low-information delayed crash and makes both human and AI-authored SPA definitions faster to diagnose while preserving the minimal three-slot API and trusting valid programmer-supplied functions.

## Duplicate and history search

Searched all bead statuses for request-fn, request function, non-fn, resource-bad-spec, mutation-bad-spec, ClassCastException, request handler, callable, and third slot; repeated description/notes searches for request-fn, request function, non-fn/non-function, and third slot. There was no matching resources issue. The only callable hit was closed rf2-6r9j.30 in reagent-slim; the only third-slot hit was closed rf2-td8oe about reg-resource-scope documentation.

Searched all Git refs by commit message and diff for the same terms plus fn?/request combinations. Commits 06303b9ade, 3d22a1d776, and 04c585b6aa introduced/migrated the strict request-fn grammar; 06261ac1a9 added metadata-slot guards; 56fe742fac introduced mutation registration. None validates request function-ness, and current-tree search finds no such guard or regression.

## Uncertainty

The contract and sibling registrar point to fn? rather than the broader ifn?. If deliberately supporting custom IFn objects is desired, that should be stated and tested explicitly; keywords/maps/sets should not become accidental request handlers merely because they are invokable on one host. Portable two-argument arity validation is intentionally outside scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- reg-resource synchronously rejects a non-function third request slot before registration, using :rf.error/resource-bad-spec with the resource ID, offending value/type, and :recovery :fix-registration in structured ex-data.
- reg-mutation does the same using :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec and the mutation ID.
- Focused tests in resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs and resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc prove the invalid entries are not introspectable after rejection and valid request functions still register unchanged.
- The regressions run in every supported host exercised by those existing CLJS/CLJC suites and assert canonical structured errors rather than only matching host exception text.
- No callback arity probing, eager request invocation, managed-HTTP return validation, or optional-callback audit is added.
notes:
REOPENED BY MERGED-PR AUDIT OF #9218. The registration validators and host-specific coverage are correct, and Spec 016 now states the callable request contract. The consolidated error catalogue in spec/009-Instrumentation.md was not updated, however. Its :rf.error/resource-bad-spec and :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec rows still say the errors cover only an omitted required key or a non-map spec; their recovery text says merely to declare :request plus :params-schema; and their payload text says :value is present only when the spec itself is not a map. The landed validators also raise these ids for a PRESENT but non-callable :request and put that offending request in :value, so both catalogue rows now understate the raised condition, prescribe an insufficient repair, and misdescribe the payload.

Minimal repair: update those two Spec 009 rows to include non-callable :request, say the handler must be a fn (or accepted Var), and state that :value carries either the bad spec or bad request as applicable. Preserve the existing ids and links and hand-check the Markdown table column counts. No implementation or test expansion is needed.

---
AUDIT-NOTE VERIFIED AT TIP, AND THE REMAINING WORK IS FENCE-BLOCKED (2026-09-05, worker coreguard-a).

The 2026-09-04T17:30:38Z reopening note is correct in every particular; re-verified at
source rather than taken on trust:

IMPLEMENTATION HAS LANDED. Both registrars now gate the third slot before any registry
mutation, with `(when-not (or (fn? (:request spec)) (var? (:request spec))) …)`:
  - re_frame/resources/registry.cljc — raises :rf.error/resource-bad-spec, ex-data
    {:resource-id … :value (:request spec)}, :where 'rf/reg-resource.
  - re_frame/resources/mutation_registry.cljc — raises :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec,
    ex-data {:mutation-id … :value (:request spec)}, :where 'rf/reg-mutation.
The predicate is `fn? OR var?`, NOT the bare `fn?` this bead's description proposed —
a deliberate, documented improvement: on the JVM `clojure.lang.Var` implements `IFn`
but not `Fn`, so `(fn? #'my-fetch)` is FALSE there and TRUE in CLJS, and `#'my-fetch`
is the idiomatic hot-reload indirection. A bare `fn?` gate would have rejected working
code on one host only. `ifn?` is deliberately still refused, for the silent-nil reason
the bead itself gives. This resolves the bead's stated Uncertainty.

TESTS HAVE LANDED: resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs (:test/nonfn-request) and
resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc (:m/nonfn-request), both asserting the canonical id,
the definition id, and that the entry is NOT introspectable after rejection.

SPEC 016 HAS LANDED: :576-585's successor now states the callable contract explicitly
("`:request` is gated on being CALLABLE, not merely present"), and 016's own local
error table row says "or its `:request` is not callable".

GATE: `clojure -M:test` in implementation/resources — 829 tests / 7537 assertions,
0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0.

WHAT REMAINS IS EXACTLY WHAT THE NOTE SAYS AND NOTHING ELSE: the two
spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue rows. spec/009-Instrumentation.md is a HOT-ZONE,
single-toucher file under this repo's dispatch convention, so this worker did NOT edit
it — stop-and-report per the fence. The rows still understate the raised condition in
all three ways the note names; the payload clause is the sharpest, since both landed
guards put the offending request in `:value` while the rows say `:value` is present
only when the spec itself was not a map.

Ready-to-apply substance for whoever holds spec/009 (preserve the existing ids, links,
Channel and tags; hand-check the Markdown column counts):
  - Condition: add "or its `:request` was present but NOT CALLABLE" alongside the
    omitted-required-key and non-map-spec cases.
  - Recovery: "declare :params-schema + :request, and make :request a fn (a Var
    holding one is also accepted)".
  - Payload: ":value carries the offending spec when the spec was not a map, or the
    offending :request when it was not callable".

NOT a new bead: this is the same bead's remaining leg, held only by the hot-zone fence.

---
CATALOGUE ROWS NOW AUTHORED (2026-09-05, worker coreguard-a). Supersedes the
"stop-and-report" paragraph above.

The coordinator widened the fence to make this worker the single toucher of
spec/009-Instrumentation.md for exactly three rows. Both rows this bead owed —
:rf.error/resource-bad-spec and :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec — are updated in commit
965f290508 on PR #9259, alongside rf2-xn13's new row, because the catalogue ratchet pins
source against the table and the halves cannot be split across PRs.

Each row now (i) names the PRESENT-but-NOT-CALLABLE :request condition beside the
omitted-key and non-map-spec cases, (ii) says the handler must be a fn, with a Var
holding one also accepted, and (iii) states that :value carries the offending spec when
the spec was not a map OR the offending :request when it was not callable. Existing ids,
links, Channel cells and tags preserved; column counts hand-checked (7 pipes each).

Gates: catalogue ratchet 30 tests / 179 assertions exit 0; full core artefact 2183 tests
/ 11283 assertions exit 0; full resources artefact 829 tests / 7537 assertions exit 0;
check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. No implementation or test change was needed, as the audit note
said. This bead has no remaining work; the coordinator closes it when #9259 merges.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS ALREADY FIXED — the premise did not hold, and the verification is the deliverable. No code was written for this bead.

WHAT HAPPENED: the bead was closed by PR #9218, then REOPENED 2026-09-04T17:30:38Z by a merged-PR audit that narrowed it. The dispatched worker's bd history walk found that audit note as the newest text-bearing mutation (notes 0->1143 chars), and the walk was CONTROLLED — it detected real changes on this item, so 'no newer change' is a finding rather than an empty-walk artefact.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE at tip: both registrars already gate the third request-fn slot BEFORE registry mutation. And the landed predicate is BETTER than the one my dispatch brief specified: (or (fn? ...) (var? ...)) rather than bare fn?, because a JVM Var implements IFn but not Fn — so (fn? #'my-fetch) is FALSE on the JVM and TRUE in CLJS, and a bare fn? guard would have rejected a var-held handler on one host while accepting it on the other. That difference resolves the bead's own recorded Uncertainty. Tests and Spec 016 prose also landed with #9218.

WHAT REMAINED, and it shipped in PR #9259 (merged, main at 86e8a8b6b1): the audit's residual was two spec/009-Instrumentation.md catalogue rows. :rf.error/resource-bad-spec and :rf.error/mutation-bad-spec each now name the present-but-non-callable :request, say the handler must be a fn with a Var holding one accepted, and correct the payload clause to 'the offending spec when not a map, OR the offending :request when not callable'. The worker verified the diff touched exactly three hunks by grepping the diff rather than by eye, and left rf2-6g6e's stale frame-destroyed row in the same file untouched.

So both halves are on main: the guard from #9218, the catalogue rows from #9259.

title: core/configure!: non-map calls silently no-op when host builds elide assertions
description:
## Slice reviewed

implementation/core/**, with the actionable center at implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc, public symbol re-frame.core/configure!. Governing contract and focused coverage inspected at spec/API.md and implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj. This is the one finding selected after source/API/spec/test/call-site/history review of the slice.

## User-visible and maintainer impact

configure! is a front-porch process-configuration API. Its public contract says it accepts one nested map and that a non-map argument fails loudly. Today that safety depends on the host compiler retaining language assertions. In a legitimate assertion-elided consumer build, a stale keyed-form call such as (rf/configure! :trace-buffer), a vector, or nil silently returns nil and applies nothing. The programmer can therefore believe trace, epoch, or elision configuration was installed when it was ignored. This is especially awkward in pre-alpha, where the retired keyed form is exactly the mistake migration can produce.

The correction is high leverage and low friction: one always-on public-boundary check, one canonical structured error, and focused dual-posture tests. It strengthens the minimal API without adding a validator framework or policing unknown map keys.

## Independently verified current behavior

At repository tip 1ad17a77fe:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2594-2596 implements the entire top-level shape check as (assert (map? config-map) ...).
- With the namespace compiled normally on Clojure 1.12.0, direct calls with :trace-buffer, [:trace-buffer {:events-retained 3}], and nil each throw java.lang.AssertionError.
- In a fresh JVM process, loading re-frame.core inside (binding [*assert* false] (require 're-frame.core)) and then making those same three calls makes every call return nil. No subsystem runs and no diagnostic is emitted.
- The upstream Clojure 1.12.0 assert macro explicitly omits its check when *assert* is false.
- The locally resolved ClojureScript 1.12.145 compiler binds *assert* false when :elide-asserts is true, and the CLJS assert macro only emits code when *assert* is true. Therefore the same source check is absent from such CLJS output.
- The current focused test command, run from implementation/core, is green: clojure -M:test -n re-frame.configure-test ran 5 tests / 28 assertions with zero failures. This demonstrates the coverage gap, not safety under assertion elision.

## Concrete evidence and history

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2554-2605 — configure! docstring and implementation; lines 2578 and 2595-2596 promise/enforce the map shape via assert.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj:281-293 — configure-non-map-arg-fails-loud explicitly couples all three examples to AssertionError, but compiles only in the ordinary assertion-on posture.
- spec/API.md:872 and :896 — the API is front-porch and says a non-map argument fails loud / MUST be a map.
- git blame attributes the assert to 6730961c897 (2026-06-19), refactor(api): configure! single nested-map entry point (rf2-dzxixe). That commit deliberately retired the keyed form and described non-map input as fail-loud, so silent acceptance under elision contradicts the intended change rather than introducing a new policy.
- bd show rf2-dzxixe reports no matching issue in the current tracker.

## Recommended change

Replace the language assert with an explicit always-on when-not map? check routed through the existing re-frame.error/throw-error! helper already required by re-frame.core. Add one canonical category (suggested name :rf.error/configure-bad-arg), with :where rf/configure!, a short recovery hint to pass one nested map, and bounded/type-oriented received context rather than echoing arbitrary application configuration. Update the error catalogue/projection where project conventions require it.

Preserve the deliberately ergonomic map behavior exactly: valid composed maps still configure known subsystems in the present order; missing keys leave state untouched; unknown top-level keys remain silent no-ops. The reason to use the existing structured-error chokepoint is consistency and AI/tool discoverability, not a broader validation system.

## Bounded implementation scope and non-goals

In scope: the top-level argument guard, its canonical error entry/projection, the focused configure tests, and a genuine assertion-elided verification posture for both runtimes.

Non-goals: do not reject unknown top-level keys; do not validate every nested subsystem option here; do not restore the retired keyed arity; do not redesign configuration schemas/order/merge semantics; do not introduce a general argument-validation abstraction.

## Duplicate search

Tracker searches were run across all statuses before filing:

- bd search "configure" --status all --limit 200 --long: no matches.
- "elide asserts configure", "non-map configure", "configure assertion", "AssertionError", "assertions disabled", and "elide-asserts": no matches.
- broad "assert" search returned four closed issues, all unrelated (routing fixture syntax, Hicasso prose, API-manifest classification, and a prefetch roster assertion).
- description search for configure! returned five unrelated surface/doc facade issues; none concerns core configure argument validation.
- The historical rf2-dzxixe reference is not present in the current tracker.

## Uncertainties

The JVM failure and silent-no-op postures were executed directly. The CLJS conclusion was verified from the resolved compiler and macro sources, but this review did not build a standalone release bundle; the acceptance criteria intentionally require that executable CLJS probe. The exact new error-id spelling should follow the catalogue owner's naming convention; the stable requirement is an always-on canonical structured error, not the suggested token.
design: Keep the patch local to the existing public boundary. A representative shape is (when-not (map? config-map) (rf.error/throw-error! ...)); re-frame.core already requires re-frame.error. Do not move known-key dispatch or tighten the additive top-level vocabulary. Prefer a focused compile-time negative control over a test that merely rebinding *assert* after re-frame.core has already loaded.
acceptance_criteria:
- A non-map passed to re-frame.core/configure! throws one canonical ExceptionInfo error in ordinary Clojure and when re-frame.core is compiled with *assert* false; tests cover at least the retired keyword form, a vector, and nil.
- A ClojureScript test/probe compiled with :elide-asserts true proves the same non-map call still throws the same :rf.error/id; an assertions-on CLJS control remains covered.
- Existing valid-map semantics stay unchanged: all known keys in one map are applied in documented order, a missing key leaves that subsystem untouched, and an unknown top-level key remains a nil-returning no-op.
- The focused tests no longer require AssertionError as the public contract; they assert the canonical id, :where, recovery/reason shape, and avoid requiring raw arbitrary config values in ex-data.
- The error catalogue/API projection is updated as required, and the implementation/core Clojure suite plus the relevant CLJS and production/elision probes pass.
notes:
---
IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED, BLOCKED ON ONE HOT-ZONE CATALOGUE ROW (2026-09-05, worker coreguard-a).
PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9259 (DRAFT, deliberately)

PREMISE CONFIRMED at tip: core.cljc's guard was `(assert (map? config-map) …)`.

CHANGE: replaced with `when-not` + `re-frame.error/throw-error!` raising
:rf.error/configure-bad-arg, :where 'rf/configure!, :recovery :pass-a-config-map,
:extra {:received (rf.error/diag-value-summary config-map)} — content-free by
construction, so no application configuration is echoed. Mirrors
re-frame.live-frame/validate-opts! (:rf.error/make-frame-bad-opts), the sibling
public-boundary map guard in the SAME artefact; no new pattern was invented, and this
was found by inspection rather than assumed. Top-level shape only: unknown top-level
keys still no-op, nested options untouched, keyed arity not restored.

DUAL-POSTURE TEST, and why it is shaped this way: a test that rebinds *assert* at CALL
time proves nothing, because `assert` is a macro and the decision was taken when
re-frame.core was COMPILED — the bead's own DESIGN field warns of exactly this.
`configure-non-map-guard-survives-assertion-elision` therefore reads configure!'s ACTUAL
source form (clojure.repl/source-fn + `read` with :read-cond :allow) and RE-COMPILES it
under `binding [*assert* false]` into a throwaway namespace carrying re-frame.core's own
aliases. Genuine compile-time control; no reload of re-frame.core, so no global suite
state is disturbed; and it cannot drift into asserting over a hand-copied guard.
Two controls, both measured:
  - ANTI-VACUITY: a language `(assert (map? x))` compiled by the same harness really
    does NOT fire. Without this the whole test could pass with nothing elided.
  - NEGATIVE CONTROL: with the previous `assert` implementation temporarily restored,
    all three non-map arguments returned nil and the suite failed 6 assertions /
    1 error. That is the defect reproduced, then caught.
The elided build is also shown to still APPLY a valid map and still no-op on an unknown
top-level key, so the guard did not become a throw-everything stub.

GATES (from implementation/core):
  - `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.configure-test` — 6 tests / 56 assertions, 0 failures,
    exit 0 (baseline before the change: 5 tests / 28 assertions).
  - `clojure -M:test` (full artefact) — 2183 tests / 11283 assertions, 1 failure,
    0 errors, exit 1.

THE ONE FAILURE IS THE BLOCKER, and it is structural rather than a defect in this
change. :rf.error/configure-bad-arg is a NEW category, and
`every-emitted-category-is-catalogued` (rf2-9fvp25) source-scans every artefact's src/
for the first literal keyword of throw-error!/thrown-ex-info and demands a matching row
in spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Error event catalogue. Measured, not inferred: the gate
was green before the change (35 tests / 207 assertions, exit 0) and reds afterwards
naming exactly #{:rf.error/configure-bad-arg} and nothing else.

Because that gate pins SOURCE against the CATALOGUE, the code and the row MUST land in
ONE commit — a code-only merge reddens main. spec/009-Instrumentation.md is a HOT-ZONE
single-toucher file, so this worker did not author the row (stop-and-report per the
fence) and the PR is held as a DRAFT. The out-of-catalogue-allow-list was considered and
REJECTED: it is a live ratchet seam, currently empty, and an entry there would suppress

title: CLAUDE.md: six measured machine hazards live only in ad-hoc dispatch text — not in the template (correctly) and not in CLAUDE.md (incorrectly)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by the mayor's method-reread loop, checking enforced rules against the tree rather than reading the method docs.

THE DRIFT. Six machine-specific hazards were MEASURED this session, each with a control, and every one of them lives ONLY in the acting mayor's ad-hoc dispatch text. Verified absent from both homes: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md reads 0 for every one of them, and CLAUDE.md reads 0 as well.

WHY THAT IS WRONG IN TWO DIRECTIONS AT ONCE. The method README says the preamble, the worktree-boundary block and the gate-mechanics block TRAVEL VERBATIM, and that the concrete values they need — gate commands, tracker commands, hot-zone lists — belong in the project's own agent-instructions file. So composing a gate block out of template content PLUS session findings breaks the first rule, and leaving the findings only in chat breaks the second. A fresh mayor inherits none of it, and the method docs are deliberately repo-agnostic so they are not the place either.

THE COST IS NOT THEORETICAL FOR AT LEAST ONE ITEM. CLAUDE.md already records that a bare `git worktree remove` followed a node_modules junction and emptied the mayor's real tree, and that "It has happened twice". Item 1 below is that same hazard reached through a different door: the REMOVAL line the mayor has been shipping in briefs all session silently does nothing.

WHAT TO ADD TO CLAUDE.md — all six measured, with the controls that established them:

1. `cmd /c` INVOKED FROM GIT BASH IS A SILENT NO-OP THAT RETURNS EXIT 0. It prints the Windows banner, drops into an interactive prompt, and runs nothing. From PowerShell the identical command works. Measured on a scratch junction: Bash `cmd /c mklink /J` -> exit 0, NO LINK; PowerShell `cmd /c mklink /J` -> "Junction created"; PowerShell `New-Item -ItemType Junction` -> link present and readable through. THE DANGEROUS HALF IS THE REMOVAL: every `cmd /c rmdir "<junction>"` cleanup line in a brief reports success and removes nothing, and a surviving junction is what later cleanup follows into the real node_modules. Prescribe PowerShell for both, and VERIFY THE EFFECT rather than the exit code (list the linked path after creating; after removing, confirm the link is gone AND the mayor's node_modules still counts 103 under `ls -A`). NOTE scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh is NOT affected — it unlinks with plain `rm` without -r and already falls back to PowerShell for creation.

2. USE THE RIPGREP-BACKED SEARCH TOOL, NOT BASH grep. Two "false zero mechanisms" previously briefed as properties of the machine were artefacts of reaching for bash grep: `grep -iF` returns EMPTY on this box (measured: `-F 'beads'` 19, `-iF 'beads'` empty, `-i 'BeAdS'` 24, control on a second file identical), and a repo-wide recursive scan can exceed the command timeout and print nothing while a pipeline swallows its status. Ripgrep does neither.

3. NEVER PIPE A CENSUS THROUGH `head` WHEN THE COUNT IS THE DELIVERABLE — the cap reports itself as the population. Measured on the mayor: a `head -8` produced "eight surviving hits" in a brief where TWENTY-FIVE existed, and the truncation hid the single most valuable one. Take the count separately from the listing; if you cap a display, write "first N of M".

4. A CENSUS NEEDS TWO TOKEN AXES, NOT JUST TWO INSTRUMENTS. The line-oriented-versus-flattened rule is about the INSTRUMENT; this is about the TARGET — the same mechanism is described in different WORDS in different files. Measured: a third stale site was found only by searching a second, rarer token, and the file a previous worker had flagged never used the first token at all.

5. A CAPTURED EXIT CODE IS NOT ALWAYS SUFFICIENT. shadow-cljs grades a reference to a REMOVED VAR as a WARNING and exits 0, so for a deletion the discriminating signal is the WARNING COUNT against a zero baseline. Independently, mkdocs grades a missing ANCHOR at INFO and --strict promotes only WARNING, so the strict build names a broken anchor on stdout and still exits 0. Both measured with planted faults. Check what a gate GRADES a finding as before trusting its status to carry one.

6. GIT BASH MANGLES `git show <ref>:<path>` WHEN BOTH THE REF AND THE PATH CONTAIN SLASHES. MSYS reads `a/b:c/d` as a colon-separated POSIX path LIST and rewrites it to `a\b;c\d`. Measured across all four combinations: HEAD:CLAUDE.md fine, HEAD:.github/workflows/test.yml fine, origin/main:CLAUDE.md fine, origin/main:.github/workflows/test.yml -> `fatal: ambiguous argument`. IT FAILS LOUDLY; it only reads as silent when stdout is piped into a counter and stderr goes unread. Fixes: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1, or `git grep -F <needle> <ref> -- <path>`, or the two-arg form. AND THE STANDING LESSON: READ STDERR.

SCOPE: CLAUDE.md only. Do NOT edit docs/the-mayor-method/** — those files are deliberately repo-agnostic and none of this belongs there. Add these where they fit the existing structure (the Workflow bullets and the worktree-removal bullet are the natural homes); do not create a new top-level section if an existing bullet owns the subject.

SEQUENCING: CLAUDE.md is read by every agent and is edited rarely. Check no other dispatch is touching it. It is not in the hot-zone list, but treat it as one-toucher for the duration.

GATES: python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci covers repo-root markdown including CLAUDE.md — check_doc_slugs.py does NOT (its roots are docs/, spec/, skills/, migration/, tools/*/spec). Nominate by PATH, not by job name: the job named verify-readme-links runs both, and the one that actually reads CLAUDE.md is check_readme_links.py. NOTHING validates the prose's truth; the check is re-running each measurement above and confirming the text matches what you observe.
notes:

The PR correctly records the measured junction hazard in CLAUDE.md, but the tracked root AGENTS.md still gives the opposite operational instruction at lines 40-43: use `cmd /c rmdir <path>` on Windows, followed by the unqualified claim that it and plain `rm` "unlink on every platform". PR #9173's own scratch-junction measurement establishes that when a worker follows that command from Git Bash it returns exit 0 while leaving the junction present — exactly the live link a later recursive removal can traverse into the mayor's real node_modules. AGENTS.md is an agent-facing execution surface and this session received it verbatim, so the omission preserves the data-loss path the PR intended to close.

Repair the junction section in AGENTS.md as the same owner: make the Windows command shell-safe (the PR verified PowerShell `[System.IO.Directory]::Delete(path, $false)`) and explicitly rule out `cmd /c` from Git Bash; retain the plain non-recursive `rm` rule for the POSIX removal script. Do not mechanically replace the other two repository mentions: scripts/remove-worker-worktree.ps1 invokes cmd from PowerShell, where #9173 verified it works, and scripts/reap-stale-test-processes.ps1 is likewise PowerShell-context prose. Validate only on a scratch junction, never through the shared node_modules target, and verify both that the link vanished and its target stayed intact.

title: method: the dispatch preamble tells every worker to walk history fields that do not exist — notes and design are absent from bd history's schema, so the currency walk fails OPEN on the one field the mayor writes rulings into
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 by worker/machvest-a, which controlled the instrument in both directions before trusting it, and re-verified by the mayor on rf2-6r9j.2.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md's common preamble instructs every worker: 'WALK ADJACENT PAIRS NEWEST-FIRST UNTIL THE FIRST CHANGE TO A TEXT-BEARING FIELD (description, notes, acceptance, design)'.

THE FIELDS A bd history --json SNAPSHOT ACTUALLY CARRIES on this build, measured:
  acceptance_criteria, close_reason, closed_at, created_at, created_by,
  description, id, issue_type, owner, priority, status, title, updated_at

So of the four the preamble names: description EXISTS; acceptance is spelled acceptance_criteria; and notes and design DO NOT EXIST AT ALL.

WHY THIS FAILS OPEN, which is the whole defect. A worker keying its walk on 'notes' or 'design' reads null in every snapshot. Null hashes constant across every adjacent pair, so the walk reports NO TEXT-BEARING CHANGE — the exact false-clean the preamble exists to prevent, arrived at by following the preamble exactly. Nothing errors and the answer is well-formed. machvest-a hit this and only caught it because it controlled the detector against a field it knew varied.

AND THE MISSING FIELD IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. 'notes' is where the mayor writes rulings, sequencing fences, audit reopenings and salvage records — via bd update --append-notes. It is the field whose currency the walk exists to establish. bd history cannot order notes by mutation time AT ALL on this build, so the instruction promises a capability the tool does not have. Workers DO see notes rendered by bd show; what they cannot do is establish WHEN a note arrived relative to a description edit, which is precisely the ordering problem the paragraph was written to solve.

THE FIX, and it needs both halves:
1. Correct the field list to what the schema carries: description and acceptance_criteria. Drop notes and design from the enumeration.
2. State the consequence rather than hiding it — that notes are NOT in the history schema, so history orders description/acceptance_criteria/title/status/priority only, and a note's arrival time cannot be established this way. Tell the worker what to do instead: read bd show's notes in full and treat the LAST note as newest by position (which is how --append-notes writes), while using history for the fields it does cover. Say plainly that this is a weaker guarantee than the paragraph currently implies.
3. Keep the existing control instruction and strengthen it: exercise the walk against a field known to vary before believing any 'no change' answer — that control is what caught this.

ALSO WORTH FIXING WHILE THERE: the same preamble's jq guidance needs to say that a history entry's fields nest under .Issue on this build. A walk keyed at the top level matches nothing and produces the identical false 'no change' — a second worker hit that separately today.

MAYOR CHECKOUT HAS A COMMIT GUARD ON METHOD DOCS, so this is filed with the fix written out rather than edited in place. Dispatch it to a worker with docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md in its fence.

RELATED: rf2-4wko covers a different defect in the same file (blocks retyped rather than extracted, and a gate paraphrase that inverts the detach ruling). Sequence the two — the file is one-toucher by contention, not by rule.
notes:
CORRECTION BY THE MAYOR, 2026-09-04 — THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS WRONG AND THE FIX MUST CHANGE. Read this note before the description; the description's headline is refuted.

WHAT I CLAIMED: 'notes and design are NOT in this build's history schema at all', with a field list I presented as the schema.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, measured across four beads chosen for differing field populations:

  bead          notes len   acc len   keys contain notes?   keys contain acceptance_criteria?
  rf2-6r9j.2        0         637            NO                        YES
  rf2-ydpr       9804           0           YES                         NO
  rf2-lo9s       1518           0           YES                         NO
  rf2-xpd8          0           0            NO                         NO

bd history --json OMITS EMPTY FIELDS. The key set is PER BEAD and tracks exactly which fields are populated on that bead. So 'keys' on one bead's snapshot is that bead's populated field set, NOT the build's schema. I derived a general claim from rf2-6r9j.2 alone, which happens to carry no notes — the same relay-without-checking error this session has made four other times, except the source was my own single measurement rather than a worker's report.

worker/ratchettool-a caught it independently while walking rf2-ydpr: notes IS carried there and DOES vary, with 7 real change points. Its control found what mine could not, because it walked a bead that has notes.

THE DEFECT IS STILL REAL, AND STILL FAILS OPEN — only the cause changes. A jq walk keyed on a field that is EMPTY on that bead sees the key ABSENT from every snapshot, so .notes yields null, null hashes constant across every adjacent pair, and the walk reports 'no text-bearing change'. Identical false clean, reached by emptiness rather than by absence-from-schema. And it is worse than it looks, because the same walk on a DIFFERENT bead works perfectly — so the instruction is not reliably broken, it is intermittently broken, which is harder to notice.

THE REVISED FIX:
1. DO NOT write 'notes is not in the history schema'. It is false. Do not write a field list presented as the schema at all — there isn't one visible this way.
2. DO say: bd history --json omits empty fields, so a key's ABSENCE from a snapshot means 'empty on this bead', not 'not tracked'. A walk must therefore treat absent and null as the same thing and must not conclude 'no change' from a field that was never populated.
3. KEEP the spelling correction: the preamble says 'acceptance'; the field is acceptance_criteria. That half was right.
4. KEEP the .Issue nesting note. That half was right and a second worker hit it independently.
5. STRENGTHEN the control instruction, which is now doubly earned: it is what caught the original defect AND what caught my wrong diagnosis of it. Exercise the walk against a field KNOWN TO VARY ON THE BEAD IN FRONT OF YOU before believing any 'no change'. A control run on a different bead proves nothing about this one.
6. 'design' — I have NOT established whether it is tracked. None of the four beads shows it, but all four may simply have it empty. Say nothing about it rather than repeating my error; or measure it and report.

The worker holding this bead (worker/methodfix-a) has been sent this correction directly.

Mayor's mid-task correction applied: notes and design ARE tracked (design measured present in 771/771 snapshots on a bead that populates it, 4 of 1685 beads), so no field list is presented as a schema. title: validate-with-schemas how-to never says validation is whole-registry per commit
description:
docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md teaches `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas` and
never states the one fact a reader needs to use them safely: validation is NOT scoped to the
paths the committing event touched. At every `:db` commit the runtime walks EVERY registered
path over the WHOLE candidate app-db with `get-in` and rejects the entire transaction if any
one of them fails (spec/010 §Per-step recovery row 4). A path nothing has written yet reads
`nil`, so a registration made before its slice is seeded rejects every commit until the seed
lands - and if the seeds are spread across separate events, the first seed is rejected by its
not-yet-seeded siblings and app-db never leaves `{}`.

That is the whole of rf2-2xzc, and rf2-ghxt is the same defect in the sibling example. Two of
the repo's own flagship applications got it wrong, so it is not an exotic corner: the two
idioms that compose into it - a bulk `reg-app-schemas` at ns-load, and a per-feature
`:*/initialise` fan-out from `:app/initialise` - are both idioms this corpus teaches.

The remedy the corpus already knows is written only in a code comment, in
examples/patterns/boot/schema.cljs: 'Each slot below starts out nil - the boot machine fills
it in later - so every registration wears a `:maybe` to stay valid through the loading
phases.' That sentence, and the reason behind it, belong in the how-to.

WANTED, roughly a paragraph plus an example: state that the registry is walked whole at every
commit; state that an unwritten path reads nil and is validated like any other value; give
the two ways out (seed the slice before or in the same commit as everything else, or wear a
`:maybe` for the boot window); and say plainly that a production build elides the validator,
so an app that gets this wrong works in release and is dead in dev - the direction of the
dev/release split that makes this so disorienting to meet.

Gate: docs/ is inside check_doc_slugs.py's roots AND is built by `mkdocs build --strict`
(docs_dir is `docs`), so both apply to an edit here. Neither validates prose, so table columns
and anchors get checked by hand.
notes: AUDIT PR #9141: The new boot paragraph conflates the :fx-only fan-out event with the child :db seed events. The shown :app/initialise is not app-db-validated, so every child dispatch fires; each child seed is then rejected while siblings remain nil. Correct the causal account and pin both shapes.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: this close REVERTED and the payload is on the trunk.

Delivered by worker/docfix-a in PR #9141, MERGED. Verified in SOURCE at origin/main, not from the PR record: docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:159 now carries the section 'Every registered path is checked on every commit'.

The worker verified the mechanism at source rather than taking it from its brief: validate-app-schema! loops storage/frame-schema-entries reading each registered path with (get-in db registered-path), and spec/010 row 4 confirms the candidate is never installed on failure. It also found the detail the brief did not have and put it in the doc — row 4 says :fx DOES NOT WALK for a rejected dispatch, which is precisely WHY a per-feature :*/initialise fan-out never fires and app-db never leaves {}. The dev/release elision direction was confirmed in spec/010 §Production builds and in the debug-enabled? gate as the outermost form of the validator.

Gates: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py captured exit 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict captured exit 0, each proved by a planted fault that went red naming the plant, restores verified by git blob hash.

WHY IT REVERTED: the documented mechanism — a worker's bd close is undone when a later 'git checkout HEAD -- .beads' reverts the export and the next checkpoint writes that revert back over the database (CLAUDE.md §Beads durability; rf2-51uz1). title: _changed-surfaces.test.cjs: audit every tier roster for phantom paths and extend the existsSync guard beyond the conformance loop
description:
`implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`'s `SECURITY_TIER_FILES` block carries the same phantom-path defect that rf2-z23f fixed one tier over in `CONFORMANCE_TIERS`, and its own comment records a previous instance of it.

FOUND 2026-09-04 by the worker on rf2-z23f (PR #9133), which repaired the conformance tier and observed that the security block IMMEDIATELY BELOW has the identical shape. That block's comment says its own replaced row asserted from a `security.cljc` that never existed — so this is the third occurrence of one bug class in one file, and the first two were each found by accident rather than by a check.

WHY IT MATTERS: a tier pin naming a file that does not exist CANNOT FAIL. The classifier believes it covers a tier it has never reached, and the mirror suite passes because the row is inert rather than because the coverage is real. That is fail-open, and it is invisible: nothing distinguishes an inert row from a satisfied one.

WHAT TO DO. Verify every path in every tier roster in that file is TRACKED, with two independent instruments and controls that fire — the rf2-z23f worker used `git log --all --diff-filter=A` (control found `7eae1212ac`) and `git rev-list --all --objects` (control found many). Repair any phantom row to the real tracked path.

THE DURABLE FIX IS THE GUARD, NOT THE ROWS. PR #9133 added an `fs.existsSync` guard in the conformance loop, and its sabotage run proved the fail-open is closed: replanting the phantom now reddens the suite where that row was green before. Extend that guard to cover EVERY tier roster in the file, so a fourth occurrence cannot be silent. If the guard already covers the security block once #9133 lands, say so and close — a verified "already covered" is a complete deliverable.

SEQUENCING: rf2-z23f landed in PR #9133. Verify it is on main by payload — `git log origin/main --oneline --grep=rf2-z23f` with dots escaped and a trailing boundary anchor — never by `git merge-base --is-ancestor` on a PR head oid, which is always false here because PRs merge with --rebase.

ONE-TOUCHER: `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` and `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` are a pair whenever a change alters what the classifier OUTPUTS or what the test PINS. rf2-z23f was measured to be a ONE-FILE repair because the classifier's full 29-key output is byte-identical for the phantom and the real paths (the arm is a directory-prefix glob at `report-changed-surfaces.sh:1428`). Establish the same for whatever you change, and say which case it is.
notes: AUDIT #9151 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. The new future-roster self-check can still fail open. It decides whether a roster is guarded with a raw source regex, so commenting out the one-line pinnedRoster call for NEW_TOOLS_JVM_LANES removes the actual existence test while the regex still matches the commented text. Its declaration regex also recognizes only bare const NAME = [ arrays; an Object.freeze([path]) roster — a live array style elsewhere in this same file — is skipped, while the scanned > 0 control remains green because six other bare arrays were found. In-memory counterexamples reproduce both readings: commented call counted as guarded=true; FUTURE_PATHS via Object.freeze seen=0 with six declarations still scanned. Prefer an executable registration Set populated by pinnedRoster for guard membership, and widen or deliberately constrain declaration discovery with sabotage cases for supported roster forms. Exact owner retained; no duplicate bead created.

Delivered by worker/tierpin-b in PR #9151, MERGED at a4a07859d3.

THE BEAD'S HEADLINE PREMISE DID NOT HOLD, and that is the more useful half of the result. SECURITY_TIER_FILES carries NO live phantom — rf2-qxg24 had already corrected its four paths. What it carried was the SHAPE: it was the only tier roster left unguarded beside a guarded one. title: re-frame2-pair skill guide still recommends the fail-open compile-only server-test command
description:
## Finding

PR #9130 corrected the pair-MCP artefact's local `:test` alias and tool-side README after proving that `shadow-cljs compile server-test` is not a test verdict: its `:autorun` prints failures but the compile still exits 0. The skill-facing testing guide still presents that exact compile-only command as the MCP server test suite in two live places:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/TESTING.md:5` says the server "carries its own test suite" under `shadow-cljs compile server-test`.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/TESTING.md:188` says the MCP server suite runs as `shadow-cljs compile server-test` plus the descriptor-manifest drift gate.

The canonical command is `npm test` from `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/`; `package.json` chains the compile to `node out/server-test.js`, and Node's exit code is the verdict. The tool-side `test/README.md` now states this explicitly.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F18 · outcome 5 · `unresolved` · `api`

**The fault I induced**

The mistake chapter 06 spends a warning box on: keying a sequence child by an
entity instead of a primitive. In the feed's sidebar, `:key {:tag tag}` instead
of `:key tag`. Chapter 06: "A complete entity changes when the entity is
edited; React also coerces non-primitive keys, which can remount or collide.
Hicasso reports `:rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key` and identifies the child."
Chapter 16 lists the same id in its complaint table.

**Whether the documented route reached it**

**No. Nothing fired at all**, at any tier I could reach.

- **L2 (`ht/tree`)**: tree built, 2 children, `console.warn` captured and empty,
  and my own view tests stayed green. A real fault, a fully green suite.
- **The dev browser build**: every console message captured from boot through
  the render. Four messages, all of them React's DevTools notice, shadow's
  ready line, and two 404s for a missing stylesheet. No `:rf.warning/…`
  anything. No React key warning either.

I tried it in both child spellings — spliced with `into`, and with the sequence
directly in child position, which is the form chapter 06's own paragraph about
where the check runs describes. Neither produced a complaint.

**What actually happens**

I read the key React received, off the fibers:

```
{"text": "intro",    "key": "{:tag \"intro\"}"}
{"text": "demo",     "key": "{:tag \"demo\"}"}
{"text": "clojure",  "key": "{:tag \"clojure\"}"}
{"text": "re-frame", "key": "{:tag \"re-frame\"}"}
```

The map is `pr-str`'d into a stable, distinct string. So the two hazards
chapter 06 names do not occur: the keys do not collide, and they are stable
across renders for an unedited entity. The behaviour is *better* than the
chapter describes — which is the most likely explanation for the silence, and
would make the missing warning correct rather than broken.

But that reading and "the warning is not raised on this surface" are
indistinguishable from outside, and I cannot tell which without reading source
I am not allowed to read. Either way the chapter is wrong about something: it
either overstates the danger ("React also coerces non-primitive keys, which can
remount or collide" — not here; Hicasso converts first) or it promises a
warning that does not arrive.

**The one that would still bite**: an entity key changes when the entity is
edited, so a favourited article's card would still get a new key and remount,
silently, with no warning. That hazard survives the `pr-str`; the collision one
does not.

**Bead**

Either raise the warning where the chapter says it is raised, or correct the
chapter to describe the `pr-str` behaviour and narrow the hazard to
edit-induced remounting.

**Trying to**

Execute step 2 of the migration chapter's three-step process. The chapter is
emphatic about the order — "Do not start with the codemod. Read the report,
port **and prove** a screen, then apply mechanical edits and run the proof
again" — and §3 is the proof: `hm/shadow!` mounts the Reagent original and the
Hicasso candidate against isolated copies of one seeded frame, drives both with
one script, and compares canonical DOM and intent streams.

**Instead**

Could not run it, for two independent reasons, and the second is the
interesting one.

**(a) It is a mounted-tier door.** `hm/shadow!` lives in
`re-frame.hicasso.test.mounted`, so it needs the DOM that P1-F12 says the
documentation never provisions. That alone blocks it.

**(b) Its premise conflicts with the chapter's own advice, in the ordinary
case.** `hm/shadow!` needs `:reference` — the Reagent original — *still
mounted*, and the sample makes that concrete with two namespaces,
`app.views.article-row-reagent` and `app.views.article-row`. So proving a port
requires keeping the original alongside the port for the length of the
migration. But the same chapter says, three paragraphs later, "When the screen
is green and its browser tests pass, remove the Reagent original." Those are
compatible in principle — keep it, prove it, then delete it — and the chapter
never says so, never shows the intermediate two-namespace state, and never
mentions that the *unported* callers (P1-F08) are pointing at one of the two.

Concretely, for a `reg-view` application (P1-F06) there is a further problem
neither half addresses: to keep a `:reference` at all I would have had to keep
the old `reg-view` **and** the old `dispatch`-closure props **and** a second
copy of every shared view, in one namespace, compiling. That is a substantial
amount of scaffolding to stand up for a comparator I then could not run.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §3 in full, including the sabotage-control
  paragraph
- `15-testing.md` "Migration shadow tests"
- `api-reference.md` `hm/shadow!` row (the `:reference` / `:candidate` /
  `:initial-events` / `:script` roster)

**Resolved by**

Nothing. I substituted a different proof, and I want to be explicit that it is
weaker in one specific way and stronger in another. Weaker: it is not a
DOM-for-DOM comparison against the original, so a cosmetic divergence I did not
think to assert on would pass unnoticed — and shadow comparison's whole value is
catching exactly that. Stronger: it drives the *real* release bundle through a
real interaction sequence (sign in → open the editor → type → publish →
navigate → page the feed → favourite a card), which the chapter's own §3 note
concedes shadow comparison does not do ("It does not prove untested paths").

I also could not perform the chapter's sabotage control, since there was no
comparator to sabotage.

**Bead**

Two: (i) `hm/shadow!` inherits the L3 DOM gap and is the single most costly
place to inherit it, since it is a named step of the migration process; (ii) §3
should show the intermediate state — original kept, port beside it, callers
pointing where — because that state is what a migrator actually has to build.

title: hic: hot reload REPLACES every DOM node (focus and caret lost) while api-reference.md says h/render! reconciles - state survives, the DOM does not, and no page says so
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 2 (LinearLite), a BLINDED
agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE.

FILED AGAINST THE PILOT S OWN CLASSIFICATION, DELIBERATELY. The pilot graded this row
published / none, and it was right to: the documented shape worked first time and nothing
it read was wrong about what it claimed. But the measurement underneath it contradicts a
sentence in api-reference.md, and a factual contradiction in a published page is a defect
whatever the row is graded. The operator files it; the grading stands.

THE CONTRADICTION IN ONE LINE. api-reference.md calls h/render! the hot-reload door and
says React reconciles the new tree against the one on the page. Measured on a hot reload,
nothing is reconciled: every DOM node is replaced, <main> included, and focus and caret go
with them. State survives completely (app-db, the resource cache, an open inline edit,
scroll position); the DOM does not. The mechanism the pilot names is that a reload
redefines each h/defview var, so React sees a new component TYPE and remounts.

Chapter 00 promises the state half and is silent on the DOM half, so a reader meets the
loss of focus mid-typing with nothing in the corpus that predicted it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F14 · outcome 4 · `published` · `none`

**Trying to** Change a Hicasso view with the build running and see what
survived. Set up first: a card created through the UI (so the **resource cache**
differed from its seeded value), an unsubmitted draft in the new-issue field, the
fail-next-write toggle armed, an inline edit open on a card, the caret parked at
offset 5 inside that edit field, and the page scrolled to y=299.

**Expected** Chapter 00 §"Hot reload": "The root, frame, app-db, and
subscriptions survive, so changing the view does not reset the counter or leak
registrations."

**Instead** Exactly that, and no more. Editing `[:h1 "Linearlite — optimistic
issue board"]` to `[:h1 "Linearlite — HOT RELOADED"]` with `npx shadow-cljs
watch app` running, measured in the live page before and after:

| Fact | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the edited `h1` | old text | **new text** — the edit arrived |
| cards on the board | `srv-3, srv-4, srv-1, srv-2` | **unchanged** — `srv-4` was created through the UI before the reload, so the **resource cache survived** |
| unsubmitted draft (app-db) | `"an unsubmitted draft"` | **unchanged** |
| fail-next-write toggle (app-db) | armed | **still armed** |
| inline edit open (app-db) | yes | **still open** |
| scroll position | 299 | **299** |
| `document.activeElement` | the edit input | **lost** — no longer the field |
| caret offset in that field | 5 | **lost** |
| the card's DOM node is the same object | — | **false** |
| that node is still in the document | — | **false** |
| even `<main>` is the same node | — | **false** |

Console confirmed the documented route ran:
`shadow-cljs: load JS linearlite/core.cljs` then
`shadow-cljs: call linearlite.core/rerender!`.

**Looked at** `00-installation.md` §"Hot reload" and §"Mount a first screen"
(the `^:dev/after-load` shape); `api-reference.md` §Roots, where `h/render!` is
"the hot-reload door: React reconciles the new tree against the one on the
page."

**Resolved by** Nothing needed — the documented shape worked first time. The
finding is in the gap between what the docs promise and what a developer
actually experiences. **State survives completely; the DOM does not.** Every
node was replaced and focus and caret went with them, because a reload redefines
each `h/defview` var, React sees a new component *type*, and a changed type is a
remount rather than a reconcile. So the api-reference's "React reconciles the new
tree against the one on the page" is true of `h/render!` in general and
misleading about the case it is named for: on a hot reload there is nothing left
to reconcile against.

That matters most for the thing you are most likely to be doing — tweaking a
form's markup while mid-edit in that form. Your app-db draft survives; your caret
does not.

**Bead** Chapter 00's hot-reload paragraph is accurate and incomplete. Add the
other half: "The DOM is rebuilt: a reload redefines each view, so React remounts
rather than reconciles, and focus, caret, scroll-into-view and any DOM-owned
state are lost. App-db, the resource cache and subscriptions are not." A reader
who knows this stops hunting for the bug when their caret jumps.
notes:
CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE SECOND BLINDED PILOT. This bead was filed from pilot 2
(LinearLite); pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit) hit hot reload keeping state and losing the DOM in the same
session, in a different application, from the same 29 pages, without either agent
seeing the other's workspace, log or output. Two independent readings landing on one
gap is the strongest signal this instrument produces, and it moves the finding out of
the range where one reader's idiosyncrasy explains it.

Pilot 1's entry, verbatim:

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F16 · outcome 4 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Change a migrated view with the build running and record what survived.

**What happened**

It works, in both directions, and the state that should survive did. Measured in
headless Chrome against the live `shadow-cljs watch`, with the app first put
into a non-default state (a tag filter applied, so the home machine's `:filter`
region is `:tagged` and the URL is `/realworld/tag/intro`):

| | before | after reload | after revert |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| banner text | "A place to share your knowledge." | "…knowledge. (hot-reloaded)" | "A place to share your knowledge." |
| route | `/realworld/tag/intro` | `/realworld/tag/intro` | `/realworld/tag/intro` |
| machine state (active chip) | `intro` | `intro` | `intro` |
| app-db (sidebar tags) | 4 tags | 4 tags | 4 tags |

**Survived**: the frame, app-db, the machine's region state, the route, and the
subscriptions feeding all of them. **Did not survive**: DOM node identity —
every node was rebuilt. I stamped a JS property on three live nodes before the
edit; all three came back `null` afterwards, including the one in the *Reagent*
shell that the edit did not touch.

**The friction**

`00-installation.md`'s hot-reload section is written for one shape — a
`defonce` root handle plus `^:dev/after-load` calling `h/render!` — and states
the guarantee as "The root, frame, app-db, and subscriptions survive". Every
word of that held here. But it says nothing about **node identity**, which is
the half a developer actually notices: a rebuilt subtree loses focus, caret,
scroll position and any uncontrolled input's text on every save.

And for a half-migrated tree there is a specific reason to expect a rebuild
that the docs never mention. `h/as-component` is "Declared once at top level,
beside the view" — a plain `def` — so a namespace reload re-evaluates it and
mints a **new React component type**. I measured that directly:

```
"after": {"bridgeIdentical": false, "toggleMarker": null}
```

`window.__probe0 === realworld_http.articles.home_page_component` is `false`
after the reload. A new component type is a remount by React's own rules, so a
bridged screen cannot reconcile across a reload of its own namespace, ever.

I want to be careful about what I proved: in this application the whole tree
was rebuilt anyway — editing `articles.cljs` reloads `core.cljs`, which
redefines the shell's own views — so I could not isolate the bridge's
contribution. What I measured is that the bridge's identity does change, which
is sufficient on its own for the subtree it heads.

**Looked at**

- `00-installation.md` "Hot reload", "Production builds"
- `09-interop.md` "Render a Hicasso view from native React"
- `api-reference.md` `h/render!` ("The hot-reload door"), `h/as-component`
- `cookbook.md` "Boot an application" (the `defonce` handle and why)

**Bead**

Say what hot reload costs as well as what it keeps, and say what
`h/as-component`'s `def` means for a reloaded namespace — it is the one door
whose identity a reload changes, and it is the door a partial migration is
built on.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9149 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. The corrected Markdown now contradicts shipped contract surfaces. implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:660-669 still tells users that reloaded code meets its existing DOM and contrasts render! with mount! discarding every node/component state. consumer_app.cljs:129-136 says nothing is torn down and DOM/component state survive; the editor, typeahead, todo, and slice example reload docstrings repeat that guarantee. The real HMR gate and hmr_remount_cljs_test assert the opposite: changed types replace nodes, lose focus/caret and child hook state, while durable re-frame state survives. Update these existing surfaces to distinguish same-root reconciliation from changed-type remount; inspect cookbook.md's same implication while doing so.

RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: same .beads race. Payload verified in the working tree at HEAD==origin/main — docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md carries 4 focus/caret references where it previously claimed reconciliation preserved the DOM.

Delivered by worker/hicinterop-a in PR #9149, MERGED. The worker CORRECTED THIS BEAD'S OWN FRAMING at source and the correction is the valuable part: 'nothing is reconciled' is wrong. h/render! calls .render on the SAME React root inside flushSync — the distinction it draws is against createRoot-ing a second time. But a reload re-evaluates the namespace, mint-view! allocates a new component and memo wrapper per evaluation, and as-component mints a fresh component per call, so React meets a CHANGED TYPE at every position, and a changed type is a remount by React's own rule. So the reconcile is real and resolves to replace-everything. State survives because none of it lived in React.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P2-F18 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `docs`

**Trying to** Honour the brief's scope note — "Leave anything else on Reagent;
the two view layers coexisting is expected and is itself worth observing" — by
keeping one view on Reagent and rendering it from the Hicasso tree.

**Expected** Some documented crossing. Chapter 00 is encouraging: "A Reagent or
UIx adapter under a Hicasso tree keeps working exactly as it did, and is what
you want when the page also renders that substrate's own components: every
React-shaped adapter writes the same frame context, so **the two subtrees
resolve one frame**." That sentence describes exactly the arrangement I wanted.

**Instead** There is no such crossing, and the corpus never says so. Measured:
a `rf/reg-view` rendered as `[reagent-footer]` from inside `board-page`
compiles clean, then refuses at first paint and **blanks the page**:

```clojure
{:head #object[cljs.core.MetaFn]
 :rf.error/id :rf.error/hicasso-bad-head
 :view "linearlite.core/board-page" …}
```

Note the head is reported as `cljs.core.MetaFn` — for this mistake the
diagnostic cannot name the offender the way it named `status_picker` in P2-F16,
because a Reagent view *is* an anonymous meta-carrying function.

The asymmetry is the finding. Hicasso **out** to a foreign parent has a named
door: `h/as-component`, "the outward bridge — a real React component for a
Hiccup head, so a native parent, a UIx component or plain JavaScript can mount a
minted view under the frame it is already in". Hicasso **in** from Reagent has
none. `[:>]` and `h/defhost` take real React components, and a Reagent view is
not one. Thirteen of the 29 pages mention Reagent and not one addresses this.

**Looked at** `00-installation.md` §"Hicasso needs a substrate adapter" and
§"More than one root"; `09-interop.md`; `10-native-tier.md`;
`escape-ladder.md`; `api-reference.md` §Markup (`h/as-component`);
`20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 and §"When not to use the full process";
grepped all 29 pages for `reagent`, `coexist`, `side by side`, `alongside`.

**Resolved by** Not resolved. I reverted the probe and finished with every view
on Hicasso. **What the two layers coexisting actually means here — and it does
work — is the SUBSTRATE, not the markup**: this application ran the entire
session on `re-frame.adapter.reagent` with a Hicasso view tree above it, exactly
as chapter 00 promises, and that half cost nothing and produced no friction at
all. What does not work is nesting one layer's *views* inside the other's.

The migration chapter's advice — "Migrate a complete screen rather than changing
all component declarations… A screen-level port gives shadow comparison a useful
unit" — turns out to be load-bearing rather than stylistic: a screen is the
smallest unit that *can* migrate, because the boundary between the two layers
has to fall at a root. Chapter 00 §"More than one root" is the mechanism for a
page that genuinely needs both (a Reagent root and a Hicasso root naming the
same `:frame`), but it is written about two Hicasso roots and never connected to
this problem.

**Bead** One short section, probably in chapter 20 beside the screen-at-a-time
advice: *a Hicasso view cannot appear inside a Reagent tree or vice versa; the
boundary is a root.* Name `h/as-component` as the one direction that has a door,
and point at §"More than one root" for a page that must show both — two roots on
one frame. Right now the encouraging sentence in chapter 00 about "the two
subtrees resolv[ing] one frame" reads like permission to interleave markup, and
a reader who tries it gets a blank page and an id that cannot name what it
refused.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9137. Premise HALF-REFUTED, and the correction is the useful half. That is what this repo's own hm/shadow! reference mount uses (test_kit mounted.cljs), what MIG-22 in skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md already documents, and what the chapter 20 that merged today relies on for its :reference. Outward confirmed real and not restated here: h/as-component and h/as-element, with foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test driving five mounting routes including a Reagent parent through both doors. No contradiction with ch20, which states the same head-position refusal in its shadow-comparison section.

### P2-F04 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `api`

**Trying to** Mount the migrated board while keeping the two things the frame
must carry: `:url-bound? true` (the frame owns the browser URL — the app is
routed) and `:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :linearlite.demo/http-stub}` (the
demo backend, without which nothing loads because the app ships no server).
Under Reagent both rode on `[rf/frame-root {…}]`.

**Expected** `h/mount!`'s config to be the Hicasso spelling of `frame-root`'s
options, since the api-reference says mounting is "`rf/frame-root`'s vocabulary
reaching this arm".

**Instead** `h/mount!`'s `config` carries **exactly three** keys — `:frame`,
`:initial-events`, `:identifier-prefix` — and the reference says so as a closed
list. Neither `:url-bound?` nor `:fx-overrides` is among them, and neither word
appears anywhere in the Hicasso corpus except in the **SSR** module's
`:frame-opts` (`api-reference.md`: "for a request needing `:images`,
`:url-strategy` or `:fx-overrides`"). So the server renderer has a documented
door for frame options and the client mount does not.

**Looked at** `api-reference.md` §Roots and §"`h/mount!` and `h/hydrate!` are
not symmetric"; `cookbook.md` §"Boot" ("Seed in one place"); `00-installation.md`
§"What `h/mount!` creates"; grepped the whole corpus for `fx-overrides`,
`url-bound`, `frame-root`.

**Resolved by** A guess, from a paragraph written as a *hazard* rather than as a
recipe. Both the reference and the cookbook warn that "if you call
`rf/make-frame` yourself first, the mount joins and your `:initial-events` never
run". I read that backwards: if the mount *joins* a frame I made, then making
the frame myself is how I get options `h/mount!` cannot express. So boot is now

```clojure
(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true
                :fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :linearlite.demo/http-stub}})
(h/mount! el {:frame :rf/default} [root-view {}])
```

It works. But nothing in the corpus says it is the intended shape, and the only
two places that mention the sequence describe it as a mistake people make. This
is the guess I would most like confirmed, and the single clearest documentation
hole I hit in the whole migration: **a Hicasso application that needs any frame
option beyond a seed has no documented way to boot.**

**Bead** Add one paragraph under §Roots: "`h/mount!` ensures a frame with
defaults. A frame needing `:url-bound?`, `:fx-overrides` or any other
`rf/make-frame` option is created first, and the mount joins it — seed from
`make-frame` in that case, not from the mount." Every routed application needs
`:url-bound?`, so this is on the critical path for most real apps, not an edge.

### P1-F06 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Map this application's actual view idiom onto Hicasso's.

**Expected**

The migration chapter's first translation row to fit. It reads: "`defn`
component returning Hiccup → `h/defview`, mounted as a Hiccup head."

**Instead**

The application has no such `defn`. Every view is `(reg-view name [props]
body)` — re-frame2 core's own macro, `:require-macros`'d from
`re-frame.core` — and inside a `reg-view` body, `subscribe` and `dispatch` are

and `#(dispatch [:home/show-page %])`. Chapter 20 never mentions `reg-view`,
and neither does any other chapter in the corpus (grepped: zero hits across all
29 pages).

This matters more than a spelling. The `reg-view` body's implicit `subscribe`
and `dispatch` bindings mean the *same source text* — `@(subscribe [:q])` —
means one thing under the old macro and is an error under Hicasso, where
chapter 02 says "A bare `rf/subscribe` is not an untracked alternative; it
throws rather than resolving." Nothing warned me that the implicit binding was
also going away; I inferred it from the fact that `h/defview` is a different
macro that installs no such bindings.

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §2 table
- `02-views-and-reads.md` (`h/sub` is "the only read form in a Hicasso body")
- `03-events-as-data.md` "Do not hand-roll an ambient dispatch closure"

Treating `reg-view` as if it were the table's `defn` row, and mechanically:
`reg-view` → `h/defview`, `@(subscribe [:q])` → `(h/sub [:q])`,

they were guesses: the chapter is written against classic Reagent and this
application is a re-frame2 application on the Reagent adapter, which is a
different starting point with the same name.

§2's table needs a re-frame2-native column, or the chapter needs a paragraph
distinguishing "a Reagent app" from "a re-frame2 app rendering through the
Reagent adapter". They migrate differently and only the second one is likely.

title: hic: the pilots package gives an agent pilot no way to LOOK at a rendered page - 4 of 7 outcomes need sight, the workspace ships no browser driver and the 29 published pages name none
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 ~17:45 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, from the
operator's chair, at pin 6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba.

THE PACKAGE ASSUMES A HUMAN AT A BROWSER, AND EVERY PILOT IS AN AGENT.
workspace.md step 5 reads "npx shadow-cljs watch app  # then open
http://localhost:8080 - pilot 2 uses 8081", and its identity check is "Confirm
by sight instead: pilot 1 renders Conduit's masthead ... and pilot 2 renders the
LinearLite board". An agent has no eyes and no browser. Neither has the pilot.

FOUR OF THE SEVEN OUTCOMES REQUIRE SEEING A RENDERED PAGE, and none of them says
how. Outcome 2 (the screen renders through Hicasso "with the same behaviour a
user sees today"), outcome 3 (a feature change on a migrated screen), outcome 4
(hot reload - "record what survived"), outcome 5 (diagnose an induced failure
through Xray, which is a browser tool), and outcome 6 explicitly ("A production
build succeeds AND THE BUILT PAGE RUNS. Both halves. A bundle that compiles and
does not boot is the interesting failure"). A pilot that cannot load a page
cannot honestly answer any of them, and the failure mode is not a red verdict -
it is a pilot that reports PASS off a green compile, which is exactly the
half-answer outcome 6 exists to refuse.

THE WORKSPACE SHIPS NO BROWSER DRIVER. workspace.md's app/package.json template
carries react, react-dom, shadow-cljs and @testing-library/dom - no playwright,
no puppeteer, no jsdom, no happy-dom. Measured on both assembled workspaces.

AND THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION DOES NOT SUPPLY ONE EITHER. Across the 29 pages
of docs/core/hicasso/, "playwright", "puppeteer" and "headless" match four pages
and none of them tells a reader how to load a page headlessly:
00-installation.md:123 names Chromium as the tested browser engine in a support
table, 00-installation.md:182 is about the plain-atom adapter, and 05-forms.md,
11-ephemeral-state.md and 18-ssr-and-hydration.md use the word in passing.
15-testing.md - the page the briefs point at for the testing ladder - matches
none of the three. So the blinded pilot has nowhere to read the answer, which
makes this a documentation defect and not only a workspace one.

WHAT THE OPERATOR HAD TO DO, WHICH A PILOT MAY NOT. Both previous operator runs
and this one drove the boot check with a hand-written playwright-core script,
resolving the module through NODE_PATH into the REPOSITORY's own
implementation/node_modules. The pilot's read fence bars implementation/
outright, so the route the operator used is not available to the instrument it
is checking. That asymmetry is the defect in one sentence: the operator proves
the page renders by a means the pilot is forbidden.

SIZE OF THE FIX. Small and squarely in the package: add playwright-core (or
puppeteer) to workspace.md's app/package.json template, and give the pilot one
documented command that prints #app's length, the page's visible text and the
console/page errors - the same three facts the operator's own check reads. That
also makes outcome 6's second half mechanically checkable and quotable, which
the friction log's "captured exit code, never a described one" rule already
demands of every other outcome.
