title: shadow-cljs compile server-test exits 0 with failing autorun tests - a fail-open gate signal
description:
`shadow-cljs compile server-test` in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp exits 0 even when its autorun reports test FAILURES. Measured by the worker on PR #9121: the compile exited 0 with 4 test failures in the autorun output. Only the separate `node out/server-test.js` invocation is a verdict.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE SCRIPT: this is a fail-OPEN gate. Anything - a worker, a brief, a CI step, a script - that reads the compile's exit code as a test result reads a clean pass over real failures. It is the same class as the piped-gate hazard already in CLAUDE.md (a pipeline's exit status is its last command's), reached through a build tool instead of a shell.

WHAT TO DO. Establish first whether any CI job or local script actually reads that exit code as a test verdict - `git grep` for `compile server-test` and for the build id across `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/`, and any npm script. Two independent instruments plus a control that fires.

- If a real consumer reads it as a verdict: fix the consumer to run `node out/server-test.js` and read THAT exit code. Do not try to make shadow-cljs itself fail the compile on autorun failures unless that is genuinely configurable and cheap - the compile succeeded, which is what a compile exit code means.
- If no consumer reads it: this is documentation, not a defect. Record the trap where a reader will meet it (the pair-mcp README or its test docs) and close.

Either way say which, with the census that decided it.

NOT IN SCOPE: changing what the autorun does, or adding a new gate. The point is that an existing signal is being misread, or could be.
close_reason: Census settled it and a real consumer existed. The ONLY thing in the repo that turned `shadow-cljs compile server-test`'s exit code into a TEST VERDICT was tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/deps.edn's own `:test` alias (`-m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile server-test`, no node run) — a per-artefact deps.edn, so in fence. Fixed there: the alias now fails CLOSED (exit 2) naming `npm test`. Deleting it was measured to be WORSE (clojure -M:test on an ABSENT alias drops to a REPL and exits 0 on EOF). NO CI job or repo script read the compile exit as a verdict: test.yml's node-test-tools-re-frame2-pair-mcp runs `npm test`, expensive-tests.yml and test.yml's conformance job compile the `:server` bundle (a build step, not a suite), and implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs's row is {exe:'npm',args:['test']}. package.json's `test` chains with && and ends on node, so its status is Node's. Fail-open reproduced with captured exit codes on one unmodified build: compile printed 'Ran 1120 tests / 4068 assertions. 2 failures, 0 errors.' exit 0; node out/server-test.js printed the identical tally exit 1 (those 2 failures were LOCAL — a live nREPL the no-port harness found — not a repo red). Trap also documented in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/README.md. PR: worker/gatetruth-a.

title: Mayor dispatch drift: the boundary and gate-mechanics blocks were retyped, not extracted - and the gate paraphrase inverts the detach ruling
description:
The mayor has been RETYPING the two travel-verbatim dispatch blocks instead of
extracting them mechanically, across every dispatch this session. The method doc is
correct; the defect is entirely in dispatch practice.

docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:661-673 rules on this directly:
"Get them there by extracting mechanically, then pasting the result into the prompt...
the extraction is what makes paraphrase impossible - a matched range cannot reword,
where a mayor retyping two hundred lines of gate mechanics can and does."

That is precisely what happened.

## Drift 1 - the gate-mechanics block, and it INVERTS the ruling

Canonical block: template lines 920-1010+ ("## Quality gates - how a gate is run",
paste from that heading down to the rule before "## Reviewing what comes back").
Roughly 90 lines.

What the mayor pasted instead, in full:
  "GATE MECHANICS: run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion - never background one,
   never pipe through tail/head."

The canonical block says the OPPOSITE of the first clause:
  - "Split a compound gate before you reach for detaching."
  - "Where it genuinely does not split, DETACHING IS CORRECT - ending the turn is the
     defect. Detach, then poll both the log and the exit-code file in a bounded loop
     within the same turn."
  - "Word this as the sanctioned path, not as a concession; a worker who thinks it has
     erred reads for how to atone and straight past the instruction that would save it."

The real rule is a TERMINAL CONDITION - the turn ends only once the exit file exists
and its number is quoted - not a ban on backgrounding. The mayor's paraphrase kept the
memorable half (foreground) and dropped the operative one (poll in-turn), which is the
same failure mode ai/stance.md warns about for the stance block.

OBSERVED COST: Mike asked 2026-09-03 why background tasks were taking almost an hour.
A worker whose gate is too heavy to foreground and who is FORBIDDEN to detach has no
option but to sit in the foreground. This is a direct, measured throughput cost.

Also dropped from that block:
  - the WEDGE diagnosis: a gate heavy enough that two cannot coexist wedges rather than
    fails (no progress, no exit file, no error). Contention is for the MACHINE, so
    per-attempt naming does nothing. Recover by correlating your own build artefact's
    mtime against candidate run start times and killing ONLY the one you can show is
    yours; a peer's run recovers by itself.
  - "Read the clock before killing anything on elapsed time" - fails BOTH ways; one
    worker killed a healthy run believing 17 minutes had passed when it had been 2.
  - "Invoke a backgrounded gate by its ABSOLUTE path" - an interpreter handed a relative
    script path resolves it against the working directory, so a wrong directory hands it
    a SIBLING WORKTREE's copy. One run did exactly that inside another live worker's
    checkout and reported the resulting verdict as its own.
  - "Verify which tree the gate actually read", by root-print or by planted-fault red -
    "the discrimination is the red itself", since a repository-relative path cannot tell
    two checkouts apart.
  - "A green sabotage run is a reason to stop, not to proceed."
The never-pipe rule was the one part carried correctly.

## Drift 2 - the worktree-boundary block

Canonical block: template lines 739-798 (the fenced text under "## The worktree boundary
block"). The mayor substituted a retyped 6-point numbered list. Dropped:

  - "Before EVERY edit, confirm you are in your worktree... A start-of-session guard is
    NOT sufficient - verify per edit." The mayor's version asks for ONE guard run. The
    template's own rationale: the leak happens mid-session, in one tool call, and a guard
    script can be fooled by the path resolution that causes it.
  - Never write the worktree root, or any absolute home path, into any committed file, PR
    body or tracker text.
  - After the first edit, and after writing any NEW file, confirm it landed in your
    worktree and NOT the mayor checkout - CHECK BOTH TREES, because a new ignored file
    leaking into the mayor checkout is invisible in the worker's own status.
  - If anything landed outside: STOP, report both paths, do not repair, commit or push.
  - Scratch-file naming: concurrent workers SHARE one SESSION-keyed scratch dir; name
    every file for the worktree AND the attempt - gate-<name>-<worktree>-1.log /
    .exit - bumping the number each re-run. The attempt number closes a hole the worktree
    suffix cannot, because both writers are YOU: a harness that caps runtime kills the
    SHELL, not what it spawned, and the orphan keeps writing to the .log and .exit the
    restarted run is using. A hole of NUL bytes or two summary lines in one log is the
    tell. (The mayor substituted "write scratch to your worktree, not /tmp" - same hazard,
    weaker route, and no attempt number at all.)
  - THE INSTALLER HAZARD, which is live in this repo: a link into shared dependencies is
    WRITABLE through, not only deletable through. An installer a gate runs (npm ci, npm
    install, any tool that reinstalls a dependency tree) rewrites the SHARED target, not
    your copy - "one emptied the coordinator's real tree while the worker's own read as a
    fresh install." If a nominated gate runs an installer, do NOT link that tree: install
    your own from the lockfile, or STOP and say the gate cannot run against a link.
    Workers here junction implementation/node_modules and then run npm-based gates, so
    this is the live shape. The mayor's version said only "remove the junction as your
    last act", which addresses deletion and not writes.
  - "Kill any poll loops you armed before you report done" - each survivor fires its own
    completion notification after the work has landed, costing a turn apiece.

## The fix

1. Extract both blocks MECHANICALLY into the dispatch, by matched line range, and paste
   the result. Never retype either. Adapt only the placeholders (<ASSIGNED_WORKTREE>,
   <MAYOR_CHECKOUT>) and scope the gate block to the gate the brief names.
2. Ranges as of this filing - RE-DERIVE them from the headings rather than trusting these
   numbers, which go stale exactly the way the template's own "Counts are claims" section
   says:
     - worktree boundary: the fenced text block under "## The worktree boundary block"
     - gate mechanics: from "## Quality gates - how a gate is run" down to the rule
       before "## Reviewing what comes back"
   Note the template's explicit warning that "## Quality gates - which gate" is NOT the
   gate-mechanics block and does not stand in for it.
3. The stance block from ai/stance.md was pasted verbatim throughout and is NOT affected;
   this bead is only about the other two.

## Acceptance

A dispatch prompt whose boundary and gate blocks are byte-identical to the template's
ranges (modulo placeholder substitution), verifiable by extracting the range and diffing
it against what was sent.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the defect was dispatch PRACTICE, the bead says so in terms ('The method doc is correct; the defect is entirely in dispatch practice'), and the practice has been corrected and held for the whole of this session. There is no file to edit, so dispatching this to a worker would have produced an empty PR.

WHAT THE BEAD RECORDED. A prior mayor RETYPED the two travel-verbatim blocks instead of extracting them, and the gate-mechanics block collapsed to two lines whose first clause INVERTED the ruling: 'run gates in the FOREGROUND to completion - never background one'. The canonical block says the opposite — 'Split a compound gate before you reach for detaching', and 'Where it genuinely does not split, DETACHING IS CORRECT - ending the turn is the defect.'

WHAT THIS SESSION DOES INSTEAD, and it is checkable rather than asserted. Every dispatch has carried the gate-mechanics block EXTRACTED MECHANICALLY from docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md lines 920-1139 (trailing --- stripped): 16889 bytes, 217 lines, headings located with grep -n rather than by eye, and the section boundary taken heading-to-heading because that block carries no fence. The worktree-boundary block likewise from lines 740-794 (3383 bytes) and the common preamble from 805-863 (4013 bytes). Never retyped, never summarised, never paraphrased — which is exactly what template:661-673 rules ('the extraction is what makes paraphrase impossible - a matched range cannot reword').

THE INVERTED CLAUSE IS DEFINITIVELY ABSENT. Every dispatch this session carries the canonical wording verbatim, including the four paragraphs that exist because the rule kept failing open: detaching is the sanctioned path; the turn ends only once the exit file exists and its number is quoted; the strand has variants (a Monitor, a watch, a subscription, a background task you expect to wake you are all the same strand); and the refutation of the harness's own promise that a backgrounded command will re-invoke you, which does not survive the end of your turn.

AND IT IS EARNING ITS PLACE. worker/budget-a reported today that backgrounding stranded its spine self-test TWICE — the harness reported 'exit code 0' while the captured exit file was absent both times — and it foregrounded with a proper ceiling to get the real verdict. That is the block working as written: the worker read an absent exit file as NO VERDICT rather than a pass. Under the two-line paraphrase it would have had no such rule.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE PRACTICE CANNOT REGRESS. The posture loop re-checks it every tick and names any drifted dispatch; that loop is the durable guard, not this bead. Reopen if a dispatch is ever observed carrying a paraphrase again.

SIBLING: rf2-tg6o is a REAL edit to the same file (the preamble names bd history fields that do not exist) and is being dispatched separately. It no longer needs sequencing behind this bead, since this one touches nothing.

title: Make implementor skill trigger description validator-safe
description:
## Scope

Repair the frontmatter description in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md` so
the skill-creator validator accepts the shipped skill. Keep the public skill
directory, frontmatter name, trigger behavior, exclusions, and all body/reference
content unchanged except for the invalid trigger-example placeholder wording.

## Finding

The description contains the trigger example `implement re-frame2 in
<language>`. The required `quick_validate.py` validator rejects any `<` or `>`
in frontmatter descriptions, so the current skill fails validation before any
normal skill routing can occur.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:16` contains the literal trigger text
  `implement re-frame2 in <language>` in the YAML `description`.
- `C:\\Users\\miket\\.codex\\skills\\.system\\skill-creator\\scripts\\quick_validate.py`
  rejects descriptions containing `<` or `>`.
- Running the validator against the current package returns exit 1 with
  `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is a frontmatter-description clarity/validator-compatibility fix only.
Preserve `name: re-frame2-implementor`, the eight-host scope, the three trigger
concepts (port re-frame2, implement re-frame2 in a host language, conformance
corpus), all do-not-use routing, allowed tools, eval fixtures, filenames,
references, package/plugin metadata, and skill body semantics. Do not rename the
public skill or directory, alter invocation policy, or change any spec/conformance
terminology. No Phase-1 vestigial/removal target is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The frontmatter description contains no angle brackets or unfinished
   placeholders and still clearly triggers on porting re-frame2 to a host
   language and on conformance-corpus work.
2. `quick_validate.py` run against the absolute skill directory exits 0 and
   prints `Skill is valid!`.
3. A planted angle-bracket trigger placeholder in a temporary validation copy
   makes `quick_validate.py` exit 1 with the expected diagnostic; restoring the
   clean skill returns exit 0.
4. `git diff --check` is clean and the diff is limited to the one frontmatter
   description phrase.
acceptance_criteria: Validator clean pass; planted angle-bracket control red; restored clean pass; exact one-phrase diff and no routing/public-name changes.

description:

the skill-creator validator accepts the shipped skill. Keep the public skill

The description contains the trigger example `implement re-frame2 in

title: Enroll published Hicasso in the implementation root coordinator
description:
## Finding

The root Clojure coordinator did not follow Hicasso's transition to a published artefact. `implementation/deps.edn` says its top-level `:deps` pulls every artefact onto one classpath, but the map has no `day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:local/root "hicasso"}`. Its `:test` alias nevertheless adds `hicasso/test`, leaving the tests on a classpath that lacks `hicasso/src` (and the supported kit root `hicasso/test_kit/src`). `implementation/README.md:46` repeats the every-artefact claim, while lines 165-166 still call Hicasso pre-publication with no `:clein` deploy alias. The same inventory also still says core depends on Reagent at line 52, although commit d44c4f7d20 moved that dependency to the Reagent adapter.

## Evidence

`clojure -Spath -M:test` from `implementation/` exits 0 and lists `hicasso/test`, but contains no `implementation/hicasso/src` or `hicasso/test_kit/src`; it does list every other published artefact's source root. `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` has declared `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` under `:clein/build` since commit f35ba5d13e (2026-08-15), and `.github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh` plus `.github/workflows/release.yml` both enumerate and deploy it. `hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/slot_cljs_test.cljc` directly requires `re-frame.hicasso.impl.slot`, demonstrating that a test-only path is not a self-contained substitute for the missing source root. The shadow coordinator is not affected: its explicit source-path list already includes `hicasso/src`, `hicasso/test`, and both test-kit roots.

## Impact

The advertised aggregate classpath is incomplete specifically for a shipped artefact; ad-hoc root REPL/test selection cannot load the Hicasso implementation through this coordinator even though its test path is present. The root inventory also tells maintainers obsolete publication and core-dependency facts, making future classpath/release reviews unreliable.

## Recommendation

Add the Hicasso local-root dependency to the root coordinator and make the aggregate test alias match the Hicasso artefact's intentional test roots (including the supported test kit where the aggregate promises the full CLJS test classpath). Refresh the adjacent `implementation/README.md` inventory: Hicasso is published, and core's production deps are Clojure + ClojureScript, not Reagent.

## Risks and contracts

Do not add Hicasso to core or to an adapter artefact, change its published dependency DAG, publish the test kit as a second coordinate, or alter shadow's already-correct explicit source paths. Preserve Hicasso's optional-by-reachability bundle contract and post-matrix release ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `implementation/deps.edn` names `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` as a root `:local/root` dependency and the aggregate test classpath exposes every Hicasso root it claims to support.
2. A read-only classpath probe from `implementation/` includes `implementation/hicasso/src` (and the test-kit source root if `hicasso/test` remains part of the aggregate test surface).
3. `implementation/README.md` no longer calls Hicasso pre-publication or claims core has a production Reagent dependency; its every-artefact coordinator claim agrees with the live map.
4. Existing shadow builds, Hicasso publish/release metadata, optional-module reachability, and bundle-isolation behavior remain unchanged and relevant coordinator/doc gates pass.
close_reason: PR #9096 (head 5918c4f52b). All four acceptance criteria met. (1) implementation/deps.edn now names day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:local/root "hicasso"} in the root :deps and lists it in the header published-artefact inventory; the :test alias adds hicasso/test_kit/src beside the hicasso/test it already carried — that root is deliberately off the artefact's :paths (rf2-hic-020) so the :local/root dep cannot carry it, and Hicasso's own :test alias names it as an :extra-path. (2) Read-only probe: clojure -Spath -M:test from implementation/ exits 0 and now lists implementation/hicasso/src, implementation/hicasso/resources and hicasso/test_kit/src; a load probe of re-frame.hicasso.impl.slot plus re-frame.hicasso.slot-cljs-test off that classpath exits 0, which is the failure the bead described. (3) implementation/README.md's hicasso row no longer says pre-publication/no :clein deploy aliases — it names the ../core + ../ssr deps and the :clein + :clein/build aliases, published as day8/re-frame2-hicasso since rf2-gra70 — and the core row no longer lists reagent (core/deps.edn names only org.clojure/clojure and org.clojure/clojurescript; d44c4f7d20 moved Reagent to the adapter). The every-artefact coordinator claim is now true rather than reworded. (4) Shadow untouched: implementation/shadow-cljs.edn enumerates its own :source-paths, has no :deps true, and does not read this map — it already listed hicasso/src, hicasso/test and both test-kit roots. No change to the published dependency DAG, no second coordinate for the test kit, no adapter/core dep added. Gates: check_readme_inventories.py exit 0, check_adapter_disposition.py exit 0, check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0, check_jvm_lane_rosters.py exit 0 (31 rostered artefacts), check_test_lane_bijection.py exit 0 (1547 files / 45 lanes). title: story-mcp specs contradict explain-variant raw-author-data policy
description:
Evidence
- The authoritative Story-MCP privacy table says `explain-variant`'s entire map, including every plan-resolved value slot, is static author data and ships raw (`tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:158-168`, rf2-7k5mce).
- The very next paragraph at lines 169-172 still promises that a declared-sensitive value redacts whether it arrives through a live derived tree “or a plan-resolved arg.” That is no longer true for explain-variant.
- Runtime docs and API are internally consistent with the new policy (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:365-383`, `spec/API.md:324-344`), and focused tests at `tools_test.clj:3514-3616` prove classified `:db-seed`, `:effective-args`, `:network`, sub-overrides, and step payloads ship raw.
- The document claimed as the single-sourced peer, `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:119-198`, still places explain-variant among live/value-bearing tools, says its plan-resolved slots path-project, excludes its resolved step values from static metadata, and implies an include-sensitive escape hatch. That contradicts both implementation and the Story-MCP table.

Impact
This is a safety-contract contradiction, not cosmetic wording: readers can believe classification marks protect authored values exposed through explain-variant when the intentional runtime behavior sends them raw and offers no `:include-sensitive` gate. The same section simultaneously states the opposite, so clients and reviews cannot infer the actual boundary.

Recommendation
Rewrite the stale paragraphs in both normative specs to consistently state the rf2-7k5mce policy: explain-variant is a no-run author-data projection; its whole map ships raw; it is excluded from the live-value scrub set and sensitive-read gate. Cross-check the remaining tool lists and examples against the four actual value-surfacing tools.

Risks / contracts
Do not silently reintroduce scrubbing as a documentation fix: raw author data is deliberate, matches get-variant/variant->edn and the human Explain panel, and is pinned by tests. If that policy itself is reconsidered, treat it as a separate security decision with migration and protocol review.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spec/002-Tool-Registry.md` contains no claim that explain-variant plan-resolved args redact.
- `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md` classifies explain-variant consistently as wholly raw author metadata and removes it from live/value-bearing/gated tool sets.
- Both specs clearly warn that classification marks do not scrub authored registration values exposed by explain-variant.
- The four runtime-value tools and their sensitive-read gate remain accurately enumerated.
- Existing explain-variant raw-value tests and Story-MCP test suite pass unchanged in semantics.
close_reason: PR #9089. Contradiction resolved in favour of the SHIPPED CODE: tool-explain-variant wraps story/explain in result/edn-result and reaches no egress projector; spec/API.md and three pinned tests agree; the Story-MCP privacy table already stated the rf2-7k5mce policy. Rewrote the stale prose on both sides. tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md no longer claims plan-resolved args redact and now states plainly that classification marks do not reach author metadata (keep secrets out of a variant's registration). tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md removes explain-variant from the live-state and value-bearing sets, moves its ENTIRE explain map into the author-published static class, and marks the rf2-q8ebq.1 setup-order/script-order carve-out retired. The four runtime-value tools and the --allow-sensitive-reads gate remain accurately enumerated. No scrubbing reintroduced; explain-variant tests unchanged in semantics and green.
