title: Rebuild the template repo-split runbook around its two real roots
description:
## Evidence

spec/005-Repo-Split.md is the still-live operator procedure; the external repository does not yet exist (gh repo view day8/re-frame2-template returns repository not found) and there are no template-v tags locally. Its post-split test architecture currently treats one repo-root as both the standalone template checkout and a sibling re-frame2 fixture. That cannot work with the current suite.

Today test-support/repo-root feeds template-owned paths (tools/template/resources), while release_gate_test reads .github/workflows/template-release.yml and repo_split_spec_test reads tools/template/spec from the same root. It also feeds framework-owned paths (VERSION, implementation/package.json, core/adapter source and node_modules) and emitted_test_run_test now reads skills/re-frame2-setup/references. If repo-root is changed to RF2_FRAMEWORK_ROOT as Shape A prescribes, the external suite reads template resources/spec/workflow from the monorepo copy that §3.5 says will be stubbed or deleted, rather than from the external checkout under test. The migration needs separate template-root and framework-root concepts.

The same runbook also inventories the pre-collapse product: root/ is said to contain Lefthook and dev files, the external test tree omits release_gate_test.clj, repo_split_spec_test.clj and the browser driver, and §3.2.1 says static/emitted tests consume Story plus old schema/Xray paths. The current twelve-file contract removed those dependencies. The tree also lists a repo-root template.edn placeholder that has never existed and has no creation/use step.

## Impact

Following the normative split procedure can either fail outright or, worse, test the soon-to-be-deleted monorepo template instead of the external artifact being released. Stale inventory makes it easy to omit current release/override guards and carry retired feature coupling into the new repository.

## Recommendation

Rewrite the procedure around two explicit roots: the external template checkout for resources, spec, workflow, VERSION and template tests; and a parameterized re-frame2 fixture root for framework sources/pins/node_modules and any setup-skill comparison retained. Enumerate every current test and driver, remove retired feature inventory, and either justify/create the top-level template.edn or remove it from the plan.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve the exact deps-new resource retarget and override-token guard. The standalone release gate must exercise the external checkout bytes while retaining live framework surface/pin and behavioural coverage; do not solve the coupling by silently dropping tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- The runbook defines distinct template-checkout and framework-fixture roots and assigns every current path consumer to the correct root.
- A post-split suite cannot read template resources, spec, or release workflow from the monorepo copy slated for removal.
- The external tree/test inventory matches all current tracked tests and the browser driver, and retired Lefthook/dev/Story/schema/Xray/SSR claims are removed.
- The unexplained top-level template.edn entry is either given a concrete required role and migration step or deleted from the planned tree.
- The documented standalone CI path retains pin, framework-surface, setup-leaf (if kept), browser, release, and published-coordinate smoke coverage against the external checkout.
close_reason: Rebuilt 005-Repo-Split around template-root and framework-root (PR #9105). Root cause confirmed at source: test_support.clj's single repo-root anchors on implementation/core/src/re_frame (a FRAMEWORK marker) yet serves four TEMPLATE consumers off it - template-resource-dir, repo_split_spec_test (the doc itself), release_gate_test (.github/workflows/template-release.yml) and test-support/dev-page-boot-proof.cjs - so the runbook's prescribed rename of repo-root to RF2_FRAMEWORK_ROOT would have pointed all four at the monorepo copy 3.5 deletes. 3.2.1 now defines template-root (resolved from the checkout under test, not an env var) and framework-root (RF2_FRAMEWORK_ROOT) with a table assigning all twelve current path consumers. Records the latent VERSION trap: both roots hold VERSION, both currently read 0.0.1.alpha, and version_lockstep_test's :rf2-version target is the FRAMEWORK one - mis-routing stays green until they diverge. Inventory corrected against git ls-files: added release_gate_test.clj, repo_split_spec_test.clj, dev-page-boot-proof.cjs, LICENSE; deleted the repo-root template.edn placeholder (never existed, no step creates or consumes it, find-root resolves on the classpath); root/ is README.md + resources/public/ only (no Lefthook, no dev/); tools/story/src/ and tools/xray/tools/story deps-rewrite claims removed - Story/Xray/schema remain only as retired-coord guards in template_test.clj. 3.2 gains the workflow-move steps (provisioning moves to framework root with release_gate_test's assertions, one change; the pre-split not-a-usable-public-scaffold Release caveat retires with the split). 5 enumerates seven coverage tiers. 2.1/2.1.1/2.1.2 and 4 untouched - all four override tokens exact, both grammar labels intact. Gates: clojure -M:test in tools/template exit 0 (39 tests/296 assertions, 0 failures) including repo_split_spec_test which reads this doc; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 and proven live (planted link+anchor -> exit 1 naming the file, restored byte-identical by git hash-object); check_skill_description_budget.py --self-test and --verbose --ci exit 0; git diff --check exit 0.

title: Stop Story-host DOM tests leaking hashchange listeners across cases
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/test/re_frame/testbed/story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs runs two tests against the real browser window.
- Each mount leaves the installed hashchange function in host/hash-listener* and registered on js/window, as production is designed to do.
- The :after fixture unmounts React roots, then reset-host-handles! resets host/hash-listener* to nil without calling removeEventListener. That discards the only exact function identity able to unregister the listener.
- The next :before repeats the reset, so the second test's mount cannot remove the first test's listener; it registers another. The final fixture similarly leaves listeners on the shared browser page.
- The fake-window Node suite does not expose this because clear-window! discards the entire fake window/Set between tests.

Impact:
The suite named no-listener-or-root-leak itself leaks real hashchange listeners between tests and into later browser namespaces. Later hash changes can invoke stale host code against a removed #app node, creating order-dependent failures; the current assertions inspect only the stored handle, not the real window registry, so they remain green.

Recommendation:
Add teardown that removes the exact recorded host/hash-listener* from js/window before resetting the atom. Add a browser-visible assertion/probe proving one test leaves no registered host listener (or otherwise prove balanced add/remove) so the cleanup cannot regress silently.

Risks/contracts:
Remove only the listener owned by the host using its recorded identity. Do not blanket-replace window handlers or weaken the production defonce/hot-reload behavior. Keep Node fake-window cleanup valid.

Acceptance:
- DOM-test teardown unregisters the recorded hashchange listener before discarding its handle.
- A regression that resets the handle without unregistering makes the browser suite red.
- Both Story-host tests can run repeatedly/in either order without accumulating listeners; browser and focused Node gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: Unregister the exact recorded host hashchange listener before fixture state is reset, add non-vacuous browser coverage for balanced listener ownership, and keep production hot-reload plus Node fake-window contracts passing.
close_reason: PR #9089. Premise held exactly as described: the DOM fixture nilled host/hash-listener* without removeEventListener, so the next mount's remove-then-add became add-only and stacked a second listener on the shared page. Fix: reset-host-handles! now unregisters the EXACT recorded listener from js/window before discarding the handle (stored identity only; no blanket handler replacement; production defonce/hot-reload untouched; Node fake-window cleanup unchanged). Added fixture-teardown-leaves-no-hashchange-listener-on-the-page, which wraps js/window's listener API for one mount+teardown cycle, asserts the census saw exactly one add (non-vacuity) and that the cycle nets to zero - so a reset-without-unregister regression makes the browser suite red. SCOPE NOTE: the file is tools/testbed-support/test/, outside this dispatch's fence; the change is confined to that one test file and is flagged in the PR body. Verified locally with the focused node build (npm run test:testbed-support): 684 files, 0 warnings, 17 tests / 63 assertions, exit 0 - the new test's body gates on (browser?) and no-ops there. The :browser-test gate that runs the real-DOM assertion was NOT run locally (needs a full browser-test compile plus Chromium); CI owns it.

title: Stop template CI fan-out from retired schemas, Story, and Xray inputs
description:
## Evidence

The changed-surface classifier still sets template_expensive for implementation/schemas/** and every non-spec Markdown change under tools/story/** or tools/xray/**. Its comments and the matching assertions in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs say the generated app loads re-frame.schemas, the Xray preload, and the with-Story entry point.

That premise ended in commit 18b9486664 (rf2-zq34m): the current twelve-file contract forbids day8/re-frame2-schemas, day8/re-frame2-xray, day8/re-frame2-story, reg-app-schema, the Xray preload/host, and every Story flag. Current emitted files require only core, the selected adapter, plain-atom test support, and substrate libraries. The setup-skill leaf is byte-locked to the same reduced emission. Core, adapter, implementation package pins, template files, and setup reference files remain real inputs and already have their own template_expensive arms.

## Impact

Schema, Story, and Xray-only PRs unnecessarily schedule the roughly 30-minute jvm-tools-template job, including npm ci and Playwright Chromium provisioning. Worse, classifier comments and tests now assert coverage the template suite cannot provide, which can mislead future maintainers about which consumer gates actually exercise those surfaces.

## Recommendation

Remove only the obsolete schemas/Story/Xray template_expensive fan-out and invert or replace the three stale classifier assertions with negative controls. Retain all actual template inputs: implementation/core, both adapters, implementation/package.json and package-lock.json, tools/template itself, and skills/re-frame2-setup/references.

## Risks and contracts

Do not narrow tools_jvm, MCP, examples, Story/Xray browser, schemas JVM/CLJS, or any other independent lane for those surfaces. This change is solely the generated-template consumer edge that no longer exists. Re-add fan-out only with a real emitted dependency and a fixture proving it.
acceptance_criteria:
- report-changed-surfaces.sh no longer sets template_expensive for a schemas-only change or a Story/Xray-only change.
- The stale rf2-jdj17.1 classifier comments and positive assertions are replaced by current-contract negative controls.
- Core, reagent/uix adapter, implementation package pin/lockfile, tools/template, and setup-skill reference changes still set template_expensive.
- The changed-surfaces classifier test suite passes and other per-surface lane outputs are unchanged.
close_reason: template_expensive no longer fires for a schemas-only or a Story/Xray-only change. Both rf2-jdj17.1 arms removed from report-changed-surfaces.sh (the implementation/schemas/* case, and the tools/{story,xray}/* default arm), plus two adjacent prose rosters that still listed template_expensive for Story macros.clj and for schemas. The three stale positive assertions in _changed-surfaces.test.cjs are replaced by negative controls that ALSO pin each surface's own lanes (tools_jvm + mcp_conformance + story_xray_browser for the tools; implementation_jvm + cljs_node_test + cljs_browser + cljs_prod + bundle_isolation for schemas), so an over-broad narrowing edit reds instead of passing. Premise verified with two instruments and a control that fired: (1) git grep -F census over tools/template/resources/ and the setup-skill leaf found 0 hits for re-frame.schemas, reg-app-schema, re-frame.story, mount-shell!, devtools/preloads and re-frame2-xray, with controls returning hits; the emitted shadow-cljs.edn declares no :devtools/preloads key at all, and the only xray/story strings in the emitted tree are two Next-steps doc links in root/README.md pointing under docs/, not tools/. (2) the classifier itself executed per surface before and after: across all 28 outputs for the three surfaces exactly three lines move, all template_expensive true->false, and every retained input still reads true (core, both adapters, implementation/package.json, package-lock.json, tools/template, skills/re-frame2-setup/references). Gate liveness proved once: planted the removed schemas arm back, the mirror test went red naming the new negative control, restored byte-identical by git hash-object. Gates: node --test _changed-surfaces.test.cjs exit 0 (335 passed); eslint exit 0. NOTE: this touches the one-toucher classifier/mirror pair in ONE commit, as required when a change alters both what the script outputs and what the test pins. PR #9091.

title: Make reply completion-time pair coverage exhaustive
description:
## Finding

The non-success completion-time matrix checks a pair only when at least one of its `*-with-time` / `*-no-time` builders exists. If both keys are deleted or misspelled, `:when (or with-builder no-builder)` silently removes that family/situation from both the primary propagation/omission test and its adversarial controls. `time-pair-exclusions` is a separate manually maintained vector, but no test proves that every omitted pair has an explicit exclusion.

## Evidence

- `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:428-460` defines the three pair axes and the three deliberate exclusions.
- Lines 616-649 assert that a half-pair is invalid, but the `:when (or with-builder no-builder)` filter means a zero-pair is invisible.
- Lines 847-871 repeat the same declared-pairs-only traversal for the drop/nil-fill controls.
- Lines 651-665 validate entries already present in `time-pair-exclusions`; they do not establish completeness or exclusivity against the supported `:error`, `:cancel`, and `:stale` builders in `families`.
- Concrete false-green: delete both `:error-with-time` and `:error-no-time` from the HTTP descriptor. HTTP still has its ordinary `:error` builder, all envelope/status/work-id validations still run, and the completion-time pair plus controls silently skip HTTP error. No exclusion is required or reported.
- The current JVM tier passes 27 tests / 533 assertions. The issue is structural non-vacuity under matrix drift, not a present production failure.

## Impact

A future descriptor refactor can remove an entire completion-time obligation while keeping the suite green. That reopens the exact umbrella gap this tier exists to close: a family can stop proving that a supplied causal completion timestamp propagates and an absent timestamp is omitted.

## Recommendation

Add an executable partition/bijection check over every supported non-success family/situation: it must declare exactly one of (a) a complete with-time/no-time pair or (b) one explicit exclusion with a reason. Unsupported baseline situations should declare neither. Reuse that validated partition to drive the primary and adversarial tests, avoiding independent skip logic.

## Risks and contracts

Do not impose `:completed-at` on terminals whose production builder deliberately does not accept or durably use it (HTTP stale, machine cancel, timer cancel). Preserve unsupported route/timer error/cancel distinctions. This is a test-matrix completeness fix, not a production timestamp policy change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every supported `:error`, `:cancel`, or `:stale` row is classified as either a complete time pair or one explicit exclusion.
2. A family/situation with neither classification fails with a diagnostic naming the family and situation.
3. A half-pair, duplicate pair-plus-exclusion, duplicate exclusion, or exclusion for an unsupported situation fails.
4. A focused mutation proves deleting both keys from one currently paired row makes the suite red.
5. Existing propagation, omission, reply validation, and drop/nil-fill controls remain green in JVM and consolidated CLJS lanes.
close_reason:
PR #9095 (head e99777468d). Premise HELD: ':when (or with-builder no-builder)' made a family/situation row with BOTH pair keys deleted invisible to the propagation/omission gate AND to its drop/nil-fill controls, with no exclusion required and no diagnostic emitted, and time-pair-exclusions had no completeness or exclusivity check against it.

Fixed test-only in implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. time-pair-partition-problems classifies EVERY family x {:error :cancel :stale} cell — exactly one of a complete with-time/no-time pair or exactly one explicit exclusion carrying a reason, and an UNSUPPORTED situation (no baseline builder) declares neither — returning family/situation-labelled problem strings. every-nonsuccess-terminal-declares-a-time-pair-or-an-exclusion asserts it empty and separately asserts the cell arithmetic (18 cells = 12 paired + 3 excluded + 3 unsupported). nonsuccess-time-pair-partition-fails-closed feeds the SAME classifier seven mutated matrices and asserts it non-empty: zero-pair, half-pair, pair-plus-exclusion, duplicate exclusion, exclusion for an unsupported situation, exclusion for a cell outside the matrix, exclusion missing its reason.

Criteria 1-3 are that classifier. Criterion 5's reuse requirement is met by paired-rows / time-paired-rows: completion-time-propagates-and-omits-across-nonsuccess-terminals and nonsuccess-completion-time-gate-fails-closed-on-drop-and-nil-fill now BOTH drive off the validated partition instead of their own independent skip logic, so a row can never be in one and absent from the other.

Criterion 4 proved by mutation: deleting :error-with-time AND :error-no-time from the HTTP descriptor (the bead's own worked example) exits 1 with the partition naming ':http / :error is a SUPPORTED terminal with neither a complete pair nor an explicit exclusion' plus the arithmetic failure '18 cells vs 11 paired + 3 excluded + 3 unsupported'. The exclusions were already correct and none was added or removed; no production timestamp policy changed, and the HTTP-stale / machine-cancel / timer-cancel exclusions are untouched. JVM lane green at 30 tests / 556 assertions (was 27 / 533); CLJS lane owned by CI (no node_modules in the worker checkout).

title: test-quiet exit-integrity regression misses both safeguarded branches
description:
## Correctness finding

The CLJS exit-integrity regression added with the two production safeguards does not exercise either safeguarded failure mode. It repeats a normal red fixture invocation that was already covered before the safeguards landed, so both safeguards can be removed while the named regression remains green.

## Evidence

- `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs:122-156` documents and implements two independent protections: catch a throw from `replay-buffered-warnings!` before `js/process.exit 1`, and seed `process.exitCode = 1` before a run so a missing `:end-run-tests` dispatch cannot drain to exit 0.
- Commit `45fbaaa4dd` introduced both protections and `deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero` together. Its parent already had the ordinary default reporter branch `(do (replay-buffered-warnings!) (js/process.exit 1))`, so a normal red run already exited 1 whenever replay completed.
- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:712-756` invokes the ordinary armed warning fixture and ordinary unarmed fixture. It neither makes replay throw nor prevents/delays the custom `:end-run-tests` method. Therefore it traverses the pre-existing normal red/green exits, not either new protection.
- The exact armed child invocation was already present before the fix in `red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn` (introduced by `a89226ca3f`): current lines 612-635 use the same namespace and `RF2_TQ_RED_WARN_FIXTURE=1`, and already assert no spawn error, no timeout, nonzero status, and the replayed marker. Current lines 636-657 already repeat the same fixture unarmed and assert exit 0 and quiet canonical output. The later test adds only `Ran`/`FAIL in` assertions to duplicate child processes.
- `end-run-tests-exit-decision` at lines 270-281 calls upstream `cljs.test/successful?` and checks only that some method exists. ClojureScript 1.12.145 itself defines a no-op `[:cljs.test/default :end-run-tests]` method at `cljs/test.cljs:359`, so method presence does not prove that test-quiet owns the exit behavior.
- All-state bead searches for the regression names, seeded exit, replay exception, copied/default predicate, and duplicate spawn found no existing issue. The legacy `rf2-jmrdhn` identifier referenced by the commit is not present in the current bead store.

## Impact

A regression can remove the replay exception guard or the seeded fallback while every current exit-integrity assertion stays green. The suite therefore claims protection against the exact false-green hazards described by the production code without discriminating them, while paying for two redundant Node child starts.

## Proposed disposition

Replace or augment the ordinary red process row with controlled process-level fixtures for the two protected branches. Add an env-gated seam that makes replay throw after a genuine failure, and a separate env-gated seam that lets a started run drain without the test-quiet `:end-run-tests` exit (for example a controlled no-op reporter dispatch). Fold the ordinary `Ran`/`FAIL in` checks into the existing warning-replay row instead of spawning the same armed/unarmed pair twice. Remove or repurpose `end-run-tests-exit-decision`; a direct pure helper is acceptable only if it is the helper the production defmethod invokes.

## Risks / retained contracts

Keep the real child-process boundary because exit status cannot be proven in-process. A control must prove its fixture ran and reached the intended exceptional/missing-dispatch state; an unrelated parse error, uncaught fixture error, timeout, or skipped suite also exits nonzero and must not satisfy it. Preserve normal red warning replay, normal green quietness, both focused and whole-suite seeding call sites, and the compile-cycle boundary that keeps `shadow-node` out of the test namespace's requires.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the existing `deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero` regression and confirm its ordinary armed-red and unarmed-green child rows pass.
2. In a disposable branch, remove the `seed-failure-exit!` calls from the focused and whole-suite entry points, leaving the ordinary reporter path intact; rerun the named regression. It remains green because the normal `:end-run-tests` path still exits 1.
3. Restore the seed, remove the `try`/`catch` around `replay-buffered-warnings!`, and rerun the same regression. It remains green because its fixture never makes replay throw.
4. Compare the child invocations with `red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn`; they use the same ordinary warning fixture, demonstrating that neither protected exceptional branch is selected.
5. Treat a future control as valid only when it emits a reached-state marker for the replay-throws or missing-dispatch branch; a generic nonzero child status is not sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real spawned red run forces warning replay itself to throw, proves a genuine test failure was reached, and still exits nonzero; removing the replay `try`/`catch` makes this control fail for the intended reason.
2. A real spawned run starts tests but deliberately bypasses or no-ops the test-quiet `:end-run-tests` exit, then drains with status 1 from the seeded `process.exitCode`; removing `seed-failure-exit!` makes this control fail with status 0.
3. Each fault fixture emits an unambiguous reached-state marker and assertions reject spawn errors, timeouts, parse failures, skipped tests, and unrelated uncaught exceptions as alternate explanations for nonzero status.
4. Ordinary armed red warning replay and unarmed green quietness remain covered once each, including `Ran`/`FAIL in`, warning marker, canonical green output, and exit status; the duplicate armed/unarmed child invocations are removed.
5. `end-run-tests-exit-decision` no longer treats upstream `successful?` behavior or mere presence of ClojureScript's default no-op method as proof of test-quiet's custom exit logic.
6. Both focused `run-test-vars` and whole-suite `run-all-tests` paths retain the seeded-failure behavior.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held. Both safeguards now have their own fault fixture in the new re-frame.test-quiet-exit-integrity-fixture-cljs-test, each proven by a plant: removing the replay try/catch reds red-replay-throw-cannot-mask-the-nonzero-exit at :833:11 (the poison message escapes as an uncaught crash - status alone cannot discriminate, since an uncaught exception also exits 1), and neutering seed-failure-exit! at both call sites reds run-that-never-dispatches-the-exit-defmethod-drains-nonzero at :867:11 with 'got status 0'. Each fixture emits a reached-state marker and the rows reject spawn errors, timeouts, parse errors, unmatched selectors and skipped suites. deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero deleted, its Ran/FAIL-in pins folded into red-run-replays-warnings-and-exits-nonzero (renamed); duplicate armed/unarmed spawn pair gone. end-run-tests-exit-decision retired - the seeded exit code makes the green process row prove defmethod ownership instead. Both seed-failure-exit! call sites retained. 16/16 contract rows green, exit 0.

title: Make reply work-id descriptor metadata fail closed
description:
## Finding

`every-work-id-is-a-comparable-edn-tuple` says every family descriptor supplies `:work-head` and that missing identity metadata fails explicitly, but its comprehension uses `:when (and builder work-head)`. A missing or accidentally renamed `:work-head` therefore removes every supported situation for that family from the work-id gate. The explicit `wid` presence, vector, expected-head, and EDN round-trip assertions never execute.

## Evidence

- `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:489-505` contains the fail-closed claim and the `work-head` skip.
- All six current descriptors at lines 315-421 carry `:work-head`; it is not an optional field. The only legitimate filter is the situation builder, because `:error`/`:cancel` can be unsupported.
- `:work-head` has no other executable consumer in the repository. Removing it from a descriptor leaves the other vocabulary/status tests green; this work-id test silently omits that family's rows.
- History confirms the mismatch is accidental residue. Commit `55c28a5558` removed the old `wid` skip specifically to make the gate fail closed and stated every descriptor has a non-nil `:work-head`, but retained the older `work-head` guard. Later commit `5806d23efe` simplified the comment to “Missing ids fail explicitly” without changing the guard.
- The current JVM tier is healthy (`clojure -M:test`: 27 tests, 533 assertions), so this is a mutation false-green rather than an existing runtime failure.

## Impact

A future family-row edit can drop or misspell the expected work-id head and silently lose the tuple/head/EDN checks for that family. That defeats the cross-family conformance tier at exactly the metadata boundary it claims to lock.

## Recommendation

Filter only on `builder`. Assert that `work-head` is present before comparing it to `(first wid)`, or validate required descriptor metadata once for every family and then run the situation matrix. Add a mutation/non-vacuity control demonstrating that a descriptor without `:work-head` makes the gate red.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve optional situation builders: route and timer legitimately omit some error/cancel paths. Do not make `:error` or `:cancel` universal. This change is test-only and must not alter reply builders or the public reply vocabulary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every descriptor with a supported situation is exercised even when `:work-head` is nil or absent.
2. Missing `:work-head` produces an explicit, family-labelled failure rather than zero assertions.
3. Existing work-id presence, vector, head, and EDN-round-trip checks remain for all current supported family/situation rows.
4. A focused mutation/control proves deleting one descriptor's `:work-head` makes the suite fail.
5. Both JVM and consolidated CLJS reply-conformance lanes remain green after restoring the real matrix.
close_reason:
PR #9095 (head e99777468d). Premise HELD and was measured before the fix: deleting :work-head from the :http descriptor left the reply-conformance suite GREEN at exit 0 with 517 assertions instead of 533 — 16 assertions silently skipped by the ':when (and builder work-head)' filter, nothing on screen.

Fixed test-only, in implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. The filter is now the situation builder ALONE (:error / :cancel stay legitimately optional for route and timer); a new family-level assertion requires :work-head to be a keyword; and work-id-head-matches? is a SHARED predicate the primary gate asserts TRUE and the new control work-id-gate-fails-closed-on-missing-descriptor-metadata asserts FALSE, so weakening it reddens one side or the other. work-id-rows makes the row set an explicit value, and the control pins that deleting :work-head does NOT reduce the visited row count — the silent-skip axis, which the value-only check would have missed.

Criterion 4 proved by mutation AFTER the fix: the same :work-head deletion now exits 1 with 556 assertions still running (five failures, family-labelled), where before it exited 0 with 16 fewer. Acceptance criteria 1-4 met; 5 (JVM lane) green at 30 tests / 556 assertions, up from 27 / 533. The CLJS lane was not run locally (no implementation/node_modules in the worker checkout) — the change is portable .cljc and CI owns that lane.

title: test-quiet CLJS var-filter regression tests only a copied predicate
description:
## Correctness finding

The CLJS shadow-node contract suite's `find-matching-test-vars-filtering` test does not execute `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars`. It tests a local copy of the predicate, so the advertised namespace-versus-qualified-var selection contract can break while the named regression remains green.

## Evidence

- `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs:173-180` is the production selector. It reads `env/get-test-vars` and filters simple symbols by namespace and qualified symbols by fully-qualified var name.
- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:148-175` explicitly says it cannot inject the registry, then defines a local `select` function at lines 157-166 that reproduces the production predicate. The assertions call only that local function; the test namespace cannot require the `:dev/always` runner because doing so forms the documented compile cycle.
- The parser assertions at lines 49-65 prove only that `--test=my.ns/a-test` becomes a symbol. `unmatched-selectors-guard` at lines 191-226 starts from an already-selected `matched-vars` collection. Neither reaches the production filter.
- The process-level `spawn-runner` calls at lines 487-756 use valid namespace selectors or deliberately absent selectors. None selects an existing fully-qualified var, and no process row proves that a namespace selector returns all vars in that namespace.
- Repository-wide `--test=` consumer searches likewise found operational scripts selecting namespaces, not a valid `ns/var`; the only positive qualified-var examples are parser/copy assertions in this test file. A production mutation that ignores `test-var-syms`, treats qualified symbols as namespace symbols, or selects only one var per namespace does not affect the local `select` function and is not discriminated by the process rows.
- Git blame/history shows the copied test was introduced in `953dffc80d` and has never called the production selector. Searches across all bead states/fields for `find-matching-test-vars`, `var filtering`, `fake-var`, `copied predicate`, `shadow-node filtering`, and the test name found no existing issue.

## Impact

The suite reports direct coverage of a supported CLI contract that it does not execute. A regression can make focused single-var runs select nothing or the wrong tests while the parser, copied unit test, unmatched-selector unit test, and ordinary whole-namespace process rows stay green. This is especially hazardous because focused runs are used to reduce large consolidated builds.

## Proposed disposition

Move the pure selection decision into the compile-cycle-safe `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node-cli` namespace (for example, a helper accepting `test-syms` and a supplied var collection), make `shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars` delegate to it with `env/get-test-vars`, and point the existing synthetic-var assertions at that shared production helper. An equivalent injectable seam is acceptable, but do not retain a second handwritten predicate in the test. Add one real focused `ns/var` process proof if the cost is acceptable; the shared-helper test is the minimum non-vacuous pin.

## Risks / retained contracts

Do not make the test namespace require `re-frame.test-quiet.shadow-node`; its `:dev/always` test-data macro dependency creates the compile cycle this split exists to avoid. Preserve input order, namespace-wide selection, exact qualified-var selection, mixed selectors, metadata shape (`{:ns :name}`), the unmatched-selector refusal, and the existing public CLI spelling.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `find-matching-test-vars-filtering` in the consolidated test-quiet Node suite and confirm it passes.
2. In a disposable branch, change production `shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars` so either qualified symbols no longer match fully qualified var names or simple symbols no longer select a namespace.
3. Rerun `find-matching-test-vars-filtering`; it still passes because the assertions invoke the test-local `select` predicate rather than the mutated production function.
4. Search the process-level rows for a successful existing `--test=namespace/var` selection; none provides a positive production-path control for the qualified-symbol branch.
5. Restore the mutation after observing the false green.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The var-filtering test invokes the same selection function used by `shadow-node/find-matching-test-vars`; it contains no local copy of the namespace/FQN predicate.
2. Tests cover a namespace selecting every matching var, an existing qualified symbol selecting exactly one var, mixed namespace/FQN selection, and absent selectors.
3. A controlled mutation that removes either the simple-symbol branch or the qualified-symbol branch makes the focused test fail.
4. The `:dev/always` runner remains out of the test namespace's require graph, and the consolidated node-test build compiles without a cycle.
5. A valid namespace-focused real runner still exits 0, an unmatched selector still exits nonzero, and (if added) a real existing `ns/var` selector runs exactly the requested test.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held. The rule moved to shadow-node-cli/select-matching-test-vars (the compile-cycle-safe ns unmatched-selectors already lives in) and find-matching-test-vars now delegates to it over env/get-test-vars; the test drives the shipped function and the copy is gone. Plants: removing the simple-symbol branch reds find-matching-test-vars-filtering at :184/:190; removing the qualified-symbol branch reds it at :187/:190 and the FQN selector then matches nothing at the real runner. Control fired: the identical whole-ns invocation on the restored tree reports 0 failures for that row vs 2 under the plant. Added the optional real ns/var process row - the green fixture ns now carries two tests so the namespace selector must see 'Ran 2 tests' and the qualified selector 'Ran 1 tests'. NOTE: driving the shipped selector immediately exposed a real defect, fixed in the same PR - (symbol <ns-symbol> <name-symbol>) keeps both parts unconverted and CLJS hashes a symbol by hashing those parts as strings, so every such symbol hashes to one constant while staying = to the reader's ns/name; a set matched it while array-map-backed (<=8) and stopped above that, so --test= selected correctly up to eight qualified selectors and NOTHING at nine (measured: 8 of 9 real vars reported unmatched). Both call sites now route through one test-var-names helper; the regression pins nine selectors.

title: ssr-node latency envelope ignores the runtime partition
description:
## Evidence

- The pre-registered condition in implementation/ssr-node/src/envelope.cjs:40 and the ENVELOPE property at :71-72 bound only state EDN text to 64 KiB.
- The measured request in test/envelope.test.cjs:67-79 contains no runtime partition and computes only the byte lengths of two state values. It omits key bytes as well.
- Runtime became a second cloned request partition in crossing commit 9a42302f7a. Current protocol.cjs:329-373 counts every UTF-8 key and value per partition, and :458-468 enforces one combined state.bytes + runtime.bytes ceiling.
- The runtime-partition change did not touch envelope.cjs or envelope.test.cjs; git log --follow shows the registration still comes solely from f39829caa6.
- As written, the claimed condition admits any runtime payload below the separate body/protocol ceiling, while the witness measures none of it. The test therefore does not falsify the published envelope over the request domain the prose now describes.
- No existing bead found by ssr-node, runtime-partition, state-budget, or envelope searches owns this drift; rf2-8arzr.3 added the combined protocol ceiling but explicitly left the latency witness outside its fence.

## Impact

The pre-registered latency promise can be read as covering a runtime-heavy request that its only witness never measures. The test also uses a byte definition different from the validator it is meant to condition, making its green verdict weaker than the stated contract.

## Disposition

Amend or version the registration without refitting the p50/p95/max ceilings: define the 64 KiB condition over state and runtime together, rename stateBudgetBytes accordingly, and have the witness send non-empty data in both partitions. Count UTF-8 key plus value bytes with the same semantics as validatePartition. Record the amendment explicitly so the original pre-measurement provenance remains auditable.

## Risks

Do not silently rewrite history or tune ceilings after measurement. The latency numbers and sample count were pre-registered and must remain unchanged unless a separately preregistered successor envelope is introduced. The reference entry allowlists constrain which runtime key can be used.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The registration and README describe one explicit 64 KiB condition over state plus runtime, while preserving the existing latency ceilings and sample count.
2. The measured request contains non-empty allowlisted state and runtime partitions.
3. The witness byte calculation includes every UTF-8 key and value and matches protocol.cjs semantics.
4. A runtime-heavy controlled request that exceeds the combined condition is rejected by the witness precondition rather than counted as an eligible sample.
5. git history or an explicit amendment note continues to distinguish the original preregistration from this contract repair.
6. The ssr-node suite is green, including the envelope row.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9078. Every element of the premise held at my tip: src/envelope.cjs bounded only state EDN text to 64 KiB (condition at the header, ENVELOPE.stateBudgetBytes); test/envelope.test.cjs's measured request carried no runtime partition and summed the byte lengths of two state VALUES, omitting every key as the bead says; and src/protocol.cjs's validatePartition counts Buffer.byteLength(key) + Buffer.byteLength(value) per partition and enforces ONE combined state.bytes + runtime.bytes ceiling.

ONE CLARIFICATION ON THE CEILING, since the two numbers differ and the difference is not a disagreement: protocol.cjs's ceiling is maxRequestBytes, default 1 << 20 = 1 MiB, a REFUSAL ceiling; the envelope's 64 KiB is a narrower pre-registered SAMPLING CONDITION under which the latency figures are claimed. Two layers, and both are kept. What they must share is how a byte is counted, and now do.

REPAIR (AC1-AC3): stateBudgetBytes -> requestBudgetBytes, same 64 KiB, restated over state + runtime together; a new exported requestBytes() counts keys and values across PARTITIONS read from protocol.cjs rather than naming the two fields locally, so a third partition cannot be added to the wire and leave the condition measuring two of three — which is exactly how this drift happened; the measured request now carries a non-empty allowlisted runtime partition (:rf.runtime/routing, the only key app/root's runtimeAllowlist permits) and is asserted inside the budget as a PRECONDITION before any sample is taken. README's condition row and a new paragraph say the same thing. Zero residual references to stateBudgetBytes repo-wide.

AC3 is pinned rather than asserted in prose: a new row admits a request at maxRequestBytes exactly N and requires validateRequest to REFUSE it at N-1, which is only true if requestBytes and validatePartition agree key for key.

AC4 PROVEN, and the false-green is MEASURED rather than argued. Permanent control row: a request busting the condition on runtime alone is over budget by requestBytes while validateRequest still accepts it — so the row is about the envelope's condition, not the protocol ceiling. Plant on the measured row (single-line anchor, match count 1 read first): runtime oversized to 70000 bytes gives 'AssertionError: the sample request must sit inside the registered 65536-byte budget; it is 70155 bytes', captured exit 1, 5 pass / 1 fail. On that SAME request the pre-repair formula computes 124 bytes and admits it — 124 vs 70155 is the size of the false green. Restore verified by git blob hash (cdee2d42bd94950c818118c2af886da811c3ddb1), not by reading a diff.

AC5: no ceiling and no sample count moved — p50 5 ms, p95 25 ms, max 250 ms, 200 samples are the values registered in f39829caa6, and an explicit AMENDMENT block in src/envelope.cjs records what was corrected (the condition's DOMAIN) and what was not (every number), keeping git log --follow provenance readable. Measured overhead with the runtime partition added: p50 0.18 ms, p95 0.28 ms, max 1.59 ms — well inside the untouched ceilings.

AC6: 9 suites green, 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base; envelope.test.cjs 4 rows -> 6.

title: ssr-node boot-once test never observes the boot hook
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/test/isolation.test.cjs:121-133 claims to prove that the module boots once per isolate, but the row only proves that two renders used the same worker thread and each observed overlapMax === 1.
- overlapMax is render-concurrency state (test/fixtures/reference.cjs:24-26,78-94). It has the same value if boot() is never called, called once, or called before every sequential render, so neither asserted outcome discriminates the stated contract.
- The fixture's only boot signal is module.exports.booted: initialized at test/fixtures/reference.cjs:73, written at :75, and never read anywhere in the repository. A whole-repo exact-identifier search finds only those two fixture sites.
- The worker's actual contract is load-bearing: src/worker.cjs invokes the optional module hook during isolate boot, and the Hicasso server bundle has a real hook that initializes its substrate. A regression in that call site would remain green in the dedicated package row.
- The row and inert booted signal date to the initial isolation witness (8ab673ea78); later egress changes did not make the assertion observe boot.

## Impact

The package gate can report that per-isolate boot is protected after the hook is removed, skipped, or moved to per-request execution. That leaves a real application initialization contract without the regression witness named for it.

## Disposition

Replace the inert boolean with a boot-call count (or an equally direct observation) owned by each loaded fixture instance, include it in the emitted observations, and assert that both sequential renders on one isolate observe exactly one boot. Keep the existing same-thread precondition so the row still proves the requests reached one isolate.

## Risks

The reference fixture is also required directly by some in-process controls, so the observation must not let the main process module cache contaminate the worker-thread measurement. Do not weaken the separate overlapMax concurrency rows; they protect a different guarantee.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The normal two-render, one-isolate case reports exactly one boot invocation on both responses.
2. A controlled mutation that removes the worker boot call makes this row fail.
3. A controlled mutation that invokes boot for each render makes this row fail.
4. The dead booted write-only boolean is removed or replaced by the direct measured signal.
5. All 9 ssr-node suites (currently 104 rows) remain green after restoring the controls.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9078. The premise held exactly: test/isolation.test.cjs's row 'the module boots once per isolate, not once per request' asserted overlapMax === 1 on two sequential responses, and overlapMax is render-concurrency state that reads 1 whether the boot hook is called never, once, or before every render. The fixture's booted boolean was written at reference.cjs:75 and read nowhere — a scoped census over implementation/ssr-node found it only at :73 and :75 as an identifier (the two other hits are prose), line-oriented and whitespace-flattened agreeing, with a control needle that fired.

REPAIR: the fixture counts boots on the isolate's own globalThis (Symbol.for key) rather than in module scope, and publishes the count in its observations. Module scope was rejected deliberately: a counter a re-require resets would report 1 for a per-request require-and-boot too, which is one of the two failures the row exists to catch. Each worker thread has its own global, so the count cannot see another isolate's boots nor the main process's copy of the fixture, which addresses the bead's stated contamination risk (the in-process controls require reference.cjs directly). AC4: the dead boolean is removed.

AC1/AC2/AC3 PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, both directions, each plant anchored to a single line with its match count read first (=1) and each restore verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff. AC1: normal case reports boots === 1 on both responses, captured exit 0. AC2: deleting 'if (typeof mod.boot === function) mod.boot();' from src/worker.cjs gives 'AssertionError: the isolate must have booted the module exactly once', actual 0 expected 1, captured exit 1, 6 pass / 1 fail. AC3: calling mod.boot() before every render gives the same row '2 !== 1', captured exit 1, 6 pass / 1 fail. Each plant failed exactly ONE row — the repaired one — so neither broke the file out from under its neighbours. Both restores hashed to e0eab3d1f6a674613277bc8ffbb1b782dd1d4086.

AC5: all 9 ssr-node suites green after restore — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0, on the final rebased base. Baseline before any edit was 104/104; the +3 are the two envelope rows and the bytes row from siblings .71 and .72. isolation.test.cjs stays at 7 rows: this was repaired in place, not added to. overlapMax remains asserted in concurrency.test.cjs where it is the subject, per the bead's risk note.

title: Resources SSR: projection metadata is computed, not recorded — docstring corrected (PR #9097); ruled B 2026-09-04: no trace op, spec/016:1609 reword -> rf2-oryb
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc:871-879 says projection-metadata is recorded by the host adapter in route/SSR diagnostics.
- Spec 016 §SSR and hydration, lines 1593-1596, requires server route handling to record serialized/redacted/omitted/key-projected/fresh/stale/refetch decisions; lines 1609-1611 specifically require diagnostics to account for withheld re-keyed rows, why they did not ride, their projected key, and refetch-on-client true.
- The production projection at ssr.cljc:978-1005 invokes project-entry but consumes metadata only for :withheld? and then discards it, returning only the resource runtime-db slice.
- The only published hook, :ssr/extend-runtime-db-projection at ssr.cljc:2407-2412, is consumed by implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:591-617 solely as a map merged into the hydration payload. No route, SSR, trace, or diagnostic implementation consumes projection-metadata anywhere in repository production code; all other callers are direct unit tests.
- git log -S projection-metadata shows the feature began in 82bb734ce2 and later projection fixes, but no diagnostic consumer was introduced.

Impact
The implementation computes and tests the promised metadata as a detached pure helper while the real server render path throws that decision record away. Withheld privacy-sensitive rows therefore vanish without the required server-side accounting, and tests can stay green without exercising a diagnostic carrier.

Proposed disposition
Integrate projection metadata into the actual request-local server route/SSR diagnostic path, preferably sharing the single project-entry evaluation with wire projection so metadata and payload cannot drift. Keep diagnostics separate from the hydration wire. If the product intentionally retracts this contract, make that an explicit specification ruling and remove the orphan helper/tests and normative MUST language rather than leaving a false promise.

Risks
The metadata base currently includes the raw scoped resource key in addition to the projected key. Any diagnostic carrier must remain trusted/request-local or apply the egress policy before leaving the process; it must not create a new sensitive-identity leak. Avoid evaluating a time-sensitive projection twice with different clocks.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `rg -n "projection-metadata|project-entry" implementation/resources implementation/ssr` and separate production callers from direct tests.
2. Inspect the production projection in `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc`: `project-resources-runtime-db` consumes `:withheld?` from the `project-entry` result and returns the projected runtime-db slice, but does not carry the remaining decision metadata onward.
3. Follow `:ssr/extend-runtime-db-projection` into `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc`; its result is merged into the hydration payload and no request-local route/SSR diagnostic consumer receives `projection-metadata`.
4. Exercise the real SSR payload path with a withheld or re-keyed row and inspect the observable diagnostic carrier. The row's wire disposition is enforced, but the detached helper's full decision record is not emitted through a framework-owned diagnostic path.
5. Reconcile this observation with the latest issue notes before implementation: the already-landed documentation correction removed the false claim that the host adapter currently records the metadata, while the remaining product decision is whether to add an explicit diagnostic contract or retire the helper.
acceptance_criteria:
- A production SSR payload/render integration test observes projection decisions through the real diagnostic path, not by directly calling projection-metadata.
- Serialized, redacted, omitted, key-projected, fresh/stale, withheld, and refetch-on-client outcomes are covered, including a row absent from the wire but present in diagnostics.
- The wire projection and diagnostic record derive from one authoritative decision and use one clock/frame target.
- Tests prove no raw sensitive scope/params are emitted to any off-box diagnostic sink.
- Spec 016 and implementation documentation match the chosen shipped contract; JVM and CLJS SSR/resource suites pass.
notes:
PARTIAL 2026-09-03 by PR #9097 (head f83a1f16c3, branch worker/falsegreen-a). LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY — read on.

THE PREMISE FAILED IN ITS FRAMING. The bead's title says 'wire promised projection metadata into real diagnostics', which assumes the WIRING is the missing half. It is not: the PROMISE was the defect. Both halves of the bead's own evidence hold verbatim — projection-metadata at ssr.cljc:881 is a public pure helper with ZERO production consumers (the only production caller of project-entry is project-resources-runtime-db, which reads :withheld? at ssr.cljc:1010 and discards the rest at :1011; every other reference in the repo is a direct unit-test call, 34 of them across 6 test files) — but the conclusion the bead draws from them does not.

NO UNMET MUST, WHICH IS WHAT CHANGES THE DISPOSITION. Checked the normative language at source rather than from the bead's summary of it. Spec 016-Resources.md:1595 addresses the cited step to '**Server route handling:**' and states it with NO MODAL — pointedly unlike its immediate neighbour at :1593, which does read 'SSR MUST use request-local frames'. Its EP ancestor is weaker still (EP-0003:1622 reads 'Server route handling **should**:'). The MUST that does exist nearby, at :1609, governs one verb — WITHHOLD — and the projection satisfies it (ssr.cljc:1010 drops the row from the wire). The three facts that MUST accompany the withholding are all genuinely present in the returned map: :disposition (ssr.cljc:857-862), :projected-key (:856), :refetch-on-client? (:877-878). The trailing clause 'so the server's own diagnostics still account for it' is an indicative purpose clause whose subject is the HOST's diagnostics. The framework does not resolve routes, own the event pump, or own the drain loop — ssr.cljc:1021-1024 says so explicitly for the adjacent step. So the specification was ACCURATE and required no change; only the implementation docstring over-claimed.

WHAT LANDED. The docstring asserted 'PURE; the host adapter records it in route/SSR diagnostics' — a statement of fact about a wiring that no adapter, example or api doc performs. Corrected to say what is true and why it is deliberate rather than unfinished, so the helper's existence is not read again as evidence that projection decisions are recorded somewhere. Two supporting sites corrected with it: the ns docstring's 'records' -> 'COMPUTES (for a host to record, if it wants to — nothing here does)', and the project-entry comment's 'The server's diagnostics still account for a withheld entry in full' -> 'These three slots are what let a server ACCOUNT for one ... carrying them to a diagnostic sink is the host's job'. Comments and docstrings only; the namespace reads to the same 49 top-level forms before and after (clojure.tools.reader, exit 0, both sides). The bead's contemplated 'remove the orphan helper/tests and normative MUST language' is NOT warranted: there is no MUST to remove, and the helper is a legitimate affordance rather than an orphan.

RECORDED FOR ANY FUTURE FIX, because it is the trap: :ssr/extend-runtime-db-projection CANNOT be the diagnostic carrier. Its single return value is merged onto the hydration WIRE payload (payload_policy.cljc:614-616), while the metadata base carries the RAW scoped :resource/key (ssr.cljc:743, annotated at :614 as 'the RAW key, as the server holds it') — precisely the identity the withholding rule exists to suppress. Routing metadata through :rf.runtime/ssr has the same defect, since payload_policy.cljc:590 copies that straight onto the payload. This is the bead's own stated risk and it is well-founded.

WHY STILL OPEN — THE GENUINE UNMADE DECISION, FOR MIKE. Whether re-frame2 should SHIP server-side projection accounting at all is a product call, not a worker's. If yes, the cheap and honest version already has its precedent in this very namespace: a catalogued :rf.resource/* trace row emitted from inside project-resources-runtime-db's EXISTING single project-entry pass (ssr.cljc:1009), reusing trace/emit! exactly as ssr.cljc:1124 already does server-side for :rf.error/resource-ssr-blocking-timeout, with resources/trace_egress.cljc already owner-classifying :resource/key for off-box egress. That shares one clock (bound once at ssr.cljc:992) and one decision, so wire and diagnostic cannot drift — which is the bead's third acceptance criterion. What it needs that a worker should not take unilaterally is a NEW OP IN THE SPEC 009 CLOSED :rf.resource/* FAMILY (009-Instrumentation.md:1061 enumerates it and has no server-projection op) — a spec-catalogue addition and a hot-zone file. It does NOT justify a new request-local diagnostic subsystem; nothing in the spec asks for one, and the errors-only accumulator at ssr/error_listener.cljc:173 is not a general ledger.

So: the false promise is gone and no false promise remains in the tree. The acceptance criteria as written (a production integration test observing decisions through a real diagnostic path) are NOT met and are not met by this PR — they presuppose the ruling above.
DOSSIER 2026-09-04 15:45:28 AUSEST (mayor, at Mike's request): decision dossier written at ai/decisions/rf2-6r9j.53.ssr-projection-diagnostics-op.md (local-only, lives until the ruling lands). RECOMMENDATION: Option A, thin form - emit one per-entry :rf.event :rf.resource/* trace row (op name for the worker to settle, e.g. :rf.resource/ssr-projected) from inside project-resources-runtime-db's existing single project-entry pass (one clock, one decision), dev-only via the existing debug-enabled? gate, raw key projected off-box by the existing trace_egress classifier; catalogue it in Spec 009's :1061 bullet, Spec 016's :1729 family list, and Xray's roster/test/specs. Option B (reword Spec 016:1609 to the shipped contract, keep the helper, close) is a clean hours-long second choice; C (leave open) is the one to avoid. FACTS THAT CORRECT THIS BEAD: (1) the "host calls projection-metadata and records it" affordance PR #9097 left in the docstring cannot deliver drift-free accounting: the helper takes clock-ms as an argument, the production pass binds its own clock privately at ssr.cljc:1009, and the hook gives the host no callback at that point - a host re-evaluates every entry under a second clock, the exact drift this bead's third criterion warns against. (2) The :rf.resource/* family is ENUMERATED (37 ops at 009:1061), not gated: Spec 009:148 calls :operation values "the open, per-concern vocabulary catalogued below"; check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py checks A/C key on :rf.error/* and :rf.warning/* only (:81-97) and the Clojure ratchet excludes (emit! :rf.event ...) (:275-282). The one hard pin is Xray's exact-set test resources_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:131-140. (3) spec/016 is NOT a hot-zone file (CLAUDE.md:100 lists 002/005/006/009 + Conventions/API/Tool-Pair/Spec-Schemas), so option B touches no hot-zone file and A touches only 009 (one bullet); Spec-Schemas.md is untouched by A. (4) Line numbers drifted: projection-metadata :884, production pass :908-1032, hook table :2438; the description still describes the pre-#9097 docstring. (5) Spec 016:1607 "Hydration rules (MUST)" already uses "diagnostics" to mean the framework's own trace surface (met by :rf.resource/hydrate-clock-skew), which weakens the "host's diagnostics" reading of :1609.
RULING 2026-09-04 21:04:43 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-6r9j.53.ssr-projection-diagnostics-op.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). Verified read-only at tip df66b1679496 (HEAD == origin/main, tree clean), 20:58-21:04 AUSEST.

THE RULING. Option B: re-frame2 does NOT ship a server-side SSR projection-decision trace op. No new :rf.resource/* operation is minted, Spec 009's family bullet, Spec 016's family list and Xray's roster/exact-set test are untouched, and projection-metadata (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc:884-906) stays as the pure, host-callable affordance PR #9097 documented it as. What remains is documentation, filed as ONE follow-up bead, rf2-oryb: (1) reword the trailing clause of the withholding MUST at spec/016-Resources.md:1609 so it states the shipped contract in words that cannot be read as a framework promise - the framework COMPUTES the record and neither records nor traces it; recording is the host's, per the modal-free "record projection metadata" step addressed to Server route handling at :1595; (2) add the clock caveat to projection-metadata's docstring so a host that does record is told to evaluate under the clock it rendered with. No executable change, no hot-zone file, hours of work.

WHY B AND NOT A, IN ONE PARAGRAPH. The dossier recommended A (one per-entry :rf.event row emitted from the single project-entry pass) on the strength of one clock / one decision, and named its own reversal condition: "if no host or tool ever reads the JVM trace surface, the op is dead weight and B is right". That condition holds at tip, and A has three further defects the dossier did not see, all verified in source: (a) the row would be FRAMELESS - implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:630-636 (stamp-frame) supplies the canonical :frame tag only when the tags carry :rf.trace/dispatch-id, and project-resources-runtime-db runs from payload assembly after the drain, as a direct call with no run in scope; the family's :rf.frame/id evidence key does not substitute (rf2-hbmeb, trace.cljc:609-622); (b) a frameless row is never retained anywhere - implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:33 and :251-259 (frameless emits skip the per-frame ring; the B3 ruling is they stream live to listeners only) and implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/capture.cljc:196-216 / :274-302 (no :frame tag means nothing is buffered, and even a site-stamped :frame with no dispatch-id and no in-flight cascade takes the orphan-drop arm) - so the row cannot reach an epoch record, and the resource egress projector, which is wired ONLY at implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1693 (the sole non-test caller of :resources/project-resource-trace-egress), would never see it; the dossier's "raw key projected off-box by trace_egress" claim is therefore vacuous for this row, and the only path that CAN observe it is a host-installed live :trace listener, which receives the raw event; (c) the emit site is a reusable pure projector with two production call sites that can both run for one request - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc:329 (render-state projection) and implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:786 (streaming final assembly), the non-streaming builder taking the already-projected slice as its :runtime-db opt (payload_policy.cljc:753-757) - so per-invocation rows couple trace cardinality to how often a helper is evaluated, not to one committed response. A catalogued op with no reachable consumer, a privacy story that does not hold for its only reachable path, and duplicate rows per request is gold plating under Mike's posture, not the thin feature the dossier priced at fifteen lines.

WHY B AND NOT "LEAVE THE SENTENCE AS IS" (the Codex position). Spec 000:565 grades obligations RFC 2119: capitalised MUST binds, lower-case does not; the MUST at 016:1609 governs the verb withhold, and the implementation satisfies it (ssr.cljc:1027 drops the row). Codex is right that this means no unmet MUST and no rewrite is REQUIRED. It is still the wrong stopping point: the same sentence has now been read as a framework promise by the audit that filed this bead and by the mayor's dossier, and as satisfied by the #9097 worker and by Codex - four readers, two readings. The colon after "MUST therefore withhold it" introduces three consequences of which "the projection metadata records ... so the server's own diagnostics still account for it" is the third, "records" ordinarily means somewhere, and the neighbouring "Hydration rules (MUST)" at :1607 uses "diagnostics" for the framework's OWN trace surface (met by :rf.resource/hydrate-clock-skew), which pulls "the server's own diagnostics" toward the same reading. The spec is the artefact; a sentence that needs a dossier to be read correctly is fixed in the sentence, once, for the cost of one PR.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S CLOSE REASON. The close (2026-09-04 09:55:23Z = 19:55:23 AUSEST, by the mayor's backlog reread) says commit 866e452d37 was "authored by Mike" and is "RESOLVED BY MIKE HIMSELF". That is a misattribution: 866e452d37 is the rebase commit of PR #9097, branch worker/falsegreen-a - a worker's PR, authored as Mike by this repo's no-AI-attribution convention - and the worker's own note above ("WHY STILL OPEN - THE GENUINE UNMADE DECISION, FOR MIKE") left the product question open deliberately. Mike did not rule by that commit; he asked for the dossier (note of 15:45:28 AUSEST) and then delegated the ruling, which is this note. The close's DISPOSITION nonetheless stands, now for the right reason: the ruling above takes the retract arm, the docstring correction that was this bead's executable content is on main, and the remaining work is separate documentation filed as a follow-up. The Codex reviewer inherited the misattribution ("the bead was closed after Mike's 866e452d37 ruling"); its technical findings are independent of it and are what the ruling rests on.

OPTIONS REJECTED.
- A, thin form (dossier): per-entry :rf.event :rf.resource/* rows from inside project-resources-runtime-db - frameless and unretained, unreachable by Xray / pair / epoch egress, raw key to the only listener that can see it, N rows per projector evaluation; no consumer in tree. Rejected as gold plating.
- A, correct form (Codex's own sketch of what A would really cost): a request-level commit point after the host commits the response, an extracted pure {wire, metadata} operation on one clock, a defined carrier with privacy at that carrier, a consumer, and only then a Spec 009 / Xray op - a subsystem nothing in the spec asks for and no host or tool needs today. Rejected; the design is recorded below for the day a consumer exists.
- C, leave as is with the bead open / deferred: rejected by all three readers; nothing to defer.
- Codex's "no spec edit at all": rejected as above - the sentence is demonstrably read two ways.
- Retire projection-metadata and its tests as a vestige: rejected (the #9097 worker, the dossier and Codex all concur) - it is the tested explanation algebra of the decision record the production pass itself uses (project-entry), and a legitimate host affordance.
- Grow the API to close the clock drift (a 3-arity project-resources-runtime-db taking a caller clock, or a hook callback): rejected - API for a hypothetical host; trust the programmer, document the caveat.
- Reopen this bead for the follow-up work: rejected - its executable content is on main; the spec/docstring edit is a distinct task and gets its own bead so the close record is corrected, not rewritten.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Dossier (mayor, 15:35 AUSEST): recommended A thin; B honest second choice; C to avoid. DISSENT on A, for the reasons above; CONCUR that C is out and that B's shape (one sentence, helper stays, no hot-zone) is right. Codex Recommendation (independent): keep the host-owned contract, add no op, no spec edit, leave closed, revisit only with a named consumer. CONCUR on no op and on keeping the helper; DISSENT on no spec edit. Distinct contributions preserved here, condensed:
- Dossier: the "host calls projection-metadata and records it" story cannot deliver drift-free accounting - the helper takes clock-ms, the production pass binds rf.interop/epoch-now-ms privately at ssr.cljc:1009 and exposes neither the clock nor a callback, so a host re-evaluates every entry under a second clock and an entry at its stale boundary can classify differently on the wire and in the record (:freshness / :refetch-on-client?). - Dossier: the trace surface is dev-only on the JVM too - emit! (trace.cljc:860, gate :881) and emit-error! (:903, gate :918) sit under rf.interop/debug-enabled?, which on the JVM is implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:298, true by default and off under -Dre-frame.debug=false / RE_FRAME_DEBUG=false; nothing in the spec asks for a production ledger.
- Dossier: implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc:173 (pending-error-traces) is an error-only per-frame buffer drained onto the response status, not a general ledger and not a home for this.

That gap is real and is accepted by this ruling; a host that wants the answer calls projection-metadata.
- Codex: Spec 000:565 RFC grading (capitalised MUST binds; lower-case prose does not) - verified; the 016:1595 step is modal-free and its EP ancestor docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md:1622-1630 reads "should".

- Codex: Spec 011:386 already states the off-box posture - Xray / pair / epoch egress redact runtime-db per projection policy, trusted-local tools opt in explicitly.
- Codex measured (this ruling did not run tests): focused SSR suite 54 tests / 220 assertions green; ring suite 50 / 121; resource egress suite 10 / 73 - all on the pre-ruling tree, all proving the epoch export boundary a frameless row cannot reach.
