Acceptance criteria, restated (the originals on this bead presupposed option A and are retired, not met): (1) spec/016-Resources.md:1609's clause states that the framework computes the projection metadata and does not record or trace it, recording being the host's per :1595, with no capitalised modal added or removed and no trace op named; (2) projection-metadata's docstring carries the clock caveat; (3) no new :rf.resource/* operation exists in implementation/, spec/009, spec/016:1729, or tools/xray (grep for ssr-projected or any new rf.resource keyword returns nothing); (4) scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict green; implementation/resources JVM and CLJS suites green; (5) PR body states the exact spec wording chosen, that prose was checked by hand, and that the tree is executable-identical (docstring/spec only).

IF THIS IS EVER REVISITED (a named consumer appears: a Ring/JVM diagnostic sink, a server-to-Xray transport, or a host requiring exact projection auditing) - the design that would be right, recorded so it is not rediscovered: that bead owns consumer and producer together; first extract one pure internal operation returning both {wire-projection, metadata} from one entries snapshot, one frame and one caller-supplied clock, with project-resources-runtime-db delegating to it; emit or call back only AFTER the host commits that projection to a response, so render-state probes and streaming retries do not masquerade as delivered projections; define privacy at the actual carrier (a live JVM listener receives raw events - prefer a record that projects or omits the raw scoped key before delivery, and never cite the epoch exporter as protection for a path it cannot reach); test the real adapter-to-sink path with a withheld row (absent from the payload, present in the record, no raw scope/params leaving the process, duplicate/retry semantics pinned); and only then mint the op in Spec 009's :1061 bullet, Spec 016's :1729 list, Xray's trace-ops + exact-set test + specs 023/024 - per-entry rows, tags = the existing meta' map plus the frame, no new fields - and if the carrier is not the trace stream, no trace keyword at all. If it IS the trace stream, the row must be correlated (carry a dispatch-id, i.e. be emitted from inside a run) or it will never be retained by any ring or epoch.

FOLLOW-UPS. Created rf2-oryb (P2, task, discovered-from rf2-6r9j.53): the spec/016:1609 reword plus the projection-metadata docstring clock caveat, description carrying the full brief above. Amended rf2-6r9j.53: this note appended; title changed from "wire promised projection metadata into real diagnostics" (the option not taken) to name what was done and ruled; status left CLOSED. No other bead touched.

RE-VERIFY AT DISPATCH. Line numbers (016:1595/1607/1609/1729; ssr.cljc:884-906/1009/1027; trace.cljc:630-636; capture.cljc:196-216/274-302; tool_pair.cljc:1693) - all drift; re-grep. Whether spec/016 has moved since a8b4eaff6a. Whether any PR in flight touches spec/016-Resources.md §SSR and hydration or ssr.cljc's docstrings (none at 21:04 AUSEST; the two open PRs were #9182 spec/009 + core, #9183 hicasso docs). Whether a JVM trace consumer has appeared in tree (grep register-listener! under implementation/ssr, examples/, tools/ - if a lifecycle-row consumer exists, the "revisit" section applies and this ruling's premise has moved).
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor's backlog reread — ALREADY RESOLVED ON MAIN, AND RESOLVED BY MIKE HIMSELF. This bead was on the mayor's held-for-Mike list as "honour or retract a normative MUST". Mike answered it on 2026-09-03 and the hold outlived the answer by a day.

THE RULING IS COMMIT 866e452d37, authored by Mike, titled "docs(resources): projection-metadata is an affordance, not a wiring (rf2-6r9j.53)" — it names this bead in its subject line. Its own words settle both halves of the question:

  "The wiring is not the half that was wrong."
  "there is no unmet MUST here and no spec change to make -- the specification
   was accurate and the docstring was not."

So the premise this bead rests on does not hold. Spec 016 addresses the step this bead cites — "record projection metadata (serialized, redacted, omitted, key-projected, fresh, stale, refetch-on-client decisions)" — to "Server route handling", and states it WITHOUT A MODAL. The only MUST nearby governs WITHHOLDING the re-keyed row, which the projection already satisfies, and the three facts that MUST accompany it (:disposition, :projected-key, :refetch-on-client?) are all genuinely present in the returned map. There was never an unhonoured MUST to honour or retract; there was a docstring asserting a wiring that no adapter ever had.

CONFIRMED IN SOURCE AT TIP, not inferred from the commit message — the check-5 rule is that a grep hit is a pointer, not a finding. implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc:890-902 now reads: "PURE, and an AFFORDANCE rather than a wiring: it computes the decision record and returns it. It does not route it anywhere, and nothing in this repository consumes it outside tests. That is deliberate ... So do not read this helper's existence as evidence that projection decisions are recorded anywhere — an earlier version of this docstring asserted that the host adapter records it, which was never true of any adapter in-tree." The correction is live.

THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ON THIS BEAD ARE FOR THE OPTION NOT TAKEN and are deliberately NOT being met. They describe the WIRE arm — a production SSR integration test observing projection decisions through a real diagnostic path, one authoritative decision feeding both wire and diagnostic, and so on. Mike took the RETRACT arm. Leaving the bead open until those criteria are met would be holding it against a contract the operator declined; that is why they are being discharged as moot rather than as satisfied, and this paragraph exists so a later reader does not reopen it on the unmet list.

THE COMMIT ALSO RECORDS A GUARD WORTH KEEPING VISIBLE, since it is the trap a future "just wire it up" would fall into: :ssr/extend-runtime-db-projection CANNOT be the carrier, because its single return value is merged onto the hydration WIRE payload while these maps carry the raw scoped :resource/key that the withholding rule exists to suppress. That is now in the docstring at :895-898, where the next person to consider wiring will meet it.

HOW THE HOLD SURVIVED ITS OWN ANSWER, worth recording because the mechanism is general: a decision can land as a COMMIT rather than as a note on the bead, and no loop reads commits against the open list except this one. The dispatch loop reads bd ready, the merge loop reads PRs, and neither would ever have noticed. That is precisely the case check 5 of the backlog reread exists to catch, and it caught it — one day late, at zero cost, because nothing was blocked behind it.

title: migration(reagent): retire nonexistent dom-node bridge compatibility path
description:
## Finding

The repository's Reagent compatibility guidance retains a bridge-only path for `dom-node` that does not exist at the pinned floor. `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:15` correctly says Reagent 2.0 dropped `reagent.dom/dom-node`, but line 19 names `reagent.core/dom-node` and delegates to M-42. The canonical M-42 text then says stock Reagent 2.x has not removed the Var, that it is available unchanged on the bridge, and that `dom-node` sites need scanning only when moving to reagent-slim.

## Independent evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
- In the resolved upstream Reagent 1.2.0 Maven source, `reagent/dom.cljs:58-62` defines `dom-node` and delegates to `react-dom/findDOMNode`; `reagent/core.cljs` contains no `dom-node`. In the resolved Reagent 2.0.1 source, neither `reagent/dom.cljs` nor `reagent/core.cljs` defines `dom-node`. This is an upstream surface deletion, not an inference from this repository's bead or prose.
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1753` lists the nonexistent spelling `reagent.core/dom-node`; lines 1755 and 1761 say the bridge keeps it and delay the sweep until slim.
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:194,224,229` repeats that `dom-node` is unchanged/available on the bridge and says to grep it only on slim.
- Real v1-shaped examples in this repository use the historical `reagent.dom` spelling: `skills/reagent-migration/evals/evals.json` contains `rdom/dom-node`, and the Reagent-to-Hicasso census classifies `dom-node` as a runtime blocker.

All-status title/description searches for `dom-node`, `M-42`, `bridge dom-node`, `reagent dom-node`, `stock Reagent has not removed`, and a full issue export scan found no bead owning this mismatch. Closed `rf2-mpmjj` added the Reagent root-render inventory row; it is limited to `render` warning/no-op discovery and repeats the existing M-42 guidance rather than covering the absent `dom-node` Var.

## Impact

A v1 app using the real historical spelling `reagent.dom/dom-node` can be moved to the classic `day8/re-frame2-reagent` bridge and fail compilation immediately, while the migration instructions explicitly tell the agent that the bridge is unaffected and that the full symbol sweep waits for slim. The wrong `reagent.core/dom-node` spelling can also make an exact inventory miss the call site. The proposed `:ref` rewrite is already correct; applicability and source namespace are not.

## Proposed disposition

Retire the nonexistent bridge compatibility claim. Make M-42 and the migration skill inventory `reagent.dom/dom-node` (including aliases such as `rdom/dom-node`) for both adapter choices and keep it Type B because ref ownership is call-site-specific. Repair the adapter README and other normative copies that name `reagent.core/dom-node` or say it remains available on the Reagent 2 bridge. Preserve the narrower truth for the other symbols: this issue does not establish that `force-update-all` or `unmount-component-at-node` Vars are absent from stock Reagent 2.0.1.

Add a focused migration fixture/eval proving a bridge-targeted v1 source with `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` plus `(rdom/dom-node this)` is surfaced for human review before compilation.

## Risks

Do not turn this documentation repair into a compatibility shim or an automatic ref rewrite. A `dom-node` consumer's parent owns the replacement ref, so the migration must remain Type B. Do not generalize the verified absence of `dom-node` to unrelated legacy Vars that 2.0.1 still defines.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Confirm `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn` pins `reagent/reagent` 2.0.1.
2. Inspect the resolved upstream sources for Reagent 1.2.0 and 2.0.1: 1.2.0 defines `reagent.dom/dom-node`, while 2.0.1 defines neither `reagent.dom/dom-node` nor `reagent.core/dom-node`.
3. Run `rg -n "dom-node|M-42" implementation/adapters/reagent migration skills/re-frame-migration skills/reagent-migration` and observe the current guidance naming `reagent.core/dom-node` or claiming the bridge retains the operation.
4. Feed a bridge-targeted v1 fixture containing `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` and `(rdom/dom-node this)` through the current migration guidance/eval. It is not consistently surfaced as a bridge migration blocker before compilation, despite the pinned dependency having removed the Var.
5. Do not infer anything about the other legacy Reagent operations from this reproduction; their availability requires separate evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The adapter README and M-42 use the historical upstream symbol `reagent.dom/dom-node`, not `reagent.core/dom-node`, and state that pinned stock Reagent 2.0.1 has already removed it.
2. The re-frame-migration inventory/guidance scans qualified and common aliased `reagent.dom/dom-node` call sites for both classic-bridge and slim targets, and classifies every hit Type B for author-owned ref placement.
3. A focused bridge-targeted fixture or eval containing `[reagent.dom :as rdom]` and `(rdom/dom-node this)` fails the old 'bridge unaffected / slim only' behavior and passes only when the site is reported before compilation.
4. Normative M-42 copies no longer claim `dom-node` is available unchanged on the bridge; references remain mutually consistent and their links/anchors pass the migration citation and documentation-slug gates.
5. The repair does not add a `dom-node` shim, does not auto-invent a ref owner, does not change dependency versions, and does not alter claims about `force-update-all` or `unmount-component-at-node` beyond evidence separately established.
notes:
Audit of PR #9090: M-42 is corrected in the primary migration guidance, but implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md still presents the bridge as React 17/18, says r/dom-node works there, and says reagent.dom/render works. The pinned bridge is React 19/Reagent 2.0.1 and dom-node is absent, so this current comparison table preserves the exact false compatibility path the bead owns. Narrow repair: align the comparison/migration-note rows with the landed bridge contract; no shim or broader redesign.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9119 — REOPENED (correctness + completeness). The PR correctly fixes the reagent-slim comparison, but it establishes evidence that leaves the exact M-42 owner internally inconsistent. Reagent 2.0.1 still DEFINES render, unmount-component-at-node and force-update-all; it does not make them usable on the React-19 bridge. Its reagent.dom/unmount-comp unconditionally calls react-dom/unmountComponentAtNode, and force-update-all routes every mounted root through re-render-component -> render-comp -> react-dom/render. Against the pinned React DOM 19.2.0, both properties are undefined (direct runtime probe: {render:"undefined", unmountComponentAtNode:"undefined"}), so those paths warn and then throw a JS TypeError. PR #9119's DESIGN-RATIONALE now says this accurately.

The canonical M-42 copies still teach the opposite: migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1755-1757 says unmount-component-at-node and force-update-all remain bridge-available and delays their sweep until slim; skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-handlers-state.md:194,224,228,230 says they are unchanged/available on the bridge, scans force-update-all only for slim, and implies bridge unmount remains usable. This contradicts the newly corrected adapter guidance and acceptance criterion 4's mutually-consistent normative copies. It can leave a bridge migration with a runtime-crashing legacy call.

Minimal repair: keep the important distinction that the Vars exist on Reagent 2.0.1 (do not call them compile-time removals), but align M-42 and its skill copies with their React-19 runtime behavior; scan force-update-all on both targets as Type B, and route legacy unmount through the same adapter-owned root migration as render. Preserve the already-landed dom-node inventory/eval work; acceptance criteria 2 and 3 are in fact present at current tip, despite the prior close reason saying otherwise. No compatibility shim or broader redesign.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED; the first close evaporated to the .beads checkout race. Landed on main as a1571886d4 (PR #9119, worker slimxray-a), on the audit's narrow ruling: align reagent-slim's comparison/migration-note rows with the landed bridge contract, no shim, no broader redesign. Measured by UNPACKING THE RESOLVED MAVEN JARS rather than trusting prose: reagent 1.2.0 defines dom-node at reagent/dom.cljs:58; 2.0.1 defines it in NEITHER dom.cljs NOR core.cljs. But 2.0.1 DOES still define render / unmount-component-at-node / force-update-all, and render's own docstring says 'Usable only with React 18 or older' - so the table now makes that distinction rather than flattening it, which honours the bead's own caution not to infer anything about the other legacy operations from the dom-node finding. Skills copies (skills/re-frame-migration, skills/reagent-migration) were reported, not edited: out of fence, and an automated pass was live across skills/**.

title: (BUG) reagent-slim error-boundary integration tests are guaranteed green
description:
## Correctness finding

Two reagent-slim tests advertised as React error-boundary integration proofs are guaranteed green without exercising React error propagation.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_cljs_test.cljs:512-532` creates `outer` and `inner` boundary classes, but never uses or mounts `outer`. It manually invokes only `inner.prototype.componentDidCatch`, then asserts `outer-fired` remains zero. `clj-kondo` independently reports the `outer` binding unused at line 519. The assertion cannot detect broken nested-boundary isolation.
- Lines 534-555 name a test `error-boundary-during-commit-via-component-did-mount`, but create no child, invoke no `componentDidMount`, and mount no React tree. They manually call the boundary's `componentDidCatch`, duplicating the direct callback-forwarding proof at lines 470-486.
- The suite header at lines 11-14 claims it proves errors during child render/commit and nested isolation. Lines 462-467 acknowledge the tests use no React render and say a real-DOM test belongs in the browser target.
- A repository-wide search for `reagent2.core/create-class` / `component-did-catch` in tests finds no real-DOM reagent-slim error-boundary scenario. The other slim DOM create-class tests cover lifecycle prev-state and shouldComponentUpdate, not error propagation.
- These tests and claims originated in `21d4b06aae`, whose commit message likewise reports child-render, commit-error, and nested-isolation coverage.

## Impact

The retained seven-key Form-3 compatibility feature can break at its React integration boundary while the suite continues to report coverage. The unused outer class also adds dead test setup and makes a tautology look like behavioral evidence.

## Proposed disposition

Replace the two pseudo-integration tests with a real browser/DOM scenario using reagent-slim's actual `create-root` and `create-class` path. Exercise a descendant render or mount-lifecycle throw beneath nested slim boundaries; prove the inner boundary handles it, the outer does not, fallback commits, and callback payload/counts are correct. Keep the direct unit test for wrapper argument forwarding. If nested/commit propagation is intentionally delegated entirely to React and not a reagent-slim contract, remove the false tests and suite claims instead of retaining guaranteed-green proxies.

## Risks

React deliberately reports caught errors to the console and development StrictMode may replay work. The harness must capture/restore expected console output, assert actual mounts/callback counts, and avoid accepting an early render failure or skipped test as green.

## Duplicate search

Searched every bead state/field for `nested boundary`, `component-did-catch`, `error boundary`, `component_cljs_test`, and reagent-slim. `rf2-08hx1` owns lifecycle argv; `rf2-wdvlp` owns a Hicasso error-boundary defect; neither covers these tests. No duplicate exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- No test named or documented as child-render, child-commit, or nested-boundary integration proves the claim by directly invoking `componentDidCatch` in isolation.
- A real-DOM reagent-slim proof mounts nested boundaries and a throwing descendant through the production renderer; it asserts the descendant path ran, the inner catch fired with the expected error/info, the fallback committed, and the outer catch count remained zero.
- The commit-phase arm proves the throwing lifecycle actually ran; the render-phase arm, if retained as a separate claim, proves its throwing render actually ran.
- A negative control that removes the inner boundary or breaks its lifecycle installation makes the focused test fail rather than merely changing console noise.
- The existing direct callback-forwarding, derived-state, rethrow, and no-boundary unit contracts remain green without duplicate tautological tests.
- Suite/header/IMPL-SPEC coverage prose names only behavior the executed tests actually prove.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip and fixed. Both tests were vacuous exactly as filed: error-boundary-nested-isolation built an outer boundary, never mounted it, invoked only the inner prototype's componentDidCatch, then asserted the outer counter was zero; error-boundary-during-commit-via-component-did-mount created no child and mounted no tree. The file's ns docstring also claimed the boundary tests 'use a real ReactDOM root' -- false since 21d4b06aae introduced both. Both removed and replaced by a mounted proof under a real React 19 createRoot: reagent2.dom.error-boundary-dom-cljs-test (child-render throw, child-commit componentDidMount throw, nested isolation), each asserting the throwing path actually ran, the fallback committed to the DOM, and React reported via the root's onCaughtError. Its outer-boundary-catches-when-inner-is-absent arm mounts the same throwing descendant under the outer boundary alone, so the nested arm's zero is a measurement. Non-vacuity proved by negative control: disabling the getDerivedStateFromError auto-install turns the browser lane red with 3 failures, one in EACH new test, each naming its own uncommitted fallback; restore verified by blob hash. Production behaviour was NOT changed and no production defect was exposed -- the boundary contract holds as specified. Browser lane green 781 tests/4249 assertions/0 failures. PR #9077.

title: (BUG) reagent-slim callable-prop regressions never reach the Fn/IFn branches
description:
## Correctness finding

The two callable-prop regression tests added for rf2-wyocr do not execute the production branches their names and comments claim to protect.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:485-486,596-618` puts `(js-val? v)` before `(fn? v)` and `(ifn? v)`. `js-val?` is true for every ordinary JavaScript function (`goog/typeOf` is `function`), so the plain `(fn ...)` values used by `convert-prop-value-fn-preserves-identity-rf2-wyocr` at test lines 197-216 return from the first branch. Deleting both explicit `fn?` arms would leave that regression green.
- ClojureScript 1.12.42's `cljs.core/with-meta` wraps a JavaScript function in object-backed `MetaFn`; `fn?` is true because `MetaFn` satisfies `Fn`, while `goog/typeOf` is `object`. That is the ordinary value shape that actually reaches the explicit `fn?` branch, but the test never supplies one.
- `convert-prop-value-non-fn-ifn-still-wrapped` at test lines 218-234 explicitly admits its keyword reaches `named?` and its map reaches `map?`. It never supplies a value reaching `(ifn? v)`, never invokes a wrapper, and would remain green if the `ifn?` arms were deleted.
- Commit `874eb9ef49` introduced both branches/tests and states the identity regression is pinned. Its claim that every fn had previously been wrapped overlooks the pre-existing `js-val?` first arm; the implementation change materially protects object-backed Fn values, not the plain JS function used in the regression.

## Impact

Future cleanup or condition reordering can silently remove MetaFn identity preservation or non-fn IFn wrapping while the named regressions stay green. Metadata-bearing callbacks would then receive fresh wrappers and defeat React memoisation; custom object-backed callable props could cease to be invokable from JavaScript.

## Proposed disposition

Make the tests branch-real: add metadata to a function for both public arities and assert exact identity; define a focused object-backed value that satisfies `IFn` but not `Fn`, `named?`, `map?`, or `coll?`, then prove conversion returns an invokable JS function with correct argument/return behavior. Correct the production docstring's examples (`keywords`, maps, sets, and vectors are intercepted by earlier branches and are not evidence for the `ifn?` wrapper).

## Risks

Do not reorder the production ladder merely to make the old examples true: map/coll/named conversion is part of the published prop-conversion behavior. The fixture must model a genuinely reachable callable object and avoid compiler-specific accidental classification.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 bead records in every state for `convert-prop-value`, `MetaFn`, `wyocr`, `callable`, `fn identity`, and the test path. The only matches (`rf2-y1jkm`, `rf2-6sqv`, `rf2-oz7wr`) concern Hicasso performance, console rendering, and UIx registry heads; none owns these reagent-slim branches.
acceptance_criteria:
- The 1-arg and 2-arg identity regressions use an object-backed metadata-bearing Fn and prove `identical?` with the input and across repeated conversions.
- A focused non-fn IFn fixture actually reaches the wrapper arm, returns a JavaScript-invokable function, forwards representative arities, and preserves the fixture's return values.
- Non-vacuity is demonstrated: removing/bypassing the `fn?` arm fails the MetaFn identity test, and removing/bypassing the `ifn?` arm fails the callable-object test.
- Plain JS functions still pass through unchanged; named values, maps, and collections retain their current earlier-branch semantics.
- The `convert-prop-value` docstring and test names no longer claim that keywords/maps/sets/vectors exercise a wrapper they cannot reach.
- Focused template tests pass in the normal CLJS test target and production build mode remains unaffected.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip. This is a TEST defect, NOT a production ordering defect -- the bead's own Risks section rules the ladder must not be reordered, and that is correct: map/coll/named conversion is published prop-conversion behaviour. js-val? is (not (identical? 'object' (goog/typeOf x))), so it is true for every plain JS function; the plain fns in convert-prop-value-fn-preserves-identity-rf2-wyocr and the keyword and map in convert-prop-value-non-fn-ifn-still-wrapped all returned from earlier arms, and both tests would have stayed green with the fn? and ifn? arms deleted. Repaired by moving each test to the value shape that actually reaches its arm: a MetaFn ((with-meta f m), object-backed and satisfying Fn) for the identity regressions in both public arities, and a deftype satisfying IFn but not Fn/named?/map?/coll? for the wrapper, proven to come back as a real JS function invoked via .call with arguments forwarded to the fixture's own -invoke. Each test now asserts its routing preconditions rather than assuming them. Non-vacuity proved both ways: removing the fn? arm reds ONLY the MetaFn test (4 failures, identity replaced by the wrapper); removing the ifn? arm reds ONLY the callable test (3 failures, 'function' vs 'object'); both restores verified by blob hash. Docstring corrected -- it cited keywords, maps, sets and vectors as ifn?-arm examples and all four are intercepted earlier; it now walks the cond in the order taken. No executable production change. PR #9077.

title: Xray: retract the dead universal value-copy affordance and its dispatcher-less copy events; correct the off-box egress inventory (B.9 lock honoured)
description:
## Finding

Xray documents a universal `⎘` value-copy affordance on every value inspector, and retains the component, CSS, event, and safe-egress contract for it, but no current inspector renders the button. The user-visible feature is unreachable and `:copy?` is now an accepted-but-ignored option.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start any current Xray build/testbed and open a panel that renders a canonical EDN inspector (for example App-DB current state or an expanded Trace value).
2. Inspect, hover, and keyboard-focus the value-inspector root.
3. Observe that no `⎘` copy control or `.rf-xray-edn-widget-copy` element is rendered, despite the README/API promise.
4. At source level, search for calls to `day8.re-frame2-xray.views.edn-widget/copy-affordance`; there are none. Passing `{:copy? true}` to the facade also has no effect because the option is ignored.

## Evidence

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget.cljs` defines public `copy-affordance` and says it rides every widget root. Repo-wide exact symbol search finds no call to `copy-affordance`; the only occurrences are its definition, comments, and the test note that prior copy-affordance tests were deleted.
- The same facade's `inspect` doc says `:copy?` is accepted but ignored, then delegates directly to `views.edn-inspector` without rendering the affordance or forwarding that option. No current `views.edn-inspector` code contains the `.rf-xray-edn-widget-copy` class.
- `theme/global_styles.cljs` still ships hover/focus CSS for `.rf-xray-edn-widget-copy`, but the only element that applies that class is the uncalled component.
- The backend event `:rf.xray/copy-value-to-clipboard` remains registered and tested in `panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs`; those tests dispatch it directly and do not prove a UI button exists. `egress.cljs` explicitly counts the universal button as one of two live off-box sinks.
- Current public/current-state docs promise the UI: `tools/xray/spec/API.md` lists "The `⎘` copy button riding every value inspector" and `tools/xray/README.md` describes two human copy surfaces. This is therefore not merely an unused internal helper.
- Git commit `0a38534c54` migrated value rendering to the first-class data-display widget, removed the old copy-affordance assertions, and stated copy chrome was deferred to a later popup phase. Subsequent inspector rewrites retained the dead component/contract but no current renderer wired it.
- Bead title searches for `copy affordance`, `copy value clipboard`, `universal copy`, and `copy chrome`, plus description search for `copy-affordance`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

The public API/security inventory claims an off-box UI operation users cannot reach, while production ships dead component/CSS and an ignored option. Tests prove the safe backend only through direct dispatch, so a missing integration can remain green indefinitely. Any repair must also preserve frame isolation and fail-closed egress; casually reattaching the raw-value button would be a security regression.

## Proposed disposition

Resolve the contract explicitly. Preferred while the README/API promise remains: render one accessible copy affordance from the canonical `views.edn-inspector` root (or its single facade), route the click back to the frame captured at render time, and exercise the full safe-egress/clipboard path. Remove the accepted-but-ignored `:copy?` shim unless a real supported per-call opt-out is defined. If product direction instead retires universal copy, remove the dead component/CSS/no-op option/backend-only surface as appropriate and retract the README/API/egress inventory together; do not leave a phantom feature.

## Risks

Clipboard output is an off-box sink. Preserve `egress/egress-value`, sensitive/large-value elision, nil/stale-target fail-closed behavior, and per-instance frame routing. Ensure hover-only styling does not hide the control from keyboard or assistive-technology users. Avoid adding one button per recursive tree node when the contract is one affordance per inspector root.

title: test(story): stop treating the no-op reg-variant row as a browser probe
description:
Finding

`tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs` classifies the `reg-variant` coverage row as a live browser `probe`, but its body only prints `SKIP` and returns. The replacement CLJS test named by the comment already landed, so this is a stale migration shim that makes the feature-load coverage report falsely claim execution.

Evidence

- The file's coverage contract at lines 28-49 defines `kind: 'probe'` to mean the function actually exercises the named feature, says a non-probed row must be `kind: 'owned-by'`, and explicitly says never wire a probe whose body does not exercise the feature.
- The `reg-variant` row at lines 1185-1219 is `kind: 'probe'`, but its `_page` body ends in only `console.warn('SKIP: reg-variant scenario · migrating to CLJS unit per rf2-8awk1'); return;`. It performs no browser or product operation. A repo-wide search finds this as the only unconditional `SKIP:` in Story source/tests/testbeds.
- The row comment says this is temporary until `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/panels_e2e/reg_variant_e2e_cljs_test.cljs` is merged. That replacement exists and says it replaces the Playwright probe; it covers the four named variants plus registration shape. Git commit `c47f1925c3` (2026-05-20) added the CLJS replacement and converted the browser row to the no-op in the same landed change, so the temporary state has already outlived its condition.
- `validateCoverageMatrix` at lines 1538-1575 checks only that a probe is a function. `assertCoverageMatrix` at lines 1578-1596 awaits the no-op and records only `owned-by` rows as declared out-of-scope. Thus the row completes green as if directly exercised, and verbose output does not disclose it among ownership skips (apart from an easy-to-miss warning inside the fake probe).
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:82` still lists `test:story-feature-load` as an owning gate and promises selecting every sidebar variant, including post-burst verification. The same file's helper table at line 425 still binds `assertMatrixVariant` to the `reg-variant` row, although this row never calls it. The separate live `Sidebar navigation` probe deliberately skips `clicked-three-times` and owns navigation, not the no-op row's claimed lifecycle/state contract.
- The adjacent `reg-decorator composition` row documents the same former no-op pattern and has already been correctly demoted to `owned-by`, providing the intended local precedent.
- Bead searches for `SKIP reg-variant`, `feature-load reg-variant`, `reg-variant scenario`, `coverage matrix no-op`, and historical id `rf2-8awk1` returned no existing issue; `bd show rf2-8awk1` also found no local issue.

Impact

A required browser coverage row is false-green: CI records a successful probe without executing the feature, the spec overstates direct browser ownership, and future reviewers can mistake a warning for coverage. The long stale block also obscures which gate actually owns the contract.

Proposed disposition

Replace the row with `kind: 'owned-by'`, naming `npm run test:cljs` and the exact CLJS replacement as its owner, and delete the no-op body/stale temporary narrative. Update spec/015 so the reg-variant lifecycle/state portions point to the CLJS test and the separately live Sidebar navigation row retains only its real browser contract. Add a policy-level guard or structural fixture that rejects `kind: 'probe'` rows whose implementation is an unconditional skip/return so this precise false-green cannot recur.

Risks

Do not remove the separate live sidebar-navigation or other `assertMatrixVariant` call sites; they cover real browser surfaces. If the coverage policy still requires every variant to be selected in a browser after the burst, implement a deterministic live probe rather than claiming the CLJS owner satisfies that browser-specific requirement.
acceptance_criteria:
- The `reg-variant` coverage row either performs a real browser assertion or is explicitly `kind: 'owned-by'` with the exact live CLJS owner; there is no unconditional warn-and-return probe.
- Verbose feature-load output reports the row honestly as executed or declared out-of-scope.
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md` accurately separates CLJS reg-variant lifecycle/registration coverage from live sidebar-navigation coverage and names no helper the row does not call.
- A policy/unit witness fails if a coverage-matrix `probe` is replaced with an unconditional `SKIP`/return implementation.
- Node syntax/policy tests, the Story CLJS replacement suite, `test:story-feature-load`, and relevant browser scenarios pass.

title: vestigial(story): retire the inert run-variant render contract
description:
Finding

Story still exposes and internally passes a `run-variant` `:render?` option, and every run result still carries `:rendered-hiccup`, but the option is unread and the result slot is permanently nil. This began as a staged placeholder and is now a retired architecture preserved as an active-looking compatibility contract.

Evidence

- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:68` puts `:rendered-hiccup nil` in `empty-result`; `record-result-map` at lines 686-694 unconditionally writes `:rendered-hiccup nil` with the comment that rendering is performed by the UI shell or `render-variant`; and the `run-variant` docstring at lines 1276-1278 explicitly says rendering is separate and the compatibility slot remains nil.
- Repo-wide source search finds no branch that reads `:render?` to render anything. Nevertheless the live shell passes it at `ui/shell.cljs:312`, `ui/canvas.cljs:432`, and `ui/workspace.cljc:328`; `prepare-run!` advertises it at `runtime.cljc:1376`; and `run_owner_cljc_test.cljc:85` passes it without asserting any rendered result. These calls are inert configuration noise.
- The documented contract claims the opposite: `spec/007-Stories.md:425,432` says `:rendered-hiccup` is populated under `:render? true` and is the screenshot-test input; `tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md:718-722`, `tools/story/spec/000-Vision.md:114`, `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:117,891`, and `docs/story/api/runtime.md:47,98-114` repeat the active-looking option/result shape.
- Story-MCP consumes the impossible slot as if live. `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:160` and `dev.cljc:170` scrub and return it; tool descriptors promise rendered output; `wire_pipeline.cljc:37,89-90` says it dominates token cost; the MCP spec/docs classify its egress. Tests manufacture non-nil hiccup in stubbed outcome maps, so they prove the scrubber but never prove that a real Story run can produce it.
- Git history proves the retirement path: `fa993fa5e4` (2026-05-11 Stage 3) introduced nil with `Stage 4 fills this in`; no later implementation populated it. `82cd4bd1c8` (2026-07-10) changed runtime prose to say rendering is outside headless orchestration and relabelled the nil as a reserved compatibility slot, while the normative/API/MCP promises remained.
- Bead searches for `rendered-hiccup`, `rendered hiccup`, `run-variant render`, and `compatibility slot` returned no existing issue.

Impact

The public and MCP contracts advertise a screenshot/tooling feature that cannot be reached, callers carry ignored options, and substantial MCP egress/dedup/token-budget prose and tests defend data that Story never emits. A consumer following the API receives nil even when explicitly requesting render. The contradictory authorities also make future work liable to test the stubbed shape rather than the real integration.

Proposed disposition

Retire `:render?` from run/prepare opts and retire `:rendered-hiccup` from the unified run-result. Keep `render-variant` as the single explicit visual-rendering API and rewrite screenshot guidance around its structured `:rendered` result. Remove the inert opts from shell/canvas/workspace. Reconcile normative Story docs, API docs, tests, Story-MCP payload projections/descriptors/specs, dedup hints, and token guidance. If `preview-variant` genuinely needs visual output, have that tool call a supported renderer explicitly and describe its substrate/capability boundary; do not infer rendering from `run-variant` or preserve a permanent nil slot.

Risks

This is a documented result-map field, so downstream destructuring may depend on key presence even though its value is always nil. Treat the removal as an API migration and update compatibility/release notes as policy requires. Story-MCP runs on a headless JVM where render capability may be unavailable; it must return an honest capability refusal/omission rather than synthesize success-shaped hiccup.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run-variant`/`prepare-run!` and shell callers no longer accept or pass the inert `:render?` option, and unified run results no longer carry a permanently nil `:rendered-hiccup` compatibility slot.
- Story normative specs, API docs, examples, and screenshot guidance consistently name `render-variant` (and its actual result shape) as the rendering authority; no text claims `run-variant` populates hiccup.
- Story-MCP run/preview payloads, egress projection, descriptors, dedup/token hints, specs, and tests reflect data reachable from real production calls. Any preview rendering is an explicit renderer call with capability/error coverage.
- An integration test exercises the real Story-to-consumer path so a stubbed non-nil outcome cannot reintroduce the false contract.
- Story JVM/CLJS, shell feature-load/static build, Story-MCP, API/spec drift, and egress tests pass.

title: pair-mcp tests: make the second nREPL candidate regression case reachable
description:
## Finding
One Pair-MCP nREPL regression test contains two independent `cljs.test/async` forms in a single `deftest`. ClojureScript runs only the first async branch, so the `.nrepl-port` fallback assertions in the second branch are unreachable.

## Evidence
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl_test.cljs`, test `discover-port-shadow-probe-surfaces-each-candidate-file`, has a first async block for `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` at lines 776-795 and a second async block for `.nrepl-port` at lines 796-814.
- `clj-kondo --lint tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test` reports `multiple-async-in-deftest` at line 797: only the first async test of a deftest will run.
- The test name and comments promise coverage of each candidate-file probe, but the second branch cannot contribute assertions or a failure.
- Git blame traces this shape to commit `8b65440c7f4`; repository/bead searches found no existing issue for this unreachable branch.

## Impact
A regression in `.nrepl-port` probe-error reporting can pass the suite because its claimed test never executes. This weakens confidence in a live, documented port-discovery fallback.

## Proposed disposition
Either split the two candidate cases into separate `deftest`s or sequence both cases under one `async`/`done` lifecycle. Make execution of both cases observable so the test cannot silently regress to one branch again.

## Risks / retained contracts
Retain both `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` and `.nrepl-port` discovery behavior; both are active compatibility paths, not removal candidates. Avoid timing-dependent assertions.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Both candidate-file probe-error cases execute in the test suite and can independently fail.
2. The test uses separate deftests or a single correctly sequenced async lifecycle; no deftest contains multiple sibling `async` forms.
3. `clj-kondo` no longer emits `multiple-async-in-deftest` for `nrepl_test.cljs`.
4. The Pair-MCP test suite passes, including an assertion/counter or equivalent negative-control proof that both candidate branches ran.
notes: AUDIT PR #9076 (2026-09-03): REOPENED. The code split is correct, but the new comment at tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl_test.cljs:776-779 repeats the mechanism this PR and the close reason explicitly disproved: it says ClojureScript runs only the first async form, so the sibling never executes, can never fail, and silently drops assertions. The recorded negative control on the original shape proves the second branch did execute and fail; the actual defect is that it ran outside the awaited lifecycle and lacked independent completion/attribution. Minimal repair: rewrite only this comment to state the real one-async-per-deftest lifecycle reason. No test or production-code redesign is needed.
close_reason: PR #9101 (2026-09-03 15:14 AUSEST). Audit repair as ruled: comment only, no test or production-code change. nrepl_test.cljs:776-779 justified the one-async-per-deftest rule by the DISPROVED mechanism ('ClojureScript runs only the FIRST async form ... a sibling never executes and can never fail'). Rewritten to the real lifecycle reason: a deftest carries ONE async lifecycle, so a sibling async runs OUTSIDE the lifecycle the runner awaits — it DOES execute and its failures DO surface, but with no completion the runner blocks on and no attribution back to the case it covers, so the suite can settle before it finishes and its red can land under the wrong name. The two-deftest split from PR #9076 is untouched and still stands. clj-kondo --lint on the file: exit 0, 0 errors 0 warnings, no multiple-async-in-deftest.

title: hic: rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b)'s 'PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE' log header vs rf2-dc0c's blinding rationale — the blank log a BLINDED pilot receives cannot both name the run's kind and stay silent about it
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 07:1x AUSEST by the operator assembly for rf2-t4jpz, at the
point of actually writing the two FRICTION-LOG.md copies. UNRESOLVED — the
operator did NOT write the header, and says so, because writing it is the
irreversible half.

THE CONFLICT. rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) says: "Each friction log's header reads
PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE and records the pinned commit."

workspace.md's rehearsal section (added under rf2-dc0c, PR #9049) says of the
two operator-applied replacements: "Both replacements are written to be read
alone. Neither names a rehearsal, a counted run, or this page, so the pilot
meets one instruction rather than a choice between two."

These pull opposite ways on the SAME artefact. The friction log is handed to a
BLINDED pilot. A header reading "PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE" tells that pilot
(a) that a section 13 exists, (b) that it is inside an experiment whose
evidence status is contested, and (c) that its own run does not count — which
is precisely the kind of framing rf2-dc0c removed from outcome 7 on the
reasoning that a blinded pilot must not be asked to reason about which kind of
run it is in. The read fence separately bars reading the tracker, and "§13" is
an in-tree design reference.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNDECIDED, and why the operator stopped rather than choosing:
METHOD (b) does not say WHO writes that header or WHEN. Part 4 of the log is
explicitly the operator's section, written after the pilot ends, so the label
can be applied at disposition time without ever reaching the pilot — which
would satisfy both texts. But that is a reading, not a ruling, and the previous
rehearsal's logs did carry the header.

TIMING NOTE. rf2-t4jpz's METHOD was written 2026-09-02, BEFORE the rf2-dc0c
operator-applied variant landed with its blinding rationale, so the newer
package text may simply refine the older method rather than contradict it.

WHAT THE OPERATOR DID on the pilotasm-a run, pending a ruling: applied
workspace.md's two mandated rehearsal edits verbatim, filled the pin and the
baseline exit code that step 1 and step 5b make the operator's, and left the
PRE-PILOT header OFF the blank logs. Rationale: adding the line later is
trivial; un-leaking a blinded pilot is impossible. Both FRICTION-LOG.md copies
therefore currently carry 0 bead-id lines, 0 workspace.md links and 0 stray
fence lines, verified against source-page controls that bite.

DECISION NEEDED BEFORE DISPATCH: does the blank log a pilot receives carry the
PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE header, or is that label applied by the operator
in Part 4 after the pilot ends? Either answer is cheap to apply to the two
assembled workspaces.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:4x AUSEST. LEAVE THE HEADER OFF THE PILOT TEMPLATE. THE OPERATOR STAMPS IT ON COLLECTION.

THE CONFLICT IS REAL AND BOTH SIDES ARE RIGHT, WHICH IS WHY IT NEEDED A RULING RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) wants a "PRE-PILOT - NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE" header on the friction log, so the archived artefact cannot later be mistaken for adoption proof. workspace.md says the operator replacements deliberately "name no rehearsal... so the pilot meets one instruction rather than a choice between two", which is the blinding rationale rf2-dc0c established.

THEY BELONG TO DIFFERENT READERS, AND THAT DISSOLVES IT. The header exists for whoever reads the log LATER - an auditor, or rf2-hic-064 section 13 checkpoint. It does nothing for the pilot except tell it it is inside an experiment, which is the one thing the blinding forbids: a pilot that knows it is rehearsing reports differently, and every outcome it records is then evidence about a pilot who knew.

THE RULING: the pilot TEMPLATE carries no such header. THE OPERATOR STAMPS IT WHEN THE LOG IS COLLECTED, before it is filed under ai/findings/. METHOD (b) purpose is fully served - the archived artefact is marked - and the blinding is untouched. That is one line of operator work at collection time and zero risk.

THE WORKER INSTINCT WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND I AM CONFIRMING RATHER THAN OVERRIDING IT: it left the header off and said "adding a line later is trivial, un-blinding a pilot is not." That is the correct asymmetry and it is the reason this ruling goes the way it does. An error in the reversible direction beats an error in the irreversible one, and only one of these two errors can be undone after the pilots run.

RECORD THE MECHANISM IN THE PACKAGE, not just here: workspace.md operator section should say the header is stamped at collection, so the next operator does not re-derive this and does not leave the artefact unmarked. That edit is NOT urgent and must NOT delay the pilot dispatch - file it or fold it into the next pilots-package pass.
close_reason: Discharged by the mayor ruling of 2026-09-03 plus its recording in the package, landed on main via PR #9064 (681ff410cd). THE RULING: the pilot friction-log TEMPLATE carries no 'PRE-PILOT — NOT §13 EVIDENCE' header; the OPERATOR STAMPS IT AT COLLECTION, before the log is filed. The conflict was real and both sides were right, which is why it needed a ruling rather than a preference — rf2-t4jpz METHOD (b) wants the archived artefact marked so it cannot later be mistaken for adoption proof, while workspace.md's rf2-dc0c rationale requires that a blinded pilot meet one instruction and never learn it is inside an experiment. They belong to different readers, and that dissolves it: the header serves whoever reads the log LATER, and does nothing for the pilot except un-blind it. METHOD (b)'s purpose is fully served and the blinding is untouched. The worker's instinct was already right and I confirmed rather than overrode it — 'adding a line later is trivial, un-blinding a pilot is not' is the correct asymmetry and the reason the ruling goes this way. IMPLEMENTATION: workspace.md's rehearsal section now records the stamp-at-collection mechanism with one clause on why, so the next operator does not re-derive it. One premise turned out already satisfied and is worth recording: friction-log.md NEVER carried the header (zero hits line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed, against a control returning 5 both ways), so no template change was needed and none was made. The only outstanding work really was the recording. Both pilots ran to completion under this ruling and neither log carries the header; the two logs now await operator collection and stamping under rf2-t4jpz.

title: hic: workspace.md step 1 records a pin but never SETS one — two pilot workspaces assembled minutes apart land on DIFFERENT commits (measured, 6 apart)
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-03 07:0x AUSEST during the operator assembly for rf2-t4jpz.

workspace.md step 1 CLONES and RECORDS a pin; it never SETS one:

    git clone https://github.com/day8/re-frame2.git
    git -C re-frame2 rev-parse HEAD    # record this in the log header

So each workspace lands on whatever `main` happened to be at the instant its
clone ran. Assembling the two pilots minutes apart therefore builds them on
DIFFERENT TREES, and nothing in the procedure notices.

MEASURED, not theorised. Two clones issued in the same tick during this run:
  pilot 1 -> ed0a0c29a7b761283eaf443c5f95f0f10d4d7c78
  pilot 2 -> 4893d007b6db5dbc2cb6f282f743429ae7d13a66
Six commits apart, including two runtime changes to implementation/core
(error_emit.cljc, frame.cljc, core_artefact.cljc under rf2-6sqv). The operator
noticed only by reading both pins back and comparing them; step 1 as written
invites recording each pin independently into its own log header, where the
divergence is invisible.

WHY IT MATTERS. rf2-hic-063's ruling explicitly PERMITS the two pilots to run
in parallel, and the whole point of two pilots is two independent readings OF
THE SAME PRODUCT. Two pilots on different commits measure two different
products, and their friction logs are then not comparable with each other, nor
against the counted run that rf2-hic-063 says is read against them. It is the
same class of defect as rf2-v6l6 (a green check that measured the wrong thing)
reached through the clone rather than through the port.

REMEDY (suggested, not ruled). Step 1 takes an operator-chosen sha and checks
it out in both workspaces, e.g. a third line `git -C re-frame2 checkout
--detach <sha>` with the surrounding prose saying the operator picks ONE sha
for both pilots and that `rev-parse HEAD` afterwards is a verification rather
than a discovery. The operator on this run did exactly that by hand and pinned
both at 4893d007b6db5dbc2cb6f282f743429ae7d13a66.

Filed by the pilotasm-a operator assembly run; not fixed here, because that run
was fenced to write nothing in the repository.

title: hic: workspace.md hardcodes :dev-http 8080 for BOTH pilots — a parallel second pilot boot-checks the FIRST pilot's app and passes
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, operator half, re-run after PR #9050 and #9049. Workspace pin cfcc30ae93. Measured, not reasoned.

SYMPTOM. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md gives BOTH pilots the identical shadow-cljs.edn line ':dev-http {8080 "public"}' and step 5 says 'npx shadow-cljs watch app  # then open http://localhost:8080'. rf2-hic-063's ruling explicitly permits the two pilots to run IN PARALLEL ('separate workspaces, no shared branch'). Those two facts are incompatible, and the failure mode is silent.

MEASURED. Both pilot watches started ~20s apart from their own assembled workspaces:
  - workspace A (realworld) binds 8080 and serves conduit.
  - workspace B (linearlite) prints, as a WARNING and not an error, ':shadow.cljs.devtools.server.dev-http/http-start-ex ... BindException Address already in use: bind' — then continues and prints '[:app] Build completed. (277 files, 0 compiled, 0 warnings, 9.82s)'.
  - With both live, the operator boot check against http://localhost:8080 returns #app innerHTML length 2350, 0 page errors, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests, and renders 'conduit / Home / Sign in / Sign up'.

That is pilot A's application, returned to pilot B, with a clean bill of health. LinearLite's own boot reading in isolation is 3535; the collided reading is 2350, i.e. entirely the other app.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT FAILS OPEN. The BindException is a WARNING sitting ABOVE the 'Build completed' line, so the last thing on screen is success. A blinded pilot executing step 5 literally gets a compile that says it worked, a page that renders, and a boot check that passes — while reading the other pilot's app. Nothing in the log the pilot is looking at contradicts it. The blinding is intact but the INSTRUMENT is cross-wired, and every outcome-1..6 observation the second pilot records would be about the wrong application.

SCOPE. This bites only when the two pilots run concurrently on one machine, which is precisely what the ruling authorises. It did not bite the first rehearsal or this one, because both ran the pilots sequentially.

REMEDY IS THE OPERATOR'S CALL, NOT FILED AS RULED. Options, cheapest first: (a) give pilot 2 a different :dev-http port in workspace.md's 'Pilot 2 uses :init-fn linearlite.core/run' sentence, which already exists as the place where pilot 2's shadow-cljs.edn is said to differ, and update step 5's URL alongside it; (b) say in step 5 that the two pilots must not run concurrently on one host, which contradicts the ruling and is worse; (c) have step 5 tell the operator to read the ':dev-http' line shadow actually prints rather than assuming 8080. (a) is the smallest change and keeps the parallel run the ruling wants.

DO NOT hand this to a blinded pilot to work out — per workspace.md's own reasoning for the outcome-7 variant, a rehearsal's differences are applied by the operator so the pilot meets one instruction rather than a choice between two.

NOT A BLOCKER for a SEQUENTIAL dispatch of rf2-t4jpz. Both pilots pass their boot check and baseline when run one at a time; see the rehearsal report on rf2-t4jpz.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058. Pilot 2 now carries :dev-http {8081 "public"} on workspace.md's existing 'Pilot 2 uses :init-fn linearlite.core/run' sentence -- the bead's own option (a), the place already designated for pilot 2's shadow-cljs.edn delta -- and step 5's command comment reads '# then open http://localhost:8080 - pilot 2 uses 8081'. Those are ALL the sites: a search of the whole package found exactly two occurrences of the port (workspace.md:114 and :190) and no other place printing a URL; neither brief mentions a port, a URL or 'shadow-cljs watch' at all. 8081 collides with nothing in-repo -- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn claims 8020-8061 and 8765, and 8080/8081 sit outside that range. ON THE 'IS A SCROLLED-PAST WARNING ACCEPTABLE' QUESTION, decided with a reason and WITHOUT machinery: no, so step 5 gains one clause asking the operator to confirm the page is THIS pilot's application (pilot 1 renders conduit's masthead, pilot 2 the LinearLite board) rather than merely counting errors. Shadow classifies BindException as a warning and nothing in this package can change that, so the collision cannot be made loud in shadow's log; it CAN be made loud in the operator check that already exists -- which is precisely the instrument that passed on the wrong app in the rehearsal. Distinct ports also change the residual failure's shape: a wrong port now yields nothing or an obviously different app rather than a plausible one. NOT RE-MEASURED WITH TWO WATCHES -- that needs two clones, two npm installs and two cold compiles on a host carrying ~20 worker worktrees. What was measured cheaply: both 8080 and 8081 bind free on this host, and a second bind of a held port raises the OSError shadow reports as a warning. The warn-and-continue behaviour is this bead's measurement, cited, not re-run.

title: PR #9043 red: the derivation-egress bundle-isolation POSITIVE CONTROL lost its sentinel when rf2-g1vu replaced the keyword with an identity value
notes:
DIAGNOSED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-03 04:0x AUSEST from the failing job log. PR #9043 is converted to DRAFT (confirmed draft=true, state=OPEN) so it cannot be merged while red.

THE RED IS REAL, IT IS CORRECT, AND IT IS THE GATE DOING EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS BUILT FOR. Job: tests :: CLJS bundle isolation (counter, rf2-51x5), run 33661478278. The failure is not the negative check — it is the POSITIVE CONTROL:

  "Positive control FAILED - a sentinel is no longer PRESENT where it should be (rf2-e6qmxk). The sentinel string has DRIFTED ... so the negative counter-bundle check above has LOST ITS TEETH for that artefact: it would pass whether or not the artefact actually leaked."
  "  - derivation-egress: only 0/1 sentinels present in emitted module derivation-egress"

THE CAUSE, and it is a genuinely instructive one. Under rf2-g1vu the worker replaced dead-frame-sentinel in implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc — correctly, on my ruling, and having first REPRODUCED the raw-secret leak — changing it from the keyword ::no-egress-frame to #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)). A keyword literal compiles into the emitted bundle as a STRING. An identity value does not. So the literal the bundle-isolation script had pinned as its positive-control sentinel for the derivation-egress module simply stopped existing in the artefact.

SO A CORRECT SECURITY FIX SILENTLY DISARMED AN UNRELATED CONTROL, AND THE ONLY REASON WE KNOW IS THAT THE CONTROL CHECKS ITSELF.
