title: framework logs ExceptionInfo to console.error as a raw CLJS object — the browser shows {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14)} instead of the error message
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, while diagnosing the route-link boot failure (rf2-nvcp). Tip d1e6a707a3.

WHAT AN ADOPTER SEES. When the runtime reports an error through its own console channel, the browser console shows:

  [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), __hash: null, cljs$: 16647951}

That is a raw cljs.core/ExceptionInfo (or its ex-data map) handed to console.error as an object. Chrome renders its JS fields. The actual message — a long, genuinely well-written recovery ladder naming the operation, the recovery and three ways to establish a frame scope — is inside the object and is never printed.

MEASURED. Captured from headless Chrome on the linearlite example at this tip: three such lines, each an ExceptionInfo. The same run's window 'error' event carried the full text, so the message exists and is reachable; only the console rendering loses it. The realworld example produced the same shape. Both were reached through ordinary page load, not through any test harness.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE PILOTS. Outcome 5 is 'diagnose one induced failure through the documented diagnostic path', and the console is where a reader looks first — chapter 16 sends them to Xray, but every reader checks the console before installing a tool. An opaque object teaches the reader that re-frame2's errors are unreadable, which is the opposite of what the error text actually achieves. Three of my own diagnostic steps were spent recovering a message the framework already had.

THE CONTRAST IS SHARP. In the same console, the framework's own reg-view warning prints perfectly as text: '[re-frame] reg-view :linearlite.core/root-view — root element is #object[cljs.core.MetaFn]; data-rf2-source-coord skipped (Spec 006 §Source-coord annotation ...)'. So the string path is fine; it is the error path that hands over an object.

LIKELY FIX. At the console sink, print (ex-message e) — and the id from (ex-data e) — as a string, and attach the object as a second argument if the inspectable value is wanted. That keeps the object expandable in devtools while making the first line readable.

NOT the same defect as rf2-nvcp. That one is why the error is raised at all; this one is that the error is unreadable when it is. Fixing route-link removes these three particular lines and leaves the rendering defect in place for the next error.

FILED, NOT FIXED — implementation/ is held by live workers.
notes:
PRODUCTION EVIDENCE, added 2026-09-03 03:00 AUSEST by the same rehearsal.

Under advanced compilation the error is not merely opaque, it is anonymous. A production release of pilot 1's workspace (npx shadow-cljs release app, exit 0, 332 files, 0 warnings, main.js 1.66MB) loads to a blank page whose only diagnostic is:

  Error: zm

That is the minified constructor name. The recovery ladder, the [:rf.error/no-frame-context] id, the :operation / :recovery / :where keys — everything an adopter could act on, and everything the catalogue could be looked up by — is gone from the shipped bundle.

This is the same underlying failure as the dev build (rf2-nvcp), seen through the release path, and it sharpens this bead in two ways. First, it is the exact case friction-log.md says outcome 6 exists to catch: 'Advanced compilation removes diagnostics and warning strings, and a bundle that compiles but does not boot is the failure this outcome exists to catch.' Second, it means the console-rendering defect recorded above degrades from unreadable to unattributable in production: in dev the message at least exists inside the logged object, and in release there is no message at all.

Worth considering alongside any fix here: whether a stable complaint id (not the minified symbol) should survive advanced compilation, so a production error can still be looked up. Chapter 16 promises stable complaint ids and a catalogue; 'Error: zm' cannot reach either. Recording the observation, not proposing the design.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9060 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9060). Two halves, both measured in headless Chromium on the linearlite dev build, not asserted in a unit test.

(1) CONSOLE CHANNEL. re-frame.error-emit/report-unowned-error! passed only the record, and a CLJS map is not a JS object — Chrome rendered PersistentArrayMap's interior fields, which is the reported '{meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), ...}' (cnt 7 = the seven-key record). A readable summary line now LEADS: the exception's ex-message, else the record's :reason, else the bare category keyword. Composes no new error text. The record AND the exception still ride as their own console arguments, so structured consumers and DevTools inspection are unchanged.

(2) THE EMIT SITE, which a console-only fix could not have reached. The bead's diagnosis was one step off and it mattered: the logged object is the error-emit RECORD, not an ExceptionInfo or its ex-data, and for :rf.error/no-frame-context that record carried NEITHER an exception NOR a reason — emit-no-frame-context! dropped the payload's composed ladder. Measured: {:error :rf.error/no-frame-context, :event :rf/redacted, :event-id nil, :frame nil, :time 334.3, :exception nil, :elapsed-ms 0}. The premise 'the message exists and is reachable, only the console rendering loses it' is therefore FALSE for this category, and so is 'the window error event carried the full text' — the pageerror message was 23 characters: cljs$core$ExceptionInfo. The emit site now threads :reason/:recovery through dispatch-on-error!'s EXISTING attrs attribution seam. Its mirrored sibling emit-bad-frame-provider-arg! had the identical shape and got the same one-line treatment.

BEFORE: [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), __hash: null, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$: 16647951, ...}
AFTER:  [re-frame2] :rf.error/no-frame-context — a frame-scoped route-link ran with no frame context — ... (full recovery ladder) ... Per Spec 002 §The error and its ladder. {meta: null, cnt: 9, root: Object, ...}

error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs pinned the old two-argument shape and is updated; two new tests pin the ladder reaching the line and the sibling's symmetry. No assertion weakened. Gates: test:cljs 11197/55794 exit 0; core JVM 2175/11144 exit 0; test:browser 778/4233 exit 0; fast-pr spine exit 0, clj-kondo errors 0.

NOT DONE (deliberately, per the stance): the production-anonymity observation in this bead's NOTES ('Error: zm' under advanced compilation) is a separate design question and is untouched.

title: pilots package: nothing tells the pilot WHERE to read the published documentation, and the read fence does not affirmatively allow docs/core/ in the checkout
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, assembling both workspaces from docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/. Tip d1e6a707a3.

THE GAP. The pilot's brief makes the published documentation the reference for everything: 'Everything you need is in the published Hicasso documentation... It is your reference for everything: what to type, what things are called, why something broke, how to test, how to build for production.' Nothing in the package then says where that documentation IS.

- workspace.md's six assembly steps never build the docs site, never copy the pages in, and never record a URL. Step 6 copies only the brief and the blank log.
- The workspace layout block lists re-frame2/, app/, BRIEF.md and FRICTION-LOG.md. No docs.
- friction-log.md's template header asks the pilot to fill in 'Docs read from: <published site URL or local build>' — a field whose answer the package never supplies. There is no published site (the installation page still says the artefact is not published), so 'published site URL' is not available, and 'local build' is never described.

AND THE FENCE DOES NOT CLEARLY PERMIT THE ONE COPY THAT EXISTS. The only copy of those 29 pages is docs/core/hicasso/ inside the re-frame2/ checkout. workspace.md's read fence is headed 'The checkout is a build input, not a reference work' and its Allowed column has exactly three rows: resolving dependencies via :local/root; running a tool a published page names, at the path that page gives; reading error text and stack traces. Reading documentation is not among them. The Not-allowed column names spec/, docs/design/ and other examples — but not docs/core/, so the page neither permits nor forbids it.

A pilot reading the fence literally concludes the checkout may not be read as a reference work, that docs/core/ is part of the checkout, and therefore that it has no reachable documentation at all. A pilot reading it loosely reads the docs and cannot tell whether it has just logged a leak. Either way the citation-enforced fence — which is the instrument rf2-hic-069's audit consumes, and the thing that makes the blinding mechanical rather than impressionistic — is ambiguous at the one point it is used on every single entry.

WHAT IT IS NOT. This is not the same as gap G1/G2/G3 in pilots/README.md. Those record that the published happy path routes through a checkout at three points. This is that the package never states where the pilot's primary reference lives, nor that reading it is allowed.

FIX (the least thing). One line in workspace.md's assembly — an explicit step naming where the pilot reads the 29 pages from, either a locally built site or the docs/core/hicasso/ path — and one row in the fence's Allowed column saying that reading docs/core/hicasso/ IS the published documentation and is clean, so a citation to it is not a leak. The friction-log header field then has a defined answer.

WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW. The package was written before any workspace was assembled; the omission is only visible to somebody executing the page, which is what this rehearsal did.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST. THE PILOT READS THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION, AND UNTIL A SITE EXISTS THE PUBLISHED DOCUMENTATION IS THE CHECKOUT COPY OF IT. The fence must say so affirmatively; ambiguity at the one point the fence is used on every task is worse than either answer.

THE RULE, and it is mechanically decidable rather than a list that will drift: ALLOWED is anything under docs/ THAT THE PUBLISHED SITE BUILDS. That set is exactly mkdocs.yml docs_dir minus its exclude_docs block, so it is checkable by running the build rather than by consulting prose — and it gives the right answer for free on the hard cases: docs/design/ is in exclude_docs, so it stays forbidden by the same rule that permits docs/core/hicasso/, with no second sentence needed. NOT ALLOWED is everything else in the checkout: spec/, implementation/ source, other examples, ai/, and the design trees.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE NARROW FORM. Writing "docs/core/hicasso/ is allowed" would work today and reintroduce the ambiguity the moment a pilot follows a link out of those 29 pages into docs/core/ or docs/ssr/ — which the pages themselves do. A real adopter browsing a site can reach any published page; the fence should model that reader, not a subdirectory.

WHAT ELSE HAS TO MOVE WITH IT, because a permission that the assembly steps do not realise is still a gap:
  - workspace.md read fence: add the Allowed row, in the table own voice, and keep the heading "The checkout is a build input, not a reference work" HONEST by saying what the exception is and why it exists — there is no published site yet, and the installation page says so.
  - friction-log.md "Docs read from:" must have a supplied answer. Give it one: the local checkout copy of the published documentation, at the path, with the note that no published site exists yet.
  - The workspace layout block lists re-frame2/, app/, BRIEF.md, FRICTION-LOG.md and no docs. Say where the docs are in that block, or the pilot has to infer it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the citation-enforced fence stays the instrument rf2-hic-069 audit consumes, and it stays MECHANICAL. This ruling makes it decidable; it does not loosen it. A pilot that reads spec/ has still leaked.
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:2x AUSEST, on the judgement call the pilotpkg-a worker referred up. THE BRIEF CHANGE STAYS. It is inside my ruling intent and the worker found a carrier I missed.

WHAT IT DID BEYOND THE RULED THREE SITES. My ruling named three things that had to move together: the read fence in workspace.md, friction-log.md "Docs read from:", and the workspace layout block. The worker also changed BOTH PILOT BRIEFS, and its reasoning is the correct one: the brief is what the assembly ACTUALLY HANDS THE PILOT, and it said the checkout may not be read "for anything other than the two mechanical uses". So with the permission recorded only in the operator page and the prohibition still in the pilot own document, THE PILOT RECEIVES THE PROHIBITION AND NEVER THE PERMISSION — which is this bead defect restated one document over.

That is not scope creep. My three-site list was an enumeration of carriers, and I enumerated it wrong; a ruling that fixes three of four carriers leaves the bug live. Outcome 7 in both briefs was correctly left untouched, which is the line I would have drawn myself.

AND THE WORKER CAUGHT A HOLE IN MY RULING OWN MECHANISM, which is the part worth recording. I wrote the permitted set as "anything under docs/ THAT THE PUBLISHED SITE BUILDS — exactly docs_dir minus exclude_docs", specifically so it would be mechanically decidable and would settle the hard case (docs/design/ is in exclude_docs, so it stays forbidden by the same rule that permits docs/core/hicasso/). IT FAILS ON A DIFFERENT HARD CASE I DID NOT CONSIDER: mkdocs_hooks.py on_pre_build STAGES ROOT spec/ INTO docs_dir, so the built site DOES serve spec/ — and a rule worded that way would have PERMITTED the one tree the fence most needs to forbid. The worker scoped the rule to the CHECKOUT docs/ tree instead, which closes it without a second sentence.

I find that instructive against myself: the staging hook is the exact mechanism I have been correcting other people about all session, after being measured wrong on it twice, and I still wrote a rule that the hook silently inverts. A mechanically-decidable rule is only as good as the mechanism you checked it against, and I checked mine against exclude_docs and not against the hook.

VERIFICATION I AM SATISFIED WITH: exclude_docs read at source (six entries) AND confirmed by RUNNING the build — site/design does not exist, site/core/hicasso/ has exactly 29 pages. That is the difference between reading a config and observing its effect.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9049 — reopened the exact owner for one missed carrier. The four edited pages correctly make the checkout copy of the published docs reachable, but docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md:30 remains untouched and still states categorically that the checkout is only a build input, that a pilot may not read it for answers, and that the permitted boundary is dependency/tool execution. That directly contradicts the new workspace/brief rule allowing the published pages under docs/ that the site builds. Minimal completion: amend this one governing-package paragraph to name the documentation exception in the same terms; do not widen the fence or reopen the settled manifest/outcome-7 work. No duplicate issue.
close_reason: FIXED in PR #9058, the one missed carrier the #9049 audit reopened this for. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md:30 now names the documentation exception in the four already-edited pages' own terms rather than a fifth phrasing: 'build input, not a reference work - with one exception' and 'an exception about where the documentation is kept, not about what may be studied' from workspace.md:39; 'anything under docs/ the site builds, which is where docs/core/hicasso/'s 29 pages live' from the read-fence table row at workspace.md:43; 'Reading them is not reading the checkout' from inside both briefs' fences; 'there is no published site yet' from friction-log.md's template header. The paragraph's second half -- the prohibition list (implementation/, spec/, docs/design/, other examples, tracker, history) and the executing-versus-browsing line -- is carried over verbatim, so the fence is not widened. The manifest and outcome 7 were not reopened. Heading text unchanged, since the audit cites headings as anchors. Verified by a planted broken link on this exact line that took check_doc_slugs.py red and was then restored and confirmed by git blob hash.

title: pilots workspace.md: the source manifest omits examples/_shared/, so both pilot workspaces 404 their stylesheet and favicon
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, executing docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md step 2 literally. Tip d1e6a707a3.

WHAT HAPPENS. Both apps' index.html (copied in by the manifest, unmodified except the script tag the page tells you to change) link three assets under a sibling _shared/ directory:

  <link rel="stylesheet" href="_shared/css/style.css">
  <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="_shared/img/favicon.svg">
  <meta property="og:image" content="_shared/img/og.png">

workspace.md's per-pilot manifest copies neither the directory nor any of those files. Measured against a workspace built exactly per the page, served from app/public:

  index.html                 200
  js/main.js                 200
  default-avatar.svg         200
  _shared/css/style.css      404
  _shared/img/favicon.svg    404

Confirmed a second time through headless Chrome: two failed requests, and body computed style falls back to "Times New Roman" on a transparent background. With the stylesheet present (the in-repo control) the same page computes Inter / rgb(247,243,236).

WHERE THE FILES ARE. examples/_shared/css/style.css (274 lines), examples/_shared/img/favicon.svg, examples/_shared/img/og.png — at the root of the examples tree, one level above each app's own directory, which is why a manifest written per-app misses them. The repo serves them through its dev-http root cascade rather than by copying, so the omission is invisible in-repo.

WHY IT MATTERS. RealWorld/Conduit is a CSS-heavy Medium clone and the shared sheet carries the 'Editorial Warm' visual identity the examples are designed against (implementation/shadow-cljs.edn cites it at the :examples/notebook and :examples/dashboard-uix builds). A pilot judging outcome 2 — 'the same behaviour a user sees today' — and an operator running step 5's boot check both meet an unstyled page, and the natural reading is that the scaffolding is broken. workspace.md step 5 exists precisely so 'the friction log records the operator's mistakes as the framework's' does not happen; this is that failure mode, in the page's own manifest.

THE PAGE ALREADY ASSUMES THE FILES ARE THERE. Its 'four project files' section says 'The copied index.html already carries each app's markup and stylesheet links. Change only the script tag' — so it knows about the stylesheet link and still never brings the stylesheet across.

FIX. Add to both manifests in workspace.md step 2, e.g.:

  cp -r re-frame2/examples/_shared app/public/_shared

Both pilots need it; the paths are identical for each.

SEPARATE FROM rf2-nvcp. That bead is the route-link boot failure, which reproduces with all _shared assets present and 0 failed requests. Fixing this one does not make either app boot.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9049 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9049). Both step-2 manifests in workspace.md now copy the directory (cp -r re-frame2/examples/_shared app/public/_shared) rather than the three named files. Proven by measurement on workspaces assembled exactly per the page and served over HTTP: all four shared assets 404 before and 200 after, for BOTH pilots. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE BEAD, both verified at tip. (1) There is a FOURTH, transitive asset the bead does not name: style.css line 14 is @import url('structure.css'), a further 256 lines owning reusable geometry and the inline-Xray layout — so a three-file manifest would still have served a partly unstyled page, which is why the fix copies the directory. (2) The dev-http root cascade claim is REFUTED: the repo stages _shared/ by RECURSIVE COPY, not by serving it from where it lives — examples/scripts/examples-staging.cjs stageShared() calls copyDirRecursive(SHARED_SRC, outDir/_shared), invoked from serve-example.cjs and serve-and-run-adapter-smokes.cjs; examples/README.md says so and warns a bare 'shadow-cljs watch' copies no _shared assets; and LinearLite's dev-http entry (port 8044) cascades only the app source dir and out/examples/linearlite, neither of which contains _shared/. The defect and its invisibility in-repo are real; only the stated mechanism was wrong.

title: tools/xray(local_render): exposed singleton keeps dead-frame sentinel registrable
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-g1vu worker (cluster code-a) while censusing the sentinel defect class. OUT OF THAT WORKER FENCE (tools/xray/**), so filed rather than fixed.

THE DEFECT, third instance of the class. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc:106 defines

  (def ^:private dead-frame-sentinel "..." ::no-egress-frame)

which expands to the ORDINARY PUBLIC KEYWORD :day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.local-render/no-egress-frame, and local-render-opts (:175) stamps it as the :frame opt whenever the named frame is nil / unreachable:

  :frame (if reachable? frame-id dead-frame-sentinel)

Its docstring carries the SAME false claim the other two carriers did: "The keyword is namespaced into this panel so it can never collide with a real frame id." make-frame validates no :id type and the frame registry is keyed by whatever id it is handed, so an app CAN register a live frame under that literal. The stamp then RESOLVES, rf/elide-wire-value takes its live-frame branch, and the value egresses under that frame empty declaration registry — the fail-CLOSED stamp becomes a fail-OPEN one. Note local-render also passes :rf.size/include-large? true and, under the :rf.egress/local-raw profile, include-sensitive?, so the blast radius differs from the off-box carriers; the leak arm is the local-redacted default.

THE CLASS, now three carriers, each found only after the previous fix scope was drawn too tight:
1. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs — ::no-frame. FIXED by rf2-7htk7 third pass, PR #8987 commit 449bfd21c7 (private identity value (js/Object.)), with a collision regression at tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs:559.
2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc — ::no-egress-frame. FIXED under rf2-g1vu on branch worker/code-a: #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) plus the collision regression g-graph-egress-nil-frame-fails-closed-under-sentinel-id-collision in implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc. The premise was REPRODUCED first: with a live frame under the literal id, project-graph with a nil frame-id egressed {:cart {:items "tenant-jwt-9f3a-SECRET"}} raw instead of :rf/redacted (captured exit 1, two failing assertions).
3. THIS BEAD — tools/xray/.../panels/local_render.cljc:106/123/175. NOT fixed.

CENSUS INSTRUMENT, so the next pass does not have to re-derive it: git grep -n "dead-frame-sentinel" over *.clj/*.cljc/*.cljs finds every carrier by its shared var name (control-checked: it returns 2 hits in the already-known egress.cljc). The class is "a keyword literal used as an unregisterable-frame substitute stamped into a :frame opt". One NEAR-MISS was inspected and CLEARED: implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1145 passes ::no-frame to elide-against-frame, but only on the branch where the caller has explicitly waived sensitive redaction, and a colliding registry there supplies :large declarations that cause MORE elision, not less — it fails closed, so it is not this defect.

FIX SHAPE, settled by precedent, no design needed: make dead-frame-sentinel a fresh host object (the file is .cljc, so #?(:clj (Object.) :cljs (js/Object.)) as in the core fix), correct the docstring sentence that claims a namespaced keyword cannot collide, and ADD A COLLISION REGRESSION — register a live frame under the literal id, leave the target unselected, assert :rf/redacted. The regression is the point: this class has now been found three times precisely because the first two fixes shipped without one covering the sibling.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9044 — REOPENED. The object replacement does not satisfy the claimed "NO frame can be registered under it" invariant because the public `local-render-opts` function returns the singleton itself in `:frame` for every nil or unreachable target. A caller need not manufacture an equal object; it receives the identical value.

Reproduced at merged commit 7369668070 on the JVM lane without editing source: take `(:frame (local-render-opts nil))`, pass that exact value to `rf/make-frame` as `:id`, then call `local-render-value` with a nil observed frame. Result: `{:same-sentinel? true, :registered? true, :rendered {:auth {:token "secret-session-jwt-abc123"}}}`. The value ships raw, so the fail-CLOSED branch is still fail-OPEN.

The added regression misses this because it registers only the retired keyword and structurally asserts merely that the replacement is not a keyword. Minimal repair: generate a fresh opaque identity for each unreachable projection (or otherwise keep the identity from being reusable across calls), then add the discriminating control: extract and register one call's `:frame`, make a subsequent `local-render-value` call, and prove it uses a distinct unreachable identity and redacts the whole value. Preserve the existing explicit `local-raw` opt-out; no profile redesign is needed.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — I CHECKED WHETHER THE SIBLING CARRIERS HAVE THE SAME ESCAPE, AND THE ANSWER IS THE USEFUL PART OF THIS NOTE.

title: conformance EDN gate accepts mismatched delimiter types because it tracks only aggregate depth
description:
DISCOVERED while fixing rf2-5mr6 (PR: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn had one extra closing brace).

GAP. No gate in the tree checks that a conformance fixture is a well-formed EDN file containing exactly ONE top-level form. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string over the whole file, which returns the FIRST form and IGNORES everything after it. A fixture whose expectation block is closed early therefore loads, runs, and reports as PASSING while the assertions that fell outside the block are silently discarded. That is exactly what rf2-5mr6 was: bracket depth -1, two trace assertions never executed, green for however long it had been there (introducing commit not bisected).

WHY IT WAS NOT ADDED IN THAT PR. No script under scripts/ or .github/ iterates spec/conformance/fixtures/ at all — check_retired_spellings.py and report-changed-surfaces.sh only NAME the directory. So the check has no existing home; it is a new script plus its own CI wiring plus a fast-PR spine entry, which is a bigger call than the one-character fix it would have guarded.

TWO SHAPES, AND THE SECOND IS THE SHARPER ONE.

(a) A corpus scanner. Python, stdlib only, in the shape of the repo's other spec-coherence gates. The scanner used to measure rf2-5mr6 works and is the algorithm to lift: walk the text, blank ;; comments to end of line, treat a double-quoted string as opaque (honouring backslash escapes), treat a backslash as introducing a one-character char literal, then count ([{ against )]}. Report a defect when final depth is not 0, when min depth ever goes negative, or when the file holds other than exactly one top-level form. Measured 2026-09-03: 247 fixtures scanned, 0 defects after the fix; the pre-fix routing-not-found.edn reports final-depth=-1 top-level-forms=1 neg-at-line=60. Exercised in BOTH directions before either result was believed.

(b) Make the LOADERS refuse trailing text. This is the better fix because it cannot drift from what the runner actually parses, and it is a few lines in each of the two host-specific loaders: implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj (load-fixture-from-file) and the JVM leaf's slurp + read-string in implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj. Read with a PushbackReader and assert EOF after the first form, or read (str "[" content "]") and assert exactly one element. A fixture with trailing text then fails LOUD at load, in the same run that would otherwise pass it, on every host that loads the corpus. The CLJS leaf inlines fixtures at compile time, so it needs the equivalent at its macro seam.

Prefer (b), or (b) plus (a) — (a) also catches a fixture that never reaches a loader because its capabilities are unclaimed, which (b) cannot see. A fixture whose capabilities are out of claim is SKIPPED by the runner, so a defect in one is invisible to (b) forever.

ACCEPTANCE. A fixture with a deliberately misplaced brace fails a gate that runs on every PR touching spec/conformance/. Prove it by planting one and showing the red, not by showing the green on a clean corpus — a search that returns zero is not a check that passed.
notes:
AUDIT OF PR #9038 (three-lens review).

CORRECTNESS. The scanner records only one aggregate depth for all three delimiter kinds, so mismatched pairs can cancel out. Measured at merge commit 46387ffee9: scan_edn("{:a [1 2)}") returns ok=True, final-depth=0, min-depth=0, top-level-forms=1, and _defect_reason returns None, even though this is not valid EDN. The unconditional gate therefore gives a false green against its stated invariant that every fixture is one well-formed EDN form.

COMPLETENESS. The self-test exercises extra, missing, and trailing delimiters, but no mismatched pair, so it cannot discriminate this failure mode. The package-reference half of the PR is complete against rf2-kgw8z: it scopes by resolved location and covers unshipped, shipped, marked, and genuinely external parent links.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / MINIMAL FIX. Keep the stdlib-only lexical design; replace aggregate-only closing with a tiny opener stack and require each closer to match the top opener. Add one compact regression such as {:a [1 2)}. No general EDN parser or broader semantic validation is needed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9046 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9046). The audit's finding reproduced exactly at base 1b64fd6396: scan_edn('{:a [1 2)}') returned ok=True, final-depth=0 min-depth=0 top-level-forms=1, _defect_reason None. scan_edn now keeps an opener stack of (char, line) and requires each closer to match the delimiter it closes; still stdlib-only and lexical, no EDN parser. Self-test gained two regressions whose aggregate numbers are IDENTICAL to a clean file's (final-depth=0 min-depth=0 top-level-forms=1), so only an opener stack discriminates them, and both assert the REASON not just a defect count: 12/12 exit 0, and exit 1 with 4 named failures when the mismatch rule is disabled. Proved on live data rather than on a clean corpus: a cancelling mismatch planted in spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn gives the pre-fix scanner exit 0 (the false green) and this one exit 1 naming file, closer, opener and line. Plant restored, verified by git hash-object blob equality 7200be9e6536eb9a61dc79c34990ee08d1f28478. Corpus counts unchanged either side of the change: 247 fixtures, 0 defects, exit 0. Two notes: the gate is confirmed unconditional AND enforced (continue-on-error steps are aggregated by test.yml's 'Report every failing invariant check', which exits 1 on any outcome=='failure'), and this bead's recorded top-level-forms=1 for the pre-fix fixture measures as 2 with the committed scanner (final-depth=-1 and neg-at-line=60 match exactly; the verdict is driven by the negative depth, so nothing turns on it).

title: CLAUDE.md Build&Test states a false gate model: mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/ (docs.yml stages it into docs/), and it catches link-resolution failures check_doc_slugs passes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by the specdrift-a worker (PR #9019) and confirmed by the mayor at source in mkdocs.yml.

WHAT CLAUDE.md SAYS, under Build & Test: that mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs is the authority on what the build cannot see from WITHIN docs_dir, and that 'docs_dir is docs, so anything outside it -- implementation/**, examples/**, tools/**, .github/**, repo-root markdown -- was never a candidate for exclusion and will never appear in that block.' A reader takes from this that spec/ is outside the strict build's reach.

WHAT IS TRUE AT TIP: the docs.yml CI step COPIES spec/ into docs/spec/, so the spec tree is STAGED INTO docs_dir and the strict build does see it. docs_dir: docs is true but not dispositive.

THE MEASUREMENT, on one tree, which is the part that makes this a defect rather than a wording quibble: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0 ('no broken links') while mkdocs build --strict exit 1 on the SAME tree, naming spec/conformance/README.md's link to ../../docs/EP/EP-0012-....md as unresolvable. The link is CORRECT repo-relative -- which is what the slug gate validates and what GitHub browsing needs -- and wrong site-relative, because from staged docs/spec/conformance/ it resolves to docs/docs/EP/. mkdocs_hooks.py rewrites ../../spec/ -> ../spec/ for exactly this class but has NO ../../docs/ rule, so a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path at all.

THE TWO GATES ARE COMPLEMENTARY, NOT REDUNDANT, and CLAUDE.md should say so: check_doc_slugs.py validates ANCHORS (which strict grades at INFO and therefore never fails on) and repo-relative targets; mkdocs --strict validates LINK RESOLUTION INSIDE THE BUILT SITE, which the slug gate cannot see. Each is blind to the other's subject.

WHY IT MATTERS: the mayor nominated gates from this model in roughly a dozen briefs this session, telling workers editing spec/ that the strict build was not their gate. Nobody was harmed -- the doc gates ran in CI regardless -- but the nomination was wrong, and a worker acting on it would hand-verify what a gate already proved or trust a green that inspected nothing.

FIX SHAPE. Correct the Build & Test paragraph so it states: (1) docs.yml stages spec/ into docs/, so the strict build covers spec/ despite docs_dir being docs; (2) the two gates check different things -- anchors and repo-relative targets vs site-relative link resolution -- and neither substitutes for the other; (3) a page under spec/ cannot reach docs/ by a relative path, because mkdocs_hooks.py has no ../../docs/ rewrite rule. Keep the existing true parts: exclude_docs, the fence blindness both gates share, and the check_readme_links roster split.

DO NOT edit CLAUDE.md from the mayor checkout -- the commit guard refuses it. Dispatch to a worker in its own worktree.

PREMISES ARE CLAIMS: re-read mkdocs.yml, docs.yml and mkdocs_hooks.py at tip before writing, and reproduce the two-gate pairing rather than quoting this bead.
notes:
MAYOR ADDENDUM, 2026-09-03 00:5x AUSEST — A SECOND HALF OF THE GATE MODEL, MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY BY TWO WORKERS AFTER THIS BEAD WAS FILED, AND THE BEAD IS INCOMPLETE WITHOUT IT.

This bead currently says 'mkdocs --strict DOES cover spec/'. True of CI, and MISLEADING AS A LOCAL GATE INSTRUCTION — which is exactly how a worker will read it, because a gate nomination is a thing you run. A BARE LOCAL 'mkdocs build --strict' DOES NOT COVER spec/ AT ALL. The coverage comes entirely from docs.yml's staging step copying spec/ into docs/spec/ BEFORE the build; run the build without replicating that staging and it inspects none of your spec/ edits and exits 0, which is a green that proves nothing.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, BY WORKERS WHO DID NOT SHARE A CONTEXT. corpus-b (PR #9026) reported it in those words and replicated the staging so its strict run genuinely covered both edited paths. specdrift-b (PR #9025) reported 'mkdocs build --strict 0, AFTER staging spec/ -> docs/spec as docs.yml does — it built spec/View-Hierarchy-Capture.md'. Two workers, two trees, same finding, neither prompted for it.

SO THE CORRECTED PARAGRAPH NEEDS A FOURTH POINT alongside the three in FIX SHAPE: (4) the strict build reaches spec/ only through docs.yml's staging step, so CI covers it and a bare local run does not — a local run must replicate the staging (copy spec/ into docs/spec/, and migration/ into docs/migration/) or be cited as CI rather than as a local pass. Say it in the same breath as (1), because (1) alone is the sentence that misleads.

THIS ALSO CORRECTS MY OWN BRIEFS AGAIN, in the opposite direction from the first correction. I spent a dozen briefs telling workers the strict build was not their gate for spec/. Then I spent several telling them it was — without the staging caveat. The second error is smaller than the first but it is the same class: a gate nomination stated without the condition that makes it true.

The TEST at :375 is the hard one: pinning the exact wire string is legitimate contract-testing, and whether that assertion moves inside the package, or reads the constant from protocol.cjs rather than restating it, is the real design question.

title: spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn has one extra closing brace — its :trace-emissions assertions are silently discarded
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 22:53 AUSEST by worker/specdrift-a while building the mechanical top-level-key census for rf2-7yth0.

DEFECT. spec/conformance/fixtures/routing-not-found.edn line 46 reads

    :error  nil}}}}

and needs THREE closing braces, not four. The fourth closes :fixture/expect's own map, which pushes :trace-emissions (line 48) and its two-event vector OUT of :fixture/expect and, with the file's final }, past the end of the top-level fixture map entirely. Final bracket depth is -1.

EVIDENCE. A bracket-depth scan of all 247 fixtures (comments blanked, strings and char literals collapsed to one opaque token, # before an opening delimiter treated as a dispatch prefix) returns final depth 0 for 246 files and -1 for this one — the only outlier in the corpus. Independently, the same scan reports :trace-emissions as a DEPTH-1 (top-level) key in this file alone; in the other 120 fixtures that carry it, it sits inside :fixture/expect where spec/conformance/README.md line 63 and spec/Spec-Schemas.md line 4597 both document it.

IMPACT — SILENT, NOT LOUD. Both loaders use clojure.edn/read-string on the whole file (implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj load-fixture-from-file, and the JVM runner's slurp + read-string). read-string returns the FIRST form and ignores trailing text, so the fixture loads with a :fixture/expect carrying only :final-app-db and :final-runtime-db. The two trace assertions — the :rf.error/no-such-handler emission with :kind :route that is the whole point of the fixture, and the not-found route's :on-match :rf.event/run-start — are DISCARDED. Nothing errors; the fixture reports as passing while verifying less than it claims. This is the exact failure mode rf2-7yth0 exists to prevent, found by rf2-7yth0's own instrument.

FIX. Delete one } from line 46. One character.

DO NOT LAND IT BLIND. The two assertions have never executed, so enabling them may red the conformance runner. Whoever takes this runs the JVM conformance corpus (implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj) and the CLJS corpus runner before and after, and reports both. If the assertions fail, the fixture's expectations — not the brace fix — are what needs correcting.

NO GATE COVERS THIS. The corpus has no EDN well-formedness or schema check: an unbalanced fixture is indistinguishable from a well-formed one to every gate in the tree, because read-string accepts it. Worth considering a corpus parse/balance check as a follow-on; filed separately if wanted.

title: bug(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render accepts recovered render errors
description:
## Finding

PR #8997 measured that Hicasso's pure compute-sub SSR reads emit recovered subscription failures with `:frame nil`, so the per-frame SSR error accumulator cannot see them. Its new `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` correctly watches the always-on error stream for the synchronous render extent and refuses the page. The sibling whole-page `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` remains unchanged: it renders markup and assembles the payload/document without the same verdict. A registered sub can therefore throw, recover to `nil`, and still produce a successful but wrong SSR page.

## Recommended action

Apply the same bounded recovered-error verdict to `render`, sharing the smallest lifecycle helper with `render-body` if that keeps the two doors aligned. Preserve the settled public spellings and response shape; this is one missing correctness check, not a renderer redesign.

## Evidence

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: `render-body` registers the `:errors` listener and refuses `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`; `render` has no corresponding check.
- `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_body_ssr_cljs_test.cljs` proves an ordinary throwing sub otherwise recovers and returns markup.
- The rf2-8arzr.5 implementation note explicitly records the standing implication that whole-page `server/render` has the same blindness.
- Duplicate searches for `whole-page Hicasso recovered render error`, `server/render blindness`, `pending-error-trace Hicasso`, `compute-sub-driven SSR`, and `ssr-render-failed` found no owner.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused test renders an ordinary registered sub that throws through `server/render` and gets `:rf.error/ssr-render-failed`, while a non-throwing control returns the existing map/document shape unchanged.
- The error listener and request frame are released on success, recovered-error refusal, and a direct render throw.
- `render-body` retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions or residue.
notes:
AUDIT REOPEN — PR #9035.

The recovered-error fix uses one fixed listener id per door, so it closes cross-door replacement but not same-door replacement. server.cljs explicitly acknowledges the remaining hole in render-body-listener-id's docstring: a door re-entering itself reuses its id, registration REPLACES the outer listener, and the inner finally unregisters it. The same mechanics apply to render-listener-id.

Concrete failure sequence: an outer render arms its atom; a view enters the same door; the inner registration replaces the outer callback; the inner finally removes that id; the outer view catches/continues, then a later subscription error recovers to nil. No listener remains to record it, so the outer render returns the same successful wrong page this bead owns. React rejecting a nested render does not make this safe: the inner finally still removes the outer listener when the view catches that direct throw.

The new test section 4 observes each door separately and proves only that their two fixed ids differ. It never nests render inside render or render-body inside render-body, so the acceptance requirement that the sibling retain refusal semantics without listener collisions is not fully met.

Minimal repair: make the registration key unique per invocation (for example, pair the door tag with the already-unique request frame id) and unregister that exact key. Add a focused same-door re-entry control that catches the inner call, emits a recovered render error afterward, and proves the outer call still fails with :rf.error/ssr-render-failed and restores the listener registry baseline. Exercise both doors compactly if the shared helper makes that cheap; do not redesign the renderer.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-09-03 (mayor) — FENCE CLEARED; THIS IS DISPATCHABLE AND IT IS P2.

Found by the done-in-tree sweep: commit 51f6641b10 "fix(hicasso-ssr): whole-page server/render now refuses a recovered render error (rf2-ypom, rf2-ct24)" cites this bead, 204 insertions / 129 deletions in implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs. A hit is a pointer, so I confirmed in source before concluding anything: the verdict IS there — render-listener-id at :149, refuse-recovered-render-error! at :175, watch-recovered-errors! at :238, and both doors call it (render at :340/:360, render-body at :465/:481). rf2-ct24 is closed.

SO THE BEAD IS CORRECTLY STILL OPEN, and the reason is the audit remainder already on it rather than an unclosed close: the two doors use FIXED per-door listener ids, so a same-door re-entrant call (render inside render) still lets the inner finally unregister the outer listener. The acceptance criterion "render-body retains the same refusal semantics without listener collisions" is therefore not met. The repair is already specified on this bead — key the registration per invocation (pair the door tag with the request frame id, which is already unique) and unregister that exact key, plus a focused same-door re-entry control.

WHAT CHANGED THIS TICK: PR #9035 merged, so implementation/hicasso/ is no longer held by a live worker. This was fenced behind that tree; the fence is gone. Nothing else blocks it.

CLASSIFYING per loops.md section 3: NEEDS-WORK-UNDER-A-DECISION-ALREADY-MADE. There is nothing for Mike or me to rule — the mechanism, the repair and the control are all written down. It goes to the next merge+dispatch tick with a free slot.

ONE THING FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT, from the commit message rather than the bead: the fix deliberately did NOT give render a :platform :server, because that would change fx gating for every existing caller. Do not "complete" it by adding one. The per-invocation key is the whole task.
close_reason:
PR #9045. The audit remainder is fixed: the registration key is now per INVOCATION, not per door — the door tag paired with the request frame id, which is already a unique gensym — and each finally unregisters that exact key. Nesting now accumulates windows instead of replacing them. render-body-listener-id's own docstring had admitted the hole ('A door re-entering ITSELF still reuses one id, where re-registering REPLACES and the outer render loses a listener').

NO :platform :server WAS ADDED to render — the #9035 author's scoped decision, flagged on this bead, is left alone.

CONTROL PROVED TO BITE against the pre-fix fixed-key form (listener-key returning [tag], keeping the vector shape so only re-entrancy changes): ONLY the new same-door re-entry row fails, and it fails by the outer render RETURNING A DOCUMENT — 'expected: (instance? ExceptionInfo thrown) / actual: cljs.core/PersistentArrayMap', which is the silent wrong page itself. Every other row stayed green, the existing section-4 two-door rows included, so the defect is isolated precisely to same-door re-entrancy. Fixed: 1177 tests/4393 assertions, 0 failures, captured exit 0. Restored, verified by git blob hash b6364c6f66025a7958057ac119ab4057f9d20c77.

TWO MEASURED FINDINGS THE BEAD DID NOT HAVE, both now recorded beside the test because each yields a GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON. (1) A VIEW cannot be the re-entry site: a nested render tears down the OUTER render's collector extent, so the next h/sub raises :rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render from impl.collector/read-key! before any recovered error can be emitted — the outer render then fails for an unrelated reason and the row passes against the broken form. The re-entry is driven from a BOOT EVENT instead, which reaches the same window without touching the collector. (2) A THROWING boot event is not a recovered error: rf/make-frame raises :rf.error/initial-events-step-failed and takes the render down before the verdict; the recovered emission is a second boot event dispatching a deliberately unregistered id (:rf.error/no-such-handler, a promoted recovered category).

A third trap caught itself and is worth the next author's attention: the handler was first written BELOW use-fixtures, where the reset fixture erases it. The dispatch silently became no-such-handler, the outer render still refused, and every assertion but the precondition passed — a green measuring no re-entrancy at all. The precondition caught it; the registration now sits above the fixture with a note.

title: api-manifest roster gate can be orphaned again because its tests bypass build-manifest
notes:
FOUND BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. The manifest gate is GREEN and still misses three public namespaces, because the gate only checks what its own hard-coded roster names.

MEASURED: `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` exits 0, "spec/api-manifest.edn in sync (494 public vars)". Note the manifest lives at spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn -- NOT implementation/api-manifest.edn, which is where rf2-8arzr.6 s own scope text and several briefs point. That path does not exist.

THE THREE NAMESPACES, all with genuinely public vars and ZERO ^:no-doc markers:
- re-frame.ssr.ring.node (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj) -- default-endpoint :128, default-timeout-ms :133, default-admission-ms :138, wire-margin-ms :145, validate-opts! :193, http-timeout-ms :230, renderer :360.
- re-frame.ssr.render-state (implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/render_state.cljc) -- validate-policy-opts! :175, project :333, serialize :365, deserialize :383, restore! :400.
- re-frame.hicasso.server (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs) -- payload-script :89, document :106, render :145, render-body :331.
grep for ssr\.ring\.node / render-state / hicasso\.server / render-body across BOTH manifest files returns zero hits each.

ROOT CAUSE: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:88-119 defines `jvm-namespaces` as a literal list. It names re-frame.ssr (:103) and re-frame.ssr.ring (:104) but not re-frame.ssr.ring.node and not re-frame.ssr.render-state. `all-jvm-vars` (:202-213) iterates that literal list plus `extra-vars` (:121-130, two entries). re-frame.hicasso.server is CLJS-only and would need a :cljs-only sidecar row in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (:63); the roster there holds only the 16 day8.re-frame2-xray.* namespaces, re-frame.adapter.reagent, re-frame.adapter.uix, re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso.

THE BACKSTOP IS DEAD, AND ITS OWN DOCSTRING SAYS WHY THAT MATTERS. gen.clj:141-162 defines `namespaces-under`, documented as "a completeness gate that quietly finds nothing is the defect it exists to prevent". A repo-wide grep for `namespaces-under` across .clj/.cljc/.cljs returns exactly ONE hit: its own definition at gen.clj:141. It is never called. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/ is empty. So a new public namespace joins the tree and nothing notices -- which is exactly what happened three times over across slices A, C and E.

WHY SLICE F DID NOT FIX IT: F was fenced to docs and manifests with an explicit "nothing under implementation/*/src/, this is not a code slice" instruction. Fixing this needs (a) a gen.clj roster change, (b) tier/owner/status classification judgement for ~16 vars, (c) a :cljs-only block for re-frame.hicasso.server, and (d) wiring namespaces-under so it cannot regress. That is a code slice with real judgement in it, and it touches a REQUIRED CI check (lint.yml job `api-manifest`, declared :592, aggregated at :786).

ALSO NOTE, for whoever takes this: spec/API.md CANNOT gain var-rows for these symbols until the manifest carries them. api_md_check.clj validates that every var-row in spec/API.md resolves to a manifest entry, so adding a row first would RED the required check. Slice F therefore recorded the three namespaces as PROSE in spec/API.md s SSR namespace note and said they are not yet manifested, citing this bead. When this lands, promote that prose to rows if the tiering warrants it.

TIERING HINT (not a ruling): all nine re-frame.ssr.ring vars are :implementation tier (spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1418-1426), and docs/api/ coverage is only gated for :front-porch / :advanced / :adapter / :testing tiers (doc_api_check.clj `check-coverage!`), so classifying these as :implementation would add no docs/api obligation.
RESOLVED BY PR #9040, 2026-09-03. The premise held and the cause was more specific than 'nobody wired it'.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE: git grep -F namespaces-under over .clj/.cljc/.cljs returns exactly ONE hit, its own definition at gen.clj:141. Controlled against all-jvm-vars — a same-shaped hyphenated symbol in the same file — which returns three hits including two call sites, so the instrument works and the one-hit result is real.

ROOT CAUSE, which the bead did not have: the gate is not new. rf2-o8xev (c504e47d11) built exactly this three-way reconciliation over implementation/freehand/src, asserted FIRST in build-manifest, with a 201-line test. The freehand retirement (rf2-0yp7w.6, c951808b47) deleted the tree and — correctly, since the gate refuses to build when a source namespace is named by neither roster — retired the rosters, the assertion AND its call site together; its own commit message says they 'retire together'. What survived was namespaces-under and source-file->ns-sym: two pure helpers with no caller. THE GATE WAS ORPHANED, NOT FORGOTTEN, which is worse, because an orphan reads like a live backstop to anyone grepping for one.

WIRED, data-driven rather than hardcoded to one tree: roster-covered-roots names the trees; a namespace is accounted for by one of THREE rosters (jvm-namespaces, a sidecar :cljs-only row, or internal-namespaces); roster-drift reports :unaccounted/:stale/:contradictory; assert-roster-complete! throws naming the namespace and both remediation paths; build-manifest calls it FIRST. Enrolment intersects jvm-namespaces with what is on disk rather than filtering by prefix — the two SSR trees share the re-frame.ssr prefix across different artefacts, so a prefix filter would mis-assign both.

ENROLLED: re-frame.ssr.render-state (5 public vars) and re-frame.ssr.ring.node (7), exactly the vars and line numbers this bead names, verified at tip. Both :tier :implementation :owner 011 :status v1 — the tiering spec/API.md:328 already states. The tiering hint was VERIFIED rather than trusted: doc_api_check.clj:148 gates docs coverage on #{:front-porch :advanced :adapter :testing}, so :implementation adds no docs/api obligation. Manifest 494 -> 506.

33 SSR namespaces recorded internal; all 37 across the two trees now classified. NO ^:no-doc was added anywhere — those trees contain zero no-doc markers of any kind, before or after.

DELIBERATE RED: before, exit 0 'in sync (494 public vars)'. Planted a new public namespace re-frame.ssr.roster-probe under a covered root: exit 2, failing BY NAME with both remediation paths. Restored, verified by git blob hash 59dd06f93953ed0306ac35bfb75e7b585481a029 equal to the committed object. 14 tests pin all three drift directions, the throw, the failure MESSAGE (it must name both remediation paths, so the reader is not sent to the nearest silencer) and the LIVE trees — the last is what fails if the gate is ever orphaned again. Suite 74 -> 88 tests.

TWO OF THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISES DID NOT HOLD, corrected here: (1) 'implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/ is empty' — it is not, six tracked test files including gen_test.clj; the new one is a seventh. (2) The spec/api-manifest.edn path correction the bead makes IS right; implementation/api-manifest.edn indeed does not exist.

NOT DONE, and each has a bead: re-frame.hicasso.server is still unscanned (rf2-3ne8) — implementation/hicasso/** was held by PR #9035 during this work, and it is CLJS-only so it needs a :cljs-only row, not a jvm-namespaces entry; the gate's third arm is already built and tested for it. spec/API.md:328's 'not yet carried by the manifest' clause goes stale on merge (rf2-63fw, post-merge only). And 243 namespaces remain under trees the gate does not cover (rf2-qvhx) — measured 276 unenrolled in total, this PR covering 33.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9040 (three-lens review).

CORRECTNESS. The landed mechanism is currently wired correctly: build-manifest calls assert-roster-complete! first, both JVM crossing namespaces resolve and contribute the expected 5 + 7 rows, and the two documentation repairs describe the live code. No runtime defect was found in the reconciliation itself.

COMPLETENESS / REGRESSION GAP. The original defect was specifically an implemented namespaces-under helper whose production call had disappeared. The new 14-test roster_completeness_test.clj suite does not call build-manifest at all. Its live-rosters-account-for-the-live-trees test says it covers the assertion build-manifest makes, but invokes roster-drift directly. The only build-manifest calls anywhere under the test tree are pre-existing duplicate-row and implementation-facade tests in gen_test.clj; they exercise later failures and cannot observe removal of the roster assertion. Thus deleting gen.clj's single line 575 call recreates the orphan while the dedicated suite remains green. The author's planted-source demonstration proves the present call works, but it is not a durable regression test.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / MINIMAL FIX. Add one behavioral integration test that redefines covered-source-namespaces to include a synthetic unaccounted namespace, invokes build-manifest with the live sidecar, and requires the named roster exception. With the production call removed, that test must fail because manifest generation succeeds. This is one compact test; no new checker or abstraction is needed.
close_reason:
PR #9045. The audit's finding held at source: build-manifest calls assert-roster-complete! first (gen.clj:575), but all 14 tests drove roster-drift/assert-roster-complete! DIRECTLY — live-rosters-account-for-the-live-trees claims to cover the build-manifest assertion while invoking roster-drift itself. The only build-manifest calls under test/ were gen_test.clj's duplicate-row and implementation-facade rows.

FIX: three tests driving the PRODUCTION entry point — the named refusal, its :unaccounted ex-data, and the ordering against the duplicate-row check (a sidecar broken both ways must surface the ROSTER refusal). Each redefines covered-source-namespaces to report one synthetic unaccounted namespace and requires build-manifest to throw. No new checker, no abstraction, as specified.

TWO-STATE PROOF: suite 88 tests/184 assertions -> 91/189, exit 0. With the line-575 call deleted, exactly the three new tests fail (captured exit 1) and THE PRE-EXISTING 88 STAY GREEN — the audit's claim measured rather than argued. Restored, verified by git blob hash 59dd06f93953ed0306ac35bfb75e7b585481a029 equal to the committed object.

title: adapters/reagent: linearlite_example_cljs_test is green only because a co-loaded sibling owns "/" (false green; 16/51 red in a single-app bundle)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by the rf2-ma8r diagnosis (PR #9000, closed no-change).

re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test passes in the consolidated :node-test
bundle for a reason unrelated to its own subject, and fails 16 of 51 assertions
across 7 of 10 tests the moment it runs in a bundle where the LinearLite app is
the only app.

MECHANISM. Its init! calls (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true})
BEFORE reinstating the :resource/:mutation registrar rows the shared fixture's
reset hook cleared. A :url-bound? frame performs a synchronous initial URL sync
at construction (frame/upsert-frame! post-create hook -> routing's
:routing/on-frame-registered! -> reconcile-url-listener!, syncing
history/current-url, which is "/" under Node). The example registers
:linearlite.app/board at "/" with :resources [{:resource :linearlite/board
:blocking? true}], so the route-entry resource plan runs INSIDE make-frame,
finds the registrar empty, and records :transition :error /
:rf.error/resource-route-plan on the slice. The suite's own navigate never
re-plans, so the error is sticky and 16 assertions read nil.

WHY IT PASSES IN-REPO. At least seven in-tree apps register a route at "/"
(infinite_feed, linearlite, resources, routing, todomvc, realworld_http,
realworld_resources), plus many test suites. In the consolidated bundle "/"
resolves to a SIBLING's route, so LinearLite's board resource is never planned
at construction and the explicit navigate is a genuine transition with
everything registered. The suite's colour therefore depends on which siblings
happen to be co-loaded — it is not evidence about its own subject, and it would
flip red on an unrelated co-load change.

MEASURED. Workspace built per docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md
on the :local/root route: committed baseline exit 0 (10 tests / 51 assertions);
adapter suite verbatim exit 1, 16 failures; changing ONLY the example's route
path from "/" to "/board" -> exit 0, 0 failures.

FIX SHAPE (one line, but NOT dispatched here — the file is inside a live peer's
fence, worker/clientroot-k5r9t owns implementation/adapters/reagent/**):
reorder init! so the registrar/register! reinstatement loop runs BEFORE
(rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}), matching the committed
pilot baseline's ordering. That removes the masking dependence entirely.

RELATED. rf2-ma8r carries the full diagnosis and stays open for Mike's ruling
on the two framework questions this exposed: whether a :url-bound? frame
planning route resources at construction is correct, and whether a FAILED route
plan should ever be retried (today an app that recovers stays wedged in
:transition :error permanently).

WORTH A SWEEP: whether any OTHER in-repo example suite is green only by the
same co-load masking. The "/" census above is where to start; the cheap test
is to build each app's suite in a single-app bundle.
notes:
FENCE 2026-09-02 20:41:11 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2-ma8r worker. Its one-line repair (reinstate the registrar rows BEFORE the :url-bound? make-frame) sits in implementation/adapters/reagent/**, which worker/clientroot-k5r9t holds. Dispatch after that PR merges. NOTE WHAT THIS BEAD IS: not a flaky test but a FALSE GREEN — the suite passes in-repo only because a co-loaded sibling owns the "/" route, so its colour is not evidence about its own subject. The worker's residual question is worth carrying into the dispatch: no other in-repo example suite has been swept for the same co-load masking, and the cheap test is one single-app bundle per app.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-02 22:52:40 AUSEST (mayor): the 20:41 fence is DISCHARGED — worker/clientroot-k5r9t's PR #8992 MERGED at cd6fd08587 (53 files, the adapter client root plus the examples sweep), so implementation/adapters/reagent/** is held by nobody. Dispatched solo this tick.

RE-DERIVE BEFORE EDITING: #8992 changed this very adapter — it added public client-root / render! / unmount! on re-frame.adapter.reagent and reagent-slim, regenerated the api manifest 491->494, and rewrote 24 example entrypoints plus 3 SSR examples to mount through the adapter's client root. The example whose route path this bead discusses is among the files it touched. Every line number here predates it.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by PR #9027 (head 051f8976a7, base c06b76dc36).

REPRODUCED FIRST, on a tree that had moved past PR #8992. The bead's mechanism
held verbatim at tip: init! still created the :url-bound? frame before the
registrar/register! reinstatement loop. Built in a single-app :node-test bundle
(ns-regexp anchored to this suite alone), the committed tree gave
"Ran 10 tests containing 51 assertions. 16 failures, 0 errors.", captured
exit 1 — the bead's 16-of-51 across 7-of-10 exactly. After the fix, same bundle:
"Ran 10 tests containing 51 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.", captured exit 0.
That red-then-green pair is the control; it is also what proves the instrument
was reading the worker's own worktree.

WHICH REPAIR. The bead's FIX SHAPE section rules for reordering init! so the
registrar reinstatement runs BEFORE the :url-bound? make-frame, matching the
committed pilot baseline. That is what landed, and it is the right call: the
alternative one-liner the bead records under MEASURED — moving the example's
route off "/" — also goes green, but only by dodging the collision, leaving the
ordering bug intact and the suite still dependent on nobody else owning "/".
Followed the baseline's stricter form (make-frame LAST, after the fx stubs and
install-routing-integration! too, not merely after the doseq), since the baseline
is what the bead nominates and it documents the rule as "the frame is made last".
The ordering constraint and its cause are now in the init! docstring so a future
edit cannot silently undo it.

SECOND DEFECT, found by the sweep and fixed in the same PR.
re-frame.resources-example-cljs-test was green by the same disease through a
different organ: examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs calls
rf/reg-machine :resources.app/reader but required neither re-frame.machines nor
anything pulling it in. Machines are an optional artefact, so the call resolves
only when a co-loaded sibling has already loaded it. Alone, the example's ns-load
throws :rf.error/machines-artefact-missing before a single test runs (captured
exit 1, 0 tests). Every other example calling reg-machine already requires
re-frame.machines in the same file; this was the sole omission. After: 9 tests /
39 assertions, 0 failures.

CO-LOAD SWEEP — the bead's residual question, answered. Fifteen example suites
each built in their own single-app bundle: 155 tests / 1180 assertions, all green
on the final base. All SEVEN apps registering a route at "/" are covered
(infinite_feed, linearlite, realworld_http, realworld_resources, resources,
routing, todomvc). A census of every reg-route form under examples/
(paren-balanced over flattened text, control-checked first) shows LinearLite is
the ONLY app with a BLOCKING route resource at "/", which is exactly why it was
the only hard failure of that mechanism.

NOT COVERED, named rather than left open: the ~11,000-test framework remainder of
the :node-test lane was not swept for co-load masking among framework suites, and
re-frame.example-frame-scoping-cljs-test is excluded by construction (it loads
seven apps deliberately; cross-app scoping is its subject). Three suites share
the make-frame-before-register! ordering and are green only because their "/"
routes declare no blocking resource — infinite_feed_example,
realworld_resources, resources_example. Latent rather than broken; carried by
rf2-djqm rather than churned here.

METHOD NOTE for the next person building a single-app bundle. Narrowing
:ns-regexp against the shared :node-test id is what rf2-6t03c forbids doing
directly, so go through scripts/compile-node-test.cjs's cache-isolation helper
(core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache.cjs). But that script clears the build cache
AFTER compiling, and a dev-target :node-test bundle SHADOW_IMPORTs its modules
from that same directory at RUN time — so running the bundle after the script
exits dies with ENOENT on goog.debug.error.js before any test executes. The run
must happen inside the isolated window: clear -> compile -> RUN -> clear.
Runtime selection (node out/node-test.js --test=<ns>) does NOT substitute: it
filters which tests RUN while leaving every sibling namespace LOADED, which is
precisely the co-load this bead is about.

STILL OPEN AND NOT ADDRESSED HERE: rf2-ma8r's two framework questions — whether a
:url-bound? frame planning route resources AT CONSTRUCTION is correct, and
whether a FAILED route plan should ever be retried (an app that recovers stays
wedged in :transition :error permanently). This fix removes the masking; it does
not answer either question.
AUDIT PR #9027: REOPENED FOR COMPLETENESS. Both repairs are source-correct, and the isolated red/green probes are persuasive, but neither repair has a durable non-vacuous gate. This matters because the PR proves the ordinary consolidated :node-test bundle was green before both fixes: a sibling route masked LinearLite's make-frame ordering, and a sibling namespace loaded re-frame.machines for the resources example. The committed diff changes only those two subjects. The fifteen single-app builds were one-off audit evidence, not a checked-in regression instrument; test:cljs-isolation also runs selectors against the already consolidated bundle and therefore cannot remove ns-load co-loading. Moving make-frame back up or deleting the new machines require can consequently leave current CI green again.

Minimal completion: add one focused, durable bundle-isolation control covering the two fixed subjects. It must compile/load each subject without sibling example namespaces, go red on the pre-fix LinearLite ordering and missing machines require, and stay cheap enough for the existing example/adapter lane; do not institutionalise the full fifteen-build sweep. Keep the three merely latent fixture orderings on rf2-djqm and the route-retry ruling on rf2-ma8r.
AUDIT COMPLETION LANDED 2026-09-03 by PR #9066 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9066), branch worker/isolation-a, merge base 4893d007b6.

PREMISE VERIFIED FIRST, not taken from the audit. Reproduced the exact pre-#9027 tree
(the resources plant restores blob 5e0060754f, byte-identical to the 'index
5e0060754f..132a287c1e' the PR's own diff header records) and ran both subject suites in
the ordinary consolidated :node-test bundle. At tip: 'Ran 19 tests containing 90
assertions. 0 failures', captured exit 0. With BOTH pre-fix states restored: identical
numbers, captured exit 0. The audit's central claim holds.

THE AUDIT ASKED FOR ONE CONTROL; IT NEEDS TWO, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The two repairs
are different KINDS of fact and no single instrument reaches both. The LinearLite repair
is an ordering inside an adapter test fixture -- it never enters any app bundle, so no
bundle grep can see it and only executing it under the isolated condition can. The
resources repair is a missing :require in an example ns form -- invisible at runtime in
any bundle that carries re-frame.machines for another reason, which is precisely the
co-load being ruled out, so only a single-app build or the ns form itself can witness it.
Neither control builds a second bundle; together they cost milliseconds plus one
in-process test. The fifteen-build sweep is NOT institutionalised.

CONTROL A -- LinearLite ordering, behavioural, in the suite it protects
(implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs section
0). Reproduces IN PROCESS the two conditions a single-app bundle supplies: '/' owned by
this app's board route alone (every rival row sequestered through the provenance-safe
sequester/reinstate pairing the suite already uses for :rf.route/not-found, restored in a
finally), and the :resource/:mutation kinds cleared. Then runs the REAL init! against a
cleared frame registry so make-frame genuinely constructs and its post-create URL sync
really runs. Calling init! itself rather than a copy is the point: a refactor that puts
the frame back in front of the registrar reinstatement BY ANY ROUTE fails there. Chosen
over a source-order text check deliberately -- a text check on a moving target degrades
to a vacuous pass, which is the failure mode this gate's own positive-control section
exists to prevent. Its FIRST assertion is its own positive control: if the sequestering
silently stops working the URL sync lands on a sibling's route id and it fails loud.

CONTROL B -- the resources machines require, an ns-form co-load rule added to
implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs. Rule: an example that CALLS an
optional artefact's registration facade must :require that artefact in its OWN ns form,
because the :require -- not the Maven dep, and not a sibling's require -- is what fires
the load-time hook registrations. Read on SOURCE deliberately, and the code says why: the
roster comment's insist-on-the-emitted-artefact rule governs claims about a bundle's
CONTENTS, while this claim is about an ns FORM, whose only possible bundle witness is the
single-app build the audit ruled out on cost. Seven facade rows (reg-machine, defmachine,
reg-route, reg-resource, reg-mutation, reg-flow, reg-app-schema) over 83 example sources:
111 call sites, each backed by its own :require, zero violations at tip. NON-VACUITY IS
BUILT INTO THE CONTRACT rather than left to a one-off plant -- a facade row that finds no
call site anywhere, or an ns reader that stops seeing requires, fails the gate; both are
exercised as mutations in check-bundle-isolation.test.cjs, which the lane already runs
FIRST, so the rule is re-proven on every CI run rather than once by me.

TWO PLANTED REDS, one per subject, blob-hash-verified restores.
(1) make-frame moved back above the registrar/register! loop: 'expected (not= :error
(:transition slice)) / actual (not (not= :error :error))' and 'expected (nil?
(:rf.error/id (:error slice))) / actual (not (nil? :rf.error/resource-route-plan))' --
exactly the bead's mechanism -- 'Ran 11 tests containing 54 assertions. 2 failures',
captured exit 1, and THE OTHER TEN TESTS STAYED GREEN, which is the false green
demonstrated directly. The positive control passed on that same run, so the setup was
real. Restored: the init! region hashes 88481e756e38c8867d6a6e186668342571b5a9d4 on both
sides and the whole-file diff is 86 additions / 0 deletions.
(2) [re-frame.machines] deleted from examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs
(blob 5e0060754f): ok=false naming the file, the call, the artefact and
rf.error/machines-artefact-missing, hits=1 and no collateral. hits=1 rather than 2 is
itself evidence the comment stripper works, since that file names rf/reg-machine in a
comment two lines above the real call. Restored to blob 132a287c1e.
BOTH REDS RE-PROVEN ON THE FINAL BASE after the rebase, since the incoming commits
touched implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc, which control A exercises.

TWO THINGS THE BUILD ITSELF CAUGHT, recorded because each is the shape that fails open.
The new self-test caught a real defect in my own checker mid-build: a facade named inside
a STRING -- (def doc "call (rf/reg-flow ...)") -- counted as a call site. Fixed in the
checker (string bodies are now blanked, not just comments) rather than by relaxing the
fixture. And one plant SILENTLY NO-OPED: a perl -0pi patch left the blob hash unchanged
(CRLF) while reporting success, and the hash check caught it before a run was spent on a
green that would have read as 'the control does not bite'.

GATES, all foreground, unfiltered, exit codes captured, ALL RE-MEASURED ON THE FINAL BASE
4893d007b6: npm run test:bundle-isolation exit 0 (23 artefacts, 40 internal sentinels
absent / 40 positive-control present, 83 example sources co-load isolated, 111 facade
call sites); gate self-test exit 0 (40 sentinel mutations + 11 new co-load mutations);
reagent adapter suite 458 tests/2459 assertions BEFORE and 459/2462 AFTER, both exit 0,
delta exactly the one control; sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh exit 0 with the full CLJS suite
at 11206 tests / 55823 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors -- which is what proves the
control leaves no registrar or trace residue for the other ~11k tests in the bundle;
check_doc_slugs.py, check_readme_links.py --ci and all 15 check_skill_*.py exit 0.
node-test compiled 1893 files with 0 warnings on every run.

SCOPE HELD. The three merely-latent fixture orderings stay on rf2-djqm; the route-retry
ruling stays on rf2-ma8r. Neither widened. Nothing weakened or deleted to reach green.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9066 — REOPENED. The new example co-load gate misclassifies rf/defmachine as a registration facade. defmachine is the re-frame.core macro for defining and source-stamping a machine-spec value; it registers nothing. Confirmed against the shipped code by requiring re-frame.core alone and macroexpanding a defmachine form: re-frame.machines remained unloaded and the expansion head was plain def. Only the later reg-machine call needs the optional artefact and its load-time hook.

A valid split can therefore define a machine value in one namespace and require re-frame.machines only in the boot namespace that registers it. The new per-file checker rejects that shape and forces an unnecessary side-effecting require into the definition namespace. Its self-test misses the distinction because one fixture contains both defmachine and reg-machine and removes their shared require.

Minimal repair: remove defmachine from OPTIONAL_ARTEFACT_FACADES while retaining reg-machine, and make the self-test distinguish the contracts: a defmachine-only namespace requiring re-frame.core is valid; a reg-machine call without re-frame.machines still fails. No parser or runtime redesign is needed.
close_reason: Reopened state (the merged-PR audit of #9066) fixed by PR #9097, head f83a1f16c3. VERIFIED THE PREMISE AT SOURCE rather than taking the audit's word: the two expanders settle it directly — expand-reg-machine emits a real (re-frame.core-machines/reg-machine ...) call, which is what needs the artefact's load-time hooks, while expand-defmachine emits (def name <stamped-spec>) and nothing else, its own docstring reading '`def` is not a registration'. So defmachine was misclassified in OPTIONAL_ARTEFACT_FACADES and the gate demanded a [re-frame.machines] require from any namespace merely DEFINING a machine value, forbidding the valid split where the boot ns alone requires the artefact. REPRODUCED FIRST: a defmachine-only fixture against the committed checker returned ok=false naming defmachine/re-frame.machines; after the fix, no violation. NO EXAMPLE WAS AFFECTED — every current defmachine caller also calls reg-machine in the same file, so the defect was LATENT (it forbade a valid shape, it did not break a present one). Live corpus before->after: 83 example sources, 0 violations both ways; facade call sites 111->100, the difference being exactly the 11 defmachine call sites that were never the gate's business; 0 dead rows, 0 unproven artefacts. WHY THE SELF-TEST MISSED IT AND WHAT NOW STOPS IT: the single compliant fixture carried reg-machine and defmachine over ONE shared require, so the drop-one-require loop implicated both rows at once and the contracts were indistinguishable. They now get a namespace each — a defmachine-only ns must PASS, and a reg-machine call in that same ns must still FAIL naming reg-machine ALONE. Restoring the roster row fails the first BY NAME: planted it back, exit 1 on that exact assertion, then restored byte-exact (git hash-object 9478af0fb3 both sides, so the plant was real and not the silent CRLF no-op recorded on the previous PR). Both new fixtures assert on violations rather than ok, deliberately: ok also folds in the corpus-level non-vacuity guards, which a one-file fixture can never satisfy, so !ok in the negative case would have held whatever the rule did and passed for an unrelated reason — the self-test caught exactly that in my own first draft.
