title: skill(re-frame2-pair): stories.md teaches the run-variant loop with no adapter prerequisite — run-variant refuses with :rf.error/no-adapter-installed on a bare launch, and the pair skill OWNS the run side
description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md teaches the run-variant / read-failures self-healing loop and states no host prerequisite for it. Grepping that file at tip: no occurrence of 'no-adapter-installed', 'plain-atom/adapter', or any adapter/substrate prerequisite at all (the only 'substrate' hit is a snapshot-identity hash tuple).

This matters more here than in the authoring skill, because the pair skill is the OWNER of the run side. skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md explicitly hands off to it: 'switch to the re-frame2-pair skill (it owns run-variant / read-failures against a running app behind shadow-cljs watch) and run the self-healing loop there'.

TRUTH AT TIP

  - tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md, section 'Running a variant needs an installed adapter (rf2-c9t52)': catalogue reads work on a bare launch; RUNNING one does not. run-variant and preview-variant allocate a variant frame, and a frame takes its state substrate from an installed re-frame adapter. The server deliberately installs none — per spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md the substrate choice belongs to the app — so a consuming project installs one in the namespace its launch alias preloads ((rf/init! plain-atom/adapter), the renderer-free choice). With none installed both lifecycle tools REFUSE before any lifecycle work: isError true, :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, plus :tool and a :recovery naming the boot. They never return a :status.
  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc implements it as a pre-flight before story/run-variant allocates, returning {:rf.error :rf.error/no-adapter-installed :tool <tool> :recovery :init-an-adapter-in-the-preloaded-namespace}. Its docstring gives the reason: with no substrate the setup dispatches reach nothing and the script plays nothing, yet the run settles the ordinary :status :pass envelope over {} and [] — a success-shaped NON-RUN indistinguishable on the wire from a genuine green (measured under rf2-3n3dk).
  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc's run-variant descriptor carries the prerequisite in the tool description an agent reads.

PREMISE CORRECTION worth recording, because a reader of rf2-2ktuc will otherwise think this is already done: that bead's TRUTH AT TIP says commit 8cae7ca102 'carried the prerequisite into ... skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md'. It did not. Reading that commit's diff for that file, the single hunk rewrites the read-a11y-violations gotcha from 'return an empty list ... expect the no-op' to the capability-unavailable refusal. The adapter prerequisite landed in that commit on tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md, spec/API.md and tools/story-mcp/README.md only.

IMPACT

An agent driving the pair skill's loop on a consumer project whose launch alias preloads no adapter gets isError true / :rf.error/no-adapter-installed on its first run-variant, with the leaf offering neither the error name nor the boot. Worse than the authoring case: the refusal is easy to misread as :cannot-run (a runner that could not attempt the plan, whose remedy is to change the runner) when it is a host prerequisite to satisfy, and the leaf teaches the :pass / :fail / :cannot-run / :error verdict vocabulary right beside it.

FIX SHAPE (one file)

Add the prerequisite where the loop is set up — the error id, that it carries :tool and :recovery and never a :status, the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot in the preloaded namespace, and that catalogue reads are unaffected. Note explicitly that the refusal is NOT a :cannot-run verdict. Cite tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md section 'Running a variant needs an installed adapter'.

Consider matching skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md, which PR #8999 gave the same treatment for preview-variant — same facts, run side instead of authoring side. Write it from the spec section and lifecycle.cljc rather than from that leaf, so the two do not become a copy that drifts.

GATE

scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py and scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pin neither this prose nor per-tool behaviour text. Verify by hand against the spec section and lifecycle.cljc; say so in the PR body. skills/re-frame2-pair/** is a serial lane — sequence, do not parallelise, against anything else touching it.

ACCEPTANCE

stories.md names :rf.error/no-adapter-installed and the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot, and distinguishes the refusal from a :cannot-run verdict; check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py and check_doc_slugs.py exit 0.

FOUND BY rf2-2ktuc's worker (PR #8999) while checking that bead's premise about which surfaces commit 8cae7ca102 reached. skills/re-frame2-pair/** was outside that dispatch's fence.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 20:55:27 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2skill-c worker as a correction to rf2-2ktuc's premise — commit 8cae7ca102 did NOT carry the adapter prerequisite into skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md, so the PAIR skill, which owns the RUN side, still has no adapter prerequisite for run-variant. The pair skill lane is FREE (PR #8996 merged at 4813c62323). Dispatchable, and it pairs with rf2-16q1 — same reading of the Story tool contract, adjacent surfaces.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02 23:38 AUSEST, PR #9020. Census confirmed the premise: stories.md had 0 hits for no-adapter-installed line-oriented AND flattened, with controls that bite in the same file (:cannot-run 2/3, run-variant 7/7).

DIVERGENCE FROM THE FIX SHAPE, recorded because it is a correction to this bead rather than a shortcut. The FIX SHAPE says to write the error id plus :tool and :recovery and never a :status, and the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot in the preloaded namespace. Those are the HEADLESS story-mcp facts, and this leaf documents the BROWSER heap over eval-cljs -- the host it explicitly disclaims in its own section Headless Story is a different task. Writing them verbatim would have created a fresh instance of the defect class this bead is about.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE. (1) tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src has NO run-variant tool (grep exit 1, zero hits; control eval-cljs exit 0 with hits in 5 files), so the pair skill run side is re-frame.story/run-variant evaluated in the browser. (2) tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1295-1301 wraps prepare-ctx! and resume-ctx! inside the promise executor under try/catch and routes every throw to handle-run-error!, which CALLS RESOLVE. So the browser path has no pre-flight refusal at all and does not reject -- the exact opposite of lifecycle.cljc:63-79, which refuses before allocating and never returns a :status. (3) The underlying condition is core's: frame.cljc:2381 reaches adapter/make-state-container, then require-adapter! in substrate/adapter.cljc:293-345, throwing :rf.error/no-adapter-installed when rf/init! never ran and :rf.error/adapter-disposed after destroy-adapter! -- two ids, two remedies. (4) plain-atom is the renderer-free choice and renders nothing, so it is wrong advice for a browser canvas.

RESOLUTION. The prerequisite is written per host: the browser contract where the loop is set up, and the headless refusal envelope including (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) inside the section that already owns that host. Every acceptance item is met -- stories.md names :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, names the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot, and distinguishes both from a :cannot-run verdict -- and check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py and check_doc_slugs.py all exit 0. Written from the spec section and the sources above rather than copied from skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md, so the two do not become a drifting copy.
close_reason: PR #9020: stories.md now carries the run-variant adapter prerequisite. Names :rf.error/no-adapter-installed, names the (rf/init! plain-atom/adapter) boot in the Headless Story section that owns that host, and distinguishes both from a :cannot-run verdict. Written per host after verifying at source that the browser path has no pre-flight refusal (runtime.cljc:1295-1301 resolves through handle-run-error!) and that the pair MCP server ships no run-variant tool -- see the appended note for the divergence from the fix shape. check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py, check_skill_mcp_drift.py and check_doc_slugs.py all exit 0.

title: spec(story-mcp): 002-Tool-Registry.md contradicts itself on list-substrates — its own list-substrates section still says the JVM host returns [], which its Host execution model section and the implementation both refuse
description:
CLAIM

tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md says two incompatible things about list-substrates on the JVM stdio host.

  - Section 'Host execution model' (near the top): 'list-substrates and read-a11y-violations return a machine-readable capability-unavailable error (isError true, :rf.error :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable) rather than a false-empty []/{:violations []} success. []/#{} is reserved for a REACHED provider that genuinely holds nothing — capability absence is not answered emptiness (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - Section '### list-substrates' (in the Docs tool catalogue, further down): 'Returns the set registered via re-frame.story/register-substrate! (Reagent canonical; UIx opt-in per host). The JVM stdio server returns [] because it has no bridge to the CLJS registry.'

TRUTH AT TIP — the implementation agrees with the FIRST, so the per-tool section is the stale one:

  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc, tool-list-substrates: '(if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result {:tool "list-substrates" :capability "substrate-registry" ...}))'. Its docstring: 'this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error — NOT a false-empty {:substrates []} success that an agent could mistake for no substrates registered (rf2-3fc89f.21).'
  - The same file's registry descriptor for list-substrates spells the JVM case out in the tool description an agent actually reads: 'when the browser registry is UNREACHABLE (the JVM stdio server has no browser bridge) this returns a machine-readable capability-unavailable error ... NOT a false-empty {:substrates []}'.

The read-a11y-violations per-tool section was already corrected (commit 8cae7ca102, rf2-6j0yl, PR #8865's follow-through) and now states the refusal at length. The list-substrates section was not — the same commit's census reached the a11y half only.

IMPACT

This is the exact confusion rf2-3fc89f.21 closed in the runtime, reopened in the document that tools and agents are pointed at. A reader who takes the per-tool section at face value writes a client that treats [] as 'no substrates registered' and never handles isError — and the whole reason the contract refuses instead of answering [] is that EMPTY (a reached registry holding nothing) and UNAVAILABLE (the host could not look) are different states.

FIX SHAPE (one file, one paragraph)

Rewrite the '### list-substrates' section's last sentence to match the Host execution model section and the shipped handler: on the JVM stdio server it returns isError true with :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable, never an empty list; an empty :substrates vec is reserved for a REACHED registry that genuinely holds nothing; read it from a browser-local Story host. Model the wording on the read-a11y-violations section, which already says exactly this.

GATE

No gate pins this prose. scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pins the tool-name allow-list split, not per-tool behaviour text. Verify by hand against dev.cljc's tool-list-substrates and its registry descriptor, and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

002-Tool-Registry.md's list-substrates section names :rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable and no longer says the JVM stdio server returns []; the two sections agree.

FOUND BY rf2-2ktuc's worker (PR #8999) while sourcing the skill leaf's list-substrates footnote — the leaf was written from the implementation and the Host execution model section, deliberately not from the stale per-tool section. tools/** was outside that dispatch's fence.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 20:55:27 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2skill-c worker. This is a SPEC self-contradiction in tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — the host-execution-model section says list-substrates is capability-unavailable while its own per-tool section says the JVM host returns an empty vector, and the implementation agrees with the FIRST. Not fenced by any live worker; tools/** is nobody's surface right now. Dispatchable, and it pairs naturally with rf2-pra5 (the pair skill still has no adapter prerequisite for run-variant) since both came out of the same reading of the Story tool contract.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:5x AUSEST — THE tools/ COMMIT STAYS. THE FENCE WAS MINE AND IT WAS WRONG.

WHAT HAPPENED: my specdrift-c brief said 'You may edit spec/** and nothing else', and this bead's file is tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md — under tools/, which that sentence forbids, while the same brief's item-1 section instructed the worker to correct exactly that file. There is no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md. The worker did the right thing in a contradiction it did not create: it followed the explicit item instruction, ISOLATED the change in its own tip commit 82c488329d so I could drop it alone, and said so rather than quietly widening or quietly skipping.

THE RULING: KEEP IT. The bead's subject is unambiguous and tools/story-mcp/spec/ is exactly where a story-mcp spec lives; the fence sentence was a copy-paste generalisation that contradicted the item it accompanied. Nothing else in the repo makes tools/ off-limits here — no live worktree holds it, and this project already has a STANDING rule pulling the other way for the sibling tool: every dispatch touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR. A tool's spec is part of that tool's surface, not a separate lane.

AND THE FIX IS SETTLED BY THE IMPLEMENTATION RATHER THAN BY EITHER SECTION'S PROSE, which is what this bead asked for: tool-list-substrates returns capability-unavailable-result when the provider is unreachable, never []. So the PER-TOOL section was the stale one and is what the worker rewrote; '## Host execution model' was already correct and is untouched. That is the right way round — a document contradicting itself has a right answer and a wrong one, and the implementation decides which, not whichever section is easier to edit.

LESSON FOR MY OWN BRIEFS, recorded here rather than only felt: a scope fence written as a blanket path glob can contradict the items it fences. When a cluster's beads name files, the fence should be derived from those files, not asserted over them — and where the two disagree, the item wins and the worker should say so, which is exactly what happened.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9032 (commit 82c488329d). Premise CONFIRMED at tip before editing: tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:298-303 still read 'The JVM stdio server returns [] because it has no bridge to the CLJS registry', contradicting its own Host execution model section at L27-33. The implementation decides, and it agrees with the FIRST: dev.cljc:196-201 tool-list-substrates is (if (cljs-resolve/substrate-provider-available?) (result/edn-result ...) (result/capability-unavailable-result ...)) -- it never returns []. So the per-tool section was the stale one and is what I rewrote; Host execution model is untouched. Modelled on the read-a11y-violations section that 8cae7ca102 corrected the same way, stating the EMPTY (registry answered, held none) vs UNAVAILABLE (host could not look) distinction explicitly. Verified by hand against dev.cljc and its registry descriptor as the bead asked, since no gate pins this prose; check_skill_mcp_drift.py exit 0. SCOPE FLAG FOR THE MAYOR: this file is tools/story-mcp/spec/, not spec/. The dispatch brief's scope fence forbade tools/** while its own item-1 section instructed correcting exactly this file, and no top-level spec/002-Tool-Registry.md exists. I followed the explicit item-1 instruction (this bead's triage records 'tools/** is nobody's surface right now'; no live worktree holds it) and isolated the change in its own tip commit so it can be dropped alone if the fence is ruled binding.

title: routing/resources: a :url-bound? make-frame plans route resources AT CONSTRUCTION and a failed plan is never retried (NOT a live-frame reprojection bug — mechanism in the original title is refuted; needs ruling)
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by rf2-xkhul (PR #8990) while running the pilot baselines from a clean external workspace built per docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md on the published :local/root route (Node 24, shadow-cljs 3.4.10, dev compile of a :node-test build, goog.DEBUG default).

SYMPTOM. implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs copied VERBATIM into app/test/ of the LinearLite workspace (deps: core, adapters/reagent, http, routing, resources, hicasso) fails 16 of 51 assertions across 7 of 10 tests, while the identical file is green on the in-repo consolidated :node-test bundle. Its init! (the fixture :init-fn) does (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}) FIRST and then registrar/register! the snapshotted :resource/:mutation rows, reg-fx :rf.http/managed (capture stub) and :rf.nav/push-url. In the workspace bundle the frame never sees anything registered after make-frame: :rf.route/navigate to :linearlite.app/board lands :transition :error with :rf.error/resource-route-plan / cause :rf.error/resource-not-registered ('no resource is registered under :linearlite/board') even though (registrar/lookup :resource :linearlite/board) is truthy at that moment; moving ONLY the resource re-registration before make-frame clears that error but the capture stub registered after make-frame is still not what the read lowers through (entry stays :loading, last-managed-args nil). Moving EVERY registration before make-frame (frame made last) -> 51/51 green. Probes confirmed the ns-load state is identical to in-repo (registrar and source store both hold the resource + 3 mutations; :routing/on-route-entry and :resources/reg-resource hooks live).

WHY IT MATTERS. re-frame.live-frame documents the sealed-generation freshener as a CORRECTNESS invariant with NO debug gate (rf2-9c2jf): make-frame installs a registration hook so a later reg-* marks the projection dirty and a read-time coalesced flush reprojects (EP-0026 / rf2-h1vqa4). In the consumer bundle that reprojection does not take effect for the make-frame -> reg-* -> dispatch sequence, which live_frame.cljc names as 'exactly the broken one'. Either the in-repo bundle carries something (a sibling suite, the test-quiet runner, an artefact only it loads) that arms the flush and a consumer never gets, or the flush is not reached on this path. Unknown which; not chased under rf2-xkhul (fence was pilots/** only).

REPRO (about 3 minutes). Build the LinearLite workspace per workspace.md at tip of PR #8990 (or main once merged); replace app/test/linearlite/baseline_test.cljs with the adapter suite verbatim (ns re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test also matches the -test$ regexp); npm test -> exit 1, 16 failures. Then in its init! move (rf/make-frame ...) to the end -> exit 0. The committed baseline under docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/linearlite/ already makes the frame last and is green; this bead is about the framework behaviour the verbatim suite exposes, and about whether any in-repo fixture is green only because the consolidated bundle masks it.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP. Reproduce with a minimal consumer test: make-frame, reg-event, dispatch-sync -> expect :rf.error/no-such-handler in the consumer bundle if the theory holds; then diff what re-frame.live-frame/ensure-reprojection-installed! and the :live-frame/flush-projection! consult do in each bundle.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-09-02 19:57:00 AUSEST (mayor): filed by the rf2-xkhul worker with a 3-minute repro. This is a FRAMEWORK bug (core/live-frame), not a hicasso or pilots one, and it is the highest-priority thing filed this session by a worker — a registration made after make-frame being invisible to that frame in a :local/root consumer bundle would bite any consumer following the published route, and it was found the only way it could be: by building a workspace outside the repo. Not fenced by any live surface. Next solo dispatch when a slot frees.
DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 20:07:19 AUSEST by the mayor. SOLO, DIAGNOSIS-FIRST, fresh worktree worker/liveframe-ma8r off origin/main 07c76826c2. Premises verified at that tip: live_frame.cljc:1790 carries the 'exactly the broken one' sentence verbatim; ensure-reprojection-installed! is referenced ~:377 and ~:512; the linearlite adapter suite has 11 deftests; the committed pilot baseline that makes the frame LAST is on main. LEAD HYPOTHESIS handed over AS A HYPOTHESIS: live_frame.cljc ~:386 reaches the flush through (late-bind/get-fn-cached :live-frame/flush-projection!) inside a when-let, so a bundle where nothing registers that publisher falls through SILENTLY — no error, no warning, exactly the observed symptom shape. The competing reading this bead names (flush reached but ineffective on this path) must be EXCLUDED rather than argued away. Worker is told the diagnosis is the deliverable, that no code change may be warranted, and to leave this bead OPEN for a ruling if the honest answer needs one.

DIAGNOSIS 2026-09-02 20:31 AUSEST (rf2-ma8r worker, PR #9000). The bead's
numbers reproduce EXACTLY (16 failures across 7 of 10 tests, 51 assertions,
exit 1, in a LinearLite workspace built per pilots/workspace.md on the
published :local/root route) — but the MECHANISM in the description is
refuted, and so is the flush-publisher hypothesis. No live-frame defect is
involved. Nothing is invisible to the frame.

WHAT IS REFUTED (each measured, not argued).

1. "Registrations made AFTER make-frame are invisible to the frame in a
   :local/root consumer node-test bundle." REFUTED. A minimal probe —
   make-frame, then reg-event, then dispatch-sync — PASSES in the very
   consumer bundle where the suite fails 16/51 (exit 0). In that same
   bundle the frame's own reprojection is demonstrably live: an explicit
   flush-pending-reprojection! taken mid-suite returns
   :added #{[:resource :linearlite/board] [:mutation :linearlite/create-issue]
   [:mutation :linearlite/edit-title] [:mutation :linearlite/change-status]}
   and :changed #{[:fx :rf.http/managed] [:fx :rf.nav/push-url]} — i.e. the
   post-make-frame registrations ARE picked up and swapped onto the frame.

2. "A late-bound :live-frame/flush-projection! that nothing registers in a
   consumer bundle makes the when-let fall through silently." REFUTED twice.
   At source: make-frame calls ensure-reprojection-installed! UNCONDITIONALLY
   (live_frame.cljc:928), and late-bind/get-fn-cached does NOT cache nil
   resolutions, so there is no negative-cache variant either. Empirically:
   in the consumer bundle the probe prints flush-publisher-resolvable? true
   and mark-dirty-publisher-resolvable? true.

3. "Or the flush is not reached on this path." REFUTED. The failing lookup
   happens strictly BEFORE the registrations exist at all, not against a
   stale generation — see below.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — a construction-time route plan, in routing/resources.

A println planted in registry/require-resource-spec!'s miss branch shows the
failing lookup happening with the registrar genuinely EMPTY
(atom-has? false, lookup-direct? false, ids-in-scope []), and — the decisive
ordering datum — it fires BEFORE the end of init!:

    PRE-MAKE-FRAME  resource-ids []
    MA8R-PLANT miss :linearlite/board where rf.resource/route-entry
                    gen-bound? true atom-has? false ids-in-scope []
    POST-MAKE-FRAME routing-slice {... :transition :error
                    :error {:rf.error/id :rf.error/resource-route-plan ...}}
    INIT-END        resource-ids [:linearlite/board] atom-has? true

So the route entry runs INSIDE (rf/make-frame {:id :rf/default :url-bound? true}).
A :url-bound? frame performs a synchronous initial URL sync at construction:
frame/upsert-frame!'s post-create hook fires routing's
:routing/on-frame-registered!, which reconciles the URL listener and "syncs
the current URL into the owner's slice" (routing/history.cljc). Under Node,
history/current-url is "/". The LinearLite example registers
:linearlite.app/board at path "/" (examples/.../linearlite/core.cljs:458-464)
and that route declares :resources [{:resource :linearlite/board :blocking? true}].
The construction-time sync therefore PLANS the board resource while the
suite's init! has not yet reinstated the :resource/:mutation rows the
fixture's reset hook cleared — init! re-registers them on the NEXT line —
and the plan fails :rf.error/resource-not-registered, recording
:transition :error on the slice.

The error is then STICKY. The test's own
(dispatch-sync [:rf.route/navigate {:to :linearlite.app/board}]) does not
re-plan: the planted probe fires EXACTLY ONCE per test, at construction, and
never again — including in a probe test where the resource was verified
present and visible inside the frame immediately beforehand. Every one of the
16 assertions then reads nil off the never-populated entry.

DECISIVE CONTROL. Changing ONLY the example's route path from "/" to "/board"
in the workspace copy takes the identical suite from 16 failures / exit 1 to
0 failures / exit 0, with the planted probe firing ZERO times. Nothing else
was touched.

WHY THE IN-REPO BUNDLE IS GREEN — and YES, THIS IS A FALSE GREEN.
This answers the bead's second question. re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test
is green in the consolidated bundle ONLY because a co-loaded sibling owns "/".
At least seven in-tree apps register a route at "/" (infinite_feed, linearlite,

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): boolean-discriminator-subs After view and eval 24 clean fixture are plain defn views with bare rf/ ops — raise :rf.error/no-frame-context under EP-0002
description:
CLAIM. `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/boolean-discriminator-subs.md:71-75` — the **After** (recommended rewrite) is a plain Reagent fn with a bare facade read:

```clojure
(defn article-page []
  (case @(rf/subscribe [:article/render]) ...))
```

The same plain-`defn` + bare `rf/` shape is the should-be-clean fixture in `evals/evals.json` #24 (`behav-neg-render-local-component-state`: `(defn search-box [] ... #(rf/dispatch [:search/query-changed ...]))`), whose expectations require the agent to "report the view as clean against the catalogue".

TRUTH AT TIP. Under EP-0002 there is no `:rf/default` floor; a plain `(defn ...)` view carries no `:contextType`, cannot read the surrounding `frame-provider`'s frame, and its ambient `rf/subscribe` / `rf/dispatch` raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/views.md:104`, `.../fundamentals/subs.md:86`, `.../fundamentals/frames.md:9,82`, `skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:30` (deferred callbacks fire on a fresh stack with no `*current-frame*`). Every shipped example view is `rf/reg-view` with the injected `subscribe` (`examples/core/todomvc/views.cljs:64-141`, `examples/core/counter/*.cljs:60-70`). The improver's own `references/view-side-hook-state.md:78` states exactly this: "A plain `(defn ...)` view with a bare `#(rf/dispatch ...)` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on click (EP-0002 — no `:rf/default` floor)."

IMPACT. Leaf 2's canonical rewrite — the thing the critique hands the programmer — throws at first render in a re-frame2 app. Leaf 6 and leaf 2 contradict each other inside one catalogue. Eval 24 grades as "clean" a snippet that is itself the plain-Reagent-fn trap, so a reviewer who correctly notes it is penalised as "inventing an unrelated anti-pattern" (expectation 4), while a reviewer who stays silent misses a real runtime defect. (The Before snippets in leaf 2 and in evals #18/#22/#27 are fine as v1-flavoured "before" code; the defect is in the After and in the clean fixture.)

FIX SHAPE. One PR, two files:
1. `references/boolean-discriminator-subs.md` After: `(rf/reg-view article-page [] (case @(subscribe [:article/render]) ...))` — injected `subscribe`, no `rf/` prefix — with the one-line reason leaf 6 already gives (or a cross-ref to it).
2. `evals/evals.json` #24: make the clean fixture idiomatic re-frame2 (a `reg-view` whose deferred handlers use the injected `dispatch`; keep the render-local `hovered?` atom the fixture exists to protect — the Reagent Form-2 closure shape may need `reg-view*` / `r/with-let` per views.md; the worker picks the smallest idiomatic spelling), so "clean" is true. Optionally add to #18's expectations: "the rewritten view is a `reg-view` (or otherwise carries its frame) — a plain defn with bare `rf/subscribe` is the EP-0002 trap".

GATE. `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --verbose`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose`, `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (all exit 0 at tip; must stay 0). No gate validates the CLJS inside a leaf — verify by hand that the After matches `views.md` §Canonical signature and say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE. Leaf 2's After view registers with `reg-view` and reads via the injected `subscribe`; eval #24's prompt is a view that is clean under EP-0002 (no bare `rf/` op inside a plain defn); no leaf or fixture in the improver presents a plain-defn view with bare `rf/subscribe` / `rf/dispatch` as a recommended or clean shape.

title: skill(re-frame2): story-mcp-loop.md says preview-variant works on a read-only launch; since rf2-c9t52 it refuses with :rf.error/no-adapter-installed unless the consumer preloads an adapter (and list-substrates is capability-unavailable on the JVM host)
description:

TRUTH AT TIP
tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md:38-56 §Running a variant needs an installed adapter (rf2-c9t52): "Catalogue reads work on a bare launch. RUNNING one does not: `run-variant` and `preview-variant` allocate a variant frame, and a frame takes its state substrate from an installed re-frame adapter. The server deliberately installs none ... a consuming project that wants headless runs installs one in the namespace its launch alias preloads (`(rf/init! plain-atom/adapter)`, the renderer-free choice). With none installed, both lifecycle tools REFUSE before any lifecycle work, returning `isError true` with `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` ... plus `:tool` and a `:recovery` naming the boot. They never return a `:status`."
:204-208 `preview-variant` "blocks on the SAME story/run-variant lifecycle ... so it carries the SAME host prerequisite"; also `:timeout-ms` default 10 s, ceiling 30 s, clamps down.
:20-36 §Host execution model: `list-substrates` and `read-a11y-violations` on the JVM host return `:rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable` (isError), never an empty success.

IMPACT
An agent following the worked pass on a consumer project whose launch alias preloads no adapter gets `isError true :rf.error/no-adapter-installed` on its first `preview-variant`; the leaf's :74 says the opposite and offers no recovery. `list-substrates` is presented as a registry read that returns a list; on the JVM host it errors by design.

FIX SHAPE (one file)
(a) §Gates and prerequisites: add "Previewing needs an installed adapter" — the server installs none; preload `(rf/init! plain-atom/adapter)` in the launch alias; the refusal is `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` carrying `:recovery`, never a `:status`; catalogue reads are unaffected. (b) :74 -> "the enumerations still work; `preview-variant` additionally needs the adapter". (c) :42 note that `list-substrates` is browser-only and returns `:rf.error/story-mcp-capability-unavailable` from the JVM host. (d) optional one clause on `:timeout-ms` (10 s default / 30 s ceiling).

GATE
scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py pins only the tool-name allow-list split; this prose has no gate. Verify by hand against spec 002 §Running a variant needs an installed adapter and §Host execution model; say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE

title: skill(re-frame2): routing.md path-pattern grammar spells the optional group /{...}? — the slash-outside form spec 012 rejects at registration (:rf.error/invalid-route-pattern); canonical is {/:name}?
description:
CLAIM
skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/routing.md:40 (the skill's only path-pattern grammar block):
    /{ ... }?     optional group; inner /:name is elided in route-url output when absent
i.e. the slash OUTSIDE the brace.

TRUTH AT TIP
spec/012-Routing.md §Path-pattern grammar, table row: "Optional segment group | `{/:name}?` or `{/literal}?` | `/articles/:id{/:slug}?`, `{/:base}?/about`". Rule 2 below the table: "the slash lives **INSIDE** the braces ... This is the **one canonical spelling** ... The slash-**outside** spelling (`/{:base}?/about`) is **not** part of the grammar and is rejected at registration — it is the shape that orphans a separator on elision (`//about`)."
spec/012-Routing.md:109 — `:rf.error/invalid-route-pattern` lists "a malformed optional group (... or spelled slash-outside `{:name}?` instead of the canonical slash-inside `{/:name}?`)". Thrown at registration, dev and prod.
implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/match.cljc:94-136 `validate-optional-group!` — "The slash-OUTSIDE spelling (`{:base}?`, a `{` directly after a `/` with a `:`-first body) is rejected. The leading `/` lives inside the braces".

IMPACT

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern resources — reg-resource-scope shown as a 2-slot {:inputs :resolve} map the runtime rejects; canonical form is 3-slot (id metadata resolve-fn)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md` §Named scope resolvers — `reg-resource-scope` (L104-107):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs  {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}    ;; declared inputs — names ↦ source descriptors
   :resolve (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]
              (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}]))})
```

L118 then describes the `{:inputs … :resolve …}` **form** as the canonical declaration ("The `{:inputs … :resolve …}` form **declares** which app facts decide identity") and offers the whole-db bare-fn as the sugar. `resources-mutations.md`, the mutation descriptors and every `{:from-db :session}` reference in both leaves build on this registration.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:15-23` — "## The `{:inputs …}` metadata + resolver-fn grammar (the ONE canonical form) … The 3-slot shape is `(scope-id metadata resolve-fn)`: the resolver is the THIRD (value) slot, not a `:resolve` key inside the metadata map." L289-300: the registration fn is `[scope-id metadata resolve-fn]`, throws `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` with the message "the :inputs / :doc reflection-config metadata map is the SECOND slot, the :resolve fn is the THIRD", and the comment at L299-300 is explicit: "A `:resolve` left INSIDE the metadata map is a mislocated key; reject it". `spec/016-Resources.md:169,586` states the same 3-slot grammar; `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/scope.cljs:105+` registers `:realworld/viewer` / `:realworld/session` in the 3-slot form. The whole-db bare-fn sugar the leaf mentions (L118) does exist (`scope_registry.cljc:55-68`) — that part is right.

## IMPACT

The one registration the whole Resources scope story hangs on is written in a shape the runtime rejects loudly (2-slot with `:resolve` mislocated). An agent copying it gets `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` at boot; every `{:from-db :session}` downstream then fails closed (unresolved scope → `:rf.error/resource-sub-unresolved-scope` on subs, dropped targets on mutations). Loud rather than silent, but it is the leaf's headline snippet and it contradicts the spec, the implementation and the canonical example at once.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/resources.md` only)

Rewrite L104-107 to the 3-slot form (lift from `scope_registry.cljc:17-20` or `scope.cljs`):

```clojure
(rf/reg-resource-scope :session
  {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}}     ;; metadata: declared inputs
  (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx]                           ;; resolver: THIRD slot, first arg = resolved inputs map
    (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))
```

and reword L118 ("The `{:inputs …}` metadata + third-slot resolver …"). Optionally add the one-line "first arg is ALWAYS the resolved inputs map; the bare-fn sugar is the only form whose first arg is the whole db" since that is the trap the grammar exists to prevent (`scope_registry.cljc:26-33`).

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences; `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run. Verify by hand against `scope_registry.cljc` §grammar and `realworld_resources/scope.cljs`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

Every `reg-resource-scope` call in `skills/re-frame2/patterns/*.md` is 3-slot `(id metadata resolve-fn)` with no `:resolve` key in the metadata map; the prose names the resolver as the third slot.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern websocket — canonical declaration does not register (4 dangling action ids → :rf.error/machine-unresolved-action) and calls an undefined current-socket? helper
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md` §Canonical declaration (L68-176) is presented as copyable code ("the canonical declaration below is the leaf-level summary" L7; "Read the source first; the declaration above is the leaf-level summary" L231). Its `:actions` map (L95-118) declares eight ids: `:record-connection-opts :rotate-cred :on-socket-lost :fail-in-flight :on-fatal-error :on-connected :flush-queue :enqueue-message`. Its states reference four more that are never declared: `:send-auth` (L147 `:authenticating {:entry :send-auth …}`), `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` (L158-159), `:send-now` (L160). Its `:trusted-frame?` guard (L91-93) calls a bare fn `(current-socket? data source-socket-id)` that the leaf never defines — `:current-socket?` exists only as a guard KEY in the same `:guards` map (L81-87), and a guard keyword is not callable from another guard's body.

## TRUTH AT TIP

Machine registration resolves action refs eagerly: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1651,1812` — "`:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` on dangling refs". So `(rf/reg-machine :ws/connection …)` as written throws at registration on `:send-auth` (the first dangling ref hit), before any state is entered. And `current-socket?` is an undeclared symbol — a CLJS compile warning / undefined var at load. The example the leaf calls ground truth already has both fixes: `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:110-118` defines the shared helper `from-live-socket?` and all three guards (`:current-socket?` L215, `:own-request-timeout?` L242, `:trusted-frame?` L266) call it; the four actions are defined at L355-364 (`:send-auth`), L404-409 (`:send-now`), and the receive/refuse pair (`:receive-message` L515+, `:refuse-frame` — note the example names it `:receive-message`, not `:route-message`).

While there, one drift worth lifting in the same edit: the example guards the lifecycle transitions too — `connection.cljs:42-46` "This covers the whole socket-sourced surface — the lifecycle transitions (`:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed`, `:ws/closed`) as much as `:ws/received`" — whereas the leaf's `:connecting {:on {:ws/opened {:target :authenticating}}}` (L146), `:authenticating` (L148-149) and the parent `:ws/closed` (L139) carry no `:current-socket?` guard, so a straggler `:ws/closed` from a torn-down socket would bounce the NEW connection into `:reconnecting`. The leaf's feature table (L26) claims the guard "rejects events from a torn-down prior socket" generally.

Everything else in the leaf checks out against the 2026-09-01/02 spec + example commits (`2ef4147f8f`, `510e758f7e`, `f552191c3d`, `3113303ff4`, `7fb6031db7`, `cc2d3e5d71`): request-reply is taught as app-level (`:origin :ws/server` / `:ws/local`, no envelope, L200), the registration-token rule is in the anti-patterns (L225-226), three doors out of `:active` settle `:in-flight` (L52-66, L139-141), and `:cred-ref` timing matches. The token / `:next-token` mechanics live in prose only, which the "example is ground truth" framing covers.

## IMPACT

The one code block an agent copies for a WebSocket machine fails at registration with `:rf.error/machine-unresolved-action` and a compile-time undefined symbol. The agent then either invents four action bodies and a helper (plausibly wrong — `:route-message` must clear the `:in-flight` slot by REGISTRATION token, which only the example shows) or abandons the leaf for the example, which is what the leaf should have handed it in the first place.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, `patterns/websocket.md` only)

- Add a `(defn current-socket? [data source-socket-id] …)` helper above the machine (mirroring the example's `from-live-socket?`) and have both guards call it; or rename to `from-live-socket?` to match the example verbatim.
- Add the four missing actions in compact form — `:send-auth` and `:send-now` are two lines each (lift from `connection.cljs:355-364, 404-409`); `:route-message` and `:refuse-frame` can be one-line stubs whose comment says "lifted in full from `connection.cljs` `:receive-message` / `:refuse-frame`" — or rename `:route-message` → `:receive-message` so the reader greps the right symbol.
- Guard `:ws/opened`, `:ws/auth-ok`, `:ws/auth-failed` and the parent `:ws/closed` with `{:guard :current-socket? …}` as the example does.
- Keep the leaf's length in mind (it is already 29 KB — see the patterns leaf-size bead); prefer lifting over adding prose.

## GATE

No gate compiles skill code fences — `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` still run (both exit 0 today; both blind to this). Verify by hand: every `:action` / `:entry` id referenced in the declaration appears in `:actions`, every bare symbol the guards call is defined in the leaf, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

The canonical `:ws/connection` declaration references no action id absent from its own `:actions` map and no undefined symbol; lifecycle transitions carry `:current-socket?`; the leaf's `:in-flight` / token prose is unchanged.

title: migration(corpus/skill): register-listener! two-arg calls are arity errors, not invalid-stream errors
description:
OUT-OF-PARTITION finding from the 2026-09-02 skills review (partition B of re-frame-migration). The corpus is not in any of the three skill partitions, and this is a broken-code claim in the authoritative document the skill routes to, so it is filed rather than only reported.

CLAIM (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md). Three rules tell a v1 author to call a listener fn the facade does not export:
  line 514 (M-13 body): "Error **observability** moves to the always-on `register-error-listener!` surface"
  line 518 (M-13 what-to-do): "moves to `register-error-listener!`"
  line 520 (M-13 why): "(`register-error-listener!` always-on, `register-listener!` dev-only)"
  line 1304 (M-26 table): "`(rf/register-listener! key cb)` / `(rf/unregister-listener! key)`"
  line 1307 (M-26 table): "`(rf/register-error-listener! key cb)` for observability"
  line 2714 (M-69 rename table): `register-error-emit-listener!` → "`register-error-listener!` / `unregister-error-listener!` / `clear-error-listeners!`"
  line 2726 (M-69 example): "(rf/register-error-listener! :sentry (fn [rec] ...))"

TRUTH AT TIP. implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc exports ONE stream-parameterized verb pair: `(defn register-listener! [stream id f] …)` (line 2126) and `(defn unregister-listener! [stream id] …)` (line 2161), with `listener-streams #{:trace :events :errors :epoch}` (line 2100) and an unknown stream throwing `:rf.error/unknown-listener-stream` (line 2115). `rg -c 'defn register-error-listener!' core.cljc` = 0; the only `register-error-listener!` in the facade is the INTERNAL alias `error-emit/register-error-listener!` it delegates to for the `:errors` stream (line 2157). spec/API.md §Error-emit (line 575+) documents the stream-first verb; spec/009-Instrumentation.md:645 says "The listener API is **one stream-parameterized verb** across the four pure observation streams". The skill leaf skills/re-frame-migration/references/error-events.md:51 already states the collapse correctly ("The former per-channel `register-(trace|event|error)-listener!` facade pairs were collapsed into this one verb").

IMPACT. An agent that follows the corpus (cardinal rule 1: the corpus is the source of truth) writes `(rf/register-error-listener! …)` — an unresolved-symbol compile error — or `(rf/register-listener! key cb)` — which throws `:rf.error/unknown-listener-stream` at boot because `key` lands in the `stream` slot. M-13 is the rule every v1 `reg-event-error-handler` user hits, and M-69's rename table maps a retired name onto another retired name.

FIX SHAPE (one file). M-13 lines 514-520: `(rf/register-listener! :errors id f)` (always-on) and `(rf/register-listener! :trace id f)` (dev-only). M-26 line 1304: `(rf/register-listener! :trace key cb)` / `(rf/unregister-listener! :trace key)` with a note that `:events` / `:errors` are the always-on streams. M-26 line 1307: `(rf/register-listener! :errors key cb)`. M-69 line 2714: the `register-error-emit-listener!` family → `(register-listener! :errors …)` / `(unregister-listener! :errors …)` (and whatever `clear-error-listeners!` maps to — check `error_emit.cljc`; if there is no public clear, say so). M-69 line 2726: `(rf/register-listener! :errors :sentry (fn [rec] ...))`. Leave M-13's heading unchanged (anchor stability, rf2-hiqtk8 note).

GATE. No script pins the corpus's listener spelling (`check_skill_migration_contract_drift.py` pins the SKILL leaves' M-13 wording, not the corpus's). `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for anchors. Verify by hand: `rg -n 'register-error-listener!|register-listener! key cb|unregister-listener! key' migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` returns 0 lines.

ACCEPTANCE. Every listener call in M-13 / M-26 / M-69 uses the stream-first `register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` verb with an explicit stream; the by-hand probe is empty; check_doc_slugs green.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern boot — :routing waits on :rf.route/resolved, an event nothing dispatches (spec Pattern-Boot shares the fiction)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/boot.md` §Canonical declaration (state-machine form), L233-234:

```clojure
:hydrating {:entry :phase-hydrate :on {:hydrate/done {:target :routing}}}
:routing   {:entry :enter-routing :on {:rf.route/resolved {:target :ready}}}
```

with `:enter-routing` (L194-197) dispatching `[:rf.route/handle-url-change (.. js/window -location -href)]`. The prose (L242) says the machine "self-initialises and starts working at birth", and `decision-trees/pick-a-pattern.md:74` names this state set (`… → :routing → :ready`) as "the canonical state set".

## TRUTH AT TIP

No framework surface dispatches `[:app/boot [:rf.route/resolved]]` — or any `:rf.route/resolved` at all: `grep -rF ":rf.route/resolved"` over `implementation/{core,routing,machines,resources,ssr,...}/src` returns 0 hits (every other `:rf.route/*` id the leaf uses resolves: `:rf.route/handle-url-change` 99 hits, `:rf.route/navigate` 84). `spec/012-Routing.md` does not define it either; the routing runtime's post-resolution surfaces are the `:rf.route/transitioned` runtime event (31 hits, dispatched top-level, never into an app machine) and the route's `:on-match` metadata, which `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/events.cljc:14-17` describes as "fire-and-forget `:on-match` dispatch … dispatches (in order, …) on a valid plan". `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:191` carries the identical `:rf.route/resolved` line — the leaf copied the spec faithfully; the spec is what drifted from the implementation (Cardinal rule 1: implementation wins).

`:hydrate/done` (L233) is fine — app-prefixed, the app dispatches it — but nothing in the leaf says so, and an agent reads the two lines as the same kind of thing.

## IMPACT

An agent copying the canonical boot machine gets one that boots, authenticates, loads the profile, hydrates, dispatches the URL-change, and then sits in `:routing` forever: `:ready` is unreachable, `:app.boot/state` never reads `:ready`, and the app's "boot complete" gate never opens. Silent — no error, no trace, the route slice does settle — so it presents as "the app loads but the boot spinner never goes away". Under `:rf/*` reservation the app cannot "just dispatch it" either (Cardinal rule 7).

## FIX SHAPE (one PR; touches the spec too, so it is hot-zone)

Replace the fictional event with the shipped seam: the initial route's `:on-match` (fire-and-forget, dispatched on a valid plan) sends an app-prefixed event into the boot machine, e.g. route metadata `{:on-match [:app/boot [:boot/route-resolved]]}` and `:routing {:entry :enter-routing :on {:boot/route-resolved {:target :ready}}}` — with one line naming `:on-match` as the producer and one line saying `:hydrate/done` is likewise app-dispatched (by the handler that finishes hydration). Make the same substitution in `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:191` (and its `:routing` prose at L450 if it names the event). Alternative if a route-plan-independent signal is wanted: a small `reg-event` that listens for the top-level `:rf.route/transitioned` and forwards — but `:on-match` is the documented hook and needs no forwarder. Update `pick-a-pattern.md:74` only if the state names change (they need not).

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (both read-only structural; neither compiles the fence). No gate compiles skill code fences — verify by hand that every `:on` key in the canonical machine is either app-prefixed and dispatched somewhere in the same snippet/prose, or a shipped `:rf.*` id present in `implementation/**`, and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`git grep -n "rf.route/resolved" -- skills spec` returns nothing; the canonical boot machine's `:routing` state exits on an event the leaf itself shows being produced (route `:on-match` or an app handler); `pick-a-pattern.md` and `boot.md` still agree on the state set.

title: skill(re-frame2): pattern ssr-loaders — teaches the spec-RETIRED SSR fan-out (Pattern-SSR-Loaders retired 2026-07-04); reroute SSR data-load to Resources and fix the 14-pattern rosters
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/ssr-loaders.md` (142 lines, 11 KB) teaches Pattern-SSR-Loaders in full as a live pattern: a `:pdp/load` machine whose `:loading` state fans out three `:rf.http/managed` children via `:spawn-all` "during drain", joins on `:on-all-complete`, and is guarded by `:after {30000 :pdp/timed-out}` — "phase-level wall-clock guard — mandatory under SSR" (L67); §The deadline (L114-116): "If one fetch hangs past the deadline, `:after` exits `:loading` … no partial render"; anti-pattern L127 "**Omitting the deadline.** A loader with no `:after` can hang until the host's outer timeout fires"; L124 "each `:rf.http/managed` blocks the drain thread on the server JVM transport". Footer: "Derived from `spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md` (Convention, not Spec) @ main".

Routed from `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md:104` ("SSR parallel data fetch before render (fan-out) → `patterns/ssr-loaders.md`") and named in the pattern rosters at `SKILL.md:9`, `skills/README.md:43`, `skills/re-frame2/README.md:7`, `docs/skills/re-frame2.md:17`; cross-linked from `patterns/form-action.md:15,225` ("on GET dispatch the page loader (Pattern-SSR-Loaders)"; "the GET-path sibling") and `references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:145,158` ("parallel data fetch via `:spawn-all` before render").

## TRUTH AT TIP

`spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md:1-4` — title "Pattern — SSR Loaders (RETIRED)", "**Status: RETIRED — do not implement.** This pattern was authored on two false premises and describes a render barrier that does not exist." Retired by commit `9f375386c3` (2026-07-04, rf2-exfavp). The two premises the leaf still teaches are both stated false there: (1) L12 "The managed-HTTP JVM transport is `java.net.http.HttpClient.sendAsync` … the drain reaches fixed point with the machine's children still in flight and renders the `:loading` skeleton"; (2) L13 "`:after` **no-ops under SSR** … The mandated server deadline is a dead remedy — it never fires. A machine that leans on it … simply hangs at `:loading`". L17 states the rule: "**Machines are synchronous-only under SSR.** Async machine work — a `:spawn` / `:spawn-all` whose children exist to drive async loads … is **outside the SSR allowed subset**. It is a programmer error". L19 names the pinning fixture `spec/conformance/fixtures/spawn-all-under-ssr-ring.edn` (`:rf.machine.timer/skipped-on-server`, snapshot stuck at `:loading`). §What to use instead (L21-31): route-owned blocking resources + `drain-blocking-resources!` (Spec 016 §SSR and hydration) — the one render barrier the runtime installs, with a real deadline that settles to `{:kind :rf.http/timeout :reason :ssr-blocking-timeout}`. L39: FormAction's "GET-path pointer to this pattern now resolves to resources-backed loading".

Independently of the retirement, the leaf's own snippet would not register: `:after {30000 :pdp/timed-out}` (L67) names `:pdp/timed-out` as an `:after` TARGET (a state), then treats it as an `:on` EVENT key (L71) — no state by that name exists, and `:after` values are state/transition targets (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:478-480` checks every `:after` target), so registration fails before the SSR question even arises.

The skill leaf has not been touched since the retirement (no commit on `skills/re-frame2/patterns/ssr-loaders.md` since 2026-07-04; the skill's SSR routing row, rosters and cross-links all predate it).

## IMPACT

An agent asked for "SSR that loads several pieces of data in parallel before render" is routed to a leaf whose canonical code is (a) a registration error and (b), once the target typo is fixed, exactly the out-of-subset shape the spec calls a programmer error — the server renders the `:loading` skeleton, the deadline never fires, and the request-scoped frame hangs at `:loading`. The right answer (route `:resources` with `:blocking? true`) already exists in the skill at `patterns/resources.md` §Route-driven loading but nothing routes SSR-shaped prompts there. Highest-impact item in this partition: the skill teaches the one SSR shape the spec says not to build.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR)

1. Retire `patterns/ssr-loaders.md` — either delete it and drop the leaf, or reduce it to a short stub (≤30 lines) that states the retirement, the machines-are-synchronous-only-under-SSR rule, and points at `patterns/resources.md` §Route-driven loading (`:blocking?`) + `spec/016-Resources.md` §SSR and hydration + `spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md`. A stub is preferable only if external consumers link the path; otherwise delete.
2. `SKILL.md:104` — replace the row with "SSR data load before render (route-owned blocking resources) → `patterns/resources.md`" (or drop it and add "…, SSR preload" to the resources row at L91).
3. Rosters — `SKILL.md:7-9` description, `skills/README.md:41-44`, `skills/re-frame2/README.md:7,34,40,77`, `docs/skills/re-frame2.md:17`: replace `SSR-Loaders` with `ResourcesMutations`. The count stays **14** (fifteen files today, one retired); today the "14" is wrong in the other direction — `patterns/` holds 15 leaves and the rosters omit `resources-mutations.md`, which `SKILL.md:92` routes to.
4. Cross-links — `patterns/form-action.md:15` ("on GET dispatch the page loader" → "on GET the route's `:resources` plan ensures the page's blocking reads"), `:225`; `references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:145,158` → point at `patterns/resources.md` §Route-driven loading and state the sync-only rule in one sentence. (`ssr-authoring.md` is a cross-cutting leaf — sibling partition — but the link retarget belongs in this PR so no dangling link lands.)
5. `examples-map.md` needs no change (it never indexed an SSR-Loaders example; `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/` is the resources-backed SSR example and is a candidate entry if one is wanted).

Do NOT "fix" the leaf's `:after` target and keep the pattern — the spec retired the shape, not the typo.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (covers `skills/**` and `docs/**` link targets + anchors — every retargeted link above), `python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py`, `mkdocs build --strict` for `docs/skills/re-frame2.md`. No gate reads the leaf's prose or the roster count — verify by hand (`ls skills/re-frame2/patterns | wc -l`) and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`git grep -n "ssr-loaders\|SSR-Loaders" -- skills docs/skills` returns only the retirement stub (if kept) and no routing row, roster entry, or "GET-path sibling" pointer; `SKILL.md`'s pattern table routes SSR data-loading to `patterns/resources.md`; the four rosters name ResourcesMutations and agree with `ls patterns/`; `check_doc_slugs.py` exit 0.

title: skill(re-frame2-setup): generator route's next commands fail pre-publish -- emitted framework coords are :mvn/version 0.0.1.alpha; add the post-emit :local/root rewrite and the -Tnew prerequisite
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:76 -- "That emits `./my-app/`; then `cd my-app && npm install && npx shadow-cljs watch app`." README.md:34 -- "Both routes land on the same canonical scaffold." SKILL.md:57 -- the generator is "a complete alternative the skill **runs itself** when the author asks for it". evals.json id 17 grades "the generator's actual exit code and the emitted files". The generator's own post-process prints the same next steps (tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:763-773).

TRUTH AT TIP. The emitted deps.edn carries the framework coords as `{:mvn/version "{{rf2-version}}"}` (tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/deps.edn:21-23; _uix/deps.edn:21-23) with hooks.clj:616 `:rf2-version "0.0.1.alpha"`. Nothing is on Clojars (repo README.md:97-99), and the skill's own references/deps-versions.md:58 says so: "a `{:mvn/version "<VERSION>"}` framework coord fails dependency resolution before it compiles". The template release gate rewrites the emission to `:local/root` before it compiles anything (.github/workflows/template-release.yml:115-128) -- the admission that the raw emission does not resolve. tests/generator_route_test.clj:257-282 (live arm) asserts exit 0 + a non-empty manifest and stops; rf2-h4q82's close reason confirms the fix was verified at emission, never past it. So the sequence README.md:76 prescribes fails at `npx shadow-cljs watch app` with a Maven "Could not find artifact day8/re-frame2 ... 0.0.1.alpha". Second, smaller: `-Tnew` is the deps-new tool installed under the alias `new`; tools/template/README.md:75-76 states that prerequisite, the skill's README section "Running the generator pre-publish" does not, and allowed-tools grants no `clojure -Ttools *`, so on a machine without it the executor's first command fails with an unknown-tool error before emission.

IMPACT. The route slice A (PR #8806) made the skill's to execute ends in a classpath failure the skill then has to explain; eval 17 stays green because it grades emission only. The manual route is unaffected (deps-versions.md already branches on publication state); this is the generator route alone.

FIX SHAPE (skills/re-frame2-setup/** only; no template change). In README section "Running the generator pre-publish", cited from SKILL.md rule 5: (a) one prerequisite line -- deps-new must be installed as tool `new` (`clojure -Ttools install-latest :lib io.github.seancorfield/deps-new :as new`); if the skill is to run that itself, grant `Bash(clojure -Ttools *)`, otherwise say so and stop. (b) One post-emit step, pre-publish only, BEFORE `npm install`: rewrite every `day8/re-frame2*` `:mvn/version` line in the emitted deps.edn to `:local/root "<RE_FRAME2>/implementation/<artefact-dir>"` -- core, adapters/reagent (or adapters/uix), schemas -- and the Xray git coord to `<RE_FRAME2>/tools/xray`, so every coord resolves from the one reviewed checkout the skill already located for the generator. That is the sibling-checkout recipe deps-versions.md:121-129 teaches with `../re-frame2`, applied with the absolute path; point at it rather than restating it. title: skill(re-frame2-xray): tab mnemonics taught as key-wired (m opens the active mode tab) — they are tooltip letters only; no bare-letter tab handler exists, tab-jump is the palette verb
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:94-95` (§The inventory): "Static mode holds **5**: **Machines · Routes · Schemas · Flows · Interceptors** (mnemonics are mode-scoped — `m` opens the active mode's tab)."

`skills/re-frame2-xray/references/panels.md:60-62` (§Static mode): "Mnemonics are mode-scoped (`m` here opens the Static Machines browse, not the Dynamic instance-inspector)."

Both sentences affirm that pressing a bare letter opens a tab.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panel_registry.cljc:44-50` (the `reg-l4-tab!` entry contract):

    :mnem   string — single-letter LABEL mnemonic, rendered into the
                     tab button's `title` ("Trace (t)") by both
                     shells and read by nothing else. Not a key: no
                     bare-letter tab handler exists in
                     `keybinding.cljs`, and tab-jump is a
                     command-palette verb (spec/007 §Trimmed pending
                     demand).

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/shell.cljs:69`: "`:mnem` into each tab button's `title` and are read by nothing else". Dynamic shell: `shell.cljs:2186` ("mnemonic letter is exposed via the `title` attribute") and `:2221` `:title (str label " (" mnem ")")`.

`keybinding.cljs` `spine-key-id` (:265-310) maps exactly Space / l / G / j / k / , / s; there is no `m`, `e`, `a`, … arm, and `handle-keydown` (:330-418) has no tab branch. The shipped keyboard-first tab jump is the palette: `palette/sources.cljc:78-91` `panel-items` → "Open <label> panel", `:368-378` `static-tab-items` → "Open <label> (Static)".

## IMPACT

A wrong hotkey taught. It contradicts the skill's own §Wired hotkeys ("Only these are wired") and §Style guidance ("Don't invent controls … cite `keybinding.cljs`"). A user told "press `m`" gets nothing, and the mode-scoping explanation is built on the false premise. The `e a v t m r s g u h` roster itself is correct (the drift gate pins the `:mnem` values) — only the "opens" verb is wrong.

## FIX SHAPE

Prose only, two files. Reword both sentences: mnemonics are the parenthesised letter in each tab button's tooltip (`Trace (t)`), a label hint, not a key; keyboard tab-jump is `Cmd/Ctrl+K` → "Open <tab> panel" / "Open <tab> (Static)". Keep the roster and the Mnem columns in panels.md / shared-components.md (relabel the column header to "Tooltip letter" if wanted). No tools/xray change.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_xray_tab_inventory_drift.py --verbose` must stay green (it pins `:mnem` values, not the verb). The wording itself: no gate — verify by hand (`git grep -n "opens the" -- skills/re-frame2-xray/`).

## ACCEPTANCE

No sentence under `skills/re-frame2-xray/` says a bare letter opens or selects a tab; the palette is named as the keyboard tab-jump; drift gate green.

title: ssr-node crossing (E/6): native-Hicasso product witness — hicasso.server body-only entry + login example server bundle
description:
Slice E of the ssr-node crossing programme — the PRODUCT witness. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 first; this description carries only E's own brief. Depends on D being MERGED. The ruling settled the witness question: it is native Hicasso; a Reagent example does NOT substitute (a Reagent root already renders on the JVM, so Reagent-over-Node proves machinery nobody would ship).

## Scope (fence)

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs`: ADD a body-only entry beside `render`; do NOT change `render`'s settled spellings (naming-ledger row 22, `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md`). Its CLJS test lives in `implementation/hicasso/test/` under the existing `:node-test-hicasso` build (no build change for the test).
- `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/`: extend the ONLY native-Hicasso example rather than start a new app — add `server.cljs` publishing the sidecar module contract (`{protocol, buildId, entries, render}`) with an entry table naming the login root, its `stateAllowlist` and the runtime-partition allowlist from slice C, and a small Clojure `server.clj` wiring `ssr-handler` + `re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer` + `:render-state` + `:payload`. Update the example README.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` (HOT-ZONE — queue): ONE `:examples/login-hicasso-server` `:node-library` build beside `:examples/login-hicasso` (~:1622).
- No Playwright spec under `examples/` (examples are test-free — rf2-8cevm); the witness lives under `implementation/hicasso/test/` or `implementation/ssr-ring/test/`.

## Do

`re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (name is the worker's within the naming ledger's rules): takes the restored snapshot via `render-state/restore!` (slice C) into a FRESH per-request frame — no boot-event replay, no `:snapshot`/`:initial-events` re-seeding — then `mount/tree` + `renderToString` with `:identifier-prefix`, returns the INNER markup only (no payload, no document), tears the frame down in a `finally`, and FAILS the render (throws, which the sidecar turns into a refusal) if the Hicasso runtime recorded a recovered render error during the pass — the JVM's post-render error accumulator cannot see inside the Node frame, so a swallowed error there would ship a wrong page as a success. The module wrapper publishes `render-body` as the entry's `render`. The client boots with `hydrate-root!` and the SAME `identifierPrefix`, reading the `__rf_payload` the JVM wrote.

## Acceptance

1. `npx shadow-cljs compile :examples/login-hicasso-server` and the `:examples/login-hicasso` client build both green; `npm run test:examples-compile` green.
2. An end-to-end test (CLJS in `implementation/hicasso/test`, or JVM in `implementation/ssr-ring/test` — worker's call) proving: the login page is server-rendered from a server-only value that is ABSENT from `__rf_payload`; route or machine runtime state is rendered (the login example has a machine — use it); build-id skew is refused with the distinct code; hydration succeeds with no recoverable error and matching `identifierPrefix`.
3. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` stays green — `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` must still find each login bundle carrying only its own view runtime, and the server bundle must not leak into the browser build.
4. `implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_optional_module_reachability.py` stays green (a browser build must not reach `server.cljs`).
5. Example README updated (build, run the sidecar, run the JVM host, open the page).

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`npm run test:cljs` or the focused `:node-test-hicasso` build (name which); `npm run test:examples-compile`; `npm run test:bundle-isolation`; the reachability script above. Cite CI for the rest.

## Stop and report to Mike

If the login root turns out to need the whole unprojected frame rather than an explicit render snapshot, or cannot hydrate cleanly from the JVM-owned payload. Leave the PR open with what works and say so on this bead.

## Traps

`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` is hot-zone — queue; the testbed/example build-ids and `:dev-http` ports live there. No Playwright under `examples/`. No `git stash`; commit then rebase. Worker worktree guard first; report `WORKTREE_ROOT`. Remove the `node_modules` junction as your last act.
notes:
DISPATCHED 2026-09-02 19:43:14 AUSEST by the mayor. SOLO, LARGE, fresh worktree worker/product-8arzr5 off origin/main 4c351a44ba — the FIRST slice whose whole chain (A #8981, B #8985, C #8982, D #8991) is MERGED beneath it, so the worker builds against the real seams. Premises verified at that tip: render_state/restore! at ~:400; ssr/ring/node.clj renderer at ~:360; hicasso/server.cljs defines payload-script/document/render and no body-only entry; examples/substrates/hicasso/login/ is README+core.cljs+index.html only; shadow-cljs.edn :examples/login-hicasso at ~:1622; both named gates exist (check_optional_module_reachability.py, test:bundle-isolation releasing six builds). Brief foregrounds the error-accumulator clause as THE risk (a swallowed recovered render error inside the Node frame ships a wrong page as a success, invisible to the JVM accumulator) and repeats the bead's STOP condition verbatim as Mike's call, not a problem to engineer around. shadow-cljs.edn authorised as the one hot-zone touch, own commit. Fence: worker/hicptr-slril is live in implementation/hicasso/** but its remaining carriers are forms.cljs + impl/mount.cljs + one test — server.cljs is NOT among them, so the two are file-disjoint; the worker re-derives before its first hicasso edit.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-02. Three findings the mayor should carry to slice F / Mike.

(1) THE ACCUMULATOR INSTRUMENT IS NOT THE ONE THE BEAD IMPLIED, and it was settled by measurement. The bead's clause names 'the JVM's post-render error accumulator' — re-frame.ssr's per-frame pending-error-traces buffer. The first cut of render-body used exactly that, and its refusal row RENDERED MARKUP: Hicasso reads its subscriptions through the pure compute-sub path (impl.collector's cold read), whose :rf.error/sub-exception record is stamped ':frame nil' BY CONSTRUCTION and documented as such in re-frame.subs ('a compute-sub-driven SSR harness that wants the per-frame projection must use the reactive subscribe path'). candidate-frame-for-error returns nil for such a record, so the buffer never fills and a per-frame check reads CLEAN on the exact failure the clause exists to catch. render-body therefore watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream (rf/register-listener! :errors) for the extent of the render — strictly stronger, since that stream is what the per-frame buffer is filled FROM, plus the frame-nil records it drops. NOTE THE STANDING IMPLICATION: server/render (the whole-page door, unchanged here) has the same blindness on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host today.

(2) ACCEPTANCE 2 ASKS FOR TWO PROPERTIES THAT CANNOT BOTH HOLD OF ONE RENDER, and this is Mike's call rather than a defect. 'Server-rendered from a server-only value ABSENT from __rf_payload' and 'hydration succeeds with no recoverable error' are incompatible on the same node: the hydrating client renders from the payload, so a node the two halves disagree about is one React recovers. That is React, not re-frame2. The witness proves BOTH, on two render-state/payload configurations of the same page, and MEASURES the tension (its section 6 is clean; its section 7 costs exactly one recovered adoption). The shipped example ships the clean configuration and the rule — a render-state key the payload does not carry must not change the markup — is stated in the README and beside the sub in core.cljs. If Mike wants the example page itself to carry a rendered server-only value, that is a decision to accept one recovered adoption per page.

(3) host.clj IS THE WIRING, NOT A RUNNING SERVER, and one file outside this slice's fence is why. A JVM host must hold the application's state, so login.model has to be loadable from Clojure; it is examples/core/login/model.cljs and the single line keeping it CLJS-only is a localStorage write in the demo session fx. Making it .cljc is a change to a file all three login arms share. Named in host.clj and in the README.

Two smaller notes for slice F (rf2-8arzr.6): spec/009's :rf.error/ssr-render-failed row now has a SECOND emitter (re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body) — the id was reused rather than a new one minted because spec/*.md was fenced out of this dispatch; and examples/substrates/README.md + examples/README.md describe the three login arms without mentioning the server build.

One deviation from the bead's text, with its reason: the Clojure host is host.clj / ns hicasso.login.host, NOT server.clj. ClojureScript implicitly requires foo/bar.clj as the MACRO namespace of a foo/bar.cljs, so a server.clj beside server.cljs would be loaded into every compile of the server bundle, as macros, on a classpath with no Ring on it.

## Post-close: PR #8997 CI fix (rf2-8arzr.5, follow-on worker, 2026-09-02)

The bead's change was complete but PR #8997 was red on one check, `tests :: JS
harness self-tests`. Fixed on the same branch without changing what the change
does. Recorded here because the PR's file set grew by two files the bead's own
work did not touch.

RED ASSERTION (implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs):
  parseExampleBuilds(shadow-cljs.edn) is non-vacuous and every build has out+init
  -> build examples/login-hicasso-server missing :init-fn

CAUSE, and it is a real one rather than a test artefact: the assertion held
out+init of EVERY `:examples/*` build, which was true only because all 43 of
them were `:browser` pages. This slice adds the first that is not. A
`:node-library` publishes an `:exports-var` for the Node sidecar to `require`;
it carries no `:init-fn` and no colocated index.html because it is not a page.

title: ssr-node crossing (D/6): JVM->Node adapter re-frame.ssr.ring.node + JVM->Node->JVM CI witness on a fixture module
description:
Slice D of the ssr-node crossing programme. Parent rf2-8arzr's RULING note (2026-09-02, delegated by Mike) is the canonical record: read its shared contract S1-S7 (S5, S6, S7 especially) first; this description carries only D's own brief. Depends on A, B and C being MERGED (not merely closed).

## Scope (fence)

- New `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/node.clj` (the adapter), `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn` (+ `org.clojure/data.json`; if `implementation/deps.edn` aliases must also see it, that file is HOT-ZONE — sequence), `implementation/ssr-ring/test/**` including a plain-JS fixture render module under `implementation/ssr-ring/test/fixtures/node/` (the eight-line `{protocol, buildId, entries, render}` shape ssr-node's own fixtures use — no React, no CLJS build).
- `.github/workflows/test.yml`: one new job (HOT-ZONE — queue behind any in-flight workflow toucher). The classifier pair (`.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` + `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs`) ONLY if a new output is genuinely needed, and then both halves in ONE commit; prefer composing the existing `ssr_node` and JVM-implementation outputs.
- `spec/011-SSR.md`: one stanza for the Node renderer's construction opts and error codes (HOT-ZONE).

## Do

`(re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer {:endpoint "http://127.0.0.1:8148" :entry "app/root" :args <edn> :build-id "..." :timeout-ms 1000 ...})` returns the fn slice A's `:renderer` opt expects. Per request, inside the frame scope: `render-state/project` on the live frame (slice C) -> per-key EDN text for both partitions -> `POST /render` with `protocol 1`, `entry`, `args`, `state`, the runtime partition (C's spelling), `buildId`, `timeoutMs`, `requestId` -> Node's body bytes returned as `:body-html`, `:render-hash nil` (a native root carries no structural hash — S1). Construction validation: entry, args, render-state policy, build id, endpoint and timeouts are required for the Node renderer; `:root-view` is not (A made it conditional).

Transport (S6): ONE `java.net.http.HttpClient` per renderer, built at construction and reused; EVERY request carries an explicit timeout = `timeoutMs` + the sidecar's admission budget + a wire margin, derived by the adapter (add a knob only if you find one necessary). JSON via `org.clojure/data.json` — accepted by the ruling as ssr-ring's one new dependency. Build skew: the sidecar already refuses on `buildId` mismatch; additionally compare `x-rf-ssr-build` on success defensively and throw a distinct code if it differs.

Errors (S5): a transport failure (connection refused, read timeout), a sidecar refusal (`x-rf-ssr-refusal` present; 4xx/503/504/500) and a sidecar render failure ALL throw at the render call site with a live frame, so ALL route through the EXISTING render-failure projection (`ssr/project-render-exception!` -> the `:error-view` side of spec/011's division, ~:1428-1450) as a projected 5xx — with DISTINCT codes (e.g. `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable`, `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused` carrying the refusal code in ex-data, `:rf.error/ssr-node-deadline`). NEVER copy the sidecar's HTTP status to the browser response. `:on-error` keeps its existing meaning. No partial success page is possible: the body render fails before any shell is assembled.

## The crossing witness (a new test.yml job, named for what it is: the JVM -> Node -> JVM crossing)

A dedicated ssr-ring test alias (`:crossing-test`, so the default `:test` alias stays Node-free) that: spawns slice B's `serve` launcher via `ProcessBuilder` with the fixture module on port 0, parses B's ready line, constructs `ssr-handler` with the Node renderer, and proves —
(a) the JVM drains `:initial-events` FIRST and the fixture receives the drained value through the state partition (the fixture echoes a state value into its markup);
(b) the response is a complete JVM-owned document — JVM head, `__rf_payload` built from the JVM app-db, JVM shell/status/headers — with Node's body bytes inserted verbatim;
(c) render-state != payload: a server-only key is rendered by the fixture and ABSENT from `__rf_payload`;
(d) ONE refusal-or-deadline arm: a fixture entry that sleeps past `timeoutMs` -> sidecar 504 -> projected 5xx through `:error-view`, distinct code, no partial page (a refusal arm — a key the entry does not allowlist — is an acceptable substitute if the deadline arm proves flaky under CI load);
(e) cleanup on success AND on failure: the JVM request frame is destroyed (frame registry empty) and the sidecar's `/health` shows no in-flight work;
(f) ONE observational complete-crossing timing printed to the job log — a number, not a threshold.
Kill the launcher in a `finally`. The job needs `setup-node` 24 and the JVM toolchain; copy the shape of the existing JVM jobs.

## Acceptance

Everything above; existing ssr-ring, ssr and ssr-node lanes green; the spec/011 stanza; and while in `test.yml`, correct the stale comment at ~:5123 ("73 rows across 7 suites" — 8 suites since before this programme; slice B raised it to 9).

## Gates (foreground, to completion)

`clojure -M:test` AND `clojure -M:crossing-test` in `implementation/ssr-ring` (Node 24 on PATH). The new CI job is the gate for the witness — cite its green run by URL in the PR body.

## Traps

Pass the FULL 40-char head oid to `gh run list --commit` (from `gh pr view --json headRefOid`); job keys need TWO leading spaces in the merge-criterion grep; `.github/workflows/*` is hot-zone; never pipe a gate through `tail`; no `git stash`; worker worktree guard first, report `WORKTREE_ROOT`.
