title: skill-improver: detection algorithm still clears validated durable body reads
description:
## Scope

Correct the durable body-read guidance and behavioural fixture in skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md and skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json (behav-schemaless-body-read-trap, id 28). Keep the existing boundary-validation lesson, catalogue shape, and tool-agnostic eval workflow.

## Correctness finding

Eval 28 explicitly treats an inline always-on Malli validation as a complete acceptable fix for query parameters read from js/window.location.search and written into app-db. Validation closes the trust boundary, but it does not turn the live host read into a recorded fact. The same event replayed after the browser URL changes folds different filters into durable state.

This is not merely incomplete prose: the fixture's expected_output and graded expectations affirmatively pass the replay-unsafe rewrite. Because SKILL.md routes by matching leaves, an agent can follow the schemaless-events leaf, satisfy every eval assertion, and leave the critical durable-write contract broken. The leaf's own later regression callout and imperative-effects.md state the opposite rule.

## Evidence

- evals/evals.json:214-222 supplies a handler that reads js/window.location.search and writes params to [:search :filters]. Lines 215 and 222 say an inline m/validate in the handler is "equally acceptable" and needs no recordable marker, despite calling the destination durable.
- references/schemaless-events.md:105-124 says this exact class crosses two boundaries: validation closes trust, while durable app-db requires a recordable generator or event payload; inline validation alone is sufficient only when the body-read does not feed durable state.
- references/imperative-effects.md:46-57 requires every host fact used by a returned :db/runtime/resource/snapshot/ledger write to be recorded, never read ambiently at the write site.
- skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/cofx.md:58-68 and 95-125 defines ambient suppliers as replayed live reads and the recordable generator as the application-owned path for localStorage/sessionStorage/other host facts feeding durable state.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:15-24 implements that distinction: ambient suppliers are never recorded and rerun on replay; recordable values are captured and replayed verbatim. Lines 1067-1077 implement verbatim delivery or token write-back.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/cofx_cljs_test.cljc:1053-1070 is the executable control: a supplied/replayed recordable value wins and the generator does not run.
- docs/EP/EP-0010-causal-world-inputs.md:387-389 states the invariant directly: a world input affecting a durable write must come from a causal token or captured recordable coeffect, not an ambient host read.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run behavioural eval id 28 with the current skill.
2. Return a critique that correctly flags missing production validation but proposes only an unconditional validation branch around params, leaving js/window.location.search and URLSearchParams construction inside the event handler before the same assoc-in write.
3. Grade that answer against expectations 221-222. It passes: both assertions explicitly accept inline m/validate/m/coerce and require recordability only when the answer happens to choose a cofx.
4. Dispatch [:search/apply-url-filters] while the host URL contains ?q=alpha&page=1&sort=asc; record the event and resulting app-db.
5. Change the host URL to ?q=beta&page=2&sort=desc and replay the same event. The inline-only rewrite rereads the host and writes beta/2/desc, so the same causal token does not reproduce the original state.
6. Control: materialise and validate the params through a reg-cofx recordable generator (or carry the already-materialised value in the event payload), replay with the captured value, and observe alpha/1/asc both times without rereading the host.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A user asks the improver to fix a boundary handler that hydrates durable search state from the URL. The critique recommends an always-on validation branch and the eval marks it correct. The deployed app now rejects malformed values, but epoch restore, SSR hydration, and time-travel still read whichever URL is live during replay. A historical event can therefore produce a new route state and trigger different downstream subscriptions/effects.

Invariant: validation and causality are independent. An untrusted host value must be validated before use; when it affects durable state it must also be represented on the causal token as an event payload or recordable coeffect. A live inline body-read cannot satisfy the second requirement.

## Recommended minimal fix

- Revise eval 28's expected_output and expectations to reject any purported complete fix that leaves the URL read inside the durable-writing handler, even when it validates params unconditionally.
- Require the normal passing rewrite to materialise and validate the URL params through an application-owned reg-cofx recordable generator (preferably using cofx :schema for the always-on gate), or to carry a previously materialised validated fact in the event payload.
- Narrow the early body-read wording in schemaless-events.md so inline m/validate/m/coerce is described as sufficient only for non-durable destinations, matching its existing regression callout. Do not duplicate the cofx tutorial; link to the existing durable/diagnostic fork.
- Exercise the revised existing fixture rather than introducing a generic eval runner or a new catalogue leaf.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eval 28 no longer calls an inline validation-only rewrite acceptable for its durable [:search :filters] write. Its expected_output and graded assertions require either a recordable coeffect or event-payload fact, plus always-on validation.
2. The positive witness proposes a reg-cofx with :recordable? true and an always-on schema/validation gate, declares it via :rf.cofx/requires, and makes the handler fold the delivered value without reading js/window.location.search.
3. The negative control is the former inline-only response: it retains the in-handler URL read and adds a correct m/validate branch. It must fail the replay-safety expectation even though it passes the trust-boundary expectation. This proves the revised grade is non-vacuous and distinguishes the two contracts.
4. A second control response that materialises a validated value in the event payload passes without requiring a cofx, proving the criterion checks recordability rather than one preferred spelling.
5. Run the updated id-28 behavioural eval through the documented with-skill workflow for three runs and record per-expectation results. All with-skill runs reject the inline-only fix and accept a replay-safe fix.
6. The catalogue text consistently says inline validation alone is sufficient only when no durable state depends on the body-read; references/schemaless-events.md, references/imperative-effects.md, and eval 28 no longer contradict one another.
7. The existing focused cofx tests covering captured/replayed values remain green, and scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py passes for the edited fixture. Restoring the phrase that inline validation is equally acceptable for the durable prompt must make the negative control fail.

## Non-goals

- No runtime cofx, epoch, schema, or replay redesign; those contracts already exist and are tested.
- No new anti-pattern leaf, generic linter, automatic source scanner, eval platform, or compatibility layer.
- No requirement that every untrusted non-durable value use a recordable coeffect; inline always-on validation remains valid when the value does not affect durable state.
- No expansion into URL parsing policy, routing architecture, Malli schema design, or unrelated improver fixtures.
- No weakening of :rf.schema/at-boundary for genuine event-payload boundaries.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title, description, and notes searches covered improver, schemaless, body-read, recordable cofx, URLSearchParams, inline validation, durable write, replay boundary, and epoch-restore. No bead owns this fixture contradiction.

rf2-uhszv is the closed broad improver workflow review; it explicitly preserved replay-determinism and did not identify or repair eval 28's inline-validation exception. rf2-ov144 concerns a public replay-by-epoch-id gesture, not whether this skill teaches recorded inputs. rf2-6eh5h concerns falsey schema declaration presence in the runtime, not ambient body-reads or the improver eval. rf2-iyjae concerns WebSocket example trust boundaries, not this URL/replay guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Eval 28 must fail an inline-validation-only answer for its durable URL read and pass both replay-safe controls (recordable validating cofx and validated event payload); the documented three-run behavioural exercise, focused cofx tests, and check_skill_eval_docs.py must pass, with the former inline-only answer retained as the non-vacuity control.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-09-01 PR #8833 — REOPEN. The revised body-read bullet, regression example, and eval 28 correctly require both always-on validation and a recorded fact for a durable write, but the same leaf normative Detection logic still says at line 17: classify event-payload vs body-read; matching gate present means not a finding. An inline always-on m/validate is the matching body-read trust gate, so this algorithm still clears exactly the former inline-only rewrite even though it remains replay-unsafe. That directly contradicts line 12 and the revised eval expectation. Minimal fix: make the decision two-stage — require a matching trust validator, then, when the body-read feeds durable state, require a recorded fact; only clear the finding when every applicable boundary is closed. No new gate or harness. The independent rf2-uhszv sibling-routing repair holds.
TREE CHECK OWED 2026-09-01 14:15 AUSEST by the mayor. A merged commit cites this item — d3f992a034 'fix(skills/improver): eval 28 requires the durable URL read be recorded, not just validated (rf2-0o5dx)', on origin/main. That is NOT sufficient to close it and I have deliberately not done so: this item's title says the detection algorithm STILL clears validated durable body reads, and 'still' is the word that suggests the item POSTDATES a partial fix rather than being satisfied by it. Closing on a commit-subject match would be the same error as validating an item against its own text — one level up.

SO THE FIRST TASK OF WHOEVER TAKES THIS is to establish, at tip and at source, whether d3f992a034 satisfies this item, partially addresses it, or is the very change the item was filed against. A verified 'already fixed' closes it; a verified 'that commit is what I am complaining about' is equally complete. Neither is assumed here.
close_reason:
Verified DONE at the tree, not at the item text. Commit d3f992a034 is an ancestor of origin/main and touches exactly the two files this items Scope names: skills/re-frame2-improver/evals/evals.json and skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md.

Negative check with a control: the phrase this item cites at evals.json:215 and :222 -- "equally acceptable" -- now returns count 0 in that file, while the control string behav-schemaless-body-read-trap returns 1, so grep did read the file. A zero without that control would not have been a check.

Positive check, which is the half a matching commit cannot supply: the fix is not a deletion of the offending clause. The rewritten expected_output requires the complete fix to close TWO independent boundaries (TRUST via an always-on validate, REPLAY via a recorded fact), and the graded expectations now REJECT as incomplete any fix leaving the js/window.location.search read inside the durable-writing handler -- inline always-on validate explicitly included. It grades recordability rather than one spelling: an application-owned recordable reg-cofx generator OR an already-materialised params map on the event payload both pass.

Better than the item asked for: the former inline-only rewrite is RETAINED as the fixtures own non-vacuity control -- it must pass the trust-boundary expectation and fail the replay-safety one, so a future regression of this exact defect makes the fixture fail rather than silently re-passing.

The items title ("still clears validated durable body reads") is false at tip. That word "still" is what made the tree check owed.

title: bug(examples): Linearlite classifies its simulated 503 as a transport failure
description:
## Scope

Correct the executable failure contract in `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs` and pin it in the existing `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs` composition suite. This is the Linearlite demo backend's armed "Fail the next write" path only; the managed-HTTP and mutation runtimes are behaving according to their published contracts.

## Correctness finding

Linearlite says its armed demo backend answers the next write with HTTP 503, but it calls the direct `:rf.http/managed-canned-failure` effect with the failure under `:failure`. That effect's locked args contract is top-level `:kind` plus `:tags`; it ignores `:failure` and therefore defaults to `{:kind :rf.http/transport}`. The mutation still receives `:status :error`, so rollback visibly works and masks the incorrect failure classification.

## Evidence

- `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:365-373` builds `{:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :status 503 :message ...}` and passes it as `:failure` to the registered canned-failure handler.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:184-208` reads only top-level `:kind` and `:tags`, defaulting them to `:rf.http/transport` and `{}`. `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1092-1097`, `spec/API.md:398`, and `docs/api/re-frame.http.md:321-336` publish that same shape.
- A JVM probe of the real canned handler with Linearlite's args produced `[:settle {:status :error, :error {:kind :rf.http/transport}}]`. The positive control using top-level `:kind :rf.http/http-5xx` and `:tags {:status 503 :message "simulated"}` produced `[:settle {:status :error, :error {:status 503, :message "simulated", :kind :rf.http/http-5xx}}]`.
- The example repeatedly promises a 503 in `core.cljs` (namespace narrative and backend comments) and `README.md:67-71,126-130`.
- The existing example suite explicitly says it bypasses the example's fail-next-write seam (`linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs:23-32`) and manually injects a correctly classified 5xx failure at lines 312-350. It proves generic mutation rollback, not the runnable backend that users execute.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Invoke the real `re-frame.http.test-support/emit-canned-failure!` handler with a stamped frame, a `:reply-to`, and the same args shape Linearlite supplies: `{:failure {:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :status 503 :message "simulated"}}`; capture the late-bound router dispatch.
2. Observe the reply is `{:status :error :error {:kind :rf.http/transport}}`: the intended kind, status, and message were discarded.
3. Repeat with the published direct-effect shape `{:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :tags {:status 503 :message "simulated"}}`.
4. Observe the control reply retains `{:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :status 503 :message "simulated"}` under `:error`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A programmer runs the example, arms "Fail the next write", and executes a mutation. The optimistic board change correctly rolls back, but `[:rf/mutation {:instance ...}]` stores a transport failure with no HTTP status rather than the promised `:rf.http/http-5xx` / 503 failure. Any Xray inspection, response middleware, or copied application branch over the documented closed HTTP failure taxonomy observes a false cause. The runnable example's invariant is: an armed write must settle through the same canonical 503 envelope the example says it synthesises, while retaining the visible optimistic-apply -> rollback arc.

## Recommended minimal fix

Pass the canned-failure effect its existing public shape directly: keep `:after-ms`, set top-level `:kind :rf.http/http-5xx`, and put `:status 503` plus the message in top-level `:tags`. Add one focused test through the actual registered Linearlite demo stub instead of another hand-built failure reply. Do not add support for the erroneous `:failure` alias to managed HTTP; this is pre-alpha and one call site should conform to the one existing contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused CLJS test drives the actual registered `:linearlite.demo/http-stub` failure path (not the suite's capturing transport and not a manually appended failure reply): it loads a board, arms `:linearlite/set-fail-next-write`, and dispatches one real example write.
- Non-vacuity: before the deferred reply settles, the test proves the write request reached the demo stub and the board contains the optimistic change; after settle, it proves the board equals its exact pre-write value and the mutation instance is terminal `:error` with `:optimistic? false`.
- The same test asserts the stored public mutation `:error` carries `:kind :rf.http/http-5xx`, `:status 503`, and the demo message, and asserts the one-shot flag was disarmed. It must fail against the current `:rf.http/transport` result.
- Positive control: an otherwise equivalent unarmed write through the same actual demo stub settles `:success` and commits, proving the test is selecting the armed branch rather than passing because every request fails or no reply ran.
- The existing create, retitle, and status optimistic apply/commit/rollback assertions remain green; no live network is contacted.
- From `implementation/`, `npm run test:cljs -- --test=re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test` passes with a non-zero test/assertion count, and `npm run test:examples-compile` still compiles `examples/linearlite`.

## Non-goals

- Changing the managed-HTTP canned-failure contract, accepting compatibility aliases, or changing failure taxonomy.
- Refactoring mutation rollback, optimistic conflict policy, the demo board, routing, mount code, or the 220 ms illustrative delay.
- Adding a browser automation suite or revising the separate capability README launch instructions.
- Generalising the demo backend or adding production transport behavior.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title, description, and notes searches covered `linearlite`, `fail next`, `fail-next-write`, `managed-canned-failure`, `canned failure`, `HTTP 503`, `http-5xx`, `rollback seam`, `generic transport`, `simulated server failure`, `failure stub`, `failure envelope`, and `failure taxonomy`. No duplicate was found. `rf2-ujdn0` concerns stale capability README launch commands only; it does not touch Linearlite runtime behavior. `rf2-lddbk` concerns successful live-response metadata through HTTP `:after` middleware, not canned failure classification. `rf2-hic-027` mentions a rollback seam on an unrelated Hicasso test facade.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A focused CLJS test uses the actual `:linearlite.demo/http-stub`, arms fail-next-write, proves an optimistic change exists before settle, then proves exact rollback, one-shot disarm, and mutation error `{:kind :rf.http/http-5xx :status 503 ...}` after settle.
2. An unarmed control through the same stub succeeds and commits; both arms prove requests/replies actually ran.
3. `npm run test:cljs -- --test=re-frame.linearlite-example-cljs-test` reports non-zero tests/assertions and passes; `npm run test:examples-compile` still compiles `examples/linearlite`.
4. No managed-HTTP alias or unrelated runtime/refactor work is introduced.
close_reason: Landed by PR #8845 (merged 2026-09-01T02:51:20Z), commits 9ddeac52ba 'fix(examples/linearlite): classify the armed demo 503 per the canned-failure contract' and 58d8ac27b3 'test(linearlite): pin the armed demo backend's 503 classification at the stub seam' — both verified present on origin/main. The bead was left in_progress because its worker did not survive to close it; the work itself is complete and merged.

title: check-examples-assets: missing main.js bootstrap passes the host-page gate
description:
## Scope

The monorepo example host-page contract in examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs and its focused executable coverage in implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs. Cover every index.html and *.index.html already enumerated by listExampleIndexHtml, including ordinary apps, auxiliary Story hosts, and baked SSR/hydration hosts. Do not change application source, the staging runner, or the test-free examples policy.

## Correctness finding

The gate proves that every example host references the shared favicon, OG raster, and stylesheet, but it does not prove that the host loads the compiled application entrypoint. BUILD_OUTPUTS contains main.js only so reference resolution can skip a generated file; absence is never an error. A host with the only <script src="main.js"></script> line deleted therefore passes the live asset scan even though the canonical runner stages and serves a page that cannot boot, render, or hydrate.

This is a cross-example false green rather than a cosmetic metadata gap. The same miss applies to all host shapes the scanner advertises as covered. The independent compile gate compiles shadow-cljs build definitions and never consumes their HTML, while headless example wrappers require namespaces directly and likewise do not prove that a browser host loads main.js.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a disposable checkout, remove the <script src="main.js"></script> line from examples/core/counter/index.html while leaving its favicon, stylesheet, and og:image references intact.
2. Run node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs. It still reports all example host pages plus the shared tree as valid and exits 0.
3. Run node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs. Its live scan also remains green because it asserts only the errors produced by the same production scanner.
4. Launch the counter through the canonical dev:example runner. The staged index has no bundle entrypoint, so the browser shows no counter and executes none of counter.core/run.

The failure is reproducible without editing the checkout by wrapping fs.readFileSync for one real page, returning its contents with the main.js script removed, and passing that io to scanPage. That exact read-only probe returned errors=[] for examples/core/counter/index.html, examples/core/login/stories.index.html, and examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/index.html.

## Evidence

- examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs:201-209 defines REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS as favicon.svg, og.png, and style.css only.
- Lines 298-300 define BUILD_OUTPUTS = new Set(['main.js']) solely to avoid resolving generated output as a repository source file.
- Lines 558-663 already classify <script src> references distinctly in the shared HTML inventory, so the scanner has the information needed for a precise boot check.
- Lines 1517-1524 skip main.js during local resolution; lines 1539-1563 enforce only REQUIRED_SHARED_ASSETS. No later scanPage branch requires a script entrypoint.
- Lines 1904-1911 run that same scanPage logic over every enumerated host. The live regression at implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs:308-316 therefore inherits the omission.
- All 32 currently enumerated hosts contain a main.js script reference, which establishes a uniform current invariant rather than an exception-driven policy.
- Removing the script in memory from one ordinary host, one *.index.html Story host, and one SSR host produced only the three remaining shared refs and zero scanner errors in each case.
- examples/TESTING.md:17-20 separates compile, headless CLJS, browser-DOM, and static asset gates. None of those other lanes visits every example host page.

## Failure scenario / invariant

Every monorepo-staged example host must contain a load-bearing script reference to the generated main.js entrypoint. If that reference is deleted, commented out, or changed into a non-loading href, the host is not runnable and the always-run host-page gate must fail. Merely mentioning main.js in an anchor, canonical link, preload, comment, or other generic href must not satisfy the invariant; the proof must come from the existing tagged <script src> inventory.

Without this invariant, an index-only change can merge with a green compile, green headless tests, and green asset scan while the documented one-command runner deterministically serves a blank or non-hydrating page.

## Recommended minimal fix

Reuse extractHtmlReferenceInventory's existing assets rows and add one explicit scanPage check for a tagged <script src> whose normalized ref is main.js. Report the host path and missing entrypoint. Keep BUILD_OUTPUTS' current resolution exemption: generated main.js should be required as a host reference, not looked up in the source tree.

Add one focused synthetic mutation test plus a tag-specific negative control. No parser replacement, build-to-page registry, browser matrix, or new gate is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. scanPage reports a clear violation naming the page and main.js when an otherwise valid host carries every shared asset but has no <script src="main.js">.
2. The check consumes the existing tagged asset inventory: <a href="main.js">, <link href="main.js">, text, and commented-out script markup do not satisfy it.
3. A canonical quoted or unquoted <script src="main.js"> remains green, including the scanner's existing query/hash normalization behavior; main.js remains exempt from source-file existence resolution.
4. A focused test mutates a real currently enumerated host in memory by removing only its live main.js script, asserts the mutation actually removed one script, and proves the production scan turns red. This is the non-vacuity control and must fail against the pre-fix implementation.
5. The live test enumerates a non-empty host set and proves every current index.html and *.index.html passes the new invariant; ordinary, auxiliary Story, and SSR hosts are represented without hard-coding a second build roster.
6. node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs, node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs, and npm run test:script-policy from implementation pass after the fix.

## Non-goals

- Running every example in Playwright or asserting application-specific DOM behavior.
- Resolving generated main.js as a repository source file or inspecting its bytes.
- Supporting alternate legacy bundle names, optional entrypoints, or a generalized HTML/build manifest when every current host uses main.js.
- Changing example apps, shared CSS/images, launch documentation, shadow-cljs builds, or staging behavior.
- Replacing the focused HTML inventory with a general-purpose parser.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for main.js example host, script src main.js, missing main.js, example host page, blank example page, check-examples-assets build output, entrypoint host page, runnable example HTML, and examples asset gate. A full all-status scan of 1,127 issue titles, descriptions, and acceptance fields for main.js, script src, blank page, host page/HTML, example asset, runnable example, and entrypoint found no issue enforcing this invariant.

Open rf2-iacw2 and rf2-ujdn0 address stale core/capability README commands and prove the existing dev runner can stage a complete page; they do not make the host scanner reject a missing boot script. Open rf2-fmns2 adds a distinct Hicasso example and bundle-isolation coverage. None is a duplicate or owns this scanner/test slice.

## Priority rationale

P2. The repository is pre-alpha and every current host is intact, so this is not an active production outage. However, one ordinary HTML-line deletion breaks the primary runnable-example contract across every example family while all mandatory gates that claim compile/host coverage remain green. The fix is small, central, and directly restores trust in an existing always-run gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- scanPage rejects an otherwise valid host that lacks a live tagged <script src="main.js"> and names both the page and entrypoint.
- Generic hrefs, preload links, text, and commented script markup containing main.js do not satisfy the requirement.
- Quoted and unquoted live main.js script references remain accepted, and generated main.js is still not resolved as a source file.
- A focused in-memory mutation of a real enumerated host removes exactly one main.js script and turns the production scanner red; the control fails on the pre-fix implementation.
- The non-empty live host inventory, including ordinary, Story auxiliary, and SSR hosts, remains green.
- The focused scanner test, scanner CLI, and implementation test:script-policy gate pass.
notes:
--- 2026-09-01 AUSEST — implemented, PR #8855 ---

FINDING CONFIRMED at tip before implementing. A read-only in-memory probe over
the real tree (wrapping readFileSync for one page, returning it with the live
main.js script removed) returned errors=[] from the pre-fix scanPage, and the
CLI still printed "all 32 pages resolve their assets and carry the required
_shared contract". The gate proved every host was DRESSED (favicon + OG raster +
stylesheet) but never that it could RUN.

FIX. scanPage gains one check reading the EXISTING tagged asset inventory for a
live <script src> whose normalised ref is main.js (new exported predicate
loadsBuildEntrypoint, a pure function over the `assets` view). No new parser, no
build-to-page manifest. Because the proof comes from the tagged view rather than
raw HTML, a mere mention does not satisfy it: preload/modulepreload links are
tagged as links not scripts, <a href> and rel=canonical never reach `assets` at
all, prose is not a tag, and commented markup is stripped before extraction.
BUILD_OUTPUTS' resolution exemption is UNCHANGED — main.js is required as a page
REFERENCE and still never resolved as a source file. Quoted/single-quoted/
unquoted forms and the existing ?query/#hash normalisation all stay green.
The CLI failure epilogue now names the boot-script cause too.

CONTROL (AC4). The non-vacuity control mutates a REAL enumerated host in memory,
one per host shape, with the shape classified from the ENUMERATED PATH rather
than a second hard-coded build roster (which could drift from
listExampleIndexHtml). It asserts exactly one script element was removed — by
byte length AND against the scanner's own inventory in both directions — then
proves the production scanner turns red for that reason alone (errors.length===1).

RED-BEFORE EVIDENCE. The check was neutralised at its scanPage call site to
reproduce the pre-fix implementation: captured exit 1, 9 failures, all of them
the new boot-contract tests; the control reported "(no errors — the pre-fix
false green)" and the CLI under the same plant still printed "all 32 pages …
valid". The other 157 assertions passed under the plant, so the fault was scoped
and stopped no other namespace. Restored and verified by git blob hash against
the committed object, not by reading a diff. An earlier plant that neutralised
the shared helper instead was discarded: it tripped the control at its inventory
assertion rather than at the production scan — weaker evidence.

GATES (foreground, exit codes captured to file, final rebased base 4e27fbbe49):
  node implementation/scripts/check-examples-assets.test.cjs  -> exit 0, 166 PASS / 0 FAIL (18 new)
  node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs             -> exit 0, all 32 hosts green
  npm run test:scripts (from implementation/)                 -> exit 0, 122 tests / 122 pass / 0 fail

AC6 PREMISE FAILURE — worth carrying forward. AC6 names `npm run
test:script-policy` from implementation. THAT SCRIPT DOES NOT EXIST, neither on
this branch's base nor on origin/main (no key matching /polic/ in
implementation/package.json in either). The covering gate for
implementation/scripts/*.test.cjs is `npm run test:scripts`, which is what ran;
it executes the focused suite as one of its files (18 new assertions confirmed
present in its log). Future beads citing this gate should name test:scripts.

LIVE SET. 32 enumerated hosts, every one carrying exactly one
`<script src="main.js">` — 30 ordinary index.html (three of them the baked
SSR/hydration hosts under examples/capabilities/ssr/) plus the two Story
auxiliary *.index.html showcase hosts. Uniform invariant, not an
exception-driven policy.

NON-GOALS HONOURED: no application source changed, no staging-runner change, no
example index.html edited (the mutation is in-memory only), examples stay
test-free, no alternate/legacy bundle names or generalised HTML/build manifest,
main.js bytes never inspected.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8855 (commit 23be46c684) — scanPage now requires a live <script src=main.js> read off the existing tagged asset inventory; BUILD_OUTPUTS' resolution exemption unchanged. Control mutates a real enumerated host in memory per host shape and proves the production scan turns red; verified red against the pre-fix implementation (9 failures, control reporting '(no errors — the pre-fix false green)'). Gates: focused suite exit 0 (166 PASS), live scan exit 0 (32 hosts), npm run test:scripts exit 0 (122/122). NB AC6's 'npm run test:script-policy' does not exist on origin/main; the covering gate is 'npm run test:scripts' — see notes.

title: UIx substrate examples require an undeclared uix.dom consumer dependency
description:
## Scope

The copyable dependency contract for the three runnable UIx examples under `examples/substrates/uix/**`, plus the canonical UIx setup snippets they point readers to in `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` and `spec/Conventions.md`. Add a focused clean-consumer regression; do not change UIx runtime behavior.

## Correctness finding

Every UIx substrate example imports `uix.dom` to create and render its React root, but the public downstream dependency recipe supplies only `day8/re-frame2` and `day8/re-frame2-uix`, and names only `com.pitch/uix.core` as the view library. `day8/re-frame2-uix` intentionally does not depend on `com.pitch/uix.dom`; it is test-only in the adapter project. A programmer who follows the documented coordinate recipe and copies any worked UIx mount therefore gets a missing `uix.dom` namespace at compile time. The examples compile in this monorepo only because the top-level Shadow configuration injects `com.pitch/uix.dom`, masking the dependency omission a clean consumer sees.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a clean CLJS consumer with the documented UIx dependency pair from `spec/Conventions.md`: core plus the UIx adapter (use the corresponding local roots before publication), with no direct `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinate.
2. Copy the namespace/mount shape from `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs`, or use the guide's snippet adapted from it. It requires `[uix.dom :as uix-dom]` and calls `uix-dom/create-root` / `uix-dom/render-root`.
3. Compile that consumer on its own classpath. Compilation fails because the required namespace `uix.dom` is unavailable.
4. Add `com.pitch/uix.dom` at the same version as `com.pitch/uix.core`; the identical source compiles. Running the example through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` does not reproduce the failure because that aggregate build injects both UIx artefacts globally.

## Evidence

- `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs` lines 22-25 and 103-112 import `uix.dom` and invoke both root functions. `uix/login/core.cljs` lines 23-31 and 121-150 and `uix/dashboard/core.cljs` lines 29-32 and 354-366 do the same.
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` lines 70-78 presents the coordinate table and lists only `com.pitch/uix.core` for UIx, then its copyable example-derived namespace at lines 89-94 immediately requires `uix.dom`.
- `spec/Conventions.md` lines 1821-1830 says a UIx consumer picks its substrate with only `day8/re-frame2` plus `day8/re-frame2-uix`; no DOM coordinate is shown.
- `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn` lines 20-30 explicitly keeps `com.pitch/uix.dom` out of shipping `:deps` and places it only under the `:test` alias. Thus aliases do not propagate it to downstream consumers.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` lines 14-16 says the aggregate build adds `com.pitch/uix.{core,dom}` so UIx examples resolve, and its top-level `:dependencies` includes both. This ambient monorepo dependency is why existing example compile coverage cannot detect the clean-consumer failure.
- The UIx project template is the positive control: `_uix/deps.edn` lines 30-31 correctly emits both `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` at version 1.4.4.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A worked example advertised as the source for a UIx app's view and mount must compile from the canonical dependency recipe on a clean consumer classpath. It must not rely on an undeclared namespace supplied only by the monorepo's aggregate build. Every namespace directly required by the copyable mount must have an explicit consumer dependency owner.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep the adapter artefact lean: it does not itself require `uix.dom`, so do not make that library transitively mandatory. Instead, make the canonical UIx application dependency recipe include direct, version-locked `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinates, and have each UIx example README point to that complete recipe. Update the guide's coordinate table/snippet and the Conventions consumer block from the same authority. Reuse the template's existing 1.4.4 pair/lockstep convention rather than introduce a second version source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused executable test creates an isolated consumer classpath from the canonical documented UIx application dependency set, without `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` or its global `:dependencies`, and compiles a namespace that requires `uix.core`, `uix.dom`, and `re-frame.adapter.uix` and exercises the example's `create-root` / `render-root` mount surface.
- The test proves the documented dependency set contains direct `com.pitch/uix.core` and `com.pitch/uix.dom` coordinates at the same version, and the clean consumer compile succeeds.
- Non-vacuity/control: removing only `com.pitch/uix.dom` from the fixture makes compilation fail specifically on the missing `uix.dom` namespace; the control must not be satisfied by the monorepo aggregate classpath.
- The counter, login, and dashboard UIx READMEs link or show the complete canonical app dependency recipe, so each runnable example has a low-friction path from source to a standalone consumer.
- The how-to coordinate table and the Conventions UIx `deps.edn` block agree with the executable fixture and the generator template's UIx core/DOM version pair.
- Existing per-example compile coverage and UIx adapter tests remain green.

## Non-goals

- Adding `com.pitch/uix.dom` to the published `day8/re-frame2-uix` POM when the adapter implementation does not require it.
- Changing example events, subscriptions, views, mount behavior, or adapter APIs.
- Redesigning the monorepo aggregate Shadow dependency model.
- Expanding this issue into React/React-DOM npm installation guidance or general project scaffolding.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for `uix.dom`, `UIx DOM dependency`, `missing UIx DOM`, `UIx downstream`, `UIx deps`, `UIx compile namespace`, `UIx copy recipe`, `documented UIx dependencies`, `uix mount dependency`, and `missing namespace uix.dom`, plus descriptions containing `com.pitch/uix.dom`; no matching issue exists. The open `rf2-oz7wr` concerns `rf/reg-view*` returning a component React cannot mount and is unrelated to dependency resolution.

title: bug(realworld-http): cross-slug detail replies overwrite the active article page
description:
## Scope

Fix the managed-HTTP RealWorld article-detail route so its route-driven article and comments reads remain owned by the active /article/:slug identity. Scope is examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs, its external production-source coverage in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs, the request-slice schema only if an explicit active slug is stored, and the managed-HTTP README sentence that currently overstates what the per-slug ids guarantee. Keep the :article/load unified :reply-to example intact as an executable teaching surface.

## Correctness finding

The article page has one unkeyed [:article] slice and one unkeyed [:comments] slice, but requests are keyed by slug. Entering /article/alpha issues request ids [:article/load "alpha"] and [:comments/load "alpha"]; entering /article/beta issues different ids. Managed HTTP supersedes only an older request with the same id, so all four requests remain eligible to deliver.

Neither reply path carries the requested slug. :article/load sends :reply-to [:article/load], while comments send :on-success [:comments/loaded] and :on-failure [:comments/load-failed]. Every success and failure handler then writes its shared slice unconditionally. A slow alpha success can therefore replace already-settled beta article/comments data while the URL and route remain beta; a slow alpha failure can mark beta's slice failed. The request-start branches also retain prior data across an identity change, and article-page renders that retained article and comments while beta is loading, so wrong-route content is observable even without an out-of-order settle.

This contradicts the README's claim that the per-slug request ids stop a slow first request from overwriting a fast second one. The same app's editor already states and implements the correct boundary: a per-slug id does not supersede a different slug, so the requested slug must ride the reply and the app must refuse a settle that no longer belongs to the screen.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Boot the managed-HTTP RealWorld production handlers with a capturing :rf.http/managed override that holds replies.
2. Handle /article/alpha; capture its article and comments requests.
3. Handle /article/beta before alpha settles; capture beta's requests. Observe that alpha and beta use distinct per-slug request ids, so no same-id supersession occurs.
4. Deliver beta's normal article and comments success targets and confirm the public article/comments subscriptions contain beta.
5. Deliver alpha's success targets afterward.

Observed: [:article :data] and [:comments :data] become alpha's values although :rf.route/id is still :realworld.article/show with slug beta. The equivalent late alpha failure writes alpha's error/status over beta. As a non-racy arm, first settle alpha, navigate to beta, hold beta, and observe alpha content remains available to article-page under beta's URL.

## Evidence

- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:103-108 dispatches both :article/load and :comments/load on every /article/:slug match.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:98-128 gives article requests a slug-specific id but a slug-free unified reply target, then writes the shared article slice without checking the current route or request identity.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:142-171 repeats the shape for comments: slug-specific ids, slug-free success/failure vectors, unconditional writes to one comments slice.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:118-120,145-148 preserves prior data when the next slug starts loading; comments.cljs:491-579 renders article/comments data without proving it belongs to the route slug.
- docs/async/http.md:312 defines supersession as reuse of the same :request-id; alpha and beta deliberately do not reuse one.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:118-127,321-371 documents this exact navigation-staleness law and fixes it by carrying the requested slug on both reply branches and refusing a mismatch.
- examples/real-apps/realworld_http/README.md:22 says the per-slug ids stop slow-first/fast-second stale overwrites, which is false for cross-slug navigation at these call sites.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:392-484 covers only one slug with immediately canned replies. Its editor coverage at lines 1766-1885 has the needed held, out-of-order cross-slug shape, but no corresponding article-page receipt.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A reader opens article alpha on a slow connection, then follows or enters a link to article beta. Beta returns first and renders correctly. Alpha returns later, and the page silently changes back to alpha's title, author controls, body, and/or comments while the address bar still says /article/beta. Actions now operate on whichever stale slug is embedded in the rendered data, not necessarily the route the reader chose.

Invariant: a route-keyed read may update current-page state only while its carried key still equals the active slice/route identity. Retained data is valid during a refresh of the same key, never during a transition to a different key.

## Recommended minimal fix

Carry the requested slug in the article unified reply target and in both comments reply targets, and gate success and failure handlers against the active requested slug before changing data, status, timestamps, errors, or UI lifecycle. Record the requested slug on each slice (or an equivalently local identity fact) when the load begins so the gate remains deterministic after navigation. On a slug change, clear the old article/comments data or otherwise make the subscriptions refuse it; preserve keep-previous behavior only for a same-slug refresh.

Keep the per-slug request ids if they remain useful for same-slug retry/supersession, but do not treat them as the correctness boundary. Reuse the small correlation spelling already present in article_editor.cljs; do not introduce a cache layer or a new framework API.

## Non-goals

- No stateful demo-backend work, CRUD persistence, filtering, or session behavior; open bead rf2-9n43e owns that separate backend defect.
- No change to the Resources variant, whose article/comments resources are already keyed by slug.
- No generic remote-data abstraction, route-owned request framework, cache migration, compatibility layer, or broad handler refactor.
- No redesign of article rendering, optimistic comment/favorite behavior, retry policy, route grammar, or the unified-reply teaching example.
- No blanket clearing that removes the intentional same-slug refresh fallback.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title searches for article detail race, stale article, comments race, cross slug, late reply, article load, request correlation, profile race, route identity, and RealWorld race, plus all-status description/notes searches for realworld_http, article detail, comments/load, stale reply, cross-slug, per-slug, wrong article, out-of-order, and navigation staleness, found no issue owning these article-page handlers.

rf2-czvc is closed and fixed the analogous editor-only race; its close record explicitly scopes the carried-slug gate to :editor/load-article, and is implementation/test precedent rather than a duplicate. rf2-9n43e is open but owns temporal semantics in the shared offline backend, not client reply correlation. rf2-1r8u is a closed, verified-no-defect investigation of duplicate route registration ids and does not overlap.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CLJS production-source integration test boots the real managed-HTTP app handlers with a capturing transport, enters /article/alpha and then /article/beta, and proves the two slugs' article/comments requests are independently deliverable rather than assuming cancellation.
- The test settles beta normally first and proves beta article plus beta comments are accepted through the public subscriptions; it then delivers alpha article and comments successes and proves the route params, beta data, statuses, errors, and timestamps remain unchanged.
- Parallel failure arms deliver alpha's article and comments failures while beta is current and prove they cannot mark beta errored or replace its lifecycle facts. A current beta failure is still accepted, providing the non-vacuity control for the failure gate.
- A loaded-alpha -> navigate-beta -> held-beta arm proves alpha's article and comments are not exposed under beta's route while beta is initially loading. A same-slug refresh control proves previously loaded beta data remains renderable while a new beta request is pending.
- Both reply styles stay exercised: :article/load remains a unified :reply-to handler and comments retain explicit success/failure handlers, with the requested slug carried on every terminal branch.
- A focused negative control that removes or inverts the slug-correlation predicate makes the late-alpha assertions fail; merely changing request ids or suppressing the simulated late delivery is not sufficient evidence.
- The managed-HTTP RealWorld CLJS suite and build pass, and README wording distinguishes same-id supersession from the app-owned cross-route correlation guarantee.
close_reason: Landed by PR #8845 (merged 2026-09-01T02:51:20Z), commit 7c69c5dc95 'fix(examples/realworld-http): article-page reads stay owned by the active /article/:slug' — verified present on origin/main. The bead was left in_progress because its worker did not survive to close it; the work itself is complete and merged.

title: patterns/websocket: clean disconnect strands every in-flight request
description:
## Scope

Fix the canonical runnable WebSocket pattern's clean-disconnect path in examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs and cover it in the external behavior wrapper implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs. Keep the existing machine topology, request/reply API, socket-epoch guard, queue/reconnect behavior, and test-free-example policy.

## Correctness finding

A clean :ws/disconnect destroys the live socket actor but neither clears nor fails requests already stored in :in-flight. Their scheduled timeouts are stamped with the destroyed socket id, so :current-socket? rejects those timeouts after teardown. The slot and its waiting :reply callback can therefore survive forever, including across a later reconnect.

The unexpected-drop path already handles exactly this invariant through :on-socket-lost; clean disconnect bypasses that action.

## Evidence

- examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:174-201 documents and implements the required loss behavior: clear all :in-flight slots and dispatch each waiting reply event with {:ok false :error :ws/connection-lost}. Its own comment explains that the old socket id makes a later timeout fail :current-socket?, otherwise leaking the slot forever.
- connection.cljs:271-293 registers each request in :in-flight and schedules :ws/request-timeout with the current :source-socket-id; lines 404-412 guard that timeout with :current-socket?.
- connection.cljs:356-364 routes unexpected :ws/closed through :on-socket-lost, but routes :ws/disconnect directly to :disconnected with no cleanup action.
- examples/patterns/websocket/messages.cljs:179-191 deliberately emits no :closed event while the actor is being destroyed, and lines 278-290 repeat that teardown must not redispatch into the dying actor. Therefore no later close event accidentally repairs the omission.
- examples/patterns/websocket/views.cljs:102-105 exposes this path as the runnable "Disconnect (clean)" button.
- implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/websocket_cljs_test.cljs:507-522 checks clean disconnect only for state/tags/socket teardown. It creates no request and never inspects :in-flight or a callback.
- The same wrapper's drop-fails-in-flight-request-test at lines 609-646 proves the intended behavior for an unexpected drop using a :silent-no-echo request: the slot clears and the callback receives an explicit failure. timeout-fails-in-flight-request-test separately proves the still-live-socket deadline path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the WebSocket example in a fresh frame and connect to the mock transport.
2. Dispatch a :ws/request whose body is {:type :silent-no-echo}, with a unique request id, a reply event, and a finite timeout. Confirm its id is present under [:data :in-flight].
3. Before the timeout, dispatch [:ws/disconnect].
4. Inspect the connection snapshot and reply-event observations. The machine is :disconnected and its actor id is gone, but the request id remains in :in-flight and no failure reaches the reply event.
5. Deliver the already-scheduled :ws/request-timeout carrying the former socket id. The :current-socket? guard rejects it because there is no live socket; the slot and callback remain stranded.
6. As a control, use the existing unexpected-drop path for the same request; it clears the slot and fires the failure callback.

## Expected Behavior

Once a request is accepted into :in-flight, it reaches exactly one explicit terminal outcome: a reply, a live-socket timeout, or a connection-termination failure. Leaving :active through clean disconnect must clear every on-wire request and notify every registered reply event exactly once.

## Actual Behavior

Clean disconnect terminates the only socket capable of replying while retaining all on-wire request records. The epoch guard then suppresses their timeout cleanup, so callers can hang indefinitely and a later reconnect inherits stale bookkeeping.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A user starts an RPC-like request over a real WebSocket and clicks the example's clean Disconnect control, or application code cleanly disconnects during navigation/logout. The transport closes successfully, but UI work awaiting the registered reply receives neither success nor failure. Reconnecting does not resolve it, and the stale :in-flight entry is permanent.

Invariant: destroying/replacing the socket that carried an on-wire request must settle that request exactly once and remove its correlation slot. Epoch rejection may prevent stale events from touching a new socket, but must not suppress the only cleanup path for the old one.

## Recommended minimal fix

Factor the existing "fail and clear every in-flight request" part of :on-socket-lost into one small action/helper. Use it both for guarded unexpected :ws/closed (alongside the retry increment) and for :ws/disconnect while leaving :active. Reuse the established explicit :ws/connection-lost result unless the example deliberately documents a distinct clean-disconnect error. Do not synthesize a socket :closed event during actor teardown.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Extend the external WebSocket wrapper with a deterministic :silent-no-echo request, assert the request is genuinely present in :in-flight, then dispatch clean :ws/disconnect.
2. After disconnect, assert :disconnected, no live socket actor id, an empty :in-flight map, and exactly one reply-event invocation naming the request id with :ok false and the documented connection-termination error.
3. Deliver or advance the old socket-stamped timeout after disconnect and assert the callback count remains exactly one and no request slot/state is resurrected. This is the at-most-once control.
4. A positive control proves the same silent request remains in flight before either disconnect or timeout; removing the clean-disconnect cleanup action makes the new test fail on both the retained id and missing callback, so the witness cannot pass vacuously.
5. Existing unexpected-drop, live-timeout, reconnect/epoch, queue, correlation, subscription, and actor-teardown tests remain green.
6. npm run test:cljs and npm run test:examples-compile pass.

## Non-goals

- A managed WebSocket facility, generalized request-cancellation API, or protocol framework.
- Replaying on-wire requests after reconnect; the current at-most-once fail-not-replay policy remains.
- Changing reconnect backoff, offline queueing, subscriptions, credential handling, inbound schema policy, or the socket actor topology.
- Adding tests inside examples/; behavior remains owned by the external wrapper.
- Broad edits to the WebSocket spec/skill or to the other pattern examples.

## Related / duplicate search

Fresh all-status title, description, and notes searches covered websocket, socket, disconnect, clean disconnect, manual disconnect, ws/disconnect, in-flight, in-flight request, connection-lost, request timeout, callback, strands, and flight. No bead owns this clean-disconnect request leak.

rf2-iyjae is adjacent but distinct: it corrects credential and inbound-frame trust boundaries and explicitly makes connection topology, correlation, timeout, and loss semantics non-goals. The existing source comments reference historical request-drop and timeout fixes (rf2-r1rkvb, rf2-vqg8l6), but those ids are not present in the current tracker and their implemented paths do not cover clean :ws/disconnect.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8839 (worker/ws-disconnect-b2jpr, d953d7e28e). Clean :ws/disconnect out of :active now settles every in-flight request exactly once: the fail-and-clear half of :on-socket-lost was factored into a fail-in-flight helper in examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs, used by both the guarded :ws/closed door (with the retry bump) and the :ws/disconnect door (without it). Topology, request/reply API, epoch guard, queue/reconnect behavior unchanged. Reply-error decision: reuse :ws/connection-lost, NOT a distinct value — the published contract (spec/Pattern-WebSocket.md §5 + pitfalls, example README) documents exactly that value for connection termination, and schema.cljs's LocalRequestFailure is a deliberately closed enum of :ws/connection-lost/:ws/timeout enforced at the release-resident RequestOutcome boundary; a distinct value would widen a closed contract for no caller benefit. Spec needed no edit (its listing omits :ws/disconnect entirely). Coverage: new wrapper deftest websocket-clean-disconnect-fails-in-flight-request (external wrapper per test-free-examples) — silent-no-echo request parked in-flight (positive control), clean disconnect -> slot cleared + exactly ONE reply with the documented body via a counting reply target forwarding through the boundary-validated :ws.app/request-reply, stale destroyed-socket timeout delivered post-disconnect AND post-reconnect resurrects nothing (at-most-once + no-leak-across-reconnect controls). Gates (local, exits captured): npm run test:cljs split compile exit 0 (1862 files, 0 warnings) + run exit 0 (11113 tests / 54529 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors); npm run test:examples-compile exit 0 (:examples/websocket compiled fresh in-run). Control: with the one-line :action :fail-in-flight routing reverted, run exit 1 with 7 failures ALL in the new test, red on both the retained slot and the missing callback; restore verified by git blob hash == HEAD object d35690f1cd, then recompile exit 0 + rerun exit 0. Follow-up filed: rf2-ni0ko (:ws/fatal door, same class, reachable only by consumer code).

title: bug(examples/flows): hot reload keeps stale boot-installed derivations
description:
## Scope

Correct the development reload path of the canonical runnable flows example in `examples/core/flows/**`. The fix should cover the two boot-installed, frame-scoped flows (`:cart/subtotal` and `:cart/total`), their Shadow CLJS entry/reload wiring, and focused executable regression coverage. Update the example's local explanation only where needed to keep the demonstrated contract truthful.

## Correctness finding

The example installs its two frame-scoped flows only when `flows.core/run` executes. Its sole `^:dev/after-load` function is `mount!`, which only re-renders. On a Shadow CLJS watch rebuild, edited code replaces `install-flows!` but no code calls that new function, so the live frame retains the old `:derive` functions. The UI reloads successfully and preserves state, yet subsequent cart events continue computing with the pre-save flow definitions. This contradicts the flows guide's executable hot-reload contract: edit a flow derive, save, and the running app swaps it in.

## Evidence

- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:57-72` explains why frame-scoped `reg-flow` calls cannot run at namespace load and wraps them in `install-flows!`.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:75-101` contains the only direct registrations of `:cart/subtotal` and `:cart/total`.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:309-316` marks only `mount!` as `^:dev/after-load`; its body creates/reuses the React root and renders, but never re-registers either flow.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:318-332` calls `install-flows!` only from `run`, alongside one-time frame construction and `:cart/initialise` seeding.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1574-1578` configures `flows.core/run` as the build's `:init-fn`; `examples/core/flows/README.md:57-64` tells users to run `shadow-cljs watch examples/flows`.
- `docs/core/flows.md:341-343` specifies that same-frame re-registration surgically replaces a flow, resets its dirty check, and is what makes save-time hot reload work. `spec/013-Flows.md:479` specifies the same replacement semantics.
- `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1809-1825` proves the runtime replacement contract works once `reg-flow` is actually called: the new derive runs on the next event even when the prior inputs were unchanged. The example omits that required call.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From `implementation/`, start the documented watcher with `shadow-cljs watch examples/flows` and open the served example.
2. Change the cart away from its seed state so state preservation is observable.
3. Edit the anonymous derive body for `:cart/total` in `examples/core/flows/core.cljs` to produce a visibly different result, then save and let Shadow report a successful reload.
4. Change a quantity in the already-running UI to drive the next flow pass.
5. Observe that the component remounts and the cart state is retained, but `:cart/total` still uses the old formula. A browser refresh/manual `install-flows!` call is required before the new formula takes effect; refreshing also forfeits the preserved in-memory session.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A successful watch reload must make the live frame use the current flow definitions without recreating or reseeding that frame. Today the example satisfies only the memory-preservation half: it keeps the frame but also keeps stale executable flow code. A normal source edit therefore creates a split runtime in which top-level event/sub registrations are current while the example's two foundational flows remain from the previous build.

## Recommended minimal fix

Keep `run`'s required boot order (`init!` -> make live frame -> install flows -> seed once -> mount). Add a dedicated Shadow after-load callback that calls the current `install-flows!` against the existing `:rf/default` frame and then mounts, and remove the after-load marker from the mount-only helper. Rely on the existing same-id surgical replacement contract; do not recreate the frame, replay `:cart/initialise`, add a reload framework, or change core flow semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented `examples/flows` watch loop re-registers the current `:cart/subtotal` and `:cart/total` definitions into the existing live frame after a successful code reload.
- A focused CLJS regression exercises the actual example reload seam against a live, non-seed cart: after substituting a distinguishable updated derive and invoking that seam, the next ordinary cart event computes the updated result while preserving the pre-reload items and quantities.
- Non-vacuity: the regression fails when the after-load seam is changed back to the current mount-only behavior; a compile-only assertion or a test that directly calls `rf/reg-flow` instead of the example reload seam is insufficient.
- Control: initial boot still installs both flows before `:cart/initialise`, so the first committed seed contains correct subtotal and total values.
- Control: reload neither calls `:cart/initialise` nor recreates/destroys `:rf/default`; user cart state survives, and each flow id has one current frame-scoped definition rather than duplicate lifecycle work.
- `cd implementation && npm run test:cljs` and `cd implementation && npm run test:examples-compile` pass, with the focused regression included in an exercised test build rather than merely compiling.

## Non-goals

- Do not change the public `reg-flow` API, flow scheduler, dirty-check, image/registrar model, or Shadow CLJS itself.
- Do not add compatibility modes, generic lifecycle abstractions, a public reload command, polling, or automatic state migration.
- Do not redesign the example's cart behavior or the separate runtime-toggle settling behavior owned by `rf2-kh73v`.
- Do not require a full page refresh as the fix; preserving the live frame is part of the advertised development contract.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all tracker statuses across title, description, notes, and acceptance criteria for `examples/core/flows`, `examples/flows`, flow plus hot reload, stale flow, `install-flows`, and `reg-flow` plus reload. No issue owns the example's mount-only reload seam or stale boot-installed derives. Open P2 `rf2-kh73v` changes automatic settling for runtime `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` toggles; it is explicitly distinct from static boot registration and hot reload, and this task does not overlap that runtime-semantics work.
close_reason: Landed by PR #8845 (merged 2026-09-01T02:51:20Z), commit 6cc27b8fb7 'fix(examples/flows): reinstall boot-installed flows on hot reload' — verified present on origin/main. The bead was left in_progress because its worker did not survive to close it; the work itself is complete and merged. Found by the backlog reread, not by the stranded sweep, which correctly starts from worktrees rather than the in_progress list.

title: mcp-conformance: project-stories execution proof is vacuous
description:
## Scope

Tighten only the consumer-project Story-MCP witness in tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/ and tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs so its run-variant phase proves that project-authored lifecycle work executed. Preserve the existing first-connect, no --allow-writes, consumer-alias launch and missing-namespace failure arms.

## Correctness finding

The new project-stories end-to-end gate claims to prove that a pre-authored project variant is runnable on first connect, but its run arm is vacuous. The fixture variant deliberately has no :setup, no :script, and no assertions. The harness accepts isError false plus :status "pass". Story's result contract intentionally assigns :pass to an empty assertion set with a clean tape, so that response is the default for doing no observable lifecycle work.

Consequently the gate proves registration, lookup, request routing, and a success-shaped result envelope, but it cannot prove the correctness claim named by phase 5: that run-variant executed the project-authored variant lifecycle.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From tools/mcp-conformance, run npm run test:story-project on the current fixture. Phase 5 reports run-variant green.
2. Read the registered variant in test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc: it has no :setup, :script, or assertion.
3. Read the phase-5 check in test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs: it accepts the response after only isError false and aggregate status "pass".
4. Compare Story's production aggregation rule: an empty assertion vector with no unmet/failure evidence returns :pass. The same gate verdict is therefore available without any project-authored lifecycle action to observe.

Expected: the execution phase requires evidence produced only by running the fixture variant.
Actual: the default empty-program pass is sufficient for the phase and the overall gate to be green.

## Evidence

- tools/mcp-conformance/test/fixtures/project-stories/src/app/stories.cljc:27-29 says the fixture has no :setup and no :script and is therefore "vacuously runnable".
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-project-stories.cjs:193-205 calls this a "vacuous pass" and checks only runResp.isError and runStruct.status.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/result.cljc:44-49 states the production rule directly: a run with zero assertions and a clean tape is :pass.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/requirements.cljc:547-555 implements that rule: with no error, failure, or unmet record, aggregate-status falls through to :pass.
- Closed bead rf2-cfq8a and the harness header describe the delivered outcome as discovering, reading, and running the project story on first connection. The current last verb has no execution-only witness.

The focused Node unit cluster is green (105 passed, 9 platform skips), which is expected: it does not make this end-to-end arm non-vacuous.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A regression can stop executing :setup and/or :script for launch-preloaded project variants while still resolving the known variant to an empty, clean run result. list-stories, get-story, and get-variant continue to pass. Phase 5 still sees isError false and status "pass", so the advertised golden path remains green even though the project's lifecycle never ran.

Invariant: any gate that claims a variant executed must assert evidence that can exist only if that variant's lifecycle executed. A default success status over an empty program is not such evidence.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the existing fixture variant perform one deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle action and emit one distinctive passing assertion. A small fixture-local event used by :setup, followed by a :script path assertion over the seeded value, is sufficient and exercises both halves without a renderer or browser. In the SDK test, assert the returned assertion record (identity, passed verdict, and expected/actual evidence), not merely the aggregate :status.

Keep this inside the existing fixture and test. No new server option, MCP tool, transport, test job, fixture project, or general assertion framework is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The existing project fixture variant contains non-empty, deterministic JVM-headless lifecycle work whose result cannot be produced without executing the variant (for example, fixture-local setup state followed by a distinctive script assertion).
2. end-to-end-project-stories.cjs still launches through the fixture project's -M:story-mcp alias before any MCP write, but now requires the run-variant response to contain the exact execution-only assertion/evidence and a passing aggregate status.
3. The test fails if run-variant returns the current empty-assertions :pass shape; checking only :status is not sufficient.
4. Non-vacuity control: temporarily make the fixture's expected value wrong, or disable the setup action that produces it, and run npm run test:story-project from tools/mcp-conformance. The command must exit non-zero and name the missing/failed execution witness. Restore the plant and require the same command to exit zero.
5. The existing missing-namespace launch arm, first-connect discovery/read arms, no --allow-writes posture, and clean SDK teardown remain covered and green.
6. Focused Story-MCP tests relevant to the chosen lifecycle action remain green; no browser, Chromium, nREPL, or Pair-MCP runtime is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Changing Story's intentional rule that an assertion-free variant is vacuously green.
- Adding a blanket requirement that every user-authored variant contain assertions.
- Testing rendering or browser-only Reagent/UIx stories in the headless JVM server.
- Expanding the tool catalogue, wire schemas, launch flags, token budgeting, or CI job matrix.
- Refactoring the mature Story runtime or adding a second consumer fixture.

## Related / duplicate search

- rf2-cfq8a (closed) delivered the first-launch project-story path and this witness. This issue is a correctness correction to its execution proof, not a duplicate of its bootstrap outcome.
- rf2-a9l6e (open) concerns one honest command/profile for running MCP compatibility and explicitly excludes new protocol assertions. It does not own this vacuous run arm.
- rf2-k9rzr (closed) mentions an unrelated vacuous assertion in bundle-isolation tooling.
- All-status tracker searches over project stories, project-story, run-variant, vacuous, mcp-conformance, dedup envelope, and serialized issue descriptions found no issue owning a non-vacuous execution witness for end-to-end-project-stories.cjs.

## Priority rationale

P2: this is a real false-green in an authoritative SDK/CI compatibility witness for the first-use Story-MCP workflow. It can allow an execution regression to ship while the named golden path stays green. It is not P1 because no current production execution failure was observed; the defect is in the gate's ability to detect one.
