title: template: after-load hooks leave the app schema stale after edits
description:
## Scope

The generated browser entry points and schema guidance under `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template`: the default Reagent scaffold, UIx scaffold, Reagent Story scaffold, and Reagent SSR client's hot-reload path. Add focused generator/emitted-project regression coverage; no framework API redesign.

## Correctness finding

Every emitted app registers its app-db schema only from the module `init`, while Shadow CLJS calls that init function once and invokes only `^:dev/after-load` hooks after a save. Those hooks rerender the retained app but never re-register the newly loaded schema value. Consequently the framework continues validating the live frame with the boot-time schema after `schema.cljs` changes, even though the generated UI and event code hot-reload. The scaffold's advertised hot-reload loop is therefore internally inconsistent and can reject a source-valid write (or accept a write forbidden by a tightened schema) until a full page refresh.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate a default app, run `npm install` and `npx shadow-cljs watch app`, and open the counter page.
2. Increment the counter so preserving live state across reload is observable.
3. In `schema.cljs`, extend the closed `CounterDb` map with an optional string key such as `[:counter/label {:optional true} :string]`.
4. Change an event handler to associate `:counter/label` with a string, then save both files and let Shadow CLJS run the emitted `^:dev/after-load` hook.
5. Dispatch that event without refreshing the page. The write is validated against the original closed map, emits `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`, and rolls back. Refreshing the page runs `init` again and makes the same write succeed.

The inverse is also incorrect: tightening a schema during the same session leaves the former permissive schema active until refresh.

## Evidence

- `_shared/schema.cljs` defines `register-schema!` with the instruction "Call once at boot (see core/init)" and passes the current `CounterDb` value to `rf/reg-app-schema`.
- `_reagent/core.cljs` lines 41-49 and `_uix/core.cljs` lines 36-45 tag `mount!` as `^:dev/after-load`, but it only retains/creates the React root and renders. Their `init` functions call `schema/register-schema!` only at lines 71 and 67 respectively.
- `_reagent/core_with_stories.cljs` lines 95-97 make `reload!` reinstall routing and render, while schema registration exists only in `init` at line 111.
- `_reagent/core_with_ssr.cljc` lines 156-164 make `render!` rerender the retained root, while the client schema is registered only in `init` at line 178.
- The emitted `root/README.md` lines 25-35 correctly says Shadow invokes `init` once and then calls after-load hooks, but lines 419-435 teach schema registration only once at boot.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc` lines 567-572 stores the schema value in `schemas-by-frame`; it does not retain a Var that follows a redefinition. Lines 698-704 explicitly define hot-reload semantics as re-registering the `(frame-id, path)` so the new value replaces the prior validation-cache entry.
- Existing HMR emission tests exercise retained-root rerendering for Reagent, UIx, Story, and SSR, but do not assert schema replacement after a reload. Initial browser smoke tests cannot expose this post-save failure.

## Failure scenario / invariant

After any successful generated-app hot reload, validation and tooling must observe the schema definitions in the just-loaded source while preserving the existing frame, app-db, React root, and routing/hydration state. A source-valid event write must not fail solely because a stale boot-time schema remains cached, and a newly invalid write must not pass for the same reason.

## Recommended minimal fix

Have each emitted `^:dev/after-load` path re-register the current app schema for its existing frame before rerendering. Preserve the current boot ordering so initial events are still validated, and do not recreate/reseed the frame. In the SSR client, re-register against `app-frame` but do not repeat hydration. Update the generated schema comments/README to describe registration at boot and after load. The runtime already makes same-frame/path re-registration atomic and hot-reload-safe, so no framework change is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused executable CLJS regression drives the actual generated after-load path (or a small extracted reload seam used by that path): it boots with the original closed schema, retains non-default counter state, substitutes a schema that admits optional `:counter/label`, invokes reload without recreating the frame, and asserts `rf/app-schema-at [] {:frame :rf/default}` returns the new schema.
- The same test dispatches an ordinary generated event that writes `:counter/label` and proves the write commits while the pre-reload counter value remains intact.
- Coverage pins schema re-registration for all four emitted browser entry variants: default Reagent, UIx, Story, and the SSR client. SSR coverage additionally proves reload does not call `ssr/hydrate!` or replay seed events.
- The proof is non-vacuous: before the production fix, the fixture observes the old schema and the new-key write is rejected/rolled back; equivalently, a mutation/control that removes the after-load registration makes the regression fail.
- Existing emitted-project compile tests, initial browser smoke tests, and retained-root HMR tests remain green.
- Generated comments and README no longer claim that registration happens only once at boot; they explain that after-load re-registration updates validation while retaining app state.

## Non-goals

- Re-running module init, initial events, frame creation, hydration, or routing setup beyond what each current reload hook already requires.
- Changing runtime schema storage, validation policy, production elision, or public schema APIs.
- Adding watcher/process orchestration when a deterministic generated-code CLJS test can prove the reload invariant.
- Compatibility machinery for older generated projects.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for `stale schema`, `after-load schema`, `schema hot reload`, `schema re-registration`, `register-schema hot reload`, `CounterDb reload`, `schema.cljs after-load`, and `template HMR`; no matching issue exists. Closed `rf2-r0kk7` fixed the distinct absence of generated after-load rerender hooks and deliberately kept one-time boot ceremony in `init`; it did not refresh the schema registry and is not a duplicate.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8897, confined to tools/template/**.

DEFECT CONFIRMED AT SOURCE in all four emitted entry points. reg-app-schema is frame-local, so the scaffold cannot call it at namespace load (a load-time call raises :rf.error/no-frame-context); it lives inside schema/register-schema!. A hot reload therefore re-evaluates the CounterDb def and re-registers nothing on its own, and every entry point called register-schema! from init alone -- which shadow runs once, at bundle load.

FIX: each ^:dev/after-load hook re-attaches the schema, BEFORE its render work. Reagent and UIx fold the call into mount!, which init already delegates to, so boot and reload traverse one path; Story (reload!) and the SSR client (render!) keep their one-time boot ceremony in init and re-attach from the hook. The SSR hook does not re-hydrate or replay seed events. Ordering matters as much as presence: the boot call still lands before frame-root creates the frame, so the :initial-events seed is validated from the first write, and a DOM-free host that skips the render still registers.

QUESTION 1 -- is hook-side re-registration correct, or does it paper over a framework gap? CORRECT; no framework change and no follow-up bead. Spec 010 Multiple-schemas-at-the-same-path makes re-registration last-write-wins and calls a hot-reload re-register benign; Spec 010 Schema-migration-on-hot-reload defines the tightened-schema case (a :rf.schema/violation warning, app-db not cleared or rewound); storage.cljc's hot-reload-semantics block makes it an atomic swap! into the map that IS the validation cache; and executable framework coverage already exists (schemas_storage_test meta-at-reflects-hot-reload-replacement, schemas_reg_side_effects_test, a hot-reload race stress test).

QUESTION 2 -- one shared helper or four parallel edits? FOUR PARALLEL EDITS. A helper would still have to be called from each hook, so it saves nothing at the call site; it could not cover all four anyway, since the SSR scaffold has no schema.cljs and its register-schema! is inline in core.cljc with a different arity; the emitted files are user-facing source, so the reader must see in the hook what a reload re-does; and fixing at the defect site leaves rf2-zq34m unprejudiced.

COVERAGE. Static and unconditional in the artefact's default clojure -M:test: every hook calls register-schema! before its render (all four variants); the SSR hook re-attaches against the live app-frame and neither re-hydrates nor replays the seed; schema.cljs keeps reg-app-schema out of the top level; both emitted READMEs teach boot AND after-load. Executable: a regression namespace copied into a generated project's test tree, compiled and run by the emitted :test build against real generated source -- it models one save (re-evaluate the def, then call what the hook calls), boots closed with a counter at 3, proves the closed schema REJECTS a :counter/label write, reloads widened, proves the live schema is replaced and the write now commits with the counter intact, then drives the inverse direction (tightening takes effect; app-db is not cleared). It rides RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS, which CI's jvm-tools-template job sets on every PR.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, both deliberate. (a) The criteria name rf/app-schema-at; that symbol does NOT exist on the re-frame.core facade -- the schemas query helpers were removed from the front porch by rf2-wad2fl and live on re-frame.schemas. The regression uses re-frame.schemas/app-schema-at. (b) The executable regression drives the extracted reload seam the criteria explicitly permit, not the hook fn itself: requiring the emitted core.cljs pulls reagent.dom.client and React into a node-test bundle, which would need a :browser-grade node_modules for no added signal. The hook's CALL is pinned statically for all four variants instead, so the composite is covered.

GATES (captured exits, post-rebase): tools/template clojure -M:test = 0 (71 tests, 728 assertions); the gated emitted-run regression = 0 (1 test, 10 assertions); check_doc_slugs.py = 0; check_readme_links.py --ci = 0; clj-kondo --fail-level error on tools/template/{src,test} = 0; splint --fail-on-errors over the template lint surface = 0. Three sabotage controls each went red naming the planted fault, and each plant was restored and verified by git blob hash.

title: bug(pair-mcp): CWD port discovery strands the session after an ephemeral-port restart
description:
## Scope

Repair restart recovery for the documented step-5 CWD-relative nREPL port discovery in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**`. The coherent surface is the discovery result in `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs`, its consumption by `server.cljs`, focused discovery/port-stability tests, and the transport README/spec wording that currently says this branch cannot retain a stable file identity.

## Correctness finding

The CWD fallback successfully reads one of three concrete port files, but returns only `{:port n}` and deliberately drops the winning filename. `discover-and-cache!` therefore stores `:port-file nil`; `ensure-connection!` only re-reads a cached endpoint when `:port-file` is non-nil. If the fallback's nREPL restarts on a new ephemeral port, every later tool call keeps the old endpoint and can only reconnect to that old port. The MCP session cannot discover the new port until the whole MCP server is restarted or the operator changes launch configuration.

The stated reason for dropping the path is incorrect: a relative candidate read against Node's process CWD has a stable, unambiguous absolute identity via `node:path.resolve` (or by joining it to `process.cwd()`). No project-home inference is needed.

This is P2: it makes a shipped, documented fallback permanently non-self-healing after a routine dynamic-port restart and turns subsequent app-facing tools into repeated transport failures, but it does not corrupt application state.

## Evidence

- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs:256-260` implements step 5 as `{:port (some read-port-file port-file-candidates)}`. It loses which candidate succeeded and returns no `:port-file`.
- The same file's `read-port-at-base` already returns `{:port ... :port-file ...}` for a winning candidate, and its comments explain why exact candidate identity is required for restart detection.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:278-297` caches the discovery result. With no project-home and no returned port-file, the CWD branch necessarily caches `:port-file nil`.
- `src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/server.cljs:426-438` re-reads only `(when port-file ...)`; a nil file takes the cached-connection path. The port-change and vanished-file recovery branches at lines 440 onward are consequently unreachable for CWD discovery.
- `test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl_test.cljs:827-843` positively asserts that the CWD result has a nil `:port-file`, so the current suite freezes the defect instead of exercising restart recovery.
- `spec/002-nREPL-Transport.md:87-104` specifies per-tool-call exact-file re-read but explicitly exempts the CWD fallback because it claims there is no stable path. `README.md:132-144` documents this fallback for environments without the Shadow HTTP path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an MCP client with no usable roots and make the Shadow HTTP probe unavailable; launch the MCP server with the app project as its CWD.
2. Put P1 in one standard relative port file, such as `.nrepl-port`, and make an app-facing tool call. Step 5 attaches successfully to P1.
3. Restart the app nREPL on a different ephemeral port P2 and rewrite the same file; leave P1 closed.
4. Make another app-facing tool call. It retains the connection object bound to P1 rather than reading P2. Repeated calls still target P1; only restarting/reconfiguring the MCP server recovers.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A file-backed endpoint change must be observed before every app-facing call. Every discovery branch that obtains its port by reading a file must retain the exact winning file identity, so a change replaces the old connection and a disappearance triggers rediscovery. The CWD branch violates that invariant solely because it throws away the filename it just read.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the step-5 scan return both the port and the exact winning candidate resolved against the process CWD. Reuse the existing file-backed result shape and the existing `ensure-connection!` replacement/disappearance branches; do not add a watcher, polling service, extra reconnect state machine, project-root inference, or new public option. Update the test and prose that currently encode the false no-stable-path premise.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused `discover-port*` test with roots unsupported and the HTTP probe unavailable proves the CWD fallback returns the successful port and an absolute `:port-file` for the exact candidate that supplied it; an earlier missing candidate must not be reported as the winner.
2. A focused server test seeds a session from that CWD discovery shape, changes the injected file read from P1 to P2, calls `ensure-connection!`, and proves the P1 connection is closed exactly once and the returned authoritative connection targets P2 without rerunning the full discovery cascade.
3. A vanished-file test proves the same CWD-derived cache enters the existing rediscovery path rather than silently reusing P1.
4. Non-vacuity: the new P1-to-P2 witness is demonstrated to fail when the CWD discovery result's `:port-file` is removed (the pre-fix behavior), and pass with the repair. Report that red/green control in the PR.
5. Control: env-var discovery remains a fixed endpoint with no invented file identity, while explicit-file, roots, and HTTP precedence/result behavior remains green. No candidate is re-read twice merely to reconstruct its identity.
6. `cd tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp && npm test` passes, including the focused discovery and port-file-stability namespaces; the relevant transport README/spec statements describe CWD fallback as file-backed and restart-aware.

## Non-goals

- No filesystem watcher, port-range probing, Shadow process monitor, background retry loop, or generic connection-lifecycle rewrite.
- No change to discovery precedence, roots elicitation, HTTP probing, explicit `--port-file`, or `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` semantics.
- No compatibility alias, migration ceremony, new flag, public tool, or additional project-home heuristic.
- No broad cleanup of port parsing or unrelated socket timeout/error handling.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status title and full title/description/notes searches covered `pair-mcp`, `nREPL`, `port`, `port-file`, `cwd`, `cwd-scan`, `cwd-relative`, `ephemeral port`, `stale port`, `restart detection`, and `reconnect`. No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead owns CWD fallback file identity or restart recovery. Historical source comments cite the earlier exact-port-file work for explicit/roots/HTTP discovery; this issue is the omitted fifth branch of that invariant, not a duplicate of an active tracker item. `rf2-ahjbc` is an open Pair-MCP stream-surface retirement and does not touch transport discovery.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8848 (commit abba851486): the step-5 CWD nREPL port fallback now resolves candidates against process.cwd() via read-port-at-base and surfaces the winning candidate as an absolute :port-file, so the server's per-tool-call re-read observes ephemeral-port restarts and vanished files on this branch exactly like steps 1/3/4; :project-home stays nil (no inference). Composed P1->P2 witness + vanished-file test in port_file_stability_test.cljs; discovery winner-identity/read-once/env-no-file tests in nrepl_test.cljs; spec/002 + README now describe the fallback as file-backed and restart-aware. npm test 1108/4011 green; pre-fix revert reds exactly the new witnesses (recorded in PR).

title: testbed-support: auto-detect skips the position probe for column-only coordinates
description:
## Scope

Correct the repository dev-server open-in-editor behavior for the already-supported `:windsurf` editor preference in `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj`, with focused server/client contract coverage. Preserve the existing endpoint-preferred, editor-URI-fallback architecture and all other editor behavior.

## Correctness finding

The endpoint advertises Windsurf as a supported editor hint but the installed `launch-editor@2.14.1` does not know how to encode a Windsurf source position. It strips `:line` and `:column`, invokes `windsurf` with only the bare file, and can exit successfully. The server then returns HTTP 200, so the browser logs endpoint success and suppresses the existing `windsurf://` fallback that would have retained the coordinate.

This breaks the core jump-to-source invariant: a successful open for a supported configured editor must land at the requested line/column, or the endpoint must decline so the coordinate-preserving fallback gets its turn.

## Evidence

- `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj:23-30` explicitly maps query value `windsurf` to command `windsurf`.
- The same file's `build-file-spec` and `launch!` pass `path:line:column` to `launch-editor`, and lines 177-183 interpret child exit 0 as `{:ok true}`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/open_endpoint.cljs` serialises keyword `:windsurf` as `editor=windsurf`; its fetch path treats every 2xx as final success and calls the URI fallback only on a non-2xx/network failure.
- Xray's documented/configured editor vocabulary includes `:windsurf`; `implementation/core` also has a coordinate-preserving `windsurf://file/<path>:<line>:<column>` URI implementation and tests.
- `implementation/package-lock.json` installs `launch-editor` 2.14.1. Its `get-args.js` has explicit position cases for `code`, `cursor`, `zed`, and JetBrains binaries, but none for `windsurf`.
- Executable probe from `implementation/`:
  `node -e "const g=require('./node_modules/launch-editor/get-args'); for (const e of ['windsurf','code']) console.log(e, JSON.stringify(g(e,'C:/repo/src/app.cljs','27','9')));"`
  produces `windsurf ["C:/repo/src/app.cljs"]` versus `code ["-r","-g","C:/repo/src/app.cljs:27:9"]`.
- The current JVM tests assert only that `editor-hint "windsurf"` equals `"windsurf"`; they never exercise the dependency's resulting argv or prove line/column survival.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a repository Story/Xray dev testbed through its wired `POST /__rf-open-in-editor` handler.
2. Configure the tool editor preference as `:windsurf`.
3. Click a source coordinate such as `{:file "src/app.cljs" :line 27 :column 9}`.
4. Observe the endpoint request includes `line=27&column=9&editor=windsurf`.
5. Inspect the installed launcher's computed arguments: Windsurf receives only the bare file, whereas VS Code receives a goto-position argument.
6. When the Windsurf command exits 0, observe the endpoint returns 200 and the client does not navigate to its coordinate-preserving `windsurf://...:27:9` fallback.

## Expected Behavior

A successful Windsurf click opens the requested file at line 27, column 9. If the installed endpoint launcher cannot guarantee that coordinate, the endpoint returns a non-2xx result so the existing Windsurf URI fallback runs exactly once.

## Actual Behavior

The endpoint can report success after launching Windsurf with only the file path. The requested line and column are lost, and the success response prevents fallback.

## Failure scenario / invariant

For any supported editor preference, endpoint success means the complete source coordinate was handed to an editor in that editor's accepted position syntax. A bare-file launch is not success for a coordinate-bearing request. This matters on every Windsurf source chip in Xray/Story: the visible action appears to work, but lands at an arbitrary prior cursor position or file start rather than the diagnostic site the programmer selected.

## Recommended minimal fix

Until `launch-editor` itself supports a Windsurf goto-position mapping, deliberately decline the Windsurf endpoint hint with a non-2xx response and let the already-implemented `windsurf://file/...:line:column` client fallback handle it. Keep this as a small explicit capability decision near the editor-hint/handler boundary; do not silently auto-detect another editor and do not build a second per-editor process launcher. If a later pinned `launch-editor` release demonstrably preserves Windsurf positions, the explicit decline can be removed with the same contract test.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A focused executable test drives a coordinate-bearing `editor=windsurf` request through the real server/client decision seam and proves one of two valid outcomes: the editor invocation demonstrably retains line 27 and column 9, or the endpoint returns non-2xx and the existing Windsurf URI fallback runs exactly once with `:27:9`. A 2xx response paired with bare-file-only Windsurf argv must fail the test.
2. The preferred minimal implementation for the currently pinned `launch-editor@2.14.1` returns a bounded launch-declined response for Windsurf before a misleading bare-file success; the browser then uses the existing `windsurf://` fallback without a second endpoint attempt.
3. Non-vacuity: a negative-control stub/path that reports successful bare-file Windsurf launch makes the focused test red. A positive control using the same coordinate with `editor=vscode` still reaches the endpoint, retains `27:9`, returns 2xx, and does not call fallback; the repair must not make every editor fall back.
4. The existing testbed-support JVM suite and the shared open-endpoint client tests pass. The supported editor vocabulary remains `:vscode`, `:cursor`, `:windsurf`, `:zed`, and `:idea`; only the transport selected for Windsurf changes while the dependency lacks coordinate support.
5. Tracker/docs comments that claim the endpoint handles every configured editor are made truthful if touched; no new configuration knob or compatibility layer is introduced.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning the endpoint path/query grammar, loopback security boundary, classpath resolution, timeout/drain logic, or checkout-root plumbing.
- Vendoring or forking `launch-editor`, teaching it a general editor capability registry, or implementing a second direct Windsurf CLI launcher.
- Changing URI syntax, editor preference vocabulary, Xray/Story source-chip UI, or behavior for VS Code, Cursor, Zed, IDEA, custom editors, and auto-detection.
- Speculative support for editors not already in the repository vocabulary.

## Related / duplicate search

- `rf2-3xq1v` (open, owned) retires checkout-root plumbing. It explicitly lists editor vocabulary and `launch-editor` behavior as non-goals, so this runtime coordinate-loss repair is distinct.
- All-status tracker title, description, and notes searches for `windsurf` found no issue. All-status `launch-editor` searches found only `rf2-3xq1v`, whose scope excludes this finding. Searches for editor hints and line/column loss found no matching testbed/open-endpoint owner.
- Historical endpoint work introduced the preferred endpoint/fallback seam, but no current or closed outcome bead owns Windsurf position preservation.
acceptance_criteria: A column-only no-hint/custom launch (`line=nil`, `column=7`) runs the same dependency capability probe as a line-bearing launch, using normalized line 1. A real-node test proves a position-blind resolved editor is declined and a position-capable editor still reaches a launch attempt; the endpoint maps the decline to 422 and fallback retains `:1:7`. Existing no-coordinate behavior stays unchanged.

title: bug(mcp-base): dedup aliases legitimate payload values as cache references
description:
## Scope

Fix the shared structural-dedup wire codec in `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc` and its JSON-side mirror in `tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs`. Keep Pair-MCP and Story-MCP tool names, arguments, opt-out behavior, and the `:rf.mcp/dedup-table` outer envelope unchanged. Update the focused specs/tests that define the reference representation.

## Correctness finding

Dedup references are not distinguishable from legitimate payload data. The Clojure/CLJS decoder classifies every symbol whose namespace is `de-dupe.cache` as a cache reference, without requiring the symbol to name a real entry. The JSON mirror is broader: after JSON erases the symbol/string distinction, it treats every string beginning `de-dupe.cache/` as a reference. Therefore `expand` is not the exact inverse promised by the codec for arbitrary persistent data. A payload scalar can become `nil`, another cached subtree, a thrown missing-reference error, or a cycle merely because its value occupies the codec's in-band namespace.

## Evidence

- `dedup.cljc:160-165` defines `cache-element?` as `symbol?` plus namespace equality only; `dedup.cljc:347-360` immediately routes every such value to `expand-entry` and reads `(get cache cache-id)` even when the table has no matching slot.
- `dedup-envelope.cjs:62-64,81-83` uses `startsWith('de-dupe.cache/')`; `dedup-envelope.cjs:137-141` then throws when that ordinary string has no table entry. JSON serialization makes real reference symbols and ordinary payload strings share this same representation.
- Both shipped consumers enable this codec on value-rich, programmer-owned data: Pair-MCP epoch/snapshot/subscribe payloads and Story-MCP run/preview/record payloads. An unrelated repeated subtree is enough to activate the wrapper, so the colliding scalar need not itself repeat.
- The current cross-host dedup suite proves common collection kinds and real references, but has no literal payload value in the reference namespace and no JSON string collision arm.

## Steps to Reproduce

Evaluate the real JVM codec with:

```clojure
(require '[re-frame.mcp-base.dedup :as d]
         '[re-frame.mcp-base.vocab :as v])
(let [shared  {:big [:repeat :me]}
      payload {:literal 'de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref
               :a shared
               :b shared}
      wrapped (d/dedup-value payload true)
      cache   (get wrapped v/dedup-table-key)]
  {:wrapped? (contains? wrapped v/dedup-table-key)
   :expanded (d/expand cache)
   :equal?   (= payload (d/expand cache))})
```

Current result is non-vacuously wrapped, but `:literal` expands to `nil` and `:equal?` is false. In the Node mirror, placing the ordinary JSON string `"de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref"` beside a real cache reference throws `cache reference ... has no matching entry`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A re-frame app legitimately stores a namespaced symbol in app-db, a story emits one in rendered/diagnostic data, or a structured payload contains a string with the same spelling. The payload also contains ordinary repeated state, which is common in epoch pairs and enables dedup. The server advertises a successful dedup envelope, but the agent reconstructs data different from the server's value (or cannot reconstruct it at all). The required invariant is: for every supported payload value `x`, `expand(de-dupe-eq(x)) = x`, and the JSON projection must preserve the same semantic value; cache references must be unambiguous from user data.

## Recommended minimal fix

Retain the outer envelope and make the existing reference tokens collision-free rather than adding a compatibility layer. During the encoder's existing discovery walk, record literal payload symbols and strings that can collide with `de-dupe.cache/cache-N`, and allocate cache ids that skip those spellings. On decode, classify only an exact cache-id token that is present in the current cache, not every value sharing the namespace/prefix. Apply the same exact-entry rule in the Node mirror. This preserves the compact wire shape while making the encoder's own output unambiguous. If a smaller closed reference representation proves simpler, change it in one pre-alpha cut across the base spec, both decoders, and conformance fixtures; do not support two formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a cross-host test in `re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test` whose payload contains (a) an ordinary `de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref` symbol, (b) an ordinary generated-looking `de-dupe.cache/cache-1` symbol, and (c) an unrelated repeated subtree. Assert the result actually contains `:rf.mcp/dedup-table` (non-vacuity/control), `expand` equals the original payload, and both literal symbols remain symbols with their exact values.
2. Add the JSON-mirror counterpart with ordinary strings `de-dupe.cache/not-a-ref` and `de-dupe.cache/cache-1` beside at least one real cache reference. Assert `decodeDedupEnvelope` reconstructs the exact strings and the real reference. As a positive control, a deliberately missing genuine reference must still fail loudly, proving reference resolution was not disabled wholesale.
3. Existing real-reference compression remains active: a repeated subtree produces more than the root cache entry and expands exactly on JVM and CLJS.
4. The reference grammar and collision rule are stated once in `tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md` and mirrored by the Node conformance decoder; no prefix-only decoder remains.
5. Focused commands pass non-vacuously: from `tools/mcp-base`, `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.mcp-base.dedup-test` and `npm run test:cljs`; from the repository root, `npm run test:dedup-envelope --prefix tools/mcp-conformance`.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning which tools are dedup-eligible, changing the default-on posture, or removing the `dedup false` escape hatch.
- Adding a general serialization framework, schema registry, compatibility alias, or dual-format decoder.
- Optimizing compression ratios or changing equality-vs-identity pooling.
- Hardening arbitrary attacker-authored cache tables beyond preserving the existing loud failure for malformed genuine references.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status tracker searches were run for `dedup`, `de-dupe`, `de-dupe.cache`, `cache reference`, `cache-ref`, `cache-N`, `cache element`, `namespaced symbol`, `symbol collision`, `payload symbol`, `unknown cache`, `dedup table`, `round-trip`, and `roundtrip`, including description and notes searches where supported. No bead describes this alias/corruption outcome. Closed `rf2-ntbd1` concerns package ownership of the epoch diff codec and explicitly leaves dedup in mcp-base; it is not a duplicate. Open dedup mentions concern recorder/stream/tool-surface design, not cache-reference representation.

title: story: variant-share-url appends stale query values instead of replacing them
description:
## Scope

Correct the public tools/story share-URL builder at tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc and add focused coverage at the builder/browser-consumer seam. The issue is limited to merging Story-owned query keys when variant-share-url receives a base-url that already has a query string.

## Correctness finding

variant-share-url appends its generated query fragments after every existing query fragment. It does not replace an existing value for a key it owns. The browser hydrator reads each key with URLSearchParams.get, whose first-value semantics select the old value. A URL requested for one variant can therefore open a different, stale variant.

This violates the explicit share invariant that a pasted URL lands on the exact same cell. It is a current public-API failure, not malformed-input hardening: variant-share-url publicly accepts base-url, and existing-query merging already has a named test.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Call variant-share-url for :story.new/b with base-url https://example.test/?variant=story.old%2Fa&from=index#/stories.
2. Observe that the returned search string contains variant=story.old%2Fa followed by variant=story.new%2Fb.
3. Construct URLSearchParams from that search string and call get("variant"), exactly as the Story browser hydrator does.
4. Observe story.old/a; share/parse-params therefore restores the old variant, not :story.new/b.

## Evidence

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:357-370 splits off the hash, detects any question mark, selects ampersand, and concatenates the generated params. It never examines or replaces existing keys.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:486-505 exposes that behavior through variant-share-url and always emits the requested variant.
- For base https://example.test/?variant=story.old%2Fa&from=index#/stories and requested variant :story.new/b, the current algorithm produces two variant entries in old-then-new order.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/url_state.cljc:358-384 constructs URLSearchParams and calls .get for variant before share/parse-params. An executable Node URLSearchParams control over the resulting order returns getAll = [story.old/a, story.new/b] but get = story.old/a.
- tools/story/test/re_frame/story_share_test.clj:84-90 covers only an unrelated from=index query and asserts the separator. It has no same-key collision or end-to-end parse assertion.
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:5-12 and 41-44, tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/url_state.cljc:14-15, and tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:203-222 state the invariant: paste/open reproduces the exact cell.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A programmer starts with a URL that already names story.old/a, calls the documented public builder to make a link for story.new/b, and shares the result. The recipient's browser reads the first variant value and hydrates story.old/a. The visible selection is not the requested selection, even though the generated URL also contains story.new/b.

Invariant: for every query key emitted by a variant-share-url call, the returned URL contains one effective value and the real browser parser observes the value generated by that call. Unrelated base query params and the hash route remain intact.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make append-query-params perform a small key-aware merge: before appending generated fragments, remove every existing occurrence of each key emitted by this call, then append one generated value in the current deterministic order. Preserve unrelated query entries, their values, and the fragment. Keep the codec and public signature unchanged; no compatibility layer or forgiving first/last-value parser is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Add a focused executable share-builder test whose base contains stale variant and modes values, unrelated from=index and embed=1 values, and #/stories; request a different variant and mode through the real public builder.
- Assert variant and modes each occur exactly once, URLSearchParams.get (or an equivalent standards-faithful browser assertion) returns the newly requested values, and share/parse-params reconstructs those values.
- Assert from=index, embed=1, and #/stories survive unchanged. Retain the existing no-collision existing-query case as the control.
- Demonstrate non-vacuity: the new collision fixture fails against the current append-only implementation because the browser-observed variant is story.old/a; include that red result or an equivalent mutation control in the implementation evidence.
- Run the focused JVM share tests and focused CLJS URL-state/share tests successfully.

## Non-goals

- No URL vocabulary redesign, route redesign, new state slots, parser precedence workaround, compatibility aliases, or broad query-library abstraction.
- No changes to unrelated URL-state hydration/default semantics.
- No normalization of unrelated third-party query parameters.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status bead titles and descriptions for share, URL, variant-share-url, URLSearchParams, duplicate query, stale variant, base-url, existing query, and append-query-params. No issue owns this collision. The returned share-related hits concern shared files/scratchpads/native-share and are unrelated.
acceptance_criteria: A focused test builds from a base containing stale variant/modes plus unrelated from/embed params and a hash route; the result has exactly one value for each emitted Story key, browser first-value parsing and share/parse-params recover the newly requested state, and unrelated params/hash survive. The fixture is shown red against the current append-only implementation (or by an equivalent mutation control), the pre-existing no-collision merge case remains green, and focused JVM plus CLJS share/url-state tests pass.

Minimal repair: make the builder own and clear the complete Story query-key set for state it controls, including omitted/default slots, while preserving unrelated params/hash; add focused JVM and real-URLSearchParams CLJS coverage for clearing stale optional values. No API redesign.

--- 2026-09-01 14:05 AUSEST — audit finding CONFIRMED and repaired, PR #8877 ---

The audit's premise HELD at tip, and is WIDER than the audit stated. Probed
through the real public builder (clojure -M -e, not the :test alias, whose
:main-opts swallows -e): a base carrying a stale value for all nine Story keys
came back carrying ALL EIGHT non-variant ones, not just the three the audit
named. modes/overrides/substrate were the audit's sample, not the extent —
workspace, mode-tab, viewport, background and tag-filter leak identically,
because every one of them is an optional slot build-params omits.

Mechanism as the audit described it: PR #8851 cleared the keys a call EMITTED;
build-params omits empty/nil/default slots to keep the URL minimal; so the
emitted set is a strict subset of the owned set whenever any optional slot is
empty, and the difference is exactly what survives. Same invariant broken as
the original bug, reached by omission rather than by first-value order.

THE COMPLETE STORY-OWNED QUERY-KEY SET — nine keys, and the answer to why the
bug existed at all. It was IMPLICIT, derived per call from build-params'
cond-> branches. It is now written down once, as share/story-query-keys in
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc, immediately under the ns form:

  [:variant :workspace :mode-tab :modes :viewport :background :tag-filter
   :overrides :substrate]

That is the §URL scheme list already in the ns docstring, and exactly what
url-state/params->getter reads and parse-params consumes. append-query-params
now clears all of it before appending, instead of the emitted subset.

embed= is deliberately NOT a member and must never become one: per
url-state/embed-flag-from-current-url it is chrome state, never round-tripped
through parse-params, so the builder PRESERVES it like any third-party param.
Both fixtures assert that.

No API redesign, per the audit's own limit: variant-share-url's signature, the
codec and the public surface are untouched; append-query-params stays private
with its single caller; no options map, no general query-merging utility.

No spec change. tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md §Share URL already states
the invariant this restores; the code moved onto the existing normative text.

LINE DELTAS vs the bead's cited numbers (PR #8851 had already moved them):
share.cljc:357-370 (append) -> query-param-key 357-365 + append-query-params
367-393 at my start, 384-420 after this change; share.cljc:486-505
(variant-share-url) -> 509-528 at my start, 542-567 after. The
story_share_test.clj:84-90 existing-query control is unchanged at 84-90.

DRIFT GUARD, because an explicit set is only as good as its agreement with the
builder: story-query-keys-is-the-whole-build-params-vocabulary pins the two
against each other over a fully-populated build-params call. Both new fixtures
are DERIVED from story-query-keys and assert they cover it, so a key added to
the vocabulary is covered without editing them.

on the final rebased base 480df6b48e:
  JVM focused share suite              -> exit 0, 34 tests / 106 assertions
  JVM full tools/story                 -> exit 0, 1879 tests / 6886 assertions
  JVM full tools/story-mcp             -> exit 0, 278 tests / 1457 assertions
  CLJS focused share + url-state       -> exit 0, 16 tests / 85 assertions
  node-test compile                    -> exit 0, 1866 files, 0 warnings

CONTROL — the property removed on ONE line (the pre-repair
(into #{} (map query-param-key) params)), red on BOTH host arms:
  JVM focused  -> exit 1, 17 failures, all in the new fixture; counts unchanged
                  at 34/106, so no crashed namespace and no truncated lane
  CLJS focused -> exit 1, 16 failures, all in the new CLJS fixture; counts
                  unchanged at 7/45
The CLJS arm was RECOMPILED between plant and run (111 files recompiled each
time), so the runtime demonstrably observed the plant rather than serving a
stale bundle — a green there would otherwise have proved nothing. Restore
verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff,
and both arms re-run green afterwards. The two pre-existing merge tests
(variant-share-url-merges-existing-query, variant-share-url-replaces-stale-
owned-keys) stayed green through both the red and the green runs, which is what
shows this EXTENDED #8851's repair rather than replacing it.

INCIDENTAL, not fixed here (worth a bead): url-state/url-from-state composes
the address-bar URL from {:pathname :hash} only, discarding location.search
wholesale — so embed=1 and any other third-party param is dropped from the
address bar on the first state change after mount, even though the share
builder preserves it. Opposite defect to this one, different surface.
AUDIT PR #8877 (2026-09-01): REOPENED. The complete-vocabulary repair still compares ownership on raw encoded key text, while the browser consumer uses URLSearchParams and therefore compares decoded names. A valid base URL containing `%76ariant=story.old%2Fa` is semantically `variant`; variant-share-url preserves it and appends literal `variant=story.new%2Fb`. Real URLSearchParams then reports getAll("variant") = ["story.old/a", "story.new/b"] and get("variant") = "story.old/a", so the shared cell is still stale. Minimal repair: decode only the existing key half for the ownership comparison on both hosts, while preserving raw unrelated entries/order and malformed entries; add focused JVM and real-URLSearchParams CLJS coverage. No general URL abstraction or normalization layer.
AUDIT PR #8884: UPDATED. This PR correctly unifies the share and address-bar writers on `apply-story-params`, so the still-open encoded-key ownership defect from PR #8877 now also affects live state-driven URL writes. Reproduction through the real `url-from-state`: location search `?%76ariant=story.old%2Fa&embed=1` plus state `:story.new/b` produces `/p/?%76ariant=story.old%2Fa&embed=1&variant=story.new%2Fb#/stories`; real URLSearchParams reports `getAll("variant") = ["story.old/a", "story.new/b"]` and `get("variant") = "story.old/a"`. The next reload therefore restores the stale cell even though this PR promises the two writers share one exact ownership boundary. Keep the repair in the shared helper, and add an address-bar regression alongside the already-requested JVM/browser share-builder probes; do not add a second merge path.

--- 2026-09-01 20:15 AUSEST - audit finding CONFIRMED and repaired, PR #8917 ---

Worked from the AUDIT PR #8884 note, confirmed the newest text-bearing
mutation by a bd history walk carried to the item's beginning (525 entries;
distinct field-snapshots at indices 0, 49, 69, 205, 206, 230, 304, 323, 324,
344, oldest at 524 with notes empty). The #8884 note is the last notes change,
at about 17:51 AUSEST; every entry after it is a checkpoint no-op with an
identical snapshot. No comments, no children, no dependencies.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE AND IT HELD, byte-for-byte. Probed through the real
public surface with clojure -M -e (not the :test alias, whose :main-opts
swallows -e). The address-bar reproduction returned exactly the string the
audit quoted, and the share-builder one alongside it. Real Node URLSearchParams
over that result returned getAll variant as story.old/a then story.new/b, and
get variant as story.old/a. So the widened finding was correct on both writers.

THE DEFECT, precisely. apply-story-params built its owned set by ENCODING the
nine story-query-keys names and compared that against the RAW key text of each
existing fragment. query-param-key's own docstring stated the reasoning that
was the bug: every Story-owned key is plain ASCII, so its encoded spelling is
its literal name. True of the names, irrelevant to the input: a BASE URL may
spell the same key with escapes, and URLSearchParams compares names after
decoding. So %76ariant survived the clear, the generated variant was appended
behind it, and .get - first value - handed the hydrator the stale cell.

HOW THE PERCENT-ENCODED KEY NAME IS HANDLED. A new tolerant url-decode sits
beside url-encode; query-param-key now returns the DECODED key half, and the
owned set is the plain names. Three properties made explicit because each is a
way to get this wrong:

  1. Decoding is an ownership TEST, never a rewrite. Kept fragments are
     re-emitted byte-for-byte in their original order, escapes and all. Only
     the key half is decoded, and only to decide membership.
  2. An undecodable key half - a lone percent, a truncated escape - yields nil
     rather than throwing or passing through. Nil is in no owned set, so the
     entry falls through and is preserved. It must never abort the merge.
  3. Plus is a space in a query component, so both hosts fold it: URLDecoder
     already does, and the CLJS arm rewrites plus to %20 before
     decodeURIComponent, which does not. Without that the two hosts could
     classify the same URL differently and the JVM tests would stop being
     evidence about the browser. Consequence worth stating: mode+tab reads as
     mode space tab, which is NOT Story's mode-tab, so it is correctly
     PRESERVED. Pinned on both hosts.

ONE MERGE PATH, as the note required. The repair is entirely inside the shared
apply-story-params; no second writer, no options map, no general query
utility. variant-share-url's signature, the codec, story-query-keys and the
public surface are untouched, and append-query-params' successor stays private
with its single caller. No spec change: 005-SOTA-Features.md Share URL already
states the invariant this restores.

COVERAGE - six fixtures plus two fixture-guards, all DERIVED from
story-query-keys so a key added to the vocabulary is covered without editing
them. Share builder: variant-share-url-owns-percent-encoded-key-spellings
(JVM) and variant-share-url-owns-percent-encoded-keys-cljs (real
URLSearchParams). Address bar, which the #8884 note asked for specifically:
url-from-state-clears-percent-encoded-story-keys and
url-from-state-clears-every-escaped-story-key (JVM),
url-from-state-clears-escaped-story-keys-through-urlsearchparams and
url-from-state-clears-every-escaped-story-key-cljs (real URLSearchParams).
Preservation: apply-story-params-preserves-undecodable-and-unowned-keys and
undecodable-and-unowned-keys-survive-cljs. The two guards
(escaped-story-keys-are-the-same-keys-to-the-browser and its CLJS sibling)
pin that the escaped spellings really ARE the owned keys after decoding
before anything relies on them - the CLJS one asserts that against
js/URLSearchParams itself. url-from-state-and-share-builder-agree-on-escaped-
keys pins that the fix reached both writers rather than one.

EVIDENCE - runner-captured exits, echo of the runner's own status in the same
shell as the redirect, on the final rebased base 261994ae5e:
  JVM focused share + url-state -> exit 0, 99 tests / 264 assertions
  JVM full tools/story          -> exit 0, 1887 tests / 6939 assertions
  JVM full tools/story-mcp      -> exit 0, 279 tests / 1476 assertions
  CLJS node-test compile        -> exit 0, 1869 files, 0 warnings
  CLJS focused share + url-state-> exit 0, 23 tests / 173 assertions
  CLJS full consolidated suite  -> exit 0, 11131 tests / 55032 assertions

CONTROL - the property removed on ONE line (url-decode replaced by identity in
query-param-key, which is exactly the pre-repair raw comparison), red on BOTH
host arms:
  JVM focused  -> exit 1, 23 failures, all in the three new fixtures; counts
                  unchanged at 99/264, so no crashed ns and no truncated lane
  CLJS focused -> exit 1, 34 failures, all in the three new CLJS fixtures;
                  counts unchanged at 23/173
The CLJS arm RECOMPILED 111 files between plant and run, and 111 again on the
restore, so the runtime demonstrably observed each change rather than serving
a stale bundle. The plant anchor was counted before each run (exactly 1 match)
so a silent no-op plant was excluded. Restore verified by git blob hash against
the committed object (a561b9db33fa2280ac927e25eaee4e3102d53d12 both sides), not
by reading a diff, and both arms re-run green afterwards.

NOT DEFANGED. Every pre-existing merge test stayed green through BOTH the red
and the green runs: variant-share-url-merges-existing-query,
variant-share-url-replaces-stale-owned-keys,
variant-share-url-clears-stale-omitted-keys,
url-from-state-preserves-unowned-query-params and
url-from-state-clears-every-stale-story-key. That is what shows this EXTENDS
the PR #8851 and #8877 repairs rather than replacing them. The change is
strictly additive to the ownership match - decoding WIDENS the owned-key match
and never narrows it, since url-encode is the identity on all nine plain-ASCII
names - so no existing assertion changed meaning.

CLJS LANE, how it was run without narrowing the shared build id: full
compile via scripts/compile-node-test.cjs node-test, then RUNTIME namespace
selection with node out/node-test.js --test=<ns>,<ns>. That is the route
rf2-6t03c's comment names as the safe one; no --config-merge against
:node-test, so no shared-cache poisoning. The compile prints its config path,
which is the lane's own proof of which tree it read.

GATE NOMINATION. The diff is five files, all under tools/story: no markdown,
no spec, no implementation runtime code, no workflows. check_doc_slugs.py and
check_readme_links.py have no path in this diff to inspect, so neither is

FIXTURE-HELPER NOTE, recorded because it is a real trap for the next reader:
the JVM key-count helper called URLDecoder/decode bare and threw on the
deliberately malformed %zz and 100% entries, where the builder catches and
falls through. Two ERRORs on the first run, in the TEST helper and not in the
production path. The helper now mirrors the builder's fall-through, which is
what makes it measure what the browser would see.

Since PR #8884 unified the share builder and url-from-state on this one helper, the defect reached live address-bar writes too; the address-bar reproduction returned the audit's quoted string byte-for-byte. title: api-manifest omits the published re-frame.hicasso door on both hosts
description:
## Scope

The generic public-API manifest pipeline in `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/**`, its committed `spec/api-manifest.edn` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` outputs, and the published public door `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc`.

## Correctness finding

The API-manifest gate promises drift detection for public vars, but `re-frame.hicasso` is absent from both host inventories: the JVM generator does not load it, and the CLJS analyzer probe does not enumerate it. Additions, removals, or renames in this published split-host public namespace can therefore remain invisible to the repository's generic API-contract gate.

## Evidence

- `implementation/hicasso/deps.edn` publishes `day8/re-frame2-hicasso` and declares `re-frame.hicasso` as its build main; the namespace describes itself as "HICASSO — the public door."
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/deps.edn` says its classpath contains core plus every optional feature artefact, but has no Hicasso local root.
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj` says `--check` detects a public var added, removed, or renamed, but its `jvm-namespaces` roster omits `re-frame.hicasso`.
- The CLJS probe `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/test/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs` neither requires `re-frame.hicasso` nor includes it in its live-public or fully-rowed namespace sets.
- Neither committed API-manifest file contains a `re-frame.hicasso` row, despite the namespace exporting JVM macros such as `defview`, `event`, and `defhost`, plus CLJS runtime aliases/functions.
- The former Hicasso-specific public-surface/naming census was removed with the other retired one-off policy gates under `rf2-6c12m.8`; no live complete census makes this generic omission harmless.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the API generator in check mode from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`; it passes while producing no `re-frame.hicasso` rows.
2. Run the existing CLJS manifest probe; it passes although its namespace roster does not contain `re-frame.hicasso`.
3. As a temporary control, add a harmless public CLJS function beside Hicasso's existing runtime aliases and rerun the probe. The current probe still cannot report that public because it never requires or enumerates the namespace. Restore the control.
4. The equivalent JVM control is a temporary public macro beside `defhost`: generator `--check` remains unaware because Hicasso is absent from both its classpath and namespace roster.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A maintainer adds or renames a Hicasso public runtime alias, or removes/renames a public macro, while updating ordinary call sites. The API generator check and CLJS manifest reconciliation can both stay green because neither host ever asks about that namespace. The required invariant is: every live public var exposed by the published `re-frame.hicasso` door is represented and reconciled on its applicable host, and stale rows are rejected.

## Recommended minimal fix

Use the existing generic machinery: add the Hicasso local root to the manifest tool classpath, enroll `re-frame.hicasso` in JVM generation, and enroll its runtime side in the existing CLJS analyzer probe/fully-rowed reconciliation. Model the `.cljc` host split with the existing classification-row and sidecar facilities, then regenerate the committed manifests. Do not add another bespoke checker or workflow job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The JVM generator loads `re-frame.hicasso`, and the committed manifest contains and reconciles its public JVM macros.
- The CLJS analyzer probe enumerates `re-frame.hicasso` and reconciles every live CLJS public runtime var for that namespace.
- An executable non-vacuity assertion fails when Hicasso coverage is absent or empty on either applicable host; merely running a green generic gate with zero Hicasso rows is not acceptance.
- A focused positive control temporarily introduces an unclassified Hicasso public on the CLJS side and proves the owning probe fails naming that var; a stale/missing JVM macro row likewise makes generator `--check` fail. After restoration, both focused gates pass.
- Existing manifest projections/consumers remain green against the regenerated authoritative rows.

## Non-goals

No resurrection of the retired Hicasso naming/budget census, no new CI job, no Hicasso API redesign, no runtime behavior change, and no attempt to make Hicasso an adapter discriminator.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status searches for `api manifest`, `manifest`, `hicasso manifest`, `public api`, `re-frame.hicasso`, and `api-manifest` found no open or in-progress duplicate. Closed `rf2-wf1ey` corrected documentation navigation and explicitly noted that Hicasso had zero manifest rows, but did not request enrollment. Closed `rf2-hxbhe`/`rf2-st1x5` concerned the former bespoke census, later deliberately removed by `rf2-6c12m.8`; extending the surviving generic manifest is distinct and preserves that consolidation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. JVM manifest generation includes and reconciles the public `re-frame.hicasso` macros.
2. The CLJS analyzer probe includes and fully reconciles the namespace's live runtime publics.
3. Coverage has an executable non-vacuity assertion: absent or empty Hicasso coverage on either applicable host fails.
4. A temporary unclassified CLJS public fails the focused probe naming the var, and a stale/missing JVM macro row fails generator `--check`; restored sources and regenerated manifests pass.
5. Existing manifest projections/consumers pass without adding a bespoke checker or CI job.
notes:
VERDICT (PR #8895, branch worker/manifest-phm7g, base 8451531aed)

BOTH ARMS OF THE FINDING HOLD, verified at source, with the distinct causes the item states.
JVM: implementation/scripts/api-manifest/deps.edn carried no Hicasso local root AND gen.clj
jvm-namespaces did not name re-frame.hicasso, so the generator could not have loaded it.
CLJS: cljs_manifest_probe_cljs_test.cljs neither required the namespace nor listed it in
live-publics or fully-rowed, so the probe never enumerated it.

INITIAL INVENTORY vs DRIFT. The generated manifest diff is exactly 14 added rows plus the
var-count line (479 -> 493). No row removed, no row changed: enrolling the door caught NO
pre-existing drift. The surface was correct all along, merely unwatched.

SPLIT-HOST MODELLING. The door is a .cljc whose arms are disjoint. Its 3 authoring macros
(defview, defhost, event) are the clj arm, rowed under :classification with :kind :macro
DERIVED by the generator from live vars. Its 11 runtime aliases are the cljs arm, rowed
under :cljs-only. :jvm-only-classification needs NO entry, and that was MEASURED not
assumed: the macros are require-macros-referred by the door own cljs arm, so the analyzer
carries them and they reconcile normally. The probe is green with those 3 rows present,
which it could not be if the analyzer omitted them.

THE REPAIR STAYED GENERIC. No Hicasso-shaped branch. Notable: emit-classification-rows,
the .cljc split-host facility, existed with ZERO call sites - this is the case it was
built for and its first user.

TWO GENERIC NON-VACUITY ASSERTIONS (acceptance criterion 3), neither naming Hicasso:
runtime-verified-rows-are-actually-covered makes the curated :runtime-verified? flag
executable (every probe check is conditional on live-publics membership, so deleting an
entry turns the probe green over a surface it stopped watching); and
every-jvm-namespace-contributes-rows asserts each rostered namespace yields at least one
committed row (--check is green whenever generated and committed AGREE, including that a
rostered namespace inventories nothing).

CONTROLS, all restores verified by git blob hash.
Positive control before believing green: added public in re-frame.epoch, exit 2 naming
re-frame.epoch/planted-control-var, restore blob dde73810a5220ec7be31969573363ed2c94b5e3e.
JVM red: 14 rows stripped from committed manifest, gen --check exit 1 naming all 14 AND
every-jvm-namespace-contributes-rows exit 1 (1 failure of 74, scoped, no cascade), restore
blob 2ae92d2e08a1b3b198f195a9932eda91ae909d53.
CLJS red: public added to the cljs arm, probe exit 1 naming
re-frame.hicasso/planted-control-public, 113 files recompiled as positive evidence the
runtime saw the plant, restore blob 03ba4a6d8411ff8ac21801fa62f39ded7761b1f0, recompiled
and re-run green.

GATES (runner exit codes, captured on the same command line, re-run on the final rebased
base): gen --check 0 (493 vars); api-md-check 0; story-spec-check 0; xray-spec-check 0;
skills-check 0; doc-guide-check 0; doc-api-check 0 (171 eligible vars have page+member);
clojure -M:test 0 (74 tests, 156 assertions); full CLJS node-test 0 (11149 tests, 54867
assertions); focused probe 0 (4 tests, 44 assertions); check_doc_slugs 0;
check_readme_links --ci 0; mkdocs build --strict 0; check_guide_samples 0.

SCOPE EXPANSION FOR THE MAYOR TO NOTE. Enrolment gave doc-api-check an opinion it never
had: every manifest var at an eligible tier needs a docs/api/NAMESPACE.md page plus a
member heading, and the door had neither. Added docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md as a terse
var index pointing at the existing 631-line docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md rather than
duplicating it, plus an mkdocs nav entry. The :doc-api-coverage-exempt hatch was
deliberately NOT used: it is for a var documented only as a facade pointer elsewhere, and
misusing it would have recreated the exact fail-open shape this item exists to close.

A STALE DISPOSITION OVERTURNED. docs/api/README.md said the door carries no api-manifest
rows and that this is deliberate rather than an oversight. That was rf2-wf1ey of
2026-08-16; this item names rf2-wf1ey and rules past it, so the paragraph described the
opposite of the tree. Rewritten: the DOOR is tracked on both hosts, its OPTIONAL MODULES
still are not.

CURATED AXES, worth a maintainer glance since the item did not rule them: :tier :advanced
throughout (restrictive-by-default per API.md Tier taxonomy, since Hicasso is an opt-in
substrate whose door is not the front-porch set the Guide loads); :owner 004C for the four
root-lifecycle verbs (Roots-and-Mount names this door impl/mount.cljs as its in-tree
realisation) and 006 for the rest.

INCIDENTAL FINDING. docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md said the door has Fifteen names
while its own code block listed fourteen. The manifest now MEASURES it - full completeness
in both directions reconciles against exactly 14 - so the prose was corrected. The

did not measure and was left alone.

ALSO OBSERVED, NOT ACTIONED: gen.clj namespaces-under is a roster-completeness gate with
no consumer anywhere in the repo (dead code since it was written).

No spec/*.md normative document touched. No new CI job. No runtime behaviour change.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8895 (branch worker/manifest-phm7g). Both host arms enrolled: JVM generator loads re-frame.hicasso (classpath local root + jvm-namespaces roster) and rows its 3 authoring macros; the CLJS analyzer probe enumerates the door and reconciles its 11 runtime aliases plus those 3 macro rows at full completeness, using the existing emit-classification-rows .cljc facility (its first call site). Manifest 479 -> 493, all 14 rows initial inventory with zero drift caught. Non-vacuity pinned generically on both hosts. Red-on-both-arms controls exercised with blob-hash-verified restores. Supersedes rf2-wf1ey deliberate-omission note in docs/api/README.md, which this item names and rules past.

title: Xray Trace drops every real FX argument by reading nonexistent singular tags
description:
## Scope

Repair the Dynamic Trace panel's FX target/detail projection in tools/xray. Scope is the raw-trace-to-row seam in day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers and its focused dual-target test. Reconcile the fixture with the framework's shipped FX vocabulary; do not redesign the panel.

## Findings

Correctness finding: target-detail reads :rf.fx/arg and :rf.fx/value, but the framework emits FX arguments under canonical :rf.fx/args. Every real :rf.fx/handled row therefore projects only its fx id, dropping the argument from the main target/detail column and hover title. The existing test is green because it fabricates the nonexistent singular :rf.fx/arg key.

## Evidence

- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:575-579 reads :rf.fx/arg / :rf.fx/value.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:1234-1239 emits successful :rf.fx/handled rows with :rf.fx/id and :rf.fx/args. Exception, skipped-platform, and no-such-fx rows use the same plural key at lines 1455-1463, 1583-1601, 1617-1626, and 1651-1660.

## Steps to Reproduce

2. Dispatch the event and open Xray's Dynamic Trace panel on that event bundle.
3. Inspect the :rf.fx/handled row. The framework trace carries {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}}, but the target/detail cell and hover title show only :app/audit.

A focused test passes a producer-shaped :rf.fx/handled event with {:rf.fx/id :app/audit, :rf.fx/args {:message "saved"}} through target-detail or project-row and asserts :app/audit -> {:message "saved"}. The fixture explicitly contains neither singular key; this non-vacuity check fails on the current implementation.

4. From tools/xray, clojure -M:test -n day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.trace-helpers-cljs-test passes, and the CLJS node-test lane containing the same .cljc namespace passes.
