- rf2-czlb (closed) fixed unknown boundary props and malformed :on-error; its scope explicitly preserved the legal vector/function arms. It does not own the accepted vector's nil-frame behavior.
- rf2-4e5b (closed) addressed the analogous but separate frameless overlay :on-dismiss state.
- No open or in-progress bead owns vector :on-error being silently dropped without a frame.
notes:
## Verdict — 2026-09-01 (PR #8871)

FINDING CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, repaired, witnessed. Every file:line on this
bead re-derived at tip and confirmed EXACT: check-props!'s :on-error arm at
boundary.cljs:219-229, frame-of 232-235, report! 237-257, the render's frame
re-establishment 309-328, api-reference.md:183, cookbook.md:408-411. One
drift only, and it is trivial: the witness citation 404-449 names the
section comment three lines above frameless-root!, whose actual span is
407-449.

The 309-328 claim also holds as stated, and it is the shape of the fix: the
boundary re-establishes the frame around the codec walk of :fallback and
:children, so an intent at either is caught and named, while :on-error is
read straight off the props map by report! and passes through no lowering at
all. That was the one intent position a frameless boundary accepted and then
dropped.

### Site chosen: check-props!, in render

Not report!. A refusal from componentDidCatch would replace the
application's real error with a complaint about the declaration and escape
to the next boundary up — the namespace docstring already argues exactly
this for the existing shape check, and React runs render before it can run
componentDidCatch. A missing frame sharpens the argument: it is the case
where refusing late is not merely worse but indistinguishable from working,
because the fallback renders either way.

Within render the guard went into check-props! rather than inline, because
all three refusals are one class — a declaration the boundary wears while
nothing consults it — and belong at one site. check-props! now takes the
caller's frame-kw; render binds frame-kw first.

report!'s when-some on frame-of was REMOVED. It is provably dead once the
same render refuses the frameless case, and left in place it would still be
the silent drop, one guard later.

### Complaint contract UNCHANGED

Reuses :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :position :on-error
and the offending :intent. impl.overlay/dismissal-handler already refuses an
unroutable :on-dismiss under that id (the rf2-4e5b analogue), and
implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md's row — "lowered or fired an
intent with no frame-locked dispatch bound" — covers this site as written.
So complaints.md is untouched, and so is invariants.md: the repair makes the
code conform to I10/I11 rather than changing what they promise. That also
avoided the three-Chromium-lane toll a spec/ prose edit carries (rf2-7rzg).

### Control

Landed RED FIRST. Commit 1 is the witness alone against unrepaired source:
exit 1, 3 failures of 54 assertions, all three in
a-frameless-boundarys-own-on-error-vector-is-refused-at-first-render, with
"Escaped: nil" — nothing raised at all, the silent acceptance stated as a
measurement. After the repair: exit 0, same 11 tests and the SAME 54
assertions, so nothing skipped or crashed out of the lane. Re-run as an
explicit sabotage afterwards (checkout of the pre-repair blob) reproduced
exit 1 with the identical three failures; shadow-cljs reported "4 compiled",
which is the positive evidence the runtime observed the plant rather than
serving a stale compile. Restore verified by git blob hash against the
committed object.

Positive controls all green and all pre-existing except one: frameless with
no :on-error still renders (row 6); the same vector under a live frame still
dispatches (row 9's near miss); with the error appended, exactly once (row
10, StrictMode). Added: a frameless boundary with a FUNCTION :on-error
catching a real descendant failure and firing once — the near miss on the
exact axis this guard could have over-reached, and it passed against
UNREPAIRED source too, so it is a genuine control rather than a co-moving
assertion.

### Gates

Local, captured exit codes: full :browser-test lane 753 tests / 4115
assertions, exit 0; :node-test 11128 tests / 54669 assertions, exit 0;
check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, and exercised against a planted broken link which
it caught (exit 1, naming file and line), so its green is a check that ran.
CI on PR #8871: 84 checks, 47 pass / 37 skipping / 0 failures — including
the three-engine cljs-hicasso-controlled gate and MkDocs build, neither of
which was runnable locally.

### One scope addition, stated

docs/core/hicasso/17-errors.md gained ONE troubleshooting row for the new
refusal, beside the fallback-intent row that raises the same id. The
complaint contract did not change, so this is teaching prose rather than
catalogue prose; without it the chapter that teaches h/error-boundary would
be silent about a user-visible refusal at its own component. It mirrors the
existing row 13-overlays-and-focus.md:353 carries for the :on-dismiss
analogue. Table column counts checked by hand across all 9 rows.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8871 (worker/hicasso-boundary-wdvlp). check-props! now takes the render's frame-kw and refuses a vector :on-error with no frame, reusing :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary with :position :on-error and the offending :intent — the same contract impl.overlay/dismissal-handler uses for an unroutable :on-dismiss (rf2-4e5b's analogue), so no complaint catalogue or invariant prose changed. report!'s when-some on frame-of removed as provably dead. Witnessed by a new row in boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test that was landed RED first (3 failures, 'Escaped: nil') and is green after; existing frameless-no-intent, live-frame-dispatch and StrictMode-once controls all still pass. See the appended Verdict note for the line-number re-derivation and gate exit codes.

title: [views] adapter switch makes the lookup cache fall back to the stale registered head
description:
## Scope

The registry-keyed UIx view path spanning `implementation/adapters/uix/**`, the adapter seam consumed by `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs`, its React-hook shared tests, and the public UIx registry-addressing contract. This is specifically the value registered by `rf/reg-view*` and returned by `rf/view` when the UIx adapter is active.

## Correctness finding

The documented UIx registry-keyed path does not return a component head that UIx/React can mount. `build-frame-aware-view` unconditionally attaches `{:contextType frame-context}` with CLJS metadata, so `(rf/view id)` is a `MetaFn` object rather than a JavaScript function component. Passing that advertised value directly to UIx `$` / React `createElement` fails React's element-type validation before the registered view renders.

The obvious partial repair—only removing the metadata—is also incorrect for UIx. UIx sends lossless CLJS props through its `argv` channel only for a native/marked UIx component head; a generic React function goes through JS-prop conversion. The registered outer wrapper therefore needs to be both genuinely mountable and on UIx's native prop-marshalling path. It must also preserve a real React component boundary for hooks rather than requiring callers to invoke the registered function inside an ad-hoc host component.

## Evidence

- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:16` tells users to use `rf/reg-view*` for registry-keyed view addressing; `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:109` and `:253-262` repeat that UIx contract.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs:496-612` (`build-frame-aware-view`) creates the registered head with `(with-meta (fn frame-aware-view ...) {:contextType frame-context})`. `reg-view*` stores and returns that value at `:614-650`.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:6610-6625` explicitly records the current defect: `(rf/view id)` is a CLJS `MetaFn`, React cannot use it as a component type directly, so the test mounts a plain JS `host` that manually invokes `render-fn`. The void-root test repeats this bypass at `:6670-6678`. Those tests therefore prove teardown below the workaround, not the advertised registry-head mount.
- `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:93-106` and `:131-138` require native `defui` shells specifically because UIx reconstructs lossless CLJS props there. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1627-1650` documents the prior failure when a plain function sat below `$`: namespaced keyword values were mangled and frame selection silently changed.
- Reading the pinned `com.pitch/uix.core` 1.4.4 sources (`uix/core.clj`, `uix/compiler/alpha.cljs`) confirms `defui` stamps a JS function as a UIx component and UIx's compiler uses that marker to carry original CLJS props in `argv`; the generic React-component branch converts props instead.
- Repository search found no UIx test that mounts `(rf/view id)` directly as the `$` component head. Existing UIx DOM coverage either mounts `wrap-view` itself or uses the manual-invocation host above.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install `uix-adapter/adapter`, define a UIx `defui` component that receives a CLJS prop and calls `uix-adapter/use-subscribe`, then register it with `(rf/reg-view* ::row row)`.
2. Under the normal UIx frame boundary, render `($ (rf/view ::row) {:payload {:tenant/id :tenant/admin}})` without an intermediate function that invokes the returned value.
3. Observe that React rejects the `MetaFn` as an invalid element type before the registered view renders. The existing shared browser test avoids this result only by mounting a plain JS host component that manually invokes `(rf/view id)`.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A registry-keyed UIx component cannot be used through the component syntax the public docs advertise. If a caller copies the test workaround, hooks and instance lifetime belong to that host and the UIx component's `argv` prop contract is bypassed.

Invariant: every public value advertised as a UIx component head must be directly mountable through `$`, receive the original CLJS props/children losslessly, own a real React hook boundary, and retain the registration wrapper's frame, tracing, source-coordinate, display-name, and unmount behavior.

## Recommended minimal fix

Make the UIx adapter's registered-view result an outer, stable, native/marked UIx component shell after the shared frame-aware/instrumentation wrapper has been composed. That shell should receive props through UIx's `argv` path and delegate them without JS round-tripping while retaining a genuine React component boundary. Adjust the shared registration seam only as much as needed to let a React-hook adapter own that outer componentization; do not merely strip `with-meta`, and do not document the manual-invocation host as the solution.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Add a focused browser test under `implementation/adapters/uix/test/` that installs the UIx adapter, registers a hook-using `defui` via `rf/reg-view*`, and mounts `($ (rf/view id) props)` directly under the normal UIx frame boundary. The test must contain no host function that calls the registered value manually.
2. Pass a nested CLJS prop containing a namespaced keyword/value through that direct mount and assert exact equality inside the registered component; include children if the chosen public form supports them.
3. Have the registered component call `uix-adapter/use-subscribe` (and/or `use-frame`), assert its initial DOM, dispatch an update, and assert the DOM rerenders. Capture browser page errors plus `console.error` and assert there is no invalid-element-type or hook-boundary failure.
4. Retain executable coverage for registered-view render traces/source coordinates, stable instance identity, and exactly-once unmount emission; remove the shared suite's manual-host rationale/bypass where the direct UIx mount now covers it.
5. Non-vacuity/control: in the same harness, directly mount an unregistered native `defui` with the same prop/hook probe and show the harness passes independently of the registry path. During implementation, temporarily restore the current metadata-wrapped returned head (or remove the new UIx componentization seam) and record that the new registry row fails while the native control remains green.
6. `npm run test:browser` from `implementation/` passes with the new direct-mount witness and the existing UIx adapter browser coverage.

## Non-goals

- No new registry API or mandatory host/wrapper ceremony for callers.
- No Reagent registration rewrite.
- No broad React interop compatibility layer or support for arbitrary non-UIx prop conventions.
- No unrelated refactor of the shared spine, tracing schema, or UIx hooks.
- No docs-only workaround.

## Related/duplicate search

Searched the full bead corpus by title and description with `bd search "UIx" --status all`, `bd search` for `MetaFn`, `reg-view*`, `registry-keyed view`, `rf/view UIx`, and `invalid element type`, plus `bd list --all --desc-contains` for `MetaFn`, `reg-view*`, `(rf/view`, and `uix-component?`. Repeated the material terms against `--status open,in_progress`; there were no matches. Closed `rf2-9hcyf` concerns a copy-pasteable UIx component test recipe, and closed `rf2-3afns` concerns Story selecting the wrong substrate; neither owns direct mountability of a registered UIx view.
acceptance_criteria: A focused CLJS test registers while a componentizing adapter is active (so the registrar stores H1), switches to a differently componentizing or non-componentizing adapter, and proves at least two consecutive `rf/view` lookups both return the new correct stable head and never H1. The cache continues to recognize its original registrar face across re-derivations, while genuine foreign re-registrations pass through untouched. Do not rewrite the registrar or add public API.
notes:
---
## Verdict (2026-09-01, PR #8874)

CONFIRMED and FIXED. Both premise checks the bead asked for hold.

**Premise (a) — line numbers.** Essentially zero drift. `build-frame-aware-view` is at views.cljs:496 exactly as cited (its body ends 612; `with-meta` closes at 578). `reg-view*` is at :614 as cited. The shared-suite citations are within ~2 lines: the manual-host rationale sits at 6610-6621 (cited 6610-6625) and the void-root repeat at 6667-6672 (cited 6670-6678).

**Premise (b) — the bypass.** Still present and still read exactly as described: both rows mounted `(fn host-cmp [_props] (render-fn))` and the comment named the MetaFn as the reason. Removed in this PR; both rows now mount `(rf/view id)` directly.

**Mechanism, verified at source rather than from the bead's summary.** `uix.compiler.alpha/component-element` (uix.core 1.4.4, read from the pinned jar) branches on `(.-uix-component? component-type)`: marked heads take `uix-component-element`, which stashes the ORIGINAL CLJS props map on `argv`; everything else takes `react-component-element` -> `interpret-attrs`, which converts props and drops keyword namespaces. A MetaFn has no marker, so it fell to the React branch and `createElement` rejected the object.

**Repair.** New OPTIONAL `:adapter/componentize-view` late-bind hook, consulted last in `reg-view*` (after the substrate wrap and the frame-aware wrapper compose, so the shell is outermost and every existing wrapper keeps its frame/tracing/source-coord/unmount behaviour). Seam split follows rf2-z7hfp's frame-provider precedent: `spine/make-componentize-view` builds the substrate-agnostic forwarding shell; the UIx adapter stamps `uix-component?` on it. The marker -- not the meta-stripping -- is what makes the mount correct. The shell is a marked FORWARDER, not a `defui`: `defui` glues `argv` for its own body, so the shell must pass the props object down untouched for the registered component (typically itself a `defui`) to read in its own idiom -- which is what keeps `(rf/reg-view* ::row row)` ceremony-free, per the bead's Non-goals. Reagent publishes no hook and is unaffected.

The head remains the callable render fn Spec 001 describes. The shell separates React's `Component(props, secondArg)` call from direct positional invocation; react-dom 19.2.0's `updateFunctionComponent` passes `void 0` as `secondArg` (read from source), so without that split a stray undefined would reach the user fn and the rf2-rpgq8 render-args capture.

**No spec change was needed, and this was checked rather than assumed.** Spec 001 s`(re-frame.core/view id)` says "the registered render fn (whatever shape)" -- the change is a strict superset. `spec/Conventions.md:1762` is a generic `:adapter/<surface>` pattern row with examples, not an enumeration, so the HOT-ZONE file stayed untouched. No new public adapter Var, so `spec/API.md` needs no row either.

**Acceptance criteria.** AC1-AC3 met by the new browser row `direct-mount-of-registered-view-head` in `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (no manual host anywhere in the file; nested namespaced-keyword prop asserted for exact equality inside the component; trailing `$` child; `use-subscribe` + `use-frame`; console.error AND window-error capture asserted clean of invalid-element-type and hook-boundary diagnostics). AC4 met: both shared-suite rows now mount the head directly, plus a third row pinning stable instance identity and continued headless callability. AC5 met (control below). AC6 met.

**Gates (captured exit codes, all on the final rebased base fd0113d5bf).** browser compile 0; browser run 0 (755 tests / 4130 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors); node lane `test:cljs` 0 (11133 / 54718, 0 failures); late-bind drift JVM 0; `:advanced` prod-elision release build 0 and its browser run 0 (91 / 289) -- run deliberately because the shell exists in production builds and `uix-component?` is a property name under a release compile.

**Control (AC5) -- the gate bites.** Restoring the metadata-wrapped head (hook key pointed at a non-existent key; source change proved by blob hash, 313 files recompiled so the runtime saw it) turned the browser run RED, exit 1: `direct-mount-of-registered-view-head` failed 9 assertions, the first reading verbatim "Element type is invalid: expected a string ... but got: object", while `native-defui-control-mounts-independently-of-the-registry` -- the same probe body and the same assertion block, mounted as an unregistered native defui -- stayed GREEN. The two de-bypassed shared-suite rows also errored, which shows the bypass removal was load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object (35f57741a4467ede665e33b162a1523e5779f426, both sides). A second control confirmed the late-bind drift gate is non-vacuous: removing the directory row reds it in both directions.

**Found beyond the brief.** `make-react-adapter` initially routed the new hook unconditionally, so every React-shaped caller supplying no factory published a NIL impl -- and `route-hook!` stores what it is handed and calls it once its adapter is installed, so the first `reg-view*` under that adapter THREW instead of declining. The browser lane could not see this; the node lane caught it as 16 errors, all on `re-frame.hicasso.substrate`, which owns its own view path (the spine's bench/test adapters are in the same position). Fixed by guarding the routing on the factory being present. Worth remembering as a general hazard of `route-hook!`: an optional routed hook must not be published at all when its impl is absent, because a routed nil is indistinguishable from a published handler until it is called.
AUDIT PR #8874 (2026-09-01): REOPENED. The new componentization is decided at registration time through a routed hook, so it still misses the repository's canonical boot order. `boot-and-mount-an-app.md` requires registration namespaces (including views) at namespace load, before `run` calls `rf/init!`. In that sequence `:adapter/componentize-view` sees no installed adapter, `route-hook!` returns nil, `apply-adapter-componentize-view` keeps the MetaFn, and `init!` only seats the adapter—it never revisits existing `:view` entries. `(rf/view id)` therefore remains a non-JS-function and the advertised direct UIx `$` mount still fails. The new browser fixture installs UIx before every `reg-view*`, so it cannot see this normal path. Minimal repair: add a register-before-init → init-UIx → direct-mount witness and make existing view registrations acquire the UIx head without requiring application authors to move top-level registrations into `run`; retain post-init registration, inactive-adapter routing, and stable lookup identity. No broad adapter redesign.

--------

## Verdict (2026-09-01, PR #8909) — the AUDIT reopen

CONFIRMED and FIXED. The audit's claim holds exactly as written, and was verified at source rather than taken from the note.

**Mechanism.** substrate-adapter/route-hook! (adapter.cljc:788) wraps every published impl in a closure that dispatches to it ONLY while same-adapter? says its adapter is the installed one, and otherwise chains to the previous handler or calls fallback-fn — (constantly nil) for this hook. reg-view* consulted it at REGISTRATION. Under boot-and-mount-an-app.md's order the registration namespaces load first, at ns-load, and run calls rf/init! afterwards, so the consultation happened with no adapter installed, returned nil, apply-adapter-componentize-view kept the MetaFn, and install-adapter! (which only seats a generation and re-arms the SSR emitter) never revisits existing :view slots. Every row that installed the adapter before registering sailed past it.

**Repair — a SEAM fix, not an adapter one.** The head is not a property of the registration; it is a property of (registration x installed substrate), and the substrate is not knowable at registration under the canonical order. So derive it at LOOKUP and memoize. views/view-head is what re-frame.core/view calls on CLJS. Validity is keyed on BOTH halves: the composed wrapper's object identity (a re-registration or hot-reload forces re-derivation, and a :view slot views.cljs did not build is handed back untouched) and the adapter spec via same-adapter? (a dispose then install of a different substrate re-derives rather than serving a UIx-marked shell to Reagent). Identity is stable within an adapter generation, so React reconciles (rf/view id) as one component type. Post-init registration is unaffected — the reg-time derivation seeds the cache and the first lookup is a hit.

**Why the registrar slot is NOT rewritten on the lazy upgrade.** registrar/register! fires every replacement hook and emits :rf.registry/handler-replaced on EVERY call (Spec 001 Hot-reload trace surface). Re-registering at lookup would publish a phantom hot-reload to devtools on the first render after boot — a worse bug than the one being fixed. The slot keeps what registration stored; the cache owns the substrate projection.

**Reagent shares the seam but not the defect, and the reason decides the fix's home.** Reagent's create-class / fn-to-class machinery reads the :contextType meta off the MetaFn and converts it into a React component type; React has no such conversion and rejects the object. So Reagent tolerates a MetaFn where React does not, publishes no componentize-view (grep for componentize across adapters/reagent/src, adapters/reagent-slim/src and hicasso/src returns zero, control search for frame-provider returns matches), and its head is the wrapper unchanged. Reagent's returned value is bit-identical in every ordering after this change, because apply-adapter-componentize-view returns the wrapper both at registration and at any re-derivation when no hook is published.

**Public contract.** docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md told users to reach for rf/reg-view* for registry-keyed view addressing and never showed what to do with the result — there was no working continuation to document. It now carries a Registry-keyed views section stating the route end to end and three properties: the head is a component rather than a function to invoke, props and children arrive losslessly through UIx's argv channel, and REGISTRATION ORDER DOES NOT MATTER. That last clause is the contract change worth naming: previously neither stated nor true.

**Witness.** New browser row boot-order-registration-yields-a-mountable-head-after-init registers at ns-load before any adapter exists and asserts that premise before mounting (no adapter at registration; the reg-time head really was the MetaFn), so it cannot decay into a copy of the post-init row. use-fixtures moved below that registration because make-reset-runtime-fixture snapshots the registrar at call time as its ns-load baseline (rf2-7hwnu).

**Gates, captured exit codes, all re-run on the final rebased base 9b96223e.** browser compile 0; browser run 0 (757 tests / 4149 assertions); node compile 0; node run 0 (11117 / 54892); late-bind drift JVM 0 (8 / 686, run from implementation/core — from implementation/ the -n selector matches nothing and the RF2_MIN_TESTS floor correctly fails the lane rather than reporting a pass); check_doc_slugs.py 0.

**Controls — both gates bite.** Browser: planting the pre-fix lookup back into re-frame.core/view (blob hash changed, 307 files recompiled so the runtime saw it) turned the run RED, exit 1, with 9 failures ALL in the new boot-order row — instance? js/Function reported cljs.core/MetaFn, and the mount threw verbatim "Element type is invalid: expected a string (for built-in components) or a class/function (for composite components) but got: object." The post-init row direct-mount-of-registered-view-head and the unregistered-native-defui control both stayed GREEN, so the red is attributable to the boot-order path and not to the harness. Restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object (6f79081b, both sides). Docs: a planted broken anchor returned exit 1 naming file, line and anchor; restored, blob hash 80e42447 both sides.

**Not fixed, and deliberately out of scope.** :adapter/wrap-view (rf2-00li) is routed and consulted at registration in the SAME pipeline, so a pre-init registration under UIx also misses the substrate wrap and falls back to the inline hiccup walk. That degrades only dev-only source-coord annotation (the walk mis-classifies a React element root and skips it) rather than the mount, so it is a separate, lower-severity bead rather than a widening of this one.
AUDIT PR #8909 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

The boot-before-init repair and its witness are sound. The cache's adapter-change claim is not. Let a post-init UIx registration compose wrapper W into head H1; the registrar slot stores H1 and the cache stores {wrapper W, head H1, adapter A1}. After dispose/install A2, the first lookup correctly misses, derives H2, overwrites the cache with {W,H2,A2}, returns H2, and deliberately leaves the registrar at H1. On the second lookup, the slot's H1 is identical to neither W nor the cache's now-current H2, so `view-head` classifies its own registration as foreign and returns stale H1. Switching UIx to Reagent similarly returns W once, then the old UIx-marked H1.

Completeness: the new test covers register-before-init and two stable lookups only when the registrar stores W; no test starts from a componentized registrar head and changes adapters. Correctness: this directly violates the PR's stated "different substrate re-derives rather than serving a UIx-marked shell to Reagent" invariant. Implementation quality: retain the immutable registrar-facing head/registration token across cache re-derivations (or equivalent) rather than rewriting the registrar; keep foreign-slot pass-through and avoid a new registry/API layer.
AUDIT PR #8919: implementation-quality/completeness update. This PR appears to repair the open adapter-switch defect in code: each cache entry now keeps :registered as the immutable object still held by the registrar, and a substrate re-derivation preserves that token while replacing :wrapper/:head/:adapter. Therefore the second lookup continues to recognize the registration instead of falling back to the old componentized registrar head.

Do not close this owner yet. The PR adds boot-order wrap/DOM tests, but no test starts with a post-init componentized registrar head, switches/disposes the adapter, and performs the two consecutive lookups this audit's acceptance requires. Repository searches for adapter switch/different adapter/second lookup find only the no-adapter-to-UIx boot rows, where the registrar stores the uncomponentized seed and therefore cannot reproduce the original H1 -> H2 -> stale-H1 failure. Remaining work is the small regression witness already in acceptance (including foreign-slot pass-through); code changes may be unnecessary if it passes. No new cache or API layer.

--------

## Verdict (2026-09-01, PR #8937) — the AUDIT PR #8919 witness

CONFIRMED ALREADY FIXED IN CODE. The witness passed on its FIRST run against tip, so
#8919's `:registered` token repair is correct and complete; the only outstanding item was
the regression witness, and this PR is it. No source change: the diff is one new file,
242 insertions, zero deletions.

**History walk.** `bd history --json` over all 627 entries, sorted by CommitDate and walked
adjacent-pair to the item's beginning: exactly 9 mutations touch a text-bearing field or
status. The newest text-bearing change is 2026-09-01T21:10:46+10:00 (notes 13865 -> 14970),
and its delta is the AUDIT PR #8919 note — the live instruction, matching the brief. The
description has never been edited since creation; no children, no comments.

**Premise checked at source, not taken from the note.** `views.cljs:803` sets
`:registered handler-fn` on a re-derived entry — the object the registrar slot still holds
— while `:wrapper`/`:head`/`:adapter` are replaced by `compose-view`. Pre-#8919
(`5bfbd25a8d`) the recognition test was `(or (identical? handler-fn wrapper) (identical?
handler-fn head))` against the CURRENT entry, which is exactly why the second lookup
misclassified its own registration.

**Why every existing row was blind to it, restated as the design constraint of the new
file.** The misclassification requires a registrar slot holding a COMPONENTIZED head. The
boot-order rows register before `rf/init!`, so the slot holds the uncomponentized wrapper
seed and the failure cannot arise at all. The new rows register AFTER install and assert
that premise (`:a1`-marked head in the slot; the switch leaves the slot at H1) so they
cannot decay into the boot-order shape.

**Witness.** `implementation/core/test/re_frame/views_adapter_switch_head_cljs_test.cljs`,
4 rows / 27 assertions:
  * `post-init-componentized-head-survives-an-adapter-switch` — the audit's exact shape:
    componentizing A1 -> componentizing A2, two consecutive lookups; the second must
    answer A2's head, not the stale H1. Plus a third lookup for reference stability.
  * `switch-to-a-non-componentizing-substrate-does-not-fall-back` — the UIx -> Reagent
    half ("W once, then the old UIx-marked H1"). Both lookups answer W; the re-derivation
    reuses the registration's own wrapper object.
  * `foreign-view-slot-passes-through-untouched-across-a-switch` — a hand-rolled
    `registrar/register!` slot served raw, before and after a switch.
  * `foreign-re-registration-over-a-composed-slot-passes-through` — a hand-rolled
    `register!` that REPLACES a composed slot wins over the stale cache entry. This is the
    acceptance's foreign-slot pass-through, and it is the row that would fail if anyone
    ever "fixed" the bug by dropping the registrar-identity check.

Substrate-agnostic: three inert `:kind :custom` adapter maps (so `same-adapter?` routes
them by object identity), `:adapter/componentize-view` impls modelled on
`spine/make-componentize-view` and published through the real `substrate-adapter/route-hook!`
so each fires only while its own map is installed and chains on otherwise. Nothing leaks
into the shared node bundle. `adapter-plain` publishes nothing, which is how the
non-componentizing half is expressed.

**Lane: node, not browser, and deliberately.** The property is WHICH OBJECT a lookup
returns, not rendered output, so no `createRoot` commit is needed. The DOM-mounting half
is already covered by the browser rows #8874/#8909/#8919 added.

**Gates, captured exit codes, all re-run on the final rebased base `de33d639e7`.**
node-test compile 0 (1875 files, 1214 compiled, 0 warnings); node-test run 0 (11156 tests /
55191 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors); JVM `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/core`
0 (2175 / 11138, 0 failures, 0 errors); focused run of the new ns 0 (4 / 27). The compile
lane's printed config path named this branch's own checkout. No docs/markdown/spec path in
the diff, so neither link gate nor `mkdocs build --strict` was a candidate.

**Control — the witness discriminates, constructed deliberately because it never went red
on its own.** Planted the revert of the #8919 token at the single line `:registered
handler-fn` (anchor matched exactly 1 line, checked before the run), keying the re-derived
entry on the NEW derivation's head instead of the immutable registrar-held object. Blob
hash `010bc3f6` -> `ef1275ce`; 978 files recompiled, so the runtime observed it. Sabotage
run exit 1, 7 failures, 0 errors, ALL in the two re-derivation rows: the second lookup
reported `(not (= :a2 :a1))` and `(identical? h1 second-lookup)` was TRUE — literally the
stale registrar head — while the non-componentizing row showed `first-lookup` a `MetaFn`
(W) and `second-lookup` the A1-marked shell, the audit's sentence verbatim. BOTH
foreign-slot pass-through rows stayed GREEN and the run reported the same 4 tests / 27
assertions as the green control, so no namespace was crashed out and the red is
attributable to the seam rather than to the harness. Restored and verified by git BLOB
hash against the committed object (`010bc3f6ebc83d2cfc025cd701043040161f1b25`, both
sides); recompiled (978 files) and the focused run returned to 4 / 27, exit 0.

**Nothing widened.** No new cache layer, no API change, no registry redesign, no spec edit;
`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` and `spec/002-Frames.md` untouched.
close_reason: Regression witness landed (PR #8937). The #8919 :registered token repair was already correct at tip: the witness — post-init componentized registrar head, adapter switch, two consecutive lookups, plus foreign-slot pass-through — passed on its first run, and no source change was needed. Discrimination proved by planting the token revert (blob 010bc3f6 -> ef1275ce, 978 files recompiled): exit 1, 7 failures, the second lookup identical? to the stale H1 and the non-componentizing row showing W-then-A1-marked-H1, while both pass-through rows stayed green. Gates on final base de33d639e7: node compile 0, node run 0 (11156/55191), JVM core 0 (2175/11138), focused 0 (4/27).

title: surface-review(skill-pair): keep Story work on the attached browser runtime
description:
## Scope

Make `skills/re-frame2-pair/` one honest live-SPA skill: every runtime operation it teaches or pre-authorises must target the browser heap reached by Pair's shadow-cljs nREPL connection. Remove the eight `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` tools and the headless-JVM procedures from Pair's published surface. Keep Story variants powerful inside a live pair session through the already-shipped browser path: `eval-cljs` over `re-frame.story/*`, followed by ordinary Pair frame reads, dispatches, traces, and diffs.

Cover the smallest coherent carrier set: Pair's frontmatter/router, the overlapping Story/variant recipes, the skill meta-docs, and the drift/prompt checks that currently enforce the hybrid split. Do not change Pair-MCP, Story-MCP, re-frame2 Story, or `re-frame2-pair.runtime` behavior.

## Findings

1. Pair's contract is one attached browser runtime. Its description, setup, and first-contact loop install the Pair MCP server plus `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, then run `discover-app` -> `orient` -> a targeted read against the live shadow-cljs build. The package/plugin metadata and human install docs do not install or configure Story-MCP. Nevertheless `SKILL.md` allow-lists eight tools from the separate `re-frame2-story-mcp` server in addition to all 33 Pair tools and five editor tools: 46 entries total.

2. The two servers cannot share runtime identity. `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md` and `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md` define Story-MCP as a headless same-JVM adapter over a process-local Story registry, with no nREPL, socket, or JVM-to-browser bridge. They define Pair's `eval-cljs` channel as the one live browser door. A keyword such as `:story.login/success` existing in both processes does not make the two frames the same object.

3. Pair's own Story leaf states the correct boundary, then contradicts it. `references/stories.md:15` says Story-MCP cannot see the browser tab's registry and instructs live work through Pair `eval-cljs`. Lines 81-116 still advertise the eight headless tools, and lines 116-171 claim every Story-MCP tool targeting a variant operates on the same frame Pair reads and teach `Pair subscribe -> Story-MCP run-variant -> Pair snapshot/dispatch`. That composition runs the variant in the JVM while Pair observes the browser, so a headless pass can leave the SPA untouched and Pair can legitimately report no such frame. `references/recipes.md:331-414` repeats the split by starting from a running Story-enabled browser but invoking headless `run-variant` and `read-failures` in the procedure.

4. No live capability requires the second server. The browser recipe already enumerates with `re-frame.story/ids` / `variants-of`, awaits `re-frame.story/run-variant` through Pair `eval-cljs`, projects the verdict before egress, and then addresses the variant through the normal Pair frame tools. The 4,004-line runtime helper has no Story runtime dependency; its only Story-specific behavior is a comment/example on generic `frame-diff`. Removing headless tool permissions therefore subtracts a wrong host choice without weakening live inspection, mutation, or variant-as-frame.

5. The hybrid also defeats progressive disclosure. `stories.md` is 187 lines / 18,177 bytes, `variant-as-frame.md` is 104 lines / 12,819 bytes, and three Story sections occupy roughly the final quarter of the 420-line recipe catalogue. A Story prompt is routed through SKILL plus both leaves and may then cross to the authoring skill, despite the router's at-most-two-references rule. One browser-native variant leaf can carry enumerate -> run -> operate/diff without a second host catalogue.

6. Existing checks preserve prose, not host correctness. `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` is 679 lines but has no canonical Story prompt and only checks that named words remain in sections. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:172-272` explicitly enforces the old HYBRID ownership and makes missing Story-MCP tools in Pair a failure. The live Pair fixture proves connect, dispatch, trace, and hot reload but never composes the two Story hosts. The impossible workflow is therefore green by construction.

7. History shows additive layering. The five Story-MCP run/assert tools entered Pair on 2026-05-13; three read-only tools followed. Commit `1967eff870` (2026-07-11, rf2-s99lw4) added the correct live-browser `eval-cljs` recipe after the one-live-door ruling, but retained the older headless integration and wrapped it in warnings instead of deleting it. This is pre-alpha surface residue, not compatibility worth preserving.

8. The rest of the live loop is coherent and should remain: Pair's preload sentinel/freshness ladder gives an honest attach, `orient` supplies bounded first contact, structured tools cover common gestures, and `eval-cljs` carries the long tail. A second process-local Story host is the outlier; no attach redesign or new tool is needed to remove it.

## Recommended Action

Take a clean single-host cut:

- Remove every `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` entry from Pair's `allowed-tools`. A published Pair invocation should require only its own MCP server plus editor tools.
- Retain one concise browser-Story procedure: enumerate the live registry with Pair `eval-cljs`; await/project `re-frame.story/run-variant`; then use `set-operating-frame`, `read-sub` / `snapshot` / `dispatch`, epoch reads, and `frame-diff` against that same browser runtime.
- Collapse `references/stories.md` and `references/variant-as-frame.md` to one live-browser leaf (keep either filename), and prune the headless tool catalogue, false same-frame compositions, self-healing cross-server loop, and duplicate Story recipes. Link outward for explicitly headless Story-MCP work; do not teach it as part of Pair.
- Remove the Story-MCP <-> Pair HYBRID mapping from `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` and replace it with the simpler invariant that Pair's MCP permissions use only the `re-frame2-pair` prefix. Reconcile `spec/design.md`, `spec/authoring-prompt.md`, `spec/inputs.md`, and current docs with that boundary.
- Add one focused row to the existing prompt-regression table for “run this variant in the app I have open”: it must route through Pair `eval-cljs` with `await`, then a Pair frame read, and must not mention the Story-MCP prefix. Extend the existing structural harness only; do not build a general conversation-eval platform for this cut.

Do not transfer compatibility aliases into Pair or add dedicated Pair Story tools. `eval-cljs` is already the explicit, powerful long-tail surface and the invoker selected a live Pair session.

## Evidence

- Pair's advertised/allowed surface: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:1-68`; current count is 33 Pair MCP names + 8 Story-MCP names + 5 editor names.
- Pair-only setup/distribution: `skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/LOCAL_DEV.md:11-43,121-128`, `README.md:152-209`, `package.json`, and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`; none configures Story-MCP.
- Normative host split: `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:41-66`; `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:72-82`; `tools/story-mcp/README.md:14-19`.
- Internal contradiction: `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md:15,75-81,116-171`; `references/recipes.md:327-414`; `SKILL.md:210`.
- Existing complete browser route: `references/stories.md:13-77`; generic variant addressing/diff: `references/variant-as-frame.md` and `preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1399-1416`.
- Runtime independence: no production `re-frame.story` or Story-MCP reference exists in `runtime.cljs` or `pure.cljc`; the helper remains a generic frame/epoch/DOM runtime.
- Enforcement gap: `tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj:76-168,167-220`; `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:172-272`; `docs/TESTING.md:126-172` explicitly calls Claude-in-loop behavior future work.
- History: Story-MCP Pair permissions originate in `5753b4211e` / `8a10d146bf`; the live-browser route lands later in `1967eff870`. The later commit added “one live door” but left the earlier cross-host procedures intact.
- Duplicate search: all-status title, description, and notes searches for Story-MCP Pair, browser registry, one live door, HYBRID split, live-session tools, cross-host, split-brain, and same-frame found no owner for this subtraction.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md` contains zero `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` permissions and no instruction to start or call a second MCP server during a live Pair workflow. Pair's editor permissions and surviving Pair-MCP permissions remain intact, subject to the separate `rf2-ahjbc` catalogue reduction.
2. Current Pair docs expose exactly one Story host: the attached browser. A copyable enumerate -> await run -> pin/read/dispatch/trace procedure operates entirely through `mcp__re-frame2-pair__*` calls and projects the run verdict before raw eval egress.
3. No Pair doc claims that a Story-MCP variant frame and a browser Pair frame are the same frame, or composes state/trace reads across the two processes. Explicitly headless/JVM Story work routes out to Story-MCP's own docs or the appropriate authoring context.
4. Pair has one Story/variant reference leaf after the router, not the current overlapping `stories.md` + `variant-as-frame.md` pair. The surviving leaf retains variant-id-as-frame semantics, mount/reset/destroy gotchas, browser enumeration/run, and cross-frame diff; headless catalogues and duplicate self-healing prose are removed. Net Pair prose decreases materially.
5. `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` no longer encodes Story-MCP <-> Pair HYBRID ownership. Its self-test and ordinary run pass while a controlled reintroduction of one `mcp__re-frame2-story-mcp__*` Pair permission makes the focused boundary check red.
6. The existing prompt regression has a Story-in-the-open-app row that requires Pair `eval-cljs`, `await`, and a same-runtime frame read and forbids the Story-MCP prefix. Existing Pair prompt/runtime structural tests remain green; no new general eval runner is introduced.
7. Skill meta-docs, README/status/capability material, routing tables, and current tool-count prose agree with the single-host boundary. Historical design records may describe the former hybrid only when clearly labelled historical, not as current instruction.
8. No Pair-MCP tool, Story-MCP tool, Story API, runtime helper function, permission gate, compatibility alias, bridge, background service, or dedicated browser-Story tool is added or changed for this outcome.

## Non-goals

- Redesigning Pair's attach/preload mechanism, `discover-app`, `orient`, the remaining Pair-MCP catalogue, or the runtime helper.
- Removing Story variants, variant-as-frame, browser `re-frame.story/*` access, frame diffs, or Pair's generic `eval-cljs` workhorse.
- Changing Story-MCP's 20-tool headless catalogue, teaching it to bridge into a browser, or deciding its complete ownership across every other skill.
- Adding a `list-stories` / `run-variant` Pair tool, generic command abstraction, compatibility shim, deprecation window, or second permission layer.
- Building a new behavioural-eval platform or broad-rewriting unrelated Pair recipes.

## Related beads

- `rf2-ahjbc` (open) retires Pair-MCP progress streams in favor of turn-shaped results. It shares `SKILL.md`, recipes/references, tests, and drift carriers; land it first or rebase this subtraction onto its reduced catalogue.
- `rf2-cfq8a` (open) makes a consumer project's headless JVM stories reachable on Story-MCP first launch and explicitly preserves Pair as the one live-browser door. Complementary, not a dependency.
- `rf2-7htk7` (open) retires Xray's duplicate agent runtime so Pair is the single out-of-process live runtime. This applies the same one-runtime boundary at the skill/tool-selection layer.
- `rf2-7dewo` (open) changes Story variant vocabulary and may sweep skills prose after its runtime slice; coordinate the surviving browser Story leaf, but neither outcome depends on the other.
- `rf2-wyza` (closed) replaced a duplicated 33-tool onboarding catalogue with routing rules after measuring the context tax. This task applies the same trust-the-agent/subtract-the-wrong-choice posture to a second-server catalogue.
- Historical lineage: `rf2-s99lw4` / commit `1967eff870` established the browser `eval-cljs` path; the one-live-door ruling is recorded in Story spec as `rf2-3fc89f.22`.

title: surface-review(skill-xray): make one debugging question land on one first Xray surface
description:
## Scope

Treat skills/re-frame2-xray/** as one distinct published tour product. Make a concrete programmer question land quickly on the one existing Xray surface to open first, then reveal only the detail needed for that surface.

Rework the top-level skill, its panel references, README/package descriptions, eval material, and the small docs mirrors that restate the skill's routing contract. Preserve Xray's shipped two-mode UI and all current panels. Keep the actor boundary explicit: Xray is the visible human panel; re-frame2-pair is the agent-facing runtime reader and driver.

## Findings

1. The file that calls itself a “compact tour/router” is already an encyclopedia. skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md is 4,723 words / 33,441 bytes / 442 lines before any reference is loaded. A basic “which panel?” request passes through the Redux analogy, launch APIs, all hotkeys, the full 10-tab Dynamic table, the 5-tab Static table, chrome, exclusions, implementation ids, and retired-control warnings before reaching an answer.

2. Progressive disclosure does not reduce the expensive case. Every deep panel question routes to one references/panels.md catalogue: 6,380 words / 49,571 bytes / 853 lines. A one-panel question can therefore load 11,103 words / 83,012 bytes across SKILL.md plus panels.md. The repository's own leaf discipline is 250 lines / 16 KB unless a catalogue cannot be split profitably; this catalogue can be split along the existing question/scope seams, so one question need not pay for fourteen unrelated tabs.

3. Xray's useful information architecture is not adequately described by the first Dynamic-versus-Static fork. Six Dynamic tabs rebind to the focused epoch; Resources mixes process-global, observed-frame, and trace evidence; Graph, Frames, and Hicasso sit in the Dynamic shell but do not rebind to the selected epoch; Static catalogues are process-global with a few per-frame live projections. The skill knows this in its scope matrix, but the normal tour remains mode-first and inventory-first. A programmer starts with “what changed?”, “why did this render?”, “what is registered?”, or “where does this value come from?”, not with an internal tab roster.

4. The package has tab descriptions but no compact panel-tour gesture. The useful daily path is: choose frame, choose event when the question is event-shaped, start at Epoch, branch to state/render/raw/specialist evidence, and use Static only for definitions. docs/xray/02-panel-tour.md states a five-step version, but SKILL.md does not make it the entry path and neither surface handles the non-epoch Dynamic tabs cleanly. The result is a list of destinations instead of a fast route through them.

5. The Pair handoff is directionally right but its slogan is wrong. “Xray owns the seeing; Pair owns the driving” implies that a read-only live-runtime inspection belongs to Xray. Pair's actual first-contact sequence is discover-app → orient → targeted read, and it owns read-sub, get-path, snapshots, trace/epoch reads, DOM/UI reads, and Hicasso evidence as well as writes. rf2-7htk7 independently establishes the desired singular boundary: Xray for the human panel, Pair for programmer/AI runtime access. The Xray evals reject one write prompt (“dispatch this”) but have no negative read-only agent prompt.

6. The same volatile inventory and caveats are copied through SKILL.md, references/panels.md, references/shared-components.md, README.md, package.json, plugin.json, eval prose, skills/README.md, and docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md. Drift is visible now: the package README's scope sentence names Graph and Frames as non-epoch exceptions but omits Hicasso; docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md lists Esc as a focus-gated spine shortcut while the owning launch leaf says it is modal-local; docs/xray/index.md says every tab rebinds to the focused epoch, contradicting the current scope matrix. More copied warnings or prose locks will not make this easier to use.

7. The 30 evals mostly protect churn facts. Fourteen answer-quality cases pin launch calls, retired labels, exact tab counts, hidden mount facades, future hotkeys, and control precedence. Those facts have value, but there is no answer-quality route for the everyday Epoch, Views, Trace, Routes, Resources, or Hicasso questions; no read-only Pair disqualifier; no score for giving one first surface without dumping the whole inventory; and no check of which reference leaf was loaded. The harness is manual and records no observed end-to-end panel-tour result.

8. History confirms an accretion loop. The package has 69 commits since its May introduction and SKILL.md itself has 39. Commit b7798297d9 tried to tighten body ownership and add progressive disclosure, yet the body is now 4,723 words and its one panel leaf is 6,380. Commit 7cc83f0d8e / rf2-5atkk repaired the sharpest failure: the skill taught nine tabs while its own eval required ten and rejected a nine-tab answer. The next improvement should reduce the number of places that must move, not preserve the catalogue in more forms.

## Recommended Action

Rebuild the published tour around one question-first route card:

- First fork on actor and interface. “Where in the visible Xray panel do I look?” stays here. “Inspect or change my running app for me” routes to re-frame2-pair, whether the requested runtime operation is read-only or mutating.
- For panel questions, route by the evidence sought: one dispatch/cascade; changed state; subscriptions/renders; raw ordering; machine or route activity; live server/runtime structure; dependency/image/Hicasso structure; registered definitions. Return the visible mode/tab label, why it is the first stop, and the first interaction (pick frame/event, open the tab, or flip Static). Name a second lens only when it is the natural next step.
- Keep one compact canonical inventory for explicit “list every tab” requests. Do not make every routine answer traverse that inventory.
- Replace the monolithic panels.md load with small one-level leaves divided by the existing evidence/scope questions. A deep question about one panel family should load only that family, not all 15 tabs. Keep normative implementation anatomy in linked Xray specs/source rather than duplicating it into the tour.
- Strip internal ids, sparse order values, source-file inventories, deleted-panel archaeology, and repeated “do not invent” clauses from the normal path unless they disambiguate a live user-visible control. Trust programmers with direct current guidance.
- Align README/package/plugin and the docs skill mirror around the role and the canonical route card. Where docs/xray/index.md or 02-panel-tour.md repeats a directly contradictory scope sentence, correct or link it; do not turn this into a broad docs rewrite.
- Repurpose the existing eval corpus toward route quality: representative questions across the existing scope families, one read-only Pair handoff, concise first-surface answers, and proof that a deep question loads only its focused leaf. Keep a small set of genuinely high-risk launch/control distinctions. Add no new runner, gate, policy layer, or generated compatibility table.

## Evidence

- skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:63-80 defines the three-question scope; :82-94 calls the body compact and sends every panel-depth question to panels.md; :199-278 carries the full Dynamic inventory and scope matrix; :380-439 carries exclusions and repeated routing cautions.
- Measured current normal path: SKILL.md 4,723 words / 33,441 bytes / 442 lines; references/panels.md 6,380 / 49,571 / 853; combined 11,103 words / 83,012 bytes for a deep one-panel answer.
- skills/README.md:241-253 sets the one-level progressive-disclosure rule and the 250-line / 16-KB leaf target, with a catalogue exception only when splitting would not reduce loaded tokens.
- skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:127-186 establishes Pair's live-runtime read path: discover-app, orient, then a targeted slice; Pair is not write-only.
- skills/re-frame2-xray/README.md:8 omits Hicasso from the non-epoch exception sentence that SKILL.md:233 names correctly.
- docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md:33 lists Esc with spine shortcuts; skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:190-193 and references/launch-modes.md:355-370 say Esc is modal-local, not a wired spine key.
- docs/xray/index.md:20 says every Dynamic tab rebinds to one epoch; skills/re-frame2-xray/SKILL.md:222-240 and references/panels.md:71-92 document the three actual scope axes.
- evals/evals.json contains 30 fixtures (22 positive, 8 negative); its 14 answer-quality cases are dominated by launch/current-control and drift-rejection facts. The only Pair disqualifier is id 13's mutating dispatch request.
- Git history: 39 commits touch SKILL.md and 69 touch the package. b7798297d9 introduced the current body/leaf/eval shape; 7cc83f0d8e fixed rf2-5atkk's skill-versus-own-eval tab-count contradiction.
- Existing-bead search: all-status searches for surface-review(skill-xray), question-first, panel-tour, progressive disclosure, router, token burden, and panels.md found no current owner for this outcome. rf2-7htk7 owns the duplicate runtime seam, not the tour information architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A concrete “where in Xray?” prompt returns one existing starting surface in the first paragraph: visible mode/tab, the reason, and the first interaction. It does not enumerate all 15 tabs unless the user asked for the inventory.
2. Representative route cases cover at least the existing focused-epoch, observed-frame/live-structure, process-global/registry, and Static-definition scopes. The answers preserve the shipped model: six focused-epoch lenses; Resources mixed; Graph/Frames/Hicasso non-epoch; Static definition catalogues process-global with their real per-frame projections. No new mode, panel, or aggregate is invented.
3. The panel-tour path is explicit and short: choose frame; choose an event only for event-shaped questions; start at Epoch for “what happened?”; branch to the exact state/render/raw/specialist lens; use Static for definitions. Non-epoch Dynamic surfaces do not pretend to follow the event.
4. The routing boundary is human panel versus agent runtime, not read versus write. A prompt asking the agent to inspect a running app routes to re-frame2-pair even when it requests no mutation; a prompt asking where a human should look in Xray remains in this skill.
5. Routine selection questions are answerable from SKILL.md alone. A deeper panel question loads SKILL.md plus at most one focused, one-level reference leaf that meets the repository's 250-line / 16-KB target. The PR reports before/after loaded words and bytes for one routine route and one deep-panel route; the 49,571-byte all-panels load is gone.
6. There is one canonical complete tab inventory and one canonical question-to-surface map inside the package. README, package/plugin descriptions, skills/README.md, and docs/skills/re-frame2-xray.md summarize the role or link to that authority instead of copying detailed tab anatomy and exception rosters.
7. Current visible guidance is retained where it changes the user's action: inline versus overlay, the visible pop-out button, passive inspect versus Reset rewind, Graph's local projection versus top-level Static mode, and the absence of a dedicated Issues tab. Internal ids/order/source paths and retired alternatives are absent from the normal route unless the question asks for them.
8. Existing evals are revised rather than surrounded by a new framework. They grade concise first-surface routing across the scope families, a read-only Pair handoff, the explicit full-inventory request, and the focused-leaf load. The PR reports observed manual outputs for those cases.
9. The skill package and its small mirrors have a net reduction in prose and no contradictory scope/hotkey sentence among the touched surfaces. Existing JSON, package, link/anchor, skill-doc, and Xray tab-inventory checks pass; no new prose-presence test, linter, generator, or CI job is added.

## Non-goals

- No Xray UI change, new panel, new mode, cross-epoch aggregate, workflow wizard, command, hotkey, runtime accessor, or Pair-MCP capability.
- No implementation of deep debugging recipes, click-to-source internals, branch-and-explore, or a replacement for the normative tools/xray specs.
- No defensive-policy layer, prompt firewall, compatibility alias, tombstone glossary, generated mirror system, or additional drift gate.
- No broad rewrite of docs/xray/**; only directly repeated routing/scope contradictions may move with the canonical tour.
- No change to Xray's preload/mount/runtime seam; rf2-7htk7 owns that separate subtraction.
- No exhaustive wording cleanup, iconography redesign, or unrelated package/release work.

## Related beads

- rf2-7htk7 (open) — makes Pair the single agent runtime and retires Xray's duplicate agent seam. This task consumes that human-panel versus agent-runtime boundary but does not touch the runtime removal; sequence shared skill/doc files if both are dispatched.

title: surface-review(examples-substrates): make login the runnable three-view-layer comparison
description:
## Scope

Make the existing login feature the canonical runnable comparison of re-frame2's three active browser view languages: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso. Keep `examples/core/login/` as the Reagent arm and `examples/substrates/uix/login/` as the UIx arm; add one Hicasso arm under `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` that requires the same substrate-free `login.model` and owns only its view/root code. Add a concise `examples/substrates/README.md` that explains which comparison to read, wire the new arm through the existing example build/runner/compile path, and extend the existing login bundle-isolation proof. Correct only directly coupled catalogue and TESTING prose.

This is one worked-example outcome, not a demo framework or a substrate selector.

## Findings

- The substrate tree has UIx counter/login/dashboard and reagent-slim counter, but no landing page and no human-facing Hicasso example. `examples/README.md` still describes the family as UIx plus reagent-slim even though Hicasso now ships its own canonical view adapter.
- Hicasso already has a complete installation counter in `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md` and a Story/Xray-owned counter testbed under `tools/story/testbeds/hicasso_counter/`. Another counter would duplicate the beginner sample or send learners into tool scaffolding; neither shows a realistic model/view boundary.
- Login is already the right comparison seam. Commit `2644f42b72` (`rf2-ppbvav`) extracted roughly 19 schemas/effects/machine/events/subscriptions and `frame-config` into one substrate-free `login.model`, leaving only views and mount code in the Reagent/UIx/Helix entries. Commit `e1f38e5ddf` (`rf2-d6epb`) removed Helix, so that deliberate three-view example became a two-view pair.
- The removal left observable drift: `examples/TESTING.md` still says counter and login "triplet", "three reactive substrates", and "three login examples" although only Reagent and UIx login builds remain. `login.model` also still speaks of "three mounts". Fixing those words alone would be minutiae; supplying the current third view language restores the useful product shape they once described.
- The three small counter files deliberately repeat their tiny event/sub dataflow so each remains readable top to bottom. Extracting a counter model would weaken the smallest-app lesson for little gain. The substantial login model already amortises sharing and has model-level tests.
- Hicasso's native root door is compatible without an API change, but the boot shape must be honest. `h/mount!` accepts only `:frame`, `:initial-events`, and `:identifier-prefix`; the login demo also needs `model/frame-config`'s `:fx-overrides`. The Hicasso entry should therefore install `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, create the frame once with the existing config, and mount into that frame. Hot reload should re-render the retained Hicasso root rather than recreate the frame.
- The existing harness already supplies the needed mechanics. A normal `:examples/login-hicasso` build whose init namespace and `index.html` live under `examples/` is discovered by `serve-example.cjs`, staged with `_shared`, and swept by `check-examples-compile.cjs`; no registry or special runner branch is needed.
- Examples are intentionally test-free. The shared login behavior is already exercised outside the tree, while `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` proves the shared model does not pull a foreign view runtime. That checker currently has only Reagent and UIx arms even though the general isolation gate already owns live Hicasso sentinels and a positive-control module.

## Recommended Action

Add `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` as a direct third view over `login.model`. Keep the same fields, messages, test ids, canned success/failure flow, and shared visual assets as the existing pair. Author the view in native Hicasso idioms (`h/defview`, `h/sub`, event vectors where they fit); preserve the password event's classified map payload rather than flattening the secret into a positional intent. Use a small `h/event` callback where constructing that map requires the DOM value.

Declare `:examples/login-hicasso` beside the two current login builds, with the standard `out/examples/login-hicasso` output. Let the existing manifest-derived runner and compile checker enroll it. Add the exact repository-local run command to the new example README, while linking the Hicasso installation chapter for dependency setup and truthfully noting that the Maven coordinate is not published yet.

Make `examples/substrates/README.md` a short decision/comparison surface with two explicit tracks:

1. Same Reagent authoring language, different adapter/package: stock counter versus reagent-slim counter.
2. One substrate-free model, different view language/root: Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso login.

Link directly to the model and three thin entry points so a programmer or coding agent can compare source, not prose excerpts. Point the root catalogue at this page and reconcile the stale parity section in `examples/TESTING.md` and directly coupled login comments/READMEs.

Extend `check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs` and `test:bundle-isolation` to release and inspect the Hicasso login. Reuse the existing Hicasso sentinels and positive control: each login bundle must contain its own view runtime and exclude the other two. Keep compile coverage plus this structural proof; do not add a per-example browser suite.

## Evidence

- `examples/README.md:9,55-61` lists only UIx and reagent-slim under Substrates; `examples/substrates/README.md` does not exist.
- `examples/TESTING.md:82-118` calls two current pairs triplets and claims three login examples while naming only two login bundles.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljs:42-57,722-742` documents the substrate-free owner and shared frame config; only `examples/core/login/core.cljs` and `examples/substrates/uix/login/core.cljs` require it today.
- `implementation/scripts/check-login-bundle-isolation.cjs:3-45,85-103,179-235` explicitly implements a two-bundle Reagent/UIx proof.
- `implementation/package.json:41-42,53` releases only the two login builds for bundle isolation and exposes the existing compile and `dev:example` doors.
- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1611-1644` declares the current login pair; `:examples/hicasso-counter` at lines 1950-1959 points to the tool-owned Story testbed instead of `examples/`.
- `node ../examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs --list` includes `examples/login` and `examples/login-uix` but not the tool-owned Hicasso counter. `node scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` does include that tool build, demonstrating why compile inventory alone is not a human learning catalogue.
- `docs/core/hicasso/index.md:3-6` defines Hicasso as re-frame2's native view layer. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2130-2138` lists Hicasso's own adapter in the canonical shipped inventory.
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:549-605` and `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:115-155` bound `h/mount!` to the three root keys and show that it joins a frame already created through `rf/make-frame`.
- `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:300-332,742-746` already defines non-dev Hicasso sentinels (`hicassoBoundary`, `rf.error/hicasso-empty-vector`) and proves them present in a dedicated positive-control module.
- History establishes the sequence: shared login model on 2026-07-11 (`2644f42b72`), Helix removal on 2026-07-22 (`e1f38e5ddf`), Hicasso's own adapter on 2026-08-18 (`4cb9e16951`), and canonical adapter registration on 2026-08-19 (`5d1fd88c3f`). The examples never gained a human Hicasso arm after that change.
- Current tag and installation evidence says the example must stay repository-local for now: `git tag --list 'v*'` is empty and `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:18-40,125` says the coordinate is unpublished and uses `:local/root`.
- Fresh open/closed title and description searches for the exact prefix, Hicasso login, login-hicasso, three-view-layer, cross-substrate, `login.model`, and `examples/substrates/hicasso` found no duplicate. The adjacent launch-command tasks `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` are distinct and explicitly remain separate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/` contains a readable Hicasso entry, host page, and concise README. It imports `login.model` and contains no duplicate auth schemas, effects, machine, events, or subscriptions.
2. The Hicasso view uses native `h/defview`/`h/sub`/intent idioms and matches the Reagent/UIx pair's visible login behavior and stable test ids. Email edits remain positional; password edits still dispatch the classified `[:auth.login/edit-password {:value ...}]` shape, and submit/success/failure behavior remains owned by the shared model.
3. Boot installs `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, constructs the frame once from `model/frame-config` so the canned HTTP effect override and initial event are honored, mounts Hicasso into that frame, and retains/re-renders one root on hot reload. No expansion or compatibility shim is added to `h/mount!`.
4. `:examples/login-hicasso` emits to the standard example output root and appears automatically in both `npm run dev:example -- --list` and `npm run test:examples-compile` inventory. Its host/shared assets are resolved by the existing staging code with no hard-coded build-to-folder entry.
5. `examples/substrates/README.md` gives the two-track comparison above and links the exact model/view/root files. `examples/README.md`, `examples/TESTING.md`, `login.model`, and the three login READMEs no longer describe deleted Helix arms or incorrect triplet counts.
6. The new README gives one truthful repository-local launch path and points greenfield setup to the Hicasso installation guide; it does not advertise an unresolved Maven version or duplicate a project template.
7. `test:bundle-isolation` releases all three login builds. The existing login checker proves own-runtime presence plus foreign-runtime absence for Reagent, UIx, and Hicasso, using a non-vacuous Hicasso positive control. The Hicasso login carries no Reagent or UIx fingerprint, and the other two carry no Hicasso fingerprint.
8. `npm run test:examples-compile`, `npm run test:bundle-isolation`, the existing example staging/runner tests, and relevant docs-link gates pass. A clean repository-local launch paints the form and exercises one validation failure plus the canned successful login; no new per-example browser gate is introduced.

## Non-goals

- No runtime view-layer switcher, multi-adapter bundle, mode flag, gallery shell, code generator, or new example manifest/framework.
- No extraction of the tiny counter registrations, sharing of view code, or conversion of every example to every view layer.
- No Hicasso variant in `tools/template`, no publication workaround, and no invented compatibility coordinate while the artifact is unpublished.
- No change to Hicasso root/adapter APIs, login business behavior, or the substrate contract.
- No promotion or relocation of the Story/Xray Hicasso counter testbed; tool testbeds remain tool-owned.
- No Hicasso SSR/Node example; `rf2-8arzr` owns that separate path.
- No sweep standardizing existing substrate README launch commands; `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` own the adjacent catalogue command policy. This task only documents the new arm and follows whichever shared wording lands.
- No per-example browser-test matrix; examples stay human learning surfaces and adapter smokes stay adapter-owned.

## Related beads

- `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` - adjacent core/capability launch-command work; not duplicated here.
- `rf2-9hcyf` - executable UIx component-testing recipe; distinct from the human example comparison.
- `rf2-8urba` - deferred Hicasso template variant, gated on publication; this task does not scaffold consumers.
- `rf2-8arzr` - native-Hicasso SSR/Node reference path; explicitly outside this browser example.
- `rf2-auiy5` and `rf2-hvr5h` - established Hicasso's canonical native adapter.
- Historical `rf2-ppbvav` / commit `2644f42b72` - created the shared login model and original three-view comparison.
- Historical `rf2-d6epb` / commit `e1f38e5ddf` - removed Helix and its example arms.
- `rf2-5czki` - added Hicasso Story support and the tool-owned testbed; this task supplies the intentionally separate human surface.

AUDIT 2026-09-02 — PR #8954 correctness/completeness finding (reopened).

title: surface-review(skill-reagent-migration): teach only Hicasso's live read and navigation doors
description:
## Scope

Update skills/reagent-migration/** so the published skill teaches only the current post-dead-weight Hicasso authoring vocabulary at the two seams changed by rf2-6c12m.15:

- h/sub is the sole public subscription-read door.
- navigation is authored through h/route-link or ordinary routing events; the navigate intent head is implementation-owned and is not written as ::h/navigate.

Cover the distributable SKILL/references and the authoring-time spec/eval material that can reintroduce the old forms. Keep this a skill-only change.

## Findings

1. The skill violates its own cardinal rule 6 (“emit only what has shipped; read the door”). Current re-frame.hicasso exports h/sub and no h/use-subs, but references/mental-model.md and references/catalog-mechanical.md still teach h/use-subs as a deliberate control, while spec/inputs.md still rosters it as public.

2. The public navigate spelling also moved. rf2-6c12m.15 demoted the navigate head to re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate; h/route-link mints that internal value. references/gotchas.md still calls ::h/navigate one of two public reserved heads and says the draft guide is incomplete without it, while spec/authoring-prompt.md preserves that claim for the next reauthor. An authored ::h/navigate now resolves to a different keyword from the internal head and is not the shipped navigation contract.

3. This is high-friction in the failure direction. An AI following the read leaf can emit an unresolved h/use-subs call; one following the gotcha can emit a vector the current intent lowering does not recognize as its navigation head. The programmer is asked to choose between doors that no longer exist instead of using the single simple path Hicasso intentionally kept.

4. Progressive disclosure currently hides, rather than contains, the drift: the top-level router says “read the door,” but the false advice appears only when the relevant read/gotcha leaf is loaded. The eval corpus has no expectation that rejects either retired form, so its behavioural fixtures do not expose the contradiction.

5. This is recent history, not a request to redesign Hicasso. Commit 4c9fa03def (rf2-6c12m.15) removed h/use-subs as below the ergonomics bar and internalised navigation as part of the open dead-weight programme. Other same-wave skill updates carried hframe, native and defhost changes, but these six live teaching references remained.

## Recommended Action

Carry rf2-6c12m.15 into this skill directly:

- Teach repeated, conditional and looped reads as ordinary h/sub calls. Remove the grouped-read alternative rather than replacing it with another abstraction.
- Remove ::h/navigate from the author-facing marker/reserved-head vocabulary. Where navigation is relevant, point to h/route-link or a normal routing event; do not expose the internal intent value.
- Correct spec/inputs.md and spec/authoring-prompt.md so a future reauthor cannot resurrect either form.
- Add or amend one focused behavioural eval that grades the live outcome: h/sub is the only read emitted, and neither h/use-subs nor ::h/navigate is proposed.

Keep the explanation short. The outcome is fewer concepts and code that compiles against the current door, not a new compatibility story.

## Evidence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc: the current public door aliases h/sub and has no use-subs export.
- docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md, “Reads”: the complete current roster contains h/sub only.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:284: navigate-head is namespaced to the implementation.
- docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:68-80: route-link owns and mints that head; application authors do not.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/mental-model.md:84 and references/catalog-mechanical.md:61 still teach h/use-subs.
- skills/reagent-migration/spec/inputs.md:17 still lists use-subs on the door.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:108,204 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:23 still teach ::h/navigate as public.
- git commit 4c9fa03def: “hicasso: drop h/use-subs, the grouped read control (rf2-6c12m.15)”.
- skills/reagent-migration/README.md says the skill is pre-alpha and has not been exercised end to end; the static eval set contains no retired-read/navigation control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No live instruction, source-of-truth roster, reauthoring prompt or eval expectation under skills/reagent-migration/** presents h/use-subs as callable or ::h/navigate as author-written.
- The read guidance has one direct answer: use h/sub at each read site, including conditional/loop/helper cases.
- Navigation guidance, if retained in this migration skill, uses only h/route-link or ordinary routing events and clearly leaves the opaque navigate head to Hicasso.
- A focused behavioural eval would fail an answer that emits h/use-subs or ::h/navigate and pass one that stays on the live public doors.
- Existing M/D/R routing, whole-view coherence, reporter/census workflow, compile/test verification and programmer-owned render check remain intact.
- JSON parses, skill/package structural checks pass, and the relevant markdown link/anchor gate passes. The handoff names the current public-door source that was checked.

## Non-goals

- No Hicasso runtime or public API change.
- No compatibility alias or shim for h/use-subs or ::h/navigate.
- No automated view rewrite engine, new linter, surface-sync gate or defensive policy.
- No broad API audit, catalogue expansion, reporter change, migration of application dataflow, or redesign of route-link.
- No unrelated polish or exhaustive wording sweep.

## Related beads

- rf2-6c12m.15 — exact landed facade-hygiene change this skill missed.
- rf2-6c12m — open Hicasso dead-weight epic; establishes the minimum-ceremony/trust-the-programmer direction.
- rf2-r3r00 — current complementary surface review reducing Hicasso’s clj-kondo export to useful macro-shape analysis; no dependency or overlap.
- rf2-r4j91 — original Reagent-migration retarget to Hicasso.
- rf2-0jl8s, rf2-6c12m.24, rf2-6c12m.30 and rf2-6c12m.13 — prior API changes successfully carried into this skill, useful history for the same bounded update pattern.
