title: surface-review(resources): make active-route resource replanning a first-class causal command
description:
## Scope

Add one public event-vector command for rerunning the active route's Resources plan when an app-db-derived identity input (principal, tenant, permission set, locale, impersonation) changes without navigation. Cover the Resources↔Routing late-bound seam, exact route-owner reconciliation, durable plan/blocking/readiness state, conformance tests, Spec 012/016 and API/resource docs, and the RealWorld-on-resources receipt. Keep Resources optional and vector-first.

## Findings

Named `{:from-db ...}` subscriptions deliberately re-key when resolver inputs change, but remain passive. The newly selected scoped key is therefore `:idle` until some causal path ensures it. Navigation normally supplies that cause, but identical navigation is intentionally a no-op and there is no public command that reruns the current route's effective resource plan without changing the URL.

The flagship works around this gap with the 39-line `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` event. That app event reads leaf `rf/handler-meta`, invokes each entry itself, and dispatches independent ensures. It is not the route planner: it omits inherited parent resources, local `:after` ordering, identity collapse, atomic planning, exact plan ownership diff, blocking-slot replacement, and route readiness/error repair; it also calls `:when` with nil instead of the planner's reserved `{}` ctx. A cold restore on a composed route can therefore omit a parent-owned read, and a successful hand-ensure after the initial nil-scope planning failure leaves the durable route plan/readiness facts stale.

The runtime already computes the authoritative answer once: the route planner materializes contributor/local-id, canonical params, resolved scope, scoped key and byte key-id; collapses and orders the effective parent chain; diffs prior identities; and returns the exact identity/blocking maps Routing commits under the active nav-token. The missing piece is a public causal door back through that machinery.

## Recommended Action

Ship one public command, `[:rf.route/replan-resources {:cause <edn>}]`, implemented through the existing late-bound Resources↔Routing integration. It should read the current resolved route and nav-token, rerun the canonical effective parent-to-leaf resource planner against the current app-db, and atomically reconcile the standing plan under the same route activation:

- retain/adopt unchanged usable identities without a forced fetch;
- ensure added or changed identities with the existing route owner and caller cause;
- remove that owner only from identities the replanned route no longer requires;
- replace the durable `:resource-plan` and `:resource-blocking` slots and re-project route transition/error from the new plan;
- preserve route id/params/query/fragment/nav-token and do not run guards, `:on-match`, history or scroll effects.

Use the ordinary fail-closed planner boundary: no partial ensures on a failed plan, and document/test the exact prior-owner cleanup and route-error result. Reuse the existing `:rf.resource/route-plan` evidence with an explicit replan cause rather than inventing a parallel planner or helper-function API.

Replace RealWorld's app-side planner copy with this event. Make its personalized feed admission explicit in route data (for example, only when the following-feed query arm is active) so confirmed-anonymous home does not contradict the existing strict nil-scope planning rule. Teach the account/tenant-switch recipe as: resolve/clear the old scope causally, commit the new identity, then replan the active route.

## Evidence

- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:35-50,84-120` — a `{:from-db ...}` sub re-keys reactively and reads the new key as idle until a route/event ensures it; subscriptions never fetch.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/auth.cljs:189-261` — `:auth/ensure-viewer-route` reconstructs the leaf route's declaration and dispatches per-entry ensures by hand.
- `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/routing.cljs:54-89` — the public home route mixes viewer/session identities and currently claims a nil session feed is simply omitted, while no `:when` admits that distinction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The documented public event replans the active route in the dispatching frame from its current registered effective parent chain and current app-db, while leaving URL, route address, fragment and nav-token byte-for-byte unchanged and firing no guard, `:on-match`, history or scroll work.
- Replan uses the same `:when`/ctx, params and scope resolution, schema/canonical identity, contributor attribution, `:after`, branch ordering, identity collapse, blocking and keep-previous semantics as ordinary route entry; there is one planner, not an app-visible approximation.
- A same-route scope change A→B is covered: unchanged identities are retained without a forced request, B identities are ensured and owned, A-only identities lose the route owner, and the durable plan/blocking maps equal the newly materialized plan.
- An initial unresolved-scope plan error followed by app-db resolution + replan is covered: no navigation occurs, route error/readiness is repaired, exact plan membership is stored, and required loads start. The inverse/failing replan proves no partial ensure and the documented prior-owner cleanup/error result.
- Parent-chain coverage proves a leaf replan restores an inherited parent resource; a regression that reads only leaf `handler-meta` must fail. Coverage also pins a conditional occurrence entering/leaving the plan.
- RealWorld deletes `:auth/ensure-viewer-route`'s planner reconstruction in favor of the public command and tests successful restore, failed restore/confirmed anonymous, and a composed-route deep link including route readiness and plan membership, not only cache-entry existence.
- Spec 012/016, the Resources API/reference/concepts or how-to docs, examples and test prose agree on the command, passive-sub boundary, nil-scope behavior and trace cause. API-manifest drift remains green; no named facade helper is added.
- Proportionate Resources/Routing/RealWorld test gates pass, with a negative control that fails when effective-parent composition or durable readiness/plan replacement is removed.

## Non-goals

- No subscription-driven fetch, committed-read demand, app-db watcher, or automatic replan on every resolver input write.
- No general route reload that reruns guards, `:on-match`, history, scroll, or arbitrary route metadata.
- No named helper-function sugar, compatibility alias/window, second query grammar, or duplicate planner.
- No silent global fallback and no global change making nil route scopes silently optional; conditional resources remain explicitly admitted.
- No refactor of ordinary explicit `:rf.resource/ensure`/`refetch` for non-route owners.

- `rf2-hic-044` — current-primitives resource-demand witness; no demand/runtime ownership model is reopened here.

title: surface-review(implementation-build): let Node discover the script test suite
description:
## Scope

Replace the hand-maintained file rosters behind `implementation/package.json`'s `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` with one canonical implementation-level JavaScript harness command. Cover the 42 conventionally named `implementation/scripts/*.test.cjs` files, the two intended out-of-tree `.test.cjs` support tests currently in the helpers chain, and the native-IME verdict self-test. Update the fast-PR, CI, documentation, and policy consumers that currently know the two-command spelling. Preserve each test file's behaviour, process isolation, and failure signal.

## Findings

The suite already has a complete naming convention but does not use it. `implementation/scripts/` contains 42 `*.test.cjs` files. `test:script-policy` names 34 of them one by one; `test:script-helpers` names the other 8, plus two out-of-tree `.test.cjs` files and one CLI `--self-test`. That is 45 literal `node` invocations across two 2,218-character package-script values. Every new conventional test needs a second registration edit to one contested JSON line.

The split has user-visible cost without an execution boundary. The fast spine and CI always chain both commands. `TESTING.md` records that running only the second half has already let a red through. `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` therefore pins the exact two-command string, and `implementation/scripts/_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs` parses `package.json` to assert that its own filename appears in the roster. These are guards around manual registration rather than product or test semantics.

History shows the mechanism repeatedly failing in the dark direction. Closed beads `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` each existed to append tests or self-tests that had landed but ran in no spine; their notes also record guaranteed conflicts because each insertion rewrote the same long `package.json` line. The recent bench retirement removed most exceptional flag-driven readers, leaving only one such CLI self-test in the current helpers command, so this is now a small simplification rather than a framework project.

CI pins Node 24. Node 24's built-in test runner discovers quoted `*.test.cjs` glob patterns, runs each matching file in an isolated child process, and treats the child's exit code as the file verdict; files are explicitly not required to use `node:test` internally. The existing standalone harness files can therefore retain their current code and output. `--test-concurrency=1` can preserve today's serial host-load posture.

## Recommended Action

Create one obvious command, `npm run test:scripts`, that uses the Node 24 test runner with quoted, repository-scoped glob patterns for the conventional `.test.cjs` populations and `--test-concurrency=1`. Keep `scripts/run-hicasso-native-ime-witness.cjs --self-test` as the one explicit prelude, or expose that verdict control through a tiny conventional `.test.cjs` wrapper; do not build a custom discovery runner.

Delete `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` rather than retain forwarding aliases. Point the fast spine, the `js-harness-self-tests` CI job, `TESTING.md`, and `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py` at the single command. Remove self-enrolment assertions and comments that tell authors to edit `package.json`; adding a correctly named test file should be the registration act.

## Evidence

- `implementation/package.json:60-61` contains the two literal rosters: 34 policy files and 11 helper invocations.
- `rg --files implementation/scripts -g '*.test.cjs'` returns 42 files; all 42 occur exactly once across those two package scripts. The helper command separately names `core/test/re_frame/bench/lane_cache_wiring.test.cjs`, `hicasso/scripts/check_modules_compile.test.cjs`, and the native-IME `--self-test`.
- `TESTING.md:20` presents both names as one JS-harness tier; `TESTING.md:181-183` says they must be chained and records that running only the second let a red through.
- `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1489-1490` and `.github/workflows/test.yml:3131` duplicate the chained spelling; `scripts/check_fast_pr_gap.py:297` pins it as an exact regular expression.
- `implementation/scripts/_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs:203-208` checks its own textual enrolment in `test:script-policy`.
- Closed registration beads `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` document tests that existed but were not executed, plus contention on the one-line roster.
- Node 24 documentation lists `**/*.test.cjs` as a default discovery shape, recommends quoted globs for portability, and states that isolated test files are judged by process exit code without needing to use `node:test`: https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/test.html#running-tests-from-the-command-line
- Exact tracker searches for `node --test`, `auto-discover`, `test:script-policy`, `test:script-helpers`, `hand-register`, and `surface-review(implementation-build)` found no open, in-progress, or deferred bead owning this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- From `implementation/`, one documented `npm run test:scripts` command runs the same 44 `.test.cjs` files and the same native-IME verdict self-test that the two old commands run today, each exactly once.
- The command uses Node's built-in discovery over explicit repository-scoped globs, with process isolation and concurrency 1; it adds no dependency and no custom file-inventory runner.
- A temporary failing `implementation/scripts/*-negative-control.test.cjs` is discovered without editing `package.json`, makes the command exit non-zero, and is named in the failure output; removing it restores green. Record the red/green control in the PR.
- Baseline and replacement runs agree on the executed file population and preserve actionable stdout/stderr from a deliberately failing existing fixture or equivalent scoped mutation.
- `test:script-policy` and `test:script-helpers` are removed, not retained as aliases. The fast spine, `js-harness-self-tests` CI job, `TESTING.md`, and fast-PR gap check all use the one canonical command.
- The self-enrolment assertion in `_reagent-slim-smoke-policy.test.cjs` and stale comments telling authors to wire individual `.test.cjs` files into `package.json` are deleted or rewritten to describe convention-based discovery.
- The focused command passes on Windows and in the Node 24 Linux CI job without increasing test-file concurrency or introducing shared-fixture collisions.

## Non-goals

- Rewriting the 44 standalone test files to the `node:test` API or changing their assertion harnesses.
- Parallelising test files, changing their internal order, suppressing their diagnostics, or weakening exit-code handling.
- Auto-running every arbitrary `--self-test` mode in the repository; only conventional `.test.cjs` files are discovered, with the one current exceptional CLI control handled explicitly or wrapped conventionally.
- Folding CLJS, browser, JVM, API-manifest, bundle, benchmark, or rigorous-local suites into this command.
- Adding a watcher, third-party test framework, generated manifest, or new inventory/policy checker.

## Related beads

- `rf2-z2xir`, `rf2-45ti9`, `rf2-9ayub`, `rf2-lr4id`, and `rf2-zu82n` are closed instances of the manual-registration failure this task removes; none replaces this outcome.
- `rf2-fal5` is closed Windows host-load work inside `test:script-policy`; preserving serial process isolation respects that evidence but does not reopen or redesign the classifier suite.
- `rf2-6c12m.1` is the closed bench re-home/retirement that removed most exceptional helper registrations and made convention-based discovery a bounded change.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead found in the tracker proposes replacing the two rosters with native Node discovery.

Mandate --test-concurrency=1 (host-load posture); keep the IME --self-test as an explicit prelude; double-quote globs inside the npm JSON string (Windows). Edit only comments that INSTRUCT registration, not historical narration (30+ files mention it). HOT ZONE: .github/workflows/test.yml:3131 one line (nobody else on it); check release.yml too. Soft overlap with rf2-qxg24 on TESTING.md (different sections). DISPATCHABLE solo.

title: surface-review(xray): make Pair the single agent runtime and retire the duplicate Xray seam
description:
## Scope

Make the human/agent boundary around Xray explicit and singular for pre-alpha users:

- Xray's preload and public API own the in-app human panel.
- `re-frame2-pair.runtime` plus `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/` own out-of-process programmer/AI inspection and mutation.
- Retire the unused `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` agent contract, its sentinel, tests, manifest rows, and documentation.
- Preserve the small fail-closed egress projection that Xray itself needs when copying app-db snapshots and diff values, but keep it internal to the panel.

Review and update the affected Xray source, specs, docs, tests, testbeds/build wiring, and repository API manifests. The desired outcome is one honest setup story, not a new capability.

## Findings

1. Xray documents an agent integration that does not exist. `tools/xray/README.md` and `tools/xray/spec/API.md` say Pair MCP evaluates `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` and that Xray's preload installs the agent sentinel with no second preload. Pair MCP instead hard-codes `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, probes `js/globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime` before runtime-backed tools, and contains zero references to the Xray runtime namespace or sentinel.
2. The two seams are not interchangeable. The canonical Pair preload supplies the current coarse-grained workflow (`orient`, `snapshot`, event-bundle/cascade reads, dispatch consequence/dry-run, recording/watch, DOM/UI reads, restore/replace). Xray's older runtime still exposes a parallel catalogue of trace/epoch/app-db/registrar/resource/subscription/mutation calls and explicitly leaves event-bundle reads to a follow-on.
3. The duplication is substantial and already drifting: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs` is about 91 KB / 1,700 lines and its dedicated CLJS test is about 115 KB / 1,884 lines. The Pair preload is about 230 KB / 4,000 lines and has continued evolving after Xray runtime's last direct change on 2026-07-11.
4. Xray itself does not need that public agent catalogue. Within `tools/xray/src`, the only functional callers of the runtime namespace outside the preload are three calls to `runtime/egress-value` in the palette snapshot and app-db diff copy paths. The preload requires the whole namespace solely to install the second sentinel.
5. The contract contradicts Xray's own product boundary. `spec/Principles.md` says Xray is the human surface and AI belongs in the separate Pair MCP; `018-Event-Spine.md` says the agent reads raw instrumentation rather than a Xray-curated facade. Xray already has a large panel/tab information architecture, and its restraint principle explicitly argues for subtraction rather than another surface.
6. Four Xray runtime exports are nevertheless published as post-v1 tooling rows in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` / generated `spec/api-manifest.edn`, turning an unused pre-alpha seam into prospective compatibility cost.
7. Testbed wiring proves the real setup: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` explicitly loads `re-frame2-pair.runtime` alongside Xray in builds that Pair MCP drives, while Xray-only and Pair-only builds load their respective preloads independently.

## Recommended Action

Take a clean pre-alpha cut:

1. Remove `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` as a public/tooling namespace, including `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime`, its preload require, external accessor catalogue, mutation helpers, streaming state, dedicated runtime test bulk, and API-manifest rows.
2. Move or re-express only the panel-local `egress-value` behavior needed by palette snapshot and app-db diff copying in a small internal Xray namespace, preferably as a thin call to the canonical framework projection. Keep its current frame-owned, fail-closed sensitive/large-value behavior and focused tests.
3. Rewrite Xray's README and specs around one accurate boundary: load `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload` for the panel; load `re-frame2-pair.runtime` and use Pair MCP for programmer/AI access. A build may opt into either or both explicitly; neither preload silently stands in for the other.
4. Remove the obsolete stable-accessor/sentinel contract and future-consumer promises from Xray's API/spec material. Link to Pair's setup and tool contract rather than duplicating it.
5. Reconcile Xray testbeds/builds and generated manifests with that boundary. Keep Pair preload entries only where the build is actually Pair-driven and Xray preload entries only where the panel is exercised.

## Evidence

- False consumer/setup claims: `tools/xray/README.md:29-32,231-235`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:56-58`; `tools/xray/spec/API.md:256,668-697,676-953`.
- Pair's actual boundary: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_form.cljs:64`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs:14-15`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:28-39,429-452`; `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs`.
- Exact searches under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` and `skills/re-frame2-pair` find no `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` or `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime` references.
- Xray-local callers: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/events.cljs:181`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_events.cljs:68-69`.
- Duplicate implementation/test: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime.cljs`; `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/runtime_cljs_test.cljs`. The Xray trace accessor itself says event-bundle reads are deferred at `runtime.cljs:544-557`.
- Product boundary: `tools/xray/spec/Principles.md:59-79,148-157,172-178`; `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:24-29`.
- Published surface: `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:183-186` and corresponding generated rows.
- Real preload topology: `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1216,1320-1423,1460,1500-1531,1822-2120`.
- History: Xray runtime's last direct commit is `d22417a0b7` (2026-07-11); Pair runtime has subsequent direct commits through `2b0b482eb3` (2026-08-06).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Tracked product source, specs, docs, test config, and manifests contain no `day8.re-frame2-xray.runtime` namespace, `__day8_re_frame2_xray_runtime` sentinel, or claim that Pair MCP consumes/arrives through Xray. No compatibility alias, tombstone namespace, or dual-probe path remains.
2. `runtime.cljs` and its agent-contract test suite are removed. Any surviving privacy tests are focused on the two panel-local copy/export behaviors rather than re-specifying Pair's tool protocol.
3. Palette app-db snapshot and app-db diff copy still project under the observed frame and default-redact sensitive/large values. A focused CLJS test proves both a normal value and a seeded sensitive value at the actual copy boundary.
4. Xray's README/API gives copy-pasteable, separate setup for the panel and for Pair MCP. It states that loading both requires both explicit preloads and links to Pair's canonical tool documentation instead of reproducing an accessor table.
5. API manifest metadata is regenerated with zero Xray runtime rows; the manifest consistency gate passes.
6. Testbed/build preload lists match intent: Xray-only panel fixtures run without Pair, Pair-driven fixtures carry `re-frame2-pair.runtime`, and combined fixtures declare both. No Xray code depends on the skill-owned Pair namespace.
7. Xray's focused JVM/CLJS tests and browser smoke for shell startup plus the two copy paths pass. Pair MCP's conformance/runtime structural suite remains green, demonstrating that the one surviving agent path was not disturbed.
8. The implementation PR reports the source/test line reduction and names any residual public Xray namespace that remains for tool access; expected answer is none.

## Non-goals

- No new panel, dashboard, AI rail, workflow wizard, event-dossier variant, or information-architecture redesign.
- No redesign or expansion of Pair MCP, its protocol, privacy flags, write gates, or preload.
- No merged Xray/Pair mega-preload and no automatic loading of Pair from Xray.
- No deprecation period, compatibility wrapper, alias namespace, sentinel fallback, or migration framework; this is pre-alpha.
- No general rewrite of the framework egress/classification machinery.
- No broad audit of `day8.re-frame2-xray.core` facade exports.

title: pair-mcp: retire the progress-stream subsystem (33 -> 29 tools)
description:
## Scope

Make live observation fit an ordinary programmer+AI tool turn. Retire Pair-MCP's progress-notification streaming subsystem: the public `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` tools; their server/runtime queue, polling, accounting, and launch-control machinery; and their schema, manifest, test, spec, skill, and conformance carriers. Establish the already-shipped result-returning tools as the one supported live-app observation workflow. Cover the smallest coherent cross-repo seam under `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/**`, the companion `re-frame2-pair.runtime` preload and Pair skill, and the MCP conformance fixtures that pin the public catalogue.

## Findings

- The source catalogue exposes 33 tools. Four are one push-streaming subsystem, and four environment/launch controls exist only to bound that subsystem (`MAX_STREAMS`, event rate, abuse threshold, abuse window). This is a large public and configuration tax for an optional observation route.
- `subscribe` does not return observations as the tool result. It holds `tools/call` open until cancellation/cap/termination, emits useful data through `notifications/progress`, then returns only a terminal summary. Pair-MCP's own live conformance witness must keep a `subscribePromise` open and issue `dispatch` concurrently to exercise it. That is a valid custom MCP-client pattern, but not the natural sequential turn shape of a coding agent; out-of-band `unsubscribe` has the same second-concurrent-call assumption.
- Every normal pairing outcome already has a turn-shaped route: `dispatch` returns its consequence or settled epoch; `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` read bounded history; `watch-until` blocks to a data predicate and returns the sample; `record` + `read-recording` cover human/intermittent interaction; and `tail-build` waits for hot reload. The rare need for a bespoke live listener remains expressible through the default-enabled `eval-cljs` escape hatch and does not justify four permanent public tools.
- Eight dedicated Pair-MCP source/test files (`subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, `get-stream-controls`, `resource-controls`, and their three largest focused suites) already total 3,056 lines / 156,022 bytes, before `resource_controls_test.cljs`, the preload's subscription queues/listener fan-out, server/config plumbing, the long catalogue sections, skill prose, and the dedicated live conformance script are counted.
- The complexity is not passive. The stream needs dual event/byte queue caps, drop-oldest accounting, a token bucket, an abuse window, dead-connection retry/termination, cancellation and out-of-band teardown, per-tick cap/dedup/elision, and two diagnostic tools to explain the controls. History records repeated follow-on repairs for lost events, uncapped progress frames, dead drain loops, privacy projection, frame scoping, and control observability.
- The generated descriptor manifest is already 88,930 bytes for the full catalogue. Removing four host-specialized tools reduces the always-advertised surface as well as implementation weight; retaining them as aliases would preserve the cost and defeat the pre-alpha simplification.

## Recommended Action

Delete `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` from the registry and remove the streaming-only server/runtime implementation: runtime subscription queues and drain API, polling controller, progress payloads, concurrent-slot/rate/abuse controls, their flags/environment variables, diagnostics, and teardown state. Do not add a generic replacement, deprecated aliases, tombstones, or a compatibility mode.

Rewrite the Pair routing guidance around returned-result workflows:

1. Use `dispatch` consequence/settle for an action the agent initiated.
2. Use `watch-epochs` or `trace-window` for retained event/trace history.
3. Use `watch-until` for a known asynchronous condition.
4. Use `record` + `read-recording` while a human or the browser drives the app.
5. Use `tail-build` for code reload.

Keep `list-subscriptions`: it reads the app's reactive subscription cache and is unrelated to MCP progress streams. Preserve the retained tools' existing privacy projection, elision, wire caps, and explicit time bounds; do not replace deleted stream controls with another permission or resource-control layer.

## Evidence

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/registry.cljs` registers the four tools as a distinct streaming/diagnostic family.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/subscribe.cljs` is 864 lines. Its contract says the call runs until abort/unsubscribe and carries observations in `notifications/progress`; the final result is a summary. `resource_controls.cljs` adds another 479 lines.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-subscribe.cjs` explicitly starts `client.callTool(subscribe)` without awaiting it, fires `dispatch` concurrently, accumulates `onprogress` callbacks, and only later awaits the terminal subscription result. The test demonstrates the concurrency contract rather than a normal one-call/one-result agent workflow.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/package.json`, `spec/API.md`, and `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` expose the stream configuration, progress wire shape, caps, filters, diagnostics, and five termination paths.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` owns the streaming queue/listener fan-out (`subscribe!`, `drain-subscription!`, `unsubscribe!`, `subscription-info`) in addition to the retained history and recorder surfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, and `get-stream-controls` are absent from `registry/tools`, `tools/list`, the canonical tool-name fixture, generated descriptor manifest, conformance corpus, package README/API/catalogue, Pair skill allow-list/routing, and current capability/status docs. No alias, deprecated descriptor, or unknown-tool special case preserves them.
2. Streaming-only Pair-MCP files and code paths are removed. The server has no progress-notification emitter, stream slot/token-bucket/abuse-window state, stream-specific launch flags or environment variables, or stream cleanup branch. The preload has no Pair-owned stream registry, bounded event queue, drain loop API, or stream-only listener fan-out. Shared framework trace/epoch facilities used by retained reads remain intact.
3. `list-subscriptions` remains and is documented/tested as the reactive app subscription-cache read, with no streaming terminology or dependency.
4. A live end-to-end witness proves the retained turn-shaped workflow without concurrent MCP calls: dispatch an event, observe its returned consequence and retained epoch/trace; a focused `watch-until` test returns a matching asynchronous sample; and the existing recorder path still captures and returns a browser/human-driven change. Each observation reaches the agent in a completed tool result, not a progress callback.
5. Tool annotations, schemas, `tool-descriptors.edn`, the stdio catalogue snapshot, and cross-server MCP conformance agree with the reduced surface. The Pair package tests, descriptor-drift check, stdio round trip, and relevant live fixture/conformance lanes pass non-vacuously.
6. Current docs state one observation decision tree using the five retained routes above. Historical design notes may record that push streaming once existed, but no current setup, recipe, status table, or diagnostic ladder instructs an agent to use it.
7. No new public tool, compatibility shim, permission gate, scheduler, queue, or background service is introduced to replace the deleted subsystem.

## Non-goals

- Removing or weakening `read-sub` / `list-subscriptions`, framework trace/epoch listeners, epoch retention, privacy projection, elision, or the ordinary per-response wire cap.
- Redesigning the remaining 29-tool catalogue, globally rewriting descriptor prose, or combining unrelated tools in this change.
- Changing MCP itself, adding a different streaming transport, or supporting dashboard/telemetry clients whose primary workload is continuous event consumption.
- Preserving compatibility for the four removed pre-alpha names, migration aliases, deprecation windows, or launch-flag no-ops.
- Tightening eval/write permissions or adding safety confirmations. The installed local Pair-MCP and explicit invoker remain the trust boundary.

title: surface-review(story-mcp): make project stories reachable on first launch
description:
## Scope

Make the published headless Story-MCP server expose a consumer project's JVM-loadable Story registry on its first MCP connection. Add one explicit launch-time namespace-loading seam, document one copyable consumer-project/MCP-host configuration, and prove the path end to end against a project-owned story. Preserve the settled boundary that live browser/CLJS stories are reached through re-frame2-pair.

## Findings

Story-MCP is a same-JVM adapter: every catalogue read, run, and write operates on the process-local Story registry. That makes loading the consumer's registration namespaces a prerequisite, not optional setup polish.

The only canonical launch is `clojure -M -m re-frame.story-mcp.server` from the tool directory. The README adds one sentence saying the launch “must preload” registry-populating JVM namespaces, but supplies no argument, alias, wrapper, MCP-host config, ordering rule, or executable example that does so. The server CLI accepts only the two gate flags and ignores every other flag; `boot!` installs canonical vocabulary and immediately enters the stdio loop. A normal launch therefore has tags/assertions but no project stories.

The integration corpus proves protocol and synthetic in-memory behavior, not the consumer workflow. `stdio-roundtrip.js` uses the bare canonical command and deliberately probes missing stories/variants. The SDK conformance harness starts the same command with `--allow-writes`, creates a synthetic variant only after connecting, and explicitly notes that a successful story read would need a registered story. No test starts the published server from a consuming project, preloads a project namespace, then discovers and runs that already-authored story.

This is the first-use bottleneck for the whole 20-tool catalogue: until a project registry is present, the documented `list-stories -> get-story/get-variant -> run/refine` workflow cannot begin. More protocol hardening or another tool would not fix it.

## Recommended Action

Add one repeatable explicit startup option, for example `--require app.stories.login`, whose values are trusted namespace names from the invoking project's classpath. In `boot!`, install Story's canonical vocabulary first, then `require` the supplied namespaces, then start the MCP loop. Let an ordinary require failure abort startup loudly; do not add namespace scanning, a custom discovery protocol, allowlists, or redundant name validation.

Document a single golden consumer path: a `deps.edn` alias that depends on `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp`, a project-root MCP-host command using that alias plus the explicit namespace option, and the write-gate flag only when the author/refine loop is wanted. State plainly that the namespace must be CLJ/CLJC-loadable in this headless JVM; a running browser's CLJS registry remains the pair's one live door.

Back the path with one consumer-shaped fixture driven through the official MCP SDK: launch from the fixture project, load its story namespace at boot, and immediately discover/read/run its pre-authored story without first calling `register-variant`.

## Evidence

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md:37-51` shows the bare tool-directory command and only the unimplemented “must preload” sentence.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:337-365` parses only `--allow-writes` and `--allow-sensitive-reads`; unknown flags are logged and ignored.
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:368-384` applies gates and installs canonical vocabulary but has no consumer-namespace load step.
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:17,74-80` and `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md:35-55` make registrations/runs process-local and define Story-MCP as the headless same-JVM host.
- `tools/story-mcp/test/stdio-roundtrip.js:45-51,247-281` calls the bare launch and verifies only missing-variant plus gated-write behavior.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-story.cjs:27,134,342-369` launches with `--allow-writes`, says a story hit needs a registered story, then synthesizes only a variant after connection.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/stories.md:15` documents the complementary browser path: Story-MCP cannot see a tab's registry; pair `eval-cljs` is the live door.
- History: initial commit `65c05d67c5` introduced the current bare command; `4cfdf55f61` added the preload caveat two months later, but no launch mechanism or consumer integration witness followed. There are 185 commits touching `tools/story-mcp`; the missing consumer bootstrap is not an unimplemented handler detail.
- Exact tracker searches across current and closed issues for `story-mcp`, project stories, JVM namespaces, preload namespace, empty registry, same-JVM registry, launch, setup, and bootstrap found no matching outcome bead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A consuming project's documented `deps.edn` alias and MCP-host configuration start the published Story-MCP main from the project root without repository-local source paths or a user-written wrapper namespace.
- One repeatable explicit namespace option loads named CLJ/CLJC registration namespaces after canonical vocabulary installation and before the server accepts MCP requests; multiple supplied namespaces preserve command order.
- An official-SDK end-to-end fixture launches through that consumer path and, before any MCP write, proves `list-stories` finds the fixture story, `get-story` or `get-variant` reads it, and `run-variant` executes its fixture variant.
- A missing or throwing supplied namespace terminates startup with a useful stderr diagnostic/non-zero exit rather than continuing with a misleading empty project registry. The implementation relies on ordinary `require` failure; it does not invent a second validation layer.
- README/spec guidance clearly distinguishes JVM-loadable project namespaces from the running browser's CLJS registry and routes the latter to re-frame2-pair.
- Existing no-namespace launches, gate semantics, the MCP method set, tool names, tool input/output schemas, and Story's public registration API remain unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Adding nREPL, a JVM-to-browser bridge, or a second live-app transport.
- Auto-discovering namespaces by scanning source roots, classpaths, files, manifests, or naming conventions.
- Hot reload, namespace watching, runtime load/unload tools, or persistence of registrations to source files.
- Adding a new MCP tool, a new Story registration primitive, or extra env/sysprop aliases/config DSLs for the same bootstrap.
- Redesigning the 20-tool catalogue, token budgeting, privacy egress, cursor protocol, or JSON-RPC lifecycle.
- Making CLJS-only story namespaces JVM-loadable.

## Related beads

- `rf2-tgci` (closed) introduced the separate-jar Story-MCP server and its canonical bare launch.
- `rf2-3fc89f.21` (closed) made browser-only reads fail as capability-unavailable rather than false-empty; this task preserves that truthfulness.
- `rf2-3fc89f.22` (closed) ruled the pair as the one live-browser Story host; this task is only the explicit headless-JVM bootstrap.
- `rf2-s99lw4` (closed) documented the pair-side browser recipe through `eval-cljs`; it is the complementary path, not a duplicate.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead matching this project-namespace bootstrap outcome was found.

title: surface-review(conformance-security): stop security-tier edits from arming production and browser gates
description:
## Scope

Correct PR changed-surface routing for the four source-less, cross-artefact test partitions under implementation/security, implementation/reply-conformance, implementation/derivation-conformance, and implementation/event-conformance. The implementation change should be confined to the classifier and its executable policy tests/comments unless a directly coupled testing-policy sentence must move with them.

## Findings

- All four partitions are test-only: each deps.edn has :paths [] and :deps {}, none has a src/ tree, and none publishes production code. Their responsibilities are substantial and distinct: reply vocabulary/egress across managed-async families; derivation algebra across five graph contributors; the event facade/runtime/isolation boundary; and adversarial security properties over schema, SSR, reply, profile, error-slot, and MCP egress.
- The suites deliberately complement artefact-local tests rather than replace them. Derivation composes family projections; event tests adversarial public seams after core-owned duplicates were removed; reply tests own cross-family vocabulary while family tests own lowering; security adds generated/sentinel/fail-closed coverage beyond fixed local pins. A broad semantic dedupe would trade away confidence for little benefit.
- CLJS already has the right shape: every namespace matches the consolidated :node-test build's cljs-test$ selector, and the focused test:security build is only a local-iteration subset. JVM CI likewise keeps four required clojure -M:test jobs. Current successful run 33307155376 reports security 92 tests/698 assertions, derivation 22/522, event 49/209, and reply 27/533.
- The changed-surface classifier treats the three *-conformance trees as source-less and sets only implementation_jvm=true plus cljs_node_test=true. The same probe on an actual security test currently also sets cljs_browser=true, examples_compile=true, cljs_prod=true, and bundle_isolation=true.
- Those four extra gates cannot observe a security-tier-only edit: :browser-test selects only *-dom-cljs-test namespaces; production and bundle-isolation builds do not require the test tree; and the all-examples compiler has no edge to it. implementation/security/deps.edn is also test-only.
- This is drift from recorded intent, not a new coverage trade. Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 says adding implementation/security/* was needed specifically to fire implementation_jvm and cljs_node_test, but placed it in a generic feature-artefact arm that sets five outputs. The later src-less conformance arm at report-changed-surfaces.sh:1202-1220 explicitly says security is the precedent for omitting browser/prod/bundle gates, while the earlier executable arm contradicts it.
- The examples-compile policy test reinforces the mistake with implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc, a path that does not exist in this intentionally src-less partition, and asserts that this imaginary file can change an example closure.
- The toll is material. Security-only commit d1fa5ff493 changed deps/test commentary and its tests workflow run 29096118890 executed the relevant JVM/Node suites plus the all-examples job (10m24s), browser, two production browser builds, and bundle isolation. The all-examples job was the critical path; current direct classifier output still arms the same unrelated surfaces.
- Search across all tracker statuses and title/description/notes for conformance, security classifier/surface/tier, src-less, examples_compile, bundle_isolation, cljs_browser, and over-classification found no issue owning this exact mismatch.

## Recommended Action

Move implementation/security/* out of both the shipped-feature classifier arm and the examples_compile input arm, and classify it alongside reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance as a source-less cross-artefact tier: implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true only.

Update the classifier's executable mirror using real tracked security paths. Preserve the jvm-security required job, the local JVM roster entry, the consolidated Node inclusion, and the focused test:security command. Keep production artefact routing unchanged, so changes to core/schemas/machines/routing/flows/SSR still run their existing production/browser/bundle gates and continue to trigger the broad JVM and Node suites.

## Evidence

- implementation/security/deps.edn and the three *-conformance/deps.edn files: empty production paths/deps, test-only aliases.
- implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:208-287 and 650-655: all four test roots feed the shared cljs-test$ Node build; security's focused selector is at 769-790.
- .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh:574 includes security in examples compilation; 973-997 includes it in the full feature fan-out; 1202-1220 gives the three sibling tiers the intended narrow routing and states that security has the same posture.
- implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs:1983-2011 asserts examples compilation from the nonexistent implementation/security/src/re_frame/security.cljc; 3283-3311 already pins the narrow sibling-tier contract.
- .github/workflows/test.yml:2149-2198 and 2482-2610: required JVM jobs; 6026 and 6040-6042: aggregator membership.
- scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh:46-90: all four JVM lanes remain in the rigorous local roster.
- Commit 5bb3cd9cd1 and workflow runs 29096118890 / 33307155376 provide the intent, observed toll, and current suite tallies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Classifying both implementation/security/deps.edn and at least one real tracked implementation/security/test/** file sets implementation_jvm=true and cljs_node_test=true, while examples_compile, cljs_browser, cljs_prod, and bundle_isolation are false.
2. Representative real files under reply-conformance, derivation-conformance, and event-conformance retain the same two-output routing.
3. The classifier policy test removes the imaginary implementation/security/src/** positive fixture, uses tracked paths for the security tier, and explicitly locks the four negative outputs so the broad arm cannot silently return.
4. jvm-security remains conditional on implementation_jvm, remains in all-required-passed, and still runs clojure -M:test from implementation/security. The local JVM roster entry, shadow :node-test root, and npm test:security focused command remain intact.
5. Production/source-bearing artefact probes retain their existing browser, production, examples, and bundle-isolation routing; this change narrows only the source-less security partition.
6. Classifier comments and TESTING.md, if touched, agree that all four source-less tiers use JVM + consolidated Node coverage and do not claim production-bundle reachability.
7. The changed-surface policy suite and gate-scheduling checks pass, with a direct classifier transcript for all four partitions included in the handoff.

## Non-goals

- Do not delete, merge, thin, or relocate semantic conformance/security tests.
- Do not combine the four JVM jobs or deps.edn files, redesign the broad implementation_jvm output, or add a new classifier output.
- Do not change security, reply, event, derivation, egress, redaction, or fail-open/fail-closed runtime behavior.
- Do not remove the focused test:security command merely because its namespaces also ride test:cljs.
- Do not narrow production artefact changes; only edits inside the source-less implementation/security partition are in scope.

## Related beads

- rf2-7rzg records the same general location-based over-classification shape for Hicasso prose, but is an independent operator decision with different observable gates; this task neither depends on nor settles it.
- Historical provenance cited by the repository: rf2-oni7gz/rf2-gj2ae established JVM security coverage; rf2-dxndhc established narrow routing for the three sibling source-less tiers; rf2-gzavkm established that examples_compile should follow actual compiled-closure inputs. title: EPIC ssr-node crossing: make the bounded Node renderer a first-class ssr-ring path (RULED 2026-09-02 — six children rf2-8arzr.1..6; do not dispatch this bead)
description:
## Scope

Make the bounded Node/React renderer a supported opt-in renderer for the non-streaming re-frame.ssr.ring request path. The outcome includes the smallest useful Ring render seam, the JVM side of the v1 crossing, an explicit post-drain render-state projection, a supported Node package/launcher entry point, and one canonical runnable native-Hicasso example with its tests and documentation. The existing JVM/Reagent renderer remains the default.

## Findings

- The three components are individually substantial and well tested, but they do not compose into a public product path. re-frame.ssr.ring owns request frames, event/resource drain, head, hydration payload, shell, response and teardown; implementation/ssr-node owns a bounded React render service; no caller joins them.
- build-full-response* resolves a JVM hiccup root and directly invokes ssr/render-to-string. That API shape cannot name a native JavaScript root which exists only in the application bundle.
- The Node request already has a stable entry, EDN root args, build identity, and allowlisted state, but its state shape is only top-level app-db key -> EDN value text. The JVM does not produce that projection, and route/machine/runtime facts needed by a real SPA have no inbound door.
- Render visibility and hydration egress are different policies. The server must be able to render from state that is intentionally absent from __rf_payload; deriving one projection from the other would either leak server-only state or silently render nil.
- The documented consumer API imports implementation/ssr-node/src/*.cjs directly. implementation/ssr-node has README.md, src/ and test/ but no package manifest/export or supported launch command of its own.
- Existing JVM and Node suites are broad but disjoint. The Node lane proves the service in isolation; there is no JVM -> Node -> JVM witness, runnable example, or generated recipe.

## Recommended Action

Add one explicit render-body boundary at the full-response body decision, selected when constructing the Ring handler. Its input should describe the post-drain request frame plus a stable render entry and serialized root arguments; it should not require a JVM hiccup value. Keep a tiny local adapter as the default so the current JVM/Reagent path and output remain unchanged.

Implement the concrete JVM-to-Node adapter for the existing bounded service. Let applications supply one render-state projector; define the serialization domain and carry the render-visible app-db and runtime/route/machine facts a native root needs. Revise the pre-alpha v1 request directly if necessary rather than adding compatibility layers. Keep the ownership line crisp: Node returns body markup only; the JVM continues to own boot-event drain, head, hydration payload, shell, status/headers/cookies/redirects, error projection, and frame teardown.

Give ssr-node a supported package entry point and runnable server command, then exercise the path in one small native-Hicasso reference app. Document that recipe at the public Ring/SSR surface and reflect any new public symbols or artifacts in the API and distribution manifests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented Ring handler option selects either the existing local renderer (the unchanged default) or the concrete Node adapter through one narrow render-body contract; no renderer registry or protocol hierarchy is introduced.
- On the Node path, the JVM drains initial events and blocking resources first, then sends a stable entry id, EDN root args, expected build id, request identity/deadline, and an application-projected render snapshot from the live request frame.
- The render snapshot can faithfully seed both app-db and the route/machine/runtime facts used by the reference native view. Its serialization rules have a round-trip corpus and one clear negative fixture for an unsupported value.
- Render-state projection is independent of hydration payload projection. An end-to-end fixture renders from a server-only value while proving that value is absent from the JVM-written __rf_payload.
- A real JVM -> Node -> JVM test launches the supported Node entry point, renders a native application entry, and proves that Node body bytes are inserted into a complete JVM-owned Ring response with JVM-owned head and payload.
- The same crossing test covers one representative refusal or deadline, shows it reaches the existing Ring error/on-error semantics without a partial success page, and proves request-frame/isolate cleanup on success and failure.
- Application authors can import and start ssr-node through a declared package export/command without reaching into implementation/ssr-node/src.
- One runnable example and one canonical documentation recipe cover build, entry-table declaration, renderer selection, state projection, startup, hydration, and build-id skew. Spec 011, public API docs/API manifest, and package/release manifests agree with the shipped surface.
- Existing SSR, Ring, and Node test lanes stay green, and CI runs the new crossing witness.

## Non-goals

- Moving HTTP request, head, payload, shell, cookies, redirects, or response ownership into Node.
- Node streaming, React Server Components, islands, or a general RPC/renderer plugin framework.
- Multi-version protocol negotiation or compatibility scaffolding; this is a pre-alpha v1 contract and may be changed coherently.
- Replacing or changing the default JVM/Reagent renderer.
- Platform-specific supervisor, container, autoscaling, or deployment automation.

== SHARED CONTRACT (every slice cites these by number) ==

S1 THE SEAM. `ssr-handler` gains ONE construction opt, `:renderer` — a plain fn, no protocol, no registry, no multimethod: `(fn [{:keys [frame-id request opts]}] -> {:body-html <string> :render-hash <string-or-nil>})`, called by `build-full-response*` at today's hard call (pipeline.clj:564) INSIDE the existing `rf/with-frame` scope, AFTER `drain-blocking-resources!` and the boot-event drain, BEFORE head resolution and the payload build consume its result. Input: the live post-drain frame by id (everything the JVM knows is reachable from it), the handler opts and the Ring request — NEVER a JVM hiccup value. Output: body markup plus an optional LOCALLY-derived render hash; nil hash => no `data-rf-render-hash` marker and no payload `:rf/render-hash`, exactly today's unresolved-root behaviour (rf2-q1b96). The default renderer wraps today's resolve-root-view -> render-document-hash -> render-to-string; the default path's bytes and errors are unchanged, and that is slice A's acceptance floor. `:root-view` is required iff the renderer is the default. `stream-handler` refuses `:renderer` at construction with `:rf.error/ssr-streaming-unsupported-opt` (the `:html-shell` precedent, spec/011-SSR.md:1695-1703); streaming over a non-local renderer is a programme non-goal.

S2 OWNERSHIP LINE (the bead's, restated because every slice cites it). Node returns body markup and nothing else. The JVM owns the request frame, boot-event drain, blocking-resource settle, head, hydration payload (`__rf_payload`), shell, status/headers/cookies/redirects, error projection and frame teardown. The sidecar's HTTP status is never copied to the browser response.

S3 RENDER STATE. The render-visible projection is DISTINCT IN POLICY from the hydration payload's but SHARES ITS ENVELOPE: the partition shape `{:rf/app-db {...} :rf/runtime-db {...}}` the payload already uses (payload.clj:5-13) and the client's `:rf/hydrate` already installs (hydrate.cljc). It is declared like `:payload` — a fail-closed allowlist per partition (top-level app-db keys; top-level runtime-db keys such as the route slice and machine snapshots) — as a new handler opt `:render-state`, with a `(fn [frame-id] -> partition-map)` escape hatch for a projector the allowlist vocabulary cannot express. The FRAMEWORK does the projecting, in a new `re-frame.ssr.render-state` cljc namespace reusing payload_policy.cljc's apply/project machinery. The serialization domain is the payload's existing EDN domain — reuse it, never invent a second one; slice C supplies the round-trip corpus and the negative fixture. The Node-side restore seeds a FRESH per-request frame with both partitions WITHOUT replaying boot events (the JVM drained them), reusing hydrate.cljc's partition-install path minus verification and DOM. This is the "second install door" the ssr-node README (:355-365) declined to invent in a sidecar; the framework decides it here, by ruling.

S4 PROTOCOL v1 REVISION (slice C; pre-alpha — revise protocol.cjs directly, no compatibility layer, `protocol` stays 1). The request carries the runtime partition beside `state`, per-key EDN text, gated by an ENTRY-owned allowlist for that partition too (absence = unrenderable, mirroring stateAllowlist at :264-273). The service still never decodes application data; allowlists stay entry-owned so a caller cannot widen its own allowance — the fail-closed guarantee is KEPT in Node, not moved to the JVM. The wire spelling (`runtime` + `runtimeAllowlist`, or one two-partition `snapshot` object) is the worker's call within those invariants. `initialEvents` / `payloadPolicy` / `head` stay refused for the reasons already in REFUSED_FIELDS.

S5 ERRORS ON THE NODE PATH route through the EXISTING render-failure projection — the `:error-view` side of spec/011's division (:1428-1450). A transport failure (connection refused, JVM read timeout), a sidecar refusal (`x-rf-ssr-refusal`; 4xx/503/504/500) and a sidecar render failure are ALL throws at the render call site with a live frame the projector can see, so all become a projected 5xx via `ssr/project-render-exception!` — with DISTINCT codes (e.g. `:rf.error/ssr-node-unreachable`, `:rf.error/ssr-node-refused` carrying the refusal code in ex-data, `:rf.error/ssr-node-deadline`) so operators can tell them apart in the trace stream. `:on-error` keeps its meaning (the net for when the projector cannot run). No partial success page is possible: the body render fails before any shell is assembled.

S6 JVM HTTP/JSON. The adapter lives in ssr-ring as ONE namespace, `re-frame.ssr.ring.node`, required only by consumers who select it. JDK `java.net.http.HttpClient`: ONE client per renderer, built at construction and reused (per-operation clients defeat pooling); EVERY request carries an explicit timeout = the request's `timeoutMs` + the sidecar's admission budget + a wire margin, derived by the adapter (a separate knob only if the worker finds one necessary). JSON via `org.clojure/data.json` added to implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn — ACCEPTED as ssr-ring's one new dependency (first-party, zero transitive deps; consumers of the default local renderer pay one small jar, which is acceptable). Rejected: a separate adapter artefact; cheshire (Jackson's transitive weight for a flat request); hand-rolled JSON.

S7 DEPLOYMENT POSTURE. Default endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8148. The adapter accepts any URL and does NOT refuse a non-loopback one (trust the programmer); the recipe states that render state may carry server-only values, so a remote sidecar is the operator's network and transport to secure. `engines: {node: ">=24"}` in ssr-node's package.json, matching CI. Build skew: the sidecar refuses on `buildId` mismatch already; the adapter additionally checks `x-rf-ssr-build` on success and throws a distinct code if it differs.

title: surface-review(http): expose successful response metadata to :after middleware and reply handlers
description:
## Scope

Close the managed-HTTP completion gap from a host-normalized 2xx response through decode/accept, canonical reply construction, the per-frame `:after` chain, and app reply delivery. Cover the JVM and CLJS transports plus HTTP test support, Spec 014, async/API documentation, and the managed-HTTP skill/example material that describes response middleware.

## Verified Findings

- Both host transports feed `handle-response!` a normalized map containing `:status`, `:status-text`, and `:headers`. The 4xx/5xx branches retain these facts, but the successful 2xx branch calls `finalise-success!` with only the accepted body value.
- `success-reply` accepts only ctx plus value and builds a canonical success reply without HTTP response metadata. Therefore neither `:after` nor `:reply-to` / `:on-success` can observe status or headers for a successful request.
- Spec 014 and `docs/async/http-going-further.md` explicitly present rate-limit-header and Cache-Control parsing as `:after` use cases.
- The two motivating JVM tests do not verify that contract: their servers emit `X-RateLimit-*` and `Cache-Control`, while the interceptors hard-code `37`, `100`, and `600` after comments acknowledge that headers do not ride on the reply. The tests pass even if the emitted headers change or disappear.
- Searches of all current beads for response headers, success headers, rate-limit, HTTP metadata, ETag, Location, Cache-Control, and after-interceptor headers found no matching task.

## Recommended Action

Thread a minimal, documented successful-response metadata value through decode/accept and success finalization into the canonical reply's existing `:meta` family-extension slot. It should contain the actual numeric status, status text, and the transport's already-normalized header map; keep `:value` as the decoded-and-accepted application payload. Run `:after` over that canonical reply and deliver its result unchanged to the selected app target.

Use the existing cross-host header normalization and existing core reply `:meta` trace-elision path. Before trace egress, apply managed HTTP's immutable and app-declared sensitive-header carrier policy so exposing useful headers to app code does not expose `Set-Cookie`, auth tokens, or custom secret headers in traces. Let canned/route stubs opt into the same metadata shape without inventing metadata when it is omitted.

Rewrite the motivating middleware tests so they parse the headers actually emitted by the local server; do not retain hard-coded stand-ins.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1310-1450`: normalized response facts enter `handle-response!`; the success tail passes only `(:accepted outcome)` to `finalise-success!`.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:507-511` and `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:181-189`: success construction takes only the accepted value.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:1191-1239`: the server emits rate-limit headers, lines 1213-1214 admit headers are absent, and lines 1221-1224 hard-code the alleged parse result.
- `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:1280-1313`: the Cache-Control server value is likewise replaced by a hard-coded map at line 1300.
- `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:768,809-814` and `docs/async/http-going-further.md:38-40`: the public contract promises response-header parsing in `:after`.
- Commit `264dc7b352` introduced `:after` and both motivating tests together; blame/history show the stand-ins have not subsequently been replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A successful live JVM request and a successful live CLJS request expose the actual response status, status text, and normalized headers at one documented location in the canonical reply seen by both `:after` and the app reply target; `:value` remains the accepted payload.
- The rate-limit and Cache-Control motivating tests read and parse the local server's real header values. Their assertions fail if those response headers are removed or changed without changing the expected parse.
- Cross-host tests pin the chosen normalized header shape, including a multi-valued header case, rather than introducing a second header representation.
- HTTP canned success and route-map stubs may supply optional response metadata so header-dependent `:after` code is testable without a network; absence remains minimal and does not fabricate lifecycle facts.
- Completion traces continue to use the shared canonical-reply elider, and tests prove built-in `Set-Cookie` plus an app-declared sensitive response-header carrier are redacted while ordinary response headers remain useful on-box. Per-call `:sensitive?` still redacts wire-bearing metadata as specified.
- Spec 014, async/API docs, and managed-HTTP skill/example material document the exact reply shape with one working header-parsing example. Manifest/conformance data is updated only if implementation introduces a new public var (the recommended shape needs none).
- Existing success decode/accept behavior, failure classification, retry, cancellation, frame routing, stale suppression, and reply-target semantics remain green on JVM and CLJS.

## Non-goals

- A Fetch/HttpClient response wrapper or host object in app state.
- New response-header parsing helpers, middleware registries, global mutable policy, or compatibility aliases.
- Upload/download progress, streaming bodies, cookie-jar behavior, or a fully realistic HTTP simulator.
- Duplicating body data or inventing status/headers for stub replies that did not supply them.

## Related beads

No matching current bead was found. Historical source/comments reference `rf2-uheqq` (the `:after` middleware work) and `rf2-ibksxg` (minimal canonical canned replies), but neither ID resolves in the current tracker; they are context, not dependencies.

Drop that surface. Dispatchable solo; owns spec/014 as its hot-zone file.

Trace egress redacts [:meta :headers] denylist ∪ app carriers (new privacy/redact-response-meta); per-call :sensitive? force-redacts :meta wholesale via the existing wire-slot walker. Canned-success + route-map stubs take optional :meta (absent = omitted, never fabricated). Motivating rate-limit/Cache-Control tests now parse the server's real headers. Cross-host shape pinned (set-cookie parity .cljc + live JVM multi-valued test + full-pipeline CLJS test). Spec 014 §Successful-response metadata + async docs updated with a working header-parsing example. No new public var — manifest untouched. Per TRIAGE note, the nonexistent managed-HTTP skill/example surface was dropped. title: surface-review(epoch): make strict replay a one-call epoch-id gesture
description:
## Scope

Close the gap between the epoch runtime's recorded replay material and the public/Tool-Pair replay gesture. Cover the smallest coherent slice across `implementation/epoch/**`, the optional core facade/late-bind hook, Pair-MCP runtime/tool wiring, Tool-Pair/API/spec prose, descriptor manifest, and focused CLJ/CLJS/tool tests.

## Findings

- Every ordinary `:rf/epoch-record` already captures the complete ingredients for a faithful strict replay: `:trigger-event`, the post-generation `:rf.cofx` token (including mid-run minted facts), and the envelope's serializable `:fx-overrides` / `:interceptor-overrides`.
- The normative Tool-Pair replay contract requires replay to re-supply all of those fields and hard-wire `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :strict`; missing facts and `:rf/fn-override` must fail loud.
- No epoch public API or late-bind hook performs that gesture from an epoch id. `re-frame.epoch` exposes history, restore, replace, listeners, config, and egress projection; Pair-MCP exposes `restore-epoch`, while its `dispatch {replay true}` merely sets strict mode and requires the caller to copy the event/cofx/override fields manually.
- That manual route is not generally available to an off-box agent: `projected-record` deliberately replaces every `:trigger-event` argument with `:rf/redacted` by default, and `:include-sensitive?` is orthogonal to `:include-event-args?`. Pair-MCP's epoch egress threads only the app-db `include-sensitive` axis, so `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` cannot return the raw arguments needed to replay a normal argument-bearing event. The remaining escape is raw `eval-cljs` over `rf/epoch-history`, which bypasses the structured privacy and tool envelope.
- Existing replay tests prove the ingredients by hand-extracting a record and calling `rf/dispatch-sync`; none proves that a programmer or tool can name one retained epoch and replay it in one supported call.

## Recommended Action

Provide one dev-only replay-by-epoch-id operation, preferably `replay-epoch!`, owned by the epoch artefact. It should resolve the retained raw record in-process, build the strict dispatch opts from the record in one place, and dispatch the recorded event without exporting its arguments/coeffects/overrides. Make source-frame and target-frame semantics explicit (same frame by default; an optional explicit target only if needed), and make clear that replay runs against the target frame's current state/code unless the caller separately restores a starting epoch.

Expose the operation through the normal optional-artefact facade and as a dedicated Pair-MCP `replay-epoch` tool (or an equally direct epoch-id mode on the existing dispatch tool). Return a structured consequence/failure envelope. Fail before dispatch for an unknown/aged-out id, a non-replayable record (synthetic/halted/missing trigger or replay token), or any recorded `:rf/fn-override`; preserve the existing strict missing-cofx failure rather than minting. Use the existing dispatch authority/annotation posture—do not invent another permission system.

## Evidence

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc` builds `:trigger-event`, post-generation `:rf.cofx`, `:fx-overrides`, and `:interceptor-overrides` into each record specifically for Tool-Pair replay.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` publishes no replay hook or public replay function; its Tool-Pair mutations are restore and replace only.
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` independently redacts trigger-event args; `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc` pins that `:include-sensitive? true` still leaves them redacted unless the separate `:include-event-args?` opt is supplied.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs` threads only `:include-sensitive?` into projected epoch pages and explicitly leaves the orthogonal event-args axis closed.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs` accepts caller-supplied event/cofx/overrides plus `replay true`; it performs no epoch-id lookup. `registry.cljs` and generated `tool-descriptors.edn` contain restore but no replay-by-id tool.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` Replay and `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` Strict replay instruct callers to read and copy the four recorded fields manually.
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`, `epoch_override_capture_test.clj`, `machine_minted_cofx_replay_token_test.clj`, and `join_strict_mint_epoch_replay_test.clj` all demonstrate replay through manual record extraction/re-dispatch.
- `implementation/epoch/deps.edn` confirms epoch is an optional, dev-elided artefact with an existing real production-gate lane; the new seam belongs under that same boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From only a retained epoch id plus explicit frame targeting, a public dev API can replay an ordinary argument-bearing event using the raw in-process `:trigger-event`, recorded `:rf.cofx`, and both recorded override maps under hard-wired `:strict` mint policy.
2. An end-to-end test records a generator-backed/mid-run coeffect and serializable fx/interceptor overrides, then replays by id and proves the generator/host is not consulted and the recorded effective chain is used. Include an event argument that the off-box projected history exposes only as `:rf/redacted`.
3. Pair-MCP offers the same one-call epoch-id gesture without requiring raw event, cofx, or override payloads on the wire; the descriptor, generated manifest, catalogue, and skill routing all agree.
4. Unknown/aged-out ids, halted/synthetic/incomplete records, and `:rf/fn-override` records return stable structured failures and do not dispatch. Missing declared recordable facts remain the canonical strict `:rf.error/missing-required-cofx`; no live mint fallback is introduced.
5. Docs state the state semantics plainly: replay does not implicitly restore, external effects may fire again, the target's current code/frame config applies, and the replayed dispatch records a new ordinary epoch.
6. Existing `projected-record` privacy defaults remain unchanged; no raw event-argument egress knob is added to make replay work.
7. Focused JVM/CLJS epoch tests, Pair-MCP tool tests, descriptor-manifest drift checks, and the existing epoch production-elision lane pass with non-vacuous assertions.

## Non-goals

- A branching timeline, redo stack, or general event-log framework.
- Automatic restore-before-replay or a promise that replay matches the historical `:db-after` when starting state/code differs.
- Replaying opaque fn-valued overrides, virtualising/undoing external effects, or weakening off-box redaction.
- Compatibility aliases, a generic command abstraction, or a second permission/gating system.

## Related beads

No open duplicate was found after title and full-description searches for replay-by-epoch-id, strict replay, trigger-event replay, and `include-event-args`. Historical implementation lineage visible in source/commit history: rf2-1xdotm (post-generation cofx capture), rf2-yigokd (override capture), rf2-v52xsr (strict replay flag), rf2-m7x0qb (Pair-MCP override re-supply), rf2-s3qjlw (epoch/restore strict-replay composition proof), and rf2-nm611o (fail-closed trigger-event args).

title: surface-review(flows): make dynamic flow toggles settle automatically
description:
## Scope

Change the runtime semantics of the existing `:rf.fx/reg-flow` and `:rf.fx/clear-flow` effects so their app-db consequences settle automatically on the dispatching frame. Keep the existing effect ids and 3-slot registration payload. This includes the flows runtime, the core fx/router integration it uses, focused tests/conformance, Spec 013, the API/core guides, and the shipped cart example.

## Verified Findings

- The reserved flow effects run after the event's flow transform. A flow registered by an event therefore has no output until another event drains; a flow cleared by an event leaves its old output in app-db until another event drains.
- The clear case is observably incoherent at the dispatch boundary: the registry row is already gone while the derived value it owned is still present.
- The documented solution makes every caller invent and dispatch a no-op event. The shipped cart defines `:cart/touch` solely for this purpose and emits it after both apply and remove. This is ceremony in the event catalogue, trace stream, tests, docs, and generated code, not application behavior.
- The current tracker contains no open, in-progress, deferred, or closed issue that owns automatic settling for flow lifecycle effects. Spec 013 itself labels synchronous re-walk as an untracked note.

## Recommended Action

After a successful `:rf.fx/reg-flow` or `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, have the runtime request one private, same-frame settling drain for the parent event. Reuse the existing run-to-completion queue and ordinary flow pass: this is the framework performing the exact follow-up drain it currently tells every application to hand-write. Keep one app-db install per individual event; do not re-run flows inline in the original fx walk. The private transport must not become an application-facing event or option.

Make this the only default. Delete the lag workaround contract instead of adding a synchronous variant, a `:settle?` flag, or compatibility behavior.

## Concrete Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:858` through `:869` calls the lag the least-obvious behavior and instructs callers to dispatch a follow-up no-op event.
- `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:1148` through `:1184` proves clear removes the registry entry while leaving `[:wizard :result]` stale until `:touch`; `:1186` through `:1220` locks the registration lag and workaround.
- `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:149` through `:191` spends a full handler plus two extra `:dispatch` pairs on `:cart/touch`, whose only purpose is to cause another flow walk.
- `docs/core/flows.md:299` through `:321`, `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md:153`, `spec/013-Flows.md` under "Sequencing"/"Open questions", and `spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-toggle-via-fx.edn` all publish or pin the same lag.
- Git history shows the behavior was documented rather than removed: `256e6693aa` (rf2-1smwp) added the mid-event signpost, and `16bbd2f349` (rf2-2qd9wp) extended the lag to in-drain clear semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dispatching one event whose only lifecycle action is `:rf.fx/reg-flow` leaves the flow registered and its initial output materialized once the synchronous/run-to-completion dispatch settles, without an app-authored follow-up event.
- Dispatching one event with `:rf.fx/clear-flow` leaves the flow absent, its output path vacated, and existing dependent flows recomputed against that absence by the same settle boundary. The cart's apply/remove actions update `:cart/discount-rate` and `:cart/total` after one user dispatch.
- Automatic settling is frame-correct, uses the normal topo/dirty-check pass, and preserves the one-app-db-install-per-event invariant and existing derive-failure reporting.
- The public effect ids and payloads do not change, and no public settle event, flag, alternate effect, or new lifecycle API is added.
- Focused CLJ and CLJS tests fail under the old lag behavior and pass under the new default. The conformance fixture is flipped from "next app event" to automatic settle.
- The cart deletes `:cart/touch` and both manual settle dispatches. Spec 013, API/core docs, comments, and tests no longer teach or assert a user-authored no-op workaround.

## Non-goals

- Do not perform a second app-db install inside the original event.
- Do not add fixed-point iteration, conditional/liveness policies, a general scheduler abstraction, or a public "run flows now" command.
- Do not redesign the 3-slot `reg-flow` grammar, static boot registration, the optional-artifact boundary, tooling projections, classification, or exact-incarnation machinery in this task.
- Do not preserve the lag behind a compatibility switch; this is pre-alpha.

## Related beads

- No duplicate owner exists in the current 1,060-issue tracker corpus (all statuses searched across title, description, notes, and close reason for the effect ids, lag, no-op follow-up, dynamic toggle, and settle terms).
- Historical rf2-1smwp documented the registration lag; historical rf2-2qd9wp made in-drain clear preserve the same next-drain behavior. They explain the current contract but do not own removing the application workaround.
- Spec 013 "Synchronous re-walk after `:rf.fx/reg-flow`" is explicitly marked post-v1 and untracked. This task takes the smaller route: automate the already-supported follow-up drain rather than re-walk inline.

VERDICT 2026-09-01 AUSEST (worker, PR #8893). NOTE-START-MARKER-KH73V.

per event (Spec 013 Drain integration property 4), and with it the
pending-effect-transform model and the atomic-commit contract. The old fx.cljc

the same thing and all make the same assumption: that closing the lag requires
a SECOND INSTALL inside the registering event. A second EVENT closes it
instead. The `:fx` walk now enqueues one framework-private `[:rf/settle-flows]`
on the dispatching frame, which drains in the same run-to-completion pass. Each
event still installs once; nothing re-runs the transform after `:fx`.

The separation buys a second property the item did not ask for and that an
inline re-walk would have LOST: the failure boundary. A newly registered flow
whose `:derive` throws now aborts the SETTLE, not the registering event, whose
own `:db` write has already committed. An inline re-walk would have made a bad
`:derive` retroactively abort the registration.

ordinary event, so a throw goes through `flows-after-interceptor`'s existing
