structural `:phase` discriminator (`:derive` vs `:output-write`) that

the registrar, not into the EP-0023 image standard registry. It resolves through
the router unresolved-handler seam (new `router/framework-private-handler-metas`,
consulted ahead of the machines actor resolver in `resolve-unhandled`). The
alternative was the `:rf/set-db` template, a private `registrar/register!`, and
it was rejected for the reason the item itself gives: registering it would put a
row into every app event catalogue, tooling projection and generated code, which
merely MOVES the ceremony from the app into the framework instead of deleting
it. The seam also removes the need for an image-standard registration, since a
generation-routed `registrar/lookup` returns nil for an unregistered id and
falls through to it. It is still listed in `events/reserved-event-ids`, for a
different reason than `:rf/set-db` is: the registrar is consulted BEFORE the
seam, so an app `(reg-event :rf/settle-flows ...)` would silently shadow the
settle and strand every lifecycle effect.

THE CART NO-OP IS GONE. `:cart/touch` and both manual settle dispatches are

It now registers its own local no-op, since it is testing the reload seam and

MECHANISM CHOSEN: an envelope flag the router head-inserts on.
:rf.flow/settle? rides the envelope (set by fx/settle-flows-if-requested!

INCIDENTAL SIMPLIFICATION, not scope creep. The queue-ordering rule was written

title: surface-review(hicasso): reduce the clj-kondo export to macro-shape analysis
description:
## Scope

Reduce Hicasso's shipped clj-kondo integration to the part that materially improves ordinary authoring: correct analysis of `h/defview`, `h/event`, and `h/defhost` as macro shapes. The scope is the export under `implementation/hicasso/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2-hicasso/`, its fixtures/checker under `implementation/hicasso/`, the `test:hicasso-lint` scheduling references, and live package/user/example prose that promises the six custom findings.

Preserve the export's classpath/package delivery. Do not change Hicasso runtime semantics or the public authoring API.

## Findings

The useful editor contract and the accidental apparatus are currently fused in one 847-line hook. The three rewrites make normal clj-kondo analysis understand view names, destructured props, callback bindings/arity, and host option references. That is high-value, general-purpose assistance.

The other half is a bespoke behavioral linter: two custom errors and four custom warnings, plus Hiccup walkers, symbol resolution, a hand-maintained lexical-scope grammar, exact-row fixture matrices, and a mutation-testing gate. Across the hook, README, config, two fixtures, and checker this surface is 2,400 lines. It also owns a required CI lane and a fast-PR step.

That analyzer has already demonstrated the wrong maintenance shape for a trust-the-programmer library. The ERROR-level `direct-view-call` rule repeatedly blocked valid code because a hook has no scope table: parameters and `let` bindings, multi-arity `letfn`, six more binding forms, `areduce`/`amap`, and method-spec grammar each required repair. The same shadowing blindness then spread to the read warnings. The current hook documents a finite roster and still tells authors to rename a legal local or disable the rule for forms outside it.

The payoff remains intrinsically narrow. The direct-call check can see only a view calling itself, not the ordinary cross-view mistake. The function-head check can see literals, not symbols. The key rule deliberately misses the common dynamic-props spelling. The a11y rule cannot see tree-level naming. The deferred-read warning explicitly admits legal synchronous callbacks can trigger it. These limits are honest, but they mean substantial custom machinery protects a small, non-authoritative slice while the actual runtime, React, and Hicasso test kit already own the relevant behavior.

For a pre-alpha surface, carrying this analyzer is worse than teaching the small set of authoring laws clearly and keeping the real failures loud at their execution boundary. It increases contributor and AI context, creates a second grammar that must track Clojure/CLJS binding forms, and turns lint maintenance into product work without making the core SPA API more expressive.

## Recommended Action

Keep the published clj-kondo export, but reduce it to the shortest honest implementation of these three shapes:

- `defview` is analyzed as a definition with its one props vector and body;
- `event` is analyzed as a function with its argument vector and body;
- `defhost` defines its name and analyzes the component/options expressions.

Delete the six `:re-frame.hicasso/*` behavioral findings, their Hiccup/scope walkers, the positive/negative behavioral matrices, and the mutation framework built to keep that custom analyzer correct. Replace the dedicated behavioral gate with one small consumer smoke, preferably folded into an existing package/lint lane, that imports the export through the artifact classpath and proves ordinary clj-kondo analysis sees the three macro shapes. Remove stale live claims and scheduling apparatus. Do not replace the deleted checks with compiler analysis, cache-backed namespace analysis, a new warning framework, or a compatibility layer.

title: client-root adoption: canonical skills and the pair fixture still own raw Reagent roots
description:
## Scope

The stock Reagent adapter's browser-root surface: `implementation/adapters/reagent/**`, the shared ratom-spine root machinery only where needed, the Spec 006/public API contract, and the Reagent boot paths in the canonical guide, adapter testbed, examples, and generated templates. Preserve the canonical-namespace parity promised by the published full and slim Reagent artefacts.

## Verified Findings

- `re-frame.adapter.reagent` exposes exactly `adapter`, `flush-views!`, and `set-hiccup-emitter!`; there is no app-facing mount/root lifecycle. Spec 006 nevertheless calls adapter `:render` the client-side mount entry point, and core implements it only at `re-frame.substrate.adapter/render`, not on the documented front porch.
- The ratom spine already does the hard work: first render can call `create-root` or `hydrate-root`, it tracks the resulting React Root, and adapter disposal drains tracked roots. But the operation returns only an unmount thunk. It cannot render a new tree through that same root, so it cannot express the ordinary Shadow hot-reload loop.
- Consequently, normal applications bypass the adapter lifecycle. The boot guide, generated Reagent templates, examples, and the adapter's own browser testbed each retain a raw React Root and call `reagent.dom.client` directly. Those roots are invisible to `destroy-adapter!`, and every caller must independently get create-once, hydrate-once, rerender, and teardown ordering right.
- The SSR template makes the missing operation especially clear: `init` chooses `hydrate-root` versus `create-root`, stores the raw root, and its `^:dev/after-load` hook later calls `rdc/render` on that root. The existing one-shot adapter entry cannot replace this correct hot-reload shape.
- Spec 006 requires the returned unmount function to be idempotent, but `track-active-root!` removes the root from its set and invokes the underlying unmount operation on every call; a second call reaches React again.

## Recommended Action

Give the canonical Reagent adapter namespace one small, explicit, reusable client-root lifecycle. A caller should be able to allocate an inert root handle at namespace load, render through it repeatedly, and unmount it explicitly:

1. the first render creates or hydrates exactly one React Root from the supplied mount point and options;
2. later renders update that same Root, which makes the same call usable from `^:dev/after-load` without caller-owned raw React state;
3. explicit unmount is idempotent, and `destroy-adapter!` releases a still-live root exactly once;
4. the raw React Root remains private to the adapter.

Back the handle with the existing active-root ownership rather than adding a second lifecycle. Keep the handle caller-owned and explicit; do not introduce a process-global mount-point registry. Name the operations plainly and document the tiny boot recipe. Full Reagent and the published slim variant must present the same canonical namespace surface.

Migrate the canonical guide, generated Reagent templates (including SSR), the adapter browser testbed, and ordinary Reagent example entrypoints to this lifecycle. After the sweep, direct `reagent.dom.client` root bookkeeping should remain only in the adapter implementation, focused lower-level DOM tests, or integrations that intentionally own a foreign React root.

## Evidence

- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.reagent.md` says requiring the namespace gives exactly three things and documents no mount operation.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:227-239` defines `(render render-tree mount-point opts) -> unmount-fn` as the client mount contract and requires idempotent unmount.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:605-613` implements the entry only in the substrate namespace; no `re-frame.core` export exists.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3432-3448` creates/hydrates and tracks a Root but exposes only the unmount thunk. `:987-1000` shows that thunk calls the underlying unmount on every invocation.
- `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:39-60` teaches `defonce react-root`, `rdc/create-root`, and `rdc/render`.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:41-49` repeats that bookkeeping. `_reagent/core_with_ssr.cljc:146-162,183-209` stores a raw hydrated/created root specifically so hot reload can rerender it.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/testbed/adapter_testbed_reagent/core.cljs:57-72` bypasses adapter `:render` in the adapter's own end-to-end mount smoke.
- A repository census finds 30 files under `examples/` and `tools/template/resources/` containing `rdc/create-root`.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn` deliberately keeps Reagent 2.0.1 in the adapter artefact and out of core, so the Reagent-specific handle belongs at the adapter boundary without adding a Reagent dependency to core.
- History shows the split accreting: `16ec884492` established the one-shot create-root/render/unmount adapter path; `cd6cf3ebf8` added adapter-owned root draining; `9cf8f2e54c` fixed generated-app hot reload by rerendering caller-owned raw roots instead of extending the adapter surface.
- Duplicate search: `bd search` over `reagent mount`, `client mount`, `root lifecycle`, `adapter-owned root`, `create-root`, `rerender root`, and `reusable root` found no matching open or closed task for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical Reagent adapter API provides a documented caller-owned client-root handle (or an equivalently small explicit lifecycle) that performs no DOM work when constructed.
- Browser contract tests prove: a cold first render calls `create-root` once; a hydrating first render calls `hydrate-root` once; two or more later renders reuse the identical Root and call neither constructor again; a hydrated root is updated with normal render rather than hydrated again.
- Calling explicit unmount more than once invokes the underlying React unmount once. Destroying the adapter releases every still-live handle once, while an already-unmounted handle is not released again.
- Normal boot requires no caller-owned raw React Root or create/hydrate branch. The core boot guide, adapter testbed, generated Reagent templates, and ordinary Reagent example entrypoints use the canonical lifecycle; the SSR template still hydrates exactly once and hot reload still rerenders without reseeding app state.
- The full and published slim Reagent variants expose the same canonical namespace API and behavior; public API docs and Spec 006 describe ownership, update, hydration, and teardown semantics.
- Focused low-level tests and deliberate foreign-root integrations may keep direct `reagent.dom.client` calls, but remaining occurrences are reviewed and explicitly outside the normal app boot path.

## Non-goals

- No implicit default adapter, implicit frame creation, automatic DOM-id lookup, or auto-mount on namespace load.
- No process-global root registry and no exposure of the substrate's raw React Root.
- No Reagent 1 or React 17/18 compatibility path.
- No redesign of `reg-view`, Form-3 component authoring, subscriptions, or render-flush helpers.
- No requirement to rewrite focused DOM tests whose subject is raw React/Reagent behavior.

## Related beads

- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed) fixed Shadow hot reload by adding `^:dev/after-load` rerenders; this task keeps that behavior while moving root ownership behind the adapter.

title: surface-review(schemas): elide Malli's dev-only humanizer from production bundles
description:
## Scope

Review and tighten the production bundle boundary of the shipped `implementation/schemas` artifact: its Malli adapter, late-bind integration with core, advanced-build A/B gate, JVM/CLJS diagnostic tests, package manifest, spec/API/how-to text, and examples that intentionally use Malli directly.

## Verified Findings

- Loading the public `re-frame.schemas` facade transitively loads `re-frame.schemas.malli`. That adapter unconditionally requires `malli.error` and publishes `malli.error/humanize` under `:schemas/humanize-explain!`, alongside the always-needed Malli validate/explain hooks.
- The humanizer has no production runtime consumer in the shipped schemas/core path. `validate.cljc` consults it only to enrich `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` dev traces with `:explain-humanized`; those emit paths are behind `interop/debug-enabled?` and are DCE-elided for advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` builds. The always-on production boundary record is deliberately structural-only and omits Malli explanation/humanization.
- The matched advanced A/B bundle report records a 41,570-byte gzip schemas margin (40.6 KB) and attributes 12.0 KB of post-Closure optimized code to `malli.error` (about 6 KB gzip in the spec's dependency guidance). Spec 010 explicitly calls this a measured exception to its own dev/test-only guidance for `malli.error`.
- Existing JVM tests pin useful development behavior, including real `:explain-humanized` payloads and symmetric redaction for sensitive values. The bundle gate bounds total margin but does not assert that the dev-only humanizer is unreachable in production.
- `implementation/schemas/deps.edn` correctly keeps Malli as the artifact's default validator dependency; this finding is about separating Malli core validation from Malli error presentation, not removing the default validator.
- The login example directly requires and calls `malli.error` for application form UX. That explicit consumer should continue paying for it; it does not justify making every schemas consumer pay through the adapter's dev-only hook.

## Recommended Action

Make publication/reachability of `:schemas/humanize-explain!` debug-only and Closure-DCE-safe in the Malli adapter while leaving `malli.core/validate` and `malli.core/explain` wired automatically in every build. Keep the public require/API unchanged. Extend the matched production build proof so it demonstrates that `malli.error` is absent from the schemas probe unless application code directly requires/uses it, then remeasure and update the two-sided bundle budget and documentation from that result.

## Evidence

- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/malli.cljc:34,54` — unconditional `malli.error` require and ns-load publication.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:305-322,548-554,839-859` — the only in-artifact humanizer reads feed dev diagnostic tags.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc` and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` — always-on boundary validation/rejection does not require a humanized payload; production reporting is structural.
- `implementation/scripts/check-schemas-bundle.cjs:36-57,126` — matched advanced control/probe, current 41,570-byte gzip margin, and `malli.error` attribution.
- `spec/010-Schemas.md:279-291,723-745` — humanization is documented as production-elided while `malli.error` is simultaneously recorded as production-reachable.
- `docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:236` and `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:272` — development diagnostic and redaction contracts.
- `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_sensitive_test.clj:1652-1770` — humanized-payload and privacy coverage to preserve.
- `implementation/schemas/deps.edn:32-34` — package boundary and default Malli dependency.
- `examples/core/login/model.cljs` — deliberate direct application use of `malli.error`, which remains outside adapter elision.
- Relevant history: `0702449fe7`, `967fd3de95`, and `81e5b2051c` established/attributed the current matched bundle budget rather than removing this reachability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Requiring `re-frame.schemas` still installs the default Malli validate/explain behavior without an extra application require in development and production; schema-implies-validation and core production-boundary behavior remain green.
- Development JVM and CLJS coverage proves failures still carry useful `:explain-humanized` data, and sensitive failures still redact raw and humanized explanations symmetrically.
- An advanced `goog.DEBUG=false` matched control/probe build proves the schemas adapter no longer retains `malli.error`; an application probe that directly uses `malli.error/humanize` still retains and works with it.
- The matched gzip margin drops measurably from the recorded 41,570 bytes. The checked-in baseline/two-sided band is re-derived from clean repeated measurements and retains its non-vacuity controls.
- Public namespace/import ergonomics and schema registration/validation semantics do not change.
- Spec 010, API/how-to material, adapter docstrings, and bundle attribution describe the resulting dev-versus-production boundary consistently.

## Non-goals

- Removing Malli or making users manually install the default validator.
- Changing schema registration, validation, recovery, privacy, or production boundary semantics.
- Preventing applications from directly requiring/using `malli.error` for product UI.
- Adding a dynamic loader, a new public configuration switch, compatibility aliases, or speculative runtime guards.
- Broadly optimizing Malli internals or unrelated schemas code.

## Related beads

- Historical/landed context: `rf2-v96fh` (schema implies validation), `rf2-kybsf` / `rf2-v4o7e` (schemas bundle attribution/gate), `rf2-2ek7t` / `rf2-qhq3f` (humanized diagnostics and redaction).
- Live tracker duplicate search on 2026-08-30 for schemas bundle, `malli.error`, `humanize-explain`, and production humanization found no owning issue.

title: surface-review(machines): make pure transition results self-describing
description:
## Scope

Redesign the application-facing result contract of re-frame.machines/machine-transition, together with its normative spec, generated API projection, guides, executable examples, manifest coverage, and focused JVM/CLJS tests. Keep runtime transition semantics and the event/effect model unchanged.

## Findings

machine-transition is presented as the simple, pure way to test a machine, but the facade currently aliases the engine function directly and leaks the re-frame.machines.result representation. Callers must require a second namespace, learn either result/ok?, result/snap, result/fx, and result/info or opaque namespaced keys (::tag, ::snap, ::fx, ::info), and reconcile documentation that calls those keys public with a namespace docstring that calls the namespace internal. This makes the most important testing seam less obvious to programmers and harder for AI tools to infer or generate correctly.

The public API manifest inventories re-frame.machines/machine-transition but does not inventory re-frame.machines.result, while the tutorial, inspection guide, API page, normative spec, and executable walkthrough all require that omitted namespace. The result representation is therefore public in practice but private-looking and absent from the authoritative public surface.

## Recommended Action

Make a clean pre-alpha break: have the public re-frame.machines/machine-transition return one transparent, self-describing ordinary map owned by the facade. A suitable contract is success {:status :ok, :snapshot snapshot, :fx [...]} and engine-reported failure {:status :error, :error diagnostic}; settle the exact spellings once in the normative spec and use them everywhere. Application code and tests should need only re-frame.machines.

Remove re-frame.machines.result from application-facing docs and examples. Delete it if the engine no longer needs it, or keep an internal representation genuinely private and normalize only at the facade boundary. Do not retain aliases, tombstones, dual shapes, or compatibility adapters.

## Evidence

- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:103 exports machine-transition as a direct alias of engine/machine-transition, so the engine representation becomes the public representation.
- implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/result.cljc:6-20 defines the ::tag/::snap/::fx/::info map and labels three keys public, while lines 43-45 describe the namespace as internal to the machines artefact.
- docs/machines/tutorial.md:320-348 and docs/machines/inspecting-machines.md:128-166 teach a second re-frame.machines.result require plus accessors solely to inspect a pure transition.
- docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:143-164 and spec/API.md:936 name re-frame.machines.result/Result as the public return type.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/examples_test.clj:867-888 imports re-frame.machines.result and destructures ::result/snap and ::result/fx in the executable public walkthrough.
- spec/api-manifest.edn contains the machine-transition row but no re-frame.machines.result rows; implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:88-111 introspects re-frame.machines but not the result namespace.
- A repository-wide search finds 45 files requiring re-frame.machines.result and 43 files consuming its accessors or namespaced keys, so this is established cross-cutting friction rather than a single stale example.
- History introduced the Result ADT and accessors in commits 964e08dc16 and 742e30bd97 on 2026-05-14. The source comment records public-key churn as the reason not to use a record; in the current pre-alpha phase that compatibility concern should not dictate a permanently awkward public seam.
- Exact tracker searches for machine-transition, re-frame.machines.result, transition result, result ADT, pure transition, machine testing, state machine testing, and machines API found no existing issue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The normative machine spec defines one exact, self-describing public return shape for successful and engine-reported failed pure transitions, including snapshot, ordered effects, and diagnostic data.
- re-frame.machines/machine-transition implements that contract without requiring consumers to know an internal namespace or qualified implementation keys.
- Existing semantics remain covered: successful snapshots and effect order are unchanged; thrown action/guard failures and depth-abort failures remain atomic and diagnostic; programmer-input errors that intentionally throw have a clearly documented boundary.
- Focused JVM and CLJS machine tests, conformance fixtures, and executable examples assert the public shape through re-frame.machines only.
- Spec 005, spec/API.md, docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, the tutorial, inspection guide, and state-machine walkthrough all use the same contract and no longer teach re-frame.machines.result.
- The API manifest/generator and drift checks accurately describe the resulting public surface; no public namespace used by the docs is omitted from that surface.
- The old application-facing Result accessors and key shape are removed in the same change, with no compatibility layer.

## Non-goals

- Changing statechart syntax, transition selection, hierarchy, action execution, effect ordering, dispatch, timers, actor ownership, or spawn semantics.
- Designing a model-based testing DSL, matcher library, or new helper namespace.
- Redesigning the broader exception taxonomy beyond documenting the existing programmer-error boundary.
- Solving eager singleton startup or synthetic start-event ergonomics.
- Preserving the old Result shape for compatibility.

## Related beads

- rf2-ys42 (closed) corrected and expanded the machines tutorial/testing documentation; it exposes this seam but did not redesign it.
- rf2-npgc (closed) restructured the machines guide and added inspecting-machines.md; it is documentation context, not duplicate implementation work.
- rf2-cnij (closed) improved facade docstrings and API notes; it did not cover the pure transition result contract.
- No open, in-progress, deferred, or closed bead matching this result-contract outcome was found.

title: surface-review(core): remove implementation-only constructors from re-frame.core
description:
## Scope

Make the `re-frame.core` facade expose the supported authoring surfaces, not the implementation-only lowering constructors behind them. Remove `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`, `re-frame.core/->interceptor`, and `re-frame.core/->interceptor*` from the public facade; relocate or delete their lowering entry points as appropriate, and update the macro/runtime consumers that legitimately need them. Keep `re-frame.core/capture-frame` and `re-frame.core/reg-interceptor` as the app-facing paths.

## Independently verified Findings

- The accepted pre-alpha facade rule says internalising an export must remove it from the facade, manifest, and current API projection; a docstring saying “internal” while `:facade? true` remains is named as the precise failure mode (`spec/Conventions.md`, “Removing or demoting a facade export — delete, don't demote”).
- That exact failure is live. `make-capture-frame` and `->interceptor` are `:tier :implementation` plus `:facade? true`; `->interceptor*` is `:tier :advanced` plus `:facade? true` even though its status and docs say “internal lowering only”. All three appear in generated `docs/api/re-frame.core.md`.
- The exposure is plumbing, not an app capability. `reg-view` expands through `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`; the interceptor macro expands through `re-frame.core/->interceptor*`; the owned runtime constructor already exists as `re-frame.interceptor/->interceptor*`. A compiler-visible Var need not live on the user facade.
- SCI copies every public runtime Var from `re-frame.core`, so the accidental surface is also presented to playground users and AI-generated examples.
- The earlier API-shrink commit `ca1fa564da` declared `capture-frame` the one public carry primitive but retiered `make-capture-frame` instead of removing it. The same repository conventions explicitly reject annotation as removal.
- The conventions say a public-facade manifest-hygiene CI check enforces this disposition, but `.github/workflows/lint.yml` records that the old check was retired. Current manifest generation accepts the contradictory rows, so the same drift can recur.

## Recommended Action

Move the capture-frame and interceptor lowering seams behind explicitly non-facade implementation namespaces (or delete a wrapper where the owning constructor already suffices). Repoint `reg-view` and interceptor macro expansion, internal/test consumers, and SCI bindings to those owned seams. Remove the three facade Vars and their manifest/API entries without compatibility aliases. Add a small generic manifest invariant that rejects implementation-only rows exported with `:facade? true`, so an internal docstring/status cannot masquerade as surface removal again.

## Evidence

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1369` — `make-capture-frame` says it is internal and public only for macro expansion; `capture-frame` begins at line 1453.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2137` — `->interceptor` says it is an internal lowering constructor and directs apps to `reg-interceptor`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:187` — emitted code calls `re-frame.core/make-capture-frame`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_call_site_macros.cljc:173-179` — emitted code calls `re-frame.core/->interceptor*`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:23` — the owned `->interceptor*` constructor already exists.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn:69-70,74,118` — the three internal constructors are facade rows beside the front-porch `capture-frame` row.
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:635-668` — metadata acknowledges the internal-only dispositions while retaining facade placement.
- `spec/Conventions.md:1235-1250` — pre-alpha delete-not-demote rule and its stated manifest guardrail.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:1471` — `capture-frame` is the one public carry primitive and `make-capture-frame` is not app API.
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:475-483,556-571` — generated public API publishes the internal constructors.
- `docs/tools/playground/sci/src/rf2_playground/sci.cljs:156,165-188` — SCI macro expansion names `make-capture-frame` and `copy-ns` exposes all public core runtime Vars.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/reg_view_injection_test.clj:298` and `implementation/core/test/re_frame/interceptor_runtime_complete_cljs_test.cljc` — tests currently pin the facade plumbing rather than its absence.
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml:627-637` — manifest checks remain, but the former facade-hygiene check is explicitly retired.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `re-frame.core` no longer resolves or documents `make-capture-frame`, `->interceptor`, or `->interceptor*` in either CLJ or CLJS, and none has a `:facade? true` manifest row.
2. `reg-view` expansion and internal interceptor construction use owned non-facade symbols; compilation, source-coordinate stamping/elision, and advanced-build behavior remain intact.
3. `capture-frame` remains the single supported carry primitive, preserving frame-incarnation fencing and injected dispatch/subscribe behavior; `reg-interceptor` remains the supported interceptor authoring form.
4. Playground SCI still supports `reg-view`, `capture-frame`, and registered interceptors without copying the removed runtime aliases into `re-frame.core`.
5. Focused tests assert both behavioral preservation and facade absence in CLJ/CLJS. Generated API/manifest projections and affected specs/docs agree with the resulting surface.
6. A generic automated check fails on a planted manifest row that combines an implementation-only disposition with `:facade? true`, and passes after the plant is removed.

## Non-goals

- No broad reclassification of the rest of `re-frame.core`, Story, or Xray.
- No redesign of capture-frame lifecycle semantics, interceptor descriptors, registration, or source-coordinate diagnostics.
- No compatibility aliases, deprecation tier, tombstones, or new public sugar; this is pre-alpha surface correction.
- No change to the public names or signatures of `capture-frame` or `reg-interceptor`.

## Related existing beads

- `rf2-2hpxo` (P3, deferred) is the broad retrospective facade-export classification sweep for external-alpha prep. This task does not duplicate it: these three exports are already classified and documented as implementation-only; the work here is to execute those settled dispositions and restore a regression check.

title: surface-review(uix-adapter): make a real UIx component test copy-pasteable and executable
description:
## Scope

Make the consumer-facing UIx component-testing path runnable from the public docs and easy to copy into a real app. Use the adapter's existing UIx/React primitives; cover the smallest honest real-DOM loop (mount a hook component under `frame-root`, drive an event, settle with `flush-views!`, assert the DOM, and tear everything down). Keep the executable witness close enough to the docs or generated scaffold that drift is caught.

## Verified Findings

- The UIx runtime surface is already substantial and well covered: `spec/api-manifest.edn:60-68` rows all nine public adapter Vars, and the adapter forwards a large shared React regression suite. This is not a request to redesign `use-subscribe`, `use-frame`, or frame scoping.
- The main view-testing guide is not substrate-neutral in practice. `docs/core/testing/views.md:5` says a view is a callable pure function returning hiccup and builds the whole recipe around JVM tree walking. A UIx `defui` that calls `use-subscribe` / `use-frame` is a React hook component and cannot use that recipe. The page's only UIx-relevant escape at line 93 says to use a real DOM and `flush-views!`, but supplies no mount, fixture, event, assertion, or cleanup shape.
- UIx's own public docs stop at the settling primitive: `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`, `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`, and `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:17` show `flush-views!` but no complete component test.
- The generated UIx app does not fill the gap. `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309` emits only `events_test.cljs`; `_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24` explicitly runs DOM-free against a headless adapter. That is good dataflow coverage, but it teaches nothing about testing the UIx view the scaffold just generated.
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128` explicitly makes Test-React local-only, React-free, DOM-free, opaque-tree, and non-reconciling. It therefore cannot execute UIx hooks and is not a missing consumer test kit to point at.
- The desired flow already exists as framework evidence: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` plus `testbed/spec.cjs` prove frame-root mount -> use-subscribe -> click/dispatch -> DOM rerender in a real browser. Commit `2d2f4aff53` introduced the per-adapter testbed; commit `b924dca1af` introduced the current hiccup-centric Test-a-view recipe. The missing work is to turn those two disconnected bodies of knowledge into one consumer-shaped, executable UIx recipe.

## Recommended Action

Publish one canonical, copy-complete UIx component test using existing APIs only. Put the explanation where a test author looks (`docs/core/testing/views.md` and the UIx adapter docs), point the generated UIx README at it, and back the exact shape with a focused browser-lane test or other named executable witness. Prefer a small fixture/helper local to the example over a new framework abstraction. The recipe should make lifecycle ownership obvious: one mount node/root, `frame-root` (or an explicitly created/scoped frame), a real DOM interaction, `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, an assertion, and guaranteed unmount/runtime cleanup.

## Concrete Evidence

- `docs/core/testing/views.md:5,93`
- `spec/008-Testing.md:36-48,107` (defines `flush-views!` and marks real React mounting CLJS-only, but illustrates only the Reagent call)
- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:178-191`
- `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:263,273`
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/root/README.md:272-274,309`
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_shared/events_test.cljs:5-7,24`
- `implementation/adapters/test-react/README.md:3,7,123-128`
- `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` and `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/spec.cjs`
- History: `2d2f4aff53` (adapter testbeds), `b924dca1af` (Test-a-view recipe), `9cf8f2e54c` (generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A copy-complete CLJS UIx test mounts a `defui` that uses `use-subscribe` and/or `use-frame` under a valid frame boundary, drives a real DOM event, settles through `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, observes the updated DOM, and guarantees unmount plus frame/adapter cleanup.
2. The published command for that test runs successfully in a named browser/DOM-capable lane; a focused executable test protects the recipe from API or lifecycle drift.
3. `docs/core/testing/views.md` explicitly distinguishes its fast hiccup-walk path from UIx hook components and links the runnable UIx recipe rather than implying the hiccup recipe applies.
4. The UIx adapter README/API and generated UIx project README make the first component-test path discoverable; the scaffold's existing DOM-free event/sub tests remain the recommended default for business logic.
5. The solution uses current public primitives. No new public helper namespace/API is added unless implementing the executable recipe demonstrates unavoidable repeated lifecycle machinery.

## Non-goals

- Do not publish or expand the internal Test-React adapter; it deliberately models class-3 lifecycle without React and cannot be made into UIx by adding shims.
- Do not build a Testing Library clone, add speculative compatibility layers, or create a full per-adapter test matrix.
- Do not change UIx hook signatures, frame semantics, adapter installation semantics, or the substrate contract.
- Do not require every generated project to run a browser suite by default if a documented, executable opt-in recipe gives the same low-friction path.

## Related beads

- `rf2-0c23j` (closed): ruled the `flush-views!` test door and documented its render-phase constraint.
- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed): repaired the generated UIx mount/hot-reload lifecycle; its one-root/after-load shape is the right lifecycle donor.
- `rf2-60aoj` (closed): established that Test-React intentionally omits React render flushing and is a different capability, not the UIx test path.

No matching open or closed bead was found by title searches for UIx testing/component tests and description searches across `uix`, `test-react`, `flush-views!`, `real DOM`, and `component test`.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, copy-complete UIx browser component test mounts a hook component under a frame boundary, drives a real event, settles with `uix-adapter/flush-views!`, asserts updated DOM, and guarantees cleanup; the exact recipe is executable in a named gate, is linked from the UIx adapter and generated-project docs, and the generic view-testing guide clearly routes UIx hook components to it. Existing public primitives are used unless the executable proof shows a helper is truly necessary.

Both successful paths finish with the flag forced to true; the async path also forces it false during polling. In a copied test suite this changes React act-warning/flush behaviour for later tests according to execution order, contradicting the page's copy-complete and unconditional-teardown promise. The shared React suite already demonstrates the bounded discipline at react_shared_suite.cljs:3280-3351: capture the previous value, use the required temporary state, restore it in guaranteed final cleanup. Apply that discipline locally to this recipe and its pinned docs block, preserving the false polling window and unconditional unmount; no public helper, abstraction, or broader test-harness redesign is owed. Completeness otherwise passes: browser execution, page/file byte pin, adapter/template pointers, fixture ownership, real click, bounded settle, and named gates are present.

Premise verified at tip (set! at :61 and :155, no capture/restore). Bounded per the audit note; in-test restore assertion added as the durable control. Worker closes on PR-ready.
AUDIT PR #8798 (2026-08-31): REOPENED. The success-path value restoration works, but it is not failure-safe. mount! sets the global before flush-views! and returns cleanup ownership only afterward; if render or act throws, no mounted token exists and the prior flag is lost. unmount! restores only after flush-views! and node.remove, so an unmount or effect-cleanup throw skips the flag restore and, in the async .finally callback, done. This contradicts the copy-complete unconditional-teardown and exactly-as-found contract and does not carry the donor final-cleanup discipline. title: hicasso defhost: infer the callback contract by position, keep :callbacks as a 2-value override, delete :handler (executes ruling rf2-6c12m.2)

This description is the condensed DO.

THE RULE: a defhost or [:>] callback contract is inferred from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (intent.cljs:1200-1210 position-contract; intent.cljs:1212-1228 lower-prop): on*-spelled -> :event, any other walked prop -> :render, :ref -> React's, declared :slots -> markup. :callbacks survives ONLY as an optional override {<prop> :event|:render} written where inference is wrong (on*-named render props: Fluent onRenderItem/onRenderCell, Ant onRow/onCell/onFilter); a declared contract outranks the spelling. :handler is DELETED (a plain fn is the handler contract and already crosses untouched at every position - intent.cljs:1225,1228; codec.cljs:2865). A vector or map at a render position (inferred or overridden) crosses as data via host-prop-value, as at a native tag. An h/event at a declared :slots position stays refused.

CODE: host-entry (codec.cljs:3040-3111) :else arm -> reuse intent/lower-prop for the event/render inference, then host-prop-value; NO second classifier, warning, or compat layer. lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1255-1302) keeps :event and :render arms, drops :handler; non-callback values at :render route through host-prop-value. Delete callback-contracts (codec.cljs:1328), the :callbacks validation arms of mint-host! (codec.cljs:1538-2053), refuse-undeclared-host-event! (:2870-2897), refuse-dispatching-carrier! (intent.cljs:1230-1253), the false branch of refuse-unclaimed-host-callback! (:2899-2954, call site :3105-3106; KEEP the node-slot? branch, :3079-3080). title: hicasso: coalesce the reaper timers - one armed timer per horizon per turn, not one per cell and per entry
description:
arm-cell-reaper! arms a 0 ms setTimeout per cell that hits zero readers (collector.cljs:625-634, from release-cell! :968); arm-entry-reaper! arms a 4 ms timer per entry at mint (:1403) AND at last unsubscribe (:1488). A cold mount of N distinct-read boundaries arms N timers during render; unmounting N rows arms up to 2N. Each timer is a heap allocation plus a scheduler entry - on the 300-row rung the runtime is tuned for, that is hundreds of timers per turn. The coalescing primitive already exists in the file (!deferred + one timer, :1040-1045).

DO: one pending array per horizon (0 ms cells, 4 ms entries) and at most one armed timer per horizon per turn; drain in a loop; semantics unchanged (a reaper still runs strictly past its horizon; quiesced! still settles past entry-reap-horizon-ms). title: RULING: src is 71% prose - docstring = contract plus one sentence of why; the essays move to docs/design/hicasso
description:
src/ is 17,113 lines of which ~12,000 are docstrings and comments (approx: codec.cljs 67%, collector.cljs 74%, controlled.cljs 78%, hicasso.cljc 87%, mount.cljs 76%). impl/ alone: 11,693 lines = 2,788 code + 7,207 docstring + 1,219 comment (72% prose). collector.cljs opens with a 393-line docstring before its first require; controlled.cljs is 688 doc lines for 155 of code; generation.cljs 102 doc lines for 26 of code. Docstrings cross-reference three others, so editing one mechanism means re-reading the essay on all of them, and finding flush! means scrolling ~1,000 lines. This is the shape problem underneath the rest of the review: nothing is short enough to be seen whole, which is why the dead weight survived, and it is why every rename is a multi-file multi-paragraph edit. docs/design/hicasso (146 files) already exists and is where HD-numbered rulings, measurement tables and rejected alternatives belong.

RECOMMENDATION: per file, docstring = what it is/returns, the contract, and one sentence of why (with a link to the design record for the argument); move measurement tables, rejected designs and ruling citations to docs/design/hicasso. Target roughly 1:1 prose:code. Best done per file alongside the cut tasks in this epic so the prose is trimmed once, after the code it describes has settled. This reverses the direction of PR #8736 (which polished the prose in place); that PR is not wasted - the survivors will be the timeless versions - but Mike should rule before a second prose pass starts.

WHAT THE ADDED REVIEW SAID AND HOW IT WAS WEIGHED. After filing, the dossier gained an independent second review ("Codex Recommendation"). It concurs with A and amends it in five ways. All five are adopted, one with a bound:
(1) A content rule, not a line-count regime: no 1:1 enforcement, no 40-line cap, no docstring-link checker, no migration machinery. Adopted. The bead's "roughly 1:1 prose:code" is the expected OUTCOME of applying the rule, not a threshold a reviewer applies.
(2) Move only durable design reasoning; DELETE duplicated, superseded and journey prose rather than preserving it ceremonially. Adopted, with a bound: the dossier's own sample found about half the essay material already on a design page, so moving it would write it twice; but the PR body still names each deleted essay and where its surviving copy is, so nothing goes silently.
(3) A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit. The epoch-floor proof beside flush! and the rf2-6c12m.19 counter-example on commit-basis are such proofs and stay; module history, benchmark narrative and repeated cross-module explanation go. Adopted.
(4) A public docstring carries the smallest complete contract a caller needs (inputs, outputs, effects, ordering, failure behaviour) plus an example only where it removes real ambiguity; a private docstring says what the var does and the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape. Adopted - it is the dossier's rule with the public/private line made explicit.
(5) One small cleanup pass over untouched files when the wave is done. Adopted as the follow-up bead.
Its lexical scan read 75.8% prose against the dossier's 72%; the methods differ on ^{:doc} metadata and comment classification, both agree the shape is about three prose lines per line of code, and the ruling does not turn on which figure is right. The one material risk it names - over-trimming caller-facing facts into the unpublished design tree - is why the public-contract clause below is stated in full rather than left to taste.

THE RULE (binding on every PR that edits a docstring or comment under implementation/hicasso/src from now on):
1. A docstring carries: (a) what the var is or returns; (b) the contract - what it takes, returns and promises, its effects, ordering and failure behaviour, in full for a public var; for a private var, what it does plus the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape; (c) one sentence of why; (d) where the argument lives, as a repo-relative path into docs/design/hicasso (docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md, docs/design/hicasso/studio/<page>.md, docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md HD-NNN). An example only where it removes real ambiguity.
2. Links are repo-relative paths, NEVER [[wikilinks]]: 892 [[...]] exist across src/ and nothing resolves them (no codox config; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py scans docs/, spec/, skills/, migration/ and tools/*/spec only - DEFAULT_ROOTS line 94; PR #8736's body says "the doc link gates do not cover source docstrings"). The worker checks each retained path exists while editing and says so in the PR body.
3. A measured figure may stay in a docstring only with its page named beside it (e.g. "2.75 vs 1.42 us/read; docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-cold-read-mount-term.md").
4. A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit (a local correctness proof). Module history, benchmark narrative, rejected alternatives, HD-ruling derivations and explanations of OTHER namespaces' mechanisms do not.
5. A content rule, not a number: no 40-line cap, no 1:1 enforcement, no docstring-link checker, no migration script.
6. Move vs delete: durable design reasoning with no home in docs/design/hicasso is MOVED there (see WHERE CUT MATERIAL GOES in the next note); prose a design page already carries, superseded prose and change-narration is DELETED. The PR body names, per essay, the path it moved to, or "deleted - duplicated at <path>" / "deleted - superseded".

(defn commit-basis
  "The number a staged read is judged against: this runtime's flush
  generation + the frame's install epoch (`frame/frame-commit-epoch`) +
  the registry epoch. Monotone within a frame incarnation; install-counting,
  so a value-equal install still advances it (one redundant re-render at
  worst, never a missed one). Pure; allocates nothing.

  Three terms because each sees a movement the other two cannot: the
  generation moves only through a committed cell's watch, the install
  epoch is a plain counter, and only the registry term carries a `reg-sub`
  landing in the render->commit gap. The generation term is load-bearing
  across a same-id reincarnation, where the frame term restarts and can
  tie: any other cell the frame holds is rewired by microtask and that
  flush bumps the generation (staged_reincarnation_basis_cljs_test); a
  frame holding no other cell ties either way, which is Spec 006
  invariant 5's `:node-key` axis, not this number's. Full argument:
  docs/design/hicasso/architecture.md, section The commit basis."
  [frame-kw]

title: RULING: the native tier is a second authoring language with one consumer - shrink it to the hooks
description:
native.cljc is 1,116 lines (71% prose), 14 public names (10 surface + 4 public-by-expansion, native.cljc:161-185), 7 refusal ids, its own {:server} roster on defcomponent that duplicates defhost (native.cljc:391-401 says so), n/memo and n/lazy wrappers whose sole job is carrying a marker, a 4-production props grammar and the n/props marker. Consumer-shaped usage across examples/, tools/*/testbeds and the 8 example apps under hicasso/test/.../examples is ONE mention - the ledger docstring saying it was not needed (ledger/views.cljs:86). The guide concedes rung 4 may be a defui and that n/use-sub / n/use-frame work inside UIx (docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md:260-265).

RECOMMENDATION: keep n/use-sub and n/use-frame (the only things React cannot supply) and the two facade bridges; let islands be UIx or raw React mounted through defhost / [:>]. If rung 3 (a defview returning native elements, measured 38% on one example) is judged worth keeping, keep $ alone and drop defcomponent / memo / lazy / props and their 5 grammar refusals (or collapse to 2). Effort: large. Also touches: HMR contract for native, bundle-isolation sentinel for the tier, three_way_parity suites (keep the parity FLOOR test as a perf guard regardless).

HOW THIS WAS DECIDED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-6c12m.3.native-tier.md, deleted after this note was verified) recommended A. A second reviewer appended a "Codex Recommendation" that also chose A and set a proportionate implementation bar. No text in the file argued for B, C or D. The delegate re-verified the evidence at tip on 2026-08-29 and adopted A WITH the Codex conditions: (1) reduce the namespace's public census to the two hooks, everything supporting them private; (2) re-spell the HMR, imperative-host and Xray fixtures in ordinary React or UIx, keeping focused proof that the hooks preserve frame isolation, subscription lifecycle, teardown and Xray visibility; (3) keep one generic direct-React-return test and a raw-React parity floor; commission NO new benchmark run to justify the deletion; retire or clearly qualify the old worked number; (4) keep the reachability rule that ordinary Hicasso does not pull in the hooks namespace; delete the grammar, marker, refusal, ledger and guide machinery that has no subject; (5) replace chapter 10 with a short islands page showing raw React/UIx through defhost and those components using n/use-sub / n/use-frame when they need Hicasso state. Posture: pre-alpha, no deprecation programme, no compatibility shim, trust the programmer - a programmer who crosses into React writes React. If real application work later shows repeated friction, add the smallest helper proven by that code then.

WHY A.
1. Only the two hooks do something React cannot. use-sub hands useSyncExternalStore the same subscribe/getSnapshot a boundary reading that key gets (collector/hook-entry), so an island's read builds the same cell, joins the same reader membership and residue census, is woken by the same commit, and is named by the same re-frame.hicasso.tool rosters Xray consumes. use-frame returns collector/frame-row's incarnation-pinned ops map: destroy :watchlist and recreate it under the same id and a callback still holding the predecessor's ops is refused by core's :rf.error/frame-destroyed fence rather than writing to whoever owns the address now; a memo keyed on the frame keyword would pass every stability test and fail exactly that one (native.cljc:792-879). Both resolve the frame through collector/resolve-frame! - one React context, no spelling reaches a sibling frame. Everything else duplicates UIx, raw React or h/defhost: defcomponent's {:server} roster is a copy of defhost's and the code says so ("A second declaration grammar for it would buy nothing", native.cljc:391-401); memo and lazy are react/memo and react/lazy carrying a marker; $ is a second element grammar with 5 refusals of its own; the 7 remaining names (el, props*, declared-server, component, marker, tier-sentinel, prop-slots) are public only because a macro expansion or a parity fixture calls them (native.cljc:161-185).
2. The second language has one non-test consumer. Consumer-shaped usage across examples/, testbeds/, tools/*/testbeds and the 8 example apps under implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples: zero calls of n/$, n/defcomponent, n/memo, n/lazy or n/props. The one mention is examples/ledger/views.cljs:86-88 - "No n/defcomponent, no ref, no effect, no imperative handle, no memo hint and no second root. The application's whole native-tier surface is h/defhost and h/event" - from the app built to need an imperative SDK. Real consumers: the HMR testbed island (holds no subscription by design), one Xray test, and the reagent-migration skill's prose.
3. The guide already concedes the design. docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md:260-265: a rung-3 defview may return a UIx element, a rung-4 island may be a defui, and n/use-sub / n/use-frame work inside UIx components. Option A makes the concession the design.
4. Performance does not need n/$. MEASUREMENT FACT: chapter 10 line 81 claims "moved a 21 ms p95 tick to 13 ms: 38% and 8 ms recovered" and NO measurement record for that figure exists anywhere under docs/design/hicasso. The repository's actual rung-3 measurement is implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md row S8 (rf2-5yn9, re-based 2026-08-18 under rf2-6zc2q; lines 397 and 1596): 0.8081x, 19.2% of mount time recovered, per-round escapes [0.6863-0.9302], observed range 7.0%-31.4% over runs A, B, C pooled across fifteen rounds on a 200-boundary mount, status UNRESOLVED because the range crosses the 20% line. The guide's own keep-rule (10:22-25) is at least 20%, or at least 2 ms at p95, or enough to move a user-visible budget from fail to pass - otherwise remove it. So by the guide's own rule the escape has not earned its place. And S8 measures skipping hiccup interpretation once a React element already exists; a raw React or UIx element returned from a defview takes that same path, so the measured benefit survives without n/$. WHICHEVER option had been chosen, the 38% figure had to be corrected to S8's numbers; under A it is retired with the chapter, and S8 stays as the record of the direct-return escape reworded from n/$ to "a defview returning a React element".
5. What keeping it costs: ~900 of native.cljc's 1,116 lines (71% prose) beyond the hooks, 12 of 14 public names, 7 refusal ids, 10 test suites (113 deftests, 6,311 lines), rows in 6 gates and ledgers, a 345-line chapter plus 114 mentions across 12 other guide pages by the dossier's grep (a broader grep that also matches the phrase "native tier" reaches 17 pages: glossary 33, api-reference 26, troubleshooting 10, 21-code-splitting 9, 18-ssr 7, escape-ladder 7), a 7-row troubleshooting table, and a second grammar with its own rules for every reader.

REJECTED.
Option B (keep n/$ and n/props for rung 3 only; drop defcomponent/memo/lazy/marker; collapse 5 grammar refusals to 2): keeps a second element grammar nobody has written outside tests, on a measurement below the guide's own threshold; would need S8 re-taken and cleared first, and the Codex bar rightly refuses to commission a benchmark to justify an API.

Option D (delete the hooks too): WRONG. The hooks share Hicasso's cell table, census and Xray rosters and the frame row is incarnation-pinned (point 1). title: RULING: defhost :callbacks roster - infer the contract from the prop position instead of declaring it
description:
defhost makes the consumer declare :callbacks {:on-close :event, :render-row :render, :x :handler} and learn a 6-row table for what one h/event means by position (docs/core/hicasso/03-events-as-data.md:113-120). But impl/intent.cljs:1200-1210 ALREADY selects the contract by position for every native tag (on* = event, else render, :ref excluded), and lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1283-1296) shows :handler has no positive behaviour: h/event -> identity, plain fn -> identity, vector -> refused - and a vector at an undeclared on* host prop is already refused (codec.cljs:2884). :handler appears in zero consumer-shaped code (only host_hatch and intent_cljs_test). The one consumer-shaped declaration in the repo (test/.../examples/ledger/views.cljs:14-16) declares two entries. 11 refusal ids exist solely to validate the defhost declaration map (codec.cljs:1538-2053), ~15 to police this grammar overall. The stated reason for the roster (value-first foreign callbacks) is already caught at runtime by intent-needs-the-event (intent.cljs:107,726).

RECOMMENDATION: infer on* -> event, everything else -> render, exactly as native tags do; keep :slots (genuinely uninferable - a vector is legal data). Delete :callbacks, :handler and ~8 ids (unknown-callback-contract, host-structural-callback, host-callback-slot-collision, intent-at-a-non-event-contract, host-undeclared-callback, host-unclaimed-callback, plus simpler macro-tail guards). Effort: medium. If ruled yes, dispatch with the refusal-shrink task.

*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-29 14:38 AUSEST by the merge+dispatch tick (mayor session re-frame2-9a). Type is decision; the epic rf2-6c12m names it as one of five rulings that gate tasks. WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.

RULING 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option B, 2 values - infer the callback contract from the prop position exactly as native tags already do (on* -> :event, anything else walked -> :render, :ref -> React's); keep :callbacks ONLY as an optional override taking :event or :render; delete :handler; keep :slots.
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:29:54 AUSEST: ruled.

WHY B (decisive facts)
- The runtime already infers for every native tag: position-contract (impl/intent.cljs:1200-1210) = ref? -> :ref, event-prop? -> :event, else :render; event-prop? is one regex ^on-[a-z]|^on[A-Z] (intent.cljs:916-926). lower-declared-prop (intent.cljs:1255-1302) routes declared :event/:render to the SAME two wrappers the native walk uses (event-callback, render-callback).
- Every declaration in the repo and the guide infers identically. The only consumer-shaped one (test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/ledger/views.cljs:14-16, :137-138: {:render-row :render :on-window :event}) is exactly what inference gives. Guide declarations :on-change/:on-close/:on-pick/:on-value-change -> event and :render-row/:item-content -> render also match; the only two that do not are the two the guide invents to illustrate the roster (:on-imperative :handler, :on-render-row :render).
- :handler has no behaviour: h/event -> identity, plain fn -> identity, vector/map -> refused. A plain function already crosses untouched at every position (intent.cljs:1220-1228; codec.cljs:2865, host-prop-value's fn? arm). Zero consumer-shaped uses, tests only. Its own docstring says a plain fn is the handler contract (intent.cljs:1279-1281). It adds vocabulary, not capability.
- The stated reason for "never infer" (a value-first foreign callback such as onChange(date), where [:x ::h/value] would read date.target) is caught at runtime regardless of any declaration: event-arg! raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event naming the position (intent.cljs:95-117, :710-738). The declaration never prevented the mistake; the runtime check does.
- [:>] gets inference for free: raw-element walks props through host-entry against an EMPTY declared roster (codec.cljs:3465), so today [:> X {:on-pick (h/event ...)}] is refused as unclaimed and [:> X {:on-pick [:x/y]}] as undeclared. Under B host-entry's :else arm infers, so [:>] and defhost share one classifier (the second reviewer's point).
- Both the dossier author and the second reviewer (Codex) recommend B with 2 values. The added review is a clear recommendation, not a partial opinion; I weighed it against the code and found nothing against it. It adds three implementation constraints adopted here: reuse the native classifier (no second one), apply the same default in defhost and the [:>] host walk, and a proportionate test bar (below).

WHY NOT A (infer, delete :callbacks): one paragraph smaller, but no first-class spelling for an on*-named prop whose RETURN the library consumes and which is interactive. Fluent UI DetailsList onRenderItem/onRenderCell/onRenderHeader return UI; Ant Design Table onFilter returns a boolean, onRow/onCell/onHeaderRow return props maps. The event wrapper always returns nil (intent.cljs:551-596), so an h/event there blanks the list or vetoes every row, silently. A plain function is the escape and suffices for predicates and props-returning callbacks, but a plain function gets no frame/dispatch rebinding (render-callback, intent.cljs:598-704), so an intent inside a row it returns raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary at click - loud, not silent, but under A the only fix is an adapter component. Under B it is one line, {:callbacks {:on-render-item :render}}, and the render wrapper supplies the owning frame. The override costs one taught paragraph and one 2-value check that folds into .11's single bad-declaration id. The roster never prevented this hard case either: declaring such a prop :event blanks it the same way (skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:160 already warns).

WHY NOT C (keep as is): the consumer keeps declaring what the library already knows; the guide keeps a rule that contradicts its own native-tag behaviour; 4 ids, 1 half-id, 1 roster and ~560 lines of validation and commentary police a grammar with no consumer.

THE RULE AFTER B (position table 6 rows -> 4)
1. on*-spelled prop (native tag, defhost, [:>]) -> :event: h/event takes the event wrapper; an intent vector or key-map lowers as at a native event position; a plain fn crosses untouched.
2. Any other walked prop -> :render: h/event takes the render wrapper (frame + dispatch rebound); a vector or map crosses AS DATA via host-prop-value/clj->js exactly as at a native tag (nobody writes {:on-render-item [:x/y]} on purpose; refusing it is a guard a trusted programmer never trips). Plain fn untouched.
3. Declared :slots position -> markup (as-element); an h/event there stays refused (a function as a ReactNode renders nothing, silently) - this is the surviving half of host-unclaimed-callback.
4. :ref -> React's (check-ref!).
Override: {:callbacks {<prop> :event|:render}}, written only where inference is wrong; a declared contract outranks the spelling. Any other value is a bad declaration.

BEFORE / AFTER
;; today
(h/defhost date-picker DatePicker {:callbacks {:on-change :event}})
(h/defhost rows vendor/virtual-rows {:callbacks {:render-row :render :on-window :event}})
(h/defhost picker Widget {:callbacks {:on-pick :event :on-imperative :handler :on-render-row :render}})
;; after
(h/defhost date-picker DatePicker)
(h/defhost rows vendor/virtual-rows)
(h/defhost fluent-list FluentList {:callbacks {:on-render-item :render}})   ; the hard case: on*-named render prop
;; call sites unchanged
[date-picker {:selected (h/sub [:task/due-date]) :on-change (h/event [date _] [:task/set-due date])}]
[:> DatePicker {:on-change (h/event [date _] [:task/set-due date])}]   ; legal now too

title: RULING: move the bench tree out of implementation/hicasso and retire the freeze gate
description:
The bench tree (implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/hicasso, 197 files / 102,650 lines) is a second, stale implementation living inside the package. 12 donor copies of the runtime = 8,990 lines, 6,202 non-blank lines byte-identical to src (front/codec.cljs 2,085 of 2,973; arm1/runtime.cljs 1,349 of 2,141, 59 of its 61 defn names also defined in src). Of 67 bench test files, 63 require re-frame.bench.hicasso.* and ZERO require re-frame.hicasso.* - so 574 deftests run on every PR (node-test/browser-test regexps select them: shadow-cljs.edn:655,1037; hicasso/test is a source path at :139) and cannot catch a regression in the shipped runtime. test:hicasso-compile compiles all 197 bench namespaces per PR (~45s). check_freeze.py (839 lines) + frozen-sources.edn (246 lines, 190 of narrative) now pin ONE 109-line donor row (front/slot.cljc); the script and manifest both carry a SUNSET clause saying they go together when the last row goes. arm1/runtime.cljs was itself edited 2026-08-21, so frozen is not literally true.

RECOMMENDATION: move the tree to a repo-root bench/hicasso/ (or an archive branch) so it leaves the package classpath and the per-PR regexps; delete the donor-pinned *_cljs_test / *_dom_cljs_test files (live counterparts exist in test/re_frame/hicasso - rf2-xofa already ported the orphaned witnesses); keep the harness (lane.cljs, run.cjs, apps) for hand-run measurement; retire check_freeze.py + frozen-sources.edn, folding the SEALED forbidden-import prefixes (re-frame.bench., re-frame.freehand.) into check_optional_module_reachability.py; drop the 18 bench self-tests from test:script-helpers (package.json:64, ~17,900 lines incl clock_exit_path.test.cjs 6,149 lines - they pin bench report prose and exit codes a consumer never sees; moots rf2-t78z, rf2-oflj7, rf2-fc7w). Touches hot-zone shadow-cljs.edn (source path, :hicasso-bench* ids), package.json, compile_gate.cjs, and ~30 studio pages under docs/design/hicasso that cite paths (check_provenance_pins.py polices them).

SUPERSEDES rf2-0wv0 (slot.cljc sunset ruling): with the freeze gate gone, impl/slot.cljc can be de-historicised like the other 27 files. Resolves rf2-x7y5 (a package pin against the bench table). Effort: medium-large; one worker, sequential (hot zone).

title: hic: frameless overlay with :on-dismiss reaches the declared-unreachable two-owners state — needs a ruling
description: Found by rf2-dr90's coverage audit; verified at source. impl/overlay.cljs's dismissal-handler returns nil when there is no frame dispatch (~:655-659), but popover-dismissal-attrs (~:746-751) reads only the props — so a popover mounted with NO frame above it and :on-dismiss written still renders popover="auto" with no handler: the platform light-dismisses it, no intent lands, and app-db keeps open? true — exactly the open-flag/second-owner desync overlay.cljs's docstring (~:80-83) declares unreachable. Same shape on the modal (closedby="closerequest", no cancel handler). The presence module ruled its frameless case explicitly (legal until a child writes an intent, presence_react ~:50-57, tested at presence_intent ~:334-365); overlay has no equivalent ruling or witness. Needs Mike's ruling on direction before any test or fix: refuse a frameless overlay that carries :on-dismiss, or degrade the attrs to manual/none when dispatch is nil. Then the witness follows the ruling.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE - NOT DISPATCHABLE. *** Banner added 2026-08-29 10:31 AUSEST by the merge+dispatch tick (mayor session re-frame2-9a). The bead's own title names the hold: the frameless-overlay :on-dismiss path reaches a state the design declares unreachable, and whether the state is admitted (design amendment) or refused (code fix) is a RULING. WHOEVER RULES STRIKES THIS BANNER IN THE SAME ACT.
2026-08-29 14:40 AUSEST - Decision dossier for Mike at ai/decisions/rf2-4e5b.frameless-overlay-on-dismiss.md (local-only, untracked): problem, options with consequences, recommendation, how to record the ruling.

If Mike rules that way, the fix rides the refusal lane (rf2-6c12m.11's wave or after) rather than a solo dispatch. Banner stands.
RULING 2026-08-29 15:31:44 AUSEST (delegated review per Mike, 2026-08-29): Option D - a frameless overlay stays legal without :on-dismiss; an OPEN one that carries :on-dismiss with no frame dispatch refuses at render with the EXISTING :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary (the presence precedent), no new id.
BANNER STRUCK 2026-08-29 15:31:44 AUSEST: ruled; dispatchable.

WHY D, AND HOW THE REVIEWS WERE WEIGHED. The dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-4e5b.frameless-overlay-on-dismiss.md, now deleted; this note carries everything it held) recommended D. A second review appended to it ("Codex Recommendation") independently chose D on the same grounds and added implementation bounds (small guard, no id, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no grammar broadening, amend the one Spec 009 row, no compat layer). The two agreed, so this is adoption of a concurring recommendation rather than a tie-break. Decisive facts: (1) :on-dismiss IS an intent - the public docstring says so (overlay.cljs:79-80 "routed back as an ordinary intent - which is what :on-dismiss is") - and every other intent position in hicasso that cannot land REFUSES (require-dispatch, intent.cljs:397-402; event-callback, intent.cljs:586-595); this is the one silent path in the module. (2) Presence and the error boundary already ruled the identical frameless case exactly this way (presence_react.cljs:51-56, boundary.cljs:153-158). (3) rf2-6c12m.11 is cutting the refusal roster from 59 to ~30; a new id (option A) would add vocabulary carrying no information the existing id does not. (4) Degrading to manual/none (option B) silently ignores a line the programmer wrote - "trust the programmer" means report the impossibility, not hide it. (5) Admitting the state (option C) documents a desync and would have the witness pin a defect as a feature. One alternative both reviews left implicit is closed here: routing :on-dismiss through intent/lower-prop (intent.cljs:1212-1228) so the emitter stays in impl.intent was considered and rejected - it changes :on-dismiss's dispatch mechanics (intent-handler's per-key policy, key-maps, placeholders), which is the grammar broadening the Codex review rules out, and the popover would still need its beforetoggle direction filter wrapped around the result. Direct guard it is.

THE MECHANISM (all paths implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ unless stated).
- impl/overlay.cljs:687-688: body resolves the frame via adapter-context/context-value->current-frame on react/useContext frame-context; with no provider above, the reader answers nil by design (core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:330).
- :702: dispatch (when frame-kw (collector/frame-dispatch frame-kw)) - nil when frameless.
- :655-656: dismissal-handler [dispatch on-dismiss closed-only?] is (when (and dispatch on-dismiss) (fn ...)) - returns nil when dispatch is nil, silently.
- :741-744 modal-dismissal-attrs and :750-751 popover-dismissal-attrs read PROPS ONLY: :on-dismiss present => closedby="closerequest" (or "any" with :light-dismiss?) / popover="auto". So the element tells the platform "you may dismiss me" while nothing listens.
- :669 own-keys strips :on-dismiss from the props before element-attrs/lowering, and :706 hands it to dismissal-handler directly, so it BYPASSES intent/with-frame (:726) and require-dispatch (intent.cljs:397-402) - the one intent position in the module that skips the loud path. Children's intents inside the overlay do take the loud path.
- :604-631 make-cell: show! (showPopover/showModal) runs ONLY from the once-attached stable ref callback; body (:681-729) has no effect. A re-render therefore does NOT re-show a platform-closed element.

USER-VISIBLE SEQUENCE (popover, :open? true, :on-dismiss written, no frame): 1. mounts, ref callback calls showPopover once on attach, element in the top layer with popover="auto". 2. user clicks outside; platform fires beforetoggle/toggle, nothing listens, panel hides. 3. the flag driving :open? is still true - no intent ran. 4. a re-render does not re-show it (stable ref, no effect). 5. to reopen the author must flip the flag false (element unmounts; hide! is a no-op) then true again - two actions for one open, and any aria-expanded mirrored from the flag lies in between. Modal: same shape with closedby="closerequest" - Escape closes the dialog, no cancel handler runs, flag stays true. This is exactly the two-owners state overlay.cljs:76-83 declares unreachable.

WHEN FRAMELESS ACTUALLY HAPPENS. Every shipped door installs a frame: h/mount! takes {:frame ::frame} (impl/mount.cljs:141); server/render allocates a per-request frame (server.cljs:333); Story wraps every variant in rf/frame-provider (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs:622, 673); a UIx/Reagent island under frame-provider or frame-root reads the same context object (context.cljs:38-40, impl/mount.cljs:33-36). An overlay under an h/defview never reaches this code because the boundary shell refuses :rf.error/no-frame-context first (impl/collector.cljs:1753-1760). So the case is reached only when the overlay is the OUTERMOST hicasso component in a React root nobody wrapped: a test mounting it alone (presence's suite does this via mount/root! with adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel), or a consumer's hand-built root / unwrapped island. Rare, mostly test-time - and it is the case where :open? cannot be an h/sub and :on-dismiss can never land, i.e. an authoring error worth naming. A frameless overlay WITHOUT :on-dismiss is a legitimate case (static manual popover, non-dismissible dialog) and stays legal.

PRECEDENT. presence_react.cljs:51-56: "No frame in scope is not an error here. Presence reads nothing, so a tray mounted outside a frame is legal until one of its children writes an intent - at which point the existing loud error fires and names the intent, which is better attribution than a generic no-frame-context throw from the tray." boundary.cljs:153-158 carries the same paragraph. Witness: test/re_frame/hicasso/presence_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:327-365 - frameless-root! (mount/root! (mount/fresh-container!) adapter-context/no-provider-sentinel hiccup); testing block 1: quiet frameless tray renders; block 2: a child with :on-click [...] under a boundary with :on-error raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary and (:intent (ex-data e)) equals the vector. overlay_dom_cljs_test.cljs has no frameless row (its manual witness is :652-655, :680-694).

OPTIONS REJECTED. A (new id e.g. :rf.error/hicasso-overlay-dismiss-without-frame): same trigger as D, but mints an overlay-specific id for the generic outside-boundary condition, costs rows in complaints.md (:129 area), the naming ledger, Spec 009 and check_complaint_catalogue.py, against rf2-6c12m.11's direction. B (thread dispatch into the two attrs fns so nil dispatch yields manual/none): one owner, docstring stays true, but the :on-dismiss the author wrote is silently dead - the only swallowed intent in hicasso. C (amend the docstring to say two-owners holds only inside a frame): honest but documents a desync; witness would pin a defect.

THE CHANGE (one guard, shared path, covers modal AND popover).
1. impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler (:633-659), called once from body at :706 for both heads while :open? is true: when on-dismiss is non-nil and dispatch is nil, (fail! :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary 're-frame.hicasso.impl.overlay/dismissal-handler "<reason>" :lower-intents-inside-a-boundary-render {:intent on-dismiss}) instead of returning nil. Keep the existing (fn [e] ...) branch untouched. Reason text names what happened and the direct recovery: the overlay carries :on-dismiss <intent> but no frame is in scope, so the platform would be told it may dismiss while nothing could route the dismissal; mount the overlay under a frame (h/mount!, rf/frame-provider, frame-root) or drop :on-dismiss if it should be non-dismissable. fail! is already referred at :108 and the anchor refusal at :218 shows the local call shape; write to fail!'s signature AT TIP (rf2-6c12m.5 may drop :recovery/:where - do not pre-empt it). Reuse the recovery keyword above so R10 of check_complaint_catalogue.py stays green without a new row. Placing the guard in body immediately after :702 is an acceptable equivalent; ONE site only, no dispatch threading through the attrs fns, no new abstraction.
2. Docstring: overlay.cljs:76-83 posture paragraph gains one paragraph modelled on presence_react.cljs:51-56 - no frame in scope is not an error for an overlay; without :on-dismiss it is manual/none and single-owner; WITH :on-dismiss and no frame it refuses at render with the existing intent-outside-boundary, naming the intent, so the two-owners state stays unreachable outside a frame too. Also correct impl/overlay.cljs dismissal-handler's first line ("or nil when there is nothing to route" -> nil when there is no :on-dismiss; the loud refusal when there is one and no frame).
3. docs/core/hicasso/13-overlays-and-focus.md: one Troubleshooting row (table at :344ff): Symptom - an open overlay raises :rf.error/hicasso-intent-outside-boundary naming the :on-dismiss intent | Cause - it has :on-dismiss but no frame above it (rendered outside h/mount!, frame-provider, frame-root or Story) | Fix - mount it under a frame, or drop :on-dismiss if it must not be dismissable. Optionally one sentence at the :on-dismiss contract (:69-71). Verify the table's column count by hand and say so in the PR body.
4. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2527 (HOT-ZONE, one-toucher): the row for this id says "THREE arms, one id ... Emitted by re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent" with :where 're-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/lower-prop on all three.
