description:
REQUESTED BY MIKE 2026-08-29 09:57 AUSEST, in chat, verbatim ask: "do a review of hicasso, improving test coverage and quality."

WHAT THIS IS. A review of implementation/hicasso/'s test suite against its actual surfaces, with two deliverables: (1) a findings review of where coverage is thin, weak, or low-quality relative to what the code does; (2) landed improvements for the clear cases, and follow-on beads (filed one at a time, ids appended to this bead's notes) for anything larger, riskier, or needing a ruling.

WHERE TO LOOK. Source surfaces: implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/ — evidence.cljs, forms.cljs, motion.cljs, native.cljc, overlay.cljs, server.cljs, substrate.cljs, tool.cljs, and the impl/ tree. Existing tests: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/ (40+ files: *_cljs_test, *_dom_cljs_test, *_ssr_* variants), plus test_kit/ and testbed/. Map each source module to the tests that exercise it and find the gaps — surfaces with no adversarial or negative case, behaviours only exercised through the happy path, error/complaint shapes never asserted, SSR/DOM parity holes.

QUALITY BAR, from the method and the stance. A coverage or rigour pass must add at least one adversarial or negative case per surface it strengthens — assertion-count growth alone only exercises the happy path. Quality also means the tests themselves: actionable failure output, no tautological assertions, no tests that pin incidental strings where they should pin behaviour (this repo has a measured history of hollow phrase-matcher guards — see rf2-2iaph/rf2-oflj7 for the shape; do NOT touch those files, see fences). Prefer strengthening a weak existing test over adding a near-duplicate.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE. The module-to-test gap map is reported (findings doc in ai/findings/, never committed); clear test improvements merged green via PR with a ## Quality gates section; follow-on beads filed for the remainder with this bead named as owner; the delta between what this bead claims and what the tree holds at dispatch time is reported.

WHAT NOT TO TOUCH.
- implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/bench/** and alloc_null_floor.cjs anywhere: held under rf2-t78z / rf2-oflj7 / rf2-fc7w awaiting Mike's rulings. Read them if useful; edit nothing.

POSTURE. Pre-alpha masterpiece: elegance, clarity, correctness, good practice. Trust the programmer. No over-engineering, no gold-plating, no nag-diagnostics, no test-count inflation. Reject a finding rather than action minutiae; a short list of sourced, load-bearing improvements beats a long plausible one.

title: mayor loop: sweep open nightly-red issues into beads each merge+dispatch tick (loops.md §2 Dispatch + CLAUDE.md Workflow; alerter unchanged)
description:
Split out of rf2-2ohy's third acceptance item, which asked whether the
rf2-6sg25 alerting failed to surface seven consecutive nightly reds.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 13:36 AUSEST, and the answer is that THE ALERT FIRED
CORRECTLY. Issue #8423 'Nightly `expensive tests` is red' was opened
2026-08-16T16:01:50Z — the first red night — labelled `nightly-red`,
assigned to mike-thompson-day8, and its body named the exact failing step:
`Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates -> Gate — production elision,
browser (test:browser-prod-elision)`. It was edited every night since and
last updated 2026-08-22T16:02:05Z carrying `reds=7 greens=0`. The
alerting self-test step passed on every one of those runs. So the first
disjunct in rf2-2ohy's premise — 'the alerting did not fire' — is FALSE.
Nothing in .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py is broken, and this
bead is NOT a request to change its signature logic.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED is the second disjunct: the issue went unseen for
seven days, and the alerter's own body says why, in its own words:

  'It is edited in place — which notifies nobody — while the same steps
  keep failing, and comments only when a step that was not failing starts
  to.'

That is a deliberate anti-spam design and it is defensible. The observed
cost of it is that a red lane produces EXACTLY ONE notification, on night
one, and then six nights of silence — and the one notification competes
with normal PR traffic in the same inbox. Seven days later the redness was
found by a manual PR-activity sweep, not by the alert, and no bead existed
until that sweep filed rf2-2ohy.

THE GAP, stated narrowly: nothing escalates a `nightly-red` issue that
stays open, and nothing bridges a GitHub issue into the beads tracker,
which is where work is actually dispatched from in this repo. The alert
lands in a channel the working loop does not read.

NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least
three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker:
  (a) re-notify on an age threshold (comment, not edit, after N reds) —
      cheapest, stays inside the existing script;
  (b) have the mayor loop read open `nightly-red` issues each tick;
  (c) have the alerter file/refresh a bead directly, so nightly redness
      enters the same queue as everything else.
(a) risks the spam the current design avoids. (c) is the most useful and
the most machinery. Mike to rule.

EVIDENCE: gh issue view 8423; gh run list --workflow expensive-tests.yml;
.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml lines 558-616 (the 'Nightly result ->
tracking issue' job, which succeeded on all seven red runs).

ACCEPTANCE: a ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night
one, and if so which shape. If the ruling is 'leave it as is, the mayor
sweep is the backstop', close this — that is a legitimate outcome and the
evidence above is the record of what that choice costs.
notes:
*** AWAITING MIKE — NOT DISPATCHABLE. WHOLLY AN OPERATOR CALL. *** Fence recorded by the mayor's dispatch tick 2026-08-23 13:41 AUSEST at tip e1a1faf9c8, quoting this bead's own description rather than re-reasoning it.

WHY IT IS NOT DISPATCHABLE: the bead states it in terms — 'NOT PROPOSING A REMEDY — this is an operator call, and there are at least three shapes with different costs, so it should not be picked by a worker.' A worker sent here would have to choose between (a) re-notify on an age threshold, (b) the mayor loop reads open nightly-red issues each tick, and (c) the alerter files or refreshes a bead directly. Those differ in cost and in how much machinery they add, which is a judgement rather than a task.

DISCHARGED BY: Mike ruling on whether nightly redness should escalate past night one, and if so which of the three shapes. 'Leave it as is, the mayor sweep is the backstop' is a legitimate ruling and closes this bead — the bead says so itself, and the evidence it carries then stands as the record of what that choice costs.

WHAT IT IS NOT, and this matters because the parent bead's premise said otherwise: the alerting is NOT broken. This bead REFUTED that premise with measurement — issue #8423 opened on the first red night, labelled, assigned, naming the exact failing step, edited every night since, with the alerting self-test passing on all seven runs. Do not dispatch anything at .github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py's signature logic; nothing there is wrong.

THE COST OF THIS HOLD, priced rather than asserted: nothing is queued behind it and no bead is blocked by it. What it costs is the thing that already happened once — seven consecutive red nights on the superset backstop, found by a manual sweep on day seven rather than by the channel built to report it. That cost recurs at the same rate as nightly redness itself, which over the last nine nights was seven times in nine.

NO HOT-ZONE SEQUENCING IS NEEDED. I had expected to fence this behind rf2-2ohy's worker because a remedy would touch .github/workflows/*, which is hot-zone and currently that worker's. That fence is unnecessary: this bead cannot be dispatched at all until it is ruled, and by then that worker will be long finished.
BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-23 17:05 AUSEST, tip 69a464c76b. THE PRICE OF THIS HOLD HAS CHANGED SINCE IT WAS RECORDED, and the bead's evidence needs the update so the ruling is made on current facts rather than on the state that prompted the bead.

WHAT THE 13:41 FENCE PRICES: "That cost recurs at the same rate as nightly redness itself, which over the last nine nights was seven times in nine."

THAT RATE WAS MEASURED WHILE THE ROOT CAUSE WAS LIVE, AND IT IS NOT LIVE NOW. Verified at source this tick, one item at a time:

  rf2-2ohy                          CLOSED (the browser-prod-elision abort, fixed by PR #8724)
  expensive-tests on main, 04:11    workflow_dispatch, completed/SUCCESS
  expensive-tests on the fix branch completed/SUCCESS at 03:38

  schedule, read from the workflow  cron "17 15 * * *" = 01:17 AUSEST

So the first SCHEDULED exercise of the fix has not happened yet; it is tonight. The lane is proven green on main by dispatch, and the 7-in-9 figure describes a condition that has been repaired.

AND THE ALERTER CARRIES A RECOVERY POLICY THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION DOES NOT MENTION. Issue #8423's body reads, at this tick, "reds=7 greens=1" and states: "This issue closes automatically after 3 consecutive green runs -- the gap exists so an intermittent gate that passes tonight does not close and reopen the issue every other night." The 04:11 dispatch already counted as the first green.

WHY THAT MATTERS TO THE RULING RATHER THAN CLOSING IT. The "edited in place, notifies nobody" characterisation is TRUE OF THE RED DIRECTION ONLY. Recovery is automatic, bounded and hysteresis-guarded; it is the escalation on SUSTAINED redness that is absent. That narrows the question rather than answering it, and narrowing is worth recording: the three shapes are still the three shapes, but option (a) -- re-notify on an age threshold -- is now visibly the mirror of a policy the alerter ALREADY implements in the other direction, which is an argument about symmetry rather than about adding machinery.

What it costs is no longer a 7-in-9 recurring toll; it is the next unrelated breakage going unreported for as many nights as it takes somebody to sweep manually. MAYOR 2026-08-24 01:57 AUSEST — THE WATCH CONDITION ON THIS BEAD HAS FIRED, AND IT FIRED GREEN.

This bead recorded: 'if tonight's scheduled run is [red], the fix did not hold under the scheduled
trigger and rf2-2ohy wants reopening.' Measured at source rather than inferred:

under the trigger that was failing, not only under manual dispatch. rf2-2ohy STAYS CLOSED — no reopen.

THE TRACKING ISSUE HAS MOVED TOO, and its own counter is the evidence: issue #8423 now reads
'reds=7 greens=2' where it read 'reds=7 greens=1' before tonight. It auto-closes after THREE
consecutive greens, so it stays open one more night by design — the gap exists so an intermittent gate
does not close and reopen the issue. Expect it to close after tomorrow's scheduled run.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DISCHARGE: this bead's own subject, which is the ALERTING gap rather than the test
failure — seven reds produced one notification. That question is untouched by tonight's green and is
still wholly an operator call. The banner stands.
RULING 2026-09-02 10:21:52 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-02, dossier review; ai/decisions/rf2-4a0c.nightly-red-escalation.md folded here and deleted — THIS NOTE IS THE CANONICAL RECORD). Ruled at tip b26c5ad33e.
BANNER STRUCK — the *** AWAITING MIKE *** banner above is discharged by this ruling.

1. DECISION: (b). The mayor's short Merge + dispatch tick reads the open nightly-red issues and ensures each one has exactly one open bead. The alerter (.github/scripts/nightly_failure_alert.py) and expensive-tests.yml are NOT touched — signature logic, thresholds, channel, all unchanged. (a), (c) and (d) rejected; one-line reasons under REJECTED in §4.

THE MECHANISM, exactly:
- WHERE: the DISPATCH half of the short tick (loops.md cadence table: "Merge + dispatch", ~10–15 min, and "on most signals"), as the first read BEFORE `bd ready` — its output is a bead, and the same tick can then dispatch it.
- THE READ, one-shot and non-blocking: `gh issue list --repo day8/re-frame2 --label nightly-red --state open --limit 100 --json number,url,title,updatedAt,body`. Check the exit code of the gh call itself. Exit 0 with `[]` = nothing red, done — the normal tick (the dossier measured the label non-empty on 12 of the last 60 days; at ruling time it is empty). Non-zero exit = "the sweep did not run this tick", retried on the next signal — NEVER read a failed query as "no nightly red" (the reviewer's invariant, adopted).
- DEDUP KEY: the canonical issue URL (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/issues/<n>), carried in the bead's `external_ref` field — a field the tracker already uses this way (15 beads carry PR URLs in it at tip) and which `bd list --json` exposes. NOT the bare number: "8423" also matches PR numbers, run counts and commit prefixes. The read: `bd list --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred,closed --limit 0 --json | jq -r --arg u "$url" '.[] | select(.external_ref==$u) | "\(.id)\t\(.status)"'` (confirm once that `--limit 0` is unbounded on this bd build, as it is for `bd ready`).
- THREE CASES per open issue:
  (i) a bead in open/in_progress/blocked carries the URL → do nothing. The issue stays the live counter and signature record; the bead is the dispatch edge; later ticks do nothing.
  (ii) no bead carries the URL → file one: `bd create "nightly red: <failing steps> (issue #<n>)" --type bug --priority 2 --external-ref <url> --description "<shape in §4>"`. P2 by default; raise with a stated reason when the failing gate warrants it.
  (iii) only CLOSED beads carry the URL → THE HYSTERESIS CASE, and the one the reviewer's draft rule ("reopen it or file a clearly linked follow-up") would get wrong. The issue closes only after THREE consecutive greens (`--close-after 3`, sized above the rf2-7jevo flake), so for two nights after every fix the expected state is "bead closed, issue still open" — that is recovery, not a new failure. Read the body's marker line `<!-- nightly-alert:v1 signature=... reds=N greens=M -->`: `decide()` (nightly_failure_alert.py:246-286) sets greens=0 on ANY red night and increments it on a green one, so `greens>=1` → recovering by design, do nothing; `greens=0` → the most recent nightly was red AFTER the bead closed — the fix did not hold, or a new step joined — so file a NEW bead per (ii) with `--deps discovered-from:<closed-id>`, citing the closed one. Never reopen the closed bead: its close reason is a normative record.
- DUPLICATE ISSUES: the label-index race can open two issues in the same minute (#7537/#7538 on 2026-08-05, recorded in `fetch_open_issues`' docstring and self-healed by `collapse_duplicates` on the next run). Two open nightly-red issues with the same title created within minutes are ONE alert: file against the lower number only.
- BINDING FROM NOW: the doctrine binds the mayor from this ruling; the doc PR is the record, not the trigger. At ruling time (`gh issue list --label nightly-red --state open`, 10:13 AUSEST) there are ZERO open nightly-red issues and the last five scheduled runs are green, so today's sweep is a no-op.

2. HOW THE OPINIONS WERE WEIGHED
Two voices in the dossier: the AUTHOR (sections "Summary", "The problem, carefully and fully", "What is waiting on this", "Options", "Recommendation", "Evidence") and the REVIEWER ("Codex Recommendation": "Independent findings", "Why this option", "Implementation invariant, risks, and next decision"). description:
Found by the 2026-08-23 PR-activity sweep. The nightly expensive-tests workflow has failed 7 consecutive runs (08-16, 08-17, 08-18, cancelled 08-19, 08-20, 08-21, 08-22; last green 08-15), same job every time: 'Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates'. ## What it is

`shadow.test.env/get-test-data` is a MACRO. It expands, at the moment the
runner namespace is compiled, into a literal map naming every test var the
compiler knows about — the test roster is frozen into the runner's compiled JS.

shadow-cljs keys its per-namespace compile cache off `:immediate-deps`, which
`shadow.build.resolve/stack-pop` fills from the ns form's own requires. The
`:browser-test` target attaches the discovered test namespaces to the runner as
`:extra-requires` (`shadow.build.test-util/inject-extra-requires`), and those
are read only by `shadow.build.compiler/par-compile-one` to ORDER compilation —
they never enter `:immediate-deps`. So the roster can change completely without
invalidating the runner's cache entry.

A namespace LEAVING the roster is the destructive direction: the stale cached
expansion still dereferences vars whose namespaces are no longer in the bundle.
Under :advanced that is a property read on undefined, uncaught, inside `init` —
zero namespaces announced, no cljs.test summary, exactly the observed abort.

## The bead's hypothesis was RIGHT about the trigger, wrong about the mechanism

The correlation with the Freehand / re-frame.ui removal is REAL and causal: PR
#8322 took fourteen `*-elision-prod-test` namespaces out of this lane on 08-16.
But nothing in the prod-elision build 'still reaches a deleted surface' in the
source sense — the source is fine, and a CLEAN local run of
`npm run test:browser-prod-elision` has been green throughout (measured: exit 0,
91 tests / 289 assertions on current main). The reach-into-deleted-surface
happens in a STALE COMPILED ARTEFACT, and it needs a warm cache to exist at all.
`expensive-tests.yml` restores `implementation/.shadow-cljs` with
`restore-keys: <os>-story-xray-shadow-`, so from 08-16 every nightly served the
pre-removal runner out of cache. That is why the failure is CI-only and why it
persisted for seven nights.

The 'me' in the message is not meaningful: it is a Closure-assigned minified

That identity is the point: the five operative contract documents rf2-ps7ia moved into implementation/hicasso/spec/ are classified exactly as production CLJS source, because the `implementation/hicasso/*` case arm does not discriminate `.md`. A one-word typo fix in a Markdown register therefore queues cljs_browser, hicasso_controlled and hicasso_hmr -- three Chromium lanes -- plus a ~10-minute CLJS compile.

WHY IT IS A CALL AND NOT A BUG. Two standing principles point opposite ways.
  FOR keeping it: TESTING.md's standing rule is 'when in doubt, over-classify'. Over-arming is the failure mode the repo deliberately prefers, and rf2-8a6s's own comment records that this arm exists precisely because a hicasso-only diff once classified to NOTHING and merged green.
  AGAINST keeping it: the comment block above the complaint-catalogue test in implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs says in terms that 'arming a ~10-minute CLJS compile for a Markdown edit is the trade TESTING.md's placement table exists to refuse'. That sentence was written about these very documents, at their old address.

THE NARROWING, IF MIKE WANTS IT. An `implementation/hicasso/spec/*.md` case placed BEFORE the `implementation/hicasso/*` arm, setting cljs_node_test only. Rationale: what these five documents actually gate is the invariants chain, which is pure Python -- check_complaint_catalogue.py, the budget-ledger reconciliation, the facade-inventory diff -- and Markdown cannot change what React puts on a page, which is the line rf2-drpa3.70 already drew for prose arms and which _changed-surfaces.test.cjs holds for every other prose arm in the file ('prose arms the JVM tier and NO browser/prod/Playwright tier').

WHAT ALREADY STANDS BEHIND THESE DOCUMENTS EITHER WAY, so the narrowing is not as exposed as it looks: all five carry UNCONDITIONAL test.yml jobs of their own -- hicasso-complaint-catalogue, hicasso-budget-ledger and hicasso-facade-inventory each carry no `needs: detect_changed_surfaces` and no `if:`, by design, precisely because a surface gate that did not cover a checker's inputs was the original defect (rf2-hic-021 / rf2-ibje). docs.yml separately arms the warm-allocation scan on implementation/hicasso/spec/budgets.md by name (rf2-ps7ia).

  TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE, and proposes no mechanism for the structure.

WHAT THE SAME RUN PRINTS, four lines above it — rounds carrying mode-2 cells:

So the clean prefix is TWO rounds long, not three. The reader's OWN preceding sentence in the
same section says so in as many words: 'round 0 alone, heavily decimated by certification :
0/22 (0.0%)' sits directly above, and the file's header comment (line ~110) states 'Rounds 0
and 1 carry NONE AT ALL'. Three statements in one file, two of them derived, disagreeing with

AND IT WAS NOT THE PHASE-4 FOLD-IN. On the 242-cell corpus the same table read round 0 at
0.0%, round 1 at 0.0% and round 2 at 6.7% (2 of 30) — the frozen studio page
docs/design/hicasso/studio/the-floor-is-two-populations.md prints exactly those rows at its
section E, and its own prose two lines above the claim says 'Rounds 0 and 1 carry none at
all'. The prefix was two rounds long then as well. This is a published error rather than a
figure the corpus moved out from under.

'CLEAN PREFIX' HAS NO OTHER DEFINITION IN THE REPO. git grep -F 'clean prefix' returns three
hits and they are this one sentence in its three copies (the .cjs header comment, the .cjs
report line, the studio page). The sentence's own follow-on — 'whether those are the SAME
THREE' — pairs it with 'warmups is 3', so 'clean prefix' can only mean the leading rounds
carrying no mode-2 cell. Control: git grep -lF 'warmups' returns 189 files, so the pattern
reaches this corpus and the three is a reading.

THE GUARD IS THE HOLLOW SHAPE THIS FAMILY OF BEADS IS ABOUT. The only check on the sentence is

  ck('the report proposes no mechanism for the round structure',
     /THIS READER HAS NOT\n;; {3}TESTED WHETHER THOSE ARE THE SAME THREE/.test(rep), true);

which asks whether a DIFFERENT CLAUSE of the same sentence is present. It passes whatever the
count says, and has done since the sentence was written.

WHY THIS IS A RULING AND NOT A WORKER'S FIX, which is why it was left rather than folded into
rf2-oflj7's PR. The number is load-bearing on the reader's conclusion: 'three' is what makes
the sentence a COINCIDENCE WORTH NOT EXPLAINING ('warmups is 3 ... has not tested whether
those are the same three'). Correcting it to two dissolves the pairing, and the reader then
either says nothing about warmups or says something new about a two-round prefix against a
three-round warmup — which is a claim about MECHANISM, and this reader's standing position is
that it proposes none. Same class as rf2-oflj7's items 5 and 6.

NOT VERIFIED HERE: whether 'warmups is 3 in every run' holds over the 16 runs. It is unguarded
too — no check reads it — but it was out of the sweep's scope.

sentence at its section E. That page is explicitly frozen at its 242-cell state by its own
banner ('left exactly as it was published'), so whether a published error inside a frozen
record is corrected in place or annotated is part of the same ruling.

title: [method] reopened-item shortcut revives the false description-is-stale rule
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-17 00:25 AUSEST on rf2-lo7uy, by the mayor making the mistake.

THE GAP. The timestamp-ordering rule exists in three places and none of them is the
one that was needed:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md (4 mentions) — WORKER-FACING.
    It is the text the mayor PASTES INTO A BRIEF, so it instructs the worker.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-backlog-reread.md (1 mention) — mayor-facing, but scoped
    to the hourly BACKLOG REREAD loop.
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md (2 mentions).
mayor-dispatch.md, which governs writing a brief FROM a bead, says nothing about it.
Grepped for 'bd history|newest|created_at|timestamp|superseded|stale.*comment' — the
only hit is an unrelated routing paragraph.

WHAT IT COST. The mayor read rf2-lo7uy top-down, took a 03:02Z mayor triage comment
splitting the bead into an EDIT half and a WINDOW half as the newest text, and
dispatched the edit half. A 04:55:51Z comment titled 'RIG HALF LANDED — THIS BEAD IS
NOW WINDOW-ONLY' already recorded that PR #8384 had merged those exact arms at
05:12:23Z the previous day.

PROCEEDING WOULD HAVE BEEN DESTRUCTIVE, NOT MERELY WASTEFUL. 'n' is an input to
lane/slot-order on that instrument, so adding two more nulls takes n from 11 to 13 and
moves EVERY arm's position footprint including the nine published ones — discarding
#8384's layout and starting a third series, on the very rig whose slot-sensitivity the
bead exists to measure.

THE WORKER CAUGHT IT. It walked 'bd history --json' newest-first across adjacent pairs,
found the 04:55:51Z comment, verified #8384 MERGED at source rather than from the
comment, wrote no code, and correctly declined to run a spine or quote an exit code for
a tree it had not changed.

THE FIX — one sentence-group appended to the 'Find + group' paragraph (line 19), whose
neighbours are already the same class of pre-dispatch verification ('A COUNT IS A CLAIM
TOO, AND THE GREP THAT CHECKS IT IS A DIFFERENT ONE'). Proposed text, to append after
'...treat a parent's remainder table as stale until re-derived.':

  **AND ESTABLISH WHICH TEXT ON THE BEAD IS NEWEST BEFORE YOU BRIEF FROM IT — by
  TIMESTAMP, never by position.** Every brief this file sends already tells the WORKER
  to do this, and mayor-backlog-reread.md tells the mayor to do it when rereading the
  backlog; the gap was here, at the one moment a brief is actually written from a bead.
  Comments do not render in timestamp order relative to notes appended into the
  description block, so the visually-last text is routinely not the newest:
  'bd comments <id> --json' sorted by created_at descending, and 'bd history <id> --json'
  walked newest-first to the first change in a text-bearing field, are the only two
  reads that answer it. **The mayor's OWN earlier note is the most dangerous stale
  source**, because it reads as authoritative and you recognise your own words.
  [then the rf2-lo7uy incident as above, and:] That is the 'where the item and this
  brief disagree, the ITEM governs' clause doing the work it is there for — but it
  should not have had to.

WORD IT YOURSELF IF YOU CAN DO IT BETTER; the above is a draft, not a specification.
Keep it PROPORTIONATE — the anti-gold-plating clause applies. Do NOT add a checklist,
a script, or a tracking field, and do NOT restate the reasoning that
dispatch-prompt-template.md already owns; this file's own line 23 warns that a second
copy of the template's text is 'the same drift one level down'.

WHY THE MAYOR DID NOT JUST EDIT IT: the pre-commit hook refused, exactly as designed —
'.claude/commands/' is a worker-tracked surface and the mayor checkout cannot commit to
it. Attempted at 00:47, refused, reverted, filed here.

CONTROLS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so do not re-derive them: 'scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci'
covers '.claude/commands/*.md' via COMMAND_FILE_PATHSPEC and was proved to bite on THIS
FILE by a planted broken link — exit 1, naming '.claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md:29'.
It is SILENT ON SUCCESS, so a green run alone proves nothing. 'check_doc_slugs.py' also
exits 0 on this file. One caution learned the hard way: the mayor planted its control on
an UNCOMMITTED edit and restored with 'git checkout --', which discarded the edit along
with the plant — commit first, then plant, and verify the restore by content hash rather
than by reading a diff.
acceptance_criteria: The dispatch template treats closed-to-open as an attention signal, not proof: it never infers that closure means merged/shipped or that a reopened item's description is necessarily stale. The existing timestamp-ordered history walk and tree check remain the authority. Prose-only correction; no new mechanism.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8906 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED.

The new closed-to-open probe is useful, but its evidence does not support its categorical wording. Completeness: three stale reopened descriptions plus one never-closed control establish a high-signal heuristic, not that every reopened description is stale; there is no reopened/current-description control. Correctness: the text says a reopened description is stale "by construction" because "the work that closed it has shipped" and the live instruction is whatever note reopened it. In this repository closure does not entail shipment (current concrete counterexample: rf2-lzrza is closed while its PR #8912 remains open/unmerged), and an issue can be reopened because the same defect regressed, leaving the original description accurate. This revives the field-based slogan this owner's prior audit deliberately removed.

Minimal completion: keep closed-to-open as a strong signal to do the already-required timestamp history walk; remove "guaranteed", "certainty", "by construction", and the inference that close means shipped or that a note necessarily supersedes the description. State that history plus the tree decides what is current. No script, checklist, tracker field, or new method layer.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8922 (merged 2026-09-01). The closed-to-open shortcut is retained as a strong signal but no longer stated as a verdict: 'guaranteed', 'certainty' and 'by construction' are gone, and the two false inferences riding on it are named explicitly — closed does not mean shipped (items here close when a PR opens, so a closed item's work may be unmerged), and a reopening does not always supersede (an item reopened on a regression has an accurate description). History and the tree decide currency. No checklist, script, tracker field or new layer, per the item. Note the item's own DESCRIPTION was stale — it targets .claude/commands/mayor-dispatch.md, under a directory that no longer exists — while its audit note was live, which is the corrected wording working as described. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_readme_links.py --ci 0, python -m mkdocs build --strict 0; sabotage exit 1 naming loops.md:582 and the planted anchor, restore verified by git blob hash ed4a0b832723ac2ba5a9833731b467889638f427 on both sides.

MAYOR 2026-08-17 01:45 AUSEST — SCOPE CORRECTION FROM A FOURTH INSTANCE, WHICH HAPPENED AFTER THIS BEAD WAS FILED. The fix as drafted would NOT have prevented it.

THIS BEAD AS FILED describes the defect as 'the mayor does not establish which TEXT on the
bead is newest before briefing'. That is true and it is not the whole shape. Instance four
shows why.

INSTANCE FOUR, rf2-2rtt6.140, 2026-08-17 01:25. I DID order by timestamp — for the
SCHEDULING question. I read the comments newest-first, established that all four tracker
dependencies had closed and that the same-surface collision had cleared, and dispatched on a
correct decision. Then I took the CONTENT of the brief — 'the two routes left', the
(W+1).perWrite squeeze table, the rung figures — straight from the DESCRIPTION, which is the
bead's OLDEST text, written 2026-08-08.

Route (a) had shipped NINE DAYS EARLIER in PR #7702: ':p0/write-page' is already the
window's DEFAULT arm and rebuilds at '(count (:cells db))', the mounted width. Route (b)
landed in the SAME PR, DELETING the masking budget — and its absence is MACHINE-PINNED at
p0_ladder_structural.test.cjs:568, 'lacks(/const ALLOC_MASK_BUDGET_B/, the budget constant is
deleted)'. So the entire squeeze arithmetic the brief was built on came from a rule that no
longer exists. My fence 'route (b) is not yours' also contradicted the bead's standing
ruling, which is the composed package: 'route (a) AND route (b)... Not (a) alone, not (b)
alone.'

The worker checked at source, refused, wrote no code, and named it exactly: 'the dispatch
DECISION was correct — fence and neighbour both cleared; only its CONTENT was nine days
stale.'

SO THE RULE NEEDS BOTH HALVES:
  (1) Establish which TEXT is newest — 'bd comments --json' by created_at DESC,
      'bd history --json' walked newest-first to the first text-bearing change.
  (2) THEN VERIFY EVERY TECHNICAL CLAIM THE BRIEF WILL CARRY AT origin/main HEAD — not
      only the blockers. A route, a constant, a file path, a threshold, a prohibition and
      a table are each a claim, and a bead saying 'the two routes left' was written when
      two routes were left.

THE COMPRESSIBLE FORM, which may serve better than the incident: **A BEAD'S DESCRIPTION IS A
HISTORICAL DOCUMENT. ITS COMMENTS ARE THE CURRENT STATE.** The description records what was
true when the bead was filed and is never rewritten as the work lands; that is not a defect
in the tracker, it is what a description is for.

STILL KEEP IT PROPORTIONATE. This is one sentence-group in the 'Find + group' paragraph, not
a checklist, not a script, not a tracking field. mayor-dispatch.md's own line 23 warns that a
second copy of the template's text is 'the same drift one level down'.

RUNNING COST OF THE CLASS, so the fix can be sized honestly: four instances in one night,
all mine, all failed SAFE — one refused by a tracker guard ('bd close' blocked by
rf2-0moc4), two refused by workers who walked the history themselves, one caught by the
pre-commit hook. Two full dispatches were spent on refusals. The 'where the item and this
brief disagree, the ITEM governs' clause is what caught the two worker cases, and it should
not have had to.

This one I am not taking, for the reason the bead gives in terms: 'do not invent the destination'. Where the published normative set LIVES is a structural decision about the artefact, and in this project the spec IS the artefact.

MIKE, THE DECISION IS A THREE-WAY SPLIT and nothing else:
  1. What graduates to spec/ — normative contracts other code obeys.
  2. What graduates to the published guide (docs/core/hicasso/) — what a reader needs.
  3. What stays a working design record in docs/design/ — provenance, measurements, decision history.

MY RECOMMENDATION, so the call is cheap: GRADUATE ANSWERS, NOT DOCUMENTS. Move no file wholesale. The published guide carries what a reader needs, stated on the page; docs/design keeps the working records with their provenance intact.

WHY, AND IT IS FROM TONIGHT'S EVIDENCE RATHER THAN PREFERENCE. rf2-75q3l was exactly this problem in miniature: three published pages routed a reader's questions into docs/design, which mkdocs excludes, so each was a dead end on the built site. The same shape generalises. budgets.md and release-policy.md are measurement and policy RECORDS whose reader-facing conclusions belong on a guide page; the records themselves belong where their provenance pins and dated windows live, which is docs/design.

WHAT THAT LEAVES FOR spec/: the genuinely normative contracts from specification.md — the things another artefact must obey. Precedent already exists both ways: spec/004C carries the mount contract and spec/006 the adapter table, while decision-brief.md is a decision record and reads like one.

A CONSTRAINT WORTH KEEPING WHICHEVER WAY YOU RULE, from the bead: this is ordinary tracked git moves landed by PR, NOT a republication — the ai/ sources are retired and must not re-enter the flow.

NOTHING IS BLOCKED BEHIND THIS. rf2-75q3l is closed, amendments continue in place under the bead-citation fence, and the interim-custody note in docs/design/hicasso/product/README.md still points here. The cost of the hold is that interim custody keeps ageing, which is precisely what this bead exists to prevent.

title: [method] workers open PRs before they are done and the mayor merges them green — use draft PRs as the interlock
description:
THE MERGE LOOP AND THE DISPATCH BRIEF CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE MAYOR IS THE ONE WHO WROTE BOTH. Twice in one session a PR was merged while its author was still working on it.

THE TWO RULES, both of them mine, both individually right:
  DISPATCH BRIEF: "PUSH AS YOU GO, not at the end — pushed commits are the only durable worker state ... OPEN THE PR as soon as commits exist; a PR is not a claim of green."
  MERGE LOOP: merge on the five-clause criterion the moment it is met, and never block on CI.

Put together they say: workers publish PRs before they are finished, and the mayor merges them the moment CI goes green. **The gap between "CI is green" and "the author is done" is where both incidents happened.**

INCIDENT 1, 2026-08-15 ~11:55. #8323 merged while worker/hicaudit-5zmul was live. GitHub's delete_branch_on_merge removed its branch server-side; the worker's next push recreated it against a main that already carried its commits, producing DUPLICATE PR #8325 with a byte-identical three-file diff. Closed by hand after verifying the duplication rather than assuming it.

INCIDENT 2, 2026-08-16 ~01:33. #8333 merged while worker/w-lane-est was still running gates. Its own words: "#8333 — MERGED by the mayor while gates were still running; full gate table posted as a comment on it." It recovered well — cherry-picked the one wording fix the merge had not carried onto current main as #8339, and re-ran the doc gates on that branch — but that is a whole extra PR and an extra review cycle for work that would have ridden the first one.

NEITHER MERGE VIOLATED THE CRITERION. Both PRs were genuinely green on all five clauses when merged. The criterion is not the defect; the missing coordination is.

*** THE FIX, and it uses a mechanism that already exists rather than inventing a rule to remember. *** Brief workers to open the PR as a DRAFT and mark it ready for review as their last act before reporting done. `gh pr merge` REFUSES a draft, so the interlock is enforced by the host rather than by anyone's memory — which is the property the stash ban and the beads-boundary hook both have and the reason they hold. It preserves everything the push-as-you-go rule buys: commits are still pushed continuously and still survive a worker's death, and the mayor can still read the diff and the gate output at any time.

WHAT TO CHANGE:
  - docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md — the push-as-you-go clause gains "open it as a DRAFT; mark it ready as your last act before reporting done."
  - docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 1 — the merge criterion gains a line noting a draft PR is not a merge candidate, and WHY: the five clauses test the CHANGE, not whether its author has finished with it.
  - .claude/commands/mayor-merge.md — the same line, concretely: skip drafts in the sweep.

THE ALTERNATIVE, rejected: have the mayor check worker liveness before every merge. It works, but it is a rule that must be remembered on every merge forever, and it re-introduces exactly the worktree-activity sweep the merge loop deliberately does not do. The draft flag costs one command at the end of a worker's run and cannot be forgotten by the mayor at all.

SCOPE FENCE: those three files. HOT ZONE method surface — SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead. Note rf2-4228y also targets loops.md; SEQUENCE the two, do not run them together.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Run mkdocs as `python -m mkdocs` — bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH, and 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass. No fenced code blocks added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body.

title: [method] added-line triage still says it settles the common case
description:
FOUND BY rf2-cyt80's WORKER, which declined to widen its own scope and flagged this instead — correctly. The mayor's bead text is the defect here, not the worker's reading of it.

WHAT HAPPENED. rf2-cyt80's drift 3 OBSERVED that "neither mayor-hygiene.md nor loops.md section 5 contains the words cherry, patch-id or patch-equivalent". Its FIX clause then named only mayor-hygiene.md. The worker implemented exactly what the fix clause said and reported the gap rather than quietly extending its fence. So the concrete command file now carries the containment test and THE GENERIC PUBLISHED METHOD STILL DOES NOT.

THE GAP. docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md section 5 ("Branches") says to delete merged branches and never one whose change is not verifiably merged. It says nothing about HOW to establish containment — and under rebase-merge the obvious test is wrong in both directions.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE GENERIC DOC SPECIFICALLY. loops.md is the method as published for other repositories, and rebase-merge is not a local quirk. A reader adopting the method there gets the rule and not the trap. Measured here on 2026-08-15 over 63 worktrees: 60 branches read "ahead of main by 1 to 3 commits" and 58 of them were FULLY MERGED, because a rebase gives every merged commit a new SHA so it never becomes an ancestor of the trunk. Deleting on ancestry would have kept all 58 forever; ignoring the reading would have destroyed worker/receipts-hic081's 3 genuinely unmerged spike commits. `git cherry <trunk> <branch>` settled both directions in one command — `-` means an equivalent patch is already upstream, `+` means genuinely new.

WHAT TO WRITE, keeping loops.md's register — GENERIC, no bd commands, no repo paths, no PowerShell, no bead ids:
  - ancestry and the ahead-count are both useless for containment when the project merges by rebase, and they fail in OPPOSITE directions;
  - the test is patch-equivalence (`git cherry`), which answers both directions at once;
  - the measured warrant, stated without repo-specific identifiers: 60 branches read ahead, 58 were merged, 1 was not, one command separated them.

Cross-reference rather than restate: loops.md section 4 and the command files already explain why the ahead count misleads for LIVENESS. This is the same trap on a different question — containment, not liveness — and saying so is cheaper and more durable than a second copy of the reasoning.

SCOPE FENCE: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md ONLY. mayor-hygiene.md already has its half from rf2-cyt80; do not touch it again. This is a hot-zone method file, so SOLE TOUCHER, never parallel with another method-file bead.

GATE: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py plus mkdocs build --strict, which DOES cover docs/the-mayor-method/. Note that bare `mkdocs` returns exit 127 in Git Bash on this box because it is not on PATH — 127 is NO VERDICT, not a pass; run it as `python -m mkdocs`. No fenced code blocks are added, so the guide-samples digest gate is untouched; say so in the PR body rather than leaving it unstated.
acceptance_criteria: loops.md consistently describes the added-line scan as a non-conclusive triage hint; no sentence says it settles or proves containment. Conclusions still require the whole-patch comparison, and the delete-only-on-minus rule remains unchanged.
notes:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #8901 — REOPENED EXACT OWNER; NO DUPLICATE.

COMPLETENESS: The PR correctly fixes the asymmetric meaning of git cherry: '-' proves patch-equivalent containment, while '+' only says that equivalence was not found. Its new one-step "discriminating test" is still incomplete, however: searching only for the commit's added lines ignores file/path and location, multiplicity, order, and every deletion. A generic added line may already exist elsewhere at the tip while the branch's actual change is wholly absent, so "all present means the content landed" is false. Conversely, upstream can preserve the change after a rename, formatting edit, or follow-on rewrite while an exact added line is absent, so "any absent means genuinely outstanding" is also false.

CORRECTNESS: Keep the safe deletion rule (delete only on '-'), but do not present added-line presence as a containment verdict. It is at most a cheap triage hint. Before concluding either landed or outstanding, inspect the full patch against the current tip at the intended paths/locations, including deletions and replacements; a three-way comparison from the branch parent is sufficient. This matters even though the prose forbids using the test to delete: the current wording can still dismiss real unmerged work as a phantom.

IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY / NARROW REMEDY: Amend only the new paragraph in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md. Downgrade the added-line scan to a heuristic and name the full-patch review needed for a conclusion, or remove the purported one-step discriminator. Do not build a containment framework or change the conservative '-' deletion criterion.
AUDIT PR #8920: reopened exact owner. The repair correctly labels the added-line scan triage and explains both false directions, but the preceding sentence still says to run it first because "it settles the common case." That directly contradicts the next sentence ("triage, not a verdict") and the PR body's claim that the scan is no longer described as settling anything. A heuristic that cannot conclude either landed or outstanding does not settle even its common case; that word is the behavioral instruction likely to make a mayor stop before the required whole-patch comparison.

Minimal correction only: say the scan is cheap and useful for prioritising/starting the common investigation, without claiming settlement. Keep the full-patch conclusion and delete-only-on-minus rule unchanged; no new containment machinery or broader method edit.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8928 (merged 2026-09-01). The added-line scan no longer claims to settle anything: 'run it first because it settles the common case' becomes 'run it first because it costs seconds and tells you where to point the real check — never because it finishes one', removing the contradiction with 'triage, not a verdict' two sentences later. The full-patch conclusion and the delete-only-on-minus criterion are unchanged, per the audit's minimal correction.

title: docs(method): equal export row counts are not tracker-state equality
description:
MERGED-PR AUDIT #7394 / ledger durability. Before advancing the cursor, the merged main ledger at 43dcd2440a22a42e77d6ab773fb8df2a43a6a5a6 and the Dolt remote each contained 1,938 issues but different facts. Git alone carried rf2-3jw04, rf2-jv36i, rf2-lhdp0 and newer closes/statuses for rf2-2rtt6.52/.63; Dolt carried three newer audit issues. scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1 exported Dolt wholesale; its row-count floor passed (1,938 == 1,938), and commit 667c744dc875e31e4d4874586afcbec2d01ceb8a silently removed the three Git-only issues and reverted .52/.63. This is the remaining equal-count/set-substitution sibling of rf2-51uz1's time-travel fault.

Recovery proved the bounded mechanism: timestamp-aware bd import of only Git issue rows into Dolt created the three missing IDs, updated exactly the two newer Git rows, skipped stale rows, preserved every newer Dolt row/cursor, and yielded a verified 1,941-ID union with zero field mismatches.

DO: before checkpoint overwrites .beads/issues.jsonl, compare HEAD's issue IDs/updated_at/status to the fresh Dolt export. Either import newer/missing Git issue rows timestamp-safely then re-export, or refuse with exact IDs/fields. Keep the existing row-count floor, but do not treat equal counts as equality. Add a regression where HEAD and Dolt have equal row counts but disjoint one-for-one substitutions plus one newer state on each side; neither fact may be lost. No generalized sync service needed.
acceptance_criteria: loops.md no longer equates equal export counts plus a clean Git tree with tracker consistency. It distinguishes working-export cleanliness from Dolt-vs-Git state and points to the existing checkpoint/export comparison for the latter after contention clears. The remote-tracking-ref rebase guidance remains unchanged; no new mechanism.
notes:
AUDIT PR #8913 (2026-09-01) — REOPENED exact GC-retired owner.

The remote-tracking-ref rebase guidance is correct and complete. The tracker-contention addition is not. Completeness: comparing the working export to Git never reads the database, so it cannot establish that a timed-out mutation/export committed, that Dolt has no newer rows, or that the store is healthy. Correctness: "equal and clean means consistent and nothing is owed" repeats this owner's measured fault. Commit 667c744dc875 deleted three Git-only issues and reverted two newer statuses at 1,938 == 1,938; equal counts hid one-for-one substitutions. A clean tree only proves the tracked export matches HEAD. The existing checkpoint guard therefore compares stable issue id, updated_at and status and says explicitly that equal counts are not equality.

Minimal completion: retain contention-until-proven-otherwise and the safe non-destructive first look, but label size/line-count plus clean-tree as evidence about the working export only. Once contention clears, verify Dolt against Git through the existing checkpoint/export comparison before saying the store is consistent or nothing is owed. No new sync service, recovery framework or probe.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #8922 (merged 2026-09-01). loops.md's tracker-contention paragraph no longer claims the cheap export check establishes store consistency. It keeps contention-until-proven-otherwise and the safe non-destructive first look, now labelled as evidence about the WORKING EXPORT and the working tree only — it never reads the database, so it cannot show that a timed-out mutation committed, that the store holds nothing newer, or that the store is healthy. Equal counts are explicitly stated not to be equality, citing this owner's own measured fault: a checkpoint passed its floor at 1,938 against 1,938 while dropping three issues and reverting two newer statuses through one-for-one substitution. Size is named as the smoke test against truncation it was built for, and verification is deferred to the existing checkpoint comparison on stable id, updated_at and status once contention clears. No sync service, recovery framework or probe. The remote-tracking-ref rebase guidance the audit called correct and complete is untouched.

title: Retrospective facade-export classification sweep (re-frame.core slice + the manifest :justification/:action axes; Story = rf2-i6kh, Xray = rf2-ar67) - external-alpha prep CALLED 2026-09-04; gates the first v0.0.1.alpha tag
description:
EXTERNAL-ALPHA PREP CALLED 2026-09-04 21:05 AUSEST by delegated ruling (Mike delegated the call on 2026-09-04; operator-reversible; full ruling, reviewer analysis and implementation guidance in the notes). This bead is now SLICE 1 of the three-slice retrospective facade-export sweep and is a dispatchable single-worker task. It GATES the first v0.0.1.alpha tag: rf2-kmqx3 depends on this bead and on the two slices split out of it, rf2-i6kh (Story) and rf2-ar67 (Xray). Nothing here waits for the tag.

## What it is

spec/Conventions.md lines 1199-1250 define the facade-export audit in two halves. The FORWARD half is active since commit 037d7b2029 (2026-06-04): every new facade export records tier, owner spec, facade-placement justification and recommended action in its PR (lines 1211-1216). The RETROSPECTIVE half is "the full retrospective sweep of every existing non-front-porch export - and the manifest table it produces", deferred to API-freeze / external-alpha prep (line 1218) - which is now called. The deadline is Conventions' own (line 1228): before the first meaningful external alpha/beta, explicitly NOT before v1, because the moment real users copy examples a namespace move becomes a breaking change, and Conventions lines 1234-1244 forbid a retained-for-migration tier after that.

## Scope of THIS bead (slice 1)

1. The two missing manifest axes. spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn carries tier/owner/status only; :justification and :action appear 0 times in it and in the generated spec/api-manifest.edn. Add both as curated axes on every :facade? true row (:action one of :keep :rename :move :internal-public), carry them through implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj into the generated rows, and make clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check refuse a :facade? true row missing :justification or carrying an unknown :action, with tests. Not required on :facade? false rows.
2. The re-frame.core table. 103 manifest rows, all :facade? true: 17 front-porch (quick keeps), 86 non-front-porch (55 advanced, 27 tooling, 4 testing) each given a disposition and justification. Consumer counts and the counting loop are in the notes (4082 in-repo file-refs across the 86; top: make-frame 687, app-db-value 301, reg-machine 276, register-listener! 235; 18 names with five or fewer files; group-by-event-with-events has zero non-test consumers).
3. Execution of the clear moves: small ones (under ~10 consumer files) in this PR; larger ones as one bead per owning subsystem, --deps discovered-from:rf2-2hpxo, with bd dep add rf2-kmqx3 <new-id> so the tag waits on the move.

Slices 2 and 3 (NOT this bead): rf2-i6kh widens the manifest's facade? predicate (gen.clj:748-753, currently re-frame.core only) to re-frame.story and reconciles its 55 :implementation facade rows, which the invariant at gen.clj:845-863 has never reached; rf2-ar67 enrols day8.re-frame2-xray.core, which has zero manifest rows against 16 public vars. Each dispatches only after the previous slice's PR has MERGED (shared files: gen.clj, the sidecar, spec/API.md).

## Discriminator (bounded freeze pass, not a carve-up)

KEEP when one import supports a coherent ordinary app-authoring workflow even if the tier is advanced/tooling (Conventions lines 1222-1226: single-import product facades stay coherent on purpose). MOVE only when an existing owning namespace is already a clearer door and ordinary facade users do not need the name; never invent a namespace to tidy a column. RENAME only for a concrete lifecycle-verb-law or vocabulary violation. INTERNAL-PUBLIC only for a deliberate supported host/tool embed seam; a var used solely by repository internals leaves the facade at :implementation. Consumer counts are evidence, never the verdict. CONTESTED (tier ambiguity, or a move on anything over ~100 consumer files): record keep with the uncertainty in :justification, list the name on this bead for Mike, and do not hold the PR or the tag on it.

## Hot zone and sequencing

spec/API.md is a one-toucher file (and spec/Conventions.md if the two fields get a sentence there; optional - the sidecar header can carry the vocabulary). This PR runs alone against any other toucher of those files. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/** and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn are otherwise isolated surfaces.

## Gates, by path, foreground to completion

From implementation/scripts/api-manifest: clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.api-md-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.story-spec-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.xray-spec-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.skills-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.doc-guide-check; clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.doc-api-check; clojure -M:test (the api-manifest job, .github/workflows/lint.yml lines 609-700). For any executed move: the substrate suites its consumers live in, scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for docs/ and spec/ pages, scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci for READMEs beside source. Nothing validates prose or table columns; say in the PR body they were checked by hand.

## Acceptance

1. :justification and :action exist in the sidecar and the generated manifest, required and validated on every :facade? true row, with unit tests in implementation/scripts/api-manifest/test/.
2. All 103 re-frame.core rows carry both fields (tier and owner confirmed while there).
3. Every ruled move or rename is executed, or has a bead that rf2-kmqx3 depends on.
4. Contested names, if any, are listed on this bead with the reason.
5. The api-manifest lint job is green.

Deferred 2026-07-25 behind S7 (rf2-vxgfnd.99), whose 2026-07-31 closure carried the substrate removal but not the tag. Edged behind rf2-kmqx3 on 2026-08-22; edge reversed by the 2026-09-04 ruling. The former "NOT a Freehand audit" paragraph is deleted: implementation/freehand was removed by PR #8322 (rf2-0yp7w) and the manifest carries no Freehand rows.

REOPENED 2026-09-05 BY THE MAYOR, CORRECTING ITS OWN WRONG RE-CLOSE. This bead was NOT a status revert. It carries a real, unaddressed post-merge audit finding, and my earlier re-close destroyed it. Nothing about the audit's obligation has been discharged; the acceptance criteria in the audit note above stand in full.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG. I discriminated "audit reopen" from "status revert" with a case-sensitive grep for a fixed marker set — AUDIT-REOPEN, "REOPENED THIS EXACT", REOPENED, "still owed", "residual" — plus a check that the notes length was unchanged across the newest few snapshots. Both halves failed, and each failed in the reassuring direction.

THE GREP: this bead's audit text opens "AUDIT 2026-09-04 — MERGED PR #NNNN: reopened because ..." — LOWERCASE "reopened", under a header matching none of my patterns. I ran a control ("external-alpha prep", 1 hit) and concluded the instrument was live. IT WAS: the grep ran fine. A CONTROL PROVES THE INSTRUMENT EXECUTES; IT DOES NOT PROVE THE PATTERN SET IS COMPLETE. To test a pattern set you must control against a POSITIVE INSTANCE OF THE THING THE PATTERNS ARE MEANT TO CATCH — here, a bead known to carry an audit note — not against arbitrary text known to be present.

THE LENGTH TEST: I compared the notes length across the immediately-adjacent snapshot pair at the reopen boundary. That assumes the status change and the note are ONE mutation. They are not: an audit commonly appends its note in a SEPARATE, LATER mutation, so the adjacent pair reads unchanged on a genuine audit. The corrected probe compares the notes length AT THE LAST CLOSE against the NEWEST notes length: growth means text was written while the bead was closed, which is exactly what an audit does and what a bare status revert never does. On this bead that probe reads a clear growth.

WHAT EXPOSED IT: running the corrected probe against a CONTROL BEAD I already believed was a genuine audit reopen. It reported "revert" for that bead, which could not be true — and that contradiction, not any new evidence about this bead, is what falsified the method. A probe that disagrees with a case you are confident about is telling you the probe is wrong.

TWO BEADS WERE WRONGLY RE-CLOSED BY THE OLD METHOD (this one and its sibling) and both are now reopened. Two others re-closed in the same session were re-checked with the corrected probe and confirmed genuine reverts: their notes did not grow while closed. Those closes stand.

THE STANDING RULE THIS VIOLATED, from the method doc: "read the item's notes before re-closing anything — the instinct to re-close a reverted item destroys a real finding and looks like tidiness." The instinct was mine, and the tidiness was the tell.
AUDIT DISCHARGED 2026-09-05 02:56 AUSEST. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9217, branch worker/epochjust-a, one commit, rebased on origin/main 8ccce0117a. Second carrier of the 2026-09-04 audit finding (the first re-close was wrong; the mayor's own correction note above records why).

WITHDRAWN — THE FALSE CLAIM IN THIS BEAD'S OWN DELIVERY RECORD. The SLICE 1 DELIVERED note above, in the paragraph beginning 'That column is empty for a MEASURED reason', asserts of the 30 optional-artefact wrappers: 'the code ships in a separate Maven artefact and the wrapper raises a documented :rf.error/<x>-artefact-missing when it is absent, so moving the export converts a guided failure into a hard require failure. Every one of the 30 was cross-checked against the 51 defwrapper forms ...; all 30 are there.' THAT SENTENCE IS WITHDRAWN. The cross-check against the 51 defwrapper forms was real and its arithmetic holds; the RAISE generalisation over all 30 does not. Seven of the 30 are epoch, and only ONE of those seven (replace-frame-state!, :on-absent :throw) raises. The correct statement is: 24 of the 30 raise, 6 degrade silently. This is an append rather than a deletion because the notes field is a 43KB append-only record and bd's --notes REPLACES it; a reader reaching that paragraph now reaches this withdrawal from the same field.

RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE, EVERY ONE OF THE SIX. implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc, read whole: epoch-history :empty-vec, restore-epoch! :false, replay-epoch! :false, register-epoch-listener! :nil, unregister-epoch-listener! :nil, epoch-silence-current? :false, clear-epoch-listeners! :nil, replace-frame-state! :throw, projected-record :nil, projected-history :empty-vec. core_artefact.cljc lines 142-153 fix the sentinel semantics (:empty-vec -> [], :empty-map -> {}). The audit's transcription of which wrapper carries which value was NOT assumed; it was read off the file.

THE CENSUS RE-RUN ON THREE AXES — THE AUDIT'S ARITHMETIC IS EXACT. (1) Rationale-text axis: 38 distinct facade rows carried the raise rationale. 39 lines match 'artefact require'; the 39th is feature-loaded?, which DESCRIBES the pattern and asserts no raise (accurate, untouched, and not a defwrapper at all). Two further 'artefact-missing' matches, at sidecar lines 879 and 904, are prose comments rather than row justifications — an awk key-carry artefact, not extra rows. (2) :on-absent axis: 51 defwrapper forms across implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_*.cljc plus implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc; 17 are non-throwing (9 epoch, 8 schemas). (3) Wrapper-name axis, run in the REVERSE direction, which is what closes the set: of those 17 non-throwing wrappers exactly SIX are re-frame.core facade rows — the audit's six. The three epoch listener wrappers were retired from the facade in API-shrink #4 and carry no re-frame.core row; the eight schemas wrappers (app-schema-at, app-schema-meta-at, app-schemas, app-schemas-digest, set-schema-validator!, set-schema-fns!, set-schema-explainer!, set-schema-printer!) are :facade? false, rowed only under re-frame.schemas, and carry no :justification, so no false record exists there. reg-head and reg-error-projector are correctly excluded: both are defreg-macro forms (core.cljc:619 and :625) over the PRIVATE -reg-error-projector / -reg-head wrappers, both :on-absent :throw. WHAT CHANGED. spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn — the six :justification strings rewritten to state the row's actual :on-absent value and the two real reasons for :keep: (a) the silent degrade is only expressible from the ALWAYS-LOADED facade, since a subnamespace door makes a leftover dev-time call site a hard require failure in a release build that omits the artefact and pulls the artefact onto the production classpath against Conventions Bundle-isolation conformance; (b) the release DCE seam — the surface is dev-tier, gated on interop/debug-enabled? and elided by Closure DCE under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false. NO CODE CHANGED — the audit ruled the :keep decisions may remain, so a code change would have been a scope change and was not made.

SOURCES CITED, READ NOT PARAPHRASED. spec/Tool-Pair.md line 88 (Time-travel, Artefact home) names the per-surface sentinels and calls replace-frame-state! 'the lone exception'. spec/009-Instrumentation.md line 2273, the :rf.error/epoch-artefact-missing catalogue row: 'The wrapper cannot degrade silently ... so it raises rather than returning a sentinel like the other epoch surfaces'. spec/Conventions.md line 1854 (Adapter shipping convention, Dependency direction): 'The epoch surface is dev-tier — its public re-exports ... degrade silently to empty-vector / false / no-op when the artefact is absent rather than throwing'. spec/API.md carries NO epoch raise claim, so nothing there needed correcting.

GATES, foreground, exit codes captured to file and quoted from the file. gen --check on the UNTOUCHED base 0 ('in sync (543 public vars)') — the before-run proving the tree started clean; gen (regenerate) 0; gen --check after 0; clojure -M:test api-manifest 0 (98/194); implementation/epoch 0 (556/7259); implementation/core 0 (2177/11194 — the peer's 2175/11142 was an older tip); gen --check and -M:test re-run on the FINAL rebased base, 0 and 0 (543 vars; 98/194); scripts/check_doc_slugs.py 0 with an empty log. PLANTED FAULT, not a green: blanking the :justification on the epoch-history row — one of the six — reddened gen --check at exit 2 naming re-frame.core/epoch-history. Restored and verified: git hash-object and git hash-object --no-filters both match the pre-plant copy and numstat returned to 22/6.

WHICH GATE ACTUALLY INSPECTS THIS CHANGE. The manifest generator's --check arm and its test suite, proven live by that plant. Both changed files are .edn and this PR touches NO markdown, so check_doc_slugs.py (run anyway, exit 0) and mkdocs build --strict inspect nothing of it; citing either as coverage would be citing a green that looked at nothing.

LEFT DELIBERATELY. replace-frame-state!'s justification is accurate as written and untouched. feature-loaded? / features / require-feature! use the same boilerplate opener but assert no raise — accurate, untouched. The 32 remaining raise-claiming rows are all correct. The eight non-throwing schemas wrappers carry no facade row and so no false record; if they are ever promoted to the facade they will need justifications written to the degrade shape, not the raise shape.

MAYOR RULING 2026-09-05 — THE APPENDED WITHDRAWAL STANDS; DO NOT EXCISE THE ORIGINAL CLAIM.

The rf2-2hpxo second carrier asked whether the mayor wants a true excision of the false "all 30 throw" sentence from this bead's delivery record, having withdrawn it by appended note instead. It was right to ask rather than do, and right in what it did. The answer is: the appended withdrawal is the correct and final form.

WHY, on three grounds.

1. THE RECORD IS APPEND-ONLY BY DESIGN, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT TRUSTWORTHY. A tracker note that can be silently rewritten is not evidence. This project's whole audit chain rests on being able to read what a carrier actually claimed at the time, then read the correction beside it. Excising the claim would leave the correction referring to something no longer present, and would erase the fact that a carrier once believed it — which is exactly the provenance a third carrier needs. The same principle already governs the design corpus: corrections restate a passage with an italic note giving its former wording, the reason and the date, rather than overwriting it.

2. THE MECHANICAL RISK IS REAL AND ASYMMETRIC. `notes` on this bead is ~43,000 characters. `bd update --notes` REPLACES the field, and CLAUDE.md records ~72,800 characters lost across five beads in one session by exactly that mistake, with rf2-9wmqd going 46,569 -> 3,294. A true excision means the documented chunked rewrite — split at line boundaries into ~18,000-character chunks, `--notes` for the first and `--append-notes` for the rest, then probe for known content from the start, middle and end rather than comparing lengths, because chunking shifts them by a byte or two. That is a multi-step destructive operation on a 43KB field to delete one sentence that is already marked false in the same field. The downside of getting it wrong dwarfs the upside of getting it right.

3. THE STATED GOAL IS ALREADY MET. The audit's acceptance wanted the false claim not to mislead. The withdrawal quotes the offending sentence verbatim and gives the corrected figure — 24 of the 30 raise, 6 degrade silently — so a reader who reaches the claim reaches its correction from the same field, in the same read. Nothing further is owed.

THE GENERAL RULE THIS SETS, for any future carrier facing the same shape: WITHDRAW BY APPENDING, NEVER BY DELETING. Quote the sentence you are withdrawing, state what is true instead, and date it. Treat an instruction to "remove" a claim from a tracker note as an instruction to NEGATE it in place unless the operator explicitly asks for excision — and say that you have, as this carrier did.

MAYOR, BACKLOG-REREAD LOOP 2026-08-15 21:52 AUSEST — STAYS DEFERRED. Its release condition READS as met and is NOT met, so I am recording the discrimination rather than leaving the next reread to re-derive it.

THE CONDITION, as written on this bead: "reopen when EITHER holds: 1. rf2-vxgfnd.99 (S7 + alpha tag) closes, or 2. Mike calls api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly."

CONDITION 1'S PROXY HAS FIRED. rf2-vxgfnd.99 is CLOSED — "EPIC S7 — Helix-removal wave + alpha tag", closed 2026-07-31. A literal read of the condition releases this bead today.

*** DO NOT RELEASE IT ON THAT READING. *** The condition names "S7 + ALPHA TAG", and the alpha tag never happened. `git ls-remote --tags origin` returns ZERO tags at this tick — nothing has ever been published from this repository. The epic closed carrying the S7 half and not the tag half, so the proxy moved while the thing it was standing for did not.

AND THE TAG IS NOT MERELY LATE — IT IS BLOCKED. rf2-uelji records that Clojars' verified-group policy refuses the FIRST publish of every day8/re-frame2-* coordinate: a new project may not be created in an unverified group, and day8 is not reverse-domain so it cannot be verified. That is an operator-only action, and it gates all 13 implementation artefacts and 5 tool jars. So "published artefact" is still exactly the moving target this bead deferred itself against.

THIS IS THE INVERSE OF THE USUAL FINDING. The loop normally catches a dependency that outlived what it was enforcing — the blocker shipped and the bead stayed blocked. Here the blocker's RECORD closed while its SUBSTANCE did not ship, so the bead reads releasable and is not. Both cases are found the same way, by testing the substance rather than the status field.

THE OPERATIVE GATE IS THEREFORE NOW: rf2-uelji clearing (which yields the tag, satisfying condition 1 in substance), OR condition 2 — the operator calling api-freeze / external-alpha prep explicitly, which needs no tag at all and remains available at any time.

Not a rejection. Conventions mandates the work; this is sequencing only, unchanged from the original disposition.

title: api(trace): delete re-frame.trace's six alias defs; migrate 97 test files to re-frame.trace.tooling
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from trace-epoch.md (ref trace-epoch.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.trace` is a third door to six fns that already have a home (`re-frame.trace.tooling`) and a facade (`re-frame.core`). `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:944-957`:

```clojure
(def register-listener!     rf.trace.tooling/register-listener!)
(def unregister-listener!   rf.trace.tooling/unregister-listener!)
(def clear-listeners!       rf.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!)
(def trace-buffer           rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer)
(def clear-trace-buffer!    rf.trace.tooling/clear-trace-buffer!)
(def configure-trace-buffer! rf.trace.tooling/configure-trace-buffer!)
```

The comment above them (`:945-949`) calls these "the canonical app-facing names" (rf2-ic1sv pick c, 2026-05-21). The stream-parameterized facade verb `(rf/register-listener! :trace id f)` superseded that on 2026-07-08 (rf2-9flalp, `89bb759305`); the door was never retired. Non-test code reaching any of the six through this namespace at tip: **core.cljc's own delegation only** (`core.cljc:2164` `:trace (rf.trace/register-listener! id f)`, `:2178`, `:2216`, `:2222`); every other hit is a comment. Tests, however, spell it everywhere: 97 test files (`register-listener!` 48, `unregister-listener!` 46, `clear-listeners!` 50, `trace-buffer` 1, the other two 0) — `git grep -l -E '(rf\.trace|re-frame\.trace)/(register-listener!|unregister-listener!|clear-listeners!|trace-buffer|clear-trace-buffer!|configure-trace-buffer!)' -- ':!ai/' | grep -E '_test\.|/test/|/tests/' | wc -l`.

The manifest rosters none of `re-frame.trace`, `re-frame.trace.tooling`, `re-frame.trace.projection` (`grep -c '"re-frame.trace' spec/api-manifest.edn` → 0), so the six are un-tiered public vars with no contract behind them.

## Target API

None added. `re-frame.trace` keeps the hot emit path (`emit!` `:860`, `emit-error!`, the bracket macros, `trace-event-frame`) and the `:trace/emit!` hook registration. The listener registry and ring are reached by the facade (`rf/register-listener! :trace …`, `rf/trace-buffer`, `rf/clear-trace-buffer!`, `(rf/configure! {:trace-buffer …})`) or, for fixtures and tools that already require it, `re-frame.trace.tooling/…`.

```clojure
;; core.cljc after: the facade delegates to the home directly
:trace  (rf.trace.tooling/register-listener! id f)      ; :2164
:trace  (rf.trace.tooling/unregister-listener! id)      ; :2178
trace-buffer        rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer        ; :2216 (fence already lifted by @trace-epoch.1)
clear-trace-buffer! rf.trace.tooling/clear-trace-buffer! ; :2222
```

`core.cljc`'s ns form gains `[re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace.tooling]` (it already requires `re-frame.trace.projection`, `:15`; tooling requires only `interop`, `late-bind`, `projection` — no cycle). The static require graph does not change (core → trace → tooling today); only the edge's spelling moves. `trace.cljc`'s own require of tooling STAYS: `trace.cljc:197` uses `rf.trace.tooling/call-with-deferred-fanout` on the JVM.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area; codex concurs on this item verbatim: "retire the unused third-door aliases and align the spec, manifest, docs, and generated eval recipes" and "Retire the duplicate public read/clear spellings in `re-frame.trace`; keep implementation functions in their owning namespace." @observability.n's table lists `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` as unrowed with 0 consumers and may propose the same deletion — the coordinator de-duplicates; this bead carries the test migration either way.

## Deletion list

- `trace.cljc:944-957` (comment block + six defs).
- The rf2-ic1sv "pick c" rationale in `trace.cljc:41-48` (rewrite: the require stays for `:197`; production DCE is by `goog.DEBUG` gating of call sites, as `:44-48` already says).
- Stale prose naming the alias: `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:339-350` (also stale on its own terms — "thin late-bind shells" describes the pre-rf2-ic1sv `5b0eb9f9b8` world; after this bead `re-frame.trace` has no wrappers at all; the sentinel and `expectedAllowListHits` are NOT changed); `core.cljc:2103` comment; `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:50` (`re-frame.trace/configure-trace-buffer!` → `re-frame.trace.tooling/…`); `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/drop_in.cljc:73`; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:27`; `testbeds/spec-helpers.cjs:9`; `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:331`; `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md:502` (Xray spec rule: every `tools/xray/` dispatch updates `tools/xray/spec/*` in the same PR).

## Consumers to migrate

- 97 test files, mechanical: `rf.trace/<name>` (158 files alias `[re-frame.trace :as rf.trace]`, 44 as `trace`) → `rf.trace.tooling/<name>`, adding `[re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace.tooling]` where absent (20 of the 97 already require it). Do NOT drop `[re-frame.trace :as rf.trace]` blindly — most of these files also use `rf.trace/emit!` / `trace-event-frame`; remove the require only where it becomes unused (the JVM linter / `npm run test:cljs-isolation` will say). Do not re-architect fixtures onto `re-frame.test-support` in this bead (5 files use both; `test_support.cljc:552` already clears via tooling) — rename only.
- Optional trivia folded here (same door, one site): Story `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:354` `(rf.trace/emit! :debug ::append-assertion-failed {…})` → `(rf/emit-trace-event! …)` (same 3-arity; file already requires `re-frame.core`; `:55` comment). The fable doc's second site, `a11y.cljs:377`, no longer exists at tip.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- **Spec:** none — verified: no `spec/` line names `re-frame.trace/<one of the six>`; `spec/Conventions.md`'s only `re-frame.trace` mentions are the `:rf.trace/*` tag namespace and `Conventions.md:762` (`group-by-event` → `re-frame.trace.projection`), both unaffected. No hot-zone file.
- **Manifest:** no rows exist for `re-frame.trace` → `gen --check` unchanged; state so.
- **Docs / skills:** `git grep -n -E '(rf\.trace|re-frame\.trace)/(register-listener!|clear-listeners!|trace-buffer)' -- docs/ skills/` → 0 at tip; re-run after the change.
- **Tests:** the 97-file rename above; no new tests.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Waits for @trace-epoch.1 (same `core.cljc:2195-2222` lines). Large mechanical diff across `implementation/**/test`, `tools/**/test`, `testbeds/`: dispatch when no other open PR is mid-flight on the trace tests (`trace_listener_*` files especially), or rebase promptly. No hot-zone file.

## Risks

- A test that pins `re-frame.trace`'s public set by reflection would red — none found (`git grep -n -E "re-frame\.trace[\"' ]" -- 'implementation/**/test/**'` finds only the tooling/projection nss).
- `check-bundle-isolation.cjs:348-350` says a `:require [re-frame.trace.tooling]` in a `core/*` ns is "most likely" how the sentinel leaks. That is a heuristic comment about a symptom, not a rule; the require was already transitively present. The gate decides: green is required, and the comment is rewritten to describe the static-alias world truthfully.

## Local dossier

`ai/findings/API-review/fable/trace-and-epoch-read-surface.md` (local-only pointer).
acceptance_criteria:
- `git grep -n -E '(rf\.trace|re-frame\.trace)/(register-listener!|unregister-listener!|clear-listeners!|trace-buffer|clear-trace-buffer!|configure-trace-buffer!)' -- ':!ai/' ':!.beads'` → 0 lines (code, tests, comments, prose).
- `grep -n -E '^\(def (register-listener!|unregister-listener!|clear-listeners!|trace-buffer|clear-trace-buffer!|configure-trace-buffer!)' implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc` → 0.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` and `sed -n '2160,2225p'` shows the four delegation sites targeting `rf.trace.tooling/…`.
- `scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh` and `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` green (foreground, to completion); `npm run test:cljs` and `npm run test:cljs-isolation` green.
- `npm run test:bundle-isolation` green; `git diff -- implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` is comment-only.
- The five prose/comment sites listed under Deletion list no longer name a `re-frame.trace/` alias; `tools/xray/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md` and `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md` name the facade or tooling form.
