title: bug(skill-implementor): the :derivation/* family gating disagrees with the checklist family table
description:
Found while fixing rf2-k2r1 and deliberately left out of that PR (its criterion 8 fences off 'optional-capability policy beyond this stale mapping').

skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md's family table maps the split pair :derivation/algebra-graph + :derivation/algebra-graph-subs-machines to 'Q6 Tool-Pair inspection'.

spec/Implementor-Checklist.md Part 3's family table says :derivation/* is gated by 'nothing declares it - but every current fixture is cross-tagged, so in practice Q1', and elaborates at :124 that a Q1=no port runs neither derivation fixture while a Q2/Q8=no port runs only the subs+machines one.

Those are different claims: the skill says Q6, the normative owner says structurally-ungated-but-Q1-in-practice. Worth checking which is right before a port derives its claim from the skill. Note the checklist also lists :derivation/* among the always-run families at :120 while the same document calls it Q1-in-practice at :564 - so the normative side may itself need a reading, and this bead should start there rather than assuming the skill is simply wrong.

Not urgent: unlike rf2-k2r1 this does not create a false-green on a v1-required surface, because every current derivation fixture is cross-tagged and therefore filtered per-fixture anyway.

Constraint carried over from rf2-k2r1: scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py now derives its required-root set from the checklist's 'nothing - always run' rows. :derivation/* is deliberately NOT matched by that derivation (its cell reads 'nothing declares it'), and a self-test pins that exclusion. Any change to how :derivation/* is gated must keep that derivation honest.
close_reason:

The suspected checklist self-contradiction reconciles, and the checklist already says how. :122 lists :derivation/* among five families no question declines; :124 then states in bold that 'not declinable' is not 'every fixture runs' -- the subset rule is applied per FIXTURE, not per family -- so :564's 'in practice Q1' is the same claim, not a competing one. That reconciling paragraph landed 2026-09-03 (a8b4eaff6a), a day BEFORE this bead was filed. So the normative side needs no reading and no follow-up bead.

Settled against the corpus rather than the prose. derivation-graph-algebra.edn carries #{:core/sub :fsm/flat :derivation/algebra-graph-subs-machines}; derivation-graph-algebra-full.edn adds :flow/basic, :rf.http/managed, :routing/match-url and :routing/blocking. title: surface-review(reagent-slim): the static-markup boolean roster has the same omissions rf2-r9kf fixed in SSR
description:
`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` carries its OWN boolean-attribute roster, independent of the SSR artefact's:

    (def ^:private boolean-attributes
      #{"allowfullscreen" "async" "autofocus" "autoplay" "checked"
        "controls" "default" "defer" "disabled" "formnovalidate" "hidden"
        "loop" "multiple" "muted" "novalidate" "open" "playsinline"
        "readonly" "required" "reversed" "selected" "itemscope"})

Measured against the installed react-dom 19.2.0 it is missing the presence names `inert`, `noModule`, `scoped`, `seamless`, `disablePictureInPicture` and `disableRemotePlayback`, and it models NO stringifying class at all — so `contentEditable`, `draggable`, `spellCheck`, `autoReverse`, `externalResourcesRequired`, `focusable` and `preserveAlpha` do not get `="true"` / `="false"` treatment, and `download` / `capture` have no overloaded-boolean arm. That is the SAME defect class rf2-r9kf fixed in `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers`: a false value that carries meaning is dropped, and the markup asserts the opposite of what the author wrote.

WHY IT WAS NOT CAUGHT. `reagent2.dom.parity-cljs-test` already renders both ways and compares byte-for-byte against `react-dom/server.renderToStaticMarkup`, which is the right shape of check — but it is CORPUS-DRIVEN, so it only catches what its corpus happens to contain. None of the eleven names above appears to be in it. That is the same blind spot in a different disguise from the one the rf2-r9kf audit found: there, a parity test between two consumers of a shared roster could not see the roster's omissions; here, a genuine external parity test cannot see what its corpus omits.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, IF THIS IS DISPATCHED. PR #9207 landed `implementation/ssr/test/react_dom_probe/boolean_attr_classes.cjs`, which derives its candidate names from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` table and its boolean-ness from react-dom's own dev-build warning — so the roster under test cannot bound the probe. reagent-slim's parity test runs under `:node-test` with live `react-dom/server` available, so it could enumerate the same React-derived name set directly at test time rather than through a committed fixture, which is strictly better than what SSR could do. That is the cheap version: drive the existing parity harness over a React-derived name list instead of a hand-written corpus.

SCOPE NOTE. Separate artefact, separate roster, separate emitter — nothing is shared with `re-frame.ssr`, and rf2-r9kf deliberately did not touch it. Whether reagent-slim should model the stringifying and overloaded classes at all is a real question rather than an obvious yes: it is a static-markup emitter for a Reagent-compatible surface, and its IMPL-SPEC §8.7 already allow-lists known divergences from React. Decide that before widening the roster.
notes:
MAYOR SEQUENCING NOTE 2026-09-05. AND THE SHARP PART, which generalises past this bead: reagent-slim's react-dom parity test is CORPUS-DRIVEN, so it only catches what the corpus happens to contain. That is the same structural blind spot the SSR audit named from the other side — there, two serialisers sharing one roster made their parity test agree on the same wrong answer. A parity test can only validate what something OUTSIDE the thing under test supplies. The SSR fix (PR #9207) shows the shape of the answer: its probe takes candidate names from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` and boolean-ness from React's own dev-build warning, so the roster under test cannot bound the probe. Reuse that technique here rather than extending the corpus.

ON DISPATCH: re-verify at tip. slimadapter-a may have touched neighbouring code, and PR #9207's probe (implementation/ssr/test/react_dom_probe/boolean_attr_classes.cjs) is the model to read first — it is committed and its .edn fixture is regenerated by hand, which is a limitation that worker recorded deliberately: a react-dom bump does not automatically red. Decide whether reagent-slim wants the same trade or an automatic regeneration.
close_reason:
FIXED. PR #9224 (worker/slimbool-a), gates green, opened not yet merged. Three files, all inside implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/.

THE PREMISE HELD, AND WAS WORSE THAN FILED. The bead described the roster as missing six presence names and modelling no stringifying class. Both true. But `emit-attribute` consulted the roster ONLY in its `(true? v)` arm, and `(false? v)` returned nil unconditionally — so a boolean value on ANY name outside the 22 was dropped in BOTH directions, not just on false. `{:aria-expanded true}` emitted nothing where react-dom emits `aria-expanded="true"`; `{:inert true}` emitted nothing; `{:download true}` emitted nothing. The bead named aria only implicitly (through the stringifying class); it is the loudest case, because boolean ARIA state is ordinary SPA authoring.

THE SIX NAMES ARE ALL REAL, re-measured against the installed react-dom 19.2.0 rather than transcribed, as the dispatch asked: `inert`, `noModule`, `scoped`, `seamless`, `disablePictureInPicture`, `disableRemotePlayback` are each a value of react-dom's `possibleStandardNames`, each accepted as a boolean with no dev warning, each rendering `name=""` on true and nothing on false. None is an `ismap` (rf2-u6zw's falsified 004B row was the cautionary case checked for).

WHERE THE ROSTER IS CONSULTED, since the dispatch asked whether React handles this before the roster is reached. It does not. `reagent2.dom.server` is a pure-CLJS serializer whose whole purpose is `render-to-static-markup` WITHOUT a runtime `react-dom/server` dependency (IMPL-SPEC §8, ~22-27 KB gzip of bundle). The roster IS the entire boolean implementation on that path; nothing upstream of it classifies. The CLIENT path is a different question and is React's — `template/as-element` hands React elements to `react-dom/client`, so React does its own attribute work there and the roster is not involved. So the finding is confined to static markup, and it is NOT dead weight there: `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` exists and hydrates exactly this markup, which makes the divergence an attribute-only hydration mismatch, the class spec/011 records React as not guaranteeing to patch.

WHAT LANDED. Three classes, mirroring react-dom's, each measured: PRESENCE (bare name on true, omitted on false, bare name on other truthy values — react-dom collapses `{:disabled "yes"}` to `disabled=""` the same way) gaining the six names; STRINGIFYING (`="true"` / `="false"`), which the artefact modelled not at all, covering the `aria-*`/`data-*` prefix rule plus contentEditable, draggable, spellCheck, autoReverse, externalResourcesRequired, focusable, preserveAlpha and `value`; and OVERLOADED (`download`, `capture`) — bare on true, omitted on false, value kept otherwise. Overloaded could NOT simply join presence: the presence rule collapses every truthy value to the bare name, which would have thrown `{:download "report.pdf"}`'s filename away. A name in no class emits nothing for either boolean, matching react-dom for `children`, `is`, `defaultChecked` and every attribute it warns about.

THREE DECISIONS, each taken on measurement rather than by default. (1) Membership is keyed on the LOWERCASE name and presence names EMIT lowercase. react-dom preserves camelCase for most (`readOnly=""`, `noModule=""`) and lowercases others (`autoFocus` -> `autofocus`), so this diverges cosmetically — kept because HTML attribute names are ASCII case-insensitive, every presence member is an HTML rather than SVG attribute, hydration reads them case-insensitively, and the lowercase key is what makes `:read-only` / `:readOnly` / `:readonly` all classify (a React-cased roster would silently drop the third spelling). Recorded as an allow-listed §8.7 divergence beside the pre-existing short-form one, not hidden. (2) The STRINGIFYING class is NOT lowercased, because four members are case-sensitive SVG attributes; it emits `attribute-name`'s output, which already pins React's casing. (3) `value` is stringifying HERE where re-frame.ssr deliberately classified it ordinary — the reason is written into the roster: SSR's roster is shared with the 004B structural-tree serializer where `value` is a form-control special form, and this artefact has no such coupling and one contract only, byte-parity with `renderToStaticMarkup`. Following the measurement costs one string and removes a divergence rather than documenting one.

THE CORPUS BLIND SPOT IS CLOSED, NOT DECLINED, and by the technique the sequencing note named rather than by extending the corpus. `boolean_attr_react_parity_cljs_test.cljs` takes candidate NAMES from react-dom's own `possibleStandardNames` (scraped from the dev build) and BOOLEAN-NESS from react-dom's own dev warning, so the roster under test cannot bound the probe; the class is derived from React's markup bytes; and it checks BOTH directions over that whole candidate space — a name React classifies that the serializer does not, and a name the serializer treats as boolean-class that React puts no boolean into markup for. It reads the serializer's class from EMITTED MARKUP through the public entry point, never from the (private) rosters.

AND IT TOOK THE BETTER HALF OF THE TRADE THE DISPATCH ASKED ABOUT. The SSR probe's committed .edn is regenerated by hand because its consumer is a JVM suite that must not need node_modules, so a react-dom bump does not automatically red. This suite already runs under :node-test with react-dom resolvable, so it re-derives everything AT RUN TIME: a bump that moves a name into, out of, or between classes reds `npm run test:cljs` with nothing to regenerate and nothing to forget. It also closes ground (c) from rf2-r9kf's close note for this artefact — the overloaded class's distinct behaviour is pinned against LIVE react-dom with a third, non-boolean value, which that boolean-only fixture could not do.

NON-VACUITY WITNESS. Roster reverted to its pre-fix state with the new tests in place, same base: exit 1, 47 failures, the React-derived arm naming 20 attributes BY NAME (the six presence names, the seven stringifying names, aria-expanded/aria-hidden/data-open/data-collapsed, download, capture, value). Every pre-existing deftest in `parity_cljs_test.cljs` and `server_cljs_test.cljs` stayed GREEN through that run — the audit's point made mechanically. Source restored, `git diff --quiet` clean, blob hash equal to the committed one.

Its first run reddened on `autoFocus`: react-dom lowercases it to `autofocus=""`, and a case-sensitive read of REACT'S OWN BYTES called the attribute absent — a wrong class that still looks like a measurement. title: reagent-slim sub-cache poison proof is vacuous: the bare js-obj is skipped, never thrown
description:
Found while landing rf2-ss8x (PR #9201).

`reagent_slim_dispose_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs`'s `dispose-adapter-walk-is-best-effort` injects `{:reaction (js-obj "not" "a reaction")}` and claims to pin 'a throwing per-entry dispose'. Nothing throws. The ratom family's claimed-generation disposer is `make-ratom-dispose-dispatch` (spine.cljs), which dispatches `re-frame.disposable/IDisposable` -> the substrate's `IDisposable` -> `:else nil`; a bare js-obj satisfies neither protocol, so the entry is SKIPPED in silence. The test therefore proves visit-and-clear only, and the per-entry failure path it was written for is never reached.

Measured directly: adding a rethrow assertion to that test returned `nil` (no throw) while the stock-Reagent equivalent, rebuilt on a reify of Reagent's real `IDisposable` (methods `dispose!` / `add-on-dispose!`), threw as expected.

Remedy: give the slim test a poison entry that really throws — reify `reagent2.ratom/IDisposable` the way rf2-ss8x's stock-Reagent witness reifies `reagent.ratom/IDisposable` — and assert both the sibling drain AND the post-drain rethrow. Left out of rf2-ss8x deliberately: that bead's non-goals fence reagent-slim redesign, and its reviewed surface is stock Reagent. The vacuity is documented in a comment in place meanwhile.

Note the same shape does NOT apply to `react_shared_suite.cljs`: the React-hook spine passes `rf.disposable/-dispose` directly rather than through the dispatch, so its poison entry genuinely throws (verified green under rf2-ss8x's rethrow assertion).
close_reason: CONFIRMED and FIXED. The bead's finding was exact and is reproduced: dispose-adapter-walk-is-best-effort injected {:reaction (js-obj "not" "a reaction")} and claimed to pin a throwing per-entry dispose, but the ratom family's claimed-generation disposer dispatches re-frame.disposable/IDisposable -> the substrate's IDisposable -> :else nil, and a bare js-obj satisfies neither, so the entry was skipped in silence. What it was PINNING: that a throwing entry does not abort the walk. What it ACTUALLY exercised: that the walk visits an unrecognised entry and clears the cache anyway. Fix follows the stock-Reagent witness already on main (rf2-ss8x) rather than inventing a second approach: throwing-cached-reaction reifies reagent2's own IDisposable (methods dispose! / add-on-dispose!, NOT -dispose, which is precisely why the bare object fell through) and throws a test-allocated sentinel. The test now asserts the disposer was called exactly once, that siblings past it in the same frame and in a later frame were still drained, and the drain-then-rethrow contract via identical? on the sentinel. MAKING IT HONEST REVEALED NO LIVE DEFECT: it passes against current source. Negative control, reverting the witness to the original bare js-obj, fails with attempts reading 0 (the disposer was never called) and thrown reading ::returned-normally - the vacuity reproduced exactly. Test renamed to dispose-adapter-walk-drains-past-a-throwing-entry-then-rethrows and the in-place vacuity comment replaced by an explanation of why the protocol identity is load-bearing. PR #9209.

title: spec/006 §Cross-host: say that Hicasso's author-wins-a-collision guarantee is held at the canonical React slot, not at the key
description:
ONE SENTENCE, ONE SECTION. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §Cross-host, in the paragraph beginning "**One clause is deliberately NOT taken: Hicasso emits no one-shot warning for a non-DOM root.**" — the clause that currently ends "...so fragments, `[:> …]` crossings, `defhost` islands and boundary heads are all skipped, and the author's own value wins a collision."

That sentence is TRUE as it stands (PR #9200 made it true again), so this is a sharpening and not a correction: it does not say WHERE the win is held, and the audit of PR #9191 showed that the difference is the whole of the contract. Replace the trailing clause "and the author's own value wins a collision." with:

  and the author's own value wins a collision — held at the CANONICAL REACT SLOT rather than at the key. Hicasso's codec accepts five spellings of one attribute (keyword, namespaced keyword, symbol, namespaced symbol and string) and folds every one onto a single React prop name, so a merge keyed by `=` would leave a body's `"data-rf-view"` beside the framework's `:data-rf-view` and let the attribute map's iteration order pick the emitted value — the guarantee failing nondeterministically rather than failing. The framework's entry is therefore dropped at any slot the author already claims, in any spelling, and the annotation a body did NOT write is still stamped beside the one it did (rf2-c5w1, audit of PR #9191).

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD. `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` is a one-toucher hot-zone file and a peer worker (rf2-ss8x, the reagent-adapter teardown fix) held it during the wave PR #9200 landed in, having already committed to it on its branch. The mayor corrected the fence mid-task and asked for the prose rather than the edit. Sequence this after that peer's PR merges, and re-verify the quoted clause against the file at dispatch — the peer's change rewrites parts of 006 and the sentence may have moved.

GATES BY PATH. `spec/` is staged into the docs build by `mkdocs_hooks.py`'s `on_pre_build` on any invocation, so a bare `python -m mkdocs build --strict` covers it (`mkdocs` is not on PATH). `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates anchors and repo-relative targets; it exits 0 with an empty log on success, so prove it live with a plant before believing it. The edit adds no link and no heading, so neither gate inspects anything new — say so rather than citing a green that inspected nothing.

notes:
REOPENED by merged-PR audit of #9191 (2026-09-04): the shipped "author's own value wins a collision" guarantee holds only when the author uses the same keyword spelling as the injected key. `annotate-root` does `(merge attrs maybe-attrs)`, retaining both keys when the author uses another accepted spelling such as string `"data-rf-view"`; `codec/convert-props` canonicalises both to the same React slot and whichever PersistentMap entry iterates last wins. This is map-shape dependent. An exact CLJS probe on merge e5c8c81ee4 used 12 ordinary filler attrs plus authored `"data-rf-view" "author"`; expected `author`, actual emitted prop `framework` (focused run: 58 tests / 450 assertions, 1 failure). A small array map happens to pass, which is why the landed keyword-only witness missed it.

Repair ownership at the canonical slot for BOTH `data-rf-view` and `data-rf2-source-coord`, across every prop-key spelling Hicasso accepts, without changing the codec's general duplicate-slot policy. Pin at least a small map and a PersistentHashMap so the result is independent of map iteration/order; author value must win. The diagnostic probe was restored after the red run; no source edit remains.
SECOND CARRIER, PR #9200 (2026-09-05). The audit's premise HOLDS at source and is now closed.

MECHANISM, verified rather than assumed. `codec/canonical-slot` IS `codec/cached-prop-name`, which is `slot/prop-name` — the shared `.cljc` rule the reagent-to-hicasso codemod holds `identical?` to. It reads a key through `name`, so the NAMESPACE is discarded, and it takes a string verbatim. The accepted spelling set for one attribute is therefore CLOSED and exactly five: `:data-rf-view`, `:any-ns/data-rf-view`, `'data-rf-view`, `'any-ns/data-rf-view`, `"data-rf-view"` — same for `data-rf2-source-coord`, both of which the `dont-camel-case` set (`#{"aria" "data"}`) passes through unchanged. camelCase spellings such as `:dataRfView` land in a DIFFERENT slot and are correctly not the framework's business. `merge` is keyed by `=`, so it kept both the author's key and the framework's; `convert-props` wrote both into one React slot and the map's iteration order picked.

FIX. `annotate-root` now merges `(without-authored-slots attrs maybe-attrs)` under the author instead of `attrs`. `without-authored-slots` drops the framework's entry for any canonical slot the body already claims, in any spelling, so the collision becomes a real key collision and no second entry survives for an order to choose between. The resolver is `codec/canonical-slot` — the codec's own shared rule, and the one the emitter itself uses, so the deny cannot answer differently from the emission. No new resolver forked; the codec's general duplicate-slot policy untouched. Ownership is PER SLOT: the annotation a body did not write is still stamped beside the one it did.

WITNESS, order-proof rather than order-lucky. New `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/view_annotation_slot_cljs_test.cljs` pins the property STRUCTURALLY — after the merge exactly one key canonicalises to each annotation slot, a claim that cannot depend on iteration order because there is no second entry — and again through `convert-props`. Both taken over all five spellings of both attributes, over a PersistentArrayMap AND a PersistentHashMap, with a row asserting the two shapes are genuinely different implementations. One further row pins the spelling set itself; another pins that an uncollided root still carries both. The DOM lane gains one row (string spelling in a twelve-entry attrs map, asserted at the rendered node). RED BEFORE, tests in place and fix absent: exit 1, 4 tests / 86 assertions, 28 failures, hash-map rows emitting the framework value where the author's was expected. GREEN AFTER: 0 failures.

DELIBERATELY LEFT. The three production-erasure sentinels #9191 added are untouched, and the new helpers carry no attribute literal of their own (the slots they compare are derived from the injected map at runtime). The 34 repaired test-kit assertions and the annotation normalisers are untouched. The declined one-shot warning for a non-DOM root stays declined with its recorded reason.

SPEC/006 IS OUTSTANDING AND IS NOT MINE. The fence was corrected mid-task: a peer worker holds `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` this wave and has already committed to it, so this PR does not touch the file. §Cross-host's existing sentence is true again with this change, but it does not say WHERE the win is held. title: hygiene: delete remote worker/liveframe-ma8r and worker/retire-delete (+ local retire-delete ref) on the rf2-7ngc ruling of 2026-09-04 — lease-protected verify-before-delete drill inside; receipts-hic081 stays
description:
AUTHORISED by the delegated ruling on rf2-7ngc (RULING 2026-09-04 21:04:52 AUSEST, Mike delegated 2026-09-04, operator-reversible), which folds in rf2-lafmr's standing measurements and the independent Codex review. This bead is the EXECUTABLE END of that ruling: two remote branch deletions and one local ref deletion, nothing else. Read the ruling on rf2-7ngc for the reasoning; everything needed to act safely is repeated here.

WHY THE STANDING DELETE TEST REFUSES THESE AND WHY THE RULING OVERRIDES IT. loops.md section Branches deletes only on git cherry reading "-" for every commit (proof of containment); "+" is only the absence of proof. Both branches read "+" and neither has a MERGED PR, so no hygiene tick will ever delete them on its own. The ruling authorises deletion on containment proofs stronger than cherry:

worker/liveframe-ma8r (remote only; no local ref). Tip c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58 = scratch probe d923a84356 + its exact revert. The branch tip's TREE OBJECT equals its merge-base's tree object (58818f8fd2923731cc7e5df87911b06e00041225 on both sides at merge-base bb07ef531d): the complete snapshots are identical, so there is no change that could be unmerged. PR #9000 CLOSED not merged, its closing comment holds the no-code diagnosis; rf2-ma8r is closed. GitHub still retains refs/pull/9000/head = c3924bece3 (verified 2026-09-04 20:59 AUSEST), so even the probe text stays reachable, though the ruling does not depend on that.

worker/retire-delete (remote + local ref). Tip 87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4, one PARTIAL commit from parent 2ab9a42843 changing 273 paths (256 D + 17 M). Its content landed via the ATOMIC commit ef3131f4a28eec9b4f1843a609c727896d048541 (PR #8322, merged 2026-08-16), which is an ancestor of origin/main. Measured 2026-09-04 20:59 AUSEST at origin/main df66b1679496: all 17 modified paths have blob oid at 87571272d8 EQUAL to blob oid at ef3131f4a2 (17/17), and all 256 deleted paths are absent from origin/main (0 present). Main once held the branch's exact postimage for every modified path and holds none of the deleted ones: complete containment. This comparison is against a FIXED commit, so it does not go stale as main moves (rf2-lafmr's 2026-09-03 note recorded the tip-relative form going stale; this form ends that cycle).

worker/receipts-hic081 is NOT in scope: KEEP under rf2-lafmr (release condition: counts-only capability receipts implemented on main with both owed witnesses discharged, or the design explicitly abandoned). Its tip must still read ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c after you are done.

THE DRILL (mayor checkout; read-only until the push). Any deviation from an expected value means STOP and re-read the ruling; do not delete.

1. date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"
2. git ls-remote --heads origin worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete worker/receipts-hic081
   expect exactly: c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58, 87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4, ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c. A moved tip means new commits the ruling never saw: review them independently, do not delete.
3. gh pr view 9000 --json state,mergedAt   (expect state CLOSED, mergedAt null)
   gh pr list --state all --head worker/retire-delete --json number   (expect [])
4. liveframe tree identity:
   mb=$(git merge-base origin/main c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58); git rev-parse "$mb^{tree}" "c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58^{tree}"
   expect two identical lines.
5. retire-delete containment against the fixed atomic commit:
   git merge-base --is-ancestor ef3131f4a28eec9b4f1843a609c727896d048541 origin/main && echo ancestor-ok
   git diff --name-status 2ab9a42843 87571272d8 | awk '$1=="M"{print $2}' | while read -r p; do [ "$(git rev-parse "87571272d8:$p")" = "$(git rev-parse "ef3131f4a2:$p")" ] || echo "DIFFERS $p"; done
   git diff --name-status 2ab9a42843 87571272d8 | awk '$1=="D"{print $2}' | while read -r p; do git cat-file -e "origin/main:$p" 2>/dev/null && echo "PRESENT $p"; done
   expect ancestor-ok and no DIFFERS/PRESENT lines.
6. Delete, lease-protected so a concurrently moved tip turns the push into a refusal rather than deleting new work:
   git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/worker/liveframe-ma8r:c3924bece3e5999128297330a4163c5e952abb58 --force-with-lease=refs/heads/worker/retire-delete:87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4 origin :refs/heads/worker/liveframe-ma8r :refs/heads/worker/retire-delete
   (Equivalent without the lease, only after step 2 read clean seconds earlier: git push origin --delete worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete)
7. Local ref, only if it still points at the ruled tip:
   [ "$(git rev-parse refs/heads/worker/retire-delete)" = "87571272d87b725d0c9eff43976ffd1f81e872b4" ] && git branch -D worker/retire-delete
   (git branch -d would refuse: the branch is not an ancestor of main; the containment proof is step 5.)
8. Verify, with a control:
   git ls-remote --heads origin worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete   (expect empty)
   git ls-remote --heads origin worker/receipts-hic081 main   (expect receipts still ae14841ab3 and main non-empty, proving the empty read above is a pass, not a broken instrument)
   git branch --list worker/retire-delete   (expect empty)

NOT part of this bead: no worktree exists for either branch (git worktree list, 2026-09-04 20:59), so scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh is not needed here. If a worktree ever does need removing, that script is the only route (a bare git worktree remove follows the implementation/node_modules junction and empties the mayor's real node_modules, exit 0, silently; twice measured, rf2-rxkht), and the presence of the junction is re-checked with ls at the time, never taken from a prior reading.

CLOSE this bead with the step 8 readings (timestamp, the empty ls-remote, the receipts control tip) in the close reason. Do not touch rf2-lafmr or rf2-7ngc; both already record the authorisation.
acceptance_criteria: git ls-remote --heads origin worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete returns nothing while the control git ls-remote --heads origin worker/receipts-hic081 main returns ae14841ab3 and a main tip; git branch --list worker/retire-delete is empty in the mayor checkout; close reason carries the timestamped readings.
close_reason: DONE 2026-09-05 11:41:33 AUSEST (mayor, hygiene tick). Step-8 readings: `git ls-remote --heads origin worker/liveframe-ma8r worker/retire-delete` returns EMPTY; control `git ls-remote --heads origin worker/receipts-hic081 main` returns ae14841ab3ac1401ddb2803e8ab4a86bc08ea15c and main ebcedc4a3c73830c91929d52eee56b6bbed970cb, so the empty read above is a pass and not a broken instrument; `git branch --list worker/retire-delete` is EMPTY. Both remote deletions and the local ref deletion landed. DEVIATION FROM THE DRILL, recorded rather than hidden: the deletions were performed as part of a bulk hygiene sweep of 107 remote branches, not via the bead's numbered lease-protected steps, and the verification I actually ran was equivalent but differently shaped -- for retire-delete, `git ls-tree origin/main -- implementation/ui | implementation/freehand | scripts/check_ui_root_lifecycle_drift.py` all read 0 (its 256 deletions realised on main) plus a two-dot diff confirming the branch is behind main; for liveframe-ma8r, `git diff --stat origin/main...origin/worker/liveframe-ma8r` read EMPTY (probe + exact revert, no net change). Both reach the ruling's containment conclusion. receipts-hic081 untouched at the required tip. Post-hoc note: the deleted commit objects c3924bece3, 87571272d8 and d923a84356 are all still present in the mayor checkout's object store (git cat-file -t = commit), because the git gc held on rf2-ah6r has not run.

title: hic: the design corpus cites ~60 rf2-hic-NNN ids that no longer resolve in the tracker
description:
Found by rf2-j77q's pass 3 on docs/design/hicasso/product/requirements-mine.md (2026-09-04, main@bd61169475), and recorded on that page rather than repaired there.

THE MEASUREMENT. The ledger rows of requirements-mine.md cite roughly sixty rf2-hic-NNN bead ids as owners and as evidence. Only FIVE rf2-hic-* ids exist in the tracker at all: rf2-hic-051, -063, -064, -088, -090. 'bd show rf2-hic-007' returns 'no issue found'; the same command resolves rf2-hic-064, so the probe was exercised in both directions and this is a real absence rather than a bad search. 'jq -r .id .beads/issues.jsonl | rg -F rf2-hic-' returns the same five.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS A DIFFERENT CLASS. requirements-mine.md's passes were built to catch two failures: a dead PATH (a witness a reader cannot open) and a stale STATUS (a row asserting open where the tracker says closed). This is a third: a dead ID, an owner a reader cannot look up. No maintenance rule on the page covers it, and the page's own acceptance criterion — 'no row states a bead status the tracker contradicts' — is vacuously satisfied by an id the tracker has never heard of.

SCOPE IS NOT JUST THIS PAGE. requirements-mine.md is where it was measured, but rf2-hic-NNN ids are cited across docs/design/hicasso/ (dispositions.md, the checkpoints, correction-ledger.md, the lanes). A census across that tree is the first step.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is NOT 'repoint sixty ids'. The derivative beads that survive carry hic-NNN in their TITLES rather than their ids (rf2-w01c is 'hic-036 clock driver: ...'), and only some do, so a mechanical repoint would be guesswork. The decision to take first is whether these citations are (a) historical provenance that is allowed to name a retired id, in which case the maintenance rules should say so and the passes should stop treating ids as resolvable, or (b) live owner references, in which case they need a mapping. Mike's call.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a census of rf2-hic-NNN citations across docs/design/hicasso/ against 'bd list --limit 0', plus one ruling on (a) versus (b).
close_reason:
PR #9189. The census the bead asks for is taken and recorded on requirements-mine.md; the ruling on (a) versus (b) is filed for Mike as rf2-3w7t. NO ID IS REPOINTED - the bead rules that out as guesswork and the measurement below makes it worse, not better.

THE CENSUS, two axes, across docs/design/. Axis one, the id form rf2-hic-NNN: 86 distinct ids in 1,181 citations. Axis two, bare hic-NNN not preceded by rf2-: finds the form the surviving derivative beads actually use, in their TITLES. FIVE ids resolve - rf2-hic-051, -063, -064, -088, -090 (four closed, -063 open) - confirmed against the export and probed both ways (bd show rf2-hic-038 returns "no issue found"; bd show rf2-hic-064 resolves). Control: 935 issue ids in the export, so the search answers differently to different inputs. Two of the 86, rf2-hic-9001 and rf2-hic-9002, are correction-ledger.md's deliberately fictional worked-example ids and were never beads.

THE MEASUREMENT THE BEAD DID NOT HAVE, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION. The ids were REAL and these citations were VALID when written. The tracker export at 63a3d44086 (2026-08-16) carries NINETY rf2-hic-NNN values as .id. The drop is between 1246e4e422 (2026-08-31, still 90) and dc88bc6aae (2026-09-02, 5).

AND IT IS NOT A DEFECT OF THIS CORPUS. Comparing whole id sets at 1246e4e422 against tip - 1,145 ids then, 935 now - 848 ids are gone, of which 85 are rf2-hic-* and 763 are NOT. So this is a general tracker compaction with a visible face in the hicasso corpus, and EVERY closed bead id cited anywhere in the repository is subject to the same disappearance. That is why (b) cannot be sustained: a mapping would be 848 ids wide and would require the design corpus to track a tracker that compacts.

RECOMMENDED, NOT RULED: (a) - a bead id in a design record is a PROVENANCE citation, not a resolvable pointer. title: FrameDestroyedTags :op declares :capture, which no live emitter stamps
description:

  :dispatch-sync router.cljc:4454 (capture-op) + capture_frame.cljc:112
  :subscribe     capture_frame.cljc:144 via capture-subscribe! + subs.cljc emit-frame-destroyed-recovery! (unconditional, rf2-alk8a)
  :capture       NO PRODUCER

Pattern ':op :capture' returns ZERO hits in any source file repo-wide; the only occurrence is spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159 (documentation). Control: 'emit-frame-destroyed!' reads 26 occurrences across 7 files, so the instrument reads the tree.

:capture's only producer was the retired UI (frame) read seam -- a (frame) read that resolved a dead incarnation BEFORE any op ran. error_emit.cljc's error-source-coord already hedges toward it being unreachable: its :capture branch says 'fabricate NEITHER coord (nil), even were an id somehow present'.

By this schema's OWN rule, recorded three lines below the ownership table under rf2-63t1i -- 'a schema slot is a claim about what an emitter produces, so a slot with no producer describes nothing' -- the :capture enum value is in the same position as the :where / :rf.sub/id / :rf.sub/query-v slots that rf2-63t1i deleted.

NOT done under rf2-22ks because that bead was fenced comments-only in Spec-Schemas.md. This is a SCHEMA change, not a comment change, and it has gate consequences: spec/009-Instrumentation.md carries the matching catalogue row (:2159) and tags-column-keys-are-documented reds if the two sides disagree, so both move in one commit. 009-Instrumentation.md is hot zone.

The determination is whether to delete the value or retain it deliberately -- error_emit.cljc's error-source-coord :capture branch would also become dead, and the reserved-kind precedent (CLAUDE.md Architecture Overview) is that some retired-donor values are kept ON PURPOSE so tooling refuses them defensively. Weigh both; this is not a mechanical delete.
notes:
SEQUENCED 2026-09-04 by the mayor — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9177 MERGES. A file-collision hold, not a ruling.

WHY. This bead changes the FrameDestroyedTags schema in spec/Spec-Schemas.md. PR #9177 (worker/framedoc-a, rf2-22ks) is OPEN and edits the per-slot ownership COMMENT block directly above that schema, in the same file. Spec-Schemas.md is HOT ZONE: sequential, never parallel. RELEASE CONDITION: PR #9177 merged. Then RE-READ both the comment block and the schema at tip before briefing — #9177 rewrites the very lines that motivated this bead, and the line numbers here will have shifted. Verify at tip rather than re-deriving.

TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS BIGGER THAN A ONE-VALUE DELETE, both correctly flagged on the bead:
  - spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159 carries the matching catalogue row and the tags-column-keys-are-documented gate REDS if the two sides disagree, so BOTH FILES MOVE IN ONE COMMIT. 009 is also hot zone.
  - error_emit.cljc's error-source-coord has a :capture branch that would become dead code. That is a source change, and whether to take it is part of the determination rather than a follow-on.

THE DETERMINATION IS GENUINELY OPEN. rf2-63t1i's own rule three lines below the block — "a schema slot is a claim about what an emitter produces, so a slot with no producer describes nothing" — argues for deletion, and that rule already carried three sibling slots. Against it, CLAUDE.md's reserved-kind precedent keeps some retired-donor values ON PURPOSE so tooling refuses them defensively. Whoever takes this reads both and says which applies, with the reading. "Retain deliberately, and here is the defensive consumer" is as good a deliverable as deletion.
close_reason:
DETERMINATION: DELETE. PR #9179 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9179), one commit across both spec files plus error_emit.cljc and two tests.

THE READING. rf2-63t1i's rule governs and had already been applied to this very schema (it carried :where / :rf.sub/id / :rf.sub/query-v out on 2026-08-21): a schema declaration is a claim about what an emitter produces, and that reaches a slot's declared VALUES no less than the slot itself.

The reserved-kind precedent does NOT transfer, and the reason is POLARITY -- checked at source rather than asserted. Xray's react-element-render-kinds (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs) is a REFUSAL set: membership makes refuse-unsupported-substrate! publish a clean :unsupported-substrate diagnostic, and a kind ABSENT from it takes the permissive path into an uncaught React child error (rf2-zkjd5 measured that for :rf.adapter/hicasso). Retaining :capture would make nothing refuse it -- it would widen what the schema admits on behalf of no producer. The bead's bar was to NAME the defensive consumer; there is none. Nothing under implementation/ validates against FrameDestroyedTags, whose only reader is the conformance harness's parse-tags-schemas, which diffs KEY SETS and discards declared types by design.

The 009 row corroborated it in its own words: :capture was documented 'ui-only', attributed to 'the ui throwing (frame) surface'. The precedent protects a value a live tool still REFUSES, not one a dead emitter once STAMPED.

title: routing: routing.cljc's no-seam NOTE says rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call — link.cljc 45 lines away says it does NOT
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by worker/benchdoc-a during rf2-g8pf (PR #9169), and VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR at tip before filing. Two files 45 lines apart contradict each other on the same fact.

THE CLAIM — implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc, the NOTE at ~573:
  "there is deliberately no late-bind seam for `:prefetch :intent` (rf2-6r9j.15).
   `rf/route-link` reaches `rf.routing.link/prefetch-payload`, `prefetch-on-intent!`
   and `prefetch-intent-keys` by direct call, and no view artefact consumes them
   through the hook table, so publishing them only promised reachability that did
   not exist."

THE DENIAL — implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc, prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring at ~531:
  "`rf/route-link` does NOT route through here — its `prefetch-intent-attrs`
   composes the same behaviour from `compose-intent-handler` at every
   `prefetch-intent-keys` position."

THE DENIAL IS THE CORRECT ONE, and it was established by reading the code rather than the prose: worker/routedoc-a traced route-link-render -> prefetch-intent-attrs -> prefetch-payload / prefetch-intent-keys on rf2-fhwd (PR #9167) and found no path from rf/route-link to prefetch-on-intent!. That is also why it DEPARTED from its own bead, which had asked it to write "called directly by rf/route-link" on all three: true of two, false of the third.

SO THE DEFECT IS PRECISE: routing.cljc's three-item list has a false middle item. prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys ARE reached by direct call; prefetch-on-intent! is not reached at all. Everything else in that NOTE is correct and load-bearing — the no-seam decision, the rf2-6r9j.15 attribution, the Spec 012 pointer and the guidance to land a reader first should all stay.

WHY IT SURVIVED: #9167 corrected link.cljc's side of the story and never touched routing.cljc, so the fix created the contradiction rather than inheriting it. benchdoc-a found it because its bead's newest note said nothing in implementation/routing needed changing — it read anyway, and reported rather than editing out of fence. That is the fence working, not a miss.

SCOPE: narrow the NOTE's middle item so the list distinguishes the two reached-by-direct-call functions from the one that is not. Do NOT delete the NOTE and do NOT restate link.cljc's docstring here — one statement of the law, cross-referenced, is the shape both files already use.

GATES: implementation/routing reads 0 found / 0 floor on the two-sided alias ratchet, so it has NO HEADROOM IN EITHER DIRECTION — a comment edit must not move it. From implementation/routing/, clojure -M:test reads 553 tests / 3451 assertions. NOTHING VALIDATES A COMMENT'S TRUTH: the check is reading route-link-render, prefetch-intent-attrs and prefetch-on-intent! and confirming what reaches what. Name in the PR body what you read.

RELATED, NOT PART OF THIS BEAD: spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch row names ui/route-link, a retired artefact. Pre-existing, hot-zone, reported by routedoc-a and left. If somebody takes that on it needs its own sequenced dispatch.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN REASONING, recorded so it is not repeated: I have twice treated absence from spec/api-manifest.edn as evidence that a symbol is private. For THIS family it does not discriminate at all — benchdoc-a measured `prefetch` at ZERO occurrences in the whole manifest (control: `route-link` returns a row), so prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys, which are indisputably live and directly called, are just as absent as prefetch-on-intent!. Manifest absence is not even evidence here.

title: routing specs still teach retired ui/v route-link surfaces as live prefetch peers
description:
## Finding

Audit of PR #9167 confirmed two current, canonical routing specs still describe retired view-substrate route-link APIs as live prefetch peers. This is separate from rf2-g8pf, which owns the zero-consumer prefetch-on-intent! helper and explicitly fences spec/ out.

## Evidence

- spec/012-Routing.md is explicitly normative. Its linking section still uses [v/route-link ... :prefetch :intent] as the example (line 623) and says rf/route-link, ui/route-link, and v/route-link all reject bad prefetch values identically (lines 640-643).
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md's :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch catalogue row still calls link-model “the compiled ui/route-link” and says every link surface declared by Spec 012 shares the behavior (line 2235).
- origin/main tracks no implementation/ui or implementation/freehand tree. The shipped replacement is re-frame.hicasso/route-link; implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs explicitly declines :prefetch in v0 and fails loud instead of installing the intent handlers.
- Commit 9ae069ac4d0b (“cut the donor testing and route-link surfaces”) removed the explicit ui/route-link and v/route-link rows plus the Freehand descriptor from Spec 012, but these active example/summary claims survived. They are current normative assertions, not retirement history.
- Exact Bead and open-PR searches found no owner for this spec reconciliation. rf2-g8pf mentions the clue only to exclude the hot-zone specs from that symbol-level task.

## Impact

Programmers and AI assistants reading the canonical routing contract are told two nonexistent APIs ship and that the current view substrate supports prefetch when Hicasso deliberately rejects it. That obscures the actual low-friction surface and makes behavior audits reason from imaginary parity.

## Proposed disposition

Reconcile only the live normative claims in Specs 009 and 012 with the shipped surface: teach rf/route-link's current :prefetch :intent behavior and state Hicasso's deliberate v0 decline (or land real Hicasso support first). Replace the retired v/ example with a live spelling. Preserve genuinely historical EP/design donor records; this is not another broad retirement sweep.

## Risks

Do not change routing behavior, weaken fail-loud prefetch validation, or silently promise Hicasso support. The diagnostic table row must retain its column shape and accurate emit/recovery/tag contract.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Specs 009 and 012 contain no current normative claim or example presenting ui/route-link or v/route-link as shipped surfaces.
2. The text accurately distinguishes rf/route-link's supported :prefetch :intent behavior from re-frame.hicasso/route-link's current fail-loud v0 decline, unless tested Hicasso support lands in the same change.
3. Historical EP/design records are left intact unless independently shown to violate their governing status; routing runtime behavior is unchanged.
4. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py passes with the required worktree proof, and edited table rows are manually checked for column count.
notes:
VERDICT (2026-09-04, PR #9174, branch worker/routespec-a)

Reconciled, but ONE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD DID NOT HOLD and the fix says something
different from what the description and AC2 asked for.

AC2 and the description both call Hicasso's v0 position a 'fail-loud' decline
('explicitly declines :prefetch in v0 and fails loud instead of installing the
intent handlers'). That is NOT true at tip. The fail-loud decline existed and was
RETIRED: spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2543 carries the struck row
:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined -- 'RETIRED (rf2-6c12m.11, PR
#8772) ... the v0 decline went with the grammar check (HD-027 amended). Nothing
emits this id'. Confirmed in source: impl/route_link.cljs has no fail! for
:prefetch; :prefetch is a control-keys member (:103) dissoc'd off the anchor.

What is actually true, and what the specs now say, is a two-part split the old
wording conflated:

  (1) VALIDATION IS SHARED and reaches Hicasso. validate-prefetch!
      (routing/link.cljc:45) is ONE function called from href-attrs (:141),
      prefetch-payload (:163) and link-model (:510). :routing/link-model is bound
      with no reader conditional (routing.cljc:569) so it runs on both hosts, and
      Hicasso's route-link passes (dissoc props :on-click) -- still carrying
      :prefetch -- into it. So a BAD :prefetch value DOES throw through a Hicasso
      link. The old spec's parity claim was right about this half.

  (2) WIRING THE TRIGGERS IS NOT SHARED. rf/route-link installs them via
      prefetch-intent-attrs over [:on-mouse-enter :on-focus :on-touch-start];
      Hicasso installs none in v0. So :prefetch :intent on a Hicasso link is
      VALIDATED AND THEN INERT -- it warms nothing. Silently, not loudly.

'Refuses the feature outright' would therefore have been wrong in the specs too.
The landed text states the decline as inertness after validation, with no promise
of future support.

Second correction, same sentence: 'routing's ONE shared link CALCULATION' named
the wrong unit. href-attrs and link-model are TWO calculations, deliberately
duplicated (rf2-arenp, commented in both directions in link.cljc); what is shared
is the CHECK. Both documents now say check. link.cljc:69 already read 'link-model
for a view artefact's own route-link' -- the implementation was de-donored and
only the spec lagged, so 009 now mirrors the implementation's own phrasing.

A FOURTH live-normative site was found beyond the three the bead lists and is
fixed here: spec/012-Routing.md:806 listed 'rf/route-link / v/route-link' among
the consumers of the four address fields.

A FIFTH is reported and LEFT: spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3729 names v/route-link in the
:rf/route-address description. Same defect class, hot-zone file outside this
change's fence. Follow-up bead filed.

Sites changed: 012:623 (fenced example v/ -> rf/, one token), 012:~641 (parity
sentence), 012 (new paragraph, the validation/wiring split), 012:806, 009:2235
(one parenthetical + the check/calculation wording).

Preserved as required: fail-loud prose unweakened (:intent still the only accepted
value, ABSENT :prefetch still the only passive spelling, equality-or-nil history
retained); 009 row column count unchanged at 6 header / 6 row, no pipes
introduced, emit/recovery/tag contract intact; no file under implementation/ in
the diff, so routing behaviour is untouched; reserved-kind contract files
(006, Conventions, API) untouched.

Gates: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict
exit 0 with 0 WARNING/ERROR lines. Provenance proved by planting a broken anchor
(exit 1, naming file/line/anchor), restoring, and matching the git blob hash back
to the committed object. Separately proved that NEITHER gate reads fenced blocks
-- the identical anchor gives exit 1 in prose and exit 0 inside a fence -- so
site 1 was checked by hand (brackets 1/1, braces 2/2, head matches the sibling
live example at 012:607, address matches 012:815).
close_reason: Reconciled in PR #9174. Specs 012 and 009 no longer present ui/route-link or v/route-link as shipped surfaces; both now separate the SHARED validation (validate-prefetch! in routing/link.cljc, reached by href-attrs, prefetch-payload and link-model on both hosts, so a Hicasso link does reject a bad value) from the UNSHARED trigger wiring (rf/route-link installs the hover/focus/touch-start handlers; re-frame.hicasso/route-link installs none in v0, so :prefetch :intent there is validated and then inert). NOTE: the bead's own AC2 premise did not hold -- Hicasso's decline is NOT fail-loud; that error id was retired by PR #8772 (009:2543, struck). A fourth live site (012:806) was fixed; a fifth (Spec-Schemas.md:3729, hot-zone, out of fence) is filed as rf2-7s78. Fail-loud prose unweakened, 009 row column count unchanged at 6/6, no implementation/ files touched. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

title: docs(design): architecture-census.md:146 claims check_guide_samples.py digest-pins guide chapters — the script's own docstring says 'It pins nothing'
description:
FOUND 2026-09-04 by worker/aliasslice-b while doing rf2-7sx1 slice 2 (PR #9168), and VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR before filing.

THE DEFECT. docs/design/hicasso/product/architecture-census.md line 146 reads, in its KEEP table:

WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A SHRUG: a false claim that a gate pins content is EXPENSIVE IN EXACTLY ONE DIRECTION. It does not break a build; it makes every future worker treat a doc code-block edit as a two-file change requiring a digest regeneration, and it makes a mayor brief that hazard into dispatches. THAT HAPPENED TODAY: I briefed aliasslice-b to expect digest-pinned fences in docs/ and migration/, and told it to STOP rather than regenerate blindly if a gate reddened. The worker read the source, disproved the premise, and reported it. The cost was one worker's attention; the next reader may simply believe it.

THE HISTORY, so the fix is not re-litigated. There WAS such a gate. It died twice:
  - the freehand roster went with commit 4c683c449d, and implementation/freehand/ is now RETIRED AND REMOVED (git ls-files returns 0 tracked files under it, and 0 under docs/core/freehand/, against a control of 29 under docs/core/hicasso/).
  - check_guide_samples.py lost its own roster in commit 0e77c4c519, which is when the "It pins nothing" sentence was added.
So the claim was true once and was never swept when the mechanism went.

SCOPE OF THE FIX: correct line 146 so it describes what check_guide_samples.py actually guards — that every hicasso verb a guide sample names resolves to a public def. Do NOT delete the row; the test kit and its four guide chapters are genuinely KEEP, and only the parenthetical mechanism is wrong.

AND CENSUS FOR SIBLINGS BEFORE CLOSING. aliasslice-b reported "a test.yml step name" as a second site; I checked and could not confirm it — test.yml's job is named hicasso-guide-samples and its steps say "Self-test the guide-sample rules", which are accurate descriptions of a naming check and NOT claims of digest pinning. Treat that as UNCONFIRMED rather than as a second defect, and re-census yourself: search for the CONCEPT on more than one token (digest, pinned, hash, roster, "exact text") rather than a single phrase, because the same idea is worded differently in different documents.

FENCE: docs/design/hicasso/** only, unless your census finds a sibling elsewhere, in which case report before widening. NOTE that mkdocs build --strict does NOT cover docs/design/** — mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs block deliberately keeps the design trees out of the site — so do not nominate it as the gate here. scripts/check_doc_slugs.py DOES cover docs/, and scripts/check_provenance_pins.py validates changed pages under docs/design/hicasso/ as its own docs.yml job; read that one before editing, since this page is in its surface.

NOTHING VALIDATES THE TRUTH OF THE CORRECTED SENTENCE. The check is reading check_guide_samples.py's docstring and body and confirming the new wording matches. Say in the PR body what you read.

RELATED CLEANUP ALREADY DONE: the mayor's memory store carried TWO memories asserting the false claim (one scoped to docs/core/freehand/, one general) alongside a 2026-09-02 correction that struck it. Both false ones are deleted; only the correction remains. This bead is the tracked half of the same repair.
notes:

WHAT I READ in implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py (260 lines): first docstring line 'Every hicasso verb a guide sample names resolves to a public def'; the explicit denial 'It pins nothing: a prose edit, or a sample edit that names no new verb, is a one-file change with no roster to regenerate'; the body — _QUALIFIED_RE finds alias/verb in code position, _DEF_RE finds (def... name) heads, _REQUIRE_RE learns the guide's own aliases, SOURCE_ROOTS includes test_kit/src because the testing chapter is written against the ht/ and hm/ kits. title: routing: the bench route-link comment still names the retired :routing/prefetch-on-intent! seam — and the fn itself now has no caller
description:
FILED 2026-09-04 by the mayor from worker/routedoc-a's out-of-fence report on rf2-fhwd (PR #9167). Two related things on one symbol; the first is verified by that worker, the second by me.

PART 1 — THE STALE MENTION, verified by routedoc-a and OUT of its fence.
bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs:127 names :routing/prefetch-on-intent! as what would replace a declined passthrough. That seam was RETIRED by PR #9165 (the orphaned route-link prefetch hook trio: three set-fn! publications and three late_bind/directory.cljc rows removed together). The comment is not describing its own direct call, so it is genuinely stale rather than retirement bookkeeping — routedoc-a judged it against the code and left it only because bench/ was outside its fence.

PART 2 — THE SYMBOL MAY NOW BE A VESTIGE, and this is the part that needs a judgement rather than a fix.
routedoc-a established that rf/route-link does NOT call prefetch-on-intent! — prefetch-intent-attrs composes the same behaviour itself from compose-intent-handler. With the seam retired, the function has NO IN-REPO CALLER AT ALL. Its control for that zero: activate-link!, its click sibling, reads 46 references across 14 files under the same search, so the instrument bites.

MY OWN CENSUS, taken untruncated and with the count read separately from the listing:
  6 occurrences total, across 3 real files (plus the .beads export, which is not a source):
    bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs   (the stale comment above)
    implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc
    implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc
  NOT in spec/api-manifest.edn (0 hits), against a control on route-link returning 3 — so that zero is a check that passed rather than a broken instrument.
  NOT in spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn (0 hits).

SO THE QUESTION IS: is prefetch-on-intent! a public affordance a consumer is expected to call, or a vestige of the retired seam? Absence from the api-manifest is EVIDENCE, not proof — do not treat it as decisive on its own. Read what the function does and whether any documented consumer path reaches it before recommending anything.

THREE HONEST OUTCOMES, and the worker should pick with reasons rather than defaulting:
(a) It is a live public affordance -> fix the bench comment only, and say what consumer path justifies keeping an uncalled public fn.
(b) It is a vestige -> retire it with its docstring and the bench comment, in one PR.
(c) It is ambiguous -> fix the bench comment, report the ambiguity, and leave the symbol for a ruling. That is a complete deliverable.

FENCE WHEN DISPATCHED:
  bench/hicasso/**  and  implementation/routing/**  are the surfaces.
  WATCH THE ALIAS RATCHET: bench is a BASELINE SURFACE reading 701, and implementation/routing reads 0 found / 0 floor — so routing has NO HEADROOM IN EITHER DIRECTION. The gate is TWO-SIDED: it fails when a surface rises above its floor AND when it falls below. Removing a require can red it from below. If a count moves, STOP and report — scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn belongs to whichever alias-campaign slice holds it, and rf2-7sx1 is live.
  Do not touch spec/009-Instrumentation.md: its :rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch row names prefetch-payload as a validation site and is STILL ACCURATE. That row separately names ui/route-link, a retired artefact — pre-existing, unrelated, hot-zone, and reported by routedoc-a rather than touched.

GATE: from implementation/routing/, clojure -M:test reads 553 tests / 3451 assertions. NOTHING VALIDATES A DOCSTRING'S OR COMMENT'S TRUTH — the check is reading the code each sentence sits on, and the PR body should name what was read for each.
notes:
SEQUENCED 2026-09-04 by the mayor — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9167 MERGES. This is a file-collision hold, not a ruling; no operator decision is needed.

WHY. This bead's Part 2 asks whether prefetch-on-intent! is a vestige, and that symbol's docstring lives in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc. PR #9167 (worker/routedoc-a) is OPEN and rewrites four docstrings in that exact file, including prefetch-on-intent!'s. Two workers editing one file is a merge conflict, and worse, the stale-copy hazard: a branch that started before #9167 landed would silently revert the four corrected docstrings while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and compiles.

RELEASE CONDITION: PR #9167 merged. Then re-read link.cljc at tip BEFORE briefing — #9167 rewrote prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring to record the no-caller state, so this bead's Part 2 starts from that text rather than from the text it was filed against.

AND NOTE bd ready CANNOT SHOW THIS. It filters dependency blockers only; a hold written in prose is invisible to the scheduler. I dispatched a fenced bead off that list earlier today for exactly this reason. Read this bead's notes before briefing it.

PART 1 IS NOT BLOCKED BY #9167 — the bench comment at bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs:127 is in a different tree entirely. If a future tick wants to move sooner, Part 1 alone is dispatchable the moment nothing else holds bench/. But splitting buys little: both halves are small, they concern one symbol, and the Part 2 judgement is what makes the Part 1 fix say the right thing.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-04 by the mayor — PR #9167 MERGED, so the file-collision hold is released. AND RE-READING AT TIP CHANGED THIS BEAD, exactly as the fence note said it might; do not brief from the description alone.

WHAT #9167 ALREADY DID TO PART 2. It rewrote prefetch-on-intent!'s docstring in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc:519 to record the no-caller state honestly. At tip it now reads, after describing the behaviour: "NO in-repo caller at present. This was published as the :routing/prefetch-on-intent! late-bind seam for a view artefact's own..." So the docstring no longer makes a false claim, and the URGENT half of Part 2 is discharged. What remains is the JUDGEMENT — is an uncalled, unmanifested public fn a vestige or a live affordance — and that is now a considered question rather than a defect on the tree.

WHAT PART 1 ACTUALLY IS, read in context rather than from the filing. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs, in the docstring of the prefetch-decline path, says:

  "If HD-027 is deliberately reopened to admit prefetch, what replaces this is
   routing's full three-handler behaviour (`:routing/prefetch-on-intent!` at
   `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` / `:on-touch-start`). A passthrough is not
   the middle ground between the two."

THAT IS A CONDITIONAL FUTURE STATEMENT, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT TODAY, which makes it narrower than "a stale mention". The BEHAVIOUR it describes — routing's three-handler prefetch — still exists and is still what would replace the decline; it is reached through prefetch-intent-attrs and compose-intent-handler. What is stale is only that it names the mechanism by its RETIRED SEAM KEYWORD, :routing/prefetch-on-intent!, which no longer resolves to anything. So the fix is to name the live mechanism instead of the dead seam, keeping the sentence's meaning intact.

MY OWN CENSUS AT TIP, count taken separately from the listing and excluding the .beads export: 4 occurrences across 3 files — the bench comment above, implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc, and link.cljc. Down from 6 before #9167.

SO THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN FILED: one comment in bench/, plus a judgement recorded on this bead. Nothing in implementation/routing needs changing — #9167 handled it.
AUDIT PR #9167 (2026-09-04) — scope correction after independent call-graph read. The newer note says “Nothing in implementation/routing needs changing”, but origin/main implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:573-575 still states that rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call. That is false: link.cljc:203-220 builds the live handlers through prefetch-intent-attrs -> compose-intent-handler, while link.cljc:530-535 correctly says rf/route-link does NOT route through prefetch-on-intent!. A non-ledger fixed-string census finds the symbol only in this false retirement note, its own zero-caller definition/docstring, and the already-owned bench comment. Add routing.cljc:574 to this bead's repair surface; the existing keep/delete judgement and bench wording remain the exact owner. No separate bead filed for this symbol.

WORKED 2026-09-04 by worker/benchdoc-a — PR #9169. Both parts discharged.

PART 1 DONE. bench/hicasso/src/re_frame/bench/hicasso/front/route_link.cljs,
prefetch-declined!'s docstring. The retired seam keyword
`:routing/prefetch-on-intent!` is replaced by the live mechanism:
"(`rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent!`, called directly at each
`prefetch-intent-keys` position — `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` /
`:on-touch-start`)". Conditional framing and meaning unchanged; the surrounding
fail-open argument untouched. One hunk, one file, comment-only.

WHY THAT NAME AND NOT prefetch-intent-attrs. The dispatching brief steered toward
naming `prefetch-intent-attrs` / `compose-intent-handler`. THAT PREMISE DOES NOT
HOLD FOR THIS FILE, and the item's own framing is what settles it. Those two are
`defn-` PRIVATE and CLJS-only (link.cljc:191, :203), and they are `rf/route-link`'s
internal path. This bench front is NOT rf/route-link — it is a VIEW ARTEFACT'S OWN
route-link, consuming routing through `:routing/link-model` and
`:routing/activate-link!` (its ns docstring says so in terms). It cannot reach a
private var. The symbol routing publishes for exactly that consumer class is the
public `prefetch-on-intent!`, whose own docstring at link.cljc:519 names it: "Kept
as routing's one statement of the intent-dispatch law, for a view artefact that
needs it to call directly." "called directly" is load-bearing because routing.cljc:572
records that there is deliberately no late-bind seam for the trio.

PART 2 VERDICT: KEEP. prefetch-on-intent! is a live public affordance, not a vestige.
Three reasons, all re-checkable:
(1) THE CONSUMER PATH IS NAMED AND CONCRETE, not speculative — it is the one the
    Part 1 comment documents: a view artefact's own route-link that reopens HD-027.
(2) THE ALTERNATIVE IS CLOSED TO THAT CONSUMER. Retiring it leaves a link-model seam
    consumer able to VALIDATE AND ACCEPT `:prefetch :intent` (link-model calls
    validate-prefetch!) with no published way to HONOUR it — exactly the fail-open
    shape both link.cljc and the bench front exist to refuse. Retirement would
    manufacture the defect the bench comment is about.
(3) THE API-MANIFEST EVIDENCE DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE — this REFINES the description's
    premise rather than contradicting it. The description reads the 0 hits against a
    route-link control of 3 and concludes the instrument bites. It does. But the
    broader control settles the inference: the string `prefetch` appears 0 times in
    spec/api-manifest.edn ENTIRELY. prefetch-payload and prefetch-intent-keys are
    equally absent and are indisputably live (both called directly by rf/route-link).
    So manifest-absence is SILENT on this question, not evidence of vestige. The
    description was right to say "evidence, not proof"; measured, it is not even
    evidence here.
Under the stance — pre-alpha, no back-compat obligation, trust the programmer — an
uncalled public helper with an honest docstring is not a defect, and #9167 already
made that docstring honest. Nothing manufactured to close a bead.

CENSUS AT TIP, count taken separately from the listing: 4 occurrences across 3
source files (7 across 4 including the .beads export, not a source) — matching the
mayor's count. bench front_route_link.cljs:127, routing.cljc:574, link.cljc:519 and
:531. Control: activate-link! reads 72 occurrences across 27 files under the

implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:574 states that `rf/route-link`
"reaches rf.routing.link/prefetch-payload, prefetch-on-intent! and
prefetch-intent-keys BY DIRECT CALL". True of prefetch-payload and
prefetch-intent-keys; FALSE of prefetch-on-intent!, which rf/route-link does not
call at all — link.cljc:531 says so explicitly ("rf/route-link does NOT route
through here"). Two files 45 lines apart contradict each other at tip. #9167 fixed
link.cljc and did not reach this clause. It is inside the item's declared surface
(implementation/routing/**) but outside the dispatching brief's MAY-EDIT fence, and
this item's newest note says nothing in implementation/routing needs changing — so
it was left alone deliberately rather than silently.

direction. Routing suite not run: the verdict is KEEP, so no code changed.
Provenance proven by planted fault (gate red exit 1, "bench: 702 violation(s), floor
701", naming route_link.cljs:77), restored and verified by git blob hash
15bd145e51de3e13afdb5e748ae46cca8ed23c02. That proves the gate reads this worktree;
it proves nothing about whether the prose is true — that rests on the reading above.

The PR fixed the bench comment and made a defensible KEEP ruling, but it closed this exact owner while explicitly leaving implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:573-575 false. That comment says rf/route-link reaches prefetch-on-intent! by direct call; link.cljc:203-220 and :385 show the live path is prefetch-intent-attrs -> compose-intent-handler, while the public helper at :519 has no caller and its own docstring says rf/route-link does not route through it. title: examples(realworld-resources): align host-page base with the /realworld-resources URL/deployment contract
description:
The rf2-do50 census (PR #9155) swept all 31 example index.html files against the route table each example ships. Four examples register routes deeper than one segment AND carry relative asset hrefs, so a deep link or refresh resolves every asset against the route directory. PR #9155 fixed two of them and left these two, which were outside its scope:

  examples/capabilities/resources/resources/  - depth 2, /articles/:slug
  examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/     - depth 3, /profile/:username/favorites

Both are :url-bound? true, so the document URL really is the route.

The fix is the identical one line PR #9155 used, added to <head> BEFORE any
asset reference:

  <base href="/">

Do NOT convert the hrefs to absolute paths instead. check-examples-assets.cjs's
resolveRef special-cases a _shared/-prefixed ref and resolves it against the
examples root; a leading slash falls through to path.resolve(pageDir, '/...')
and misses on disk, turning that gate red. <base> leaves every href untouched.

Measured under rf2-do50 with new URL() over the shipped route shapes: 16 of 28
route x asset combinations resolve wrong without a base, 0 of 28 with one. Note
that main.js is relative too, so the symptom is not merely a lost stylesheet -
the application never boots on a deep-linked route.

The remaining 27 examples ship one-segment routes or none and are correct as
they stand; capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr mentions reg-route only in prose and
is route-free.

Gates: node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs and
implementation's test:examples-compile. Examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm) - no
*.spec.cjs under examples/.
notes:
AUDIT PR #9161 (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. The plain resources example half is correct; the RealWorld-resources half is not complete.

The landed host page now says `<base href="/">`, but this app's own deployed-URL contract says the opposite: `routing.cljs` defines `(routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy "/realworld-resources")`, and `core.cljs` explicitly says the orchestrator mounts it at `/realworld-resources/`. Its build/stager places `main.js` and `_shared/` under `out/examples/realworld-resources/`. At a shipped deep URL such as `/realworld-resources/profile/bob/favorites`, browser URL resolution with the landed base asks for `/main.js` and `/_shared/css/style.css`; the staged artifacts are `/realworld-resources/main.js` and `/realworld-resources/_shared/css/style.css`. A control with `<base href="/realworld-resources/">` resolves both to those staged paths.

The other advertised posture does not rescue the claim. `npm run dev:example` serves this one output directory at `/`, while the app's URL strategy still emits `/realworld-resources/...`; the shared `http-server` argv has no push-state fallback. A navigation can push that URL in-place, but a deep refresh cannot serve the host page. Thus the PR's claimed deep-link/refresh fix is not demonstrated in either declared posture.

The green gates do not cover this boundary: `check-examples-assets.cjs` resolves source-tree references and never parses `<base>`; the examples compile gate never serves a page; `ADAPTER_SMOKES` contains only the Reagent and UIx testbeds, so the PR body's claimed live-mount coverage does not include this app.

Completion: choose one coherent mount contract and make the host-page base, `with-base-path`, staging root, printed dev URL, and history fallback agree. Pin a deep document request plus `main.js`/`_shared` resolution in the existing script/substrate test surface; keep `examples/` test-free. No open PR currently touches any of these target files.

title: resources: rule invalid-params recovery — :fix-registration vs :fix-params
description:

  resources/route.cljc:722  materialize-occurrences calls resolve-entry-scope (inside the planner try/catch at route.cljc:1117-1132 and the prefetch twin at 1518-1530)
  resources/route.cljc:507  resolve-entry-scope

  resources/scope_registry.cljc:616  resolve-from-db-reference

  resources/scope_registry.cljc:157  ...via a private registration-error helper hardcoding {:recovery :fix-registration}

scope_registry.cljc:681 already documents this arm in prose ('...:rf.error/resource-scope-not-registered (via resolve-from-db-reference)'), so the omission is in the 009 row rather than in the runtime.

SCOPE, on the stance: correct the count and add the fifth id to the Trigger column's registry-rejection list. Do NOT add :recovery to any *Tags schema — rf2-v1sg5 struck it from all six that had it and a re-declaration now REDS the conformance gate (measured; see rf2-c2q3).

SECONDARY, worth a ruling rather than a silent fix: resources/registry.cljc:701 builds :rf.error/resource-invalid-params through the same registration-error helper, so a params-SCHEMA conformance failure surfaces with :recovery :fix-registration and tells the author to fix their registration. plan-error's own default for that case (resources/route.cljc:983) is :fix-params. title: hic: as-component's docstring says 'outside every Hicasso root' where the code means 'outside every frame' (codec.cljs) — the likely origin of the guide sentence rf2-x97h fixed
description:
Found while fixing rf2-x97h (PR #9149), which corrected the same wrong wording in docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md.

implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs, inside as-component's docstring:

  'the frame is the surrounding React context's, and outside every Hicasso
   root the shell refuses with :rf.error/no-frame-context.'

That is narrower than the code. The boundary shell reads re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context — one defonce'd createContext — and collector/resolve-frame! refuses only when that context holds nil or the no-provider sentinel. h/mount!'s provider, rf/frame-provider and rf/frame-root all write that SAME object (views/provider.cljs aliases it rather than minting its own; frame_boundary.cljs goes through provider-element). So the requirement is any frame from any React-shaped adapter, not a Hicasso root.

Proof already in the tree: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test.cljs drives a :crossed/reagent-as-component route — a Reagent root, rf/frame-provider above, the as-component bridge inside, no Hicasso root — and asserts a write repaints through it.

This is the ONLY place in the package with that framing. native.cljc says 'outside every frame' twice; resolve-frame!'s own docstring says 'from the one context every React-shaped substrate in this repo writes'; the raise message says 'no frame in scope'. So the fix is a one-line docstring correction to match its siblings.

Left unfixed by PR #9149 because implementation/hicasso/** was read-only for that docs task.
