title: spec: ResourceRoutePlanTags declares no :recovery key though every emitted route-plan record carries one
description:
REPORTED 2026-09-04 by worker/specdocs-a while landing rf2-ma8r (i). OUT OF ITS FENCE — spec/Spec-Schemas.md is HOT-ZONE and that worker did not hold it — so this is reported, not patched, and it is a CLAIM to check at source.

spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1729, the ResourceRoutePlanTags schema, declares NO :recovery key. Every emitted route-plan record carries one: the worker verified at source that :fix-registration is set at implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:116-124 and inherited via route.cljc:983.

SAME DRIFT CLASS as the defect rf2-ma8r (i) just repaired one file over — a normative record that is silent about a field the runtime actually emits — which is why it is worth fixing rather than filing and forgetting: the pair of them is a pattern, not a one-off.

WORTH KNOWING WHILE YOU FIX IT, and it is the detail that defeats a reader tracing the category: the recovery discriminator rides NESTED under :cause, not at the top level. And :fix-registration covers FOUR planner-reachable registry rejections, not only the unregistered-resource one — the worker measured that while widening spec/009's row, and it is the number to check before writing the schema.

SEQUENCING: spec/Spec-Schemas.md is hot-zone — sequential, never parallel. Confirm no live worker holds it before dispatching.

GATE: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py (spec/ is inside its roots — anchors and repo-relative targets) AND python -m mkdocs build --strict from the repo root, which DOES cover spec/ because mkdocs_hooks.py's on_pre_build stages it into docs_dir before MkDocs scans anything. The two are complementary and neither substitutes for the other. Neither looks inside a fenced code block, and Spec-Schemas.md is mostly fences — so if your edit is confined to a fenced schema, NEITHER GATE IS THE GATE: check it by hand and say so.
notes:
VERDICT: PREMISE REFUTED. ResourceRoutePlanTags is CORRECT as it stands; no edit made, no PR opened.

The literal observation is true — spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1729 declares no :recovery key (its keys are :category :route-id :resource-id :contributor :nav-token :plan-cause :replan-cause :cause :reason). But that silence is DELIBERATE and load-bearing, not drift.

WHY. A *Tags schema describes the :tags map, and :recovery is never in it. re-frame.trace/build-event DISSOCS :recovery from :tags (core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:693) and ASSOCS it on the envelope top level (trace.cljc:721, defaulting to :no-recovery on the error branch). The normative record declares it at that layer instead: TraceEvent (Spec-Schemas.md:799) and ErrorEvent (Spec-Schemas.md:869), both '[:recovery {:optional true} Recovery]' annotated as hoisted. Of 109 *Tags schemas in the file, ZERO declare :recovery — that uniformity is the post-rf2-v1sg5 invariant.

rf2-v1sg5 (commit 13f8e64aca, 'spec(schemas): type the :where slot and strike the dead :recovery declarations') struck :recovery from the six *Tags schemas that had it (MalformedSchemaTags, NoFrameContextTags, BadFrameProviderArgTags, EffectHandlerBadReturnTags, PrefetchBadAddressTags, NoAdapterSpecifiedTags) and narrowed envelope-only-tag-keys to #{:category}. Its own message: 'a schema re-declaring :recovery under :tags now reds instead of being absolved.' Adding the key would revert that commit's intent.

MEASURED, not reasoned. Gate: implementation/core, clojure -M:test -n re-frame.error-catalogue-channel-conformance-test.
  - clean tree: captured exit 0, 'Ran 30 tests containing 179 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.'
  - with :recovery planted into ResourceRoutePlanTags: captured exit 1, 2 failures in two arms (tags-column-keys-are-documented at test line 1492, and the mutation-proof arm at 2381), reporting exactly [[:rf.error/resource-route-plan "ResourceRoutePlanTags" (:recovery)]].
  Plant restored and verified by git blob hash (working == committed, 847bde4673c0221729de8c45028dc17fe74d8561).
  Note the two arms are a PINCER: tags-column-findings reds if the SCHEMA declares :recovery while the 009 row does not list it, and tags-column-recovery-listings reds any row whose :tags CELL lists :recovery. So :recovery may appear in neither side — there is no variant of this fix that greens.

THE FIELD IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED, in its own column. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2047's Default :recovery column carries the full disposition: :fix-params, :fix-when, :fix-scope, :fix-after, :fix-parent, and :fix-registration for a registry rejection.

TWO BRIEF CLAIMS DID NOT HOLD.
(1) PATHS: the runtime is implementation/RESOURCES/, not implementation/routing/. The line numbers were right: resources/registry.cljc:124 (inside a private registration-error helper) and resources/route.cljc:983. re_frame/routing/route.cljc does not exist.
(2) 'the recovery discriminator rides NESTED under :cause, not at the top level' is INVERTED for :recovery itself. All three builders put :recovery at the TOP LEVEL of the emitted record: branch-plan-error (route.cljc:913, :fix-parent), collapse-cycle-error (route.cljc:935, :fix-after), plan-error (route.cljc:983, (get data :recovery :fix-params)). resources/test/re_frame/resources_route_plan_recovery_cljs_test.cljc:126-130 pins both readings in one form: (:recovery e) top level, (:rf.error/id (:cause e)) nested. What IS nested under :cause is the rejection's own :rf.error/id — which 009:2047 already states. Had the brief been followed literally the schema would have gained a NEW defect.

The record does carry :recovery at top level on the ROUTE SLICE (:error), which is where the test reads it; it is only the TRACE :tags that build-event strips. One record, two surfaces — and ResourceRoutePlanTags is the schema for the surface that does not carry it.

title: examples(realworld-http): align host-page base with the /realworld URL/deployment contract
description:
`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html` carries a RELATIVE asset href (`href="_shared/css/style.css"`) beside a route with a path parameter. That is latently the rf2-g1gt defect in the repo's own routing example: on a one-segment route the relative path resolves to `/_shared/css/style.css` and works; on a deeper route it resolves against the route's directory (e.g. `/issues/_shared/css/style.css`) and the page silently loses its stylesheet.

VERIFIED MECHANISM (from rf2-g1gt, PR #9137, measured with `new URL()` over four cases): `_shared/css/style.css` on `/` -> `/_shared/…`; on `/issues/srv-1` -> `/issues/_shared/…`. Browser behaviour, not a Hicasso or re-frame2 behaviour.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN NOTING: an example is a teaching surface, and this one teaches routing specifically. A reader who copies its `index.html` inherits a bug that only appears once their routes get deeper than one segment — which is exactly when they stop reading the example and start writing their own routes.

BUT VERIFY BEFORE CHANGING: establish whether this example's routes actually GO deeper than one segment today. If every route it ships is one segment, the page is correct as it stands and the fix is a comment rather than an edit — a verified "correct today, fragile if extended" is a complete deliverable, and saying that plainly may serve a reader better than a silent correction.

THE TWO REMEDIES, both already verified in this repo and now documented in `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md`: absolute paths (which `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md`'s own `index.html` already uses), or `<base href="/">`, with `rf.routing/with-base-path` for a sub-path deploy (present at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc`). Prefer whichever the repo's other examples already use — check them rather than choosing fresh.

SCOPE: `examples/**` only. **EXAMPLES ARE TEST-FREE (locked 2026-05-19, rf2-8cevm)** — no `*.spec.cjs` may be added under `examples/`. If this warrants regression coverage it belongs in a substrate contract test; say so rather than adding one.

CHECK THE OTHER EXAMPLES TOO. A census of relative asset hrefs across every `examples/**/index.html` against the route depth each example ships is the real deliverable — one confirmed instance means the pattern is worth a sweep. Two independent instruments plus a control that fires; note that `git grep` with a pattern STARTING WITH `/` is MSYS path-mangled on this host and silently returns zero for everything, so use `grep -rn` as the second instrument rather than a second `git grep` pattern.

Discovered on PR #9137 (rf2-g1gt), reported by that worker and deliberately left unfixed as out of fence.
notes:
AUDIT PR #9161 sibling control (2026-09-04) — REOPENED. PR #9155 gave `realworld_http/index.html` the same root base and therefore left the same defect in the earlier half of this census.

`realworld_http/routing.cljs` defines `(routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy "/realworld")`; `core.cljs` says the orchestrator serves the app under `/realworld/`; the build stages its bundle and `_shared` tree under `out/examples/realworld/`. At `/realworld/profile/bob/favorites`, `<base href="/">` resolves `main.js` and `_shared/css/style.css` to `/main.js` and `/_shared/...`, not the staged `/realworld/...` paths. `<base href="/realworld/">` is the matching control.

As with the resources sibling, the standalone runner instead serves the app output directory at `/` while the URL strategy emits the prefixed route, and its `http-server` invocation has no history fallback. The existing asset scanner ignores `<base>`, the compile gate never serves, and no current adapter smoke mounts either RealWorld app. Align the base tag, route strategy, staging/serve root, printed URL, and deep-route fallback, then pin the served deep-route/asset contract outside the test-free `examples/` tree. No open PR currently touches the target files.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: same .beads race, and the SECOND time this bead has needed it. Payload is on the trunk in commit d8bb970fb7, 'fix(examples,reagent-slim): three isolated defects (rf2-do50, rf2-sefb, rf2-3hqm)', delivered by worker/exfix-a in PR #9155, MERGED.

Its commit body states the mechanism exactly, and it is the general form of what its sibling rf2-pxzf later fixed in two more examples: a page's relative URLs resolve against the DOCUMENT url, and under the default history strategy the document url IS the route. So a deep route makes every relative asset href resolve one or more segments too deep.

THE CENSUS THIS BEAD PRODUCED IS WHY THE SIBLING EXISTED. exfix-a swept examples/ for deep-routed pages and found four; it fixed two here and filed the remaining two as rf2-pxzf, which landed in PR #9161 and is closed. The four are now complete: 8 files under examples/ contain reg-route, exactly 4 are deep-routed, all 4 carry <base href="/">.

Verified independently just now rather than inferred from the commit: both of this bead's examples still carry their fix on the trunk, and its sibling's two do as well.

title: hic docs: chapter 20 falsely says scriptless shadow! checkpoints every committed render
description:
PR #9131 rewrote chapter 20 section 3 to make shadow comparison executable, but retained an incorrect scriptless-mode claim at docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:387-388: omit :script and each committed render becomes a checkpoint.

The authoritative hm/shadow! implementation says the opposite. Its public docstring states that automatic per-commit checkpoints are not built because the runtime publishes no commit callback. Scriptless shadow! returns a live handle with :checkpoint! and :stop!; the caller decides when to call :checkpoint!, which settles both mounts and records that reading. The implementation comment at mounted.cljs:2104-2106 repeats that the caller chooses when a reading is a checkpoint.

As written, an interactive migrator can exercise both mounts believing comparisons are being recorded when no checkpoint is taken. This is a correctness gap in the same named migration proof step PR #9131 aimed to make executable.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the automatic-checkpoint claim with the actual scriptless contract: retain the returned handle, drive the two live mounts, explicitly invoke :checkpoint! at each comparison point, and invoke :stop! when finished. Keep the chapter consistent with hm/shadow!'s public docstring and verify the documentation gates.
notes: AUDIT PR #9139: Fix skills/reagent-migration/references/procedure.md:201-202, which still repeats the disproved automatic-checkpoint claim. Also make docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:583 state the bifurcated contract: scripted calls return green/red and tear down; omitting :script returns the live handle with explicit :checkpoint! and :stop!.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: this close REVERTED and the payload is on the trunk.

Delivered by worker/hicch20-b in PR #9139, MERGED. Verified in SOURCE at origin/main, not from the PR record. The false claim is GONE — a fixed-string search for 'each committed render becomes a checkpoint' and for 'omit :script' returns zero across the chapter — and the real contract is in its place at docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md:406-417: 'Retain the handle, drive both mounts by hand, call :checkpoint! at each ...', with a worked ((:checkpoint! s)) call returning {:status :green :checkpoints 1}, and the sentence 'Each :checkpoint! call settles both mounts, compares them, and numbers the ...'.

That matches hm/shadow!'s public docstring, which says automatic per-commit checkpoints are NOT built because the runtime publishes no commit callback, and the implementation comment at mounted.cljs:2104-2106 that repeats it. An interactive migrator can no longer drive both mounts believing comparisons are being recorded when no checkpoint is taken.

Gates on that PR: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, check_guide_samples.py --self-test and live both exit 0 (74 verbs, 384 sites, 29 pages), mkdocs build --strict exit 0 — with a planted broken anchor driving the slug gate red at 20-migration-from-reagent.md:34 and the restore verified by git blob hash.

WHY IT REVERTED: the documented .beads checkout/checkpoint race (CLAUDE.md §Beads durability; rf2-51uz1). Note the PARTIAL shape: rf2-o80n, closed by the SAME worker in the SAME PR, did not revert — so the race is per-close, not per-PR, and verifying one bead of a set does not clear the others. That is the second partial revert observed today, after rf2-rrp6/rf2-ma8r.

title: hic tooling: hm/shadow!'s own docstring example crosses :article-id, which reaches a reactified Reagent original as :articleId
notes:
FOUND while fixing chapter 20 §3 for rf2-z1cz (PR #9131). NOT RUN - derived by reading source on both sides, not by executing a shadow comparison.

implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs, shadow!'s docstring, opens with:

    :reference [:> (r/reactify-component old/article-row) {:article-id 7}]

The crossing renames the prop, silently, and the original's destructuring of :article-id gets nil:

- Hicasso side: impl.codec/host-entry - 'The caller (host-entry) camelCases the top-level KEY' - so {:article-id 7} is emitted as #js{articleId: 7}.
- Reagent side: reactify-component -> impl.component/as-class; a React parent's props carry no .argv, so props-argv falls to [(.-constructor c) (util/shallow-obj-to-map p)], and shallow-obj-to-map is (keyword k) on the RAW JS key name. "articleId" becomes :articleId, not :article-id.

The asymmetry is real rather than a bug in either half: codec/prop-key decodes "articleId" back to :article-id on the INWARD route (h/as-component), so names round-trip there. Nothing performs that decode on the OUTWARD route into a reactified Reagent component.

Two other infelicities in the same example, both minor:
- (r/reactify-component ...) is called INLINE, so a fresh component type is allocated per evaluation. as-component's own docstring states the law for the mirror-image case ('Call it ONCE, at top level ... a fresh one per render is a fresh element type that remounts the subtree, React.memo's own law').
- There is no in-repo witness for a FOREIGN :reference at all: test_kit/test/re_frame/hicasso/shadow_dom_cljs_test.cljs uses Hicasso views on both sides of every row. So the documented migration route is the one the door's own witness does not drive.

REMEDY, in preference order: cross a single-word prop (:id) in the example, hoist the reactify-component call to a top-level def, and consider a shadow_dom_cljs_test row with a genuinely foreign :reference so the route has a witness.

Chapter 20 §3 was corrected to :id and a hoisted def in PR #9131 and now states the renaming rule; this bead is the docstring and the missing witness, both under implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**, which was outside that dispatch's fence.

FENCE: implementation/hicasso/test_kit/**. A docstring-only edit does not change what check_guide_samples.py resolves; a test row is a CLJS browser-lane change (-dom-cljs-test).

title: hic docs: 09-interop.md's h/as-component section does not say what a Reagent parent's props do at the crossing
notes:
FOUND while closing rf2-4387 (PR #9131, chapter 20).

09-interop.md "Render a Hicasso view from native React" names "UIx, raw React, JavaScript, or TypeScript parents" and does not name Reagent - the one parent a *migration from Reagent* guarantees you have. It then says React props return "with canonical names ... and identity-preserved values", which is true of the DECODE half and says nothing about what the parent did before the decode.

The statement to add, verified against Reagent 2.0.1 (the version implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn declares) and against implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/codec.cljs:

- reagent.impl.template/convert-prop-value: a keyword or symbol becomes its `name`; a CLJS map becomes a camel-cased JS object with its values recursively converted; any other `coll?` goes through `clj->js` (deep); anything `js-val?` - strings, numbers, booleans, nil, functions - crosses unchanged.
- Prop NAMES round-trip on this route: reagent.impl.util/dash-to-prop-name camel-cases `:article-id` to "articleId" and codec/prop-key reads "articleId" back to `:article-id`. VALUES do not.

So a Reagent parent rendering `[:> bridged {...}]` hands the Hicasso view converted values under correctly-spelled keys. The practical consequence - cross an id and read the rest with h/sub - is now written in chapter 20's new "Views shared across the boundary" section; 09-interop.md wants the mechanism sentence at h/as-component so a reader who never opens chapter 20 still meets it.

NOTE this refutes half of rf2-4387's reported observation: the pilot recorded a CLJS map and a vector surviving "intact", which Reagent's source contradicts for both.

FENCE: docs/core/hicasso/09-interop.md. Gates: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and mkdocs build --strict (both apply; the page is under docs/ and not under docs/design/). implementation/hicasso/scripts/check_guide_samples.py gates any h/ verb in a new fence.

The patch fixes 09-interop.md but not the complete public contract. docs/core/hicasso/glossary.md:382-384 and api-reference.md:193 still enumerate React/UIx/JavaScript parents without Reagent, the migration path this issue is about. The new conversion text also omits symbols even though Reagent 2.0.1 convert-prop-value uses named? (keywords and symbols), and its categorical “values do not” sits beside primitives/functions crossing unchanged; state this as structured-value conversion or loss of guaranteed identity/shape. The source as-component docstring carries the same parent/props half-truth; rf2-ip7a owns that exact docstring and was updated instead of duplicating it.

title: hic docs: nothing chooses between a seq as a child and (into [:div] ...) when a for produces a view's children
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F14 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Decide how to write a `for` that produces a view's children. I had two
spellings available and no way to choose between them:

```clojure
[:div.tag-list (for [tag tags] [:a.tag-pill {:key tag} tag])]   ;; sequence as a child
(into [:div.tag-list] (for [tag tags] [:a.tag-pill {:key tag} tag]))  ;; spliced
```

**Expected**

The corpus to prefer one. It uses both: chapter 06 and the cookbook write the
sequence directly in child position; chapter 02's `card` example splices with
`(into [:section.card …] children)`. Neither says the two differ.

**Instead**

They do differ, and I only found out while inducing a fault. Chapter 06 says
the entity-key check "runs where React never looks: **a sequence** passed as a
Hicasso view's children is flattened before reaching React, and the flattened
elements already appear validated to it." That sentence describes the sequence
form. I had written `into` throughout the port — five sites — which produces an
ordinary vector of children with no sequence for that check to inspect.

I could not confirm the consequence, because the check did not fire for me in
either spelling (P1-F16). But the asymmetry is real in the prose, and I chose
`into` for a reason that had nothing to do with it: I was translating
`^{:key …}` metadata sites and `into` made the rewrite mechanical.

**Looked at**

- `06-lists-and-collections.md` "Use stable domain keys", and the paragraph
  about where the check runs
- `02-views-and-reads.md` "Props, children, and fragments" (`card`/`into`)
- `cookbook.md` "A list, a row, and an intent"

**Resolved by**

Nothing definitive. I kept `into`. Recording it because a guess about which of
two documented spellings to use, made for an unrelated reason, may have
disabled a documented safety check — and that is exactly the kind of thing a
migrator cannot see.

A small self-inflicted note from the same edit, kept because the instruction was
to write down the small stuff: converting one `(into [tag] (for …))` back to
`[tag (for …)]` is a paren change as well as a bracket change, and I got it
wrong by one. The build failure was immediate, precise and named the line — no
friction at all, but it cost me a full measurement cycle because I did not check
the watch log before re-running the browser, and read the stale page as a real
result.
close_reason: Done in PR #9140. Chapter 06 - the page that owns lists and collections - gained a section 'Write the sequence in child position' that chooses the sequence form over (into [:div] ...) and gives the verified reason. Both spellings were checked at source and both work, but they diagnose differently: as-element routes a seq to expand-seq, which runs check-member-key! over every member, while a vector child goes to vec->element where nothing walks members; realize-children runs the same check at a boundary crossing's one-level flatten. into splices the sequence away before Hicasso ever sees one, so the entity-key check cannot run - and the spliced children arrive as direct createElement arguments, which React treats as already validated, so React's own missing-key warning does not fire either. The pilot's suspicion that its into rewrite had silently disabled a documented safety check was therefore correct, and it is now written down. The section also says when into is still right (assembling one children vector from several pieces), with the caveat that keyed members inside it are no longer inspected. Gates: check_guide_samples.py exit 0 (the new fenced sample's h/ verbs resolve), check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

description:

BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F10 · outcome 1 · `inferred` · `docs`

**Trying to**

Assert that `pagination` renders nothing when there is only one page — the body
is `(when (> page-count 1) …)`, so it returns `nil`.

**Expected**

`(nil? (ht/tree …))`. Chapter 15's troubleshooting has a row for exactly this
symptom: "Tree assertion sees `nil` | A `when` returned `nil`; it renders
nothing but still appears in authored data | Assert that `nil`, or filter it
before comparing."

**Instead**

```
expected: (nil? (ht/tree [articles/pagination {…}] {:subs {}}))
  actual: (not (nil? {:rf.ui/tree-version 1, :children []}))
```

The troubleshooting row is about a `nil` **child** inside a tree. A body whose
whole return is `nil` still answers a versioned root with no children, and the
chapter does not say so anywhere — `ht/tree` is described as answering "its
versioned semantic tree" with no statement about the empty case.

**Looked at**

- `15-testing.md` L2 section and its troubleshooting table
- `api-reference.md` `ht/tree` row

**Resolved by**

Asserting `(empty? (:children tree))` instead, plus a positive check that no
`<nav>` wrapper exists. Correct, and arguably a better assertion — but reached
by failure, not by reading.

**Bead**

### P1-F07 · outcome 2 · `inferred` · `api`

**Trying to**

Port `pagination`, a shared control whose Reagent contract was
`:on-select` — a one-argument closure, `#(dispatch [:home/show-page %])`, so
each caller decides where its own `?page=` lands.

**Expected**

A recipe. Passing a parameterised handler to a child is not exotic; it is how
every reusable control in every codebase is written.

**Instead**

Nothing in the corpus covers it. The chapters teach three callback shapes and
each is about the *leaf*: an intent vector at an `on*` prop, `h/event` where the
callback's own arguments matter, and a plain function for imperative work. The
missing case is one level up — **a parent handing a child the identity of an
event the child will parameterise**. Chapter 02 tells you what not to do
(a function prop "defeats the bail-out on every parent render"); chapter 03
tells you a hand-rolled dispatch closure raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.
So both obvious spellings are ruled out and none is offered.

**Looked at**

- `03-events-as-data.md` "One callback form: `h/event`", "Ordinary functions
  remain available"
- `02-views-and-reads.md` "Equal props skip the body"
- `04-controlled-inputs.md` "Forward caller attributes safely" — the closest
  thing, but it is about forwarding *attributes*, not a handler contract
- `cookbook.md` — read all nine recipes; the list recipe's row builds its own
  intents from its own props, so the question never arises there

**Resolved by**

Guessing that an **intent prefix** is the intended idiom: the parent passes
`[:home/show-page]`, the child appends its own argument —
`[::h/prevent (conj on-select page)]`. It works, and it is better than what it
replaced: a vector compares by value, so unlike the old closure it does not
defeat the props bail-out. But it changes the prop's published contract, which
means every caller has to move, and I had no documented ground for choosing it
over the alternatives (an `h/event` closing over a captured frame; a keyword
event-id; splitting the control per caller).

**Bead**

Cookbook recipe: "a reusable control the caller parameterises" — intent prefix
plus `conj`, and why it beats a closure prop.
close_reason: Done in PR #9140. New cookbook recipe 'A reusable control the caller parameterises', placed straight after the buffered-field recipe because that recipe already shows the same contract from the caller's side (:on-commit passed as [::events/title-committed id] and dispatched with the draft appended). The idiom was verified as shipped framework contract rather than invented: forms/buffered-field dispatches (conj on-commit candidate), impl/boundary.cljs accepts a vector :on-error and dispatches (conj on-error error), and chapter 13's combo passes the prefix through to its handler; forms_cljs_test.cljs and forms_dom_cljs_test.cljs witness the prefix shape. The recipe uses the pilot's own pagination case and teaches both arms of the one contract - conj in the body when the argument is a render-time fact (a page number), conj in the handler when it is only known when the event fires (a combo's active item) - plus the ::h/value case where the marker IS the argument. The 'why it beats a closure prop' half is grounded in verified guide claims: a vector compares by value so the child keeps the equal-props bail-out that a fresh closure defeats on every parent render (ch02), and an ambient rf/dispatch from a callback raises :rf.error/no-frame-context because the rendering extent has gone (ch03). h/event is scoped to callbacks whose own arguments matter. accident while saying nothing about why.

stable. Guessed, and I am confident it is right, but nothing told me.

title: hic tooling: the migration reporter's bare form silently writes its report into the tool's own directory inside the checkout
description:

close_reason: PR #9132 (head d98e796bb5).
