title: reagent-slim pr-atom: the *ratom-context* nil binding pops before pr-writer runs, so it guards nothing
description:
In reagent-slim's `ratom.cljs`, `pr-atom` reads:

  (pr-writer (binding [*ratom-context* nil] body) writer opts)

The `binding` scopes the nil `*ratom-context*` to evaluating `body` — which is an ALREADY-COMPUTED LOCAL — and pops the binding before `pr-writer` ever runs. So the guard covers no nested printing whatsoever.

The apparent intent is to stop printing from being captured as a reactive dependency: printing a ratom dereferences it, and doing that inside a live `*ratom-context*` would register a spurious dependency on whatever is currently tracking. If that is the intent, the binding must wrap the `pr-writer` call, not the argument.

ESTABLISH THE INTENT BEFORE MOVING IT. Two possibilities and they have different repairs:
- The guard is meant to cover the whole print, and its position is a bug. Repair: move the `binding` to wrap `pr-writer`. Prove it with a plant — construct a print inside a live `*ratom-context*` and show a dependency IS registered today and is NOT after the fix.
- The dereference genuinely all happens while computing `body`, and `pr-writer` cannot deref anything. Then the binding is correctly placed and merely looks wrong, and the deliverable is a comment saying so. A verified "this is correct as written" is a complete deliverable.

Do NOT move it on the strength of how it reads. This is a reactive-substrate seam; a wrong move here changes dependency capture.

CONTEXT: found while working rf2-6r9j.29 (PR #9127), which removed `pr-atom`'s unused receiver argument and ADDED the print pins that were previously absent — the suite had asserted nothing about either type's printed form, so "representation unchanged" had no instrument at all. Those new pins are your starting instrument. The line was explicitly outside .29's fence and is unchanged by its diff.

Surface: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs`.
close_reason: PR #9155. Intent ESTABLISHED, not assumed: the guard is real but mispositioned - the bead's first branch. binding wrapped 'body', an already-computed local, so it popped before pr-writer ran; but pr-writer recurses into the value and a NESTED ratom's own -pr-writer derefs it, and -deref calls notify-deref-watcher!. Demonstrated with a new test that prints a ratom-inside-a-ratom inside a live reactive context: BEFORE the fix both assertions failed - the nested ratom was in the reaction's .-watching set, and the printer re-ran (2 vs 1) when that nested ratom changed; AFTER moving the binding to wrap the pr-writer call both pass, suite totals unchanged at 11174 tests / 55752 assertions, 0 failures. Deliberately NOT changed: the receiver's own deref stays at the call site ({:val (-deref a)} in both -pr-writer methods), because a Reaction's -deref branches on *ratom-context* and a nil context additionally forces flush! plus an on-demand recompute - draining the reaction queue from inside pr-str is a behaviour change beyond suppressing capture, and is the wrong move at this seam the bead warns about. Rationale and residual recorded in the source comment. PR #9127 did not cause this; the shape dates from the file's first commit.

title: hic: every outward link in the app README the manifest copies is dead in the workspace (12/12 resolve outside the pilot root) and most aim into spec/, which the read fence bars
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 ~18:1x AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, from the
operator's chair, at pin 6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba.

workspace.md step 2 copies each application's README.md into the pilot's app/
verbatim, and workspace.md's own section "On the app's own README" invites the
pilot to read it: "That is the pilot's own codebase and a real adopter would
have exactly this." Both briefs repeat the invitation - "Its README explains
what the application does and which patterns it is built from - read it freely."

BUT THE README'S LINKS ARE WRITTEN FOR ITS POSITION IN THE REPOSITORY, and the
copy sits somewhere else entirely. Measured on the assembled pilot 1 workspace:
of the 31 links in app/README.md that leave app/, there are 12 unique ../
targets, and ALL TWELVE resolve OUTSIDE the pilot root and NONE of them exists.
They land in the directory ABOVE the pilot root - the parent folder the pilot
was never told about - because the README's paths count levels from
examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ and the copy is two levels shallower. Pilot 2
is the same shape at a different depth: 14 leaving links, targets computed from
examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/.

So a pilot reading its own README as instructed meets a document with dozens of
references it cannot follow, and no explanation, in the FIRST hour, in the one
file it has been told is unambiguously its own.

AND THE DEAD ONES POINT AT THE FORBIDDEN TREES. Ten of pilot 1's and two of
pilot 2's aim into spec/ - spec/014-HTTPRequests.md, spec/005-StateMachines.md,
spec/012-Routing.md, spec/016-Resources.md and more - which the read fence bars
by name ("Reading spec/, docs/design/, or any other example under examples/"),
and others aim at sibling examples (../../core/flows/, ../resources/,
../infinite_feed/), barred by the same row. The briefs do cover this ("Any file
your app's README links to outside app/. The README is yours; the things it
point at are not"), so the blinding holds - but the package is handing the pilot
a 35 KB document whose every outward reference is simultaneously dead and
forbidden. A pilot that tries one, finds nothing, and tries a second is spending
its attention on the instrument rather than on Hicasso.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC. The friction log's "Looked at" field is the
blinding evidence, and its rule is that "an entry citing anything that is not a
published page is a recorded leak". A README full of paths INTO spec/ is the
single most likely way an honest pilot generates a leak row it did not mean to,
and the audit rf2-hic-069 consumes cannot tell "followed a link and read the
spec" from "tried a link and found nothing" unless the pilot happens to say so.

CHEAPEST HONEST FIXES, in increasing order of work: (a) step 2 strips or
de-links the outward references when it copies the README, which is one sed in
the manifest and makes the copy self-consistent; (b) the copy keeps them but
step 2 appends one line saying the references point into the framework's own
repository and are not part of this project; (c) leave it and accept the noise.
(a) is the only one that leaves the pilot with a document that is true about
where it now lives.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #9138. PREMISE RE-MEASURED AND IT HOLDS, with one clarification: the 12/12 is a count of unique FILE targets, not of links. Pilot 1's README carries 31 relative links across 12 distinct files; all 12 land above <pilot-root> (two levels, not one) and none exists. Pilot 2 has 14 relative links, 12 landing above <pilot-root> and two inside it at paths that do not exist. Two genuinely different instruments were used - a Python link parser and grep -oE over the raw bytes - each run line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed, agreeing at 33 and 14 inline links; no target begins with '/', so the MSYS pattern-mangling trap does not bite here (']( /' reads 0 against a '](../' control reading 14 lines). No link sits inside a fenced block. THE FIX IS NOT A BLANKET DELETION, because the fence and the targets disagree. REPAIRED, 29 links: every docs/ target either README names is under a tree the site builds - docs/core/glossary.md, docs/machines/glossary.md, docs/machines/concepts.md, docs/resources/glossary.md, docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md, none under an exclude_docs prefix - which the read fence ALREADY ADMITS since rf2-lpfz, so stripping them would deny the pilot something it is allowed to read. They are repointed at ../re-frame2/docs/ and all 29 resolve from app/ afterwards with every anchor present, verified by assembling a workspace and resolving each link. DE-LINKED, 16 links: 11 for pilot 1 (10 into spec/, one sibling example) and 5 for pilot 2 (2 into spec/, three sibling examples) - the trees the fence bars by name. Link text stays, so no prose is lost. EXPLAINED: readme-note.md joins the package and step 2b prepends it to the copy, one paragraph saying where the framework's documentation now lives and why the named spec/ files and sibling examples do not resolve here; it names no bead, no experiment and no repository path, so blinding is untouched. That is the bead's option (a) and (b) together, applied per link. The mechanism is three sed/cat commands in workspace.md step 2b, identical for both pilots and depth-agnostic, and they were run verbatim in an assembled workspace rather than reasoned about, because neither link gate reads inside a fenced block. ONE ADJACENT DEFECT FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: workspace.md's 'On the app's own README' said 'Its links into spec/ AND docs/ ... following one is a logged leak', which has contradicted the fence's own documentation row since rf2-lpfz amended it; the paragraph now matches the table. The two app READMEs under examples/ are NOT edited - the repair happens at copy time. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py 0, check_provenance_pins.py 0, check_readme_links.py --ci 0, each with a planted-fault control that went red, restores verified by git blob hash, all re-run post-rebase.

title: TESTING.md's surface-signal table does not know about test_react_jvm (rf2-6r9j.87 follow-up)
description:
PR #9125 (rf2-6r9j.87) added a `test_react_jvm` output to .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and carved implementation/adapters/test-react/** out of the generic shipped-adapter arm. TESTING.md is the canonical surface-signal table (CLAUDE.md names it as such) and was outside that dispatch's fence, so it now carries a falsehood plus an omission.

WHAT IS WRONG, precisely, at TESTING.md as of PR #9125:

1. Line 193, the `adapter_diagnostic` row. Its TRIGGER column reads 'an adapter artefact changes (and implementation/core/**, which every adapter resolves by :local/root)'. That is now false for one of the four adapters: a change under implementation/adapters/test-react/ no longer sets adapter_diagnostic at all. The row's GATES column is still correct -- jvm-adapters-test-react IS still gated on adapter_diagnostic, because the job condition is now a DISJUNCTION and adapter_diagnostic is the reverse edge from core, which the fixture depends on. So the fix is to the trigger clause, not the gates clause.

2. There is no row for the new `test_react_jvm` output. It should read roughly: trigger = implementation/adapters/test-react/{src,test}/** or its deps.edn; gates = jvm-adapters-test-react. Note the asymmetry worth stating in the row: src/test also arm cljs_node_test (the fixture is CLJC so it runs under BOTH hosts, which is the point of it), while deps.edn arms the JVM lane only, because shadow reads its source paths from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and its deps from implementation/deps.edn and so cannot see this artefact's own deps.edn. A prose-only README edit arms NOTHING executable -- its markdown links and inventory are still covered by the always-on verify-readme-links job.

3. Line 241, the 'Adapter JVM classpath probes' row, says 'Two siblings on the same adapter_diagnostic gate' and names jvm-reagent-slim and jvm-adapters-test-react. After #9125 jvm-adapters-test-react is no longer on the SAME gate -- it is on a superset. The substance of the row (it is real coverage, 35 deftests, not a skip-ok probe) is unchanged and worth keeping.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN #9125: the dispatch fence was report-changed-surfaces.sh + its mirror + test.yml + test-fast-pr.sh, plus implementation/adapters/test-react/**. TESTING.md is none of those. It is not on CLAUDE.md's hot-zone list either, so this should be a low-conflict single-file edit for whoever picks it up.

VERIFY AFTER EDITING: no gate validates TESTING.md's prose or its table semantics. Its markdown links and heading anchors are covered by scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci (repo-root markdown is that gate's surface, NOT check_doc_slugs.py's -- nominate by path, not by job name), which runs in test.yml's always-on verify-readme-links job. Column counts and the truth of the trigger clauses have to be checked by hand and said so in the PR body.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9133 (branch worker/tierpin-a). All three defects corrected in TESTING.md. (1) The adapter_diagnostic row's TRIGGER no longer claims 'an adapter artefact changes' unqualified -- it names the implementation/adapters/test-react/** carve-out and routes the reader to the new output, and it now also explains why jvm-adapters-test-react still appears in the GATES column: adapter_diagnostic is the REVERSE edge (the fixture depends on core), so the job reads a disjunction rather than either output alone. (2) A test_react_jvm row was added, stating the asymmetry the bead asked for: src/** and test/** also arm cljs_node_test because the fixture is .cljc and runs under both hosts, while deps.edn arms the JVM lane ONLY, since shadow takes its source paths from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn and its deps from implementation/deps.edn and cannot see this artefact's own deps.edn; a prose-only README edit arms nothing executable and is still covered by the always-on verify-readme-links job. (3) The skip-ok table's 'Two siblings on the same adapter_diagnostic gate' is reworded -- jvm-reagent-slim is on adapter_diagnostic alone while jvm-adapters-test-react is on the superset -- and the row's substance (real coverage, not a probe) is kept. MEASURED, not read off the script: every trigger claim was exercised against the classifier using the real tracked paths, controls firing. test-react src/test/deps/README all return adapter_diagnostic=false, while reagent-slim src and core src both return adapter_diagnostic=true with test_react_jvm=false. The superset claim was checked against the job's actual if: condition in test.yml. HAND-VERIFIED because no gate covers it: column counts across all eight TESTING.md tables are uniform. That check caught a real defect before it landed -- a draft of the skip-ok row wrote the gate as a code span containing two pipe characters, and GitHub splits table rows on a pipe even inside a code span, taking that row to 5 pipes against the table's 3; reworded as prose. GATES: check_readme_links.py --ci captured exit 0 (the correct gate by path -- check_doc_slugs.py does not cover repo-root markdown), and a planted broken link in TESTING.md prose returned captured exit 1 naming TESTING.md:242, proving the gate read this worktree. Restore verified by git blob hash.

title: hic: pilot workspaces 404 on every deep link - no :push-state fallback in the shadow-cljs template, and workspace.md never mentions RealWorld's /realworld base path
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 ~17:45 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. Two defects with one cause; filed
together because the fix is one change to workspace.md's project-file templates.

(1) THE REALWORLD EXAMPLE IS SERVED FROM A SUB-PATH AND workspace.md NEVER SAYS SO.
routing.cljs:254 wires (routing/with-base-path routing/history-url-strategy
"/realworld"), and its own docstring says "this example is served from a sub-path".
The workspace serves app/public at the ROOT of :dev-http, and step 5 tells the
operator to open http://localhost:8080 - a URL outside the app's own base path.
The consequence is visible the moment anything is clicked: the app's links
navigate to /realworld/tag/clojure, /realworld/login and so on, which is a
different address space from the one the page was loaded at.

(2) NEITHER PILOT'S :dev-http HAS A PUSH-STATE FALLBACK, so every one of those
URLs 404s on reload. Measured on the assembled workspaces:
  http://localhost:8080/realworld       404
  http://localhost:8080/realworld/      404
  http://localhost:8081/board           404
  http://localhost:8081/index.html      200
  http://localhost:8081/nope            404
shadow-cljs' :dev-http takes :push-state/index for exactly this; workspace.md's
template is {:dev-http {8080 "public"}} with nothing else, and the published
installation page (00-installation.md:83) prints the same bare line, so a pilot
reading the documentation finds no answer either.

WHY A PILOT MEETS THIS EARLY AND MISREADS IT. Outcome 4 is hot reload - "change a
migrated view with the build running and record what survived". Reloading the
browser after navigating anywhere inside either app lands on a 404 from the dev
server, which reads as the framework's routing being broken rather than as the
dev server lacking a fallback. rf2-nvcp's own investigation hit the same wall
from the other side: linearlite's /index.html falls through to not-found-page
because index.html is not a route.

SCOPE OF THE FIX. Add :push-state/index (or the equivalent) to workspace.md's
app/shadow-cljs.edn template for both pilots, and say in one sentence that
RealWorld carries a /realworld base path so its links live under that prefix.
Whether 00-installation.md's own :dev-http line should carry the same is a
judgement for whoever owns that page - it is the published documentation, and a
pilot on outcome 4 reads it.
close_reason:
WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, ~20 minutes after filing, because the instrument was wrong. NOT A DEFECT.

The 404s in the description were measured with curl, which sends Accept: */*. shadow-cljs' :dev-http serves index.html for ANY path when the client accepts HTML, so it already does the push-state fallback the bead asked for. Re-measured on the same live server, same URLs, one header apart:

  /             accept */* -> 404    accept text/html -> 200
  /board        accept */* -> 404    accept text/html -> 200
  /nope         accept */* -> 404    accept text/html -> 200
  /index.html   accept */* -> 200    accept text/html -> 200

A browser sends the HTML Accept header, so no pilot and no user ever sees the 404. The tell was that playwright had already loaded a page at a URL curl called 404 — two instruments disagreeing about the same request. That disagreement is the whole finding, and it is the "a search that returns zero is not a check that passed" hazard reached through HTTP: curl answered a question I did not ask.

The second half - that workspace.md never mentions RealWorld's /realworld base path (routing.cljs:254 wires with-base-path ... "/realworld") - is TRUE but is not a defect either, and falls with the first half: because the fallback works, /realworld/tag/clojure reloads to index.html, the base path strips, the route matches, and the app is correct at both / and /realworld/*. Nothing to fix, nothing for a pilot to trip over.

rf2-2xzc (the empty Global Feed) is UNAFFECTED - it was measured through the browser throughout, never through curl, and reproduces at /, at /realworld, and after an in-app navigation to /realworld/tag/clojure.

title: schemas storage.cljc: the schema-validator-unavailable diagnostic may advise a require the facade already does
description:
`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc`'s `:rf.warning/schema-validator-unavailable` diagnostic still advises the developer to "Require `re-frame.schemas.malli` at app boot".

That instruction is now stale in the same way the twelve test-level requires retired by rf2-6r9j.51 (PR #9121) were: the facade loads the malli adapter automatically. Verified there by the strong route - deleting the FACADE's own require turns the JVM schemas suite to 494 failures / 1 error, which is what proves the facade is the loader.

The distinction from rf2-6r9j.51, and the reason this is its own bead rather than part of it: .51 was about TEST POSTURE - requires in test namespaces. This is a RUNTIME DIAGNOSTIC shown to a consuming developer, so getting it wrong sends a real user to add a require they do not need, and it is read at exactly the moment they are already confused about validation not working.

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE EDITING. The advice may still be correct for a consumer who has NOT required the facade - that is plausibly the whole population who can see this warning, since the warning fires when the validator is unavailable. So establish what actually reaches this diagnostic: if the facade is required, is the adapter always wired, making the warning unreachable? If the warning is reachable WITH the facade loaded, the advice may be right and the bead's premise fails. If it is reachable only WITHOUT the facade, the advice should name the facade, not the adapter.

A verified "the advice is correct as written" is a complete deliverable. Do not reword a diagnostic without establishing which population reads it.

Surface: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc`. Discovered on PR #9121 (rf2-6r9j.51).
notes:
--- INVESTIGATION 2026-09-03 (worker gatetruth-a) — PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD; NO CHANGE MADE ---

VERDICT: the advice is CORRECT AS WRITTEN for every population that can
actually reach the diagnostic, and both the bead's premise AND the bead's own
named refutation are refuted. Left open for a mayor/Mike disposition only
because the one improvement worth considering needs a HOT-ZONE spec touch
(see LAST SECTION); the investigation itself is complete.

HOW ESTABLISHED — three JVM probes run from implementation/schemas, each
captured to an exit-code FILE (all three exit 0; probes print their own result):

  A2  public route, facade LOADED
      require re-frame.core + re-frame.schemas; explicit {:frame ...} so the
      registration COMPLETES rather than tripping :rf.error/no-frame-context
        -> :schemas/malli-validate bound = TRUE
        -> reg-app-schema COMPLETED
        -> validator-unavailable warnings = 0        (SUPPRESSED)

  B   public route, facade NOT loaded
      require re-frame.core ONLY, then call rf/reg-app-schema
        -> :schemas/malli-validate bound = FALSE
        -> :schemas/reg-app-schema  bound = FALSE
        -> reg-app-schema THREW :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing
        -> validator-unavailable warnings = 0        (NEVER REACHED)

  C   facade BYPASSED into the internal ns
      require re-frame.schemas.storage directly, call storage/reg-app-schema
        -> facade ns loaded = FALSE, malli adapter ns loaded = FALSE
        -> storage/reg-app-schema COMPLETED
        -> validator-unavailable warnings = 1        (THE DIAGNOSTIC FIRES)

SO THE DIAGNOSTIC IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE SUPPORTED PUBLIC API IN BOTH
DIRECTIONS. With the facade, re-frame.schemas.cljc:21 requires
re-frame.schemas.malli, whose body publishes :schemas/malli-validate in EVERY
build (malli.cljc ns docstring), so the gate
`(nil? (late-bind/get-fn :schemas/malli-validate))` is false and the warning
is suppressed. Without the facade, core_schemas.cljc:148 declares the
:schemas/reg-app-schema hook `:on-absent :throw` and re-frame.schemas.cljc:128
is its ONLY publisher, so rf/reg-app-schema throws
:rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing and storage.cljc's warn site is never
reached. Namespace loading is depth-first, so there is no load-order window
either: .malli's body runs before re-frame.schemas' own set-fn! forms.

WHY THE BEAD'S NAMED REFUTATION ALSO FAILS. The bead expected the readers to
be "people who have NOT required the facade, for whom the advice is correct".
That population does not exist on the supported route — probe B shows they get
a throw, not a warning. The actual reachable populations are narrower:

  (1) a caller that reaches PAST the facade into the internal
      re-frame.schemas.storage ns (probe C). The advice WORKS for them:
      requiring re-frame.schemas.malli does bind the hook and does activate
      Malli validation.
  (2) a substitute-validator port or fixture that leaves :schemas/malli-validate
      unbound while the framework-default validator is still installed. For
      them the FIRST clause is the wrong steer, but the SECOND clause
      (`set-schema-validator!`) is the right one and is ALREADY in the string.
  (3) anything that mutates the late-bind hook table at runtime.

This is not a new finding in the tree — the JVM suite's own ns docstring
(schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj) already records it:
"Post-rf2-v96fh the re-frame.schemas facade auto-requires the Malli adapter,
so the common path keeps the hook bound and the warning is effectively
reserved for a substitute-validator port or this test's deliberate unbind."

TWO REASONS NOT TO REWORD, beyond the verdict itself:
  * spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2118 PINS the reason's content ("names the two
    fixes — require re-frame.schemas.malli at app boot, or call
    set-schema-validator! with a non-default fn"). That file is hot-zone /
    one-toucher and was not this worker's to touch.
  * schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj:110 asserts
    (re-find #"re-frame\.schemas\.malli" (:reason tags)), so dropping the ns
    name reds the JVM schemas suite.

THE ONE THING A FUTURE TICK MIGHT STILL WANT (a Mike call, not a defect).
malli.cljc's own ns docstring says "Applications do not require this namespace
explicitly: the re-frame.schemas facade requires it for its ns-load side
effect." The diagnostic therefore steers its one real-world reader (population
1) at an ns the adapter tells applications not to require, when the idiomatic
repair for them is `(:require [re-frame.schemas])`. ADDING a facade mention
alongside the existing one would keep the test green; it would still touch
spec/009-Instrumentation.md. Given the diagnostic is unreachable on the
supported path, the pre-alpha posture ("not litigating every last fine
detail") says leave it. Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it.
close_reason: Investigation completed with no defect to fix. Three controlled JVM probes established that the warning is unreachable through the supported public API: loading the facade binds Malli and suppresses it; omitting the facade throws :rf.error/schemas-artefact-missing before the warning site. The only reachable internal/substitute-validator populations already receive correct advice, including set-schema-validator!. Per this bead's own criterion, that verified verdict is a complete deliverable; the optional hot-zone wording refinement would be unnecessary detail under the pre-alpha posture.

title: Repo-wide syntax-aware require-alias dialect ratchet (scripts/ + lint.yml)
description:
Both parent beads of the rf.* require-alias migration (rf2-6r9j.161 core, rf2-6r9j.167 routing, rf2-j5or machines) list a syntax-aware CI ratchet in their acceptance criteria, and all three deliberately did not build it: scripts/ and .github/workflows/ are hot-zone and the ratchet should be ONE repo-wide instrument, not one per artefact. Per-artefact is exactly what let machines go unowned — .161 and .167 each fenced their own tree and nothing covered the third.

The full design, with the four textual traps measured on the machines sweep, the derived (not listed) exemption rule, the per-surface floor shape and the positive-fixture requirement, is written up in the notes on rf2-j5or (PR #9114). Read it there rather than re-deriving; every trap in it was hit for real, and one of them silently rewrote 42 late-bind keys on a first pass.

Summary of the design:
- scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py (Python, no JVM start-up) + one job in .github/workflows/lint.yml, which already owns lint_surface gating. Not a new workflow file.
- Find libspec vectors by BALANCED BRACKET scan, never by line: a multi-line [re-frame.machines.result :as result / :refer [...]] defeats any single-line regex and the miss is silent (116 use sites skipped on a clean-looking run).
- Distinguish ::alias/key (auto-resolved, MUST move) from :alias/key (a literal keyword, MUST NOT); machines alone carries 179 of the latter against 7 of the former.
- Skip fully-qualified re-frame.x/y and quoted 're-frame.x/y; do NOT skip #'alias/y var-quotes. Skip repo-relative paths whose first segment collides with an alias (spec/conformance/..., docs/machines/...).
- Exemption is DERIVED: an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file is the host-conditional reader-arm shape and is exempt. No path allowlist, which would go stale on the first rename.
- Dedup .cljc reader arms: count per (file, ns, alias) triple.
- Ship as a PER-SURFACE FLOOR (scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn: surface -> allowed count), not a zero gate — core/routing/http/machines are clean, adapters, schemas, flows, epoch, resources, ssr, ssr-node, security, tools, examples, testbeds and skills are not. Same shape as scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh.
- MUST ship with a positive fixture under scripts/_test_fixtures/ asserting the checker names a planted bare alias: a checker whose subject is ABSENCE reads green when it stops firing, which is the defect class this repo keeps finding in its own instruments (cf. lint.yml's hicasso kondo fixture-witness step).

Hot-zone: scripts/ and .github/workflows/lint.yml. One toucher, sequenced against other workflow edits.
notes:
ADDITIONAL FINDING FROM THE MACHINES SWEEP (PR #9114) — a scanner the ratchet should also account for.

scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK B reads every :rf.* keyword NAMESPACE out of implementation/**/src and demands a matching `:rf.<ns>/*` row in spec/Conventions.md's reserved set. Its extractor (_RF_KEYWORD_RE = r":(rf(?:\.[a-z][\w.-]*)?)/[\w.*+!?<>=-]+") CANNOT TELL `::rf.x/y` FROM `:rf.x/y`.

That matters because the canonical `rf.<tail>` require alias TEXTUALLY SHADOWS the `:rf.<area>` reserved keyword root. An auto-resolved `::rf.machines.result/depth-abort?` denotes `:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?` and reserves nothing at all, but the checker reads it as a literal reserved-root keyword and demands a Conventions row that would be a FALSE reservation.

Machines is the first artefact to produce one: `git grep '::rf\.' -- implementation/*/src` returned NOTHING on main before PR #9114, which is why the core and routing sweeps never met it. Every remaining artefact with an auto-resolved keyword in src will meet it — schemas, flows, epoch, resources, ssr, ssr-node, security, adapters.

PR #9114 resolved its one instance INSIDE its fence, by spelling the sentinel fully-qualified (`:re-frame.machines.result/depth-abort?`) with a comment recording why, rather than by editing scripts/. That is defensible on the merits — a fully-qualified literal says the same thing to a reader and to a scanner — but it is a per-site remedy, and the scanner gap is still open.

The one-line correction, when a lane owns scripts/: add a negative lookbehind for the second colon, `(?<!:):(rf(?:\.[a-z][\w.-]*)?)/...`. It is strictly safe — `::x/y` ALWAYS resolves through an alias, and every framework namespace is `re-frame.*`, so no `::` form can ever denote a literal `:rf.*` value. Pair it with a self-test fixture asserting that `::rf.foo/bar` does NOT fire CHECK B while `:rf.foo/bar` still does; the checker already carries a self-test suite in the same shape.

Worth deciding at the same time whether the ratchet should simply FORBID `::rf.<tail>/key` in framework source, which is the stronger and simpler rule: the fully-qualified spelling is unambiguous to every consumer (Xray, the MCP catalogues, this checker and any future one), and the auto-resolved form buys only brevity.
SEQUENCING FENCE (mayor, this tick): do NOT dispatch this ratchet until rf2-6r9j.161 (core) AND rf2-6r9j.209 (resources) have LANDED ON MAIN. The ratchet is repo-wide by design - that is the whole point of it, per this bead's own rationale that per-artefact is what let machines go unowned. But a repo-wide instrument landing while core or resources still speak the bare dialect reds the trunk on arrival, and the fix would then be to weaken the ratchet, which defeats it. machines is done (rf2-j5or, PR #9114, on main as 32701c1260). Verify the other two by payload - git log origin/main --oneline --grep=<id> - never by git merge-base --is-ancestor on a PR head oid, which is always false here because PRs merge with --rebase. Also carried on this bead already: the scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK B gap that machalias-a hit, where the checker cannot tell ::rf.x/y from :rf.x/y and would demand a false reservation row in the one-toucher spec/Conventions.md. That fix belongs to whichever lane owns scripts/, which is this one.
RATCHET SCOPE CORRECTION, measured on the core sweep (rf2-6r9j.161, PR #9128) — this changes the design recorded above, do not build the ratchet without it.

The core residue after PR #9103 was exactly ONE edge in ONE file, and the reason it survived is the reason this ratchet must be wider than currently specified: it is NOT an (ns ... (:require ...)) edge at all. It is a runtime TOP-LEVEL (require '[re-frame.late-bind.directory :as directory]).

clj-kondo's namespace-usage analysis does not report runtime require forms. That is precisely why the bead's own clj-kondo census read 1616 where a textual scan of the same tree read 1617 — the one-edge delta IS this edge, and it is why a whole 312-file sweep missed it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: the balanced-bracket libspec scan specified above is necessary but NOT sufficient. Runtime (require ...) forms must be in the ratchet's scan surface, or it reproduces this exact miss and reports a clean run over it. Add a positive fixture for the runtime-require shape specifically, not only the ns-form shape.

TWO MORE MEASUREMENTS worth having before building it:
- Core carries ZERO host-conditional exemptions (derived predicate over all 349 files, 143 of them .cljc). rf2-j5or's notes say 'core one'; that is refuted. Core's re-frame requires sit in the common part of reader conditionals. Machines has 1 file, routing 8, resources 12 (24 edges, all one alias 'substrate').
- Trap 1 IS live in core: 39 libspec vectors span lines, all already canonical — which is exactly why a line-oriented census would have reported a clean run anyway. The line-spanning hazard is real here and invisible to the obvious instrument.

PREREQUISITE STATUS: machines (rf2-j5or) is MERGED. core (rf2-6r9j.161, PR #9128) and resources (rf2-6r9j.209, PR #9129) are CLOSED but their PRs were still OPEN when this note was written — verify all three by payload before dispatching, per the sequencing fence above.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9135 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. check_require_alias_dialect.py calls its mask reader-level but does not consume the Clojure #_ discard macro. In-memory reproduction against the merged code: read_file on (ns x (:require #_[re-frame.machines :as machines] [re-frame.core :as rf])) reports re-frame.machines -> machines as a live edge even though the reader discards that entire libspec. The same mechanism also scans a #_(require ...) body. This makes the new required repo-wide gate false-red on valid discarded code; #_ is live vocabulary here (37 occurrences across 18 tracked Clojure files), even though no current occurrence immediately wraps a framework require. Repair the mask/scanner so a discard consumes exactly its next reader form while preserving offsets. Add negative fixtures for a discarded ns libspec and discarded runtime require, plus identical live twins that must still fire; run the self-test and live ratchet.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9144 (2026-09-04): the two manual floor reductions are correct, but this PR documents a second live tool hazard for the ratchet owner. --write-baseline rewrites every existing surface floor to the current count and returns success, so if any surface has regressed above its floor the advertised repair command silently raises that floor and blesses the regression. The #9144 worker had to diff and hand-apply only downward moves. Make the default baseline writer monotonic for existing surfaces: refuse/report any proposed increase rather than writing it, while retaining an explicit path for adding a genuinely new surface. Add self-tests proving a downward refresh succeeds and an upward refresh cannot alter the baseline. Also ensure the write path refuses unparseable input rather than bypassing the normal usability check.
SEQUENCING FENCE, set by the mayor 2026-09-04 10:1x AUSEST. DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9142 IS ON MAIN.

This bead now owns TWO merged-PR audit remainders, both in scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py — the #_ discard mis-read (from the #9135 audit) and the --write-baseline monotonicity hole (from the #9144 audit). Both are repairs to THE TOOL.

WHY THE FENCE. worker/httpfix-a is live on PR #9142 right now, measuring implementation/http against that exact tool and rewriting its baseline row from 272 to whatever the tool reports. Changing what the tool COUNTS while a worker is deriving a baseline number FROM it produces a baseline that is correct against neither version. Two workers here do not conflict on files — the tool and the baseline are different paths — they conflict on the MEASUREMENT, which no merge check can see.

BOTH REMAINDERS ARE REAL AND THE FIRST IS A LIVE RISK TO THE MERGE QUEUE, so this is a fence rather than a downgrade:

(1) THE #_ DISCARD. The gate is REQUIRED and repo-wide as of #9135. Its mask is called reader-level but does not consume Clojure's #_ discard macro, so a discarded libspec reads as a live edge. Measured this tick: 18 tracked Clojure files carry #_. No current occurrence immediately wraps a framework require, so the gate is not false-red TODAY — it is one ordinary edit away from being so, and when it fires it will block every open PR exactly as the floor bug did this morning (rf2-ril5). Treat it as a latent trunk-red, not a nicety.

(2) --write-baseline IS NOT MONOTONIC. It rewrites every surface floor to the current count and exits 0, so where a surface has regressed ABOVE its floor the advertised repair command silently RAISES that floor and blesses the regression. Confirmed independently twice: the #9144 audit reached it by reading the code, and #9144's own worker hit it in practice and had to diff and hand-apply only the downward moves.

A THIRD HAZARD, FOUND BY #9144's WORKER AND NOT YET ON THIS BEAD, WHICH INVERTS THE OBVIOUS FIX: :min-edges is NOT a ratchet floor. It is a blind-scanner guard checked as total < min_edges -> fail, so LOWERING it LOOSENS the gate. A monotonicity rule written as 'floors may only decrease' would therefore be exactly WRONG for that key, and --write-baseline recomputes it as int(len(edges) * 0.9) on every run. Whatever guard you add must treat :min-edges as the opposite case and say so in the code, or the next worker reading the rule applies it to :min-edges and quietly gives up the anti-blindness floor. #9144 held it at 9692 by hand for this reason.

DISPATCH WHEN #9142 MERGES. Verify by payload (git log origin/main --grep, dots escaped and boundary-anchored) rather than by PR state alone.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9154 — reopened exact scanner owner. The new discard parser still has the silent-green failure it is designed to prevent: form_end treats every otherwise-unmatched # dispatch as a tagged literal that owns a following form. Clojure's ##Inf, ##-Inf, and ##NaN are self-contained symbolic values, so #_ ##Inf [re-frame.machines :as machines] discards only ##Inf and leaves the libspec live. Against the merged checker, an identical live control reports machines, while inserting #_ ##Inf makes the checker report none and mask away both the symbolic value and live libspec; Babashka's reader confirms [#_ ##Inf :live] reads as [:live]. Add an explicit symbolic-value case that ends at that token rather than consuming the next form, with a live-twin self-test covering the over-consumption direction. The monotonic baseline-writer repair and the existing discard fixtures are otherwise unaffected.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: the .beads checkout/checkpoint race, twelfth instance today. Payload verified in the WORKING TREE at HEAD==origin/main — self-test reads '79 passed, 0 failed' (was 40 before this work), and both discard fixtures are present under scripts/_test_fixtures/check_require_alias_dialect/negative/.

Delivered by worker/ratchettool-a in PR #9154, MERGED at 4c6de72231.

BOTH AUDIT REMAINDERS CLOSED, plus the inversion trap handled:
1. The #_ DISCARD MIS-READ (latent trunk-red, from #9135's audit) — the scanner now consumes exactly the next reader form after a #_, with offsets preserved so file:line reporting stays correct. Its three-way live-corpus witness is the proof: a live plant reddened at core_flows.cljc:40, the SAME line discarded stayed green, and that same discarded tree under the PRE-CHANGE checker went red — the bug reproduced on real files, in both directions.
2. --write-baseline NOT MONOTONIC (from #9144's audit) — at source it never read the existing baseline at all: it set every surface to counts.get(s, 0), recomputed :min-edges, wrote and returned 0 before parse_baseline was called and without running assert_usable. All three hazards in five lines. Now refuses a proposed INCREASE for an existing surface while keeping an explicit path for a genuinely new one.
3. THE :min-edges INVERSION I flagged in the brief was handled as the opposite case rather than folded into one rule: surface floors may only FALL, :min-edges may only RISE, implemented as two deliberately opposed comparisons with a block comment stating that a single 'floors may only fall' rule is exactly wrong for half the file. Against the pre-change writer on one scratch input, the old code lowered :min-edges 5->4 AND raised a regressed floor 1->2 — both silent, both exit 0.

REPO-WIDE COUNT UNMOVED: 2773 files / 10773 edges / 5640 non-canonical, before and after. That is the DISCRIMINATING result rather than a null one — over-consumption of #_ would have DROPPED the count. Every surface still exactly at its floor, so no baseline correction is implied and no open PR was affected. Baseline data untouched; origin/main...HEAD carries no hunk in it.

#_ CENSUS, three instruments: 37 raw occurrences across 18 files line-oriented, but only 11 in CODE POSITION across 8 files once reader-masked — the other 26 sit in strings and comments. Adjacency searched line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened, the latter being the only pass that can see a #_ newline-separated from its libspec: ZERO discards currently wrap a framework require. Latent, exactly as filed.

TWO BRIEF PREMISES DID NOT HOLD: there is no Python linter in this repo (no ruff/flake8/mypy, and scripts/lint_kondo.py is a clj-kondo gate for Clojure), so my gate 4 did not exist; and my bd history schema warning was half wrong — notes IS carried, which that worker demonstrated with 7 real change points. Both recorded.

title: Machines namespaces: canonical rf.* require-alias migration
description:
Sibling of rf2-6r9j.161 (core, landed in PR #9103) and rf2-6r9j.167 (routing, same PR). implementation/machines was NOT covered by either bead and has no owner.

Measured on the PR #9103 tree with the same scanner that reproduced both beads' clj-kondo censuses exactly (core 1616, routing 438):

  implementation/machines: 835 noncanonical require edges across 192 files.

The rule is spec/Conventions.md §Require-alias dialect: re-frame.core keeps the bare root alias rf, every other re-frame.<tail> takes the dotted rf.<tail>, and the bare leaf form is reserved for application namespaces. Machines currently spells them bare throughout (machines/, mtest/, plain-atom/, frame/, trace/, timer/, parallel/, spawn-order/ …).

Two things the core/routing pass learned, which this one will meet again:

1. HOST-CONDITIONAL ALIASES ARE AN EXEMPTION, NOT A MISS. birth_always_cljs_test.cljc binds one alias to two namespaces across reader arms — #?(:clj [re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as substrate-adapter] :cljs [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as substrate-adapter]). The shared name IS the point; per-arm dotted tails would give the single use site two names. Leave it and say so. (Eight routing suites had the same shape.)

2. SOURCE-SCANNING GATES READ CALL SITES AS TEXT. destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test.clj:468 matches the fixed string "trace/emit!" — that one still matches after the rename because rf.trace/emit! contains it, but the class is real: core's late_bind_drift_test and warn_once_clear_governance_test both had to widen, and the governance one would have FAILED OPEN (it forbids a call shape, so a spelling it cannot see is an offender it waves through). Grep for regex/fixed-string gates over machines src before assuming a green means anything.

Scope note: PR #9103 deliberately left the three machines test files it renamed (rf2-6r9j.164) in the artefact's current dialect rather than migrating them mid-move — a half-migrated artefact reads worse than a uniformly unmigrated one. This bead migrates the artefact as a whole.

The syntax-aware CI ratchet both parent beads asked for is still unbuilt (see rf2-6r9j.161 acceptance); it belongs in scripts/ + .github/workflows/ and should be one ratchet for the whole repo, not one per artefact.
notes:
SWEEP LANDED — PR #9114 (head 69d26d2e23c4a719d42718b9a7a456eef02d861c), branch worker/machalias-a.

839 noncanonical require edges across 194 files migrated to the dotted rf.<tail> dialect, plus the 3449 qualified use sites that move with them (auto-resolved ::alias/key keywords included — ::result/depth-abort? and ::rf.machines.result/depth-abort? denote the same keyword). The bead's 835/192 reproduces: a textual scan counts 841 edges across 194 files, of which 2 are the documented host-conditional exemption in ONE file, leaving exactly 835 in 192 files once .cljc reader arms are deduplicated the way the bead's clj-kondo census did.

EXEMPTION HONOURED, exactly as the bead predicted: birth_always_cljs_test.cljc binds one alias `substrate-adapter` to two namespaces across reader arms. It is the ONLY such shape in machines, and the check that found it is DERIVED rather than listed — an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file — so it cannot rot.

SOURCE-SCANNING GATES: NO WIDENING NEEDED, and this was measured rather than assumed. late_bind_drift_test and warn_once_clear_governance_test were already widened by PR #9103 to accept both spellings via an optional rf. prefix, so machines' rename lands inside a pattern that already covers it. Re-run against the migrated tree: 9 tests / 696 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0. destroyed_reason_channel_conformance_test.clj's (str/includes? s "trace/emit!") pre-filter still matches because rf.trace/emit! contains it, and its structural call-name reads (name (first form)), which is alias-insensitive. tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab reads five machines source files but reader-parses them and asserts on keyword map keys — 94 tests / 1031 assertions green. No route-hook! call site exists in machines src, so the drift gate's substrate-adapter/route-hook! pattern has no machines subject.

GATES: machines JVM 1241 tests / 4495 assertions exit 0; node bundle 11170 tests / 55746 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo identical to a pristine baseline of the same tree once columns and alias text are normalised (1623 warnings both sides, zero delta; the single kondo error-level finding is in implementation/epoch, present on the baseline, and an artefact of local kondo v2025.10.23 vs CI's pinned 2026.04.15). JVM gate proven live first: a planted rf.machines.pathsX/snapshot-path returned exit 1 naming classification.cljc:110:9, and restoring returned blob 0aa312e11b024e2a9de853c26cdacfe305d76fcd.

===========================================================================
DESIGN FOR THE REPO-WIDE SYNTAX-AWARE RATCHET (not built here — scripts/ + .github/workflows/ are hot-zone; this is for a workflow lane)
===========================================================================

WHERE. One checker, scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py, in the same Python house style as check_doc_slugs.py / check_readme_links.py (no JVM start-up, so it can also join the fast-PR spine). One job in .github/workflows/lint.yml, which already owns the lint_surface gating — NOT a new workflow file, and NOT one ratchet per artefact. Per-artefact is what makes this rot: machines went unowned precisely because rf2-6r9j.161 and rf2-6r9j.167 each fenced their own tree.

WHY SYNTAX-AWARE AND NOT GREP. Four textual traps, each measured on this sweep, each of which a line-oriented regex ratchet gets wrong:

  (1) A LITERAL SINGLE-COLON KEYWORD IS NOT AN ALIAS REFERENCE, AND A DOUBLE-COLON ONE IS. machines carries 179 sites of the shape :machines/rearm-after-hydration!, :router/dispatch!, :cofx/eval-recordable-sub, :frame/destroyed, :corner.timer/scoped — late-bind keys, trace channels and frame ids whose first segment collides with a live alias — against 7 sites of ::result/... , which MUST move. A first pass here that treated the colon as a word boundary rewrote 42 late-bind keys into new keyword values; nothing failed, because a renamed late-bind key is only read back by another renamed site in the same file. The control that caught it was counting :rf.machines/ — 0 before, 42 after, a count that should have been constant.

  (2) FULLY-QUALIFIED, QUOTED AND VAR-QUOTED FORMS EACH NEED DIFFERENT HANDLING. re-frame.machines.paths/snapshot-path must not move; a quoted 're-frame.fx/dispatch-later-timers and (requiring-resolve 're-frame.conformance/eval-value*) must not move; but #'parallel/reduce-regions MUST move, and an apostrophe is both a quote reader macro and a legal symbol-body character, so the two are told apart only by what precedes the quote.

  (3) REPO-RELATIVE DOC PATHS SHARE A FIRST SEGMENT WITH LIVE ALIASES. spec/conformance/fixtures/, docs/machines/..., core/test/re_frame, ../../spec/conformance. This is the same class the core sweep met as spec/API.md (33 spared sites) and it recurs in every artefact.

  (4) MULTI-LINE REQUIRE VECTORS DEFEAT ANY SINGLE-LINE REGEX, AND THE MISS IS SILENT. parallel.cljc opens [re-frame.machines.result :as result and closes the vector on the NEXT line. A regex anchored on the closing bracket skipped that libspec and, with it, 116 use sites — while reporting a clean run. The scanner has to find the libspec vector by balanced brackets, not by line.

MECHANISM. For each git-tracked .clj/.cljs/.cljc under implementation/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/ and skills/: locate every libspec vector whose head symbol is re-frame or starts re-frame. by balanced-bracket scan; read its :as / :as-alias; require the alias to be rf for re-frame.core and rf.<tail> otherwise. Count edges per (file, ns, alias) triple so a .cljc binding the same alias in both reader arms is ONE edge, not two — that is the dedup the bead's own census applied and the reason a naive count reads 841 where the bead reads 835.

EXEMPTION RULE, DERIVED NOT LISTED. A libspec is exempt when the SAME alias is bound to two or more distinct namespaces within the same file. That is exactly the host-conditional reader-arm shape and it needs no allowlist to maintain — machines has one instance, routing had eight, core one. An allowlist of file paths would go stale on the first rename; this predicate cannot.

SHAPE: A PER-SURFACE FLOOR, NOT A ZERO GATE. core, routing, http and (with this PR) machines are clean, but adapters/, schemas/, flows/, epoch/, resources/, ssr/, ssr-node/, security/, tools/, examples/, testbeds/ and skills/ are NOT — skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:72 still spells [re-frame.machines :as machines], and docs/, migration/ and spec/006 line 2022 carry noncanonical examples in prose. So: a checked-in scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn mapping top-level surface to allowed violation count, failing when a surface EXCEEDS its baseline. Migrated surfaces sit at 0 and can never regress; unmigrated ones ratchet down as beads land. Same shape as scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh, which is the in-repo precedent.

IT MUST SHIP WITH A POSITIVE FIXTURE. A checker whose subject is ABSENCE is green when it stops firing — the defect class this repo keeps finding in its own instruments, and the reason lint.yml already carries a fixture-witness step for hicasso's kondo export. Plant one bare alias under scripts/_test_fixtures/ and assert the checker names it, in the same job.

FOLLOW-ON (separate beads, not this ratchet): the noncanonical spellings left OUTSIDE implementation/machines that this sweep observed but did not own — skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs, docs/resources/tutorial/05-test-and-ship.md, docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md, docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/**, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md line 1698, spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md line 2022, and the ~15 reagent-adapter examples across docs/. The user-facing machines docs (docs/machines/*, docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, spec/005, spec/008) already teach rf.machines and need nothing.

title: Fix angle-bracket placeholder in pair-retro skill description
description:
## Finding

The public frontmatter description in `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` uses
the angle-bracket placeholder `<kw>` in the post-error examples (lines 16 and
34). The skill-creator validator rejects angle brackets in descriptions, so the
required quick validation gate exits non-zero on an otherwise valid skill.

## Ambiguity cost

`<kw>` is a terse placeholder whose role is not obvious to readers scanning a
trigger description, and it makes the package fail the validator before trigger
fixtures or runtime behavior can be trusted.

## Compatibility and Phase-1 exclusions

This is a frontmatter wording-only correction. Preserve the public skill name,
directory, frontmatter fields, trigger vocabulary and boundaries, allowed-tools,
routing, references, package metadata, and all runtime behavior. Do not rename
the skill or alter its explicit-pull/post-error activation semantics. Do not
touch any Phase-1 target or public/wire identifier.

## Acceptance criteria

- Replace the angle-bracket placeholder with an explicit non-angle-bracket role
  such as `reason-keyword` in every affected frontmatter/example occurrence.
- The description remains semantically equivalent and keeps the same trigger
  terms and post-error boundary.
- `quick_validate.py skills/re-frame2-pair-retro` exits 0.
- Package reference, docs/link, eval-doc, description-budget, and duplicate
  search gates remain green.
acceptance_criteria: Replace every angle-bracket placeholder in the public description/examples with the concrete keyword placeholder :error-kind; retain a user-supplied recap wording (without 'of one'); preserve skill name, frontmatter, trigger vocabulary, routing, references, IDs, paths, and behavior; quick_validate, description-budget, package-reference, docs/link, eval-doc, and duplicate-search gates all exit 0.
close_reason: Replaced invalid <kw> description placeholders with :error-kind and tightened redundant wording without changing triggers; all final skill/package/docs/eval/budget/duplicate-search gates pass.

title: spec/Security.md's decisions log has an empty Bead column and a preamble pointing at ids it no longer carries
description:

The Bead cell is blank on all 49; the only non-blank first cell is a bare '(part 1)' fragment carrying no id.

So RESTORING the ids is the wrong direction — it would reverse a ruling, and the ids do not resolve anyway (implementation/SECURITY.md:145 records that its own 45 sit below the tracker's 2026-07-11 retention floor).

TWO ARTEFACTS THE STRIP LEFT BEHIND, which are why this is worth a bead rather than nothing:

Dropping it makes the table | Call | Rationale |; the '(part 1)' fragment on the MCP-tool-authority row goes with it (it is orphaned punctuation from the id that used to precede it).

FENCE: spec/Security.md only. Not on the hot-zone one-toucher list but frequently touched; verify no live toucher at dispatch.

title: adapters README + core adapter.cljc count test-react as one of the 'six shipped adapter kinds'; Spec 006 says hicasso is the sixth
notes:
Found while landing rf2-6r9j.85 (PR #9100), out of that worker's fence.

implementation/adapters/README.md:37 reads: '3 of the 6 shipped adapter kinds install it — Reagent, reagent-slim and UIx. The other 3 omit it deliberately: plain-atom (in core) and the SSR substrate render without a live commit, so there is nothing to flush, and the test-react fixture hands the render clock to the test.'

That makes the six: reagent, reagent-slim, uix, plain-atom, ssr, test-react. Spec 006's canonical inventory (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2155-2160) lists a different six: reagent, reagent-slim, uix, HICASSO, plain-atom, ssr — and its repository-home paragraph says test-react has 'no :kind in the shipped set'. So the README substitutes test-react for hicasso.

The wording is not local to the README. implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:643-647 says almost the same thing in the flush-render! docstring: 'Three of the six shipped adapter kinds install one — Reagent, reagent-slim and UIx. The other three omit it, each for its own reason: plain-atom and SSR render without a live React commit ... and test-react hands the render clock to the test'. The two must move together or the README ends up contradicting core.

Before editing, MEASURE which adapters actually carry a :flush-render! slot rather than trusting either text — the question is whether hicasso installs one, which decides whether the corrected sentence reads 'three of six' or 'four of six'. git grep -n -F 'flush-render!' -- implementation/ (excluding test dirs) is the starting instrument; implementation/hicasso/ is the surface to settle.

Not urgent and not a correctness bug — it is a roster count in two docstrings. Sequence it behind whoever holds implementation/core.
close_reason: PR #9112. MEASURED, not inherited: FOUR of the six shipped kinds install :flush-render!, not three. Reagent + reagent-slim inject it into make-ratom-spine (reagent.cljs:113, reagent_slim.cljs:50) and make-ratom-adapter re-emits it (spine.cljs:3848); UIx AND HICASSO both get it from make-react-adapter (spine.cljs:3371), which wires (:flush-render! spine-fns) unconditionally over make-react-spine's own top-level defn (spine.cljs:1773, :3239). plain-atom (plain_atom.cljc:153-162) and SSR (ssr/substrate.cljc:80-88) carry no such key. So the corrected sentence reads 'four of six' and the two omissions share ONE reason (no live React commit to flush) rather than the old three-way split. Corrected in ONE commit in both mirrored texts: implementation/adapters/README.md:37 and implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:643-647. Spec 006 read, NOT edited (hot-zone one-toucher); its inventory is the source of truth and test-react correctly has no :kind in the shipped set. Also fixed the README's factory-family bullet, which said the React-hook pair was UIx-only and would have contradicted the new sentence. RESERVED-VALUE CALL: nothing deleted from any kind roster; the :rf.adapter/ui and :rf.adapter/freehand reserved-kind rows and the struck-through retirement bookkeeping are untouched. title: Clarify boot pattern callback locals in re-frame2 skill
description:
## Finding

The canonical machine declaration in `skills/re-frame2/patterns/boot.md` uses one-letter locals in its callback examples: `:record-config` destructures `c`, `:record-user` destructures `u`, `:record-error` destructures `e`, and the four phase actions destructure `d` for machine data (lines 39-55). The surrounding prose teaches these snippets as the canonical boot shape, so these names are likely to be copied into application code.

## Ambiguity cost

The callback context has several similarly shaped values (`:data`, `:event`, and nested payloads). A reader must look at each `assoc` target to determine whether `c`, `u`, and `e` are config, user, and error payloads, while `d` changes meaning only by convention. The shorthand makes the canonical example harder to scan and increases the chance of writing a phase action against an event payload or confusing machine data with a phase value.

## Phase-1 exclusions / compatibility

Docs-example local names only. Preserve the public skill invocation name/directory, YAML frontmatter, trigger wording, reference paths, pattern names, event IDs, machine state/data keys, callback signatures, effect shapes, and all code semantics. Do not rename `re-frame2`, `Boot`, `:app/boot`, `:phase`, or any public API/keyword. Do not alter skill routing, allowed-tools, or the existing public pattern vocabulary.

## Acceptance criteria

- The four record/phase callback examples use explicit role names such as `config-value`, `user-value`, `error-value`, and `machine-data` consistently.
- Code examples remain structurally and semantically identical apart from local binding names; all referenced keys and dispatch/event IDs are unchanged.
- No one-letter `c`, `u`, `e`, or `d` locals remain in the affected canonical declaration examples.
- `scripts/quick_validate.py skills/re-frame2` passes, and docs/link validation for the skill package remains green.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit role names in boot callback examples; identical public keys/IDs/semantics; quick validation and docs/link checks pass; no trigger/frontmatter/routing changes.
close_reason: Renamed only local bindings in canonical boot pattern examples; quick validation, doc slugs, MCP drift self-tests, and skill contracts pass.

title: Clarify duplicated nine-states todo generator names
description:
## Finding
The live and Story variants of the nine-states pattern copy the same private todo generator but call it the abbreviated gen-todos, with one-letter count/index locals. The surrounding prose calls this a generator and the helper is example-facing teaching code, so the role should be explicit.

## Evidence
- examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:148 mentions the demo server's gen-todos; :204 defines (defn- gen-todos [n]) and the for binding [i (range n)]; :229 invokes it from the managed demo stub.
- examples/patterns/nine_states/stories.cljs:108-113 defines the copied private (defn- gen-todos [n]) and [i (range n)]; :128 invokes it for the Story request value.
- Both helpers produce the same Todo shape, making the duplicated abbreviated name especially likely to be copied into future example code without communicating that it generates synthetic todos.

## Ambiguity cost
Readers must expand gen to generate and infer whether n is an item count and i is a row index in two parallel implementations; this is avoidable ambiguity in the canonical pattern example and its Story twin.

## Recommendation
Rename the two private helpers to generate-todos and their count/index locals to todo-count/index, updating only local references and the explanatory comment. Keep all event names, :n query keys, /api/todos URLs, :value payload slot, Todo schema, generated values, and control flow unchanged.

## Compatibility, exclusions, and Phase-1 fence
These helpers are private and have no public API or selector contract. Do not rename the public run/mount!/register-all! entry points, namespace/file paths (including nine_states), event/sub/machine IDs, DOM/test/build IDs, routes, serialized keys, or behavior. Do not migrate naming across other examples or touch any existing Phase-1 removal/vestigial target, shared pattern docs, or files outside examples/patterns/nine_states; risky cross-example/public migrations remain open work.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Both private gen-todos definitions and all in-slice references become generate-todos; no stale token remains in this pattern.
2. The helper arguments and loops use todo-count/index consistently, with no change to generated Todo IDs/titles/counts.
3. A semantic review confirms :n, :value, event IDs, URLs, schemas, routes, DOM/build selectors, and test-facing entry points are unchanged.
4. Focused example CLJS/JVM/lint gates and git diff --check pass.
close_reason: Implemented in the two nine-states private helpers and verified: generate-todos replaces gen-todos in core.cljs and stories.cljs; todo-count/index clarify local roles; :n query keys, :value payloads, event IDs, URLs, schemas, routes, and behavior unchanged. title: Clarify Hicasso reverse-edge MCP tool name
description:
Scope: public Hicasso reverse-edge operation naming across tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp. Exact evidence: src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs defines read-read-attribution with wire name read-read-attribution; tools/hicasso_tool.cljs exports read-read-attribution-tool and registry.cljs binds the handler; tool-descriptors.edn, README.md, spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md, test/fixtures/tool-names.json, live-hicasso-wire.cjs, and conformance_test.cljs repeat the operation name. The doubled read verb obscures that this operation is the reverse edge from subscription to reading boundaries, while the payload already calls the concept read-attribution. Ambiguity cost is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction, plus inconsistent source symbol versus payload vocabulary. Compatibility constraint: this is a public MCP tools/call name embedded in generated descriptor artifacts, closed-world allowlists, live fixtures, and wire conformance; do not silently rename or change payload keys, schemas, IDs, paths, handler behavior, or fixtures. Phase-1 fences: do not touch unrelated vestigial or generated-manifest cleanup targets, and do not alter MCP conformance wire-vocabulary scanner beads rf2-6r9j.239, .240, or .241. Recommendation: choose a migration-compatible canonical name such as read-attribution, retain the old name as an explicitly deprecated alias for a compatibility window, update descriptors and generated manifest together, then update docs, allowlists, tests, and live fixtures. Acceptance: canonical and deprecated alias behavior is specified; tools/list advertises the policy without duplicate ambiguous entries; both names produce identical reverse-edge envelopes during migration; old callers remain functional until the documented removal gate; tool-descriptors.edn is regenerated and drift-check passes; focused CLJS conformance and live-wire tests pass; no public JSON or EDN schema keys change.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A canonical reverse-edge wire name and a time-bounded deprecation policy for `read-read-attribution` are documented before the public rename lands.
2. During the compatibility window, canonical and deprecated names invoke the same handler and return identical envelopes; tools/list presents an unambiguous discovery policy.
3. Descriptor source, registry binding, generated `tool-descriptors.edn`, docs, fixture allowlists, conformance tests, and live-wire tests move together.
4. Descriptor drift, focused CLJS conformance, and live Hicasso wire checks pass for the migration.
5. Payload keys, schemas, IDs, paths, handler behavior, and unrelated MCP vocabulary remain unchanged.

notes:
2026-09-03 — PREMISE REFUTED for the RENAME half; the CLARIFY half landed in PR #9121 (head e78349f355e683ea5a7acbdd08228c8b201f4d34). LEFT OPEN for a ruling, because meeting acceptance criteria 1-3 as written would override an existing naming ruling, which is not a worker's call.

Three grounds, each checked at source.

(1) IT IS ALREADY RULED. docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md row 51 (rf2-hic-065) reads the re-frame.hicasso.tool reader door name by name — read-mounted-boundaries, read-read-attribution, read-intents, explain-render — and rules 'keep all four as shipped', with a stated reason rather than a default: the read- prefix is 'load-bearing rather than decorative', marking the reads as pure PROJECTIONS of state the runtime already retains, against a namespace whose whole design is no accumulator, no occurrence index, no history store and no second knob. explain-render is deliberately unprefixed because it FOLDS Spec 009's ring rather than reading a current table. The same row is restated in naming-packet.md row 249. This bead's evidence section does not cite that ruling.

(2) THE WIRE NAME IS THE PROVIDER FN NAME — one string, not two. hicasso_tool.cljs's projection-form interpolates (pr-str read-fn) into (cljs.core/unchecked-get d (cljs.core/munge ...)), so the literal 'read-read-attribution' passed to door-read-tool is munged and looked up on the door's namespace object at RUNTIME. The ns docstring states the invariant outright ('The wire names and the framework fn names AGREE, exactly') and hicasso_wire_test.cljs is the both-sides witness: it parses the ACTUAL EMITTED FORM and asserts every reader fn named there is defined publicly in the provider's own source.

MEASURED, not argued. Renaming the wire string to 'read-attribution' while the provider keeps read-read-attribution reds four suites: hicasso-wire-test/every-emitted-read-is-defined-by-the-provider, hicasso-wire-test/the-emitter-names-nothing-the-provider-does-not-publish, hicasso-tool-test/each-tool-emits-a-runtime-resolved-door-call, and the pair-mcp conformance corpus (4 failures, 0 errors). Control applied and restored; the restored suite is green at 1120 tests / 4070 assertions, exit 0. So a wire-only rename is not available: it would require decoupling wire name from emitted fn name — a structural change contradicting the invariant the witness exists to keep — or renaming the provider fn, which is in implementation/hicasso/ and consumed by tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/hicasso_reads.cljs, skills/re-frame2-pair/, spec/api-manifest.edn and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn.

(3) THE STATED AMBIGUITY COST IS ALREADY PAID. The bead's harm is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction, and the descriptor's FIRST CLAUSE already reads 'Which boundaries read each subscription — the reverse edge, exactly.' A model reading tools/list is not left guessing what the operation does; the descriptor also names the provider fn and gives three worked examples. Nothing about tool selection is improved by the rename, and lengthening the description would add tokens to every tools/list for a naming footnote.

Also worth stating: acceptance criteria 1 and 2 require a deprecated alias and a compatibility window. That is a back-compat shim, and the standing posture is pre-alpha with no back-compat shims. If Mike ever does rule the rename in, the right shape here is a clean cut across provider + wire + xray + skills + manifests in one PR, not an alias.

WHAT DID LAND (PR #9121, docstring only): hicasso_tool.cljs now explains the doubled verb beside the wire/provider table — the outer read- is the door's own prefix marking a pure projection, read-attribution is the payload's noun and the literal the envelope's :read slot carries — cites row 51, and records that the string is both the wire tool name and the provider fn name so the two move together or not at all. No wire name, payload key, schema, id, path, handler or fixture changed. tool-descriptors.edn untouched; its drift check is in sync (30 tools, exit 0). descriptors_data.cljs was deliberately NOT edited: its description already leads with the reverse edge.

TO WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the question for Mike is narrow — override naming-ledger row 51 for this one name, or close this bead as ruled-against. The mechanics are settled and recorded above; do not re-litigate them, and do not attempt a wire-only rename, which is measured red.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS RULED-AGAINST 2026-09-04 by the mayor, on the project's stated stance rather than by a new decision. This was held for Mike across many ticks; re-reading it, it does not need him, and holding it was the over-deference the method warns about.

THE PRIOR WORKER LEFT THE QUESTION NARROW and did the work properly (PR #9121 landed the clarify half, docstring only). Its stated question: override naming-ledger row 51 for this one name, or close as ruled-against. Four grounds settle it against, and none is mine — all four are already on the record:

(1) IT IS ALREADY RULED, WITH A REASON. docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md row 51 (rf2-hic-065) names the four reader-door operations and rules 'keep all four as shipped'. The reason is stated rather than defaulted: the read- prefix is LOAD-BEARING, marking these as pure PROJECTIONS of state the runtime already retains, against a namespace whose whole design is no accumulator, no occurrence index, no history store and no second knob — and explain-render is deliberately unprefixed because it FOLDS Spec 009's ring rather than reading a current table. Restated at naming-packet.md row 249. Overriding a reasoned ruling needs a reason of comparable weight, and the bead offers an aesthetic one.

(2) THE STATED HARM IS ALREADY PAID. The bead's cost is discoverability and prompt/tool-selection friction. The descriptor's FIRST CLAUSE reads 'Which boundaries read each subscription — the reverse edge, exactly.' A model reading tools/list is not guessing. Nothing about tool selection improves; lengthening the description would add tokens to every tools/list for a naming footnote.

(3) THE CHEAP REMEDY IS MEASURED RED. The wire name IS the provider fn name — one string, munged and looked up on the door's namespace object at runtime, with hicasso_wire_test.cljs as the both-sides witness and the ns docstring stating the invariant outright. A wire-only rename reds four suites (measured by that worker, control applied and restored, restored suite green at 1120 tests / 4070 assertions). So the only available shapes are decoupling wire from fn name — a structural change contradicting the invariant a witness exists to keep — or a clean cut across implementation/hicasso, tools/xray, skills/re-frame2-pair and two api-manifest files. That is a large, risky diff to buy a shorter name.

(4) ITS OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA VIOLATE THE POSTURE. Criteria 1 and 2 require a deprecated alias and a time-bounded compatibility window. We are PRE-ALPHA WITH NO BACK-COMPAT SHIMS. The bead cannot be satisfied as written without contradicting the stance.

ON THE STANCE, THEREFORE: 'we are not over-engineering or gold plating... we do not need to litigate every last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.' A doubled verb whose meaning is already stated in the first line of its own descriptor, protected by a reasoned ruling, whose repair is structurally contradicted and whose acceptance criteria require a shim we do not do — that is the minutia the stance names.

IF MIKE WANTS IT ANYWAY, the shape is recorded and does not need rediscovering: a clean cut across provider + wire + xray + skills + manifests in ONE PR, no alias. Reopen with that instruction and it is a straightforward dispatch. What I will not do is keep it open as a question when the project's own stated position answers it.

NOT CLOSING THE UNDERLYING WORK: PR #9121's docstring already explains the doubled verb beside the wire/provider table, cites row 51, and records that the string is both the wire tool name and the provider fn name so the two move together or not at all. A future reader meets the explanation where the confusion arises.

title: Clarify private testbed editor process-stream lifecycle locals
description:
## Finding

The private process/stream lifecycle code in `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj` uses short locals at the concurrency boundary. `drain-stream` binds `sb` for the retained diagnostic builder, `buf` for the character buffer, `cap` for the retained-character limit, `r` for the UTF-8 reader, and `n` for each read count. `launch!` binds `pb` for the process builder, `proc` for the child process, and `err-drain` for the stderr-drain future. These names sit at the timeout/pipe-concurrency boundary where each value has a distinct lifecycle role.

## Ambiguity cost

A maintainer must infer whether `cap` bounds the stream or only retained text, whether `n` is bytes or characters, and whether `err-drain` is a stream or future. The generic builder/process names also obscure which object owns stdout redirection versus stderr draining. This risks breaking deadlock prevention, UTF-8 accounting, or timeout lifecycle while ordinary tests stay green.

## Phase-1 exclusions and compatibility

This is private/local naming only. Preserve `launch!`, `drain-stream`, endpoint paths, `file`/`line`/`column`/`editor` flags, JSON keys, error tokens, exit codes, editor vocabulary, subprocess argv and ordering, stdout/stderr redirection, timeout/termination behavior, UTF-8 decoding, diagnostic cap, fixtures, and browser/JVM behavior. Exclude every vestigial, public, and test-file migration target.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rename those locals explicitly by role without changing behavior or output.
- Focused JVM and testbed-support CLJS/browser gates pass.
- No `sb`/`buf`/`cap`/`n`/`r`/`pb`/`proc`/`err-drain` binding remains for these roles.
- The diff is limited to private names and adjacent comments in this file.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit process/stream lifecycle locals; unchanged subprocess, timeout, diagnostics, and response contracts; focused JVM and testbed-support gates pass; diff limited to private names/comments.
