title: Correct the private dedup cacheability predicate spelling
description:
## Finding

`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/dedup.cljc` defines the private predicate `cachable?` and invokes it at the cache-counting and dedup traversal sites. The established English term in this artefact and its consumers is “cacheable”; the misspelling makes the predicate harder to search and obscures its role in a codec whose cache-element vocabulary is security-sensitive.

## Evidence

A fixed-symbol search finds exactly one definition and three private call sites in `dedup.cljc`, with no public export, protocol method, serialized key, CLI option, MCP operation, or fixture depending on that spelling. Repository search finds only explanatory comments in `tools/mcp-conformance/lib/dedup-envelope.cjs` and its test, not callable consumers. History shows the predicate entered with the vendored dedup codec and retained the typo through subsequent collision/escaping fixes. The predicate answers whether a form is eligible for pooling, so `cacheable?` is the precise role name.

## Recommendation

Rename only the private predicate and its three in-file calls from `cachable?` to `cacheable?`. Update explanatory comments only if necessary and do not alter conformance contracts. Preserve `de-dupe-eq`, `dedup-value`, cache marker spellings, `cache-element-ns`, marker grammar, map-entry behavior, public namespace/file, and all wire/protocol keys.

## Risks / contracts

This is private source vocabulary and should be behavior-neutral, but dedup marker names and serialized payload shapes are contracts. Do not rename public functions, namespaces, files, MCP operations, JSON/EDN keys, test fixture identifiers, or protocol terms. Exclude Phase-1/vestigial beads rf2-6r9j.104, .105, .65, .19 and active mcp-conformance transport/codec work; those targets are fenced.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `cachable?` is absent from mcp-base source and the private predicate is consistently named `cacheable?`.
2. No public var, marker, key, operation, or behavior changes; a repository diff confirms only private spelling.
3. mcp-base JVM and CLJS suites, pinned clj-kondo, and relevant dedup/conformance checks pass.
4. A planted edited-line syntax/arity fault makes each no-banner focused gate red, then exact source restoration returns both gates green.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 6fb6d39c68: renamed private dedup predicate cachable? to cacheable? and corrected the adjacent prose, preserving all public and wire contracts. JVM 288 tests/998 assertions, CLJS 48/289 assertions, pinned clj-kondo 0 warnings, and dedup conformance 21/21 passed; edited-line fault controls were red and restoration reruns green.

title: Clarify private routed-edge geometry locals in machines-viz
description:
## Finding

The private SVG route helpers in `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/edges.cljs` use generic geometry names at the points where multiple coordinate systems and path stages meet. `poly-path` (lines 70-108) calls the point count `n`, accumulator `sb`, points `a`/`b`, `prev`/`cur`/`nxt`, rounding radius `r`, entry/exit coordinates `ex`/`ey`/`xx`/`xy`, and terminal `last-pt`; `path-midpoint` (lines 115-124) repeats `n`/`i`/`a`/`b`; `cross-hierarchy-label-anchor` (lines 140-169) repeats `n`/`a`/`b` and uses `len`/`bx`/`by`. These helpers are the sole implementation of routed-edge path geometry, and the same short names recur across branches with different roles (route endpoints, bend points, label anchor, and SVG command accumulator).

## Ambiguity cost

A reader auditing route correctness must repeatedly reconstruct whether `a`/`b` are endpoints, incident points, or a segment; whether `r` is the configured corner radius or a clamped per-corner radius; and whether `bx`/`by` are a bend point or biased label coordinates. This makes geometry review and future changes prone to swapping source/target or incoming/outgoing coordinates. The code is private, so this is a local clarity-only migration.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Rename locals and private helper bindings only. Preserve `edge-path`'s public result keys (`:d`, `:label-x`, `:label-y`, `:routed?`), SVG command ordering/formatting, ELK point interpretation, label-anchor coordinates, and all render/test contracts. Do not rename `edge-path`, `transition-edge`, `chart-constants`, any data keys, graph/schema identifiers, test filenames/namespaces, or any targets owned by Phase-1 beads rf2-6r9j.109/.164. This bead excludes vestigial removal and test-file migration work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `poly-path`, `path-midpoint`, and `cross-hierarchy-label-anchor` use explicit local names for point count, endpoints/incident points, path-command accumulator, corner radius, and label-anchor coordinates.
- No behavior or output changes: existing edge geometry tests remain green and a focused before/after result comparison covers two-point, multi-bend, and cross-hierarchy paths.
- `rg` confirms no generic `n`, `a`, `b`, `sb`, `r`, `ex`, `ey`, `xx`, `xy`, or `last-pt` bindings remain in these three helpers (ordinary coordinate math may retain conventional `dx`/`dy`).
- The machines-viz artifact-owned CLJS test bundle and the proportional JVM/CLJS gates pass.
acceptance_criteria: See description acceptance criteria: explicit geometry locals in the three private route helpers; unchanged SVG/output and tests; no generic bindings in those helpers; artifact-owned gates pass.
close_reason: Renamed only private routed-edge geometry locals in chart/edges.cljs; final artifact-owned JVM and CLJS gates pass with unchanged path/output contracts.

title: Clarify private locals in reply vocabulary conformance matrices
description:
## Finding
The reply vocabulary conformance suite uses one-letter or abbreviated private lexical bindings in its EDN helper, family matrix loops, correlation helper, and time-pair loops.

## Evidence
implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:51 defines edn-roundtrip [x]; lines 467, 492, 619, 849, 862 bind family specs as :as f; lines 619-622 and 849-864 bind descriptor keys as with-k/no-k; lines 746-804 bind projected replies as out in correlation helpers and stale-row loops. These names are lexical only and do not alter vocabulary keys.

## Impact
The suite has a large cross-product of reply families and situations. Abbreviated bindings make it harder to distinguish family descriptors, key names, and projected outcomes while reviewing conformance failures, increasing maintenance and review ambiguity.

## Recommendation
Rename only lexical bindings to role-revealing names (value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome or equivalent), updating local references mechanically. Keep all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, and control-flow predicates byte-for-byte semantic equivalents.

## Compatibility and exclusions
No public API, namespace, file, operation keyword, wire/storage key, or behavior change. Do not change the matrix predicates or coverage owned by rf2-6r9j.88/.90, nor stale descriptor/inventory/path targets owned by rf2-6r9j.91 (including :error-work-status and the phantom filename); docs and files outside this bounded surface are excluded.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. All identified abbreviated locals at lines 51, 467, 492, 619-622, 746-804, and 849-864 are renamed consistently with no missed references.
2. Matrix cardinality, predicate semantics, test names, reply keys, statuses, and assertion counts remain unchanged.
3. Focused CLJS/JVM test and lint gates pass, and git diff --check is clean.
notes: Detailed scope: exact evidence is implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc lines 51 ([x] in edn-roundtrip), 467 and 492 (:as f family descriptor aliases), 619-622 (with-k/no-k descriptor key locals), 746-804 (out projected outcome helper/control locals), and 849-864 (with-k/no-k time-pair controls). Ambiguity cost is reviewer inference across a large family x situation matrix. Rename lexical bindings only to value, family-spec, with-key/no-key, outcome; preserve all descriptor map keys, test names, statuses, payloads, predicates, cardinality, and assertion counts. Explicitly exclude semantic matrix predicates and coverage in rf2-6r9j.88/.90 and stale :error-work-status, phantom filename, inventory/docs targets in rf2-6r9j.91. Acceptance is a lexical-only diff, no public/wire/storage change, green focused CLJS/JVM/kondo and git diff --check.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No k3- or perm- private fixture symbol remains in this namespace.
2. Replacement names state the actual role (non-route live composition versus registration-permutation canonical-edge fixture; navigation token, scoped key, generation, work ID, contributors, sub node, resource key, route, expected edges, and permutation generator).

4. Focused derivation-conformance JVM and shared CLJS node tests pass with unchanged test/assertion totals; focused lint introduces no naming or unused-binding diagnostics.

title: Disambiguate Event Conformance reply and correlation values
description:
## Finding

The two retained reply/event integration cases use generic locals at the boundary where four distinct values coexist: the reply target, the completed event vector, the reply envelope delivered on that vector, and carried/current correlation state. `observe-stale-reply!` destructures a local named `reply` beside the `reply` namespace alias, yielding `reply/complete target reply`; the success row similarly calls both the source envelope and delivered envelope `reply`, while `completed` omits that it is an event. The observer row uses `pool`, `img`, `target`, `carried`, `current`, `outcome`, and `delivered`, obscuring image setup and suppression roles.

## Evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:74-76` visually overloads the `reply` namespace alias and local envelope in one expression.
- Lines 83-114 distinguish observed event/coeffects, completion, and delivered envelope using `seen-cofx`, `target`, `reply`, `completed`, and `delivered`.
- Lines 130-196 build an explicit image-loaded frame and a stale-suppression correlation pair under `pool`, `img`, `target`, `carried`, `current`, `outcome`, and `delivered`.
- Managed-Effects names these concepts reply target, completed event, reply map/envelope, carried/current correlation facts, and stale-suppression outcome. EP-0023 names registration sets and image values.
- History shows the observer helper replaced an older delivery gate; its current local names were inherited through that semantic shift.
- No all-status bead owns these naming changes. Phase-1 bead `rf2-6r9j.97` owns the separate vacuous stale non-delivery row, which is excluded entirely.

## Recommendation

Rename retained-case locals to `seen-coeffects`, `reply-target`, `completed-event`, `delivered-reply`, `stale-reply`, `dispatch-options`, `image-registrations`, `event-image`, `carried-correlation`, `current-correlation`, `suppression-outcome`, and `handler-call-count`. Update the observer helper's destructuring explicitly so the namespace alias is never shadowed. Preserve all registered ids and reply/correlation map keys.

## Risks / contracts

This is test-private naming only. Do not change the canonical reply envelope, `:deliver?`, correlation data, reply target shape, registered event/image/frame ids, dispatch options, handler routing, assertions, or namespace/file names. Do not edit the `rf2-6r9j.97` deletion/replacement target or its namespace prose.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The retained success and observer paths clearly distinguish target, completed event, delivered/stale reply, image setup, correlation inputs, and suppression outcome.
2. No local reply envelope shadows the `reply` namespace alias in retained code.
3. The Phase-1-owned stale non-delivery test remains unchanged.
4. Event-conformance JVM and consolidated CLJS Node suites, focused lint, exact searches, and diff checks pass.

title: Name test-quiet subprocess harness process and stream roles
description:
## Naming finding

These are central diagnostic paths where a confused process, stream, or timeout result produces misleading gate evidence.

## Proposed names

Use `invoke-quiet-runner` / `invoke-quiet-runner-with-env`, `process`, `stdout-future`, `stderr-future`, `exited?`, `path-separator`, `classpath`, `command`, `process-builder`, and `child-environment`. In the lifecycle suite use `drain-process`, `run-lifecycle-program`, `program-source`, `program-file`, and `windows?`. In the CLJS spawn harness use `runner-script` and `spawn-result`. title: spec-resource race control: name cold-load actors and phases
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`implementation/spec-resource/test/re_frame/build/spec_resource_test.clj` is the deterministic control for the cold-load race closed by `resolve-after-require`. Its concurrency harness uses generic names that obscure which actor and phase each value belongs to: `counter` generates unique namespace and gate names, `fixture-root` is specifically a temporary classpath root, `generate-fixture!` writes a namespace whose initializer is deliberately blocked, and `run-probe` observes a resolver while that load is held open. Inside the probe, `answer`, `loaded`, `armed`, `observed`, `loader`, `observer`, `sym`, and `in-window` require repeated backtracking to distinguish loader-thread results, observer-thread results before/after release, the probe Var, and the held-open phase. The returned keys repeat that ambiguity (`:sym`, `:in-window`, `:observed`, `:loaded`).

This matters because the test's proof depends on actor and phase identity: the known-broken resolver must return an unbound Var during the held-open load, while the shipped resolver must block and both actors must see a bound Var after release. Misreading `loaded` as a load-status flag or `observed` as the during-window observation weakens review of the one deterministic witness for the defect.

History confirms these are original names from `5311835961`, when the whole control was introduced. Searches across all-status beads for `spec-resource`, `run-probe`, `recording-slurp`, and `resolve-after-require` found only Phase-1 removal beads `rf2-6r9j.80` and `.82`; neither owns this retained race control.

## Recommendation

Rename private test helpers, locals, and result keys by role and phase: for example `cold-load-iterations`, `unique-name-sequence`, `fixture-classpath-root`, `write-blocked-fixture-namespace!`, `observe-resolver-during-load`, `probe-var-symbol`, `observe-var-state`, `loader-result`, `observer-entered-resolver`, `observer-result`, `loader-thread`, `observer-thread`, and `:during-load` / `:observer-result` / `:loader-result`. Update docstrings and every test consumer together.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is test-private vocabulary only. Preserve the public namespace/file names, `resolve-after-require`, `slurp-resource`, the known-broken `requiring-resolve` control, thread/gate timing, assertion semantics, and production serialized data. title: Clarify test-quiet reporter namespace-banner state and callbacks
description:
## Naming finding

The shared CLJC reporter uses compressed `ns` terminology and names its state by incidental representation rather than domain role. In `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet.cljc:91-266`, `printed-banners` is actually a set of namespace symbols, `ns-stack` is the balanced stack of open test namespaces, and helpers such as `failing-ns`, `event-ns`, and `banner-ns` represent three distinct namespace sources. The current names force readers to repeatedly consult docstrings to distinguish stored namespace identity from rendered banner text and failure-var versus report-event versus fallback selection.

## Proposed names

Use explicit private roles: `printed-banner-namespaces`, `open-test-namespace-stack`, `open-test-namespace!`, `close-test-namespace!`, `current-test-namespace`, `namespace-banner-printed?`, `mark-namespace-banner-printed!`, `print-namespace-banner!`, `failing-test-namespace`, `report-event-namespace`, and `failure-banner-namespace`. Spell out private parameters/locals such as `namespace-symbol`, `test-var`, and `test-namespace`. Update both CLJ and CLJS branches and all comments/references together.

## Ambiguity cost

This reporter is intentionally stateful across nested `run-tests` calls. The abbreviated names obscure which namespace source is authoritative at each event and make future lifecycle fixes more likely to mutate the wrong state or mark the wrong banner as printed.

## Compatibility / risk

All proposed Vars are private and repository-wide searches find no out-of-namespace consumers or serialized use. Preserve the public namespace, reporter multimethod dispatch keys, output text/shape, nesting semantics, reload-safe default-method captures, and public runtime entry points. No Phase-1 bead targets these helpers; existing Phase-1 test-quiet beads concern copied selector coverage, exit-integrity coverage, and duplicate subprocess rows.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every private banner-state Var/helper names its namespace role explicitly in both reader-condition branches, with all references and docstrings updated.
2. No old compressed helper/state name remains in executable code or prose where it denotes the renamed construct.
3. JVM and consolidated CLJS reporter tests preserve green output shape, red banner selection, nested-run behavior, and test-ns-hook fallback.
4. Public namespaces, report dispatch IDs, emitted text, and callable entry points are unchanged.

title: ssr-node HTTP launcher: name buffers, parsed requests, and launch settings
description:
## Coverage and evidence

The HTTP/launcher edge has several names that conceal the represented phase. `src/http.cjs:92-123` calls buffered request chunks `parts`, the over-ceiling state `over`, and each chunk/error `c`/`e`; `handleRender` calls the decoded protocol request `parsed` and buffered response HTML `buffered`. `bin/serve.cjs` calls its numeric parser `integer`, the parsed number `n`, and the combined numeric launch settings `limits` even though the map also includes `port`; the live transport is `http` and its bound address is only `bound`. These all descend from the initial transport/launcher commits (b2b35bf6e9 and 608b2a24b1).

The ambiguity costs the most at boundaries: `parts` could be decoded request partitions, `buffered` could be a boolean mode, `limits.port` is not a limit, and `http` does not say that it is the closeable transport returned by `serve`.

## Recommendation

Use edge-role names such as `bodyChunks`, `receivedBytes`, `overLimit`, `chunk`, `renderRequest`, `bufferedHtmlChunks`, `parseIntegerFlag`, `minimum`, `numericOptions`, `transport`, and `boundAddress`. Keep conventional Node handler `req`/`res` names, public transport API, CLI flags, and wire fields unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is private/local identifier work only. Preserve exported `serve`, `statusFor`, `STATUS`, the returned `{server, port, host, close}` object, CLI flags/help/ready-line/exit codes, request selection semantics, response headers, and serialized body/refusal shapes. Do not edit the stale help/README wording owned by rf2-6r9j.86 or the retired-selector behavior pinned by rf2-6r9j.72.
acceptance_criteria:

2. Launcher names distinguish flag parsing, numeric launch options, the running transport, and its bound address.

title: ssr-node isolate pool: name lifecycle state by ownership and phase
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`src/isolate.cjs` and `src/pool.cjs` implement the worker lifecycle. The isolate's private state machine uses `_nextRequestSeq` for an internal render-dispatch ID distinct from public `requestId`, `_settle(id, act)`, `_fail`, `_die`, and repeated `p`/`w`/`msg` locals. The pool calls its boot-and-register operation `_spawn`, its replacement-only race-safe wrapper `_spawnTracked`, stores only replacement boots in a generic `spawning` set, and stores the full membership in `all`; teardown and replacement paths use `fresh`, `w`, `i`, and another `all`. `_spawnTracked`/`spawning` were added by 8ab673ea78 specifically to close the replacement-vs-close race, so their lifecycle purpose is stable and more precise than the mechanism name.

These names blur ownership and phase in code whose correctness depends on exactly those distinctions: public versus isolate-local IDs, initial boots versus replacement boots, pending render settlement versus worker termination, and all isolates versus idle isolates.

## Recommendation

Use private role names such as `_nextRenderId`, `_settlePendingRender`, `_failPendingRender`, `_terminateWorker`, `pendingRender`, `worker`, `_startIsolate`, `_startReplacement`, `startingReplacements`, `isolates`, `startedIsolates`, `failedStart`, and `replacement`. Keep public stats and refusal payload keys unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

The affected methods/fields are package-private and have no repository consumer outside these two files. Preserve public `Isolate.render/start/close`, `Pool.acquire/release/stats/close`, `busy`, worker message keys, refusal detail keys, and health JSON. Do not remove `renders` or the `WORKER_PATH` export; rf2-6r9j.84 owns those vestiges.

4. rf2-6r9j.84 deletion targets remain untouched.

title: ssr-node render pipeline: distinguish frames, dispatch IDs, and module returns
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`src/service.cjs` bridges an isolate callback into the public async generator with `req`, `queue`, `wake`, `nudge`, `finished`, `failure`, `terminal`, and `run`. The names hide which side owns each value: the queue holds pending public frames, `wake` is the suspended generator continuation, `terminal` is the isolate's render result, and `run` is the completion/release promise. `src/worker.cjs` uses `mod`, `post`, `id`, `seq`, `snapshot`, `call`, and especially `out` for the application module's returned value at the fail-closed egress check. These names date to b2b35bf6e9; the body-only egress hardening in 67d4d9338a made the returned value security-significant without renaming it.

A reader currently has to infer whether `id` is the caller's `requestId` or the isolate-local render ID, and whether `out` is emitted HTML or the forbidden second-channel return. The callback/generator bridge similarly makes `run` and `terminal` easy to confuse with frames.

## Recommendation

Name service values by asynchronous role (`validatedRequest`, `pendingFrames`, `resumeConsumer`, `wakeConsumer`, `renderFinished`, `renderFailure`, `renderResult`, `renderCompletion`). Name worker-private values by boundary role (`renderModule`, `renderId`, `chunkSeq`, `stateSnapshot`, `runtimeSnapshot`, `renderCall`, `moduleReturnValue`, `postMessage`). Update comments and internal calls together.

## Compatibility and exclusions

Do not rename public `Service`, `renderFrames`, `renderToString`, `createService`, the render-module `render`/`emit` contract, message discriminators or keys (`t`, `id`, `seq`), request/frame fields, or serialized refusal details. Do not edit the worker `stack` payloads owned for removal by rf2-6r9j.77, and do not absorb the `chunkFrame` integration owned by rf2-6r9j.74.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Service bridge bindings identify pending frames, the suspended consumer, render completion, result, and failure without generic `queue`/`wake`/`run`/`terminal` names.
2. Worker bindings distinguish the isolate-local render ID, state/runtime snapshots, render call, and forbidden module return value.
3. Public APIs, render-module contract, worker message schema, frame schema, refusal behavior, and stack-removal target remain byte/shape compatible.
4. Exact old/new searches, lint, focused egress/streaming tests, and the full ssr-node gate pass.

title: ssr-node protocol validation: name boundary values by role
description:
## Coverage and evidence

`implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs` is the fail-closed module/request grammar. Its internal validation names obscure the values being adjudicated: `validateAllowlist(where, id, entry, { allowlist, keys })` uses `keys` for the human partition label (`app-db`/`runtime-db`), not keys; `validateModule(mod, where)` hides that `where` is a diagnostic module label; `validatePartition(req, entry, entryId, ...)` then uses `k`, `v`, and `bytes` at the security boundary; `validateRequest(req, tables)` names the two validation results `state` and `runtime` even though each is `{partition, bytes}`, and `why` is the deliberate-refusal explanation. These names date to initial commit b2b35bf6e9; 9a42302f7a added the second partition without resolving the role ambiguity.

The ambiguity makes review of the most security-sensitive path need repeated lookups: `keys` sounds like a collection, `entry` alternates between an ID and a config, and `state`/`runtime` sometimes mean maps and sometimes validation results.

## Recommendation

Use role names such as `moduleLabel`, `entryId`, `entryConfig`, `allowlistField`, `partitionLabel`, `partitionField`, `partitionKey`, `ednText`, `partitionBytes`, `stateValidation`, `runtimeValidation`, `requestBytes`, and `intentionalRefusalReason`. Keep the public/exported validator names and every field/refusal spelling unchanged.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is identifier-only: JavaScript parameter names and private locals are not call contracts. Preserve exported `validateModule`/`validateRequest`, `PARTITIONS`, `CODE`, all serialized request/detail keys, and the `STATE_KEY_NOT_ALLOWED` wire member. Do not touch `chunkFrame`, `KEY_TEXT`/`refuse` exports, or other residue owned by rf2-6r9j.74/.84.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every protocol validation argument/local states whether it is a module label, entry ID/config, partition field/label/key, EDN value, validation result, or byte total.

title: Routing namespaces: finish the canonical rf.* require-alias migration
description:
Partition: implementation/routing namespace and require-alias vocabulary across production source, tests, recipes, and helpers.

Evidence:
- `spec/Conventions.md` §Require-alias dialect requires `re-frame.core` to use `rf` and every framework subsystem `re-frame.<tail>` to use the dotted `rf.<tail>` alias; it explicitly reserves bare leaf aliases such as `routing` for application namespaces.
- A clj-kondo namespace-usage census over all 88 routing code files, deduplicated by `[file target alias]` so CLJC host analysis does not double-count, found 438 noncanonical aliased framework edges in 83 files: 145 in 26 production files and 293 in 57 test/recipe files. Common examples are `re-frame.routing :as routing` (40), `re-frame.frame :as frame` (27), `re-frame.interop :as interop` (25), `re-frame.fx :as fx` (23), and `re-frame.late-bind :as late-bind` (21).
- The facade and internal routing namespaces also alias routing siblings inconsistently (`registry`, `routing-events`, `routing-subs`, `route-reply`) instead of deriving the canonical aliases from their namespace tails (`rf.routing.registry`, `rf.routing.events`, `rf.routing.subs`, `rf.routing.reply`).
- Commit `d848371f60` made the alias rule normative while explicitly deferring SCOPE 2, the repo-wide implementation sweep. Two later routing naming passes (`2df2d88a37`, `eed266f99a`) deliberately limited themselves to local/private names. All-status searches for bare framework aliases and routing namespace aliases found only the new core-specific sibling `rf2-6r9j.161` plus closed docs/machines rulings, not a routing implementation owner.

Ambiguity cost:
Routing source currently contradicts the normative and published dialect, and bare framework aliases consume names the convention reserves for application namespaces. At call sites, a reader cannot tell whether `routing/...`, `frame/...`, or `events/...` denotes framework code or an application's same-named feature without consulting the ns form. Inconsistent aliases for routing siblings add a second local dialect.

Recommendation:
Migrate routing in reviewable namespace families to exact dotted aliases (`re-frame.routing` -> `rf.routing`, `re-frame.routing.registry` -> `rf.routing.registry`, `re-frame.frame` -> `rf.frame`, etc.), keeping `re-frame.core` -> `rf` as the sole root exemption and leaving side-effect-only unaliased requires alone. Update every qualified use with syntax-aware tooling. Add or extend a parsed CI ratchet so new noncanonical framework aliases cannot enter while the broader migration proceeds.

Risks/contracts:
Aliases are compile-time source vocabulary, not runtime API, but this is a high-churn 83-file CLJ/CLJS/CLJC change with reader conditionals, macros, test fixtures, and app-like recipe namespaces. Mechanical replacement must not touch keyword/event/fx/late-bind IDs, namespace symbols, quoted data, public vars, external library aliases, or genuine application aliases. Stage separately from semantic routing changes and coordinate the ratchet with sibling surface bead `rf2-6r9j.161` rather than building duplicate enforcement.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every tracked implementation/routing source/test namespace aliases `re-frame.core` as `rf` and other framework subsystem namespaces with the canonical `rf.<namespace-tail>` spelling, except documented convention exemptions and unaliased side-effect requires.
- Every qualified use is updated; a parsed, CLJC-deduplicated census reports zero non-exempt routing-surface violations.
- A shared syntax-aware CI ratchet prevents regressions without duplicating the enforcement planned by `rf2-6r9j.161`.
- Routing JVM tests, all routing CLJS builds/tests, lint, production-gate/bundle-isolation gates where applicable, and git diff --check pass.
- No public var, namespace declaration, keyword/event/fx/late-bind ID, serialized value, quoted symbol/data, external dependency alias, or application namespace alias changes.
close_reason:
PR #9103. All 438 noncanonical framework require edges in implementation/routing (83 files) migrated to the spec/Conventions.md dialect: re-frame.core keeps rf, every other re-frame.<tail> takes the dotted rf.<tail>, every qualified use moved with it.

title: Replace opaque machines regression-test filenames with semantic suites
description:
## Locations and evidence

Three tracked test namespaces use provenance/churn names rather than the behaviors they own:
- `machine_remediation_ee38b_test.clj` mixes root `:on` fallback, unhandled/microstep traces, forbidden `:db`, update-snapshot, history placement, and callback-ref validation.
- `trace_enhancements_rf2_82a0u_test.clj` mixes action phase/guard traces with timer cancellation traces.
- `machine_remaining_lifecycle_tail_fence_test.clj` covers destroy continuation fencing, timer subscription release, spawn-all iteration, and classification removal.

All file/namespace mappings are mechanically valid, but the names are opaque to a reader and make test discovery by feature difficult. History shows the first two retain implementation bead/commit labels from their introduction rather than stable behavior names.

## Ambiguity cost

A contributor searching for root fallback, guard failure, timer cancellation, or destroy-incarnation fencing cannot predict which suite owns it. “remediation”, “enhancements”, and “remaining” communicate project history rather than the contract under test, and broad mixed suites become accidental dumping grounds.

## Recommendation

Split/rename by stable behavior, preserving tests and history with moves: root fallback/validation, action+guard traces, timer cancellation traces, and destroy-incarnation fencing. Prefer existing focused suites when a test can be moved without duplication; use semantic namespaces matching filenames. Update any exact path references and test classifier manifests.

## Compatibility / migration risk

Test namespaces/files are not runtime API, but classifier discovery, targeted commands, doc references, and history followability are contracts. Use history-preserving moves, verify every original deftest appears exactly once, and avoid merging behavior changes into the reorganization.
acceptance_criteria:
- No machines test filename/namespace contains `remediation`, `enhancements-rf2`, or `remaining-lifecycle`.
- Replacement suites have semantic filenames/namespaces and every original deftest is retained exactly once.
- Repository exact-path references and classifier enrollment are updated.
- Focused replacement suites plus full machines JVM/CLJS gates pass.
- The reorganization is committed separately from behavioral changes.
close_reason:
PR #9103. No machines test filename or namespace now contains remediation, enhancements-rf2 or remaining-lifecycle; census confirms the three old namespace names 1 -> 0 each and the five new ones 0 -> 1 each, with nested-validation-test as the control that fired and held at 1 -> 1.

Two of the three were renames ONLY, because the bead's split recommendation does not apply to a suite that is already one thing:
  machine_remaining_lifecycle_tail_fence_test -> machine_destroy_tail_incarnation_fence_test (it fences the ordinary :rf.machine/destroy teardown tail to its exact incarnation across three sub-paths, and rejoins the *_incarnation_fence_test family it completes)
  trace_enhancements_rf2_82a0u_test -> machine_trace_payload_shapes_test (it pins the CLOSED payload vocabularies three machine trace events carry — :phase, :outcome, :reason)

The third genuinely was not one thing — 14 deftests over six unrelated Spec 005 rules — so it split three ways along seams a reader can predict:

title: Make after-timer cancellation race helpers name their protocol
description:
## Locations and evidence

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:351-475` implements a delicate reserve/announce/claim cancellation protocol with private names `*announcing*`, `announced!`, and `claim-emit-release!`. The dynamic var is specifically a set of attempt tokens; `announced!` completes an announcement-cell CAS; the claim helper claims a cancellation, emits/delegates its cancelled row, and releases resources. At `after-cancel-fx` line 1117, local `snap` is a vector snapshot of timer entries, while `snap` elsewhere in the same file means a machine snapshot. `successor-published?-fn` also binds generic `captured` for a frame incarnation token.

## Ambiguity cost

These names force readers of concurrency-sensitive code to reconstruct which object is announcing/claimed/released and make `snap` mean two incompatible values in one namespace. That raises review risk around a protocol whose ordering comments explicitly say branch order is load-bearing.

## Recommendation

Identifier-only rename: `*announcing*` -> `*announcing-attempt-tokens*`, `announced!` -> `finish-announcement!`, `claim-emit-release!` -> `claim-cancel-and-release!`, `captured` -> `captured-incarnation`, and the non-machine `snap` -> `timer-entry-snapshot`. Update timer source comments and the race-test docstring.

## Compatibility / migration risk

All renamed vars except the local are private; repository search shows only in-file calls plus explanatory test prose. Do not reorder expressions, change CAS operations, alter dynamic binding scope, or change trace/serialized keys. Concurrency behavior must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact search finds no old private helper/dynamic-var spellings and no non-machine local named `snap` in `after-cancel-fx`.
- Reservation, scheduled-row, deferred-cancellation, claim, and release ordering is unchanged.

title: Core namespaces: finish the canonical rf.* require-alias migration
description:
Partition: implementation/core namespace and require-alias vocabulary across source and tests.

Evidence:
- spec/Conventions.md, Require-alias dialect, requires re-frame.core to use rf and every framework subsystem re-frame.<leaf> to use the dotted rf.<leaf> alias; bare leaf aliases are reserved for application namespaces.
- A clj-kondo namespace-usage census over all 88 source and 272 test files found 1,616 distinct noncanonical framework require edges in 311 files after deduplicating CLJC host analysis: 328 edges in 68 source files and 1,288 in 243 test files. Examples include re-frame.late-bind :as late-bind, re-frame.frame :as frame, re-frame.trace :as trace, and re-frame.trace.tooling :as trace-tooling.
- Commit d848371f60 established the rule and explicitly deferred SCOPE 2, the repository-wide sweep. Current history shows narrow routing/machines documentation follow-ups but no core implementation sweep.
- All-status bead searches found only closed narrow machines/docs residues (rf2-qt7au, rf2-ur6kh, rf2-lzrza), not a core-wide migration.

Ambiguity cost:
Core currently teaches a different alias language from its own normative convention. Bare framework aliases collide conceptually with the application aliases the rule reserves, and readers cannot distinguish framework-owned dependencies at call sites without checking each ns form.

Recommendation:
Migrate core in coherent, reviewable families to the exact dotted namespace-tail aliases (for example re-frame.frame -> rf.frame, re-frame.late-bind -> rf.late-bind, re-frame.trace.tooling -> rf.trace.tooling), updating every qualified use. Keep re-frame.core -> rf as the explicit exemption. Add an automated ratchet based on parsed namespace usages so new bare framework aliases cannot enter while migration proceeds or after it reaches zero.

Risks/contracts:
Aliases are compile-time source vocabulary rather than runtime API, but this is a high-churn 311-file change spanning CLJ, CLJS, CLJC reader conditionals, macros, and test helpers. Mechanical replacement must avoid keyword roots, quoted data, late-bind keys, public symbols, prose, app namespaces, and external library aliases. Stage and gate it separately rather than folding it into unrelated semantic edits.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every tracked implementation/core source and test namespace aliases re-frame.core as rf and other re-frame subsystem namespaces with the canonical rf.<namespace-tail> spelling, unless an explicit convention exemption is documented.
- Every qualified symbol use is updated and exact parsed census reports zero non-exempt bare framework aliases.
- A syntax-aware CI ratchet rejects newly introduced violations and handles CLJC reader conditionals without double counting.
- Core JVM tests, relevant CLJS builds/tests, bundle-isolation checks, lint, and git diff --check pass.
- No keyword IDs, late-bind keys, serialized data, public vars, or application/external namespace aliases are changed.
notes: MERGED-PR AUDIT #9103: reopened for one non-exempt core alias the migration census missed. implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj uses a real top-level (require ...) form at line 36, binding re-frame.late-bind.directory as bare directory, then calls directory/hooks, directory/hook-keys, and directory/entry. Spec Conventions reserves the bare leaf form for application namespaces; this must be rf.late-bind.directory with its qualified uses moved. A post-merge scan of every [re-frame.* :as *] form found 31 apparent exceptions: 16 documented host-conditional substrate bindings, 11 routing fixture strings, 3 user-facing/example forms, and this single executable core miss. Keep rf2-j5or as the existing owner of the shared future ratchet; no second ratchet is needed here.
close_reason:
PR #9128 (head fec380e7d83ce18dedb45196ba94c23d5c39ab39, branch worker/corealias-a). The residue behind PR #9103 was ONE edge in ONE file, and the merged-PR audit note on this bead named it exactly: implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj:36. Migrated to rf.late-bind.directory with its 8 qualified use sites. implementation/core now reads 0 non-exempt noncanonical require edges.

CENSUS, by balanced-bracket scan of every [re-frame...] libspec vector over 349 tracked core .clj/.cljs/.cljc files (1795 re-frame require edges total): pre-#9103 tree (1db71eac77^) 1617 non-exempt noncanonical edges across 311 files; post-#9103 origin/main 1 edge in 1 file; this branch 0. PR #9103 itself touched 312 core files, +11168/-11155.

WHY #9103 MISSED IT, and the account is exact rather than a guess. The edge is not an (ns ... (:require ...)) edge at all — it is a runtime top-level (require '[re-frame.late-bind.directory :as directory]), which clj-kondo's namespace-usage analysis does not report. That is why the bead's clj-kondo census read 1616 where a textual balanced-bracket scan of the SAME tree reads 1617: the one-edge delta IS this edge. Worth carrying to rf2-ydpr's ratchet design, which currently specifies scanning libspec vectors but does not say that runtime (require ...) forms must be in scope — they must, or the ratchet reproduces this exact miss.

LITERAL-KEYWORD MULTISET CONTROL: IDENTICAL before and after, 0 entries changed — 3652 distinct literal single-colon :ns/name keywords, 22833 occurrences, across all of implementation/core. Not a claim; the diff of the two multisets is empty.

HOST-CONDITIONAL EXEMPTIONS: ZERO in core, by the DERIVED predicate (an alias bound to 2+ distinct namespaces within one file), not a path list. This refines rf2-j5or's note, which said 'machines has one instance, routing had eight, core one'. Core has none: the predicate found no alias bound to two namespaces in any of the 349 files, including the 143 core .cljc files that carry BOTH reader conditionals and re-frame requires. Textual edge count equals deduplicated edge count (1795 = 1795), so no core file binds the same libspec twice across reader arms either — core's re-frame requires sit in the common part.

TRAP 1 CONFIRMED LIVE IN CORE: 39 libspec vectors in core SPAN LINES, e.g. [re-frame.trace :as rf.trace / #?@(:cljs [:include-macros true])]. A line-anchored regex would have missed every one. BOTH LIVE GATES PROVEN TO BITE AND TO BE READING THIS CHECKOUT. A planted rf.late-bind.directoryX/hooks returned exit 1 naming rf.late-bind.directoryX — a token existing only in this worktree, so a run that had wandered into a sibling would have come back green; restored and verified by blob hash 0c3b55026700f8569e0b998fc76a3d4a50c89ef7. Several private helpers in the reagent-slim adapter contract tests are harder to understand than the production behavior they isolate: `fresh-slim`, `fake-root`, `spy-rdc!`, `of-kind`, `a-mock-emitter`, `with-cleared-emitter`, and repeated `mk-fake-root` spellings. The Root API spy also uses single-letter root/mount/tree locals in call records whose argument identity is the test's subject.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_client_root_cljs_test.cljs:16-54` uses `fresh-slim`, `fake-root`, `spy-rdc!`, and `of-kind`; only the spy docstring reveals it runs a body and returns captured Root API calls. `rdc` is a namespace alias, not the behavior under test, and `of-kind` does not say it filters calls.
- `test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_cljs_test.cljs:36-52` names a real fixture callback `a-mock-emitter` and omits `hiccup` from the clearing helper.
- `reagent_slim_dispose_drain_roots_cljs_test.cljs` and `reagent_slim_render_cljs_test.cljs` independently use the non-idiomatic `mk-fake-root`, while the sibling client-root suite spells the same concept `fake-root`.
- Exact searches show these are file-private/test-only helpers. No production API, discovery namespace, selector, operation keyword, or fixture registration contract depends on their spelling.

## Recommendation

Rename to `with-fresh-slim-adapter`, `make-fake-root`, `record-root-api-calls`, `calls-of-kind`, `mock-hiccup-emitter`, and `with-cleared-hiccup-emitter`. Expand the Root API spy's ambiguous local/parameter names (`remaining-roots`, `next-root!`, `mount-point`, `root`, `render-tree`).

## Contracts and risk

Keep every test namespace/file name, deftest name unless directly tied to a renamed production helper, fixture order, adapter reset/install/dispose sequence, recorded call vector shape, assertions, selectors, and production code unchanged. Do not remove imports or `static-prop`; that cleanup belongs to `rf2-6r9j.34`.

## Duplicate search

All-status beads were searched for the exact helper names and test-helper naming concepts. No existing bead owns these renames; `rf2-6r9j.34` is strictly dead test declarations and is non-overlapping.

title: Name schemas validation callbacks, outcomes, and trace paths by role
description:
Partition: implementation/schemas validation pipeline.

Locations and evidence:
- implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:321-322 abbreviates the humanizer callback as `hum-fn`.
- validate.cljc:378-382, 457-504, and 656-704 use `vf`, `result`, `ex`, and `base` around a three-way validator outcome (`true`, `false`, or `[:malformed throwable]`). The short names make the security-sensitive malformed-schema branch harder to audit.
- validate.cljc:665-670 abbreviates the registered path/value as `reg-path` and `reg-slice`.
- validate.cljc:843-848 calls the path selected for trace emission `path-in` and then `leaf-path`, even though it may contain redaction sentinels and is specifically the trace-safe path.

Ambiguity cost:
The validator's return value is not an ordinary boolean, and the two path forms have different privacy guarantees. Generic abbreviations obscure when code is handling a callback versus its tagged outcome, a raw Malli `:in` path versus its sanitized trace representation, and a registered root versus the value read from app-db. That increases review cost precisely on fail-closed and redaction branches.

Proposed names:
- `hum-fn` -> `humanize-fn`
- `vf` -> `validate-fn`
- `result` -> `validation-result`; `ex` -> `validator-error`; `base` -> `base-tags`
- `reg-path` -> `registered-path`; `reg-slice` -> `registered-value`; `schema-meta` -> `registration-metadata`
- `path-in` -> `trace-in-path`; `leaf-path` -> `trace-path`

Compatibility and migration risk:
Change lexical bindings only. Preserve public validate-* arglists, private function names, schema and trace operation IDs, serialized tags/reasons, recovery values, validation order, continuation semantics, and late-bind hooks. Do not touch `walk-schema?`, which is owned by the existing vestigial-code bead rf2-6r9j.45.
acceptance_criteria: Validation locals clearly distinguish callbacks, tagged outcomes, validator errors, registration roots/values, and trace-safe paths; emitted maps and public arglists remain unchanged; rf2-6r9j.45-owned code is untouched; exact searches, focused JVM/CLJS tests, lint, and diff checks pass.
notes: Completion evidence: commit 40d0d59c011294203e6cbe969b27c4152d6737e6 (refactor(schemas): clarify internal names) changed schemas validation callback/outcome/path naming; available full clj-kondo gate gate-kondo-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (errors 0), consolidated CLJS gate implementation/gate-cljs-codex-naming-07-1.exit=0 (11,209 tests, 55,849 assertions, 0 failures/errors).

title: reagent-slim static renderer: name helpers by serialized output role
description:
## Finding

The pure static HTML serializer in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs` mixes abbreviated attribute/value names with helpers whose names describe input representation rather than emitted output: `attr-name`, `emit-attr(s)`, `merge-shorthand`, `react-component-comment`, `emit-dom-vector`, and `emit-vector`.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- `attr-name`, `named->str`, `style-value->str`, and `attr-value-string` span lines 355-515; each sits in security/parity-sensitive serialization code where spelling out attribute/string roles reduces context switching.
- `emit-attr`/`emit-attrs` at lines 618-694 perform filtering plus mutation of the output buffer, not merely attribute formatting.
- `merge-shorthand` at lines 704-725 merges parsed tag id/class shorthand; the unqualified name does not say what shorthand.
- `react-component-comment` at lines 733-737 is an emitting operation that appends the opaque placeholder.
- `emit-dom-vector` and `emit-vector` at lines 744-890 require readers to remember one emits a DOM element and the other dispatches every Hiccup vector head.
- The serializer's only external surface is `render-to-static-markup`; exact searches show these candidates are private. Targeted history traces them to the original Stage 4-E serializer, with no compatibility consumers.

## Recommendation

Adopt consistent `attribute`/`string` spellings and emitted-shape names: `attribute-name`, `named-value->string`, `style-value->string`, `attribute-value-string`, `emit-attribute`, `emit-attributes`, `merge-tag-shorthand`, `emit-react-component-placeholder`, `emit-dom-element`, and `emit-hiccup-vector`; align private constant names and in-slice comments/spec references where needed.

## Contracts and risk

Preserve byte-for-byte HTML output, attribute order/filtering, escaping, React casing tables, boolean/style/event behavior, placeholder literal, exception payloads, and public `render-to-static-markup`. The names are private; no compatibility aliases should be introduced. The IMPL-SPEC reconciliation owned by `rf2-6r9j.33` must not be broadened here: only mechanically update names directly made stale by this patch.

title: Clarify frame-ID and registration-value names in schemas storage
description:
Partition: implementation/schemas registry and storage.

Locations and evidence:
- implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:99-116 names a private helper `best-effort-frame`, although its documented and actual result is a frame-id keyword (or nil), never a frame value.
- storage.cljc:618-619 carries that ID as `batch-frame`, obscuring the same frame-value/frame-id distinction that this module explicitly normalizes.
- storage.cljc:45-60, 475-507, and 640-643 use generic `override`, `vf`, `db`, `live-val`, and `m` names at frame resolution, hot-reload validation, and schema lookup boundaries.

Ambiguity cost:
EP-0024 makes frame values and frame IDs distinct accepted inputs. Calling a resolved ID a `frame` makes future changes likely to pass the wrong representation into error tags or registry keys. The hot-reload validation and lookup locals also hide whether a value is the callback, entire app-db, live registered value, or stored registration metadata.

Proposed names:
- `best-effort-frame` -> `best-effort-frame-id`
- `batch-frame` -> `batch-frame-id`
- `override` -> `frame-target`
- `vf` -> `validate-fn`; `db` -> `app-db`; `live-val` -> `live-value`
- lookup `m` -> `registration-metadata`

Compatibility and migration risk:
All proposed symbols are private functions or lexical bindings. Keep public `resolve-frame`, `coerce-opts`, registry shape, `:frame` tags, registered schema IDs, error IDs/reasons, source coordinates, and late-bind contracts byte-for-byte stable. Update every in-slice reference and prove old private/local spellings are gone where intended.
acceptance_criteria: Private/local names distinguish frame targets, frame IDs, app-db values, live registered values, validator callbacks, and registration metadata; every consumer is updated; no public function, namespace, file, registry key, error field, reason, or late-bind contract changes; focused schemas tests and lint pass.

title: reagent-slim template: clarify prop conversion, key lookup, and shared interop path
description:
## Finding

The private Hiccup/React conversion pipeline in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs` obscures three important distinctions with abbreviated or misleading names: nested versus top-level prop mutation (`kv-conv`/`top-prop-conv`), the already-located key rule versus argv key lookup (`react-key`/`get-react-key`), and the shared DOM-plus-`:>` path named `native-element` even though the source explicitly says it handles foreign React components too.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- Lines 490-548 show both `*-conv` helpers mutate a JS accumulator with `aset`; only their long docstrings reveal nested-map versus target-aware top-level behavior, and neither name signals mutation.
- Lines 740-789 distinguish a rule receiving an already-located props slot from a finder that searches argv, but `react-key` and `get-react-key` do not communicate that distinction.
- Lines 988-996 name the value tested by `props-slot?` `head`, then immediately warn in prose that it is a slot value, not a vector head.
- Lines 998-1033 state `native-element` is the path for both native DOM tags and `:>` interop; lines 1148-1158 create a synthetic tag for the foreign component and call it. The current name therefore makes the interop call look categorically wrong.
- `dont-camel-case` and `capitalize` at lines 358-381 omit that the values are prop-name prefixes/segments.
- Exact searches find no external Var consumers because these candidates are private. The remaining matches are comments/spec text, tests, or independent benchmark-local functions. History shows `native-element` began as a DOM path and later accumulated interop responsibilities, explaining the drift.

## Recommendation

Use `add-converted-nested-prop!`, `add-converted-top-level-prop!`, `react-key-from-meta-or-props`, `react-key-from-argv`, `converted-props-element`, `verbatim-prop-prefixes`, and `capitalize-prop-segment`; rename `head` to `slot-value`, `native?` to `dom-element?`, and `synth-*` locals to `synthetic-*`. Update every in-slice source/test/doc reference.

## Contracts and risk

Preserve public template Vars, Hiccup sentinel heads, dynamic vars, metadata/prop keys, React element/props shapes, cache objects, mutation and lookup order, source-coordinate consumption, and hot-path allocation behavior. Do not rename namespaces/files or add compatibility wrappers. Do not change the callable-prop branches/tests owned by `rf2-6r9j.30`.

## Duplicate search

All-status bead data was searched for each old name plus template/interop naming concepts. No bead owns this naming cluster; `rf2-6r9j.30` is a separate test-validity/correctness task and remains untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- The proposed private/local names replace their ambiguous predecessors in template source and all directly referencing reagent-slim comments/tests/docs.
- Exact old-name searches over `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` are empty, apart from any explicitly retained historical quotation that is justified in the bead close notes.

title: reagent-slim component lifecycle: name helpers and locals by role
description:

- `validate-spec!` at lines 135-155 validates specifically a `create-class` spec against the seven-key cap, not an arbitrary spec.
- `prev-argv-from` at lines 358-362 extracts `__rfArgv` specifically from React previous props; the omitted source is the important distinction fixed/documented by `rf2-08hx1`.

title: reagent-slim ratom runtime: replace compressed private helper names
description:
## Finding

The private reactive-kernel helpers in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs` use compressed names inherited from an early implementation: `arr-len`, `arr-eq`, `in-context`, `add-w`, `remove-w`, and `notify-w`. The names hide key semantics: the array comparison is identity-based, the context helper invokes a callback under `*ratom-context*`, and the watch helpers mutate watch state or invoke callbacks.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- Lines 75-85 implement array length plus element-by-element `identical?`; `arr-eq` can be read as Clojure value equality even though it is stricter identity comparison.
- Lines 87-108 use `in-context` only to call the Reaction body under the dynamic context; the preposition does not disclose that this is a callback runner.
- Lines 120-141 define the watch mutation/notification trio. `add-w`/`remove-w` also invalidate `watchesArr`, while `notify-w` materializes that cache and invokes every watcher; none of those effects is visible in the abbreviations.
- Repository-wide exact searches show all six definitions and calls are confined to this namespace. Targeted `git log -S` traces them to the initial Stage 4-A implementation, with no compatibility migration or external-consumer history.

## Recommendation

Rename them to `array-length`, `arrays-identical?`, `call-with-ratom-context`, `add-watch-entry!`, `remove-watch-entry!`, and `notify-watches!`. Expand nearby one-letter helper locals where their roles are otherwise unclear, and update in-slice explanatory/test comments.

## Contracts and risk

All candidates are private Vars. Preserve the public `RAtom`, `Reaction`, `IReactiveAtom`, `IDisposable`, `rea-schedule`, public function names, protocol method names, deftype field names, mutation order, identity comparison, and callback order. Do not touch `pr-atom`; its unused argument is independently owned by `rf2-6r9j.29`.

## Duplicate search

All-status bead data was searched by exact symbol and by ratom/reactive-helper naming concepts. No existing bead owns these renames; `rf2-6r9j.29` is the separate vestigial `pr-atom` receiver removal.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Make UIx registered-view diagnostic facts self-describing
description:
## Scope

The UIx registered-view diagnostic test family:
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_boot_order_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs
- implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_source_coord_dom_elision_prod_test.cljs

This partition covers private helpers, locals, and private result-map keys only.

## Naming finding

Two capture helpers misstate their channels: with-captured-errors also records console.warn and window error events, while capture-warnings also records console.error. Their internal calls/orig-* names and returned :msgs facts conceal that the values are diagnostic messages. The direct-mount result uses context-free :initial, :after, :child, :children, and :ops keys; the source-coordinate result similarly uses :node?, :coord, and :view. Production-elision rows use user-fn/render/out for the registered view function, component head, and rendered React element.

## Ambiguity cost

These tests distinguish several subtle failure channels and multiple phases of one mount. Generic or channel-inaccurate names make an assertion's provenance unclear and encourage future coverage to inspect the wrong channel or confuse a view head with its rendered element.

## Proposed names

- with-captured-errors -> capture-render-diagnostics; capture-warnings -> capture-console-diagnostics.
- calls -> messages; orig-warn/orig-error -> original-warn/original-error; matching -> matching-messages; re/msg(s) -> pattern/message(s).
- Direct-mount facts: :msgs -> :diagnostics, :initial -> :initial-text, :after -> :updated-text, :child -> :child-text, :payload -> :observed-payload, :children -> :children-present?, :ops -> :frame-ops; give corresponding locals full names.
- Source-coordinate facts: :msgs -> :diagnostics, :node? -> :view-root-present?, :coord -> :source-coordinate, :view -> :view-id-attribute; expand output locals.
- Production-elision locals: user-fn -> view-fn, render/wrapped -> view-head, out -> rendered-element, props -> element-props where applicable.

## Compatibility and risks

All names are private to tests. Preserve public rf/reg-view*, rf/view, adapter functions, UIx/React interop properties, data-rf2-source-coord/data-rf-view attributes, regex contents, event ids, and classifier filenames. Result-map key changes must update every producer/destructure/assertion atomically.

## Acceptance criteria

- Helper names accurately describe every channel they capture.
- Result facts distinguish mount phase, DOM text, observed CLJS values, hook operations, and annotation attributes without reading producer code.
- Repository searches find no stale old private helper names or old result-key destructures in these files.
- Focused registered-view browser and production-elision tests pass.
- git diff --check and focused lint pass with no new warnings.
