title: Test-React inspection API: distinguish components from roots and live children
description:
## Naming finding

The public inspection helpers in `implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:539-554` no longer name the population they return:

- `mounted-roots` returns every live `MountedComponent` in `active-mounts`, including recursively mounted children. Its own docstring calls the result "the whole live forest, parents AND recursively-mounted children." The name predates child mounting (`fefee4a403`); commit `8e3dfe545f` added child roots and broadened the result without changing the original name.
- `children` filters the record's retained `:children` vector to only still-mounted entries. Unqualified `children` can be read as all recorded children, while the function intentionally returns only mounted children.

No tracked code outside this local-only adapter consumes either helper, but both are public vars in the documented test-kit namespace and therefore remain compatibility contracts.

## Ambiguity cost

Tests use the first helper as a leak detector over the entire mounted forest, not a root count. Calling it a root query makes assertions such as "parent + child = 2 roots" conceptually wrong and obscures why an orphaned descendant is visible. The second name hides its liveness filter, so a post-unmount empty result can be mistaken for removal from the record rather than filtering of retained dead child records.

## Proposed change

Add precise canonical helpers `mounted-components` and `mounted-children`. Move the current implementations/docstrings under those names and update the adapter's tests and README to use them. Retain `mounted-roots` and `children` as deprecated delegating compatibility wrappers with explicit historical-name documentation; do not make an unannounced breaking rename.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Preserve return collection shapes/order, `MountedComponent`, the serialized/record `:children` field, public mount/update/unmount names, lifecycle log keys/phases, and React interop. Do not touch the duplicate cache section or stale UIx/CI prose already owned by Phase-1 beads `rf2-6r9j.81` and `rf2-6r9j.85`. All-status searches for `mounted-roots`, mounted components/children, and live-forest Test-React vocabulary found no existing owning bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- New code and documentation use `mounted-components` for the complete live forest and `mounted-children` for one mount's live children.
- Historical public vars `mounted-roots` and `children` remain callable compatibility wrappers, are visibly deprecated, and state their misleading legacy semantics.
- Canonical and legacy helpers preserve the existing lazy-sequence/vector return shapes, order, and mounted-state filtering.
- Exact searches show legacy names only in their compatibility definitions/documentation; no call site continues teaching the ambiguous vocabulary.
- Test-React JVM and CLJS suites pass with the public mount/lifecycle/error and record contracts unchanged.
notes: Implemented mounted-components and mounted-children as canonical helpers; retained mounted-roots and children as ^:deprecated delegating wrappers with precise legacy-semantics docstrings. All production/test teaching uses canonical names except two explicit compatibility tests, which dereference the legacy Vars, assert :deprecated metadata, and verify delegation on JVM and CLJS without compiler warnings or changing the 35/160 count. README updated. Broad CLJS namespace run separately encountered only the pre-existing duplicated sub-cache test failures owned by rf2-6r9j.81; all naming/lifecycle contract selectors passed.
close_reason: Implemented canonical inspection names with deprecated compatibility wrappers, migrated callers/docs, and verified metadata, delegation, shapes, and host behavior.

title: Test-React runtime: name descendant teardown by its real scope
description:
## Naming finding

`implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:204-237` names a recursive helper `roll-back-speculative-children!`, but that is only one of its two call contexts. It recursively force-tears down every descendant under the supplied mount.

The name was accurate when commit `488bf70df6` introduced it for failed initial-mount rollback. Six hours later commit `bd14ef705e` added `force-teardown-subtree!` for failed updates and reused the helper on an already-committed live root. In that path the descendants explicitly include pre-existing children as well as children speculatively mounted by the failed attempt (`:225-226`), so "roll back speculative children" understates both the operation (forced teardown) and population (all descendants).

## Ambiguity cost

This is teardown code whose correctness depends on draining pre-existing and newly-mounted descendants alike. A maintainer following the old name can reasonably narrow the walk to attempt-local children or assume it is unsafe to reuse for adapter disposal/future forced teardown, reintroducing the live-child leak the failed-update path exists to prevent. The surrounding docstring currently has to explain the contradiction.

## Proposed change

Rename the private helper to `force-teardown-descendants!`, update its recursive call, both callers, and source commentary. Keep `force-teardown-record!` for one record and `force-teardown-subtree!` for descendants plus root; the three names then express the actual hierarchy. This is private and has no repo consumer outside the source file.

## Compatibility / exclusions

Do not alter recursion order, lifecycle phases, the `:children` record field, render-error propagation, or public APIs. Do not touch the Phase-1 `log-phase!` extras arm (`rf2-6r9j.83`) or duplicate cache tests (`rf2-6r9j.81`), both already assigned their own removals. All-status searches for the old/new terms and Test-React teardown naming found no owning bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- The recursive descendant-only primitive is named `force-teardown-descendants!`; `roll-back-speculative-children!` has no source/test/doc occurrence.
- `force-teardown-subtree!` calls the descendant primitive before tearing down its root, and failed initial mount calls it only for the never-committed parent's descendants.
- Leaf-upward order, clearing/eviction, exactly-one `:forced-teardown` per mounted record, and original-exception propagation are unchanged.
- Focused Test-React JVM and CLJS suites pass, including failed-initial, failed-update, nested-subtree, and sibling-scope cases.
- No Phase-1 removal target is renamed or otherwise changed.
notes: Implemented the private force-teardown-descendants! rename across recursion, failed-initial rollback, failed-update subtree teardown, and commentary. Exact old-name search is empty. JVM: 35 tests/160 assertions, exit 0. CLJS: warning-free node-test compile plus 15 changed-contract tests/95 assertions, exits 0, covering failed-initial, failed-update, nested, sibling, and leaf-upward order. Pinned focused clj-kondo: exit 0.
close_reason: Implemented scope-accurate private teardown naming and verified unchanged descendant-first semantics on JVM and CLJS.

title: Retire the drifted tools-root Shadow build mirror
description:
## Finding

`tools/shadow-cljs.edn` is an ungated, handwritten duplicate that still claims to mirror the tool tier's per-tool CLJS builds but has not followed that tier's evolution. It exposes only namespaced copies of Pair MCP's `server` and `server-test` builds.

## Evidence

- `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` was introduced 2026-05-15 and its last change was the 2026-05-24 Causa/Xray rename. Its comments still say Pair MCP is the only tool with a Shadow surface and call mcp-base JVM-only.
- `tools/mcp-base/shadow-cljs.edn` has provided a canonical `cljs-test` build since 2026-05-21.
- Pair MCP added the build-time `descriptor-gen` build on 2026-06-01; its descriptor check is CI-enforced, but the root mirror never added the build. A bounded probe from `tools/`, `clojure -M -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile re-frame2-pair-mcp/descriptor-gen`, exits 1 with known builds only `re-frame2-pair-mcp/server` and `re-frame2-pair-mcp/server-test` (plus Shadow's implicit `npm`).
- `tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn` added its owned `machines-viz-node-test` lane on 2026-07-26. It requires a per-tool `:cljs-test` alias and JS package path, another evolution absent from the root mirror.
- Exact searches find no workflow, package script, gate, or documentation outside the root README invoking either namespaced root build ID. CI and npm scripts invoke each tool's adjacent canonical config. `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` records the root Shadow coordinator as having no CI consumer.
- All-status `bd search` by `tools shadow coordinator`, `root shadow mirror`, `descriptor-gen shadow`, `re-frame2-pair-mcp/descriptor-gen`, `tools/shadow-cljs.edn`, and `rf2-nuuk3`, plus direct tracker search, found no existing bead owning this outcome.

## Impact

The advertised alternate root build surface is incomplete and silently drifts while the per-tool configurations are the only exercised authority. A contributor can reasonably expect a root mirror to expose the descriptor generator or newer CLJS lanes and receive a build-not-found error. The duplicate Pair server definitions also create a future second place for release-affecting compiler options to diverge.

## Recommendation

Delete `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` and the root README's mirrored-build promise; direct all builds to the per-tool configs that their package scripts and CI already exercise. Then remove any `tools/deps.edn` base dependencies that existed only to feed this mirror, subject to the separate JVM-aggregate decision. If a root Shadow entry point is intentionally retained, narrow and name its contract honestly, generate/validate its inventory against every canonical per-tool config, include Pair's descriptor build, and add a real consumer that makes drift red.

## Risks / contracts

Preserve Pair's output paths/npm `bin`, production closure define, test reporter, descriptor-manifest gate, mcp-base's optional-validation CLJS lane, and machines-viz's isolated alias/npm resolution. Do not merge their incompatible classpath options into a nominal aggregate without proving each build under its own required lane.
acceptance_criteria:
- There is one exercised authority for each tool Shadow build; no ungated handwritten root copy can drift from Pair MCP, mcp-base, or machines-viz.
- Root documentation no longer claims that `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` mirrors all per-tool CLJS builds unless an automated inventory/parity test proves it.
- Pair's server, server-test, and descriptor-gen commands still work through the canonical config, including identical production compiler options and output locations.
- mcp-base and machines-viz retain their per-tool alias and JS-resolution semantics.
- If the root coordinator is retained, the previously failing root descriptor-gen probe succeeds, new per-tool build additions make a negative-control parity test fail, and the root surface gains a real CI/package consumer; otherwise root-only build IDs and stale docs are removed.
- Changed-surface classification is updated to match the resulting live/retired root surface.
close_reason: PR #9093: tools/shadow-cljs.edn deleted and tools/README.md's mirrored-build promise removed. Proved unconsumed with two independent instruments plus a control that fired: a fixed-string census (git grep -F, .beads excluded) found re-frame2-pair-mcp/server only in the file itself and one README sentence, zero hits under .github/, while the same census for the live build id machines-viz-viewer returned workflow steps, an npm script and pinned assertions; and _changed-surfaces.test.cjs's tools declared-hole entry already MEASURED that no workflow runs from tools/ and that CI compiles pair-mcp from its own shadow-cljs.edn. Execution: clojure -Spath exits 0 from tools/ and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ after the deletion, and the per-tool config is byte-identical to main with server/server-test/descriptor-gen, same closure-defines, same out/server.js. Post-change census finds no namespaced root build id anywhere. The changed-surface tools note is updated to the three files now under tools/ (last acceptance criterion); the classifier itself is untouched and its self-test still passes 335.

title: Retire or ratchet the stale tools-root JVM aggregate
description:
## Finding

The optional `cd tools && clojure -M:test` coordinator no longer satisfies its own documented contract. `tools/README.md` lines 78-94 and `tools/deps.edn` lines 81-86/121-138 call it the aggregate for every JVM-runnable tool, but `:extra-paths` and the runner `-d` list contain only xray, mcp-base, story, story-mcp, and template.

## Evidence

- `clojure -Spath -M:test` from `tools/` resolves none of `machines-viz/test`, `testbed-support/src`, `testbed-support/test`, or `mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test`; controls `xray/test` and `story/test` are present.
- `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` is the maintained JVM inventory and includes `tools/machines-viz`, `tools/testbed-support`, and `tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab` (lines 19, 32, 33). `scripts/check_jvm_lane_rosters.py` holds that roster against required CI jobs.
- `tools/machines-viz` is not JVM-test-free: its per-tool gate runs 632 tests / 2537 assertions and two `.cljc` namespaces (`engine-grammar-parity-test`, `mermaid-public-smoke-test`) have no other JVM lane. The root coordinator's comments still label the artefact CLJS-only.
- `tools/testbed-support/deps.edn` and its `.clj` endpoint suite landed 2026-06-15, but the root alias never adopted them. The per-tool lane runs 32 tests.
- The changed-surface classifier explicitly records both root build coordinators as having no CI consumer; therefore a root aggregate false-green cannot be caught by the per-tool required jobs.
- All-status `bd search` by `tools-root aggregate`, `JVM aggregate machines-viz`, `testbed-support aggregate`, `every JVM-runnable tool`, and `root tools test alias`, plus direct tracker search, found no existing bead owning this outcome.

## Impact

A developer using the advertised single-command sanity check can get green while skipping active JVM-only contracts. CI remains protected by per-tool jobs, which makes the alternate root command's narrower result especially easy to mistake for equivalent coverage.

## Recommendation

Prefer retiring the duplicated root `:test` aggregate and point the root README at the already-complete `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` roster. If the convenience alias is retained, derive or ratchet its directory/dependency inventory against the canonical roster (with explicit, tested exemptions for non-composable entries) instead of maintaining another hand-written list. Remove the obsolete machines-viz CLJS-only rationale either way.

## Risks / contracts

Preserve per-artefact `clojure -M:test` commands, required CI jobs, template's JVM-only resource isolation, and the dedicated CLJS lanes. Do not flatten tools into one release/classpath contract merely to preserve this convenience command.
acceptance_criteria:
- The documented tool-tier JVM command either routes to the canonical `scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` roster or has an automated parity check against it.
- Machines-viz's JVM-only suites, testbed-support's JVM suite, and wire-vocab are not silently omitted from a command described as covering every JVM-runnable tool; any deliberate exclusion is named and mechanically held.
- A negative-control test that removes/adds a roster entry makes the parity guard fail.
- Existing per-tool JVM/CLJS CI lanes and template placeholder isolation remain green.
- Root README and `tools/deps.edn` comments no longer promise broader coverage than the command executes.
close_reason: PR #9093: RETIRED, not ratcheted. The aggregate :test alias is removed from tools/deps.edn and tools/README.md now points at scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh, which satisfies acceptance clause 1 by the routing branch (so the parity-guard and negative-control clauses do not apply). Verified the gap at source: :extra-paths and the runner -d list named only xray, mcp-base, story, story-mcp, template, while machines-viz (engine_grammar_parity_test.cljc and mermaid_public_smoke_test.cljc have no other JVM lane), testbed-support and mcp-conformance/wire-vocab were absent; scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh carries all eight and check_jvm_lane_rosters.py holds it against the required CI jobs. Ratcheting was rejected on the stance: it would add a parity guard plus a negative-control test to keep a duplicate honest for a convenience with zero CI consumers, and the parity would not even be clean since that roster deliberately also carries two migration/*/codemod artefacts that are not tools. The base :deps map stays (a REPL from tools/ still sees the tier; clojure -Spath exits 0). The obsolete machines-viz CLJS-only rationale and the Why-Xray-IS-in-the-aggregate block are gone. The Why template is NOT in the base :deps map heading is deliberately KEPT and restated: .clj-kondo/config.edn and two comments in .github/workflows/lint.yml cite it by name.

title: Repair stale implementation security catalogue entries
description:
## Finding

`implementation/SECURITY.md` is an intended catalogue of concrete shipped controls, but its inventory contains a duplicate row and several stale/incorrect control descriptions.

## Evidence

- The `project-egress` control appears twice, at lines 25 and 41, with the same bead and implementation link; both rows entered together in commit `926ac87cb2`.
- Lines 45-46 assign Reagent Slim controls to `day8/re-frame2-reagent`; the published coordinate in `implementation/reagent-slim/deps.edn` is `day8/reagent-slim`.
- Line 46 says `reserved-prop-key?` checks “over set `reserved-prop-keys`”. Since commit `5eb32a331d`, the predicate itself is the roster (three identity comparisons), and its source docstring explicitly records removal of the set.
- The introduction says “Four sections” while listing five. The audit heading says “38-bead audit trail”, but a deterministic first-column count yields 49 table rows and 45 distinct `rf2-*` IDs; the nearby statement of 45 distinct IDs is current.

## Impact

The source controls remain live, but the security catalogue misattributes an artefact, describes an implementation that no longer exists, and gives conflicting provenance totals. That weakens the document as an audit and release-review index.

## Recommendation

Remove the duplicate catalogue row; correct the Reagent Slim coordinate and predicate description; and update the section/count labels from the table's live inventory.

## Risks and contracts

This is catalogue repair, not authorization to remove or weaken source controls. Preserve all distinct security checks and historical bead/provenance links, retain the correct 45-distinct-ID statement, and make no runtime or gate behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `project-egress` has one catalogue entry and no distinct control/provenance row is lost.
2. Reagent Slim rows name the published `day8/reagent-slim` coordinate and describe the current predicate implementation without referring to a removed reserved-key set.
3. The introductory section count and audit-trail heading agree with the live document/table inventory, while the correct 45-distinct-ID statement remains accurate.
4. Source controls and gate behavior are unchanged, and relevant Markdown link/table validation passes.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. All four evidence claims re-derived at source; all four held. Two path details in the bead text were slightly off — noted below.

1. DUPLICATE ROW — CONFIRMED, MERGED rather than deleted. project-egress appeared at SECURITY.md:25 and :41, same fn, same owning namespace (re-frame.projection), both entered by 926ac87cb2. The surviving row sits at the first position (natural order: value primitive, then record primitive) and carries every clause of BOTH — the :rf.egress/* profile + known :frame resolution, frame-owned classification, delegation of every tree-shaped slot to elide-wire-value, "the required step before any off-box sink" (row 41's phrasing), and the "(Spec 015 SS-Direct reads)" fail-closed pointer that only row 41 had. Nothing distinct lost. Acceptance 1 met.

2. REAGENT-SLIM COORDINATE — CONFIRMED, with a path correction. The bead cites implementation/reagent-slim/deps.edn; the real path is implementation/ADAPTERS/reagent-slim/deps.edn (git ls-files finds no implementation/reagent-slim). The claim itself is exactly right: that file's clein block declares lib day8/reagent-slim, while day8/re-frame2-reagent is a DIFFERENT artefact — implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn — whose own header calls itself the "stock Reagent adapter" and which the slim deps.edn calls "the bridge that continues to ship in parallel". So the two rows misattributed reagent2.dom.server and reagent2.impl.template to the bridge. Both now name day8/reagent-slim.

3. PREDICATE DESCRIPTION — CONFIRMED. reserved-prop-key? at implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:243 is three identity comparisons, and its docstring header reads "THE ROSTER IS THE FUNCTION BODY (rf2-lhdp0)" with the costing that motivated dropping the PersistentHashSet. No reserved-prop-keys var exists anywhere in the artefact — grep returns only reserved-prop-key? call sites. The row now describes the shipped implementation AND records that the set was removed under rf2-lhdp0, so the history survives. Acceptance 2 met.

4. COUNTS — CONFIRMED by independent count. "Four sections" introduced a five-item list, now "Five sections". The decisions log: 49 data rows (48 with an rf2- first cell plus one "EP-0017 Security Considerations" row), 51 total id occurrences, 45 DISTINCT — exactly the bead's figures. Heading moved 38-bead to 45-bead, the number the document's own next-but-one sentence ("All 45 distinct ids in the Bead column...") already asserted. That sentence is untouched and still accurate. title: Refresh shadow coordinator comments after the examples concept split
description:
## Finding

The shadow coordinator's executable source-path and build maps match the current concept-grouped examples tree, but several present-tense comments still describe the removed `examples/reagent/<name>` / `examples/<substrate>/<name>` topology.

## Evidence

- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1177-1182` says hand-written examples live under `examples/<substrate>/<name>` and that Playwright specs sit beside each example/7GUIs under `examples/reagent`; the live examples tree is concept-grouped and the source-path inventory at lines 392-419 correctly describes that model.
- Line 1249 points Counter to `examples/reagent/counter/core.cljs`; the live file is `examples/core/counter/core.cljs`.
- Lines 1678 and 1756 describe RealWorld and Linearlite as using `../examples/reagent`; their live roots are `../examples/real-apps` plus capability/resource roots.
- Line 1772 points SSR to sibling `examples/reagent/ssr`; the live root is `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr`.
- Lines 1835/1846 and 1863/1875 point Nine States and Login to old Reagent paths; the live roots are `examples/patterns/nine_states` and `examples/core/login`.
- `Test-Path implementation/examples/reagent` is false, while every configured source path exists. Commit `210f812fe2` performed the concept reorganization.

## Impact

These comments are maintainer-facing documentation embedded in the authoritative build coordinator. They send reviewers and future editors to nonexistent locations and make an otherwise-correct build map look inconsistent.

## Recommendation

Update only the present-tense build comments to name the current concept-grouped roots and current test ownership. Keep the source-path/build data unchanged.

## Risks and contracts

Do not erase intentional archaeology: line 350 explicitly says a path was “formerly under” the old tree and line 1813 says a test was “relocated from” it. Preserve those clearly past-tense references, every build id, compiler option, module dependency, dev server, and source-path entry.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No present-tense coordinator comment points Counter, RealWorld, Linearlite, SSR, Nine States, Login, or Playwright ownership at the removed `examples/reagent` / substrate-first topology.
2. Historical references explicitly marked “formerly” or “relocated from” remain available as archaeology.
3. The EDN build/source-path structure is unchanged, all configured source paths still exist, and relevant config/documentation checks pass.

title: Prune retired root-verb metadata from the API.md parser
description:

- documented-kind exists solely to populate ignored :doc-kind. The var marker still has a live purpose—classifying API table rows—so marker recognition must remain, but retaining each marker's manifest kind no longer affects a verdict.

title: mcp-conformance: remove the stale descriptor exemption from the indicator gate
description:
Evidence
- indicator_field_test.clj's no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper skips every file in inline-emit-whitelist before reading and applying fx/strip-comments-and-strings.
- The whitelist includes tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors.cljs solely because its descriptor docstrings mention :dropped-sensitive and :elided-large.
- Commit efd0c8dbf32 changed this gate to strip comments, docstrings, and strings before matching specifically so descriptor prose no longer needs exclusion.
- Executing the gate's actual stripper and variant-regex against descriptors.cljs returns false for both indicator literals. Therefore removing that path from the whitelist is green today.
- Because the pre-read whitelist bypasses the whole file, any future real code emission of either slot in descriptors.cljs would also be skipped and the conformance gate would falsely pass. wire.cljs is different: it is the deliberate central helper location and remains a valid exception.

Impact
A compatibility exemption outlived the false-positive it addressed and now forms a whole-file blind spot in a MUST-level single-emit-path gate. The current source is conformant, but a later inline emission in descriptors.cljs would evade CI.

Recommendation
Remove descriptors.cljs from inline-emit-whitelist and update the surrounding comments/docstring to describe only the central wire.cljs helper exception. Continue stripping strings before the scan so user-facing descriptor prose remains permitted.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the wire.cljs exception or forbid indicator names in descriptor documentation. Preserve keyword-boundary matching, filesystem source discovery, and the central with-indicators contract. This change tightens only test coverage; it does not alter an MCP tool/schema/protocol surface.
acceptance_criteria:
- descriptors.cljs is scanned by no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper after comments/docstrings/strings are stripped.
- wire.cljs remains the explicit central-helper exception.
- The current wire-vocab Clojure suite passes.
- A temporary real-code occurrence such as (assoc envelope :dropped-sensitive 1) in descriptors.cljs makes the focused test fail, while existing descriptor prose does not.
- Comments no longer describe descriptors.cljs as whitelisted.
close_reason: PR #9086 (head 79b2ee56a6). descriptors.cljs removed from inline-emit-whitelist; wire.cljs remains the sole central-helper exception; the surrounding comment and docstring no longer describe descriptors.cljs as whitelisted, and the docstring now records WHY prose needs no row (the gate strips comments/docstrings/strings first, per efd0c8dbf32) and that a row is strictly stronger because it skips the file whole. So the exemption was doubly stale and the recommendation held. Gate liveness proved directly, both directions: planting (assoc envelope :dropped-sensitive 1) in descriptors.cljs turned no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper RED naming the file and the literal (exit 1, 119 assertions); with the same fault in place, temporarily restoring the old whitelist row turned it GREEN (exit 0, 117 assertions) — the whole-file blind spot reproduced exactly as the bead describes. title: mcp-conformance: remove the zero-consumer transport handle from the runner contract
description:
Evidence
- tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs:15-29 constructs a StdioClientTransport, gives it to client.connect(), then returns { client, transport }.
- runWithWatchdog at lines 55-90 retains a transport local solely to call body(client, transport).
- Repo-wide call-site inspection found 11 runWithWatchdog bodies and the direct connectServer consumers; every body uses only client, direct callers destructure only { client } or read aux.client, and no consumer reads .transport or a second callback argument.
- The extra parameter dates to d16cf18641, which centralized the old per-test ceremony and documented async (client, transport), but no current test exercises that part of the private contract.
- The pinned @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 contract says Protocol assumes ownership of the Transport. Its close() calls this._transport?.close(), matching _runner's existing closeQuietly(client) teardown.

Impact
The runner advertises and threads a second teardown handle that callers must not own under the SDK contract. This widens a private harness API, obscures the single owner, and creates needless destructuring/local state without providing any current capability.

Recommendation
Keep transport local to connectServer long enough to wire stderr and call client.connect(transport), but return only the connected client handle (or { client }, whichever minimizes call-site churn). Remove runWithWatchdog's transport local and invoke body(client). Update the private contract comments.

Risks and contracts
Preserve onClient publication before the initialize await, AUX_CLIENTS registration, prefixed stderr, connect-failure closeQuietly(client), watchdog behavior, and all 0/1/2 exit grading. Do not close the transport separately: Client owns it. This package is private and _runner.cjs is not a published API, but all in-repo direct callers must update atomically.

title: Remove unreachable legacy region scan from machines-viz raw-node-at
description:
Evidence
- chart/layout.cljc raw-node-at has a no-:region fallback: after a top-level lookup misses, it scans every parallel region for the same path.
- Its sole source call is attach-consumer-requires, which passes nodes produced by project-definition. project-parallel assigns :region to every region state and the synthetic region container; the layout regression suite explicitly asserts every parallel state knows its region.
- Flat and compound nodes lack :region but live under definition :states, so their first lookup resolves. Synthetic root nodes have empty paths and are rejected before lookup.
- Therefore the cross-region scan can run only for a hand-built obsolete node shape: non-empty region-relative path with its required :region identity removed. No source/test/Xray caller constructs that shape, and raw-node-at is absent from spec/API.md's enumerated public surface.
- The fallback was deliberately retained as legacy wording in commit 700767339d4 when region-aware identity fixed wrong-region lifecycle metadata; retaining it now preserves the ambiguous behavior that fix made unnecessary.

Impact
The dead branch encodes a dangerous first-region-wins lookup. If a malformed projected node loses :region, silently borrowing a sibling region's lifecycle requirements is worse than returning nil and exposes the old correctness bug as compatibility behavior.

Recommendation
For nodes without :region, resolve only under top-level :states. Remove the region scan and legacy wording; keep strict region-qualified lookup for parallel nodes.

Risks and contracts
Preserve flat/compound lookup, strict per-region resolution, empty/synthetic-node nil behavior, and lifecycle requirement projection. Do not change the machine grammar or region-scoped IDs. Reassess only if a supported external constructor of raw projected nodes is identified.
acceptance_criteria:
- raw-node-at never scans all regions for a node missing :region.
- Flat/compound nodes still resolve through top-level :states; valid parallel nodes resolve only through their own region.
- A regression proves a no-:region region-relative node returns nil rather than first-region data.
- Existing duplicate-path parallel-region lifecycle requirement tests pass on JVM and CLJS.
- raw-node-at remains absent from the documented public API, or any newly discovered compatibility obligation is documented before changing behavior.
close_reason: PR #9085: raw-node-at's no-:region cross-region fallback removed. Verified unreachable — project-parallel stamps :region on every region state and the region container, the parallel-root chip's path segment is the namespaced :rf.machines-viz.layout/parallel-root (cannot name a real state), the machine-root chip has an empty path, and a flat definition has no :regions to scan. New regression raw-node-at-no-region-node-never-borrows-a-sibling-region pins nil-not-first-region plus unchanged flat/nested/absent/empty-path lookup; gate liveness proved by restoring the scan (red at layout_cljs_test.cljc:1543, actual {:entry :enter-a}) then restoring to the identical blob. raw-node-at absent from spec/API.md and tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md — no compatibility obligation found.

title: story-mcp: remove unreachable JVM CLJS-var auto-probes
description:
Evidence
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cljs_resolve.cljc:77-113` retains `resolve-cljs-var`, `registered-substrates-var`, and `violations-by-frame-var`; their only production purpose is to auto-discover two browser-side providers from the JVM process.
- Both targets are impossible in the shipped JVM artifact: `re-frame.story/registered-substrates` is defined only inside `#?(:cljs ...)` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:1816-1822`), and `re-frame.story.ui.a11y/violations-by-frame` lives in a `.cljs` namespace (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs:59-64`). Story-MCP is JVM-only and has no in-process browser bridge.
- Commit `82ec7aa84f` established the symmetric contract: neither provider auto-wires; a future bridge binds both dynamic seams. The old CLJ probe defaults at lines 132-133 and 190-191 survived that migration.
- Repo-wide usage finds no consumer of `resolve-cljs-var` outside its dedicated unit test (`tools_test.clj:637-644`); the two private probe vars are source-only. `[re-frame.story]` at line 75 exists only to support this probe path.

Impact
The package loads the large Story facade and maintains/test-documents an auto-wiring mechanism that can never make either capability available. This obscures the actual explicit-provider contract and creates false confidence that browser state may be reachable from the JVM.

Recommendation
Remove the resolver, both private probes, the resolver-only test, and the resolver-only Story facade require. Initialize both dynamic provider vars to nil on every platform, while retaining the dynamic provider seams, availability predicates, accessor semantics, and capability-unavailable behavior.

Risks / contracts
`resolve-cljs-var` is a public var in an internal namespace even though it is absent from Story-MCP's documented/package/protocol API. Check downstream source consumers before deletion. Do not remove or rename `*substrate-provider*`, `*a11y-provider*`, `substrate-provider-available?`, `a11y-provider-available?`, or their explicit binding behavior; those are deliberate test/future-bridge seams.
acceptance_criteria:
- A repo-wide consumer check documents that no supported caller depends on `resolve-cljs-var`.
- The resolver, its two cached probe vars, resolver-only test, and now-unused Story facade require are removed (or a concrete supported external contract is documented instead).
- Both provider vars default to nil and remain independently bindable; availability distinguishes absent providers from reached providers returning empty data.
- Story-MCP unit tests, descriptor drift check, and stdio round-trip pass.
close_reason: PR #9089. Premise held. Removed resolve-cljs-var, registered-substrates-var, violations-by-frame-var, the resolver-only unit test, and the [re-frame.story] require that existed only to feed the probe; both provider vars now read a plain nil on every platform. Consumer check: repo-wide search finds resolve-cljs-var only in its own ns and the deleted test - absent from the documented/package/protocol API. Seams kept intact: *substrate-provider*, *a11y-provider*, substrate-provider-available?, a11y-provider-available?, accessors, capability-unavailable routing. Verified: clojure -M:test exit 0 (278 tests / 1473 assertions), clojure -M:gen --check exit 0 (in sync, 19 tools). Gate proved live by planting the exact removed auto-wire ((fn [] []) as the substrate default): exit 1, 9 failures including list-substrates returning a false-empty {:substrates []} success.

title: Remove unnecessary re-frame adapter boot from the machines-viz viewer
description:
Evidence
- page/.../viewer.cljs calls rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter, then mounts viewer-view directly with reagent.dom.client/create-root and render. It registers no frame, event, subscription, or re-frame view.
- MachineChart is a Reagent component and does not consult re-frame.core or the installed substrate adapter. The chart DOM suite independently mounts that same component through adapters.react-chart/chart-element plus raw react-dom/client createRoot without rf/init!, proving adapter boot is not a rendering prerequisite.
- The only machines-viz require/use of re-frame.adapter.reagent is this viewer. The :cljs-test alias carries day8/re-frame2-reagent solely to compile it.
- rf/init! installs a framework substrate and reseeds framework registrations; it does not initialise Reagent rendering. The viewer's direct Reagent root already does that.
- The mistaken rationale dates to initial viewer commit 9644e0b4d8 and now drives lengthy coupling commentary across viewer.cljs, deps.edn, README.md, and API.md.

Impact
A presentation-only static viewer performs unrelated framework-global boot, loads an adapter dependency, and documents a false requirement. This increases bundle/classpath coupling and makes embedding/reusing the page more stateful than its no-runtime contract promises.

Remove the re-frame.core and re-frame.adapter.reagent requires and the rf/init! call from viewer/run; remove day8/re-frame2-reagent from :cljs-test; update the affected docs to say the page mounts Reagent directly. Keep viewer.cljs in page/ because it remains an application entry and non-jar delivery surface.

Do not remove the main day8/re-frame2 dependency: library namespaces still use re-frame.error, trace, and interop. Preserve the exported run symbol, URL decoding, DOM output, read-only behavior, page/source-root split, and staged viewer artifact.

title: Truth the template substrate spec to the adapter-owned Reagent root
description:
## Evidence

The normative substrate spec still describes the Reagent generated core as rf/frame-root rendered through reagent.dom.client and says the scaffold calls reagent.dom.client/create-root directly (tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md, table and What each variant emits).

Commit 7f104b4de9 (rf2-k5r9t) deliberately replaced that path. The emitted _reagent/core.cljs now allocates an inert reagent-adapter/client-root handle and calls reagent-adapter/render!. The adapter owns the underlying React Root, lazily creates or hydrates it on first render, tracks it for destroy-adapter!, and reuses it across hot reloads. The resource comments and template_emission_test.clj were updated and pin this adapter-owned contract; spec/001 was not.

## Impact

The current capability document teaches consumers to bypass the ownership API the generated scaffold is specifically designed to demonstrate. It also hides the meaningful Reagent/UIx distinction: adapter-owned opaque handle versus caller-owned uix.dom root.

## Recommendation

Update both spec/001 descriptions to name reagent-adapter/client-root plus render!, and explain that direct reagent.dom.client construction is encapsulated by the adapter. Reconcile any nearby generated-shape wording that says the emitted source directly calls create-root.

## Risks and contracts

This is documentation truthing, not an API rename. Preserve UIx create-root/render-root wording and the shared one-root/hot-reload lifecycle contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- The substrate summary and detailed Reagent core description match the emitted _reagent/core.cljs byte-level API calls.
- Reagent is described as using the adapter-owned client-root/render! surface, not direct reagent.dom.client/create-root.
- UIx remains accurately described as owning a uix.dom root.
- Documentation link/slug checks pass for the touched spec pages.
close_reason: spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md now describes the Reagent variant as it is emitted since rf2-k5r9t: an inert reagent-adapter/client-root handle rendered through reagent-adapter/render!, with the adapter owning the React Root (create-or-hydrate on first render, reuse across hot reloads, release from destroy-adapter!) and direct reagent.dom.client construction encapsulated. Both the substrate table cell and the 'What each variant emits' core.cljs entry are updated, and the entry now states the Reagent/UIx ownership distinction the old wording hid. UIx wording preserved (uix.dom/create-root + render-root, caller-owned). spec/002-Generated-Shape.md's hot-reload contract and its 'exactly one create-root' pin reconciled to what template_emission_test.clj actually asserts per substrate. Gates: check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; tools/template clojure -M:test exit 0 (39 tests, 296 assertions, 0 failures). PR #9091.

title: Remove discarded stderr write from open-in-editor capability decline
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj's private launch-shim writes editor-position-unsupported to stderr and immediately exits with position-unsupported-exit (3).
- launch! always drains that stderr, but on exit 3 it returns the namespace constant position-unsupported-error directly. The retained err value is consulted only by the generic non-3 failure branch.
- Repository-wide search finds no consumer of the private shim's decline stderr; tests and the Ring handler observe only launch!'s returned map/status.
- Both the write and exit-code mapping arrived in d6cd8f086f; the surrounding comment explicitly says the verdict is intentionally read from the exit code rather than scraped from stderr.

Impact:
The decline path performs dead output I/O and suggests a second diagnostic contract that does not exist. It also adds noise to the already delicate subprocess shim.

Recommendation:
Remove the position-decline process.stderr.write call and retain only the distinct exit code. Keep stderr emission for actual launch-editor callback failures.

Risks/contracts:
Do not change exit code 3, the returned editor-position-unsupported token, generic stderr diagnostics, pipe draining, or the endpoint's 422 mapping.

Acceptance:
- The capability-decline branch exits with position-unsupported-exit without writing an unread token.
- launch! still maps exit 3 to position-unsupported-error.
- real-node capability tests and JVM endpoint tests pass with required probes armed.
acceptance_criteria: Delete only the unread capability-decline stderr emission; retain exit-code classification, generic launch failure diagnostics, pipe draining, and the client-visible 422/token contract; JVM real-node probes pass.
close_reason: PR #9087. Removed the unread stderr write from launch-shim's position-decline branch; exit code 3, the client-visible editor-position-unsupported token, the generic launch-failure stderr, pipe draining and the endpoint's 422 mapping are all untouched. Verified two ways. Census: git grep -F editor-position-unsupported over tracked files finds it only in README prose, the source constant, and tests asserting launch!'s returned map or the JSON body - never scraped from child stderr; the control census on the token that IS scraped ('launch-editor: ') finds both the write and the test reading it back. Runtime control: diverting the shim's decline exit to 9 while launch! still compared against 3 turned three real-node assertions red with :message 'launch-editor exited 9' (the empty-stderr fallback), proving the suite is live on this path AND that stderr now carries nothing there; restored by blob hash. Worth recording for the next worker: mutating position-unsupported-exit itself is NOT a valid control - it changes both sides of the comparison and stays green, a reassuring non-result. testbed-support JVM 42 tests/260 assertions green with RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES=1 armed, so the node probes really ran.

title: Collapse Story-host router indirection left by retired project-root setup
description:
Evidence:
- tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs defines private mount-router! at lines 57-66, and the only repository reference is the public mount-with-hash-routing! calling it at line 77.
- git history shows mount-router! was introduced in a25e4c08bc specifically so the then-two-arity public entry could configure the browser-side Story project root before delegating to routing.
- 2eb0df5bdd retired that project-root/source-subdir feature and reduced the public entry to one arity, but left the now-single-use delegation behind.

Impact:
The private layer no longer represents a separate operation or reuse seam. It makes the public host entry harder to follow and preserves structure belonging to a retired feature.

Recommendation:
Move the listener replacement and initial route-selection body into mount-with-hash-routing! and remove mount-router!.

Risks/contracts:
Preserve the exact hot-reload contract: store root-view, remove the previously stored hashchange function identity, add the current identity, record it, and immediately mount the selected surface. Do not change the public arity or consumer call sites.

Acceptance:
- mount-router! is gone and has no repository references.
- mount-with-hash-routing! directly performs the same ordered operations.
- focused Node Story-host tests and the browser DOM handoff suite pass.
acceptance_criteria: Remove the single-use mount-router! layer without changing mount-with-hash-routing!'s public arity, listener replacement order, immediate route selection, or consumer behavior; focused Node and browser Story-host tests pass.
close_reason:
PR #9092 (worker/catvest-a), head 8b3ffa3fe1. Premise re-derived at source and held on every line.

CONFIRMED. mount-router! was private, defined at tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/story_host.cljs:57-66, and git grep found exactly one reference in the whole repository: mount-with-hash-routing! calling it at :77. a25e4c08bc introduced it — "Move project-root config onto the shared story-host helper: a consumer declares its tool-relative source subdir via a new :story-subdir opt to mount-with-hash-routing!" — i.e. it existed so the then-two-arity public entry could configure the browser-side Story project root BEFORE delegating to routing. 2eb0df5bdd retired that feature ("mount-with-hash-routing! is one-arity; no alias, no compatibility arity") and left the delegation behind with nothing on either side of it.

WHAT CHANGED. The body moved into mount-with-hash-routing! verbatim, comment included, in the same order: reset! root-view*, remove the previously stored hashchange identity if any, addEventListener the current on-hash-change! identity, reset! hash-listener* to that identity, then call on-hash-change! to mount the selected surface immediately. Public arity, docstring and consumer call sites unchanged. git grep mount-router now returns nothing outside the tracker export.

WHY THE HOT-RELOAD CONTRACT IS SAFE. The four operations that make it self-balancing across a reload — the stored-identity removal before the add, and the re-record after — are the same four statements in the same sequence; nothing was reordered, nothing dropped, and no new var was introduced. The reference form for on-hash-change! is identical to what mount-router! used, so with-redefs resolution at the call site is unchanged too, which matters because the DOM suite redefines it.

GATE, AND THE COLLISION IT SAT NEXT TO. npm run test:testbed-support (the focused :node-test-testbed-support build) green: exit 0, 16 tests / 62 assertions. clj-kondo clean. The browser DOM handoff suite is deliberately left to CI, for a reason worth recording: PR #9089 (worker/storyq-a, rf2-6r9j.116) was open on story_host_dom_cljs_test.cljs at dispatch — +90/-1 — so a local run here would have exercised a version about to be replaced. The collision check the brief asked for came back CLEAN on the file this bead edits: #9089 touched only the DOM TEST, never story_host.cljs, so there was no source overlap and no race. #9089 has since merged, and its merged test was read against this change: it drives only the public mount-with-hash-routing! plus the three private atoms (hash-listener*, root-view*, app-root) and on-hash-change!, every one of which this refactor preserves; it never mentions mount-router!. GitHub tests the PR merge commit, so that merged suite runs against this source change on #9092's cljs_browser lane. Acceptance met on all three clauses.

title: Drop inert :root-ref from the machines-viz overlay scaffold constructor
description:
Evidence
- make-resizing-overlay-class in chart/overlays/overlay_scaffold.cljs destructures only display-name, remeasure!, and render. It never reads :root-ref.
- after_rings.cljs, spawn_all_join.cljs, and cancellation_cascade.cljs all pass :root-ref to that constructor anyway.
- Each overlay actually consumes its root-ref through its own remeasure! closure and through overlay-root-props; those paths are separate from the constructor argument.
- The scaffold docstring admits the constructor key is unused and retained only so a hypothetical future variant can change teardown without changing the signature. Git history shows this inert argument arrived with the scaffold extraction in b8b7cb99cd.
- The constructor is internal and :root-ref is not part of spec/API.md's public MachineChart contract.

Impact
Every overlay advertises and supplies a parameter that has zero effect. The misleading doc even claims the scaffold gates teardown with it, while unmount simply removes the window listener unconditionally. This adds false coupling and obscures the real ownership of measurement state.

Recommendation
Remove :root-ref from the make-resizing-overlay-class argument documentation and from all three constructor maps. Keep each overlay's local root-ref atom and its overlay-root-props/remeasure! use.

Risks and contracts
Do not remove the local root ref, offsetParent capture, measurement closure, resize listener, or teardown. Preserve the public :overlays descriptors and all DOM positioning behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- make-resizing-overlay-class exposes only the three values it reads: display-name, remeasure!, and render.
- No caller passes :root-ref to that constructor.
- Each overlay still captures offsetParent through overlay-root-props and remeasures on mount, update, and resize.
- Overlay geometry, rendered DOM, lifecycle, and browser tests pass for after rings, spawn-all join, and cancellation cascade.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9094 (branch worker/mvizb-a, commit 2f6dbe2264). Premise HELD and was confirmed at source: make-resizing-overlay-class destructures {:keys [display-name remeasure! render]} and never reads :root-ref, while its docstring claimed the scaffold 'reads it only to gate the resize listener teardown' - :component-will-unmount removes the resize listener unconditionally. :root-ref is gone from the docstring and from all three constructor maps (after_rings.cljs, spawn_all_join.cljs, cancellation_cascade.cljs); the ns docstring's claim that the root-ref atom lives in the scaffold was corrected too (each overlay owns it; the scaffold owns the overlay-root-props :ref that fills it). title: Remove unreachable schemas/Xray rewrites from the template smoke harness
description:
## Evidence

The private rewrite-deps-for-local-run! helper in tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/emitted_test_run_test.clj has conditional rewrites for day8/re-frame2-schemas and day8/re-frame2-xray. Its only two call sites are compile-and-run-emitted-test! immediately after run-template!, and mount-skill-scaffold! immediately after materialising skills/re-frame2-setup/references/first-counter.md. The template manifest and template_test.clj explicitly forbid both coordinates. The setup fixture asserts reduced-day-one-coords exactly before calling the helper, and that set also excludes both coordinates. Repo-wide search finds no other caller. Therefore neither conditional can be true in any current test execution.

History confirms these are remnants of the pre-rf2-zq34m scaffold: the reduced-template commit removed schemas and Xray from every generated project, while the helper retained presence-gated branches. A follow-up comment now explicitly says neither current caller names them.

## Impact

The dead arms imply broader dependency coverage than the behavioural tier provides and retain cross-surface knowledge of two deliberately post-generation features. They add misleading maintenance work when schemas or Xray paths change.

## Recommendation

Delete both conditional rewrites and narrow the helper documentation to core plus the selected adapter. Keep the local-root rewrite itself and every node/browser/release tooth intact.

## Risks and contracts

Do not weaken the two live rewrites or the pre-publish local-root test model. If a future fixture intentionally adds an optional feature, add its rewrite with that fixture and a test that exercises the branch rather than retaining speculative arms.

title: Make the security runtime harness fail honestly
description:
Scope: `with-runtime*` in implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/validation_redaction_invariant_security_cljs_test.cljc.

Evidence: the namespace's outer `make-reset-runtime-fixture {:clear-app-schemas? true}` disposes any installed adapter before every test and, in its post-test finally, resets frames and calls the loaded flows reset hook. `with-runtime*` nevertheless catches every Throwable/default value from `rf/init!` and ignores it, even though `rf/init!` is documented as idempotent; in this fixture state an exception indicates a real setup failure or partial initialization and should fail the security test. The helper's own finally also catches and ignores a flow reset immediately before the outer fixture performs the same reset without swallowing failure. Finally, its docstring promises "then dispose" and says "we dispose eagerly too", but the implementation never disposes the adapter; disposal occurs only on the next fixture setup. All current callers use the helper once around their production-path test body, so no demonstrated intra-test lifecycle requires these hidden fallback paths. The broad catch and inaccurate lifetime prose have been present since the helper was introduced in b58952c673.

Impact: a broken runtime setup can become a misleading downstream assertion failure or even a false green, cleanup failures can be hidden, and future maintainers are told the adapter lifetime is shorter than it really is.

Recommendation: let initialization failures propagate; choose and document one truthful lifetime (either actually dispose in the helper's finally or explicitly delegate disposal to the outer fixture); and remove the duplicate swallowed flow cleanup unless a concrete within-test isolation need is demonstrated.

Risks/contracts: preserve the adapter-less behavior needed by app-schema rows, the plain-atom runtime for the flow/subscription production-path rows, per-test flow/schema/frame isolation, and CLJ/CLJS fixture compatibility. Do not move all tests onto an adapter if that would synthesize frame state for cases intentionally testing context behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `with-runtime*` no longer blanket-catches and discards `rf/init!` failures; a targeted setup-failure control proves such an error reaches the test runner.
2. Its adapter-lifetime documentation matches behavior: disposal is either performed in its finally or accurately delegated to the outer fixture.
3. Duplicate flow cleanup is removed, or a distinct within-test requirement is documented and cleanup failure is not silently swallowed.
4. Adapter-less app-schema/context tests and plain-atom flow/subscription tests retain their intended setup.
5. `clojure -M:test` from implementation/security and `npm run test:security` from implementation both pass.
close_reason: with-runtime* no longer blanket-catches rf/init!; setup failures propagate. Adapter-lifetime docstring now names the outer make-reset-runtime-fixture (reset-runtime! -> dispose-adapter! on the way IN) instead of promising a disposal the helper never performed; the duplicate swallowed :flows/reset-flows! removed (finish-runtime-reset! already does it unswallowed in the fixture finally). title: Collapse the duplicate event-wrapper conformance test
description:
## Finding

Two adjacent tests in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` assert the same registration shape. `reg-event-registers-under-event-kind-with-the-one-wrapper` requires `(mapv :id (:interceptors meta))` to equal exactly `[:rf/event-handler]`, then checks the sole wrapper id and `:rf/default?`. `reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive` registers another ordinary event, converts the same interceptor ids to a set, again requires exactly `#{:rf/event-handler}`, and separately asserts that `:rf/db-handler`, `:rf/fx-handler`, and `:rf/ctx-handler` are absent. Those three negatives are logical consequences of the exact singleton equality in the first test, so the second row exercises no additional branch, runtime, or metadata path.

## Recommendation

Delete `reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive`, keeping the first test as the canonical wrapper lock. If the named retired ids are valuable migration documentation, mention them in the first test's assertion message/comment without executing a second registration. Alternatively parameterize a genuinely distinct historical registration path; currently there is none because all calls use the one `reg-event` form.

## Risks and contracts

Keep the exact ordered interceptor vector assertion, the wrapper's `:rf/default? true`, handler-fn reachability, and absence of `:event/kind`. Do not weaken singleton equality to only a membership check.

## Evidence

The first test at lines 652-669 asserts the exact one-element vector and wrapper metadata. The second at lines 671-679 asserts the set form of the same one-element vector plus redundant non-membership checks. Both use the same public registrar, fixture, platform matrix, and ordinary no-metadata `reg-event` path.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Only one ordinary-registration test owns the exact singleton `:rf/event-handler` wrapper contract.
2. That surviving test still fails for any extra wrapper, any retired per-kind wrapper, wrong order/id, missing handler-fn, or missing `:rf/default? true`.
3. Test/docs commentary no longer implies the duplicate registration covers a distinct path.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass with the expected lower test/assertion tally.
close_reason: Premise held. Verified by plant, not census: renaming events/event-handler-interceptor-id :rf/event-handler -> :rf/db-handler (a retired per-kind id, exactly what the duplicate's three negatives claim to guard) reds BOTH rows -- survivor reg-event-registers-under-event-kind-with-the-one-wrapper exit 1 with 2 failures/6 assertions, duplicate reg-event-no-per-kind-wrapper-ids-survive exit 1 with 2 failures/4. The survivor's exact-vector equality (= [:rf/event-handler] (mapv :id ...)) entails the set equality and all three non-memberships, and additionally refuses an extra wrapper and a wrong order, so the duplicate exercised no branch, runtime or metadata path the survivor misses. Deleted; the retired ids ride as commentary on the exact-vector assertion per the bead's own recommendation. AC1-4 met: one owner, unweakened singleton equality, no prose implying a distinct path, event-conformance JVM 44 tests/186 assertions exit 0 and the consolidated node suite 11163/55721 exit 0. PR #9123.

title: Make the event-conformance explicit-live test discriminate the policy override
description:
## Finding

`reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-mints-the-declared-nondeterminism-escape` in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_model_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` dispatches into the fixture's ordinary `:rf/default` frame, whose no-config mint policy is already `:live`. A missing generator-backed fact therefore mints whether `{:rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live}` is honored, ignored, renamed, or removed. The test cannot detect the policy behavior named by its title; it only repeats the immediately preceding live-generation coverage.

Core's dual-runtime `explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates` has the discriminating setup: a `:preset :test` frame defaults to `:strict`, the per-call `:explicit-live` value must override it, and the generator/run result prove the escape was used. Core also separately proves strict refuses the same class of missing fact.

## Recommendation

Remove the non-discriminating conformance row as a strict subset of the core owner, or reshape it around a strict frame with a paired control: without the per-call override, the generator stays at zero and dispatch fails missing-required; with `:explicit-live`, it runs exactly once and delivers the fact. Prefer one canonical dual-runtime owner rather than two copies.

## Risks and contracts

Preserve the public dispatch-options path and dual JVM/CLJS coverage for `:explicit-live`; do not replace it with a direct call to the internal policy resolver. The negative and positive legs must use equivalent frame/fact setup so the option is the only discriminator.

## Evidence

The conformance row creates no strict/test frame and supplies only `:rf.cofx/mint-policy :explicit-live`; the documented/default runtime policy is `:live`. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/cofx_cljs_test.cljc` already contains `router-default-is-live-generates`, `test-preset-default-is-strict-does-not-generate`, and `explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates`, all through `rf/dispatch-sync` in a `.cljc` suite.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The event-conformance row is removed or changed so ignoring/removing the `:explicit-live` option makes it fail.
2. If retained, the test establishes a strict baseline/control and then proves the per-call option alone enables one mint and handler delivery.
3. Dual-runtime public-dispatch coverage remains in at least one canonical suite.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass.
close_reason: Premise held, proven by plant. Planting cofx/resolve-mint-policy to DROP its per-call argument -- the option honoured nowhere -- left the old row reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-mints-the-declared-nondeterminism-escape GREEN at exit 0 while core's explicit-live-overrides-strict-frame-generates went exit 1. Chose the bead's RESHAPE option over removal (the title asks for a discriminating row, and the public dispatch-options path is worth keeping at the conformance tier): renamed to reg-event-explicit-live-mint-policy-overrides-a-strict-frame, built on a :preset :test frame whose mint policy defaults to :strict, with a paired CONTROL that dispatches WITHOUT the opt (asserts :rf.error/missing-required-cofx, zero generator calls, handler never ran) and then the same dispatch WITH :explicit-live (exactly one mint, flat delivery). The new row was re-planted in BOTH directions: per-call ignored -> exit 1, escape leg errors missing-required; frame :strict ignored -> exit 1, control leg 4 failures. AC1-4 met: ignoring the option now makes it fail, the strict baseline/control is established, core keeps the dual-runtime owner, gates green (event-conformance JVM 44/186 exit 0, node suite 11163/55721 exit 0). PR #9123.

title: Replace the vacuous stale non-delivery event-conformance case
description:
## Finding

`a-stale-completion-is-non-delivering-without-an-explicit-observer` in `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` builds global and image handlers, then calls only the pure `reply/suppress` function. It never calls `dispatch`, `dispatch-sync`, a delivery helper, or any managed-effect completion path. Therefore its zero call count and unchanged app-db assertions follow from the test performing no delivery operation at all; they cannot detect a runtime that ignores `:deliver?` and dispatches stale app replies.

The row had real teeth before commit `ca7fd0bd93`: it invoked `deliver-through-gate!`, which consumed `:deliver?`. That commit correctly deleted the delivery gate under the new observer-self-dispatch model, but left the negative row's handler/frame apparatus after removing its sole dispatch site. Its remaining pure assertions (`:deliver? false`, valid `:stale`/`:suppressed` envelope, no `:value`) are already owned more strongly by core's `suppress-does-not-deliver-app-target` and `suppress-is-universally-non-delivering`, the cross-family reply-conformance stale matrix, and the production-elision stale suite.

## Recommendation

Delete this row and update the namespace prose from “both stale cases,” unless a real production-path integration gap exists. If app non-delivery needs an event-conformance test, drive an actual managed-effect family completion/lowering path that conditionally could dispatch the target; assert that a superseded completion reaches the suppression branch and leaves both explicit and ambient frames untouched. Do not simulate non-delivery by simply omitting the delivery call.

## Risks and contracts

Retain `an-observer-self-dispatches-a-stale-reply-on-its-own-authority`, which genuinely composes `suppress` + `complete` + frame-targeted dispatch and proves the authorized observation path. Retain the natural success dispatch case. A replacement must depend on production code that consumes the suppression outcome, not a new test-local gate that merely restates it.

## Evidence

The current row's only operational call after setup is `reply/suppress`; `seen-event`, `call-count`, and both app-db values are read before any dispatch. `ca7fd0bd93` removed `deliver-through-gate! outcome ...` from exactly this row. Core and reply-conformance already assert universal suppression and envelope shape in dual-runtime suites.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The no-operation stale case is removed, or replaced by a test that executes a real production completion path with a reachable delivery branch.
2. A replacement demonstrably fails when that production path dispatches despite `:deliver? false`; zero calls cannot be established merely by never invoking delivery code.
3. The observer self-dispatch and natural-success event-pipeline cases remain green on JVM and CLJS.
4. Namespace/deps commentary accurately names the integration boundaries still exercised, and focused JVM plus consolidated Node tests pass.
close_reason: Premise held; vacuity proven by plant. Planting reply/complete's :append leg to stop appending the reply reds reply-completion-is-an-ordinary-reg-event-dispatch (13 failures) and an-observer-self-dispatches-a-stale-reply-on-its-own-authority (6), and leaves a-stale-completion-is-non-delivering-without-an-explicit-observer with ZERO failures -- it is blind to the entire delivery path it names. REMOVED rather than replaced, and the reason is a finding worth keeping: NO production code anywhere reads :deliver?. reply/suppress returns false unconditionally with no branch, and every family (http/registry, http/transport, resources/reply_handlers, routing/nav_token, machines/reply) branches on its OWN staleness decision instead, never on the outcome's :deliver?. So AC1's alternative -- 'a real production completion path with a reachable delivery branch' -- has no target that does not first re-invent the delivery gate ca7fd0bd93 deliberately deleted, which the bead's own risk note forbids. Coverage is not lost: the RETAINED observer row keeps a LIVE non-delivery tooth (zero call-count read BEFORE the observer self-dispatch, exactly-one AFTER, so a runtime that app-delivered a stale reply itself fails the pair), and the pure suppress laws (universal :deliver? false, stale envelope shape, absent :value) are re-frame.reply-cljs-test's across six target shapes including forged stale-authority. AC2 moot under removal; AC3 both retained rows green on JVM and CLJS; AC4 ns prose rewritten to name the narrower ownership. PR #9123.

title: Prune strict-subset frame-resolution cases from event-conformance
description:
## Finding

`implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_frame_isolation_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` carries three cases whose observable contract is already exercised more strongly by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/live_run_frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc`:

- `two-frames-sharing-one-image-keep-independent-app-db` repeats the same image, seeds (0/100), three-dispatch stream, distinct runnable ids, numeric results, and non-global resolution as core's `two-frames-from-one-image-keep-independent-state`; the core owner additionally proves independent subscription values and cache identity. The conformance-only second `not= :global` is implied by the exact `= 101` assertion.
- `absence-is-default-no-image-frame-uses-the-global-registrar` repeats core's `no-image-frame-resolves-through-the-global-registrar`: same image-less explicit frame, global event + sub, committed marker, subscription value, and nil generation binding.
- `the-global-sentinel-is-genuinely-registered` repeats that same absence/default path again. The headline isolation test registers its sentinel in its own fixture scope, and its exact `:todo` / `:counter` results already establish that the image handlers ran; a cross-test registration probe cannot arm another fixture's sentinel.

Both files are `.cljc` namespaces ending `-cljs-test`, so all of these rows ride the consolidated Node suite and JVM test lanes. The duplication adds maintenance and runtime without another platform or code-path boundary.

## Recommendation

Delete the three strict-subset cases, or consolidate their genuinely useful assertion into the canonical core owner. Keep the conformance rows that add independent teeth: exact two-image app-db shape + distinct generations, runtime-db partition isolation, and child-dispatch sibling-frame isolation. Update suite commentary/counts to describe that narrower ownership.

## Risks and contracts

Do not weaken dual-runtime coverage of image resolution or delete the unique runtime-db/sibling-isolation assertions. Preserve at least one positive absence-is-default event+subscription test and one directly armed global-fallback sentinel in the canonical owner.

## Evidence

The event-conformance file has 6 tests; the core owner has the corresponding live-run cases plus stronger state/sub-cache assertions. History shows core's live resolution suite predates the conformance copy (`22229d483c` / `78d4d2eca8` before `4bacc2f05c`), and both remain enrolled through `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn` plus their JVM aliases.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The three strict-subset cases are removed or reduced to assertions not present in the core owner.
2. The canonical core suite still proves image-less global event+sub resolution, nil generation, and shared-image independent event/sub-cache state on JVM and CLJS.
3. Event-conformance retains the distinct-generation/exact-db headline, runtime-db isolation, and child/sibling isolation teeth.
4. Event-conformance JVM tests and the consolidated CLJS Node suite pass, with updated test/assertion tallies and no stale ownership prose.
close_reason: Premise held for all three; containment demonstrated per case. (1) absence-is-default-no-image-frame-uses-the-global-registrar is OPERATIONALLY IDENTICAL to core's no-image-frame-resolves-through-the-global-registrar -- same frame id, event, sub and three assertions, differing only in prose strings (verified by a paren-balanced form extraction and string-elided compare: identical True). Two copies of one program cannot be distinguished by any fault, which is stronger evidence than a plant. (2) the-global-sentinel-is-genuinely-registered repeats that same path plus a registrar/lookup some? probe; the probe's value is real but its PLACEMENT was not -- the :each fixture means it could never arm another test's sentinel -- so it was MOVED INTO the headline isolation row, where it backs the not= :global assertions that actually depend on it. (3) two-frames-sharing-one-image-keep-independent-app-db: five of its six assertions are textually identical to core's two-frames-from-one-image-keep-independent-state; the sixth (not= :global on frame B) is entailed by the exact = 101. Core adds frame-object?, subscription values and sub-cache identity. Plant (a constant frame/anon-frame-id collapsing two no-id frames onto one record) reds both: conformance 3 failures/6 assertions, core 6 failures/11 -- core strictly stronger. All three deleted. AC1-4 met: core still owns image-less global event+sub resolution and nil generation and shared-image independent state on JVM+CLJS; event-conformance retains its three teeth (exact two-image app-db with distinct generations, runtime-db partition isolation with untouched sibling, child/sibling isolation); ns prose rewritten to name the narrower ownership; JVM 44 tests/186 assertions exit 0 and node suite 11163/55721 exit 0. shadow-cljs.edn NOT touched -- the file stays enrolled, no build-id change needed. PR #9123.

title: Prune unused default-seed arities from the security generator
description:
Scope: implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/gen.cljc and its repository-wide consumers.

Evidence: `sample` exposes a two-argument `[g n]` form that silently selects seed 0 plus the used `[g n seed]` form. `for-all` similarly exposes `[g n pred]` plus `[g n seed pred]`. A repository-wide symbol search found no consumer of either default-seed arity: the parity test calls sample with three arguments, and every security property calls for-all with an explicit seed. No namespace outside implementation/security imports re-frame.security.gen. Targeted history shows the unused overloads were present from the helper's initial commit (05ca3070f8) while its initial callers were already explicitly seeded.

Impact: these dead overloads expand a test-helper API, imply an unsupported convention around an invisible global seed, and create two ways to express every property without serving a compatibility consumer.

Recommendation: remove the two default-seed arities and make the seeded signatures the only API; update docstrings/spec prose if necessary to state that determinism is explicit.

Risks/contracts: preserve generator parity across CLJ and CLJS, stable replay for existing explicit seeds, shrink/reproduction diagnostics, and every current property call. This helper is internal to the security tier, but search again before removal in case a new consumer has appeared.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `sample` and `for-all` expose only their explicitly seeded forms, unless a concrete live consumer of a default-seed form is documented.
2. All repository call sites remain explicitly seeded and deterministic.
3. Generator parity coverage remains intact in both runtimes.
4. `clojure -M:test` from implementation/security and `npm run test:security` from implementation both pass.
close_reason: PR #9111. Removed sample's [g n] and for-all's [g n pred] default-seed arities; the seeded signatures are now the only API, and both docstrings state that determinism is explicit rather than defaulted. Premise re-verified at HEAD with two independent instruments plus controls that fired. git grep -F over tracked files: 17 gen/for-all sites, ALL four-argument; 2 gen/sample sites (5 calls), ALL three-argument; control gen/gen-elem = 9, a non-existent name = 0. clj-kondo var-usages into re-frame.security.gen: for-all appears only at arity 4 (36 usages across both reader-conditional arms), sample only at arity 3 (12). The sole uses of the default-seed forms were the two self-delegating bodies removed. No namespace outside implementation/security requires the ns; the only two other files naming it (.github/workflows/test.yml, scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh) do so in prose comments about the LCG cross-runtime contract, not in code. No spec or docs page documents the helper API, so no fenced/hot-zone file needed a change. Generator parity and seed replay unchanged -- every call site was already explicitly seeded. Security JVM 92/717 and npm run test:security 93/724, 0 failures 0 errors; clj-kondo over implementation/security reports 1 warning, byte-identical to the origin/main baseline (mask32 unused under the :cljs reader arm, pre-existing).

description:

The tests arrived minutes apart in the same June 17 merge batch (80f78d8377 and 98777011dc), consistent with overlapping concurrent coverage rather than a distinct reply invariant.

Impact: the mislocated duplicate adds maintenance and runtime cost while making the reply suite appear to cover a reply-specific path that it does not touch.

Recommendation: remove reply-value-projects-through-project-egress from the reply-envelope suite. Keep every test that actually constructs or projects a reply envelope, and keep the canonical generic projector coverage in public_profile_projection_security_cljs_test.cljc.

Risks/contracts: do not weaken reply-envelope coverage, the public/on-box projection contract, framed off-box redaction, frameless fail-closed behavior, or deterministic large-value elision. This is test deduplication only; production behavior must not change.
