description:
Evidence
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:1238-1265 defines claim-delayed-silence!, a reserve-only operation. Its own contract says it emits an unqualified signal, leaves a claim-to-emit race, and remains only for staged tests or hypothetical callers that cannot race registry mutation.
- state.cljc:1377-1388 defines the matching rollback-delayed-silence!. Exact repository search finds both functions called only from epoch tests; there is no production, tool, example, skill, specification, or API consumer.
- The live destroy path at implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc:478-507 calls claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! instead. That current helper uses the same private eligible-and-reserve! primitive and implements compare-and-prune rollback in its exception path at state.cljc:1355-1375.
- Commit e9475426bf moved production publication to claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! so the generation-qualified emit runs outside ledger locks and avoids the ledger-to-drain-lock deadlock. The older reserve/rollback pair remained as a test seam, not a runtime path.
- Existing direct users are tests at epoch_silencing_lineage_285_test.clj:235-246,344, epoch_cljs_test.cljs:719, and docstring assertions in epoch_silence_contract_test.clj:170-189.

Impact
The shipped source exposes two operations for delayed-silence claiming although only the integrated generation-qualified operation is safe on the live concurrent path. The test-only pair duplicates rollback protocol, preserves an incomplete unqualified-call workflow, and can invite a future caller onto the known race-prone seam.

Proposed disposition
Remove claim-delayed-silence! and rollback-delayed-silence! while retaining eligible-and-reserve! as the private shared implementation and claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! as the sole live operation. Rewrite staged tests through integrated behavior or a test-local/private seam, and update source comments/docstring ratchets that describe the retired pair.

Risks
The helper pair currently makes reservation ordering and compare-and-prune behavior easy to test and seeds marks in CLJ/CLJS reset tests. Preserve equivalent behavioral coverage: one winner, failed publication permits retry, a stale rollback cannot remove a fresher mark, and reset/cleanup boundedness. Do not move external publish under either ledger lock or remove observed-gen qualification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No executable or documented reference to claim-delayed-silence! or rollback-delayed-silence! remains.
2. claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! remains the sole delayed-silence entry and still reserves under both ledger locks, publishes outside them, carries observed-gen at the caller, and compare-prunes only its own failed reservation.
3. Tests cover single-winner claiming, publish-throw rollback and retry, protection of fresher marks, CLJ/CLJS reset cleanup, and the same-generation/replacement/re-arm races without using a shipped reserve-only API.
4. Epoch JVM and CLJS suites, concurrency stress coverage, and production-elision checks pass.
close_reason: PR #9098. Premise held. Successor named and quoted: claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! (state.cljc) reserves through the SAME private eligible-and-reserve! primitive under both ledger locks, publishes outside them, and implements compare-and-prune rollback in its catch — 'release OUR reservation (only while it still stands)'. It is the only production caller's path (listeners.cljc:505, the destroy fan). Fixed-string census over tracked files (.beads excluded): claim-delayed-silence! and rollback-delayed-silence! appeared ONLY in epoch src docstrings/comments and epoch tests — no production, tool, example, skill, spec or API consumer. Control fired: same census for claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! returned 7 files. Both removed; eligible-and-reserve! stays private and shared. Tests rebuilt on the shipped operation: failed-delivery-rolls-back-the-reservation-only-then now drives a throwing publish (rollback, retry, single-winner refusal); NEW a-failed-publish-prunes-only-its-own-seq-never-a-fresher-mark replaces the old stale-seq case by claiming from inside the failing publish; CLJ and CLJS reset-listeners! tests seed through the integrated op; the source-contract ratchet swaps three reserve-only docstring assertions for a tooth forbidding either name's return. Two planted faults both fired RED (unconditional prune; retired names reintroduced), each restored byte-identical by git hash-object. Also corrected a pre-existing docstring error: the fn returns nil (when-let short-circuit), not false, when ineligible. Green: silencing suites (16 tests / 3650 assertions), concurrency stress + aba + same-generation-rearm + decision-atomicity + receiver-public-api (28 tests), epoch-test (219), prod-gate elision (25). CLJS node build left to CI.

title: Stop serializing ssr-node worker stacks that receivers discard
description:
## Evidence

- The worker serializes err.stack into both cross-thread error messages: boot-error at implementation/ssr-node/src/worker.cjs:80-86 and render error at :210-223.
- The boot receiver at src/isolate.cjs:91-95 reads only msg.code and msg.message, then creates detail containing modulePath. It never reads msg.stack.
- The render receiver at src/isolate.cjs:186-195 reads code, message, detail, and afterChunks. It never reads msg.stack.
- A whole-repository search finds no consumer of either posted stack field. The stack assertions in egress.test.cjs concern the parent-created Refusal stack, not these worker-message properties.
- The separate Worker error-event handler at isolate.cjs:98-101 reads err.stack directly; that live diagnostic does not depend on the message fields and must remain.
- Both discarded message properties date to b2b35bf6e9. No existing bead found by worker stack, boot-error stack, render-error stack, or ssr-node searches owns them.

## Impact

Every application boot/render exception needlessly serializes a potentially large, path-bearing stack across the worker boundary and then drops it. The presence of the field falsely suggests that this diagnostic survives into the service refusal, which makes debugging and egress review harder.

## Disposition

Remove stack from the worker's boot-error and render-error payloads. Preserve the live Worker error-event stack handling and the normal parent Refusal stack. Do not wire an application stack into HTTP/client egress as a way to make the field live; the existing boundary intentionally limits diagnostics.

## Risks

The worker error payloads are security-sensitive egress. Removing the dead field is safer than broadening the receiver, but tests should continue proving that refusal objects and HTTP bodies do not leak application stack contents. Avoid conflating an application-thrown render error with a worker_threads error event.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Neither boot-error nor render-error worker messages serialize err.stack.
2. No application stack is added to the parent detail or HTTP refusal body.
3. The live Worker error-event path still retains err.stack in its internal Refusal detail.
4. Boot failure, render failure, post-chunk failure, egress, and full ssr-node tests remain green.
close_reason: PR #9099. Discard proven at BOTH receivers before the sends were removed. Boot receiver: isolate.cjs handleBootMessage reads message.code and message.message only, then builds new Refusal(code, message, {modulePath: this.modulePath}) -- the detail is the parent's own field, message.stack never appears. Render receiver: _handleRenderMessage's message.t==='error' branch reads code, message, detail and afterChunks, spreading message.detail only. Those two handlers are the whole of worker.on('message') in the parent, so no third consumer exists. err.stack removed from both worker.cjs payloads (boot-error and render error). The live worker.on('error') handler, which holds the real Error, still keeps err.stack in its internal Refusal detail (criterion 3). No stack added to parent detail or HTTP refusal body. egress.test.cjs:292's stack assertion was always about the parent-created Refusal's own JS stack, not these message properties -- verified. Suite 9/9 green, 108 rows; eslint exit 0.

title: Epoch: remove the redundant pre-state argument from the halt hook
description:
Evidence
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:353 declares frame-state-before in the single-arity commit-halt-record! hook, but lines 355-372 never read it; clj-kondo reports that exact binding as unused.
- The only production caller is implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3420-3422, which passes fs-now in both the before and after positions.
- The documented and implemented contract at epoch.cljc:334-370 deliberately derives both halted-depth snapshots from the last retained record :frame-state-after, falling back only to the supplied frame-state-after when no epoch has settled. The pre-state value cannot affect the record.
- Repository-wide hook inventory finds no other executable consumer. The late-bind directory and specifications name :epoch/commit-halt-record! but do not promise its arity.
- History shows frame-state-before became inert when commit 27a4b1d77e9 made last-settled :frame-state-after authoritative; later exact-incarnation work retained the redundant slot.

Impact
The optional epoch artefact and core router maintain a misleading extra protocol argument. The duplicate fs-now call implies two meaningful snapshots even though the halt event never ran and the implementation always commits one durable value into both slots.

Proposed disposition
Remove frame-state-before from the private hook signature and remove one fs-now argument at the sole router call. Keep the hook single-arity, preserve exact-owner-token gating, causal committed-at, residual-buffer harvest, last-settled lookup, first-halt fallback, and equal before/after snapshots.

Risks
This is a late-bound cross-artefact seam, so core and epoch must change atomically. Do not introduce a compatibility multi-arity: the source documents that multi-arity changed Closure advanced reachability and violated production elision (rf2-cprm0q).
acceptance_criteria:
1. commit-halt-record! has no frame-state-before parameter and the router passes one frame-state value.
2. Halted-depth records still use the last settled canonical frame-state, use the router value only for the no-prior-record fallback, and store equal :frame-state-before/:frame-state-after.
3. Exact-incarnation owner loss still cannot harvest or commit a same-id successor store.
4. Focused core/epoch JVM and CLJS tests pass, and the epoch production-elision gate stays green.
5. clj-kondo no longer reports the epoch.cljc unused binding.
close_reason: PR #9098. Premise held: frame-state-before was declared and never read (clj-kondo epoch.cljc:353 before, clean after). Removed from the private hook and one fs-now dropped at the sole caller router.cljc:3421 — core and epoch in ONE commit because the seam is late-bound and an arity mismatch is a runtime fault. Kept single-arity (rf2-cprm0q elision trap). Full caller/implementor sweep: router.cljc:3421 (only executable caller), epoch.cljc:329 (only implementor), epoch.cljc:737 registration, late_bind/directory.cljc:823 (describes the key, promises no arity), spec/002-Frames.md:2023 (illustrative 3-arg pseudocode, carries no frame-state at all), spec/Conventions.md + migration README + conformance fixture (name the key only) — NO spec change needed, no hot-zone file touched. Liveness control: restoring the two-snapshot call reds re-frame.epoch-test/depth-exceeded-commits-halted-record with ArityException (8 args), so the halt seam is exercised end to end. Green: epoch-test (219), core frame-destroy-incarnation-jvm-test (29), scripts/test-epoch-prod-gate.sh (25). NOTED GAP, pre-existing and unaltered: no test covers the first-cascade fallback arm where the router-passed frame-state is the value actually used.

title: Use the orphaned ssr-node chunk-frame constructor at its live boundary
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/src/protocol.cjs:497-498 defines chunkFrame(seq, html) as the canonical public body-frame constructor and exports it at :528.
- A whole-repository exact-identifier search finds no call to chunkFrame; its only sites are the definition and export.
- The actual worker-to-service boundary independently rebuilds the identical object literal at src/isolate.cjs:165-168: { type: 'chunk', seq: msg.seq, html: msg.html }.
- The adjacent completeFrame constructor is live: service.cjs imports and calls it to create the terminal public frame. The chunk constructor is the orphaned half of that intended pair.
- Both the helper and duplicate literal have existed since the initial implementation b2b35bf6e9. No existing bead found by chunkFrame, chunk-frame, or ssr-node searches owns the duplication.

## Impact

There are two sources of truth for the public chunk-frame shape, but only the hand-written isolate copy is exercised. A future field-list or hardening change can update the named protocol constructor while leaving every real response unchanged, or update the live literal while leaving a misleading exported helper behind.

## Disposition

Import chunkFrame into isolate.cjs and use it exactly where the parent translates a worker chunk into the public service frame. This mirrors completeFrame and preserves the boundary's explicit named-field projection. If the helper is rejected as an abstraction, delete it instead; do not retain both representations.

## Risks

Do not pass or spread the raw worker message. The explicit projection is an egress boundary that intentionally drops unrecognized application-controlled fields. The constructor must continue accepting only seq and html and returning only type, seq, and html.
acceptance_criteria:
1. There is one source of truth for the public chunk-frame object shape.
2. The live Isolate chunk path exercises chunkFrame, or the unused helper/export is removed completely.
3. No raw worker-message spread or extra field crosses the boundary.
4. Protocol, bytes, egress, and full ssr-node tests remain green.
5. A focused assertion or coverage reading shows the retained constructor executes on a streamed response.
close_reason: PR #9099. chunkFrame is now the single source of truth for the public chunk-frame shape: isolate.cjs imports it and calls it at the worker->service boundary, mirroring completeFrame's live use in service.cjs. No raw-message spread, no extra field; the constructor still takes only seq/html and returns only type/seq/html. A new egress.test.cjs row reads a MULTI-chunk response and asserts each frame's key set is exactly html/seq/type, so the retained constructor is proven to execute on a streamed response (criterion 5). Control fired: with the boundary spreading the raw worker message instead, the row reds on the t and id fields. Suite 9/9 green, 108 rows, eslint exit 0.

title: Remove ssr-node compatibility guards below its Node 24 floor
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares engines.node >=24, a deliberate crossing requirement recorded by closed feature rf2-8arzr.2.
- The code still treats four much older core APIs as optional: bootTimer.unref?.() at src/isolate.cjs:81, render timer.unref?.() at :154, waiter.timer.unref?.() at src/pool.cjs:148, and server.closeAllConnections?.() at src/http.cjs:250.
- Node's official API history records Timeout.unref() since v0.9.1 and http.Server.closeAllConnections() since v18.2.0. Both methods are unconditional under the supported Node 24+ floor:
  https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/timers.html#timeoutunref
  https://nodejs.org/download/release/latest-v24.x/docs/api/http.html#servercloseallconnections
- Every call receives a real Node Timeout or http.Server; no repository test double omits these methods.
- These guards predate the package manifest/floor: isolate/pool came from b2b35bf6e9 and HTTP from 939d439ad9, while the Node >=24 package contract landed later in rf2-8arzr.2.
- No existing bead found by ssr-node, unref, closeAllConnections, or Node-floor searches owns these compatibility remnants.

## Impact

The impossible fallback paths imply that failure to detach lifecycle timers or force-close active HTTP connections is an accepted runtime mode. That obscures the actual shutdown/timeout guarantees and leaves below-floor compatibility code after the project chose a firm runtime floor.

## Disposition

Call unref() and closeAllConnections() directly. Preserve the calls themselves and their ordering; only retire the optional compatibility branches. Keep this separate from any redesign of graceful shutdown.

## Risks

server.closeAllConnections() is still needed for active connections even though modern server.close() also reaps idle connections. Do not remove it. Direct calls intentionally make an unsupported or malformed runtime fail loudly rather than degrade lifecycle behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No optional call remains for Timeout.unref or Server.closeAllConnections in implementation/ssr-node.
2. The three timers are still unrefed and HTTP shutdown still force-closes active connections before completing.
3. The Node >=24 engine floor remains explicit.
4. Timeout, admission, shutdown, serve, and full ssr-node tests are green.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9078. THE FLOOR WAS RE-VERIFIED FIRST, since it is the whole justification: implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares engines.node '>=24' at my tip, unchanged; every .github/workflows/*.yml that pins a runtime pins node-version '24'; and the node running these gates is v24.13.0. Probed both APIs on that runtime directly rather than trusting the docs: typeof setTimeout(...).unref === 'function' and typeof http.createServer().closeAllConnections === 'function' both true. Timeout.unref() has existed since v0.9.1 and http.Server.closeAllConnections() since v18.2.0, so both are unconditional under the declared floor.

All four sites were exactly where the bead said, re-derived at my tip: src/isolate.cjs:81 (bootTimer.unref?.()), src/isolate.cjs:154 (render timer.unref?.()), src/pool.cjs:148 (waiter.timer.unref?.()), src/http.cjs:250 (server.closeAllConnections?.()). Each patch was anchored to a single line with its match count read first (=1 in every case). AC1: a repo-wide grep for 'unref?.' and 'closeAllConnections?.' under implementation/ssr-node now returns nothing.

AC2: the calls and their ordering are untouched — the three timers are still unrefed at the same points, and closeServer still calls closeAllConnections() before server.close(), which the bead's risk note is explicit about keeping (server.close() reaps idle connections only; active ones still need the force-close). Only the branches that could never be taken are gone, so an unsupported or malformed runtime now fails loudly instead of silently degrading shutdown behaviour, which was the stated intent.

AC3: the >=24 engine floor is untouched and still pinned by test/serve.test.cjs's row 'the manifest points its bin at this launcher, exports the two entry points, and pins the Node CI runs'. package.json was not edited — this bead reads the floor, it does not move it.

AC4: timeout, concurrency (admission), serve and all 9 ssr-node suites green — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base. Note the shutdown paths are genuinely exercised rather than merely compiled: serve.test.cjs spawns bin/serve.cjs as a real process and stops it on SIGTERM, and timeout.test.cjs drives real render deadlines and isolate termination, so the unrefed timers and the force-close both ran.

title: Retire ssr-node alternate streaming selectors with no consumers
description:
## Evidence

- implementation/ssr-node/src/http.cjs:145-147 selects streaming through three routes: documented query stream=1, undocumented request header x-rf-ssr-stream: 1, or the serve option streamingDefault unless query stream=0.
- A whole-repository search finds x-rf-ssr-stream only at that branch and streamingDefault only in handleRender/serve plumbing at http.cjs:127,147,221,226. No CLI flag, README contract, test, JVM adapter, example, or build wiring sets either one.
- The only exercised and documented selector is POST /render?stream=1 (README.md:516 and test/bytes.test.cjs:112).
- The stream=0 exception is reachable only when the zero-consumer streamingDefault option is enabled.
- Both alternate selectors were introduced in the first HTTP implementation (939d439ad9) and have never acquired a consumer or contract.
- The package is private and version 0.1.0; its explicit exports expose serve, but the repository's consumer-facing README does not advertise either alternate path. No existing streaming bead concerns this surface; rf2-6r9j.42 is about an unrelated Ring streaming-root retention.

## Impact

The HTTP entry point carries two invisible ways to change response framing plus an otherwise meaningless stream=0 branch. They expand the behavior and compatibility surface without a witness. A caller can accidentally receive chunked semantics from a magic header or unpinned in-process option that the operational docs do not teach.

## Disposition

Keep the documented and byte-tested stream=1 query selector. Remove x-rf-ssr-stream, streamingDefault plumbing, and its stream=0 exception after one final supported-consumer check. Pin the remaining default as buffered and the query opt-in as streamed.

## Risks

Changing framing can break an out-of-repository checkout consumer even though the selectors are undocumented and the package cannot currently be published. Check release notes and known deployment config before removal; if a real supported consumer is found, promote that selector into the README and tests instead of leaving it implicit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The supported streaming contract has one documented selector: query stream=1.
2. Normal POST /render remains buffered and byte-identical; query stream=1 remains chunked and byte-identical.
3. x-rf-ssr-stream, streamingDefault, and the stream=0-only override have no production plumbing after the supported-consumer check.
4. A focused HTTP row pins that the former magic header no longer silently changes framing, unless a real supported consumer caused it to be documented and retained instead.
5. The bytes, serve, and full ssr-node suites are green.
close_reason:
Confirmed and retired in PR #9078. The reachability census reproduced the bead's claim exactly, run per the anti-false-negative discipline: fixed-string matching (never -F combined with -i, which returns 0 on this GNU grep 3.0 where -F alone returns hits), over git-tracked files, .beads/issues.jsonl and .beads/metadata.json excluded, each census run TWICE — once line-oriented and once whitespace-flattened — and every run paired with a CONTROL needle known to be live.

CONTROL FIRED: 'stream=1' returned exactly its two known sites, README.md:516 and test/bytes.test.cjs:112, in both instruments. TARGETS: 'x-rf-ssr-stream' -> 1 hit, src/http.cjs:146 and nowhere else. 'streamingDefault' -> 4 hits, all src/http.cjs (:127, :147, :221, :226), i.e. the handleRender/serve plumbing passing it to itself. Both instruments agreed. The supported-consumer check the disposition asks for: bin/serve.cjs sets neither (its only serve() call passes port, host and maxRequestBytes); README's in-process serve example sets neither; no CLI flag, test, JVM adapter, example or build wiring anywhere. The literal 'stream=0' returns 0 hits because the source spells it as searchParams.get('stream') !== '0' — the bead described that branch semantically and correctly.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: kept the documented and byte-tested ?stream=1 query; removed the x-rf-ssr-stream header branch, the streamingDefault parameter from both handleRender and serve, and the ?stream=0 escape, which was reachable only when streamingDefault was on. Buffered is now the default and the query is the opt-in, unconditionally (AC1, AC3).

AC4: a new focused row in test/bytes.test.cjs sends the retired header and requires the response to come back BUFFERED — content-length equal to the UTF-8 length of the body, which a chunked response cannot carry, and bytes sha256-identical to the plain POST. The pin is load-bearing, not decorative: restoring the header branch in src/http.cjs (single-line anchor, match count 1 read first) makes it fail with 'the header must not have selected streaming — a streamed response carries no content-length', captured exit 1, 15 pass / 1 fail. Restore verified by git blob hash 6e761df8f7421b52a898c98fa3c734c4dfc41a0d.

AC2/AC5: bytes, serve and all 9 ssr-node suites green — 107 tests, 107 pass, 0 fail, captured exit 0 on the final rebased base. The pre-existing row asserting that streamed and buffered output are byte-identical still passes, so ?stream=1 remains chunked and a plain POST remains buffered and byte-identical. No README change was needed for AC1: neither retired selector was ever documented there, so ?stream=1 was already the sole documented selector.

title: Reader-condition seven SSR definitions and imports to their live host
description:
## Finding

Seven definitions/dependency edges in SSR `.cljc` files are live on exactly one host but are currently compiled on both. Reader conditionals already isolate every call site, leaving the opposite-host copies mechanically unreachable.

## Evidence

Focused clj-kondo runs report host-qualified findings:

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/suspense.cljc:192`: private `subtree` is unused on `:clj`; its only call is inside `boundary`'s `:cljs` arm.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/emit.cljc:20-21`: `clojure.string :as str` and `re-frame.error :as error` are unused on `:cljs`; every `str/` and `error/` call is inside the JVM `ld-json-string` arm, while CLJS uses `js/JSON.stringify`.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc:63`: `re-frame.interop :as interop` is unused on `:cljs`; its only executable read is the JVM-only `with-redefs [interop/debug-enabled? ...]` test arm.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_component_cljs_test.cljc:44-53`: private `card-skeleton`, `card-view`, and `throwing-card` are unused on `:cljs`; every reference is inside JVM-only streaming tests.

Exact source searches confirm each finding has live uses on the stated host and no use on the opposite host. The production `subtree` Var and all three test helper Vars were introduced in `80faa4f2c2` as part of reader-conditional server/client behavior; the definitions themselves were never host-scoped.

This does not classify the public `boundary` component, `re-frame.ssr` facade load, cross-host test namespace, or either host behavior as vestigial. Duplicate searches for "SSR reader conditional", "suspense subtree", "head emit unused namespace", "failed root isolation interop", and "streaming component card-skeleton" found no owning bead.

## Impact

The JVM ships a private Var that can never be called, CLJS carries two irrelevant production dependency edges, and both test targets compile host-inapplicable scaffolding. The seven predictable lint findings also obscure genuinely unreferenced definitions in future audits.

## Proposed disposition

Reader-condition `subtree` to CLJS; reader-condition the `clojure.string` and `re-frame.error` head-emitter requires to CLJ; reader-condition the isolation test's `re-frame.interop` require to CLJ; and reader-condition the three streaming-component test helpers to CLJ. Do not delete or rewrite the live host implementations. Leave the `re-frame.ssr` facade require and other possible registration/side-effect loads unchanged.

## Risks

Malformed `.cljc` require syntax or scoping a helper to the wrong host can break compilation before tests run. Both JVM and CLJS builds must be exercised. In particular, preserve the JVM JSON-LD error paths, the CLJS boundary body/fallback behavior, and the server-side streaming fixture markup exactly.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of the seven listed definitions/requires is reader-conditioned to its only consuming host.
- Focused clj-kondo runs no longer report those host-qualified unused findings; unrelated intentional side-effect-load findings are not removed to make lint superficially green.
- The SSR JVM suite passes, including head JSON-LD and server streaming-component tests.
- The Node and browser CLJS builds compile and pass the suspense boundary and failed-root isolation coverage.
- Public facade exports, namespace-load registrations, emitted markup/JSON, error ids, and test discovery are unchanged.
close_reason: PR #9106. All seven reader-conditioned to the host verified as their only consumer. :cljs — suspense/subtree (sole call at suspense.cljc:239, inside boundary's :cljs arm). :clj — head/emit's clojure.string and re-frame.error (every str/ and error/ use at emit.cljc lines 82-181, all inside ld-json-string's :clj letfn; the :cljs arm is js/JSON.stringify), failed_root_isolation_cljs_test's re-frame.interop (sole executable read at line 428 inside the #?(:clj ...) block; line 92 is docstring), and streaming_component_cljs_test's card-skeleton, card-view, throwing-card (all references at lines 104/105/132/133/167/168/176/177, every one inside a #?(:clj ...) deftest). None of the seven is used on both hosts. BOTH hosts run green: implementation/ssr clojure -M:test 623 tests/3172 assertions exit 0; implementation npm run test:cljs 11170 tests/55749 assertions exit 0. Gate liveness proved on each host with a wrong-host plant: #?(:clj (def wrong-host-probe (subtree ...))) gave SSR JVM exit 1 'Unable to resolve symbol: subtree'; #?(:cljs (def wrong-host-probe (card-view ...))) gave node-test compile exit 1 'Use of undeclared Var ... card-view'. Both plants reverted and the restored files verified byte-identical by git hash-object against the committed blobs (b661585278..., 910a8eed6b...). No live host implementation deleted or rewritten; facade exports, registrations, emitted markup and error ids unchanged.

title: Flows tests: remove unused routing/SSR deps and conformance import
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/deps.edn:23-24` and `:34-35` add `day8/re-frame2-routing` and `day8/re-frame2-ssr` to both `:test` and `:slow-test`.
- Exact searches across every flows source and test namespace find no `re-frame.routing` or `re-frame.ssr` require/reference; the dependency coordinates occur only in those four alias entries.
- The adjacent comment says the shared reset fixture reloads optional artefacts when present. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:332-482` only calls already-registered late-bound reset hooks via `late-bind/get-fn`; it never requires or loads routing/SSR. title: Remove seven dead helpers and imports from SSR tests
description:
## Finding

The SSR test slice retains two private helpers with no caller and five imports/refers with no symbol use or unique namespace-load role. They are mechanically dead test scaffolding, distinct from the deliberate side-effect/dynamic-resolution requires in the same suite.

## Evidence

A focused `clj-kondo --lint implementation/ssr/src implementation/ssr/test` pass plus exact per-file symbol searches reports:

- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_client_dom_cljs_test.cljs:117-119`: `final-payload-html` is defined but never called. A whole-repository exact-name search finds only this definition. `constants/payload-script-id` remains used by live assertions at lines 220 and 612, so removing the helper does not orphan that require.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/streaming_hydration_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs:172-173`: `app-db-seed` is defined but never read; the fixture continues to spell the seed inline at lines 99, 225, and 446.
- The same lifecycle test requires `re-frame.frame :as frame` at line 57 but has no `frame/` read; `re-frame.core` already loads `re-frame.frame`.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:155` requires `re-frame.substrate.adapter :as substrate-adapter` but has no qualified read. The suite initializes through `re-frame.ssr.test-fixture`, and its direct `re-frame.core` dependency already loads the adapter namespace.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_route_slice_projection_test.clj:37` requires `re-frame.core :as rf` but contains no `rf/` form. Its shared test fixture already loads the core facade.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_render_state_jvm_test.clj:20` refers `clojure.test/testing` but contains no `(testing ...)` form.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_streaming_hydration_egress_test.clj:21` requires `re-frame.frame :as frame` but contains no `frame/` read; its direct core dependency already loads the namespace.
- History searches show `final-payload-html` was introduced by `5a0232e9f2` and `app-db-seed` by `80faa4f2c2`; neither name has ever had a recorded caller.

This excludes `re-frame.ssr.head` in the conformance runner and `re-frame.ssr` in the head test: their aliases are statically unused, but requiring the namespaces publishes hooks/registrations used through `resolve` or teardown and is intentional. It also excludes imports/helpers used by only one reader-conditional host.

Duplicate searches for the helper names, "SSR unused test helpers", "unused SSR imports", "ssr conformance substrate adapter", "route slice projection core", "render state testing", and "streaming hydration egress frame" found no owning bead.

## Impact

The residue adds false fixture/dependency signals and seven avoidable linter findings, making real dead-code warnings harder to distinguish from noise. The unused seed constant is especially misleading because three live fixtures bypass it.

## Proposed disposition

Delete `final-payload-html`, `app-db-seed`, the four redundant namespace requires, and the unused `testing` refer. Leave the existing inline seed values and live test behavior unchanged. Preserve side-effect-only and dynamic-resolution requires, even when static lint cannot see their consumption.

## Risks

This must remain a mechanical cleanup: do not rewrite payload fixtures, alter test enrollment, remove hook-publishing namespace loads, or fold platform-specific helpers into this issue. Confirm each removed namespace is still loaded where needed through the existing direct dependency before accepting.
acceptance_criteria:
- The two unused helper definitions and five unused require/refer entries listed in the finding are absent.
- Exact-name/alias searches find no stale reference, and focused clj-kondo output no longer reports those seven locations.
- `re-frame.ssr.head` dynamic-resolution loading, `re-frame.ssr` registration loading, reader-conditional imports, and all live helper definitions remain intact.
- SSR JVM tests plus the Node and browser CLJS test builds still discover and pass the affected namespaces.
- Payload bytes, fixture seed maps, assertions, and runtime setup/teardown behavior are unchanged.
close_reason: PR #9106. Removed final-payload-html and app-db-seed (both definition-only: git grep -F over tracked files returned 1 hit each, while controls payload-script-id and failed-chunk-html returned 3 and 5 in the same files) plus the five requires/refers with no symbol read: re-frame.frame in streaming_hydration_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test and ssr_streaming_hydration_egress_test, re-frame.substrate.adapter in ssr_conformance_test, re-frame.core in ssr_route_slice_projection_test, clojure.test/testing in ssr_render_state_jvm_test. Load coverage verified at source: re-frame.core requires re-frame.frame (core.cljc:31) and re-frame.substrate.adapter (core.cljc:142); re-frame.ssr.test-fixture requires re-frame.core (test_fixture.clj:55). constants/payload-script-id kept (two live assertions). re-frame.ssr.head in the conformance runner and re-frame.ssr in the head test left alone as the bead directs. title: Remove Root Descriptor key inventories stranded by re-frame.ui retirement
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.ssr.manifest/descriptor-keys` and `extension-keys` are production data inventories whose only stated purpose was to make the Root Descriptor -> Root Manifest subset property mechanically checkable. The sole descriptor producer and the compiler-backed subset suite were retired with `re-frame.ui`, but both inventories and prose claiming that suite still pins the property remain.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/manifest.cljc:94-116` defines the two sets. A repository-wide exact-symbol search across `implementation/`, `tools/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, `spec/`, and `docs/` finds no reads; each name occurs only at its definition.
- The namespace docstring at lines 23-24 and `problems` docstring at line 155 still say "the subset-property test" pins the invariant. `spec/011-SSR.md:474-475` likewise claims the reference suite checks the real compiler output.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/root_manifest_cljs_test.cljc:11-21` now explicitly records that the subset-property suite was deleted because `re-frame.ui` was retired and no remaining substrate emits a Root Descriptor.
- Commit `b24c6ab015` introduced the sets and compiler-backed suite together. Commit `a3e5e17e73` removed the producer, its test dependency, and the 11 descriptor-coupled tests, but left the production inventories and stale claims.
- `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj` classifies `re-frame.ssr.manifest` as an internal namespace. Spec 011's artefact roster names `problems`, `valid?`, `validate!`, `manifest`, `script-html`, `read-manifest`, and `discover`; it does not expose either key-set Var.

Duplicate searches for `descriptor-keys`, `extension-keys`, "root manifest subset", "retired descriptor inventory", `a3e5e17`, and `rf2-0yp7w` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The two dead Vars carry a retired compiler model in the shipped SSR artefact and can drift independently from the live validator. The stale prose falsely suggests a real-producer integration check still exists, obscuring the deliberate coverage gap documented by the surviving test namespace.

## Proposed disposition

Delete `descriptor-keys` and `extension-keys`. Update the three stale subset-suite claims in the manifest source and Spec 011 to describe the current hand-built validator coverage and the absence of a live descriptor producer. Preserve the normative rule that only `:rf.root/schema-version` is required and extension keys are optional. Keep `schema-version`, `dev-only-keys`, validation, assembly, wire, discovery, and late-bind behavior unchanged.

## Risks

Do not turn this cleanup into a schema contraction: unknown keys must remain accepted, every extension key must remain optional, and descriptor-shaped maps must still validate. The removed Vars are internal and have no repository consumers, but the implementation should still run the API-manifest check so an accidental public-surface change elsewhere is caught.
acceptance_criteria:
- `descriptor-keys` and `extension-keys` are absent, with no replacement duplicate inventory.
- Source and Spec 011 no longer claim a deleted real-compiler subset-property suite is running; the documented absence of a descriptor producer remains explicit.
- `problems` still accepts `{:rf.root/schema-version 1}`, ignores unknown keys, and shape-checks optional extension keys only when present.
- Existing Root Manifest JVM and CLJS tests pass, including schema-version-only validity, assembly, exact EDN round-trip, and discovery coverage.
- The API-manifest gate still classifies `re-frame.ssr.manifest` as internal and passes.

DONOR-REFERENCE CATEGORY CALL, per item. descriptor-keys: NOT retirement bookkeeping (no dated statement naming rf2-0yp7w, no struck-through catalogue row - its docstring asserts a LIVE checkable property) and NOT the reserved-kind contract (it rosters :rf.root/* descriptor keys, not :rf.adapter/ui or :rf.adapter/freehand reserved values that tooling refuses defensively against a stale co-loaded build); genuinely unreachable inventory, removed. extension-keys: same two calls, same verdict - and specifically NOT a reserved-value roster, because the live validator problems already encodes all six keys in its own destructure and contains? checks, and the namespace docstring's markdown table is the documentation; the set was a duplicate with no reader. dev-only-keys: RETAINED - it has a live consumer on the emit path (manifest.cljc:421, apply dissoc). The three stale claims that a real-compiler subset-property suite still pins the invariant were corrected rather than deleted, so the RECORD survives: the ns docstring and problems docstring now say validation is checked over hand-built manifests because re-frame.ui was retired (rf2-0yp7w) and no remaining substrate emits a Root Descriptor, pointing at re-frame.ssr.root-manifest-cljs-test which already records the deliberate gap; spec/011-SSR.md:473-475 likewise. title: Remove evaluate-flow!'s unread dirty-result slot
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:214-296` documents and returns `[db dirty?]`: `[db false]` on equal inputs and `[new-db true]` after a computation.
- The private function has one call, at lines 330-336. That caller checks the separate `stale-incarnation` marker and then reads only `(first result)`; no source, test, tool, trace, or public API reads the Boolean slot.
- `210a7d0908` removed `run-flows-on-db`'s dead `any-dirty?` accumulator because the router always consumes the transformed db and per-flow skip/computed traces carry the observable dirty signal. Its commit message explicitly says the tuple's dirty slot is discarded at the call; later exact-owner changes retained that discard.
- Exact repository searches find no destructuring or indexing of the second result element.

Impact and disposition
Every non-stale flow visit constructs a two-element result whose second value has no consumer, and the docstring advertises a dirty contract the cascade intentionally retired. Remove the Boolean slot and simplify the sole caller/result contract while preserving the transformed-db left fold and the distinct stale-incarnation outcome.

Risk
Owner-loss short-circuiting, derive/output-write error attribution, dirty-cache rollback, validation, trace ordering/elision, and the documented three-argument compatibility path of `run-flows-on-db` are deliberate contracts and must remain unchanged. Do not make a legitimate pending db indistinguishable from the stale marker.
acceptance_criteria:
- `evaluate-flow!` no longer returns or documents an unread dirty Boolean.
- Its sole caller consumes the simplified successful result without a second-slot discard.
- Tests cover both equal-input skip and computed-output paths plus owner loss before/after the derive callback, with the same transformed db and stale behavior as today.
- Flow failure attribution and rollback tests, default JVM/CLJS flows suites, and exact-incarnation tests pass.
close_reason: PREMISE HELD — evaluate-flow! now returns the transformed db rather than [db dirty?] (PR #9082). The bead's evidence was truncated at the point where it said what the caller checks, so the caller was read directly: at flows.cljc:330-336 it does (if (= stale-incarnation result) stale-incarnation (recur (rest remaining) (first result))) — it discriminates the stale marker and then takes (first result), and NEVER reads the second element. Census: no source, test, tool, trace, spec or public API destructures or indexes it; every tree-wide mention of evaluate-flow! outside its own file is a comment, a docstring or spec prose, and no test reaches the private var through #'. No new marker ambiguity, which was the bead's stated risk: run-flows-on-db* ALREADY returns either a bare db or stale-incarnation to its own caller (both its (empty? remaining) and empty-flow-map arms return db unwrapped), so evaluate-flow! now returns the same two outcomes its enclosing fold does, discriminated the same way. Owner-loss short-circuiting, derive/output-write phase attribution, dirty-cache rollback, validation, trace ordering/elision and the three-argument run-flows-on-db path are untouched. title: Resources optimistic settle: retire the superseded revision-conflict predicate
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:819-835 defines revision-conflict?. Exact repository search finds no production call; all executable calls are direct tests in resources_revision_substrate_cljs_test.cljc, plus comments that claim settle consumes it.
- Production optimistic settlement owns a different predicate: implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_runtime.cljc:490-508 defines optimistic-conflict?, called by rollback-entry-disposition at :534 and then by the settle paths.
- The semantics are intentionally different. state/revision-conflict? compares current revision with the pre-apply observed revision, so the optimistic apply's own bump appears conflicting. optimistic-conflict? compares with the post-apply applied revision and handles applied-removed-revision so an absent entry after an optimistic remove is not a conflict.
- Commit 2687c1551d introduced the state helper. Commit 177caced60 introduced the real settle helper and used it from inception, but left comments at mutation_runtime.cljc:448, mutation_events.cljc:321/536, and state.cljc:815 pointing to the older helper.

Impact
Tests preserve a conflict algorithm that the product cannot safely use and comments identify the wrong authority. A maintainer following those pointers could reintroduce false conflicts or mishandle optimistic removes.

Proposed disposition
Remove state/revision-conflict? and tests that directly pin its obsolete pre-apply comparison. Update comments/spec references to identify mutation-runtime/optimistic-conflict? and applied-revision as the live rule. Preserve entry-revision and bump-revision, and strengthen tests at rollback-entry-disposition/live settle boundaries.

Risks
Do not mechanically replace optimistic-conflict? with the state helper: doing so changes behavior. Preserve both numeric applied revisions and the removed sentinel, as well as the bias-safe invalidation/force conflict policies.
acceptance_criteria:
- state/revision-conflict? has no definition/calls and source comments point to the live applied-revision comparison.
- Non-vacuous tests cover no-conflict after the apply's own numeric bump, conflict after a later write, absent-after-remove as no conflict, re-created-after-remove as conflict, and both invalidate/force settle dispositions.
- Optimistic mutation JVM/CLJS suites pass and normative revision prose matches the applied-revision algorithm.

title: Remove flows tooling's obsolete private bundle sentinel
description:
Evidence
- `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/tooling.cljc:91-98` declares private `bundle-isolation-sentinel` and claims the bundle-isolation gate searches its unique literal.
- An exact repository search for `rf.flows.tooling/sentinel:rf2-s8w3nw-2026-06-12:do-not-rename` finds only that definition; no production, test, build, or tooling consumer reads the var or literal. clj-kondo 2025.10.23 reports it as an unused private var.
- The live checker is `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:382-399`: the `flows-tooling` row searches emitted output for `after-event`, which is reached through `flow-algebra-view`; `implementation/scripts/bundle-isolation-positive-control/src/re_frame/bundle_isolation_positive_control/flows_tooling.cljs:1-6` imports that public projection.
- `4e43784ec7` changed bundle-isolation controls to inspect emitted modules and selected the live `after-event` classification. The planted private var remained behind even though Closure advanced compilation can discard an unread private definition. The same checker documents this exact failure mode for the since-removed derivation-egress planted sentinel at lines 515-526.

Impact and disposition
The var has no runtime consumer and cannot prove emitted reachability, while its stale comment directs maintainers toward a known-vacuous sentinel pattern. Remove the private definition and its obsolete sentinel block. Keep the live `:evaluation :after-event` projection and the emitted-module isolation control.

Risk
Do not weaken or remove the current positive control: the focused flows-tooling module must still reach `flow-algebra-view`, and the live emitted marker must remain absent from disallowed modules.
acceptance_criteria:
- Remove `bundle-isolation-sentinel` and the comment that claims the checker searches its literal.
- The obsolete `rf.flows.tooling/sentinel:rf2-s8w3nw-2026-06-12:do-not-rename` literal is absent from the repository.
- Bundle-isolation checker tests pass.
- The focused bundle-isolation positive-control build still finds the live flows-tooling sentinel in its allowed emitted module and zero occurrences in disallowed modules.
close_reason: Removed the defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel and its false comment from flows/tooling.cljc (PR #9082). Premise held. Three-legged emitted-module measurement on a fresh build: planted literal in out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/flows-tooling.js = 0; live 'after-event' in the SAME file with the SAME instrument = 1 (control); literal in pre-change source = 1. The zero is Closure DCE of an unread private var, so do-not-rename guarded nothing. check-bundle-isolation.cjs needed NO edit: fixed-string search of the checker for the flows literal = 0 against the rf.derivation.egress twin = 1 as the control that fires; its flows row needle is sentinel: 'after-event'. Comment removed with the var per the rf2-f8fo ruling, no replacement added. Gate proved live by sabotage witness: renaming the live keyword drove check-bundle-isolation.cjs to exit 1 naming exactly "emitted module 'flows-tooling' present ... expected >= 1, was 0"; restored and verified by git blob hash, counts back to 40 absent / 40 present.

title: Resources ledger: remove prune-record superseded by indexed batch pruning
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:516-526 defines prune-record, but exact repository search finds no production caller; its only executable consumer is a direct unit test at resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc:843.
- The live operation is prune-terminal-for-key at work_ledger.cljc:548-599. It already holds byte work-id ids and removes all drop-ids in one reduce, then updates the inverse-index bucket in bulk; it cannot use prune-record, which accepts a structured work-id and recomputes its byte identity.
- Comments at work_ledger.cljc:416 and :562 nevertheless claim the live index is maintained through put-record/prune-record.
- Commit 0813d08aa1 introduced prune-record. Commit b0edd0265c added the inverse index and the batch prune implementation, leaving the now-superseded helper, its direct test, and stale comments.

Impact
A superseded single-row deletion API and its direct-only test imply that production pruning exercises code it bypasses. The stale comments obscure the actual atomic/batched inverse-index maintenance path and can misdirect future fixes.

Proposed disposition
Remove prune-record and replace/delete its direct-only test in favor of assertions through prune-terminal-for-key. Correct comments to name put-record plus the batch prune as the live incremental maintainers. Preserve bounded tail retention, non-terminal rows, byte-key isolation, index self-heal, and empty-bucket cleanup.

Risks
Do not regress the O(rows-for-key) index path into a whole-ledger scan or repeated structured-id conversion. Internal namespace consumers outside the repository are not a documented API but should be considered under normal release policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- prune-record is absent and comments describe the actual batch prune path.
- Tests through prune-terminal-for-key prove old terminal rows and their inverse-index members are removed, the retained tail/non-terminal rows survive, empty buckets disappear, and an absent installed index self-heals.
- Vector/list identity collision coverage and resource work-ledger JVM/CLJS suites pass.
close_reason: Removed work-ledger/prune-record (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc) and corrected the two comments (at the inverse-index preamble and inside prune-terminal-for-key) that named it as a live incremental index maintainer. Premise verified at tip by two instruments: fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis. Both agree: ZERO production callers; the only executable consumer was the resources work-ledger test. Control put-record fired in both, across 6 namespaces incl. production events and mutation-events. CASCADE NOT NAMED IN THE BEAD: prune-record was the sole caller of the private index-remove, so that helper is removed with it (leaving it would have added an Unused-private-var warning - the after-lint confirms none appeared). The live path is unchanged: prune-terminal-for-key still holds byte work-id ids, removes all drop-ids in one reduce and updates the inverse-index bucket in bulk, with no regression to a whole-ledger scan or repeated structured-id conversion. WHAT THE DELETED TEST WAS GUARANTEEING, and whether the live path still does: prune-record's only executable consumer was NOT a dedicated unit test of it but one of three operations interleaved in a randomised 500-op property test asserting the incrementally-maintained inverse index equals a full rebuild after EVERY op, with no empty buckets. That property is retained over the two remaining operations, and the criteria this bead sets are already met by dedicated tests that were not touched: prune-terminal-for-key-matches-full-scan-reference (old terminal rows and their index members removed, retained tail and non-terminal rows survive), prune-self-heals-on-wholesale-installed-ledger (absent installed index self-heals), the randomised test's own no-empty-buckets assertion, and the event-level succeeded-completes-and-prunes-record / succeeded-prunes-old-terminal-rows-beyond-tail. No guarantee was dropped. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Resources state: remove the inert lifecycle-states constant
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:174-179 defines lifecycle-states and says the closed set is pinned so sibling namespaces agree.
- Exact repository search finds no source caller, validator, test, documentation reference, or API-manifest entry for this var. Resource handlers and state constructors use status literals directly.
- clj-kondo usage analysis likewise reports no consumer. The constant was added in the initial resources skeleton commit 2cd05677fb and has never been wired into the runtime.

Impact
The var is inert documentation masquerading as an enforcement/source-of-truth mechanism. Because siblings do not read it, adding or removing a lifecycle state can leave the claimed closed set stale without any failure.

Proposed disposition
Remove lifecycle-states and its false source-of-truth claim. If the project wants a machine-readable closed set, first connect it to a real schema/validator or exhaustive transition check and test that contract; do not retain a decorative constant.

Risks
Do not alter the five shipped lifecycle states or transition behavior as part of this cleanup. Search for macro/generated consumers before deletion and retain normative FSM prose in Spec 016.
acceptance_criteria:
- lifecycle-states is removed, or a real runtime/schema/tooling consumer enforces it with a non-vacuous test.
- No documentation claims sibling agreement through an unread var.
- Existing idle/loading/fetching/loaded/error transition and serialization tests pass on JVM and CLJS.
close_reason: Removed state/lifecycle-states (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc). Premise verified at tip by two independent instruments before deletion: a fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened, .beads exports excluded) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis over implementation/ + tools/. Both found ZERO usages of any kind - no source caller, validator, test, doc reference or API-manifest entry. Controls in the same namespace fired in both instruments (terminal-work-statuses: 6 files incl. the production work_ledger consumer; entry-revision: 4 namespaces incl. production mutation-runtime). The only other repo hit was an unrelated hicasso deftest NAME containing the substring, not a consumer. The var's docstring claimed the closed set was pinned so siblings agree on it; since no sibling read it, adding or removing a lifecycle state could leave that claim stale with nothing failing - inert documentation masquerading as enforcement, exactly as filed. The five shipped states and their transition behaviour are untouched. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Resources routing: remove the zero-consumer plan-identities getter
description:
Evidence
- implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:176-181 defines plan-identities as a wrapper around get-in(runtime-db, plan-path(nav-token)). Exact repository search finds no caller, test, documentation, or API-manifest entry for the symbol.

- plan-path, plan-slots-map-path, and clear-plan-slot are independently used and remain live; only the getter is orphaned.
- Commit 39142d0d6a added the helper with EP-0037 R2, but no production consumer was ever introduced. Routing deliberately avoids a static dependency on the optional resources artefact, so replacing its direct read with this resources-namespace helper would violate the existing late-bound boundary.

Impact
The unused getter suggests one authoritative access path while the actual owners use another. It adds an unsupported internal seam and maintenance surface without abstracting any live behavior.

Proposed disposition
Remove only plan-identities. Keep the slot path constructors, clear behavior, direct routing reads, and optional-artifact boundary unchanged.

Risks
Do not remove the :resource-plan slot or plan-path/clear-plan-slot functions; those are live persistence and cleanup contracts. Out-of-repository code should not rely on this internal namespace, but release notes may mention removal if policy requires it.
acceptance_criteria:
- The plan-identities symbol is absent and no dead direct test is introduced for it.
- Route activation and replan still diff against the prior nav-token resource-plan slot, including failed-plan recovery and attach-before-release behavior.
- Routing remains buildable without a static resources dependency and bundle optionality checks remain green.
- Resource/routing integration suites pass.
close_reason: Removed route/plan-identities (implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc). Premise verified at tip by two independent instruments: a fixed-string census over 4818 tracked files (line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened) and clj-kondo var-usage analysis. Both found ZERO usages of any kind - the symbol appeared in exactly one file, its own definition. Controls fired in both (plan-path; put-record across 6 namespaces incl. production). Confirmed the bead's mechanism: both live plan-diff consumers read the routing slot path directly, which is what keeps routing free of a static dependency on the optional resources artefact - so the getter was an unsupported internal seam abstracting no live behaviour. plan-path, plan-slots-map-path, clear-plan-slot and the :resource-plan slot are all retained per the ruling. That holds for clear-plan-slot (called from events.cljc) and for plan-slots-map-path (called from clear-plan-slot), but NOT for plan-path: its only non-test caller was plan-identities itself, so with the getter gone plan-path is now referenced by three route tests and no production code. It was kept as the ruling directs and nothing was changed about it; flagging only because a future vestige sweep will find it and should have this context rather than re-deriving it. Landed in PR #9079.

title: Resources: remove input-db-paths left by retired sensitivity propagation
description:

If retention is preferred, first identify and wire a concrete shipped consumer rather than preserving a speculative seam.

title: Remove dead imports and bindings from schemas tests
description:
## Finding

The schemas test slice contains a bounded set of imports, local bindings, and nested `let` wrappers with no reader or behavioral effect. They are test-maintenance residue from earlier fixture/reset and handler shapes, distinct from namespaces intentionally required only for load/build side effects.

## Evidence

A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/schemas/src` and `implementation/schemas/test`, followed by manual symbol and history checks, proves:

- Seven dead namespace aliases/imports: `re-frame.schemas.digest` in `schemas_concurrency_stress_test.clj`; `re-frame.substrate.adapter` in both `schemas_conformance_test.clj` and `schemas_reg_side_effects_test.clj`; `re-frame.schemas.validator` in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj`; `re-frame.registrar` and `re-frame.trace` in `schemas_test.clj`; and `re-frame.trace` in `schemas_validator_unavailable_warning_test.clj`. Repository searches find no qualified use of any alias in its file.
- Fifteen unused locals: three `db` destructurings in `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` (currently lines 62, 85, 342); two in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj` (169, 246); five in `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (1561, 1597, 1632, 1728, 1753); four in `schemas_test.clj` (97, 124, 165, 297); plus the never-read `secret` binding in `schemas_sensitive_test.clj` (1161). The affected init handlers return fixed maps, so replacing their unused cofx destructure with `_` is behavior-neutral; the secret test dispatches integer `12345`, not that binding.
- Four single-body nested `let` forms in `schemas_fail_open_test.clj` (currently 178, 233, 255, 273) merely wrap an immediately enclosing `let` and are reported as redundant. Merging binding vectors preserves evaluation and assertion order.
- History ties several imports to superseded local reset fixtures. For example `c6017e7f32` moved registrar/frame/adapter cleanup to `schemas.test-fixture/reset-runtime` but left some caller imports behind.
- All-status bead searches for schemas test imports, schemas unused bindings, lint, and the named test paths found no owning issue.

## Deliberate exclusions

Do not remove `re-frame.core` from `schemas_bundle_control.cljs` or `schemas_bundle_probe.cljs`: both files explain that the unused alias is an intentional matched-build require and removing it invalidates the A/B. Do not blindly remove effect-only `re-frame.schemas` loads, unresolved macro/API references, or the app-db source's nested `let` around stale-incarnation checkpoints. Redundant direct Malli adapter test requires and their stale posture are owned separately by `rf2-6r9j.51`.

## Impact

Dead imports make test dependency boundaries look broader than they are; unused handler bindings and wrapper lets add noise to already large security/error-path suites and keep focused lint output noisy enough to hide new regressions. There is no intended runtime, public API, diagnostic, or fixture-isolation contract behind these items.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the seven proven-unused imports, replace only the fifteen unused locals with appropriately ignored parameters or delete the inert binding, and flatten the four test-only nested lets without changing their assertions or setup/cleanup order.

## Risks

Clojure namespace loads can be side-effectful and the bundle fixtures deliberately exploit that. Keep the change to the enumerated items, verify each require's absence does not alter hook/adapter initialization, and preserve `try/finally`, trace recorder, and stale-incarnation ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
- Focused clj-kondo no longer reports the seven enumerated unused namespaces, fifteen enumerated unused bindings, or four enumerated redundant lets.
- The intentional unused `re-frame.core` requires in both matched schemas bundle fixtures remain, with their explanatory contract intact.
- Effect-only facade/adapter wiring required for schema validation remains covered by `schemas_implies_validation_test` and `rf2-6r9j.51`; no load-order regression is introduced.
- Schemas JVM and CLJS suites pass, including conformance, fail-open, sensitive redaction, concurrency stress, validator-unavailable warning, and production boundary targets.
- Test names, assertion counts/semantics, `try/finally` restoration, and trace capture order are unchanged except for removal of inert syntax.
close_reason: PR #9111. All three enumerated groups landed; focused clj-kondo over implementation/schemas/{src,test} went 33 -> 7 warnings with errors 0, and the 26 cleared are exactly the enumerated set. Seven unused requires removed (schemas.digest in concurrency-stress; substrate.adapter in conformance and reg-side-effects; schemas.validator in fail-open; registrar and trace in schemas_test; trace in validator-unavailable-warning), each proven by TWO instruments -- a boundary-anchored git grep for the alias in its own file plus clj-kondo's alias resolution -- with a control alias in the SAME file returning a stable non-zero count every time. Worth recording: a naive substring grep for 'digest/' and 'trace/' returns FALSE HITS inside the qualified keywords :utdxg.digest/seed and :rf.trace/phase; the anchored form reads 0. Fifteen locals: fourteen cofx destructures on fixed-map init handlers replaced with _, plus the never-read secret binding at the container-level sensitive test (which dispatches the integer 12345, not the binding) -- adjacent sibling handlers that DO read db were left alone. Four single-body nested lets in fail-open merged into their enclosing let; the inner init depends on the outer binding so evaluation and assertion order are preserved. Kept per the bead's exclusions: both matched-build re-frame.core requires in the schemas bundle fixtures, the effect-only re-frame.schemas loads in conformance and reg-side-effects, and validate.cljc's nested let. Gates: schemas JVM 372 tests / 19221 assertions and npm run test:cljs 11168 / 55740, both exit 0, 0 failures 0 errors. Gate proven live by planting (is (neg? (count mal))) inside a FLATTENED let -- exit 1 naming schemas_fail_open_test.clj:178, the flattened block's own body line -- then restoring, hash-object identical. Test names, assertion counts and try/finally ordering unchanged.

title: Remove resources tooling obsolete private bundle sentinel
description:

Impact
The dead declaration creates a lint warning and its comment falsely describes the safety gate. It can mislead maintainers into preserving or renaming an identifier that the compiled bundle cannot contain.

Proposed disposition
Delete bundle-isolation-sentinel and its stale do-not-rename/checker comment. Preserve resource-process as the live bundle witness and keep the checker non-vacuous.

- Exact repository search finds the event only in registration/handler code, reserved-event prose, and tests that dispatch the internal event directly. Commit f08e41dfcd explicitly described this handler as legacy after moving it onto the canonical reply path; the original skeleton was 2cd05677fb.

Impact
The package carries two cancellation settlement entrances although only the failed-event entrance is reachable from the live transport. This preserves a second internal protocol, duplicated tests, registration, event census, and stale documentation that can drift from canonical reply behavior.

Proposed disposition
Remove the :rf.resource.internal/aborted registration, aborted-event-failure, and aborted-handler. Re-express or delete the direct-dispatch tests through :rf.resource.internal/failed with a canonical cancellation reply so live/stale, cross-frame, ledger, completed-at, readiness, route, invalidation, and Epoch behavior stays covered on the production path. Reconcile Spec 016, Conventions, EP event rosters, and comments that reserve or describe the retired member.

Risks
Although user code is explicitly forbidden to dispatch this internal namespace, out-of-repository code may have done so. Check release/migration policy and call out the retirement. Do not weaken cancellation classification or stale-reply suppression while collapsing the path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repository search has no :rf.resource.internal/aborted registration or executable dispatch after the migration (except an intentional migration note if required).
- Managed HTTP abort coverage proves the canonical :rf.resource.internal/failed path yields cancelled settlement, including stale/cross-frame suppression, completed-at, ledger/reply targets, and blocking-readiness behavior.
- Internal-event rosters and normative prose match the shipped event set.
- Resource JVM and CLJS suites pass.

GATES (foreground, exit codes captured to files and read from the files): resources 0 (828 tests / 7475 assertions), epoch 0 (552 / 7237), ssr-ring 0 (231 / 1163), core error-catalogue ns 0 (30 / 179). clj-kondo over `implementation` exits 3 on ONE error in epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:939 — a file byte-identical to origin/main on this branch, reproducing on its origin/main content standalone; local kondo is v2025.10.23 against CI's pinned v2026.04.15. That sentence reads: "The handlers that carry it: ... and the internal replies `:rf.resource.internal/succeeded` / `:rf.resource.internal/failed` / `:rf.resource.internal/aborted` / `:rf.resource.internal/stale-fired` / ...". EXACT EDIT: delete the two tokens "`:rf.resource.internal/aborted` / " from that list. Nothing else on the line changes.

spec/016-Resources.md:645 needs NO change — it is a reserved-member roster of the `:rf.resource.internal/*` sub-namespace, the same shape as the Conventions rows the ruling keeps.

Nothing mechanical reads it. This is bookkeeping, not a correctness gap, and closing this bead as-is and letting the line ride until someone next opens spec/016 is a defensible call.

SPEC/016:460 RULED — NO EDIT. Worker specfin-a, 2026-09-03 (hot-zone serial lane; PR #9118 carries this tick's other two beads, spec/016 deliberately untouched).

PREMISE FAILURE FIRST, because it changes the question. The brief I was given, and the note above, both say the code half "LANDED in PR #9116". IT HAS NOT. gh pr view 9116 returns state OPEN, mergedAt null. The handler is still registered on origin/main at implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:529, and it still carries the framework-authority stamp. So deleting the two tokens from :460 TODAY would make the spec assert that a shipped, stamped handler does not exist. That is strictly worse than the staleness it would fix, and it is the catalogue-vs-code drift the "dispatch code-dependent follow-up only after the source PR MERGES" rule exists to prevent. (Landing was tested by payload, not by ancestry: git log origin/main --grep for each of .52/.47/.80 returns nothing.)

THE CALIBRATION HOLDS, AND IS STRONGER THAN THE NOTE ABOVE RECORDED. The note said :460 already omits four registered internal handlers. Measured at source, the omission is NINE of TWENTY-ONE.

:460 names 6 public + 6 internal = 12. resources.cljc registers 11 public + 10 internal = 21. Omitted: public load-more, adopt-owner, release-owner-identities, window-focused, network-reconnected; internal refetch-page, page-succeeded, page-failed, poll-fired.

And every one of those 21 DOES carry the stamp, which is the part that settles it. The stamp is not written per registration — it comes from three meta vars, and generation-meta (resources.cljc:393) and time-meta (:377) are each (assoc framework-authority-meta ...). So all three derive from framework-authority-meta and every registered resource event is stamped. A list naming 12 of 21 stamped handlers under the words "The handlers that carry it" is therefore ILLUSTRATIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, not a roster that a retirement falsifies. Nothing mechanical reads it (no gate resolves symbols named in prose here).

Deleting one token from an already-9-short illustration buys nothing, and the sentence does not become false when the handler goes — it was never claiming completeness. :645 needs no change either, as already established (reserved-member roster, same shape as the Conventions rows the mayor ruling keeps).

title: Finish schema-implies-validation migration in schemas tests
description:
## Finding

The schemas test surface did not complete the `schema implies validation` migration. Twelve test namespaces that already require the public `re-frame.schemas` facade still separately require `re-frame.schemas.malli`, and two CLJS suites continue to describe that direct adapter require as the canonical application opt-in. One test named `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` models an application posture that the facade deliberately made impossible; what it actually exercises is the supported defensive missing-hook/substitute-port fallback.

## Evidence

- Current source and Spec 010 state that `re-frame.schemas` itself requires `re-frame.schemas.malli`; requiring the artefact automatically publishes the Malli validate/explain hooks. Commit `d0b95fdc54` made this Ruling A specifically to eliminate the "schemas loaded but adapter not required" posture.
- A line-oriented census finds 12 direct `[re-frame.schemas.malli]` requires under `implementation/schemas/test`; every one of those namespaces also directly requires `re-frame.schemas`. No test calls an adapter var (the adapter is load-side-effect-only). The dedicated `schemas_implies_validation_test.clj` intentionally requires only the facade and already proves the transitive wiring contract.
- `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` (currently lines 18-25 and 96-111) still says direct adapter require is the "canonical opt-in" and that omitting it soft-passes. Its `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` test (currently around lines 136-161) manually clears late-bind hooks; because the same namespace requires the facade, this is not an app-without-adapter scenario.
- `schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs` (currently lines 48-55) repeats the obsolete instruction that CLJS apps must require the adapter at boot, despite also requiring the facade on line 58.
- Spec 010 currently says there is "nothing extra to opt into" (around lines 652-660) and reserves the soft-pass for a cross-port default-absent posture or an explicitly installed substitute validator. The stale test prose contradicts that normative contract.
- Blame dates the obsolete CLJS comments/direct requires to `80119fc1a9`, before Ruling A. The June 15 vestigial sweep `2980649a9c` edited the same file but only repaired a retired event-registration spelling, leaving this older posture untouched.
- All-status title/description searches for `adapter require`, `schema implies validation tests`, `canonical opt-in`, and `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` found no owning issue. Closed `rf2-tiymn` covers production elision of Malli's humanizer, not test import/posture cleanup.

## Impact

The redundant requires make broad schemas tests bypass the public load contract they are ostensibly exercising and stale comments teach consumers the exact extra boot step Ruling A retired. The no-adapter test name/text presents a reachable consumer configuration that cannot occur after loading the facade, obscuring the real reason the soft-pass branch remains: alternate ports or deliberate hook invalidation.

## Proposed disposition

Remove redundant direct adapter requires from schemas tests that already load the facade, leaving the dedicated facade-only regression as the authority. Rewrite the two CLJS comment blocks to state automatic facade wiring. Keep the missing-hook behavior test, but rename/reword it around deliberate hook absence/substitute-port fallback rather than an app forgetting a separate require.

## Risks

Do not remove `re-frame.schemas.malli` from the facade or change the default validator. Do not delete the defensive soft-pass branch/test: alternate ports and deliberate unbinding still need it. Preserve the production boundary build's validator/humanizer assertions and the matched bundle probes.
acceptance_criteria:
- No schemas test namespace that already requires `re-frame.schemas` separately requires `[re-frame.schemas.malli]`; the facade remains the single default-adapter wiring boundary.
- `schemas_cljs_test.cljs` and `schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs` no longer describe a separate Malli adapter require as canonical or omission as a normal application posture.
- The former `cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes` test is named and documented as a deliberate missing-hook/substitute-port fallback and still proves the default validator soft-passes when that hook is explicitly absent.
- `schemas_implies_validation_test.clj` still proves that requiring only the facade binds validate/explain hooks and makes a bad registered value fail.
- Schemas JVM, ordinary CLJS, production-boundary CLJS, and bundle A/B gates pass; a negative control removing the facade's adapter require makes the facade-only regression fail.
- Public schema registration, custom-validator installation, nil-validator opt-out, and production boundary semantics are unchanged.

worker/sectier-a holds rf2-6r9j.55 and has UNCOMMITTED edits to implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_cljs_test.cljs — three hunks replacing unused {:keys [db]} destructures with _ at the lines the .55 evidence names (62, 85, 342). A positive control through the same command shape (ls-remote for worker/uixring-a, which has open PR #9110) returned a sha, so the instrument was live and the branch genuinely did not exist remotely. The work was found only in git worktree list: the branch exists LOCALLY at C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/sectier-a with a dirty tree. Check the local worktree list, not just origin, before concluding a peer worker has not started.

PR #9113 deliberately touched no ns form in that file for this reason.

Independent of the collision, one .51 premise is worth re-checking at source: the description says twelve test namespaces carry a direct [re-frame.schemas.malli] require. Re-run that census before acting; PR #9113 changed neither the count nor any require, but rf2-6r9j.55 merging first may.
