All 12 removed; schemas_implies_validation_test.clj untouched as the facade-only authority. The two CLJS comment blocks (schemas_cljs_test.cljs, schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs) now state automatic facade wiring instead of a second require at app boot. cljs-no-adapter-soft-passes renamed cljs-unbound-validate-hook-soft-passes and reworded around a substitute validator port / deliberate unbinding per Spec 010 Recommended soft-pass; the behaviour under test is unchanged. Two facade requires whose ALIAS clj-kondo reports unused (schemas_conformance_test, schemas_reg_side_effects_test) now carry a note that the require is load-bearing regardless, so a future dead-import sweep does not take the last thing wiring the hooks. Gates, exit codes captured to file: schemas JVM clojure -M:test 373 tests / 19223 assertions 0 failures exit 0; node-test focused over the four schemas CLJS namespaces 23 tests / 163 assertions exit 0; npm run test:browser-schemas-boundary-prod 11 tests / 20 assertions exit 0; clj-kondo errors 0 exit 0. Negative control fired and was restored: deleting [re-frame.schemas.malli] from the facade ns-form reds the JVM suite 494 failures / 1 error exit 1, malli-hook-is-wired-by-requiring-the-facade among them. sectier-a's rf2-6r9j.55 had already landed as 35af375015 and had NOT moved anything this bead describes: the requires, both comment blocks and the soft-pass test were all exactly where the evidence said.

title: Clear ssr-ring's remaining proven no-op lint residue
description:
## Finding

A focused clj-kondo pass over all ssr-ring source and tests identifies seven small, mechanically proven residues beyond the separately owned dead var/argument: three unused imports, one unused destructured binding, and three no-op wrapper forms. None provides compatibility or test coverage; all can be removed without changing evaluated values.

## Evidence

`clj-kondo --lint implementation/ssr-ring/src implementation/ssr-ring/test --cache false` reports:

- `test/re_frame/ssr/ring/concurrency_stress_test.clj:89,91`: imported `IOException` and `TimeUnit` are never referenced. The test catches `Throwable`, and any time-unit usage is absent.
- `test/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming_robustness_test.clj:87`: imported base `OutputStream` is never referenced; concrete `PipedOutputStream` is used and prose mentions do not consume an import.
- `test/re_frame/ssr/ring_streaming_test.clj:29`: `db` is destructured but ignored by a fixture event that replaces the db with `{:articles arts}`.
- `src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj:45`: `(and debug? (and non-nil? non-string?))` contains a redundant nested `and`; flattening it is identical for these pure predicates.
- `test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:92`: `(str <string-literal>)` has one already-string argument.
- `test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:2619-2622`: `(or (second (re-find ...)))` has one arm and always returns that arm.

Every item is also confirmed by direct symbol/form search. The imported types and `db` binding have no read, and the one-argument/nested forms cannot select an alternate result. These are not the deliberate post-shell redirect backstop, retired-key rejection tests, or other documented compatibility defenses.

Duplicate searches for `ssr-ring unused imports clj-kondo`, `streaming robustness OutputStream import`, and `ring_test single arg or` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The unused imports/binding obscure which state and Java types the stress/robustness fixtures actually depend on. The no-op wrappers add false branching/coercion signals, and all seven findings add avoidable lint noise that makes substantive dead-code warnings easier to miss.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the three imports and unused `db` destructuring; flatten the nested `and`; remove the single-argument `str` and `or` wrappers. Keep test inputs, regex, catch breadth, database replacement semantics, debug gating, and warning behavior unchanged.

## Risks

Treat this as a mechanical cleanup. In particular, do not narrow the robustness test's `catch Throwable`, change the CR/LF hostile literal, merge/retain prior db state, or move the debug guard around trace payload construction.
acceptance_criteria:
- The three unused imports and unused `db` binding are absent; the relevant tests retain their existing behavior and assertions.
- The headers predicate is a single flat `and`, and the two test expressions no longer use one-argument `str`/`or`; evaluated values are unchanged.
- A focused clj-kondo run no longer reports these seven locations.
- Default ssr-ring tests pass, and the slow/stress aliases still discover the concurrency and streaming robustness namespaces.
- No deliberate compatibility/backstop branch or retired-key rejection coverage is removed as part of this cleanup.
close_reason: PR #9110. All seven residues re-verified from scratch rather than inherited, then removed: IOException + TimeUnit (concurrency_stress_test), bare OutputStream (streaming_robustness_test), the unread db destructure in ring_streaming_test, the nested and in headers.clj, and the single-arg str + single-arm or in ring_test. Retained because genuinely used: IOException in streaming_robustness_test at (catch IOException _ true), and InputStream/CountDownLatch/AtomicInteger/AtomicLong on the same import forms — clj-kondo flags exactly the unused entries and stays silent on the used ones, which is the control that fires. Word-boundary greps were needed because PipedOutputStream contains OutputStream. Unchanged as required: catch Throwable breadth, the regex, db-replacement semantics, the debug gate, the CR/LF hostile literal (byte-identical; only the (str ...) wrapper went) and the sibling two-arg (str "evil.com" (char 0) "nul"). pipeline.clj's separately-owned dead var + unused resp binding left alone. Gates: clj-kondo ssr-ring set diff = exactly the 7 target lines gone, nothing else changed (35 -> 28 lines); clojure -M:test = 231 tests, 1163 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0; -n concurrency-stress-test -n streaming-robustness-test loads + 7 tests green exit 0 (compile proof the imports were unreferenced, and proof the slow/stress namespaces still discover). headers.clj is the only production change so its gate was proven LIVE: inverting (some? header-value) to (nil? header-value) made pipeline_materialiser_test red (5 failures, exit 1); restored and verified by git hash-object against 7f8814a23b622662fef4d9f97f035b45b988ae1a, full suite re-run green.

title: Remove inert machine-timer rewrite from schemas fixture loader
description:
## Finding

The schemas conformance loader rewrites every bare auto-resolved keyword `::name` to `:rf.machine.timer/name`, even though no schema fixture contains such a token and the timer namespace belongs to the machines corpus. The code and its `clojure.string` dependency are an inert copy retained only "for symmetry"; if it ever activates on a future schemas fixture, it assigns an unrelated namespace rather than resolving that fixture's namespace.

## Evidence

- `load-fixture` in `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` (currently lines 146-156) slurps text, applies `str/replace` with `#"::([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)"` to `":rf.machine.timer/$1"`, then parses it.
- Its own docstring states that schemas fixtures do not use auto-resolved keywords, that the rewrite is for machines/SSR timer events, and that it is a no-op on this subset.
- The runner's exact selected corpus is five files: `error-schema-failure.edn` plus the four `schema-*.edn` fixtures. A controlled token census over those files returns zero `::name` matches, so `raw` and `fixed` are identical for every reachable input today.
- Applying the transform to a probe `::probe` yields `:rf.machine.timer/probe`, proving the claimed future robustness is not schema-generic; it silently invents a machines timer identity.
- The rewrite and commentary entered with the initial schemas runner in `54a3531931` and have never had a schemas-corpus consumer.
- All-status title/description searches for `auto-resolved`, `timer rewrite`, `rf.machine.timer`, and schemas conformance found no issue owning this residue. The one bead description mentioning `rf.machine.timer` concerns retired SSR skill guidance and is unrelated.

## Impact

Every current schemas fixture pays an unnecessary textual preprocessing step and the runner advertises support it does not implement correctly. A future schema fixture using `::foo` would not be rejected or resolved in its authoring namespace; it would be silently changed to a machine timer keyword, potentially making expectations pass or fail under a false identity.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the schemas-only auto-resolved-keyword rewrite, its now-unused `clojure.string` require if nothing else consumes it, and the copied timer-specific prose. Parse the original fixture text directly with `read-one-form`. If schema fixtures later need an alias/namespace facility, define it explicitly in the conformance format instead of borrowing a machines rewrite.

## Risks

Do not remove the analogous transform from machine/SSR/core runners without auditing their selected fixtures; this issue proves only that the schemas subset has zero consumers. Preserve exact-one-form throwing behavior and fixture filename diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
- `load-fixture` passes the original schemas fixture text directly to `read-one-form`; it contains no `:rf.machine.timer/$1` replacement or claim of auto-resolved-keyword support.
- `clojure.string` is removed from the schemas conformance namespace if the rewrite was its last use.
- The five selected schemas fixtures still parse and execute with unchanged IDs, capabilities, expectations, and results.
- A focused regression demonstrates that an injected bare `::probe` is not silently reclassified as `:rf.machine.timer/probe` (a parse failure is acceptable until the format defines such syntax).
- Schemas conformance and the full schemas JVM suite pass; machine, SSR, flows, and core fixture loaders are untouched by this slice-local cleanup.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). load-fixture now passes the fixture text to read-one-form verbatim; the ::name -> :rf.machine.timer/name rewrite and the copied timer prose are gone. A focused regression (loader-does-not-restamp-auto-resolved-keywords) pins that a bare ::probe never arrives as :rf.machine.timer/probe; it is live, verified by a negative control that restored the rewrite and turned both assertions red with actual :rf.machine.timer/probe, reproducing the exact silent restamping the bead describes. edn/read rejects ::probe outright (Invalid token), so the loader throws, which the bead permits. The five selected fixtures still load and execute unchanged (373 tests / 19223 assertions, exit 0). PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD: the conditional criterion 'remove clojure.string if the rewrite was its last use' does not fire — schema-fixture-file? still calls str/starts-with? and str/ends-with?, so clojure.string stays in the ns. Machine, SSR, flows and core fixture loaders untouched.

title: Delete unreachable schemas conformance load-error skip branch
description:
## Finding

`implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` retains a `(:fixture/load-error fixture)` skip branch even though its loader can no longer return that datum. The branch became unreachable when fixture parsing was changed to throw on every load failure.

## Evidence

- `read-one-form` (currently lines 118-144) throws for an empty fixture, malformed EDN, or more than one top-level form. Its docstring explicitly says it throws rather than returning `:fixture/load-error` because the runner classifies that shape as a skip.
- `load-fixture` (currently lines 146-156) has no catch and returns only the parsed EDN form; `all-schemas-fixtures` invokes it directly before entering the test result loop.
- Nevertheless `run-schemas-conformance-corpus` (currently lines 508-514) still tests `(:fixture/load-error fixture)` and appends a `{:skipped? true :reason "load error" ...}` result. No loader output reaches this arm. The skipped-summary fallback `(:error s)` exists only for this retired result shape.
- Commit `b6e26366a8` removed every loader catch and `{:fixture/load-error ...}` producer specifically because a parse failure must fail the suite rather than disappear as a skip, but it left this consumer branch behind. The follow-up PushbackReader implementation (`f2b899cc497`) preserves the throwing contract.
- All-status title/description searches for `fixture/load-error`, `load error`, and `schemas conformance` found no owning issue. Closed `rf2-98ni` owns the exactly-one-form loader fix; it does not remove this unreachable runner residue.

## Impact

The dead arm preserves and documents precisely the failure policy the loader migration retired: malformed fixtures represented as skips. It makes the runner harder to audit and invites a future loader change to reuse the stale shape, silently weakening the conformance gate. The extra `:error` summary fallback similarly suggests skipped parse failures remain supported.

## Proposed disposition

Delete the `:fixture/load-error` condition/result arm and its error-only skipped-summary rendering from the schemas conformance runner. Keep spec-version and out-of-capability skips intact. Load/parse errors must continue to escape before the result loop and fail the test process.

## Risks

Do not convert thrown fixture errors into ordinary failed or skipped corpus records. The security property of `rf2-98ni` is that malformed/trailing fixtures abort the gate. Preserve the non-empty runnable floor, capability filtering, and ordinary runtime `run-fixture` exception reporting.
acceptance_criteria:
- `rg -n ":fixture/load-error|reason +\"load error\"" implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_conformance_test.clj` finds only explanatory historical text if retained, and no executable branch/result construction.
- A malformed, empty, and two-form selected schemas fixture each makes the focused conformance invocation exit nonzero before results are summarized; none is counted as skipped.
- The five current selected fixtures still load and execute, and the runnable-floor assertions remain non-vacuous.
- Spec-version and unsupported-capability fixtures, when exercised, retain their current explicit skip behavior.
- The schemas JVM suite passes; a planted trailing-form negative control turns the focused gate red and restoring the fixture turns it green.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). Deleted the (:fixture/load-error fixture) cond arm and its skip-result construction from run-schemas-conformance-corpus, plus the (:error s) slot in the skipped-summary that existed only to render that retired shape. A comment in its place records why there is no such arm. Unreachability proven by execution probe, not census alone: a marker in the load-error arm fired 0 times while the same marker in the live :else arm fired 5, matching the five selected fixtures exactly. Negative control fired: a trailing form planted in schema-event-payload-validates.edn turned the focused run red with 1 ERROR and exit 1 ('must hold exactly ONE top-level EDN form'), counted as an error and NOT as a skip; the fixture was restored and verified identical by git hash-object (88cf0752). rg for :fixture/load-error and reason "load error" in the file now finds nothing. Spec-version and capability skips, the runnable-floor assertions (pos? and >= 4) and run-fixture's ordinary runtime exception reporting are untouched. Schemas JVM suite exit 0, 373 tests / 19223 assertions.

title: Remove the inert status-record source-of-truth constant
description:
## Finding

`status-defect-record-slots` is presented as the closed source of truth from which the production always-on status-defect record is built, but it has never been read. The emitted map is a separate literal and the test compares that literal's output only with its own separate expected set. The constant is inert and several comments/spec statements make a security assurance the implementation does not perform.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:62-88` defines private `status-defect-record-slots`; repository symbol search finds no executable reference. `clj-kondo` reports it as an unused private var.
- `report-non-integer-status!` at lines 90-139 directly constructs the seven-key map passed to `emit-always-on-error!`; it neither selects nor builds keys from the set.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/status_rewrite_always_on_test.clj:67-75` defines a separate `expected-record-slots`, while its assertion at lines 125-130 compares that set with the emitted record's keys. It never resolves or compares the production constant. Its claim that "the two are pinned equal" is therefore false: changing only `status-defect-record-slots` leaves every test green.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` calls the unused var the source of truth, and comments in the pipeline and core catalogue test repeat that characterization. The real behavioral authority is the emitted map plus the exact-key and forbidden-value tests.
- Commit `c2baf05dc4` introduced both the set and literal together and claimed the record was "BUILT FROM" the set, but the diff confirms no use existed even at introduction. Commit `ec6d07b834` added the test-side set without reading the production var.
- The private constant is not part of the façade or API manifest; the observable contract is the seven record keys catalogued in Spec 009.

Duplicate searches for `status defect record slots`, `status-defect-record-slots unused`, and `ssr ring status source of truth` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The dead var creates a lint warning and, more importantly, gives reviewers a false impression that a closed allow-list mechanically constrains egress. There are actually three manually synchronized spellings (dead constant, emitted map, test expectation), so the inert one can drift while the tests remain green and maintenance pays for a source-of-truth that has no authority.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `status-defect-record-slots`. Rewrite its surrounding pipeline/test/spec/core-test prose to state the actual enforcement: the production emit site constructs only the closed seven-key record, and the independent exact-key test plus explicit absence checks guard it. Preserve the emitted record and its privacy contract unchanged; do not add a post-hoc `select-keys` filter merely to make the obsolete constant appear useful.

## Risks

The emitted record is an off-box security boundary. Do not relax the exact key set, add the raw offending `:status`, remove the explicit forbidden-slot assertions, or change the dev-trace/always-on asymmetry. The disposition is removal of a false authority, not removal of the closed-record contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- The unused private `status-defect-record-slots` var is removed and focused clj-kondo no longer reports it.
- `report-non-integer-status!` still emits exactly `#{:error :frame :time :where :status-type :reason :recovery}` on the always-on axis, with raw `:status` confined to the development trace.
- The exact-key and forbidden-slot tests remain independent behavioral checks and still fail if a new production record key is added.
- Pipeline docstrings, `status_rewrite_always_on_test`, Spec 009, and the core catalogue test no longer claim that records are built from or tests compare against the removed constant.
- Production-disabled and development status-rewrite tests plus error-catalogue/channel conformance gates pass with unchanged wire status and record counts.

So the bead is right: the var is inert and three manually-synchronised spellings exist where the prose claims one authority.

WHY IT WAS NOT LANDED. Two reasons, either sufficient:

  1. THE ARTEFACT IS IN THE SSR FAMILY. implementation/ssr-ring/ was outside this dispatch's fence (implementation/ssr and implementation/ssr-node named explicitly, and this brief's own instruction was to STOP if the named artefact turned out to sit in a tree another worker holds - security, schemas, http, machines, ssr).

THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CANNOT BE MET WITHOUT A HOT-ZONE EDIT. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2126 is the statement that makes the false assurance normative - it names the var as 'the source of truth being re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline/status-defect-record-slots'. spec/009 is a hot-zone one-toucher file this dispatch was barred from editing. title: http source/tests: remove sixteen proven dead imports and bindings
description:
## Finding

The HTTP source/test slice retains sixteen statically proven dead imports, aliases, referred macros, or local destructurings after excluding reader-conditional and intentional load-time registrations.

## Evidence

A clean `clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false` plus exact-symbol searches identifies:

Production (4 findings):
- `reply.cljc:169`: explicitly destructured `origin-event` and `issuance` locals are unused; `:as ctx` is what `work-id` consumes, so the keys remain available without these local bindings.
- `transport.cljc:1248`: `request-id` is destructured in `maybe-retry!` but never referenced.
- `transport_jvm.cljc:40`: `java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture` is imported but never used or type-hinted in that adapter (the shared `transport.cljc` has its own live import/use).

Tests (12 findings):
- `http_jvm_headers_shape_test.clj:34`: unused `java.util.List` import.
- `http_managed_test.clj:18`: unused `re-frame.http.encoding` alias, plus unused `server` destructurings at lines 402, 426, 455, and 491 (`srv` is retained for teardown and `port` is the only key read).
- `http_privacy_integration_test.clj:20`: unused `re-frame.registrar` alias.
- `http_restore_quiesce_test.clj:28`: unused `re-frame.http.transport` alias; the namespace is already reached through the required `re-frame.http.managed` closure.
- `http_transport_security_test.clj:4,6`: unused `use-fixtures` refer and unused `re-frame.http.privacy` alias; transport already loads privacy.
- `http_url_percent_encoded_redaction_cljs_test.cljc:17-18`: unused `use-fixtures` refer on both CLJ and CLJS branches.

Exact searches find no symbol use in the owning files. History explains several leftovers (for example privacy integration/core registration tests and transport security changed while their old imports remained). Bead title/description searches for these imports and lint findings found no existing HTTP cleanup issue.

The audit deliberately excludes clj-kondo noise that is not dead: opposite-host adapter requires and `ctx`/`abort-signal` are reader-conditional; explicit `re-frame.http.managed` test requires trigger effect/hook registration; `with-new-frame [f ...]` establishes dynamic frame scope even where the local symbol is unread; test interleave and registry snapshots are documented diagnostics.

## Impact

These remnants imply dependencies/dataflow that do not exist and keep the HTTP lint baseline noisy, making a newly introduced unused binding easier to miss. The four stale server locals and duplicate imports also obscure what each test actually controls.

## Proposed disposition

Remove only the listed unused imports/requires/refers and narrow the listed destructuring forms. Do not mechanically delete load-bearing side-effect requires or cross-host bindings.

## Risks / retained contracts

Namespace requires can be intentional for load effects. For each removal, run the owning namespace in its normal and focused/isolated lane; if an alleged alias is proven load-bearing despite its transitive closure, retain it with a local comment explaining the effect. Preserve `:as ctx`, `srv`, frame macros, and platform reader branches.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The sixteen listed clj-kondo findings are removed, or any demonstrated load-bearing require is retained with an explicit side-effect comment and evidence.
2. `clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false` no longer reports these findings; opposite-host reader-conditional warnings are not “fixed” by breaking platform namespaces.
3. Focused HTTP JVM namespaces and the full HTTP JVM suite pass with unchanged test counts; consolidated CLJS tests pass, including the cross-host URL test.
4. Tests that rely on `re-frame.http.managed` registration, frame-scoping macros, transport adapter selection, and diagnostic seams retain those contracts.
5. No unrelated formatting, naming, or behavior change is bundled into the cleanup.
close_reason: PR #9115. Census RE-DERIVED from the current tree (post-PR #9081) rather than taken from the bead: all SIXTEEN listed findings were still present, only line numbers had moved (transport.cljc 1248 -> 1243), and #9081 had created no new orphan in this artefact. All sixteen removed. clj-kondo --lint implementation/http/src implementation/http/test --cache false went 50 -> 34 warnings, the diff being exactly those sixteen lines with no new finding surfaced. Each deletion proven with two instruments plus a firing control (exact git grep -F over tracked files + clj-kondo var-usage); the control earned its keep - a coarse grep -F 'rf/' read 59 hits in http_privacy_test.clj that are all the :rf/redacted KEYWORD, not an alias. Transitive closures verified rather than assumed: re-frame.http.transport reached via managed -> handlers -> transport (handlers.cljc:29), re-frame.http.privacy via that same transport require. The four server destructurings narrowed to {:keys [port] :as srv}, the form 27 sibling sites in the file already use. Dangling prose fixed rather than deleted: http_transport_security_test.clj:203 now reads re-frame.http.privacy/prepare-emit-tags. Gates: http JVM 506 tests/3882 assertions 0 failures exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11169 tests/55740 assertions exit 0. Gate proven LIVE - a planted assertion break in http_reply_lowering_test.clj reddened the JVM suite (exit 1, FAIL in work-id-head), restored and verified byte-identical by git hash-object cedc9166ab43. title: Remove unreachable walk-schema? branch from schemas validation
description:
## Finding

The private `run-validation` helper in `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc` still accepts a `walk-schema?` boolean and guards both schema sensitivity/opacity inspection and `:large?` inspection with it, but every surviving production caller passes the literal `true`. The false branch is unreachable residue from a retired validation topology.

## Evidence

- `run-validation` declares `[reg-meta value walk-schema? build-base-tags continue?]` (currently line 454).
- Its only reads are the guards around `walker/schema-has-sensitive?` / `schema-has-opaque-child?` (currently lines 544-546) and `walker/schema-has-large?` (currently lines 553-555).
- Repository caller census finds exactly three source calls: `validate-event!`, `validate-sub!`, and `validate-fx!` (currently lines 921, 957, and 1003). Each passes literal `true`; there is no dynamic caller and `run-validation` is private.
- History establishes why the knob existed and why it no longer does. Commit `f899bdd8e4` introduced it as `false` for event validation and `true` for cofx/fx/sub. Commit `14a91d956f` changed event validation to `true` so event payload schemas could drive fail-closed sensitive redaction. Injection-time cofx validation was subsequently retired (`99d37fa6bf`, `f56f5495e7`). The three remaining callers are therefore all on the walking arm.
- All-status bead title and description searches for `walk-schema`, `run-validation walk`, and the validate helper/path found no issue owning this residue.

## Impact

The parameter and two conditional branches advertise a per-surface privacy/size policy choice that no caller can make. That obscures the current invariant: every meta-bearing validation failure consults its schema for sensitivity, opaque children, and large-value elision. A future caller could accidentally pass false and bypass fail-closed diagnostic protection even though no supported contract needs that posture.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `walk-schema?` from the private helper's parameter vector and from all three calls. Make the existing sensitivity/opacity and large-schema walks unconditional within the already-failing branch, preserving sensitive-wins-over-large ordering and all existing redaction markers/tags.

## Risks

This is privacy-sensitive code. Do not move either walk onto the successful hot path, weaken opaque-schema fail-closed handling, change the whole-payload versus leaf-scoped decisions, or disturb the outer `interop/debug-enabled?` gates required for production DCE. Keep the edit mechanical and behavior-neutral for every reachable call.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run-validation` no longer declares or documents `walk-schema?`, and its three callers no longer pass a boolean in that slot.
- A source census shows no `walk-schema?` occurrence and exactly the same three private-helper callers.
- Event, fx, and sub-return tests prove sensitive schema slots and nested opaque children still redact failure payloads; non-sensitive failures remain verbatim.
- Large-schema tests prove non-sensitive values still use `:rf.size/large-elided`, while sensitivity continues to win over large classification.
- Schemas JVM and CLJS suites pass, including stale-incarnation checkpoints.
- The schemas production bundle/elision gate remains green and confirms the dev-only validation body is not newly retained under `:advanced` plus `goog.DEBUG=false`.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). Removed walk-schema? from run-validation's parameter vector and from all three callers (validate-event!/sub!/fx!), which each passed the literal true; both the sensitivity/opacity walk and the :large? walk are now unconditional inside the already-failing branch. Sensitive-wins-over-large ordering, fail-closed opaque handling, whole-payload decision scope, redaction markers and the outer interop/debug-enabled? gates are unchanged. Unreachability proven by execution probe, not census alone: a marker in the false direction fired 0 times across the schemas JVM suite while the same marker in the live true arm fired 50. The parameter bullet's substance was folded into the fn's opening prose rather than deleted. Schemas JVM suite exit 0 (373 tests / 19223 assertions); clj-kondo exit 0, errors 0, and identical findings on the HEAD and changed versions of the file. One walk-schema? token survives repo-wide: a dated past-tense comment at schemas_sensitive_test.clj:1118 recording the rf2-a5kzs fix, which is accurate history in a file rf2-6r9j.55 owns, deliberately left alone.

title: Remove the response argument superseded by the post-render flush
description:
## Finding

The non-streaming response builder still accepts and forwards a pre-render `resp` argument that no longer participates in response materialisation. Both the private implementation and its internal public wrapper preserve an obsolete arity from before the pipeline began re-reading the live accumulator after rendering.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:569-658` defines private `build-full-response*` as `[frame-id resp opts]`; its body never reads `resp`. `clj-kondo` reports `pipeline.clj:576:13: warning: unused binding resp`.
- The wrapper at lines 709-765 also accepts `resp`, but only forwards it to the private helper. Its catch arm derives the current response from `ssr/peek-response` through `project-render-throw->ring-response`; it does not need the argument.
- The sole production call at `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:325` passes the response obtained before rendering. Three focused tests call the private helper with a dummy `{:status 200}` (`resource_payload_projection_test.clj:178,230,306`); no other code call exists.
- History identifies the superseding change. Before commit `2a97334c07` (2026-06-05), `build-full-response*` materialised from `resp`. That fail-closed fix replaced the read with `post-render-resp = (ssr/flush-response! frame-id)` so render-time response effects and projected failures cannot be lost, but left both parameter vectors and every call argument intact. Commit `555038b12f` later strengthened that re-read to `flush-response-result!`; the old input remained irrelevant.
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline` is explicitly internal in the API-manifest generator. The façade API is `ssr-handler`; no API page or spec promises this helper's arity.

Duplicate searches for `ssr-ring unused resp build-full-response`, `build-full-response obsolete response argument`, and `post-render-resp unused parameter` found no owning bead.

## Impact

The argument falsely suggests the wire result may be based on a pre-render response snapshot, obscuring the load-bearing invariant that response status/headers/cookies and post-render error projection are re-read after the render walk. Test calls reinforce the obsolete model with meaningless dummy maps, and the binding leaves a permanent lint warning.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `resp` from `build-full-response*`, `build-full-response`, the façade call, and the three direct private-helper tests. Preserve the pre-render `response` binding in `ssr-handler`, because redirect and projected-5xx branches still consume it before the happy-path builder.

## Risks

Do not replace the post-render flush with the caller snapshot or move it earlier. Render-time `:rf.server/*` effects, recovered-to-nil sub failures, projected 5xx diversion, and render-throw response materialisation must continue to use the live per-frame accumulator.
acceptance_criteria:
- `build-full-response*` and `build-full-response` accept only `frame-id` and `opts`; their production and test callers pass no dummy response map.
- The `ssr-handler` drain result still feeds redirect and projected-5xx branches, while the happy path calls the updated builder arity.
- `build-full-response*` still calls `flush-response-result!` after body/head/payload/shell work and materialises from `post-render-resp`; no behavior is changed to use a stale pre-render snapshot.
- Focused clj-kondo no longer reports the unused `resp` binding.
- ssr-ring tests pass, especially render-time sub fail-closed, drain-time projection, response headers/cookies accumulated during render, resource payload projection, and renderer-seam coverage.
notes: 2026-09-03 (httpvest-b worker, PR #9115 session) — NOT STARTED, premise mismatch in the dispatch, not in the bead. This bead was dispatched to me in a bundle briefed as 'all in implementation/http', with a fence that explicitly excluded implementation/ssr-ring because another worker holds it. Every file this bead names is in ssr-ring: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj (build-full-response* at 578, build-full-response at 724, the forwarding call at 771), implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:325 (the sole production call), and implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/resource_payload_projection_test.clj:178,230,306 (the three dummy {:status 200} calls). Verified by git grep -F 'build-full-response' over tracked files: zero hits under implementation/http. NOTHING was done on this bead and no ssr-ring file was touched by PR #9115. The bead's own evidence and disposition still look sound on inspection — the dataflow claim was NOT disproved, merely not tested, because proving it requires reading and running ssr-ring, which was out of fence. Re-dispatch to whoever holds implementation/ssr-ring. Note for that worker: the .46 sibling in this bundle also names a JVM/CLJS gate pair, but the gate for this one is the ssr-ring suite, and the acceptance criteria call out render-time sub fail-closed, drain-time projection, response headers/cookies accumulated during render, resource payload projection and renderer-seam coverage specifically.
close_reason: PR #9162: build-full-response*/build-full-response drop the pre-render resp argument superseded by the post-render flush (2a97334c07, strengthened by 555038b12f). Body never read it; wrapper only forwarded it. ssr-handler keeps its pre-render response binding, still consumed by the redirect and projected-5xx branches. Three focused tests stop passing a dummy {:status 200}. ssr-ring suite exit 0 (231 tests/1163 assertions); reinstating the 3-arity call reds it with ArityException. Bead line numbers had drifted (588 not 569) because the :renderer seam landed in between; the dataflow claim held exactly.

title: http reply: remove the never-consumed duplicate transport-request-id helper
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id` is a never-consumed duplicate constructor for `[:rf.req frame-id work-id]`. The only shipped producer of that token is the Resources work-ledger’s separate `managed-request-id` implementation.

## Evidence

- Fixed-string and resolved-var searches across implementation, tools, examples, skills, docs, and specs find no production call to `http-reply/transport-request-id` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/reply.cljc:99-107`). Its only calls are shape assertions in `http_reply_lowering_test.clj:138-140` and `http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:38-40`; the remaining hit is its own namespace prose.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc:148-169` defines the byte-for-byte equivalent `managed-request-id` and is the actual runtime authority. Resources transport/teardown code and multiple Resources tests use that function to issue, supersede, and abort managed HTTP work.
- History makes the duplication explicit: Resources added `managed-request-id` in `450cdd44a1` at 11:53 on 2026-06-11. HTTP added the identical helper later that day in `b6789084b2` while introducing reply lowering, but no runtime call edge was ever added; `git log -S` shows creation only.
- The HTTP artifact accepts a caller-chosen `:request-id` and does not itself know when a caller needs frame qualification. The frame-local Resources owner is therefore the layer that has both identities and constructs the transport token.
- The helper is absent from the generated API manifest and HTTP user facade/docs. Specs require the token shape, not this unused constructor. Exact-symbol, title, description, and broader transport-correlation bead searches found no existing issue.

## Impact

Two implementations claim authority for a security-relevant process-global correlation identity, while HTTP’s copy has no consumer. Its focused tests can stay green if the real Resources constructor or lowering path changes, overstating coverage and inviting tuple-shape drift.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id`, its two direct shape assertions, and the namespace sentence claiming it builds the identity. Keep the canonical token shape documented and tested through the live `re-frame.resources.work-ledger/managed-request-id` path. Do not add an HTTP -> Resources dependency. If a second production owner emerges, extract one genuinely shared lower-layer constructor rather than retaining parallel copies.

## Risks / retained contracts

The var is public at the namespace level but is unmanifested and has never had an in-repo production caller, so an unknown downstream direct-require is the only compatibility risk. Preserve `http-reply/work-id` and all reply correlation behavior; this finding concerns only the unused frame-qualification helper, not the `:request-id` accepted by managed HTTP.
acceptance_criteria:
1. HTTP reply code no longer ships an unconsumed duplicate `transport-request-id`, or a concrete production caller and ownership rationale is added.
2. The `[:rf.req frame-id work-id]` contract remains implemented once on the live Resources lowering/teardown path (or in a truly shared dependency-safe owner) and is covered on JVM/CLJS as applicable.
3. HTTP reply-lowering tests continue to cover HTTP work IDs and canonical replies without asserting a helper the runtime never invokes.
4. Resources managed-HTTP issuance, cross-frame isolation, supersession, and opportunistic-abort tests pass; HTTP JVM/CLJS suites pass.
5. Repo-wide searches show no stale HTTP helper/doc reference and no new HTTP -> Resources dependency cycle.
close_reason: PR #9115. Removed re-frame.http.reply/transport-request-id, its two shape assertions (http_reply_lowering_test.clj:138-140, http_reply_lowering_cljs_test.cljc:38-40) and the namespace sentence claiming it builds the identity. Proven unconsumed with two instruments plus firing controls: repo-wide git grep -F over tracked files returned only its own defn, its own prose and the two test assertions (control 'success-reply' hit 24 files); clj-kondo var-usage analysis over implementation/ returned 3 usage records, all test namespaces, 0 from src (controls: success-reply 21, work-id 33). Surviving original named and verified equivalent: re-frame.resources.work-ledger/managed-request-id at work_ledger.cljc:148, identical body [frame-id work-id] -> [:rf.req frame-id work-id], with four production callers (resources/events.cljc 653/977/1149, resources/mutation_events.cljc 1271). Namespace prose now names that constructor so the token shape stays documented; no HTTP -> Resources dependency added. CLJS deftest work-id-and-transport-id renamed work-id-head (no other reference existed). Gates: http JVM 506 tests/3882 assertions exit 0; npm run test:cljs 11169 tests/55740 assertions exit 0.

title: Stop retaining the unused streaming root Hiccup tree
description:
## Finding

`render-streaming-shell!` returns the fully resolved root tree in `rendered[:hiccup]`, but the streaming writer no longer reads that field. The detached writer receives a map that can retain an arbitrarily large Hiccup tree for the lifetime of the stream even though every live operation uses `:shell-html`, `:doc-hash`, and (when continuations exist) a fresh post-drain root resolution.

## Evidence

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:123-210` documents and returns `:hiccup hiccup`.
- The sole production consumer, `run-streaming-writer!` at lines 270-404, destructures `head-html`, attribute bags, `doc-hash`, `head-hash`, `shell-html`, and `continuations`; it never reads `:hiccup`.
- Final payload hashing at lines 383-399 either re-resolves `root-view` after a continuation drain or reuses `doc-hash`; the carried tree participates in neither arm.
- A repository search finds no read of this result key. The only other ssr-ring occurrences are three hand-built writer-test maps (`streaming_writer_trace_test.clj:83,332` and `streaming_robustness_test.clj:207`), where it is an ignored extra key.
- History proves the disconnect: commit `375fc36ec2` introduced the field for the writer's final-hash computation. Commit `185c149a53` stopped destructuring it when hashing moved to `doc-hash`; later commit `80d28623a4` moved continuation-sensitive final hashing to a fresh `root-view` resolution. Old comments retained it "for diagnostics", but no diagnostic path ever consumes it, and the current docstring still incorrectly says it is "for the final-hash".
- `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming` is explicitly on the API-manifest generator's internal-namespace roster (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj`); the public façade, API docs, specs, examples, and Node crossing expose `stream-handler`, not this intermediate result shape.

Duplicate searches for `render-streaming-shell hiccup final hash`, `streaming hiccup rendered map`, and `ssr-ring hiccup retention` found no owning bead.

## Impact

Every streamed request retains both rendered HTML and the original in-memory tree across the daemon writer, with the worst retention on slow clients or long continuation drains. The stale field and docstring also suggest final-hash logic depends on a pre-drain tree when the correctness fix deliberately made it post-drain-sensitive.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `:hiccup` from the internal rendered map and its result-shape docstring, and remove the three ignored fixture keys. Keep the local `hiccup` binding: it remains required to build `doc-hash` and `shell-html`. Do not change root resolution count or hash timing.

## Risks

The common no-continuation path must still resolve a fn-form root exactly once and reuse `doc-hash`; continuation requests must still re-resolve after draining. This cleanup must not move shell rendering onto the writer thread, alter failure projection, or expose a new public result contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- `render-streaming-shell!` no longer returns or documents a `:hiccup` field, and writer-test fixtures do not carry the ignored key.
- The local resolved tree remains used to compute `doc-hash` and call `streaming/render-shell`; shell bytes are unchanged.
- `run-streaming-writer!` still uses `doc-hash` when no continuation exists and a fresh post-drain `root-view` resolution when continuations exist.
- Streaming tests pass, including exact-once root resolution, post-drain hash/state parity, writer trace/failure, and nested continuation ordering coverage.
- A repo-wide search within ssr-ring finds no stale claim that the carried Hiccup tree drives the final hash.
close_reason:
Confirmed and fixed in PR #9081. NOTE FOR THE EPIC: this bead's subject is implementation/ssr-ring/, not implementation/http/ — it was dispatched clustered with three http beads as one artefact, and only the other three are http.

WHAT HELD THE TREE ALIVE, established before the fix. stream-rendered-response builds the daemon writer as an anonymous fn closing over the WHOLE rendered map and hands that closure to a Thread. The holder is the closure FIELD, not a stack local, so Clojure's locals-clearing never reaches it, and the thread lives until the stream drains — bounded by the client's read rate through a 16 KiB PipedInputStream, so a slow-loris client extends it arbitrarily. Chain: live Thread -> closure field -> rendered -> :hiccup -> the whole resolved root tree, retained alongside the rendered HTML for the request's lifetime. That is the bead's stated impact, confirmed.

THAT THE WRITER NEVER READS IT. run-streaming-writer! destructures exactly seven keys (head-html, html-attrs, body-attrs, doc-hash, head-hash, shell-html, continuations); :hiccup is not among them. The symbol rendered occurs at only three executable sites in streaming.clj — created at the handler, passed to stream-rendered-response, destructured once in the writer — with no (:hiccup rendered), no get, and no other key access (the reduced? check only derefs). Two-instrument census over git-tracked ssr-ring files, line-oriented and whitespace-flattened AGREEING: :hiccup at exactly 5 sites — streaming.clj:128 (docstring row) and :201 (map construction), plus the three ignored writer-test fixture keys the bead named (streaming_robustness_test.clj:207, streaming_writer_trace_test.clj:83 and :332). Every line number in the bead re-derived and correct. CONTROL needle shell-html fired at 22 line-oriented / 23 flattened.

MEASURED. A WeakReference harness reproducing the exact shape — a parked thread holding a closure over the map, the tree scoped out of the constructing frame so the map is the only holder, identical GC pressure both runs — reads tree-retained-by-live-writer? true WITH the field and false WITHOUT it. The field is the only difference between the runs. Two earlier harness shapes were discarded as inconclusive rather than reported: the first held the tree in a live local of the GC frame (both runs read retained), the second let locals-clearing drop the map after its destructure (both read collectable). Sample tree serialises to 106,986 pr-str chars; real magnitude is page size, unbounded.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: :hiccup gone from the returned map and from the result-shape docstring row (which still claimed 'for the final-hash'); the three ignored fixture keys gone. The local hiccup binding KEPT — it still builds doc-hash and feeds streaming/render-shell. Root-resolution count and hash timing untouched: the no-continuation path still reuses doc-hash and the continuation path still re-resolves post-drain. AC5: no stale claim that the carried tree drives the final hash survives in ssr-ring.

GATES: ssr-ring clojure -M:test 231 tests / 1163 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0 — identical to the pre-change baseline, and re-run green on the rebased final base. clj-kondo --cache false over ssr-ring src+test: 0 errors / 31 warnings, identical to its merge base.

title: http privacy-body: remove the orphaned direct-projector helper layer
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.privacy-body` ships a test-only direct-projection layer that is disconnected from the actual off-box path: `off-box-classify-body` plus `off-box-body-marker`. The same namespace also exposes `whole-body-sensitive-mark?`, a zero-production-consumer predicate duplicating behavior already exercised through `classify-decoded`.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide resolved-var analysis and fixed-string searches find zero production calls to `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` (`privacy_body.cljc:219`), `off-box-classify-body` (`:309`), or `off-box-body-marker` (`:237`). Their only executable consumers are focused assertions in `http_privacy_body_test.clj:102-108,182-224`; remaining hits are self-docstrings/comments.
- The shipped off-box path is different. HTTP emit sites call `off-box-body-disposition` and stamp `:rf.http/off-box-body` on trace tags (`transport.cljc:435,768` and other raw-failure paths). `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1430-1512` reads that stamp and applies its own `omit-off-box-http-bodies` projection; it cannot call the HTTP helper because Epoch deliberately has no HTTP-artifact dependency.
- The real projector is extensively covered in `epoch_egress_trace_events_test.clj` and `epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`; HTTP integration tests cover the emit-side `:omit` / `:classify` stamps. Removing the disconnected helper tests does not remove runtime-path coverage.
- Current privacy-body namespace prose and `off-box-body-disposition` docs incorrectly claim Epoch “applies” `off-box-classify-body`. The integration-test comment around `http_privacy_integration_test.clj:551-556` similarly treats its unit test as part of the end-to-end path, although no call edge exists.
- `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` only asks whether `(decode-schema-marks decode)` contains root path `[]`. The neighboring `whole-body-root-sensitive-redacts-everything` test already proves the product behavior through `classify-decoded`; the standalone predicate is neither used to decide runtime policy nor listed in the API manifest.
- History confirms these were never connected: `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` arrived in `59bffbceaf`; `off-box-classify-body`/marker arrived in `39dcc2c889`, while that same commit implemented the actual stamp/Epoch projector split. Subsequent history added no production consumer. Bead searches by all three exact symbols and off-box/body terms found no existing issue.

## Impact

The orphaned layer adds public vars and tests for code the product never executes, duplicates the Epoch projector semantics in a package that cannot be its authority, and leaves architecture documentation claiming a nonexistent call path. Future security fixes could update the helper, turn its tests green, and still leave the real off-box projector unchanged.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `off-box-classify-body`, `off-box-body-marker`, and `whole-body-sensitive-mark?` plus only their direct self-tests. Correct namespace/doc/test comments to describe the real stamp -> Epoch enforcement path. Preserve `off-box-body-disposition`, `introspectable-schema-decode?`, `decode-schema-marks`, `classify-decoded`, all emit-side stamping, and the Epoch projector/tests.

## Risks / retained contracts

The vars are public at the namespace level but are absent from the generated API manifest and user API docs; an unknown downstream direct-require remains possible. Do not weaken fail-closed behavior or remove tests that exercise the actual projector. Keep schema root-mark behavior covered through `classify-decoded` and keep opaque schemas classified `:omit` by the live disposition function.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The three zero-production-consumer vars and their direct self-tests are removed, or a real shipped consumer is added and the documented call path is made true.
2. Privacy-body and integration-test prose names `off-box-body-disposition` stamping plus Epoch `omit-off-box-http-bodies` as the actual off-box path; it does not claim Epoch calls an HTTP direct projector.
3. Root sensitive and large marks remain tested through `classify-decoded`; introspectable schemas still stamp `:classify`, and unschematized/opaque decodes still stamp `:omit`.
4. Existing Epoch JVM/CLJS off-box projection tests and HTTP privacy JVM/CLJS tests pass, including raw 4xx/5xx/decode-failure and retry-body fail-closed cases.
5. Repo-wide searches show no stale reference to the removed helper/marker names and the API manifest remains unchanged unless compatibility policy explicitly promotes a retained API.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9081. This is PRIVACY code, so the disposition was gated on two questions answered before anything was deleted.

ONE — DOES THE LIVE OFF-BOX PATH DEPEND ON IT? No, and it never could have. The shipped path is: the emit site applies classify-decoded ON-BOX (transport.cljc:401 for :rf.http/replied's :value, :868 for :rf.http/accept-failure's :decoded, :1466) and stamps off-box-body-disposition forward under :rf.http/off-box-body (transport.cljc:435, :768); re-frame.epoch.tool-pair's omit-off-box-http-bodies then reads that stamp and substitutes :rf/redacted at the operation's body-slot paths for an :omit event, passing a :classify event through because its per-slot marks were already applied on-box. Epoch deliberately carries no HTTP-artefact dependency, so it could not call off-box-classify-body even in principle — the bead's claim that the documented call path does not exist is correct.

TWO — IS ANY PRIVACY GUARANTEE DROPPED? No: the live composition is EXACTLY the removed function on both arms. Introspectable schema -> classify-decoded applied on-box, stamp :classify, Epoch passes through = off-box-classify-body's first arm. Anything else — unschematized, opaque keyword registry ref, compiled schema object — -> classify-decoded is an identity or mark-less no-op, but the stamp is :omit and Epoch substitutes :rf/redacted, the SAME sentinel off-box-body-marker held = its second arm. The fail-closed property for an opaque ref (rf2-y1pgdl) comes from the stamp gating on introspectable-schema-decode?, not from the removed helper, so it is untouched.

AND NO DELETED TEST WAS THE SOLE ASSERTION OF AN INVARIANT. Each removed row has a live counterpart on the shipped path, checked one by one: unschematized omission and opaque-registry-ref / compiled-schema omission are asserted through off-box-body-disposition returning :omit (off-box-disposition-omits-* rows, kept), and schema classification through the classify-decoded per-slot rows (kept). For whole-body-sensitive-mark? the deftest whole-body-root-sensitive-redacts-everything asserted BOTH the predicate and the PRODUCT behaviour; only the predicate's own call was dropped and the (= :rf/redacted (classify-decoded ...)) assertion beside it was KEPT (AC3). Nothing that exercises the actual projector was touched.

CENSUS. Two instruments over git-tracked files with .beads excluded, line-oriented and whitespace-flattened, AGREEING exactly: off-box-classify-body 20/20, whole-body-sensitive-mark? 4/4, off-box-body-marker 5/5 — all confined to privacy_body.cljc's own definitions and docstrings plus their own test file (and one prose mention in http_privacy_integration_test.clj). ZERO production consumers, and zero references in spec/, docs/, tools/ or examples/, so no spec change was needed (AC5). CONTROL needle off-box-body-disposition fired at 17/17 across five files INCLUDING transport.cljc and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md — a live control, not a zero.
