title: http privacy: retire inert origin-event and frame-opts compatibility arguments
description:
## Finding

The HTTP privacy orchestrator retains three compatibility inputs after both of the features they carried were removed: `request-sensitive?` still accepts an origin event it ignores, and `prepare-emit-tags` / `prepare-emit-failure` still accept an opts map whose frame is ignored.

## Evidence

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/privacy.cljc:421-437` defines `[args-map _origin-event]`; the body reads only the two per-call flags in `args-map`. Commit `dd7c1f0df5` removed handler-registration `:sensitive?`, deleted `handler-sensitive?`, and changed the parameter to `_origin-event`, explicitly stating that origin metadata is no longer consulted.
- All production callers still manufacture/pass that retired provenance: `handlers.cljc:227,333,363`, `test_support.cljc:93`, and `privacy.cljc:465` (nil). Unit tests at `http_privacy_test.clj:165-206` also pass differing origin values only to prove they do nothing.
- `privacy.cljc:477-546` defines two/three-arity `prepare-emit-tags` and `prepare-emit-failure`; both three-arity bodies bind `_opts` and never read it. Their docs explicitly say the third argument is “kept for call-site compatibility”.
- Commit `e4c9b11341` moved carrier lookup from frame policy to process-global `:rf.http/managed` registration metadata. The composers now call `managed-carriers` with no frame. Eleven source call sites across `middleware.cljc`, `registry.cljc`, `transport.cljc`, `transport_cljs.cljc`, and `transport_jvm.cljc` nevertheless still build/pass `{:frame ...}`; several adjacent comments describe that frame as attribution even though the composer cannot use it.
- The generated API manifest exposes only the `re-frame.http` verb facade; none of these orchestrator helpers is a manifested user API. Spec 014 names the operations conceptually but does not promise these obsolete arities. Repo-wide consumer and bead searches found no external-in-repo caller or existing issue requiring compatibility.

## Impact

The signatures and call sites carry false dataflow: readers can reasonably conclude handler provenance or frame identity influences redaction when neither can. Every emit site allocates a throwaway frame map, and future privacy work could mistakenly rely on values the callee discards.

## Proposed disposition

Use the current contracts directly: make `request-sensitive?` a one-argument function and make both composers canonical two-argument functions. Update every caller, focused test, docstring, and stale frame-attribution comment. Do not change carrier lookup or sensitivity semantics.

## Risks / retained contracts

These vars are public Clojure vars despite being artefact-internal and unmanifested, so an unpublished downstream direct-require could depend on the old arities. Confirm the project’s pre-release compatibility posture; if an arity must be retained, document it as an intentional public contract instead of leaving anonymous `_...` compatibility. Preserve handler-metadata non-participation and process-global carrier resolution.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `request-sensitive?` has one canonical input and all callers/tests stop passing origin-event solely for retired handler metadata.
2. `prepare-emit-tags` and `prepare-emit-failure` have canonical two-argument call paths; no source caller constructs an inert `{:frame ...}` opts map for them.
3. Privacy docs/comments state that sensitivity is per-call and carriers come from the process-global `:rf.http/managed` registration, without implying these composers consult frame attribution.
4. Existing request-privacy, carrier-extension, middleware-failure, abort, retry, and JVM/CLJS warning tests preserve redaction and stamping behavior.
5. HTTP JVM and consolidated CLJS suites pass, and source lint reports no compatibility placeholder introduced by this cleanup.
notes: Audit of PR #9081: acceptance criterion 3 remains unmet in implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/handlers.cljc. The comment beside check-cljs-only-keys! still says "The frame is threaded for the warning-path trace stamp", but this PR removed the frame argument and the live call now passes only args-map and sensitive?. Remove or correct that false dataflow sentence; behavior is otherwise sound.
close_reason: PR #9109 (b4238a79c5). Satisfies the PR #9081 audit ruling exactly and only: acceptance criterion 3 was unmet because handlers.cljc still carried 'The frame is threaded for the warning-path trace stamp' beside check-cljs-only-keys!, while #9081 had removed the frame argument and the live call passes only args-map' and sensitive?'. That false dataflow sentence is corrected in place; the true half (HTTP carrier redaction is process-global, resolved from the :rf.http/managed :carriers registration per EP-0025) is kept. No code change, as the audit directed. HTTP JVM suite 506 tests / 3884 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors; clj-kondo over implementation/http/src has findings byte-identical to the pre-change baseline. Noted and deliberately NOT changed: transport_jvm.cljc's emit-cljs-only-skipped! comment says 'The frame supplies general trace attribution and elision' - that describes the AMBIENT frame trace/emit! resolves, not a threaded argument, so it is not the false-dataflow class the audit named.

title: http decode: remove the unreachable raw-body fallback
description:
## Finding

`re-frame.http.decode/decode-response-body` ends with a raw `body-text` fallback that is unreachable under the decoder normalization immediately above it.

## Evidence

- In `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/decode.cljc:248-340`, `requested-decode` maps a nil `:decode` to `:auto`, preserves `:auto`, and otherwise preserves the supplied value. It therefore cannot be nil.
- `resolved` maps `:auto` through `sniff-decoder`; `sniff-decoder` has an exhaustive `cond` returning exactly `:json`, `:text`, or `:blob`. For every non-`:auto` input, `resolved` is the already-non-nil `requested-decode`. Thus `resolved` cannot be nil.
- The main `cond` first handles a decoder fn, JSON, text, and the binary modes. Its next predicate is `(some? resolved)`, which is necessarily true for every remaining input. The final `:else body-text` at lines 339-340 has no possible input.
- History shows this shape arrived with the decode extraction (`c8f80850c9`) and survived the later strict malformed-JSON correction (`5abbf20977`). The live schema/unknown-decoder arm deliberately parses JSON and propagates parse failure; the dead tail is not the earlier malformed-JSON fallback fixed by that commit.
- Repository and bead searches for the symbol, decoder normalization, decode fallback, and HTTP decode found no issue covering this unreachable branch.

## Impact

The dead tail falsely suggests a nil/unknown decoder can bypass schema/JSON handling and return raw text. That makes security-sensitive malformed-JSON reasoning harder and creates a branch no test can honestly exercise.

## Proposed disposition

Make the schema/unknown-decoder arm the final `:else` and remove the unreachable trailing fallback. Keep the binary arm's separate synthetic-context `body-binary` -> `body-text` fallback intact.

## Risks / retained contracts

This is intended to be behavior-neutral. Preserve nil/omitted `:decode` as `:auto`, custom decoder raw-text ownership, unknown non-mode values as schema candidates, strict malformed-JSON propagation, and binary response behavior on both hosts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `decode-response-body` has no trailing branch that requires `resolved` to be nil; the schema/unknown-decoder path is structurally exhaustive.
2. Omitted/nil and explicit `:auto`, `:json`, `:text`, all binary modes, custom fns, valid Malli schemas, invalid schemas, unknown keyword refs, malformed JSON, and empty-body parity retain their current results/errors.
3. The JVM HTTP decode suite and consolidated CLJS HTTP tests pass.
4. A source search and/or focused branch proof confirms there is no unreachable raw-body fallback, while the intentional binary synthetic-context fallback remains.
close_reason:
Confirmed and removed in PR #9081. The premise held exactly, and was proved two independent ways rather than by reading alone.

BY CONTROL FLOW. requested-decode maps nil :decode to :auto, preserves :auto, and otherwise preserves the supplied value, so it is never nil. resolved then maps :auto through sniff-decoder — an exhaustive cond returning exactly :json, :text or :blob — and otherwise IS requested-decode. So resolved is never nil. The main cond's penultimate predicate (some? resolved) was therefore true for everything that reached it, and the trailing :else body-text required resolved to be nil. Unreachable. One edge worth recording because it is the arm where a naive reading goes wrong: a :decode of FALSE also reaches the schema arm, not the fallback — some? is (not (nil? x)), so false passes it.

BY PROBE, WITH A CONTROL THAT FIRED. A side-effecting probe was planted in the fallback — a marker file rather than a throw, since a throw is caught by the transport's decode try/catch and classified as :rf.http/decode-failure, which could have been swallowed into a passing test. Across the whole 514-test suite the marker was ABSENT: the branch was never entered. The SAME probe mechanism planted in the live (= :text resolved) arm produced the marker with 2 hits. Zero versus two, same suite, same run shape, so the instrument works and the fallback is genuinely dead. (A first plant attempt was paren-unbalanced and failed to read the file — treated as NO VERDICT and redone, not interpreted.) Both plants restored and verified by git blob hash against the committed object, not by reading a diff.

DISPOSITION AS ORDERED: the schema/unknown-decoder arm is now the final :else and the trailing fallback is gone, so the cond is structurally exhaustive with no branch requiring a nil resolved (AC1, AC4). The binary arm's separate synthetic-context body-binary -> body-text fallback is INTACT — that one is deliberate and fires for a test ctx that populated only :body-text (AC2, retained contract).

Behaviour-neutral as intended: http clojure -M:test 506 tests / 3884 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0, with the empty-body-parity, binary-decode, malformed-JSON and schema decode rows all still green (AC2, AC3). The consolidated CLJS bundle — where a cross-host decode divergence would surface — ran 11209 tests / 55849 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0.

ONE PREMISE CORRECTION, cosmetic but worth the record: the bead cites the symbol as util-json/json-parse at decode.cljc:248-340. Main renamed that alias to http-json between filing and landing (commit f148f863c2), which is what the rebase conflicted on; resolved by keeping BOTH intents — main's rename and this removal.

title: Remove three dead imports and bindings from the UIx test slice
description:
## Scope

Remove three mechanically dead bindings in the UIx adapter's test and smoke-testbed slice. No runtime API, event behavior, fixture shape, dependency recipe, or test intent changes.

## Vestigial finding

The UIx tree carries one unused namespace require and two event-handler destructures whose db values are never read:

1. implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj:29 requires clojure.string as str, but the file never refers to str.
2. implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:683 destructures db in the ::dollar-shape-seed handler, then replaces :db with a literal map without reading the old value.
3. implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:20 destructures db in :counter/init, then replaces :db with the literal initial counter without reading the old value.

## Evidence

A read-only clj-kondo pass over implementation/adapters/uix/{src,test,testbed} reports exactly these as unused-namespace/unused-binding findings:

- uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj:29, namespace clojure.string is required but never used;
- uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:683, unused binding db;
- adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:20, unused binding db.

Manual repository-wide/source inspection confirms no str-qualified call in the recipe test and no read of either destructured db before the literal replacement. The other linter warnings in this pass are unresolved cross-namespace CLJS vars caused by the standalone analysis classpath/macros and are deliberately excluded from this bead.

## Impact

These names imply dependencies on string helpers and prior database state that do not exist. That adds noise to a dependency-governance test and to the minimal adapter smoke whose source explicitly says not to grow it. It also prevents a focused unused-binding lint pass from being clean.

## Recommended disposition

Delete the clojure.string alias and name the unused event-handler parameters as intentionally ignored (or otherwise avoid destructuring them), keeping the event results byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Risks

Very low. The only risk is accidentally changing the literal seed maps or handler arity while cleaning the argument names; focused tests and smoke compile/runtime behavior cover that.
acceptance_criteria:
- Remove [clojure.string :as str] from uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj; no string helper is introduced as a substitute.
- The ::dollar-shape-seed and :counter/init handlers no longer bind db they do not read, while preserving their two-argument event-handler shape and exact returned :db maps.
- A focused clj-kondo pass reports no unused-namespace or unused-binding finding under implementation/adapters/uix/{src,test,testbed}. Do not broaden this task to unrelated unresolved-var diagnostics from standalone CLJS analysis.
- The UIx consumer dependency recipe JVM test, affected UIx browser test, and adapter-testbed smoke/compile remain green.
- No public API, dependency coordinate, initial counter value, frame behavior, or test assertion changes.
close_reason: PR #9110. Removed [clojure.string :as str] from uix_consumer_deps_recipe_test.clj (no str/-qualified call in the file; every bare str is clojure.core/str, which the alias never shadowed) and the unread db destructures in ::dollar-shape-seed and :counter/init, both keeping their two-arg shape and returning identical :db maps. Proof: git grep -F census (control: str/ reads 0 in the target, 3 in a sibling in the same directory) + clj-kondo. clj-kondo over adapters/uix/{src,test,testbed} went 3 findings/exit 2 -> 0 findings/exit 0. implementation/adapters/uix clojure -M:test: 4 tests, 34 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, exit 0 (the recipe test is 3 of those 4, so the gate is live on the edited file).

title: Remove UIx's no-doc direct warn-cache reset export
description:
## Scope

Remove only the undocumented direct UIx namespace export re-frame.adapter.uix/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! and the tests/configuration that keep that export alive. Preserve the spine's private clear thunk, its registration in the canonical :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! chain, the warn-once cache itself, and fixture isolation. Reconcile the UIx public-surface guard with the actual supported UIx API while touching that stale roster.

## Vestigial finding

The UIx adapter exposes a ^:no-doc cache-reset Var that has no caller outside its own legacy shared-suite configuration. The reset behavior was superseded by the canonical chained reset hook, which the standard fixture and governance tests already drive. The namespace export is therefore a second, unsupported door to an internal test seam.

## Evidence and reachability proof

- implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:192-197 defines ^:no-doc clear-warned-non-dom-roots! as a direct alias of the spine thunk.
- A repository-wide exact search for uix-adapter/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! finds only implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:75 and :88. There are no production, documentation, example, skill, tool, or other test consumers.
- spec/api-manifest.edn:59-67 enumerates the supported UIx namespace as adapter plus eight functions and deliberately omits this ^:no-doc Var. The generated API docs and Spec 006 likewise omit it.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3405-3410 consumes the underlying (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! spine-fns) directly and registers it through install-clear-warn-once-step!, independent of the UIx namespace alias.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:450-472 makes :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! a post-dispose reset hook; all UIx tests using make-reset-runtime-fixture therefore reach the canonical chain without calling the namespace Var.
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:1219-1240 already proves the chain re-arms the same warning id end-to-end. implementation/core/test/re_frame/warn_once_clear_governance_cljs_test.cljs:109-133 independently arms every enrolled cache, fires the canonical chain, and proves each cache cleared.
- The only direct-seam proof is react_shared_suite.cljs:1242-1255, fed by the UIx cfg's :clear-warn! key. It duplicates behavior already proven at the public fixture/chained boundary.
- The same shared suite's so-called public-surface roster is stale: react_shared_suite.cljs:2497-2534 and the UIx cfg at :78-88 call seven functions public, omit the supported frame-root and use-frame exports, but include this unsupported no-doc reset. The manifest instead has eight supported functions.
- git history shows the standalone alias arrived with the original fixture-cache repair (724a018b49, 2026-05-12), was moved through the shared spine (e0a659445d), and was marked ^:no-doc during API-manifest governance (994c4e3489, 2026-06-01). No later consumer appeared.

## Impact

The extra Var expands the callable namespace surface without an API contract, encourages tests to bypass the reset mechanism whose chaining/governance is the actual invariant, and makes the "public surface" test guard assert the wrong API. Because that guard omits frame-root and use-frame, it can stay green if a real supported export disappears while failing if an internal reset alias is removed.

## Recommended disposition

Delete the UIx alias. Remove or internalize the direct-clear shared-suite row and its :clear-warn! configuration so tests exercise the canonical hook/fixture boundary. Update the UIx public-surface roster to the eight supported functions from the API manifest: add frame-root and use-frame, omit clear-warned-non-dom-roots!, and avoid maintaining another contradictory hand-written API count if the manifest metadata can drive the assertion.

## Risks

The Var is technically callable by an external program despite ^:no-doc, so removal can break an unsupported caller that discovered it from source. Do not delete the underlying spine thunk or chain registration: that would recreate cross-test warn suppression and is explicitly outside this task. Hicasso reads its private spine map in the shared suite; preserve its internal coverage or migrate it to the same canonical chain rather than treating that map key as a public Hicasso export.
acceptance_criteria:
- re-frame.adapter.uix no longer defines clear-warned-non-dom-roots!, and no UIx test/config refers to it.
- The spine still creates the per-adapter warn cache, registers its clear thunk through install-clear-warn-once-step!, and exposes no new public reset API.
- make-reset-runtime-fixture still fires :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! after disposal; a focused UIx proof emits once, suppresses a duplicate, runs the canonical reset, and observes the same id emit once again.
- The warn-once governance test still enumerates and clears the UIx/Hicasso spine cache. Non-vacuity/control: disabling the spine's chain registration makes the focused or governance proof fail.
- Remove or internalize the direct-only assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly test and :clear-warn! cfg dependency; do not replace the public alias with another test-only namespace export.
- The UIx public-surface guard matches the supported manifest surface: eight functions (set-hiccup-emitter!, use-current-frame, frame-provider, frame-root, use-subscribe, use-frame, flush-views!, wrap-view), with adapter checked separately. It omits the internal cache reset.
- Reconcile shared-suite comments/assertion counts so they do not claim a seven-Var cross-adapter public surface that conflicts with the UIx API manifest or treat Hicasso's private spine map as an exported namespace.
- API manifest output remains unchanged for UIx, and the UIx/shared React-adapter, fixture-isolation, and warn-once governance suites remain green.
notes:
2026-09-03, worker/uixring-a (PR #9110 landed .38 and .50 only). NOT DONE — fence-blocked, not premise-failed. The public-surface question is settled in favour of removal: re-frame.adapter.uix/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! is ^:no-doc; spec/api-manifest.edn lists re-frame.adapter.uix as 'adapter' plus EIGHT fns (flush-views!, frame-provider, frame-root, set-hiccup-emitter!, use-current-frame, use-frame, use-subscribe, wrap-view) and deliberately omits it, so it was never a documented or supported export; and a repo-wide exact census of 'uix-adapter/clear-warned-non-dom-roots!' over tracked files excluding .beads returns exactly TWO hits, both in its own shared-suite entry file (uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:75 as :clear-warn! and :88 inside :public-surface). Zero production, docs, examples, skills, tools or other-artefact consumers. Every other clear-warned-non-dom-roots! hit in the repo reaches the seam through a DIFFERENT door — re-frame.views/, warn-once/, or (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! spine-fns) — so none routes through the UIx namespace and none breaks.

WHY IT COULD NOT LAND HERE. The change set spans four files, three outside this worker's fence (implementation/adapters/uix/**, implementation/ssr-ring/**, tools/machines-viz/**), and partial application is strictly worse than none:
  1. implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:192-197 — delete the alias. IN FENCE.
  2. implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:75,88 — drop :clear-warn! and fix :public-surface. IN FENCE.
  3. implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs — OUT OF FENCE. Holds def ^:private public-surface-keys (:2527-2534), a SHARED cross-adapter roster naming all seven keys including :clear-warned-non-dom-roots!, iterated by assert-public-vars-present-and-callable as (is (fn? (get public-surface k))). Also holds assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly (:1242-1255), which calls (clear-warn!).
  4. implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite_tests.clj:172 — OUT OF FENCE. The forwarder row {:fn 'assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly}.
  5. implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/substrate_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs:63,66 — OUT OF FENCE. The ONLY other supplier of :clear-warn! / :public-surface, feeding them from (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! substrate/spine-fns).
Removing the two keys from the UIx cfg alone makes (get public-surface :clear-warned-non-dom-roots!) return nil -> (fn? nil) false -> RED, and (clear-warn!) on nil -> RED. Deleting the alias without also editing the UIx cfg is a compile error.

DISPATCH SHAPE. This needs ONE worker holding implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/** + implementation/hicasso/test/** + implementation/adapters/uix/**, in a single PR. Note the acceptance criterion's eight-function roster adds frame-root and use-frame, which the shared seven-key roster does not carry at all — so public-surface-keys must become per-adapter (cfg-supplied) rather than a shared constant, since Hicasso's supported set is not UIx's. Only UIx and Hicasso drive that assertion; reagent and reagent-slim supply neither key.
close_reason: Landed in PR #9117 (head 9ee10373af). re-frame.adapter.uix/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! DELETED. Public-surface account: ^:no-doc, no spec/api-manifest.edn row (UIx is rowed as adapter + eight fns; the generator drops ^:no-doc vars, so manifest output is unchanged and 'clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check' exits 0 with 'in sync (528 public vars)' and spec/ untouched); exact census of uix-adapter/clear-warned-non-dom-roots! returned exactly two hits, both in its own shared-suite entry file, zero production/docs/example/skill/tool callers; every other clear-warned-non-dom-roots! hit reaches the seam via re-frame.views/, warn-once/ or (:clear-warned-non-dom-roots! spine-fns) and is unaffected. Spine unchanged: per-adapter warn cache, install-clear-warn-once-step! registration and governance enrolment all intact. The :clear-warn! cfg key is GONE from the shared-suite contract and both entry files; MUST(3) idempotent-post-dispose and the G5 fire-once re-arm now fire the chained :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! late-bind hook (exactly what make-reset-runtime-fixture does after disposal), and assert-clear-warned-non-dom-roots-resets-directly plus its test-specs forwarder row are deleted as a duplicate of assert-chained-clear-warn-once-empties-cache. Seven-key-vs-eight-fn wrinkle resolved by making the roster cfg-supplied per adapter (:public-surface-keys): UIx now carries its eight manifest fns (frame-root and use-frame ADDED, clear thunk dropped), Hicasso its six published spine surfaces, and a new assertion pins roster == :public-surface map keys so neither side can drift into decoration; assert-public-vars-distinct-fns derives its count from the roster instead of hard-coding 7. Gates: npm run test:cljs (consolidated node-test covering core + UIx + Hicasso) exit 0, 11167 tests / 55739 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors; liveness control (dropping :frame-root from the UIx :public-surface map only) exit 1 with 2 failures both naming frame-root in the new roster machinery, then reverted and confirmed byte-identical by git hash-object.

title: Retire React 18 act fallbacks below the React 19 adapter floor
description:
## Scope

Retire the pre-React-19 act-resolution compatibility path discovered in the UIx adapter audit, across the one shared runtime and every live test harness that copied it. Preserve the public flush-views! entry points and their React-19 test behavior. This includes:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs (the resolver used by UIx, Hicasso, and stock Reagent's adapter-level flush);
- implementation/adapters/uix/src plus its five DOM harness copies;
- the three stock-Reagent DOM harness copies;
- the shared React-adapter suite, SSR hydration harness, two machines-viz harnesses, and Story harness;
- the stale reagent-slim resolver commentary and its inert (or (.-act react) nil) shape.

Root rendering, flush-render!, scheduler ordering, and support for React 18 applications are not being redesigned here.

## Vestigial finding

The repository now has an explicit React-19 floor, but the shared spine still probes react-dom/test-utils as a React-18 fallback, the UIx public helper promises both React 18 and 19, and fourteen live source/test files require react-dom/test-utils. That fallback predates the current floor and no longer provides a valid path on any supported build.

## Evidence and reachability proof

- docs/core/25-from-re-frame-v1.md:49 says every re-frame2 adapter targets React 19 and React 17/18 applications must bump.
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/floor-gate.md:7-11 repeats that React-19 floor and specifically says UIx hits it.
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:286-290 and :1336-1338 define adapter flush-views! as a dev/test boundary around direct React 19 act.
- implementation/package.json:19-20 pins react and react-dom 19.2.0. tools/template/src/day8/re_frame2_template/hooks.clj:191 pins generated consumers to 19.2.0, with a lockstep test against package.json.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1717-1744 still documents users on React 18.x, probes React.act, then requires react-dom/test-utils. UIx repeats the React-18 promise at implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:173-181.
- The exact require appears in fourteen files: core spine; core react_shared_suite; five UIx DOM tests; three stock-Reagent DOM tests; one SSR DOM test; two machines-viz DOM tests; and one Story DOM test. Repository-wide rg found no other live require sites.
- Runtime proof against the installed lock: with the React 19.2 development build, typeof React.act is "function", so the fallback is unreachable. With NODE_ENV=production, typeof React.act is "undefined"; react-dom/test-utils exports a function, but implementation/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-test-utils.production.js:14-22 shows it is only a deprecated forwarding wrapper. Invoking it prints the deprecation and throws TypeError: React.act is not a function. It therefore cannot rescue the supported production build either.
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:73-113 already says this artifact is React-19-only and probes only React.act, but still claims implementation tests use React 18.3, claims the shared fallback remains load-bearing, and spells the resolver as (or (.-act react) nil). implementation/package.json disproves the test-tree claim.
- git blame attributes the shared fallback to e0a659445d (2026-05-14), before the current dependency floor and template pin.

## Impact

The branch and its copies preserve a support promise the product explicitly rejects, add deprecated module edges to browser test bundles, and obscure the actual contract. In React 19 development they are dead. In React 19 production the apparent rescue is worse than a no-op: the deprecated wrapper calls a missing React.act and throws. The copied compatibility prose also makes future audits and dependency changes reason from an obsolete React-18 test matrix.

## Recommended disposition

Use React.act as the sole supported dev/test implementation. In shared code, retain the current unavailable-act no-op only where production elision/node safety requires it, but remove the react-dom/test-utils require. Simplify local test helpers to React.act, remove stale React-18 compatibility prose, and simplify reagent-slim's resolver to its one real expression. Do not rename or remove any public flush-views! function and do not change its nil return contract.

## Risks

Some downstream project may have relied on the undocumented implementation detail that this helper happened to work on React 18, despite the explicit React-19 migration gate. That unsupported compatibility is the only behavior removed. React's production bundle intentionally omits act, so the shared helper must keep its documented safe behavior there rather than unconditionally calling an absent export.

title: reagent-slim tests: remove five dead imports and static-prop
description:
## Finding

The reagent-slim test slice carries one unreachable private helper and five unused imports/referred macros.

## Evidence

`clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test --cache false` reports:

- `test/reagent2/impl/component_cljs_test.cljs:33` — npm namespace `react` required but never used.
- `component_cljs_test.cljs:57` — private `static-prop` Var is never referenced anywhere.
- `test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs:33` and `reagent_slim_view_id_attr_cljs_test.cljs:31` — `re-frame.core/reg-view` is referred as a macro but never used; both files invoke `rf/reg-view` through the existing alias.
- `reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs:78` and `reagent_slim_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs:40` — `cljs.test/testing` is referred but never used.

Exact symbol/path searches confirm no hidden use. Conventional unused callback parameters (`db`) and the unused `outer` in the separately actionable vacuous boundary test are excluded from this cleanup.

## Impact

These dead declarations add false dependency/macro edges and persistent lint noise. In this audit the noise obscured the materially vacuous `outer` boundary setup, demonstrating a concrete cost beyond tidiness.

## Proposed disposition

Delete only the unused require/refer entries and `static-prop` helper. Do not rename callback parameters, alter test discovery, or change assertions as part of this task.

## Risks

CLJS macro resolution can be subtle; retain `[re-frame.core :as rf]`, which is the qualifier actually used. Verify all affected namespaces still compile under their real node/browser selectors rather than relying only on lint.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead records/fields for `static-prop`, `unused import`, the file paths, and reagent-slim test lint. `rf2-6r9j.12` is an analogous cleanup limited to pair-mcp and does not overlap this surface. No duplicate exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- `static-prop` is removed and exact repository search finds no declaration/reference.
- The unused `react`, two `reg-view` macro refers, and two `testing` refers are removed without deleting their live sibling requires.
- `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test --cache false` reports none of the six cited warnings; unrelated callback/naming/unresolved-namespace warnings are not suppressed or bundled into this task.
- Affected JVM/CLJS namespaces compile in their normal test builds, including the DOM-selector namespaces.
- Test discovery counts and assertions remain unchanged.

title: reagent-slim IMPL-SPEC still specifies retired defview/util architecture
description:
## Finding

`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md` mixes a shipped disposition with earlier sections that still present retired or never-created Stage-4 architecture as the current implementation.

## Evidence

- The current source tree has no `reagent2.impl.util` namespace, yet the canonical layout lists `impl/util.cljs` at line 51 and §2.10 lines 354-361 specifies that file plus `fun-name`, `*non-reactive*`, and `dont-camel-case-pattern`. Exact repository searches find none of those slim symbols/files.
- The layout and current API inventory at lines 53, 318, 324, 337-338, 503, 522-548, 1090, and 1185 say `reagent2.impl.component/defview` ships. The same document's final disposition at line 1189 says it is not shipped; current `component.clj:10-12` and `component.cljs:31-33` agree with the disposition.
- §2.4 line 288 specifies an internal `apply-hiccup` used by render/hydrate; no such def exists. Both production entry points directly call `reagent2.impl.template/as-element`.
- §2.8 lines 326-334 lists nonexistent current component helpers (`do-render`, `wrap-funs`, `cancel-cleanup`, `queue-cleanup`) while omitting the actual lifecycle helper structure.
- §2.9 and the scheduler narrative describe separate atom-backed `dirty-set`, `scheduled?`, and `after-render-queue`; current batching uses one `RenderQueue` instance with fields and arrays.
- History shows §14 was amended to record the no-defview decision (`rf2-prkgge` referenced in the heading), but the earlier prescriptive sections were not reconciled.

## Impact

The document calls itself the implementation contract and is linked as such from README. Readers and coding agents can infer nonexistent public APIs, files, helpers, and state models, or spend work restoring deliberately rejected features. Contradictory current-tense claims also make it impossible to use the spec as a reachability inventory.

## Proposed disposition

Reconcile every current architecture/API inventory with the shipped tree. Remove or explicitly mark superseded Stage sketches as historical; make the no-defview disposition authoritative throughout; delete the nonexistent util/apply-hiccup/helper inventories; and describe the actual RenderQueue/component seams at contract-level detail. Preserve useful decision history and rejected-surface rationale without presenting it as shipped code.

## Risks

This is not permission to rewrite historical decisions or expand the slim API. Keep explicitly historical Stage rationale, public compatibility commitments, and rejected-surface explanations; change only statements presented as current/shipped architecture.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 bead records in every state for `IMPL-SPEC`, `defview`, `util.cljs`, `apply-hiccup`, and reagent-slim. `rf2-b9l8o` fixed the reaction macro and `rf2-08hx1` fixes lifecycle argv; Hicasso defview matches are a different namespace. No active or closed bead owns this reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria:
- A systematic inventory of every file/symbol named as current in §§2, 4, 5, 12, and 14 resolves to tracked shipped source or is explicitly labeled historical/rejected.
- No current-tense section says reagent-slim ships `defview`, `reagent2.impl.util`, `apply-hiccup`, `do-render`, `wrap-funs`, `cancel-cleanup`, or `queue-cleanup`.
- The scheduler description matches the `RenderQueue` representation and preserves the observable queue/flush contract without over-specifying dead internals.
- The canonical layout matches `rg --files implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src` exactly at namespace/file granularity.
- README, component namespace docs, and IMPL-SPEC agree that compile-time classification is folded into `reg-view` and no separate `defview` surface ships.
- Relevant docs-link/slug checks pass, and manual review confirms headings/tables remain coherent; no source/API behavior changes are included.
close_reason:
FIXED by PR #9119, https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9119, head 62983abf92. Every premise verified at source before editing; all of them held.

VERIFIED ABSENT from the shipped tree (git grep -F over tracked src+test, no -i, .beads excluded): reagent2.impl.util / impl/util.cljs, fun-name, *non-reactive*, dont-camel-case-pattern, apply-hiccup, do-render, wrap-funs, cancel-cleanup, queue-cleanup — zero files each. defview appears only in the two source docstrings that say it is NOT shipped, one test that asserts the same, and this document.

CORRECTED AS FALSE CURRENT-TENSE ARCHITECTURE (the doc calls itself the implementation contract and README links it as such, so each of these was buildable-against): §1.1 canonical layout (listed impl/util.cljs, duplicated the impl/ node, labelled component.clj "defview macro", omitted impl/diag.cljs, and used a _test.cljs test-file convention the tree does not use) — now mirrors git ls-files .../src file-for-file, which is the acceptance criterion. §2.4 internal apply-hiccup (render and hydrate-root each call template/as-element directly) and its omission of flush-render!, which ships. §2.7 "the defview macro lives in component.clj". §2.8 four nonexistent lifecycle helpers, replaced with the actual private structure at contract level (validate-class-spec!, install-lifecycle-methods!, make-render-method, argv-should-update?, sync-error-state!, ->react-element, and the argv/form-tag feeders) plus the correction that disposal is INLINE in an always-installed componentWillUnmount, not a deferred cleanup queue. §2.9 + §4.1 + §4.5 atom-backed dirty-set/scheduled? and set-membership dedup — the shipped scheduler is ONE RenderQueue deftype with three mutable fields and lazily allocated JS arrays, and dedup is a cljsIsDirty flag on the component instance (stock Reagent field name, kept so introspection hooks keep working). §2.10 entire nonexistent reagent2.impl.util namespace, replaced by reagent2.impl.diag, which DOES ship and which §2 documented nowhere. §4.2 flush-views! pseudocode and its "Stage 4 finalises the invocation; the import is react :refer [act]" forward-looking note. §5 defview framing; §5.1 wrap-render sketch (wrong arity, wrong cached-field name, no mention of the compile-time fold); §5.2, now describing the fold that actually ships — classify-form-body / tag-form-meta, called from the reg-view expansion — which is what the component.clj ns docstring already cites "§5.2 + §14.1" as. §12.1 and §12.5 test filenames.

PRESERVED AS DELIBERATE HISTORY — the retirement-category call the brief asked for. Every §14 "Disposition (as shipped)" record stays verbatim; §14.3-§14.6 rationale stays; every "not shipped" / DECISION-n row stays. §14.1 was the one needing judgement: its opening TWO PARAGRAPHS were written in the present tense ("Stage 4 ships reagent2.impl.component/defview...") directly ABOVE a disposition saying it was never shipped. Deleting them would have destroyed the question the rf2-yfbx decision answers, so they are marked as the question AS IT STOOD BEFORE STAGE 4 and left otherwise word-for-word. Only the tense was lying. Likewise R-003 in the risk register: reframed as retired-with-reason (no defview surface ships, so the risk cannot occur) rather than deleted, since the row records a real Stage-2 concern.

ONE IN-FENCE SOURCE DOCSTRING corrected alongside, same defect class: the component.cljs ns doc named a "reagent2.impl.component/-form-tag meta" that does not exist. The real meta key is :reagent2/form, built by tag-form-meta on the CLJ side.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: layout matches src exactly at file granularity; no current-tense section says slim ships defview, reagent2.impl.util, apply-hiccup, do-render, wrap-funs, cancel-cleanup or queue-cleanup; the scheduler description matches the RenderQueue representation and keeps the observable queue/flush contract (next-turn cascade holding and per-callback throw isolation are called out as contract, not incidental); README, the component ns docs and IMPL-SPEC now agree that compile-time classification is folded into reg-view and no separate defview surface ships. No source or API behaviour changed.

GATES: scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0 — this is the gate for markdown beside source, since check_doc_slugs.py roots do not reach implementation/ and nominating it here would have been the wrong gate — proved live by a planted broken link returning exit 1 with file, line and missing target. check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. clj-kondo exit 0 on the changed source. npm run test:cljs exit 0, 11169 tests / 55731 assertions. mkdocs build --strict NOT nominated: docs_dir is docs, and the hook stages only spec/ and migration/, neither of which this path is under. Headings and table column counts checked by hand — no gate validates markdown prose, tables or rendering.

title: reagent-slim StrictMode test still says the fixed bug fails by design
description:
## Finding

The live StrictMode regression test still tells contributors that its assertions fail by design and that the production bug is unfixed, although the fix landed immediately afterward and the test is now a required green regression.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_strict_mode_dom_cljs_test.cljs:6-12` says assertions `(a)` and `(b)` `FAIL BY DESIGN`, the substrate does not honor the contract, and the fix belongs to a separate bead.
- Its `FINDING` block at lines 29-51 speaks in present tense: StrictMode leaves every slim component reactively dead and a production fix is still needed.
- Commit `2c4a87e3df` (`fix(adapters/reagent-slim): re-establish render Reaction after StrictMode remount (rf2-6b6pex)`) landed the repair after test commit `66e9e2af0e`.
- Current production code at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:389-415,432-442` installs a remount marker, queues a render on the second `componentDidMount`, and documents the fixed sequence.
- The test remains discovered by both browser and node selectors, so this is live test guidance rather than archived design history.

## Impact

The header normalizes red output from a required acceptance test and directs maintainers to file/fix work that is already complete. During a genuine regression, a reader could dismiss the failure as expected.

## Proposed disposition

Rewrite the header as regression history: state the former failure, name the fixing commit/bead, and describe the invariants the now-green test protects. Remove all present-tense `FAIL BY DESIGN`, `not yet honour`, and separate-fix instructions. Do not weaken the assertions or erase the useful explanation of the StrictMode lifecycle sequence.

## Risks

The historical diagnosis is valuable and should remain clearly marked as past behavior. Avoid turning the header into a terse comment that loses the reason for the remount marker or the two non-vacuous assertions.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead states/fields for `StrictMode`, `a07937`, `6b6pex`, `FAIL BY DESIGN`, the test filename, and `reagent-slim`. StrictMode matches concern Hicasso or unrelated surfaces; the historical IDs are no longer live bead records. No current bead owns this stale header.
acceptance_criteria:
- The live test file contains no present-tense claim that its assertions are expected to fail or that production lacks the repair.
- The header records the former failure and fixing commit/bead as history, then states the current green invariants: post-remount reactive update and watch-count cleanup.
- The production/test explanation agrees on the remount marker and forced re-render path.
- The StrictMode DOM test remains enrolled and passes; a focused negative control that disables the reattach behavior makes its reactive-update assertion fail.
- Any now-unused `cljs.test/testing` import may be removed, but no assertion or browser gating is weakened.
close_reason: Confirmed at tip: the STATUS block still read FAIL BY DESIGN and directed maintainers to file work already complete, and the FINDING block was present tense. Verified 2c4a87e3df (rf2-6b6pex) exists and landed 2026-07-12, the same day as the test's own commit 66e9e2af0e. Header rewritten as dated history rather than erased, per the standing rule on retired states: STATUS now says the file is a required green regression, then records what it used to say and when that ended; the FINDING block is retitled FORMER BUG, moved to past tense and KEPT because it is the diagnosis the remount marker was built from; a new section describes the fix (cljsRemountReattach set by the transient componentWillUnmount, read by the now-unconditional componentDidMount, which queues a render so make-render-method recreates the Reaction) and states what each assertion fails on. Those claims were verified rather than asserted: disabling the reattach reds the test with exactly (not (= 'n=2' 'n=1')) for (a) and (not (= 1 0)) twice for (b) -- the two failure modes the new prose names; restore verified by blob hash. No assertion or browser gating weakened; the now-unused cljs.test/testing refer removed as the acceptance criteria permit. PR #9077.

title: reagent-slim: remove the unused pr-atom receiver argument
description:
## Finding

The private `reagent2.ratom/pr-atom` helper carries an unused receiver argument. Both call sites compute the printable body before entering the helper, so the argument cannot affect output, dispatch, identity, or reactive capture.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/ratom.cljs:143-153` defines `(defn- pr-atom [a writer opts type-tag body] ...)`; `a` is never referenced.
- The only calls are the `IPrintWithWriter` methods at lines 234 and 459: each passes its receiver as the first argument but separately dereferences it to construct `body` before the call.
- `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src --cache false` reports exactly `ratom.cljs:143:17 warning: unused binding a` for this helper.
- Repository-wide search finds no other call, and the helper is private, so there is no external arity contract.

## Impact

The vestigial parameter suggests the helper needs the ratom identity and obscures the actual contract: it only formats a supplied type tag/body to a writer. It also leaves a permanent production lint warning that can hide new warnings.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `a` from the private helper's parameter vector and both call sites. Do not alter when the RAtom/Reaction is dereferenced or the `*ratom-context* nil` binding around nested printing.

## Risks

Moving the deref into the helper could change reactive-capture timing; that is explicitly out of scope. This task is only the mechanical deletion of the unused argument while preserving the existing precomputed `body` expression.

## Duplicate search

Searched all bead states and descriptions for `pr-atom`, `ratom print`, `IPrintWithWriter`, `unused receiver`, and the path. No match owns this finding.
acceptance_criteria:
- `pr-atom` has only `[writer opts type-tag body]`, and both RAtom and Reaction print methods call that arity.
- Existing exact printed representations for RAtom and Reaction remain unchanged, including nested-value printing and the `*ratom-context* nil` guard.
- Focused ratom print tests pass for both types.
- `clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src --cache false` no longer reports the `ratom.cljs:143` unused-binding warning; the intentional namespace-load `installed?` warning is not papered over as part of this task.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9127 (branch worker/slimdead-a, head c7d4c437f0). The unused receiver argument is REMOVED from pr-atom's signature and from both call sites, not renamed to _: the helper is defn- with exactly two call sites, both the IPrintWithWriter methods in ratom.cljs itself and both changed in the same commit, so there is no external arity contract that a rename would have to preserve. The *ratom-context* nil binding and the point at which each receiver is dereferenced are untouched, per the bead's fence.

Census, tracked files with .beads excluded, run twice (line-oriented, then over whitespace-flattened text since neither result is a superset of the other): three sites, all in ratom.cljs, all in the diff.

The 'printed representation unchanged' criterion had NO instrument on main - the suite asserted nothing about either type's printed form. ratom_cljs_test.cljs now pins the exact #object[reagent2.ratom.RAtom ...] / #object[reagent2.ratom.Reaction ...] strings, recursive value printing, and a nested ratom printing through the same helper.

Gates, exit codes captured to a file and read from the file: CLJS node-test focused on reagent2.ratom-cljs-test COMPILE=0 RUN=0, 24 tests / 66 assertions / 0 failures; clj-kondo exit 2 (warnings) with 2 warnings, both pre-existing in batching.cljs.

Control: on unmodified main the same clj-kondo invocation reports THREE warnings including ratom.cljs:146:17 warning: unused binding a. On the branch it reports two - that one gone, the deliberate batching/installed? namespace-load warning untouched and not papered over. Separately the CLJS gate bit before it passed: its first run came back red on an assertion existing only in this branch (CLJS pr-str emits a comma between map entries), so a run that had wandered into another checkout would have been green.

Premise drift, substance unaffected: the bead's line numbers are three low - the defn is at ratom.cljs:146 not 143, the call sites at 237 and 462 not 234 and 459. And the bead says clj-kondo reports 'exactly' the one warning; it reports three on main, the other two in batching.cljs and left alone.

Finding raised in the PR body rather than acted on, because the bead explicitly fences the binding: in pr-atom, (pr-writer (binding [*ratom-context* nil] body) writer opts) scopes the nil binding to evaluating body - an already-computed local - and pops it before pr-writer runs, so the guard covers no nested printing at all. Unchanged by this diff, but it is not doing what its position implies.

title: docs(reagent-adapter): repair stale Reagent dependency pointer
description:
## Finding

`implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:11` says Reagent 2.0.1 is pinned in `implementation/core/deps.edn` and links to `../../core/deps.edn`. That manifest no longer contains the stock Reagent coordinate. The actual pin is `reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "2.0.1"}` at `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn:15`.

## Evidence

`implementation/core/deps.edn:18-25` explicitly says stock `reagent/reagent` is intentionally not a core dependency and that the Reagent adapter artifact is its sole owner. Commit `d44c4f7d20` (`fix(deps): move stock-reagent dep from core to the reagent adapter (rf2-enmvx6)`, 2026-07-11) removed the coordinate from core and added it to the adapter. `git blame` shows the README's current line was restyled later in commit `b22a0fef4c` on 2026-08-19 but retained the pre-move destination.

All-status bead searches for `reagent readme`, `dependency ownership`, `stock reagent`, `stale deps`, and description scans for `adapters/reagent/README`, `pinned.*core/deps`, and `implementation/core/deps.edn` found no current owner for this stale pointer. Historical dependency-move bead `rf2-enmvx6` is no longer present in the active bead store and its landed change did not repair this README.

## Impact

The adapter's own support-floor document directs maintainers and consumers to a manifest that proves the opposite dependency relationship. It obscures the deliberate artifact boundary, can lead audits to conclude that core still transitively installs Reagent, and leaves the stated version detached from its authoritative coordinate.

## Proposed disposition

Change the sentence to point at the adapter-owned `deps.edn` and make ownership explicit, for example: Reagent 2.x is currently pinned to 2.0.1 in this adapter's `deps.edn`. Keep the documented Reagent 2.x / React 19 floor unchanged.

## Risks

This is documentation-only, but the relative Markdown target must resolve from `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md`. Do not move the dependency or broaden compatibility as part of the repair.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` and follow the link attached to the stated Reagent 2.0.1 pin; it points to `implementation/core/deps.edn`.
2. Search that core manifest for `reagent/reagent`; the coordinate is absent and its comments state that stock Reagent is intentionally not core-owned.
3. Open `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn`; it contains `reagent/reagent {:mvn/version "2.0.1"}`, proving the README points at the wrong authority.
4. Use `git show d44c4f7d20` to verify that dependency ownership moved from core to the adapter while the README pointer was not repaired.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md` links the 2.0.1 pin to `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn`, not `implementation/core/deps.edn`.
2. The wording accurately states that the adapter artifact owns the stock Reagent coordinate while core intentionally does not.
3. The documented Reagent 2.x / React 19 support floor and no-compat-shim policy are unchanged.
4. The repository documentation-link checker passes for the changed README, and a direct source check confirms the linked manifest contains the stated 2.0.1 coordinate.
close_reason: PR #9122: implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md:11 now points the 2.0.1 pin at the adapter's own deps.edn and states the ownership split. Premise verified at source: core/deps.edn carries no reagent/reagent coordinate (only prose), 'clojure -Spath' from implementation/core resolves no reagent jar, and from implementation/adapters/reagent resolves reagent-2.0.1.jar whose META-INF pom reads <version>2.0.1</version> - the version was right, only the pointer was wrong. scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0; a planted broken target at that same line returned exit 1 naming it.

title: reagent-slim: remove the zero-consumer tag-form-meta compile helper
description:
## Finding

`reagent2.impl.component/tag-form-meta` is a public-looking compile-time helper with no production consumer. It has been test-only since its introduction and duplicates the literal metadata construction already performed by the only real consumer of this namespace.

## Evidence

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.clj:14-25,71-76` advertises `tag-form-meta` as consumed by `reg-view` and defines it as only `{:reagent2/form form-tag}`.
- A repository-wide exact-symbol search finds only that source declaration/docstring and its dedicated test at `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/impl/component_test.clj:60-68`; there is no production call.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:60-73` dynamically resolves only `classify-form-body`. The expansion constructs slot metadata directly with `(assoc :reagent2/form form-tag)` at lines 132-138 and fn metadata directly with `with-meta` at lines 196-197.
- `git log -S tag-form-meta` finds only its introduction in `21d4b06aae` and a later comment pass `0eeb8d079a`; history contains no consumer.
- This is not a shipped compatibility promise: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/README.md:3-10` identifies `reagent2.core`/the adapter as the target surface and says reagent-slim is pre-alpha and has never shipped. No README or implementation-spec API table promises this helper.

## Impact

The extra public Var and dedicated test imply an extension seam that does not exist in the actual `reg-view` integration. They add maintenance and invite downstream coupling to an accidental one-line abstraction.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `tag-form-meta`, its dedicated unit test, and the false namespace-doc claim that `reg-view` consumes it. Keep `classify-form-body` and the macro expansion's current direct metadata construction unchanged. Do not add a deprecation shim to an unpublished, zero-consumer helper.

## Risks

A local, out-of-repository macro could have called the public Var despite the absence of a documented/released contract. Before removal, repeat exact searches over any maintained external consumer corpus if one exists; otherwise the explicit pre-alpha status makes removal the safer pre-release choice.

## Duplicate search

Searched all 575 current bead records (all states; title, description, notes, acceptance) for `tag-form-meta`, `reagent2.impl.component`, `compile-time form`, `metadata`, and the source path. No bead owns this finding. `rf2-08hx1` concerns Form-3 lifecycle argv and is unrelated.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tag-form-meta` and its test-only coverage are removed; `rg tag-form-meta` is empty across tracked source/tests/docs.
- `classify-form-body` remains the only CLJ helper dynamically resolved by core, and Form-1/Form-2 macroexpansion metadata remains byte-for-byte equivalent in meaning.
- The component namespace documentation names only helpers with a real consumer and does not claim a general macro-extension contract unless one is deliberately specified and tested.
- Reagent-slim JVM tests and the core `reg-view` macroexpansion tests pass; a negative control that removes the classifier resolution makes the focused fold test fail.
- No compatibility alias or dead forwarding wrapper replaces the removed helper.
notes: AUDIT 2026-09-03 — PR #9127 (merge 213a43ae7791dbe0a7feadab3a46077a38d804a9) correctly removed the zero-consumer `tag-form-meta` Var and its dedicated test, but the integrated tree still contains three claims that the helper exists: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:609`, its coverage table at `:1128`, and `src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:26`. At the same merge, exact searches of `component.clj` and `component_test.clj` return zero definitions/tests. This violates the existing acceptance criterion that tracked source/tests/docs contain no `tag-form-meta` and leaves runtime/developer documentation pointing at a removed Var. Reopened this exact owner rather than creating a duplicate. Reconcile those three references with the surviving `classify-form-body` plus the metadata construction in `re-frame.core/expand-reg-view`; do not restore the dead helper.
close_reason: RE-CLOSED; the first close evaporated to the .beads checkout race. Landed on main as 213a43ae77 (PR #9127, worker slimdead-a): the zero-consumer tag-form-meta compile helper removed from reagent-slim's impl/component.clj. A macro-time consumer was ruled out FOUR ways, which matters because a runtime var-usage census cannot see macroexpansion-time use: (1) census line-oriented AND whitespace-flattened found only docstring, defn and test; (2) every external reference to the namespace enumerated and read, all naming classify-form-body / wrap-render / create-class* / reagent-class?; (3) both requiring-resolve sites pass a LITERAL symbol, and a sweep for dynamically-constructed symbols - the one shape a literal census misses - found none; (4) the removal is itself the macro-time instrument, since the JVM suite macroexpands reg-view through expand-reg-view, so a surviving macro-time consumer would fail to COMPILE. Green. Control fired: planting a fault in classify-form-body's Form-2 branch took the JVM gate to exit 1 with four failures including fold-reg-view-form-2-expansion-tags-form-2, proving the fold test is not passing vacuously.

title: vestige(reagent-adapter): remove ten redundant test imports
description:
## Finding

The Reagent adapter test surface retains ten imports/refers that have no live use:

- `:require-macros [re-frame.core :refer [reg-view]]` is unused in seven namespaces: `reg_view_devtools_cljs_test.cljs`, `source_coord_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `source_coord_warn_once_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_rendered_op_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_id_attr_cljs_test.cljs`, `view_render_trigger_handler_cljs_test.cljs`, and `view_side_capture_cljs_test.cljs`.
- `[re-frame.trace :as trace]` is unused in `render_key_cljs_test.cljs` and `view_render_trigger_handler_cljs_test.cljs`.
- `testing` is referred but unused in `views_synthetic_event_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs`.

## Evidence

`clj-kondo --lint implementation/adapters/reagent --cache false` reports each of these exact clauses as referred/required but never used. Repo-wide lexical inspection confirms there are no unqualified `reg-view` calls in the seven listed namespaces: they use `rf/reg-view`, or only the plain function `rf/reg-view*`. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` lines 170-188 explicitly self-requires its macros and states that `(:require [re-frame.core :as rf])` is the only import CLJS callers need; many neighboring Reagent tests compile with `rf/reg-view` and no explicit macro refer. The two trace aliases have no `trace/` reference; each namespace already requires `re-frame.core`, which itself requires `re-frame.trace`, and their recorder macro comes from `re-frame.test-support`, which requires `re-frame.trace.tooling`. The synthetic-event test contains no `(testing ...)` form.

All-status bead searches for `reagent unused`, `reagent require`, `unused require`, `macro import`, `test imports`, plus description scans for `require-macros`, `dead import`, and every affected file name found no existing owner. `rf2-6r9j.12` is limited to dead imports in pair-mcp tests and is a different slice.

title: Xray Epoch: prune fourteen unreachable private helpers and styles
description:
## Finding

The live Xray Epoch implementation retains fourteen private definitions that are statically unreachable: two projection helpers and twelve view helpers/styles. Several adjacent comments still describe these dead values as active maintenance contracts.

## Evidence

- A clean `clj-kondo --lint tools/xray/src` reports `Unused private var` for exactly these Epoch projection definitions: `op->row-kind` and `state-keyword-or-leaf` in `panels/epoch/projection.cljc`.
- The same run reports the following private definitions in `panels/epoch/view.cljs`: `link-button-nowrap-style`, `table-glyph-cell-header-style`, `disposed-th-60-style`, `disposed-th-40-style`, `views-th-50-style`, `schema-violation-headline-style`, `schema-violation-headline-id-style`, `schema-violation-explain-toggle-style`, `coeffect-row-view`, `source-coord-display`, `schema-violation-where-label`, and `where->handler-kind`.
- Repo-wide exact-symbol searches find no executable call/reference for any of the fourteen. The only extra hits are comments: for example the projection doc instructs maintainers to update the unused `op->row-kind` table, and the live view contains a "companion swap" comment naming unused `coeffect-row-view`.
- Every definition is private, so there is no supported external var contract to preserve. Current render/projection paths use other helpers/inline styles and compile without reaching these names.
- File history shows the values are residue across successive Epoch view/projection revisions rather than entries in a reflection-driven registry; no dynamic symbol-resolution mechanism or string-key catalogue names them.
- Bead searches for `unreachable Epoch helpers`, `dead Epoch helpers`, `unused private definitions`, and description search for `op->row-kind` found no existing issue.

## Impact

These definitions add false branches and false styling authorities inside two already-large Epoch namespaces, keep standing lint warnings noisy, and misdirect maintainers with comments that require updates to tables/components the runtime never reads.

## Proposed disposition

Delete only the fourteen listed private definitions and repair the comments that present them as live. Keep behavior-bearing callers and the currently selected styles/helpers unchanged. Treat any newly discovered computed consumer as evidence to retain and document that one definition rather than broadening the cleanup.

## Risks

The Epoch view is large and some similarly named helpers are live. Make the change symbol-by-symbol, avoid adjoining style consolidation, and verify no macro/string/dynamic resolution exists. Preserve all current Epoch projection rows, schema-violation rendering, source-link behavior, and coeffect display.

title: Remove redaction helper pair superseded by collect-redaction-paths
description:
Evidence

Why this is vestigial
The old half-walk and its private predicate are a superseded implementation path. They duplicate the fused collector's logic and leave misleading reachability documentation around privacy plumbing.

Privacy behavior is security-sensitive. This cleanup must not change path collection order/deduplication, the handler's raw event, pre-chain trace projection, schema/classification overlap, or egress redaction. Treat `schema-redaction-paths`' explicit compatibility retention as authoritative.

title: Xray: retire the unused perf-tier module
description:

No production Xray namespace calls it; only its dedicated test and a theme variable-resolution test require it, while its namespace contract still presents retired panels as live consumers.

- The namespace doc says the Performance panel re-exports it and marks `performance` and `event_detail` tier-dot surfaces `LIVE`. Commit `646e38273d` removed the Performance panel and helpers in the dead-panel sweep. Commit `aeb34400c0` retired the Handler/Event panel and its caller. No replacement consumer was introduced.

Current `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures.cljs` mentions perf-tier dots only in fixture prose/data; it does not require or call this module, so fixture comments do not establish reachability.
- `tools/xray/spec/014-Registry-Catalogue.md` retains active-looking Performance-panel catalogue prose despite the feature-matrix documentation recording that panel as retired; the source ledger is similarly stale.

## Impact

The bundle and test matrix maintain a design-system abstraction with no rendering consumer, while source/spec prose incorrectly says retired panels are live. This creates a false extension point and lets future duration thresholds drift between actual UI code and an unused supposed authority.

Remove the orphaned module and tests that exist only to pin it, and reconcile stale Performance/Event catalogue and source-ledger claims. If a current tier-dot surface genuinely needs the shared classifier, wire that caller and add integration coverage before retaining the module; do not treat fixture prose as a consumer.

## Risks

Preserve any live duration display implemented independently in surviving panels. Recheck concurrent work for a newly landed require and published API policy before deletion; the module is currently internal and not facade-exported.

Commit `02aae4c239` removed Trace's require and `film-strip/header` render because the L2 list owns navigation. Commit `aeb34400c0` retired the Handler/Event panel, removing another former caller. - Bead title searches for `film strip header` and `film-strip`, plus description search for `film_strip/header`, found no existing issue.

## Impact

The shipped bundle retains an unreachable component and a large self-test suite that proves only the orphan itself. Contradictory docs tell panel authors to reuse a component the current navigation architecture deliberately stopped mounting, increasing the chance of reviving a superseded L4 navigation model.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the orphaned namespace and its dedicated test. Reconcile active Xray specs/skill references so the L2 Epoch list is the single stated navigation owner; retain genuinely historical design notes only when clearly marked superseded. If a current panel is intentionally meant to restore the header, first identify and land that real consumer rather than preserving the component speculatively.

## Risks

Do not remove Epoch/L2 navigation, issue filtering, or the current panel focus events. Recheck concurrent panel work and out-of-repo published API policy before deletion, although the component is not facade-exported and no current in-repo caller exists.

title: Retire the orphaned route-link prefetch hook trio
description:
## Problem

Routing still publishes three optional-artifact hooks for a substrate-neutral `:prefetch :intent` route-link integration, but no current code reads any of them. Their original view-artifact consumer was retired, and the shipped replacement view explicitly declines this integration. The hook directory nevertheless says Hicasso consumes all three, so the integration catalogue describes reachability that does not exist.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string searches find `:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys` only at their `late-bind/set-fn!` publications in `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:572-580`, their catalogue rows in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:540-551`, and prose/comments. There is no `late-bind/get-fn`, `require-fn!`, wrapper, or other reader for any key.
- The shipped Hicasso route-link consumes only `:routing/link-model` and `:routing/activate-link!` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs`). Its namespace contract explicitly says the prefetch trio is "Not wired in v0", and `control-keys` merely prevents `:prefetch` leaking into HTML. `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:144-163` likewise teaches authors to dispatch `:rf.route/prefetch` themselves and states that `h/route-link` installs none of routing's prefetch handlers.
- The ordinary Reagent `rf/route-link` is still a live consumer of `link/prefetch-payload`, `link/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `link/prefetch-intent-keys`, but calls them directly inside the routing artifact. It does not traverse these hooks, so deleting only the publications does not remove route-link prefetch.
- History confirms the lost-consumer path: commit `fa3bc36bae4` introduced the first two hooks for `ui/Freehand consumers`; commit `4da020a5af2` added the intent-key hook and changed `implementation/freehand/src/re_frame/freehand/route_link_seam.cljc`. Those view artifacts are retired. Commit `c07b9f84674` later rewrote the directory prose to name Hicasso, but today's Hicasso implementation never adopted the hooks.
- Bead searches for each exact hook name, `substrate-neutral prefetch`, and `Hicasso prefetch` found no existing issue covering the orphaned trio.

## Impact

Every routing load installs three unread global hook-table entries, including one host-conditional operation and a thunk whose only purpose was cross-artifact sharing. More importantly, the authoritative late-bind directory falsely promises a supported Hicasso integration, making drift checks green while maintainers reason from an imaginary consumer.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the three `late-bind/set-fn!` publications and their directory rows, and update the nearby routing comments that describe them as seams. Keep the underlying `re-frame.routing.link` functions/data and the documented `rf/route-link :prefetch :intent` behavior unchanged because those are directly consumed. If a non-Reagent route-link is intentionally being changed to support prefetch, land that real reader first and keep only the keys it actually needs rather than preserving speculative hooks.

## Risks

The directory may be consumed by generic drift tooling, so publisher and catalogue changes must land together. Recheck any concurrent Hicasso work before removal because recent design notes discuss a possible future acceptance even though current runtime and user guide explicitly decline it. Do not delete or change the underlying prefetch event, resource warm-plan, or Reagent route-link behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, and `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys` are either removed from both publisher and late-bind directory, or each retained key has a shipped, tested `get-fn`/`require-fn!` consumer; catalogue prose names only real consumers.
2. `rf/route-link {:prefetch :intent}` still validates on both hosts and installs its CLJS hover/focus/touch behavior through the live direct `re-frame.routing.link` functions.
3. Hicasso route-link tests and documentation agree on whether `:prefetch` is supported; no key is silently stripped under a catalogue claim that it is consumed.
4. Routing tests plus core late-bind directory drift/coverage tests pass, and repo-wide fixed-string searches show no orphaned reader or publisher.
close_reason: PR #9165. The three prefetch late-bind publications and their three directory rows removed together; verified at tip that no get-fn/require-fn!/wrapper read any of them, with :routing/link-model as a control that DOES have real readers. rf/route-link's :prefetch :intent is untouched (it calls re-frame.routing.link directly), and :prefetch stays in Hicasso's control-keys so it still never reaches the anchor. Hicasso's route-link contract corrected: it claimed routing published a trio it no longer does. Gates: late-bind drift JVM 8 tests/683 assertions exit 0 (pins both directions), routing JVM 553 tests/3451 assertions exit 0, CLJS 11175/55753 exit 0, browser 783/4253 exit 0. Deletion run backwards: re-adding one publication without its directory row turned the drift test exit 1 with exactly one failure naming :routing/prefetch-payload. NOTE the bead's file list was stale in two ways: the implementation/freehand/ path it cites is retirement HISTORY (rf2-0yp7w / PR #8322, git ls-files returns zero) and needed no work, and three docstrings in re-frame.routing.link still call these functions late-bind seams - out of this fence, follow-up filed.

title: vestigial(story): retire the standalone duplicate extends resolver
description:
Finding

`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/extends.cljc` is a 155-line standalone `:extends` resolver that is no longer on Story's runtime path. It is a duplicate, now-divergent implementation whose only actual consumer is a pair of focused tests of the duplicate itself.

Evidence

- Repo-wide search for `re-frame.story.extends`, `extends/resolve-extends`, and `extends/*max-extends-depth*` finds only: the namespace itself; the require at `tools/story/test/re_frame/story_test.clj:26`; calls in `extends-cycle-detection` and `extends-depth-cap` at lines 312/333; and a docstring cross-reference in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/plan.cljc:163`.
