- The registration test immediately above those self-tests states that registered bodies keep raw `:extends` and that `re-frame.story.plan` is the single merge authority. Runtime compilation calls `plan/resolve-source-chain` (`plan.cljc:161-212`) and plan-owned merge logic; it never calls this namespace.
- The two implementations no longer express the same operation. `extends/resolve-extends` performs a straight parent-first map merge plus optional exclusive key groups. The compiled-plan authority applies field-specific semantics (for example setup append, local script/assertion ownership, deep/context merges). A passing standalone test therefore cannot prove the shipped runtime.
- `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/plan_test.cljc:229` already tests cycle failure through the actual plan compiler. Runtime inheritance/decorator behavior is also exercised in `story_test.clj`, `story_authoring_surface_test.clj`, and `story_decorator_chain_test.clj`; only the depth-cap witness still targets the duplicate rather than `plan/*max-extends-depth*`.
- History shows the standalone implementation arrived in `660fead138` (2026-05-11). The compiled-plan authority arrived later; by `82cd4bd1c8` (2026-07-10) the namespace doc explicitly acknowledged `re-frame.story.plan` as runtime authority and described this copy only as a helper for tooling/focused tests. No tooling consumer exists. The August vocabulary edit was mechanical (`:play-script` -> `:script`) and did not add a consumer.
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md:303` still cites `story_test.clj`'s standalone bare-merge test as coverage even though runtime merge authority and semantics have moved to the plan compiler.
- Bead searches for `re-frame.story.extends`, `resolve-extends`, `extends resolver`, `Story extends`, `max-extends-depth`, and `standalone pure helper` returned no existing issue.

Impact

The duplicate ships code and a second public dynamic depth knob without a runtime/tooling consumer, lets tests go green against behavior the product does not execute, and invites error-id/depth/merge semantics to drift from the plan compiler. The coverage matrix overstates runtime coverage by naming the stale test.

Proposed disposition

Remove `re-frame.story.extends`. Move the still-useful depth-cap witness (and any missing unknown/cycle witness) to `re-frame.story.plan` through `variant-plan`/`resolve-source-chain`; delete redundant self-tests; remove the stale plan docstring cross-reference and update the spec/015 coverage row to name runtime-authority tests. Do not introduce a third facade shim. If a previously unknown downstream direct-require is discovered, consolidate both callers on one shared resolver rather than retaining divergent implementations.

Risks

Although the namespace is not facade-exported or documented as public API, a downstream project could direct-require it. Check published artifact/API policy and call out the removal in migration notes if required. Preserve the runtime error ids and the configurable depth-cap behavior at the plan authority.
acceptance_criteria:
- Repo-wide search finds no `re-frame.story.extends` namespace/file, `extends/resolve-extends`, or `extends/*max-extends-depth*` reference.
- The actual plan/runtime path has tests for unknown parent, cycle detection, the bound at `plan/*max-extends-depth*`, and representative field-specific inheritance (including setup/script/decorator behavior).
- `tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md` names tests that execute the plan/runtime authority and no longer claims the standalone bare merge proves runtime behavior.
- Story JVM and CLJS suites, source lint, API/spec drift checks, and affected feature-load/static build gates pass.
close_reason:
Done in PR #9075. Reachability re-proved at tip before deleting, twice per needle (line-oriented and whitespace-flattened over 4810 tracked files, .beads excluded) and each against a live control in the same files with the same instrument: `re-frame.story.extends` 3 hits / control `re-frame.story.plan` 74; `resolve-extends` 5 / control `resolve-source-chain` 4; `extends/*max-extends-depth*` only inside the namespace and its self-test. The two censuses agreed everywhere, so nothing was broken across a line. After the change `git grep -nF resolve-extends` returns nothing (exit 1) while `resolve-source-chain` still returns four.

The two self-tests were READ before being dropped, per the rule that a test encoding a guarantee the live resolver should also have is a finding rather than something to delete. Cycle was already witnessed at the live authority (plan_test.cljc extends-cycle-fails) and unknown-parent twice over (plan_test.cljc missing-parent-fails; story_test.clj extends-unknown-parent, which goes through plan/variant-plan). The DEPTH CAP was not — its only witness bound extends/*max-extends-depth*. That is the finding, and it is fixed rather than reported: the witness now lives at plan_test.cljc extends-depth-cap-fails, bound on plan/*max-extends-depth* and driven through variant-plan. plan/resolve-source-chain raises the identical three error ids with the same messages, so no guarantee is dropped.

Reach measured, not assumed: `.cljc` makes the witness host-free but buys no second gate — the :node-test build selects on "cljs-test$" and a plain -test ns does not match, so it runs under jvm-tools-story only. That is exactly the reach the JVM-only witnesses it replaced had. A first commit claimed CLJS reach too; a follow-up commit corrects it.

Also corrected: plan.cljc's docstring cross-reference to the retired namespace; a stale narration in story_authoring_validation_test.clj naming resolve-extends as the mechanism (registration stores the raw body and the compiler lowers :script/:plays to one slot); and spec/015's :extends row, which cited story_test.clj §extends-resolves-at-registration-time — a test name that no longer exists — now naming the tests that execute the plan/runtime authority.

Two `re-frame.story.extends` mentions survive on purpose, both in comments this PR wrote recording where the retired tests went: retirement bookkeeping, not live references.

Gates (captured exits): jvm-tools-story 1889/6959 0 failures exit 0 (and a planted wrong error id in the new witness took it to exit 1 with test/assertion counts unchanged, proving the plant stopped no namespace); npm run test:cljs 11209/55849 exit 0; test-fast-pr.sh exit 0; check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. All re-run after rebase onto current origin/main.

title: pair-mcp tests: remove eight dead imports and bindings
description:

title: pair-mcp: remove four zero-consumer helper definitions
description:
## Finding
Four public Pair-MCP helper definitions have no production, test, build, or repository consumer and expose misleading or obsolete surface:
- `roots_discovery.cljs`: `project-home->candidate` and `candidates-from-edns`
- `tools/wire.cljs`: `structured-content` and `arg-keyword`

## Evidence and reachability proof
- Whole-repository symbol searches find each name only at its definition/docstring/comment; no invocation exists.
- `clj-kondo` var-usage analysis across Pair-MCP source and tests reports zero source uses and zero test uses for all four definitions.
- Production root discovery calls `discover-via-roots*` with concrete dependencies, and that seam calls `candidates-from-edns*`; tests also call the starred seams directly. The two unstarred wrappers are bypassed. The docstring for `project-home->candidate*` nevertheless claims production callers use the dead wrapper.
- All structured response envelopes call `wire/result`, whose implementation uses private `structured-of`; `structured-content` has had no client since it was introduced alongside `result` in commit `834af6cdd9`.
- `arg-keyword` was used by the progress-stream/list-streams operations removed in commit `89bb4d49f1`; no current frame parser calls it.
- `package.json` publishes compiled `out/server.js`, README, and LICENSE—not these CLJS namespaces as a supported library API.
- Dynamic zero-static-use entrypoints such as `server/main` and `descriptor-manifest-gen/-main` were explicitly excluded because `shadow-cljs.edn` proves their build reachability.

## Impact
The dead definitions enlarge an apparent API, retain stream-era residue, and leave a false production-call claim in a root-discovery docstring. Future maintainers can mistakenly preserve or test paths the server cannot take.

## Proposed disposition
Delete the four zero-consumer definitions and correct the starred root-discovery seam documentation to describe the actual production path. Keep the live starred injection seams, `wire/result`, and private `structured-of` unchanged.

## Risks / retained contracts
Re-run whole-repository searches before deletion to catch concurrent clients. Do not classify build entrypoints or deliberate test seams as dead merely because ordinary static call analysis cannot see them. Do not change response envelope shape or root candidate ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The four listed zero-consumer definitions are removed (or a newly discovered concrete consumer is documented and the applicable definition retained).
2. Root-discovery docstrings accurately describe the real production and test call paths.
3. Whole-repository searches show no dangling references to the removed symbols.
4. Pair-MCP build and tests pass; descriptor generation/check and registry fixture checks remain unchanged/green.
5. Public MCP response envelopes and roots-discovery behavior are unchanged.
close_reason: Done in PR #9076. Reachability premise re-verified at tip and HELD for all four. Two independent instruments, each run against live controls in the same files: (a) line-oriented fixed-string search over tracked files, (b) a whitespace-flattened per-file census over 4810 tracked files. Both returned ZERO call heads for project-home->candidate, candidates-from-edns, structured-content and arg-keyword; controls wire/result, wire/arg, rd/project-home->candidate*, candidates-from-edns* and rd/discover-via-roots* all fired non-zero. Production path confirmed at source: discover-via-roots -> discover-via-roots* -> candidates-from-edns* -> project-home->candidate*, bypassing both unstarred wrappers. structured-content's docstring named server.cljs, cache.cljs and cap.cljs as its consumers; checked each — all three call wire/result instead (cache.cljs:283, server.cljs:586/626, cap.cljs:145). The sibling unstarred walk-for-shadow-edns is LIVE (passed to discover-via-roots* at roots_discovery.cljs:303) and was deliberately left alone — the audit was right to name only two of the three wrappers. Docstring trap fixed: project-home->candidate*'s 'production callers use [[project-home->candidate]]' was false and pointed at a deleted var; it now describes the real call path. Two comments in dispatch.cljs and trace_window.cljs cited wire/arg-keyword as the coercion NOT to use and would have dangled; they now say (keyword ...) directly. No dangling references remain. Envelope shape and root candidate ordering unchanged. Suite green: 1120 tests, 4070 assertions, 0 failures (captured exit 0).

title: Remove the unread :routing/route-sub-fn late-bind hook
description:
## Problem

The routing facade publishes `route-sub-fn` twice: it directly registers the function as the `:rf/route` subscription and also writes it to the optional-artefact hook table as `:routing/route-sub-fn`. Nothing ever reads that hook. The public direct function remains documented, but the late-bind publication and its directory entry are vestigial plumbing.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string search for `:routing/route-sub-fn` returns exactly two current locations: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:489` (`late-bind/set-fn!`) and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:518` (catalog metadata). There is no `late-bind/get-fn`, `require-fn!`, wrapper, reset-hook roster, or other call site for the key.
- The real subscription registration is direct in the already-loaded routing facade: `(subs/reg-runtime-sub :rf/route ... route-sub-fn)` at `routing.cljc:387-389`. It neither needs nor consults late binding.
- `re-frame.core-routing` contains only the two required optional-artifact wrappers, `reg-route` and `route-link`; it has no route-sub function wrapper.
- `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md` documents `route-sub-fn` as a direct owned-namespace function, so removing the dead hook does not remove that supported function.
- History shows `:routing/route-sub-fn` was added mechanically during the artifact split in `c435165251`. That same change moved the `:rf/route` registration into `re-frame.routing`, leaving no core consumer; no later commit has added a hook read.

## Impact

Every routing load mutates the process-global hook table with an unreachable entry, and the central late-bind directory advertises a cross-artifact seam that does not exist in practice. This enlarges the optional-artifact integration vocabulary and can mislead maintainers into preserving or using a needless indirection.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the `late-bind/set-fn! :routing/route-sub-fn` publication and the matching directory entry. Keep `re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn` and its direct `:rf/route` registration unchanged because those are live/documented surfaces.

## Risks

Late-bind tables can be inspected generically, so rerun the directory drift/coverage checks after removing both sides together. Recheck for computed-key consumers; current code consistently uses literal hook keys and the exhaustive fixed-string search found none. Do not remove the direct public function or subscription registration as part of this cleanup.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `:routing/route-sub-fn` is absent from both the routing publisher and the core late-bind directory, with no remaining lookup or documentation of that hook.
2. `re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn` remains available and `:rf/route` remains directly registered to it after normal load and `:reload` following `registrar/clear-all!`.
3. Routing subscription tests and core late-bind directory drift/coverage tests pass.
4. A repo-wide fixed-string search confirms no computed or literal consumer was orphaned.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip: a fixed-string search for :routing/route-sub-fn returned exactly the two sites the bead named — routing.cljc:489 (late-bind/set-fn!) and late_bind/directory.cljc:518 (catalogue row) — with no get-fn, require-fn!, wrapper, reset-hook roster or computed-key consumer anywhere. Removed both sides together. KEPT, as the bead requires: the public re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn alias (routing.cljc:115) and the direct (subs/reg-runtime-sub :rf/route ... route-sub-fn) registration; docs/api/re-frame.routing.md still documents it and spec/api-manifest.edn's re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn row is unchanged, so the supported function is untouched. core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj:192 resolves that direct var, not the hook, and is unaffected. Gate: implementation/core clojure -M:test -n re-frame.late-bind-drift-test exit 0, 8 tests / 692 assertions / 0 failures — the bidirectional scan the bead's risk section names, which hardcodes no key but walks every set-fn! call site under implementation/**/src against the directory. That gate was proven non-vacuous for exactly this change: restoring the directory row while leaving the publication removed turned it red naming :routing/route-sub-fn as an entry with no publication, which is also why both sides had to move together. The file was restored and verified byte-identical by git blob hash. npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11168 tests / 55728 assertions / 0 failures) covers the core artefact and the routing subscription registration.

title: pair-mcp docs: retire stale bash-shim compatibility promises
description:
## Finding
The Pair-MCP package still presents the retired bash/babashka shims as a supported, mix-and-match transport in several current-state documents, although the shim implementation was deleted.

## Evidence
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md` lines 7-9 and 651-657 say the shims still ship, still work, and are not slated for removal.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/Principles.md` lines 117-143 and `spec/API.md` lines 379-405 make the same current compatibility promise.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md` Design Lock #6 (roughly lines 485-541) and its summary row (around line 958) still say both transports ship side-by-side with no removal scheduled.
- `git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts` returns no files. Commit `31594b44c3` (`chore(pair): remove retired bash/babashka transport`) deleted the wrappers, operations, and shim tests under rf2-dduetj.
- Current repository documentation elsewhere already records MCP as the only implementation (`skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md`, `docs/TESTING.md`, and Pair-MCP input/design specs).

A related closed predecessor, rf2-435ah, corrected this claim only in `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/**`; it did not cover the Pair-MCP README/spec tree listed above.

## Impact
Operators and agent authors can spend time looking for nonexistent scripts or design integrations around a transport that cannot be invoked. The stale promise also obscures the deliberate MCP-only migration.

## Proposed disposition
Rewrite current-state sections to say Pair MCP is the sole supported transport. Preserve genuinely historical comparisons, but mark Design Lock #6 and its summary entry as superseded by rf2-dduetj / commit `31594b44c3` instead of silently deleting the design history.

## Risks / retained contracts
Do not erase historical rationale or unrelated references that explain why MCP replaced the shim. Do not alter the live MCP protocol or compatibility guarantees.
acceptance_criteria:
1. README, Principles, and API no longer claim that bash/babashka shims ship, work, or may be mixed with MCP.
2. DESIGN-RATIONALE marks Lock #6 and its summary row as superseded, naming the MCP-only decision/removal lineage.
3. A repository search finds no present-tense support promise for the deleted shim; any surviving mentions are unambiguously historical.
4. Documentation link/slug checks covering the touched files pass, and changed tables/headings are manually checked where no renderer/gate applies.
close_reason: Done in PR #9076. Design Lock #6 keeps its question, options, pick, reasoning and date VERBATIM under a dated DISCHARGED banner naming rf2-dduetj / 31594b44c3 — the lock was not overturned, it played out as its own final Why bullet anticipated ('future removal is cheap ... the decision is reversible'); summary-table row 6 marked discharged in-place. Name-mapping tables retained and relabelled historical so an old runbook naming a deleted script still resolves. Two present-tense claims BEYOND the bead's list were found and past-tensed: DESIGN-RATIONALE lines 280 and 299 ('The bash shims ship six') inside Lock #4's evolution narrative. title: Collapse vestigial duplicate source-id branch in machines tooling
description:
## Evidence

`machine-instance-algebra-view` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/tooling.cljc` computes `source-id` with three `cond` arms (currently lines 393-396): keyword `machine-type` returns that keyword, `spawned?` returns `actor-id`, and `:else` also returns `actor-id`. Splint reports the adjacent `spawned?` / `:else` arms as identical (`tooling.cljc:395:35 [lint/identical-branches]`). The equivalent expression is `(if (keyword? machine-type) machine-type actor-id)`; `spawned?` continues to serve its real uses in spec resolution and the emitted `:spawned?` field, but cannot discriminate `source-id`.

`git blame` shows all three arms have been unchanged since the tooling view was introduced in commit `85379652c5f` (2026-06-12). The function's documented contract confirms the two non-keyword cases intentionally share identity: an inline-definition spawn uses `actor-id`, and a singleton is its own `actor-id`. Tests and downstream graph consumers observe the resulting node, not this private branch structure.

Bead searches for `machine-instance-algebra-view source-id`, `tooling source-id spawned actor-id`, `spawned source-id conditional`, and `identical branches machines tooling` found no existing issue covering the redundant branch.

## Impact

The redundant arm suggests a semantic distinction between inline-definition spawned actors and singletons at the source-id boundary even though both deliberately use `actor-id`. That false branch adds cognitive load in a tooling projection whose main job is to make identity rules explicit, and it leaves a standing identical-branches lint warning.

## Proposed disposition

Collapse `source-id` to a two-way expression: use the keyword `machine-type` for registered-type spawns, otherwise use `actor-id`. Preserve the separate `spawned?` binding because it still selects spec resolution and is emitted on the node.

## Risks

This projection feeds Xray and derivation-conformance tooling. Keep the change expression-only; do not alter `spec`, `spawned?`, registrar lookup, source form, owner, or state projection.
acceptance_criteria:
- `source-id` has exactly two outcomes: keyword `machine-type` when present, otherwise `actor-id`; no identical conditional arms remain.
- `spawned?` still selects spawned-vs-singleton spec resolution and still appears in the output node.
- Splint no longer reports `lint/identical-branches` at `tooling.cljc` for this expression.
- Machines algebra-view tests and derivation-conformance JVM/CLJS tests pass, covering registered-type spawns, inline-definition spawns, and singleton nodes.
- Xray derivation-graph consumer tests pass and node output is unchanged for all three identity cases.
close_reason: PR #9150: collapsed machine-instance-algebra-view's three-arm source-id cond to (if (keyword? machine-type) machine-type actor-id) in tooling.cljc; the spawned? and :else arms both yielded actor-id. spawned? deliberately kept — it still selects spawned-vs-singleton spec resolution and is still emitted as the node's :spawned? field. Re-measured at branch tip: my own splint run over tooling.cljc went exit 1 with tooling.cljc:395:35 [lint/identical-branches] to exit 0 with 0 style warnings. Machines JVM suite exit 0 (1241 tests/4495 assertions) and npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11173/55748), so node output is unchanged for registered-type spawns, inline-definition spawns and singletons.

title: Remove retired cancel-on-decision spec argument from join resolution helper
description:
## Evidence

Private helper `build-resolution-fx` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc` declares `[frame-id parent-id invoke-id spec join-state'' child-id child-extra resolution]` (currently lines 790-910), but the body never reads `spec`. Its sole production call (currently line 1217) still passes `spec`. A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/machines/src` reports `join.cljc:807:33: warning: unused binding spec`; repository search finds no other call.

The dead argument is direct residue from a retired feature. Before commit `4842757f6c` (`refactor(machines): cut :spawn-all join grammar to :all/:any`, 2026-07-04), `build-resolution-fx` read `(:cancel-on-decision? spec)` to decide whether survivor cancellation should run. That commit removed the read and made cancellation unconditional, while retaining the parameter and call argument. Current validation rejects `:cancel-on-decision?`, and Spec 005 explicitly says there is no such key or non-cancelling-join protocol. Thus `spec` can no longer affect this helper by contract or implementation.

Bead searches for `build-resolution-fx`, `join resolution unused spec`, `unused spec machines join`, and `redundant spec join` found no existing issue covering this residue.

## Impact

The stale argument falsely suggests resolution fx assembly still depends on the spawn-all specification, obscuring the current invariant that survivor teardown is unconditional. It also leaves a permanent lint warning and preserves a code-level trace of the removed `:cancel-on-decision?` protocol after the grammar, validator, specs, and tests have all retired it.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `spec` from `build-resolution-fx`'s private parameter vector and from its sole call. Do not otherwise alter cancellation, completed-child reap, trace emission, or parent resolution-event ordering.

## Risks

This helper owns join-resolution teardown and dispatch ordering. Keep the change mechanical: the accepted `:all` / `:any` grammar, unconditional child destruction, cancellation reply facts, completed-child reap form, and final parent dispatch vector must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
acceptance_criteria:
- `build-resolution-fx` no longer accepts `spec`, and its sole caller no longer passes it.
- `rg -n "build-resolution-fx" implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc` shows only the updated definition, explanatory references, and the updated call; no stale arity remains.
- A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/machines/src` no longer reports `unused binding spec` at this helper.
- Existing spawn-all/join JVM and CLJS tests pass, including cancellation, completed-child reap, reply-envelope, and resolution-order coverage; the full machines JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/machines`) and consolidated CLJS suite (`npm run test:cljs` from `implementation`) remain green.
- No `:cancel-on-decision?` runtime read is reintroduced; the retired spelling remains only in explicit rejection/anti-regression documentation and tests.
close_reason: PR #9150: dropped the retired `spec` parameter from join.cljc's private `build-resolution-fx` and from its sole call. Confirmed at branch tip that the body never references spec (only occurrence in lines 790-911 was the parameter vector itself), and that the residue traces to 4842757f6c removing the (:cancel-on-decision? spec) read. clj-kondo's join.cljc:807:33 'unused binding spec' is gone; machines JVM suite exit 0 (1241 tests/4495 assertions) and npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11173/55748, 0 compile warnings), so cancellation, completed-child reap, trace emission and parent resolution ordering are unchanged.

title: Retire the unconsumed routing plan-projection helper
description:
## Problem

`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc` carries an R0 `plan-projection` helper plus `r0-projection-keys`, but no runtime, Xray, trace tool, example, skill, or conformance consumer calls it. Its only caller is the dedicated unit test. Executed navigation exposes plan evidence through the separate live `plan-trace-tags` mapping, so the on-demand projection described as a tooling feature has no remaining/realized consumer.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide symbol search finds `plan-projection` only in `resolve.cljc`, the facade's internal-seam comment, and `routing_plan_seam_test.clj`; no `tools/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, or other implementation namespace calls it.
- `r0-projection-keys` occurs only in its definition, `plan-projection`, and that same unit test.
- Whole-routing `clj-kondo` analysis reports zero production-source usages of `plan-projection` and one test usage.
- `resolve.cljc:365+` implements `plan-trace-tags`, and `navigate.cljc` plus `url_change.cljc` call that mapping on real commit branches. It does not delegate to `plan-projection` because the trace projection intentionally summarizes/redacts carrier values.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` names `:rf.route/planned`/`plan-trace-tags` as the observable projection. No API or tooling page promises the internal function.
- The API-manifest generator classifies `re-frame.routing.resolve` as internal, and the facade explicitly declines to re-export a RoutePlan constructor/projection (`routing.cljc:89-96`).
- Both helper and key list arrived in `da9c355466`; subsequent work made the trace mapping reachable but introduced no on-demand tool consumer.

## Impact

This is a test-maintained parallel feature with no consumer. It duplicates the notion of a plan projection while differing intentionally from the actual observable trace mapping, which makes future plan-field changes pay for and reason about a second projection that no product path reads. Its docstring currently overstates that Xray/trace tooling reads it.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `plan-projection`, `r0-projection-keys`, and the test whose only purpose is pinning them; update source comments that claim a tool reads the helper. Preserve the live route-plan construction and `plan-trace-tags` behavior. If an actual tool consumer is intentionally pending, require that concrete consumer and a supported access boundary to land before retaining this helper rather than keeping an internal speculative API indefinitely.

## Risks

Do not collapse `plan-trace-tags` into a raw `select-keys`: its bounded/redacted trace shape deliberately differs from the internal carrier-bearing plan. Preserve the `:rf.route/planned` contract and all real navigation-door coverage. Recheck out-of-repo/public-release commitments before deleting even though current API/manifests classify the namespace internal.

2. `:rf.route/planned` remains emitted through the live `plan-trace-tags` path from every navigation commit door with its current bounded/redacted shape.
3. Routing plan-seam, navigation, URL-change, and instrumentation tests pass, including non-vacuity for the real emitted projection.
4. Repo-wide symbol and API-manifest checks show no orphaned reference or accidental public contract after the disposition.

title: Remove the inert internal RouteAddress schema constant
description:
## Problem

`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/address.cljc` defines a public `RouteAddress` Malli-form value, but routing never reads it. Validation is independently hand-coded in `valid-address?`; the optional Schemas artefact does not import it; and the API-manifest generator classifies `re-frame.routing.address` as internal rather than an authoring namespace. The value is therefore a second, inert spelling of the route-address contract.

## Evidence

- A repo-wide symbol search finds code symbol `RouteAddress` only at `address.cljc:99`; every other hit is prose or the separate normative schema example in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`.
- `clj-kondo` whole-routing analysis reports zero var usages for `re-frame.routing.address/RouteAddress` in both source and tests.
- `valid-address?` checks `address-keys`, `:to`, `:params`, `:query`, and `:fragment` directly and never derives behavior from the Malli form.
- No namespace under `implementation/schemas/src`, core, tools, examples, or skills requires or resolves this var.
- `re-frame.routing` deliberately does not re-export address internals (`routing.cljc:89-96`), and the API-manifest generator puts `re-frame.routing.address` on its internal-namespace roster (`gen.clj:363-388`).
- Git history shows the value arrived with EP-0037 R0b in `da9c355466`; no later commit introduced a consumer.

## Impact

The dead value adds an apparent schema authority that has no enforcement role and can drift from both `valid-address?` and the normative `:rf/route-address` schema text. Because it is a public var in an internal namespace, it also creates an accidental surface that readers may mistake for a supported schema API.

## Proposed disposition

Remove the unused `RouteAddress` var and revise the nearby comments/docstrings to point to the normative `:rf/route-address` schema plus the live `valid-address?` structural gate. Do not change the accepted address shape or add a Malli dependency to the routing hot path merely to preserve the dead constant.

## Risks

Although the namespace is explicitly internal and has no in-repo consumer, search release notes and migration/API docs once more before deletion for any intentional promise of the var itself. Preserve the route-address behavior and the normative schema; this is removal of an inert implementation symbol, not removal of the RouteAddress concept.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `re-frame.routing.address/RouteAddress` is removed, while `valid-address?` accepts/rejects exactly the currently documented closed shape.
2. Address comments and docs no longer imply that routing carries or executes a Malli-form value it does not consume.
3. Focused routing address/prefetch/route-url tests pass on both relevant hosts, including closed-key, required `:to`, and typed optional-field cases.
4. API-manifest and repo-wide symbol checks show no promised public row or remaining code reference to the removed var.
5. The normative `:rf/route-address` schema in `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` remains unchanged unless an independently justified contract change is made.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip: a repo-wide search found the CODE symbol RouteAddress only at address.cljc:99 and at spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3732 (the normative schema example); every other hit is prose. No qualified (address/RouteAddress) or :refer consumer exists anywhere in implementation, tools, examples or skills. Deleted the def and replaced it with a comment pointing at the two real authorities — the normative :rf/route-address schema and the live valid-address? structural gate. The accepted address shape is unchanged and no Malli dependency was added. The hot-zone spec/Spec-Schemas.md normative example was NOT touched, per the bead's own caution. Gate: implementation/routing clojure -M:test exit 0, 553 tests / 3451 assertions / 0 failures, covering the address-extraction, prefetch and route-url closed-key, required-:to and typed-optional cases. No api-manifest row and no docs/api page named the removed var, so neither needed an edit.

title: Remove vestigial states argument from machine cofx target resolver
description:
## Evidence

`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc` defines private helper `resolve-target-path` as `[states decl-path target]` (currently lines 345-357), but its body never reads `states`; it derives the result solely from `decl-path` and `target`. A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/machines/src` reports `cofx_attach.cljc:352:4: warning: unused binding states`. Repository search finds exactly four call sites, all in the same namespace (currently lines 409, 524, 566, and 639), and each redundantly passes `states`. `git blame` / `git log -S"defn- resolve-target-path"` show the parameter has been unused since the helper was introduced in commit `9895cbd53d0` (2026-06-14), rather than being a recently disconnected input. The helper is private and has no external callers.

Searches for `resolve-target-path`, `cofx attach unused states`, `unused parameter machines cofx`, `unused binding`, and `cofx-attach` found no existing bead covering this cleanup.

## Impact

The unused argument is vestigial API inside the namespace: its name and the docstring phrase "within states" imply that target resolution validates or consults the state tree, while the function only normalises target coordinates. Every caller carries a value with no effect, and the stale parameter creates a standing lint warning that makes genuine unused bindings harder to notice.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `states` from the private helper's parameter vector, update its docstring to describe coordinate normalisation without implying a tree read, and update the four in-namespace call sites to pass only `decl-path` and `target`. Preserve the existing nil / `:same-state`, keyword sibling, vector absolute, and malformed-target cases exactly; this is a behavior-neutral arity cleanup, not a change to machine target semantics.

## Risks

The helper participates in static coeffect ensure-set closure calculation, including `:always`, `:on-done`, `:after`, and ordinary event candidates. An over-broad refactor could accidentally change those paths. Keep the change mechanical and retain all existing target branches and surrounding state-tree reads.
acceptance_criteria:
- `resolve-target-path` has two parameters (`decl-path`, `target`) and no caller passes the redundant state tree.
- `rg -n "resolve-target-path" implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/cofx_attach.cljc` shows the definition plus the same four updated call sites and no three-argument use.
- A focused clj-kondo run over `implementation/machines/src` no longer reports `unused binding states` for `cofx_attach.cljc`.
- The machines JVM suite (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/machines`) and consolidated CLJS suite (`npm run test:cljs` from `implementation`) pass, demonstrating unchanged ensure-set behavior on both runtimes.
close_reason: PR #9150: dropped the never-read `states` parameter from cofx_attach's private `resolve-target-path` and the redundant argument at its four in-namespace call sites; docstring reworded to describe coordinate normalisation rather than a state-tree read. Re-measured at branch tip: clj-kondo over implementation/machines/src went 37 warnings (incl. cofx_attach.cljc:352:4 unused binding states) to 35 with 0 unused bindings. Machines JVM suite exit 0 (1241 tests/4495 assertions); npm run test:cljs exit 0 (11173/55748, 0 compile warnings). A planted 3-arg call took the CLJS compile to exit 1 with 'Wrong number of args (3) passed to re-frame.machines.cofx-attach/resolve-target-path', confirming the gate catches a missed call site.

title: Remove routing tooling's obsolete private bundle sentinel
description:
## Problem

`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/tooling.cljc` still defines the private `bundle-isolation-sentinel` string `rf.routing.tooling/sentinel:rf2-eiiifu-2026-06-12:do-not-rename`, with a comment asserting that `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` checks that exact string. That stopped being true in commit `4e43784ec7`: the routing-tooling gate now uses the live `route-fact` node-kind literal (checker lines 422-440), while the private var has no reader.

## Evidence

- Repo-wide fixed-string search finds the opaque string only at its definition; no checker, source, test, doc, example, or tool consumes it.
- `clj-kondo` reports `re-frame.routing.tooling/bundle-isolation-sentinel` as an unused private var on both CLJ/CLJS analysis.
- The current bundle-isolation checker names `route-fact` as the routing-tooling sentinel and its positive-control module emits that live literal.
- An existing compiled positive-control bundle contains `route-fact` but not the opaque private sentinel, confirming that the old value makes no gate claim under advanced compilation.
- The checker's derivation-egress commentary (lines 504-529) documents the same failure mode: unused private sentinels are dropped by Closure, and the prior derivation-egress var was removed after its gate moved to a live literal.
- `git blame` shows the checker switched routing-tooling to `route-fact` in `4e43784ec7`, but the source var/comment remain from `119e28916c0`/`f44a288a3d5`.

## Impact

This is dead production-source data plus actively false maintenance guidance. A reader is told to keep an unobserved string in lockstep with a checker that cannot see it, and may choose the dead value when extending or debugging the isolation gate.

## Proposed disposition

Delete the private var and its stale sentinel block. Keep the gate on the live `route-fact` marker and, if source-side guidance is useful, replace the block with a short pointer to the checker's live-sentinel rationale rather than planting another unused private value.

## Risks

Do not remove or rename the checker's live `route-fact` sentinel without updating its positive-control proof. Confirm no release/source scan outside `check-bundle-isolation.cjs` relies on the old opaque value before deletion; current repo-wide searches show none.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `bundle-isolation-sentinel` and `rf.routing.tooling/sentinel:rf2-eiiifu-2026-06-12:do-not-rename` are absent from routing production source, with no stale comment claiming the checker reads them.
2. `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` still uses a live emitted routing-tooling sentinel and its routing-tooling positive control is non-vacuous.
3. The focused bundle-isolation checker/tests pass, including both absence from the counter bundle and presence in the routing-tooling positive-control module.
4. A repo-wide fixed-string search confirms there is no remaining reference that expected the removed opaque value.
close_reason: Removed in PR #9148 (worker/routevest-a). Premise re-verified at branch tip before deleting: check-bundle-isolation.cjs's routing-tooling arm asserts the live route-fact node kind (sentinel: 'route-fact'), not the opaque string, so the private var had no reader. Repo-wide fixed-string search (excluding .beads) found 'rf.routing.tooling/sentinel:rf2-eiiifu-2026-06-12:do-not-rename' at its definition only, line-oriented and via a null-data whole-file sweep; the definition site itself was the control that proved the search bites. Deleted the defonce and replaced the false comment with the house-style pointer used by resources.tooling (rf2-6r9j.54) and derivation.egress (rf2-yk2d), naming node-for and route-slice-algebra-view as the live route-fact minting paths; also corrected the self-referential ns-header sentence claiming an explicit sentinel at the foot of the ns. Gates: npm run test:bundle-isolation exit 0 (release-building lane deliberately chosen over test:scripts because only it runs check-bundle-isolation.cjs itself) reporting 40 internal sentinels absent and 40 emitted positive-control sentinels present, with its self-test's 40 sentinel-removal mutations passing; pinned clj-kondo 2026.04.15 exit 0, errors 0, and re-frame.routing.tooling/bundle-isolation-sentinel no longer appears as an unused private var.

title: core/derivation/graph.cljc:819-836 repeats rf2-yk2d's dead do-not-rename sentinel and its two false claims
description:
Found while fixing rf2-yk2d in PR #9070. implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/graph.cljc:819-836 carries the IDENTICAL defect that rf2-yk2d recorded for its egress sibling, and it was left standing because #9070's file fence did not include graph.cljc.

  (2) "The string survives :advanced because string literals are not renamed" - the var is `^:private` and nothing consumes its value, so Closure DCEs it exactly as it does the egress one.

SAME HISTORY, and the tree already records it: commit 4e43784ec7 (2026-07-15, "test: require emitted bundle isolation controls") moved BOTH entries - egress and its derivation-graph sibling, the latter onto `rf/family` - off the planted strings when these controls became emitted-module greps. check-bundle-isolation.cjs's roster comment says so in as many words. Both vars were simply left behind; #9070 removed one.

MEASURE BEFORE ACTING, do not take this bead's word for it. The check that settles it is a fixed-string grep of the EMITTED module, never the .cljc:
  grep -cF "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel:rf2-6xm07h-2026-06-12:do-not-rename" implementation/out/bundle-isolation-positive-control/derivation-graph.js
Expect 0. Run a control in the same file with the same instrument - `grep -cF "rf/family"` on the same artefact - so a zero is a measurement rather than a broken needle. Build the artefact with `npm run test:bundle-isolation` (or just the `shadow-cljs release ... bundle-isolation-positive-control` half of it) first.

SUGGESTED FIX, matching what #9070 did for egress so the two siblings stay symmetrical: remove the var, and replace the comment with one that says the sentinel for this namespace is not in this file, names `rf/family` as the literal the gate actually greps, and records that the defonce was removed. Weigh removal against keeping-and-correcting on its own merits - #9070's reasoning for removing was that a corrected comment still leaves the false `do-not-rename` instruction inside the string literal itself, and that the roster already teaches a removed literal perfectly well (its first named trap, `re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame`, no longer exists in source either).

IF THE VAR IS REMOVED, check whether check-bundle-isolation.cjs's roster comment needs a matching correction the way egress's did - #9070 had to change "still planted at the bottom of egress.cljc" to past tense. Read the `derivation-graph` roster entry's comment before deciding; the two records must agree afterwards.

DO NOT change the live sentinel (`rf/family`) or any gate behaviour. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` must still read exit 0 with 40 internal sentinels absent and 40 positive-control sentinels present - both numbers were unmoved by #9070's removal of the egress twin, which is the evidence that removing a Closure-dropped var cannot move them.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 08:2x AUSEST. REMOVE THE VAR AND ITS COMMENT BLOCK, MATCHING WHAT #9070 DID TO THE EGRESS SIBLING. AND THIS BEAD IS NOT FENCED — I measured the overlap rather than assuming it.

NOT FENCED, MEASURED. I expected this to be sequenced behind PR #9070 because that PR holds implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs, and I checked instead of assuming:
  grep -F "rf.derivation.graph/sentinel" check-bundle-isolation.cjs  -> NO HITS
  grep -F "rf.derivation.egress/sentinel" check-bundle-isolation.cjs -> ONE HIT at :515 (the control, proving the instrument works)

So nothing in that file claims the graph literal is planted, and nothing in it needs to change. THIS IS A SINGLE-FILE CHANGE TO graph.cljc.

THE RULING: REMOVE, do not correct. PR #9070's worker removed the egress var rather than correcting its comment, and gave the reason: a corrected comment still leaves the false `do-not-rename` instruction inside the STRING LITERAL ITSELF, where the next reader meets it first. That reasoning applies here unchanged and the two sites should not diverge. It also confirmed nothing consumed the egress var before removing it; do the same here.

WHAT COMES OUT: the `defonce ^:private bundle-isolation-sentinel` at graph.cljc:835-836 and the seventeen-line comment block above it at :819-833. That block asserts two things this bead measured false — that check-bundle-isolation.cjs greps the counter bundle for this exact string, and that the string survives `:advanced`. It also asserts the string "sits outside any `interop/debug-enabled?` gate so DCE cannot drop the literal independently", which is beside the point once the var itself is dropped.

MEASURE FIRST, as the bead already instructs, and do not take either the bead's word or mine. The check that settles it is a fixed-string grep of the EMITTED module, never the .cljc, with a same-file same-instrument control so a zero is a measurement rather than a broken needle. #9070's worker ran exactly this pattern and got 0 for the planted literal against a control of 1 for the live `rf.resource/opaque`.

WHAT IS NOT RULED AND STAYS THE WORKER'S CALL: whether to add a do-not-re-plant note for graph alongside the one #9070 added for egress. IF YOU CONCLUDE check-bundle-isolation.cjs NEEDS ANY EDIT, REPORT IT — DO NOT MAKE IT. That file is inside PR #9070's diff and a second toucher conflicts. MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 11:2x AUSEST, on the conflict the worker reported rather than resolving unilaterally. NO FOLLOW-UP IS WANTED. graph.cljc stays as it landed, with no sentinel comment at all.

THE CONFLICT WAS REAL AND THE WORKER WAS RIGHT TO SURFACE IT. This bead's ruling said "REMOVE THE VAR AND ITS COMMENT BLOCK, MATCHING WHAT #9070 DID TO THE EGRESS SIBLING" and enumerated both under WHAT COMES OUT. But #9070 merged mid-run and the worker read the LANDED diff rather than trusting the description: #9070 removed the var and KEPT a comment, replacing the false block with a corrected account that now opens "THE SENTINEL FOR THIS NAMESPACE IS NOT IN THIS FILE" and names rf.resource/opaque. IT FOLLOWED THE EXPLICIT ENUMERATED ACTION, which is the correct tie-break: an enumerated action outranks a comparison to a sibling that moved after the ruling was written.

WHY NO SYMMETRY FOLLOW-UP. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) The stance refuses it: "not over-engineering or gold plating... we don't need to litigate every last fine detail". A comment added so two files look alike, rather than because a reader needs it, is precisely that. (2) The two cases are NOT symmetrical in substance, which is the worker's own argument and it holds: egress MINTED a keyword and needed to explain where its sentinel went; graph ASSOCS a family marker (rf/family) it does not own, so there is less to explain. Equal treatment of unequal cases is not consistency. (3) The account already exists in two places a reader reaches first -- the roster entry (source 're-frame.derivation.graph family marker', sentinel rf/family) and check-bundle-isolation.cjs at ~:521, which the worker re-measured and found already records the graph sibling's history correctly.

title: skills: add a gate for the SKILL.md description cap — truncation is now CONFIRMED at 1,536 chars, and a second whole-listing budget can drop a description entirely
description:
Filed 2026-09-03 04:44:00 AUSEST from the skillsize-a cluster. rf2-cupfi said 'do not add a gate unless truncation is confirmed'. IT IS NOW CONFIRMED — but at a different number than that bead assumed, and the gate could not be written in that bead's PR because scripts/ was outside its fence.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, against the shipped Claude Code v2.1.258 runtime on this machine rather than from documentation:

1. THE 1,024-CHARACTER FIGURE IS NOT ENFORCED. It comes from the Agent Skills packaging spec. Claude Code's own SKILL.md frontmatter validator checks that description is a string and warns when it is missing; it applies NO length check whatsoever. No repo gate checks one either.

2. THE ENFORCED CAP IS 1,536, PER SKILL. The setting is skillListingMaxDescChars, default 1536. The listing builder applies it as a hard slice — no ellipsis, no warning in the listing the model reads, and the cut lands mid-word. The value capped is the description alone, or '<description> - <when_to_use>' when a when_to_use field is present. So the TAIL is always what is lost, which is exactly the risk rf2-cupfi identified even though it had the wrong threshold.

3. THERE IS A SECOND, BLUNTER MECHANISM rf2-cupfi did not know about. The listing also carries a TOTAL budget: context window x 4 bytes/token x skillListingBudgetFraction (default 0.01) — roughly 8,000 characters at a 200K window. When the listing exceeds it, Claude Code stops truncating tails and starts dropping ENTIRE descriptions, lowest-priority first, rendering those skills as a bare '- <name>' with nothing to route on. Skills BUNDLED with Claude Code are exempt from that pass; consumer-installed skills — every skill in skills/ — are not. This family alone totals ~10.8K characters of listing across nine skills, i.e. already past an 8,000-character budget before the consumer adds a single skill of their own.

STATE AFTER PR (all nine descriptions now load intact): re-frame2-xray 1,482 (was 1,713 and being silently cut by 177 chars — and what was cut was precisely its re-frame2-pair disqualifier, mid-word); reagent-migration 1,487; re-frame2-pair-retro 1,203; re-frame2 1,251; re-frame2-implementor 1,186; re-frame2-improver 1,150; re-frame2-setup 1,068; re-frame-migration 963; re-frame2-pair 747.

NOTE re-frame2-implementor AT 1,186: it is a SEVENTH description over the 1,024 figure that rf2-cupfi's list of six did not include. It is comfortably under the enforced 1,536 so nothing is being cut, and it was outside that bead's edit fence, so it was left alone deliberately.

WHAT THE GATE SHOULD DO, and the ordering matters more than the number:
  - fail any SKILL.md whose resolved description (folded YAML, plus ' - ' + when_to_use where present) exceeds 1,536 characters;
  - warn when the sum across skills/*/SKILL.md approaches the ~8,000-character listing budget, since that mechanism drops whole descriptions and no per-skill check can see it;
  - ideally assert that a '**Do not use**' / disqualifier clause appears BEFORE the trigger-phrase list, because ordering is what makes a truncation survivable and it is the half that actually protects routing.

The mechanism and both numbers are already recorded for authors in skills/README.md '§SKILL.md frontmatter description — the cap that actually bites'; this bead is only the machine-checked half.

CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING: 1,536 and 0.01 are DEFAULTS of user-configurable settings, and both were read out of one shipped version. Pin the gate to the documented default and cite the version, rather than treating either as a constant of the platform.
notes:

The gate now hard-fails at the portable 1,024-character Agent Skills package ceiling, retains 1,536 only as a diagnostic escalation, and separately ratchets family footprint. Update this user-visible help so it states the live contract.

The module docstring at :2 is already CORRECT ('the portable 1,024 and the Claude 1,536'), so the file contradicts itself, which is worth saying in the fix. Pair with rf2-bn5f: one worker, one contract statement across the help text and both integration comments.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9153 — exact whole-listing-budget owner reopened. The new argparse/help and both integration comments repeat that nine routing contracts cannot fit in 8,000 characters however written, so an absolute gate would have no in-repo remedy. The arithmetic disproves the premise behind that conclusion: the current footprint is 8,860, including 8,674 description characters, so clearing 8,000 needs 860 characters of trimming — about 10 percent, or 96 characters per skill on average. Bringing each description below the 1,024 maximum did not show that further shortening is impossible; a maximum is not a minimum, and several descriptions still carry long trigger/catalogue lists. This matters because the measured runtime drops whole descriptions beyond the budget. Repair the one contract across the checker docstring/help, skills/README.md, test.yml, and test-fast-pr.sh: first attempt the bounded 860-character reduction while preserving routing quality and make 8,000 the guard if it succeeds; otherwise record evidence for the product tradeoff rather than asserting mathematical impossibility. It is not: the surviving mention is in the CORRECTED text at :598-604 — 'Guard the SKILL.md description limits: the portable 1,024 and the Claude 1,536. Hard-fails a description over the 1,024-char Agent Skills packaging cap, and escalates that message when the description is ALSO past Claude Code's 1,536-char hard slice (skillListingMaxDescChars), which is otherwise only reported.' Reading the CONTEXT rather than trusting the count is what distinguished it, and a control (PACKAGE_MAX_DESC_CHARS = 12 hits) had already proved the instrument was reading the file.

title: skills: the 16 KB per-leaf byte ceiling is routinely wrong for dense teaching leaves — four beads have now ended in a recorded exception rather than a split
description:
OBSERVATION FILED, NOT ACTIONED. Filed 2026-09-03 04:44:00 AUSEST from the skillsize-a cluster (rf2-cupfi / rf2-ytkt / rf2-j5na). The brief's instruction was explicit: file this, do NOT change the ceiling — that is a maintainer's call and it is bigger than any of the individual beads.

THE PATTERN. Four beads have now reached the same disposition on the 16 KB per-leaf byte ceiling in skills/README.md 'Leaf size discipline', and in every one the honest answer was a recorded exception rather than a split:

  rf2-baso  skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md  261 L / 39,701 B  2.4x
  rf2-ytkt  skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/reg-machine.md 208 L / 20,599 B  1.26x
  rf2-ytkt  skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/spawn.md       199 L / 19,236 B  1.17x
  rf2-j5na  skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md                   220 L / 46,461 B  2.84x
  (and recipes.md, 424 L / 46,086 B, bound by the same rf2-j5na record)

All byte figures LF-normalised and re-measured at 495e70b600.

THE SHAPE OF THE EVIDENCE. rf2-ytkt's own notes record eight FURTHER leaves across three more partitions hitting the identical wall (websocket, resources, form-action, resources-mutations, testing, privacy-and-elision, routing, stories), so the count of leaves is roughly ten, not four. Two leaves WERE brought inside both ceilings by de-duplication (cofx.md 18,865->16,311; forms.md 17,510->16,310) and testing.md was genuinely split, so the ceiling is NOT unreachable in general — the point is narrower and therefore more interesting.

WHY THE CEILING MISFIRES ON THESE LEAVES SPECIFICALLY. The overrun is DENSITY, not duplication. These leaves run 57-78 prose lines carrying 16-23 KB, i.e. 236-315 BYTES PER PROSE LINE (reg-machine.md 68 prose lines / 17,765 B = 261 B/line; spawn.md 65 / 15,360 = 236 B/line). Only 2,680 B of reg-machine.md and 3,757 B of spawn.md are code fences. skills/README.md says the byte ceiling exists precisely to catch leaves whose long unwrapped prose lines pass the line count while still loading tokens — so on these leaves the catch is a TRUE POSITIVE about density that has no available remedy, because both remedies the contract offers are measured unavailable:

  (a) de-duplication is exhausted — a shingle scan over reg-machine.md returns ZERO intra-file near-duplicate pairs at a 0.30 Jaccard threshold;
  (b) splitting fails the catalogue test's OWN criterion in the direction that FORBIDS it — an author needs the whole of one canonical declaration, so a split raises tokens-per-session rather than lowering it, and it costs SKILL.md routing rows and cross-partition roster rows.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS CONCRETE, re-measured at my own base rather than quoted: spawn.md's :spawn-all section is exactly 1,950 B. Moving it WHOLESALE to a new leaf leaves 17,286 B — still 902 B OVER the ceiling. A remedy that provably cannot reach its own target is not a remedy, and that is what turned rf2-ytkt from a re-run into a ruling.

THE QUESTION FOR THE MAINTAINER, which is a question about the CONTRACT rather than about any leaf. When four rulings in one session all end in 'recorded exception', the exception has stopped being exceptional. Options, none of which this bead takes:
  1. Leave the ceiling and keep recording exceptions (status quo; the cost is that each one needs a mayor ruling).
  2. Raise the byte ceiling for reference/catalogue leaves specifically, keeping the 250-line half as the primary discriminator.
  3. Replace the flat byte ceiling with the test that is already doing the real work — 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?' — and keep bytes as a prompt to ask that question rather than as a threshold.
  4. Express the ceiling per PROSE LINE (the 236-315 B/line figures above) so density is measured directly instead of inferred.

DO NOT ACT ON THIS WITHOUT MIKE. Nothing is broken, no gate is red, and every affected leaf now carries a recorded exception with its reasoning, so the tree is self-consistent as it stands.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 07:2x AUSEST. WIDEN THE CARVE-OUT; DO NOT MOVE THE NUMBER, DO NOT ADD A GATE, DO NOT SPLIT THE LEAVES.

TWO PREMISES I CHECKED AT SOURCE RATHER THAN INHERITING, AND ONE OF THEM CHANGES WHAT THIS BEAD IS ABOUT.

(1) THE RULE IS ALREADY "SHOULD", NOT "MUST". skills/README.md:240 reads "each leaf file SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (target ~150 lines / ~10 KB)".

(2) NOTHING ENFORCES IT. Measured: a fixed-string search for "16 KB", "16384" and "16_384" across scripts/, implementation/scripts/ and .github/ returns ZERO files. There is no gate. So no bead has ever gone red on this ceiling, and none can.

THAT REFRAMES THE COST. The bead reads as "a ceiling is wrong and keeps failing people". It is not failing anything mechanical. What it costs is FOUR-PLUS WORKER CYCLES SPENT RE-DERIVING THE SAME EXCEPTION, each recorded on its own bead where the next author will not find it. The defect is that the page does not carry the answer, so every author reaches it alone.

AND THE PAGE ALREADY HAS THE RIGHT TEST. skills/README.md:246-253 carves out catalogue-shaped leaves on a real test: "would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?", with known-frictions.md worked through it - one trigger, scanned whole, a reader cannot know in advance which half holds their case, so a split loads both.

THE DENSE TEACHING LEAF PASSES THAT SAME TEST FOR A DIFFERENT REASON, AND THE PAGE NAMES ONLY THE FIRST REASON. A catalogue is scanned whole because it is unordered; a teaching leaf is READ whole because it is a single arc - reg-machine.md is not a bag of entries, it teaches one thing end to end, and half of it loads on the same trigger as the other half. Same test, same answer, second shape.

THE RULING.

1. Widen the carve-out to name the dense-teaching-leaf shape alongside the catalogue shape, under the UNCHANGED token test. One added shape, one worked example - reg-machine.md or ops.md, pick whichever reads clearer.

2. Record the measured leaves as exempt on that test, with their figures, so the next author CITES the record instead of re-deriving it. That is the whole point of the edit: turn four scattered bead-notes into one line on the page that owns the rule.

3. The 16 KB figure and the 250-line figure BOTH STAY. They are right for most leaves and the corpus audit behind them is cited at :255-257. Raising a number to stop it being exceeded is how a target stops meaning anything.

4. NO GATE. There is no gate today and adding one would convert a judgement into a refusal, on a rule whose whole content is "apply this test". That is the gold-plating this project's stance names.

WHY THIS WAY UNDER THE STANCE. "Trust the programmer" and "do not drown in the minutiae" both point the same way here: the author applying a stated test is the mechanism, and the repair is one prose edit to the section that already owns it. The alternative readings - move the number, gate the number, split ten dense leaves - each cost more and buy less.

WHAT I AM NOT RULING. Whether any INDIVIDUAL leaf should still be split on its merits. That stays the author's call at the time, which is exactly what a SHOULD is for.
close_reason: Landed on main via PR #9065 (89c56b38cd), one file, skills/README.md +30/-1. The mayor ruling of 2026-09-03 implemented as written: the Leaf size discipline carve-out now names the dense-teaching-leaf shape alongside the catalogue shape under the UNCHANGED token test, the measured exempt leaves are recorded with their figures so the next author cites them instead of re-deriving them, and the honest qualifier stays (two leaves were brought inside both ceilings by de-duplication, testing.md was genuinely split). Neither the 16 KB nor the 250-line figure moved, no gate was added, no leaf was split. The worker corrected three of my premises and I accepted all three: ops.md is catalogue-shaped rather than dense-teaching so reg-machine.md became the worked example; testing.md is still 1.48x over after its split, so the page says only that it was split; and a LEAF-SIZE gate does exist (check_skill_migration_o1617_router_drift.py, MAX_LEAF_LINES = 60) though it enforces a different rule on two named router leaves, leaving my premise that nothing enforces the README ceiling intact. Gates: check_doc_slugs self-test and live scan both exit 0, check_skill_package_refs self-test and --ci both exit 0, check_readme_links --ci exit 0; coverage established from both sides at source and proved by a planted fault that reds doc-slugs and leaves readme-links silent. Follow-up rf2-szwq filed for the two authoring-prompt files that restate the figures instead of deferring.

title: defwrapper CALLS a hook whose value may be a COMPONENT — the sharp edge under rf2-nvcp
description:
Discovered while fixing rf2-nvcp (PR #9050). NOT urgent: no known live instance
remains, and this is a design question rather than a defect.

`defwrapper` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_artefact.cljc) emits, for an
`:apply` arity, a body of the shape `(if-let [f (late-bind/get-fn <hook>)] (apply f args) <absent>)`.
That is correct for every hook whose value is a FUNCTION. It is silently wrong for
a hook whose value is a COMPONENT, because a component that is CALLED never becomes
a component: on Reagent it renders inside its caller's component instance, so it
reads that instance's React context rather than its own, and any `:contextType`
the head carries is inert.

That is exactly how rf2-nvcp blanked every routed application. `rf/route-link` is
a defwrapper over `:routing/route-link`, whose value was the registered
`:route/link` view head. The head was called, not mounted, so `(.-context cmp)`
answered React's empty default and route-link-render's render-time
`require-current-frame!` raised `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on FIRST RENDER.

rf2-nvcp fixed it at the PUBLICATION side — the hook now carries an
element-emitting shim, `[(views/view-head :route/link) props & children]` — which
is the right fix for that bead and leaves defwrapper untouched. `route-link` is
the only component-valued hook in the table today, so nothing else is currently
broken.

THE QUESTION, for whoever holds core: should `defwrapper` be able to say "this
hook's value is a component, emit an element rather than a call" — a body-kind
beside `:delegate` / `:apply` / the recursion form — so the next
component-valued hook cannot repeat this by construction? Or is
publish-an-element the convention, in which case the constraint belongs in the
late-bind directory's contract prose for any such hook rather than in the macro?

Note the failure mode when weighing it: nothing errors, nothing warns, the unit
suites stay green (they call the render fn directly under `rf/with-frame`, which
answers from the dynamic-var tier), and the symptom is a blank page in a real
browser only. rf2-nvcp went ~2.5 months undetected on exactly that profile.

Fence note: rf2-nvcp's worker could not touch `core_routing.cljc` or
`core_artefact.cljc` (held / out of fence), which is why this is filed rather
than folded in.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 04:5x AUSEST. MEASURE FIRST, AND THE MEASUREMENT DECIDES. Do not start by designing a defwrapper change.

THE BEAD IS RIGHT THAT THIS IS A DESIGN QUESTION AND NOT URGENT — the publication-side fix landed with rf2-nvcp and route-link is no longer an instance. But "no KNOWN live instance" is not "no live instance", and the whole reason this class is dangerous is that it fails SILENTLY: a component that is called instead of mounted reads its callers React context, any :contextType on the head is inert, and nothing errors until something downstream needs the context. rf2-nvcp is what that looks like when it finally surfaces — every routed application blank on first render, for two and a half months, with every existing test green.

STEP 1, AND IT SETTLES THE REST: CENSUS EVERY defwrapper HOOK AND CLASSIFY ITS VALUE AS FUNCTION OR COMPONENT. That is a bounded, mechanical question with a real answer. Report the full list, not just the hits.
  - IF THE CENSUS FINDS ANOTHER COMPONENT-VALUED HOOK, this stops being a design question: it is a live defect of the same class that blanked every routed app, and it should be reported as such before anything is designed. Fix it the way rf2-nvcp did — at the PUBLICATION side, with an element-emitting shim — because that fix is proven and leaves defwrapper untouched.
  - IF THE CENSUS FINDS NONE, the honest answer under the stance is to RECORD THE CONSTRAINT where the next author will meet it: a defwrapper :apply hook value must be a FUNCTION, because the emitted body CALLS it, and a component that is called never becomes a component. Put that in defwrapper own docstring in core_artefact.cljc, with rf2-nvcp named as the worked instance. Do not build a runtime check for a constraint with zero live violations — that is gold plating, and the stance says so.

WHAT I AM EXPLICITLY NOT ORDERING: do not change defwrapper emission shape to handle component values. The :apply arity is correct for functions, which is what every other hook is; teaching it a second calling convention to accommodate one case that has already been fixed elsewhere buys nothing and costs a fork in a hot code path.

AND IF THE CENSUS TURNS OUT TO BE HARD TO RUN — if hook values are not statically determinable — SAY SO AND STOP. That is a finding, and it would mean the constraint cannot be checked by any means, which changes the answer to the docstring option by default rather than by preference.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9050 — reopened the exact follow-on for two residual contract carriers. The runtime repair is correct, and PR #9060 later documented the general defwrapper constraint, but current tip still says the opposite at the worked instance: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_routing.cljc:67-69 says the CLJS hook publishes the Reagent-wrapped render fn returned by reg-view*, and implementation/routing/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:87-89 repeats that model. PR #9050 deliberately changed the hook to publish route-link-element, an element-emitting shim that resolves and mounts the current view head; publishing the head itself is the failure shape that blanked routed apps. Minimal completion: update these two statements to the element-emitting contract. No runtime/macro change or new gate.

title: spec(008-Testing): the poll-until CLJS example calls done in a downstream .catch — the carrier the skill copied from
description:

half did not: spec/ was outside that dispatch's allowed paths.

TRUTH AT TIP, verified by reading: spec/008-Testing.md, under "#### poll-until
example", carries the CLJS fence

    (deftest cross-frame-drain
      (async done
        (-> (ts/poll-until ...)
            (.then (fn [_] (is ...) (done)))
            (.catch (fn [e] (is false ...) (done))))))

which is exactly the shape implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc
warns against in poll-until's own CLJS docstring: "Put the rejection handler
UPSTREAM of the single trailing step that calls `done`, and call `done` exactly
once with nothing after it (rf2-d3tc / rf2-qpns / rf2-fyba). `cljs.test/run-block`
hands `done` a continuation that runs the WHOLE REMAINDER of the run
synchronously, so a `.catch` sitting downstream of `done` claims whatever a
later namespace throws as this row's failure -- printing it against this row's
label -- and then calls `done` a SECOND time, which re-forces `run-block`'s
unrealized delay and re-runs the offending namespace."

#9034 cited this exact fence as its authority. Leaving it means the next skill
pass can re-derive the defective shape from it, which is the loop the rf2-519x5
audit note explicitly asked to close ("repair both carriers rather than letting
the skill copy it again").

FIX SHAPE: rewrite that one fence to the docstring's prescribed shape --
assertion .then, rejection .catch that reports and returns nil, ONE trailing
.then that calls done. Consider whether the surrounding prose should name the
run-block reason, as the skill leaf now does. Nothing else in 008 moves.

HOT ZONE: spec/008-Testing.md is a spec file -- sequence it, do not parallel it
with another spec toucher.
