title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): known-frictions.md is saturated at 3 bytes under the 16 KB leaf ceiling — the next addition forces a split
description:
CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md sits at 241 lines / 16,381 LF-normalised bytes against the family ceiling in skills/README.md (Leaf size discipline: each leaf SHOULD be <=250 lines AND <=16 KB, i.e. 16,384 bytes). That is 3 bytes of headroom and 9 lines. Measured at tip after PR #9016.

HISTORY. PR #9006 left it at 241 lines / 16,336 bytes (48 B headroom) and its author predicted the next addition would force a split. rf2-wz1qa (PR #9016) was that next addition: its three corrections cost ~96 bytes gross, which did not fit, so two genuine restatements were trimmed to pay for them -- 'cross-reference the live catalogue rather than the skill's docs alone -- a live-catalogue check is' shortened to 'cross-reference the live catalogue -- that check is', and 'the pair-MCP conformance corpus' to 'the conformance corpus'. Both were honest de-duplications, and that seam is now spent: there is no comparable restatement left to trade.

IMPACT. The leaf is the skill's one on-demand reference and is still growing (rf2-vdqr9 is an open item against this same file, and would breach on its own). The next author either breaches the ceiling silently -- nothing gates it, wc -l -c is the only instrument -- or trims load-bearing content under time pressure.

DECISION NEEDED (not taken here, deliberately). Three options, and this is a judgement call rather than a mechanical fix:
(a) SPLIT the leaf by friction family. But SKILL.md routes to exactly one on-demand leaf and the family rule is one-level routing, so a split needs a routing decision, not just a file move.
(b) CLAIM the catalogue exemption. skills/README.md already carves one out: 'catalogue-shaped leaves (for example re-frame2-pair/references/recipes.md) may exceed the ceiling if splitting would multiply file-handle overhead without reducing tokens-per-session.' known-frictions.md is a catalogue of friction classes and plausibly qualifies -- the stated test is 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?', and since the whole leaf loads on one trigger, a split arguably would not.
(c) TRIM content rather than structure, accepting the loss.

(b) looks strongest on the file's own shape and is much the cheapest, but it is a family-contract call the mayor/Mike should make, not a worker.

GATE. None -- the ceiling has no gate. wc -l -c before and after, plus check_doc_slugs.py if the routing changes.

Filed from PR #9016 (rf2-wz1qa + rf2-fpeig) rather than splitting on worker initiative, per the dispatch brief.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 00:1x AUSEST — OPTION (b), THE CATALOGUE EXEMPTION, IS TAKEN. Recorded as MY call rather than Mike's so he can reverse it cheaply; the bead correctly refused to take it on worker initiative.

MEASURED AT bddc39f415 BEFORE RULING: 241 lines, 16,622 raw bytes, 16,381 LF-normalised. Ceiling at skills/README.md:239 is <=250 lines AND <=16 KB (16,384). So 3 bytes and 9 lines of headroom — the bead's figures reproduce exactly.

WHY (b) AND NOT (a) OR (c). The exemption at skills/README.md:245-248 states its own test: 'would splitting reduce total tokens loaded per session?' known-frictions.md is loaded on ONE trigger — the retro's pattern-check step, SKILL.md:81 — and the whole leaf is consulted to answer 'is this a one-off or a product gap?', which is a question you answer by scanning the classes until one matches. A session cannot know in advance WHICH half holds its friction, so a split into two sibling leaves would load both on most sessions and add a file handle and a routing hop for nothing. The test therefore answers NO for this leaf, which is precisely the case the exemption exists for. (a) is refused on that reasoning, not on the routing objection the bead raises — a split into two siblings is still one level deep and would not be a SKILL->A->B chain. title: re-frame.hicasso.server/render is blind to sub exceptions on a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host: cold reads go through compute-sub, whose :rf.error/sub-exception is stamped :frame nil
notes:
CARRIED FORWARD FROM SLICE E (rf2-8arzr.5, now closed) BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. Filed so a measured finding does not die with the bead that found it.

THE FINDING, as slice E measured it: the per-frame `pending-error-trace?` buffer reads CLEAN on exactly the failure it was named for. Hicasso s cold reads go through pure `compute-sub`, and `compute-sub` s `:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION -- it is a pure fn with no frame in scope to stamp. `re-frame.ssr.error-listener` buckets by frame address (`pending-error-traces` swap at error_listener.cljc:178, keyed by `frame/frame-address`), so a `:frame nil` record is not in any frame s bucket and a per-frame peek finds nothing.

WHAT SLICE E DID ABOUT IT: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (the new body-only entry, implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:331) watches the ALWAYS-ON error-emit stream instead of the per-frame buffer, so the new crossing path is not affected. That was the right local fix and it shipped.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN: `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` (server.cljs:145), the DOCUMENT door used by a JVM-local Hicasso SSR host, has the same blindness today and was not changed. A sub that throws during a Hicasso server render can therefore go unreported on that path.

NOT A DOCS PROBLEM -- CHECKED. Slice F was asked to verify whether any doc describes the blind instrument as though it worked, and none does. docs/core/hicasso/18-ssr-and-hydration.md s error content is declaration/boot errors (`:rf.error/hicasso-host-bad-ssr-policy`, `:rf.error/hicasso-bad-host-declaration`, `:rf.error/ssr-missing-payload-policy`) and the `window is not defined` Render-assertion case; it makes no claim about sub-exception detection during a server render. spec/009:2125 s `pending-error-trace peek` sentence is about `:rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed`, a DIFFERENT path (error-view rendering under the Ring host) that IS frame-stamped and does work. So nothing needed correcting in prose, and slice F corrected nothing here.

SIZING NOTE for whoever takes it: the likely fix is the one slice E already made one file over -- move `render` s detection to the always-on error-emit stream the way `render-body` does -- so this is probably small and has a worked precedent in the same namespace. Worth confirming that `:frame nil` is the only leak before changing anything: `error_listener.cljc:85-100` carries a long comment about a related skip whose reasoning is adjacent and worth reading first.
MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-03 00:3x AUSEST — THIS AND rf2-ypom ARE ONE DEFECT, REACHED FROM TWO DIRECTIONS, AND THEY ARE DISPATCHED TOGETHER. rf2-ct24 was carried forward from slice E; rf2-ypom was filed by the PR #8997 audit. Both name re-frame.hicasso.server/render (server.cljs:145) as blind to recovered sub errors, and both prescribe the same fix: give it the verdict render-body already has. Verified at source at 76ffd860b4 — render is at :145, render-body at :331, and the :errors listener is registered at :323 and unregistered at :413, entirely inside render-body's extent. render has no corresponding registration.

NEITHER IS CLOSED AS A DUPLICATE, because each carries measured evidence the other does not: rf2-ct24 has slice E's mechanism (compute-sub stamps :frame nil BY CONSTRUCTION, being a pure fn with no frame in scope, so error_listener.cljc's per-frame bucketing at ~:178 can never see it) plus the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom has the acceptance criteria (a throwing sub through server/render must get :rf.error/ssr-render-failed, a non-throwing control must return the existing shape unchanged, and the listener and request frame must be released on success, on refusal, and on a direct render throw). One PR closes both with a cross-reference each way.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9035 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9035), the same PR that closes rf2-ypom — SAME DEFECT reached from two directions, cross-referenced both ways. This bead carried slice E's measured mechanism and the instruction to read error_listener.cljc:85-100 first; rf2-ypom carried the acceptance criteria. One fix, one PR.

THE FIX: re-frame.hicasso.server/render now watches the always-on :errors stream for its render extent and raises :rf.error/ssr-render-failed on any recovered record — the fix this bead's sizing note predicted, the one slice E had already made one file over. The doors share the lifecycle helpers but register under DIFFERENT ids (::render-recovered-error / ::render-body-recovered-error), because the shipped single id's justification rested on the sidecar isolate's one-render-at-a-time guarantee, which is render-body's premise and not render's.

THE BEAD'S QUESTION ANSWERED: ':frame nil is the only leak' — NO, and error_listener.cljc:85-100 is exactly where the adjacent reasoning starts. Those lines are the :rf.error/ssr-ring-error-view-failed paragraph, the second member of non-projection-eligible-errors: a record that is well-formed AND frame-stamped and still never reaches the buffer, skipped so a re-buffered trace cannot flip a 4xx to a 5xx under a custom projector plus a future re-flush. Reading error-emit-projection-listener out, it buffers only when ALL THREE hold: (1) the category is outside that skip set; (2) (:frame record) is non-nil — the leak this bead names, which compute-sub produces by construction; (3) (error-projector/server-frame? frame-id), i.e. the frame's :platform is :server.

CONDITION 3 IS A SECOND LEAK ON THIS DOOR SPECIFICALLY, and it is the finding worth more than the fix: render does NOT set :platform :server on its per-request frame — only render-body does — so on render the buffer could not fill even for a correctly frame-stamped record. Leaks 2 and 3 each independently suffice. NOT repaired here: giving render a :platform would change client-only-fx gating for every existing caller, well outside a bounded correctness fix. Flagged for whoever wants it.

The fix is unaffected and better justified than argued: the always-on stream sits upstream of all three conditions. refuse-recovered-render-error!'s docstring previously asserted the false premise this bug is made of — that a JVM host is survivable because the same process holds the record — and now states the three measured conditions instead.

WITNESS: implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/server_render_recovered_error_ssr_cljs_test.cljs (refusal, non-throwing control, release of frame AND listener on all three exits, and the two doors' ids read from INSIDE each render). One existing row changed — see rf2-ypom's close reason for the frame_doors_ssr ambient-read row and the deliberate bluntness of the verdict.

GATES on the rebased tree: hicasso node lane 1176 tests / 4386 assertions / 0 failures, captured exit 0; fast-PR spine captured exit 0.

title: skill(re-frame2-setup): first_counter_derivation.clj silently regenerates on any argument, and its writeback dirties the tree on Windows (LF + a stray blank line)
description:
FOUND while running gates for PR #9012 (rf2-pygpw/0ddz3/6uq6n cluster).

CLAIM. skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/first_counter_derivation.clj is documented in README.md and spec/design.md as the script that renders the two generated regions from the template. A worker reasonably reaches for a no-write verification mode.

TRUTH AT TIP. There is no such mode and no argument parsing at all: the script has no reference to *command-line-args*, and its last act is an unconditional (spit leaf (replace-region (slurp leaf) region)) at line 246. So 'bb tests/first_counter_derivation.clj --check' does NOT check — the argument is ignored, the script runs its normal generate-and-write path, exits 0, and the operator reads the 0 as a passing check. That is the failure-open shape: a well-formed green from an instrument that did the opposite of what was asked.

SECOND, and what makes it visible: the writeback is not byte-idempotent on Windows. Running it against an unmodified tip checkout leaves BOTH leaves modified — references/first-counter.md and references/entry-namespace.md — each with exactly one added blank line, plus git warning 'LF will be replaced by CRLF the next time Git touches it' on both. The committed files are CRLF; the script writes LF. The content is otherwise correct: bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj Lock 0 (first-counter-region-is-the-template-render) passes at 35 tests / 271 assertions both before and after, so this is a line-ending and trailing-newline artifact of the writeback, NOT drift in the rendered region.

IMPACT. Low severity, but it fails open twice over. A worker who runs it 'to verify' gets a green that verified nothing AND a dirty tree carrying two files they did not edit — which, staged with a careless 'git add', lands a spurious whitespace diff on two drift-locked generated leaves. It was caught here only because the tree was checked for staged .beads before pushing.

FIX SHAPE (skills/re-frame2-setup/** only). Either (a) reject unknown arguments — fail closed with a usage line, which is the cheap half and kills the failure-open read on its own; and/or (b) add a real --check that renders and diffs without writing, since that is what callers evidently want. Separately, make the writeback preserve the leaf's existing line endings (or normalise on read) so a no-op regeneration is a no-op on Windows too.

GATE. bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj stays the drift gate and is unaffected. Verify by hand: from a clean tip checkout, run the script with a junk argument and assert git status is clean afterwards.

ACCEPTANCE. An unrecognised argument does not silently trigger a write; a no-op regeneration on Windows leaves git status clean.

NOT a blocker for PR #9012 — the two files were restored there and verified identical by git blob hash.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #9036 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9036). Both symptoms reproduced from a clean checkout first, then fixed.

(1) Ignored argument. 'bb tests/first_counter_derivation.clj --check' wrote both leaves and exited 0 - the script parsed no arguments at all. It now fails CLOSED on any argument before a byte is written, mirroring the template's own hooks/gate-arg-keys! (which this script already loads for its substitution values). Chose the bead's option (a), not (b): the script only ever writes, so no argument is meaningful, and rather than growing a second checker the usage line routes the caller to the no-write check that already exists - 'bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj'. That avoids a divergent second source of truth. Junk argument now exits 2 with nothing written.

(2) Dirty tree - two distinct causes, and separating them was the substance. A REAL content change: replace-region emitted a newline the tail already carried, appending a blank line per leaf. The bead says 'exactly one'; it is in fact CUMULATIVE - three runs produced three added lines per leaf. A PHANTOM modification: the LF writeback over CRLF-checked-out leaves is not a content change at all (git diff empty, git hash-object --path matches the committed blob) but git status reports the file modified and every later git command warns 'LF will be replaced by CRLF'. Fixed by rendering on LF (the convention setup_drift_test.clj already uses, since LF is what git stores) and restoring the leaf's existing endings on write.

Verified: three consecutive regenerations leave git status CLEAN, both leaves' blob hashes identical to the committed objects, CRLF preserved (401/185 CRLF, 0 bare LF). bb tests/setup_drift_test.clj green at 35 tests / 271 assertions, captured exit 0, and proven to read this worktree by planted fault (exit 1, 11 failures naming the plant; restore verified by blob hash 99af663ea1a3137cf5861b55e995f811b8b701d4).

title: ssr-node has no distribution channel: package.json is private:true and the repo publishes no npm artefact, so the crossing recipe cannot tell an operator how to obtain the sidecar
notes:
FOUND BY SLICE F (rf2-8arzr.6), 2026-09-02, at base de3f2a00038. Slice F was told to "locate the release/distribution roster by grepping re-frame2-ssr-ring under .github/workflows/ and scripts/, and add the ssr-node package wherever shippable artefacts are enumerated". THAT PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD: there is nowhere honest to add it, because ssr-node is not a shippable artefact today and making it one is an operator decision rather than a docs sweep.

MEASURED at that base:
- implementation/ssr-node/package.json declares `"private": true` (and `"name": "@day8/re-frame2-ssr-node"`, `"version": "0.1.0"`). npm refuses to publish a private package.
- `grep -rn "npm publish|NPM_TOKEN|registry.npmjs" .github/ scripts/` returns NOTHING. The repo has no npm publishing path at all, for any package.
- .github/workflows/release.yml publishes Maven/Clojars artefacts only. Its jobs are verify-version-lockstep, test, deploy-core, deploy-leaf, deploy-ssr-ring, deploy-hicasso, github-release. The GitHub-release body (:936-949) enumerates fourteen `day8/re-frame2-*` Clojars coordinates and nothing else.
- .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh:100-140 keys ARTEFACT_PATHS off implementation/*/deps.edn entries carrying a :clein/build alias. ssr-node has NO deps.edn and no :clein/build, so the inventory guard at that site correctly leaves it alone -- it is not an omission there, it is out of that mechanism s domain entirely.

So the roster is a Clojars/Maven roster. Adding a plain Node package to it would be wrong in kind, not merely premature.

WHAT THE README ALREADY ASSUMES: implementation/ssr-node/README.md s Deployment section tells an operator to run `re-frame2-ssr-node --module <bundle>` -- the `bin` name from that same private manifest. There is no documented way to get that binary onto a production host. Today the honest answer is "from a checkout of this repo", and the recipe slice F wrote (docs/ssr/concepts.md §Render on Node) uses the bare command without claiming an install channel, which is accurate but incomplete.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS (Mike s, not a worker s): does the sidecar ship? Three coherent answers.
(a) Publish to npm -- drop `private: true`, add an npm publish job to release.yml with a token, and put the package on the release body s roster beside the Clojars coordinates. Version lockstep would then need a fourth mechanism, since the existing one is deps.edn/:clein-shaped.
(b) Vendored-only, deliberately -- keep it private, and say so in the README and the recipe: operators copy the package tree into their deployment. Cheapest, and defensible pre-alpha.
(c) Ship it inside an existing artefact s jar as a resource the JVM host can unpack.

Until one of those is ruled, the recipe and the README should not imply an install channel that does not exist. NOT URGENT: pre-alpha, and (b) is the de facto status quo and works.
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST — SPLIT THE BEAD. DO THE HONEST-DOCS HALF NOW; THE SHIPPABILITY HALF IS MIKE'S AND GOES BEHIND THE PUBLISHING CHAIN.

Slice F refuted its OWN dispatch premise here and that refutation is the bead's most valuable content: it was told to grep for the release roster and add ssr-node wherever shippable artefacts are enumerated, and it established there is NOWHERE HONEST TO ADD IT. Measured: package.json declares private:true; a grep for npm publish / NPM_TOKEN / registry.npmjs across .github/ and scripts/ returns NOTHING, so the repo has no npm publishing path AT ALL for any package; release.yml publishes Maven/Clojars only and its GitHub-release body enumerates fourteen Clojars coordinates and nothing else; and verify-version-lockstep.sh keys its inventory off implementation/*/deps.edn entries carrying a :clein/build alias, which ssr-node has none of — so the inventory guard is not omitting it, it is correctly out of scope there. A worker sent to 'add it to the roster' would have had to invent a roster.

THE HALF THAT IS MIKE'S. Publishing an npm artefact from a repo that publishes none is a new distribution capability, not a docs sweep — a product call about what this project ships and supports. It also belongs behind the publishing chain that already holds seven items (rf2-uelji -> rf2-fo4ng -> rf2-kmqx3), because the same question — what gets published under what identity, and who verifies the group — is unresolved one level up. Surfaced to Mike; not dispatched.

THE HALF THAT IS DISPATCHABLE TODAY, and it is the half the bead's TITLE actually names: 'the crossing recipe cannot tell an operator how to obtain the sidecar'. That is a docs-truth defect with an honest answer available right now — say how an operator obtains it TODAY (from the repo, by the route that actually works) and state plainly that no published artefact exists and none is planned as of this writing. That is shippable, costs nothing, and does not pre-empt the product call. What it must NOT do is imply a package is coming, or invent a coordinate; a recipe that names an unpublished coordinate is worse than one that says there is none.

VERIFY BEFORE WRITING: re-run the three measurements above at current tip rather than trusting them — they were taken at de3f2a00038 and #9024 has since changed that tree.
DOCS HALF RESOLVED BY PR #9040, 2026-09-03. THE SHIPPABILITY HALF IS NOT ADDRESSED AND REMAINS HELD FOR MIKE — this bead is closed on the docs half ONLY, per the mayor ruling above, and the product call is untouched.

THE THREE MEASUREMENTS RE-RUN AT CURRENT TIP, as the ruling required. All three still hold; the premise has not moved since de3f2a00038:
(a) implementation/ssr-node/package.json still declares private: true, name @day8/re-frame2-ssr-node, version 0.1.0, bin re-frame2-ssr-node -> ./bin/serve.cjs.
(b) grep -rnE 'npm publish|NPM_TOKEN|registry.npmjs' .github/ scripts/ returns ZERO hits (exit 1). CONTROLLED: the same instrument over CLOJARS_USERNAME|CLOJARS_PASSWORD returns four workflow files, so the zero is a real absence rather than a broken pattern.
(c) release.yml's jobs are exactly verify-version-lockstep, test, deploy-core, deploy-leaf, deploy-ssr-ring, deploy-hicasso, github-release; the release body enumerates 14 day8/re-frame2-* Clojars coordinates and nothing else.

ONE THING THIS BEAD DID NOT MEASURE, now measured: there are FOUR release workflows, not one — release.yml plus release-story, release-xray, release-machines-viz. Measurement (b) spans all of .github/, so 'the repo has no npm publishing path at all' is confirmed across all four rather than inferred from one. That strengthens the bead's conclusion rather than weakening it.

ONE OF THIS BEAD'S PREMISES DID NOT HOLD AS STATED. It says 'There is no documented way to get that binary onto a production host.' The README's 'Using it' section already documented one — private, 'installed from its directory rather than a registry', npm install <checkout>/implementation/ssr-node or a file: entry — and it PREDATES this bead (added by 4bab8df1ae, an ancestor of this bead's own base de3f2a00038). What was genuinely missing is what this bead's TITLE names, and that is what was fixed: the crossing recipe's step 5 gave the bare command with no account of its provenance, the README's Deployment recipe named the binary at step 2 the same way, and NEITHER said that no published artefact exists.

WHAT LANDED: docs/ssr/concepts.md section Render on Node step 5, and implementation/ssr-node/README.md section Deployment, both now state plainly that there is no published artefact, the package is not on npm, it has no Clojars coordinate, none is planned as of this writing, and the repository publishes JVM artefacts only. The route that works TODAY is a checkout — installed from the package directory, a file: entry to the same effect, or the tree copied onto the host and run with node bin/serve.cjs. Because the manifest resolves nothing, copying the tree IS the install, and the version deployed is the checkout it came from, so pin that checkout as deliberately as the JVM artefact versions in the same release. NO COORDINATE IS INVENTED AND NO PACKAGE IS IMPLIED.

STILL HELD, UNTOUCHED, MIKE'S CALL: whether the sidecar ships. package.json keeps private: true, no npm publish job was added, release.yml was not edited, and the three options this bead sets out — (a) publish to npm, (b) vendored-only by decision, (c) ship inside an existing artefact's jar — remain open, behind the publishing chain rf2-uelji -> rf2-fo4ng -> rf2-kmqx3 as the ruling placed them. title: MIGRATION.md M-51 calls the unary reg-fx failure a language-level arity error; the skill's three leaves class it SILENT on CLJS (the failure-visibility axis that picks the sweep method)
notes:
FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING rf2-a75ai (PR #9010), which added an M-51 section to skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md. Not fixed there: MIGRATION.md is a one-toucher hot-zone file and the worker's write scope was skills/re-frame-migration/** only.

THE TENSION.
- CORPUS, migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1984 (inside M-51, heading :1980, Type line :1982 'Type A - pre-1.0 spec lock; mechanical rewrite.'): 'The runtime invokes every registered fx handler with two args; a unary handler raises a language-level arity error at the call site (ArityException on JVM, TypeError / "Cannot read ... of undefined" or similar on CLJS depending on shape).' That leads with the LOUD reading.
- SKILL, three leaves, mutually consistent and all SILENT for CLJS:
  - breaking-changes.md:208 (failure-visibility axis row): 'on CLJS (no arity check) the runtime context-map binds to args and the real fx args are silently dropped - the handler runs against the wrong value, no error (on JVM it throws an ArityException - loud - but v1 migration targets are CLJS)'.
  - inventory-and-plan.md:66 lists 'unary reg-fx handlers -> M-51' among the rules that 'compile clean and break only at runtime'; :81 repeats the silent-drop mechanism.
  - sequencing.md:82 row 14a: 'Type A but SILENT-fail - so swept by an exhaustive up-front grep'.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic). Loud-vs-silent is the axis that selects the SWEEP METHOD, and the skill says so explicitly: silent-fail rules get an exhaustive up-front grep and 'never march-the-wall', because a loud rule can be found by following compile/runtime errors while a silent one cannot. A reader who takes the corpus sentence at face value would conclude M-51 is discoverable by running the app and reading errors, and could legitimately skip the exhaustive grep - on a rule that fires in nearly every real v1 app with a custom reg-fx.

WHICH SIDE LOOKS RIGHT. The skill's, on CLJS. A single-arity CLJS (fn [request] ...) compiles to a one-parameter JS function; JS silently ignores extra arguments, so the v2 call with two args binds the CONTEXT MAP to request and drops the real fx args, with no ArityException and no TypeError at the call site. Any TypeError arrives LATER and elsewhere - when the handler destructures the context map and downstream code uses the nils - which is a different failure at a different place from 'at the call site'. The corpus's JVM half (ArityException) is correct; note the skill's own remark that v1 migration targets are CLJS. The corpus does hedge with 'or similar ... depending on shape', so this is an emphasis/accuracy problem rather than a flat contradiction - but the sentence's leading clause is the part a reader acts on.

SUGGESTED FIX (corpus side, one sentence, whoever holds the MIGRATION.md token next): split the claim by platform rather than presenting one failure with a parenthetical - JVM raises ArityException (loud); CLJS raises nothing at the call site, binds the context map to the unary parameter and silently drops the real fx args, surfacing later as wrong-value behaviour. Then M-51's existing rg -U sweep and 'apply to every unary reg-fx handler' instruction read as the consequence they already are.

NOT VERIFIED AT RUNTIME by this worker - the reasoning above is from CLJS/JS calling semantics plus the skill's three concurring statements, not from an executed repro. Anyone actioning this should confirm with a two-arg call into a single-arity CLJS fn before rewording the corpus.
FIXED in PR #9026 (worker cluster corpus-b). The bead's author flagged this as NOT verified at runtime; it has now been EXECUTED, and the skill's three leaves are confirmed right while the corpus was wrong. Probe: ClojureScript 1.12.145 on Node v24 via cljs.main -re node. A single-fixed-arity (fn [request] ...) reached through a registry lookup — the real fx path — called with two args threw NOTHING at the call site: it returned normally, the context map bound to the unary parameter (verified equal to the context map), and the real fx args were dropped. A statically-known direct call produced only a COMPILER WARNING ('Wrong number of args (2) passed to ...') and still no runtime throw; that warning does not reach the fx path, because there the call goes through a registry lookup, so on the path that matters nothing warns and nothing throws. CONTROL that makes the silence a finding rather than a swallowed exception: a MULTI-arity CLJS fn called at an unsupported arity DID throw 'Invalid arity: 3', so the probe can see throws. Downstream, (:real wrongly-bound) is nil. The corpus sentence is now split by platform — JVM ArityException (loud), CLJS silent — and M-51 is marked a silent-fail rule so its existing exhaustive rg -U sweep reads as the consequence it already is. skills/re-frame-migration/** deliberately untouched: its three leaves were already correct, so there is nothing to file against the skill.
close_reason: M-51's failure-visibility sentence split by platform in PR #9026 and marked a silent-fail rule. Executed CLJS probe (cljs 1.12.145 on Node): a unary handler called with two args through a registry lookup throws nothing, binds the context map to the unary param and drops the fx args; multi-arity control DID throw 'Invalid arity: 3'. The skill's three leaves were correct, so nothing filed against the skill.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): breaking-changes.md and inventory-and-plan.md teach the post-unwrap handler as (fn [_ {:keys [a b]}] ...) — the v1 reshaped shape; a v2 reg-event handler takes the event VECTOR
description:
CLAIM

Two leaves teach the post-`unwrap` handler as a **one-arg-map** destructure, which is the
v1 unwrap-reshaped shape, not a v2 handler:

- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md` (the preserved-surfaces
  interceptor bullet): "the simplest v2 destination is plain **handler destructuring** —
  `(fn [_ {:keys [a b]}] ...)` — with no interceptor at all".
- `skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md` (the `unwrap` add-on-scan
  bullet): "the simplest fix is plain handler destructuring (`(fn [_ {:keys [...]}] ...)`,
  no interceptor)".

TRUTH AT TIP

A v2 `reg-event` handler takes the **coeffects map** and the **event vector**. Corpus M-59's
own worked example writes the destination as:

    (rf/reg-event :api/payload
      (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ {:keys [order-id total]}]] ...))

The payload map is the second element of the event vector, not the second argument. What
the two leaves show is what `unwrap` USED to hand the handler in v1 — which is precisely
the shape the migration is removing. An agent applying it writes a handler whose second
parameter is destructured as a map against a vector.

IMPACT

The class the migration-skill review keeps finding: a leaf teaching a form that does not
work. Milder than the retired-symbol cases in that `{:keys [...]}` against a vector binds
nils rather than throwing, which makes it a SILENT wrong-shape rather than a loud one.

Not asserted by rf2-c0b3e, which is why it was left standing when that bead's `unwrap`
fixes landed: the phrase appears identically in both leaves, so correcting one alone would
introduce a divergence between them.

FIX SHAPE (two files, one clause each)

Bring both arglists to corpus M-59's shape — `(fn [{:keys [db]} [_ {:keys [a b]}]] …)` —
and keep the two leaves reading the same. Check `guided-interceptors-subs.md` for the same
phrase while there.

title: docs/core/hicasso/15-testing.md: the published :local/root test-kit route (:extra-paths to ../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src) prints a Clojure CLI deprecation warning on every build
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 by rf2-xkhul (PR #8990) while running the pilot baselines from a clean external workspace built on the published route (Clojure CLI 1.12.4.1618, shadow-cljs 3.4.10).

The published testing chapter (docs/core/hicasso/15-testing.md, 'Put the test kit on the classpath', :local/root case) tells a reader to add
  :test {:extra-paths ["../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src"]}
and the pilot workspace page copies that. Every shadow-cljs invocation then prints, before compiling:
  WARNING: Use of :paths external to the project has been deprecated, please remove: ../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src
tools.deps has deprecated paths that escape the project root. Nothing fails today, but (a) a pilot following the published chapter meets a deprecation warning on the first build, which the friction log will (correctly) record against the published docs; (b) a future Clojure CLI may refuse it, at which point the published route breaks. The chapter is outside rf2-xkhul's fence (docs/core/hicasso is the published guide), so this is filed rather than fixed.

OPTIONS, not ruled. (1) Publish the kit through a coordinate instead of a path: a second :local/root to a tiny deps.edn placed in test_kit/ (e.g. day8/re-frame2-hicasso-test-kit {:local/root "../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit"} with test_kit/deps.edn {:paths ["src"]}) is inside the project boundary of THAT root and prints nothing; the chapter's line changes shape but stays one line. (2) Put test_kit/src on the hicasso artefact's :paths (rejected before, rf2-hic-020 kept it off :paths so a no-test app carries none of it; but reachability already keeps it out of a bundle that never requires ht/hm, per the chapter's own 'From a published coordinate' paragraph). (3) Leave it and add one sentence to the chapter naming the warning as expected. Whoever takes this should re-run the pilot workspace step 5b afterwards (docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md) since the copy-ready deps.edn there mirrors the chapter.
notes:
PARTIAL: option (3) landed; the bead STAYS OPEN because the warning still
prints. worker/docsdrift-a, commit edc0a3606e.

THE NON-DEPRECATED SPELLING IS OPTION (1), AND IT IS NOW MEASURED rather than
assumed. Run against the CLI this bead names (1.12.4.1618) on a minimal
throwaway project, three variants, same shape each time:

  V1  :extra-paths ["../kit/src"]          -> WARNING reproduced VERBATIM,
      (the currently published shape)         "Use of :paths external to the
                                              project has been deprecated,
                                              please remove: ../kit/src";
                                              root IS on the classpath.
                                              This is the control: it bites.
  V2  :local/root "../kit", NO deps.edn    -> HARD FAILURE, not a clean route:
      inside kit/                             "Error building classpath.
                                              Manifest file not found for
                                              day8/kit in coordinate ..."
  V3  :local/root "../kit", WITH           -> NO warning at all, and kit/src
      kit/deps.edn = {:paths ["src"]}         on the classpath. THE ANSWER.

SO THE DURABLE FIX IS TWO FILES, NOT ONE, AND V2 IS WHY. The chapter's line
cannot simply change shape: a coordinate pointing at test_kit/ with no
deps.edn in it does not merely keep warning, it BREAKS the published route
with a hard classpath error. implementation/hicasso/test_kit/ currently
contains only src/ and test/ — there is no deps.edn there today. So:
  1. NEW FILE implementation/hicasso/test_kit/deps.edn carrying {:paths ["src"]}
  2. THEN docs/core/hicasso/15-testing.md's :test alias becomes
     :extra-deps {day8/re-frame2-hicasso-test-kit
                  {:local/root "../re-frame2/implementation/hicasso/test_kit"}}
  3. AND docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md step 5b, whose
     copy-ready deps.edn mirrors the chapter (named in this bead's own
     description). Note that page is under docs/design/hicasso/, which
     mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs hides from the strict build, so it needs
     check_provenance_pins.py and a hand read rather than the docs build.
Step 1 is under implementation/, outside the docsdrift-a fence and inside a
live peer's (ssrnode-red holds implementation/hicasso/**), so it was NOT taken.

OPTION (2) STAYS REJECTED and should not be revisited casually: the
implementation/hicasso/deps.edn header spends several paragraphs on why
test_kit/src is deliberately off :paths while being on :clein/build's
:src-dirs — "the two keys are not the same lever and this artefact is the one
place they diverge" — with check_production_erasure.cjs enforcing the

title: core(derivation/egress): dead-frame-sentinel is a registrable keyword, so a colliding live frame fails the graph egress open
description: implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc defines dead-frame-sentinel as ::no-egress-frame (the public keyword :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame) and stamps it as elide-wire-value's :frame opt whenever project-graph's governing frame is nil or unreachable, so the walker takes its unresolvable-frame arm. Its docstring says the keyword is namespaced into this ns so it can never collide with a real frame id. That claim does not hold: make-frame validates no :id type and the frame registry is keyed by whatever public keyword it is handed, so an app that registers a frame under that literal id turns the fail-closed stamp into a live-frame walk under that frame's empty declaration registry, and the graph's value-bearing fields ship raw. This is exactly the class the rf2-7htk7 audit of PR #8972 named for Xray's ::no-frame, which the third pass (PR #8987) fixed by making the substitute a private identity value (a fresh host object) that no registration can equal, with a collision regression (register a live frame under the literal id, leave the target unselected, assert :rf/redacted). Not done in PR #8987 because that audit note scoped the completion to Xray and forbade widening. Remedy options, smallest first: (a) make dead-frame-sentinel a private identity value the same way, plus a collision regression in the derivation egress tests; (b) have elide-wire-value distinguish a present nil :frame key from an absent one, which retires both sentinels but changes the :frame opt's documented override semantics (spec/API.md elide-wire-value and project-egress rows, spec/015 §Projection promise fallback to the carried scope when the record's own :frame is unknown) and so drags hot-zone spec prose. Verify the premise first: register a frame under :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, call project-graph with a nil frame-id on a graph carrying a sensitive value under an ambient live frame, and observe whether the value egresses raw.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-03 02:4x AUSEST — OPTION (a), THE PRIVATE IDENTITY VALUE, PLUS THE COLLISION REGRESSION. Option (b) is refused.

WHY (a). It is not a new design decision — it is the SAME fix this repo already made for the SAME defect class one artefact over. The rf2-7htk7 audit of PR #8972 named this class for Xray's ::no-frame, and PR #8987 fixed it by making the substitute a private identity value (a fresh host object) that no registration can equal, with a collision regression that registers a live frame under the literal id, leaves the target unselected, and asserts :rf/redacted. That is a worked precedent with a shipped test shape, so this is applying a settled answer rather than choosing one. The bead itself records that (a) was not done then only because the audit note scoped the completion to Xray and forbade widening — the scope, not the reasoning, is what kept it out.

WHY NOT (b). Two reasons, and the second is what settles it. First, it changes the :frame opt's DOCUMENTED override semantics, which is a public-contract change made in service of an internal sentinel — the tail wagging the dog. Second, it drags hot-zone spec prose (spec/API.md's elide-wire-value and project-egress rows, and spec/015's Projection promise fallback), and a worker is live in spec/** right now, so (b) would be a lane collision on top of a larger change. Neither reason alone would be decisive; together they are.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST, and the bead tells you exactly how, so do it rather than trusting the docstring's claim OR mine: register a frame under the literal :re-frame.derivation.egress/no-egress-frame, call project-graph with a nil frame-id on a graph carrying a sensitive value under an ambient live frame, and observe whether the value egresses raw. IF IT DOES NOT, the premise fails and saying so is the whole deliverable — the docstring's collision claim would then be true and there is nothing to fix.

THE REGRESSION IS NOT OPTIONAL. A private identity value with no test asserting the collision case is the same fix without the thing that keeps it fixed, and this defect has now been found twice in two artefacts because the first fix's scope was drawn too tight.
RESOLVED 2026-09-03 by PR #9043 (branch worker/code-a, commit 5276cf4b0a).

title: skill(re-frame-migration): xray-replaces-10x parity table claims a bottom-rail scrubber and a side-by-side hydration debugger Xray does not ship (018: no bottom rail; panels.md: hydration inline, no tab)

title: skill(re-frame-migration): evals.json eval 21 grades in-handler dispatch-sync as Type B (cites M-3) - corpus M-9 is Type A and the auto leaf rewrites it mechanically

Corpus M-1 (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:92-133), row `re-frame.registrar/get-handler`: "it returns the registration *metadata map*, not the raw handler fn ... title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): post-error trigger names 'red CI' while §Session evidence excludes CI runs, and never names the :ok? false / :reason envelopes and :rf.error/:rf.epoch traces the pair tools actually raise
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

Post-error trigger (b) is defined in four places with "red CI" as a firing condition:

- `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:11-12` (frontmatter description): "**post-error within a re-frame2-pair session** — after a stack trace, failed dispatch, red CI, or a runtime error during live pair work"
- `SKILL.md:37`: "a stack trace, failed dispatch, red CI, or an `:rf.error/*` event fired during live re-frame2-pair work"
- `spec/design.md:106` and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:55` repeat "red CI".

But `SKILL.md:72` (§Session evidence): "**Exclude unrelated activity.** Background workers, CI runs, shell commands, code-review threads, and app-authoring edits are out of scope unless the user explicitly names one as pair-session friction."

## TRUTH AT TIP

A CI run is not something a pair tool raises, and the family disqualifier `skills/README.md:166` puts "post-mortems on shell sessions, IDE workflows, or test-suite runs" out of scope. What the pair tools DO raise, and what a post-error offer should recognise:

- `{:ok? false :reason <kw>}` envelopes — the discover-app ladder `:nrepl-unreachable` / `:build-not-running` / `:no-runtime-connected` / `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/probe.cljs:302-310`), `:ambiguous-frame` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:173`), `:restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`), `:reset-rejected` (`tools/replace_app_db.cljs:114`), `:missing-baseline` / `:baseline-without-probe` (`tools/tail_build.cljs:148,172`), `:debug-disabled` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md:8`).
- Error trace ops — `:rf.error/*` (`errors.md:43-47`, e.g. `:rf.error/handler-exception`) and the seven `restore-epoch!` failure ops (`spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126`, six `:rf.epoch/restore-*` plus `:rf.error/no-such-handler` kind `:frame`).

The existing evals already model the boundary correctly (ids 4, 17, 18 positive; id 19 "wants it FIXED" negative) and none uses CI.

## IMPACT

The trigger admits an input (a red CI run) that the skill's own evidence rules then discard, so the offer fires with nothing to retro; and it gives the agent no vocabulary for the failures that SHOULD fire it — a refused write or a ladder miss looks like "ordinary pair operation" under the current wording, so the post-error offer under-fires exactly where pair friction is densest.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR: drop "red CI" from the four sites and define (b) in one clause — "a pair tool returned `:ok? false` with a `:reason`, or an `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/restore-*` trace fired, during live re-frame2-pair work" — without restating the reason catalogue (that is the pair skill's errors.md). Keep "stack trace" (a handler exception is a runtime error). No evals change required; re-score ids 4, 17, 18, 19 by reading.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py` (description edited; evals untouched) and `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` (SKILL.md re-read). Prose by hand.

## ACCEPTANCE

No occurrence of "red CI" under `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/`; trigger (b) names the `:ok? false`/`:reason` envelope and the `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/restore-*` trace families; §Session evidence :72 unchanged; both gates exit 0.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): re-authoring sources still drop the new draft-ownership citation contract
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md:87` (§Issue drafts): "A good draft carries, in natural prose: the concrete session evidence, the missing `re-frame2-pair` or `re-frame2` behaviour, one implementable desired outcome, and a completion signal ... with the pair-tool-versus-framework ownership plain in the title and body."

That is the whole instruction on ownership. SKILL.md never names `spec/Tool-Pair.md` (grep: lines 6 and 62 say "Tool-Pair contract" / "Tool-Pair surfaces" without a path or a section), never says WHAT a framework-shaped draft must cite, and carries no worked example of either title. README.md:38 lists surface families in prose only.

## TRUTH AT TIP

`skills/README.md:183` (family contract, §Routing for friction found mid-pair retro): "framework / Tool-Pair contract friction — ... Name the specific Tool-Pair surface from the consolidated capability table in `spec/Tool-Pair.md` (the shipped tool catalogue is `re-frame2-pair/README.md`)." `skills/README.md:185`: "The draft contract lives in `re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` §Issue drafts."

`spec/Tool-Pair.md:36-52` §What re-frame2 commits to (the runtime contract) — the `| Capability | re-frame2 surface | Spec |` table, e.g. row: `| **Read registry** | (rf/registrations kind), (rf/handler-meta kind id), (rf/frame-ids), (rf/frame-meta id) | 001-Registration, 002 |`; and `spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126` the restore-failure table (seven rows, `:operation` + `:tags`).

The skill is self-contained by lock (design.md L7: "Nothing loads from outside the package root"), so the family-contract sentence is unreachable from inside a retro unless SKILL.md restates it.

## IMPACT

The family contract promises that a framework-shaped draft names a capability-table row; the skill that owns the draft contract does not instruct it. A framework-shaped draft therefore lands as "re-frame2 should surface X" with no row and no tool named — the vague draft that §Anti-patterns :97 ("without naming the concrete missing behaviour") forbids — and a maintainer cannot tell a Tool-Pair gap from a pair-skill recipe gap from the title.

One PR against `skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/SKILL.md` §Issue drafts, at most 10 lines:

1. One sentence: a framework-shaped draft names the row of `spec/Tool-Pair.md` §What re-frame2 commits to (or the §Time-travel restore-failure row) it falls short of, and the shipped pair tool that exposed the gap (catalogue: `skills/re-frame2-pair/README.md`); a tool-shaped draft names the pair-skill leaf or tool descriptor to change.
2. Two two-line worked examples, titles from the safe alphabet (letters, digits, spaces, `- . , / ( ) :`): tool-shaped — `pair-tool (discover-app): ladder hint for no-runtime-connected should say reload the tab`; framework-shaped — `framework (Tool-Pair Time-travel, restore-epoch): restore-unknown-epoch tags should carry the oldest retained epoch id` with a body line that quotes the row.

§Issue drafts instructs a framework-shaped draft to name a Tool-Pair capability-table row and the shipped tool, a tool-shaped draft to name the pair-skill leaf/descriptor, and shows one worked title+body line of each; `bb tests/duplicate_search_test.clj` exit 0.

TRUTH AT TIP
- The 245 fixtures carry 20 distinct top-level `:fixture/*` keys (`grep -rhoE ':fixture/[a-z?-]+' spec/conformance/fixtures/ | sort | uniq -c`). IMPACT
The skill's derive-at-the-pin posture rests on "the README is the contract"; on the fixture-file shape the README demonstrably lags the fixtures by eight keys. A port harness built from README + skill supports registry / handlers / frame-config / dispatches / expect / calls and none of the four floors fires when a fixture arrives with `:fixture/interceptor-fired` or `:fixture/frames`: the setup or expectation is ignored and the fixture can pass vacuously (an interceptor-fired expectation never checked) — the exact silent-skip shape the floors exist to forbid. On `:data-classification/*` (gate 1) a harness that has not implemented the classification-effects step fails loudly, which is fine; the eight undocumented keys are the quiet ones.

1. conformance.md §The harness: add a fifth floor — "**Unknown fixture key.** A top-level `:fixture/*` key the harness does not implement fails the run naming it — the corpus adds setup/expectation keys ahead of the README."

Spec side (report, not this bead): document the eight keys in spec/conformance/README.md §Fixture format and in Spec-Schemas §`:rf/fixture-file`; that is a corpus README gap and belongs to spec/.

No gate — verify by hand: run the new grep at tip and confirm it lists 20 keys; check_skill_implementor_order.py --verbose stays green (it scans conformance.md for the family roots only).

title: skill(re-frame2-improver): correct deferred effect-map candidate for classification effects and fail-closed refusal
description:
CLAIM. The catalogue (`references/README.md:7-14`) is 6 leaves; `spec/design.md` §4 "Deferred catalogue candidates" (`:86-91`) holds 2. Compared against the 15 pattern leaves under `skills/re-frame2/patterns/`, the fundamentals leaves, `spec/Principles.md`, and Mike's standing rules (frames are isolated contexts; no raw atoms through views; no frame-ids as view args; no over-engineering), the common consumer misuses below have no leaf and are not queued. L6 (`design.md:57`) says a leaf lands only after 3+ real reviews — so the landable shape is the DEFERRED LIST, ranked, with detection signals, so the growth procedure has a queue rather than a blank.

TRUTH AT TIP — 13 candidates, ranked (source that discourages it -> canonical idiom):
1. Frame leakage / frame-ids as view args — a sub or handler reading another frame (`rf/app-db-value other-frame` in a sub; `(rf/dispatch ... {:frame :other})` from inside a handler of a different frame; views taking `frame-id` args and threading `capture-frame`). `fundamentals/frames.md:9,82`; Mike's rule "frames are isolated contexts". Already deferred as "foreign-frame write"; widen to reads + view args. Signals: `app-db-value` / `{:frame ...}` inside `reg-sub` / `reg-event` bodies; view params named `frame` / `frame-id`.
2. Views that fetch / boot in a mount hook — `:component-did-mount`, `use-effect`, `r/with-let` init dispatching `:*/load` / `:*/fetch` / `[:rf.resource/ensure ...]`. `patterns/resources.md:9,29` ("views are passive reads — they never trigger a fetch"), `patterns/boot.md:138` ("Boot logic in a view's `:on-mount`"). Fix: route entry / `:initial-events` / machine `:entry`.
3. Secrets in machine `:data` or `app-db` — bearer/refresh tokens in `:data`, passwords retained in a form's `:submitted` / `:draft`. `patterns/websocket.md:30,216`, `patterns/forms.md:34-36`. Signals: `:token` / `:bearer` / `:password` keys assoc'd into `:data` / db without `:sensitive`.
4. App code reading runtime-db through `:db` — `(get-in db [:rf.runtime/machines :snapshots ...])` in a sub/handler instead of `[:rf/machine id]` / `[:rf.route/*]`. `fundamentals/frames.md:33`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md:146` (MUST NOT). Greppable: `:rf.runtime/` in app source.
5. Host reads in machine callbacks folded into `:data` — `(js/Date.now)` / `(random-uuid)` in `:action` / `:entry` / `:guard`. `spec/005` §Causal host facts, `patterns/websocket.md:198`. A leaf-5 extension (its signals are scoped to `reg-event` bodies; only `subscribe-once` is covered for callbacks).
6. Ad-hoc HTTP fx bypassing `:rf.http/managed` — a `reg-fx` wrapping `js/fetch` / `cljs-http`, or `:http-xhrio`, with no `:status` envelope, stale suppression or failure taxonomy. `patterns/managed-http.md:5,27`. Today flagged only when a retry loop is also present.
7. Positional multi-arg event payloads — `[:cart/add id qty price]`. `spec/Principles.md` §Name over place; migration M-19. Signal: `(fn [_ [_ a b c]] ...)` with 2+ positional args.
8. Top-level `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-later` keys outside `:fx` — dropped with `:rf.error/effect-map-shape` (`fundamentals/fx.md:36,87`). A v1 habit; fails at runtime as a trace, not a throw.
9. Reactive `@(subscribe ...)` in a lifecycle hook — `patterns/stateful-components.md:98`. Sibling of leaf-5's reactive-read rule, on the view side.
10. Post-mutation watcher reactions for workflow -> call-site `:reply-to`. `patterns/stale-detection.md:24`.
11. Anonymous `:on-click` doing logic beyond one dispatch — `spec/Principles.md` §Named things over anonymous things.
12. View renders only the happy state — already deferred (`design.md:90`); keep.
13. Boot dispatched after `make-frame` instead of `:initial-events` — `fundamentals/frames.md:164`, `spec/002-Frames.md:660`; an idempotent `frame-root` re-mount does not replay them.

IMPACT. None of these is a false critique today (the catalogue is honest); the gap is coverage — a consumer review misses the frame-isolation and view-fetch misuses that re-frame2's own principles name most loudly, and the growth procedure has no ranked queue to draw from.

FIX SHAPE. One PR to `spec/design.md` §4 Deferred catalogue candidates: replace the 2-item list with the ranked list above (one line each: name -> signals -> canonical idiom), keeping L6's 3+-review bar. If Mike wants to pre-empt L6 for #1 (his standing rule), promote it as a seventh leaf in the L5 five-section format plus catalogue + routing rows in `references/README.md` — a separate PR, not this one.

GATE. `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (design.md is under `skills/`, a docs-gate root). The ranking is prose — no gate; say so.

ACCEPTANCE. `design.md` §4 lists the ranked candidates with a detection signal and a canonical-idiom pointer each; `references/README.md:33` still points at it as the deferred-candidate owner.

description:

TRUTH AT TIP. `evals/evals.json` grades ONLY the activation half. #5 ("Spot any anti-patterns in cart/handlers.cljs?") is `kind: trigger` with no behavioural expectations; nothing checks what the skill DOES when the named path does not resolve. Every behavioural fixture (#17-#31) pastes its snippet inline (`evals/README.md:63-65` — "so trigger filter 2 is satisfied"), so the read-the-named-path branch and its failure mode are exercised by no fixture. `SKILL.md:86` names fabrication the cardinal failure and `evals/README.md:170-173` makes fabricated findings release-blocking at 1.0 — yet the one input shape most likely to induce fabrication (a confident, unresolvable file name) has no fixture.

Secondary gap, same file: `SKILL.md:70` ("highest consequence first") is graded by no fixture — #21 and #27 each contain a correctness finding beside a maintainability one, but no expectation checks order.

IMPACT. A regression in which the skill answers "Spot any anti-patterns in cart/handlers.cljs?" with invented `path:line` findings for a file it never read passes the whole suite.

FIX SHAPE. One PR to `evals/evals.json` (+ `evals/README.md` only if its prose needs a word; it deliberately does not restate the inventory):
- Add a behavioural fixture, dimension `false-positive-avoidance`, e.g. `behav-neg-unresolvable-path`: the prompt names a concrete `.cljs` path that does not exist in the eval workspace, with review phrasing. title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): dry-run/write friction conflates runtime rejection with the --allow-writes gate
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` §re-frame2-specific classes (:82-196) carries nine classes. None covers the four frictions the pair skill itself flags as its commonest footguns, and its only observation class is framework-listener-shaped:

- grep for `privacy|elide|elision` hits only §Production-elision confusion (:121-132), which is BUILD elision (`goog.DEBUG=false`), not wire-boundary privacy elision.
- grep for `wire-size|truncat|max-tokens|dedup|cursor` — no hits.
- grep for `tail-build|baseline` — no hits.
- grep for `dry-run|undo|allow-writes|replace-app-db` — no hits.
- §Wrong listener for the question :96-106 reasons about `register-listener!`'s `:trace` vs `:epoch` streams ("default to the `:epoch` stream ... reach for the `:trace` stream only for per-emit detail") — the FRAMEWORK listener API, not the MCP tools a pair session actually calls.

## TRUTH AT TIP

- Privacy carve-out: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:218` — structured reads (`snapshot`, `get-path`, `read-sub`, `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`, `dispatch-dry-run`, recorders) elide server-side (`:rf/redacted`, `:rf.size/large-elided`) under `--allow-sensitive-reads` (OFF by default); `eval-cljs` is un-elided and default-ON. Two friction shapes follow: an agent reading `:rf/redacted` as "the data is missing/broken", or reaching for raw eval and shipping secrets.
- Wire-size caps: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:193` + `references/wire-size-budget.md` — `max-tokens`, `:rf.mcp/dedup-table`, `limit`/`cursor`, `max-buffered-*`; a truncated page read as a complete answer is a classic weak-trust-signal friction with a re-frame2-specific shape.
- tail-build baseline: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:111` — "Capture your probe's current value BEFORE the edit (that's the `baseline`)... or you'll interact with pre-reload code"; `tools/tail_build.cljs:148,172` refuse with `:baseline-without-probe` / `:missing-baseline`.
- Dry-run / write gate: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:207-208, 219` — `dispatch-dry-run` rolls back and fires no fx; a live `dispatch` of a handler returning `{:db <bare-map>}` REPLACES app-db wholesale ("unrecoverable without `restore-epoch`"); `restore-epoch` / `replace-app-db` are gated by `--allow-writes` (OFF by default) and refuse with `:restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`) / `:reset-rejected` (`tools/replace_app_db.cljs:114`).
- Observation after PR #8815 (2026-08-31): `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-streams`, `get-stream-controls` are gone from the registry (29 tools; grep of `descriptors_data.cljs` finds no such `:name`). `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:208`: "`watch-epochs` polls the assembled-epoch history — the one live-watch route, and every observation arrives as a completed tool result." The returned-result routes a session chooses between are `dispatch` (settled envelope with the assembled epoch, `spec/Tool-Pair.md:79`), `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`, `watch-until`, and `record` / `read-recording` — all registry names.

## IMPACT

The retro's pattern-check leaf is where "is this a one-off or a product gap?" is decided (SKILL.md:81, design.md L6). A session that burned time on `:rf/redacted` confusion, a truncated `snapshot`, a `tail-build` timeout from a missing baseline, a wholesale app-db replace, or a write refused by the OFF-by-default gate finds no class and gets scored as a one-off — or worse, a "why didn't they just subscribe?" reasoning path that no longer exists. These are the frictions the pair skill's own style guidance spends the most words warning about, so they are the likeliest retro inputs.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR against `known-frictions.md`: add four re-frame2-specific classes in the existing Signals / Typical improvements shape (≤12 lines each) — (1) privacy elision vs raw-eval carve-out, (2) wire-size caps and pagination, (3) hot-reload baseline misuse, (4) dry-run vs live write and the write gate — and add one line to §Wrong listener mapping the framework streams onto the tool routes (`dispatch` envelope / `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `watch-until` / `record`+`read-recording`), noting that live-watch is poll-only and no subscription tool exists. The leaf is 195 L / 12.7 KB; ~50 lines fits under 250 L / 16 KB. If it does not, split the re-frame2-specific classes into a second leaf linked from SKILL.md:81 (still one level deep).

## GATE

No gate — verify by hand: every tool name against the `descriptors_data.cljs` `:name` list; `wc -l -c` on the leaf under 250 / 16384; `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` if a new leaf/link is added.

## ACCEPTANCE

known-frictions.md carries a class for each of: privacy elision/raw-eval, wire-size caps, tail-build baseline, dry-run/write gate; §Wrong listener names the five returned-result tool routes and states that no subscription tool exists; leaf within ceiling.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair-retro): known-frictions.md proposes as improvements five behaviours the 29-tool catalogue already ships (operating-frame trio, discover-app :debug-enabled?, restore-epoch refusal, stream prose, errors recipe)
description:
## CLAIM (file:line, quoted)

`skills/re-frame2-pair-retro/references/known-frictions.md` — the on-demand leaf SKILL.md:81 tells the retro to consult so "a match raises the finding's priority" — lists, under "Typical improvements", behaviours the current 29-tool Pair-MCP catalogue already ships:

2. §Wrong listener for the question :106 — "short prose in SKILL.md naming the two streams and when each wins".
3. §Time-travel restore failures :116-118 — "structured presentation of the seven named failure modes ... with a next-best-action per mode" / "preflight check before restore" / "surface `:history-size` and `:schema-digest-recorded`/`:current` in the tool's output".
4. §Production-elision confusion :130-131 — "preflight check that reads `re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?` and reports the answer" / "make 'I am attached to a production-elided build' a first-class result state".
5. §Error observability :147 — "prefer a recipe over a doc paragraph when the friction is 'I didn't know how to pull recent errors at the REPL'".

## TRUTH AT TIP

Registry: `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs` — 29 `:name` entries, including `get-operating-frame`, `set-operating-frame`, `reset-operating-frame`, `discover-app`, `restore-epoch`, `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`.

1. Frame: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:169-173` — the four-tier operating-frame cascade; "every other frame-targeted op refuses with `:ambiguous-frame` rather than guess"; `discover-app` returns `:frames [...]` (descriptors_data.cljs:186). The "explicit `:frame` or surface the choice" improvement IS the shipped design.
2. Streams: `skills/re-frame2-pair/SKILL.md:216` — "Use the assembled epoch stream by default; reach for the raw trace stream when you need detail the projection drops." The prose already exists.
3. Restore: the dedicated `restore-epoch` tool returns a structured refusal `:reason :restore-rejected` (`tools/restore_epoch.cljs:50`); the seven failure ops and their `:tags` (`:history-size`, `:schema-digest-recorded`, `:schema-digest-current`) are pinned at `spec/Tool-Pair.md:116-126`.
4. Elision: `tools/discover_app.cljs:191-194` — `discover-app` returns `:debug-enabled?` and a hint "re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? is false ..." (descriptors_data.cljs:186 shows `:debug-enabled? true` in the example result). The preflight exists.

A retro that pattern-matches a session onto one of these classes is told to propose, as the "smallest credible product change", a surface that already ships — and §Issue drafts then emits a draft asking `day8/re-frame2` for it. That is the wrong owner AND the wrong finding: when the session had `discover-app`'s `:debug-enabled?` or the operating-frame trio available and did not reach for them, the friction is discoverability in the pair skill's wording/recipes (tool-shaped), not a missing surface. The leaf's own inputs.md:56 update rule ("a new structured op ships → check whether known-frictions has a 'missing op' pattern that this resolves") was not applied when these landed.

## FIX SHAPE

> **Claude**: *(starts a recorder, then reads it back between your clicks — every observation arrives as a completed tool result)* — I'll `record` now; after each step I'll `read-recording` and pull the matching epochs with `watch-epochs` (pred `:event-id-prefix ":checkout"`, `since-id` from the last pull), narrating each one with its effect cascade.

The README is the human-facing catalogue (skills/README.md names it "the shipped tool catalogue") and its Examples are what a developer pattern-matches their first prompts against. description:
CLAIM

skills/re-frame2-pair/references/errors.md is the leaf SKILL.md:194 routes to for "Translate a structured `{:ok? false :reason ...}` to plain English; suggest the recovery". Two of the reasons it lists are emitted by nothing, and the failure family an agent hits most often in a pair session is absent from it entirely.

Phantom ids:
- errors.md:9 — "`:ns-not-loaded :missing :re-frame2` → re-frame2 isn't loaded; check the user's deps."
- errors.md:22 — "`:handler-error` inside an epoch → the user's handler threw; surface the `:rf.error/handler-exception` trace event ..."

Missing family — `eval-cljs` is the workhorse (SKILL.md:206) and its own failures are:
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-compile-error` (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs:330)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-threw` (grep `:reason` over tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-timeout` (eval_cljs.cljs:190)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-rejected` (eval_cljs.cljs:183 — the nREPL session refused the form)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled` (eval_cljs.cljs:255 — server launched with `--no-eval`)
- `:rf.error/eval-cljs-mailbox-missing` / `-await-wrap-failed` (eval_cljs.cljs:198,203 — the `await: true` path)

TRUTH AT TIP

`grep -rhoE ':reason :[a-zA-Z0-9./?-]+' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload | sort -u` (~100 distinct ids) contains neither `:ns-not-loaded` nor `:handler-error`; a wider `grep -rn ns-not-loaded tools/ implementation/ skills/re-frame2-pair/preload` finds nothing at all. The re-frame2-not-loaded case cannot surface as its own reason: the preload namespace requires re-frame.core, so an app without re-frame2 never installs the marker and `discover-app` reports the ladder's `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing` (errors.md:19 already covers it). `:rf.error/handler-exception` (errors.md:22's own body) is the real trace op; `:handler-error` is not a `:reason` any tool returns. Across the whole skill only two of the eval-cljs ids appear anywhere (`-timeout` and `-rejected`, once each, in references/ops.md:83); `-compile-error`, `-threw`, `-disabled` are taught nowhere (`grep -rn 'eval-cljs-(compile-error|threw|disabled)' skills/re-frame2-pair` is empty).

Keep it to ~12 lines; errors.md is 8.9 KB and stays under the leaf ceiling.

title: skill(re-frame2): patterns managed-http and boot — the 401-refresh auth-machine worked example is promised by each leaf to the other and exists in neither (spec/Pattern-Boot §Worked example has it)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md:127`: "The full auth-machine worked example combining 5xx-retry-at-transport AND 401-refresh-at-semantic lives in `patterns/boot.md`." Again at L154: "For the machine-form wrapper in production, see the auth-flow in `patterns/boot.md`." and L160 "Retry-ownership worked example → `patterns/boot.md`".

`skills/re-frame2/patterns/boot.md:264` (§Variations, *The retry-ownership boundary*): "Mixed transport-vs-semantic retry — e.g. auth machine handling 401-then-refresh-then-retry — sits at the boundary … Both compose. See `patterns/managed-http.md`." and L298 "Retry-ownership boundary → `patterns/managed-http.md`".

## TRUTH AT TIP

Neither leaf contains the example. `boot.md`'s canonical machine spawns an app child `:auth/restore-session` and retries it with a fixed `:after {2000 …}` (L212-222) — no 401 detection, no refresh-then-loop-back, no `:rf.http/managed` `:retry` on the auth request. `managed-http.md` has the retry-ownership TABLE (L117-125) and an `:app/auth` wrapper sketch (L76-92) that transitions `:failed → :login-failed` with no refresh path. The example does exist — in the spec: `spec/Pattern-Boot.md:297-330` "Semantic retry — state machine handles 401-vs-200-vs-fatal" (`:got-401?` guard L318-320; "`:failed` whose `:error` is `{:kind :rf.http/http-4xx :status 401}` → `:refreshing` … loops back to `:loading-me`" L300-306), and `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:446` points at "Pattern-Boot §Worked example — auth-machine and the retry-ownership boundary" for it. The skill leaves point at each other instead of at that section.

## IMPACT

The single worked example the skill offers for the boundary it makes load-bearing ("does the retry decision depend on anything other than failure category and attempt count?") is a circular pointer. An agent asked to "refresh the token on 401 and retry" loads both leaves, finds the table and the rule, and no shape — and the shape has a trap (the refresh request is itself a managed request; the loop-back target must be the ORIGINAL request's state, not `:refreshing`) that the spec example resolves and the leaves do not. Gap, not contradiction: P3.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, both leaves; ~30 lines net)

Either (a) lift a compact `:refreshing` branch into `boot.md`'s canonical machine — `:got-401?` guard on `:authenticating`'s `:failed`, a `:refreshing` state that `:spawn`s the refresh `:rf.http/managed` and on `:succeeded` targets `:authenticating` (the loop-back), with the 5xx `:retry` map on the auth request — and make `managed-http.md:127,154,160` point at `boot.md` §Canonical declaration by anchor; or (b) leave `boot.md` as is and retarget all three `managed-http.md` pointers plus `boot.md:264,298` at `SKILL-REDIRECT.md → Pattern — Boot §Worked example — auth-machine and the retry-ownership boundary`, the way `managed-http.md:158` already routes the full 014 spec. title: skill(reagent-migration): the fully-migrated end state is untaught — with zero Reagent views left, (rf/init! substrate/adapter) retires the Reagent dependency
description:
## CLAIM

- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:259-270` (MIG-15): "**`(rf/init! ...)` stays** ... Keep the app's existing adapter install; it is not Reagent-specific scaffolding to be deleted. ... Hicasso does ship an adapter of its own (`re-frame.hicasso.substrate`), but it is an optional module nothing under Hicasso's own source requires, so `h/mount!` neither installs it nor displaces what the app has."
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:283-293` (MIG-24): "drop `reagent.*` requires **only when the namespace has zero remaining uses**".
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md:390-394` (MIG-23, the one mention, buried in the SSR recipe): "Adapter selection is not part of this migration ... (a Hicasso-only app may deliberately choose `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter`, but that is its own decision)."
- `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:138-150` Done checklist and hand-off: "Views rewritten into Hicasso where it made sense; the rest stay on Reagent" — nothing for the case where nothing stays.
- `evals/evals.json` notes: "Do NOT re-grade this fixture [25] as 'switch to the Hicasso adapter': choosing an adapter is not part of this migration." (Correct for the part-migrated boot it grades; this bead does not touch it.)

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:1-25` — "Hicasso's own reactive-substrate adapter — the value an application installs with `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` ... what lets a Hicasso application depend on core plus Hicasso and nothing else: without this namespace an interactive one would have to add a SECOND dependency coordinate — `day8/re-frame2-uix` or a Reagent one — purely to obtain the second half, and then never write a line of that substrate's notation."
- `docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md:144-160` §Hicasso needs a substrate adapter: "every Hicasso application calls `rf/init!` with an adapter ... `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` ... ships inside `day8/re-frame2-hicasso`, so that line costs no coordinate."
- rf2-hvr5h (closed 2026-08-19, PR #8512): "a Hicasso application depends on core plus Hicasso and nothing else". `spec/Conventions.md:103` rosters `:rf.adapter/hicasso`.

## IMPACT

The part-migrated guidance is right and stays: while any Reagent view remains, the Reagent adapter stays. But the skill never names the END state. Once every view is converted, `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is the last `reagent.*` require standing, and its only job was the substrate. Read together, MIG-15's "not scaffolding to be deleted" and MIG-24's "zero remaining uses" tell that author to keep `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and `reagent` in `deps.edn` indefinitely — exactly the second-coordinate cost rf2-hvr5h built the substrate to remove. For a consumer that migrates to completion (the trigger the skill exists for), the skill leaves a dead dependency and never says the option exists. Trust-the-programmer means naming the choice, not withholding it.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill files only; eval 25's part-migrated grading unchanged)

1. `references/catalog-mechanical.md` MIG-24 — one closing paragraph: "When the last Reagent view is gone, `re-frame.adapter.reagent` is the last `reagent.*` require, and it was only ever the substrate. `(rf/init! substrate/adapter)` from `[re-frame.hicasso.substrate :as substrate]` (`:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso`) replaces that line and lets the app drop `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and `reagent` from `deps.edn`. The author's call, not this skill's (cardinal rule 5), and never while a Reagent view remains." Add a one-line pointer from MIG-15's "stays" bullet.
2. `SKILL.md` Done checklist — one line: "If no Reagent view remains, the author was told the adapter choice is now open (MIG-24) — not switched for them."
3. Optional: a new M-tier behavioural eval ("every view is converted — can I drop Reagent now?") passing an answer that names `substrate/adapter` and the dependency drop as the author's decision, failing one that says the Reagent adapter must stay.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --ci`. The `substrate/adapter` spelling and `:kind` verified by hand against `substrate.cljs` (no gate reads prose).

## ACCEPTANCE

MIG-24 names the completed-migration option with the exact require, the `rf/init!` line and the two dependencies it retires; the done checklist carries the line; eval 25 unchanged; gates exit 0.
