title: skill(reagent-migration): three leftover-Reagent failures, three ids — the render-time refusal seam (:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused) and the complaint shape are untaught
description:
## CLAIM

- `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-judgment.md:306-325` (MIG-26): "Under Hicasso an `h/sub` from an ordinary `defn` **is legal** ... What fails is a read or a dispatch with **no active render**: a timer, a callback the browser invokes later, a foreign listener." and "An ambient `rf/dispatch` from a callback raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — **core's id, not a `hicasso-*` one** — at click time."
- `skills/reagent-migration/SKILL.md:104` (cardinal rule 2): "A converted `h/defview` has no ambient `subscribe`/`dispatch`, so a body with some sites rewritten and some not does not work." — states the law, never the diagnostic.
- `skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:7-31`: only the click-time closure trap is taught. Every diagnostic id the skill names anywhere (grep over the package): `:rf.error/no-frame-context` x9, `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` x9, `hicasso-intent-needs-the-event`, `hicasso-intent-outside-boundary`, `hicasso-malformed-prevent`, `:rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key`, `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`. Neither `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` nor `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` appears in any file.
- Nothing in the skill says what a Hicasso complaint IS (the four ex-data slots) or where the index lives.

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:64-118` — `with-frame` binds `frame/*ambient-frame-refusal*` for the whole render extent "so ambient `rf/subscribe` and `rf/dispatch` refuse for the extent (HD-002 clause (a))"; the substrate's `:reason` names the recovery verbatim: "Read through the boundary's own collector (`sub`) ... and dispatch through an intent at a handler position ...".
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:595-601, 637-640` — that refusal surfaces as **`:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`**, "rather than the generic `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — a refused ambient read and a genuinely frameless one are different mistakes and must not share a diagnostic". `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1991` rows it; firing case "a Hicasso boundary body".
- `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:584` — `h/sub` invoked outside a body raises **`:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render`** (`implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:102`; guide `docs/core/hicasso/02-views-and-reads.md:241`, `16-diagnostics.md:158`).
- `implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md:27-42` — every complaint is an `ex-info` whose `ex-data` carries four required slots: `:rf.error/id` (branch on this), `:where`, `:reason` (names the fix), `:recovery`; `:view`/`:source` are dev-only context. That file is the index; meaning per id is Spec 009 §Hicasso.

So the three commonest leftovers in a converted Reagent view map to three DIFFERENT ids at three DIFFERENT times:

| leftover | fails when | id |
|---|---|---|
| `@(rf/subscribe ...)` or `(rf/dispatch ...)` in a converted body, or in a helper `defn` it calls | at RENDER | `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` |
| `#(rf/dispatch ...)` closure surviving at an `:on-*` | at CLICK | `:rf.error/no-frame-context` |
| an `(h/sub ...)` moved into a callback / timer / promise | at FIRE | `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` |

## IMPACT

The skill teaches only row 2. An author who converts a view whose helper `defn` still derefs `rf/subscribe` — the most common shape in a Reagent codebase — gets `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused` at FIRST RENDER, and the skill's text points them at a click-time / frameless problem with the wrong id. MIG-26's "if it runs during render, leave it in the helper — that is the supported shape" is true only once the helper reads through `h/sub`; the skill never says the helper is ALSO deref-dropped (MIG-02 reaches helpers). And the complaint catalogue with stable ids is a headline Hicasso feature; the skill hands the author no way to read one, so the `:reason` that names the fix goes unread.

## FIX SHAPE (one PR, skill files only)

1. `references/gotchas.md` — extend the lead trap into "Three leftovers, three ids" with the table above, and add a short "Reading a complaint" paragraph: the four slots, branch on `:rf.error/id`, `:reason` names the fix, index at `implementation/hicasso/spec/complaints.md`, meaning in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Hicasso.
2. `references/catalog-judgment.md` MIG-26 — add the render-time arm: a leftover ambient `rf/subscribe`/`rf/dispatch` anywhere inside the render extent (body OR helper) refuses at render with `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`, whose reason names `h/sub` / an intent; deref-drop the helper too. Name `:rf.error/hicasso-sub-outside-render` for the hoist-to-render-time case.
3. `SKILL.md` §Gotchas: one line pointing at the three ids. `evals/evals.json`: eval 17 (or a new M-tier eval) gains an expectation that distinguishes the render-time refusal id from the click-time one.

Keep it tight — one table and two paragraphs, not a catalogue restatement.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`, `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --ci` (all exit 0 at tip). description:

 (d) neither Type line mentions M-31a (corpus: Type B).

TRUTH AT TIP (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md).
 (a) The corpus has ONE `### M-73.` heading (line 879) and the machine-identity rule is now `### M-74.` (line 2817). `python scripts/check_skill_migration_cites.py --verbose` reports "MIGRATION.md defines 80 rule ids; skill references cite 79 distinct ids" — M-74 is the one id no skill leaf cites (`rg -n 'M-74' skills/re-frame-migration/` returns nothing). Line 88's disambiguation advice now sends an agent looking for a heading that does not exist.
 (b) Corpus M-58 (line 2348): "**Type B** (semantic — the rewrite depends on which data was being scrubbed and where it lives)". Corpus M-59 (line 2384): "**Type A** for the `at-boundary` boundary-validation ref; **Type B** for `unwrap`". The at-a-glance paragraph contradicts both. (Both rules are v2-pre-rename-only and live in pre-rename-upgrades.md, so a v1→v2 reader is not harmed — but this paragraph is the file's own second classification copy, and it is the copy that has drifted.)
 (c) Corpus M-72 (lines 836-878): "**Type B** for the durable-read judgment, **Type A** for the mechanical reshape" — a v1 surface (v1 apps used `inject-cofx` and `:now`/UUID cofx).  (d) Corpus M-31a (line 1433): "**Type B** (touch test-namespace requires)" — the at-a-glance paragraph enumerates every other pre-rename id (M-55..M-69) and omits this one.

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): spec/ re-authoring triad still says shims are on disk, tests are smoke-only, and names hot-reload/wait + an unemitted connect reason
description:
## CLAIM

The re-authoring scaffolding under `skills/re-frame2-pair/spec/` is labelled "exists to re-author the skill from inputs" (each file's banner). Four statements in it no longer describe the skill as shipped, and one contradicts a sibling sentence in the same file:

1. `spec/inputs.md:42` — "**Bash shims** — `skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts/*.sh`. Retired from the skill's tool surface …; **on disk only for the project's own e2e harness and ad-hoc shell use**."
2. `spec/design.md:274` (OQ3) — "`tests/` exists but **only carries connection smoke tests**."
3. `spec/design.md:105` — "the skill returns `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair` on connect."
4. `spec/design.md:156` (L4) and `spec/authoring-prompt.md:57` (cardinal rule 4) — "the AI **must** call `hot-reload/wait` before dispatching"; `design.md:251` "Skipping `hot-reload/wait`".
5. `spec/inputs.md:26` lists `register-epoch-listener!` among `re-frame.core`'s "public single-import API"; `authoring-prompt.md:51,55` and `design.md:138` use the same name as a facade surface.

## TRUTH AT TIP

1. `git ls-files skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/e2e skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/shim` returns nothing — no `scripts/` dir exists; `tests/shim/` on disk is an untracked empty `target/` leftover. The same file says so eleven paragraphs later (`inputs.md:69` §7.5: "has been **removed**"), as do `design.md:161` (OQ1 "Resolved: yes, removed"), `docs/TESTING.md:5` and `docs/initial-spec.md:15-20`. §4 is the one surviving copy of the pre-removal wording.
2. `tests/` today: `fixture/` (a shadow-cljs counter app + the `:pure-test` node-test build with 27 deftests over the shipped `pure.cljc`), `runtime/` (12 Babashka AST pins), `prompts/` (prompt_regression_test.clj, ~25 deftests). `docs/TESTING.md` §1–3 describe all three. There are no "connection smoke tests".
3. `grep -rn 're-frame2-tool-pair' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload` returns nothing. The connect verdicts the server actually emits are the `discover-app` ladder in `tools/discover_app.cljs:25-26,193,207` (`:debug-disabled`, `:no-frames-registered`, `:build-not-running`, `:no-runtime-connected`, `:nrepl-unreachable`, `:runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing`), catalogued in `references/errors.md`.
4. There is no op named `hot-reload/wait` in `references/ops.md`; the protocol is `tail-build` with a pre-edit `baseline` (`ops.md:249-275`, post rf2-1f60u). The name is a pre-MCP placeholder the shipped catalogue never used.
5. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` has no `defn register-epoch-listener!`; the facade is the stream-parameterised `(rf/register-listener! :epoch id cb)` (`core.cljc:2158` dispatches to `rf-epoch/register-epoch-listener!` on the epoch artefact). `SKILL.md:79` and `design.md:137` (L1) already state the facade form correctly — the `register-epoch-listener!` mentions are the older name surviving beside it.

`python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py --verbose` is green on all of this (it scans for retired tool/transport *names*, and none of these five is on its list).

## IMPACT

authoring-prompt.md is a one-shot "drop into a fresh session and it produces the skill" prompt. A re-author following it would (1) go looking for `scripts/*.sh` to keep "on disk for the e2e harness", (2) treat `tests/` as smoke-only and not know the pure-core node-test and AST pins are the behaviour + wiring gates, (3) teach a connect reason the server never emits, (4) teach an op name that does not exist instead of `tail-build` + baseline, (5) cite a facade fn that does not exist. Each is a P3 "historical claim not labelled historical" — here it is worse than initial-spec.md because these files are NOT labelled historical; they are labelled as the current re-authoring inputs.

## FIX SHAPE

One PR, three files, prose only:
- `inputs.md:42` — replace the bullet with the §7.5 wording (removed; MCP is the one implementation; live coverage in `live-e2e-fixture.cjs`), or delete it and let §7.5 stand.
- `inputs.md:26` — move `register-epoch-listener!` off the core.cljc list; name `(rf/register-listener! :epoch …)` as the facade form (matching L1 in design.md:137).
- `design.md:105` — cite the real ladder (`references/errors.md`) instead of `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair`.
- `design.md:156,251` + `authoring-prompt.md:57` — `hot-reload/wait` → "`tail-build` with the pre-edit `baseline` (ops.md §Hot-reload coordination)".
- `design.md:274` OQ3 — restate: `tests/` carries the fixture + pure-core node-test, the AST pins and prompt regression; AI-response evals remain deferred.
- `authoring-prompt.md:51,55` — `register-epoch-listener!` → `register-listener! :epoch`.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_pair_authoring_drift.py --verbose` (must stay green — do not reintroduce a retired name while rewording) and `bb tests/prompts/prompt_regression_test.clj` (`gated-write-tools-stay-allow-listed-in-reauthoring-docs` and `catalogue-count-matches-live-manifest` read all three spec files and `docs/initial-spec.md`). Nothing checks the corrected claims themselves — verify by hand against the cited paths and say so.

## ACCEPTANCE

`spec/inputs.md` §4 agrees with §7.5 that the shims are removed; no spec/ file names `hot-reload/wait`, `:missing :re-frame2-tool-pair`, or `register-epoch-listener!` as a facade fn; OQ3 describes the three test surfaces; both gates green.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 on 2026-09-02 11:04:06 AUSEST (skills review, partition B).
acceptance_criteria: spec/inputs.md §4 agrees with §7.5 (shims removed); no spec/ file names hot-reload/wait, :missing :re-frame2-tool-pair, or register-epoch-listener! as a facade fn; OQ3 describes the three test surfaces; authoring-drift + prompt_regression gates green

(1) shims: git ls-files for scripts/, tests/e2e, tests/shim returns 0 (control tests/runtime returns 13); 4 now says removed and points at 7.5. (2) OQ3 now names the three real test surfaces (fixture pure-core node-test, Babashka AST pins, prompt regression) with AI-response evals as the remaining deferred gap. (3) :missing :re-frame2-tool-pair is emitted nowhere in server or preload; design.md now cites the discover-app preload-failure ladder and :runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing, catalogued in references/errors.md. (4) hot-reload/wait has no ops.md row; replaced with the pre-edit probe baseline + tail-build protocol. (5) CONFIRMED, not refuted: core.cljc carries an explicit comment that the facade register-epoch-listener! / unregister-epoch-listener! pair was deliberately retired under API-shrink #4; the epoch stream is (rf/register-listener! :epoch id f). The one surviving mention in inputs.md:26 is in an explicit 'there are deliberately no facade exports' framing, which is the acceptance's 'not named as a facade fn'. title: skill(re-frame2-pair): LOCAL_DEV.md troubleshooting describes a port-discovery mechanism the server does not have (mtime pick, implementation/ scan)
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-pair/docs/LOCAL_DEV.md:153` (§Troubleshooting → "`discover-app` can't find the nREPL"):

> The MCP server discovers the port automatically (it scans `target/shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`, `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`, `.nrepl-port` at the CWD and under `implementation/`, and picks the most-recently-modified one).

## TRUTH AT TIP

`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/nrepl.cljs` (`discover-port*` docstring, :123-175) and `server.cljs:18-35`: discovery is a **five-step cascade** — (1) `--port-file`, (2) `$SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT`, (3) MCP `roots/list` workspace walk for `shadow-cljs.edn` + adjacent port file (one hit attaches; several → `elicitation/create`; `roots_discovery.cljs:79` skips `node_modules` / `.git` / `.shadow-cljs` / `target` / `out` / `.cpcache`), (4) shadow HTTP probe `GET :9630/api/project-info` → `:project-home`, (5) CWD-relative scan of the three candidates in fixed order (`nrepl.cljs:48-50`, `(some read-port-file port-file-candidates)` — **first hit wins**).

- There is no modification-time comparison anywhere in the server: `grep -rnE 'mtime|lastModified|statSync' tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src` returns nothing. "picks the most-recently-modified one" is invented.
- There is no cwd scan "under `implementation/`". The only `implementation/` mention is `roots_discovery.cljs:23,59` — the roots walk (step 3) treats `<root>/implementation/` as a typical `shadow-cljs.edn` location. The sentence conflates the roots walk with the cwd scan.
- The sentence omits the two paths that actually resolve most sessions (steps 3 and 4), so an operator reading this section when discovery misses will look at the wrong thing (port-file mtimes) instead of the right ones (is the workspace root exposed via `roots/list`; is shadow's HTTP server on 9630 or does `--http-port` need setting).

The skill's own transport leaf has the correct description at `references/mcp-transport.md:38-47` (five steps, in order, with the restart-absorption note).

## IMPACT

Wrong mental model in the one place an operator goes when attach fails. The `--port-file` / `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` override advice in the next paragraph (:161) is still correct, so the operator can escape — but only by skipping the diagnosis the section pretends to give.

## FIX SHAPE

Replace the parenthetical at `docs/LOCAL_DEV.md:153` with a one-sentence pointer: "The MCP server discovers the port through a five-step cascade (`--port-file` → `$SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` → MCP `roots/list` walk → shadow HTTP probe → cwd scan) — see [`references/mcp-transport.md` §Install / configure](../references/mcp-transport.md#install--configure-one-time)." Do not restate the cascade; the transport leaf is the single source. While there, the same section's :161 mention of `--port-file` / `SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` is correct and stays.

## GATE

No gate covers this prose. `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` validates the new relative link + anchor (skills/ is in its roots). Verify the cascade wording by hand against `nrepl.cljs` `discover-port*` and say so in the PR body.

## ACCEPTANCE

`docs/LOCAL_DEV.md` no longer claims an mtime pick or an `implementation/` cwd scan; its discovery sentence names the five-step cascade (or links to mcp-transport.md's description); `check_doc_slugs.py` green.

Reviewed at tip 72df4dd915 on 2026-09-02 11:04:06 AUSEST (skills review, partition B).
acceptance_criteria: LOCAL_DEV.md no longer claims an mtime pick or implementation/ cwd scan and names/links the five-step cascade in mcp-transport.md; check_doc_slugs.py green
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9007 (commit 2c389e03a4, rebased 75765280c4). docs/LOCAL_DEV.md's discovery sentence (line 152, not the cited 153) no longer claims an mtime pick or an implementation/ cwd scan. It now names the five-step cascade in precedence order and links to references/mcp-transport.md #install--configure-one-time as the single source, then points the operator at steps 3-4 -- the two that resolve most sessions -- instead of at port-file mtimes. Verified by hand against nrepl.cljs discover-port* (five-step precedence; step 5 is (some read-port-file port-file-candidates), first hit wins) and roots_discovery.cljs (the only implementation/ mention, and it is the step-3 roots walk). No mtime comparison exists in the server: mtime|lastModified|statSync|birthtime returns 0 hits, control readFileSync returns 8. check_doc_slugs.py exit 0, and proven to read this worktree by a planted broken anchor on this very link (went exit 1 naming it; restored, blob hash verified).

title: skill(re-frame2-pair): mcp-transport.md dispatch-dry-run row advertises fx-overrides (schema-absent, runtime-refused) and omits cofx
description:
## CLAIM

`skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md:90` (the "MCP tool reference (args)" table — the transport index the drift gate cross-checks):

> | `dispatch-dry-run` | `{event, frame?, fx-overrides?}` — simulate WITHOUT committing; not `--allow-writes`-gated | [`ops.md` §Write](ops.md#write) |

## TRUTH AT TIP

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs` — the `dispatch-dry-run` descriptor's `inputSchema` properties are `event, frame, cofx, elision, include-sensitive, include-fx-args, build` with `:additionalProperties false`. There is no `fx-overrides` property.
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch_dry_run.cljs:93-100` ("## Rejects fx-overrides"): a caller `:fx-overrides` is REJECTED loudly with `:reason :fx-overrides-unsupported` (isError); `fx-overrides-rejected` at :132.
- The skill's own semantics home already says so: `references/ops.md:79` — "A caller `:fx-overrides` is **rejected** (`:reason :fx-overrides-unsupported`)". `tests/runtime/dry_run_sink_pin_test.clj` (`dispatch-dry-run-rejects-caller-fx-overrides`) pins the refusal in the preload.
- `cofx` IS accepted on dry-run (descriptor + `dispatch_dry_run.cljs`), and the fixture's `:counter/stamp` event exists precisely for scripted-cofx dispatches — the transport row omits it.

## IMPACT

The two leaves contradict each other on one tool: the transport index advertises `fx-overrides?` as an accepted arg while the semantics leaf and the server refuse it. An agent composing a dry-run from the arg table gets an isError round-trip it did not expect; an agent wanting a reproducible dry-run cannot see from the index that `cofx` is available. Low blast radius (the `tools/list` descriptor is what the agent sees at call time, and it is right) — hence P3, not P2 — but it is a one-line contradiction inside the skill's own contract, on the one table the family README calls "complete by gate".

## FIX SHAPE

One row in `references/mcp-transport.md`: `{event, frame?, cofx?}` — and keep the row's existing "not `--allow-writes`-gated" note. Optionally add "(a caller `fx-overrides` is refused — see ops.md §Write)". No other file.

## GATE

`python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose` (doc-coverage axis: the row must still be present, 29 = 29). No gate reads the arg-signature column — verify the new signature by hand against the descriptor's `:properties` in `descriptors_data.cljs`, and say so in the PR body.

title: skill(re-frame2): xstate-translation.md has no row for three shipped transition-grammar features — :ns/* and :* wildcards, :reenter? self-transitions, cross-region :tags/:all-state guard ctx (the stateIn analog)
description:
CLAIM
- `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/xstate-translation.md:11-37` — the translation table; `reg-machine.md:20` calls it "The full 27-row translation key — every concept, convergence and divergence"; SKILL.md cardinal rule 3 names it the standing mental model ("think in xstate, then map onto re-frame2 … a handful re-frame2 renames or omits, and those divergences are the trap").
- `xstate-translation.md:7` lists `stateIn` among the v5 helper creators v6 "removes … which re-frame2 never had" — with no row saying what re-frame2 ships for the cross-region-coordination *concept*.
- `reg-machine.md:118-132` (§Transition shape): the `:on` value forms — bare target / map / guarded vector. Nothing on event-descriptor tiers.
- `reg-machine.md:153-155` (§Guard/action contract): "Every callback receives one context map — `{:keys [data event state meta] cofx :rf.cofx}` … the runtime always delivers the full context map".
- `regions.md` has no section on how one region's guard reads a sibling region's state.
- `git grep -nEi "reenter|wildcard|:ns/\*|all-state|stateIn" skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/ skills/re-frame2/decision-trees/` hits only the L7 preamble above.

TRUTH AT TIP — three shipped transition-grammar features with no row and no leaf
1. Wildcard / partial event descriptors. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:289-330` (§Wildcard transitions, §Namespaced (partial) event descriptors — `:ns/*`): `:on` resolves three tiers, exact → `:ns/*` → `:*`, least-priority *enabled* candidate at each level. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:800` (`:event-key <matched :on key, else nil> ;; exact / :ns/* / :* key`). XState spelling: `'*'` and `'mouse.*'` wildcard keys — a v4/v5/v6 constant an xstate-trained agent will reach for.
2. `:reenter?` self-transitions. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:332-360` (§Self-transitions — internal default vs external `:reenter?`): four geometries — targetless (action only, children preserved), self/ancestor target without `:reenter?` (re-resolves descendants to `:initial`), descendant target from a compound (re-enters the child), `:reenter? true` (exit + entry, timers restart, `:spawn` children respawn). `transition.cljc:1512-1522` implements the opt-in. XState spelling: `reenter: true` (v5/v6), `internal: false` (v4).
3. Cross-region coordination — the `stateIn` analog. `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1750-1836` (§Cross-region coordination — tags as `stateIn`): a guard/action running inside a parallel region gets two extra ctx keys, `:tags` (machine-wide tag union — "**the** documented `stateIn` equivalent") and `:all-state` (region-name → active-state map, `(= :valid (:form (:all-state ctx)))`), frozen at the start of the selection round; flat/compound ctx stays exactly `{:data :event :state :meta}`. `transition.cljc:284-333` (`callback-ctx`: "additionally receives `:tags` + `:all-state`" for region callbacks).

IMPACT
These are precisely the "xstate-trained intuition steers you wrong" cases the leaf exists for, and today each ends in a hand-roll: duplicating a transition per event id instead of `:mouse/*`; exiting-and-re-entering via an intermediate state to get `:after` timers to restart, or writing an action that resets `:data` because "self-transition re-resolves children" is unknown; coupling regions through shared `:data` flags because the guard contract paragraph says the ctx is *exactly* `{data event state meta}`. Item 3 is also a correctness bug in `reg-machine.md:153-155` as written for parallel machines.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, three files)
- `xstate-translation.md`: three rows — **wildcard transitions** (`'*'` / `'ns.*'` → `:*` / `:ns/*`, convergence, note the enabled-fallthrough rule); **`reenter`** (`reenter: true` → `:reenter? true`; default = xstate "internal" geometry; targetless = action-only); **`stateIn` / `In()`** (→ read `(:tags ctx)` or `(:all-state ctx)` inside a region guard; flat machines use their own `:state`). Fix L7 so `stateIn` points at its row rather than reading as "never had".
- `reg-machine.md` §Transition shape: one line naming the three descriptor tiers; §Guard/action contract: "flat / compound: exactly `{data event state meta}`; inside a parallel region also `:tags` and `:all-state` — see regions.md". Fix "27-row" to the real count (the table has 25 rows today; 28 after).
- `regions.md`: a short §Cross-region coordination (the `:submit`-guarded-on-sibling-validity example from spec §1772, ~10 lines) and one gotcha on the frozen-config rule.
Watch the byte ceiling: reg-machine.md is already 19.8 KB (separate size bead); keep the additions to one line each there.

title: skill(re-frame2): cancellation.md teaches one auto-released resource kind; the runtime releases three (:after timers, :rf.resource/* owners under [:machine actor-id])
description:
CLAIM
`skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/cancellation.md`:
- L5 (§When to load): "The cleanup is automatic; this leaf tells you what is guaranteed and what to add by hand for non-HTTP side effects."
- L11 (§The guarantee): "When the runtime destroys a spawned actor by **any** trigger, every in-flight `:rf.http/managed` request the actor had issued is aborted." — the only guarantee the leaf states.
- L57 (§Cooperative cleanup for non-HTTP side effects): "The framework's automatic abort hook covers `:rf.http/managed`. For anything else a child holds — a websocket, **a timer**, a subscription on an external stream — wire your own cleanup into the child's `:exit` action."
- L100-102 (§Why one mechanism, not two): restates the HTTP-only hook.

TRUTH AT TIP
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3607-3619` (§What auto-cancels on destroy — exactly three framework-managed resource kinds): "1. In-flight `:rf.http/managed` requests … 2. Armed `:after` timers the actor scheduled — cancelled by `cancel-actor-timers!` on the same destroy path … 3. `:rf.resource/*` owners the actor holds under its `[:machine <actor-id>]` owner — released by dispatching the existing `:rf.resource/release-owner` effect on the same destroy path … The release fires on every destroy trigger". Then: "Any other resource a child actor holds is NOT auto-released — a `setInterval` / raw `setTimeout` issued via a custom fx, a WebSocket subscription, …".
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/resource_release.cljc` (ns docstring): machine teardown releases the actor's `[:machine actor-id]` resource owners by keyword-dispatching `:rf.resource/release-owner`, guarded by `release-owner-registered?` so it is a no-op without the resources artefact; "Together these cover EVERY destroy cause".
- `timer/cancel-actor-timers!` is called from `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:256` and `lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc:640`.

IMPACT
Two consumer-visible errors. (a) The leaf says "a timer" is the author's job — an agent reads that as "wire `:exit` cleanup for my `:after`", which the runtime already cancels; the correct scope is *raw* `setTimeout` / `setInterval` issued through a custom fx. title: skill(re-frame2): state-machines leaves teach def-then-reg-machine, the one shape that loses per-element source coords — teach rf/defmachine (every example uses it)
description:
CLAIM
- `skills/re-frame2/references/state-machines/reg-machine.md:43-73` (§Declaration shape, "The basic form"): `(def my-machine {...})` then `(rf/reg-machine :my/feature my-machine)`.
- `reg-machine.md:211` (§Common gotchas): "Use `reg-machine` (macro), not `reg-machine*` (fn). The macro stamps per-element source coords that tools rely on".
- `regions.md:17-45`: `(def tags-machine {...})` … `(rf/reg-machine :realworld/tags tags-machine)` — "Adapted from `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/tags.cljs`".
- `regions.md:54-69`: `(def nine-states-machine {...})` … `(rf/reg-machine :ui/nine-states nine-states-machine)`.
- `defmachine` appears in the partition once, in passing (`reg-machine.md:197`, inside the make-machine-handler advanced note: "the `reg-machine` / `defmachine` registration macros stay on the `rf/` façade"). No leaf says what it is for or when to use it.

TRUTH AT TIP
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:682-731` (`defmachine` docstring): "The common app shape is `(def door-machine {…}) … (reg-machine :door/main door-machine)` — `reg-machine` sees only the `door-machine` symbol, so its compile-time literal-walk captures nothing … `defmachine` is the `def`-replacement that walks the inline literal AT THE DEFINITION SITE and co-locates per-element source onto each `:guards` / `:actions` / `:on-spawn-actions` entry … Use `defmachine` for the `def`-then-register shape; use the `reg-machine` macro directly when registering an inline literal."
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:1110-1142` (§Value-registered machines — `defmachine`): same rule, normative; "Without `defmachine`, the Epoch machine-cascade (and any tool reading `cascade-row-coord` / `cascade-row-source-form`) has no per-element source to render for value-registered machines".
- `examples/**` (L2 — canonical, per SKILL.md cardinal rule 5): every def-then-register machine uses `rf/defmachine` — 11 sites, including the two files the leaves cite as their source: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/tags.cljs:67` (`(rf/defmachine tags-machine`) and `examples/patterns/nine_states/core.cljs:259` (`(rf/defmachine nine-states-machine`). `git grep -nE "^\(rf/defmachine" examples/` lists them; the only plain `(def …-machine` left in examples is `examples/core/login/model.cljs:293`.
- The pattern leaves (`patterns/*.md`) all register an inline literal `(rf/reg-machine :id {...})`, which the macro walks — they are fine. Only the two state-machines leaves above teach the value-registered shape, and both teach it with plain `def`.

IMPACT
The skill's own stated reason for preferring the `reg-*` macros (SKILL.md cardinal rule 8, `reg-machine.md:211`) is per-element source coordinates — and the canonical declaration it hands the agent is exactly the shape that loses them. An agent matching the leaf produces machines whose guards/actions are invisible to `(rf/handler-meta :machine-guard [id guard-id])`, Xray's machine inspector and the Epoch machine-cascade source rendering, while the example it is told to cross-check against (`tags.cljs`) uses `defmachine`. The code runs; the tooling story the skill sells does not.

FIX SHAPE (one PR, three files in this partition)
1. `reg-machine.md` §Declaration shape: change `(def my-machine` to `(rf/defmachine my-machine` and add one sentence under the block: "`defmachine` is `def` for a literal machine map — it captures per-element source at the definition site so the value carries it into `reg-machine`; use `reg-machine` on an inline literal, `defmachine` + `reg-machine` for the named-value shape." Add a matching line to §Common gotchas beside the `reg-machine*` bullet.
2. `regions.md:17` and `:54`: `(def …` → `(rf/defmachine …` (matches the cited examples verbatim).
3. `reg-machine.md:197`: keep the passing mention; it is now backed by the recipe.
Cross-partition note (do not fix here, name it in the PR body): `references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md` §Machines has no `defmachine` row (partition B); SKILL.md cardinal rule 8 could name `defmachine` beside `reg-machine*` (partition A).

GATE
`python scripts/check_skill_re_frame2_drift.py --verbose` (must stay green — rule 4 forbids a fenced `reg-event` + `make-machine-handler` recipe, which this change does not touch) and `python scripts/check_skill_package_refs.py --verbose`. THREE THINGS THE RECIPE MUST NOT SAY, all measured on PR #9054.

(a) :render-state IS NOT AN ssr-handler OPT. It is an opt on the RENDERER (re-frame.ssr.ring.node/renderer), because the renderer is what projects. host.clj carried a top-level :render-state that ssr-handler silently ignored while reading exactly like the live policy — a dead key that any recipe copying the old file would propagate. It is gone.

(b) THE POLICY IS ONE Var IN A .cljc NAMESPACE, hicasso.login.policy/render-state-policy (and root-entry beside it), required by both host.clj and server.cljs. Do not show the recipe writing the list twice: neither file can be read by the other's compiler, so two copies can only be kept in step by hand, and the drift the sidecar CANNOT refuse is the safe-looking one — a host asking for FEWER keys than the entry allows is served a page rendered from incomplete state with no refusal. A .cljc policy namespace is the shape the recipe should teach.

(c) ON THE SHIPPED LOGIN CONFIGURATION THE RUNTIME PARTITION CROSSES EMPTY. :auth.login/flow is self-seeding — it materialises a snapshot the first time it is dispatched at or subscribed to — and the JVM host does neither, because the render happens in Node. So :rf.runtime/machines is on the render-state list for the host that HAS driven the flow (a session-restoring one), not for this one; Node's own per-request frame seeds :idle and draws the form, which is the correct page. Both halves are asserted in the JVM witness. The example README has been corrected to say this; the recipe should not repeat the older, stronger claim that the shipped example needs that partition to render correctly.

title: hic: chapter 20 step 1 — the migration reporter must run from a clean workspace with no re-frame2 checkout (pilots README gap G2 does NOT move with the first tag)
description:
FILED 2026-09-02 by the delegated ruling on rf2-hic-063 (the RULING note of that date on that bead is the authority). Tip b26c5ad33e. Depends on rf2-kmqx3 (a published Hicasso coordinate must exist first). Blocks rf2-hic-063: a counted pilot must be able to begin outcome 2 from the published site alone.

THE DEFECT. docs/core/hicasso/20-migration-from-reagent.md makes the migration report step 1 of the published process and tells the reader `cd re-frame2/migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod` then `clojure -M:run path/to/your/src/` (lines 22-32). That is a path inside the source checkout: the codemod is not in .github/workflows/release.yml's deploy DAG (a grep for codemod there returns nothing), and its deps.edn puts `../../../implementation/hicasso/src` on `:paths` so the tool and the runtime share ONE slot-rule implementation (rf2-ani6y / rf2-r4j91 — a deliberate design; keep the sharing). docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/README.md records this as gap G2 and says "No bead filed: it is the same root cause as G1 and is expected to move with it". It will NOT move with it: rf2-kmqx3 publishes the Hicasso jar, not the reporter. After the tag, a counted pilot following the public page still cannot run step 1 without a re-frame2 checkout beside its project — which is exactly the contamination the artefact gate exists to remove — or must skip the reporter and lose the "what the migration report said before the port" evidence outcome 2 requires.

THE FIX — the least thing that makes the printed command true without a checkout. Trust the programmer; do NOT build a "released tool" or a second coordinate. Candidates, cheapest first: (1) a one-line `clojure -Sdeps` / `-T` invocation resolving the codemod as a git dep of the tagged release (`:git/tag` + `:git/sha` + `:deps/root "migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod"`), with the shared slot rule reached through the published `io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso` jar rather than the relative `:paths` entry; (2) if the relative entry must stay for the in-repo `identical?` pin (shared_rule_test.clj), an alias that swaps it for the jar when run outside the repo. Whichever is chosen, chapter 20 step 1 prints the exact public command.

ACCEPTANCE. The command printed on the public page runs the reporter against a sample source directory from an EMPTY directory with no re-frame2 checkout anywhere beside it and an isolated Maven cache (`:mvn/local-repo`); chapter 20 updated; pilots/README.md's G2 row transitions to closed under that page's own protocol; the codemod's `clojure -M:test` still green.

GATES. The codemod's `clojure -M:test` (migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod); scripts/check_doc_slugs.py for the docs/core/ page and scripts/check_provenance_pins.py for the pilots README; mkdocs build --strict for chapter 20 (inside docs_dir, not excluded). Hot zone: none expected — if a workflow job is added, sequence against rf2-kmqx3, which touches .github/workflows/*.

description:
FILED 2026-09-02 by the delegated ruling on rf2-hic-063 (that bead's RULING note of the same date is the authority; the Codex review that surfaced this defect is folded there). Tip b26c5ad33e.

THE DEFECT. docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/workspace.md step 2 creates `app/test/` for both pilots and copies nothing into it; its source manifest copies only application source, index.html, the avatar and the README. friction-log.md outcome 1 is "The app's behavioural tests are preserved across the migration — the test command and its captured exit code, before and after", and workspace.md:134 says both pilots need the test kit "from the first hour, because outcome 1 is to preserve the app's behavioural tests". But the pilots' behavioural tests do not live with the apps — the examples tree is test-free by policy (rf2-8cevm) — they live in the adapter test tree: implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs (broad RealWorld integration coverage) and implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs (ten optimistic commit/rollback tests). `grep -rn "realworld_cljs_test\|linearlite_example_cljs_test\|adapters/reagent/test" docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/` returns nothing. As assembled, a pilot is told to run the app's suite before migrating and receives no suite and no test build: outcome 1 is BLOCKED at hour zero for both pilots, and it would be recorded as the framework's friction when it is the operator's scaffolding.

THE FIX. workspace.md is the OPERATOR's page — the pilot never reads it — so in-tree knowledge is allowed here; it must not leak into the two briefs.
1. Give each workspace an app-owned behavioural baseline under `app/test/` that runs from the clean workspace: extract the subset of the two adapter suites that exercises the nominated screens (RealWorld: feed + article editor + the routing they need; LinearLite: the board's create / retitle / change-status optimistic patches, commit and rollback), standing on cljs.test plus whatever the workspace can resolve from the published route (the Hicasso test kit on its `:test` alias, core test support) — NOT on the in-repo harness. Both suites currently use `re-frame.test-support` snapshot/restore and canned-stub helpers that live in the adapter test tree; whatever the copied tests need travels with them. Scope to the named screens — the whole RealWorld suite is not required.
2. Add the test build to the copy-ready shadow-cljs.edn in workspace.md (a `:node-test` or `:browser-test` target) and the one-line test command, so "the test command and its captured exit code" exists.
3. Add a step 5b to the six-step setup: run the baseline with the app still on Reagent and record its exit code in the log header beside the pinned commit. A baseline that is not green before the pilot starts is the operator's problem, not the pilot's.
4. Update the per-pilot source manifest so a second operator can rebuild the workspace by following the page alone.

ACCEPTANCE. From a workspace built by following workspace.md alone, `app/` runs its baseline green on Reagent before any Hicasso change; the two briefs are unchanged, or changed only to name the test command — no in-tree path may appear in either brief (rf2-hic-069's fresh-reader fence). Anchors and table column counts verified by hand and stated in the PR body.

GATES. Edit confined to docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/ (plus any extracted test files, if committed as a fixture under that directory rather than inline): scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and scripts/check_provenance_pins.py; mkdocs build --strict is NOT the gate (exclude_docs). No hot-zone file. Parallel-safe.

title: release: post-publish consumer artefact-install gate in release.yml — cold-repo resolution of io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso (+core, +ssr) after every v* tag
description:
FILED 2026-09-02 10:15 AUSEST by the delegated ruling on rf2-kmqx3 (tip b26c5ad33e). This bead is the REPEATABLE form of rf2-kmqx3's artefact-install proof: a post-publish job in release.yml that resolves the just-published set from Clojars into a cold Maven local repo and compiles a minimal consumer. It publishes nothing and gates nothing irreversible; it observes.

BLOCKED ON rf2-kmqx3, and the block is structural: this job resolves a PUBLISHED artefact, so it cannot be authored, run or exercised before io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso 0.0.1.alpha exists on Clojars and the one-off proof on rf2-kmqx3 has passed. Do not dispatch before rf2-kmqx3 closes. rf2-fo4ng (the 19-coordinate rename) is upstream of rf2-kmqx3 and will have merged by then.

HOT ZONE — .github/workflows/release.yml. One workflow toucher at a time: at dispatch, re-measure `bd list --status=open --limit 0 --desc-contains ".github/workflows"` and sequence behind any live one. At filing time rf2-zq34m, rf2-4a0c and rf2-8arzr named .github/workflows in their descriptions; do not trust that list.

## Deliverable

1. One new job `verify-consumer-install` in .github/workflows/release.yml with `needs: [github-release]` (runs on the same tag run, after the whole publish DAG and the GitHub Release). No deploy job's `needs` changes. No second trigger on release.yml — the v* glob at lines 162-165 stays the only one; the DAG policy test pins that shape.

2. A script .github/scripts/verify-consumer-install.sh (POSIX sh, CI-only, runnable under Git Bash locally) taking VERSION as its argument, so the worker can run it against the already-published 0.0.1.alpha — the exercised half of acceptance, because a tag-only workflow cannot be run on a PR. The job passes `${{ needs.deploy-core.outputs.version }}` (the value the release body at ~926-939 already uses).

3. What the script does, in order:
   a. `mktemp -d` a scratch directory OUTSIDE $GITHUB_WORKSPACE; never read the repo's deps.edn.
   b. Write deps.edn: `{:paths ["src"] :deps {io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:mvn/version "<VERSION>"}} :mvn/local-repo "<fresh empty dir>"}`. Do NOT declare core or ssr — they must arrive transitively through the published pom; that transitivity working is the proof.
   c. `clojure -Srepro -P` with a bounded retry for Clojars propagation lag (e.g. up to ~10 minutes, 30s apart) before failing. `-Srepro` ignores ~/.clojure/deps.edn so no mirror or local-repo override leaks in. Never use an actions/cache-warmed ~/.m2 as the resolution source; the fresh :mvn/local-repo is what makes the gate honest even when a cache action is present.
   d. `clojure -Srepro -Stree` captured to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and asserted: io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso, io.github.day8/re-frame2 and io.github.day8/re-frame2-ssr all present at exactly VERSION, and ZERO old-group `day8/` coordinates anywhere in the tree (an old-group dependency surviving in a pom is the rename campaign's miss, and this is where it shows).
   e. Minimal compile: `npm i react@19.2 react-dom@19.2 shadow-cljs@3.4.10` in the scratch dir (npm, not the repo's node_modules); a shadow-cljs.edn with `:deps true` and one :browser build whose single namespace requires re-frame.core and re-frame.hicasso; `npx shadow-cljs compile app` exits 0. This catches a jar that resolves but is missing packed content (hicasso's :src-dirs are ["src" "resources" "test_kit/src"], implementation/hicasso/deps.edn 169-176). Versions per the compatibility matrix in docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md.

4. SCOPE: hicasso is the mandatory entry point because it exercises the deepest transitive chain (core + ssr). Extending to all 14 framework coordinates is RECOMMENDED if it is one loop and the list is DERIVED — from .github/scripts/verify-version-lockstep.sh's ARTEFACTS inventory (line 139 at filing) or from the workflow's own matrix — never a hand roster in the new job or script. A roster cannot report what it does not list (the lesson recorded at the top of preflight-tool-package.sh). If the 14-loop is included, the compile step stays hicasso-only; resolution runs per coordinate.

5. Policy test: implementation/scripts/_release-dag-policy.test.cjs asserts exactly 14 publishers (line ~282) and the ordering edges. The new job publishes nothing and must not be discovered as a publisher. Add a negative-control case asserting (i) `verify-consumer-install` is not in the publisher set, (ii) no deploy job lists it in `needs`, (iii) publisher count is still 14.

6. Failure semantics, written as the job's header comment AND as one paragraph in docs/release-process.md (under §Topological deploy DAG or a short new §Post-publish consumer gate): the job is post-publish and can un-publish nothing. Red from propagation lag → re-run the failed job only (`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed`); NEVER re-push the tag (deploy-core 409s on the duplicate upload; docs/release-process.md §Recovery). Red from an unresolvable pom or missing packed content → bump-and-supersede per §Recovery (0.0.1.alpha → 0.0.1.alpha-1).

## Acceptance

- release.yml carries the one new job with `needs: [github-release]`; `git diff` shows no change to any deploy job's `needs`, matrix or steps, and no new trigger.
- The DAG policy test passes with the new negative-control case; publisher count 14.
- The script, run locally by the worker from a fresh :mvn/local-repo against the published 0.0.1.alpha, exits 0; its -Stree output is pasted in the PR body and shows the three coordinates at 0.0.1.alpha and no day8/* coordinate.
- The same script against a deliberately absent version (e.g. 9.9.9) exits non-zero after its bounded retry — the gate has teeth.
- No hand-rostered coordinate list beyond the hicasso entry point; if the 14-loop is included it derives from the lockstep inventory or the workflow.
- docs/release-process.md paragraph landed; scripts/check_doc_slugs.py green; verify-version-lockstep.sh --self-test green; fast-PR spine green; actionlint if the repo runs it. Gates foreground, to completion, never backgrounded or piped through a filter.
- First real CI exercise is the NEXT v* tag (0.0.1.alpha-1 or 0.0.2.alpha); say so in the PR body rather than claiming the YAML ran.

## Traps

Warm ~/.m2 or a cache action = a green that asked Clojars nothing; Clojars propagation lag after publish is minutes — retry, do not conclude; no yank exists; same-tag re-run 409s; no :local/root, no :git/url, no `clein install` anywhere in the proof (clein install is a pre-tag pom REHEARSAL, never the proof); do not touch the deploy DAG; hot-zone sequencing; the worker is on Windows-capable Git Bash locally but the script targets ubuntu-latest — keep it POSIX sh.

## Provenance

Ruled on rf2-kmqx3 (RULING 2026-09-02, delegated by Mike). The one-off proof that precedes this bead is defined there and on docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md's compatibility matrix; the release DAG facts are release.yml 162-165, 176-902 and docs/release-process.md 15-19, 128-160, 198-225 at tip b26c5ad33e.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-04 21:1x AUSEST from the delegated ruling on rf2-kmqx3 (tip 1ad17a77fe; the RULING note of that timestamp on rf2-kmqx3 is the authority). Two things for this bead's worker, neither changing its status or scope.

(1) BINDING — the compile fixture in Deliverable 3e is wrong as written. A shadow-cljs.edn with a bare :deps true reads deps.edn WITHOUT aliases, finds no thheller/shadow-cljs on the classpath and dies before compiling anything ("Could not locate shadow/cljs/devtools/cli"); installing the npm launcher does not supply the JVM artefact. The repository's own docs/core/hicasso/00-installation.md says exactly this at lines 37-45 and 90-93 (tip 1ad17a77fe). Use the corrected fixture from the rf2-kmqx3 ruling: deps.edn keeps exactly ONE declared re-frame2 dependency and isolates the compiler behind an alias —
  {:paths ["src"]
   :deps {io.github.day8/re-frame2-hicasso {:mvn/version "<VERSION>"}}
   :mvn/local-repo "<fresh empty dir>"
   :aliases {:shadow {:extra-deps {thheller/shadow-cljs {:mvn/version "3.4.10"}}}}}
and shadow-cljs.edn uses {:deps {:aliases [:shadow]} ...}. Keep the two proofs separate: clojure -Srepro -P then clojure -Srepro -Stree WITHOUT the alias is the resolution proof (three coordinates at VERSION, zero old-group day8/*, no :local/root, no git coordinate); the compile is the packed-content proof and is best invoked directly so no user config leaks in: clojure -Srepro -M:shadow -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile app (npm i react@19.2.0 react-dom@19.2.0 shadow-cljs@3.4.10 still needed in the scratch dir for React and the process shim). Record the download/tree transcript as well as the compile exit, so a setup failure is not mistaken for a broken jar.

(2) FOR THE WORKER TO DECIDE, not ruled: the independent reviewer of the rf2-kmqx3 dossier recommended that this verifier sit BETWEEN the deploy stages and github-release (needs: [deploy-core, deploy-leaf, deploy-ssr-ring, deploy-hicasso], with github-release adding needs: verify-consumer-install), on the ground that a post-github-release observer can detect a broken publication but cannot stop the repository announcing it. The trade-off: a propagation-lag red then delays the GitHub Release until gh run rerun --failed clears it (which re-runs the verifier and then github-release), and the DAG policy test's negative control must still hold (not a publisher, publisher count 14, no DEPLOY job's needs changes — github-release is not a deploy job). This bead's Deliverable 1 says needs: [github-release]; the reviewer's shape is the stricter one and costs one needs: line. Pick one, say why in the PR body.

title: test(ssr): four more fixtures nest :config so their frames are never platform-tagged
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-umi1w (PR #8934), which fixed the same defect in multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc and deliberately did NOT sweep the rest — a general audit was out of scope there.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): `rf/make-frame` opts are FLAT — `:platform` is a top-level record-config key, per make-frame's own docstring. These four sites pass `{:id fid :config {:platform :client}}`, which nests as `:config {:config {...}}`, so the frames are never platform-tagged at all:

  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc  (lines 89 and 298)
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/failed_root_isolation_dom_cljs_test.cljs  (line 45)
  implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/multi_root_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs  (line 42)

Line numbers are as measured on 2026-09-01 and should be re-derived at tip.

WHY IT MATTERS: harmless TODAY only because the runtime falls back to the host-wide platform marker — `(or (-> rec :config :platform) (interop/active-platform))` — and that marker is already `:client` on CLJS. So each fixture gets the platform it meant by accident, and no assertion in these files discriminates a tagged frame from an untagged one.

THE FIX, mirroring rf2-umi1w: flatten the opts to `{:id fid :platform :client}`, and add ONE assertion per fixture reading the tag back through `rf/frame-meta`. That accessor is `(merge (:config f) (:lifecycle f) {:id (:id f)})` — it flattens the frame's OWN config and does NOT fall back to the host-wide marker, which is what makes it discriminating. Verified on rf2-umi1w: restoring the nesting turns such an assertion red with `actual: (not (= :client nil))`.

NOTE the two `_dom_cljs_test.cljs` files are browser-gated, not covered by the ssr JVM suite or the consolidated node-test — gate them accordingly.

PRECEDENT: machine_after_rearm_cljs_test.cljc and multi_root_hydration_cljs_test.cljc both now use the flat form and carry a docstring warning about the trap.

SURFACE: test-only, implementation/ssr/test/.

The merged code correctly flattens all four `make-frame` opts maps. The new regression proof, however, reaches only three sites: each `the-fixture-frames-are-actually-platform-tagged` test calls that file's `fresh-frame!` helper. The fourth corrected site is the direct teardown/rebuild call in `failed_root_isolation_cljs_test.cljc` (`rf/make-frame {:id fid :platform :client}` inside `a-root-whose-seed-does-not-land-releases-its-claim`), which bypasses `fresh-frame!` and has no `frame-meta` assertion.

That gap is discriminating, not hypothetical. Returning only this rebuild to `{:config {:platform :client}}` leaves all three new tests green because they exercise the still-flat helpers. The rebuild test then checks only that hydration lands; the PR's own red-before established that the pre-existing behavioral tests pass when the tag is absent because runtime platform lookup falls back to the host marker. Thus the exact silent defect can recur at one of the four audited sites with the whole suite green, contrary to the close note's claim that one gate covers all four.

Completeness: four sites were fixed but only three are guarded. Correctness: the rebuilt frame can again carry `:platform nil` without a failure. Implementation quality: the repeated prose says the rebuilt frame "must carry" the tag, but the executable contract never reads it.

Minimal outcome: immediately assert the rebuilt frame's `rf/frame-meta` platform at that existing call site (or route both constructions through one equally small checked helper). No broader sweep, new fixture, or abstraction is needed.

title: ci(testbed-support): the jvm lane installs no node deps, so the real-node launch probes self-skip
description:
DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-1i1ec (PR #8932), reported by that worker as an observation it deliberately did not fix.

THE FINDING (verify at source before acting): CI's `jvm-tools-testbed-support` job runs no `npm ci`, so `launch-editor-installed?` is false and every node-backed block in the suite self-skips. The job reports **42 tests / 229 assertions** where a local run with the dependency present reports **42 / 260**.

WHY IT MATTERS: the exit code cannot distinguish a run from a skip. The suite is green either way, so the real-node launch probes — including the column-only refusal that PR #8932 added precisely because no existing test could reach that path — are exercised only on a developer's machine and never in CI. The 31-assertion delta is the only signal that the block ran at all, and nothing checks it.

WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: this is a pre-existing property of the lane, not something #8932 introduced, and the remedy is a CI decision rather than a test fix. Two shapes are available and they differ in cost: install the node dependency in that job so the blocks run, or assert the expected assertion count so a silent skip fails loudly. The second is cheap and catches the regression; the first is what actually buys the coverage.

SURFACE: `.github/workflows/` is HOT-ZONE and one-toucher — sequence this against any other workflow work. Adjacent: rf2-ohfym is the sibling observation for the http lane (no solo-namespace ordering), also workflow-touching; consider whether one dispatch should take both.
notes:
MAYOR RULING, 2026-09-01: install the node dependency in the jvm-tools-testbed-support job so the probes actually run. The assertion-count assert is the FALLBACK, not the answer.

The bead states the trade exactly: the count assert is cheap and catches the regression; installing the dependency is what buys the coverage. Take the coverage. PR #8932 added the column-only refusal precisely because no existing test could reach that path - a test written to cover an otherwise-unreachable refusal, which then never runs in CI, is dead weight, and dead weight is what the stance is against. Asserting the count converts silent non-coverage into loud non-coverage; that is an improvement over today but it is a guard on the hole rather than the fix, and it would leave the 31 assertions permanently unexercised outside a developer's machine.

FALLBACK WITH A MEASURABLE DISCRIMINATOR: if arming that job drags the whole implementation dependency tree in for one small package, the cost is disproportionate and the count assert is then correct. Decide it by measuring, not by estimating - check whether the launch-editor dependency can be installed on its own, and report the added wall-clock either way. If you take the fallback, say what you measured and why it crossed the line.

Either way the job must stop being able to report green on a run that skipped every node-backed block. That is the acceptance.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8943 (branch worker/cilanes). Took the RULING'S PRIMARY BRANCH — install the node dependency — not the assertion-count fallback, and decided it by measuring as the ruling required.

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE, both directions, before any edit: tools/testbed-support 'clojure -M:test' with implementation/node_modules absent captured exit 0 at 'Ran 42 tests containing 229 assertions'; with launch-editor present, exit 0 at 42 / 260. The 229-vs-260 claim and the 31-assertion delta hold exactly.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE BRANCH. The fallback was to be taken only if arming the job dragged the whole implementation dependency tree in for one small package. It does not. launch-editor@2.14.1 is a devDependency of implementation/package.json, so it comes from the same lockfile; 'npm ci' there installs 110 packages and fetches NO browsers (nothing in that lockfile carries an install script on Linux — only fsevents, macOS-only; playwright is not flagged hasInstallScript). Locally 10.9s cold-ish and 2.9s warm. On the runner it was better still: the PR's own job shows 'added 110 packages, and audited 111 packages in 2s', and the added wall clock from the run's step timings is 5 SECONDS (setup-node 2s + npm ci 3s) against a 23s whole-job time and a timeout-minutes: 10 budget. Nowhere near disproportionate, so the coverage branch is correct and the count assert is not needed.

CI EVIDENCE ON THE PR HEAD: 'JVM tools/testbed-support (clojure -M:test)' conclusion success, 'Ran 42 tests containing 260 assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.' — 260, not 229. The launch-editor probes ran in CI for the first time, including the column-only refusal PR #8932 added because no existing test could reach that path.

THE ACCEPTANCE ('the job must stop being able to report green on a run that skipped every node-backed block') NEEDED MORE THAN THE INSTALL. Installing makes the blocks run today but leaves the self-skip in place, so the job could go green on a skip again tomorrow (the step breaking, a package rename, a classifier change). RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES now turns each self-skip into a FAILURE naming the missing prerequisite (skip-or-fail), and the job sets it; a node-less developer box, which sets nothing, still skips exactly as before, and it is one assertion either way so the suite's count does not move with the skip. All four combinations exercised locally with captured exits: deps absent + flag unset = 0 (42/229, developer box preserved); deps present + flag unset = 0 (42/260); deps present + flag set = 0 (42/260, the CI shape); deps ABSENT + flag SET = 1 (42/229, 2 failures naming the prerequisite). That last row is the acceptance.

SURFACE: .github/workflows/test.yml only (hot-zone, one-toucher, sole workflow change in the diff) plus the test namespace. .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh and its mirror were READ, never edited — rf2-f9f3p's worker holds that pair.

`skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/fixture/deps.edn` directly resolves all five in-repo artefacts because the shipped preload requires their public surfaces. At #8903, production classifier probes report `skills_structural=false` for both `src/*` and `deps.edn` under:

- `implementation/epoch`
- `implementation/schemas`
- `implementation/machines`

The `re-frame2-pair-fixture-pure` job is therefore accepted as skipped on a change to three fifths of its in-repo classpath. Epoch happens to arm a different MCP-live gate, but schemas and machines arm neither Pair fixture; none of those substitutions makes this job's shipped-preload compile and pure-function contract run.

## Three lenses

Completeness: the new reverse-edge comment and mirror enumerate only the MIG-23 roots, while the incidental Pair claim stops after the two shared roots and leaves the rest of that fixture's declared local-root roster uncovered.

Correctness: an owned-namespace API or behavior change in schemas/machines/epoch can break `re_frame2_pair.pure` or its runtime preload while the one job that compiles/tests that shipped source is skipped; a skipped required job is an accepted result.

Implementation quality / narrow direction: extend the existing `skills_structural` reverse-edge shape to the remaining Pair local roots at `src/*` plus `deps.edn`, accepting the same small over-fire trade #8903 already chose for ssr/hicasso. Do not add a workflow, fixture, generic dependency engine, or a 29th output.

## Duplicate search

All-status searches covered pair fixture, shipped-preload pure, reverse edge, local root, `skills_structural`, epoch, schemas, and machines. No exact owner exists. `rf2-bbe91` owns the MIG-23 fixture's four roots and is correctly closed; this is its sibling Pair fixture rather than unfinished MIG-23 work.

title: core_machines.cljc emits :where (quote rf/reg-machine*) for a var that is :facade? false
description:
Surfaced by rf2-lzrza (PR #8912) while correcting source-file prose, and deliberately NOT changed there because it is an error-payload behaviour change rather than a prose fix.

implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc lines 137 and 139:

  (reg-machine-impl (quote rf/reg-machine*) machine-id machine)

The :where symbol names the re-frame.core facade spelling. But reg-machine* is :facade? false in spec/api-manifest.edn and is NOT a facade export - core.cljc line 391 says so explicitly (front-porch shrink, rf2-wad2fl): reach it through re-frame.machines/reg-machine*. So an error raised from this path tells the programmer to look at a var that is not on the namespace the message names.

The docstring at line 146 describes this faithfully and was left intact by PR #8912 for exactly that reason - it is TRUE about what the code emits. Line 149, which was caller GUIDANCE rather than a description of behaviour, was corrected to rf.machines/reg-machine*.

The sibling reg-machine (lines 157/159) emits (quote rf/reg-machine), which IS correct - that macro is a real facade export.

Decide whether the :where symbol should become rf.machines/reg-machine*. If it changes, the docstring at line 146 changes with it in the same commit.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-01 20:47 AUSEST — YES, CHANGE IT to rf.machines/reg-machine*.

The :where symbol exists to tell a programmer where to look. reg-machine* is :facade? false in spec/api-manifest.edn and core.cljc states outright that it is not a facade export (front-porch shrink, rf2-wad2fl), so an error raised from this path currently names a var that does not exist on the namespace the message implies. That is a worse failure than an unhelpful message: it sends the reader to a namespace, they find nothing, and the natural conclusion is that their build is broken rather than that the message is wrong. Naming the reachable spelling costs nothing and the pre-alpha posture has no back-compat claim on an error payload.

SCOPE: lines 137 and 139 of implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_machines.cljc, and the line 146 docstring in the SAME commit — that docstring is currently TRUE about what the code emits, which is exactly why PR #8912 left it alone, so it becomes false the moment the emission changes. Line 149 was already corrected by #8912 and needs nothing.

DO NOT TOUCH the sibling reg-machine at lines 157/159: it emits (quote rf/reg-machine) and that IS correct, because reg-machine is a real facade export. Changing it would introduce the defect this bead is closing.

CHECK FOR TEST PINS before editing: any test asserting the error payload's :where will pin the old symbol and must move in the same commit. Search for the literal both line-oriented and flattened.

NOT WANTED: a general audit of every :where symbol in the tree, a lint rule tying :where symbols to the facade manifest, or any change to the error's shape.
VERDICT 2026-09-01 22:11 AUSEST — RULING IMPLEMENTED as written. PR #8934 (draft at time of writing), commit 3c8541797b.

PREMISE HELD AT TIP, verified at source: spec/api-manifest.edn carries {:namespace "re-frame.machines", :var "reg-machine*", :tier :advanced, :kind :fn, :owner "005", :status "v1", :facade? false, ...}, and the sibling is {:namespace "re-frame.core", :var "reg-machine", :kind :macro, ..., :facade? true, ...}. So the ruling's two halves are both grounded: reg-machine* is not reachable as rf/reg-machine*, and reg-machine genuinely is rf/reg-machine.

LINE NUMBERS RE-DERIVED AT TIP rather than trusted (PR #8912 had moved lines in this file): emissions at 137 and 139, docstring at 144-146, sibling at 157/159 — all five matched the ruling exactly. After the edit the docstring block grows from 3 lines to 5, so the UNTOUCHED sibling now sits at 159/161. Line 149 was already rf.machines/reg-machine* from #8912 and needed nothing, as the ruling said.

WHAT CHANGED: lines 137/139 now emit 'rf.machines/reg-machine*, and the 144-146 docstring moved with them in the SAME commit — it had described the old emission truthfully, which is why #8912 left it alone, so it would have gone false the instant the emission changed. The sibling reg-machine at 159/161 still emits 'rf/reg-machine, untouched.

TEST PINS: NONE existed, so nothing had to move. Searched for the literal both ways as instructed. Line-oriented found 3 sites, whitespace-flattened found 4 — the discrepancy is line 146 carrying two occurrences, reconciled by counting occurrences per line rather than counting lines, not a line-broken pin. The control term 'rf/reg-machine' returned 1440 line hits / 1443 flattened, so the search was live rather than silently matching nothing. All hits were in core_machines.cljc itself; no test anywhere pins this symbol. The two :where pins that DO exist are on the sibling — machines/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:75-76 and machine_pure_error_contract_test.clj:389 — and late_bind_missing_test.clj:24 states in prose that it covers reg-machine only.

CONTROLS — TWO, because the specified one cannot bite, and the reason is itself the finding. Reverting the symbol on line 137 and re-running the machines suite came back GREEN (captured exit 0, 1220 tests / 4289 assertions, 0 failures). That is not a broken control: it is the measured explanation for how this defect survived, and it agrees exactly with the pin search above.

Because a green run proves nothing about WHICH TREE the gate read, a second and COVERED fault was planted at a line adjacent to the edit — the sibling's 'rf/reg-machine replaced with 'rf/BOGUS-SENTINEL-UUQEK. The machines gate went red naming it: captured exit 1, exactly 1 failure, 'actual: (not (= rf/reg-machine rf/BOGUS-SENTINEL-UUQEK))', totals otherwise unchanged. The sentinel existed only in this worktree, so a run that had strayed into another checkout would have come back green. That establishes the gate read the right tree AND that this file's :where mechanism is genuinely under test — which is the direct evidence for the ruling's DO-NOT-TOUCH constraint on the sibling.

Both plants restored and verified by git BLOB hash against the committed object (line endings are translated here, so a byte digest of the working file is not sound). Each plant's anchor match count was read as exactly 1 BEFORE the gate was spent.

GATES, all on the final rebased base cdb9652c0f, exit captured on one command line:
  core JVM clojure -M:test       exit 0   2174 tests / 11130 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  machines JVM clojure -M:test   exit 0   1220 tests / 4289 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  ssr JVM clojure -M:test        exit 0   610 tests / 2991 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
  CLJS node-test compile / run   exit 0   1874 files, 0 warnings / 11150 tests / 55135 assertions

NOT WANTED, and not done: no general :where audit, no lint rule tying :where symbols to the facade manifest, no change to the error's shape, no edit to spec/api-manifest.edn, spec/API.md or spec/005-StateMachines.md (all read-only here, hot-zone).

OPERATIONAL NOTE for whoever times this locally: the core JVM suite takes ~8m50s, which sits just under a 10-minute harness ceiling. Three runs were killed at that ceiling while a peer shadow-cljs compile competed for the machine, each leaving a ZERO-BYTE log and no exit file. Those were treated as NO VERDICT rather than as passes, and the gate was re-run to completion.
close_reason: Mayor ruling implemented as written in PR #8934 (commit 3c8541797b). Lines 137/139 now emit 'rf.machines/reg-machine*, and the 144-146 docstring moved in the same commit; sibling reg-machine untouched (now at 159/161 after the docstring grew two lines). Line numbers re-derived at tip and all matched. No test pinned the old symbol — searched line-oriented and flattened, with a live control term. Two controls: reverting the symbol is GREEN, which is the measured reason the defect survived; a covered sentinel planted at the adjacent sibling line went red naming it, proving the gate read this worktree and that the sibling's :where is genuinely pinned. core 2174/11130, machines 1220/4289, ssr 610/2991, CLJS 11150/55135 — all exit 0.

title: spec/005-StateMachines.md:4100 is the last bare :as machines call spelling in the corpus (residue of rf2-qt7au)
description:
rf2-qt7au (PR #8912) moved every published bare machines/<helper> call spelling to the canonical rf.machines/ alias that Conventions section Require-alias dialect makes normative - 18 sites across six documents. One site was out of that dispatch fence and remains:

  spec/005-StateMachines.md line 4100:  (machines/machine-transition definition snapshot event)

It sits inside a clojure code fence with NO require beside it, so a reader copying the fence gets an alias that is never introduced. PR #8905 corrected the rf/-prefixed spellings in that file and did not touch bare-alias ones, which is why it survived both passes.

This is the LAST of the class: a census over every tracked markdown file under docs/, spec/, migration/ and skills/ at PR #8912 tip returns exactly this one hit and nothing else.

One line. Needs a dispatch that is allowed to touch spec/005-StateMachines.md.
notes:
VERDICT (rf2-ur6kh) -- PR #8916, one line in spec/005-StateMachines.md.

THE FIX. Line 4100 now reads (rf.machines/machine-transition definition snapshot
event) instead of the bare-alias spelling. That is the whole diff: one file, one
insertion, one deletion, confirmed by a three-dot diff against the merge base
before push, which showed nothing else and in particular nothing reverted.

NO REQUIRE CLAUSE ADDED, AND THE REASON CORRECTS THE DESCRIPTION. The description
reads the site as a fence "with no require beside it, so a reader copying the
fence gets an alias that is never introduced". That is right about the defect and
is why the bare spelling had to go, but it is not right that the document leaves
the canonical alias uninstroduced. spec/005-StateMachines.md line 3932 already
introduces it once for the whole file: it tells the reader to require it under
the conventional dotted alias re-frame.machines :as rf.machines, cites Conventions
Require-alias dialect, and says in terms that the rf.machines/ spellings BELOW
assume exactly that alias. The corrected line is 168 lines below that sentence, so
it is covered verbatim. Two further facts point the same way: 44 other rf.machines/
call spellings already live in this file (PR #8905's work) and not one carries a
local require, line 3932 being the file's single deliberate introduction; and the
sibling Level 2 fence eleven lines below already spells
rf.machines/make-machine-handler bare of any require. A require here alone would
have contradicted the document's own design. So: rename only.

CENSUS, RE-DERIVED. Class = the bare alias token machines qualifying a PUBLISHED
re-frame.machines helper. The 23-name helper roster was DERIVED from the
"### re-frame.machines/<name>" headings of docs/api/re-frame.machines.md, not
hardcoded. Scope: all 974 tracked markdown files, wider than the description's
docs/ spec/ migration/ skills/. Total and per-file rows come from ONE command.

  AFTER   23 hits in 6 files; the 005 row is gone, every other row unchanged.

"LAST OF THE CLASS" -- CORRECT BUT CONDITIONAL, AND NOT YET TRUE OF MAIN. 23 of

c50fb15a86, on branch worker/machnames-lzrza. The description's census was taken

That is the one premise of the brief that did not hold as stated.

THE TWO CENSUS TRAPS, HANDLED. (1) Keyword form excluded deliberately: a
fixed-string search for machines/ also matches the leading-colon keyword spelling

class, dropping 27 keyword occurrences that are not call sites; the same lookbehind

OUT OF SCOPE, DELIBERATELY. Live :as machines require aliases in implementation/
