title: test(http,examples): deterministic overlap witness for Nine States newest-intent-wins
description:
Follow-up to rf2-t9va. That bead's fix landed the shared stable `:request-id`
(`nine-states.core/data-load-request-id`) on both live request shapes and both
Story twins, entirely inside `examples/patterns/**`. Its acceptance criteria
ALSO called for a deterministic CLJS regression proving newest-intent-wins.
That test cannot live in the example tree — examples are test-free (rf2-8cevm,
no `*.spec.cjs` under `examples/`) — and the worker's fence excluded
`implementation/**` (a peer was live on `implementation/adapters/reagent/test`
in the same wave), so the witness was deferred here rather than smuggled into a
locked/fenced tree.

## What to write

A single-frame CLJS test on a CONTROLLED/deferred managed-HTTP transport (not
the synchronous canned stub, and not a hand-dispatched `:fetch-succeeded`):

- hold request A open; issue B through the shipped example event
  (`:nine-states.demo/load`) before A settles;
- prove A's later success or failure reaches NO app target and cannot move or
  mutate the `:ui/nine-states` machine (supersession suppresses the superseded
  attempt's app reply — `registry/supersede!`, `:reason
  :request-id-superseded`);
- settle B and prove exactly B's `:items` / `:error`, the `:data` region state
  and tags, and the `:ui/render` result;
- include at least one CROSS-KIND row (old success vs new failure, or old
  failure vs new success) so `:nine-states.demo/load` and
  `:nine-states.demo/load-with-failure` are proven to share one replacement
  lane;
- cover reset-then-new-load: `:reset` alone does not abort the in-flight
  request, so the protection there is the same-id supersession on the reload,
  not the existing `reset`-to-`:nothing` test (which settles a completion while
  still at `:nothing`, where it is trivially ignored);
- a negative control: removing or changing the shared id makes the overlap
  witness FAIL.

## Where

Natural home is beside the existing example suite,
`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/nine_states_cljs_test.cljs`
(reached by `npm run test:cljs` — `adapters/reagent/test` is on the `:node-test`
classpath). `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_cljs_test.cljs` already
carries the transport-level same-id supersession regression and is the harness
precedent to follow rather than inventing a new controlled-fetch helper.

## Why the example alone is not enough

The shipped app routes `:rf.http/managed` through an `:fx-overrides` demo stub,
which REPLACES the effect outright — the framework's in-flight registry, and
with it supersession, never runs there, and canned replies settle
synchronously. So no gate currently executes the superseding path for this
example; the fix is compile-verified and contract-verified only.
close_reason: PR #9275. Witness landed at implementation/http/test/re_frame/nine_states_overlap_cljs_test.cljs — NOT under examples/ (test-free, rf2-8cevm) and NOT in the adapters/reagent tree the bead nominated, which was fenced to a peer worker this wave. The http artefact is the right shelf on the merits: the subject is the managed-HTTP in-flight registry and its same-:request-id supersession, this artefact's own contract, and http_managed_demo_frame_isolation_cljs_test.cljs is the standing precedent for an example-behaviour regression parked there. shadow-cljs.edn's own comment on the ../examples/* source roots states the rule outright. Deterministic by construction: js/fetch is stubbed with a transport that PARKS each attempt inside its own body read, so the test holds the resolver and PLACES the interleaving rather than racing for it — the multi-attempt form of re-frame.http-cljs-test's with-controlled-body-fetch. Frames carry no :fx-overrides so the real effect runs. Covers three overlap rows including cross-kind in BOTH directions; each settles the older attempt first and proves the machine did not move before settling the newer and proving exactly its :items/:error, data-region state, tag and :ui/render. Reset-then-reload asserts :reset does NOT abort the in-flight attempt, so the protection is the same-id supersession on the reload. Negative control is an executable assertion rather than a one-shot mutation: a test-local event issues the identical request under a DIFFERENT :request-id and the witness inverts (stale reply lands and clobbers the machine). Per-row isolation is inside the driver, not a fixture (a :each fixture resets once per deftest, not per table row); one row is additionally pinned running alone. Gates: http JVM 525/3969 exit 0; clj-kondo 0 errors 0 warnings; both ratchets exit 0, with the alias gate confirmed to SEE the new file (census 2793->2794 files, 10851->10857 edges, non-canonical unchanged at 2446, so all six re-frame aliases are canonical). npm run test:cljs deliberately NOT run — it is the only lane executing this file, but it compiles a shadow-cljs build and concurrent workers were live; CI owns it. Every framework API the file calls was verified against its definition first. No production or example change.

title: Canonical reply integration/security fixtures pin ledger work keys instead of envelope keys
description:
## Finding

Two contract-support suites build hand-authored maps that they call canonical managed-async reply envelopes, but put work identity on bare `:work/id` / `:work/kind`. Those are the durable work-ledger / verification-payload spellings. A transient reply envelope is single-rooted under `:rf.reply/work-id` / `:rf.reply/work-kind`.

This is not merely prose drift: the tests assert the bare keys and therefore positively pin the wrong record layer.

## Exact evidence

- `implementation/event-conformance/test/re_frame/event_reply_envelope_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:52-59` defines `canonical-reply` with top-level `:work/id` and `:work/kind`. Lines 87-91 call it a canonical uniform envelope; lines 114-124 call these canonical reply facts and assert the bare keys after ordinary event delivery. `rf.reply/valid-reply?` does not expose the mistake because the canonical work fields are conditional/optional to the generic validator and the unknown bare fields are allowed.
- `implementation/security/test/re_frame/security/reply_envelope_egress_security_cljs_test.cljc:52-88` feeds `trace-summary` a reply with bare `:work/id`, then explicitly calls the returned bare key canonical. The same stale spelling recurs in its framed, frameless, generated, suppression, and host-handle reply fixtures (notably lines 97-126, 131-160, 181-201, and 234-252). `trace-summary` projects only wire slots and otherwise preserves the supplied map, so these tests can stay green without ever proving that the canonical namespaced identity survives egress.
- `spec/Managed-Effects.md:92-100` shows live delivery with `:rf.reply/work-id`; lines 122-154 define the reply map, and line 151 explicitly distinguishes namespaced transient-envelope keys from bare durable-ledger / verification / `:current-work` keys. `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3582-3587` and 3622-3624 carry the same boundary.
- The comparison surface is already correct: `implementation/reply-conformance/test/re_frame/reply_egress_projection_conformance_cljs_test.cljc:91-105,174-176,212,253-254,277-278,370` uses and asserts `:rf.reply/work-id` / `:rf.reply/work-kind`; `reply_vocab_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` also reads family builders through those keys.
- History makes this an evidenced missed migration. Commits `01d9e4ae2f` (production), `084892baa2` / `e5e5a4aa84` (reply tests), and `2b1e536514` (spec) migrated the envelope to `:rf.reply/*` on 2026-07-09 under rf2-l7s7b7. Blame shows the bare fixture keys in both files remain from their 2026-06-17 introductions. Later 2026-09-03 event-conformance cleanup edited the surrounding assertions without correcting this layer mismatch.

## Impact

A regression that drops or reintroduces the wrong work-identity spelling at ordinary reply-event delivery or trace egress can leave these integration/security suites green, even though app handlers and tools consume the namespaced envelope contract for correlation. The fixtures also serve as executable examples, so preserving the ledger spelling here teaches a caller to read a key real family replies do not expose. The production builders currently appear correct; this is a meaningful contract-pin defect, not evidence of a current runtime leak.

## Bounded recommendation

Correct the two suites at the reply-map boundary:

1. Use `:rf.reply/work-id` and `:rf.reply/work-kind` for every top-level reply envelope and corresponding assertion.
2. Keep bare `:work/id` only where it is genuinely correlation/verification/ledger data, such as the carried/current maps passed to `reply/suppress`; do not mechanically rename those nested facts.
3. Add a small explicit tooth at each distinct boundary: ordinary delivered event and trace/suppression summary must retain the namespaced identity and must not grow top-level bare aliases.
4. Keep the existing status, redaction, stale non-delivery, and host-handle assertions intact.

## Non-goals

- No production API or runtime change.
- Do not rename durable work-ledger, verification-payload, entry `:current-work`, or carried/current gate keys.
- Do not tighten the generic reply validator into inferring whether arbitrary data is ledger-backed.
- Do not expand the family matrix, invent a second schema, or duplicate the broader egress suite.

## Posture rationale

This is a small correction at a user/tool-visible contract seam: one fact should have one spelling per record layer. Fixing the executable examples is lower-friction and more valuable than adding machinery. It protects ergonomic SPA continuation handling and debuggable correlation without litigating unrelated reply details.

## Duplicate search

An all-status in-memory scan covered 935 current beads across title, description, notes, design, acceptance criteria, and external ref for `rf.reply/work`, bare `work/id`, cross-record spelling, both fixture names, and work-id spelling. No bead owns this residual. The nearest closed issues are distinct: rf2-6r9j.217 renamed private event/reply roles only; rf2-6r9j.97 replaced a vacuous stale non-delivery row; rf2-6r9j.94 removed a duplicate generic projector row. Historical rf2-l7s7b7 is visible in the migration commits above, but its landed test migration missed these two files.

## Uncertainty

The runtime builders and the dedicated reply-conformance matrix appear canonical today, so the immediate risk is a false-green/misleading-fixture seam rather than a demonstrated production failure. The security file overlaps some projection coverage with reply-conformance, but its adversarial stale/host-handle rows remain independently useful; this issue asks only that their envelope inputs stop modeling the wrong layer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every top-level reply envelope constructed in the two named suites uses `:rf.reply/work-id` and, where kind is present, `:rf.reply/work-kind`; bare `:work/id` remains only in genuine ledger/verification/carried-current correlation data.
2. The event integration test proves ordinary delivery preserves the namespaced work id/kind and does not expose top-level bare aliases.
3. The security reply-egress tests prove framed/frameless projection and stale suppression preserve canonical namespaced identity while retaining their existing leak, redaction, non-delivery, and data-only teeth.
4. Focused JVM and consolidated CLJS Node coverage for both suites passes.
5. A temporary focused mutation that removes or replaces the canonical namespaced work-id at each distinct boundary makes the new assertion red; the mutation is restored before handoff.
close_reason: PR #9275. Both suites' top-level reply envelopes now use :rf.reply/work-id / :rf.reply/work-kind; assertions renamed (never loosened to accept both spellings). Bare :work/id kept only on the data-only carried/current stale-gate maps, with a new assertion pinning that they were NOT renamed. New teeth at each distinct boundary (ordinary delivery, stale suppression, framed egress, frameless fail-closed egress, 300-row generated corpus) assert the namespaced identity survives AND that no top-level bare alias grows beside it. Found a live false green in passing: suppress reads its trace work id off :rf.reply/work-id, so the security fixture's ledger spelling left (:rf.reply/work-id trace) nil while the suite stayed green. AC5 mutation control: reverting each envelope construction to the ledger spelling makes event-conformance red (exit 1, 10 failures, both boundaries) and security red (exit 1, 11 failures, all four boundaries); restores verified by sha256 byte-hash. Green: event-conformance 44/194 exit 0 (was 44/186), security 92/725 exit 0 (was 92/717). No production or spec change.

Correctness: js/Boolean implements native truthiness including0n/1n/NaN without widening other attribute classes; mutation table uses in-contract single-row replies, asserts both pending instances, peer survival, writer commit and exact final board. Each driver invocation resets frame runtime and reinitializes registrations before load, eliminating first-revision row leakage. title: story: Step Debugger Start runs the script before step 1
description:
## Finding

The Test-mode Step Debugger does not start from pre-play state for the normal/default `:script` shape. `re-frame.story.ui.test-mode.stepper-state/begin!` says it re-allocates the frame "so the run starts fresh," but at `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state.cljs:104-147` it calls `(rf.story.runtime/reset-variant variant-id)` and waits for that promise before calling `begin-stepper!` and publishing cursor 0. `reset-variant` is deliberately a full rerun: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc:1715-1728` destroys the frame and delegates to `run-variant`; `run-variant` enters `run-phase-4!` (`runtime.cljc:979ff`, `:1260ff`), where `auto-runnable-plays` executes the script. Bare `:script` defaults `:auto-run?` to true (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner.cljc:324-356`). `begin-stepper!` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play.cljc:366-385`) then merely seeds the complete script into `:remaining`; it does not restore setup state. The UI therefore says "ready · N steps" with cursor 0 while app-db already reflects all N mutating steps.

This is reproduced against current production JVM primitives at HEAD `2c61dafd702db9672163ee9d2028db34c70c978d`, not inferred from prose. A registered variant with `:setup [[:probe/seed 0]]` and three default-auto-run `[:dispatch-sync [:probe/inc]]` steps, followed by the same `reset-variant -> begin-stepper!` sequence used by the CLJS UI, printed:

`{:after-reset {:count 3}, :frame-db {:count 3}, :stepper {:remaining [inc inc inc], :ran []}}`

The existing prepare-only lifecycle proves the expected shape is already available: the same probe through `runtime/prepare-run!` (documented at `runtime.cljc:1364-1378` as phases 0-2 "WITHOUT executing the play script") printed:

`{:prepared-frame-db {:count 0}, :stepper {:remaining [inc inc inc], :ran []}}`

The repository's own exemplary `:story.counter/clicked-three-times` makes the user-visible failure concrete (`tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories.cljs:353-375`): setup seeds 0 and the script increments three times. Pressing Start first advances it to 3 while displaying cursor 0; pressing Step once advances it to 4 while displaying "step 1". Rewind restores the incorrectly captured post-script epoch (3), not the specified initial state (0). This contradicts `tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md:462` (`begin!` re-allocate + prime), `:465`, `:482`, and `:498-501` (rewind restores the pre-play state), plus `tools/story/README.md:28-34` (canvas reflects each step's app-db).

## Impact

This is not a cosmetic counter mismatch: the debugger repeats every default-auto-run interaction and side effect before the programmer can inspect step 1. State mutations, HTTP stubs/effects, DOM gestures, and assertions may execute twice, and displayed cursor/outcomes describe a different run from the frame being debugged. A debugging tool that changes the program before presenting its initial state is actively misleading to both SPA authors and agents.

## Bounded recommendation

Make Step Debugger Start allocate/prepare the variant only through the pre-play lifecycle (loaders/setup, phases 0-2), then capture that epoch and seed `begin-stepper!`; do not call a full `reset-variant`/phase-4 run. Reuse the existing prepare-only runtime path or extract the narrow shared primitive it already embodies rather than duplicating lifecycle logic. Keep `reset-variant`, ordinary shell auto-run, and `:auto-run?` semantics unchanged.

Non-goals: redesigning the stepper controls or script DSL; changing normal run/reset behavior; changing the default `:auto-run?`; solving multi-play selection; a broad runtime ownership rewrite.

## Acceptance

1. Add a CLJS/browser regression using a mutating default-auto-run script: immediately after Start, cursor is 0 and frame app-db is setup state (for example count 0), not post-script state (3).
2. The first Step executes exactly the first script step once (count 1); subsequent steps remain 1:1 with cursor, and Rewind returns to setup/pre-play state (count 0).
3. Assert no script checkpoint, effect, or terminal phase-4 work runs as part of Start itself; failures in preparation still return the section to an honest inactive/error state.
4. Existing `run-variant`/`reset-variant` full-run behavior and ordinary on-mount auto-run remain unchanged.
5. Exercise `begin!` itself (or the Start DOM path), not only a directly seeded local slot.

## Why the current gates miss it

`tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/stepper_state_cljs_test.cljs:25-27` explicitly seeds slots "without going through begin!" and has no begin test. The only live Start probe is `tools/story/test/story_feature_load.cjs:829-881`; it uses `:story.counter/loaded`, whose script is assertions only (`stories.cljs:340-346`), and checks controls/progress but never frame app-db. Thus the full `clojure -M:test` suite is green (1889 tests, 6959 assertions, 0 failures/errors) while this path is wrong.

## Duplicate and history check

Targeted `rg` against `.beads/issues.jsonl` found no title/body occurrence of `stepper-state`, `step-debugger`, `play stepper`, `begin-stepper!`, `pre-play epoch`, or `step-by-step run`; broader title scans for reset/auto-run/debugger found no matching Story issue. Git history shows the reset-before-begin sequence dates to the feature's original commit `c5f6ca44c15` / rf2-ulw5m (#1390). That commit advertised a full Start -> Step -> Back -> Rewind -> Stop browser flow but deliberately used `:story.counter/loaded`; later `c438c6cfaf` / rf2-4e545l fixed step-back epoch indexing while continuing to assume `begin!`'s seed was truly pre-play. No commit fixes or tracks this start-state defect.

## Uncertainty

The CLJS browser lane was not run because this dedicated review worktree has no `node_modules` and the review assignment forbade creating a link. The exact production lifecycle composition reproduces on the JVM, and the CLJS `begin!` calls those same cross-platform runtime/play functions around a JS Promise. The implementation worker should choose the cleanest way to carry the current shell run context into the existing prepare-only seam, but that integration choice does not affect the demonstrated phase-4-before-cursor bug.

## Posture fit

This is one high-leverage correction to a marquee programming tool, using an existing lifecycle split. It removes deception and friction without adding author-facing API or general machinery.
notes:
Post-merge audit — PR #9214 (completeness + correctness): `prepare-variant` promises to REJECT for a throwing loader / `:setup` handler, and `stepper-state/begin!` relies exclusively on that rejection (`.catch`) to leave the debugger inactive. The reused phase machinery deliberately does not throw for normal re-frame pipeline failures: `run-events!` / `run-loaders!` capture handler/cofx/interceptor exceptions into `:rf.story/assertions` and return, after which `prepare-variant` resolves `nil`. title: dispatch briefs omit the require-alias canonical dialect, so every new file trips the per-surface ratchet — three PRs in one wave
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by the mayor across one dispatch wave. This is a defect in the MAYOR'S BRIEF TEMPLATE, not in any worker or in the gate.

THE PATTERN. Three PRs from one wave went RED on 'Require-alias dialect ratchet' plus its 'Lint required' aggregator, each for the same reason and each needing a fix round-trip:
  #9264 worker/epoch-a     implementation/adapters 339 vs floor 337 (+2), implementation/epoch 199 vs 196 (+3)
  #9267 worker/ssrhelp-a   (same pair red; diagnosis routed to its author)
  #9270 worker/schemadoc-a implementation/schemas 119 vs floor 112 (+7)
Re-measure these figures rather than quoting them; floors move as the debt is walked down.

THE MECHANISM. scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py enforces a PER-SURFACE FLOOR, not an absolute count. A surface with baselined debt is green at its floor and red one alias above it. So ANY new file added to such a surface reds the gate unless it uses the canonical rf.* spelling from spec/Conventions.md Require-alias dialect. Nearly every editing dispatch adds a test file. The gate is behaving exactly as designed; what is missing is that the brief never tells the worker the dialect exists.

WHY IT COSTS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The failure surfaces only in CI, after the worker has reported done and marked the PR ready. Recovering it costs: converting the PR back to draft, a fix dispatch, a rebase, a re-run of the artefact suite (mandatory, because an alias rename that misses one call site fails at RUNTIME rather than at read time), and a second review pass. Three of those in one wave.

THE FIX IS ONE PARAGRAPH IN THE DISPATCH TEMPLATE, and it belongs in the gate-mechanics block that already travels verbatim into every editing brief: name the canonical dialect, name spec/Conventions.md as its authority, say that the ratchet is a per-surface FLOOR so a new file trips it, and tell the worker to run python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose BEFORE opening the PR. That last clause is the whole repair — the gate prints the exact required spelling for every violation, so a worker who runs it once needs no further guidance.

TWO THINGS THE PARAGRAPH MUST ALSO SAY, both learned by getting them wrong. (1) NEVER raise a floor or edit a baseline file to admit the new debt — that inverts the ratchet, and walking the debt down is rf2-7sx1's job. (2) DO NOT fix pre-existing violations in untouched files: implementation/adapters alone carries 337, so a well-meaning sweep is unbounded scope sprawl into another bead's surface.

A THIRD LESSON, ABOUT READING THE LOG RATHER THAN THE FIRST LINE OF IT. On #9264 I quoted a single surface from the CI output into the fix brief. The log had named TWO surfaces over floor, and had the worker fixed only the one I named the gate would have stayed red — it caught this and said so. So the brief must tell the fix worker to run the gate and read its FULL output, never to trust a surface list quoted by the mayor.

SCOPE: this is a change to docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md, in the gate-mechanics block. It is the MAYOR'S OWN REPAIR, so per loops.md section 6 it goes through a mayor-occupied worktree rather than the mayor checkout, where the pre-commit hook will refuse it. Check first whether the same class of per-surface ratchet exists for other gates (splint, clj-kondo, api-manifest) and cover the class rather than this one instance if so.
notes:
SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME BRIEF TEMPLATE, MEASURED THE SAME WAVE — and this one is a rule the template ALREADY carries, which is the more damning shape.

WHAT HAPPENED. The fix dispatch for PR #9263 ended its turn saying it would 'wait for the monitor event rather than continue polling'. That wait can never complete: a Monitor, watch, subscription or background task an agent arms stops when that agent stops, so the worker is the only thing that can read its own exit file and can only do so while its turn is running. The completion event goes to the coordinator instead. The worker was recovered intact by a single status message, which is the documented outcome for every instance of this strand.

THE CAUSE IS MINE AND IT IS SPECIFIC: I wrote that fix brief as a CONDENSED gate-mechanics section instead of pasting the block verbatim. The block already states this rule, already names the class rather than the instances (a Monitor, a watch, a subscription, a background task you expect to wake you), and already refutes the belief that keeps re-arming it — that the harness's own promise to notify survives the end of a turn. None of that reached the worker, because I summarised.

SO THIS BEAD NOW HAS TWO HALVES, and they are different in kind. The first (require-alias dialect) is content MISSING from the template and needs a new paragraph. This second one needs NO new text at all — the text exists and works; what failed is that the mayor did not paste it. dispatch-prompt-template.md says exactly this under Pasting a block: 'no dispatch is small enough to earn a condensed block', and notes the temptation is strongest precisely where the block dwarfs the task, which a two-file alias rename is.

IMPLICATION FOR THE FIX, and it should be stated in whatever lands: adding the require-alias paragraph makes the gate-mechanics block LONGER, which increases the pressure to condense it on small dispatches — the exact pressure that produced this strand. So the repair must not stop at more text. Either the block is pasted mechanically every time by construction (an extraction step the mayor cannot skip), or the fix dispatches keep failing this way while the template gets steadily better and steadily less likely to be used in full.

Recorded here rather than as a separate bead because both defects have one root: the mayor's brief is the scarce output, and both instances are it being degraded on the way to the worker — once by omission, once by summary.
A THIRD GATE OF THIS CLASS, measured 2026-09-05 on PR #9269 — so this bead is about a CLASS of gate, not about the require-alias one.

'No retired view-lifetime vocabulary, repo-wide' (scripts/check_view_lifetime_residue.py) is a repo-wide BANNED-WORD ratchet at a permitted count of ZERO. It fired on PR #9269 for a single word in an explanatory COMMENT — implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/registry.cljc:747, the sentence 'No lock, tombstone, lease or ...' saying what the fix does NOT need. The implementation was correct; the prose used a retired term.

WHY IT BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN AS ITS OWN BEAD: identical shape to the require-alias case. A gate the brief never names, enforcing a project vocabulary a worker cannot infer, surfacing only in CI after the worker has reported done and marked the PR ready, and costing a full recovery round-trip. Three distinct gates now: require-alias dialect (per-surface floor), lease/view-lifetime residue (repo-wide, zero permitted), and the lint.yml aggregator that reports whichever of them failed.

SO THE FIX IS NOT A LIST OF GATES — IT IS A DISCOVERY INSTRUCTION. A list drifts, and this bead would need amending on every fourth gate. What a worker needs is: before opening the PR, run the ratchet/vocabulary gates that cover the paths you touched, and treat the gate's own output as the authority on what it wants. Point at how to find them (scripts/check_*.py plus the lint.yml and test.yml job lists) rather than enumerating them here, for the same reason the method already gives about counts going stale first.

AND NOTE THESE GATES GRADE PROSE, NOT ONLY CODE. That is the non-obvious half: a worker who has carefully gated the code it changed will not think to gate a comment it wrote, and the require-alias case has the same property in reverse — it grades a require form nobody considers part of the change. The paragraph must say the ratchets read the WHOLE tracked file, comments and docstrings included.

WORKER RESULT 2026-09-05 — PR #9274 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9274), one file, 39 insertions, 0 deletions.

RATCHET CLASS IS FAR BROADER THAN THREE. The bead asked whether the per-surface-ratchet class has other members. Census of scripts/ by docstring self-description (ratchet | residue | retired | permitted count | baseline | floor): 18 gates, including check_retired_spellings, check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_failure_corpus_residue, check_ambient_durable_reads, check_thrown_error_messages, check_keyword_catalogue_drift and check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh, plus the skill-drift family. Only ONE per-surface floor DATA file exists (scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn); the rest are zero-tolerance or scoped-carve-out scans. So the bead's "the fix is NOT a list" ruling is confirmed with a wider margin than the three gates it names — an enumeration would have been stale before it merged.

CORRECTION TO ONE PREMISE IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF (not in this bead): the brief asserted that BOTH named gates "read the whole tracked file, comments and docstrings included". That is true of check_view_lifetime_residue.py, which scans tracked content and paths, but FALSE of check_require_alias_dialect.py, which deliberately strips comments, strings, char literals and #_ discards before grading — precisely so a require form quoted in a docstring does not count. The bead itself is accurate here and was followed instead: the residue gates grade prose, and the alias gate grades "a require form nobody considers part of the change". The landed wording states both halves separately rather than merging them.

SHAPE OF THE FIX. Half one: two paragraphs in the gate-mechanics block, beside the other pre-push obligations. Discovery instruction plus the two non-obvious properties; no markdown link, because the travelling block contains zero links and the page forbids pointing a worker at a section it cannot see. Half two: placed in Pasting a block — mayor-facing prose OUTSIDE the travelling block — so the add-more-text-makes-condensing-likelier tension is not worsened by its own repair; it records the measured case where condensing DID strand a worker (the section previously had only a case where it did not), names which part a condensing mayor drops (the harness mechanics), and states that no wording fixes the pressure because the block only ever grows.

GATES (captured exits): check_doc_slugs.py 0; check_readme_links.py --ci 0; check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose 0; check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose 0. All re-run on the final base after rebase. Non-vacuity: planted broken anchor -> doc-slugs exit 1 naming file/line/anchor; the SAME planted tree left check_readme_links green, which is the finding that check_readme_links excludes DOCS_GATE_ROOTS and does not cover docs/the-mayor-method/ at all. Restore verified by git blob hash (db7c9891...), byte-identical.

Bead left in_progress for the mayor to close on merge; the worker did not close it.
MAYOR-SIDE CORRECTION FROM THE WORKER THAT FIXED THIS BEAD, recorded because the fix brief got a fact wrong that this bead's own text gets right.

I WROTE, in the dispatch brief: 'both named gates read the whole tracked file, comments and docstrings included'. That is TRUE of check_view_lifetime_residue.py and FALSE of check_require_alias_dialect.py, which deliberately STRIPS comments, strings, character literals and #_ discards — precisely so a require form quoted inside a docstring does not count against a surface. The worker checked at source, followed the bead over my brief, and stated the two halves separately in what landed.

THE BEAD WAS ALREADY ACCURATE: its text says residue gates grade prose, and separately that the alias gate grades 'a require form nobody considers part of the change'. Two different non-obvious properties, and I collapsed them into one wrong generalisation. So the corrected statement, for anyone re-reading this bead: a RESIDUE ratchet reads the whole file including comments and commit messages; the ALIAS ratchet reads only real code and catches you on an import edge you did not think of as part of your diff. Both surprise a worker, for opposite reasons.

THE CLASS IS FAR BIGGER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED — 18 GATES, not the three it names. Measured by the worker as a docstring census over scripts/ on the markers ratchet | residue | retired | permitted count | baseline | floor: check_retired_spellings, check_retired_composition_vocab, check_retired_image_keys, check_inject_cofx_residue, check_failure_corpus_residue, check_ambient_durable_reads, check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh, the skill-drift family, and more. Exactly ONE per-surface floor DATA file exists (scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn); every other member is a zero-tolerance or scoped-carve-out scan. That confirms this bead's own 'do not write a list' ruling by a wider margin than the ruling claimed — a list of three would have been wrong within the hour.

ONE MORE PREMISE OF MINE THAT POINTED THE WRONG WAY: I told the worker mkdocs build --strict was not the gate for docs/the-mayor-method/. It IS — exclude_docs lists only tools/playground/, the two codemod trees and design/freehand|hicasso|retirement/, and the-mayor-method sits under docs_dir. The worker skipped it for DIFFERENT and correct reasons (the change adds zero links, --strict does not gate anchors, siblings live) and said so rather than inheriting my wrong reason. It also found check_readme_links.py --ci VACUOUS on this path — it excludes DOCS_GATE_ROOTS — and reported it as vacuous rather than banking its exit 0 as a pass. That is the right handling of a green that inspected nothing.
close_reason:
PR #9274 merged (c974dbfc63). The dispatch-prompt-template now names the two repo-wide ratchet gates, so a brief that omits them is a brief that departed from the template rather than one the template allowed.

Filed after FOUR PRs in one session bounced on ratchets no brief had mentioned: #9264, #9267 and #9270 on check_require_alias_dialect.py, #9269 on check_view_lifetime_residue.py. The two gates are different animals and the template now says which is which — the alias gate is a PER-SURFACE FLOOR baselined in scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn that grades IMPORT EDGES only (it strips comments, strings, char literals and #_ discards); the residue gate is a REPO-WIDE BANNED-WORD scan at permitted count ZERO that DOES read comments, docstrings and commit messages. Briefing them as one thing is how #9269's reworded explanatory comment got missed.

The bead's second half was the stranded fix worker: it ended its turn on a monitor because the brief carried a CONDENSED gate-mechanics section instead of the block, which already names that class. title: ssr-node: render exceptions can leak application data and spoof refusal status
description:
## Evidence

- The package states the response law repeatedly: README.md:275 and :668 say Node returns body markup and nothing else; test/egress.test.cjs:31-37 tightens that to “nothing the render module authored” outside chunk HTML and says a refusal must not carry the payload through the error channel.
- The success/return-value door enforces that law, but the exception door does not. In src/worker.cjs:221-225 the render catch copies application-authored error.code, error.message, and error.detail into the worker error message. src/isolate.cjs:200-208 preserves the code/message and spreads detail into the public Refusal. src/http.cjs:67-76 serializes that Refusal to JSON and statusFor maps the copied code to HTTP status.
- A read-only worker probe loaded an in-memory render module whose render threw an Error built from allowlisted request state. The module set message to "message:state-secret-7b2", detail to {echo:"state-secret-7b2"}, and no custom code. The actual worker output was:
  {"t":"error","id":7,"code":":rf.ssr-node/render-threw","message":"message:state-secret-7b2","detail":{"echo":"state-secret-7b2"},"afterChunks":0}
  This proves the state sentinel crosses both live fields; it is not inferred from source alone.
- The repository's own throws fixture provides the HTTP half without a synthetic file: POSTing app/before returned HTTP 500 with JSON message "fell over immediately", the exact string authored at test/fixtures/throws.cjs:20.
- error.code is the same untrusted path. A render module can set it to a known protocol member such as :rf.ssr-node/unknown-entry, service-saturated, or render-timeout; statusFor will then present an application render bug as HTTP 400, 503, or 504 instead of the documented render-threw 500. It can also emit an arbitrary refusal-code string.
- The green egress row at test/egress.test.cjs:311-323 exercises only a module that returns a payload. It does not throw an Error carrying code/message/detail, so the package gate remains green (108 rows, 9 suites) while the second channel is live.
- History localizes the gap: git log -S "err.detail" attributes the pass-through to the initial service commit b2b35bf6e9. The later response-egress hardening (67d4d9338a, b34fe600fa) closed returned values but did not touch this catch.

## Impact

A routine renderer exception can put server-only render state, environment-derived data, or other application values into the in-process Refusal and the sidecar's HTTP JSON response. The JVM consumer then retains the sidecar message/detail on its internal ssr-node-refused error. Independently, application code can spoof the closed refusal taxonomy and its caller-fault/deadline/saturation status, sending operators and retry policy down the wrong path. This is a correctness and boundary failure, not a request from hostile code: error messages that interpolate the value being processed are ordinary.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a valid module with an app/root entry and an allowlisted :secret state key.
2. In render, construct an Error whose code, message, and nested detail are derived from state[":secret"], then throw it before emit.
3. Call Service.renderFrames or POST /render.
4. Observe the module's message/detail in the Refusal/JSON. If code is set to a known non-render member, observe the corresponding non-500 HTTP status.

The read-only probe above establishes steps 1-3 at the worker boundary, and the checked-in throws fixture establishes the message-to-HTTP leg.

## Recommended bounded repair

Close the exception path at src/worker.cjs, the first boundary that can enforce it. A caught render-module exception should always cross as CODE.RENDER_THREW with service-owned wording and a small service-owned detail shape (for example entry plus the existing afterChunks fact); do not copy error.code, error.message, error.detail, or other module properties. Preserve the existing pre-chunk refusal versus post-chunk torn-response behavior. If retaining full diagnostics locally is required, keep that as a sidecar-local logging decision rather than putting application-authored values on the response protocol.

Add the focused adversarial case to test/egress.test.cjs with a fixture that demonstrably throws distinct sentinels in code, message, and nested detail, and check both the in-process Refusal and HTTP response.

## Posture rationale

This is one missing closure on an existing boundary, not a new subsystem. The ergonomic rule should be simple for SPA authors: throw from a renderer and get one honest render-threw failure; never learn a redaction DSL or remember which Error properties are safe. A fixed service-owned refusal is smaller, safer, and easier for people and AI-generated integration code to reason about than configurable projection.

## Non-goals

- No new refusal code, public option, redaction framework, safe-key registry, or exception wrapper API.
- No change to successful chunk/complete frames, request validation, allowlists, timeout, pool replacement, or JVM/browser error projection.
- No redesign of sidecar logging or observability; local diagnostics may be decided separately.
- Do not broaden this into boot-error handling. Module boot fails before the service listens and has different operator-diagnostic needs.
- Do not terminate a healthy isolate merely because application render code threw; current reuse semantics are separate.

## Related and duplicate search

Searched all 935 tracker records, including closed/deferred, across title, description, notes, and close reason for ssr-node, body markup, egress, render-threw, err.code/err.detail, render exception message/detail, diagnostic-shaped leak, refusal-code spoofing, and application-authored error data. No issue owns this exception pass-through. Closest is closed rf2-6r9j.77, which removed worker stack fields because receivers discarded them; this finding is distinct because code/message/detail are live and serialized. Closed rf2-6r9j.70-.74/.84/.86 and .176-.179 cover boot-test validity, envelope scope, selector/residue cleanup, and naming. The crossing parent rf2-8arzr and success-egress commits establish the law but do not close this path.

## Uncertainties

The repair must choose the exact service-owned message/detail wording and whether the original exception is logged only on sidecar stderr. Those choices do not alter the required boundary: no application-authored exception property may enter a public Refusal or HTTP frame. The JVM host sanitizes what reaches the browser, but that is downstream defense and does not repair the Node service's own public in-process and HTTP contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A controlled render module throws an Error whose code, message, and nested detail each carry distinct sentinels sourced from request state; a direct fixture control proves all sentinels really exist before the service handles it.
2. Service.renderFrames/renderToString rejects that render with exactly :rf.ssr-node/render-threw, service-owned wording, correct afterChunks, and no sentinel anywhere in the public Refusal (code, message, detail, stack serialization).
3. The same request over HTTP returns 500 with x-rf-ssr-refusal :rf.ssr-node/render-threw; its JSON body and headers contain no sentinel. Choosing known 400/503/504 protocol codes in the thrown Error cannot change that outcome.
4. Both pre-emit and post-emit exceptions are covered: pre-emit is a clean refusal; post-emit remains a torn response and streaming HTTP destroys rather than completes the socket.
5. A negative control restoring any code/message/detail pass-through makes the new egress test fail.
6. Existing successful rendering, ordinary throw, return-value egress, timeout, byte-fidelity, and all ssr-node suites remain green.

title: examples(routing): advertised route schema has no validator or observable effect
description:
## Finding

The canonical routing example presents its article-detail declaration as a working Malli route contract, but the app never loads the optional schemas artefact.

`examples/capabilities/routing/routing/core.cljs:49-51` declares `:params [:map [:id :string]]`; `README.md:24-28` explicitly calls out the Malli `:params` schema as a demonstrated feature. Yet the namespace requires only `re-frame.routing` and the Reagent adapter (`core.cljs:24-31`), and the `:examples/routing` build has no schema preload (`implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1544-1548`). Having `schemas/src` on the compiler source path does not execute the namespace.

Routing deliberately does not require schemas: `implementation/routing/deps.edn:33-40` gives the production artefact only core, while `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:1190-1210` documents and implements `[false nil]` when no validator hook is registered. The hook is published only when `re-frame.schemas` loads (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:93,122`). The public guide is explicit that the require itself wires the validator (`docs/core/how-to/validate-with-schemas.md:20,39-41`), and Spec 010 lines 7 and 766 say schema implies validation only after requiring that artefact; omitting it is the Malli-free posture.

This instance hides the defect especially well: path captures are already strings, and routing's schema-derived coercion treats `:string` as passthrough (`registry.cljc:635-680`), so the declaration has no observable effect and the app still works. Routing can inspect other Malli-shaped metadata for limited coercion without loading schemas; the finding is specifically that validation is absent, not that every route schema is universally inert.

## Impact

This is a canonical teaching surface for programmers and coding agents, so it demonstrates a silent half-configuration as the happy path. Copying it and changing `:string` to `:int`, an enum, constraints, or a closed map can appear to work for valid input because routing derives coercions, while malformed input remains unvalidated. The registry's schema-free tests pin the revealing behavior: `?flag=maybe` and `?n=abc` remain strings (`implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_registry_test.clj:1257-1269`); with no validator the declared boundary does not reject them. Programmatic `route-url` validation likewise no-ops (`registry.cljc:1909-1915`). That is precisely the kind of subtle API lesson an example should not teach.

## Bounded recommendation

Keep this example minimal and routing-focused: remove the unnecessary `:params [:map [:id :string]]` from article-detail and remove the README parenthetical claiming it demonstrates Malli. The path param remains a string and visible behavior is unchanged. A terse cross-link may mention that route validation requires `[re-frame.schemas]`, but do not add that artefact merely to preserve a declaration with no visible learning payoff: Spec 010's measured matched A/B cost is +39.9 KB gzip (`spec/010-Schemas.md:726-733`). If a future example intentionally teaches route validation, it should load schemas and visibly exercise valid and invalid input; that is outside this bead.

## Non-goals

No change to routing's schemas-optional packaging, late-bind soft-pass, coercion rules, validator APIs, route IDs/URLs/navigation, article data, other examples, or a new browser/test harness. Do not make routing depend on schemas or add generic schema machinery.

## History and duplicate search

The schema line dates to initial import `8c6e5a5060` (2026-05-06); routing became its own optional artefact in `c435165251` (2026-05-09); schema-implies-validation landed in `d0b95fdc54` (2026-06-01); README's Malli claim came later in `fdecf54a1fc` (2026-06-26). The declaration survived those contract shifts untouched.

Exact `rg` searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` for this example plus schema/Malli/validation and the current `HEAD..origin/main` beads delta found no owner. Nearby but non-duplicate: `rf2-nvcp` (route-link boot failure), `rf2-ujdn0` (one-command README launcher), `rf2-g1gt` / `rf2-do50` (relative asset/deep-link hosting), and `rf2-6r9j.3` (unconsumed internal RouteAddress constant). The standalone-server history-fallback candidate was discarded because existing beads already discuss that mechanism.

## Uncertainty

No runtime was executed during this read-only review. The namespace load graph and explicit missing-hook branch are direct evidence; the recommended source/prose deletion preserves the currently observed string-param behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `routing.core` no longer presents a route schema while loading only routing (preferred: article-detail metadata retains only `:doc`), and `/articles/:id` still supplies the same string `:id` to the existing detail view.
2. The routing README no longer claims this app demonstrates or carries a Malli `:params` schema; its route-table description stays accurate.
3. If a schema note is retained, it states that loading `re-frame.schemas` is required for validation; this minimal example gains no schema dependency solely for the inert `:string` declaration.
4. `:examples/routing` compiles cleanly through the existing example compile gate. No bespoke runtime suite or scanner is introduced for this two-line teaching correction.
5. No runtime, package, coercion, or other-example behavior changes.

title: examples(resources-ssr): client boot never acquires the route-free resource
description:
## Slice

`examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/**`, checked against the Resources/SSR implementation, Specs 011/016, the runnable Shadow build, example tests, tracker, and focused git history.

## Correctness finding

The route-free resource SSR example never causes its resource on the browser side. Its only `:rf.resource/ensure` is emitted by `:rf/server-init`, whose registration is server-only. Browser `run` creates the client frame, calls `rf.ssr/hydrate!`, and immediately renders `:app/root`; that view only dereferences the intentionally passive `[:rf/resource ...]` subscription. There is no client `ensure`/`refetch`, no live client owner, and no matching client release lifecycle.

Hydration cannot supply that missing liveness. The resource reconcile deliberately drops the baked `[:ssr request-id nav-token]` owner because it belongs to the completed server request. It computes/emits a hydration refetch plan, but does not issue those requests itself; the contract leaves issuance to a still-live route/consumer. This example explicitly has no route.

The result has three user-visible/semantic failures hidden behind one omission:

1. A client-only/no-payload load leaves the resource absent. `hydrate!` returns nil without seeding; the passive subscription projects the absent entry as `:idle`; `articles-page` falls through to an empty `<ul>`; nothing ever fetches.
2. The checked-in forever-fresh payload initially renders, but after hydration its SSR owner is removed and no client owner replaces it. The entry is not an active consumer: tag invalidation and focus/reconnect revalidation leave it stale instead of refetching, and the client ownership/GC lifecycle is never established.
3. A stale/no-data hydration disposition is only classified in `hydrate-refetch-plan`; this route-free boot never causes the load. The README nevertheless says stale/redacted/omitted entries refetch and that the client reconcile + refetch plan run end to end.

This is a teaching correctness bug, not a request for subscription-driven fetching. A programmer or AI copying the example learns that `hydrate!` plus a passive read is sufficient to acquire and keep a resource live, precisely opposite to the library's causal-command model.

## Evidence

- `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:112-119` registers `:articles/list`.
- `core.cljc:136-148` is the only acquisition: server-only `:rf/server-init` dispatches `:rf.resource/ensure` under an SSR owner.
- `core.cljc:154-182` correctly says the view is passive; `core.cljc:395-413` hydrates and mounts without any client resource command while claiming an absent entry refetches.
- `README.md:99-110` claims fresh avoids a double-fetch and stale/redacted/omitted refetch; `README.md:122-125` says the refetch plan runs end to end.
- `index.html:69-90` bakes a `:loaded`, `:stale-at nil` entry with only an SSR owner. That deliberately easy fixture makes the documented run command look correct while avoiding every failing branch.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/subs.cljc:1-14` states subscriptions are pure passive reads; `:332-347` projects a missing entry as `:idle` with no loading/fetching signal.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc:154-163,323-327` skips hydration when no payload exists.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/ssr.cljc:1324-1431` drops SSR owners; `:1495-1503,1626-1633,2311-2319` computes the refetch plan and says a live route issues it.
- `spec/016-Resources.md:303-306` defines attach/hold/release/GC; `:1187,1197` says stale hydration refetches on mount and that the client ensure/fresh-skip re-establishes ownership; `:1597,1603-1607` conditions hydration refetch on a resource the route still needs.

It asserts the fresh plan is empty, but never executes the browser startup with no payload/stale data, never asserts a client owner, and never proves an actual refetch after invalidation.

## History

The client acquisition omission dates to the initial example. Commit `48dd1b928e` fixed the baked payload's storage key and made it permanently fresh, then added a regression that only proves fresh hydration/no immediate refetch. Commit `cd6fd08587` moved the client mount onto the adapter handle while retaining the omission and the explicit “absent one refetches” claim. This is not a new runtime regression; the static fixture and coverage have continually selected the one branch that passes without acquisition.

## Recommended bounded repair

Keep the example route-free. After hydration and before the first client render, cause one explicit client acquisition of `:articles/list` with the same global scope/params and a named app/page owner. Give that app-minted owner a matching release path. For this example's real resource:

- a fresh hydrated entry must take `ensure`'s cache-hit/fresh-skip path, attach the client owner, and issue zero transport requests;
- an absent/no-payload or stale entry must issue exactly one request;
- later invalidation must refetch because the resource now has a live client owner.

Keep views passive. Correct the prose to distinguish “hydration reconciles/classifies” from “the live client acquisition causes work.” This resource declares no sensitive/large policy, so remove the claim that this particular route-free demo executes redacted/omitted refetch unless the implementation and test actually cause those cases; linking to the normative generic contract is enough.

## Non-goals

- Do not make subscriptions fetch.
- Do not add a route/router merely to obtain an owner; route-free is a useful minimal SSR shape.
- Do not add a general hydration orchestration API or redesign resource ownership.
- Do not add mutation, GraphQL, polling, or broad resource examples here.
- Do not turn this into a full failure-matrix exercise; cover the small startup/liveness invariant.

## Duplicate audit

All-status `rg` searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered `resources_ssr`, `resources-ssr`, `client-only`, `no payload`, `passive`, `hydrate`, `owner`, `ensure`, `idle`, and `refetch`, including title combinations for hydrated owner/acquisition and SSR client fallback. No bead owns this outcome. Nearest hits are closed `rf2-6r9j.53` (projection metadata recording), closed `rf2-ujdn0` (copyable example run commands), and closed `rf2-ghxt` (a different RealWorld resources app-db schema boot defect).

## Uncertainty

This review was static by review-worker constraint: no runtime/browser/test execution. The documented runner always stages the forever-fresh payload, so the cold-load failure is masked in that command rather than visibly reproduced there. The causal absence is direct in source and contract, and the ownerless hydrated branch affects that documented fresh run after startup.

THE MAYOR MUST RUN `bd history <id> --json` BEFORE WRITING A BRIEF, not just tell the worker to. Measured twice in one wave (2026-09-05), both times costing a worker its opening context.

WHAT HAPPENS. `bd show` prints the DESCRIPTION first, and the description is the OLDEST text on a bead. This project's merged-PR audit process appends the LIVE instruction as a NOTE, and it does so on beads it has REOPENED — so the bead reads open/in_progress, its description describes a defect that is already fixed on main, and the actual work is a bounded follow-up recorded 200 lines below. A mayor writing a brief from `bd show` briefs the archaeology.

TWO INSTANCES, SAME WAVE:
- rf2-c38b (ssr-node exception egress). I briefed the original finding — worker.cjs copying application-authored code/message/detail onto the public Refusal. Already merged as PR #9258 and an ANCESTOR OF THE WORKER'S OWN BRANCH. The newest text-bearing mutation was a closed->open audit reopening at 13:04:27 naming a different, narrower hole: the SCHEDULED-CALLBACK path (app/uncaught) still leaked where the awaited path (app/rejected) was clean.
- rf2-61i5 (Xray pop-out keyboard). I briefed the two-halved implementation fix as unbuilt. It was on main in `d4dee410d0` + `95aaa46598`, merged as PR #9263 at 04:21Z THE SAME DAY. Every line citation I gave verified at tip and was describing history. The live instruction — the only text-bearing change in 760 history entries, at 14:35:22 — was an audit of #9263 saying KEEP the implementation and asking for a bounded follow-up on the browser witness.

WHY THE EXISTING MITIGATION IS NOT ENOUGH. The common preamble already tells workers to walk the history and both workers did, correctly, and delivered the right thing. So nothing reached the trunk. But the preamble converts a mayor error into a worker's discovery cost: each of these spent a worker's opening context on refuting a brief. The method doc's own line is the point — the mayor's scarce output is an accurate brief, and checking a claim while writing takes seconds where discovering it was wrong takes a worker's whole context.

THE FIX, and it is cheap: before writing any brief, run `bd history <id> --json`, walk adjacent pairs newest-first for the first change to `.Issue.description` / `.Issue.notes` / `.Issue.acceptance_criteria` / `.Issue.design`, and brief from THAT. Fields nest under `.Issue`; a walk keyed at the top level matches nothing and says "no change" without erroring. The snapshot omits empty fields, so control the walk against a field known to vary ON THAT BEAD — `notes` is usually it, and is the field audits write to.

THE TELL THAT SHOULD TRIGGER THE WALK EVEN WHEN BUDGET IS TIGHT: a bead that is OPEN or IN_PROGRESS while a merged PR names its id. Cross-check the bead id against recent merged PR titles before briefing — both instances would have been caught by that one check, and it costs one `gh pr list` for a whole wave.

title: mcp-conformance: AC4 needs a WINDOWS hermetic-suite run — both suite jobs are ubuntu-latest, where the tree reaper is inert
description:

A green rollup on either job is silent about this code path.

Closing AC4 therefore needs a Windows runner leg for the hermetic suite in a workflow file. That is HOT-ZONE (.github/workflows/*), so it is sequenced separately rather than folded into a tools/mcp-conformance PR. The unit-level Windows coverage that DOES exist is runner-cleanup.test.cjs's real-process witness (a cross-spawn'd .cmd wrapper exiting with a live grandchild), which runs unskipped on a Windows developer machine and is skipped on CI for exactly the same reason.

Scope: add a Windows leg that runs the hermetic suite twice in sequence and asserts nothing is left listening on the fixture's port 8030 between and after the runs. Decide first whether the cost of a Windows shadow-cljs/JVM/Playwright boot belongs in expensive-tests.yml (nightly) rather than test.yml (per-PR) — nightly is the likelier fit.

title: hygiene: remove-worker-worktree.sh reached CANARY_AFTER but printed no REMOVED=/OK: for a bare-name argument — reproduce and settle the argument contract
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 12:0x AUSEST. This is a CLAIM needing reproduction, not a confirmed defect, and the observation is partly spoiled by my own instrument error — recorded that way on purpose.

WHAT I RAN, from the mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2:
  sh scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh xraygate-a 2>&1 | tail -6; echo "remove exit: $?"
i.e. a BARE WORKTREE NAME, not an absolute path.

WHAT I OBSERVED: six CANARY_AFTER= lines and nothing else in the visible tail. No REMOVED= line and no 'OK: worktree removal complete.' line — and per the script's own CONTRACT block (scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh:55-66) OK: is the last line on success, so the run did NOT report success. The worktree was still registered afterwards (git worktree list showed it) and 'git branch -D worker/xraygate-a' refused with 'used by worktree at ...'. I then removed it myself with 'git worktree remove --force' and the mayor implementation/node_modules canary held at 103 entries either side.

TWO THINGS I CANNOT STATE, and both are my fault rather than the script's:
(1) THE EXIT CODE IS UNKNOWN. I piped the script through 'tail' and read $? — which is TAIL's status, not the script's. That is exactly the failure loops.md and CLAUDE.md both warn about ('never pipe a gate through a filter'; a pipeline's status is its last command's), reached through a maintenance script instead of a gate. So 'remove exit: 0' in my transcript is worthless.
(2) ANY REFUSAL MESSAGE IS UNKNOWN. tail -6 discarded everything above the canary block, so if the script explained itself I destroyed the explanation.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH REPRODUCING: reaching CANARY_AFTER is not the shape of an early usage refusal. An unrecognised argument should be refused before the canary is taken, so a run that canaries and then stops without REMOVED= is either (a) a legitimate refusal that happens late, or (b) a path that does real work and then declines to finish. Those want different remedies and the tail cannot tell them apart.

THE ARGUMENT CONTRACT IS THE LIKELY EXPLANATION AND IS ALSO WORTH PINNING. The script normalises its target by 'cd'-ing to it (scripts/remove-worker-worktree.sh:221-223, _np_in=$(cd "$_np_in" && pwd)), which is CWD-relative — so a bare name run from the mayor checkout resolves against the MAYOR CHECKOUT, not the worktree parent, and names a directory that does not exist. If that is the whole story, the script behaved correctly and the repair is documentation plus a clearer refusal, not code.

title: bug(pair-mcp): trace-window and watch-epochs turn operating-frame ambiguity into a false empty epoch ring
description:
Sibling of rf2-q17a on the same axis, found by the census that bead's fix required. rf2-q17a fixed get-path only; these two were left because the bead scoped itself to get-path and its Non-goals forbid widening.

## Mechanism

Both tools emit an implicit-frame read and neither guards the tier-4 nil:

  - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/trace_window.cljs
    builds history-call as (rt-call 'epoch-history) when no sticky-frame.
  - tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/watch_epochs.cljs
    builds epochs-since-call as (rt-call 'epochs-since after) and
    history-call as (rt-call 'epoch-history), same condition.

Runtime epoch-history/1 and epochs-since/1 both default to (current-frame)
(runtime.cljs:1274-1281, 1311-1320), which is nil under two-plus app frames
with no pin. rf/epoch-history nil bottoms out in state/history-for
(implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:219-222), which returns
[] for an unknown frame. So the tools report :count 0 — 'nothing happened' —
when the truth is 'I could not tell which frame you meant'. watch-epochs
adds a second falsehood: with an empty history the caller's cursor id is
not found, so epochs-since answers :id-aged-out? true, telling the agent its
cursor fell out of the ring.

trace-window's :count-0 advisory cannot catch this: the advisory reads the
same implicit (epoch-history) call, so both sides are empty together.

## Shape

Identical to rf2-q17a's: an implicit-frame read whose runtime callee is
nil-tolerant, so ambiguity is reported as absence rather than refused. The
repair technique is the one rf2-q17a landed — resolve once in the emitted
form via (current-frame <override>), refuse with ambiguous-frame-error when
nil, otherwise read against the resolved id. Reuse the existing envelope;
do not mint new vocabulary.

Extra care these two need that get-path did not: both are cursor-paged and
carry sticky :frame state in the cursor, so the refusal must not clobber or
half-advance a cursor, and the sticky-frame tier must be honoured before the
session pin.

## Census that produced this (controlled)

Ran over every rt-call the pair-mcp tools emit, cross-referenced against the
runtime fns that call ambiguous-frame-error. Control: read-sub!,
sub-cache-info, describe-image, start-recording!, sample-signals all report
the refusal, so the instrument detects the pattern.

Already refusing (no action): read-sub, list-subscriptions, read-dom,
read-ui, describe-image, dispatch, dispatch-dry-run, replay-epoch, record,
watch-until.

Checked and NOT defects: precheck (emits only for an :explicit frame; nil
means 'no precheck, proceed'), replace-app-db (nil frame fails loudly with
:no-such-frame), restore-epoch (nil frame returns false, surfaced as a
structured failure), probe/health (reports the operating frame honestly),
snapshot (deliberately a broad multi-frame mega-op — explicit rf2-q17a
non-goal).

## Acceptance

With two app frames, no pin and no frame arg, trace-window and watch-epochs
each return isError with :reason :ambiguous-frame, :available-frames and the
recovery hint, and do NOT return :count 0 or :id-aged-out? true. Explicit
frame, session pin, sticky cursor frame and sole-app-frame sessions keep
their existing shapes. Witness asserts the error shape, not merely that it
errors.
notes:
PR #9262 audit residual (2026-09-05): resolve-once/refuse-before-read fixes the original ambiguous first call. The existing cursor ownership defect remains at this newly reviewed resolution seam: trace_window.cljs:94,177-183 and watch_epochs.cljs:93,182-194 set sticky-frame from only the input cursor/frame argument and encode that value into next-cursor. For the normal no-frame argument call, a session pin or sole app frame is resolved browser-side to fid, but neither successful eval result carries fid back to the cursor builder. Page 1 therefore stores :frame nil, even though it actually read :stories.

If the session is pinned to :rf/default before page 2, the returned opaque cursor resolves the new pin and queries a different ring. A live :after-id from :stories is then reported cursor-stale/id-aged-out; with overlapping IDs it could silently continue another ring. Similarly, starting with one app frame and registering a second before continuation turns a valid page into ambiguous-frame. title: dev:example advertises a live SPA before the first watch build exists
description:
## Scope

Make the default `npm run dev:example -- <build-id>` watch path advertise a runnable SPA only after that run's first browser bundle exists. Keep the current manifest-derived build selection, clean staging, shadow-cljs watch, loopback http-server, ownership-token handshake, and test-free examples policy. The synchronous `--no-watch` path is already ordered correctly and should remain so.

## Finding

The runner announces that an example "is live" after proving only that http-server owns the selected output directory. In the default watch path it has deliberately deleted the previous `main.js`, starts `shadow-cljs watch` asynchronously, and never waits for the first successful compile before printing the URL. On a cold or otherwise slower compile, the printed page therefore serves its host and shared assets while its required `main.js` is still absent. Opening it in that interval requests a missing script and leaves a blank/non-booted app. Because no bundle loaded, no shadow client is present to turn the later compile into recovery; the programmer has to notice the compiler finished and manually reload.

This is a small but high-leverage ergonomics defect in the catalogue's canonical one-command front door. The command's strongest status line says the SPA is live when only the static server is live.

## Independently established evidence

- `examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs:186-202` applies the correct clean-stage boundary and removes the selected output directory, including every prior `main.js`.
- The runner itself records the consequence at `serve-example.cjs:204-210`: in watch mode the cleaned directory has no `main.js` until the first compile lands.
- `serve-example.cjs:222-224` stages `index.html`, `_shared`, and declared static assets; it does not produce the compiled entrypoint.
- `serve-example.cjs:241-264` spawns `shadow-cljs watch` as a long-running asynchronous child. There is no first-build promise, emitted-file wait, or successful-compile signal in this path.
- `serve-example.cjs:275-286` then calls `startLocalHttpServer`; immediately after its `ready` result, lines 288-293 print `serve-example: <build> is live at ... (shadow-cljs watch running - edits recompile live)`.
- `implementation/scripts/lib/local-browser-harness.cjs:636-722` defines that readiness narrowly and correctly for its own purpose: publish and fetch `/.rf-harness-token` to prove the responder serves this run's root. It does not inspect or request `main.js`, so a clean staged root with only HTML/assets is `ready: true`.
- The current example inventory has 33 `index.html` / `*.index.html` host pages that load `<script src="main.js">`; `check-examples-assets.cjs` makes a live `main.js` script reference mandatory but exempts the generated file from source-tree existence checks. Thus host correctness depends on the compile product that server readiness does not cover.
- `examples/README.md:15-23` makes this runner the canonical command and says it "serves the result ... and prints the URL to open"; raw watch is explicitly contrasted with `dev:example` as compiler-only, while `dev:example` is the route to "the running app."
- The `--no-watch` branch at `serve-example.cjs:211-219` runs `shadow-cljs compile` synchronously and rejects nonzero status before staging/server startup, so the defect is confined to the default watch lifecycle.

No application, browser, build, or network operation was run during this review. The race follows from the explicit process ordering. Whether a particular warm-cache launch exposes it depends on scheduling; the cold/slow-compile case is the material witness to add.

## History and why existing coverage misses it

- Commit `a4636f853f` introduced the one-command runner with the current asynchronous watch-before-server shape.
- Commit `1d62730eb1` (`rf2-rg2tze`) fixed a worse stale-output false green by cleaning first. Its commit message and current comments explicitly say `main.js` is now visibly absent until the first compile. That is the right stale-file policy, but it exposes the remaining readiness mismatch rather than resolving it.
- Commit `3686d3ffd0` (`rf2-35lfqo`) made unexpected child failures nonzero; it does not establish first-build success while a healthy watcher is compiling or waiting after a compile error.
- Commit `0b438394dc` centralized local-server readiness around an ownership token. That helper is behaving as designed: server ownership and application-build readiness are different facts. The example runner is the layer that must compose them.
- `implementation/scripts/_examples-staging.test.cjs:411-481` proves stale `main.js` removal and call order. Its lifecycle tests cover child exit classification, not the interval between server readiness and first output. The static asset tests prove the host references `main.js`, not that the dev runner waits until it is served.

## Recommended bounded fix

Keep the existing architecture. In watch mode, distinguish two states in the runner:

1. The local server owns the staged root, but the first build is still pending. If this state is logged at all, call it "waiting for initial build," not live/openable.
2. The current run's `main.js` is present, non-empty, and retrievable from the owned server while the watch child remains alive. Only then print the existing live URL/status.

A small runner-local wait/predicate is sufficient. It may poll the selected output plus the already-owned loopback server; do not parse shadow-cljs's human log format. While waiting, retain the current long-running development behavior: a compile error may be fixed by editing source, and Ctrl+C still tears down the process tree. An unexpected watch exit must abort the wait and remain nonzero.

## Acceptance criteria

- With a fake/delayed watch child and an initially clean output directory, the runner does not emit its `is live`/open-this-URL signal while `main.js` is absent, zero-length, or not served successfully.
- When that same child publishes a valid non-empty `main.js`, the runner emits the live URL once and continues watching/serving as today.
- If the watch child exits before first-build readiness, the runner does not announce the app as live, tears down the server, and exits nonzero with a direct initial-build diagnostic.
- A compile error from a still-running watcher does not require restarting the runner: after the programmer fixes source and the first successful output lands, the URL becomes live.
- The existing ownership-token handshake remains the authority for "this server serves this run's root"; first-build readiness is composed in `serve-example`, not generalized into every local-browser harness consumer.
- `--no-watch` still compiles once before server startup and reports compile failure nonzero. `--list`, build-id normalization, staging, per-example assets, free-port selection, reload caching policy, and cleanup remain unchanged.
- Add focused script-level coverage for delayed artifact, successful first publication, and watch-before-build failure. Demonstrate the new check failing against the current ordering, then run the existing examples staging/script tests.

## Non-goals

- No new launcher, build registry, dev server, compiler wrapper, or shadow-cljs protocol.
- No parsing of compiler console text and no dependence on a particular shadow-cljs log phrase.
- No browser auto-open, page-level smoke for every example, HMR redesign, service worker, retry UI, or generalized file-watching abstraction.
- No change to example application code, public re-frame2 APIs, shared visual assets, or the test-free `examples/` policy.
- No attempt to make every later recompile atomic; this issue owns only the first truthful runnable status after a clean launch.

## Duplicate distinctions

Targeted all-status searches of `.beads/issues.jsonl` covered `serve-example`, `dev:example`, `initial compile`, `first compile`, `main.js` with live/ready/404/blank, and frozen bundle; no bead owns first-build readiness.

- Historical `rf2-rg2tze` removes stale output and intentionally leaves `main.js` absent until the first compile; this finding is the remaining live-status/readiness seam.
- Closed `rf2-iacw2` and `rf2-ujdn0` correct documentation so programmers invoke `dev:example`; they do not change when that command's URL becomes runnable.
- Closed `rf2-y1kbf` requires host HTML to contain a live `<script src="main.js">`; it does not verify the generated script exists at launch time.
- Historical `rf2-35lfqo` handles watcher/server crashes. A healthy but not-yet-successful first compile is not a child-exit outcome.
- The shared ownership-token work (`rf2-slapfs`) prevents a foreign server false green and should not be broadened; it cannot prove application artifacts by design.

## Uncertainty

No cold compile was launched under the review's no-runtime constraint, so the exact user-visible duration is cache and machine dependent. A sufficiently fast warm build can land before http-server readiness and hide the race. The unsynchronized state is nevertheless explicit in source and guaranteed to be reachable whenever initial compilation takes longer than server startup. The implementer should capture that case deterministically with a fake delayed producer rather than relying on machine timing.

title: tools/xray(popout): detached shell has no keyboard listener, so its keyboard workflow is inert
description:
CLAIM
`mount/popout!` renders a live shell into a second document, but Xray never attaches its keyboard listener to that document. DOM key events do not cross from the pop-out document to the opener document, so the keyboard-first Xray workflow is inert whenever focus is in the pop-out. The existing handler is also opener-surface-aware rather than pop-out-aware: its bare spine branch gates on `mount/visible?` (which reads only `mount-state`), and Cmd/Ctrl+K can call `mount/toggle!`, which controls the in-app shell rather than the already-visible pop-out.

EVIDENCE AT REVIEW TIP
Reviewed `cacace4e1803cfe6441d32b7ededa3b8da1a7fc1`; local `origin/main` has no later change to the relevant files.

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:435-455`, `attach!`: a process-wide `attached-state` CAS installs exactly one capture listener, always on opener-realm `js/document`. `detach!` at :458-482 removes from that same `js/document`. There is no API for a second document.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:1457-1541`, `popout!`: creates `win` / `doc`, injects styles, renders `shell-view`, installs opener-gone/lifecycle listeners, and records `popout-state`; it never installs a `keydown` listener on `doc`. `register-popout-unload-cleanup!` is pagehide/unload cleanup only.
- `mount.cljs:100-121`, `visible?` / `status`: visibility is derived only from `mount-state`; `popout-state` is a separate singleton. `keybinding.cljs:389-433`, `handle-keydown`: Cmd/Ctrl+K routes through `mount/toggle!` when that in-app state is hidden, while bare Space/L/j/k/G require `mount/visible?`. Even mechanically reusing the handler on the pop-out document without surface context would therefore be wrong when no inline shell is visible.
- `tools/xray/spec/API.md:842-849` explicitly describes `popout!` as its own document context with its own React root, theme cascade, and keybinding. `tools/xray/README.md:243-251` documents Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, and the in-shell Space/L/j/k/G workflow; its “not bound to a global chord” sentence is specifically about LAUNCHING the pop-out, not disabling keyboard operation inside it.
- Existing proof misses this boundary. `tools/xray/testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs:554-599` proves only that the pop-out root/shell exists; :1758-1845 proves shared cascade rendering under load, but sends no key in the pop-out. `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount_cljs_test.cljs:1485-1498` asserts only pagehide/unload registrations on the pop-out window. `keybinding_cljs_test.cljs` stubs the single ambient `js/document`, never a second document.

VERIFIED IMPACT
A programmer who moves Xray to a second monitor and gives that window focus cannot use the documented keyboard-first operations there: Cmd/Ctrl+K, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+M, Space/L/j/k/G, comma/s, or the contextual Esc path are never received by Xray. This is not an edge-case protocol concern; pop-out is a shipped top-bar action and the keyboard map is a primary low-friction debugging surface. Mouse controls and live data rendering still work, which makes the failure look like intermittent shortcut breakage rather than an unsupported mode.

BOUNDED RECOMMENDATION
Give each live pop-out document one lifecycle-owned keydown listener that reuses the canonical predicates/dispatch logic with explicit surface context. For a pop-out, “visible shell” means the pop-out shell, and Cmd/Ctrl+K must open its palette without mounting/reopening the in-app shell.
