title: instrument: a 129-way grep -E alternation silently returns ZERO on this box, and a tail-spliced control passes anyway
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-05 by the mayor, after a read-only backlog audit refuted a sweep the mayor had run and believed.

THE FAILURE. The already-done sweep in loops.md section 3 ('for each open id, search the trunk's merged history for that id') was run as a single alternation of every open bead id:
  PAT=$(paste -sd'|' ids.txt)          # 129 ids, 1475 characters
  git log origin/main --format='%h %s' -1500 | grep -cE "($PAT)"
It returned 0. The true answer is 36.

MEASURED THREE WAYS ON THE SAME 1500 COMMITS, same shell, same box:
  single id, grep -c 'rf2-6g6e'          -> 1      (correct)
  129-way alternation, grep -cE          -> 0      (WRONG)
  grep -F -f ids.txt                     -> 36     (correct)
The falsifier that started this: commit c20d7ee62d, 'docs(009): frame-destroyed stops narrating the retired ui bundle as live, and :op is public (rf2-6g6e)', 268 commits from HEAD and therefore well inside the window, on a bead that is OPEN.

WHY THE CONTROL DID NOT CATCH IT, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. A control WAS run at the time, and it passed. It spliced one known-present closed id onto the END of the same alternation and read 1. So it exercised the alternation's TAIL and proved nothing about its body — a control constructed so that it avoids the case it exists to catch, which is the exact defect class this project's own method tells you to hunt. Splicing at the end is the natural place to splice, which is what makes it dangerous.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, and it is one flag: pass the ids as a PATTERN FILE with fixed-string matching, grep -F -f <file>. It has no alternation to overflow, needs no escaping, and was measured correct here. If an alternation is genuinely wanted, splice the control id into the MIDDLE, never the end.

WHAT THE MISS COST: fifteen open beads had landed trunk commits naming them and the sweep reported none. It did not cause a wrong close — the audit caught it first — but the whole point of that sweep is to stop a worker being dispatched at finished work, and a silent zero is the one answer that reads as a clean bill of health.

RELATION TO WHAT IS ALREADY WRITTEN. CLAUDE.md already records that this box's GNU grep 3.0 under MSYS ABORTS on the flag pair -iF (SIGABRT, exit 134, nothing on stdout). This is a DIFFERENT failure on the same tool — no abort, exit 0, a confident zero — so the existing bullet does not cover it and would not have warned anybody. Whether the root cause is a regex-size limit, an MSYS argument-length limit, or something else was NOT established; establishing it is part of this bead, but the remedy above does not depend on the answer.

SCOPE: (1) reproduce the three measurements above and bisect roughly where the alternation starts failing (try 2, 10, 50, 100, 129 ids) so the failure has a stated shape rather than a folk rule; (2) add a bullet to CLAUDE.md's 'Four ways the INSTRUMENTS misreport on this machine' list — it will become five — carrying the measurement, the grep -F -f remedy, and the tail-splice trap; (3) grep the repo for other multi-id or multi-term alternations built the same way and report them, without necessarily fixing them. Do NOT weaken or remove the existing -iF bullet; both are real and they are different.
notes:
A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, measured 2026-09-05 by the mayor about half an hour after the first — and this bead should be read as being about the CLASS rather than about grep alternations specifically.

WHAT HAPPENED. A beads checkpoint aborted on a git index.lock collision (a concurrent process in the mayor checkout). To check whether four bd closes had survived into the pushed export, I read HEAD's .beads/issues.jsonl with:
  git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | grep -F "\"<id>\"" | head -1 | jq -r '.status'
It reported four beads as still OPEN. They were closed. I re-ran the checkpoint, the reading did not change, and for a moment that looked like a durability failure in the tracker — the most alarming class of finding available.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG, NOT THE DATA. The export is one JSON record per line, and a bead id appears in OTHER beads' records too — dependency lists, discovered-from edges, close-reason prose. So grep matched a record that MENTIONS the id and head -1 took it, and that record's own .status was reported as the target's. Control, run once the suspicion formed: 4 records MENTION rf2-s4dp, exactly 1 IS it. The correct read is a select on the identity field:
  git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl | jq -r --arg i "<id>" 'select(.id==$i)|.status'
which reports all four closed, matching the live database.

WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS BEAD. Same shape as the 129-way alternation: an instrument returning a WELL-FORMED, PLAUSIBLE, WRONG answer with no error, where the failure is in how the question was asked rather than in what was asked about. And the same near-miss on the control — the first instance had a control that exercised the pattern's tail and proved nothing; this one had NO control until suspicion prompted one, and the control is what settled it in a single command.

THE GENERALISATION WORTH WRITING INTO WHATEVER LANDS: when reading a RECORD out of a line-oriented record file, match on the IDENTITY FIELD, never on the identifier appearing anywhere in the line. A grep for an id in a file where ids cross-reference each other answers 'some record containing this id', which is a different question and is right only when nothing cross-references. The mention-versus-is count is the one-line control that distinguishes them, and it is cheap enough to run every time.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING FOR THE SCOPE OF THIS BEAD: the git index.lock collision itself is normal contention in the mayor checkout, not corruption — CLAUDE.md already documents concurrent git processes there. The correct response was to inspect state (lock gone, tree clean, HEAD == origin/main, row counts equal) rather than to retry into it or to 'recover' by restoring an older export from history, which would have time-travelled the tracker. No recovery was needed and none was attempted.
DELIVERED 2026-09-05 by worker claudemd-a — PR #9283 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9283), branch worker/claudemd-a, NOT closed, left in_progress.

ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED, and it is NOT a size or argument-length limit. jq on this box writes CRLF. paste -sd'|' therefore joins ids that each end in a carriage return, so every alternative except the LAST ends in \r and matches nothing.

REPRODUCED 2026-09-05, 1500 trunk commits, 99 open ids, one shell:
  grep -F -f ids.txt                     -> 22  (correct)
  paste -sd'|' alternation of same file  ->  1  (wrong)
  same alternation after tr -d '\r'      -> 22  (correct)
The one line the alternation matched named rf2-yo4s — the LAST id in the file, the only alternative without a trailing \r.

BISECT, alternation vs grep -F -f on the same first-N subset:
  N=10  (99 chars)   alt 0   -F -f 3
  N=50  (587 chars)  alt 0   -F -f 16
  N=90  (1078 chars) alt 0   -F -f 18
  N=99  (1169 chars) alt 1   -F -f 22
It already fails at 10 ids / 99 characters, so the size hypothesis in the description is refuted.

PRODUCER ISOLATED TO jq (jq-1.8.1), not bd and not the shell: bd list --json ends its lines LF; echo '[{"id":"aaa"}]' | jq -r '.[].id' ends them CRLF; a single-value $( ... | jq -r ... ) capture comes back clean. So the defect bites exactly where those lines are JOINED or read as patterns.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PROPOSED REMEDY, by measurement. The description concludes 'splice the control id into the MIDDLE, never the end'. Measured: the tail splice reads 1 and passes, AND the middle splice also reads 1 and also passes — a spliced shell literal carries no \r wherever it sits, so position does not discriminate at all. The rule that DOES discriminate: the control must be drawn FROM the same file that produced the pattern, i.e. travel the same pipeline as the data. The landed text says that, not 'splice into the middle'.

SCOPE ITEM 3 (other alternations built the same way): swept the tracked tree for paste -sd, tr '\n' '|', join("|") and grep -E over a shell-built variable. The only hit outside CLAUDE.md is .beads/issues.jsonl (this bead's own text). No script in the repo builds a pattern this way; nothing to fix beyond the record.

Neither existing item weakened, restated or removed. The bead's NOTES instance (mention-vs-is on .beads/issues.jsonl) is folded into (e) as its closing sentence with the identity-field remedy.

The tail splice does read 1 and pass — AND SO DOES THE MIDDLE SPLICE, also 1, because a spliced shell literal carries no `\r` wherever it sits. The rule that actually discriminates is that THE CONTROL MUST BE DRAWN FROM THE SAME FILE THAT PRODUCED THE PATTERN. That is what landed, and it is a better rule than mine because it generalises past this one mechanism: a control constructed by hand shares none of the pipeline's corruptions.

title: merge criterion: the clause-5 job-key discriminator counts job keys in workflows that have no pull_request trigger, so a nightly-only job reads as a check-set change
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 from a live merge of PR #9277, where the discriminator read jobkeys=1 and the correct answer was "the PR check set did not change".

THE MECHANIC AS RECORDED. CLAUDE.md's trap (a) under the merge-criterion bullet gives the clause-5 discriminator as:

  git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -cE '^\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$'

and the whole of that paragraph is about the TWO LEADING SPACES: the unindented form matches nothing, reads a reassuring zero, and fails OPEN. That half is right, is exercised in both directions, and is not what this bead is about.

WHAT IS MISSING. The discriminator counts job keys across EVERY file under .github/workflows/, but clause 5 is about the set of checks a PULL REQUEST will be graded on. A workflow with no `pull_request` trigger contributes no checks to any PR rollup, so a job added to one moves the count and not the band.

MEASURED, 2026-09-05, on PR #9277 (worker/specxray-a):
  merge-base b86310b3c1 .. origin/main  ->  wf=271  jobkeys=1
  the single key is `mcp-live-windows`, added to .github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml by PR #9276
  expensive-tests.yml `on:` is `schedule: cron "17 15 * * *"` + `workflow_dispatch` — no pull_request
  empirical corroboration: the band was 87 on the four PRs merged AFTER #9276 landed, and #9277's own rollup was 87

So the flag was real (the trunk's workflow tree did gain a job) and the inference it invites was wrong.

WHICH DIRECTION IT FAILS, because that decides the priority. This one fails CLOSED: it flags a merge that should proceed, where every other trap recorded in that bullet ADMITS a merge that should have been blocked. That makes it much less dangerous than its neighbours and is why this is P3 rather than P2. But it is not harmless, for two reasons: (i) it will fire on every nightly job addition, and a flag that is usually spurious trains the reader to wave it through, which is how a real one gets waved through too; (ii) the mayor that hit it verified the trigger AFTER merging rather than before, i.e. the recorded mechanic did not carry the check that discharges it — which is exactly the "hazard recorded without the test that discharges it" shape that loops.md §6 says to fix in the document.

THE REPAIR IS ONE CLAUSE, NOT A REWRITE. Trap (a) should say that a non-zero count is a question and not an answer, and name the question: read the `on:` block of the workflow file the key was added to, and count only keys in files carrying a `pull_request` trigger. The `+++ b/<path>` lines in the same diff already name the file, so the follow-up costs one command:

  git diff <merge-base> origin/main -- .github/workflows/ | grep -E '^(\+\+\+|\+  [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$)'

DO NOT WEAKEN THE TWO-SPACE RULE OR THE FAIL-OPEN FRAMING while editing that paragraph. The paragraph's subject is three traps that each fail open; this addition is a qualification to (a), not a fourth trap, and it must not dilute the sentence that says a constant zero is the reassuring answer.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING, per the standing rule that this brief's premises are claims: re-read trap (a) at tip, confirm expensive-tests.yml still has no pull_request trigger, and confirm test.yml still keeps its pull_request trigger UNFILTERED (the phantom-pending trap rf2-dtvmb fixed) — the qualification must not read as licence to discount test.yml.

ALSO CONSIDER whether the same clause belongs in docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md §1 clause 5, which is the normative statement CLAUDE.md's bullet says it is not restating. If clause 5 already says "the trunk's current workflow matrix" in a way that covers this, the CLAUDE.md concretion is the only edit needed — say which and why.

SEQUENCING: CLAUDE.md is a hot file. rf2-u62e is live on it right now (worker hygiene-b, worktree C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/hygiene-b). This bead waits for that PR to merge. rf2-jwlh is also queued behind it.

title: Xray: focused-value copy designed from the data owner outward (reopens B.9; deferred until demand and Mike's go)
description:
DEFERRED DESIGN BEAD, filed 2026-09-04 by the delegated ruling agent for rf2-6r9j.24 (Mike's delegation of 2026-09-04). NOT dispatchable as filed: it exists so the design analysis two reviewers produced is not lost when the dossier is deleted. It becomes live only if Mike says there is demand for per-value copy in Xray AND agrees to reopen the B.9 lock; either signal alone is not enough.

## What was decided upstream

rf2-6r9j.24 RETRACTED the dead universal value-copy affordance (the edn-widget copy-affordance glyph, its CSS, the :copy? no-op, and the dispatcher-less :rf.xray/copy-value-to-clipboard and :rf.xray/copy-path-to-clipboard events) and honoured tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md sections 10.1 and 10.5 (LOCKED per B.9: no copy-path, no copy-value on the canonical renderer; re-proposals must reopen the lock with the mayor first). The published skill (skills/re-frame2-xray/references/shared-components.md:22-26) carries the same contract. This bead is the ONLY sanctioned route back.

## Why a universal root glyph was wrong, so the next design does not repeat it

The retracted event received only [_ value] with no absolute path, origin, partition or record kind. Xray's egress.cljs:53-58 and spec/API.md (Off-box egress section) say a slice egress'd in isolation must pass its absolute app-db :path or the path-keyed :sensitive / :large declarations cannot match. The canonical inspector is handed: app-db slices at a path (panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs), raw managed-fx request/response/handler values (panels/managed_fx_template.cljs) which spec/Security.md section Epoch privacy posture says are NOT app-db-rooted and MUST be default-redacted off-box, raw trace before/after (panels/trace.cljs), registry values (static flows/routes/schemas), and runtime-db machine snapshots. Those do not share one projection rule; a shared renderer cannot infer provenance from a naked value. The old tests proved only app-db-root-shaped fixtures through direct dispatch.

## What is lost without it (the case FOR building this, kept honest)

Browser text selection copies the render projection: collapsed nodes give their {N keys} / [N items] preview, diff annotations come along, and the app-db path is lost. Snapshot app-db is the whole focused-frame db, much coarser. There is no route for "paste this event's :fx vector / this exception's ex-data / this sub's value into a bug report or REPL". Demand evidence is nil either way: the glyph was user-reachable four days (2026-05-21 to 05-25) and nobody asked for it in the ~100 days after.

## Design sketch (from the Codex review, corrected at tip)

- Design from the DATA OWNER outward. Each enabled call site supplies a typed copy projection rather than a value: an app-db slice with its absolute :path; a projected trace/epoch record (record-aware, fx :args redacted by default, per Security.md); a runtime-db projection under its own axis; registry/static values that are value-free by contract and may ride the fx directly (the Copy Mermaid pattern at static/machines/panel.cljs).
- Opt-in per call site where such a projection exists; never default-on from the renderer root. App-DB stays OUT unless Mike changes it (his rf2-ilubp ruling, 95d92180bb).
- Precedent: re-frame-10x (upstream a3c309430d, src/day8/re_frame_10x/popup.cljs) exposes copy CONTEXTUALLY as Copy Path and Copy Subtree in the inspector popup, derived from the selected data path. The natural home here is therefore the edn-inspector popup (views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs), which at tip has only a close button — an action strip would be new chrome, not existing chrome. Do not stack a second absolute-positioned button at right: 2px beside the popup affordance.
- Egress: every value-bearing projection goes through day8.re-frame2-xray.egress/egress-value naming :frame (the fail-closed gesture; nil / destroyed / colliding-id frames egress :rf/redacted — pinned by the re-pointed rf2-7htk7 proofs in test/.../panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs) and passing :path for slices. The clipboard fx :rf.xray.fx/copy-to-clipboard already offers :on-success / :on-failure; use them for honest Copied / Copy failed feedback.
- Acceptance for that future bead: a REAL rendered click through frame routing (N parallel shells isolated; captured dispatch-fn pattern of popup-affordance-button in views/edn_inspector.cljs), each privacy axis, stale/nil frame, clipboard rejection (NotAllowedError), keyboard focus, and browser user-activation — the current suites stub the fx or run on node, and nobody has established that queuing rf/dispatch from the click before writeText keeps activation in supported browsers.
- Spec: reopen B.9 explicitly in 021 section 10.5 (and 10.1) with the narrow form chosen; update the skill's shared-components.md in the same PR; correct spec/API.md's Off-box egress inventory and README.md to enumerate the new sink; any PR touching tools/xray/ updates tools/xray/spec/* in the same PR or states why the spec is unchanged.

## Not this bead

The 007-UX-IA long-keyword click-to-copy glyph on elided keywords is a separate design. The 018-Event-Spine Copy path / Ctrl+click copy cascade-id items are tracked separately (see the sibling bead filed from rf2-6r9j.24).
notes:
HOLD MADE HONEST BY THE MAYOR, 2026-09-05, from a §3 backlog reread.

THIS BEAD WAS DEFERRED WITH NO DEFER DATE. Every other deferred bead in this tracker carries one (the current cluster all share 2026-09-16). A deferral with no date never resurfaces: it is functionally closed while still counting as open work, which is the worst of both — it neither gets done nor gets decided, and nobody meets it again.

Its stated release condition is "demand plus Mike's go", which is a real condition and not a stalling one. But a condition nobody is scheduled to re-evaluate is not a condition. Defer date set to 2026-10-06.

SETTING A DATE RATHER THAN CLOSING IT, deliberately. Under the project stance a bead may die with its reasoning recorded instead of consuming a worker, and for a P4 design idea awaiting demand that would be defensible. It is not being closed because the DESIGN in this bead is the valuable part and closing it buries the design, whereas the deferral only needed to become visible again. So the fix is the date, not the disposition.

No design decision is made or implied here. When it next surfaces the question is still the one the bead asks: has demand appeared, and does Mike want it.

title: bug(realworld-http): profile replies can overwrite a newer username route
description:
## Scope

Review surface: `examples/real-apps/**`, specifically the managed-HTTP RealWorld profile page. The resources-based RealWorld variant was compared and is already keyed by canonical resource params; it is not part of the fix.

## Correctness finding

`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs` binds each request URL and request ID to the current `:username`, but every banner/authored/favorites reply target omits that identity and every terminal handler writes the one shared `:profile`, `:profile.articles`, or `:profile.favorites` slice unconditionally. Follow/unfollow similarly captures the route username only in the URL, then applies success or rollback to whichever profile slice is current.

Navigating Alice -> Bob leaves Alice and Bob under distinct request IDs, so managed HTTP may legally deliver both. A late Alice settle can therefore replace Bob data, statuses, errors, timestamps, or following state. It can also corrupt the current state-machine presentation.

## Evidence

- Routes `/profile/:username` and `/profile/:username/favorites` run profile plus list loads on each match: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:110-126`.
- The page has shared unkeyed slices initialized once: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:39-46,147-153`.
- Banner request ID is `[:profile/load username]`, but targets are `[:profile/loaded]` and `[:profile/load-failed]`; both handlers write unconditionally: `profile.cljs:159-198`.
- Authored requests are keyed by username but their targets omit it and their handlers write unconditionally: `profile.cljs:200-239`. Favorites repeats the defect: `profile.cljs:241-280`.
- Follow/unfollow paths use the current username, while `:profile/followed`, `:profile/unfollowed`, and rollback handlers mutate the shared current profile without issuer identity: `profile.cljs:286-331`.
- The view consumes only those shared slices (`profile.cljs:380-389,438-502`), so stale Alice can be rendered and acted upon under Bob's URL.
- This is not just a cosmetic flash. If late Alice failure arrives while Bob is loading, it can send the data machine to `:error`; a later Bob success writes DB data, but the `:error` state has no `fetch-succeeded` transition (`profile.cljs:86-121`), leaving the page stranded in an error presentation.
- Managed HTTP only supersedes an old request when a new request has the same request ID (`docs/async/http.md:312-316`; `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1573-1580`). Alice and Bob IDs differ, so route staleness remains application-owned.
- The local canonical precedent already fixes the equivalent article defect: `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:152-157,242-284,317-364` carries the slug through targets and rejects replies that do not match the active slug (closed `rf2-iy3d6`).
- The resources variant is immune by construction: identity includes canonical params (`examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/resources.cljs:13-18`), profile/list resources include username/page (`resources.cljs:172-233`), and routes plan those keyed resources (`realworld_resources/routing.cljs:206-245`).
- Existing profile coverage (`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs:2860-2897`) uses immediate canned replies for one username and cannot expose ordering. The same suite's held-request cross-slug tests around lines 1900-2130 provide a suitable pattern.
- History traces this shape to managed-HTTP conversion `36436af528`; the current `origin/main` profile blob is identical to this review worktree's blob.

## Impact

This canonical realistic example teaches programmers and AI that username-keyed request IDs alone provide navigation stale suppression. Under ordinary network reordering it can show or mutate the wrong user's profile, authored/favorited articles, and following state. The machine can remain in an error presentation even after current data succeeds.

## Recommended bounded fix

Use one local correlation convention, mirroring `comments.cljs`:

1. Carry the issuing username in every banner and social terminal target; carry the relevant username/page key (or equivalent generation) in list targets.
2. Record or compare the active logical key and reject stale success, failure, rollback, status, timestamp, and machine writes before mutation.
3. On username identity change, clear or hide prior-user data. Retaining data for a same-key refresh remains valid.
4. Correlate follow/unfollow settlements to their issuing profile. A stable per-profile social request ID may additionally supersede rapid same-profile toggles, but generic framework machinery is unnecessary.

## Non-goals

Do not migrate this page to resources, add a cache framework or generic remote-data abstraction, change the route/HTTP API, redesign the UI, or modify the already identity-keyed resources variant.

## Duplicate review

Searched `.beads/issues.jsonl` and the `origin/main` tracker for cross-profile/cross-username/late-profile/profile-race/wrong-profile terms, every affected handler name, request-id/profile, and out-of-order/profile. Only closed `rf2-iy3d6` matched because its article defect recorded `profile race` as a search term. Generic profile-file/page searches found closed article/comment social work (`rf2-amhpk`, `rf2-84iek`, `rf2-iy3d6`) and unrelated base-href work (`rf2-do50`). Those are precedents, not owners of profile replies. No open or closed duplicate owns this behavior.

## Uncertainty

The review is static by review-pool constraint, but the delivery branch follows directly from the documented same-ID-only suppression and the distinct username IDs. The exact internal key shape, and whether a reply after leaving and returning to the same username should be accepted, are implementation choices. The required invariant is that a settle cannot mutate a different active profile identity.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Add deterministic held-transport CLJS coverage for Alice -> Bob navigation across banner, authored, and favorites requests. Settle Bob first and then Alice success/failure; Alice cannot change Bob data, status, error, timestamps, or machine presentation.
2. Prove non-vacuity: the corresponding current-Bob success/failure is accepted. A late prior-profile failure cannot strand the current machine, and current success can present loaded data.
3. While Bob is pending, previously settled Alice banner/list data is not exposed under Bob's route. Same-identity refresh retention remains allowed.
4. Hold Alice follow/unfollow, navigate to Bob, then settle Alice. Neither success nor rollback mutates Bob; current-profile settlements still work.
5. Production reply vectors carry enough identity for every state-changing terminal path to reject stale work.
6. Demonstrate a red negative control by removing or inverting the correlation guard, then restore it and pass the focused RealWorld CLJS suite and applicable build/type gates.
notes:
PR #9236 audit residual (2026-09-05): the new profile.cljs:425-430 comment declines :request-id because aborting an in-flight write is unsafe, then says “the last click's own settle is authoritative regardless.” The first point is defensible; the conclusion is false. Starting unfollowed, :profile/follow optimistically sets true and emits POST success [:profile/followed "alice"]; the now-visible Unfollow button can immediately set false and emit DELETE success [:profile/unfollowed "alice"]. If DELETE settles first and the older POST settles last, both replies match [:profile :username] "alice", so both pass reply-for-current-profile? and the older POST re-seeds the whole banner with :following true. Rollback order can similarly undo a newer accepted intent. No pending flag, operation generation, or request id distinguishes them.

The cross-username fix and its tests remain valid. Bounded follow-up: state and test an explicit same-profile mutation policy. The smallest honest policy is to serialize this one toggle (handler and button refuse/disable a second intent while one is pending, clearing pending on correlated success/failure); if rapid replacement is retained, carry a generation and reconcile server truth rather than treating abort as proof a write did not occur. Add a held-transport Follow→Unfollow ordering witness and remove the false “authoritative regardless” claim. Do not introduce a generic mutation manager.
PR #9260 audit residual (2026-09-05): the new follow-pending? latch fixes immediate same-page Follow -> Unfollow, but :profile/load discards it on a username change (profile.cljs:253-259). Alice -> Bob -> Alice while Alice POST is still pending therefore returns to an unlocked Alice banner. A return GET can truthfully report following=true once the server has applied that POST, while its response remains held. Unfollow now emits a DELETE for Alice. Both response vectors still carry only username, so the old POST response passes reply-for-current-profile?, overwrites the newer intent, and releases the newer DELETE latch (:profile/followed 509-513). Delivering DELETE first and old POST last leaves following=true even though the final accepted intent/server state is false.

Verified against the exact merged 12a75a5c907cd22c690d896ff23b69b064b27c8e handler forms in an isolated JVM Clojure source-handler probe. Immediate same-page Unfollow was correctly refused (control). After Alice -> Bob -> Alice and a truthful followed GET, DELETE was emitted while the earlier POST response remained pending. Old POST during DELETE changed following to true and follow-pending? to false; DELETE then old POST also ended true. The probe evaluates the actual pure handler forms, stubbing only rh/request/schema constants; it does not claim a full CLJS router/transport run. Artifacts: ai/pr-audit-9260/probe.clj and audit-pr9260-re-frame2-1.log/.exit (exit 0).

Bounded continuation of the existing same-profile serialization owner: retain ownership of an outstanding profile mutation across navigation/return and ensure its reply cannot clear another operation's latch or overwrite a newer accepted intent. Add a held-transport Alice -> Bob -> Alice witness alongside the immediate-toggle and cross-username controls, including old success/rollback while a newer operation is pending. Keep the one-toggle policy small; dropping old replies alone or treating abort as proof of no server write does not establish serialization. Correct the prose claiming navigation needs no handling. Original criteria and the working cross-username protection remain intact.
Delivery (PR #9284, 2026-09-05): the PR #9260 audit residual is closed. The follow latch moves off the banner slice into a top-level, username-keyed :profile.follow-pending set that :profile/load never touches, so it survives alice -> bob -> alice with the POST still in flight. Each of the three follow settles now splits between two owners, the comments.cljs TWO QUESTIONS shape: the banner write stays gated on reply-for-current-profile?, while the latch release is the mutation's own and therefore unconditional — keying is what makes that safe, since alice's reply can only release alice. (fnil conj #{}) is load-bearing: hydration is :replace-frame-state and the set is deliberately absent from ssr-app-slice-keys, now stated in ssr.cljc. Prose corrected in profile.cljs, schema.cljs and ssr.cljc, including the false 'navigating away needs no handling of its own' claim.

Two CLJS witnesses in implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs: profile-follow-latch-survives-a-walk-away-and-back-test (new held-transport alice -> bob -> alice; return GET reports server truth, alice comes back latched, the Unfollow is refused and issues no second request, then the held POST seeds AND releases and the toggle works again) and profile-follow-latch-does-not-leak-to-a-bystander-test (replaces profile-follow-latch-does-not-outlive-its-profile-test, which pinned the behaviour this fixes: bob stays live while alice is out, two profiles latched at once, an older success and an older rollback each release their own username alone under a newer pending operation). Cross-username protection and immediate-toggle serialisation unchanged and still pinned.

Both bead premises verified at source and both HOLD, though the citations had drifted: same-request-id-only supersede is docs/async/http.md:312 and spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:1610 (not :312-316/:1573-1580); the resources variant is immune via [scope resource-id canonical-params] and was not touched. The bead's profile.cljs line ranges are all stale — the file is 774 lines at tip against a largest citation of 502.

The stranded-:error half needs NO further work and no follow-up bead: #9236 already made it unreachable rather than merely unused (no cross-identity :fetch-failed reaches the machine, and every path to :loaded for the current identity passes through :fetch-started first), pinned by profile-cross-username-late-failure-is-refused-test.

Planted-fault control: restoring the old latch-dies-with-the-slice line took the suite to exit 1 with 5 failures, all inside the new alice -> bob -> alice witness, at identical test/assertion counts; restore verified by blob hash.

OUTSIDE THE FENCE, for the mayor: main is currently RED on compile-node-test's zero-warning gate. Two :uix.linter/interop-ref-read warnings in implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120 and :139 ('use-ref hook in UIx returns Atom-like ref, use @ instead of .-current'). title: ssr html-helpers: presence attributes with a non-boolean value emit name="value" where react-dom emits name=""
description:
Filed by the mayor 2026-09-05 from an observation the rf2-owml worker made, verified, and deliberately did NOT act on because `implementation/ssr/**` was outside its fence. It filed nothing and said "your call". This bead is that call being put where it will not be lost.

THE OBSERVATION. `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` takes a different branch entirely for a NON-BOOLEAN value on a presence attribute: it emits `name="value"` with no collapse, so `{:disabled "yes"}` renders `disabled="yes"`, where react-dom renders `disabled=""`. The reagent-slim serializer, after PR #9244, collapses both spellings on the EMPTY VALUE and matches react-dom.

WHY THIS IS A QUESTION AND NOT YET A DEFECT — and this is the part to settle before writing any code. It depends entirely on WHICH CONTRACT that serializer is held to:
  * If `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` is held to REACT-DOM BYTE-PARITY, this is a divergence and should be fixed the way #9244 fixed the slim path.
  * If it is held to the SPEC 004B CONTRACT, it may be correct as written. IMPL-SPEC already records that 004B is DELIBERATELY different from react-dom for `value`, so a deliberate difference here would have precedent rather than being an oversight.
**Establish which, from the spec and from IMPL-SPEC, before touching the code.** A worker that assumes byte-parity and "fixes" a deliberate difference has broken a contract to satisfy a comparison nobody asked for.

WHY IT MATTERS IF IT IS A DIVERGENCE, and this is the argument for P3 rather than P4: `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` hydrates server-rendered markup, and `spec/011` records that React does NOT guarantee to patch an attribute-only hydration mismatch. So a server emitting `disabled="yes"` against a client expecting `disabled=""` is exactly the class that survives into production silently. That is the same mechanism the whole #9207/#9224 line of work has been closing.

THE PROBE THAT SETTLES THE FACTS, already run once on the slim side and worth repeating here: probe react-dom 19.2.0 directly for all 28 presence names with the values `""`, `0`, `"0"`, `"yes"` and `true`. The rf2-owml worker measured 28/28 with zero anomalies on the slim path — react-dom OMITS on `""` and `0` and EMITS on `"yes"` and `true` — and pinned the asymmetry that invites a second bug: the STRING `"0"` is truthy, only the NUMBER `0` is not.

A CAUTION FROM THE SAME WORK, because it nearly caused damage. The slim test's own docstring claimed React 19 emits the bare short form and only React 18 emits `disabled=""`. **That was false** — probing react-dom 19.2.0 showed it emits `disabled=""`, which made the canonicalisation load-bearing rather than vestigial. **Do not trust a docstring's claim about React's output; probe the installed react-dom.** A tempting "just delete the special case" reading would have reddened the suite.

SEQUENCING: `implementation/ssr/**` is not hot zone, but check it is free — it has taken merges recently (#9215, and #9207 before it).
notes:
--- worker ssrhelp-a, PR #9267 ---
THE CONTRACT QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND NOT BY PREFERENCE. 004B §Booleans and
their neighbours already RULES this case, in its `hidden` row: a boolean
attribute is "a pure boolean attr, not an enumerated exception: true /
'until-found' / ANY TRUTHY -> bare presence", and the pre-probe draft's
string-value carve-out is recorded there as FALSIFIED. So the spec and
react-dom agree and the implementation contradicted both. It is a defect, not
a deliberate 004B divergence.

was an INTERNAL one. `re-frame.ssr.ui-tree` (the structural-tree serialiser
sharing these rosters) already collapsed a non-boolean value, so for
`{:disabled "yes"}` the two SSR pipelines emitted `disabled=""` and
`disabled="yes"` respectively. `ssr_boolean_attr_react_parity_test` exists to
stop exactly that drift and could not reach it: it drove `[true false]` only.

`:overloaded` are INDISTINGUISHABLE for a boolean — both render name="" for
true and nothing for false. They part only on a non-boolean value. So a
boolean-only probe cannot DERIVE the split and a boolean-only drive cannot
CATCH a serialiser getting it wrong; `boolean-attr-class` had merged the two
classes with every assertion passing.

REPAIR IS THE CLASS, not the attribute: `:overloaded` is now its own class,
and `attr-string` asks the class BEFORE the value. `presence-value-truthy?`
states react-dom's JS truthiness once, total over nil and booleans, spelled
out (no host cast — .cljc, and the render-tree hash compares both runtimes'
bytes). `ui-tree` now reaches it instead of its own near-miss copy, which read
the NUMBER 0 as present and a whitespace string as absent.

prior 144 evidence strings byte-identical):

incomplete in two ways worth recording: a FALSY non-boolean emits nothing at
all, and the overloaded pair (download, capture) keeps the value — which is
what today's `:else` branch already got right and had to keep.

from `hidden`, and the divergence is strictly smaller than the boolean one

attribute being PRESENT when it must be ABSENT. The operative rule is
spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md line 566, the `hidden` probe-corrected row:

THE RESIDUAL IS SHARPER THAN "does not work for the boxed argument". On the JVM
`(not= v v)` is DEAD CODE in this position -- false for EVERY value, not merely
wrong for NaN. clojure.lang.Util/equiv short-circuits on reference identity
before comparing numerically, and a predicate parameter hands ONE boxed object
to both argument positions, so `(= v v)` is true for every value a caller can
supply. Measured with an Object-typed parameter, Clojure 1.12.4, over

rows; `(== v v)` false for exactly the two NaNs; `(NaN? v)` true for exactly
the two NaNs. The idiom IS correct in ClojureScript (`=` on numbers reaches
`identical?`, `NaN === NaN` is false), which is what made it look
cross-platform: right on one runtime, inert on the other, and the JVM is the
runtime that renders server-side.

clojure.core's since 1.11 and cljs.core's, correct for a boxed argument on both
hosts, and self-describing. `==` also discriminates correctly (Numbers/equiv
takes no identity shortcut) but has to be decoded before it reads as a NaN test.

reintroduced. No new abstraction or API; the presence/overloaded split and the
documented ismap divergence are untouched.

title: api(registry): add 5 missing CLJS registrar aliases, pin macro/alias concordance, fix table drift
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref spellings.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.core` emits its 15 `reg-*` registration macros from ONE generator — `defreg-macro` / `defreg-event-macro` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:250` / `:311`), table at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:442-632` — but the Convention-A same-name CLJS value aliases (`#?(:cljs (def reg-x owning/reg-x))`) are a SECOND, hand-written list (`core.cljc:262-352`). The two lists have drifted:

- Aliases exist for 10 of the 15 registrars (`reg-event` :272, `reg-sub` :276, `reg-fx` :280, `reg-cofx` :287, `reg-interceptor` :295, `reg-route` :304, `reg-resource` :315, `reg-resource-scope` :325, `reg-app-schema` :339, `reg-app-schemas` :351). **Missing: `reg-flow`, `reg-mutation`, `reg-head`, `reg-error-projector`, `reg-http-interceptor`.** So on CLJS `(map rf/reg-resource …)` compiles and `(map rf/reg-mutation …)` does not, inside one artefact.
- `spec/Conventions.md:1481-1483` (Convention A) enumerates a DIFFERENT set: it names `reg-flow` (absent in code) and omits `reg-resource` / `reg-resource-scope` (present).
- `spec/API.md` rows four macros as **Fn**: `reg-flow` :108, `reg-resource` :459, `reg-mutation` :461, `reg-resource-scope` :463 — while `spec/api-manifest.edn:147,153,154,155` says `:kind :macro` (and the code is `defreg-macro` at `core.cljc:506/529/543/558`). The spec contradicts its own manifest.

Three more stale lines in the same tables, all true at tip:

- Conventions `*`-pair table (:1466-1469) tables `reg-machine` / `reg-machine*` as a current facade pair. `reg-machine*` left the facade under rf2-wad2fl (`core.cljc:391-394`); its home is `re-frame.machines/reg-machine*`. `spec/005-StateMachines.md` and `API.md:939` already say so.
- Conventions :1586-1587 shows `(rf/clear-flow :flow-id)` / `(rf/clear-flow :flow-id {:frame :session})`; `clear-flow` is `re-frame.flows/clear-flow`, off the facade (`core.cljc:1036-1048`).
- Conventions tear-down roster (:1376) lists six `clear-*` names; the facade carries nine — `clear-resource` (`core.cljc:1501`), `clear-mutation` (:1545), `clear-resource-scope` (:1573) are absent from the roster.

Nothing in the corpus trips on the alias gap today (no value-position `rf/reg-flow` etc. in code — only prose), which is exactly why a hand list drifts unnoticed.

## Evidence (re-run at tip)

```sh
grep -n -E 'defreg-(event-)?macro reg-' implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc     # 15 rows
grep -n -E '^\s+reg-[a-z-]+\s+rf\.' implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc          # 10 aliases (+ the 3 retired reg-event-* stubs at :416-430)
grep -n -E ':var "(reg-flow|reg-resource|reg-mutation|reg-resource-scope)"' spec/api-manifest.edn   # all :kind :macro
sed -n '108p;459p;461p;463p' spec/API.md | cut -c1-40                                 # all "| Fn |"
```

## Target

Codex's "smallest repair" (its cross-check: prefer missing aliases plus a concordance check over a generator unless one declaration can serve both hosts without new build machinery — the generator question is @spellings.3 Q1):

1. **Add the five aliases** to the CLJS block. Delegates are the same late-bind wrappers the macros splice to:
   - `reg-flow` → `rf.core-flows/reg-flow` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_flows.cljc:23`)
   - `reg-mutation` → `rf.core-resources/reg-mutation` (`core_resources.cljc:103`)
   - `reg-head` → `rf.core-ssr/-reg-head` (`core_ssr.cljc:65`)
   - `reg-error-projector` → `rf.core-ssr/-reg-error-projector` (`core_ssr.cljc:40`)
   - `reg-http-interceptor` → `rf.core-http/reg-http-interceptor` (`core_http.cljc:50`)

   Docstrings follow the existing pattern ("Fn-alias of the `reg-x` macro for HoF / programmatic registration (no source-coord capture) …", `core.cljc:267-352`) and say where the implementation ships (`day8/re-frame2-flows` etc., as the `reg-route` / `reg-resource` aliases do).

2. **Pin concordance so the list cannot drift again.** The rule, not a list: every `re-frame.core` `reg-*` macro that does NOT def a Var or walk a literal (`reg-view` :807, `reg-machine` :651, `defmachine` :699 are the only three — none are `defreg-macro` rows) has a same-named CLJS value. Mechanism: the api-manifest CLJS probe (`implementation/scripts/api-manifest/probe/src/re_frame/api_manifest/cljs_probe.cljc`) already reconciles live CLJS publics against manifest rows in the consolidated `:node-test` build; extend it (or add a sibling probe for `re-frame.core`) so that for every `re-frame.core` manifest row with `:kind :macro` whose var starts with `reg-` and is outside `#{reg-view reg-machine defmachine}`, a same-named live CLJS public var exists. EXISTENCE only — the probe's docstring records why `:kind` is not reconciled on CLJS. Negative control in the PR body: remove one alias locally, watch it go red.

3. **Conventions.md** (HOT): replace the enumerated Convention-A list (:1483) with the rule sentence ("every `reg-*` macro that does not def a Var or walk a literal, plus `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` / `subscribe`") and a pointer to the concordance check; the `*` table row for `reg-machine*` names `re-frame.machines` as its home; :1586-1587 → `re-frame.flows/clear-flow`; the tear-down roster lists all nine facade `clear-*` names (or defers to API.md §Clearing registrations). Do NOT touch the reserved-fx-id paragraphs (:474-486 — @spellings.2) or the `clear-*` DESIGN (@spellings.3).

4. **API.md** (HOT): rows :108 / :459 / :461 / :463 `Fn` → `M`.

5. **docs**: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:200` states the Convention-A pattern without a list — confirm; check `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md`, `re-frame.resources.md`, `re-frame.ssr.md`, `re-frame.http.md` for any "value position" sentence that names the alias set.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer (README). Codex's cross-check on this doc: "repair the alias/documentation drift; … fill genuine Convention-A omissions without reopening [the star-twin] work … Prefer the smallest repair — missing aliases plus a concordance check". This bead IS that repair; the generator is left to @spellings.3.

## Deletion list

None (additive). The three retired `reg-event-db/-fx/-ctx` throwing stubs at `core.cljc:416-430` are out of scope.

## Consumers to migrate

None. No value-position use of the five names exists in `examples/`, `tools/`, `testbeds/`, `implementation/**/test` (the gap was latent).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/Conventions.md` (HOT-ZONE), `spec/API.md` (HOT-ZONE) as above.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: run `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/` — expect NO row change: the manifest's `re-frame.core` rows are JVM-derived and the new `def`s are CLJS-only values behind macros that already row as `:macro`.
- Skills: `git grep -n -E 'rf/reg-(flow|mutation|head|error-projector|http-interceptor)' -- skills` in value position → none expected; nothing to change.
- Tests: the probe extension (+ its JVM unit test if the probe has one), `npm run test:cljs` (the consolidated node bundle compiles the five defs).
- Migration README: no v1-era name changes.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches TWO hot-zone files (Conventions.md, API.md). Shares Conventions.md with @spellings.2 and, if ruled, with @spellings.3's implementation bead — the mayor serialises; this one goes first (the others edit adjacent paragraphs). Independent of @spellings.4 and of the testing beads.

## Risks

Low. Additive `def`s of wrappers the macros already delegate to; no change at the macro door; source-coord capture and production elision unchanged (the alias path never captured coords). The only trap is reconciling `:kind` in the probe — do not.

title: bug(machines-viz): SCXML import turns executable-content elements into fake states
description:
## Scope

Correct only the `tools/machines-viz` SCXML import boundary so non-state SCXML children cannot become re-frame2 `:states` entries and `scxml->spec` never returns a structurally invalid machine definition. Preserve the public `spec->scxml` / `scxml->spec` signatures, the supported topology mapping, the existing regex-reader posture, the id codec, and exporter round-trips.

## Correctness finding

`scxml->spec` silently turns ordinary SCXML executable-content elements into fake machine states. `group-children-by-state` says it pairs only `<state>` / `<final>` blocks, but after special-casing `<transition>` its `:self` and `:start` branches accept every tag. `consume-transitions` leaves non-transition elements such as `<onentry>`, `<onexit>`, `<datamodel>`, `<data>`, `<invoke>`, and `<log>` in `:children-tokens`; `parse-state-block` then feeds them to that broad grouper and maps every resulting block through `parse-state-block`. An element with no `id` becomes a state keyed by `nil` (`id-string->abs-path nil` -> `[nil]` -> local key `nil`). Multiple such elements can also overwrite one another in the resulting map.

The import path has no final canonical grammar check. `spec->scxml` validates with `grammar/valid-definition?` at `scxml.cljc:840-863`, and share/AI/Mermaid use the same projectability boundary, but `scxml->spec` returns its assembled map directly at lines 1462-1602. Thus the public importer can report success with a definition that `reg-machine`, `MachineChart`, every sibling emitter, and `grammar/valid-definition?` reject.

## Reproduction

A conforming SCXML 1.0 state may contain `<onentry>`; an empty `<onentry/>` is enough:

```clojure
(def xml
  "<scxml xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2005/07/scxml' version='1.0' initial='idle'><state id='idle'><onentry/></state></scxml>")
(let [spec (scxml/scxml->spec xml)]
  {:spec spec
   :valid? (grammar/valid-definition? spec)
   :defect (grammar/definition-defect spec)})
```

Measured on current HEAD:

```clojure
{:spec {:states {:idle {:states {nil {}}}}, :initial :idle},
 :valid? false,
 :defect {:category :rf.error/machine-compound-state-missing-initial,
          :path [:idle]}}
```

A second measured case with `<onentry><log .../></onentry>` and a real `:go -> :done` transition preserved the transition but returned nested `{nil {:states {nil {}}}}`, proving this is not merely an empty-document edge.

W3C SCXML 1.0 section 3.3 explicitly permits `<onentry>` under `<state>`; the importer advertises interchange with external SCXML tooling and says unsupported executable bodies are lossy. Lossy/ignored is coherent. Inventing an occupiable nil-id state and returning an unusable definition is not.

## Evidence

- `tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/scxml.cljc:1253-1314`: the child grouper's contract names `<state>` / `<final>`, but all non-transition `:self` / `:start` tokens are collected.
- `scxml.cljc:1137-1248`: only direct `<transition>` tokens are consumed/removed; other SCXML child elements remain for the broad grouper.
- `scxml.cljc:1340-1391`: `parse-state-block` derives every block's key from optional `id`, recursively treats grouped blocks as child states, and never checks the tag.
- `scxml.cljc:1462-1602`: `scxml->spec` checks non-string, missing root, unclosed containers, and empty top-level states, but never validates the returned definition.
- The public docstring at lines 1473-1478 says missing required structure throws `:scxml/invalid-spec`; returning invalid structure contradicts that error boundary.
- `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:2200-2231,2343-2354` presents `scxml->spec` as the inverse import and the canonical recursive grammar gate as the invalid-spec boundary.
- `tools/machines-viz/test/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/scxml_cljs_test.cljc` heavily covers emitter-owned round-trips plus non-string/missing-root failures, but contains no `<onentry>`, `<onexit>`, `<datamodel>`, `<invoke>`, or unknown-element import case; emitter output never creates the triggering tokens.
- W3C authority: https://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/#state — `<onentry>` and `<onexit>` are valid `<state>` children.
- History: `git blame` attributes the broad grouper and return shape to the initial SCXML implementation, commit `1403ca5a69e` (2026-05-21). Later grammar and SCXML fixes hardened export, ids, action comments, history, and root-parallel transitions, but no history entry filters imported state children or validates the completed import.

## Impact

A programmer importing a normal external SCXML document can receive a plausible-looking EDN map that is unusable by the library. Failure is displaced to later registration/render/export, where it reports a misleading compound-state error about a state the programmer never authored. This defeats the ergonomic value of the interop seam and is especially hostile to AI/tooling pipelines, which reasonably trust `scxml->spec` success as its postcondition.

## Recommended bounded repair

1. Make the direct-child block collector classify only the tags the re-frame2 importer actually models (`state`, `final`, and `history`). Skip an unsupported self-closing element, and skip an unsupported open element together with its whole subtree so nested markup cannot be promoted accidentally. Continue handling direct transitions through the existing transition consumer.
2. Before returning from `scxml->spec`, validate the assembled definition with the existing `grammar/valid-definition?`. If parser output is not projectable, throw the documented `:scxml/invalid-spec` through the existing error builder with a value-free `grammar/definition-summary`; never return malformed data and never include the raw XML.
3. State the narrow import behavior in API/docs: unsupported executable/datamodel/invoke content is ignored/lossy; it is not reinterpreted as topology.

This is one tag allowlist at the existing collection boundary plus one shared postcondition check, not a new XML framework.

## Posture fit

This removes surprising behavior at a public conversion seam and reuses machinery already present. SPA programmers and agents get a simple law: successful import yields a machine the rest of re-frame2 accepts. No new public options, compatibility modes, AST, schema system, or abstraction is needed.

## Non-goals

- No execution or round-trip support for SCXML `<onentry>`, `<onexit>`, `<script>`, `<assign>`, `<log>`, `<datamodel>`, `<invoke>`, or other executable/data-model constructs.
- No replacement of the deliberately small regex reader with a full XML/SCXML processor.
- No expansion to XState JSON/Stately formats, nested-parallel semantics, or arbitrary namespace handling.
- No W3C omitted-`initial` defaulting or `<initial>`-element implementation in this task; preserve the currently documented requirement/rejection rather than broadening this repair.
- No change to export syntax, id encoding, action-comment lifting, or supported round-trip equality.

## Related / duplicate search

Tracked `.beads/issues.jsonl` searches for `SCXML default initial`, `SCXML first child`, `SCXML <initial>`, `group-children-by-state`, `fake/bogus nil state`, `non-state child`, `unknown XML element`, `SCXML onentry`, and `SCXML datamodel` found no relevant bead; no current issue title contains `SCXML`. Closed `rf2-sxw06` is the distinct one-click Mermaid workflow and closed `rf2-x19xi` is stale ELK arbitration. Historical SCXML commits (`rf2-mnp93.*`, `rf2-qgtcvy`, `rf2-j538f7.18`) address id/action/export/grammar issues, not this import classification.

## Uncertainty

The parser explicitly promises best-effort behavior for unsupported XML, so either ignore or a controlled parse error could be defensible for some foreign tags. The hard invariant is not ambiguous: success must never invent topology or return a definition the canonical grammar rejects. Ignoring standard executable/data-model children best matches the existing lossy contract and preserves useful topology import.

- A JVM+CLJS regression imports the conforming `<scxml ...><state id='idle'><onentry/></state></scxml>` fixture and produces no nil/phantom state; the returned definition passes `grammar/valid-definition?`.

- An unsupported element containing a nested `<state>` does not promote that nested element into the parent's re-frame2 `:states`; only direct recognized state/history children are collected.
- Every successful `scxml->spec` result passes the canonical recursive grammar gate. Parser output that cannot be represented as a valid re-frame2 definition throws `:scxml/invalid-spec` with a value-free definition summary and no raw XML/content.
- Existing flat/compound/parallel/history/action/reenter/id-codec round-trips remain byte/value-equivalent, and malformed-root/unclosed-input error ids remain unchanged.
- Negative control: restoring the current catch-all self/start branches makes the new onentry fixture produce a nil-key state and fail the validity assertion.
- API/ns prose accurately describes unsupported SCXML child content as lossy/ignored and does not imply executable semantics were added.

THE RECORDED RULE, which is in the method doc's gate-mechanics block and which I brief constantly: run a search twice, once line-oriented and once over the text with whitespace collapsed, because neither result is a superset of the other.

title: ssr-node: two remaining error-text paths onto public refusals — pool.cjs ISOLATE_LOST boot diagnostics, service.cjs last-resort String(error)
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 from the ssrnode-b worker's report on PR #9278 (rf2-c38b, merged 5e7acf5a4e). Both were found while closing the exception-door leak, both were judged outside that bead's non-goals fence, and both were reported rather than changed. That judgement was right; this bead is the ruling they need.

THE TWO SITES. Verify each at tip — these are the worker's claims, and line numbers move.

1. src/pool.cjs:178 interpolates err.message into an ISOLATE_LOST refusal handed to WAITING CALLERS when a REPLACEMENT isolate fails to boot. So boot diagnostics reach a caller at runtime. rf2-c38b's non-goals fenced boot off, which is why it was left.

2. src/service.cjs:108 puts String(error) on a public refusal in a last-resort arm. The worker judged this NOT worth changing and gave a reason worth preserving: it is unreachable today (every isolate.render() path rejects with a Refusal) and would carry only THIS PACKAGE's own error text, unlike the analogous worker.cjs arm that PR #9258 hardened, which is application-adjacent.

WHY THIS IS ONE BEAD AND NOT TWO. They differ on both axes that decide the answer — reachability and whose text they carry — and ruling them together is what makes the boundary legible. The question is not "is any error text on a refusal bad" but "which side of the trust boundary authored it, and can a caller reach it". A ruling that answers only site 1 leaves the next reader re-litigating site 2 from scratch.

THE RULING NEEDED, and the stance bears on it directly. Under 'trust the programmer' and 'don't litigate the minutiae', an unreachable last-resort arm carrying the package's own text may simply be correct as written, and a bead can die with its reasoning recorded instead of consuming a worker. Under 'fail closed' and the response-egress law the package states in its own README, a refusal that can carry ANY interpolated text is a door that will be walked through eventually. Both readings are honest. Pick one per site, with the reason, and if the answer is 'leave it', say so ON the code so the next audit does not re-raise it.

WHAT WOULD MAKE SITE 1 ACTIONABLE WITHOUT A RULING, if a worker takes this: the same shape rf2-c38b landed — the diagnostic goes to the sidecar's own stderr where the operator running it can see it, and the public refusal carries the closed-taxonomy code and a fixed message. If that shape applies cleanly to pool.cjs, this is implementation rather than a decision, and the ruling is only needed for site 2.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: this brief's premises are the worker's claims. Confirm site 2 is genuinely unreachable today (the worker's basis was that every isolate.render() path rejects with a Refusal — prove it with a control, not a bare grep), and confirm site 1's refusal really does reach waiting callers rather than only the log.

FENCE if dispatched: implementation/ssr-node/** only. spec/Conventions.md catalogues the :rf.ssr-node/* code MEMBERS and is hot-zone — if a member changes, that is a separate sequenced edit, not part of this.

THE jq CRLF DEFECT HAS A THIRD DOOR: A SET COMPARISON BETWEEN A jq-PRODUCED FILE AND A NON-jq-PRODUCED ONE. Measured 2026-09-05 18:0x AUSEST by the mayor, on its own §3 backlog reread.

WHAT IS ALREADY RECORDED (CLAUDE.md, instruments item (e)): jq-1.8.1 on this box writes CRLF, so a pattern JOINED from `jq -r` output matches nothing but its last alternative, and a grep pattern file built that way misbehaves. Both recorded doors are about PATTERNS.

THE THIRD DOOR IS `comm`, `join`, `diff`, or any line-keyed set operation. I built the in_progress bead list with `jq -r ... | sort` and the held-by-worktree list with `git worktree list | ... | awk | sort`, then ran `comm -23`. It reported ALL SEVEN in_progress beads as orphans with no live worktree — which, if believed, is the stranded-worker signature whose remedy is to reopen and redispatch every one of them.

The two lists were VISUALLY IDENTICAL on screen. The difference was invisible: `od -c` showed the jq side ending `\r \n` and the awk side ending `\n`, so every key differed by one byte and comm correctly reported two disjoint sets.

WHY THIS DOOR IS WORTH ITS OWN NOTE. The recorded doors fail toward a FALSE ALL-CLEAR (a search reads zero). This one failed toward a FALSE ALARM, which is the more visible direction and is how it got caught. BUT THE MIRROR CASE IS SILENT: `comm -13` or an intersection keyed the same way would report "nothing in common" or drop a real member, and a set comparison that returns a plausible-looking subset raises nothing. The direction of failure depends on which side of the comparison jq is on, so neither direction can be trusted.

THE TELL AND THE FIX. The tell is a set operation reporting NO OVERLAP AT ALL between two lists that visibly share members — total disjointness is almost never the real answer. The fix is one of:
  - `tr -d '\r'` between jq and any file destined for a line-keyed operation;
  - keep BOTH sides in jq (a jq-to-jq comparison is self-consistent and gets the right answer, which is why this hides);
  - or do the comparison inside jq itself.
And CONTROL IT: append a needle you know is unique to one side and confirm the operation reports it. My control was `rf2-FAKE` spliced into one list, which comm correctly returned — proving the instrument works once the line endings agree, and that the seven-orphan reading was an artefact.

THE GENERAL RULE THIS BELONGS TO, which is already in the gate-mechanics block and keeps earning its place: ANY instrument that can answer "nothing here" gives the same answer when misused, and a misused one raises no error. Exercise it once against an input it should flag. That applies to set operations exactly as it applies to searches.

That is FALSE for a job added to a workflow that no pull request runs. Clause 5's general instruction gestures at the right idea, but the ENUMERATED BULLET A READER LANDS ON gives the wrong verdict, and an enumerated example beats a general instruction every time — which is exactly why this needs fixing rather than leaving to the general text.

Clause 5 currently enumerates THREE cases (cache steps / job-name addition / display-name rename). This is a FOURTH it does not carry: a job key added to a workflow whose `on:` block has no `pull_request` trigger contributes NO check to any PR rollup, so the check set is unchanged and the merge should proceed.

The claudemd-a worker added a further measurement worth carrying over: SEVEN OF THE ELEVEN workflow files in this repo carry no `pull_request` trigger at all, so this is the common case rather than an exotic one.

DIRECTION MATTERS AND MUST BE STATED. This case fails CLOSED — it flags a merge that should proceed — whereas the traps CLAUDE.md enumerates all fail OPEN. That asymmetry is why the CLAUDE.md fix was written as a QUALIFICATION to trap (a) rather than a fourth trap: adding it as a peer would have falsified that bullet's framing sentence ("each fails OPEN"). names both the count and the file, after which you read that file's `on:` block.

A BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA CAN BE A CLAIM TOO, AND EXECUTING ONE AS WRITTEN CAN CREATE THE DEFECT IT DESCRIBES. Measured 2026-09-05 on rf2-kuky.28 (PR #9301, hicdoc-a worker).

WHAT HAPPENED. The bead said a sentence appearing across several files — that `flush-views!` no-ops — was FALSE and should be rewritten. Its first acceptance criterion directed exactly that rewrite. The worker checked at source and found the phrase is TRUE at six of those sites, so obeying the criterion would have turned five true statements false and shipped the defect the bead was filed to remove.

THE MECHANISM, verified independently by the mayor at implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs: THERE ARE TWO SPINES, not one. `make-react-spine` (:2750) and `make-ratom-spine` (:3643). The shared `flush-views!` at :1908-1916 is `(when-let [act (resolve-act-fn)] (act f))` — so when `act` is absent it NO-OPS and `f` never runs. The ratom spine takes the other branch at :3880, `(if flush-render-op (flush-render-op f) (f))` — so `f` RUNS and the queue drains. Both Reagent adapters bind the ratom spine and inject a `:flush-render!` op; only uix takes the react spine. The file's own comment at :3873 says it outright: "unlike the React-hook spine `flush-views!`, which no-ops".

So the sentence is true for the uix path and false for the Reagent path, and a bead written from one path's evidence generalised it to all of them.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is one level up from the recorded brief-premises rule. The method doc already says a BRIEF's premises are claims to check at source. This says the same of the BEAD's acceptance criteria — including criteria the mayor did not write. A worker that treats acceptance criteria as instructions rather than claims will execute a wrong one faithfully, and the resulting PR looks correct: it satisfies every stated criterion.

THE TELL: a criterion that says "this phrase is false, rewrite it" over MULTIPLE FILES. One wrong site is a defect; the same phrase at six sites is more likely a distinction the bead missed. Count the sites and check whether they share a code path before rewriting any of them.

WHAT A WORKER SHOULD DO, and what this one did: refute the criterion with evidence, DO the part that survives (here, exactly one of the three unnamed docstrings was genuinely wrong — the one whose sole caller is the React-hook spine), and flag the criterion as one to STRIKE rather than silently ignoring it. That is a complete deliverable, not a partial one.

AND IT ARGUES FOR THE PATHSPEC WIDENING that found it: the bead's own acceptance pathspec did not reach implementation/core/test/ at all, so the single genuinely-wrong docstring would have survived a green acceptance. A criterion can be wrong AND its scope too narrow at the same time.

DEFECT 1 — spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159 describes a REMOVED surface in the present tense.

The :rf.error/frame-destroyed catalogue row narrates the retired implementation/ui (frame) operation bundle as a live throwing surface. Verbatim, at tip: "A substrate's (frame) operation bundle (rf2-vxgfnd.230) is a further throwing surface for the SAME category ... The incarnation fence emits at the ui source BEFORE delegating to core's dispatch/subscribe, so the same failure is never ALSO fanned by the router/subs recover-and-emit path ... all four bundle arms route through one ui-frame emit-and-throw helper so their two-channel contract cannot drift."

implementation/ui was RETIRED AND REMOVED (rf2-0yp7w, executed by PR #8322 on 2026-08-16); git ls-files returns nothing under it. So there is no ui source emitting anything, no incarnation fence, and no four bundle arms. A reader takes this row as a description of live behaviour because every verb in it is present tense.

SCOPE AGAINST #9179, and this is the part to get right: #9179 removes the :capture enum value and the clauses that attribute it to the ui surface. IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE REST OF THE PASSAGE. So do not read a merged #9179 as having fixed this — check what survives, then decide per sentence whether it is (a) live behaviour that outlived the ui and should be re-attributed to router/subs, (b) retirement bookkeeping that should be past-tensed and dated to rf2-0yp7w, or (c) a claim about a surface that no longer exists and describes nothing, which is rf2-63t1i's rule and the ground #9179 stood on.

CLAUDE.md's Architecture Overview is the governing distinction: a donor reference is either retirement bookkeeping or the reserved-kind contract, and is never a surface to build on. Neither exemption obviously covers a present-tense operational narration, but read both before deleting anything.

DEFECT 2 — the tree contradicts itself on whether :op is PUBLIC or PRIVATE.

  spec/Spec-Schemas.md:1201            ";; enum ratified PUBLIC on this category (per the 009 catalogue row)"
  spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2159     ":op (the failing operation realm ... a small closed-enum public realm attribution"
  implementation/core/test/re_frame/on_error_cljs_test.cljc:823
                                       ";; PRIVATE steering input (read from the record's attribution, never promoted to"

Two normative documents say PUBLIC; a test header says PRIVATE and never-promoted. One of the three is wrong. This matters beyond tidiness because :op's publicness is what licenses consumers to switch on it, and a test header is exactly where an implementer looks to learn whether a slot is contractual.

DETERMINE WHICH IS AUTHORITATIVE RATHER THAN HARMONISING THE WORDING. The spec is the artefact and the code is downstream, so the presumption is that the two spec documents govern and the test header is stale — but check whether the header is describing something narrower and true (:op as a steering input to error-source-coord's realm-exact resolution, which IS an internal use) that has merely been worded as a global claim. If so the fix is to narrow the header, not to invert it.

FENCE — DO NOT DISPATCH UNTIL PR #9179 MERGES. Both spec/Spec-Schemas.md and spec/009-Instrumentation.md are HOT ZONE and #9179 edits BOTH in one commit. The hazard is the stale-copy revert: a branch cut before #9179 lands silently undoes its :capture removal while passing every gate, because a revert of a merged change is well-formed and every checker reads it as clean. RE-READ BOTH FILES AT TIP AFTER IT MERGES; the line numbers above will have moved.

GATES. Run them for the 009 prose row, but hand-check the fenced block and the row's pipe count (7, matching its siblings) and say so in the PR body. mkdocs is not on PATH here; use python -m mkdocs.

title: TRUNK RED: compile-node-test zero-warning gate fails on two :uix.linter/interop-ref-read warnings from 570d07d286
description:
TRUNK IS RED. Reported INDEPENDENTLY by two workers within an hour on 2026-09-05, on files byte-identical to origin/main, and confirmed by the mayor at source.

THE FAILURE. `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` exits 1 on two `:uix.linter/interop-ref-read` warnings under a zero-warning gate:
  implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120
  implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:139
Both are `(.-current ref)` inside a `uix/use-effect` body. The linter's message: "use-ref hook in UIx returns Atom-like ref, use `@` instead of `.-current`".

IT IS THE COMPILE STEP, NOT THE TEST STEP. The node test step is GREEN. That distinction matters because it is why this was not caught at merge and why it presents confusingly: the tests pass, the compile that produces them does not.

PROVENANCE, established at source: commit `570d07d286` (2026-09-05 14:14:05 +1000, "fix(uix): the imperative effect recipe follows its frame (rf2-tug6)") added the 251-line test file carrying both reads. It IS an ancestor of origin/main. Both reporting workers confirmed the file is byte-identical to origin/main in their branches, so this is trunk state and not any worker's diff.

BLAST RADIUS. This reds `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` and `npm run test:cljs` LOCALLY for any diff. In CI the `cljs_node_test` job is surface-gated by the classifier, so a PR that does not arm the CLJS surface gets it SKIPPED — and a skip counts as passed in the rollup, which is exactly why PRs kept merging green all afternoon while this sat on main. A PR that DOES arm the surface will red on it, through no fault of its own.

WHY P1: multiple workers are live on CLJS surfaces right now, every one of them will hit this, and each will spend time establishing that it is not their fault. Two already have. The fix is two lines.

THE FIX, on the merits. The linter is telling the truth: UIx's `use-ref` returns an atom-like ref, so `@ref` is the idiomatic read and `.-current` is interop reaching through the abstraction. Change both reads. BUT VERIFY THE SEMANTICS BEFORE CHANGING THEM — read UIx's own `use-ref` implementation and confirm `@` and `.-current` return the same thing here, because these two sites read a DOM node out of the ref inside an effect body, and a test that silently starts reading something else would be worse than the warning. If they are not equivalent at these sites, say so and STOP: that would make this a real defect in `570d07d286` rather than a lint.

CHECK WHETHER OTHER SITES CARRY THE SAME PATTERN. Two token axes, line-oriented AND whitespace-collapsed, with a control that shares the target's shape. If the same read appears elsewhere under the UIx adapter and is NOT flagged, establish why before assuming the gate is inconsistent — the linter may be scoped to hook bodies.

DO NOT SUPPRESS THE WARNING. Adding an ignore, lowering the gate, or excluding the file are all wrong: the zero-warning gate is the thing that caught a real idiom violation within hours of it landing, which is the gate working.

ACCEPTANCE: `node implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` (or whatever the real entry point is — read it) exits 0 on the tree, and the node test step still reports its full count with zero failures. Quote both captured exit codes and both counts. Confirm the tests still assert what they asserted: a green suite after changing what a test READS is not evidence unless the counts hold and a fault plant still bites.
