title: dispatch-prompt-template: the two-axis search rule needs a third comment-stripped axis — measured zero on both existing axes
description:
The gate-mechanics block in docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md tells every worker to run a search on TWO axes:

  "Run the search twice — once line-oriented, once over the text with whitespace collapsed — because neither result is a superset of the other."

MEASURED 2026-09-05 (schemas-a worker, rf2-fxp5 / PR #9295): TWO AXES ARE NOT ENOUGH, and the case that defeats them is common in this repo rather than exotic.

Searching spec/Spec-Schemas.md for the phrase "FOUR live emitters" returned ZERO on the line-oriented axis AND ZERO on the whitespace-collapsed axis. The phrase breaks across lines, and the continuation line carries a ';;' comment prefix that SURVIVES a plain flatten — the flattened text reads "...the FOUR ;; live emitters..." and matches nothing. Only stripping comment markers and THEN flattening found it, and that third pass also surfaced a second stale site the first two had missed.

The control was shape-matched rather than convenient, which is what makes the measurement stand: a positive control equally line-broken and equally comment-prefixed read line=0 / flat=0 / flat+decomment=1; a negative control read 0 throughout.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CORNER. It bites any census over COMMENTED CODE or a FENCED SCHEMA SAMPLE. spec/Spec-Schemas.md is the worst case because its schemas carry heavy ';;' commentary inside fences, but every Clojure docstring and comment block has the same shape — and prose/comment correction is what a large share of this repo's beads actually are. On the SAME DAY, a sibling worker on the same bead family missed a fifth site on a different axis (it spelled the term 'UI-bundle' rather than '(frame)-bundle', reachable only once flattened). Two adjacent misses in one day on one bead family is the argument.

THE EDIT: extend that paragraph to THREE passes — line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed, and comment-markers-stripped-then-collapsed — and extend the control rule alongside it, because the two move together: the control must share the target's SHAPE ON EVERY AXIS BEING CLAIMED (line-broken if the target is line-broken, comment-prefixed if the target is comment-prefixed). A single-clean-line control proves nothing about any of the three, and the existing text already makes the shape-sharing argument for the punctuation and backslash cases — this is the same argument reaching one level further.

KEEP THE EXISTING PARAGRAPH'S STRUCTURE AND ITS MEASUREMENTS. It already records that a census found one site line-oriented and missed four line-broken ones, then found those four flattened and missed the first. Do not replace that; the new axis is an addition to the same finding, and the paragraph's closing point — that wrapped text is the common case, not the exotic one — is strengthened rather than changed.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: this brief's premises are claims. Re-read the paragraph at tip (it sits in the gate-mechanics block, under the sentence beginning "A search that returns ZERO is not a check that passed"), and confirm the two-axis wording is still as quoted — that block was edited on 2026-09-05 by PR #9274 and may move again.

CONSIDER, and say which you chose: whether the third axis belongs as a third named pass in the same sentence, or as a short following sentence scoped to commented code. The block is already long and its length is a known cost; the stance's "don't litigate the minutiae" argues for the shortest form that survives a worker skimming it.

FENCE. IN: docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md ONLY.
OUT: docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md (a separate bead, rf2-n7tb, owns a clause-5 correction there), CLAUDE.md (its instruments bullet was edited today by PR #9283 and carries the related grep-alternation item as (e) — do not duplicate this there), and every spec/ and implementation/ path.
notes:
2026-09-05 (tmplaxis-a worker) — PR #9302 opened, ready for review, one file, +17/-9. NOT closed; close when it is on main.

PREMISES CHECKED AT TIP, ALL HELD. The two-axis wording was verbatim as the description quotes it, at docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md:1080-1082 pre-edit (post-edit the paragraph runs 1077-1096). History walk: 45 snapshots, 2026-09-05 17:42:45 to 18:25:12, and NOT ONE field varies across them — description hash f4cfc845 constant, notes/acceptance_criteria/design absent (empty on this item), no comments, no children. So the walk found NOTHING rather than 'no change', and there is no control field on this item to walk against; what makes it safe is that the oldest snapshot IS the creation snapshot, so the description is both the oldest and the newest text. The 45 entries are checkpoint no-ops.

FORM CHOSEN: the third pass is named INSIDE the existing bolded imperative sentence ('Run the search three times — once line-oriented, once over the text with whitespace collapsed, and once with comment markers stripped before collapsing'), NOT as a following sentence scoped to commented code. Reason: the bold sentence is what survives a skim, so leaving it reading 'twice' while a later sentence said three would put a contradiction inside one paragraph, and a skimmer resolves that in favour of the bold text. The measurement is one short following sentence. Net +17/-9 on a block whose length is a known cost.

ACCURACY REPAIR MADE DELIBERATELY: the original clause read 'because neither result is a superset of the other', which cannot be extended to three passes as written — stripping comment markers then collapsing is very nearly a superset of collapsing alone. The claim is now split and both halves are true: 'Neither of the first two is a superset of the other, and the third reaches what neither can.'

CONTROL RULE EXTENDED alongside it, in the preceding paragraph: the feature list gains 'or sits behind a comment marker', plus the conjunction point — the control must carry EVERY one of those features the target has, AT ONCE, because a control that matches on the axis it shares says nothing about the axis it does not. That is the same argument the block already makes for punctuation and backslashes, reaching one level further.

STRUCTURE AND MEASUREMENTS KEPT: 'Measured four times in one session' and its four enumerated instances are unchanged; the new measurement is from a different session and is NOT folded into that count. The closing 'Wrapped text is the common case, not the exotic one' is kept and strengthened ('every commented block and fenced sample puts a marker at the break').

  python scripts/check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose exit 0 — reads prose repo-wide at permitted count ZERO, so it genuinely grades this diff; proved by planted fault

TWO PLANTED FAULTS, BOTH BIT, both applied through the editor rather than the shell, both match-counted before the run, both restored and verified by git BLOB hash ea8d53a3918a6c846aae6951478df50f2b0bd4ef (identical to the committed object). Edits were committed BEFORE any plant so the 'git checkout HEAD --' restore could not discard the work under test.
  (1) check_doc_slugs.py: broken in-page anchor, 0 -> 1 matches, gate exit 1 naming file:1097 and the anchor. The plant existed only in this worktree, so a run that had wandered into a sibling's checkout would have come back green.
  (2) check_view_lifetime_residue.py: one banned-stem token, counted with the GATE'S OWN REGEX before and after (0 -> 1) rather than with a plain grep — worth recording, because a plain 'grep -ci' reads 1 on the UNTOUCHED file: the tree already contains the survivor word 'released', which the gate's (?<!re) lookbehind excludes. A worker who match-counted with grep would have read that 1 as its own plant landing and, on restore, as a plant that never cleared. Gate exit 1 naming file, line and the planted text.

HAND CHECKS (nothing validates prose, tables or rendering): both edited paragraphs still read as ONE paragraph each (blank lines at 1076 and 1097 only); count words match their items — 'three times' vs three named passes, 'Neither of the first two' vs two, 'four times in one session' vs the four existing instances; fence toggles even and UNCHANGED at 4 (the two text blocks at 756/812 and 821/902); no links or headings added, so no new anchors and no nav change.

A CENSUS THAT DEMONSTRATES ITS OWN RULE: swept the tracked tree on all three axes for duplicate copies of the paragraph. Only this file and the .beads export carry it. The needle 'neither result is a superset of the other' read line=4 / flat=6 — and the single hit in this file is INVISIBLE line-oriented, because it spans lines 1081->1082. The rule the block already carried is live in the block itself.

BRIEF PREMISE THAT DID NOT HOLD (reported, not acted on): the dispatch brief stated 'the gate-mechanics block is largely fenced (it is a pasteable deliverable)'. It is not. The file carries exactly FOUR fence markers, at 756/812 and 821/902 — the common preamble and the worktree boundary block — and NONE in the gate-mechanics region (958 onward). So check_doc_slugs.py's FENCED_DOC_LINK_TREES coverage of this tree, while real, was not exercised by this diff: the region is ordinary prose and any link in it is graded the ordinary way. Nothing in the edit depended on the claim.

FENCE HELD: one file. loops.md, CLAUDE.md, spec/*, implementation/* and .beads/** untouched by the commit. Kept out of CLAUDE.md's territory deliberately — its instruments bullet carries the related grep item as (e) (a jq/CRLF alternation defect in a specific toolchain); this finding is a different mechanism and is written tool-agnostically, naming no tool, flag or shell, matching the surrounding block. Per loops.md:10-16, CLAUDE.md is the CLI concretion and the method doc the generic body.

Either way no public surface changes.

## (b) Two adapter docstrings describe a fallback the shared spine does not have

`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:121-130` says "Calls (act (fn [] (reagent.core/flush))) … When act() is unreachable in the current React build it degrades to a plain synchronous flush (still runs `f` and drains the render queue)"; `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:58-70` says the same with `(batching/flush!)`. The uix docstring (`uix.cljs:173-181`) is correct — use its wording for both. `git grep -n 'degrades to a plain synchronous flush' -- docs spec implementation` to catch any doc copy.

## (c) reagent-slim's second `flush-views!` — write the discriminator on both sides, no rename

`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:153-180` is a second `flush-views!`: Promise return, 3-phase microtask/act/microtask drain, `goog.DEBUG`-gated, and it DOES carry the "degrade to a plain synchronous flush" branch the adapter docstrings were describing. The pointer runs one way: the client docstring does not name the adapter's converged nil-returning twin. Recorded for another area, NOT actioned here: `spec/008-Testing.md:1013` still teaches `subscribe-once` (extant, `subs.cljc:1817`) as the canonical read-then-discard primitive beside `compute-sub`; wave 1's rf2-ihkk6l ruled it RETAINED, so the sentence is not wrong, but the state-reads area owns its wording.

ASKING WHICH WORKER HOLDS A HOT FILE HAS TWO WRONG INSTRUMENTS, AND THEY FAIL IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS (measured 2026-09-05, five live worktrees).

THE DELIVERABLE is the fence question from loops.md S3: which of the hot-zone files (spec/009, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md, spec/Spec-Schemas.md, spec/006, spec/Tool-Pair.md ...) is currently held by a live worker, so a bead touching it stays sequenced rather than dispatched.

WRONG INSTRUMENT 1 - ASKING THE OPEN PRS. 'gh pr list --json files' enumerates only workers that have OPENED a PR. A worker mid-task has a worktree and commits but no PR, so it holds nothing visible. Measured: spec/009-Instrumentation.md read FREE by the PR sweep while devcon-a was actively editing it on worker/devcon-a. This UNDER-reports, and it fails OPEN - the reassuring answer is the wrong one, and dispatching on it manufactures the conflict the fence exists to prevent. ENUMERATE FROM 'git worktree list', not from PRs. (Same shape as the loops.md S4 instruction to start the stranded sweep from the WORKTREE list rather than the in_progress list - one door, two loops.)

WRONG INSTRUMENT 2 - TWO-DOT DIFF AGAINST origin/main. Having switched to worktrees, the natural query is 'git -C $w diff origin/main --name-only'. Two-dot reports files differing in EITHER direction, so for a branch whose base is stale it lists everything MAIN changed since the fork as well as what the WORKER changed. Measured on testfix-a: two-dot named 6 spec files, three-dot named 1. Four of the five extras (spec/006, spec/API.md, spec/Conventions.md, spec/Spec-Schemas.md) were trunk movement, not worker edits. This OVER-reports, holding four hot slots against nobody - it fails CLOSED, so it costs throughput rather than correctness, but it is the harder one to notice because a fence that is merely too tight never produces a symptom.

THE CORRECT READ combines both fixes and adds uncommitted work, since a worker mid-edit may not have committed yet:

  git worktree list | grep re-frame2-worktrees | awk '{print $1}' | while read -r w; do
    { git -C "$w" status --porcelain | awk '{print $2}'
      git -C "$w" diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only; } | tr -d '\r' | sort -u
  done

The 'tr -d $'\r'' is not decoration - see the jq/CRLF family; git is clean here but the pipeline is often joined with jq output.

CONTROL THAT DISCRIMINATES: run two-dot and three-dot on the same worktree and compare counts. Equal counts mean the branch is current and the two instruments agree by luck; differing counts localise the staleness to that worktree and tell you the two-dot answer was inflated. A single instrument agreeing with itself proves nothing.

THE SITE: implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:61 carries `(.-current ref)` inside the canonical imperative-effect recipe — the SAME expression, in the SAME shape, that rf2-8crk just fixed at implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120 and :139.

WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE REDDING NOTHING. Markdown is never compiled, so no gate touches it and it will sit there indefinitely. But it is the SOURCE THE NEXT TRANSCRIPTION COPIES: rf2-8crk's own trunk-red arrived exactly that way — commit 570d07d286 added a 251-line test transcribing this recipe, and the two `.-current` reads came with it, redding the zero-warning compile gate for EVERY CLJS diff in the repo until the fix landed. Leaving the README as-is means the next person who follows the documented recipe re-creates the same repo-wide red.

THE FIX IS THE IDIOM, AND ITS EQUIVALENCE IS ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE rather than assumed — the rf2-8crk worker read com.pitch/uix.core 1.4.4's uix/core.cljs and found `use-ref` returns `(specify! #js {:current value} IDeref (-deref [this] (.-current this)) ...)`. So `-deref` IS `(.-current this)`: same property, same object, no coercion. That object is also what `($ :div {:ref ref})` hands React, so React writes the DOM node into the very `.current` both forms read. `@ref` and `(.-current ref)` are therefore interchangeable AT THESE SITES, and the linter's preference is idiom rather than correctness.

SO THIS IS A ONE-EXPRESSION PROSE FIX, and its value is preventing a recurrence rather than fixing a defect. Change the recipe to `@ref` and, if the surrounding prose explains the ref read, make the explanation match. Nothing else.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING — these are the worker's claims and mine, not findings:
- Re-derive the line number; :61 was measured before #9293 merged.
- Confirm the expression is inside the recipe rather than in a passage deliberately contrasting the two forms. If the README is teaching the interop read on purpose, the right answer may be to keep it and ADD the linter's preference — say so rather than silently rewriting a deliberate contrast.
- Run the census on all three axes (line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed, comment-markers-stripped-then-collapsed) with a control sharing the target's shape. The rf2-8crk census found 3 `.-current` under the UIx adapter — the two fixed sites plus this README — and 18 more repo-wide, none flagged. Confirm that at tip: if another README or doc under a DIFFERENT adapter carries the same recipe, it has the same problem and belongs in this bead.

WHY THE LINTER DOES NOT CATCH THE OTHER 18, established by the same worker and worth not re-deriving: `interop-ref-read?` requires the target's LOCAL BINDING INIT FORM to be a `use-ref` call, and `lint-body!` is reached only via `uix.linter/lint!`, which `uix.core` calls from `defui` / `uix.core/fn` alone. So the gate is scoped to UIx component bodies by construction — it is not inconsistent, and no ratchet needs adjusting.

FENCE. IN: `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md`, plus any sibling adapter README the census proves carries the identical recipe.
OUT: `implementation/adapters/uix/test/**` (rf2-8crk owns the test fix), `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` and every linter or gate configuration (the gate is correct — it caught a real idiom violation within hours), and all of `spec/`.

GATE: `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the gate for a README beside source — NOT `check_doc_slugs.py`, whose roots exclude it, so nominating that one returns a green that inspected nothing. Neither reads inside a fenced code block, and this edit is almost certainly INSIDE a fence, so BOTH are blind to it: check any link or anchor in the block by hand and say so. The real verification here is reading the recipe against uix.core's `use-ref` and confirming the replacement compiles in the adapter's own testbed.
notes:
2026-09-05 — PR #9303 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9303), branch worker/uixdoc-a, left in_progress.

PREMISE HELD. Line number re-derived at tip: still :61 (the file is 87 lines; #9293 touches only test/, so the README did not move).

JUDGEMENT CALL — RECIPE, not a deliberate contrast. Decided on three grounds: (1) the README mentions @ref / deref / the atom-like nature of use-ref NOWHERE, and a contrast needs both forms present — repo-wide, @ref appears in ZERO markdown files; (2) the '4 things matter' list under the block teaches four points (frame api via hook, mandatory cleanup, deps vector, no use-subscribe in the effect body), none about the ref read, so the read is incidental mechanism; (3) it was in fact transcribed verbatim into a test, which is what a recipe is for. Fixed to @ref plus ONE clause of inline comment in the block's own existing trailing-;; idiom (lines 58 and 66 already carry such comments) so the next reader does not revert it — flagged in the PR as one line beyond the bead's 'nothing else', trim if unwanted.

EQUIVALENCE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE from the pinned jar (com.pitch/uix.core 1.4.4, uix/core.cljs:104-131), not taken on the bead's word: use-ref returns the specify!'d #js {:current value} object itself and its IDeref -deref IS (.-current this). Same property, same object, no coercion; that object is also what ($ :div {:ref ref}) hands React. uix/linter.clj:283's own error message names the wanted spelling: 'use @ instead of .-current'. Empirical: #9293 makes the identical change in the identical shape at the two transcribed sites and carries CLJS :node-test and :browser-test SUCCESS — so @ref compiles clean and introduces no missing-deps warning with the deps vector unchanged.

CENSUS, three axes with two shape-sharing controls that each bite (line-broken interop form: 0 line / 1 flat; phrase spanning a ;; continuation: 0 line / 0 flat / 1 stripped). '.-current' = 65 matching lines across 19 files line-oriented, 81 occurrences flattened and marker-stripped. Under implementation/adapters/ it occurs in exactly TWO files: this README (1) and the uix_effect_frame_deps test (2, #9293's, untouched). Markdown-wide only two files carry it repo-wide — this README and docs/design/freehand/fable-design.md, whose single hit is (.-currentTarget e), a different DOM property in the retired-freehand design tree.

NO SIBLING README BELONGS IN THIS BEAD. All four sibling adapter READMEs (implementation/adapters/README.md, reagent/, reagent-slim/, test-react/) carry zero .-current. The only other markdown carrying use-ref is migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md, whose two hits are prose about the Form-2-closure to hook substitution and the placement rule — no ref read, no recipe.

GATES, foreground, exit captured on the same command line as the redirect, re-run on the final rebased base d3e7052b26: check_readme_links.py --ci = 0; check_require_alias_dialect.py --verbose = 0 (import edges only — honest but UNINFORMATIVE, a markdown-only diff cannot move it); check_view_lifetime_residue.py --verbose = 0 (reads prose, so it does grade the added comment). Nine further ratchets that could grade a README under implementation/adapters/ or scan prose repo-wide all 0: readme_inventories, adapter_disposition, retired_spellings, retired_composition_vocab, retired_image_keys, inject_cofx_residue, allocation_non_claim, failure_corpus_residue, runtime_subsystem_grading. check_doc_slugs.py deliberately NOT nominated — its roots exclude implementation/.

GATE PROVED BY PLANTED FAULT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (it prints no root). Prose plant, broken link on line 9: exit 1 naming implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:9 and the planted target — the fault existed only in this worktree, so that red is what proves the gate read this tree and that this file is in its roster. In-fence plant, same class of broken link on line 57: exit 0, silent — confirming both link gates strip fences and are blind to the region actually edited. Both plants made from a committed tree, anchor match count read as 1 before each run, restored and verified by git BLOB hash 06f4c99cad27ac95aedceebcfa8634d23843b94a before and after each.

LINKS/ANCHORS IN THE FENCED BLOCK CHECKED BY HAND, since no gate can see them: the block (lines 49-73) contains zero markdown link or anchor constructs — it is pure Clojure — and the added comment introduces none. Control for that zero: the same pattern over lines 1-48 of the same file reads 3.

OUT OF FENCE, UNTOUCHED: git diff origin/main -- implementation/adapters/uix/test/ is EMPTY on this branch. #9293 was still OPEN when this landed (86 checks: 65 SUCCESS, 20 SKIPPED, 1 pending), so this base still carries the two :uix.linter/interop-ref-read warnings at uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120,139 — the known trunk condition, deliberately not fixed here. No linter or gate configuration touched.
close_reason: Merged as PR #9303 (rebased onto main at 7f97ac03b6). Five-clause merge criterion met at band 87 measured this tick: total 87, 20 skipped + 67 success, zero failures, zero non-terminal; 4 workflow runs at full head oid 61723e325c875a041b3f2f310ccf125c91fbb08b all completed/success; .github/workflows/ diff from merge-base to trunk was 0 lines, so the check set is current against the trunk matrix.

title: ssr-node render(): validation/clone TOCTOU reads the caller's object twice, and a throwing postMessage leaves the isolate stuck busy
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the ssrnode-c worker while landing rf2-2hmg (PR #9297). Inside the fence but outside that bead's question, so reported rather than fixed. TWO separate defects in one file, filed together because they share a cause: `render()` does work in an order that assumes `postMessage` cannot throw.

DEFECT 1 — VALIDATION/CLONE TOCTOU. `validatePartition` returns the CALLER'S OWN OBJECT rather than a copy, so the validator and the structured clone read one object TWICE. An accessor can therefore be a well-formed string on read 1 and unclonable on read 2. This is not theoretical: it is the mechanism the worker used to reach `service.cjs:108`, driving a real non-Refusal through the real Service with a caller-authored Symbol, and observing it cross onto a public refusal as `"DataCloneError: Symbol(...) could not be cloned."`.

DEFECT 2 — STUCK ISOLATE. `render()` sets `pendingRender` BEFORE `postMessage`, so a throwing `postMessage` leaves the isolate marked busy until the deadline fires. The window is bounded by the deadline rather than unbounded, which is why this is P3 and not higher.

WHY THEY ARE ONE BEAD: both are `render()`'s ordering, and a repair to either that does not consider the other is likely to move the problem rather than close it. Defect 1's fix (clone or freeze before validating) may make defect 2 unreachable by removing the throw; defect 2's fix (set `pendingRender` after a successful post) closes it regardless. Decide whether one repair subsumes the other, and say so.

BOTH FAIL CLOSED AND SELF-LIMIT — this is P3 deliberately. Defect 1 produces a refusal rather than a wrong render; defect 2 releases at the deadline. Neither corrupts output. Under the stance's "don't litigate the minutiae", a verified "the bounded window is acceptable" for defect 2 IS a legitimate outcome if the repair costs more than the exposure — but say so with the deadline value quoted, rather than leaving it unexamined.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING — these are the worker's claims, not findings of mine. Confirm `validatePartition` really does return the caller's object (not a copy) at tip; confirm `pendingRender` is really set before the `postMessage` call; and re-derive both line numbers, since #9297 rewrote parts of this file.

A TEST-DESIGN NOTE THE WORKER ESTABLISHED AND WORTH REUSING: the witness for defect 1 must assert the partition value is READ TWICE, because only the clone reads it again — a test that merely passes a bad value proves nothing about the TOCTOU. That control is fix-independent, so it stays valid after the repair.

FENCE. IN: `implementation/ssr-node/**`. OUT: `spec/Conventions.md` catalogues the `:rf.ssr-node/*` code MEMBERS and is hot-zone — if a member changes, that is a separate sequenced edit, not part of this. #9297 established the bar: it added and removed no member, so no spec edit was owed.
notes:
2026-09-05 — WORKED, PR #9304 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9304), branch worker/ssrnode-d. NOT CLOSED; awaiting merge.

BOTH PREMISES VERIFIED AT SOURCE at tip 68961fe037, line numbers re-derived after #9297:
- validatePartition really did return the caller's own object — protocol.cjs:490 read `request[partitionField]`, :533 returned it unchanged.
- pendingRender really was set before the post — isolate.cjs:222 assigned it, :230 called postMessage.

BOTH FIXED. NEITHER REPAIR SUBSUMES THE OTHER, and the answer to the bead's question is that fixing one and citing it as cover for the other would have moved the problem. Read-once removes the CALLER's route to the throw, so through service.renderFrames defect 2 became unreachable — but not closed, because Isolate.render() takes an unvalidated request and the reorder closes the stranding whatever throws. Defect 2's fix alone would have left a well-formed request still refused for a value nobody validated.

DEFECT 1 IS WIDER THAN FILED. validateRequest built its returned request from fresh reads for every scalar too. Measured on the unfixed tree, reads per field on one validating request: entry 7, timeoutMs 5, buildId 4, args 3, requestId 3. The repair is the principle rather than the instance — read once, validate what you read, return what you validated — so the partitions come back as fresh objects of the checked values and no second read is left to disagree with the first. No defensive copy, no freeze, no re-check.

DEFECT 2's EXPOSURE IS WORSE THAN "a bounded busy window", which is why it was not accepted as-is under don't-litigate-the-minutiae. Deadline quoted: createService's defaultTimeoutMs = 1000, maxTimeoutMs = 5000 — so at most 5000 ms, 1000 ms by default. But `dead` stayed false, so pool.release() returned the isolate to the idle list STILL MARKED BUSY and the next caller was refused SERVICE_SATURATED by an isolate doing nothing; then the deadline's own callback ran _terminateWorker(), killing a healthy thread, forcing a pool replacement, and burning one further request on ISOLATE_LOST before it healed. Fix cost: three lines of reordering, no new state.

REDS QUOTED BEFORE THE FIX (each witness written first, watched fail, then fixed): "the normalized request must not alias the caller's own partition object"; "the request must carry the EDN text that was validated" with actual Symbol(rf2-ey07-second-read); "these fields were read more than once" listing entry (7) buildId (4) args (3) requestId (3) timeoutMs (5); and "a post that threw must leave nothing in flight", true !== false.

THE READ-COUNT WITNESS #9297 ESTABLISHED IS KEPT and now reads 1 where it read 2, with the render succeeding on the first-read value. egress §7's other three rows went red on the fix because the fix removed their route — that red is the evidence the caller route is closed. The last-resort arm is NOT removed (it is what guarantees renderFrames throws nothing but a Refusal); with no caller able to reach it, it is driven at the seam it guards, a Service over a stand-in pool, and §7's header says plainly that this is the weaker witness rather than dressing it up.

A postMessage that throws still rejects RAW, deliberately: service.cjs's last receiver is the only thing that both writes the operator's stderr copy and publishes the contract's wording, so building a Refusal in the isolate would have left the operator no copy at all. render()'s docstring now names the exception instead of overstating itself.

NO SPEC EDIT OWED: no :rf.ssr-node/* code member added or removed, the same bar #9297 met. Nothing outside implementation/ssr-node/** touched. service.cjs's comment and the README both described the closed route in the present tense and were corrected in the same commit.

GATES, captured exits: ssr-node suite 0 (9 suites, 133 rows, up from 128); ssr-ring crossing-test 0 (10 tests / 107 assertions); ESLint 0 (armed by the .cjs extension via lint.yml's own classifier — not nominated in the brief); check_readme_links.py --ci 0, proven to bite by a planted broken link + anchor that returned exit 1 naming README.md:163, restored and verified by blob hash; check_require_alias_dialect.py 0 (honest but uninformative — a .cjs/Markdown diff cannot move an import edge); check_view_lifetime_residue.py 0 (does read this content); all 42 scripts/check_*.py 0.

SURFACE CLASSIFIER: the six changed PATHS report exactly ssr_node=true. Controlled both ways — a core path arms 12 surfaces, and the misuse the brief warns about (passing `origin/main HEAD` as paths) reproduces here as zero surfaces true.
close_reason: Merged as PR #9304 (rebased onto main at 85d7b49fe5). Five-clause merge criterion met at band 87 measured this tick: total 87, 63 skipped + 24 success, zero failures, zero non-terminal; 4 workflow runs at full head oid debe244f6e33d182a17a92e4ab5785ab773c85ad all completed/success; .github/workflows/ diff from merge-base to trunk was 0 lines. Landed 400 insertions across ssr-node protocol/isolate/service plus three test files.

value:
THE rf2-kuky API-REVIEW FAMILY IS ONE SERIALISED SURFACE, NOT ~30 PARALLELISABLE BEADS — dispatch it as CLUSTERS OF FOUR THROUGH A SINGLE WORKER, never as parallel workers (measured 2026-09-05).

WHAT I MEASURED. Of the 60 ready beads this tick, 23 were rf2-kuky.* and I mapped the spec surfaces each one names. Nearly every one names spec/API.md, and the ones that do not are mostly beads that ADD or DELETE public names — which moves spec/API.md and BOTH manifest sidecars (spec/api-manifest.edn, spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn) whether the bead text mentions them or not. rf2-kuky.58 is the clean example: its text names only spec/002, spec/006 and docs/, but its target API adds h/frame-root and h/frame-provider as public Hicasso heads, so it necessarily moves the manifest.

WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. spec/API.md is a hot-zone file, so the fence permits exactly ONE holder at a time. A backlog that reads as 23 independent P2/P3 items is therefore a QUEUE OF DEPTH 23 behind a single lock. Saturating six workers on it is not merely inadvisable, it is impossible — five of the six would be fenced off the file they need, and any that were not would conflict on merge.

I LEARNED THIS THE EXPENSIVE WAY IN MINIATURE: I fenced spec/api-manifest*.edn OUT of rf2-kuky.27's scope on the reasoning that the bead was about test vars. Wrong — deleting four public v1 vars necessarily moves manifest rows, and PR #9298 went red on 'Public-API manifest drift-check' as a direct result. THE RULE: if a bead adds, deletes or renames a PUBLIC name, it touches spec/API.md and both manifest sidecars. Do not reason from the bead's prose about which files it names; reason from whether the public surface moves.

THE DISPATCH PATTERN THAT FOLLOWS. The loop body already licenses it — 'for P2, P3 and P4, if possible, cluster up to 4 beads with the same surface area into a single dispatch'. For this family that is not an optimisation, it is the ONLY way to get throughput: one worker holding the API.md lock, carrying four kuky beads, making one coherent edit to the shared files and one manifest regeneration. Four beads per lock-acquisition instead of one. Cluster by sub-domain so the four cohere — observability (.17/.19/.20/.21), views (.56/.58/.60/.61), machines (.14/.15/.16/.26), ssr (.42/.43/.44), registry (.24/.25/.30/.32), boot (.1/.2/.3/.4), schema (.39/.40), routing (.36/.37/.38).

TWO SEPARATORS WHEN BUILDING A CLUSTER. (1) Exclude the RULING/DECISION beads — they need Mike, and bundling one into an implementation cluster stalls the whole cluster behind a hold. (2) Check the sub-domain against what is CURRENTLY held: the observability cluster was unbuildable this tick because .17/.19/.20 all name spec/009-Instrumentation.md, which devcon-a held via PR #9306.

SO THE STEADY STATE IS ONE KUKY WORKER AT A TIME, and the rest of the fleet's saturation has to come from OUTSIDE the family — tools/xray, tools/mcp-conformance, skills/, implementation/ internals. Plan the tick that way rather than discovering it at dispatch time.

PR #9303 merged 2026-09-05T09:13:56Z at 7f97ac03b627afe728fa666ce8885368d6502f9c reviewed independently for completeness, correctness and implementation quality. Completeness: the canonical UIx README imperative-effect recipe now dereferences its use-ref object and briefly explains the idiom; exact owner rf2-coka is closed and fulfilled. No remaining (.-current ref) recipe found in the nine adapter Markdown files after comment-marker stripping and whitespace collapsing. Correctness: independently read pinned com.pitch/uix.core 1.4.4 jar again; use-ref returns the same object passed to React, whose IDeref implementation reads its current property. The replacement preserves the listener target, cleanup and dependency vector. The recipe transcription test blob is unchanged from #9293, whose zero-warning compile and browser results were independently verified in that review. Implementation quality: one expression plus a useful inline explanation prevents copying the earlier lint violation, with no runtime, gate or API expansion. All 87 PR checks succeeded or skipped. The edited fenced block contains no Markdown links or anchors; no redundant runtime suite rerun for this documentation-only change. Beads created: none; updated/reopened: none.

A GREEN ROLLUP WHOSE RELEVANT GATE WAS *SKIPPED* IS NOT EVIDENCE THE GATE WOULD PASS — and clause 2 of the merge criterion cannot see the difference (measured 2026-09-05 on PR #9306).

THE SITUATION. PR #9306 (rf2-kuky.18) removed a Story-shell page-wide no-op :errors listener that had been MASKING 8 real Xray errors. Its own worker measured `npm run test:story-feature-load` RED on the change and told me to sequence the PR behind the fix (rf2-avi7). Then the rollup came in at 87/87: 10 skipped, 77 success, zero failures, zero non-terminal. All FIVE clauses of the merge criterion were satisfied. The obvious read — 'the worker was wrong, CI is the authority, merge it' — is the trap.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY TRUE. The job named 'Story/Xray browser gates (PR-smoke)' RAN and SUCCEEDED, which is what makes this convincing: it is not an absent job, it is a GREEN job. But its step 'Run the FULL Story feature-load gate (direct-runner change, rf2-65ajl)' was SKIPPED inside it. Read from the API rather than inferred:
  gh api repos/<o>/<r>/actions/jobs/<job_id> -q '.steps[] | "\(.conclusion // .status)\t\(.name)"'
gave 'skipped  Run the FULL Story feature-load gate'. The step is gated on the classifier output `story_full_gate`, which by design arms ONLY on the feature-load gate's own spec modules and its run/serve orchestration — NOT on ordinary Story/Xray runtime changes (test.yml ~4100-4127 explains the reasoning at length; it exists so a normal Story PR does not pay for an extra testbed compile). #9306 changed observability runtime code, so it did not arm.

AND THE NIGHTLY RUNS IT UNCONDITIONALLY. expensive-tests.yml has 'Gate — Story feature-load' under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`. So merging #9306 on its green rollup would not have produced a red PR anywhere — it would have produced a RED NIGHTLY, discovered by the nightly-red channel that CLAUDE.md itself records taking SEVEN DAYS to reach a human on the last occasion (rf2-4a0c, issue #8423).

THE GENERAL RULE. Clause 2 accepts 'skipped' as passed, and it is right to — path-filtered jobs are the normal case and a skipped job usually means 'your diff cannot affect this'. But SKIPPED IS THE ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, NOT EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE. The five clauses are a FLOOR: they establish that nothing CI ran objected. They are not a licence to merge in the face of positive, measured evidence of a defect that CI did not run. When a worker reports a gate red and the rollup is green, the discriminator is NOT 'who do I believe' — it is 'did that gate actually execute on this head?', answered at the STEP level, because a skipped step hides inside a green job and the rollup shows only the job.

HOW TO CHECK IT CHEAPLY. Probe the rollup for the gate by name (`jq '.statusCheckRollup[] | select((.name|ascii_downcase)|test("<gate>"))'`), and TAKE A CONTROL from another PR — here #9298 showed the same check SKIPPED where #9306 showed it SUCCESS, which is what first proved the two PRs were being graded differently. Then descend to the step list via the jobs API. A job-level green with a step-level skip is invisible at every level above the last one.

SO: HOLD THE PR, and say plainly that the hold is not a clause failure. The bead's own worker was right and the rollup was also right; they were answering different questions.

title: test(core): no :elide-asserts build exists anywhere, so the assertion-elided posture is proved by construction and never executed
description:
FILED BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05, from worker coreguard-a's rf2-xn13 report. The worker DECLINED to claim a probe it could not execute, and this bead exists so that decline is recorded as work rather than lost as a caveat.

THE MEASUREMENT, from that worker: there is NO :elide-asserts build anywhere in this repository — zero hits across *.edn, *.cjs, *.yml, *.sh and *.md. Re-run that census at tip before acting; it is a count and counts go stale first.

WHY IT MATTERS. rf2-xn13's whole subject is that (assert (map? config-map) ...) is ELIDABLE, so a legitimate consumer build with assertions off silently accepted a non-map and applied nothing. The fix replaces the assert with an always-on when-not + throw-error!, and the accompanying dual-posture test is genuinely clever: it reads configure!'s ACTUAL source form and re-compiles it under *assert* false into a throwaway namespace, with an anti-vacuity control proving the harness really elides. That is a compile-time control on the JVM and it is the right test.

WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN, and it is a narrow gap rather than a hole: nothing in CI ever COMPILES this codebase with assertions elided, on either host. The rf2-xn13 criterion holds by construction — the source is host-neutral .cljc and no assert form remains in the guard — but 'by construction' is an argument, and every other guard in this repo that was believed by construction and never executed is why the method keeps saying a search returning zero is not a check that passed.

THE QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS, and it is a real fork rather than a foregone conclusion: is a permanent :elide-asserts build worth its cost? Arguments against are strong and the stance backs them — adding one touches implementation/shadow-cljs.edn, which is hot-zone and a standing serial bottleneck; it adds a compile to the matrix for a posture no shipped consumer has yet reported using; and 'not over-engineering or gold plating' is exactly the clause that rejects a whole build id to prove one guard. Arguments for: the elided posture is a REAL consumer configuration, it is the one this bug lived in, and it is currently unobserved on every artefact rather than just this one.

A CHEAPER MIDDLE OPTION worth costing first: assert the property by source inspection across the public boundary rather than by compilation — a gate that refuses a bare (assert ...) as the sole guard on a public-facing argument check. That catches the class rather than this instance, needs no new build, and touches no hot-zone file.

DO NOT dispatch this as an implementation task before that fork is settled. The deliverable of a first pass is the cost of each option, not a build.
notes:
=== FORK SETTLED 2026-09-05 19:30 AUSEST (worker elide-a, trunk 85d7b49fe5) ===
RULING: do NOT add an :elide-asserts build, and do NOT add a source-inspection
gate. Closing as not-worth-doing. No code change; no PR. Evidence below.

1. THE PREMISE HOLDS, re-measured at tip with biting controls.
   `git grep -F ':elide-asserts' -- '*.edn'` => 0 hits (control ':compiler-options'
   over the same file set via the same instrument => 5 files, so the instrument
   bites). `git grep -F 'elide-asserts' -- '*.yml' '*.sh' '*.cjs' '*.js' '*.json'`
   => 0 hits (control 'shadow-cljs' same set => hits). Carriers of the literal
   are 4 files and only 4: core.cljc (2, one of them a COMMENT quoting the
   retired form), configure_test.clj (1), spec/009-Instrumentation.md (1), and
   this bead's own export. Note 'elide' alone is a heavily overloaded DOMAIN word
   here (wire elision, trace elision, DCE) - that axis is noise, not signal.

2. BUT THE POSTURE IS ALREADY PROVEN BY EXECUTION, NOT BY CONSTRUCTION - and I
   PROVED THE TEST DISCRIMINATES rather than trusting it.
   `configure-non-map-guard-survives-assertion-elision` recompiles configure!'s
   ACTUAL source form under *assert* false and exercises it. I planted the
   original rf2-xn13 bug back into core.cljc as a one-line change - the bare
   `(assert (map? config-map))` restored as the SOLE guard with the throw-error!
   made dead code under `(when-not true ...)` - and the suite went RED with the
   original bug's exact signature:
     FAIL configure-non-map-guard-survives-assertion-elision (configure_test.clj:380)
     "assertion-elided build still fails loud on :trace-buffer"

THE node_modules CANARY IS 103 WITH `ls -A` AND 101 WITH PLAIN `ls` — BOTH ARE CORRECT, AND A BRIEF THAT NAMES A NUMBER WITHOUT THE FLAG MANUFACTURES A FALSE ALARM SHAPED EXACTLY LIKE THE REAL DISASTER (measured 2026-09-05).

THE NUMBERS. In the mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2:
  ls -A implementation/node_modules | wc -l   ->  103
  ls    implementation/node_modules | wc -l   ->  101
The difference is exactly two dot-entries that plain ls omits: `.bin` and `.package-lock.json`. Nothing is missing in either reading.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COUNTING QUIBBLE. The canary exists to detect ONE specific catastrophe: a worker worktree junctions implementation/node_modules at the mayor's real one, and a bare `git worktree remove` follows the junction and EMPTIES the mayor's node_modules — exit 0, silently, breaking every local build. It has happened twice. So the canary is the tripwire, and a tripwire that fires on a flag difference is worse than none: the next reader either (a) sees 101 against a briefed 103 and reports damage that did not occur, burning a cycle and possibly triggering an unnecessary `npm ci`, or (b) — far worse — is briefed 101, reads 101 after a genuine partial loss that happened to leave 101 non-dot entries, and clears it.

MY OWN BRIEFS CARRIED THE DEFECT. I had been writing 'confirm the mayor's implementation/node_modules still counts 103 entries' with no flag. A worker on rf2-y0pr ran plain `ls`, read 101, and correctly flagged my number as stale — it was not stale, it was under-specified. The historical canary recorded in the old MEMORY.md entry as '~101' is a plain-ls reading, so the two records disagreed with each other for the same reason and neither said which instrument it used.

THE RULE. Never write a canary count without the exact command. Brief it as: `ls -A implementation/node_modules | wc -l` must print 103. And when a worker reports a canary mismatch, THE FIRST CHECK IS THE FLAG, not the directory — run both forms and diff the entry LISTS, not the counts, before concluding anything was lost. `ls -A | grep '^\.'` names the delta in one line.

GENERALISATION WORTH KEEPING. This is the same failure class as the two-dot/three-dot diff and the `git grep -c | wc -l` files-versus-hits slip: a count is not a measurement unless the instrument travels with it. Any number that crosses a brief boundary — mayor to worker, session to session, note to note — carries its command or it is not evidence.

IN A jq REGEX ON THIS BOX, WRITE `[.]` NOT `\.` — THE BACKSLASH IS COLLAPSED BEFORE jq SEES IT AND THE FILTER DIES AS A COMPILE ERROR (measured 2026-09-05, twice in one session).

WHAT HAPPENS. A jq filter containing test("spellings\.1") reaches jq as test("spellings\.1") minus one backslash, i.e. the JSON string contains a bare backslash-dot, which is not a valid JSON escape. jq refuses to compile:
  jq: error: Invalid escape at line 1, column 4 (while parsing '"\."')
Doubling the backslash inside single quotes did NOT survive either — the error message shows jq receiving the single-backslash form both ways, so this is not the ordinary shell-quoting rule people expect.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A SYNTAX NIGGLE. A jq COMPILE error exits non-zero and prints to STDERR. Inside a pipeline whose stdout is being counted, or with `2>/dev/null` anywhere in the chain, it looks exactly like an honest empty result. The first time this bit me today the filter was `test("kuky\.(33|18|51|28)")` in a merged-PR cross-check, and my `|| echo "(none above = clean)"` fallback printed a REASSURING answer for a query that had never run. The second time it silently returned nothing for a bead-sequencing lookup where an empty result would have meant 'no blocker' and would have authorised a dispatch.

THE FIX, and it needs no escaping at all: use a CHARACTER CLASS.
  test("ref spellings[.]")            not  test("ref spellings\.")
  capture("spellings[.](?<n>[0-9]+)")  not  capture("spellings\.(?<n>[0-9]+)")
A one-character class is exactly a literal dot in every regex dialect, is immune to every layer of quoting between here and jq, and reads fine.

THE DISCIPLINE THAT CATCHES IT REGARDLESS. Any jq filter whose EMPTINESS would be read as a finding needs a CONTROL THAT MUST MATCH. I now pair every such query with a probe I know must return a row — e.g. after searching all beads for 'ref spellings.N', re-run the same capture against rf2-kuky.24 alone, which declares spellings.2, and assert it prints 2. If the control comes back empty the filter is broken, not the data. Take the control from the DATA, not spliced in as a shell literal, for the same reason as the CRLF case: a literal never travels the pipeline the data travelled.

RELATED, SAME FAMILY: jq writes CRLF here, so a pattern JOINED from jq output matches only its last alternative, and a jq-produced list compared with comm/join/diff reports everything as different. `tr -d '\r'` after any jq that feeds a join or a set operation.

### Cross-cutting themes (read these before the docs)

1. **Facade re-exports of home namespaces protect nobody.** SSR (seven copies), trace/epoch (the facade spelling the spec teaches is JVM-only), observability (every stream 4–5 ways) and registry introspection all found the same shape: the "documented facade exception" exists for single-import ergonomics, and the corpus shows every consumer already requiring the home namespace. The bundle-DCE argument that justified the home-ns verbs is contradicted by the actual require graph (`re-frame.core → re-frame.trace → re-frame.trace.tooling` is unconditional). One rule would settle four docs: a surface has ONE home; the facade carries registrars and the front porch, nothing else.
2. **Per-kind aliases beside a generic grammar.** Fifteen introspection fns, seven HTTP verb helpers, seven schema-setter names: each family is a projection of a grammar that already exists and that the tools already use. The demand bar (Principles) has ruled on them retroactively.
3. **Imperative pairs the frame lifecycle should own.** Routing already folded `install-url-listener!`/`remove-` into `:url-bound? true` on the frame (rf2-g8pbwg); resources' revalidation pair is the same shape with one caller.
4. **Substrate naming drift.** Hicasso arrived with its own spellings for view definition, sub reads, hooks and mount verbs where UIx and Reagent had already settled on others; the mechanisms differ where the substrate forces it, but the names diverge where it does not (`use-subscribe` vs `use-sub`, `render!` vs `mount!`, `defview` around `reg-view*`).
5. **Parked surfaces whose park has lapsed.** Machines' `:system-id` family was parked in July "until the facade audit rules"; that audit (rf2-2hpxo) closed 2026-09-04 without it in scope. # Implementation API: fewer ways, stronger concepts

Review date: 2026-09-05. Tracking bead: `rf2-snkw`.

This began as an independent source review and now incorporates selected, source-checked insights from the [Fable corpus](../fable/README.md), at the user's request. It is not an implementation change. Proposed forms below are design proposals, not instructions for using the currently shipped API.

## Findings

| Area | Overlap | Recommendation | Judgment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Subscription inputs](subscription-inputs.md) | Arrow chains and input-producing functions describe the same dependency relation, but change the computation's argument shape. | One named `:inputs` slot; consistently vector-valued derived inputs. | Also enables derived inline-image subs and earlier literal checking; explicit migration required. |
| [Registration inspection](registration-inspection.md) | Generic registry reads, feature-specific getters, and positional/map source-selection forms. | Two generic reads with one explicit source-selection grammar; ordinary collection operations for projections. | High tooling payoff; preserve genuine source-store versus frame-generation distinctions. |
| [HTTP request construction](http-requests.md) | Seven verb functions merely construct the already-public managed-effect data. | Make the effect data canonical; remove the verb-constructor family. | Straightforward reduction, but common GET calls become longer. |
| [HTTP reply addressing](http-replies.md) | Unified and split destinations can be mixed, requiring override precedence. | Keep both useful styles, but make `:reply-to` mutually exclusive with `:on-*`. | Revised after Fable's login evidence: deleting split routing would add application ceremony. |
| [Schema backend configuration](schema-backend.md) | Three scalar setters duplicate an existing partial-map installer. | Keep `set-schema-fns!`; separate fixture restoration from application configuration. | Small, clear cleanup; modest application impact. |
| [Resource lifecycle and scope](resource-lifecycle-and-scope.md) | Manual listener setup repeats frame lifecycle ownership; resolver sugar changes callback input meaning. | Frame-owned revalidation; one declared-input resolver contract. | New from Fable; removes an actual boot-order obligation and a callback-shape exception. |
| [View adapter ergonomics](view-adapter-ergonomics.md) | Root recipes, hook names and view descriptor shapes drift across adapters. | Shared root-handle grammar, `use-sub` for value hooks, consistent view lookup. | New from Fable; preserve substrate machinery while reducing application boilerplate. |
| [Machine child completion](machine-child-completion.md) | Single-child finality and fan-out's hand-dispatched completion encode the same terminal fact differently. | Final-state completion works under both `:spawn` and `:spawn-all`. | New from Fable; a reusable child no longer knows its parent's join vocabulary. |
| [Trace and epoch inspection](trace-and-epoch-inspection.md) | Trace reads have platform-specific aliases; a tool's data-clear action calls a policy-reset helper; whole-history projection duplicates record composition. | One platform-complete read surface; policy-preserving trace clear; record-level projection. | Added on the second reread; clearer tool behavior without merging history systems. |

The strongest next design discussions are subscriptions, inspection and reusable child completion. The clearest everyday ergonomic wins are frame-owned revalidation and consistent adapter boot. Schema configuration remains an easy small cleanup. Neither list size nor deleted-function count is the objective: the objective is fewer concepts a programmer or AI must remember to accomplish a real SPA task.

## What Fable added or changed

Fable's most useful contribution is distinguishing surface reduction from application simplification. Its login example changed my reply recommendation; its resource and UIx examples identify setup code the library should own; its child-completion comparison exposes avoidable coupling between otherwise reusable machines. The [synthesis notes](intermediate/fable-synthesis.md) record which proposals were adopted, narrowed or left out and why.

The [second reread](intermediate/fable-reread-2.md) adds concrete capability and migration evidence to subscriptions and one focused trace/epoch finding. It also records Fable's withdrawal of the bulk-schema deletion and adoption of explicit registry source selection. This is now nine focused areas; agreement between reviews is not counted as fresh evidence where one review simply adopted the other's proposal.

I did not import every deletion. In particular, retain bulk app-schema registration's up-front path validation, keep distinct state stores out of the generic registrar merely for symmetry, and do not use diagnostic traces as a machine control protocol. This corpus remains focused on a manageable set of improvements, not a catalogue of every questionable key.

## Method and bounds

I used the [API reference](../../../../spec/API.md) and [generated API manifest](../../../../spec/api-manifest.edn) as discovery aids, then examined implementations, registration metadata, and actual consumers. The manifest also covers tool namespaces; its total row count is not a count of implementation APIs reviewed.

The review followed core registration, frames, dispatch, subscriptions, images, configuration, introspection and listeners; feature surfaces including routing, resources/mutations, machines, schemas and HTTP; and rendering/SSR and test-support boundaries. Candidate findings were checked against authored Clojure/CLJS source in `/examples` and `/tools`, with focused implementation tests used to identify supported cases absent from the applications. Each finding names the evidence and the use-case distinctions it must preserve.

The [intermediate evidence ledger](intermediate/evidence-ledger.md) records useful implementation observations, search boundaries, and rejected simplification candidates. All deliverables are in the mayor's checkout; intermediate notes are confined to `intermediate/`.

“Known use cases” means those found in this repository during this review, not a claim about every external application. Searches establish checked-in examples, not production popularity or the absence of dynamically resolved calls. Tests were read as evidence of contracts; I did not execute runtime tests or benchmark proposed APIs. This is not a line-by-line correctness certification of the entire implementation.

The philosophical yardsticks are the user's pre-alpha posture and the repository's [Vision](../../../../spec/000-Vision.md) and [Principles](../../../../spec/Principles.md): a small computational model, data before magic, regularity, addressable definitions, and useful public inspection. The existing spec also values migration compatibility. Where these pull in different directions, the finding states the conflict instead of describing a proposed break as an existing obligation.

## Similar-looking operations I would keep

| Surface | Why the distinction earns its place |
| --- | --- |
| `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` | Enqueueing and synchronous run-to-completion have different ordering and reentrancy contracts. |
| `subscribe` / `subscribe-once` / `compute-sub` | Owned reactive observation, a released live-runtime snapshot, and computation over supplied state have different lifetimes and inputs. |
| Frame scoping / frame ownership / `capture-frame` | Ambient synchronous scope, creating and disposing a frame, and carrying a frame capability across asynchronous work solve different problems. |
| Registration macros / function entry points | Source capture at a literal definition site and higher-order/computed registration are distinct capabilities. |
| Resource ensure / refetch / release / invalidate | Establishing demand, requesting freshness, ending ownership, and marking data stale are not synonyms. |
| Raw resource state / resource subscriptions | Durable runtime entries and derived presentation status are different representations, not aliases. |

| Flows / subscriptions | Drain-time materialization and reactive derivation have different execution semantics. |
| Mount / hydrate / render / unmount semantics | These remain distinct transitions. The adapter finding nevertheless standardizes their handle grammar and expresses hydration as an explicit first-render mode. |
| Single / bulk app-schema registration | The bulk operation validates its input before applying registrations; it is not simply an interchangeable spelling of an arbitrary loop. |
| Scoped test overrides / explicit stub installation | Automatically restored fixture scope and deliberately installed testbed behavior have different ownership. |

These decisions follow the relevant implementations in [core](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc), [resources](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc), [Hicasso](../../../../implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc), [schemas](../../../../implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc), and [HTTP test support](../../../../implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc).

Several apparent cleanup targets have already been retired or consolidated, including the old event-registration variants, multiple frame-construction helpers, per-setting core configuration setters, and per-stream listener names. Throwing retirement stubs are migration diagnostics, not additional working APIs; they are not counted as findings here.

## Recommendation

Prefer subtraction that leaves ordinary Clojure values and functions doing more of the work. Do not replace these families with a larger options language, a generic plugin framework, or a compatibility matrix. Equally, do not merge operations whose timing, ownership, or meaning differs merely to shorten the API index.

Each linked finding contains its own use-case inventory, proposed API, counterargument, migration implications, and focused acceptance evidence. No runtime code or normative specification was changed by this review.

## Corrections and boundaries that matter

**Bulk schemas are not equivalent to `run!`.** Fable's proposed replacement omits the current up-front batch/path validation and vector return. [Storage](../../../../../implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc) makes both visible. Preserve the convenient batch operation rather than pushing that coordination into application code.

**Completion traces are not a control API.** `:rf.machine/done` in finalization is an emitted diagnostic trace. The proposed universal completion behavior requires runtime-owned delivery to joins; it should not depend on listeners or trace availability. The current join source also expressly describes its exact-attempt record as causal correlation in a trusted program, not authentication. Preserve that correlation without importing security ceremony.

**Consistent root names do not make lifecycle differences disappear.** I initially retained mount/hydrate/render distinctions outright. The stronger conclusion is to preserve their semantics while adopting one handle grammar. I favor the existing Reagent `render!` name over Fable's proposed broad rename to `mount!`; the valuable change is the shared recipe.

**A captured frame does not subscribe a React component.** A direct `capture-frame` operation may help callbacks, but it cannot substitute for a value hook's re-render contract. Scope a subtree when eliminating an explicit-frame hook spelling.

**Fifteen getters need not imply fifteen true registrar kinds.** Fable's broader registry proposal absorbs side tables and virtual kinds. The Codex target keeps actual event descriptors for machines and preserves specialized frame-state collections where they represent other facts. Simpler querying should not require a larger conceptual registry.

**Zero observed calls is evidence, not a deletion algorithm.** It is strong support for removing a redundant convenience already covered by data. It is weaker evidence that a specialized lifecycle capability is equivalent to another operation. The accepted additions show actual application boilerplate or coupling, not just low counts.

## Remaining Fable themes: not imported as a second backlog

The index also proposes changes to observability/egress, trace and epoch reads, SSR/head access, machine system IDs, boot/configuration, registration clearing, routing internals and test isolation. These remain useful dossiers in Fable's corpus; I did not copy their full deletion lists into Codex or mark their claims independently verified.

A promising cross-cutting guideline is one documented home for an operation, with facade convenience justified by real authoring benefit. It supports the already-accepted inspection and adapter cleanup. It does not, by itself, justify removing every facade export, collapsing frame-owned sinks into dev streams, merging schema enforcement policies, or creating a universal clear/query/configure language. Those are separate design decisions with more scope than the high-value changes above.

The resulting corpus now contains eight focused areas, not the sum of both reviewers' proposed deletions. It retains the user's posture: elegant, powerful SPA authoring; low friction; ordinary data and functions; no new framework merely to tidy the old one.

Final read-only document validation: 11 Markdown files, 156 relative link targets, consistent table columns and paired code fences; exit 0. No runtime code or normative specification was changed.

| Backend installation is not transactional. | The same implementation writes three atoms, and `snapshot-schema-fns` documents quiescent configuration. A public vocabulary cleanup should not casually promise atomicity or add speculative concurrency machinery. |

| Bulk app-schema registration is not a bare loop. | [Schema storage](../../../../../implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc), `reg-app-schemas`: validates the batch and all path shapes before applying individual registrations. This defeated a superficial singular-versus-plural duplication argument. |

## Tempting reductions not promoted to findings

`dispatch` and `dispatch-sync` differ in scheduling and permitted contexts. `subscribe`, `subscribe-once`, and `compute-sub` differ in ownership and state source. `capture-frame` is a capability carried across asynchronous work, not a spelling of synchronous scope. Resource state accessors and resource subscriptions expose raw versus derived facts. Rendering, mounting, hydration and unmounting represent distinct transitions. Source-capturing macros and higher-order registration functions serve different definition sites. Scoped test overrides and deliberately installed testbed stubs have different cleanup lifetimes.

The final index summarizes these boundaries. The rejection criterion was practical: if deletion moves an unavoidable semantic distinction into less visible flags, timing rules, or caller boilerplate, it is not automatically an improvement.

# Bead-drafting brief — API review wave 3 (fable + codex), 2026-09-05

You are drafting BEAD SPECS for one review area. You do not create beads; the coordinator creates them from your spec file. You write exactly one file: `ai/findings/API-review/fable/intermediate/beads/<area>.md`. Read-only everywhere else. No `bd` mutations (`bd list` / `bd show` are fine), no git state changes, no builds, no edits to any repository file.

## Posture (Mike, verbatim)
Pre-alpha, focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece. Not over-engineering or gold plating. We trust the programmer. High productivity for the programmer and the AI they use via a library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every last fine detail and drown in the minutiae. No back-compat shims: a redundant spelling is deleted, not deprecated.

## Inputs
1. Your fable doc(s) in `ai/findings/API-review/fable/` — read in full, INCLUDING the `## Codex cross-check` section at the end (it revises the recommendation in several docs).
2. The codex doc(s) named in your prompt under `ai/findings/API-review/codex/`, plus `codex/intermediate/fable-synthesis.md` §Corrections.
3. `ai/findings/API-review/fable/README.md` §Relationship to the parallel codex review — it says which findings are two-reviewer and which are one-reviewer.
4. The open-bead roster: run `bd list --status open,in_progress,blocked,deferred --limit 0 --json` and grep it for your area's names; the coordinator has listed likely overlaps in your prompt. Never duplicate an existing bead; reference it. Never propose amending an `in_progress` bead.
5. Verify at tip anything you put in a bead that a worker will act on (file:line, arity, consumer counts). Re-measure if the doc's tip differs from HEAD.

## What a bead is here
- One bead = one independently shippable, single-worker unit (roughly ≤ one worker-day), split by hot-zone ownership. Hot-zone files (one-toucher, serialised): `spec/Conventions.md`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`, `spec/API.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `implementation/deps.edn`, `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn`, `.github/workflows/*`.
- The docs, spec, examples, skills, tests and manifest updates for a change go IN THE SAME bead as the code change. Do not file separate "update docs" beads. Exception: one consolidated "doc drift" bead per area for stale lines no code bead will touch.
- **Two-reviewer findings** (README lists them) → implementation beads, dispatchable, `ruling: none`, unless the doc itself says a ruling is needed for that slice.

- **One-reviewer larger design decisions** (README lists them) → ONE `type: decision` bead per area, `ruling: RULING`, carrying the options, the recommendation, codex's caution, and the list of implementation beads to file when ruled. PLUS separate implementation beads for the ruling-independent parts: dead code with zero consumers, defects the review found (silent drops, fenced-out facade fns, stale eval forms), and doc drift.
- Every implementation bead description MUST be self-contained (the `ai/` dossier is local-only and may be deleted) and MUST enumerate: the target API (signatures, before/after code), the deletion list, consumers to migrate by file with counts (examples/, tools/, testbeds/, implementation/**/test), spec pages (flag hot-zone ones), docs pages, examples, skills (`skills/**`), tests to add or change, `spec/api-manifest.edn` regeneration, the conformance corpus / mcp-conformance if affected, migration README entry if a v1-era name changes, and the acceptance evidence.

- Priority: P2 for two-reviewer implementation beads and for defects; P2 for the High decision (observability); P3 for one-reviewer medium decisions and drift; P4 only for genuine nice-to-haves.
- Fold trivia into the nearest bead rather than filing it. Aim for the SMALLEST number of beads that carries all the work; typically 2–5 per area.
