A MERGED-BUT-UNREAPED WORKTREE STILL REPORTS AS A HOT-FILE HOLDER UNDER A THREE-DOT DIFF — TEST MERGED-NESS WITH `git cherry` AND EXCLUDE IT (measured 2026-09-05). This is the THIRD correction to the holder check and it fails CLOSED, so it silently costs throughput rather than correctness.

THE SITUATION. resources-a's PR #9305 had MERGED and its changes were on main. Its worktree still existed at the old branch head, never rebased. `git -C <wt> diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` therefore still listed spec/016-Resources.md, spec/API.md, both api-manifest sidecars and implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc — because three-dot compares against the MERGE BASE, and a merged-then-unrebased branch still differs from its old base by exactly the commits that already landed. Every one of those files read HELD. All of them were free. I had been carrying spec/API.md as locked across three ticks partly on this reading, and it had been open the whole time.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS `git cherry`, WHICH ANSWERS 'ARE THESE COMMITS ALREADY UPSTREAM' RATHER THAN 'DO THESE TREES DIFFER':
    git cherry origin/main worker/<name>
Lines beginning `-` are already on main (matched by patch-id, so a REBASE MERGE still matches — which is exactly why the diff cannot see it and this can). Lines beginning `+` are genuinely unmerged. A branch whose output is all `-`, or empty, holds NOTHING: skip it entirely in the holder census, and reap it.

MEASURED, WITH A CONTROL THAT DISCRIMINATES — the point being that a rule which calls every worktree free is as useless as one that calls them all held:
    resources-a  merged(-)=1  unmerged(+)=0   <- PR merged; holds nothing
    ssrnode-d    merged(-)=1  unmerged(+)=0   <- PR merged; holds nothing
    uixdoc-a     merged(-)=1  unmerged(+)=0   <- PR merged; holds nothing
    devcon-a     merged(-)=0  unmerged(+)=1   <- PR #9306 OPEN; genuinely holds spec/009
    testfix-a    merged(-)=0  unmerged(+)=2   <- PR #9298 OPEN; genuinely holds its files
The two with open PRs separated cleanly from the three without.

SO THE HOLDER CHECK NOW HAS THREE CORRECTIONS, AND THEY FAIL IN DIFFERENT DIRECTIONS — which is why each had to be found separately:
  (1) Enumerate from `git worktree list`, NOT from open PRs. A worker with no PR yet holds files invisibly. Fails OPEN.
  (2) Use THREE-dot, not two-dot. Two-dot reports what MAIN changed on a stale branch. Fails CLOSED.
  (3) Skip worktrees whose branch `git cherry` says is already upstream. Fails CLOSED.
Plus `git status --porcelain` for uncommitted work, since a worker mid-edit may not have committed.

THE STANDING LESSON UNDERNEATH ALL THREE: reaping is not merely tidiness. An unreaped worktree actively corrupts the dispatch fence and throttles the fleet, and the symptom — 'nothing is dispatchable this tick' — looks exactly like a genuinely busy backlog. When saturation is blocked by locks, RE-VERIFY THE LOCKS before believing them; do not carry a lock forward across ticks on a previous tick's reading.

title: api(testing): fold the four sequester-/reinstate-app-* vars into a make-reset-runtime-fixture :app-ns option
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref testing.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.test-support` grew four public `v1`-status vars (`8b969af7c4`, 2026-07-12, rf2-h1vqa4 slice 2) that spell ONE idea twice, with a different selector shape AND a different state model each time (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc`):

| var | selector | captured rows live | lowers to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequester-app-registration!` `[kind id provenance-ns]` (:168) | one row | returned to the caller, who `def`s it and hands it back | ownership-guarded `swap! registrar dissoc` (:203-212) + `source-store/forget-descriptor!` (:214) |
| `reinstate-app-registration!` `[descriptor]` (:221) | that value | — | `registrar/register!` (registrar + source store in lockstep) |
| `sequester-app-namespaces!` `[ns-prefix]` (:237) | every row whose provenance ns starts with the prefix | a module-level memo atom `sequestered-namespace-rows` (:231), captured ONCE per prefix | the same two legs in a `doseq` (:262-274) |
| `reinstate-app-namespaces!` `[ns-prefix]` (:280) | the memo | — | `registrar/register!` over the memo |

They exist for one condition: the consolidated CLJS node bundle loads every example app before any test runs; two apps register the same per-app id (`:rf.route/not-found`; the RealWorld twins share `:settings/load`, `:auth/initialise`, …); the source store keeps both provenance rows; any suite whose fixture BASELINE is captured after the second app loads fails `make-frame {}` loud with `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`. That is a baseline concern, and `make-reset-runtime-fixture` (:580) already OWNS the baseline: it captures `ns-load-baseline` and `source-store-baseline*` at build time (:818-819) and restores both around every test (`reinstate-and-snapshot!` :513, `finish-runtime-reset!` :565). The four verbs re-implement the fixture's own capture/restore cycle beside it — once as a value, once as a global.

Measured costs of the memo model: it captures ONCE, so a call before the sibling app finishes loading pins an incomplete set for every later suite (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs:84-88`: `:home/show-global-feed` left unsequestered, a sibling suite's frame creation failed); and because it is global rather than per-fixture, `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:200` has to re-sequester the sibling on EVERY test from its `init!`. Behaviour determined by load order, not visible inputs (`spec/Principles.md` low-hidden-context).

Neither `spec/008-Testing.md` nor `spec/API.md` rows them (`grep -c sequester` → 0 in both), yet `spec/api-manifest.edn:564-568` tiers them `:testing` / `:owner "008"` / `v1`. The consumer pitch is `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md:89-181` ("Bundle co-load hygiene"), and the pilots README says the opposite: "None of that applies to a workspace with one app in it, and none of it travels" (`docs/design/hicasso/product/pilots/baseline/README.md:14`). Four permanent obligations on every conforming port for a harness-internal condition.

## Evidence

```sh
git grep -n -E 'sequester-app-|reinstate-app-|sequestered-namespace-rows' -- ':!implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc' ':!ai/' ':!.beads/'
```
Consumers by class: impl-test 6 files (5 reagent example suites + the own unit test); Story 0; Xray 0; examples 0; skills 0; pilots 0.

## Target API

Zero new verbs. One option on the fixture that already owns the baseline:

```clojure
(use-fixtures :each
  (ts/make-reset-runtime-fixture
    {:adapter reagent-adapter/adapter
     :app-ns  "realworld-http."      ;; rows whose provenance ns starts here are THIS suite's app
     :init-fn init!}))
```

- `:app-ns` — a string prefix, or a set of prefixes, matched against each source-store descriptor's provenance ns (`:rf.provenance/ns`, exactly as `sequester-app-namespaces!` matches at :248-252). The rule for callers: name your OWN app's root namespace; never a sibling's.
- **Build time** (this ns's load, after its `:require` chain — i.e. inside `make-reset-runtime-fixture`, BEFORE `ns-load-baseline` / `source-store-baseline*` are taken at :818-819): capture every matching row and remove it from the live registrar and the source store. The remover is the existing ownership-guarded two-leg form (registrar slot dropped ONLY when its current writer is under the prefix, :265-273; `forget-descriptor!` per provenance row) kept as a `defn-` inside test-support. **Not `registrar/unregister!`**: it forgets EVERY provenance slot for `(kind, id)` (`registrar.cljc:713-724`) and would clobber a sibling's row for a shared id.
- **Captured rows go into a fixture-internal registry keyed by prefix that UNIONS across fixture builds** — never first-capture-wins. This is what answers codex's objection ("CLJS loads a required namespace once; if suite A captures and removes an app's rows, suite B's later `:require` of that already-loaded app does not register them again") and the boot-seed memo trap: a second suite for the same app finds the rows already gone, captures whatever NEW rows its own requires registered, and reinstates the union; a late-loading part of the app is captured by whichever fixture builds after it. Repeated suites for one app are a LIVE case: `realworld_cljs_test`, `example_realworld_boot_seed_cljs_test`, `example_realworld_password_classification_cljs_test`, `example_frame_scoping_cljs_test` all load parts of `realworld-http.*`; `realworld_resources_cljs_test` and `example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test` both load `realworld-resources.*`. The registry is internal; its whole contract is one docstring line — "rows under `:app-ns` are this suite's app: absent from every baseline, live during this suite's tests".
- **Per test**: after `reset-runtime!` (adapter installed, `:rf/default` ensured, :538) and BEFORE `:init-fn` runs, reinstate the union through `rf.registrar/register!` (registrar + source store in lockstep, as `reinstate-app-registration!` :221-229 does today). Setup ordering codex asked to preserve is preserved: the RealWorld resources `init!` still registers plans and stubs before it makes its URL-bound frame, because `:init-fn` runs after reinstatement exactly where it runs now.
- **Teardown**: `finish-runtime-reset!` (:565) already resets the source store to the suite's baseline (which excludes the app rows). Verify after each test that no `:app-ns` row remains in the SOURCE STORE (image assembly reads the store; the merge-form registrar restore may leave resolver slots — today's behaviour, and harmless for the same reason). The per-test re-scrub at `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:200` becomes unnecessary because a sibling's rows never enter any baseline.

Before / after per use case:

| use case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| hide my own `:rf.route/not-found` row; reinstate per test (5 suites) | `(def ^:private row (ts/sequester-app-registration! :route :rf.route/not-found "x.core"))` + `(ts/reinstate-app-registration! row)` in `init!` | `:app-ns "x."` |
| hide a sibling's whole tree; sibling reinstates per test (2 suites) | `sequester-app-namespaces! "realworld-http."` at load AND per test in one suite; `reinstate-app-namespaces!` in the other | `:app-ns "realworld-http."` in one, `:app-ns "realworld-resources."` in the other; neither names the other |
| in-body rival-"/" removal for one deftest (`linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs:296-330`) | `sequester-app-registration!` per rival, `reinstate-app-registration!` in `finally` | a LOCAL `defn-` in that test doing both legs (ownership-guarded registrar dissoc + `source-store/forget-descriptor!`) and `registrar/register!` in `finally`. Codex: an L1/L2 `snapshot-registrar` / `restore-registrar!` bracket touches only the resolver atom and would leave the source store mutated — both stores, always. It stays because its rivals can come from suites that do not self-hide. |
| own unit test (`sequester_app_registration_cljs_test.cljc`, 168 lines) | three rf2-22vzb guard cases on the pair | the same three cases as `:app-ns` cases in the fixture's own test |

## Corroboration

One-reviewer. Fable: "the cleanest proposal in the wave — ship it". Codex: "the four public bundle-hygiene verbs expose a real harness concern, and the memoized-prefix mechanism has a concrete weakness … the proposed `:app-ns` fixture option is not yet a complete or low-risk replacement" — with four gaps this bead answers explicitly: (1) repeated suites for one app → the prefix-keyed union above; (2) prefix ≠ one `[kind id provenance]` row → the single-row case is the prefix case with a narrower prefix, and the ownership guard means a sibling's live slot for a shared id is never touched; (3) the in-body fallback must restore both stores → the Linearlite rewrite names both legs; (4) the option ships only if a concrete implementation handles repeated suites, shared prefixes, late registration and coordinated restoration "without a new hidden global protocol" → the union registry is internal and prefix-keyed, and the regression matrix below is codex's own. Codex's preferred alternative — a repo-local, non-shipped helper holding an explicit captured app-descriptor value shared among an app's suites — is the fallback named under Risks.

## Deletion list

- `test_support.cljc`: `sequester-app-registration!` (:168), `reinstate-app-registration!` (:221), `sequestered-namespace-rows` (:231), `sequester-app-namespaces!` (:237), `reinstate-app-namespaces!` (:280). The ownership-guarded remover survives as a `defn-` for the fixture.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn:564,565,567,568` and `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1544-1547` (4 rows each) — regenerated, not hand-edited.
- `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md:89-181` ("Bundle co-load hygiene") → one `:app-ns` row in the `make-reset-runtime-fixture` opts table (:66-75).
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/sequester_app_registration_cljs_test.cljc` → folded into the fixture's test.

Net: `re-frame.test-support` returns to the shape the July sweep named (fixture + primitives + `poll-until` + `with-trace-recorder!` + `assert-path-equals`).

## Consumers to migrate (all `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/`; parallel-safe, no hot-zone)

- `infinite_feed_example_cljs_test.cljs:97,127`
- `linearlite_example_cljs_test.cljs:111,149` (+ the in-body bracket :296-330, above)
- `realworld_cljs_test.cljs:145,170-172` (drop the sibling-naming `reinstate-app-namespaces!`)
- `realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs:156,166,200-201` (drop both `sequester-app-namespaces! "realworld-http."` calls)
- `resources_example_cljs_test.cljs:104,134`

15 call sites, 5 suites. For each, read the existing third argument (`"linearlite.core"`, `"realworld-http.routing"`, `"realworld-resources.routing"`, …) and choose the prefix that covers the app's WHOLE tree (`"linearlite."`, `"realworld-http."`, …), not the one ns.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/008-Testing.md`: one sentence/row for `:app-ns` under the L3 rung (:271-284) or Pattern 5 (:192-215) — an addition, since the four vars were never rowed. NOT hot-zone.
- `spec/API.md`: UNTOUCHED (never rowed; the one-toucher file stays closed).
- `docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md` as above. Skills: `git grep -n sequester -- skills` → 0. Migration README: not v1-era. Conformance / mcp-conformance: unaffected.
- Manifest: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/` (four rows out; `:app-ns` is an option, not a var), then `--check` green.
- Tests to add (in the fixture's existing test ns — find it with `git grep -l make-reset-runtime-fixture -- implementation/core/test | grep -i 'test_support\|fixture'`), codex's matrix: two suites for one app (second fixture builds after the first removed the rows; both see the full app under test); two conflicting apps (a shared id such as `:rf.route/not-found` / `:settings/load`); reversed suite order; an absent requested prefix (true no-op, nothing touched, nil rows); exceptional teardown (test throws → store restored, app rows gone). Every case asserts BOTH registrar lookup AND default-image assembly (`make-frame {}` does not raise `:rf.error/image-duplicate-id`). Regression net: the five reagent example suites plus the four `example_realworld_*` / `example_frame_scoping` core suites in the consolidated bundle (`npm run test:cljs`, foreground, to completion).

## Sequencing and hot-zone

No hot-zone file. Independent of every registration bead and of @testing.2. One worker.

## Risks

Medium-low. The failure the vars guard is LOUD (`:rf.error/image-duplicate-id` at `make-frame {}`), and the example suites are the net. Prefix over-selection (`"realworld."` covering both twins) is the caller's and is documented as such. If the union model cannot pass the matrix WITHOUT a caller-visible protocol, STOP and report on the bead rather than shipping a second global — codex's fallback (a repo-local, non-shipped app-descriptor capture shared among an app's suites; the public names still go) is the alternative to bring back for a ruling.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: the four public bundle-hygiene verbs expose a real harness concern, and the memoized-prefix mechanism has a concrete weakness. The proposed `:app-ns` fixture option is not yet a complete or low-risk replacement.**

The diagnosis of hidden first-capture state is confirmed by [`sequester-app-namespaces!`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc) and the [boot-seed regression commentary](../../../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/example_realworld_resources_boot_seed_cljs_test.cljs): capture before an application's full namespace tree has loaded can permanently omit later registrations.

But moving capture into each fixture closure does not itself remove load-order coupling. ClojureScript loads a required namespace once. If suite A captures and removes an application's rows, suite B's later `:require` of that already-loaded app does not register them again. Suite B can capture an empty or incomplete set even though its own requires have finished. A per-fixture owner is therefore insufficient when multiple suites exercise the same app.

There are two further gaps:

- A prefix selector is not equivalent to selecting one `[kind id provenance]` row. It removes unrelated registrations under the same namespace and can affect suites sharing those definitions.
- The proposed in-body fallback does not restore everything it changes. `snapshot-registrar` and `restore-registrar!` touch only the resolver atom; `forget-descriptor!` mutates the separate source store. Wrapping that operation in a registrar snapshot bracket leaves image-visible source rows removed. Preserve both stores coherently or reinstate the captured descriptors through `registrar/register!`.

Consider the actual alternatives before adding a shipped fixture option:

1. Keep a small, **repo-local bundle helper** with an explicit captured app-descriptor value. Capture once at an app-support boundary after its complete registration graph loads; share that immutable value among its suites.
2. Use explicit app image selection for tests that do not need to test default-image assembly. This avoids treating every co-loaded app as part of one application, although suites exercising boot's default selection still need faithful isolation.
3. Put conflicting app integration suites in separate bundles. This costs runner setup but removes the collision instead of making global baseline choreography more sophisticated.
4. Add the fixture option only if a concrete implementation handles repeated suites, shared prefixes, late registration, and coordinated source-store/registrar restoration without a new hidden global protocol.

For the present, I favor the first approach: consolidate ownership locally and remove public names once the existing suites migrate. Do not promote a repository-specific multiplexing problem into every port's testing contract just to reduce the visible function count.

Keep setup ordering explicit. [`reset-runtime!`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc) installs an adapter and can establish a default frame; the [RealWorld resources setup](../../../../implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_resources_cljs_test.cljs) deliberately registers resource plans and stubs before creating its URL-bound frame. A new fixture path must preserve that ordering rather than merely reinstate rows somewhere before the test body.

A focused regression matrix is enough: two suites for one app, two conflicting apps, reversed suite order, an absent requested row, and exceptional teardown. Assert both registrar lookup and image assembly. This is useful harness repair, not a reason to invent a general namespace-ownership framework.

**Verdict: this was a useful simplification and is now substantially implemented. Preserve the resulting composition; do not turn the historical inventory into another cleanup campaign.**

Current [`test_helpers.cljc`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_helpers.cljc) no longer contains the redundant `wait-until`, `with-app-fixture`, `expect-text`, or event-sequence/whole-db helpers. [`test_support.cljc`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc) keeps `merge-registrar-snapshots` private and no longer exports `with-fresh-registrar`. The newer [test-isolation dossier](test-isolation-surface.md) is the relevant account of the remaining surface.

The central recommendation still reads well: reset the runtime with a fixture, inspect the view with small walkers, and wait through one bounded poll. Runtime-state support and view-tree inspection are different responsibilities; combining their namespaces would change names without simplifying the model. Likewise, `find-by-testid` earns its convenience role alongside generic attribute lookup. It serves the dominant readable form without concealing different behavior or lifecycle.

The original “sweep all hand-rolled fixtures” instruction needs its documented qualification. The remaining [Story counter fixture](../../../../tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/stories_cljs_test.cljs) restores a stable source-store baseline that contains the application registrations its selected images need. Its commentary records why replacing it with another namespace's incomplete baseline lost those registrations. Until the shared fixture can express that requirement straightforwardly, keeping this local bracket is better than either forcing the migration or growing a speculative fixture framework.

Raw registrar snapshots are also intentionally narrower than whole-runtime snapshots. They are appropriate for scoped resolver assertions, but must not be presented as undoing source-store changes. If a test mutates provenance descriptors or constructs images from them, its bracket needs the corresponding source-store restoration. That qualification belongs beside the primitive's teaching example, not in another public snapshot API unless a named consumer truly requires it.

For implementation today, the proportionate action is documentation status and recipe maintenance: identify this dossier's retired names as completed work, point remaining bundle-isolation work to its separate dossier, and retain one short example of the adopted fixture/walkers/poll composition. No new runtime change follows from this historical review alone.

If a future fixture consolidation is attempted, verify the test body actually executes on both hosts: the existing `:async?` option deliberately returns a CLJS map fixture but a JVM function fixture. Also check async teardown and exception cleanup rather than counting migrated files. These are the useful semantic boundaries; the precise count of helpers or local wrappers is not the quality target.

The Clojure lesson here is successful composition, not a universal ban on convenience functions. Stop once the supported pieces are understandable, orthogonal, and pleasant to use.

A PILE OF 'AWAITING RULING' BEADS IS NOT A BOTTLENECK UNTIL YOU COMPUTE THE blocks CLOSURE — COUNT WHAT EACH ONE GATES, NOT HOW MANY THERE ARE (measured 2026-09-05).

WHAT I BELIEVED AND SAID, IN A DISPATCH BRIEF: '24 open beads are parked awaiting an operator ruling. They are blocking the largest queue in the backlog — most of the rf2-kuky API-review family is behind them.'

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT SHOWED, over the transitive blocks closure across all 80 open beads: of the 25 items (my prose count was off by one), EXACTLY TWO gate any open work at all.

Those are different graph properties, and only the second one costs throughput. A backlog can hold thirty undispatchable items and still have every dispatchable item free.

THE INSTRUMENT: build the blocks closure from the dependency edges and count DEPENDENTS per held bead, then rank. Two cautions that bit the measurement itself: (i) 'bd show --json' returns an ARRAY and in that form dependency entries expose .id, NOT .depends_on_id — reading the wrong field reported 'null:null' on an edge that had actually landed; (ii) a text predicate over titles/notes for RULING|DECISION|OPERATOR over-matches (38 hits against a hand list of 25) AND under-matches — one genuine ruling bead carried no marker in any field and was invisible to text search entirely. title: xray: :rf.xray/set-target-frame reads a DESTROYED target frame's epoch history, emitting :rf.error/frame-destroyed once per Story variant mount
description:
Discovered by rf2-kuky.18 (PR #9306), which removed the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener. That claim had been MASKING these errors; with it gone they reach the console and `npm run test:story-feature-load` is RED at 8 console errors (a PR gate, test.yml:4127).

They are XRAY's, not Story's. A diagnostic :errors listener captured all eight records, identical in shape:

  {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed
   :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame
   :frame :rf/xray
   :source-coord {:ns day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch
                  :file "tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs" :line 108}}

MECHANISM. Xray holds a STALE TARGET FRAME across a Story variant switch. The :rf.xray/set-target-frame handler (epoch.cljs:108) evaluates (rf/epoch-history target) where target is the previously observed frame; Story has destroyed it, so the read recover-but-emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed. Once per variant mount, 8 across the feature-load run. The record is attributed to :frame :rf/xray, which is ALIVE - the destroyed frame is the READ TARGET, not the record's owning frame.

WHY THE rf2-kuky.18 SINK ARM CANNOT COVER IT. The new console-fallback predicate owns a record when its frame routed it to a registered :observability :errors sink. route-frame? is false for EVERY frame-destroyed emission (rf2-bf0io, so a dead incarnation's bare id can never resolve to a same-id successor's sink), so the route is suppressed and the delivered-count is necessarily 0. Giving :rf/xray an :observability :errors policy would NOT silence these. The fix has to be in Xray.

LIKELY FIX (not ruled). Either clear/repoint :target-frame when the targeted frame is destroyed, or guard the (rf/epoch-history target) read against an unresolved frame. The general case matters beyond Story: any app that destroys a frame Xray is targeting hits this. Do NOT fix it from the Story side - that would paper over it at the wrong layer and leave the general case broken.

SCOPE. tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/epoch.cljs plus the tools/xray/spec update every Xray dispatch carries. Needs a regression test.

SEQUENCING. PR #9306 should not merge until this lands, because test:story-feature-load is a per-PR gate and #9306 turns it red by revealing this.
notes:
WORKER xrayepoch-a, 2026-09-05. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9312 (open, ready for review). Branch worker/xrayepoch-a, rebased onto ba9b78acb1.

THIS BEAD DIAGNOSED THE WRONG MECHANISM. The description says Xray "reads (rf/epoch-history target) against the destroyed frame" and that "the record is attributed to :rf/xray, which is alive". Both halves are refuted at source, and the second is backwards.

REFUTATION AT SOURCE. rf/epoch-history -> re-frame.core-epoch/epoch-history (a defwrapper with :on-absent :empty-vec) -> late-bind :epoch/epoch-history -> re-frame.epoch/epoch-history -> re-frame.epoch.state/history-for, whose whole body is (or (get @histories frame-id) []). It consults NO frame registry, so it cannot raise :rf.error/frame-destroyed for any target, destroyed or otherwise.

WHERE THE RECORD ACTUALLY COMES FROM. router/emit-frame-destroyed! stamps :frame with the DISPATCH TARGET ((:frame envelope)), and error-emit/error-source-coord resolves a frame-destroyed :source-coord out of the [:event id] registry — i.e. the reg-event registration line. So {:frame :rf/xray, :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame, :source-coord epoch.cljs:108} reads: a dispatch of :rf.xray/set-target-frame into :rf/xray was rejected because :rf/xray IS THE MISSING FRAME. The coord names the handler, not the caller — which is exactly what made the record look like an epoch.cljs bug.

MEASURED, three-way probe on the node-test runner (probe deleted before the PR opened):
  A  :rf/xray ALIVE, read target DESTROYED  -> [] , nothing emitted   <- the bead claim, refuted
  B  :rf/xray ABSENT                        -> the exact field-report record
  C  :rf/xray DESTROYED                     -> the exact field-report record

THE REAL GENERAL CASE. Xray registers its whole :rf.xray/* instruction set at preload, but :rf/xray was created by open! — a React commit. In between, Xray is ADDRESSABLE BUT NOT WRITABLE: any dispatch into it recovers-but-emits, drops the host intent, and misattributes the diagnostic. A host that sets :rf.xray/auto-open? false (both Story testbeds do, in their run fns) never leaves that window until it opens a panel.

THE FIX. :rf/xray genuinely cannot be seated at preload LOAD time — rf/make-frame goes through rf.substrate.adapter/make-state-container, which raises :rf.error/no-adapter-installed with no adapter; that is what rf2-e9s81 reverted, and it is about the ADAPTER, not about opening. The preload already runs a bounded readiness loop watching for adapter install, so the seat moved there. auto-open-inline! -> boot-on-runtime-ready!; the open is now the conditional half. The first-mount seed/hydrate fan-out stays lazy behind seeded-frame-ids. Statement: Xrays frame exists as soon as the host runtime does, not when its UI opens. NOT a guard on the epoch read — probe A shows there is nothing there to guard, and a guard would have left the dropped-dispatch general case untouched while looking fixed.

EFFECT ON THE GATE, measured on ONE tree carrying both this change and #9306, against the SAME tree with this commit reverted (git revert, an exact counterfactual rather than a hand-plant):
  reverted:  97 frame-destroyed + 4 drain-depth-exceeded = 101 console errors, exit 1
  fixed:      2 frame-destroyed + 4 drain-depth-exceeded =   6 console errors, exit 1
Removed AT SOURCE, not masked: the regression test asserts the dispatch lands and core/target-frame reads back :app/main.

#9306 IS NOT UNBLOCKED BY THIS PR ALONE. The remaining 6 are two other defects, both outside this bead fence and both filed:
  rf2-88f1 (P2) — the residual 2. Story shell.cljs:406 hand-rolls (rf/with-frame :rf/xray (rf/dispatch-sync ...)) into another tools frame in the same breath as rf/init!, at t=546.9ms / t=561.9ms, inside the readiness polls 50ms window. No Xray-side change reaches it.
  rf2-chs7 (P2) — the 4 drain-depth-exceeded. Xrays own :rf.xray/epoch-recorded fan-out floods :rf/xray queue (:queue-size 101, :depth 100) under the 20-event load; identical count in BOTH columns, so pre-existing and unrelated.
The rf2-kuky.18 MAYOR HOLD note should be read against this: its close condition (story-feature-load passes on a tree carrying both) needs all three beads, not just this one.

ALSO NOTE, for whoever re-measures: the discovering worker counted 8 console errors on base f61402a652; on base 85d7b49fe5 the same tree counts 101. The trunk moved. Re-measure rather than comparing to a quoted figure.

GATES (captured exit codes, final base ba9b78acb1): node-test compile 0 with 0 warnings; node run 0 (11275 tests / 56928 assertions, 0 failures); test:browser 0 (786 / 4311, 0 failures); test:examples-compile 0 (all 58 swept builds); test-jvm-tools.sh 0; test:mcp-conformance 0 (6/6 default profile); test:xray-feature-gate:smoke 0 (5 scenarios, 10 matrix rows); test:story-play-scripts 0 (31 rows); test:story-feature-load 0 ON THIS BRANCH (the mask is still on main, so this is the required per-PR gate rather than the acceptance measurement above); check_doc_slugs.py 0; check_readme_links.py --ci 0. Surfaces derived from report-changed-surfaces.sh over the changed PATHS: cljs_node_test, cljs_browser, examples_compile, tools_jvm, mcp_conformance, story_xray_browser (story_full_gate FALSE, so CI will skip test:story-feature-load on this PR exactly as it did on #9306).

PRE-FIX RED: planting the seat removal on the committed tree gives 6 failures, all in the new namespace, the first naming the field-report record verbatim. Restored, blob 7bf43b6676de38dd2a4bd7715df604737e1cd97d identical before and after. The control deftest stayed green under the plant, as it must.
close_reason:
Merged as PR #9312 (rebased onto main at 3efb9a7d76). Five clauses met at band 87: 87 total, 37 success + 50 skipped, zero failures, zero non-terminal; 4 runs at full head oid all completed/success; workflows diff 0 lines.

THE BEAD'S OWN MECHANISM WAS REFUTED, and the refutation is the valuable part. rf/epoch-history resolves to re-frame.epoch.state/history-for = (or (get @histories frame-id) []) — a ring lookup consulting no frame registry, so it CANNOT emit frame-destroyed. The record only looked like an epoch.cljs bug because router/emit-frame-destroyed! stamps :frame with the DISPATCH TARGET and resolves :source-coord from the [:event id] registry, i.e. the reg-event line rather than the failing expression. A three-way node-test probe settled it: target-destroyed-but-xray-alive produced NOTHING; :rf/xray absent, and :rf/xray destroyed, each produced the exact field-report record. The destroyed frame was Xray's OWN and it was the dispatch target.

FIX: Xray registered its whole instruction set at preload but created :rf/xray in open! (a React commit), leaving it addressable but not writable in between. The seat moved to the preload's existing adapter-readiness poll (auto-open-inline! -> boot-on-runtime-ready!); the open became the conditional half. Guarding the epoch read was explicitly REJECTED — the probe shows nothing there to guard, and it would have left the dropped-dispatch general case broken while looking fixed.

title: api(resources): fold install-/remove-revalidation-listeners! into a :revalidate-on frame-config key owned by the frame lifecycle
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from resources.md (ref resources.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Focus/reconnect revalidation is spelled as an imperative pair the app must sequence by hand: `(rf/install-revalidation-listeners! frame-id)` AFTER the render that created the frame, and `(rf/remove-revalidation-listeners! frame-id)` to stop. Routing already folded the identical shape (`install-url-listener!` / `remove-url-listener!` / `install-history-listener!`) into a frame-config key, `:url-bound? true`, with no shim (commit `5b9bab33fa`, "API-shrink #6"): creation installs, re-registration reconciles, destroy removes, and no function exists to call. Resources uses only the destroy half of that lifecycle (`:resources/on-frame-destroyed!`) and leaves install/remove to the app.

The cost is visible in the ONLY consumer: `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs` carries a 12-line comment (`:295–296`, `:326–334`) explaining that the call at `:335` "has to run AFTER the render that created it, never before" and that re-running on hot reload "never stacks" — ordering knowledge the `:url-bound? true` key on the SAME opts map (`:319–325`) already carries for free. `remove-revalidation-listeners!` has zero consumers outside its own test file. The manifest sidecar records the verb pair as unresolved against the Lifecycle-verb law (`spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1031–1036`; rf2-uimu); the fold dissolves the question — the answer to "which verb" is "no verb".

## Evidence (HEAD `6445d0611b`)

Census, one `git grep -n -E "(install|remove)-revalidation-listeners!"` over `examples tools testbeds docs skills spec migration implementation`, 62 lines:

| Root | Lines | Where |
|---|---|---|
| examples | 2 | `realworld_resources/core.cljs:295` (comment), `:335` (the one call) |
| tools / testbeds | 0 | — |
| implementation src | 25 | `core.cljc:1529,1532,1535`; `core_resources.cljc:75–99`; `late_bind/directory.cljc:640–648`; `resources.cljc:141–148,708–709`; `resources/revalidate_listeners.cljc:32,144,199–222,241`; `scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:559` (comment) |
| implementation test | 4 | `resources/test/re_frame/resources_revalidation_cljs_test.cljc:368,436,460,485` |
| docs | 16 | `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1631–1641`; `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:16,308–343`; `docs/resources/coming-from-tanstack-query.md:27,191`; `docs/resources/concepts.md:248` |
| skills | 1 | `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:101` |

## Target API

```clojure
;; revalidation is a FRAME property, like URL ownership. No fns.
(rf/make-frame {:id :app :url-bound? true :revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}})
[rf/frame-root {:id app-frame :url-bound? true :revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}} [root-view]]
```

Contract:
- `:revalidate-on` is an optional frame-config key: a SET drawn from the closed enum `#{:focus :reconnect}`. `:focus` = window `focus` AND document `visibilitychange`→visible (ONE setting — codex: not two public settings); `:reconnect` = window `online`.
- Absent key, or `#{}` → no host listeners. An explicit empty set is a legitimate "none".
- First registration: after the container is live (the same hook point routing uses), install exactly the selected subset. The installer must honour the subset (today it installs all three).
- Re-registration (a deliberate `make-frame` / `frame-root` against an existing id — the surgical update, `spec/002-Frames.md:824`): reconcile, replace-don't-stack. A re-registration WITHOUT the key removes the listeners (the `:url-bound? false` relinquish rule, `url_bound.cljc:100–108`). Repeated `frame-root` renders with identical opts cause no listener churn. An incidental ensure/dispatch is never a configuration update (codex).
- Destroy: unchanged — `:resources/on-frame-destroyed!` removes.
- JVM / SSR / no-DOM hosts: inert (the CLJS arm is the only installer; a JVM `:revalidate-on` config registers with no listener-table entry).
- Validation: a non-set value or an unknown member fails LOUD at registration with zero residue (no frame registered; a failed re-registration preserves every committed value), via the same preflight seam routing uses. A config declaring `:revalidate-on` while `re-frame.resources` is not loaded fails loud with the existing `:rf.error/resources-artefact-missing` (mirror of the `:url-strategy`-without-routing rule at `frame.cljc:3238–3247`). Name the malformed-value id `:rf.error/invalid-revalidate-on` (sibling of `:rf.error/invalid-url-strategy`) and add its 009 catalogue row.

title: RULING: ##NaN vs NaN stringification on non-presence attributes — spec/004B contradicts itself and the repair feeds the render-tree hash
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the ssrhtml-a worker while landing rf2-u82a (PR #9286). Reported and deliberately NOT fixed, because the repair touches a hash input and 004B points two ways. This bead is the ruling that needs making.

THE OBSERVATION, measured against react-dom 19.2.0. On NON-presence attribute classes, re-frame2 emits `download="##NaN"` and `title="##NaN"` where react-dom emits `="NaN"`. Both re-frame2 hosts (JVM and CLJS) agree with each other, so the `##` prefix is self-consistent rather than a platform split — it is a deliberate spelling, not a bug in one host.

WHY IT IS A RULING AND NOT A REPAIR. spec/004B contains two passages that point opposite ways:
  - one says the emitter uses "JavaScript spellings", which argues for `NaN`;
  - one says "`##NaN` is not data ... rejected at the site that recorded them", which argues the `##` form is the deliberate canonical spelling and the value should never have reached the attribute at all.
Both are in the same document. Whichever way this is ruled, one of those passages needs amending, which is itself a spec edit on a hot-zone page.

AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS WHY A WORKER SHOULD NOT DECIDE IT. The repair touches `canonical-number`, WHICH FEEDS THE RENDER-TREE HASH. A change there is not a rendering tweak: it changes hash inputs, so it can move every recorded hash in the corpus and anything pinned against them. Establish that blast radius before proposing a fix — count what pins a render-tree hash today, with a control.

THE THREE OPTIONS, as I read them:
  (a) EMIT `NaN` on these classes, matching react-dom. Smallest visible change; but if `canonical-number` is the only place to do it, it is not small underneath.
  (b) KEEP `##NaN` and amend the "JavaScript spellings" passage to name this exception. Zero code change, and defensible if the `##` form is genuinely canonical — a deliberate divergence with precedent, exactly as 004B already records for `value`.
  (c) REFUSE THE VALUE AT THE RECORDING SITE, which is what the second passage literally says should already happen. Largest change, and the only one that makes the contradiction go away rather than choosing a side of it.

RELEVANT PRECEDENT, already settled and worth not re-litigating: spec/011-SSR.md rules byte-for-byte HTML equality explicitly OUT, permitting differences in "boolean-attribute spelling". So react-dom parity is NOT in itself a reason to prefer (a) — the project has already said it is not held to byte-parity. What decided the SIBLING case (rf2-u82a, PR #9286) was not parity but the 004B class contract: an attribute being PRESENT WHEN IT MUST BE ABSENT is not a spelling difference. `##NaN` versus `NaN` on a non-presence attribute IS a spelling difference, which is the strongest single argument for (b).

STANCE BEARING: "don't litigate the minutiae" and "trust the programmer" both point at (b) — a self-consistent spelling on both hosts, in a place no consumer has complained about, is a candidate for dying with its reasoning recorded. Against that, "fail closed, fail loudly" and the second 004B passage point at (c). What is NOT defensible is leaving the two passages contradicting each other, whichever code path stands.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING: every claim above is the reporting worker's or mine. Re-read both 004B passages at tip and quote them; confirm both hosts really do agree; confirm `canonical-number` really is the shared path and really does feed the hash.

FENCE if this is dispatched after a ruling: the code half is `implementation/ssr/**`. The spec half is `spec/004B` — HOT-ZONE and single-toucher, so sequence it against whoever holds that file, and do NOT bundle the two halves into one worker unless the ruling makes them one change.

AT TIP aa3c616e46, spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:
  :234  "`-0.0` renders `"0"`; `NaN` and the infinities take their JavaScript spellings."
  :318-324  "And `##NaN` is not data either, because the promise is that the tree prints and reads back **equal**: `##NaN` is the one value that survives print/read while never comparing equal to itself, so a tree carrying one is not equal to itself -- and the tree is an equality input ... Both are rejected exactly as any other non-data value is, at the site that recorded them."

NEITHER PASSAGE ENDORSES `##NaN`. :234 names the JavaScript spelling, which is `NaN`. :324 says a NaN never reaches the tree at all, because it is refused where it was recorded. This description reads :318-324 as arguing "the `##` form is the deliberate canonical spelling"; the passage says the opposite — that `##NaN` is NOT DATA. So option (b) — keep `##NaN` and amend the JavaScript-spellings passage — is the ONE option no 004B sentence supports.

THE ANSWER 004B ALREADY IMPLIES is option (c): refuse the value at the recording site. And spec/011-SSR.md's byte-parity-out ruling independently removes react-dom parity as a reason for (a) — which this description already says.

title: api(registry): write the registrar fx-form rule into Conventions (frame-scoped, positional args verbatim)
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref spellings.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Two registrars have fx forms, and they disagree on shape:

| fx | where | args |
|---|---|---|
| `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` | `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:992` / `:1003` | the registrar's positional triple `[flow-id metadata derive-fn]` / the id, verbatim |
| `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` / `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor` | `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc:226-244` / `:247-260` | a re-spelled MAP `{:id :before :after :frame}` / `{:id :frame}` |

No written rule says WHICH registrars get an fx form or what SHAPE its args take. `spec/013-Flows.md:425-447` gives the flows mechanism (a handler cannot call a registrar because that is an effect; the fx threads the dispatching frame in as `:frame`, :447). `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` §Middleware (:827 ff.) has no fx rationale at all. `spec/Conventions.md:478-482` places the flows pair under `:rf.fx/*` as a "single principled exception" — a NAMING rule, not an existence rule. The only stated reason for the http pair is a source comment (`managed.cljc:222-225`: "a clean alternative to the fn-call shape for codebases that prefer to drive bootstrap through the dispatch surface"). The data form and the fn form of one registration disagree on shape, and nothing says they must not.

## Evidence

- Flows fx, handler-time consumers: `examples/core/flows/core.cljs:162` (`[:rf.fx/reg-flow …]` feature gate) and `:178` (`[:rf.fx/clear-flow :cart/discount-rate]`); `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:302`. A designed dual with a mechanism discriminator (013:447).
- Http fx: `git grep -n -E ':rf\.fx/(reg|clear)-http-interceptor' -- examples testbeds tools ':!**/test/**'` → nothing. Both shipped http examples register at boot with the macro (`examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:445`, `realworld_resources/core.cljs:358`). Consumers are `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:880-1030` and the conformance corpus (`spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn`, `http-interceptor-clear.edn`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc:267-380`, `spec/conformance/README.md:539-540`).

## Target

One paragraph in `spec/Conventions.md`, in the reserved-fx-ids section beside the `:rf.fx/*` carve-out (:478-482), with its own heading so 013 and 014 can anchor to it:

> **When a registrar has an fx form.** An fx form exists for a registrar only when the registrar is frame-scoped — the effect threads the dispatching frame in as `:frame` — and a handler-time registration has a named consumer. Its args are the registrar's positional argument vector, verbatim: the effect is `(apply reg-x args)` with the frame threaded, and the fx form never re-spells the registrar's arguments. Members: `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow` (013 §Dynamic toggle via fx).

Plus, until @spellings.3 Q3 is ruled, ONE sentence: "`:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` / `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor` carry map args and have no shipped handler-time consumer; their disposition is open under <@spellings.3's id>." The ruling's implementation bead deletes or rewrites that sentence.

Cross-pointers (not hot-zone): `spec/013-Flows.md:425-447` cites the rule; `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` §Middleware gains one sentence beside its fx mention pointing at the rule; `managed.cljc:222-225` comment cites the rule instead of restating its own rationale.

Do NOT delete, reshape or re-document the http pair here — @spellings.3 Q3.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer. Codex agrees a written rule is the missing piece and corrects one clause: "HTTP interceptors ARE frame-scoped and their effects deliberately carry the dispatching frame. They satisfy that half of the proposed rule; what is absent is a shipped handler-time consumer." The paragraph above is written so both statements are true at tip.

## Deletion list

None.

## Consumers to migrate

None.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/Conventions.md` (HOT-ZONE): the paragraph. `spec/013-Flows.md`, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md`: one pointer each. `spec/API.md`: untouched.
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc:222-225`: comment.
- No manifest change (no var moves). No skills change (`skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:86` documents the http fx as it is; leave for Q3).
- Gates: `mkdocs build --strict` (spec/ staged by the hook) and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the new anchor; the paragraph is prose, so verify the anchor and the 013/014 links by hand and say so in the PR body.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Conventions.md is HOT-ZONE — serialise AFTER @spellings.1 (which rewrites the adjacent Convention-A / `*` tables). Not blocked by @spellings.3: the rule is tip-true; the ruling edits one sentence.

## Risks

Prose only. The one way to get it wrong is to write the consumer clause as if the http pair already failed it — that is the ruling's to say.

title: hic: RULING — a bead id in the design corpus is provenance, not a live pointer (rf2-wx96 census)
description:
Filed by rf2-wx96's census (2026-09-04, main@cf4a98a084). The census is taken; what is left is one ruling on (a) versus (b), which rf2-wx96 says is Mike's call.

THE CENSUS, across docs/design/. 86 distinct rf2-hic-NNN ids in 1,181 citations. FIVE resolve in the tracker: rf2-hic-051, -063, -064, -088, -090 (four closed, rf2-hic-063 open). Probed both ways: bd show rf2-hic-038 returns "no issue found", bd show rf2-hic-064 resolves. Two of the 86 - rf2-hic-9001 and rf2-hic-9002 - are correction-ledger.md's deliberately fictional worked-example ids and were never beads.

THE MEASUREMENT rf2-wx96 DID NOT HAVE, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION. The ids were REAL and the citations were VALID when written. The tracker export at 63a3d44086 (2026-08-16) carries NINETY rf2-hic-NNN values as .id. The drop is between 1246e4e422 (2026-08-31, still 90) and dc88bc6aae (2026-09-02, 5).

AND IT IS NOT SPECIFIC TO THIS CORPUS. Comparing the whole id set at 1246e4e422 against tip: 1,145 ids then, 935 now, 848 gone - of which 85 are rf2-hic-* and 763 are not. So this is a general tracker compaction with a visible face in the hicasso corpus, not a hicasso bookkeeping defect, and EVERY closed bead id cited anywhere in the repository is subject to the same disappearance.

WHY THAT DECIDES (a) VERSUS (b) ON THE EVIDENCE. Option (b), "live owner references needing a mapping", cannot be sustained: it would require the design corpus to track a tracker that compacts, and the mapping would be 848 ids wide rather than 60. The surviving convention already reads the other way - the derivative beads that outlive a programme item carry hic-NNN in their TITLE and an ordinary rf2-<slug> id of their own (rf2-w01c is "hic-036 clock driver: ...", rf2-85og2 is "hic-071 remainder: ..."), and the five ids that DO resolve are all titled "hic-NNN - <name>", so id and title-prefix agree only where the bead survives.

RECOMMENDED RULING (a): a bead id in a design record is a PROVENANCE CITATION - the name of the bead under which a change was made - and not a resolvable pointer. Consequences if ruled: requirements-mine.md's "How to read a row" defines Owner as "the bead accountable for carrying the answer to done", which reads as resolvable and would need one sentence saying it need not be; the maintenance rules gain a rule for what a dead owner-id means; and the passes stop treating ids as look-ups, so a dead id is not a finding. What stays a finding is a row asserting a STATUS the tracker contradicts, which only binds ids the tracker still holds.

NOT DONE HERE, AND DELIBERATELY: no id was repointed. rf2-wx96 rules a mechanical repoint out as guesswork and that judgement stands - the compaction figures above make it worse, not better.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one ruling on (a) versus (b). If (a), the wording lands on requirements-mine.md's maintenance rules and its "How to read a row" table.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE STANDING BEADS-GC INSTRUCTION, BOTH DATA-LOSS-ADJACENT, MEASURED 2026-09-06 FROM --help AND DRY RUNS.

(1) `bd gc` PHASE 1 'DECAY' *IS* A PRUNE (default 90 days). The recurring GC instruction describes gc as 'decay old issues, compact Dolt commits, run Dolt GC' and describes prune separately as the deleting one — which reads as though gc is the safe verb and prune the dangerous one. They are not disjoint: running `bd gc` without `--skip-decay` DELETES closed beads. **`--skip-decay` is mandatory on this project**, where close reasons are normative records and bead ids are cross-file citations. With --skip-decay, gc's phase 2 is informational only (it prints 'use bd flatten to squash') and phase 3 is DOLT_GC(), neither of which deletes a bead.

(2) `bd restore` DOES NOT RECOVER FROM `bd compact`. The instruction says 'note bd restore exists to recover a compacted issue's pre-compaction content', which invites treating `bd compact` as reversible. It is not. `bd restore` pairs with `bd admin compact` (semantic summarisation that discards original bead text). Plain `bd compact` is a Dolt COMMIT squash — it cherry-picks survivors and SWAPS MAIN — and is irreversible; anything landing in the swap window is discarded.

THIRD FACT THAT DECIDES THE WHOLE TASK ON THIS INSTALL: Dolt runs EMBEDDED (in-process), not as a server — every `bd` invocation is its own OS process sharing .beads/embeddeddolt/.dolt/noms. Dolt's GC safepoint protocol is per-SERVER, and there is no server, so DOLT_GC() rewriting the chunk store while another process writes is a CORRUPTION path rather than mere lock contention. **Every compaction/GC verb is therefore fleet-zero work**, not something to run while workers hold beads.

AND THE PAYOFF IS SMALL, IN THE SAME SHAPE AS THE PRUNE PREMISE: `bd compact --dry-run` reads 16,441 Dolt commits of which only 1,785 are older than 30 days — an 11% reduction. At 150-200 tracker commits a day, recent history dominates, exactly as recent closures dominate the closed-bead population.

WHERE THE SPACE ACTUALLY IS (.beads = 6.2 GB): the live database is 472 MB of noms, i.e. 7.6%. 5.0 GB is .beads/backup/ — of which ~2.5 GB is an ORPHANED quarantine directory local-diverged-remnant-20260803-095318/ left by a 2026-08-03 divergence recovery. **No bd verb reaches it**; it is a filesystem delete and the single biggest safe win. Another 685 MB is a regenerable git-remote-cache.

TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT MISREPORT HERE, both exit 0 with a reassuring answer: `bd admin compact --dolt` probes .beads\dolt, which does not exist on this install (the real directory is .beads\embeddeddolt, per `bd dolt show`), and prints 'No local Dolt directory found; nothing to collect' — reading as 'already tidy' having never looked. And `bd doctor --check artifacts`, the only bd-native cruft cleaner, prints 'not yet supported in embedded mode'. So there is no working isolated Dolt-GC verb on this install.

`gh pr view --json ... > file` CAN FAIL ITS **WRITE** AND LEAVE AN EMPTY FILE, AND THE DOWNSTREAM jq THEN REPORTS BLANK FIELDS THAT READ LIKE 'THIS PR HAS NO CHECKS' (measured twice, 2026-09-06).

WHAT HAPPENED. In two consecutive merge ticks, a loop of `gh pr view <n> --json number,headRefOid,isDraft,headRefName,statusCheckRollup > /tmp/k<n>.json` failed for the SAME two PRs (#9306, #9316) while succeeding for a third (#9317) in the same loop. The shell reported `jq: error: Could not open file ...: Invalid argument` on stderr, and the formatted row printed with every field EMPTY:
  #9306 draft=      total=    ok=    skip=    FAIL=   PEND=
An immediate manual retry of the identical command exited 0 and wrote 27,145 bytes, and `gh api rate_limit` read 5000 remaining — so gh was healthy and this is transient, not an outage or a throttle.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN ANNOYING. The merge criterion's clause 1 is 'a NON-EMPTY rollup in the band measured this tick'. A blank read is not a rollup at all, but formatted into a table beside real rows it looks like a PR that simply has no checks yet — i.e. 'not a candidate, skip it'. That fails SAFE for merging (you skip a PR you could have merged) but fails OPEN for reporting: I would have told Mike a green PR was still building. And the failure is INTERMITTENT and correlated with the LARGER payloads, so the PRs most likely to be affected are the ones with the fullest rollups — exactly the merge candidates.

THE TELL, AND IT IS THE ONLY RELIABLE ONE: blank is not zero. A PR with genuinely no checks yet returns total=0, not total=<empty>. Print the write's EXIT STATUS beside each row (`> file; w=$?`) and treat any non-zero as 'unmeasured', never as 'nothing there'. A count of 0 and an empty string must never format identically.

THE FIX: skip the intermediate file. Read the fields directly with gh's own jq:
  gh pr view <n> --repo <o/r> --json statusCheckRollup -q '[.statusCheckRollup[]] | "total=\(length) ok=\([.[]|select(.conclusion=="SUCCESS")]|length) fail=\([.[]|select(.conclusion=="FAILURE" or .conclusion=="CANCELLED")]|length) pend=\([.[]|select(.status!="COMPLETED")]|length)"'
That removed the failure entirely on the same two PRs in the same shell. If a file IS needed (e.g. to query the same payload several ways), write it under the session scratchpad rather than /tmp, check the exit status, and re-read on non-zero.

SAME FAMILY AS THE REST: an instrument whose FAILURE is indistinguishable from a legitimate answer. jq's CRLF joins, `grep -iF` aborting to an empty stdout, `grep -P` refusing in this locale, `bd` swallowing a while-loop's stdin, a skipped CI step inside a green job — every one hands back something that reads like data.

A SESSION RATE LIMIT KILLS EVERY BACKGROUND WORKER AT ONCE, AND THEIR WORK IS RECOVERABLE — DO NOT REDISPATCH, PUSH THEN RESUME (measured 2026-09-06).

WHAT HAPPENED. Four workers died within seconds of each other on HTTP 429 'session limit'. Each notification carried a partial last line ('Now smoke_test.clj', 'Now fix the double-deref in the seeding test', 'Now the doc gates and CLJS'), which is the tell that they were mid-task rather than finishing.

FIRST MEASURE, DO NOT REDISPATCH. Redispatching would have thrown away 14 commits and three files of finished edits. The state per worktree, taken from the WORKTREE list per loops.md S4:
  attrgate-a   clean tree, 2 substantive commits, 6 UNPUSHED
  ssrdel-a     clean tree, 5 substantive commits, 8 UNPUSHED
  machtest-a   3 files modified, ZERO commits  <- most at risk
  xraydrain-a  clean, 1 commit, nothing unpushed, junction left in place
So the loop's own remedy applies: 'push existing commits, reopen with a note, redispatch' — and the push is the urgent half, because a second kill loses uncommitted and unpushed work alike.

THE PUSH FAILS NON-FAST-FORWARD, AND THAT IS EXPECTED. A worker that rebased before dying leaves its branch DIVERGED from its own remote (local ahead N, remote ahead M). A plain push is refused.

TWO TRAPS IN THE RECOVERY, both of which I hit:
(1) I ran `git push ... 2>&1 | tail -2` and read 'push exit: 0'. THAT WAS TAIL'S EXIT STATUS. The push had been REJECTED. Piping a mutating git command through a filter reports the filter's status — the identical hazard CLAUDE.md records for the beads durability sequence, reached through a different door. Never pipe a push, a merge, a rebase or a checkpoint.
(2) The reflex on a rejected push is --force. Prove it is safe FIRST:
      git -C <worktree> cherry HEAD origin/worker/<name>
    Lines prefixed '+' are commits on the REMOTE that are NOT patch-present locally — i.e. work that a force-push would destroy. A count of 0 means the local branch is a rebased superset and forcing loses nothing. Both branches read 0 here; only then did I push, with --force-with-lease, unpiped, and read the real exit code.

WHAT NOT TO DO: never force-push main, and never force a worker branch on which the cherry check shows '+'. In that case the remote carries something local does not, and the right move is to hand it back to the worker.

THEN RESUME RATHER THAN RESPAWN. SendMessage to the same agentId restores its full context — a fresh dispatch starts from nothing and re-does the work. Resume in value order and CHECK THE FIRST ONE LIVES before sending the rest: if the limit is still in force the agent dies immediately and you learn it for the cost of one message instead of four. Tell each worker exactly what you did to its branch, quote the verification, and quote its own last words back so it knows where it stopped.

AND TELL IT WHAT DID NOT CHANGE. Trunk had not moved, and no fence had shifted; saying so explicitly stops a resumed worker re-deriving the world. A worker killed mid-gate also has no idea whether its junction survived — say so, because a second junction created over a live one is how the mayor's node_modules gets emptied.

title: api(observability): configure! {:observability …} process default + frameless/unresolved-owner routing
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:23:54 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.22 ruling (delegated by Mike). RULING on rf2-kuky.22: **A — one production observation door.** This is bead **A1**, SECOND of the fixed chain A0 (rf2-kuky.65) → A1 → A2 (id appended below). The full ruling — the seven routing answers, Codex's three distinctions and how they were weighed, the drift table — is the RULING note on rf2-kuky.22; the dossier is attached to it verbatim. Line numbers below are from the dossier's tip `6d513ba07f` unless marked (desc) = the description's HEAD `6445d0611b`; re-measure at dispatch._

## Problem

Production observation is declared per FRAME only: `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame` / `frame-root` and `configure!` (`core.cljc:2620`) has no such key. Consequences: a multi-frame app restates its Sentry policy on every frame; and three producers emit records with `:frame nil` that NO frame policy can route, so today they reach only the corpus-wide `register-listener! :errors` stream — the door A2 retires. Retiring it before this bead exists opens a gap where those records reach nobody; the ordering A1 → A2 is structural, not a preference.

The frameless producers, verified at tip:
1. `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:804-952` (`no-frame-context-payload` `:834`, `emit-no-frame-context!` `:906`): by construction there is no frame to stamp.
2. The pre-frame SSR hydration-parse arm of `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` — `error_emit.cljc:815-830` documents the union shape's `:frame <id-or-nil>` "(the pre-frame hydration-parse FRAMELESS case …)"; the late-bind entry `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` (`late_bind/directory.cljc:902`) names it.
3. hicasso `compute-sub` errors — `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:221-222`: "`:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION"; its `watch-recovered-errors!` (`:254-295`) registers on `:errors` for exactly this reason (the per-frame SSR buffer read CLEAN on the failure it exists to catch).

The sink route refuses them by design: `route-error-record!` is a no-op when `:frame` is unresolved, "incl. the FRAMELESS `:frame nil` records" (`observability.cljc:322-324`); `frame-observability` (`:150-157`) returns nil on a nil id; `error_emit.cljc:909` repeats it at the call site.

A second dependency underneath: "project under NO frame" is not expressible today — `elision.cljc:1128` resolves the governing frame as `(or (:frame opts) (rf.frame/resolve-current-frame))`, so an explicit nil falls through to the AMBIENT frame, and `projection.cljc:572-575` seeds `:frame` from the record by truthiness the same way. rf2-kuky.5 makes explicit nil fail closed. This bead is blocked on it.

## Target

```clojure
;; Declared once per process, or per frame — the same closed entry grammar
;; (Spec-Schemas.md FrameSinkEntry, minus :opts per rf2-kuky.17).
(rf/configure! {:observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry}]}})       ;; process default
(rf/make-frame {:id :admin
                :observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/public-error}]}})
(rf/register-observability-sink! :app/sentry (fn [projected-record] …))
```

Routing rules — RULED on rf2-kuky.22, implement verbatim:
- **Q1 Precedence, per STREAM.** A frame that declares a stream (even `[]`) uses its own entries for that stream; a frame that omits the stream inherits the default's entries for it. Whole-map replacement is rejected.
- **Q2 Absent vs empty.** `[]` on a frame is the opt-out; `(rf/configure! {:observability nil})` clears the default. Validation reuses `frame_classification.cljc`'s validator (`:205-260` desc) at call time, fail-loud, `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` with `:where 'rf/configure!` — no new category. NOT an `assert`: rf2-xn13 is closed and the runtime `when-not` / `throw-error!` guard at `core.cljc:2668-2683` is the model.
- **Q3 Frameless (`:frame nil`).** Process default ONLY; projected with the governing frame EXPLICITLY nil → `spec/015:251` case 3 (tree slots `:rf/redacted`, summary ids intact).
- **Q4 Records whose `:frame` no longer resolves** (destroyed frame, dissociated incarnation, exact-incarnation teardown report). Route to the PROCESS DEFAULT under fail-closed projection exactly as Q3; the stale `:frame` id is KEPT in the summary as a diagnostic. NEVER consult any frame's policy for such a record and NEVER re-resolve the stale id — a same-id successor is not the owner (`015:296`). **Producer-seam trap (Codex):** `error_emit.cljc:614` and `dispatch-error-record*` (`:859`) gate the WHOLE late-bound sink call on `route-frame?`, so a fallback added only inside `observability.cljc` is never reached for these records. `route-frame? false` must come to mean "no frame authority — process default still delivers", not "no sink route". Also `frame-observability` (`:150-157`) cannot distinguish "never registered" from "dissociated"; do not add an unresolved-id test that a successor would pass — carry the authority bit from the producer. `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc`'s pin (dissociated id must not reach a same-id successor's sink) STANDS and gains a sibling asserting process-default delivery of the same record under a live, unrelated ambient frame.
- **Q5 Duplicate delivery.** Exactly ONE policy source per record per stream; a sink id present in both the frame's entries and the default's is invoked once.
- **Q6 Raw cross-frame hook.** An explicit `{:sink … :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/local-raw}` entry on the process default (enum member: `projection.cljc:91-97`, `015:264`). A projection profile on the `:rf.observe/*` record — not the substrate record.
- **Q7 Console fallback.** Composes with rf2-kuky.18: a process-default delivery to a REGISTERED sink owns the record; an entry naming an unregistered sink does not.
- Do NOT add an "additive global observer" beside the frame policy to recover corpus-wide parity — that is a third routing model. Q1–Q5 are the model.

## Change list

Code:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` `configure!` (`:2620`; `:2554-2605` desc) — gains `:observability`; docstring; delegates to a `re-frame.observability/configure!` over a `defonce` default atom; `current-config` is the boot/config area's (rf2-kuky.4), not this bead's — but if `current-config` lands first, the default must show in it.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc` — the default atom + `configure!`; `frame-observability` resolves PER STREAM against the default; `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` / `route-handled-event!` gain the frameless + unresolved-owner arms; the duplicate-delivery rule; a `clear-*` for fixtures beside `clear-observability-sinks!` (fixture-tier, `core.cljc:2184-2194` desc is the pattern — do not export a facade `clear-*`, `Conventions.md:1327-1331`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc` `:614-619`, `:859-865` — the producer seam for Q4 (see trap).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc` — validator reused at `configure!` time.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc` / `elision.cljc` — nothing beyond what rf2-kuky.5 lands; if .5 has not landed, STOP and wait.

Spec (HOT-ZONE marked):
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270-302` — process default, per-stream precedence, frameless routing, unresolved-owner rule, duplicate rule.
- `spec/API.md` §Configure keys (`:895-935`) + the `:873` row (desc) + §Frame-owned sinks (`:699-706`) — HOT-ZONE. A new `configure!` key is a Spec change by the fixed-and-additive rule (`API.md` §Fixed-and-additive) — additive, fine.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` — the configure `:observability` shape beside FrameSinkEntry (`:4341-4350`) — HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:647-659` — one sentence on inheritance — HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` — the configure key row, then regenerate.

Conformance: one new fixture beside `spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-observability-sink-receives-projected-record.edn` (default routes; frameless record projects fail-closed; frame policy wins per stream; `[]` opts out).

Tests: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc`, `non_event_observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc`, `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc`, `configure_test.clj`. Codex's list: default inheritance vs `[]`; registered / missing / throwing sinks; stale-owner fallback under a live unrelated ambient frame; frameless record reaches the default and no frame's sink.

Docs / skills (after rf2-kuky.21 — .21 owns the teaching ORDER; this bead adds the declare-once form): `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md` §1 (the `configure!` form beside the frame form), `docs/core/observability.md:481-506`, `docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md:140-143`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md:1-17`, `skills/re-frame2/references/api-cheatsheet.md:153`, `skills/re-frame2/references/privacy-and-elision.md:130-152`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` (`configure!` entry).

## Sequencing / hot zone

Blocked by: A0 (rf2-kuky.65 — same `observability.cljc` / `error_emit.cljc` / `Spec-Schemas.md`; A0 first), rf2-kuky.5 (explicit nil fails closed — the real blocker), rf2-kuky.17 (closed entry grammar; same Spec-Schemas region), rf2-kuky.21 (how-to / observability.md / docs/api — same files; .21 first). Never beside rf2-kuky.18's PR #9306 (same two core files). A2 is blocked on this bead. Hot-zone files: `spec/API.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` — sequential with .17 / .20 / .21 and with A0 / A2.

Worker worktree guard before any edit (`sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh`); gates foreground to completion; no `git stash` — commit, then `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main`.

## Acceptance

- `(rf/configure! {:observability {:errors [{:sink :s}]}})` + a registered `:s`: an error on a frame with NO `:observability` reaches `:s` once, projected under that frame's classification; on a frame declaring `{:errors []}` reaches nothing; on a frame declaring `{:errors [{:sink :s}]}` reaches `:s` once (Q5); on a frame declaring `{:handled-events […]}` only, its `:errors` still inherit the default (per-stream).

title: api(observability): route-error! drops producer attribution — :failing-id/:reason/:flow-id/:source-coord
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:23:19 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.22 ruling (delegated by Mike). RULING on rf2-kuky.22: **A — one production observation door.** This is bead **A0**, FIRST of the fixed chain A0 → A1 → A2 (A1/A2 ids are in the ruling note on rf2-kuky.22 and appended below). The finding is Codex's, from the `## Codex Recommendation` section attached to rf2-kuky.22, confirmed at tip `13884f326f`._

## Problem

The frame-owned sink route loses the producer's component attribution BEFORE projection.

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc` `dispatch-on-error!` builds the corpus-wide record at `:581-590`: `attribution` (`:failing-id` / `:reason` for the interceptor + cofx categories, `:flow-id` + `:where :flow-eval` for flow-eval — rf2-z1332c, "so its attribution SURVIVES an egress profile that drops `:exception`") merged under the base fields, plus `:source-coord` when present. Then at `:614-619` it calls the late-bound `route-error!` POSITIONALLY — `(route-error! error-kw event event-id frame-id exception elapsed-ms time nil raw-identity-event?)` — with NONE of the attribution slots, no `:source-coord`, and `correlation` as literal `nil`.

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc` `route-error!` (`:228-272`) builds the `:rf.observe/error` record from exactly those positionals (`:261-268`), so a sink never learns WHICH interceptor / cofx / flow failed, and changing the egress profile cannot restore what the record never carried. The non-event route `route-error-record!` (`:299-347`) already lifts every non-summary slot onto `:tags`; the event route has no equivalent.

Once A2 retires the corpus-wide `:errors` stream, the sink is the ONLY production door, so this becomes lost diagnosis, not redundancy. Codex: "Losing which coeffect/interceptor failed is material to a productive production-monitoring API; fix or explicitly settle this before presenting sinks as a fully equivalent replacement." This bead improves the recommended monitoring path under every outcome.

## Target

The projected `:rf.observe/error` record identifies the failing component with the SAME structural attribution the corpus record carries. Enumerate the slots from the producer (`error_emit.cljc:571-590` and the `dispatch-on-error!` docstring `:452-470`): `:failing-id`, `:reason`, `:flow-id`, `:where`, `:source-coord`. Do not invent slots.

Decide per slot, and write the decision into `spec/015`:
- SUMMARY slots (structural identifiers; pass the projector unchanged): `:failing-id`, `:flow-id`, `:where`, `:source-coord` — the producer comment says "callers keep these to tight identifiers — this record is production-surviving and NOT privacy-gated".
- TREE slot lifted onto `:tags` (walked + redacted under frame classification): `:reason` is a string that may fold an app value; the non-event route already redacts `:reason` under `:tags` (`observability.cljc:315-318`) — be consistent with it.
NOT a blanket merge of arbitrary attrs into public summaries (Codex). Preserve query-vector identity (`raw-identity-event?`) and every existing category meaning.
