title: api(routing): h/route-link accepts :prefetch :intent and warms nothing — wire routing's prefetch intent
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from routing.md (ref routing.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.hicasso/route-link` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:477` → `hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs:140-168`) ACCEPTS `:prefetch :intent` and does nothing with it. `:prefetch` is in its `control-keys` (`route_link.cljs:103`) so it is stripped off the anchor; the value is validated on both hosts through the `:routing/link-model` seam (`routing/link.cljc:504 (validate-prefetch! target)`), so `:prefetch :render` throws `:rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch` — but `:intent`, the ONE accepted value, installs no handler. The result is precisely the failure `validate-prefetch!`'s own docstring names as the one a prefetch can least afford (`link.cljc:58-63`): "a passive link looks identical to a working one until you measure". `rf/route-link` on the same props warms the destination on hover / focus / touch-start (`link.cljc:43 prefetch-intent-keys`, `prefetch-intent-attrs`); the two link surfaces Spec 012 declares behaviourally identical disagree on the one behaviour key they share.

The tree carries two contradictory records of intent. Spec 012:653-662, `docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:198-215` + `:412`, `glossary.md:553` and `route_link.cljs:57-63` all say v0 DECLINES `:prefetch` ("deliberate v0 decline rather than an oversight … an author spells the warm-up directly"). But the shipped design record says the opposite: `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md:71` row 36 — "`:prefetch :intent` accepted on `route-link` … **keep as taught** — routing's own `:rf.route/prefetch` event and its `:intent` value are attested, so only the link-side acceptance is new, and **it is the designed end state**. The prototype's v0 decline id `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined` is retired and must not be reused" (applied, rf2-hic-065 / rf2-hic-093), and Spec 009:2547 records that retirement (rf2-6c12m.11, PR #8772). rf2-g8pf (closed 2026-09-04) then KEPT `rf.routing.link/prefetch-on-intent!` with no caller on exactly this argument: "Retiring it would leave a link-model seam consumer able to validate and ACCEPT `:prefetch :intent` — with no published way to honour it. That is the exact fail-open shape both files exist to refuse." So the designed end state is WIRED; what shipped is the prototype's decline minus its refusal. This bead wires it.

Two pieces of doc drift ride along: `docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md:532` names `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-bad-prefetch`, an id that appears NOWHERE in Spec 009 (neither live nor struck — `grep -n hicasso-route-link-bad-prefetch spec/009-Instrumentation.md` is empty); `implementation/hicasso/spec/server-policy.md:68` (HS-40) says "the declined-`:prefetch` refusal fires during the server render" — no refusal exists on either host.

## Evidence

- `route_link.cljs:140-168`: `attrs` = props minus `control-keys` plus `:href` and the `[intent/navigate-head …]` `:on-click`; no branch reads `:prefetch`.
- `link.cljc:458-516 link-model` returns `{:href :payload :native?}`; `prefetch-payload` (`:149-169`) is PURE on both hosts and returns `[:rf.route/prefetch {:to … ?:params ?:query}]` (no `:fragment`) or nil — the one prefetch calculation, currently reached only by `rf/route-link`.
- Hicasso lowers a VECTOR at any `on-*` position into an intent dispatch on the ambient frame — `hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:390-394 event-prop?`, `:568-580 lower-prop` (`(vector? v) (intent-handler k v)`), `:607-620 lower-props` — so the guide's manual spelling `:on-mouse-enter [:rf.route/prefetch {…}]` (`07-routing-and-navigation.md:207-211`) already works; the sugar is those three positions filled from the seam.
- Corpus: `:prefetch :intent` sites — examples 3 lines (one site, `examples/capabilities/infinite_feed/core.cljs:264-265`, on `rf/route-link`), Hicasso examples/tests 0 real uses; `hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/route_link_cljs_test.cljs:144-152 a-prefetch-key-never-reaches-the-anchor` pins the inert state; `examples/navigation/conduct_dom_cljs_test.cljs:76-84` docstring records it as "a naming-ledger question that is still open (row 36)" — row 36 is applied.
- The retired late-bind trio (`:routing/prefetch-payload`, `:routing/prefetch-on-intent!`, `:routing/prefetch-intent-keys`, rf2-6r9j.15 / PR #9165) is NOT re-published: the payload rides the seam Hicasso already consumes.

## Target API

```clojure
;; re-frame.routing.link/link-model — one more key; PURE, both hosts, same validation
(link-model target render-frame)
;; => {:href     <strategy-encoded href>
;;     :payload  [:rf.route/url-requested {…}]
;;     :native?  <bool>
;;     :prefetch <[:rf.route/prefetch {:to … ?:params ?:query}] | nil>}    ;; (prefetch-payload target)

;; re-frame.hicasso/route-link — data, no hook, no boundary, no new seam
(h/route-link {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"} :prefetch :intent} "Read more")
;; renders
[:a {:href           "/articles/intro"
     :on-click       [intent/navigate-head {…}]
     :on-mouse-enter [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]
     :on-focus       [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]
     :on-touch-start [:rf.route/prefetch {:to :app/article :params {:id "intro"}}]}
 "Read more"]
;; :prefetch absent → none of the three positions is touched (passive by construction, as today)
```

The three positions are `rf.routing.link/prefetch-intent-keys` (`link.cljc:43`) — read them off routing rather than restating the list; if the seam needs to carry them, add a `:prefetch-keys` entry to the same `link-model` map rather than a second hook.

**One closed rule for a caller value at a claimed position.** `:prefetch :intent` CLAIMS the three intent positions; a caller-supplied `:on-mouse-enter` / `:on-focus` / `:on-touch-start` alongside `:prefetch :intent` is refused AT RENDER, fail-loud, naming the position — the same shape and the same law as `on-click-roster!` (`route_link.cljs:105-125`: "the click already produces the one routing intent"); here the hover already produces the one prefetch intent, and Hicasso's in-band grammar carries one intent per position. An author who needs both spells the prefetch by hand at that position (the guide's existing form) and omits the sugar. The refusal needs a catalogued id: add ONE row to `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Hicasso rows beside `:2545-2546` (**hot-zone**; suggested `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-claimed-intent-position`) and its `docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md` entry. Do NOT reuse `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-prefetch-declined` (struck at 009:2547; naming-ledger row 36 forbids it) and do NOT emit routing's `:rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch` for it (that id means "bad value"; `:intent` is the good value). No silent-skip and no partial fill is admissible — either every claimed position carries the prefetch intent or the render throws.

Server: event props are data the server render drops with every other `on-*`; `link-model` already validates `:prefetch` on the JVM, so the SSR shell rejects what the client rejects and emits what the client emits minus handlers — HS-40 restates that.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer on the fable side; codex INDEPENDENTLY called this "the most concrete user-visible defect here … Prefer wiring the existing routing-owned intent behavior if the published option remains supported; otherwise reject it clearly. A silent no-op is poor ergonomics even for trusted programmers. Verify focus, pointer intent, existing user handlers, navigation cancellation, and frame capture; do not build another prefetch policy subsystem." Wiring is chosen over rejection because (a) naming-ledger row 36 rules acceptance the designed end state and retired the decline id, (b) rf2-g8pf's KEEP verdict presumes the seam consumer can honour the value, (c) rejection would also need a 009 row and would make the two link surfaces disagree on a key Spec 012:640 calls "a routing control key on every link surface". Codex's checklist maps to the acceptance: focus + pointer + touch = the three positions; existing user handlers = the closed rule; navigation cancellation = untouched (`:on-click` / `::h/prevent` path is not read by this change); frame capture = the intent vector lowers on the boundary's ambient frame, the same frame `require-frame!` pinned the click to.

## Deletion list

- The "Not wired in v0" paragraph (`route_link.cljs:57-63`) and the `control-keys` comment "Hicasso wires none of the prefetch handlers in v0" (`:99-102`) — replaced by the wired contract.
- `docs/core/hicasso/troubleshooting.md:532` row naming the non-existent `:rf.error/hicasso-route-link-bad-prefetch` (replace with the routing id `:rf.error/route-link-bad-prefetch` for a bad value, plus the new claimed-position id).
- Test `a-prefetch-key-never-reaches-the-anchor`'s inert-state assertion (`hicasso/test/…/route_link_cljs_test.cljs:144-152`) — the "never reaches the anchor" half stays true and stays pinned; the "wires none" docstring goes.

Testbeds: 0. `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/examples/{navigation,slice,todo}/views.cljs` (10 `h/route-link` sites) carry no `:prefetch` — unchanged. title: api(registry): one query map, `{:source :store}` XOR `{:frame f}`, on registrations / handler-meta
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registry-introspection.md (ref registry-introspection.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The public registry read has two shapes whose documented meaning the tree contradicts. `re-frame.core/registrations` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1783`; arities `[arg]` / `[kind pred-fn]`) and `handler-meta` (`:1836`; `[arg]` map-only / `[kind id]`) document the positional-keyword arity as "the default source store" (`spec/API.md:520-521`, `core.cljc` docstrings), but they delegate to `rf.registrar/registrations` (`registrar.cljc:873`) and `rf.registrar/lookup` (`:828`), which consult the dynamic `*generation*` (`:224`) FIRST. `re-frame.live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution` (`live_frame.cljc:330`) binds it around every subscribe build / dispatch / fx / view resolution against an image-loaded frame — and since `make-frame` seals a generation unconditionally, every frame is one. So a "store" read issued inside a sub computation or handler silently reads THAT frame's image instead. Measured cost: Xray runs in its own `:rf/xray` frame and had to write `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/host_registry.cljs`, which derefs the private atom `re-frame.registrar/kind->id->metadata` to see the host app at all (its ns docstring explains the mechanism; 15 call lines in 7 files, required by 9); `spec/API.md:514` then BLESSES that private read ("reads the process source store directly via `re-frame.registrar`"). A public inspection request must say which source it means; a bare keyword cannot.

Second silent swallow on the same door: `:flow` and `:frame` sit in the closed `kinds` set (`registrar.cljc:98-146`) as reserved-EMPTY slots, so `(rf/registrations :flow)` returns `{}` while flows exist in `re-frame.flows`' per-frame store — it bit Xray (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/flows/panel.cljs:24-29` records the read going dead) and pair-MCP still offers `"flow"` / `"frame"` in its kind enum (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs:1709`, `:1775`).

## Target API

Two operations, one map grammar, exactly one source selector:

```clojure
;; store reads — the process-global registrar, NEVER routed through a bound *generation*
(rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event})                 ; => {id meta} or {}
(rf/handler-meta  {:source :store :kind :event :id :cart/add})   ; => meta or nil
(rf/handler-meta  {:source :store :kind :machine-guard :id [:auth/login :form-valid?]}) ; derived, unchanged meaning

;; frame reads — resolved through live frame f's OWN sealed image generation (today's map form, unchanged)
(rf/registrations {:frame app-frame :kind :event})
(rf/handler-meta  {:frame app-frame :kind :resource :id :articles/list})

;; projections are Clojure, not library operations
(keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :route}))
(into {} (filter (fn [[_ m]] (:rf/machine? m))) (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event}))
(:rf/resource (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :resource :id :articles/list}))
```

Rules: a map with BOTH `:source` and `:frame`, or NEITHER, or a non-map argument, throws a catalogued error — rename today's `:rf.error/registrar-query-needs-frame` (`core.cljc:1672` `assert-registrar-query-has-frame!`; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2302`; 16 lines / 2 test files consume the id) to `:rf.error/registrar-query-needs-source`, since "needs frame" is no longer the truth. `:source` admits only `:store` (leave the door open for a future value; reject anything else). `:frame` keeps `resolve-live-frame-object` (`core.cljc:1632`) + `call-with-frame-resolution` and its `:rf.error/frame-no-generation` failure — no fallback. `:kind` outside `rf.registrar/kinds` → the existing `:rf.error/unknown-registry-kind` (`registrar.cljc:588`, currently thrown by `register-handler`; throw it from the query path too with `where` naming the query fn). `:kind :flow` or `:frame` (reserved-empty slots) → a new catalogued `:rf.error/registrar-kind-not-queryable` whose message names the real door (`re-frame.flows/flows-snapshot` / `flow-meta-at`; `rf/frame-ids` / `frame-meta`) — never `{}`. `:frame` + `:machine-guard` / `:machine-action` stays `nil` as documented today (pair-mcp refuses before emitting); codex: extending frame-targeted derived lookups is not required.

Implementation of `:source :store`: read the atom without consulting `*generation*` — add `rf.registrar/store-registrations` / `store-lookup` (`(get @(active-registrar) kind {})` / paired `get`) and call them from the facade. Do NOT change `rf.registrar/registrations` / `lookup` / `ids` / `handler-meta` themselves: 80 internal call lines in 35 files resolve events / fx / subs / views through them and MUST stay generation-routed (codex: "implement this distinction at the public inspection boundary, not by globally changing `registrar/lookup`"). Both facade fns are `.cljc`; the grammar is identical on the JVM.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Codex `registration-inspection.md` §Proposed smaller API ("Give both the same map grammar with exactly one source selector: `:source :store`, or `:frame f` … Supplying both, or neither, is an invalid query … Retire positional reads, the generic predicate overloads"; §Codex Thoughts: "Reject reserved-but-empty query kinds clearly rather than silently returning an apparently authoritative empty catalogue"). Fable §Codex cross-check item 1 adopts it verbatim ("the positional keyword form goes with the aliases"; the map form was fable's own target). Fable's Grok section concurs ("Adopt Codex's explicit source map … Retire positional reads. This kills `host-registry` and makes the API.md promise true").

## Deletion list

- `re-frame.core/registrations` arities `([kind])`, `([kind pred-fn])` and the map key `:pred`; `re-frame.core/handler-meta` arity `([kind id])`. Filtering is `filter` over the returned map (3 positional-pred sites in 2 test files; 8 impl-test lines + 2 preload lines use map `:pred`).
- `assert-registrar-query-has-frame!` (`core.cljc:1672`) → `assert-registrar-query-source!` with the new error id; `:rf.error/registrar-query-needs-frame` leaves the catalogue.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/host_registry.cljs` — delete; its 9 requiring files (`mount.cljs`, `palette/subs.cljs`, `panels/epoch_panel.cljs`, `panels/machine_inspector.cljs`, `panels/resources.cljs`, `panels/routing.cljs`, `static/flows/panel.cljs`, `static/interceptors/panel.cljs`, `static/schemas/panel.cljs`) switch their 15 `host-registry/registrations` / `handler-meta` calls to `{:source :store …}`; delete the docstrings explaining the bypass (`machine_inspector.cljs:673-705` and siblings).
- `spec/API.md:514`'s sentence blessing direct `re-frame.registrar` reads.

## Consumers to migrate (measured; `rf/`-prefixed positional call lines, code not comments)

- `examples/` 0, `testbeds/` 0 — the front porch is untouched.
- tools src 54 lines / 17 files: Xray 46/12 (largest: `panels/epoch/view.cljs` 18, `panels/resources_helpers.cljc` 8, `static/interceptors/panel.cljs` 6, `panels/resources.cljs` 6, `panels/epoch_panel.cljs` 5, `static/schemas/panel.cljs` 4, `static/flows/panel.cljs` 3, `panels/routing.cljs` 3, `panels/machine_inspector.cljs` 3, `registry.cljs` 2, `panels/reactive_panel_view.cljs` 2, `panels/epoch/projection.cljc` 2); Story 5/4 (`frames.cljc`, `identity.cljc`, `plan.cljc`, `args.cljc` — Story's OWN `re-frame.story/registrations` over Story kinds is a different product and is NOT migrated); pair preload 3/1 (`runtime.cljs:605-609` `registrar-list`, `:720-751` `registrar-describe`, `registrar-handler-ref`) plus the map-`:pred` lines.
- tools tests 28 lines: `tools/xray/test` 13/6, `tools/story/test` 10/2, `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests` 5/2.
- implementation tests 207 lines / 51 files — a scripted rewrite: `(rf/registrations :k)` → `(rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :k})`; `(rf/handler-meta :k id)` → `(rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :k :id id})`; pred forms → `filter`.
- framework src via the facade: 0 code sites (12 hits are docstrings naming `(rf/handler-meta :view id)` etc. — update the prose).
- Codex's caution binds every site: review each positional call for its INTENDED source rather than rewriting all to `:store` — Story's frame composition (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc`) and any read issued inside a frame-resolved context that wants the frame become `{:frame f …}`. Do not promise the old helpers' vector order; `(vec (keys …))` only where a consumer needs a vector.

## Problem

Every way an application can HEAR about production events and errors, at HEAD `6445d0611b` (non-test consumers = call sites in `examples/`, `tools/`, `testbeds/`, `skills/`, `implementation/**/src`):

Two production doors for one job, both with zero application consumers (`examples/`, 22 apps: zero registrations of any kind, zero `sentry|datadog|honeycomb`). The spec calls the sink normal and the streams advanced (`API.md:585`, `009:1258-1262`, `015:270`); the how-to teaches the advanced one first (observability.5 fixes the ORDER, not the count). The "raw `:exception`" discriminator is not one (`projection.cljc:352-363` drops it only under `:rf.egress/public-error`). What door (a) genuinely carries that the sink does not: (i) FRAMELESS records (`:frame nil`) — `:rf.error/no-frame-context` (`frame.cljc:804-808`, `error_emit.cljc:810`), the pre-frame SSR hydration-parse path of `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` (`late_bind/directory.cljc:906`), hicasso's `compute-sub` errors (`server.cljs:259-267`); `route-error-record!` documents them as "carry no frame-owned sink policy by definition" (`observability.cljc:321-325`); and (ii) declaring once per process rather than per frame — `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame` / `frame-root` only; `configure!` (`core.cljc:2554-2605`) has no such key.

Test breadth is where the corpus-wide streams live: `:errors` facade 61 test files, `:events` facade 16 (`git grep -lE "register-listener! :<s>" -- 'implementation/*test*' 'tools/*test*' 'skills/*test*' 'examples/*test*'`); `:errors` home verb 22, `:events` home verb 1. Teaching sites for the two streams: docs 4 files, spec 2, skills 9, migration README 1 (list below).

## Options

**A — one production door (fable, Grok; RECOMMENDED).** `register-listener!` keeps only the raw dev streams: `#{:trace :epoch}` (`core.cljc:2107-2109`). Production observation is ONE door: frame `:observability` policy (today) PLUS a new process default `(rf/configure! {:observability {:handled-events […] :errors […]}})` with the same closed entry grammar (observability.1), wired by `register-observability-sink!`. `re-frame.error-emit` / `re-frame.event-emit` stay as IMPLEMENTATION namespaces (`^:no-doc`, not rowed as public) for the four framework capture sites and for tests; `:events` / `:errors` leave the public vocabulary. Rules that make it one door: a record routes to the owning frame's policy when the frame resolves and declares the stream, else to the process default, else nowhere (fail-closed, unchanged); a frameless record routes to the process default and projects under NO frame — `015:251` case 3: tree slots → `:rf/redacted`, summary ids intact; the raw cross-frame hook becomes an explicit entry `{:sink … :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/local-raw}` on the process default (profile already in the closed enum, `015:258`) instead of an ambient unprojected fan-out.

**B — keep the corpus-wide door as the documented advanced hook (codex).** Everything in observability.1-5 lands; `:events` / `:errors` stay public; no process default; the one missing sentence (observability.5) states the two unique carries. Codex: "Raw synchronous capture and projected delivery are different operations, even if both ultimately register callbacks in maps. Two empty application consumer lists do not establish equivalence… Trusting programmers supports an explicitly advanced raw hook beside the normal projected path… Do not add a process default merely to make deletion of an existing door possible."

**C — the process default now, retirement later (Grok's "third, cheaper path").** Add `configure! {:observability …}` (the declare-once and frameless home) without retiring the streams; revisit retirement once a real Sentry bridge exists in the corpus. Grok: "Zero in-repo app consumers of either door means we do not yet know how a Sentry bridge will actually be written. Deleting the advanced door before the replacement exists is the one way this can fail closed on frameless records."

## Recommendation

A, shipped as two implementation beads in order (the process default FIRST, the retirement SECOND — never the reverse), because: the spec already ruled which door is normal and the surface should say what the spec says; door (a) is fail-open by design (unprojected, no policy, raw throwable) and is the one the how-to hands a first-time reader; `register-listener!` then means one thing (raw dev stream, both members DCE'd) and `register-observability-sink!` one thing (projected production egress) — today the vocabulary mixes two DCE'd streams with two always-on ones and the reader consults a table (`API.md:596-606`) to learn which is which; and the four framework capture sites keep the implementation registry they already use. Codex's caution is carried as the HARD CONSTRAINT below and as the questions the ruling must settle; if Mike prefers to see a real bridge first, C is A1 alone.

## The hard constraint

The `configure!` process default MUST land in the SAME change as (before) the stream retirement, or frameless records reach nobody — the one real gap door (a) closes today (`observability.cljc:321-325`). Frameless projection additionally depends on the egress explicit-nil fix (`@egress.1`): today `project-egress` seeds the governing frame by truthiness and `elide-wire-value` falls through to the AMBIENT frame on `:frame nil` (`elision.cljc:1128` per the egress dossier), so "project under no frame" is not expressible until explicit nil fails closed. A1 is blocked on that bead.

## Questions the ruling must settle (codex's list), with recommended answers

1. **Precedence** — per STREAM: a frame that declares a stream (even `[]`) uses its own entries for that stream; a frame that omits the stream inherits the process default's entries for it; explicit `[]` is the opt-out. (Whole-map replacement rejected: it forces every frame wanting one custom sink to restate the default.)
2. **Absent vs explicit empty** — as in 1; `configure!` with `{:observability nil}` clears the default; validation reuses `frame_classification.cljc`'s `validate-observability!` at call time, fail-loud. Whether to reuse `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` (with `:where 'rf/configure!`) or mint a category is the ruling's; recommend reuse, no new category. The check must not be an `assert` (rf2-xn13).
3. **Frameless records** — process default only; projected with `{:frame nil}` → fail-closed per `015:251` case 3. Blocked on `@egress.1`.
4. **Records whose `:frame` no longer resolves** (destroyed / dissociated incarnation — `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc` pins that a dissociated id must not resolve to a same-id successor's policy) — today a fail-closed no-op. Recommend: route to the process default under fail-closed projection — `015`'s rule forbids borrowing ANOTHER FRAME's policy; the process default is not a frame's. Ruling needed.
5. **Duplicate delivery** — exactly one policy source per record (frame policy if the frame resolves and declares the stream, else process default); a sink id present in both is invoked once.
6. **Raw cross-frame hook** — `:rf.egress/local-raw` on a process-default entry; coordinate the profile name with `@egress.1`.
7. **Console fallback** — composes with observability.2: a process-default delivery to a registered sink owns the record.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer, High. Codex prefers B ("prefer the narrower Target B… Fix swallowed options and teach projected sinks first; do not require process policy inheritance to delete raw hooks"; "sinks construct a bounded `:rf.observe/*` shape and project payloads, whereas the always-on stream exposes the error/event substrate's record for synchronous integration and capture. Hicasso's shipped capture-intents helper is evidence for the latter"). Grok: A in two steps, sequenced behind the egress profile enum. Fable's own "honest costs": (i) the default must land in the same change; (ii) ~77 test files migrate; (iii) rf2-xpd8's ruling names the listener and needs one sentence; (iv) a library wanting a cross-frame hook without frame config uses the one-line `configure!` default.

**Status:** High (the spec names the frame sink the *normal* production door and the corpus-wide `:errors` stream the *advanced* one, yet the how-to teaches the advanced door for seven sections and both doors have zero non-test consumers; the home-namespace verbs are justified by a DCE rationale that `trace.cljc:48` and `install.cljs:13` disprove; the sink's `:opts` bag is validated and then dropped; wave 3, 2026-09-05 09:09:26 AUSEST, tip 7d7ec09bd7 — main advanced to 90bdedcc17 during the read, see Provenance)
**Surfaces:** `rf/register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` over `:trace` `:events` `:errors` `:epoch` (`core.cljc:2135-2182`); home verbs `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` (`tooling.cljc:81`), `re-frame.event-emit/register-event-listener!` (`event_emit.cljc:95`), `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!` (`error_emit.cljc:75`), `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` (`epoch.cljc:151`); the aliases `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` (`trace.cljc:951`) and the whole `re-frame.emit` namespace (`emit.cljc`); the late-bind hooks `:trace.tooling/register-listener!` (`directory.cljc:1114`) and `:error-emit/register-error-listener!` (`directory.cljc:907`); `rf/register-observability-sink!` / `unregister-observability-sink!` + frame `:observability` policy (`observability.cljc:111-135`, `frame_classification.cljc:145-256`); the dev console fallback (`error_emit.cljc:90-231`); `reg-error-projector` / `project-error` / `:ssr {:public-error-id}` (`error_projector.cljc:240,314`); `:rf.trace/no-emit?` / `:rf.trace/frame-no-emit?` (`trace.cljc:238,370`, `frame.cljc:3282`).

Three facts the table surfaces:

1. **Two production doors, one job, both empty.** The spec calls the frame sink "the NORMAL production observation surface" and the `:errors` stream an "advanced corpus-wide hook" (`spec/API.md:585`, `009:1258-1262`). Neither has a consumer outside tests. `examples/` (22 apps) contains zero registrations of any kind and zero occurrences of `sentry|datadog|honeycomb`. The teaching corpus disagrees with the spec: `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md` builds the Sentry bridge on `register-listener! :errors` across §1–§7 (lines 19–272) and reaches the sink only at §8 (line 273, "Prefer the frame sink…"); `configure-dev-and-prod.md:33` names the streams first, then "or — the normal off-box path — declare a frame sink"; the Conduit tutorial (`05-test-and-ship.md:300-308`), `observability.md:481`, and the skill (`production-observability.md:3`) teach the sink first. Three orderings for one question.

2. **The "raw exception" discriminator is not one.** The corpus-wide door is justified as the post-mortem route because "`:exception` rides RAW" (`API.md:585`). But the sink also delivers the exception under its default profile: `projection.cljc:356-360` drops `:exception` only under `:rf.egress/public-error` and otherwise passes an opaque host object through the walker unchanged; the how-to says so itself (`report-errors-in-production.md:298`, "leaving the profile off keeps the exception"). What genuinely distinguishes door (a) is only (i) frameless records (`:frame nil` — no-frame-context, pre-frame SSR parse) which no frame policy can route, and (ii) not having to declare a policy on every frame — because `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame` / `frame-root` only, never on `configure!` (0 hits for a process-level default).

3. **The DCE tier rule's premise is false at tip.** `spec/Tool-Pair.md:635` (landed by rf2-rfid2x, `eba72089b0`): "canonical devtools attach via the per-stream home-namespace verbs … because a tool preload MUST NOT require `re-frame.core` into a production build". Measured: `re-frame.trace` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` **unconditionally on both platforms** (`trace.cljc:48-49`; the facade's `:trace` arm and the home verb are literally one var, `trace.cljc:951`), and `re-frame.core` requires `re-frame.trace` (`core.cljc:52`) — so every bundle that has the facade already has the tooling registry, and the only DCE lever is the `goog.DEBUG` gate around the *call site*, which both spellings need equally (`trace.cljc:28-33` says exactly this). The exemplar the rule was lifted from, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs`, requires `re-frame.core` at line 13 (for `rf/with-frame` + `rf/dispatch` at 75-76) two lines above the comment saying it uses the home namespace "so the dev-only tooling surface remains independently elidable". Seven of the ten home-verb `:trace` call sites also require `re-frame.core` (measured below). And `:events` / `:errors` are always-on — there is nothing to elide. The rule protects nothing; it only licenses a second spelling.

4. **`:opts` is swallowed.** A sink entry's `:opts` map is validated for shape at `make-frame` (`frame_classification.cljc:240-251`, fails loud on a non-map; tested at `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:190-203`) and appears in every teaching sample (`observability.cljc:22`, `015:281`, `API.md:701`). `route-stream!` reads only `:sink` and `:rf.egress/profile` (`observability.cljc:161-171`); `deliver-to-sink!` calls `(f projected)` (`:149`). The bag reaches nobody. Spec-Schemas rows it as "vendor-specific, framework does not own the vocabulary" (`Spec-Schemas.md:4332`) — a slot designed as a pass-through that does not pass through. This is the exact shape Principles §No silent swallow forbids ("an unknown opts key … a callback whose return it drops").

5. **Ownership is a side effect.** The dev console fallback goes quiet when *any* `:errors` listener exists, "even if that listener ignores this category" (`error_emit.cljc:120-128`). Story therefore registers `(fn [_record] nil)` purely to claim the stream (`shell.cljs:1153`, rf2-8yyd — 227 console lines per feature-load run otherwise). A tool with its own error surface has no honest way to say "I own errors" except a fake registration on a door it does not read.

## Simpler elegant target

**One dev verb over raw streams; one production door with a policy; nothing in between.**

```clojure
;; DEV — raw streams, DCE'd. The closed vocabulary shrinks to the two streams
;; that are actually raw-and-dev: :trace and :epoch.
(rf/register-listener!   stream id f)        ; stream ∈ #{:trace :epoch}
(rf/unregister-listener! stream id)

;; PRODUCTION — declared policy, projected delivery, always-on.
;; The policy is data on the frame (today) AND, new, a process default on
;; configure! — the same knob/frame precedence ladder :fx-overrides already
;; uses, so multi-frame apps declare once and frameless records have a home.
(rf/configure! {:observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability}]}})
(rf/make-frame {:id :admin :observability {:errors [{:sink :app/sentry
                                                     :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/public-error}]}})
(rf/register-observability-sink! :app/sentry (fn [projected-record] …))
```


Rules that make it one door: a record routes to the owning frame's policy when it has one, else to the process default, else nowhere (fail-closed, unchanged). A frameless record routes to the process default and projects under *no* frame — which `015:251` case 3 already defines as whole-tree `:rf/redacted`, summary ids intact. The raw cross-frame case that door (a) served becomes an explicit opt-in on the sink entry (`:rf.egress/local-raw`, `015` case 4) instead of an ambient unprojected fan-out. The console fallback keys on "no entry routed this record" rather than "the listener atom is empty" — so Story's frames declare `{:observability {:errors [{:sink :rf.story/errors}]}}` and own their errors honestly.

## Why this is better (ethos)

**One way for the common case; power available, not ambient** (README ethos bar). The spec has already ruled which door is normal (`API.md:575,585`, `009:1258`, `015:270`). The surface disagrees with the ruling: the normal door has zero consumers and is taught last; the advanced door has the how-to. Deleting the advanced door from the app-facing vocabulary makes the surface say what the spec says.

**Privacy by default, honestly.** Door (a) is fail-open by design — unprojected, no frame policy, raw throwable — and it is the door the how-to hands a first-time reader at line 30. `015:321` distinguishes classification's fail-open from the projector's fail-closed carefully; a public verb that bypasses the projector entirely is a third posture the spec never names. Trust the programmer means giving them the projected record and an explicit `:rf.egress/local-raw` opt-in, not an ambient raw fan-out they must remember not to reach for.

**No silent swallow.** `:opts` is recognised, validated, documented, and dropped. Conventions §No silent swallow is the normative rule; this is its textbook violation, on the very door the spec calls normal.

**Low hidden context.** Registering any `:errors` listener silences the console for every category (`error_emit.cljc:120-128`). Story's `(fn [_record] nil)` is the corpus telling us the off-switch is in the wrong place — a registration on a door nobody reads, to change behaviour on a door nobody registered. Keying the fallback on routing makes "who owns this record" a fact of the policy data, readable by anyone.

**Regularity over cleverness.** After the change `register-listener!` means one thing (raw dev stream; both members DCE'd) and `register-observability-sink!` means one thing (projected production egress). Today the stream vocabulary mixes two DCE'd streams with two always-on ones and the reader must consult a table (`API.md:596-603`) to learn which is which.

**Clojure ethos.** The sink registry and the four listener registries are the *same data structure* — `(defonce ^:private … (atom {}))`, `swap! assoc`, return the id, `try/catch` per callback (`observability.cljc:109-135` vs `error_emit.cljc:66-85`, `tooling.cljc:79-99`). Two registries for one shape is not the smell; the smell is that the framework exposes the raw registry *and* the routed one as peers. Registration should be one plain map; routing should be declared as data on the frame. Data over imperative wiring. And a rule that exists "because of DCE" must be true of the dependency graph — measured, not remembered — or it is folklore wearing a contract's clothes.

**Honest costs.** (i) The process-level default must land in the same change as the stream retirement, or frameless records reach nobody — the one real gap door (a) closes today. (ii) Breadth: ~77 test files on the two production streams migrate to the implementation namespaces or a `test-support` helper; mechanical, but wide, and `hicasso` test-kit's `capture-intents` is a shipped surface. (iii) The rf2-xpd8 ruling (2026-09-04) reasons in terms of "listener, sink, console"; its producer routes through `dispatch-error-record!`, which feeds the sink route and the console identically, so nothing there moves — but the ruling text names the listener and will need one sentence. (iv) A library that wants a cross-frame hook without touching frame config loses the ambient route; the answer is the `configure!` default, which is also one line.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes. Two production doors for one job, the how-to teaching the fail-open one first, a DCE tier rule whose require-graph premise is false, and a sink `:opts` bag that is validated then dropped. That last one is a textbook No-silent-swallow violation on the door the spec calls *normal*.

**Diagnosis.** Correct and unusually complete. I re-read `deliver-to-sink!` — it calls `(f projected)` and never looks at `:opts`. `route-stream!` reads only `:sink` and `:rf.egress/profile`. The DCE claim is also right: `core.cljc` requires `re-frame.trace` unconditionally and `trace.cljc` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` on both platforms, so the home-ns verbs do not buy elision the facade verb would lose. What genuinely distinguishes the corpus-wide `:errors` stream is frameless records plus “declare once, not per frame.” Target A’s process default is the replacement for that second unique carry; without it, stream retirement drops a real capability.

**Options.** Target A vs Target B is the right fork. Missing a third, cheaper path: fix honesty *without* retiring streams yet (delete or pass `:opts`, add the `configure!` default, rekey the console fallback, rewrite the how-to so the sink is §1). Zero in-repo app consumers of *either* door means we do not yet know how a Sentry bridge will actually be written. Deleting the advanced door before the replacement exists is the one way this can fail closed on frameless records.

**Recommendation.** Ship Target A, but as two beads, not one.

1. **Honesty bead (do now).** Delete `:opts` (the sink fn closes over its own config; if per-frame vendor tags are wanted later, pass them as a second argument — never accept-and-drop). Add `(rf/configure! {:observability …})` with the same knob/frame precedence `:fx-overrides` already uses. Key the console fallback on “no policy routed this record.” Rewrite `report-errors-in-production.md` so the sink is the first recipe. Fix the Tool-Pair DCE sentence to the preload truth: tools stay out of production via `:devtools/preloads`, not via which namespace they require.
2. **Retirement bead (after 1 is in).** Remove `:events`/`:errors` from the *public* stream vocabulary. Keep `re-frame.error-emit` / `re-frame.event-emit` as implementation registries for the four framework window-capture sites and for tests. Delete `re-frame.emit`, the `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` aliases, and the unused late-bind listener hooks.

Do not merge the sink with the raw streams. `reg-error-projector` is a different job; leave it. Do not implement this until the egress profile enum (including `:rf.egress/local-raw` as the explicit opt-in that replaces ambient raw fan-out) is stable — this design leans on that hatch.

**Implement.** One process default, one routing fallback branch, a wide but mechanical test migration (~77 files). Sequence behind `egress-and-redaction.md` for the profile names, and share the `register-listener!` vocabulary change with `trace-and-epoch-read-surface.md` so those two docs do not fork the stream set. `current-config` belongs in the boot/config bead, not here.

## Codex Thoughts

### Verdict: worthwhile diagnosis, but prefer the narrower Target B


The ignored sink `:opts` and conflicting teaching paths deserve action. Retiring public `:errors`/`:events` listeners and adding process-wide policy inheritance is a larger redesign than the evidence presently earns. Raw synchronous capture and projected delivery are different operations, even if both ultimately register callbacks in maps. Two empty application consumer lists do not establish equivalence.

The source confirms the concrete defect: [frame validation](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc) accepts an `:opts` map, while [sink routing](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc) passes only the projected record. Choose explicitly between removing the unused slot and passing it as a documented second callback argument. For today's measured consumers I favor removal, with configuration captured in the registered function and existing `:frame` attribution available for lookups. If one shared vendor sink genuinely needs different per-frame configuration, the second argument is a small legitimate alternative, not necessarily over-engineering. Either choice must remove the accept-and-drop contract from code and examples.

### Correct the diagnosis before choosing the door

The sink does preserve opaque host exceptions under its default profile; raw exception presence is therefore not a sufficient discriminator. However the distinction is broader than frameless records: sinks construct a bounded `:rf.observe/*` shape and project payloads, whereas the always-on stream exposes the error/event substrate's record for synchronous integration and capture. [Hicasso's shipped capture-intents helper](../../../../implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs) is evidence for the latter, not merely an implementation detail to move out of sight. Trusting programmers supports an explicitly advanced raw hook beside the normal projected path.

The DCE criticism usefully invalidates an unsupported blanket teaching rule. A namespace dependency graph alone does not prove the size or contents of an advanced compiled bundle: reachable exports and gated call sites still matter. Prefer one documented registration facade and preserve genuinely necessary implementation namespaces, load-cycle hooks, and optional epoch loading. Verify any claimed bundle improvement with the existing positive-control build, not source greps alone.

### Recommended implementation

Lead the production how-to with a frame-owned projected sink. State plainly what is projected, what happens to exceptions, and when the advanced corpus-wide listener is appropriate. Reconcile the manifest, tool guidance, and examples around that distinction. Remove proven unused aliases independently; internal fan-out and late binding need not become public synonyms.

Do not add a process default merely to make deletion of an existing door possible. If a real multi-frame integration later needs it, specify absent policy versus explicit empty policy, per-stream inheritance versus whole-map replacement, frameless records, teardown records whose owner no longer resolves, and prevention of duplicate delivery. These are semantic choices, not simply one fallback branch. Frameless projection also depends on fixing the explicit-nil ownership defect discussed in [egress and redaction](egress-and-redaction.md).

The console issue is real but should remain small. [The current fallback](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc) deliberately treats any listener as corpus-wide ownership. Changing that to “an entry routed” can hide an error when a named sink is missing or throws; Story also suppresses errors outside a single variant frame. Keep today's behavior documented while evaluating an explicit host-level ownership choice, or define successful handoff precisely before changing it. Do not invent per-category routing, acknowledgements, or a suppression framework for this cleanup.

Acceptance should cover sink option handling, normal projected delivery, raw temporary capture, frameless errors, listener removal, missing/throwing sinks, and whichever console rule is actually chosen. The elegant result is clear defaults and honest escape hatches—not a smaller verb count purchased with more ambient configuration.

# Listener registration — one verb in the spec, two forms per stream in practice

**Status:** medium (the dual is tiered, but the tier rule is folklore; wave 2, 2026-07-10 14:30 AUSEST, Fable-authored)
**Surfaces:** `rf/register-listener!` (facade; closed streams `:trace` `:events` `:errors` `:epoch`), the four home-namespace verbs (`trace.tooling/register-listener!`, `event-emit/register-event-listener!`, `error-emit/register-error-listener!`, `epoch/register-epoch-listener!`), plus the distinct-job pair `register-observability-sink!` and `reg-error-projector`

---

## The problem

The spec's design is genuinely elegant: **one stream-parameterized verb over a closed four-stream
vocabulary** (API-shrink #4 already deleted the per-channel facade twins). But every stream remains
reachable **two ways** — facade or home namespace — and the corpus's own canonical tools straddle the
two *inconsistently*:

| Consumer | `:trace` | `:epoch` |
|---|---|---|
| Xray (`install.cljs:79,112`) | home ns | **facade** |
| Story (`frames.cljc:212`, `invariants.cljc:395`) | home ns | **facade** |
| pair preload (`runtime.cljs:1474,1330`) | home ns | **facade** |

Same tools, two same-axis dev streams, two call-site conventions. The reason for the home-ns form is
real and important — keeping `re-frame.core` out of production bundles so DCE holds — but it lives in
one Xray comment (`install.cljs:42-49`), not in any contract.

---

## Empirical use cases

### 1. Canonical tool attaches a trace collector

Xray, Story (5 sites incl. its own `trace-buffer` wrapper), pair preload — all via
`re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`, all for the bundle-DCE reason.

### 2. Canonical tool attaches an epoch collector

Same three tools — all via the **facade** `rf/register-listener! :epoch`, despite
`re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` existing (`docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md:113` explicitly names
both routes as the same registry).

### 3. Framework-internal error listeners

SSR error projection registers on `:errors` (always-on) *and* `:trace` (dev) under one logical id
(`ssr.cljc:459,475`) — deliberate cross-axis coverage; the router uses the home error verb likewise.

The how-to's stated reason to prefer it — the corpus-wide record "carries the raw `:exception`" (`API.md:585`, `009:1235`, how-to `:275`) — is not a discriminator: the sink delivers `:exception` too under its default profile. `projection.cljc:352-360` drops it only under `:rf.egress/public-error`, and the how-to says so itself at `:305` ("leaving the profile off keeps the exception"). What the raw door genuinely carries that the sink does not is (i) FRAMELESS records and (ii) declaring once per process — `:observability` is accepted on `make-frame`/`frame-root` only; `configure!` (`core.cljc:2620`) has no such key.
- **AI agent.** Two spellings for one job, the spec and the teaching corpus in disagreement, and a how-to sentence ("That's the whole surface for now", `:35`) that is false about the surface the spec calls normal. `spec/Principles.md` §Regularity over cleverness: "there is one obvious way to do a thing."
- **Tool author.** Registering ANY `:errors` listener silences the dev console for every frame, "even if that listener ignores this category" (`error_emit.cljc:121-132`); Story registers a no-op to claim the stream (`shell.cljs:1153`). rf2-kuky.18 (in progress, PR #9306) is keying the console on nothing-routed-this-record so Story owns errors as frame policy instead. Once that lands, the raw door's last tool-tier use is hicasso's one-render window.

### The hard constraint: frameless records — verified at tip

Three producers emit records with `:frame nil`, and today those records reach ONLY the corpus-wide stream:

1. `:rf.error/no-frame-context` — `frame.cljc:804-952` (`no-frame-context-payload` at `:834`, `emit-no-frame-context!` at `:906`); by construction there is no frame to stamp.
2. The pre-frame SSR hydration-parse arm of `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` — `error_emit.cljc:815-830` documents the union shape's `:frame <id-or-nil>` "(the pre-frame hydration-parse FRAMELESS case …)"; the late-bind directory entry `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` (`directory.cljc:902`) names it explicitly.
3. hicasso's `compute-sub` errors — `server.cljs:221-222`: "`:rf.error/sub-exception` is stamped `:frame nil` BY CONSTRUCTION — a pure fn has no frame in scope to stamp". Its `watch-recovered-errors!` (`:254-295`) registers on `:errors` for exactly this reason, "measured rather than stylistic" — the per-frame SSR buffer read CLEAN on the failure it exists to catch.

The sink route refuses them by design: `route-error-record!` is "a NO-OP when the record's `:frame` is unresolved … incl. the FRAMELESS `:frame nil` records, which carry no frame-owned sink policy by definition" (`observability.cljc:317-322`; `frame-observability` at `:150-157` returns nil on a nil id; `error_emit.cljc:909` repeats it at the call site). So **retiring the stream before the process default exists opens a gap: those three categories reach nobody.** A1 (the default) must land before A2 (the retirement), and the ordering is structural, not a preference.

A second dependency underneath: "project under no frame" is not expressible today. `elision.cljc:1128` resolves the governing frame as `(or (:frame opts) (rf.frame/resolve-current-frame))`, so an explicit nil falls through to the AMBIENT frame; `projection.cljc:572-575` seeds `:frame` from the record by truthiness the same way. rf2-kuky.5 (open, dispatchable) makes explicit nil fail closed. A1 is blocked on it.

### The strongest counter-evidence

Codex holds the opposite position and said so without hedging. From the epic (rf2-kuky notes, "One-reviewer findings"): "this corpus only; **codex explicitly did not verify them and calls them larger design decisions** … Codex's caution on these is worth carrying: one documented home per operation supports the accepted cleanups, but does not by itself justify removing every facade export or building a universal clear/query/configure language." From the observability doc itself: "Retiring public `:errors`/`:events` listeners and adding process-wide policy inheritance is a larger redesign than the evidence presently earns. Raw synchronous capture and projected delivery are different operations, even if both ultimately register callbacks in maps. Two empty application consumer lists do not establish equivalence." And: "Do not add a process default merely to make deletion of an existing door possible. If a real multi-frame integration later needs it, specify absent policy versus explicit empty policy, per-stream inheritance versus whole-map replacement, frameless records, teardown records whose owner no longer resolves, and prevention of duplicate delivery. These are semantic choices, not simply one fallback branch."

The tree gives Codex two real facts. hicasso's `capture-intents` (`test.cljs:567-603`) is a shipped test-kit port built on the corpus-wide `:events` record and filtered by `:frame` — a synchronous raw capture, not a projected egress. And hicasso `server.cljs:254-295` chose the raw stream after measuring the projected route failing on frameless records. Both survive under A — through `re-frame.event-emit` / `re-frame.error-emit` directly, implementation tier — but "moved out of sight" is exactly Codex's objection. Note also that `spec/Principles.md` §Regularity permits "the documented alternative with a stated use case"; A's answer is that the stated use case (raw exception) is false and the true ones (frameless, declare-once) are what A1 absorbs.

Grok took the middle: A, but in two beads, and "Zero in-repo app consumers of either door means we do not yet know how a Sentry bridge will actually be written. Deleting the advanced door before the replacement exists is the one way this can fail closed on frameless records."

## The decision

**Which door(s) does the library offer an application for production observation of errors and events?**

- **A.** One door. Frame `:observability` + a `configure! {:observability …}` process default, wired by `register-observability-sink!`. `register-listener!` keeps `#{:trace :epoch}`. Two implementation beads, A1 then A2.
- **B.** Two doors, as designed. `:events`/`:errors` stay public as the documented advanced corpus-wide hook; no process default; rf2-kuky.21's §8 "Advanced" section becomes the permanent home, with the one discriminator sentence.
- **C.** The process default now (A1 alone); retirement revisited once a real Sentry bridge exists in the corpus.

Under A or C the ruling also settles seven routing questions. Recommended answers, for Mike to accept "as recommended" or amend:

| # | Question | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Precedence | per STREAM: a frame that declares a stream (even `[]`) uses its own entries; a frame that omits it inherits the default's entries for that stream. Whole-map replacement rejected (forces every frame with one custom sink to restate the default). |
| 2 | Absent vs explicit empty | as 1; `[]` is the opt-out; `{:observability nil}` on `configure!` clears the default. Validation reuses `frame_classification.cljc`'s validator at call time, fail-loud, reusing `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` with `:where 'rf/configure!` — no new category. Not an `assert` (rf2-xn13's rule; the existing guard at `core.cljc:2668-2683` is the model). |
| 3 | Frameless records | process default only; projected with `{:frame nil}` → fail-closed per `015:251` case 3. Blocked on rf2-kuky.5. |
| 4 | Records whose `:frame` no longer resolves (destroyed / dissociated incarnation) | route to the process default under fail-closed projection. `015:296` forbids borrowing ANOTHER FRAME's policy; the process default is not a frame's. `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc` pins only that a dissociated id must not resolve to a same-id successor — compatible. **This is the one answer with no precedent in the tree; it needs Mike's actual choice.** |
| 5 | Duplicate delivery | exactly one policy source per record; a sink id present in both frame and default is invoked once. |
| 6 | Raw cross-frame hook | an explicit `:rf.egress/local-raw` entry on the process default (enum member verified). |
| 7 | Console fallback | composes with rf2-kuky.18: a process-default delivery to a registered sink owns the record. |

## Options

### A. One door — process default first, retirement second (fable, Grok; recommended)
DOSSIER ATTACHMENT (continued, piece 2/3, verbatim, contiguous with the previous piece):
**What changes.** A1: `configure!` gains `:observability` (`core.cljc:2620`, delegating to a `re-frame.observability/configure!` over a `defonce` default atom); `frame-observability` resolves per stream against the default; `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` / `route-handled-event!` gain the frameless and unresolved-owner arms; one conformance fixture beside `spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-observability-sink-receives-projected-record.edn`. A2: `listener-streams` → `#{:trace :epoch}`; the `:events`/`:errors` `case` arms, docstring and `unknown-listener-stream!` message; four consumers migrate (hicasso `server.cljs:287` → `re-frame.error-emit`, `test.cljs:597,603` → `re-frame.event-emit`, `elision_demo.cljs:243,249` → a `:handled-events` sink on its frame, Story `shell.cljs:1153` already gone under .18); `frame.cljc:2810,3948` and `ssr.cljc:388` are already on the implementation registry and do not move. A3: one note on rf2-xpd8 (closed 2026-09-05) that "listener" in its ruling now names `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!`.

**What it costs.** Breadth, not depth. Tests: 66 files on the `:errors` facade + 16 on `:events` at tip (bead said 61 + 16) migrate to the implementation namespaces or — better — to a `re-frame.test-support` capture bracket, the sibling of rf2-64iuw's trace-recorder bracket. Teaching: 16 files (docs 4, spec 2, skills 9, migration README 1 — list in the bead). Hot zone, sequential: `spec/API.md` (§Event-emit/§Error-emit `:571-591` fold into §Frame-owned sinks `:699`, §Observation listeners `:593-606`, §Configure keys `:895`), `spec/009` (`:643`, `:1124`, `:1214-1284`, `:1285`, `:2689`), `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4341-4350`, `spec/002-Frames.md:647-659`, `spec/Conventions.md:1327-1331`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md` attach table, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` M-13 rows, `api-manifest-metadata.edn` then regenerate. A new `configure` key is a Spec change by the fixed-and-additive rule (`API.md` §Fixed-and-additive) — fine, additive. Removing two members of a closed stream vocabulary is a Spec-ulation "breakage"; the posture answers it (pre-alpha, a redundant spelling is deleted). Risk: fail-open ONLY if A2 lands before A1 — which the bead ordering forbids — and frameless projection is only as safe as rf2-kuky.5. Behaviour change for a library that wanted a cross-frame hook without touching frame config: it now calls `configure!` once.

**What it buys.** The surface says what the spec says. `register-listener!` means one thing (raw dev stream, both members DCE'd); `register-observability-sink!` means one thing (projected production egress). A multi-frame app declares once. Frameless records get a projected home for the first time (today they have only the raw one). The fail-open door leaves the first-search path.

### B. Two doors, as designed — the raw stream stays the documented advanced hook (Codex)

**What changes.** Nothing beyond rf2-kuky.17–.21. The how-to's §8 "Advanced — the corpus-wide listener" (as .21 rewrites it) is the permanent home; `spec/API.md:585` and `spec/009:1235` gain .21's one sentence: the sink also delivers `:exception` under the default profile; what the corpus-wide stream alone carries is a frameless record and a declaration made once per process.

**What it costs.** Two production doors persist for one job, with the fail-open one still one search away and still the simpler-looking one (one call, no frame config). `register-listener!` keeps mixing DCE'd and always-on streams. A multi-frame app declares a policy on every frame. Frameless records stay raw-only. The rf2-xpd8 vocabulary needs nothing. Zero migration.

**What it buys.** Zero churn against ~82 test files and 16 teaching files. Keeps hicasso's measured one-render window on the public verb, and keeps `capture-intents` on the public `:events` port. Matches Codex: "Trusting programmers supports an explicitly advanced raw hook beside the normal projected path." Honest reading of Principles §Regularity, which allows a documented alternative with a stated use case — once .21 states the true one.

### C. Process default now, retirement later (Grok's "third, cheaper path")

**What changes.** A1 only: `configure! {:observability …}`, frameless routing, unresolved-owner routing, the conformance fixture. `:events`/`:errors` stay public.

**What it costs.** All of A1's semantic work (questions 1–7) for a knob with zero consumers today, while the interval has THREE ways to declare production observation (frame policy, process default, raw stream) — the count goes up before it comes down, and "later" has no trigger unless the ruling names one (recommended un-park trigger: the first real bridge in `examples/` or a consumer app, per Principles §The demand bar's "pre-settled promotion shape"). Blocked on rf2-kuky.5 exactly as A1 is.

**What it buys.** The cheapest reversible position. The frameless home is built before anything is deleted, so nothing can fail closed on those records; a real bridge can be written on the sink + default and observed before the raw door goes. If it is never missed, A2 files itself.

## Recommendation

**A, as two beads in order — and the fallback is C, which is A1 alone.** The spec already ruled which door is normal (`API.md:585`, `009:1235`, `015:270`), and a surface that contradicts its own spec's ruling is the thing this wave exists to fix; Principles §Regularity over cleverness wants "one obvious way", and the one stated use case that licensed the alternative (raw exception) is false at tip (`projection.cljc:352-360`). The two true carries — frameless records and declare-once — are precisely what A1 delivers, and A1 gives frameless records a PROJECTED home they have never had, closing a fail-open posture the spec never names (a public verb that bypasses the projector entirely; Principles §Low hidden context). After A2, both members of `register-listener!` are DCE'd and both members of the production door are projected: the vocabulary carries the tier. The masterpiece posture is the tiebreaker against Codex's "larger redesign than the evidence earns": the cost is mechanical breadth in tests, the depth is one atom and one fallback branch, and pre-alpha is when a redundant public door is deleted rather than documented. The implementation registries Codex wants preserved ARE preserved, just not as public spellings — which is the same one-home-per-operation rule Codex endorsed for the accepted cleanups. Precedent for a process default with per-frame override already lives inside `configure!`: `:trace-buffer {:events-retained N}` applies "to `:rf/default` and to every frame that did not set its own `:rf.trace/events-retained` metadata" (`core.cljc:2622-2631`).

**If Mike disagrees:** C is the right hedge, not B — B leaves frameless records raw-only and the count at two; C builds the home, keeps the door, and lets a real bridge decide. Choose B only if Mike wants the raw synchronous-capture door to be a permanent PUBLIC contract for tools like hicasso's test-kit, rather than an implementation seam.

**Filed / dispatched on each outcome.**
- **A:** file A1 (`blocks:` rf2-kuky.5 and rf2-kuky.17; rf2-xn13 is CLOSED at tip so the bead's third blocker has lapsed — the guard is already always-on at `core.cljc:2668-2683`), carrying the seven answers verbatim; file A2 blocked on A1, rf2-kuky.18, .19, .21, with consumer counts re-measured at filing; post A3 as a note on rf2-xpd8 (closed; a note is fine). Hot-zone sequencing: A1 and A2 each touch `spec/API.md`, `spec/002`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`; neither may run beside .17, .20 or .21 on the same file.
- **B:** close rf2-kuky.22 with the reason; name rf2-kuky.21's §8 the permanent home; nothing else files.
- **C:** file A1 only, with the un-park trigger for A2 written into A1's description.

- **rf2-kuky.17** (delete the sink-entry `:opts` bag) — open, dispatchable, lands under every outcome. A1's entry grammar is the closed map .17 leaves.

## Provenance

- Tip: `6d513ba07f` (`6d513ba07fd3bb021ad3e36c6d1ba1b2ad9ae0b4`), `main`, clean. Written 2026-09-06 16:23:38 AUSEST. Read-only: no repository edits, no `bd` mutations, no git state changes.

## Codex Recommendation

### Choose B: retain independent observation; make projected delivery the obvious default

The teaching problem is real, but these are not equivalent operations. Keep `:events` and `:errors` on the public listener verb; lead ordinary production integration with frame-owned projected sinks. Do not add process-wide inheritance solely to remove two stream keywords. This recommendation follows a fresh source review, not the earlier Codex position quoted above.

The strongest case for A is good: configure monitoring once, cover frameless failures, and avoid teaching every integration to reconstruct projection. That could earn a process default independently. However, A's proposed fallback does **not** replace the existing cross-frame observation contract, and the implementation is deeper than an atom plus a fallback branch. Pre-alpha permits breaking changes; it does not make different operations redundant.

### Three distinctions the decision must retain

**1. A default is not an independent observer.** Under the proposed per-stream precedence, `{:errors []}` or a frame's custom error entries prevent the process default from receiving that frame's errors. Consequently a process-default `:rf.egress/local-raw` entry is not a replacement for a listener that watches every emission regardless of that frame's monitoring configuration. This is a direct consequence of A's routing rules, not a hypothetical implementation bug. Independent listeners also compose by id without integrations replacing a shared process-policy value.

The distinction already has concrete consumers: [Hicasso's `capture-intents`](../../implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test.cljs) installs and removes an observer around a synchronous operation without changing the observed frame's configuration; [its server render watcher](../../implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs) captures recovered, potentially frameless failures during one render. Moving those implementations to private registries preserves the framework's own privileges, but deliberately withdraws the same composable observation primitive from other programmers. That may be Mike's choice; it is not merely deleting another spelling.
DOSSIER ATTACHMENT (continued, piece 3/3, verbatim, contiguous with the previous piece):
**2. `local-raw` does not recover the substrate record.** [The event substrate](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/event_emit.cljc) publishes `:time` and `:outcome`; [observability routing](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc) constructs a different record with `:status`, effects and correlation, but no event timestamp. Non-event error attributes move under `:tags`. [Projection](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc) still applies event-registration redaction before its frame-policy walker, even for `local-raw`. These can be sensible monitoring choices, but a profile changes projection, not the producer's record contract. Nor is the current event listener literally unprocessed raw data: its event vector is already wire-elided.

More importantly, the current event-centric sink route loses useful diagnosis **before projection**. [The error producer](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc), `dispatch-on-error!`, builds `:source-coord` and category attribution such as `:failing-id`, `:reason`, `:flow-id` and `:op` into its corpus record, then calls `route-error!` without those attributes. Changing the egress profile cannot restore them. Losing which coeffect/interceptor failed is material to a productive production-monitoring API; fix or explicitly settle this before presenting sinks as a fully equivalent replacement.

**3. Dead-incarnation coverage cannot be implemented solely inside the routing fallback.** The same producer gates the entire sink call on `route-frame?`; `dispatch-error-record*` does likewise for post-dissociation teardown reports. When it is false, a new default inside `observability.cljc` is never reached. Moreover, the stale record's id may resolve successfully to a successor, so an unresolved-id test alone is insufficient. The [reincarnation regression](../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc) expressly preserves corpus delivery while suppressing successor-frame routing. An A1 implementation must carry this distinction through the producer seam: no authority to use a frame's policy, but permission to deliver through process policy, projecting with an explicitly absent owner. It must not re-resolve the stale id.

### Proportionate implementation and alternatives

For B, finish the already separated option-honesty, alias and teaching work; do not reopen the in-flight console change here. Update [the production how-to](../../docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md) and [API contract](../../spec/API.md) to state the real discriminator: **independent corpus observation versus policy-selected projected delivery**, including frameless and stale-incarnation coverage. Raw exception presence alone is indeed not the discriminator. Do not imply that default projection sanitizes arbitrary exception contents; its opaque-exception residual remains.

Separately, repair the dropped diagnostic attribution using an explicit set of structural fields and appropriate projected tree slots, not a blanket merge of arbitrary attributes into public summaries. Preserve query-vector identity and the existing category meanings. This improves the recommended monitoring path under every outcome.

If repeated configuration is the actual inconvenience, an application-owned shared policy value or frame-construction function is a smaller alternative; it solves repetition, not frameless delivery. If an actual host integration needs projected frameless delivery, C is a reasonable additive feature after rf2-kuky.5, but does not by itself justify later retirement. A is defensible only with an explicit ruling that independent public observation is being withdrawn, plus the attribution and producer-seam work above. Do not quietly turn a fallback into an additive global observer to recover parity: that is another routing model.

Focused acceptance for B: one sink and one temporary listener observe the same live failure with their documented shapes; listener capture still works with empty frame policy; removing it ends capture; and frameless/reincarnated failures retain the existing independent delivery without reaching a successor's sink. Attribution changes need a coeffect/interceptor example proving the projected record identifies the actual failing component. For A/C additionally test default inheritance versus `[]`, registered/missing/throwing sinks, and stale-owner fallback under a live unrelated ambient frame. These are meaningful cases, not a broad new observability framework.

The ethos here is a clear default plus an honest, small independent primitive. [Regularity and low hidden context](../../spec/Principles.md) favor that over reducing keyword count by adding ambient policy coupling.

## Problem

Three dead spellings of the listener registries survive beside the one app-facing verb `rf/register-listener!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2135-2168`) and the home namespaces:

1. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/emit.cljc` (77 lines): six `def` re-exports of `re-frame.event-emit` / `re-frame.error-emit`. Its docstring (:5) calls itself "the single public registration facade", contradicting `core.cljc:2224-2238` (the registries are reached through `register-listener!`'s `:events` / `:errors` streams and the home namespaces). No manifest row (`grep '"re-frame.emit"' spec/api-manifest.edn` → 0), no `docs/api` page. Consumers: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:13,388`; `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:43,204`; one test, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_r1_purge_test.clj:31,80,98,132,158,185`.
2. `re-frame.trace/register-listener!`, `unregister-listener!`, `clear-listeners!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:951-953`): `def` aliases of `re-frame.trace.tooling/*` (`trace/tooling.cljc:81,88,95`). rf2-ic1sv pick c called them "the canonical app-facing names" (`trace.cljc:21-26`, `:943-949`); the facade `:trace` arm superseded that, and `spec/API.md:596-606` and the manifest (0 `"re-frame.trace"` rows) know only the facade. Non-test consumers: 0 (`core.cljc:2164,2178` call the alias for the `:trace` arm; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:27` and `drop_in.cljc:73` mention it in prose). Test consumers: 97 files (`git grep -lE "(rf\.trace|re-frame\.trace)/(register-listener!|unregister-listener!|clear-listeners!)" -- 'implementation/*test*' 'tools/*test*' 'testbeds/*' 'skills/*'`), of which 49 register/unregister and the rest call `clear-listeners!` in fixtures.
3. Late-bind hooks `:trace.tooling/register-listener!` / `:unregister-listener!` (`trace/tooling.cljc:1300-1301`; directory entries `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:1114-1121`). The directory entry itself says the hook is "retained for the directory contract" and that every live consumer calls `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` directly; the one real consumer moved to `:error-emit/register-error-listener!` under rf2-87f7fb (`directory.cljc:907-914`). `git grep -n "get-fn :trace.tooling/\(un\)\?register-listener!"` → 0.

Plus `routing.cljc:195-204`: an idempotent purge, on every façade load, of the `:rf.route/on-match-error-trap` listener id retired with EP-0037 R1 — a shim for an HMR session spanning a change that landed months ago; no shipped code registers that id.

## Evidence

Measured at HEAD as above. Also: `trace.cljc:39-49` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally on both platforms, so the aliases buy no elision the facade lacks (the `trace.cljc:28-34` DCE note is about the buffer/configure surface at `:955-957`, which stays and belongs to `@trace-epoch.1`). `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:338-347` describes the aliases as "thin late-bind shells whose `:trace.tooling/*` lookups resolve to nil" — stale; they are `def`s, and the `trace-events` sentinel reads 0 in the counter bundle because Closure drops the unreachable buffer fns, not because the namespace is absent from the graph.

## Target API

One home per verb, nothing else names a registry:

- `rf/register-listener!` / `rf/unregister-listener!` — the only app-facing spelling (unchanged).
- `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` / `clear-listeners!` — the `:trace` registry's home: core's `:trace` arm, SSR's own listener (`ssr.cljc:404`), the test-support bracket (`test_support.cljc:1221`), fixture clears (`test_support.cljc:552`).
- `re-frame.error-emit/*` / `re-frame.event-emit/*` — the always-on registries' homes: framework-internal consumers and the late-bind hooks (`frame.cljc:2810,3909`).

```clojure
;; core.cljc:2164 / :2178 — before
:trace (rf.trace/register-listener! id f)
;; after (add [re-frame.trace.tooling :as rf.trace.tooling] to core's requires;
;; trace.cljc:49 already requires it on both platforms, so reachability is unchanged)
:trace (rf.trace.tooling/register-listener! id f)

;; ssr.cljc:388 — before
(rf-emit/register-error-listener! ::error-projection error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener)
;; after
(rf.error-emit/register-error-listener! ::error-projection error-listener/error-emit-projection-listener)
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer; codex: "Remove proven unused aliases independently; internal fan-out and late binding need not become public synonyms." Grok's retirement bead lists all three. Independent of the observability.6 ruling.

## Deletion list

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/emit.cljc` — whole file.
- `trace.cljc:943-953` (section comment + three defs); trim the pick-c paragraphs at `:21-26` and the require comment `:41-48` to what remains true (tooling is required for the buffer/configure defs at `:955-957`, which `@trace-epoch.1` owns — do not touch `:955-957` here; sequence with that bead since both edit `:940-957`).
- `trace/tooling.cljc:1291-1301` (comment + two `set-fn!`), `:57` docstring bullet.
- `directory.cljc:1114-1121` (two entries) — `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj` pins both directions (`every-published-key-has-a-directory-entry`, `every-directory-entry-is-actually-published`), so entry and publication go together.
- `routing.cljc:43` (require) and `:204`; the comment `:195-201` says "exactly these three" → two (the two `clear-event` purges at `:202-203` are routing's and stay).
- `check-bundle-isolation.cjs:338-347` comment — rewritten to the measured mechanism (aliases gone; tooling reachable via `re-frame.trace`; sentinel held by DCE of unreachable fns).

## Consumers to migrate

- `core.cljc:2164,2178` → `rf.trace.tooling/*` (+ require).
- `ssr.cljc:13,388` → `re-frame.error-emit`.
- `routing_r1_purge_test.clj`: `::user-probe` / `::channel-probe` registrations (:98,132,158,185) → `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!` / `unregister-error-listener!`; the `retired-trap` arm (:10, :51, :80, the three `error-listener-registered? retired-trap` assertions, the deftest title "three") deleted; acceptance criterion 2 (`::channel-probe`) kept.
- 97 test files: `rf.trace/clear-listeners!` → `rf.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!` in fixtures; `rf.trace/register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` → `rf/register-listener! :trace` / `rf/unregister-listener! :trace` where the file already requires `re-frame.core`, else `rf.trace.tooling/*`; require aliases per `spec/Conventions.md`'s canonical `rf.*` dialect. `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machines/test_support.cljc:115-140` is a shared helper — migrate it once. Mechanical; `git grep` the two regexes above until both read 0.
- `test_support.cljc:1127` comment (names the tooling verb — still right; touch only if the sentence reads wrong).
- Prose: `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md:331` (`re-frame.trace/register-listener!` → `rf/register-listener! :trace`); `install.cljs:27` and `drop_in.cljc:73` comments.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- HOT-ZONE `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2222-2223` — the hook-rename table rows `:trace.tooling/register-trace-cb! → :trace.tooling/register-listener!` / `remove-trace-cb! → unregister-listener!` name a target hook that no longer exists → "removed (no consumer; call `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` directly, or `rf/register-listener! :trace`)". Same table in `skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md:135-136`.
- `spec/API.md:606` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:657-660` already name `re-frame.trace.tooling/clear-listeners!` — no change.
- Manifest: no rowed var changes; run `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` (no regeneration expected).
- Examples: 0 consumers. Conformance: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj:236-238` uses the alias — part of the test migration; `spec/conformance/fixtures` name no listener verb.
- Tests to add: none beyond the migrated ones; `late_bind_drift_test` is the hook-roster gate.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

One hot-zone file (migration README, one row) — serialise with observability.5's one-line edit there. Sequence with `@trace-epoch.1` on `trace.cljc:940-957` (whichever lands second rebases a ten-line region). Independent of observability.1/2/4 and of the ruling.

## Risks

Breadth, not depth: ~97 test files, all mechanical. The `core.cljc` require of `re-frame.trace.tooling` looks like the thing the bundle-isolation comment warns against — it is not (trace already requires it); the gate proves it. A downstream consumer using `re-frame.emit` or `re-frame.trace/register-listener!` gets a compile-time unresolved-var error naming the old symbol — pre-alpha, no shim; the migration README's M-26 table already routes v1 names to the facade.
