title: api(observability): delete the sink-entry :opts bag that make-frame validates and route-stream! never delivers
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

A frame's `:observability` sink entry accepts an `:opts` map. `make-frame` validates its shape and fails loud on a non-map (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc:240-252`, pinned by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:189-206` `fail-loud-on-bad-observability-opts`). Nothing ever reads it: `route-stream!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc:172-189`) reads only `:sink` (:181) and `:rf.egress/profile` (:183), and `deliver-to-sink!` (:159-170) calls `(f projected)` (:168) with the record alone. Every teaching sample carries the bag (`:opts {:service "checkout-spa" :env "prod"}`): `observability.cljc:22`, `frame_classification.cljc:14`, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:281-285`, `spec/API.md:701`, `spec/002-Frames.md:654`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4325-4332` (`FrameSinkEntry`, rowed "vendor-specific, framework does not own the vocabulary"), `docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md:143`, `docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:254,258`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:153`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md:140,143,152`. A slot designed as a pass-through that does not pass through is the textbook `spec/Principles.md` §No silent swallow violation, on the door the spec calls the NORMAL production observation surface (`spec/API.md:585`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1258`, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270`).

## Evidence

- `observability.cljc:159-170` `deliver-to-sink!` — `(f projected)`; `:172-189` `route-stream!` — `(:sink entry)`, `(get entry :rf.egress/profile default-profile)`; no other key is read anywhere in the namespace (`grep -n ":opts" observability.cljc` → line 22 only, the docstring sample).
- `frame_classification.cljc:240-252` — the validation; `:143-150` the section comment naming `:opts` as part of the entry grammar; `:84` lists `:opts` among the bare keys of the frame config.
- Consumers writing `:opts` outside docs/spec/skills: 0 (`git grep -n ":opts {:service"` → only the files above plus `observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc:78` and `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:109,156`). `register-observability-sink!` has 0 non-test callers (expected — `spec/015:292`), so no external sink relies on the bag.
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-observability-sink-receives-projected-record.edn` does not carry `:opts` — the conformance corpus is unaffected.

## Target API

The sink entry becomes a CLOSED map. Vendor configuration is the sink fn's own business (it closes over it); per-frame branching reads the record's `:frame` slot, which every projected record carries.

```clojure
;; before
(rf/make-frame {:id :app/main
                :observability {:errors [{:sink :my-app.sinks/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability
                                          :opts {:service "checkout-spa" :env "prod"}}]}})
(rf/register-observability-sink! :my-app.sinks/sentry (fn [record] (sentry/capture record)))

;; after — the entry is {:sink kw} + optional :rf.egress/profile, nothing else;
;; an unknown key (`:opts` included) fails loud at make-frame like a bad profile does.
(rf/make-frame {:id :app/main
                :observability {:errors [{:sink :my-app.sinks/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability}]}})
(let [tags {:service "checkout-spa" :env "prod"}]
  (rf/register-observability-sink! :my-app.sinks/sentry
    (fn [record] (sentry/capture (assoc record :tags tags)))))
```

`validate-sink-entry!` gains one clause: any key outside `#{:sink :rf.egress/profile}` throws `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` with `:bad-key [:observability <stream> <k>]` and `:bad-entry entry` (the same shape the profile clause uses at :228-239). Deleting the `:opts` clause WITHOUT closing the map would leave `:opts` silently ignored — the same accept-and-drop shape, one validator short — so the closed map is part of the fix, not gold plating. (If a shared vendor sink ever needs per-frame configuration, the record's `:frame` is the key; delivering a second argument is the documented alternative and is NOT done here — codex and fable both favour removal on the measured consumers.)

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area; codex cross-check confirmed this defect at source ("frame validation accepts an `:opts` map, while sink routing passes only the projected record… For today's measured consumers I favor removal, with configuration captured in the registered function and existing `:frame` attribution available… Either choice must remove the accept-and-drop contract from code and examples"). Grok: "Delete `:opts`… never accept-and-drop."

## Deletion list

- `frame_classification.cljc:240-252` (the `:opts` clause) — replaced by the closed-map clause; `:143-150` comment and `:84` and `:14` docstring mentions.
- `observability.cljc:22` docstring sample.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4325-4332` — the `[:opts {:optional true} [:map-of :keyword :any]]` row of `FrameSinkEntry` and the comment line "`:rf.egress/profile` and `:opts` are optional"; make the map closed (`{:closed true}`) so the schema says what the validator does. HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:206` (principle 4: "Vendor-specific sink fields live under a local `:opts` map" → vendor configuration is closed over by the sink fn; the sink id stays outside the framework namespace), `:281-285` sample, `:289` ("or a non-map `:opts`" → "or any key beyond `:sink` / `:rf.egress/profile`"). Not hot-zone.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:654` ("with an optional `:rf.egress/profile` and `:opts` map"). HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/API.md:701` (`{:handled-events [{:sink <id> :rf.egress/profile … :opts {…}}] …}`). HOT-ZONE.
- Docs: `configure-dev-and-prod.md:143`, `keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:254,258`.
- Skills: `api-cheatsheet.md:153`, `privacy-and-elision.md:140,143,152`.
- Tests: `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:109` (drop `:opts` from the good entry), `:156` (the missing-`:sink` bad entry `{:opts {:service "x"}}` — keep the case, spell the entry without `:opts`), `:189-206` (replace `fail-loud-on-bad-observability-opts` with `fail-loud-on-unknown-sink-entry-key`, asserting `:bad-key [:observability :handled-events :opts]` for `{:sink :x :opts {}}` and a second unknown key), `observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc:78`.
- `docs/EP/EP-0015-frame-owned-egress-policy.md:440,692,696` — an EP is a dated design record, not normative; leave it, and say so in the PR body.

## Consumers to migrate

None in code (0 non-test `register-observability-sink!` callers; 0 non-test `:opts` writers). Examples: 0 (`examples/` contains no `:observability` policy).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

As listed. `spec/api-manifest.edn` — no var changes, no regeneration; run `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` anyway. Conformance corpus and mcp-conformance: unaffected (measured above). Migration README: no v1-era name involved.

Gate note: the `Spec-Schemas.md` edit is inside a fenced block — neither `check_doc_slugs.py` nor `mkdocs build --strict` inspects it; hand-check the schema reads as valid Malli and say so in the PR body. The 002/API/015 edits are prose; both link gates apply.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches three one-toucher files (`Spec-Schemas.md`, `002-Frames.md`, `API.md`). Serialise with observability.5 (also `API.md`) and with any `@egress` bead editing `Spec-Schemas.md`'s `:rf/project-egress-opts` — different sections, same file. Independent of observability.2/3/4 and of the ruling in observability.6 (whose process-default entry grammar inherits the closed map).

## Risks

Low. A consumer outside the repo passing `:opts` fails loud at `make-frame` with the key named — pre-alpha, no shim. Fail direction is closed (a frame that fails to register routes nothing).

## Local dossier

ai/findings/API-review/fable/observability-doors.md (§The problem, fact 4; §Deletion list) — local-only pointer.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -n ":opts" implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc` → 0 hits.
- `(rf/make-frame {:id :t :observability {:errors [{:sink :x :opts {}}]}})` throws `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` with `(:bad-key data)` = `[:observability :errors :opts]`; the same with `{:sink :x :vendor 1}` names `:vendor`; `{:sink :x :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/public-error}` still registers.
- A registered sink fn receives the projected record and its `:frame` slot (existing `observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc` stays green with `:opts` removed).
- `git grep -n ":opts {:service"` → hits only under `docs/EP/`.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` `FrameSinkEntry` is `{:closed true}` with two keys; hand-verified and stated in the PR body.
- `implementation/core`: `clojure -M:test` green; `npm run test:cljs` green.

title: api(machines): child completion is :final?/:output-key under :spawn and :spawn-all; delete :on-child-done/-error
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from machines.md (ref machines.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

A machine child has two ways to say "I am done", and which one it must use depends on how its PARENT spawned it:

- Under `:spawn`, the child enters a `:final?` leaf; the runtime (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc`, `finalize-machine` :187) reads `:output-key`, folds the parent's `:spawn :on-done` / routes `:spawn :on-error`, emits the `:rf.machine/done` trace, and auto-destroys the child (005 §Final states, D4).
- Under `:spawn-all`, the child must hand-dispatch `[parent-id [<the parent's :on-child-done keyword> child-id & extra]]` from its terminal state's `:entry`. `join.cljc` intercepts that at the PARENT's handler boundary (`intercept-spawn-all-event` :912), after `stamp-join-completion-fx` (:377, called from `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:787`) rewrote the carrier into the reserved `:rf.machine/join-dispatch` transport fx (:164; registered `machines.cljc:378-380`) so the exact-attempt coordinate can ride the recordable `:rf.machine/join-attempt` cofx fact.

So the child has to know its parent's join vocabulary, and a child meant to be reusable under both parents implements BOTH protocols: `testbeds/deep_machine/core.cljs:96-99` is `:final? true` AND `:entry :dispatch-child-done`. There is no bridge from finality to the join: `join.cljc:860-871` says a completed child's terminal "is NOT necessarily `:final?`", and `lifecycle_fx/traces.cljc:64` says a joined child's terminal state "was NOT `:final?`, so it stays a LIVE actor that the join tears down at resolution or parent exit". A `:final?` join child that does NOT hand-dispatch auto-destroys without folding the join, and the join hangs. `skills/re-frame2/patterns/long-running-work.md:136` nevertheless tells authors that `:spawn-all` "recognises completion natively" via `:final?` — false at tip; this bead makes it true.

## Evidence (tip `6445d0611b`)

- `:on-child-done` / `:on-child-error` authors: examples 2 — `examples/patterns/long_running_work/worker.cljs:313-314` (child action `:dispatch-done` :145-152, `:done` `:entry :dispatch-done` :195-200), `examples/patterns/boot/boot.cljs:310-311` (child actions `:dispatch-done` :138-153 / `:dispatch-error` :155-161, `:done`/`:failed` :192-193 — NOT `:final?`, `:meta {:terminal? true}` only); testbeds 1 — `testbeds/deep_machine/core.cljs:254-255` (action :76-87, leaf :96-99). Tools 0 (machines-viz `grammar.cljc` does not validate the `:spawn-all` shape, :533-534). 336 occurrences across 73 files repo-wide, 44 of them under `implementation/machines/test`.
- App-author `:final?` sites outside tools: 1 (`deep_machine:97`, the double-protocol child). The working single-`:spawn` consumer is `tools/xray/testbeds/machine_epochs/machines.cljs:223-245` (`:final?` + `:output-key :token` + parent `:on-done`) — unchanged by this bead, a regression surface.
- The resolution event today is `[parent-id (concat <on-all-complete ev> [decisive-child-id] child-extra)]` (`join.cljc:908`), `child-extra` being whatever the child hand-forwarded (:680, :986-993).
- `:on-done` is applied by a direct write to the parent's snapshot `:data` (`finalize.cljc:594`), NOT through a parent macrostep — the parent's `:always` cascade never sees the fold. `:on-error` by contrast is delivered as a dispatched `[:rf.machine.spawn/error …]` event into the parent (`finalize.cljc:398-405`). Boot's `:configuring` phase today ADVANCES on the child's hand-dispatched event (`boot.cljs:143-145`, action `:promote-staged`); after this bead the child dispatches nothing, so the parent must be able to advance on `:on-done`.
- `known-spawn-spec-keys` (`lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc:1478-1495`) is one set for `:spawn` AND `:spawn-all` children and already admits `:on-done` / `:on-error` on a child spec; nothing honours them on a `:spawn-all` child and 005:3684 omits them from the child-spec key list.
- Codex's three corrections, all verified in source: `:rf.machine/done` is emitted (`finalize.cljc:452-480`) and consumed nowhere as control; `join.cljc:19-27,97,412-413` and 005:3876 say the exact-attempt coordinate is "a replayable correlation record, NOT authentication"; a joined child today lives on after reporting done (`traces.cljc:55-70`; `:rf.machine/join-reaped` exists for exactly that) while `:final?` tears down synchronously (D4).

## Target API

```clojure
;; CHILD — one completion convention, whatever the parent used.
:done   {:final? true :output-key :result}                ;; success: result = (:result data)
:failed {:final? true :error? true :output-key :reason}   ;; failure: the existing error-terminal grammar (005 §Final states)

;; PARENT, single child — grammar unchanged
:spawn {:machine-id :work/processor :data (fn [{snap :snapshot}] …)
        :on-done  (fn [{:keys [data result]}] (assoc data :answer result))   ;; fold
        :on-error {:target :failed}}                                          ;; transition

;; PARENT, fan-out + join — the child-vocabulary keys are gone
:spawn-all {:children [{:id :s1 :machine-id :work/processor :data …
                        :on-done (fn [{:keys [data result]}] (assoc-in data [:results :s1] result))}  ;; optional per-child fold
                       {:id :s2 …} {:id :s3 …}]
            :join            :all                 ;; or :any
            :on-all-complete [:work/all-done]     ;; :on-some-complete for :any
            :on-any-failed   [:work/any-failed]}
```

Before / after for the worker example (`worker.cljs`):

```clojure
;; before
:spawn-all {:children […] :join :all
            :on-child-done :work/child-done :on-child-error :work/child-error
            :on-all-complete [:work/all-done] :on-any-failed [:work/any-failed]}
;; child
:dispatch-done (fn [{:keys [data]}] {:fx [[:dispatch [parent-id [:work/child-done (:shard data)]]]]})
:done {:meta {:terminal? true} :tags #{:work/done} :entry :dispatch-done}

;; after
:spawn-all {:children […] :join :all
            :on-all-complete [:work/all-done] :on-any-failed [:work/any-failed]}
;; child
:done {:final? true :output-key :shard :tags #{:work/done}}
```

Rules of the target:

1. **Completion is finality.** A child under either parent form completes by entering `:final?`; `:output-key` selects the result; `:error? true` marks failure. The child carries no parent vocabulary. Progress and other milestones remain ordinary `[:dispatch [parent-id …]]` messages and are never reinterpreted as completion (codex correction 3).
2. **The parent decides how results combine.** `:spawn-all` keeps `:join`, `:on-all-complete` / `:on-some-complete`, `:on-any-failed`. The resolution event keeps its shape `[parent-id [<resolution-ev…> <decisive-child-id> <result>]]` where `<result>` is now the decisive child's `:output-key` value (its error payload on `:on-any-failed`) — one value, not a vector of extras. A `:spawn-all` child invoke-spec additionally honours `:on-done` (the same `(fn [{:keys [data result]}] new-data)` fold as `:spawn :on-done`, run against the parent's `:data` at that child's finality, before the join fold). This is not a new envelope: the validator already admits the key on a child spec; honouring it is what lets the boot example delete its app-db staging slot (`boot.cljs:83,150` `:boot/stage-payload`). `:on-error` on a `:spawn-all` child is NOT honoured — failure control flow under a join is `:on-any-failed` — so remove it from the child-spec key set (split `known-spawn-spec-keys`) and let the existing `:rf.error/machine-unknown-spawn-key` fire; no new error category.
3. **Runtime-owned path (codex correction 1).** `finalize-machine` already computes `result` / `error-leaf?` and reads `:rf/join-child` (:340) for the reply facts. When the finishing actor carries `:rf/join-child`, finalize hands `{parent-id invoke-id child-id spawned-id attempt work-generation kind result}` straight to a join fold entry point in `join.cljc` (the runtime calls it; keep `intercept-fold` :1166, `compute-resolution` :621, `build-resolution-fx` :790, the `emit-*` trace fns, `suppress-stale-completion!` :451). No event is dispatched by the child, no trace is subscribed to; `:rf.machine/done` is EMITTED from the result exactly as today (:480).
4. **Correlation preserved, not ceremonised (codex correction 2).** The exact-attempt gate (`join-attempt-current?` :422, `join-work-generation` :438) keeps working from the coordinate the runtime stamped into `:rf/join-child` at spawn (`spawn.cljc:296-330`, incl. the `:work-generation` discriminator :313 for `:fixed-actor-id` children that reuse ids across attempts, :1184). Duplicate suppression (`:rf.machine.spawn-all/duplicate-completion`), `attempt-superseded` / `attempt-unverified`, post-resolution `late-completion`, the non-decisive `child-completed` terminal (one per child — `join_child_terminal_cljs_test`), sibling cancellation with `cancelled-on-join-resolution`, and the parent-exit cascade all keep their outcomes. Describe the gate in spec and docstrings as causal correlation; do not add a capability/secret.
5. **Recorded / replayed completion.** The coordinate rode the recordable `:rf.machine/join-attempt` cofx fact only because the carrier was a PUBLIC app event that had to survive EDN recording and `:dispatch-later` (005:3882). With the fold inside the child's own finalize step, replaying the child's terminal event replays the fold; there is no separate carrier. Rewrite `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/join_strict_mint_epoch_replay_test.clj` and `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/join_strict_mint_cljs_test.cljc` to drive children to `:final?` and still prove: strict-mint replay folds exactly once per child, no host generation, identical resolution.
6. **Parent advancement on a single child's completion — the measured gap you must close.** Pick ONE delivery mechanism and use it for both forms: (a) keep the synchronous fold (API.md:951 "fires synchronously", 005 D4) and run the parent's `:always` cascade after it, inside finalize, as one macrostep; or (b) deliver completion as ONE reserved internal parent event, the way `:on-error` already does, routed at the parent boundary to the `:on-done` fold / `:on-error` transition / join fold — which moves `:on-done` from same-tick to next-macrostep and must carry 005 §Final states step 3 and API.md:951 with it. Do NOT add an event-vector `:on-done` spelling or any completion-policy grammar (codex: "do not add a general completion-policy language"). The boot example's `:configuring` phase (single `:spawn`, must advance to `:loading-deps` on the loader's finality) is the acceptance case that forces the answer.
7. **Finality means teardown (codex correction 3) — make it explicit and check cleanup.** Under `:final?` a joined child is destroyed synchronously at completion with `:reason :rf.machine/finished`; it no longer "reports done and lives on". Consequences: (i) `:rf.machine/join-reaped` (post-terminal cleanup of a LIVE completed child) has no producer left, and neither has the verified-reap destroy form `{:rf/reap true :rf/parent-id :rf/invoke-id :rf/child-id}` that `build-resolution-fx` emits for completed children (`join.cljc:885-900`; `destroy.cljc:34-45,618,714,830-870`) nor the `:unverified-reap` / `:unresolved-join` causes of `:rf.error/machine-destroy-bad-arg` (`traces.cljc:111`; 009:2217) — delete them (list below); if you find a live producer, keep it and say so in the PR. Survivors still go `:explicit` + `cancelled-on-join-resolution`. (ii) `worker.cljs` and `boot.cljs` already treat done as terminal (`:meta {:terminal? true}`; `worker.cljs:196-197` "the exit cascade then sweeps the child away"); verify by test that nothing dispatches to a completed child afterwards (a dispatch to the destroyed address is `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, D5). (iii) `:meta {:terminal? true}` on those leaves is redundant with `:final?` — drop it in the migrated sites.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Fable proposed the collapse (`fable/machine-child-lifecycle-and-addressing.md` §Completion); codex checked it against `finalize.cljc` / `join.cljc` and calls it "the strongest compositional improvement in either corpus" (`codex/machine-child-completion.md`), adopting it with three corrections that this bead honours verbatim: the join must not be implemented by listening to the `:rf.machine/done` trace; the exact-attempt coordinates are causal correlation, not authentication, and are preserved inside the unified path; finality tears the child down immediately, so "done means terminal" is made explicit and worker/boot cleanup is checked. `fable/README.md` §Relationship lists "child completion unified under `:final?` for `:spawn` and `:spawn-all`" as two-reviewer. Codex bounds the finding to terminal completion and says it ships on its own — the `:system-id` question is @machines.2, separately.

acceptance_criteria:
- One child machine registered once (e.g. `:work/processor`) is used under a `:spawn` parent and under a `:spawn-all` parent with no parent vocabulary in the child. Under `:spawn`: the parent's `:on-done` receives the `:output-key` value and the parent transitions to its next state with no dispatch from the child. Under `:spawn-all :join :all`: three children reaching `:final?` fire `:on-all-complete` exactly once with the decisive child's id and result. Under `:join :any`: the first `:final?` fires `:on-some-complete`; survivors are destroyed with `:rf.machine.spawn/cancelled-on-join-resolution`.
- Error: `{:final? true :error? true :output-key :reason}` under `:spawn` fires the parent's `:on-error` transition with the payload; under `:spawn-all` fires `:on-any-failed` (when declared) and cancels survivors; without `:on-any-failed` the existing unsatisfiable-join diagnostic (`join.cljc:589-593`) still fires.
- Per-child `:on-done` on a `:spawn-all` child folds the parent's `:data` before the join fold; `:on-error` on a `:spawn-all` child is rejected at registration with `:rf.error/machine-unknown-spawn-key`.
- Progress: an ordinary `[:dispatch [parent-id [:progress …]]]` from a live child leaves the join's `:done` set unchanged.
- Cancel / restart: parent exits the `:spawn-all` state mid-flight → every child destroyed `:explicit`; re-entry mints a new attempt; a completion carrying the prior attempt's coordinate (a `:fixed-actor-id` child) is suppressed `:rf.machine.spawn-all/attempt-superseded`; a replayed record for an already-folded child is suppressed `duplicate-completion`.
- Cleanup: after resolution no child snapshot, no `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent> <invoke-id> :children]` entry and no registrar handler remains; a dispatch to a completed child's address yields `:rf.error/no-such-handler`; no `:rf.machine/join-reaped` destroy is emitted anywhere in the suite (or the PR names the surviving producer).

description:
RULED 2026-09-04 21:03:56 AUSEST (delegated ruling; see the RULING note for the full analysis, the reviewer positions, the contract wording, the implementation guidance, traps and acceptance criteria). This bead is PR1 of Option A: in a DEV build, an app-db candidate rejection (:rf.error/schema-validation-failure, :where :app-db, :rollback? true) ALSO fans one STRUCTURAL-ONLY record per failing registered path onto the always-on :errors stream, from inside validate-app-schema!'s existing debug-enabled? gate, through the :error-emit/dispatch-error-record late-bind hook (the union-record helper the :rf.schema/at-boundary arm uses). The dev trace stays byte-identical; production is untouched by construction; the rf2-fu75 dev console fallback then prints the rejection for free when nothing owns the stream. This is an additive SPEC AMENDMENT (spec/009 promotion criterion + row 1984, spec/010 row 4) plus code in implementation/schemas, a docstring in error_emit.cljc, three docs pages and tests. spec/009 and spec/010 are one-toucher hot-zone files - sequence at dispatch. PR2 (machine-data + malformed-schema rollback sites) is the follow-up bead created from this one and waits for this PR to MERGE.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-09-04 on worker/dispatchlater-a, with a control that fired). :rf.error/schema-validation-failure (:where :app-db) is emitted through re-frame.trace/emit-error! only - implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc, emit-validation-failure! and its emit-malformed-schema! sibling - and NOT through the both-axes emitter the router uses for other errors (re-frame.error-emit/emit-error-both!). So it reaches the DEV-ONLY :trace stream and never the always-on :errors stream. On one live page, one frame, one dispatch: a listener on :errors recorded 0 records while a listener on :trace recorded 17 :rf.error/schema-validation-failure records with :rollback? true for the SAME dispatch, whose :events-stream outcome was :rolled-back. The ruling: the promotion criterion governs what MUST ride the always-on axis in every build; it does not forbid a check that is compiled out of production from reporting, in the build where it runs, that it discarded a whole transaction. Always-on describes the stream's survival, not a promise that every producer exists in every build.

The added tests exercise only `nil` and a ClojureScript string, so the fallback is unpinned.

Keep the per-registration record, type hint, dev gate, and trace ordering. Make the reason's type classifier total and closed over foreign CLJS values (for example a trusted host classification with a constant fallback, never the object's overridable `constructor` value or `toString`), and add a focused CLJS regression with a planted own `constructor` sentinel proving neither the record nor its reason contains it. title: api(registry): add (rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f}) and delete the nine clear-* names
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:18:53 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.25 ruling agent (delegated by Mike); parent epic rf2-kuky; discovered-from rf2-kuky.25 (Q2 ruled **E**). The full decision dossier, both reviewers' analyses, the census and the ruling are attached as notes on rf2-kuky.25 — read them there; nothing under `ai/` is tracked._

## Ruling (verbatim from rf2-kuky.25)

> Q2 → **E**: one kind-keyed `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})` on `re-frame.core`, dispatching to each kind's OWNING lifecycle fn and never short-cutting a kind that owns runtime state to `registrar/unregister!`; opts EXACTLY `{:frame f}` and fail-closed, accepted for the two frame-scoped kinds only; unknown kind fails closed; returns the id for every kind; every per-kind public `clear-*` registrar-inverse name is deleted — no shim, no alias, no deprecation. Parity through the EXISTING resource-dispose / route-trace / flow-settle tests is the acceptance bar.

## Problem

The registrar is one map, `(kind, id) → metadata` (`spec/001-Registration.md:89`). The read side already speaks that grammar — `(handler-meta kind id)`, `(registrations kind)`. The inverse does not: nine public names in three shapes, differing on FOUR axes (where the name lives — 7 on the facade, 2 off it; whether a nilary clear-all exists — 3 of 9; how the frame is named — none / tolerant / exact; what comes back — nil for the core five, the id for the other four), and SIX registrar kinds with no public inverse at all (`:cofx :interceptor :view :head :error-projector`, plus per-path app-schemas) although `registrar/unregister!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:713`) already takes `(kind id)` for every registrar kind, forgets provenance, marks the live-frame projection dirty and emits `:rf.registry/handler-cleared`.

**The motivating defect (live at HEAD `13884f326f`).** `re-frame.flows/clear-flow` destructures its opts tolerantly — `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:846-847` is `([id] (clear-flow id {}))` / `([id {:keys [frame] :as _opts}] …)` — so `(flows/clear-flow :cart/total {:fram :session})` binds `frame` to nil, `require-current-frame!` resolves the AMBIENT frame, and the wrong frame's flow is cleared with no signal. That is the exact silent mis-clear rf2-s32bf closed for `clear-http-interceptor` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc:231-243`, `valid-clear-opts?` — exactly `{:frame target}`, present, non-nil, no other key, non-map rejected; raises `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` BEFORE any ambient frame is touched), applied to one of two identically-shaped surfaces and not the other. `spec/Principles.md:81` (No silent swallow): a recognised-but-unhonourable input MUST signal. One door with one validator closes it for every frame-scoped kind at once.

## Target API

```clojure
(rf/clear :sub  :cart/total)                       ;; registrar kind → registrar/unregister!; returns :cart/total
(rf/clear :flow :cart/total)                       ;; ambient frame; settles dependents (Spec 013 §Sequencing)
(rf/clear :flow :cart/total {:frame :session})     ;; explicit frame — opts EXACTLY {:frame f}
(rf/clear :flow :cart/total {:fram :session})      ;; THROWS (today: silently clears the AMBIENT frame's flow)
(rf/clear :sub  :cart/total {:frame :session})     ;; THROWS — :sub is not frame-scoped; opts rejected
(rf/clear :cofx :now)                              ;; THE SIX HOLES CLOSE with zero new names
(rf/clear :widget :x)                              ;; THROWS — unknown kind; the message names the closed set
;; (rf/clear :resource :feed) with no resources artefact → the documented :rf.error/resources-artefact-missing

;; HoF position — the only non-test consumer in the corpus, tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs
(run! #(rf/clear :sub %)   schema-5-subs-removed)   ;; was (run! rf/clear-sub …)
```

`:rf.fx/clear-flow` is UNCHANGED (it has consumers and takes the same id). `clear-sub-cache!`, `clear-trace-buffer!` and every cache / buffer / test-fixture `clear-*!` are OUT OF SCOPE — this bead is the registrar-inverse arm of the tear-down axis only.

## Closed kind set and dispatch table

`clear`'s kind set is its OWN closed set, documented in `spec/001-Registration.md`'s kind table as a new clear column — it is the registrar's kind set (`registrar.cljc:144-145`) MINUS `:frame` (frames are a live runtime object torn down by `destroy-frame!`, 001:99) PLUS `:http-interceptor` (a per-frame side table owned by the http artefact, not a registrar kind). `:app-schema` is deliberately NOT included (001:112 — not a registrar kind; per-path app-schemas have only `clear-schemas-by-frame!`; nobody has asked — the demand bar).

| kind | routes to | why not `unregister!` | `{:frame f}` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:event` `:sub` `:fx` | `registrar/unregister!` | PARITY BY INSPECTION: `events.cljc:1509`, `subs.cljc:367`, `fx.cljc:162` are literally `(rf.registrar/unregister! kind id)` in their 1-arity | rejected |
| `:cofx` `:interceptor` `:view` `:head` `:error-projector` | `registrar/unregister!` | no owning fn exists today; `unregister!` is the substrate every kind already shares | rejected |
| `:route` | a NEW `rf.core-routing/clear-route` defwrapper → `re-frame.routing.registry/clear-route` (`routing/registry.cljc:594`) | emits `:rf.route/cleared` | rejected |
| `:flow` | `rf.core-flows/clear-flow` (`core_flows.cljc:15`) → `flows/registry.cljc:833` | vacates the output leaf and, outside a drain, SETTLES dependents (rf2-g1zb, PRs #9204/#9257) | accepted |
| `:http-interceptor` | `rf.core-http/clear-http-interceptor` (`core_http.cljc:86`) → `http/middleware.cljc:245` | per-frame chain + `:rf.http.interceptor/cleared` trace | accepted |
| `:resource` `:mutation` `:resource-scope` | `rf.core-resources/clear-resource` / `clear-mutation` / `clear-resource-scope` (`core_resources.cljc:36/96/160`) | `clear-resource` disposes cache entries, timers and in-flight work across ALL frames (`resources/registry.cljc:647-671`) — a `{:frame}` on it is meaningless, hence rejected | rejected |

Artefact-absent still raises the documented `:rf.error/<artefact>-artefact-missing` because the dispatch goes THROUGH the existing defwrappers (the facade row IS the optional-capability mechanism — the manifest's own justification on rows 93-96).

**Two corrections the second reviewer proved against the dossier's sketch, both verified at HEAD — do not copy the sketch literally:**

1. **There is no `rf.core-routing/clear-route` delegate.** `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_routing.cljc:15-26` records that the czn2m0 D1 ruling deleted the dormant `clear-route` defwrapper AND its `:routing/clear-route` late-bind hook because nothing consumed them. `rf/clear :route` is now a consumer: add the defwrapper (`:hook :routing/clear-route :artefact routing-artefact :on-absent :throw`), the `set-fn!` in `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc` (beside `:routing/reg-route` at :479), and the directory row in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` (the `:routing/*` block starts :504; the directory test reconciles published hooks against rows, so both go together). Rewrite that :15-26 comment — it will be false.
2. **Omitted opts must reach the owning AMBIENT arity.** `valid-clear-opts?` rejects `nil` and `{}`; the 2-arity `(clear kind id)` therefore calls the owning 1-arity and NEVER normalises an omitted opts to `{}`/`nil` and forwards it into the owning 2-arity. `core_flows.cljc:20`'s `([id] [id {}])` has the same bug in waiting once flows are hardened — make it delegate to the owning 1-arity.

## Opts contract — one validator, three users

- `{:frame f}` is accepted for EXACTLY the two per-frame kinds (`:flow`, `:http-interceptor`), validated with rf2-s32bf's rule (map, sole key `:frame`, value a frame-id keyword or a live frame value — `rf.frame/frame-value?`) BEFORE anything is resolved or mutated. Any opts on any other kind throws. Unknown kind throws.
- LIFT the validator into core (beside `rf.frame/frame-value?`, which it already needs) and use it from THREE places: `rf/clear`, `flows/registry.cljc:847` (harden: the 2-arity becomes exact and fail-closed; the 1-arity stays ambient — it is still the `:flows/clear-flow` hook target and the `:rf.fx/clear-flow` fx reaches it), and `middleware.cljc:231` (replace the private copy). One validator, not two copies.
- ONE new error id for the door's own validation (unknown kind / malformed opts / opts on a non-frame-scoped kind), ex-data carrying `:kind`, `:reason` and the closed set; catalogue it in `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` or `python scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` reds (CHECK A). `:rf.error/http-bad-interceptor` stays for the http fn's own arg validation.
- Return the id for every kind (ends the nil-vs-id split; the `reg-*` return-value convention). Nilary clear-all arities are DROPPED — their only callers are tests, which already have `registrar/clear-kind!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:561`).

## Deletion list (HEAD `13884f326f` line numbers; the dossier's `6d513ba07f` numbers still hold)

- Facade: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` `:1151` `clear-event`, `:1157` `clear-sub`, `:1162` `clear-fx`, `:1583` `clear-resource`, `:1611` `clear-mutation`, `:1639` `clear-resource-scope`, `:2611` `clear-http-interceptor` — seven def-alias lines plus their surrounding doc comments (`:1118-1130` explains the off-facade placement of `clear-flow` / `clear-route`; rewrite to describe `clear`). TRAP: these are def-alias forms, so `grep -E '\((def|defn) clear-event'` returns an honest-looking ZERO on a name that IS exported — search the bare name and read the line (rf2-uhk4's instrument note).
- Owning-namespace public exports: `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:48` (`(def clear-flow registry/clear-flow)` — re-point the `set-fn! :flows/clear-flow` at `:485` to `registry/clear-flow`), `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:78`, `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources.cljc:92/118/135` (check what their `set-fn!`s reference before deleting). The registry-level fns (`flows/registry.cljc:833`, `routing/registry.cljc:594`, `resources/registry.cljc:647`, `mutation_registry.cljc:321`, `scope_registry.cljc:400`, `http/middleware.cljc:245`) STAY as hook targets; the nilary arities of `events.cljc:1509` / `subs.cljc:367` / `fx.cljc:162` go and the 1-arities may go with them (the dispatcher calls `unregister!` directly).
- Manifest: `spec/api-manifest.edn` rows `:91-97` (facade seven), `:202` (`re-frame.flows/clear-flow`), `:285-287` (`re-frame.resources` trio), `:304` (`re-frame.routing/clear-route`) — TWELVE public rows → ONE (`re-frame.core/clear`, `:tier :advanced`, `:owner "001"`); regenerate (`clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/`) and curate the new row's `:justification` in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`. Rows `:98` `clear-sub-cache!` / `:99` `clear-trace-buffer!` are NOT touched.

## Consumers to migrate (dossier census at `6d513ba07f`; re-measure)

- Non-test: THREE lines in ONE file — `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:352` `(run! rf/clear-sub …)`, `:411` `(run! rf/clear-sub …)`, `:412` `(run! rf/clear-event …)` → `#(rf/clear :sub %)` / `#(rf/clear :event %)`. Every other `clear-*` has 0 non-test consumers in `examples/ testbeds/ tools/`.
- Tests: ~130 call sites in 51 files — 66 through `rf/`, 43 `flows/clear-flow` across 23 files aliasing `re-frame.flows`, the rest owning-namespace aliases (per name: clear-event 7, clear-sub 15, clear-fx 4, clear-flow 50, clear-route 5, clear-http-interceptor 27, clear-resource 12, clear-mutation 10, clear-resource-scope 1). Mechanical. Test fixtures reach `registrar/clear-all!` / `clear-kind!`, not the public names — leave them.
- `:rf.fx/clear-flow` consumers (`examples/core/flows/core.cljs:178` etc.): untouched.

## Spec, docs, skills, migration

- **Hot-zone (one-toucher — sequence, see below):** `spec/API.md` — `:22` front-porch paragraph (names `clear-route` / `clear-flow` as owning-namespace helpers; `clear` is the facade inverse), `:158-166` §Clearing registrations (three rows → one `clear` row; `:166` `clear-sub-cache!` stays), `:178` `unsubscribe` carve-out prose (cites `clear-sub` — reword), `:402` (delete the row; the `:404` fx row belongs to rf2-kuky.13), `:444`, `:460/:462/:464` (delete), `:475`, `:839-852` (`clear-flow` prose). `spec/Conventions.md` — `:1267` Lifecycle-verb law `clear-*` row (the registrar inverse is now the kind-keyed `clear`; the cache arm keeps `clear-*!` names — reword, add no verb; rf2-uimu is the verb-roster bead and is NOT reopened here), `:1299`, `:1318`, `:1321` / `:1325` (bang-axis illustration), `:1380-1384` §Tear-down verb axis roster, `:1415`, `:1584` / `:1594-1597` (the `clear-flow` sample), `:1600`, `:1824`. `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md` — NEW row: `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` are v1-PRESERVED names (`API.md:162-164`) → `(rf/clear :event id)` etc. (precedent: `clear-subscription-cache!` → `clear-sub-cache!` at `:96-130`); `:130` names `clear-fx` / `clear-cofx` / `clear-sub` as siblings (`clear-cofx` never existed — fix while there); `:2108`; `:2132` (`unsubscribe` carve-out cites `rf/clear-sub`).

title: api(views): one hook frame-resolution rule — use-frame / use-sub read React context only (UIx + Hicasso)
description:
_Filed from the rf2-kuky.61 ruling (option A, context-only; ruled 2026-09-06 on Mike's behalf by the dossier agent). Parent epic rf2-kuky. Source lines below were verified at tip 13884f326f (2026-09-06 17:08 AUSEST); re-check before editing — rf2-kuky.57 lands in the same files first._

## Problem

Two shipped React hook families share a name, a return value and a docstring promise ("`rf/capture-frame`'s bundle, in hook position") but not a frame-resolution rule:

- **UIx / shared spine — dynamic-var FIRST.** `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-frame` (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:148-171`; docstring `:160-162` says "dynamic-var tier first, then the surrounding frame-provider / frame-root") re-exports `re-frame.adapter.use-frame/use-frame` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs`), whose body calls `React/useContext` at `:104` purely to re-render on a provider swap and DISCARDS the value, then resolves at `:108` through `rf.frame/require-current-frame!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:1167`) → `resolve-current-frame` → `function-component-current-frame` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/context.cljs:335`): `(or rf.frame/*current-frame* <context slot>)`. The spine's 1-arity `use-subscribe` does the same at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3363-3373` (`require-current-frame!` at `:3369`), and its comment at `:3352-3361` gives the reason: "single-sources resolution with `rf.subs/subscribe`'s 1-arity — the hook and the imperative read can never diverge".
- **Hicasso — React context ONLY.** `re-frame.hicasso.native/use-frame` and `use-sub` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:41` and `:68`) pass the raw `useContext` value to `collector/resolve-frame!` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:1113-1130`), whose docstring (`:1118-1122`) refuses the dynamic-var chain on purpose: "a body's extent has unwound by the time React renders the component it returned, so the var tier can only answer for a different render than the one asking."

The divergence is observable whenever a component body runs on the same stack as a `with-frame`: `act()` in tests (the rf2-4mi2zj assertion says so in its own docstring), synchronous server rendering, and Hicasso's shipped `render!`, which commits inside `flushSync` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/mount.cljs:13-14, :49, :95`) — so this is a production path, not only a test-time one. Under the dynamic-first rule the reset fixture's ambient `:rf/default` binding (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:703-713`, resolved at `:872-874`, bound at `:936` / `:960`) shadows any provider a hook test mounts under, which is why 150 test files (196 occurrences at tip; re-measure) carry `:ambient-frame nil`, three of them saying in prose that it is load-bearing (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:4150-4153`; `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/boundary_intent_dom_cljs_test.cljs:154-158`; `implementation/machines/test/.../machine_view_unmount_teardown_mounted_dom_cljs_test.cljs:72-76`), and why the Hicasso studio's three-rendering parity gate failed live (`docs/design/hicasso/studio/arm1-lean-react-dogfood-judgement.md:497-510`).

## Ruled target (rf2-kuky.61, option A)

**A React hook resolves its frame from React context ONLY.** `use-frame` and `use-sub` (UIx and Hicasso alike) consult the `frame-provider` / `frame-root` context the boundary above installed and nothing else. No provider above → `:rf.error/no-frame-context`, on both families, in both context-reading environments (client `_currentValue`, Fizz server `_currentValue2` — `context.cljs:255-259`). A `with-frame` / `bind-fn` dynamic scope around a synchronous render does NOT reach a hook; the explicit override for a test or a harness is a `frame-provider` wrapper, which survives scheduling changes. Dynamic scope stays the imperative tier's: `rf/dispatch`, `rf/subscribe`, `(rf/capture-frame)` 0-arity, `rf/current-frame-id`, handlers, `reg-view` injection and the Reagent class-component chain (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:287-291`) keep dynamic-var → context → error and are OUT OF SCOPE. No fallback tier, no compatibility flag, no `{:frame}` opt on a hook, no `capture-frame` in render as a replacement for a reactive hook.

The design requirement, stated once for the spec: the same component tree resolves the same frame under either scheduling mode (a scheduled concurrent render and a synchronous `act()` / `flushSync` / server render) — a hook must not depend on which imperative scope happens to surround a flush, including work that scope did not schedule.

## Code changes

1. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs:104-109` — keep the `React/useContext` call (it is what re-renders the component on a provider swap) but CONSUME its return value: classify it with the existing `re-frame.adapter.context/context-value->current-frame` (`context.cljs:298`; keep the corruption diagnostic `emit-frame-context-corrupted!` at `:226` and the no-provider sentinel handling). When the classification yields nil, raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context` with the same `:op :use-frame` diagnostic shape `require-current-frame!` emits today, so error reporting is preserved. Stop calling `require-current-frame!` on this path. The incarnation-pinned memo at `:110-129` (rf2-40kv) is untouched.
2. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3363-3373` — same change for the 1-arity hook (`require-current-frame!` at `:3369` goes). Rewrite the comment at `:3352-3361`: the single-sourcing argument is given up DELIBERATELY, and the comment must say why (a hook is the hold face of `capture-frame`; scope evaporates at the render hop; a hook that reads a JS-thread global during a React render is hidden context in the one place React identity matters — Principles §Low hidden context, `spec/Principles.md:87-91`).
3. Docstrings: `use_frame.cljs:33` and `:82`; `uix.cljs:160-162`. (`uix.cljs:76` is `use-current-frame`'s docstring — rf2-kuky.57 deletes that public var; whichever bead lands second reconciles the residue.)
4. `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc` — NO body change is required; it is already context-only. Do NOT replace the native hooks with the spine hooks: the collector owns their cells, reader membership and read-set entries (`collector.cljs`), and `impl/frames.cljs` shares captured ops per frame incarnation — that ownership and its Xray visibility stay. Share the classification rule (the context tier via `context-value->current-frame`), not hook bodies. If `collector/resolve-frame!` can delegate its classification to the core helper without changing its diagnostics, do so; otherwise leave it.
5. NOT touched: `frame.cljc` `require-current-frame!` / `resolve-current-frame` (the imperative chain), `views/provider.cljs`, `ssr/boot.cljc`, `frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc`, `live_run_frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc` (they pin the imperative chain and stay green as-is).

## Deletion list

- The dynamic-var tier from the two hook resolution sites (`use_frame.cljs:108`, `spine.cljs:3369`) and the single-sourcing rationale comment (`spine.cljs:3352-3361`, rewritten).
- The "dynamic-var tier first" sentences: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2091` (Decision 3: "resolved through the same carried-invariant chain as the ambient `use-subscribe`") and the UIx column of the `:2117` table row ("Same chain; React-context tier read via `use-context`"); `spec/API.md:243` (the `use-frame` row's "resolves through the same carried-invariant chain as the ambient `use-subscribe`"); `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:100` and `:120`; `uix.cljs:160-162`; `use_frame.cljs:33`, `:82`.
- The rf2-4mi2zj precedence assertion IN ITS CURRENT DIRECTION — rewritten into the witness, not deleted (below).

## Tests (the witness — this is what makes the ruling un-silent)

- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs:4209` `assert-use-subscribe-dynamic-var-precedence-over-provider` (the rf2-4mi2zj repair; rf2-4mi2zj no longer resolves in `bd show`, the record is the comment block at `:4133-4157`) asserts the exact behaviour this bead reverses. Rewrite it to assert the OPPOSITE — provider `:b` wins over a live `with-frame :a` — and rename it (e.g. `assert-use-subscribe-provider-precedence-over-dynamic-var`); rewrite the header comment at `:4133-4157` so it no longer says "dynamic-var MUST win over React-context" and instead records rf2-kuky.61's rule and why. Its only caller is `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:483-484` (the deftest name changes with it). rf2-kuky.57 renames `use-subscribe` → `use-sub` and may rename these first: find them by the `rf2-4mi2zj` comment, never by name. `assert-use-subscribe-provider-tier-resolution-ambient-cleared` (`:4160`) and the no-scope assertion already assert context-tier behaviour and stay.
- Witness matrix, both hook families, per the Codex acceptance list adopted by the ruling:
  1. Seed distinct values in frames `:a` and `:b`; render synchronously beneath `frame-provider {:frame :b}` while `(rf/with-frame :a …)` is live around the render (`act()` runs the body on the calling stack). `use-frame`'s `:frame` reads `:b` and the `use-sub` / 1-arity `use-subscribe` value is `:b`'s. After the binding unwinds, invoke THE `dispatch` OBTAINED FROM `use-frame` and verify only `:b` changed. (A fresh qualified `rf/dispatch` call is not a captured callback — do not describe it as one; 002 §The invariant already covers the captured case.)
  2. Same probe with NO provider while `:a` is dynamically bound: both families raise `:rf.error/no-frame-context`. This is the NEW case (today UIx answers `:a`). Cover an ordinary scheduled update (non-`act`, so `*current-frame*` is unbound when the body runs) and one server render (`react-dom/server`, the `_currentValue2` slot) so both context-reading environments are exercised.
  3. Retain the existing provider-swap, incarnation and subscription-release checks: rf2-tug6's regression (`implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, merged PR #9264 — it clears the ambient `:rf/default` explicitly; keep it), the rf2-40kv incarnation memo checks, and the native reader census under StrictMode.
- Hicasso: run the witness against the REAL `n/use-frame` / `n/use-sub` exports — `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/hooks_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs` already imports both (`:139-140`, `:162-163`) and opts out of the ambient frame at `:243`. `substrate_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` reads SPINE surfaces (`:69-81` read `substrate/spine-fns`) and excludes native authoring, so running the shared-suite assertion under the Hicasso adapter covers the spine hook there but NOT the native hooks; do the native-suite witness regardless, and the shared-suite one under the Hicasso adapter too if the cfg keys allow it without inventing new ones (unverified — if it needs extra cfg keys, say so in the PR body and skip it). `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/hicasso_causal_native_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs` is the ownership-sensitive consumer; it must stay green unchanged.
- The `:ambient-frame nil` opt-outs are NOT swept by this bead. Under A the fixture's ambient `:rf/default` no longer shadows a provider for HOOK components, so the opt-out stops being load-bearing for hook tests only; many of the 150 files carry it for imperative reasons. Drop it only in tests this bead touches; a measured sweep, if wanted, is a separate chore filed from this bead.

## Spec / docs / skills / examples

- **Hot-zone (sequential, one toucher):** `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` (`:2091` Decision 3; `:2117` table row UIx column → "React-context ONLY — the surrounding `frame-provider` / `frame-root`; no dynamic-var tier; raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` with no provider"; `:2122` hold row and `:2126` callout read consistently once the row is fixed; check §Frame-provider via React context at `:1899` for the same sentence); `spec/002-Frames.md` (`:99` scope-table row lists `with-frame` and `frame-provider` as peer scope surfaces — add the one clause that a React hook reads the `frame-provider` / `frame-root` tier only and `with-frame` around a synchronous render does not reach it; `:1396` describes the tiered reader for the imperative path — make the hook exception explicit there or beside it, wherever 002 otherwise implies universal precedence; `:117` "hold is the primary mental model; scope is sugar" is the sentence the rule rests on); `spec/API.md:243` (the `use-frame` row). The spec statement should be one rule with one reason, not a per-substrate table.
- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:100` and `:120` — rewrite to the context-only wording; `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.native.md:60-62` already states the rule ("the one React context the boundary shell reads, and no argument reaches another") and is the wording to copy. `docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md:119-129` — verify consistent (it is at tip). `docs/core/glossary.md` has no `use-frame` entry at tip; if rf2-kuky.57 / views.2 adds one before this lands, carry the sentence.
- Skills: `skills/re-frame2/patterns/stateful-components.md:33` already teaches context-only ("Both hooks read the surrounding `frame-provider` / `frame-root` from React context") — under A it is correct as written; `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/views.md:88,94`; `skills/reagent-migration/references/mental-model.md:176-189` — verify, no change expected.
- Examples: `examples/substrates/uix/{counter,dashboard,login}/core.cljs` comments already say the hooks resolve "through React context" (counter `:84-90`, dashboard `:354`, README `:109-110`) and use no `with-frame` (0 at tip; also 0 in `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed` and `tools/template/.../_uix`) — behaviourally unaffected.
- Manifest: `spec/api-manifest.edn:84-85` (uix `use-frame` / `use-subscribe`) and `:233-234` (hicasso.native `use-frame` / `use-sub`, `:advanced`) carry no resolution axis and do not change; the native rows STAY (roster is keyed by namespace + var, and `re-frame.hicasso.native/use-frame` remains a public var whatever its body).

## Consumers (by file / count)

Zero app sites depend on either order. Tests: exactly one assertion flips (`react_shared_suite.cljs:4209`, called from `uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs:483-484`). Of the eight test files that both call a hook and bind `with-frame`, every other `with-frame` is test-body seeding or an imperative read outside render (`hooks_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs:264,457,782,797`; `sub_memo_flush_path_cljs_test.cljs:150,198,258,303` wrap Reagent-tier code; `core/test/re_frame/bench/read_attribution_cljs.cljs` is a false positive on `call-with-frame-resolution`).

## Sequencing and hot-zone

- **After rf2-kuky.57 MERGES** (not merely opens): both beads edit `spine.cljs:3318-3374`, `uix.cljs:140-171`, `spec/API.md` §UIx rows, `spec/006` Decision 1/3 and the `:2117` table, `react_shared_suite.cljs` and `uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs`. .57 is the rename / deletion bead and does NOT change the resolution order — this bead is the only one that does.
- rf2-tug6 is CLOSED (PR #9264, 2026-09-05): the incarnation-keyed memo and the effect-deps recipe it corrected are on main; retain them.
- Hot-zone files: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/API.md`. No `deps.edn` / `shadow-cljs.edn` / workflow change.

## Traps

- The reset fixture binds `*current-frame*` to `:rf/default` unless `:ambient-frame nil` — a witness that forgets this reads green for the wrong reason (the exact trap rf2-4mi2zj's header comment and rf2-tug6's close reason both describe). For case 2 bind the dynamic var yourself and mount with no provider.
- React 18 `act()` runs the body on the calling stack, so the `with-frame` must wrap the `act`/render call, not just the element construction. StrictMode double-invokes bodies; the incarnation memo must survive it (it does today).
- `grep -iF` aborts on this machine (SIGABRT, silent zero) — use the ripgrep-backed search tool.
- The test header comment cites "Spec 006 §734 / §1058"; those line numbers no longer point at resolution text — replace with the current 006 anchor when rewriting the comment.
- The dossier cited `context-value->current-frame` at `context.cljs:368-369`; at tip it is `:298` (and `function-component-current-frame` `:335`).

## Acceptance

- Witness green on UIx (rewritten shared-suite assertion via `uix_use_subscribe_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, plus a `use-frame` probe) and on Hicasso's native DOM suite; the new no-provider-with-dynamic-bound case raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on both families; the captured-`dispatch`-after-unwind check targets only `:b`.
- `frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc`, `live_run_frame_resolution_cljs_test.cljc`, `uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `hicasso_causal_native_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs` unchanged and green.
- 006 / 002 / API.md / docs/api uix page state ONE rule with its reason; `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.native.md` and the uix page agree word-for-word on the rule. Gates: `mkdocs build --strict` (covers `spec/` via the staging hook) and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the doc edits; the UIx artefact suite and the Hicasso CLJS suite foreground to completion; `npm run test:cljs`. PR body names the gates run and states the deliberate loss of the spine's single-sourcing argument.
- Manifest rows unchanged; no new public var; no compatibility flag.

description:

(rf/reg-machine <id> {spec}) — the spec map de-indents by 2 and loses one
closing paren. Verify by paren balance, not by eye.

title: api(views): RULING — one frame-resolution rule for the React hook family (use-sub / use-frame): context-only or dynamic-var-first
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.6); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## The question

Two shipped hooks share a name and a contract but not a resolution rule. `re-frame.adapter.uix/use-frame` (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:148-171` → `re-frame.adapter.use-frame/use-frame`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/adapter/use_frame.cljs:108-129`) resolves the frame DYNAMIC-VAR FIRST (`require-current-frame!`: `with-frame` / `bind-fn` scope wins over the surrounding `frame-provider` / `frame-root`), the same chain the 1-arity `use-subscribe` hook uses (`spine.cljs:3320-3362`, per Spec 006 §Frame resolution (1-arg form) and 006:2106 "Same chain"). `re-frame.hicasso.native/use-frame` and `use-sub` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/native.cljc:19-44,46-82`) resolve REACT CONTEXT ONLY through `collector/resolve-frame!`, which deliberately refuses the dynamic var (`collector.cljs:1113-1122` at the doc's tip: a dynamic scope can belong to a different render). Both lower to the same `make-capture-frame` bundle (one primitive; verified clean by both reviewers) — the disagreement is which tier a HOOK consults. Two homes with two rules and one name is an unwritten discriminator (README ethos bar), and it is a semantics decision, not a rename: it changes which frame a synchronous test render under `with-frame` resolves to. Both reviewers asked for a ruling and a witness rather than a mechanical re-export.

## Options

- **(A) Context-only for every hook** — adopt Hicasso's rule for the shared core hook (`use_frame.cljs`) and for the spine's 1-arity `use-sub`; a hook consults the React context the boundary above installed and nothing else; `with-frame` around a synchronous render does not reach a hook (dynamic scope stays the imperative tier's: `rf/dispatch`, `rf/subscribe`, handlers). Recommended by fable and Grok: "A hook that consults a dynamic var is hidden context in the one place React identity matters … Do not 'unify' by averaging the two orders." Cost: 006:2080 and :2106 change; any test that relies on `with-frame` beating a provider inside a hook component flips (find them with the witness below); the UIx 1-arity hook's documented chain (`spine.cljs:3320-3328`, rf2-4mi2zj) is rewritten, and the "hook and imperative read can never diverge" single-sourcing argument at `spine.cljs:3359-3361` is given up deliberately.
- **(B) Dynamic-var-first for every hook** — Hicasso's native hooks adopt UIx's chain. Keeps the spec's stated tier precedence (dynamic-var MUST win, 006 §Frame resolution) and the spine's single-sourcing with `rf.subs/subscribe`; costs Hicasso's stated correctness reason (a `with-frame` scope belonging to a different render leaking into an island).
- **(C) Keep both, write the discriminator** — status quo, plus a sentence in 006 saying islands under Hicasso are context-only and UIx hooks are dynamic-var-first. Rejected by both reviewers as an unwritten-dual-with-a-uniform unless a real reason for the difference is named; nothing in the corpus needs it (0 app sites depend on either order).

## Recommendation

(A), with a witness that makes the choice un-silent: a synchronous render under `(rf/with-frame :a …)` of a component beneath `frame-provider {:frame :b}` pins which frame `use-frame` / `use-sub` resolve on BOTH adapters, and the same test asserts that `rf/dispatch` in a callback fired after render still carries the captured frame (002 §The invariant). Codex's caution, carried verbatim: "This is a genuine contract disagreement requiring a small witness and a ruling, not a mechanical re-export opportunity … Implement the naming/documentation cleanup separately from frame-resolution semantics. Verify provider changes, same-id frame reincarnation, cleanup under StrictMode, a callback fired after render, and a synchronous render where dynamic scope conflicts with provider context." rf2-tug6 (open) is about the incarnation-stability half of `use-frame` and does not depend on this ruling; it should land first so the recipe it corrects is not rewritten twice.

## Implementation beads to file when ruled

1. `api(views): one use-frame / use-sub resolution rule — <ruled order>`: unify `re-frame.adapter.use-frame/use-frame` and `re-frame.hicasso.native/use-frame` onto one core hook with the ruled rule (Hicasso re-exports the core hook, or the core hook adopts the collector's context-only resolver — Hicasso's `use-sub` keeps its collector-owned tracking either way; share vocabulary and the resolution rule, not hook bodies); the spine's 1-arity `use-sub` follows the same rule; witness test above on UIx and on the Hicasso substrate adapter; `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` Decision 3 (:2080) and table row :2106; `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:120`; `uix.cljs:160-162` and `use_frame.cljs:108` docstrings; `docs/core/hicasso/10-native-tier.md`; `docs/core/glossary.md` `use-frame` entry (added by views.2). Hot-zone: 006. P3.
2. If (C): the one-sentence discriminator in 006 and nothing else.

## Local dossier

ai/findings/API-review/fable/in-view-reads-and-frame-access.md (local-only pointer; may be deleted).

# View authoring and mounting — three substrates, one registry contract that only one of them honours, and three root doors where the spec asks for one

**Status:** medium-high (mounting: three app-facing root grammars for one job, one of them absent where Spec 006 says it SHOULD exist; authoring: the defining macros are substrate-forced and clean, but Hicasso's `defview` registers around `reg-view*` so `(rf/view id)` answers `nil` on one substrate; wave 3, 2026-09-05 09:00:55 AUSEST, tip 7d7ec09bd7)

**Surfaces:** `re-frame.core/reg-view` (macro, `core.cljc:807`, front-porch) · `reg-view*` (`core.cljc:757` → `re-frame.views/reg-view*` `views.cljs:812`, advanced) · `view` (`core.cljc:788` → `views/view-head` `views.cljs:771`, advanced) · `frame-provider` / `frame-root` (`core.cljc:1439/1464` → `views/provider.cljs:167`, front-porch) · `init!` (`core.cljc:2660`, front-porch) · `re-frame.adapter.reagent/client-root` `render!` `unmount!` (`reagent.cljs:142/160/179`, tier `:adapter`; impl is the ratom spine, `spine.cljs:3639-3747`) · `re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim` same trio (`reagent_slim.cljs:79/86/102`) · `re-frame.adapter.uix/frame-provider` `frame-root` (`defui`, `uix.cljs:83/110`) `use-frame` (`:148`) `wrap-view` (`:183`) — **no root door**; `make-react-spine` (`spine.cljs:2702`) publishes none · `re-frame.hicasso/defview` (`hicasso.cljc:82`) `defhost` (`:316`) `error-boundary` (`:431`) `reg-state` (`:440`) `portal` (`:445`) `as-element` (`:479`) `as-component` (`:522`) `mount!` (`:552`) `hydrate!` (`:610`) `render!` (`:663`) `unmount!` (`:676`) — all `:advanced` in `spec/api-manifest.edn:212-225` · `re-frame.hicasso.impl.collector/publish-view-alias!` (`collector.cljs:1204`) · `re-frame.hicasso.impl.mount/ensure-frame!` `root!` (`mount.cljs:116/139`, `react-dom-client/createRoot` at `:157`) · `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/frame-provider` (`defn-`, private, `substrate.cljs:108`) · `re-frame.hicasso.native/use-frame` (`native.cljc:19`) · `re-frame.hicasso.server/render-body` (`server.cljs:424`, `:implementation`).

Wave-1 rulings (`reg-frame` deleted; `frame-root`/`frame-provider` ENSURE/SCOPE split, rf2-nyea0r; `use-frame` as capture-frame-in-hook-position; view tiering) are respected here and not re-litigated — the tree agrees with them everywhere I looked. The new ground is Hicasso (`day8/re-frame2-hicasso`, rostered as the fourth view adapter in 006 §CLJS reference scope) and the UIx root gap.

## The problem

Two questions, three substrates. Each cell is what the author writes and what it lowers to.

| Job | Reagent / reagent-slim | UIx | Hicasso |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Define a view** | `(rf/reg-view name [args] body)` → `defs` name, id `(keyword *ns* sym)`, injects `dispatch`/`subscribe`, `reg-view*` → `registrar/register! :view` with `:handler-fn` = the substrate head (`views.cljs:862`) | `(defui name [props] …)` + `use-subscribe`/`use-frame` — **unregistered**; `(rf/reg-view* ::id name)` optional (API.md §UIx Decision 4) | `(h/defview name [props] body)` → `defs` a real React component; dev-only `registrar/register! :view` with `:hicasso/component` and **no `:handler-fn`** (`collector.cljs:1227`) |
| **Look a view up** | `(rf/view id)` → mountable head | `(rf/view id)` → UIx-marked shell (rf2-oz7wr) | `(rf/view id)` → **`nil`** (docstring: "answers nil for this entry", `hicasso.cljc:208`) |
| **Own the React root** | `(defonce h (adapter/client-root))` inert; `(adapter/render! h tree el {:hydrate? b})` creates-or-updates; `(adapter/unmount! h)` — in the adapter's active-root set, so `rf/destroy-adapter!` releases it | hand-rolled: `(defonce react-root (atom nil))` + `uix-dom/create-root` + `uix-dom/render-root` — no adapter surface, not in the active-root set | `(h/mount! el config tree)` → handle (root created at once, so callers wrap it in an atom); `(h/hydrate! el config tree)`; `(h/render! handle tree)`; `(h/unmount! handle)` — `createRoot` called directly (`mount.cljs:157`), outside the spine's client-root path |
| **ENSURE the app frame** | `[rf/frame-root {…any make-frame opt…} [app]]` in the tree, commit-owned two-pass | `($ uix/frame-root {…} ($ app))` same | `h/mount!` config, **closed at three keys** `:frame :initial-events :identifier-prefix`; anything else "ignored without complaint" (guide 20-migration:243-248) — so `:fx-overrides`/`:url-bound?`/`:images` need a separate `rf/make-frame` first (`examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:287-290`) |
| **SCOPE an existing frame in-tree** | `[rf/frame-provider {:frame f} …]` | `($ uix/frame-provider {:frame f} …)` | none public (`substrate/frame-provider` is `defn-`); a second frame is a second `h/mount!` root |
| **Hydrate** | `{:hydrate? true}` opt on first `render!` | hand-rolled `hydrate-root` | separate verb `h/hydrate!`, which — unlike `mount!` — does NOT ensure (api-reference §"not symmetric") |

Plus two tool-internal mount routes: raw `reagent.dom.client/create-root` + `render` under `[rf/frame-provider …]` (all 20 testbeds, Story shell `shell.cljs:1187`, `testbed-support/story_host.cljs:35`, machines-viz `viewer.cljs:183`) and the one-shot `rf.substrate.adapter/render` slot (Xray shell, `mount.cljs:363,1512`). Those are framework-authored and fine as such; they are listed because they are what the app-facing doors are supposed to wrap.

So: **three spellings of "define a view"** — genuinely substrate-forced (a Reagent view is a hiccup fn, a UIx view is a hook component, a Hicasso view is a compiled boundary), and NOT the problem — sitting on **two registration paths and a lookup that is true on two substrates and false on the third**. And **three app-facing spellings of "put my app on the page"** for one React-level job, where Spec 006 §The client root already says a browser adapter SHOULD publish one shape (`client-root` / `render!` / `unmount!`), the Reagent pair does, UIx does not, and Hicasso publishes a fourth shape under different names, arg order and return value.

## Empirical use cases

Grep commands (all from repo root, tip 7d7ec09bd7; `--include=*.cljs --include=*.cljc`, `node_modules` excluded, comment lines excluded where noted):

```
grep -rE '\(rf/reg-view |\(reg-view ' examples | wc -l                      # 142
grep -rE 'reg-view\*' examples | wc -l                                      # 0
grep -rE '\(rf/view ' examples | wc -l                                      # 16  (all in capabilities/ssr/*)
grep -rE '\(defui ' examples | wc -l                                        # 12
grep -rlE '^\s+\[rf/frame-root \{' examples | wc -l                          # 23
grep -rlE '\(rf.adapter.reagent(-slim)?/client-root\)' examples | wc -l     # 27
grep -rlE 'defonce react-root \(atom nil\)' examples | wc -l                # 3   (all UIx)
grep -rlE 'rf.hicasso/mount!' examples | wc -l                              # 1
grep -rnE 'rdc/create-root' testbeds tools/xray/testbeds | wc -l            # 20
```

| Spelling | app-authored (examples) | tool-authored (tools/, testbeds/) | framework-internal (impl tests) | docs / skills mentions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rf/reg-view` | 142 | 87 (xray 70, story 15, template 2) | 176 lines / 37 files | 116 / 47 |
| `rf/reg-view*` | 0 | 12 real sites (story panels ×4 computed ids; xray `panel_gallery` testbed ×8) | 285 / 74 | 19 / 36 |
| `(rf/view id)` | 16 (SSR: `[(rf/view :app/root)]` late-binds the root by id) | 5 (story render seam ×4, xray ×1) | — | 38 / 11 |
| UIx `defui` + hooks | 12 | 3 | — | — |
| `uix-adapter/wrap-view` | **0** | **0** | 89 / 10 (tests only) | 7 / 0 |
| `h/defview` | 5 (one example) | 0 | 295 / 83 | 157 / 43 |
| `h/defhost` / `as-element` / `as-component` / `reg-state` / `portal` / `error-boundary` | **0 each** | story uses `as-element` for its hicasso substrate | 5 / 3 (`as-component`) | 447 / 123 / 39 / 74 / 10 / 69 |
| `client-root`+`render!`+`unmount!` (Reagent/slim) | 27 files | template `_reagent`, both ratom adapter testbeds | 40 / 7 | 23+21 / 17+32 |
| hand-rolled `uix-dom/create-root` | 3 | template `_uix`, uix adapter testbed | — | 3 / — |
| `h/mount!`/`hydrate!`/`render!`/`unmount!` | 1 file | both hicasso testbeds (`hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:888` — on the **UIx** adapter) | 31 / 13 | 70+36+23 / 12 |
| raw `rdc/create-root` + `[rf/frame-provider …]` | 0 | 20 testbeds + Story + story_host + machines-viz | 67 / 28 | 0 |

Numbered use cases the corpus actually exercises:

1. **Boot a single-frame browser app, hot-reload safe.** 23 Reagent examples spell it identically (`examples/core/todomvc/core.cljs:46-59`): `(defonce app-root (rf.adapter.reagent/client-root))` / `(defn ^:dev/after-load mount! [] (rf.adapter.reagent/render! app-root [rf/frame-root {:id app-frame :initial-events […]} [app]] el))` / `(defn run [] (rf/init! adapter) (mount!))`. Note every example names its own wrapper `mount!`. The UIx twins (`examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:81-111`) do the same job with an atom, `when-not @react-root`, `create-root`, `render-root` — the ceremony the Reagent trio was built to delete (rf2-k5r9t). The Hicasso twin (`examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:255-299`) needs `(defonce !root (atom nil))`, a `make-frame` because its `:fx-overrides` cannot ride the mount config, a `mount!`/`hydrate!` branch, and a separate `re-render!` calling `h/render!`.
2. **Hydrate a server-rendered page.** Reagent: `{:hydrate? (some? payload)}` on the first `render!` (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/mount.cljs:36`), tree wrapped in `frame-provider` because `ssr/hydrate!` made the frame. Hicasso: a second verb `h/hydrate!` with its own config and the no-ensure asymmetry the api-reference has to spend a section on.
3. **Late-bind the root view by id** (SSR examples ×3, Story): `[(rf/view :app/root)]` — works for `reg-view`/`reg-view*` registrations on Reagent and UIx; for a `defview` it returns `nil`, which is why Story carries a second substrate hook for Hicasso (`multi_substrate.cljs:83-97`, `h/as-element`) instead of the one `rf/view` seam it uses for Reagent (`:232`).
4. **Register a view with a computed id** (Story panels, panel_gallery): `rf/reg-view*` — 12 real sites, all tool-authored. Earns its advanced tier.
5. **Tools enumerating views** (Xray Views panel, Pair `ui/read`, `handler-meta :view`): read the `:view` registrar. Hicasso's alias slot carries coords and `:doc` so `handler-meta` works; the head lives under a private key `:hicasso/component` no tool reads generically.
6. **Multi-root / multi-frame pages** (Hicasso HMR testbed `hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:451-458`): one `h/mount!` per frame, because Hicasso has no public in-tree frame boundary. Reagent/UIx nest `frame-root`/`frame-provider`.
7. **Foreign React components** (Hicasso `defhost`; Reagent `[:> C]`; UIx `($ C)`): substrate-forced, 0 app consumers, 447 doc mentions — a tier signal (see non-goals).

## Simpler elegant target

**A. One registration door, one lookup contract (authoring).** Keep all three defining macros — their difference is real. Make them agree on what registration means:

```clojure
;; every substrate's defining macro registers through the ONE fn door,
;; storing the substrate's mountable head as :handler-fn — so this is true everywhere:
(rf/view id)  ;=> the installed substrate's mountable head for `id`, or nil if unregistered
```

- `h/defview` calls `rf/reg-view*` with the minted head (and the coords + `:doc` it already computes) instead of `registrar/register!` with a private slot shape. `publish-view-alias!`'s stated reason for the bypass — "`reg-view*` … consults the `:adapter/wrap-view` hook at registration time, which at namespace load precedes `rf/init!`" (`collector.cljs:1218-1221`) — is stale at tip: `view-head` re-derives lazily against the adapter installed at lookup time precisely so that ordering is "not a correctness input" (`views.cljs:771-810`, rf2-oz7wr/rf2-8mkmb). Hicasso keeps its `debug-enabled?` gate if it wants a registry-free production bundle; that is a `when`, not a second path.
- Delete `re-frame.adapter.uix/wrap-view` from the public surface (0 consumers outside its own tests; it is the payload of the `:adapter/wrap-view` late-bind hook, which `reg-view*` already consumes). Manifest row `api-manifest.edn:86` goes.
- Retire the `:hicasso/component` / `:executable-key` slot keys once the head is `:handler-fn`.

**B. One root door, one shape, every view adapter (mounting).** Spec 006 §The client root already states the shape; make the tree match the spec on all four rows of the adapter inventory:

```clojure
(adapter/client-root)                              ;=> inert handle; defonce-safe, no DOM at load
(adapter/mount! handle tree el)                    ; first call creates the root and renders; every later call re-renders
(adapter/mount! handle tree el {:hydrate? true :identifier-prefix "main"})  ; first call hydrates instead; React root opts pass through
(adapter/unmount! handle)                          ;=> nil; idempotent; also released by rf/destroy-adapter!
```

- **Name.** `mount!`/`unmount!` is the closed roster's pair for "put a UI shell into / out of the DOM" (Conventions §Lifecycle-verb law); `render!` is not in the roster; every example, Xray (`mount-shell-into!`) and Story (`mount-shell!`) already say *mount*. - **Hicasso** re-shapes to the same trio. `h/hydrate!` folds into `{:hydrate? true}`; `h/render!` is deleted (a second `mount!` through the handle IS the re-render, as it is on Reagent today); `h/mount!`'s three-key config disappears; `:identifier-prefix` becomes a root opt (it is React's `createRoot` option and belongs on the root call for every React adapter). - **ENSURE spelled once.** Hicasso gets an in-tree `h/frame-root` head (a hicasso-owned React component like `h/portal`/`h/error-boundary`, realised on the shared `frame-root-fc` via `frame_boundary.cljs:370 frame-root-react-element`, exactly as UIx's `frame-root` is) taking the full `make-frame` opts, and `h/frame-provider` (promote the private `substrate/frame-provider`). - **Spec-ulation / the spec is the artefact**: 006 §The client root already asks for this shape; today the tree contradicts it on two of four adapters. The proposal is the spec winning.
