title: api(routing): DECISION — delete :rf.route/transitioned; the link door dispatches handle-url-change with cause :link
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from routing.md (ref routing.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The URL-driven route commit is spelled as two event ids that are ONE function called with two constants. `:rf.route/transitioned` (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:312-314` → `routing/url_change.cljc:462-507 transitioned-handler`) and `:rf.route/handle-url-change` (`:315-317` → `:546-589 handle-url-change-handler`) both destructure the same cofx, call `require-frame-stamp!`, and hand the same map to `url-change-fx` — the ONLY differences are `:default-scroll :top` + `:cause :link` versus `:default-scroll :restore` + `:cause (url-change-cause frame opts)`. `handle-url-change` already discriminates its three doors by a data rider (`:rf.route/cause` ∈ `#{:popstate :initial :ssr}`, Spec 012:452, 531; `docs/routing/testing.md:108-127` "Say which door you meant"); the fourth door is spelled as a second event id where a fourth rider value would do, and the default scroll is a pure function of the cause. The app-facing porch is NOT in question and re-verified clean at HEAD: apps use exactly two navigation doors (`[:rf.route/navigate …]` 42 example dispatches, `[rf/route-link …]` 59 example renders; 0 example dispatches of `transitioned` / `handle-url-change` / `url-requested` / `:rf.nav/*`) and the granular `:rf.route/id|params|query` subs stay (22 app read sites, ten of them `:<-` chain inputs; the equality cut is the point). This is a framework-internal tier that tests, tools, docs and AI agents must learn.

## Evidence (all at HEAD 6445d0611ba0)

- No app dispatches either id (examples: 0 / 0); no app or tool re-registers either (`reg-event :rf.route/(transitioned|handle-url-change|url-requested)` outside routing src: 0).
- The test corpus treats them as two spellings of "go to this URL": `[:rf.route/transitioned` literals — 160 in 20 files under `implementation/routing/test` (`routing_navigation_test.clj` 45, `routing_nav_token_test.clj` 23, `routing_classification_test.clj` 23, `routing_can_leave_test.clj` 17, `routing_nav_counters_test.clj` 11, `routing_nav_allocation_record_replay_test.clj` 11, `routing_egress_test.clj` 8, …), 33 in 7 files outside it (`ssr/test/…/flows_integration_test.clj` 8, `adapters/reagent/test/…/routing_cljs_test.cljs` 5, `core/test/…/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs` 5, `core/test/…/trace_test.clj` 5, `http/test/…/routing_http_composed_corners_test.clj` 5, `ssr/test/…/framework_zero_ownership_diagnostics_test.clj` 3, `ssr/test/…/ssr_routing_egress_production_test.clj` 2); `[:rf.route/handle-url-change` — 72 inside, 100 outside. Writers chose by habit, not by door.
- **Conformance corpus** (not in the fable count): 33 `[:rf.route/transitioned …]` dispatch literals in 22 fixtures under `spec/conformance/fixtures/` (`routing-multi-frame.edn` 3, `routing-fragment-as-slice.edn` 3, `route-fragment-change.edn` 3, eight fixtures at 2, eleven at 1), run by the JVM runner and, via the compile-time macro in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_fixtures.clj`, by the CLJS node/browser runners. No fixture pins the id in `:trace-emissions` (`:rf.trace/event-id :rf.route/transitioned` = 0 hits); one pins `:cause :link` in a comment (`route-navigation-blocked.edn:59`).
- The link door synthesises it: `routing/decisions.cljc:455-460` `[:dispatch [:rf.route/transitioned app-url {:rf.route/decided? true}]]`.
- **Codex's source correction, confirmed**: `url-change-cause` (`url_change.cljc:509-545`) honours ANY member of `rf.routing.resolve/causes` = `#{:link :navigate :popstate :initial :ssr}` (`resolve.cljc:46-53`; the read is `(contains? rf.routing.resolve/causes riden) riden`). So `[:rf.route/handle-url-change url {:rf.route/cause :link}]` is honoured TODAY; the only thing it gets wrong is `:default-scroll :restore`. There is no closed three-value set in code to widen — the three-value set is prose (012:452, 531). A rider-free client dispatch resolves `:initial`, a server frame `:ssr`: preserve both; never reinterpret an omitted rider as `:link`.
- The algebra view exposes the pair as data: `routing/tooling.cljc:107-111 route-transition-inputs` = `[[:event :rf.route/navigate] [:event :rf.route/transitioned] [:event :rf.route/handle-url-change]]`, mirrored in `spec/Derivations.md:622, 780`, `docs/EP/EP-0014-derivation-and-process-algebra.md:1056`, `docs/core/derivations-and-algebra-views.md:389`, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:214`.

## Options

**A — Collapse (recommended).** Delete `:rf.route/transitioned`. The link door dispatches `[:rf.route/handle-url-change app-url {:rf.route/cause :link :rf.route/decided? true}]`; the surviving handler derives `:default-scroll (if (= :link cause) :top :restore)`; the cause set THIS door honours is written as `#{:link :popstate :initial :ssr}` (a `:navigate` rider falls through to the rider-free resolution — `navigate` commits inline and never enters this door; `url-change-cause` gains that one exclusion or a docstring sentence, whichever is smaller). Everything else `url-change-fx` already owns — URL-before-state ordering for link activation, the `:rf.route/decided?` guard, fragment-only short-circuit, nav-token allocation, the SSR `:frame` threading — is unchanged because both handlers already pass the same map.

```clojure
;; decisions.cljc url-requested-handler, allowed branch — after
{:fx [(if replace? [:rf.nav/replace-url app-url] [:rf.nav/push-url app-url])
      [:dispatch [:rf.route/handle-url-change app-url
                  {:rf.route/cause :link :rf.route/decided? true}]]]}

;; url_change.cljc — one handler; transitioned-handler deleted
(defn handle-url-change-handler [cofx [_ url opts]]
  (let [cause (url-change-cause frame opts)]              ;; honoured set on this door: #{:link :popstate :initial :ssr}
    (url-change-fx {… :cause          cause
                      :default-scroll (if (= :link cause) :top :restore) …})))
```

Before/after for the tier that changes: a test writes `[:rf.route/handle-url-change "/x"]` and adds `{:rf.route/cause :link}` only when the cause matters (today it picks one of two ids by habit); the link door's child epoch reads `EVENT :rf.route/handle-url-change {:rf.route/cause :link}` instead of `EVENT :rf.route/transitioned`; Xray's cascade-root docstring (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing_helpers.cljc:452`) becomes "root ∈ {navigate, handle-url-change}" — its detection already reads the `nav-token/allocated` emit, not the event id, so no logic moves; popstate / initial / SSR unchanged.

**B — Keep both ids (status quo).** Codex: "Retaining separate well-named ingress events over the shared helper is also viable; a constant-specialised event can communicate intent without constituting another computation model." Cost: nothing moves; the written discriminator (012:37-38, 530-533, 1157-1158 "co-equal sibling handlers, not a delegate pair") stays as written; the trace row keeps reading `transitioned`.

**C — A plus rename the survivor to `:rf.route/url-changed`** (the only `:rf.route/*` event id carrying an imperative `handle-` prefix). Only defensible in the SAME PR as A: M-60 (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2433-2454`) shows this id was renamed once already (`:rf/url-changed` → `:rf.route/transitioned`), so a second move should be the last. Both the fable grok pass and codex lean against it ("avoid the optional extra event rename unless it clearly improves the resulting vocabulary; the implementation value comes from removing the redundant branch, not restyling every trace"). Roughly doubles the churn of A.

## Recommendation

A, without C. *Regularity over cleverness* (Principles:18): `:rf.route/planned` already carries `:cause ∈ {:navigate :link :popstate :initial :ssr}` (012:98) and three of the four URL-driven doors already ride one event with one rider; the fourth being an event id is the irregularity. *Data before magic* (Principles:46): `{:rf.route/cause :link}` is a map a test can build, assert on and diff; a second id is a name a reader must know is an alias. *One name per fact* (EP-0007, cited at 012:1146): "a link caused this URL change" is one fact with two spellings today — an id and a tag. Clojure's answer to two functions that differ by a constant is one function and the constant as an argument; `url-change-fx` already IS that function, and the two handlers are the wrapper the ethos says not to write.

## The counter (carried in full)

- **The discriminator IS written.** Spec 012:37-38 (events table: "Co-equal with …"), 012:530-533 ("Neither delegates to the other — they are sibling handlers over one shared slice-rewrite"), 012:1157-1158 (standard runtime events table: "co-equal sibling handlers, not a delegate pair"), `spec/API.md:281-282`, `spec/Construction-Prompts.md:875` ("Routing has two co-equal URL-change events"). The "co-equal, not a delegate" sentence records that neither CALLS the other; it does not record a reason for two ids — but it is a written discriminator, and the ethos bar admits a dual whose discriminator is written.
- **The id was already renamed once.** M-60 (`migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2433-2454`, a hot-zone file) maps `:rf/url-changed` → `:rf.route/transitioned`; M-20 (`:1028`) maps v1 `:route/url-changed` → `:rf.route/transitioned`; three skill references mirror it (`skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md:38`, `pre-rename-upgrades.md:19`, `sequencing.md:94`). Every move on this id costs a migration-README row and a skills sweep; A retargets M-20/M-60 onto `:rf.route/handle-url-change` + `{:rf.route/cause :link}`.
- **The churn is real and mostly mechanical**: 193 test dispatch literals (160 + 33) + 33 conformance-fixture literals; TWO Xray spec pages (`tools/xray/spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:452-457`, `018-Event-Spine.md:1075`) and one helper docstring/comment (`routing_helpers.cljc:452`, `:723`); ~18 lines of Spec 012 (`:37-38, :102, :451, :530-533, :598, :1041, :1061, :1073, :1157-1161, :1172, :1409, :1413, :1424, :1474, :1603, :1625, :1829`); FIVE hot-zone files (`spec/API.md:281-282`, `spec/Conventions.md:76, :1813`, `spec/002-Frames.md:554`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:236`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1028, :1368, :1373, :1610, :2433-2454, :2989`); non-hot-zone spec prose (`Runtime-Subsystems.md:91, :128`, `Derivations.md:622, :780`, `Construction-Prompts.md:777, :875`); docs (`docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:163, :214, :502-503`, `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1390`, `docs/EP/EP-0002-frame-target-resolution.md:482`, `EP-0014…:1056`, `docs/core/derivations-and-algebra-views.md:389`); routing src docstrings (`routing.cljc:36, :225, :231`, `decisions.cljc:243, :405, :412`, `events.cljc:71`, `nav_counters.cljc:78`, `navigate.cljc:115`, `plan.cljc:3`, `registry.cljc:108`, `url.cljc:363`, `url_change.cljc:3, :6, :106, :123, :182, :194`), the algebra input vector (`tooling.cljc:109`, `:233`), and two core mentions (`core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1772` comment, `core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:32` docstring).
- **A readable trace row is traded for a cause rider.** `EVENT :rf.route/transitioned` reads better in an epoch than `EVENT :rf.route/handle-url-change {:rf.route/cause :link}`; C buys the aesthetics back at roughly double the churn.

## The problem

Apps have exactly two navigation doors and three route reads, and use nothing else — the July "verified clean" reading still holds at the porch. The overlap lives in the tier apps never touch but tests, tools, docs and AI agents must learn: the URL-driven commit is spelled twice.

| Spelling | Lowers to | Written discriminator |
|---|---|---|
| `[:rf.route/handle-url-change url opts]` | `url-change-fx {… :default-scroll :restore :cause (url-change-cause frame opts)}` (url_change.cljc:581-589); cause read off the `:rf.route/cause` rider ∈ `#{:popstate :initial :ssr}` | "popstate / initial / SSR; default scroll `:restore`" (spec 012:37, 531) |
| `[:rf.route/transitioned url opts]` | `url-change-fx {… :default-scroll :top :cause :link}` (url_change.cljc:499-505) — the SAME fn, two constants | "forward nav from a link click; default scroll `:top`; co-equal sibling, not a delegate" (spec 012:38, 530-533, 1157; API.md:281-282) |
| `[:rf.route/url-requested {:url :to :params :query :fragment & policy}]` | classify external → decide leave/enter → `[:rf.nav/push-url]` + `[:dispatch [:rf.route/transitioned url {:rf.route/decided? true}]]` (decisions.cljc:455-460) | the link door: a browser-side URL change modelled as an inbound event, URL-then-state (spec 012:1157-1161) |
| `[:rf.route/navigate {:url s}]` | inline commit, state-then-URL, same open-redirect classifier (spec 012:504-511, 1165) | the programmatic escape hatch (spec 012:509) |

Two things are wrong in that table, one Medium and one Low.

1. **`:rf.route/transitioned` is a name for a value.** `handle-url-change` already discriminates its three doors by a data rider (`:rf.route/cause`, spec 012:449-452), and the docs teach tests to "say which door you meant" by passing it (docs/routing/testing.md:108-127). The fourth door is spelled as a second event id instead of a fourth rider value, and the only other difference — the default scroll — is a pure function of the cause (`:link` → `:top`, everything else → `:restore`). The "co-equal, not a delegate" sentence records that neither *calls* the other; it does not record a reason for two ids. Empirically the discriminator is not load-bearing:
   - no app dispatches either (example code lines: 0 / 0);
   - no app or tool re-registers either (`reg-event :rf.route/(transitioned|handle-url-change|url-requested)` outside routing src: 0);
   - the test corpus treats them as two spellings of "go to this URL" — 26 direct `transitioned` dispatches vs 111 `handle-url-change` outside `implementation/routing`, 154 vs 66 inside it, and one file using both (`ssr/test/re_frame/framework_zero_ownership_diagnostics_test.clj:162-201`).
2. **The link door's payload violates the request grammar's own rule 2.** `url-requested-payload` (link.cljc:171-188) emits `{:url path-url :to …}` plus `:params` / `:query` / `:fragment`; the handler destructures `url replace? bypass-leave?` and `normalize-policy` selects only `:replace?` / `:scroll` (decisions.cljc:420, 160-165). Nothing in `implementation/routing/src` reads `:to` off that payload. The navigate door rejects exactly this shape — "`:url` excludes `:params`, `:query` … a raw URL IS the address" (spec 012:462) — so the two URL-string doors disagree about what an address is, and tests pin the disagreement (route_link_test.clj:185, route_link_seam_cljs_test.cljs:76, 120).

Everything else in this area is a designed dual with a written discriminator, or a single door; those are recorded under *Non-goals / verified clean*, with four low-severity trims listed in the target.

## Simpler elegant target

**One URL-driven event, four causes.** Delete `:rf.route/transitioned`; the link door synthesises the surviving event with its cause as data:

```clojure
;; decisions.cljc url-requested-handler, allowed branch — after
{:fx [(if replace? [:rf.nav/replace-url app-url] [:rf.nav/push-url app-url])
      [:dispatch [:rf.route/handle-url-change app-url
                  {:rf.route/cause :link :rf.route/decided? true}]]]}

;; url_change.cljc — one handler; the default scroll is derived from the cause
(defn handle-url-change-handler [cofx [_ url opts]]
  (let [cause (url-change-cause frame opts)]        ;; closed set becomes #{:link :popstate :initial :ssr}
    (url-change-fx {… :cause          cause
                      :default-scroll (if (= :link cause) :top :restore)})))
```

## Why this is better (ethos)

*Regularity over cleverness* (Principles:18): every other door discriminates by a cause value — `:rf.route/planned` carries `:cause ∈ {:navigate :link :popstate :initial :ssr}` (spec 012:98) — and three of the four URL-driven doors already ride one event with one rider. The fourth being an event id is the irregularity; after the collapse "which door" is asked one way everywhere. *Data before magic* (Principles:46): `{:rf.route/cause :link}` is a map a test can build, assert on and diff; a second event id is a name a reader must know is an alias. *One name per fact* (EP-0007, cited at spec 012:1146): "a link caused this URL change" is one fact and currently has two spellings — an id and a tag. Clojure's own answer to "two functions that differ by a constant" is one function and the constant as an argument; `url-change-fx` already IS that function, and the two handlers are the wrapper the ethos says not to write.

The honest counter-weight, and why the sub family is left alone: in re-frame, cheap layer-2 subs are the idiom and their equality cut is the point. `:rf.route/id` is more than `(:route-id @(subscribe [:rf/route]))` — a `case` over it does not re-run when `:query-merge` pagination rewrites the slice, and ten of the twenty-two app read sites are `:<-` chain inputs, which need a vector to name (Conventions §Reserved sub-ids: "a sugar fn could never ride inside a `:<-` vector"). The whole-read-plus-projections shape is shared by machine, resource and mutation reads — one grammar across four features. The zero-consumer projections (`error`, `fragment`, `chain`) are the read half of shipped features and cost three lines each; the demand bar is noted, not enforced.

Costs of the collapse: ~180 mechanical test-line edits (the 154 inside `implementation/routing/test` are the bulk), three Xray spec pages and one helper, two migration-README rows, and a trace row that reads `handle-url-change {:cause :link}` where `transitioned` read prettier — the optional rename buys the aesthetics back at roughly double the churn.

## Codex Thoughts

The public routing API is largely already elegant. Keep navigation commands, link rendering, pending-navigation decisions, prefetch, and replan distinct. Their purposes differ, and the granular subscriptions provide useful reactive equality boundaries. This document correctly avoids replacing ordinary SPA authoring with a larger generic routing command.

Collapsing the two URL-commit events is defensible internal simplification, but its benefit is modest compared with changing an app-facing API: both handlers already delegate to one [implementation](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc). Do it alongside routing cleanup rather than commission a broad migration solely to reduce one event name. Retaining separate well-named ingress events over the shared helper is also viable; a constant-specialised event can communicate intent without constituting another computation model. The case for consolidation is that cause already travels as data throughout this pipeline.

One source correction matters: `url-change-cause` already accepts every member of [`resolve/causes`](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc), including both `:link` and `:navigate`. There is no current closed three-value implementation set to expand. The actual change is to make scroll defaults consistent with the selected URL-driven cause, update the link's emitted event, and decide/document which existing causes this ingress supports. Do not silently reinterpret an omitted rider as `:link`; direct client feeds currently default to `:initial`, server feeds to `:ssr`.

If consolidated, preserve URL-before-state ordering for link activation, the already-decided guard rider, fragment-only behavior, and navigation allocation. Programmatic `navigate` is not another spelling to delete: its state-before-URL ordering remains meaningful. Avoid the optional extra event rename unless it clearly improves the resulting vocabulary; the implementation value comes from removing the redundant branch, not restyling every trace.

The link payload's repeated address fields are removable if they are genuinely unused, but the diagnosis should distinguish command inputs from trace provenance. [The link builder](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/link.cljc) carries both authored destination and resolved URL; a successful `planned` trace is not necessarily a substitute for original intent on a malformed or unsuccessful route. Check actual trace consumers before removing those fields, then teach one authoritative address representation. Do not invent a second metadata envelope just to preserve speculative diagnostic demand.

The most concrete user-visible defect here is accepting `:prefetch :intent` without implementing it in [Hicasso route-link](../../../../implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/route_link.cljs). Prefer wiring the existing routing-owned intent behavior if the published option remains supported; otherwise reject it clearly. A silent no-op is poor ergonomics even for trusted programmers. Verify focus, pointer intent, existing user handlers, navigation cancellation, and frame capture; do not build another prefetch policy subsystem.

The small export removals are optional maintenance, not prerequisites. Keep pure URL algebra available to tooling, and don't substitute private runtime-state access merely to delete a helper. Prioritise honest link behavior and accurate cause semantics over polishing the last internal noun.

## Codex Recommendation

**Choose A: consolidate on `:rf.route/handle-url-change`, without an alias or another rename. Treat this as worthwhile, low-priority routing simplification, not an urgent correctness repair.** Refine A in two ways: preserve the old calls' cause semantics during migration, and retain the existing cause resolver rather than coupling this removal to a new four-member acceptance restriction.

Independently checked at `0ae438352476914f558c5ece11fad65597fbecf7`, **2026-09-06T16:31:07+10:00**. Both handlers and registrations remain present; `rf2-kuky.36`, `.37`, and `.38` are all open. This proposal has not landed.

### Why consolidation is justified — and what it does not prove

[The complete URL-change implementation](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/url_change.cljc) confirms one substantial computation with two wrappers selecting cause and scroll defaults. Both already carry the same frame and allocation coeffects. [The link decision handler](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/decisions.cljc) pushes/replaces the URL before dispatching the commit event, whereas [the history listener](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/history.cljc) already expresses its initial/popstate distinction as data. Extending that existing representation to links is a useful regularity: callers describe the navigation's origin using the vocabulary the plan already carries.

The justification is **not** that two constant-specialised handlers violate Clojure. Such handlers can be an excellent way to name distinct intentions. The strongest alternative is therefore C in this dossier: keep the pair and correct its documentation. The implementation is already factored; ordinary SPA authors predominantly use `navigate` and `route-link`, not either commit event. Searches of examples, tools, and skills found no example dispatch of `transitioned`, while the Xray routes testbed and boot skill use the survivor. Consolidation improves the advanced/test vocabulary more than day-to-day app authoring. That modest benefit is sufficient during the planned routing cleanup, but not grounds for inventing a new routing abstraction.

Nor is this exclusively internal work. [The routing contract](../../spec/012-Routing.md#standard-runtime-events) expressly permits users to dispatch and override these events. The absence of in-repository overrides limits measured migration cost; it does not erase the contract. This is an intentional pre-alpha API change.

### Refinements that keep the change honest

**Preserve cause before simplifying tests.** The default migration for every old `transitioned` dispatch should associate `:rf.route/cause :link` into its existing opts, retaining other keys. It must override any conflicting old cause rider: `transitioned-handler` currently hardcodes `:link`. Do not automatically make apparently generic URL-setup tests rider-free. Apart from scroll, `decide` publishes cause in pending-navigation and entry-denial payloads. A fixture can stop exercising link behavior without an assertion failing. Deliberately converting a fixture to initial-load coverage is a separate, explained test change. Existing [scroll tests](../../implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_scroll_test.clj) demonstrate that the distinction is observable, not merely descriptive.

**Retain the existing five-member resolver in this consolidation.** Framework-produced URL feeds should be documented as link/popstate/initial/SSR, but [the shared cause vocabulary](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/resolve.cljc) also includes `:navigate`, which `url-change-cause` already accepts. I found no explicit `:navigate` rider consumer; equally, no demonstrated problem requires a second accepted-cause subset. Silently converting that rider into `:initial` or `:ssr` is an independent behavior change, not a prerequisite for deleting an event. Preserve current unknown-value fallback and rider-free client/server defaults. If Mike specifically wants four accepted causes, make that a recorded additional ruling and executable resolver change; a docstring cannot implement the exclusion.


**Do not revive `:rf.route/url-changed`.** [M-60](../../migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md) records that exact keyword as the former *fragment trace operation*. Reusing it for the surviving event reintroduces a vocabulary collision in migration/history material, beyond the extra churn. Update the existing migration story instead. A custom `transitioned` override needs particular care: renaming its registration would now also intercept Back/Forward and SSR. Explain the widened scope and require intentional cause-aware adaptation, not a blind registration rename.

### Proportionate implementation and acceptance

Delete the wrapper/registration; resolve cause once in the survivor; derive default scroll as `:top` only for `:link`; retarget the link's dispatch while preserving `:rf.route/decided?`. Keep the dispatch hop, allocation metadata, frame attribution, and shared commit helper intact. Do not fold programmatic `navigate` into this event: its state-before-URL ordering remains a distinct operation.

Migrate tests and conformance data with cause preserved, then remove the redundant [algebra input](../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/tooling.cljc). Update contract, migration/skills, and Xray prose together with the coordinated change. [Xray's detector](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/routing_helpers.cljc) already scans allocation operations, so no event-name detector rewrite is needed. Serialize overlapping routing/hot-zone ownership; do not ship a prolonged interval where the runtime removes the name but the migration guide still recommends it.

Focused acceptance should establish:

- Link commit: URL mutation precedes the child commit, guards run once, and cause/default scroll remain `:link`/`:top`.
- Initial, popstate, and server feeds retain their existing cause/defaults; route-level scroll overrides and suppression still work.
- Exact no-op and fragment-only navigation preserve token and `:on-match` behavior; rejection preserves pending/denial cause and URL restoration.
- The obsolete registration/algebra row is absent, migrated fixtures run on JVM and CLJS, and a recorded replay retains allocation/frame behavior.

This was a source-and-contract review, including the full bead description and notes, not an executed equivalence proof. No builds or runtime tests were run; repository searches cannot establish what external applications override. The recommendation adds no compatibility shim, new policy subsystem, or extra API door.

## Problem

Four small exports at the routing read/link edge have zero or one consumer after months of corpus growth, and the link door's request payload carries four keys nothing reads. None of these depends on any ruling. The app-facing porch (`rf/route-link`, `[:rf.route/navigate …]`, the `:rf.route/*` granular subs) is untouched.

1. **`re-frame.routing/current-url`** (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:148-150` → `routing/history.cljc:73-84`) is `history-url-strategy`'s `:decode` (`routing/strategy.cljc:81`, published as `:decode` at `:131`) under a general name. Qualified callers outside its own two facade-pin tests: **0** (`git grep -n -E '(routing|rf\.routing|re-frame\.routing)/current-url'`). Its two would-be tool consumers rolled their own: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:513` and `tools/xray/testbeds/routes_epochs/core.cljs:442` both `(defn- current-url [] …)`. The 24 + 13 + 4 `current-url` lines in `routing_history_cljs_test.cljs`, `routing_url_strategy_cljs_test.cljs` and `routing_nav_fx_schemas_cljs_test.cljs` are a DIFFERENT function — the test helper `routing_browser_test_support.cljs:46 (defn current-url [history-state] …)` — and stay.
2. **`re-frame.routing/route-sub-fn`** (`routing.cljc:115`, alias of `routing/subs.cljc:27-33`) — consumers: **1**, `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj:191-192`, which hand-registers `:rf/route` through `re-frame.subs/reg-sub` (an app-db sub!) one line before `(require 're-frame.routing :reload)` at `:193` re-registers it correctly as a runtime sub. The slice path `[:rf.runtime/routing :current]` is normative (Conventions §Reserved runtime-db keys) and tools already spell it (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc:289`). rf2-6r9j.8 (closed, PR #9148) removed the dead `:routing/route-sub-fn` late-bind hook and deliberately KEPT this alias "because it is documented"; the documentation is the only thing holding it.
3. **`re-frame.routing/route-link`** (`routing.cljc:424-432`, CLJS-only `(def route-link (rf.views/reg-view* :route/link …))`) — a public def holding the `reg-view*` return that nothing dereferences: qualified consumers **0** (`git grep -n -P '(?<![\w.-])(rf\.routing|routing|re-frame\.routing)/route-link(?![\w-])'` returns only the `:routing/route-link` HOOK key). The `:clj` arm at `:433-436` is already a bare `register!` for effect. The manifest itself records the asymmetry: `spec/api-manifest.edn:175` justification — "the routing-ns form is CLJS-only and unrowed". **`re-frame.routing/route-link-render`** (`routing.cljc:153`, alias of `routing/link.cljc:303`) exists "so tests can call it directly" (`docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:478`); its 15 call sites are all tests and can call `rf.routing.link/route-link-render` (the parity test `route_link_ssr_parity_cljs_test.cljc` already does).
4. **The `:rf.route/url-requested` payload** violates the request grammar's own rule (Spec 012:462 — "`:url` excludes `:params`, `:query` … a raw URL IS the address"). `url-requested-payload` (`routing/link.cljc:171-188`) emits `{:url path-url :to to}` plus `:params` / `:query` / `:fragment`; the handler destructures only `url replace? bypass-leave?` (`routing/decisions.cljc:420`) and `normalize-policy` selects only `[:replace? :scroll]` (`:154-165`); `decide` gets its `:target` from `target-of-url app-url` (`:437`), never from the request. Readers of `:to`/`:params`/`:query`/`:fragment` off this payload in `implementation/routing/src`: **0**. Tool readers: **0** (`tools/xray/src` mentions `url-requested` once, in prose, `static/routes/simulate_nav.cljs:20`). Codex's caution — "distinguish command inputs from trace provenance; check actual trace consumers" — was checked: the `:rf.event/dispatched` trace carries the whole event vector (the URL is visible on a malformed or unsuccessful route), `:rf.route/planned` carries `:route-id`, and no panel projects the request map's address keys.
5. **`spec/API.md`'s cofx table** (`:317-321`) rows `:rf.route/nav-token` only; its companion `:rf.route/route-id` cofx (`routing.cljc:334-342`, Spec 012:1077-1102, `docs/api/re-frame.routing.md:547`) has no row. Folded here because this bead is API.md's one toucher for the area.

title: api(registry): RULING — defreg generator; kind-keyed (rf/clear kind id) vs nine clear-* names; http fx pair
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registration-and-testing.md (ref spellings.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

Three design questions from the registration-spellings review, one ruling bead. All one-reviewer (fable); codex reviewed the doc and cautions on each. @spellings.1 (aliases + concordance + table drift) and @spellings.2 (the written fx-form rule) are ruling-independent and already filed; nothing here blocks them.

## Q1 — generate both faces of a registrar from one `defreg`

**Today.** `defreg-macro` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc:250`, under `#?(:clj …)`) emits the JVM `defmacro` that captures `(meta &form)` / `*file*` / `*ns*` and splices to the owning fn. The CLJS same-name value alias is a separate hand-written `#?(:cljs (do (def reg-x …)))` block (`core.cljc:262-352`) — the list that drifted (10 of 15; @spellings.1 fills it and pins concordance).

**Options.** (a) One `defreg` row per registrar emits the macro on JVM and `(def reg-x delegate)` on CLJS — the expansion is host-aware (`(:ns &env)` discriminates a CLJS expansion), carries the docstring once, and applies the same `:doc` DCE gating (rf2-9wwkcm) the macros already have. Removes ~90 lines and makes a missing alias impossible by construction. (b) Keep two lists, pinned by @spellings.1's concordance check.

**Codex.** "The generator sketch is not an implementation: the existing macro generator is JVM-reader-gated and emits JVM macros. Simply teaching it to emit another reader branch does not ensure the CLJS compilation gets its value definition. Prefer the smallest repair — missing aliases plus a concordance check — unless one shared declaration can serve both host compilation paths without new build machinery. … The rule must exclude macros that walk syntax, not just macros that define a Var."

**Recommendation.** (b) now — it is @spellings.1 — and (a) only as a follow-up if the concordance check proves noisy or the block keeps growing. Fable prefers (a); the difference is ~90 lines against one more compile-time mechanism in the facade.

## Q2 — one kind-keyed inverse vs the nine `clear-*` names

**Today.** Nine public `clear-*` names in THREE shapes, and six registrar kinds with no inverse at all:

| shape | names | where |
|---|---|---|
| nilary clear-all + `(id)` | `clear-event`, `clear-sub`, `clear-fx` | `core.cljc:1069/1075/1080` → `events.cljc:1509`, `subs.cljc:367`, `fx.cljc:162` |
| `(id)` / `(id {:frame f})`, TOLERANT opts (`{:keys [frame]}`) | `re-frame.flows/clear-flow` | `flows/registry.cljc:833` — off the facade (`core.cljc:1036-1048`, rf2-wad2fl) |
| `(id)` / `(id {:frame f})`, EXACT fail-closed opts | `clear-http-interceptor` | `core.cljc:2545` → `http/middleware.cljc:245` (rf2-s32bf) |
| `(id)` only | `re-frame.routing/clear-route` (off facade), `clear-resource`, `clear-mutation`, `clear-resource-scope` | `routing/registry.cljc:594`; `core.cljc:1501/1545/1573` |

No inverse: `:cofx`, `:interceptor`, `:view`, `:head`, `:error-projector`, `:app-schema` (per-path). The substrate is uniform — `re-frame.registrar/unregister!` (`registrar.cljc:713`) takes `(kind id)` for every registrar kind (and forgets every provenance slot for the id, :724). The read side already speaks kinds: `(handler-meta kind id)` (`API.md` §Introspection), `(registrations kind)`; the kind table is `spec/001-Registration.md:87-117`.

**Consumers.** Non-test: THREE calls in ONE file — `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:352` (`run! rf/clear-sub`), `:411-412` (`run! rf/clear-sub`, `run! rf/clear-event`). Every other `clear-*` (route, http-interceptor, the resource trio, `flows/clear-flow`): 0 non-test. Test calls (impl + tools): clear-event 7, clear-sub 19, clear-fx 4, clear-flow 4, clear-route 3, clear-http-interceptor 30, clear-resource 6, clear-mutation 10, clear-resource-scope 0 → 83. Fixtures reach `registrar/clear-all!` / `clear-kind!`, not the public names.

**rf2-uhk4** (open, P4) records the facade asymmetry — `clear-flow` off the facade, the other eight on — and asks which direction to make consistent. This ruling SUBSUMES that question; do not act on rf2-uhk4 separately, close or re-point it with this bead's ruling.

**Options.**
- **(E) one verb.** `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})`: opts EXACTLY `{:frame f}`, fail-closed (rf2-s32bf applied to every frame-scoped kind at once), rejected for non-frame-scoped kinds; unknown kind fails closed. Registrar kinds route to `registrar/unregister!`; side-table / lifecycle kinds (`:flow`, `:http-interceptor`, `:route`, `:resource`, `:mutation`, `:resource-scope`, `:app-schema`) route by late-bind to the OWNING lifecycle fn — the same hooks the fx forms already call. Delete the nine names and the nilary clear-all arities (tests use `registrar/clear-kind!`). Completeness for `:cofx` / `:interceptor` / `:view` / `:head` / `:error-projector` / `:app-schema` falls out with zero new names. `:rf.fx/clear-flow` stays (its arg is the same id). Mirrors `handler-meta`.
- **(F) complete the family.** Six new names, ONE shape `(id)` / `(id {:frame f})` exact, nilary dropped; reunite `clear-flow` on the facade (rf2-uhk4's first reading). Same rule, more names.
- **(G) leave it.** Close rf2-uhk4 as won't-fix.

**Codex (carry into the ruling).** "The universal `clear` proposal is underdiagnosed. Resource clearing removes the registration AND disposes live cache entries, timers and in-flight work across frames (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc`). Route clearing emits its dedicated lifecycle trace. Flow clearing vacates an output leaf and settles dependents (`flows/registry.cljc:833` docstring; see rf2-g1zb for a live bug in exactly that settle). Therefore routing every registrar kind through `registrar/unregister!` is not behaviour-preserving; the nine names are not nine spellings of `dissoc-in`. A generic inverse remains possible as a thin dispatcher to owning lifecycle operations, but then its kind-specific semantics, scope rules and return values still exist. With three observed non-test clear call sites, there is no strong ergonomic case to build a universal teardown abstraction or invent six missing inverses merely for symmetry." Fable's honest costs: `rf/clear :sub` is less greppable than `rf/clear-sub`; `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` are v1-preserved (`API.md:162-164`) so a migration README row is owed; the generic verb cannot carry per-kind docstrings — the 001 kind table becomes the doc.

**Recommendation.** (E), with codex's parity condition as the acceptance bar: the dispatcher routes each kind to its OWNING lifecycle fn and never short-cuts a kind that owns runtime state to `unregister!`; the PR shows resource disposal, route trace and flow settle preserved by the EXISTING tests for those three. If that parity cannot be shown cheaply, (F) is the fallback — but (F) is how the family reached nine names in three shapes. Not (G): three shapes with six holes is option soup wearing a uniform, and pre-alpha is the cheap moment.

## Q3 — the http interceptor fx pair

**Today.** `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` / `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc:226-260`, ns docstring :12-19, rationale comment :212-225). Zero consumers in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/` after ~200 registration opportunities; both shipped http examples register at boot with the macro. Args are a re-spelled map (`{:id …}`), which @spellings.2's rule would forbid.

**Consumers the fable census did not class.** The conformance corpus drives BOTH fxs as pure data (rf2-yhfgf): `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn` (6 mentions), `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-interceptor-clear.edn` (8), the DSL realisation arm `implementation/core/src/re_frame/conformance.cljc:267-380` (the interceptor's `:before` body is a DSL body realised into a fn), `spec/conformance/README.md:539-540`. `spec/conformance/` is port-facing, so deleting the pair is a conformance-corpus change, not only an fx removal. Plus `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj:880-1030` (rf2-oyd1b tests), `spec/API.md:403-404`, `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` (2 mentions), `docs/api/re-frame.http.md:255-283`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2528`, `skills/re-frame-migration/references/pre-rename-upgrades.md:23`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:86`, `middleware.cljc:214,273` (comments).

**Codex.** "HTTP interceptors are frame-scoped, and their effects deliberately carry the dispatching frame. They satisfy that half of the proposed rule; what is absent is a shipped handler-time consumer. Removing or demoting those effects is a reasonable low-priority pruning decision, not proof that effects and boot-time function calls are equivalent. Do not manufacture an application-specific wrapper just to improve the public-name count."

**Options.** (H) delete the pair and its fixtures, park with the un-park trigger "a shipped example installs an interceptor from a handler (post-login bearer token)" and the pre-settled POSITIONAL shape `[:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor [id interceptor-map]]` per @spellings.2's rule. (I) keep, re-shape args to positional per the rule (breaking to zero app consumers; fixtures and tests update). (J) keep as is, recorded as the rule's exception.

**Recommendation.** (H). The demand bar has ruled; the two conformance fixtures exercise the fx TRANSPORT, not the middleware chain (which `http_interceptors_test.clj` covers through the fn form), so no port obligation is lost except the fx itself. **Coordination:** `http-request-surface.md` proposes the same deletion; if the http area's spec file carries it, the coordinator keeps one bead and re-points the other.

## Implementation beads to file when ruled

- **Q1 (a)** → `api(registry): emit the CLJS same-name alias from defreg-macro; delete the hand-written alias block (core.cljc:262-352)`. After @spellings.1 (its concordance check is the regression net). Non-hot except Conventions' one sentence.
- **Q2 (E)** → `api(registry): add (rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f}) and delete the nine clear-* names`. Code: `core.cljc` new `clear` dispatching on kind → `registrar/unregister!` or late-bind hooks (`:flows/clear-flow`, `:http/clear-http-interceptor`, routing's, resources' three, a new `:schemas/clear-app-schema`); `flows/registry.cljc:833` opts hardened to the exact shape; delete `core.cljc:1069-1080, 1501, 1545, 1573, 2545` and the public re-exports in `flows.cljc:48` / `routing.cljc:78` (owning fns stay as hook targets). Consumers: Xray `registry.cljs:352,411,412`; ~83 test calls. Spec (HOT): `API.md` §Clearing registrations :156-166 → one row, rows :402 / :460 / :462 / :464, :839-852; `Conventions.md` :1370-1378 tear-down roster, :1586. Non-hot: `001-Registration.md:87-117` (clear column), `013` / `014` / `016` (`clear-*` mentions: 2 / 2 / 5). Docs: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` (8), `re-frame.http.md` (1), `re-frame.resources.md` (3), `docs/core/flows.md` (1), `docs/async/http-going-further.md` (1), `docs/EP/EP-0003-resource-queries.md` (2). Skills: `api-cheatsheet.md:86,95,187`. Migration README: new row `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` → `(rf/clear :event id)` etc. Manifest: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` (nine rows out, one in; `docs/api` projection check). Close rf2-uhk4 citing the ruling.
- **Q2 (F)** → `api(registry): complete the clear-* family — six names, one exact-opts shape, clear-flow back on the facade`. Closes rf2-uhk4.
- **Q3 (H)** → `api(http): delete :rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor / :rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor, their conformance fixtures and DSL arm` (or the http area's equivalent). Deletion list as enumerated above; `spec/conformance/README.md` rows; then @spellings.2's open-disposition sentence is removed. mcp-conformance: `git grep` finds no tool reference to the two fixtures, but the worker re-checks the conformance runner's fixture roster.

## Priority

P3: medium, one-reviewer, codex cautions on all three. Q2's v1-preserved names and Q3's fx ids ARE surface at the first alpha tag, so a ruling before the tag avoids a post-tag break.

## Simpler elegant target


**A. One form per registrar, both faces generated.** Fold the CLJS alias block (F:262-352) into `defreg-macro`: on the CLJS reader branch the same form emits `(def reg-x owning/reg-x)` with the macro's docstring; on the JVM it emits the macro as today. Every one of the 15 non-Var-defining registrars then has Convention A by construction — the five missing aliases appear, and the list in Conventions.md:1483 is replaced by "every `reg-*` that does not def a Var". The facade's registration table becomes literally one table.

```clojure
;; core.cljc — one row per registrar, no second list
(defreg reg-flow rf.core-flows/reg-flow "…" {:arglists '([flow-id metadata derive-fn])})
;; JVM  ⇒ (defmacro reg-flow …)  captures coords, splices to rf.core-flows/reg-flow
;; CLJS ⇒ (def reg-flow rf.core-flows/reg-flow)  value position; macro still wins call position
```

**The written rule (one paragraph, for Conventions.md).** A registrar is a macro in call position and a fn in value position, under one name, on every host that has macros; the macro's only job is provenance capture and it is generated, never hand-written. A `*`-suffixed fn exists only where the macro also does syntactic work a value cannot (defs a Var, walks a literal) — today `reg-view*` on the facade and `reg-machine*` in its owning namespace. An fx form exists only for a frame-scoped registrar with a named handler-time consumer and takes the registrar's positional args verbatim. The inverse of every registration is `(clear kind id ?opts)`; there are no per-kind clear names.

## Why this is better (ethos)

- **The macro is the right axis, and it is Clojure's own.** `defn` stamps `:line` / `:file` on the Var; definition forms carry provenance, and Clojure spells them as macros. `reg-*` are re-frame2's definition forms — the same reason `assert` and `is` are macros. Runtime stack capture (001:181 lists it for TypeScript ports) costs a `js/Error` per registration, depends on source maps, has no JVM parity, and cannot be DCE'd; the macro path is compile-time and strips to nothing in production (001:193-206). What was wrong was never the macro, it was naming the fn twice — `let` / `let*` cuts both ways: `let*` earns its star because it is a *different* form (no destructuring), while a `*` that only forgets the line number is a name for nothing. rf2-m90brg said this; A makes it structurally impossible to need one again.
- **Regularity over cleverness (Principles:18).** Two hand lists that must agree will not; the tree proves it (five aliases missing, two unlisted, four wrong M/Fn rows). One generator, one table, one sentence of convention.
- **Many definers, one un-definer.** Clojure has `def`, `defn`, `defmacro`, `defmulti` — and `ns-unmap`. The registrar is one map; nine `clear-*` names for `dissoc-in` on it is the "one fact, many names" hazard Principles §The demand bar (:124) exists to prevent, and the missing six show the per-kind naming cannot even stay complete. `clear` mirrors `handler-meta`: kinds are data (Principles §Data is code, :103), and the tear-down axis collapses to one verb with one opts contract — so the rf2-s32bf hardening applies to every frame-scoped kind at once instead of one.
- **Data is code, literally.** An fx form is the fn form written as data; the http pair re-spelled the args, so the two spellings of one registration disagreed on shape. Rule C fixes the shape by construction: `(apply reg-x args)`.
- **The demand bar has already ruled** on the http fx pair (0 takers, ~200 opportunities), on `reg-app-schemas` (3 takers for a `run!`), and *for* the flows pair (two boot-time and two handler-time consumers — a designed dual with a mechanism discriminator).
- **Honest costs.** `rf/clear :sub` is less greppable than `rf/clear-sub` (mitigated: the kind keyword is greppable, and only three non-test call sites exist). `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` are v1-preserved names (API.md:162-164) — a migration row is owed. The generic `clear` cannot carry per-kind docstrings; the kind table in 001:87 becomes the doc. A/E touch the two hottest spec files.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes for the hand-kept alias table (10 of 15, a different 12 listed in Conventions, `(map rf/reg-resource …)` compiles on CLJS and `(map rf/reg-mutation …)` does not). Yes for the HTTP interceptor fx pair (zero consumers; `registration-spellings` and `http-request-surface` agree). The generic `(rf/clear kind id)` is a real design question, not a cleanup. Item D (`reg-app-schemas`) is withdrawn — the Status line and the opening sentence still name it as a target and should not.

**Diagnosis.** The macro/value-alias axis is right and already collapsed (rf2-m90brg). What is left is generation drift, an unwritten fx-form rule, and an inverse family that cannot stay complete (six kinds have no `clear-*`, three shapes among the nine that do). API.md's Fn/macro mismatch on four rows is a spec bug independent of any ruling.

**Options.** For the inverse: (E) one kind-keyed `clear`, or complete the per-kind family (six new names, one shape). Completing the family is how this got to nine names in three shapes. I would take (E) pre-alpha. For fx forms the written rule is the missing piece; once it exists the HTTP pair fails both clauses and goes.

**Recommendation.**

- **A. Do it.** Fold the CLJS alias into `defreg-macro`. Every non-Var-defining `reg-*` is a value on CLJS by construction. Replace the Conventions list with that sentence. This is the only way the table stops drifting.
- **B.** Already true at tip. Fix the stale `reg-machine*` facade row in Conventions.md:1466-1469.

- **C. Do it**, in lockstep with the HTTP doc. Rule: an fx form exists only for a frame-scoped registrar with a named handler-time consumer; args are the registrar's positional vector verbatim (`(apply reg-x args)` plus `:frame`). Flows stay. HTTP interceptor fxs go, parked with the positional shape pre-settled.
- **D. Withdrawn.** Keep `reg-app-schemas`.
- **E. Do it, as its own bead.** `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})`, fail-closed opts, rejected for non-frame-scoped kinds. Drop nilary clear-all (tests already have `registrar/clear-kind!`). Delete the nine public names. Completeness falls out (`:cofx`, `:view`, `:head`, …). Cost: `clear-event` / `clear-sub` / `clear-fx` are v1-preserved — owe a migration row. Greppability of `rf/clear :sub` is worse than `rf/clear-sub`; three non-test call sites, all in one Xray file.
- **F.** Sweep the two testbed compositions onto `reg-machine`; lead 005 §Registration with the macro.

Do not replace per-kind `reg-*` with one generic `rf/reg` — the grammars differ. Regularity belongs at the inverse.

**Implement.** A is mechanical and should not wait on E. C shares a PR with `http-request-surface.md`. E after A, so the kind table in 001 is the doc for both query and clear. Fix the four API.md M/Fn rows and the `clear-flow` "on the facade" sentence regardless.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: repair the alias/documentation drift; do not adopt this entire package as one simplification.** The macro/value distinction is useful Clojure machinery, and the remaining `reg-view*` and machine construction seams perform additional syntactic or programmatic jobs. The original star-twin cleanup is already landed. Correct teaching material and fill genuine Convention-A omissions without reopening that work.

[The current facade](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) still maintains a separate CLJS alias block. A common descriptor can prevent drift, but the generator sketch is not an implementation: [the existing macro generator](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_macros.cljc) is JVM-reader-gated and emits JVM macros. Simply teaching it to emit another reader branch does not ensure the CLJS compilation gets its value definition. Prefer the smallest repair—missing aliases plus a concordance check—unless one shared declaration can serve both host compilation paths without new build machinery. Check value-position calls as well as literal macro calls, and preserve coordinate capture and production elision. The rule must exclude macros that walk syntax, not just macros that define a Var.

**The universal `clear` proposal is underdiagnosed.** [Resource clearing](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc) removes the registration **and** disposes live cache entries, timers and in-flight work across frames. [Route clearing](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc) emits its dedicated lifecycle trace. [Flow clearing](../../../../implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc) vacates an output leaf and settles dependents. Therefore, routing every registrar kind through `registrar/unregister!` is not behavior-preserving; the nine names are not nine spellings of `dissoc-in`. A generic inverse remains possible as a thin dispatcher to owning lifecycle operations, but then its kind-specific semantics, scope rules and return values still exist. With three observed non-test clear call sites, there is no strong ergonomic case to build a universal teardown abstraction or invent six missing inverses merely for symmetry. Keep the existing lifecycle doors for now; remove demonstrably unnecessary public exposure separately.

The HTTP effect-pair argument also needs correction: [HTTP interceptors are frame-scoped](../../../../implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/middleware.cljc), and [their effects](../../../../implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/managed.cljc) deliberately carry the dispatching frame. They satisfy that half of the proposed rule; what is absent is a shipped handler-time consumer. Removing or demoting those effects is a reasonable low-priority pruning decision, not proof that effects and boot-time function calls are equivalent. Do not manufacture an application-specific wrapper just to improve the public-name count.

Keep `reg-app-schemas`, as the cross-check already concludes. Its up-front path validation protects feature registration from partial application caused by a bad path. Precisely, this is **prevalidation**, not a general transaction rolling back every possible later failure. No new transactional machinery is required.

Implementation should therefore be small and separable: alias conformance and stale documentation first; optional HTTP-effect pruning second. If generic clearing is reconsidered, first demonstrate parity for resource disposal, flow settling and route evidence, rather than treating lifecycle correctness as a follow-up. Elegance is fewer concepts, not merely fewer exported names.

import re, subprocess, sys, collections, os
os.chdir(r"C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2")
files = subprocess.check_output(["git","ls-files"], text=True, encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
exts = (".clj",".cljc",".cljs",".edn",".md")
def cls(p):
    if p.startswith("examples/"): return "examples"
    if p.startswith("tools/"):
        return "tools-test" if "/test/" in p else "tools"
    if p.startswith("testbeds/"): return "testbeds"
    if p.startswith("docs/"): return "docs"
    if p.startswith("skills/"): return "skills"
    if p.startswith("migration/"): return "migration"
    if p.startswith("spec/"): return "spec"
    if p.startswith("implementation/"):
        return "impl-test" if "/test/" in p else "impl-src"
    return None
names = ["reg-event","reg-sub","reg-fx","reg-cofx","reg-interceptor","reg-view","reg-view*",
         "reg-machine","reg-machine*","defmachine","make-machine-handler",
         "reg-app-schema","reg-app-schemas","reg-flow","clear-flow","reg-route","clear-route",
         "reg-head","reg-error-projector","reg-http-interceptor","clear-http-interceptor",
         "reg-resource","reg-mutation","reg-resource-scope","clear-resource","clear-mutation","clear-resource-scope",
         "with-managed-request-stubs","with-managed-request-stubs*",
         "register-listener!","unregister-listener!","register-observability-sink!","unregister-observability-sink!",
         "clear-event","clear-sub","clear-fx","clear-cofx","clear-interceptor","clear-view","clear-machine",
         "clear-app-schema","clear-head","clear-error-projector"]
fxs = [":rf.fx/reg-flow",":rf.fx/clear-flow",":rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor",":rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor"]
# counts[name][cls][spelling] -> n ; spelling in {call:<alias>, value:<alias>, bare-call}
counts = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter))
examples = collections.defaultdict(list)
fxcounts = collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter)
fxex = collections.defaultdict(list)
name_re = {n: re.compile(r"(?<![\w.*!?/-])(?:([\w.*!?-]+)/)?" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![\w*!?-])") for n in names}
for p in files:
    if not p.endswith(exts): continue
    c = cls(p)
    if c is None: continue
    try:
        txt = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except Exception: continue
    for n in names:
        if n not in txt: continue
        for m in name_re[n].finditer(txt):
            alias = m.group(1)
            start = m.start()
            prev = txt[start-1] if start>0 else ""
            # skip definitions
            line_start = txt.rfind("\n",0,start)+1
            line = txt[line_start: txt.find("\n",start) if txt.find("\n",start)!=-1 else len(txt)]
            if re.match(r"\s*\((defn-?|defmacro|def)\s+" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![\w*!?-])", line): continue
            if re.match(r"\s*" + re.escape(n) + r"\s+[\w.-]+/" , line) and alias is None: continue  # def alias line
            if alias is None and prev != "(":
                continue  # bare symbol not in call position: ambiguous (refer lists, prose) — skip
            kind = ("call" if prev == "(" else "value")
            if alias is None: sp = "bare-call"
            else: sp = f"{kind}:{alias}"
            counts[n][c][sp] += 1
            lineno = txt.count("\n",0,start)+1
            if len(examples[(n,c,sp)]) < 4:
                examples[(n,c,sp)].append(f"{p}:{lineno}: {line.strip()[:110]}")
    for fx in fxs:
        if fx not in txt: continue
        for m in re.finditer(re.escape(fx)+r"(?![\w-])", txt):
            fxcounts[fx][c]+=1
            lineno = txt.count("\n",0,m.start())+1
            line_start = txt.rfind("\n",0,m.start())+1
            line = txt[line_start: txt.find("\n",m.start())]
            if len(fxex[(fx,c)])<4: fxex[(fx,c)].append(f"{p}:{lineno}: {line.strip()[:110]}")
order = ["examples","testbeds","tools","tools-test","docs","skills","migration","spec","impl-src","impl-test"]
for n in names:
    print(f"\n=== {n}")
    for c in order:
        if counts[n][c]:
            print(f"  {c:10s} " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k,v in sorted(counts[n][c].items(), key=lambda kv:-kv[1])))
print("\n=== fx forms")
for fx in fxs:
    print(f"  {fx}: " + ", ".join(f"{c}={fxcounts[fx][c]}" for c in order if fxcounts[fx][c]))
if "--examples" in sys.argv:
    print("\n=== example lines")
    for k,v in examples.items():
        if k[1] in ("examples","testbeds","tools","docs","skills"):
            print(k); [print("   ",x) for x in v]
    for k,v in fxex.items():
        if k[1] in ("examples","testbeds","tools","docs","skills"):
            print(k); [print("   ",x) for x in v]

## The problem

The registrar is one map, `(kind, id) → metadata` (`spec/001-Registration.md:89`; the closed kind set is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:144-145`). The **read** side already speaks that grammar: `(handler-meta kind id)`, `(registrations kind)` (`spec/API.md:520-521`). The **write** side is per-kind by design — `reg-event`, `reg-sub`, `reg-flow` … — because each registrar's argument grammar differs, and that is not in question here. What is in question is the third verb, the **inverse**, which is neither uniform like the read side nor principled like the write side. Three questions came out of the wave-3 registration-spellings review; two sibling beads from the same review (rf2-kuky.23, rf2-kuky.24) have already merged and changed the ground under Q1 and Q3, so each question is stated as it stands at tip, not as filed.

### Q1 — the macro table and the alias table

`re-frame.core` emits its fifteen `reg-*` macros from one generator, `defreg-macro` / `defreg-event-macro` (`core_reg_macros.cljc:250` / `:311`, both under `#?(:clj …)`), with the fifteen rows at `core.cljc:499-689`. Each macro captures `(meta &form)` / `*file*` / `*ns*` and splices to the owning fn. The CLJS same-name value alias — `(def reg-flow rf.core-flows/reg-flow)` for HoF / programmatic callers — is a **second, hand-written list** at `core.cljc:277-408`.

When the review ran, that second list had drifted: aliases for 10 of 15, and the spec's roster named a different 12. **That is fixed.** PR #9291 (rf2-kuky.23, merged 2026-09-05) added the five missing aliases and landed `implementation/core/test/re_frame/registrar_alias_concordance_cljs_test.cljc`, which reads `core.cljc` itself once under `:features #{:clj}` and once under `#{:cljs}` and fails the suite when the two halves differ — no third list to drift. `Conventions.md:1491` now states Convention A as a rule, not a roster, and cites the pin. The comment at `core.cljc:265-275` records the same.

So Q1 today is not "how do we stop the drift" — it is "having stopped it with a derived test, do we also want the generator to make a gap impossible by construction, at the cost of host-dispatch machinery inside the facade's one compile-time mechanism". The .23 worker considered exactly that and declined: *one declaration serving both hosts would need host dispatch plus lifting the 15-row table out of its reader conditional — new machinery, and the generator is itself the open ruling on rf2-kuky.25*.

**Who it hurts, concretely.** The app author doing hot reload or per-tenant teardown — the audience `docs/core/flows.md` sends to the plain fns — writes `(flows/clear-flow :cart/total {:fram :session})` and the typo is swallowed: `registry.cljc:847` destructures `{:keys [frame]}`, `frame` is nil, `require-current-frame!` resolves the **ambient** frame, and the wrong frame's flow is cleared with no signal. That is precisely the silent mis-clear rf2-s32bf closed for `clear-http-interceptor` (`middleware.cljc:231-243`, `valid-clear-opts?`) — applied to one of the two identically-shaped surfaces and not the other. `spec/Principles.md:81` (No silent swallow) says a recognised-but-unhonourable input MUST signal. Honest reading of that diff: the one-verb form is a keystroke *worse* in HoF position, and `rg clear-sub` becomes `rg 'clear :sub'`. Those are the real ergonomic costs; they are small, and they are the whole of them.

**The strongest counter-evidence is codex's, and it is correct as far as it goes.** The nine are not nine spellings of `dissoc-in`. `clear-resource` removes the registration **and** disposes every frame's cache entries, timers and in-flight work (`registry.cljc:647-671`); `clear-route` emits `:rf.route/cleared` (`routing/registry.cljc:594-606`); `clear-flow` vacates the output leaf and, outside a drain, settles dependents — and rf2-g1zb was a live P2 bug in exactly that settle (a dependent flow kept publishing a value derived from a producer that no longer existed), fixed by PRs #9204 and #9257. So a `clear` that short-cuts every kind to `unregister!` would be a behaviour change, and codex's conclusion is that with three call sites there is *no strong ergonomic case to build a universal teardown abstraction*. Read carefully, though, rf2-g1zb cuts both ways: it proves that clear is **lifecycle, not dissoc** — which is an argument for a dispatcher rather than against a single door, and it means today's nine names were *hiding* that the operations differ. Under one verb the difference sits in one docstring's kind table instead of nine files.

## The decision

- **Q1.** Build a host-aware `defreg` that emits the CLJS alias from the same row (**A**), or keep the two hand-written lists pinned by the landed concordance test (**B**)?
- **Q2.** One kind-keyed `(rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f})` replacing the nine names (**E**); complete the per-kind family — six new names, one exact-opts shape, `clear-flow` back on the facade (**F**); or leave the family as it is (**G**)?
- **Q3.** Delete the fx pair, fixtures and DSL arm (**H**); keep it and re-shape its args to positional per the rule (**I**); or keep it as-is as the rule's recorded exception (**J**)?

## Options

### Q1

#### A. Fold the CLJS alias into `defreg-macro`

### Q2

#### E. One verb: `(rf/clear kind id)` / `(rf/clear kind id {:frame f})`

*What changes.* One facade fn. Registrar kinds (`:event :sub :fx :cofx :interceptor :view :head :error-projector`) route to `registrar/unregister!`; `:route` to `routing/clear-route` (trace preserved); `:flow` / `:http-interceptor` / `:resource` / `:mutation` / `:resource-scope` late-bind to the owning lifecycle fns through the `defwrapper`s that already exist (`core_flows.cljc:15`, `core_http.cljc:86`, `core_resources.cljc:43/:101/:166`) — so artefact-absent still raises the documented `:rf.error/<artefact>-artefact-missing`. Opts are exactly `{:frame f}`, fail-closed (rf2-s32bf's `valid-clear-opts?` applied to `:flow` too), **rejected** for non-frame-scoped kinds; an unknown kind raises `:rf.error/clear-unknown-kind` naming the closed set; return the id uniformly (the `reg-*` return-value convention); nilary clear-all arities dropped (tests already use `registrar/clear-kind!` — `test_support.cljc:561`). The whole implementation is the dispatch table; this is the shape Mike is ruling on, not a sketch of new machinery:

```clojure
(defn clear
```

Two design points fall out of writing it down and belong in the ruling rather than the PR: `:frame` is meaningful for exactly two kinds (flows and http interceptors are per-frame side tables; everything else is process-level, and `clear-resource` deliberately disposes *every* frame), so `{:frame f}` on any other kind is a recognised-but-unhonourable input and MUST throw; and the return value is the id for all kinds, ending today's nil-vs-id split.
