MAYOR — BACKLOG REREAD 2026-08-19 11:05 AUSEST. THE HOLD IS REAL, EXTERNAL, AND WORTH WRITING A COST AGAINST.

RE-TESTED AT SOURCE. rf2-uelji reads DEFERRED with deferred_until 2026-09-16, and its description states the mechanism: Clojars requires a NEW project to live in a VERIFIED group, verification requires a reverse-domain group name, and 'day8' is not reverse-domain and therefore cannot be verified. Existing projects in an old group may publish new versions; a new project may not be created. So no worker clears this — it is a policy question about a coordinate, not work.

WHAT THE HOLD IS COSTING, recorded because a hold with no cost written on it reads as free. This bead is the ONLY thing between Hicasso and a consumable artefact. Measured this morning: 86 of 90 hic-NNN beads closed, 28 source files and ~17,200 lines shipping under implementation/hicasso/src, 446 test files, 29 published guide pages carried in mkdocs nav, and the adapter registered in every roster. The documentary half of the original rf2-hic-061 clause — versioning and release automation, the 14-row compatibility matrix, the upgrade policy including complaint-id stability — is done and closed. What cannot be demonstrated is the one clause that matters to a consumer: that an app can install Hicasso from the artefact rather than from this repository.

THE DECISION THIS SURFACES FOR MIKE, and it is his because it names the project in public and is not cheaply reversed: the group coordinate. io.github.day8/* is the reverse-domain form Clojars will verify, and it is what rf2-uelji's deferral implicitly assumes; this bead's own title already says io.github.day8/*. If that is the intended coordinate, verification can start now rather than in September, and the deferral date is measuring a wait nobody is actually blocked on. If a different coordinate is wanted, that is the call to make.

I am not ruling it. Publishing under a coordinate is outward-facing and effectively permanent, which is the class the standing grant reserves.

title: story: rename unreg-global-decorator! — a fresh un-* prefix Conventions :1306 forbids (rf2-uimu follow-up)
description:
Filed 2026-09-06 by the rf2-uimu ruling (delegated by Mike, ruled by the dossier agent). Worker-scoped application of the Lifecycle-verb law, not a decision: the law already forbids this spelling. Sequence AFTER rf2-uimu's Conventions PR merges, so the amended law text this cites is on main.

## Problem
`re-frame.story/unreg-global-decorator!` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:766 at tip 13884f326f) is a fresh `un-*` prefix -- exactly what spec/Conventions.md §Lifecycle-verb law :1306 forbids ("file a bead against this section rather than coining `dispose-` / `teardown-` / `shutdown-` / a fresh `un-*`"). It sits on the Story facade (spec/api-manifest.edn:530, `:facade? true`, tier :tooling, owner 007).

Shape, measured: its twin `reg-global-decorator` (story.cljc:731) is registrar-shaped and has no bang (§Naming bucket 1) -- it registers the decorator body via `rf.story.registrar/reg-decorator*` AND appends `[id & ref-args]` to the global-decorators config vector (`rf.story.config/add-global-decorator!`). `unreg-global-decorator!` removes ONLY the vector entry (`rf.story.config/remove-global-decorator!`), is idempotent, and leaves the body registered -- that is `unregister!` (:981, `[kind id]`) 's job.

## Target
Name it by the ladder (Conventions :1299-1305 at tip; re-anchor by text after rf2-uimu lands), not by taste. Step 1: "drop registrations / a cache → `clear-*`; remove one hook by id → `unregister-*`". Default, per the rf2-uimu dossier: **`clear-global-decorator`** -- `clear-*` is the roster's stated symmetric inverse of `reg-*` and the add half here is `reg-global-decorator`; no bang, because the `reg-*` twin has none and the bang axis is decided per pair, not per direction. Use `unregister-global-decorator!` ONLY if the worker shows the global-decorators vector is a runtime hook table the framework invokes from arbitrary call sites (bucket 2) rather than a registrar-shaped config entry -- and say so in the PR body. Do not coin a third spelling; if the ladder is genuinely ambiguous, note it here and stop.

`re-frame.story/unregister!` (:981) uses a rostered verb; confirm it needs no change and leave it.

## Deletion list
The `unreg-global-decorator!` spelling. Pre-alpha: no alias, no deprecation shim (posture: a redundant spelling is deleted, not deprecated).

## Consumers (measured 2026-09-06 at 13884f326f; re-measure)
- defining file: tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:766 (docstring too)
- tools/story/spec/API.md:237 (the Story API row)
- docs/story/api/reference.md:47
- docs/story/api/registration.md:240,244
- spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:2124 (curated row -- rename the key)
- spec/api-manifest.edn:530 (GENERATED -- regenerate, never hand-edit: `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` from implementation/scripts/api-manifest/, then its `--check`)
- tests under tools/story/test: not measured -- `git grep -n -F 'unreg-global-decorator' -- tools/story` before editing
- skills/ and examples/: `git grep -l -F 'unreg-global-decorator'` repo-wide; the count above was taken over tools/story/src, tools/story/spec, spec and docs/story only

## Files to touch
story.cljc; tools/story/spec/API.md (if that spec keeps a Removed / renamed ledger, add one line; do not add a shim); docs/story/api/reference.md; docs/story/api/registration.md; spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn + regenerated spec/api-manifest.edn; any test that calls it; any skill that teaches it.

## Hot-zone
None of the files above is on the hot-zone list. Do NOT touch spec/Conventions.md (rf2-uimu owns it) or spec/API.md.

## Acceptance
- `git grep -F 'unreg-global-decorator'` over tracked files returns zero hits (a single deliberate ledger line in tools/story/spec/API.md is the only permitted survivor, and only if that spec already keeps such a ledger).
- Story JVM tests green: `clojure -M:test` from tools/story.
- Manifest `--check` green; the renamed var appears in spec/api-manifest.edn under the new name with the same tier/owner/status.
- `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` green (docs/story is in its roots); `mkdocs build --strict` green.
- PR body states which ladder step chose the name.

title: facade sweep follow-up: clear-flow sits off the facade while clear-event/clear-sub/clear-fx/clear-resource/clear-mutation sit on it (asymmetry recorded by rf2-2hpxo)
description:
Observed while classifying the 103 re-frame.core facade rows for rf2-2hpxo. Recorded, NOT acted on: acting would mean ADDING a facade export, which slice 1 explicitly does not do on its own initiative.

THE ASYMMETRY. The Conventions Lifecycle-verb law makes clear-* the symmetric inverse of reg-*. On re-frame.core today:

  reg-event      + clear-event       both on the facade
  reg-sub        + clear-sub         both on the facade
  reg-fx         + clear-fx          both on the facade
  reg-resource   + clear-resource    both on the facade
  reg-mutation   + clear-mutation    both on the facade
  reg-http-interceptor + clear-http-interceptor  both on the facade
  reg-resource-scope + clear-resource-scope      both on the facade
  reg-flow       + (no clear-flow)   registrar ONLY

rf2-wad2fl (the front-porch shrink) moved clear-flow to re-frame.flows and kept reg-flow on the facade. Every other registrar/clear pair kept both halves together. So either the flows pair should be reunited (add clear-flow back to the facade as a late-bind wrapper -- the wrapper already exists in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_flows.cljc and is simply not re-exported), or the OTHER seven pairs are the anomaly and rf2-wad2fl's reasoning should extend to them.

EVIDENCE THE FIRST READING IS RIGHT: the defwrapper for clear-flow is already written and live -- it is one of the 51 wrappers in implementation/core/src/re_frame/*.cljc -- so restoring the export is a re-export line, not new machinery. But this is pre-alpha and the surface is deliberately small, so it is Mike's call which direction to make consistent, not a worker's.

P4: a coherence nit, not a correctness one. Not a tag blocker; rf2-2hpxo does not hold on it.
notes:
FENCED — WAITS ON A RULING THAT OWNS THE SAME QUESTION (mayor, 2026-09-05, merge+dispatch tick). Do NOT dispatch this bead until rf2-kuky.25 is ruled.

WHY: this bead asks why clear-flow sits OFF the facade while clear-event/clear-sub/clear-fx/clear-resource/clear-mutation sit ON it — i.e. whether to add a sixth clear-* export for symmetry. rf2-kuky.25 (API review wave 3, filed 2026-09-05) is titled 'RULING — defreg generator; kind-keyed (rf/clear kind id) vs nine clear-* names; http fx pair' and is deciding whether the nine clear-* names should exist AT ALL, or collapse into one kind-keyed (rf/clear kind id) door.

The two answers are incompatible in the obvious way: actioning this bead ADDS a tenth clear-* name, while rf2-kuky.25 may delete all nine. Dispatching this first would be work against a surface the ruling may retire, and would then have to be un-done — which is exactly the shape the merge-conflict-avoidance rule exists to prevent, reached through a decision rather than a file.

RELEASE CONDITION: rf2-kuky.25 ruled. If the ruling KEEPS the clear-* family, this bead is dispatchable as written and is a small, clear fix. If the ruling collapses them to a kind-keyed door, close this bead as moot with a cross-reference rather than actioning it — the asymmetry it reports disappears with the family.

Recorded here rather than on rf2-kuky.25 because a fence belongs on the bead it fences, where its own reader will meet it.


--- MAYOR §3 BACKLOG REREAD, 2026-09-05 (premise re-verified at trunk) ---
PREMISE HOLDS, but it is narrower than 'facade gap' and this changes what the bead is.

MEASURED at HEAD in implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:
  :1126  clear-event rf.events/clear-event      <- a real facade export (def-alias form)
  :1098  ';; public home: reach them through `re-frame.flows` (`clear-flow`) and'   <- a COMMENT
clear-flow has NO export line anywhere in core.cljc; its only occurrence is that comment.

So the asymmetry is REAL and CURRENT — but :1098 records it as DELIBERATE, naming re-frame.flows as clear-flow's public home. That makes this a RULING bead ('is the asymmetry intended, and should the comment or the facade move?') rather than a mechanical fix. DO NOT dispatch a worker to simply add clear-flow to the facade: that would overturn a stated design position without a ruling, and per project posture we trust the programmer and do not litigate minutiae — the answer may well be 'the comment is right, close this'.

INSTRUMENT NOTE for whoever picks this up: core.cljc exports via a def-alias form, NOT `def`/`defn`. A grep for '(def|defn) +clear-event' returns 0 — an honest-looking zero on a name that IS exported. Search for the bare name and read the line.

--- TRIAGE PASS 2026-09-05 19:49 AUSEST (worker rulings-a; read-only classification pass; no status change, no code, no PR) ---
BUCKET (C) — SUBSUMED, by explicit instruction on the bead that owns the question. Not an independent ruling and should come off any "awaiting Mike" list.

rf2-kuky.25's own text: "rf2-uhk4 (open, P4) records the facade asymmetry -- `clear-flow` off the facade, the other eight on -- and asks which direction to make consistent. This ruling SUBSUMES that question; do not act on rf2-uhk4 separately, close or re-point it with this bead's ruling." rf2-kuky.25 is deciding whether the nine `clear-*` names exist AT ALL or collapse into one `(rf/clear kind id)` door, so actioning this bead would add a TENTH name to a family that may be deleted.

The asymmetry itself is still real at tip aa3c616e46, so this is subsumption rather than a false premise: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc carries `clear-flow` ONLY as a comment at :1108 ("public home: reach them through `re-frame.flows` (`clear-flow`)") with no export line anywhere in the file, while `clear-event` is a live def-alias at :1126. That also confirms the instrument note already on this bead — the exports are def-alias forms, so a `(def|defn) clear-event` grep returns an honest-looking zero on a name that IS exported.

DISPOSITION WHEN rf2-kuky.25 IS RULED, unchanged from the fence already recorded here: if the `clear-*` family is KEPT, this is dispatchable as written and is a small clear fix; if it collapses to the kind-keyed door, close as moot with a cross-reference.

LEFT OPEN — this pass changes no status. GATING: zero open beads.
close_reason: RULED by rf2-kuky.25 (2026-09-06 17:26:58 AUSEST, delegated by Mike): Q2 → E — the nine per-kind clear-* names and the owning-namespace exports collapse into one kind-keyed (rf/clear kind id ?{:frame f}) on re-frame.core, implemented by rf2-kuky.80. The clear-flow-off-the-facade asymmetry this bead reports disappears with the family instead of being resolved in either direction — subsumed/moot, exactly the disposition the fence above recorded. Do NOT add clear-flow to the facade. The instrument note here (def-alias exports; honest-looking zero on a (def|defn) grep) is carried into rf2-kuky.80's description.

title: api(registry): delete the ten per-kind `*-ids` / `*-meta` aliases; resource-meta / mutation-meta go private
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registry-introspection.md (ref registry-introspection.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Beside the generic `{id meta}` grammar every tool already uses, each artefact grew a `<kind>-ids` / `<kind>-meta` pair that is a one-line alias of it (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc:609-613` says so in its own comment: "The `<thing>-ids` + `<thing>-meta` enumerate pair every sibling registry carries"). Ten public names encode a registrar kind into an identifier — the "multiple equivalent encodings" `spec/Principles.md:18` (Regularity over cleverness) names as a tax on tooling and generated code, and the tax was paid: pair-MCP pinned a facade spelling that then moved (@registry-introspection.1). Zero app consumers, zero tool code callers; the only tool-side users are the pair preload's two wrappers, and Xray deliberately re-derives `machines` over the generic read (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs:673-705`).

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b; each lowering verified)

| Name | Defined | Lowers to | Facade re-exports | Manifest rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `route-ids` | `routing/registry.cljc:615` | `(vec (rf.registrar/ids :route))` | `routing.cljc:86` | `spec/api-manifest.edn:323` |
| `route-meta` | `routing/registry.cljc:623` | `(rf.registrar/lookup :route id)` | `routing.cljc:87` | `:325` |
| `resource-ids` | `resources/registry.cljc:685` | `(vec (rf.registrar/ids :resource))` | `resources.cljc:94` | `:302` |
| `mutation-ids` | `resources/mutation_registry.cljc:350` | `(vec (rf.registrar/ids :mutation))` | `resources.cljc:120` | `:291` |
| `scope-resolver-ids` | `resources/scope_registry.cljc:422` | `(vec (rf.registrar/ids :resource-scope))` | `resources.cljc:138` | `:306` |
| `scope-resolver-meta` | `resources/scope_registry.cljc:414` | `(:rf/resource-scope (lookup :resource-scope id))` | `resources.cljc:137` | `:307` |
| `resource-meta` | `resources/registry.cljc:676` | `(:rf/resource (lookup :resource id))` | `resources.cljc:93`; `re-frame.core` (`core.cljc` ~1507 via `core_resources.cljc` `defwrapper resource-meta`, hook `:resources/resource-meta`) | `:303`, `:171` |
| `mutation-meta` | `resources/mutation_registry.cljc:340` | `(:rf/mutation (lookup :mutation id))` | `resources.cljc:119`; `re-frame.core` (~1550, `core_resources.cljc`, hook `:resources/mutation-meta`) | `:292`, `:135` |
| `machines` | `machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:180` | `(->> (registrations :event) (keep #(when (:rf/machine? (val %)) (key %))) vec)` | — | `:268` |
| `machine-meta` | `machines.cljc:189` | `resolver/spec-from-registry` = `(:rf/machine (lookup :event id))` when `:rf/machine?` (`lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc:47`) | — (late-bind hook `:machines/machine-meta`, `machines.cljc:520`; directory `late_bind/directory.cljc:425`) | `:264` |

Consumers (code lines, excluding defs/comments): `examples/` 0 and `testbeds/` 0 for every name; tools src 0 except `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` (`machines-list` `:1139`, `machine-describe` `:1144`) and the pair-mcp strings .1 removes; `resource-meta` / `mutation-meta` framework-internal 29 + 9 lines in 9 + 6 files, ALL inside `implementation/resources/src` (`events.cljc` 11, `mutation_events.cljc` 9, `trace_egress.cljc` 4, `ssr.cljc` 2, `subs.cljc` 2, `resources.cljc` 6, …) plus the two `re-frame.core` wrappers; `scope-resolver-meta` internal 2 (`scope_registry.cljc`, `resources/tooling.cljc:217`); `resource-ids` / `mutation-ids` internal only from `resources.cljc`'s `resources` / `mutations` (`:150`, `:229`) and `resources/tooling.cljc`; `machine-meta` internal via the `:machines/machine-meta` late-bind hook (`data_validation.cljc:374`). Tests pinning the alias call forms: 22 files (`machine_source_coord_test.clj` 20 lines, `machine_source_coord_cljs_test.cljs` 15, core `smoke_test.clj` 13, `resources_scope_registry_cljs_test.cljc` 10, `resources_mutation_cljs_test.cljc` 5, `machine_schema_test.clj` 5, `machine_schema_arity_test.clj` 4, `resources_runtime_cljs_test.cljc` 3, `recipes/async_nav_l0_cljs_test.cljs` 2, `machine_schemas_grammar_test.clj` 2, `machine_output_schema_test.clj` 2, adapters/reagent `login_cljs_test.cljs` 2, and 1 line each in 4 Xray tests, `story_runtime_test.clj`, `routing_classification_test.clj`, `resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs`, `resources_derived_scope_sensitivity_cljs_test.cljc`, `parallel_test.clj`, `boot_cljs_test.cljs`).

The spec already teaches the generic read for routes (`spec/012-Routing.md:401, 546, 1783` use `rf/handler-meta :route`; no spec page calls `route-ids`) and says of machines "There is no `:machine` registry kind … `(rf.machines/machines)` is a `filter` call, not a separate index … One-line implementation" (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:3994-3996`).

## Target API (spelled in @registry-introspection.2's grammar)

```clojure
;; before                                   ;; after
(rf.routing/route-ids)                      (keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :route}))
(rf.routing/route-meta id)                  (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :route :id id})
(rf.resources/resource-ids)                 (keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :resource}))
(rf.resources/resource-meta id)             (:rf/resource       (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :resource       :id id}))
(rf.resources/mutation-meta id)             (:rf/mutation       (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :mutation       :id id}))
(rf.resources/scope-resolver-meta id)       (:rf/resource-scope (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :resource-scope :id id}))
(rf.machines/machines)                      (into {} (filter (fn [[_ m]] (:rf/machine? m))) (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event}))  ; keys for ids
(rf.machines/machine-meta id)               (:rf/machine (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :event :id id}))   ; nil unless :rf/machine?
```

The inner-key projection becomes a DOCUMENTED contract, not a helper: a `:resource` / `:mutation` / `:resource-scope` registration carries its spec under `:rf/resource` / `:rf/mutation` / `:rf/resource-scope`; a machine is an `:event` registration with `:rf/machine? true` carrying its spec under `:rf/machine` (both reviewers). Machines stay a filter over `:event` (codex floor); a virtual `:machine` KIND is @registry-introspection.4's ruling, not this bead.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Codex §Proposed smaller API ("Retire … the ten feature-specific public getters above … Inner metadata keys become an explicitly supported projection contract … Feature internals may keep private helpers, and tools may retain user-friendly commands such as 'list machines'"); fable §Simpler elegant target Deleted list and §Codex cross-check ("It concurs on deleting the per-kind pairs and on the inner-key projection contract"). Codex keeps `resource-meta`-style helpers PRIVATE where they clarify runtime code — hence the artefact-private fate for the two with 38 internal callers.

description:

Line numbers measured at tip `13884f326f` (= origin/main, 2026-09-06 17:18 AUSEST) unless marked "dossier tip" (`6d513ba07f`, single-digit drift). Grep by NAME before editing — lines drift._

## Problem

`:on-spawn` is a spawn-spec callback `(fn [{:keys [data id]}] _)` that the runtime invokes PRE-COMMIT inside the transition fold (`apply-on-spawn`, `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` ~:2320-2380), discards the return of, and then warns about when it is non-nil (`:rf.warning/on-spawn-return-ignored`, ~:2367; remedy vector ~:2374). The one plausible thing an author does with a spawned id — record it — is the thing the hook refuses; the transition reducer already binds it under `[:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>]` (`transition.cljc:562`). Consumers: **0** — the two example hits (`examples/patterns/websocket/core.cljs:42`, `connection.cljs:69`) are prose saying "no `:on-spawn`". It drags along a root-level `:on-spawn-actions` registration slot, a `MachineElementEntry` schema row, source-coord stamping in the `reg-machine` macro, an action-ref id `:rf.machine.spawn/on-spawn` on the exception path, a conformance DSL arm, a four-mechanism 005 §Recording the spawned id section that exists only because the hook invites the wrong one, and a migration rule whose "after" block (M-35) shows the exact no-op as the correct migrated form.

**Ruling A (rf2-kuky.15): delete the family.** Not because the hook "can do nothing" — Codex is right that it runs application code pre-commit and a throw becomes machine-action failure with rollback (`spawn_on_spawn_throw_test.clj` pins that) — but because no consumer needs a pre-commit observer and its position complicates the otherwise data-oriented fold. The data path (`:rf/spawned` on the parent; `:rf/self-id` / `:rf/parent-id` on the child) becomes the one id-recording story. No shim, no deprecation, no "retired key" diagnostic.

## Target

- The spawn-spec vocabulary (`:spawn` and `:spawn-all` children, and `[:rf.machine/spawn]` args) loses `:on-spawn`; a spec that still carries it fails the EXISTING closed-vocabulary unknown-key diagnostic (`lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc` `known-spawn-spec-keys`).

- `:rf.warning/on-spawn-return-ignored` (009 row + emission) and the `:rf.machine.spawn/on-spawn` action-ref are deleted.
- 005 §Recording the spawned id user-side (~:2985-3000) collapses to one sentence: "the reducer binds it under `[:data :rf/spawned <invoke-id>]` (the `{child-id actor-id}` map for `:spawn-all`); tools read `[:rf.runtime/machines :spawned <parent> <invoke-id>]`." Logging a spawn is what the `:rf.machine.lifecycle/spawned` / `:rf.machine.spawn/spawned` traces are for.

title: api(machines): fix four addressing drifts; make-machine-handler leaves the registration tables (2 door consumers)
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from machines.md (ref machines.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Four normative statements contradict the tree or each other, and readers act on them (a migrator following the skill will address a boot singleton by `:system-id`, which the pattern spec forbids). Independently, `make-machine-handler` is still presented as a registration door in two API tables and in 005 §Registration's lead, while the framework's registration entry point is `reg-machine` / `defmachine` + `reg-machine`; two sites still use the door composition. All are ruling-free; each is fixed where it stands. (If @machines.2 is ruled "delete" before this dispatches, items 1 and 3 collapse into that deletion — drop them from this bead and say so.)

## Evidence (tip `6445d0611b`)

1. `spec/Conventions.md:441` — the `:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system` row ends "The fx counterpart to the `dispatch-to-system` fn (`re-frame.core`)". That fn was deleted (rf2-c6xkmn; `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1082-1085,1650-1653` record it; `docs/api/re-frame.machines.md:17` and `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:2957` already say "there is no `dispatch-to-system` var").
2. `spec/Conventions.md:439` — the `:rf.machine/spawn` row says "record its id into the parent's `:data` via `:on-spawn`". `:on-spawn`'s return is dropped (`transition.cljc:2320-2380`; 005:2984 "a callback like `(assoc data :pending id)` is a no-op"); the pure reducer binds the id under `:rf/spawned` (`transition.cljc:533-562`; 005:2986-2990). title: api(ssr): one (ssr/head-model frame-id ?opts) replaces render-head / active-head; retarget ssr-ring lifecycle
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 by the ruling on rf2-kuky.44 (option A, single door). Bead 2 of 2 — blocked on bead 1: the `rf/` copies must be gone first, so there is no façade copy of the new fn to write and then delete. Line numbers at tip 2b6e8a44cf; re-grep before editing._

## Problem

Two public reads answer one question — "what is this frame's head model?": `render-head` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:128-155`; a keyword-OR-map second argument — the placeful dispatch on type that `spec/Principles.md:30` asks to retire) and `active-head` (`:179-207`; route `:head` → `render-head`, else `default-head`; no route override). Zero app or tool consumers; one framework consumer (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:178`). RULED: ONE read, `head-model`, defined at home and re-exported from `re-frame.ssr`.

## Why `head-model` and not `head`

The dossier proposed `(ssr/head …)`. That name COLLIDES in ClojureScript: `re-frame.ssr` requires `re-frame.ssr.head`, so the namespace object `re_frame.ssr.head` (carrying `.registry`, `.emit` and the head ns's own vars) exists first, and `(def head …)` in `re-frame.ssr` then emits `re_frame.ssr.head = fn`, clobbering it; the analyzer shipped here (clojurescript 1.12.42, `cljs/analyzer.cljc:1980,3198`) warns `:ns-var-clash` and the runtime breaks. The ruling refused relocating the three-namespace head subtree (the second reviewer's remedy — it breaks the dotted `re-frame.ssr.*` family for a one-word name) and instead names the fn for what it returns: `head-model`, pairing with the existing `head-model->html`. DO NOT name it `head`; do NOT rename `re-frame.ssr.head`.

## Target

```clojure
(ssr/head-model frame-id)                              ; = today's active-head
(ssr/head-model frame-id {:head-id id :route r})       ; = today's render-head; opts map only, no keyword dispatch
(ssr/head-model->html (ssr/head-model frame-id))       ; model -> inner-head HTML (bead 1 lifted it onto re-frame.ssr)
```

ONE selection rule — pin every clause in tests:
1. nil `frame-id` → `:rf.error/no-frame-context` via `require-frame-stamp!` (event `:rf.ssr/head-model`, `:where 're-frame.ssr/head-model` or whichever symbol convention bead 1 settled for the other `:where` values).
2. Resolve the effective route ONCE: `(contains? opts :route)` → that value (an explicit `:route nil` means "no route"); else the frame's runtime-db route slice (`frame-current-route`).
3. `:head-id` supplied → that registration, `:rf.error/no-such-head` if unregistered; else the effective route's `:head` id, if any → that registration, `:rf.error/no-such-head` if unregistered; else `(default-head frame-id)`.
4. The head fn is evaluated against the SAME effective route, so `(head-model f {:route r})` without `:head-id` selects r's head and evaluates it against r.

Return the model and nothing else — no side channel, no HTML mode, no cache. `default-head` stays public; `render-head*` / `route-head-id` / `frame-current-route` stay private (fold or rename as `head-model*`).

## Code

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc`: replace `render-head` (:128) and `active-head` (:179) with `head-model`; rewrite the ns docstring (:8-16); `:where` symbols at `:103,:115,:199`; delete the keyword-or-map branch.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc:40,41` → `(def head-model registry/head-model)`; docstrings `:2,:19-20`; `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/emit.cljc:17` docstring.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc`: `(def head-model head/head-model)` beside `head-model->html`.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:178` → `(ssr/head-model frame-id)`; docstrings `:168,:278,:282`; drop the `[re-frame.ssr.head :as head]` require bead 1 added if nothing else uses it; `pipeline.clj:606` comment.
- SILENT-FAILURE EDGE: `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj:787` guards a check with `(when-let [active (resolve 're-frame.ssr.head/active-head)] …)` — left behind, that check silently stops running. Retarget it to `head-model`, and turn BOTH guards (`:787`, `:796`) into direct calls through a required alias so a future rename fails loudly (the artefact is on the test classpath).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_artefact.cljc:124-125` docstring if bead 1 left it naming `render-head`.

## Tests

- `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:2724` and the `with-redefs` at `:2815,:2866` → `ssr/head-model` (the var lifecycle now calls); `:847,:2038` comments; `render_hash_tier_test.clj:184`, `ring_streaming_test.clj:1294` prose.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_head_test.clj` (every `render-head :id {:frame f}` / `render-head :id f` → `(head-model f {:head-id :id})`, every `active-head f` → `(head-model f)`), `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj`, `ssr/test_fixture.clj`, `ssr/head_emit_cljs_test.cljc`, `ssr_head_resolution_no_project_test.clj`, `ssr_keyword_head_contract_test.clj` — enumerate with `git grep -n -E '\b(render-head|active-head)\b' -- implementation/ssr/test`.
- New pins (JVM, and CLJS where the suite is cljc): route `:head` → registered model; no route `:head` → `default-head`; unregistered `:head-id` → `:rf.error/no-such-head`; unregistered route-declared `:head` → `:rf.error/no-such-head`; `{:route nil}` vs absent `:route` differ; `{:route r}` WITHOUT `:head-id` selects r's `:head` and evaluates against r; nil frame → `:rf.error/no-frame-context`; a CLJS compile plus one `head-model` call after ns load (the collision guard).
- Unchanged and must stay green: the head-hash channel (`implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/render_hash_tier_test.clj`, `ring_streaming_test.clj:1289-1354`); byte-identical `<head>` on the Ring e2e fixtures.

## Spec / docs / skills

- HOT ZONE `spec/API.md:339-340` two rows → one `head-model` row (`(head-model frame-id)` / `(head-model frame-id {:head-id :route})` → `:rf/head-model`; carry over the "frame is carried, not ambient" sentence from the `active-head` row); `:29,:327` head-reads sentences → `head-model` / `head-model->html` on `re-frame.ssr`.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:70` (`active-head` → `head-model`), `:1204` status banner, `:1255-1264` §Default flow steps 3 and 5, `:1266-1276` §`render-head` → §`head-model` (heading AND anchor — check inbound `#render-head` anchors with `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`), `:1286-1287`. `spec/Ownership.md:56`. HOT ZONE `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2127`: the `:rf.error/ssr-head-resolution-failed` row names `rf/active-head` / `rf/head-model->html` — touch only that row text.
- `docs/ssr/head.md:55,76`; `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md` §The head model (`:254` on), `:681,:719`; `docs/ssr/coming-from-nextjs.md:66` if it names the reads; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:47-67`; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:132-133` → one `ssr/head-model` row.
- UNTOUCHED: `:ssr/active-head` as a conformance capability / EXPECT id (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:233,252`, `spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-head-emits.edn:38`, `ssr-head-hydration.edn:68`) — vocabulary, not a fn name; say so in the PR body.
- Regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` (the `re-frame.ssr.head` `render-head` / `active-head` rows → `head-model`; add the `re-frame.ssr` `head-model` row) and the matching `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn` entries.

## Hot zone / sequencing

`spec/API.md` and one row of `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — one-toucher; lands after bead 1's PR merges. rf2-kuky.42 / rf2-kuky.43 are closed and on main.

## Problem

Six SSR query fns carry two public spellings for one job: the home def (`re-frame.ssr` for `render-to-string` / `render-tree-hash` / `project-error`; `re-frame.ssr.head` for `render-head` / `active-head` / `head-model->html`) and a late-bound copy on `re-frame.core` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:880-917` → `core_ssr.cljc` defwrappers → hooks `:ssr/render-to-string` `:ssr/render-tree-hash` `:ssr/project-error` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:415,416,418`) and `:ssr/render-head` `:ssr/active-head` `:ssr/head-model-html` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc:53,54,59`) → directory rows `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:730,733,743,762,766,770`). The copy's stated purpose (`spec/API.md:327`, `spec/Conventions.md:1744`) is a guided `:rf.error/ssr-artefact-missing` for an app that calls an SSR fn without the artefact. But loading `re-frame.ssr` is what registers `:rf/hydrate`, the `:rf.ssr/check-*` fx, the seven `:rf.server/*` fx and the `:rf.server/request` cofx, so no SSR app can be that app; every measured call site already sits in a file that requires the artefact ns. RULED on rf2-kuky.44: `re-frame.ssr` is the only SSR QUERY door; `re-frame.core` keeps only the two REGISTRARS `reg-head` / `reg-error-projector`.

## Target

title: docs(migration): O-13 must pass the UIx adapter to init!
description:
The UIx opt-in migration recipe in migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md, O-13 Adapter install (line 3032 at merge ad46ea8ef62b75412ce53cc9780f4c893a810ce0), says requiring re-frame.adapter.uix auto-registers a default adapter and instructs an app to replace its explicit adapter argument with (rf/init!). Following it turns a working app boot into an arity error.

The shipped implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc init! (2767-2790) has exactly [adapter-map], explicitly documents that no default-adapter registry exists, and installs that supplied map. M-40 in the same migration guide and Spec 006 Adapter selection at boot already teach the correct explicit adapter recipe. O-13 should bind re-frame.adapter.uix and pass its adapter value to init!, preserving the opt-in nature of the substrate migration.

This is pre-existing documentation drift discovered while auditing PR #9313, not a regression from its alias changes. rf2-lwx8 already mentions the contradiction in notes but was closed after its intentionally narrow alias fix; its accepted cosmetic-sweep disposition should remain closed. The historical runtime owner rf2-agql no longer exists in the live ledger. Searched all 969 live/exported issue records across statuses; no exact owner for this O-13 boot correction was found. No runtime API change is needed.

title: api(resources): reg-resource-scope takes one arity with :inputs required; delete the whole-db sugar and the :doc-only variant
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from resources.md (ref resources.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`reg-resource-scope` has two arities (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc:350–399`; the 2-arity at `:381` forwards `{}` metadata), and `canonical-spec` (`:248–347`) selects the "whole-db form" whenever the metadata map lacks an `:inputs` key (`:323`) — which includes a THREE-argument call carrying only `:doc` (codex's correction: deleting the 2-arity alone leaves the exception alive). In that form ALONE the resolver's first argument is the raw db rather than the inputs map — a documented "deliberate, cost-marked exception" and "first-arg meaning-shift" (`scope_registry.cljc:55–71`; `spec/016-Resources.md:192–203`, "a marked convenience, not a peer"). The implementation immediately wraps the sugar back into the canonical shape: a synthetic `:inputs {:db [:db []]}`, a wrapper `(fn [{:keys [db]} ctx] (f db ctx))`, and an authored flag `:whole-db? true` (`:342–346`). So the sugar buys one fewer map literal at the price of the one place in the resources grammar where a positional argument changes meaning.

The corpus never reaches for it: all 3 app/testbed registrations use the 3-slot form with `:inputs` (`examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/scope.cljs:106,135`; `testbeds/tenant_switcher/core.cljs:96`). The sugar's only occurrences are 2 test lines, one ns-docstring snippet, one spec snippet, one docs/api signature line and one historical EP snippet.

A second, related teaching fault: the same `{:from-db …}` reference is repeated at use sites that already inherit it from the registration. `realworld_resources/routing.cljs:97` repeats `resources.cljs:283` on the feed route entry; `examples/capabilities/resources/linearlite/core.cljs:163` (`board-query`) repeats the `:rf.scope/global` claim at `:133` on the sub query; Spec 016's own worked example (`:1744–1790`) writes `{:from-db :realworld/session}` three times (registration `:1756`, route entry `:1770`, subscription `:1778`) and calls that "the one scope-resolution currency" (`:1789`). The runtime already inherits: a route entry with no `:scope` returns nil from `resolve-entry-scope` (`route.cljc:507`) and `resolve-scope-for-event` tier 3a resolves the spec's `{:from-db …}` against db (`registry.cljc:846–849`); the sub side resolves the spec policy per `016:115`, and `resources.cljs:263` states "no view ever passes a `:scope` payload". The other 7 route plans and every other sub in `examples/` omit `:scope` and inherit.

Folded drift: `spec/Ownership.md:64` still names the grammar `{:inputs … :resolve …}` — the pre-rf2-td8oe 2-slot shape the runtime rejects (`:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec`, `scope_registry.cljc:300–310`).

## Evidence (HEAD `6445d0611b`)

- 2-arity / whole-db sugar sites (`git grep -n -A1 -E "reg-resource-scope +:[A-Za-z0-9./-]+\s*$" … | grep -B1 "(fn \[db"`): `scope_registry.cljc:57–58` (docstring), `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_scope_registry_cljs_test.cljc:189,282`, `spec/016-Resources.md:197–198`, `docs/EP/EP-0016-resource-mutation-completion.md:641` (historical record). Facade docstrings and arglists advertise it: `core.cljc:316–325` (fn alias), `core.cljc:558–575` (`defreg-macro`, `:arglists '([scope-id metadata resolve-fn] [scope-id resolve-fn])` at `:575`), `core_resources.cljc:164–186` (`:arglists` `:182`, the 2-arity delegate `:184`). `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:224–225,230`.
- `:whole-db?` exact-keyword consumers (`git grep -n -E ":whole-db\?"`): `scope_registry.cljc` ×11 (stored spec `:340,:345`; trace `:568`; egress `:473–510`; meta `:414`); `resources/tooling.cljc` ×1; `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc` ×5, `panels/resources.cljs` ×2; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs` ×1, `descriptors_data.cljs` ×1, `tool-descriptors.edn` ×1, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` ×1; `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs` ×2, `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md` ×2; tests: `resources_scope_registry_cljs_test.cljc` ×7, `resources_from_db_scope_cljs_test.cljc` ×2, `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_resource_scope_test.clj` ×1, pair-mcp `handler_meta_test.cljs` ×3, xray `resources_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` ×8, `resources_cljs_test.cljs` ×2, `skills/re-frame2-pair/tests/runtime/registrar_describe_test.clj` ×1; `spec/016-Resources.md:203`; `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:287,291`.
- Redundant use-site repeats: `realworld_resources/routing.cljs:97` ↔ `resources.cljs:283`; `linearlite/core.cljs:163` ↔ `:133` (`:157` `board-key` is a mutation `:optimistic` / `:patches` map-form target — only drop its `:scope` if 016 §Map-form exact resource targets (`:994`) inherits the registration policy; verify, else leave).

## Target API

```clojure
;; ONE arity. :inputs is REQUIRED. The callback's first arg is ALWAYS the inputs map.
(rf/reg-resource-scope :realworld/session
  {:inputs {:username [:db [:auth :user :username]]}}
  (fn [{:keys [username]} _ctx] (when username [:rf.scope/session {:username username}])))

;; whole-db, spelled as what it is
(rf/reg-resource-scope :app/everything
  {:inputs {:db [:db []]}}
  (fn [{:keys [db]} _ctx] …))
```

- `reg-resource-scope [scope-id metadata resolve-fn]` only. Metadata MUST be a map carrying `:inputs` (a map). A missing `:inputs`, a non-map metadata, or the old 2-arity spelling (which lands the fn in the metadata slot) all raise the existing `:rf.error/invalid-resource-scope-spec` with a message that names the whole-db spelling `{:inputs {:db [:db []]}}`.
- `:whole-db?` STAYS on the stored spec, on `scope-resolver-meta`, in the `:rf.resource/scope-resolved` trace and the egress projection — but DERIVED, never authored: true iff some declared input descriptor is the root path `[:db []]`. Every tool consumer above is unchanged (codex: "derive whole-db tooling information from the declaration instead of maintaining a second authored mode"). Do NOT add an unpacking flag to recreate the old callback convention.
- Teaching rule (codex + fable, adopted): registration-level `:scope` is the DEFAULT; a use-site `:scope` (route entry, sub query, event payload) is an OVERRIDE for the admin-reads-tenant-X case — never a required repetition. Delete the repeats that equal the registration; keep explicit overrides as worked examples where they differ.

## Corroboration (two-reviewer)

Codex: "For named scope resolvers, retain one callback contract: the first argument is always the declared inputs map. Require `:inputs` and remove the whole-db sugar, including the doc-only metadata variant … The whole-db case remains possible and honest about what it reads. Do not add an unpacking flag." And: "Teach registration-level scope as the default and use-site scope as an override. Remove needless repeated declarations in examples when they equal the registration." Grok Thoughts: "C. Do it." `fable/README.md` lists "one `reg-resource-scope` contract" under two-reviewer findings. rf2-td8oe (closed 2026-09-02, PR #8989) already moved the skill snippet to the 3-slot form; this bead removes the exception the skill still describes in prose.

## Deletion list

- The 2-arity of `reg-resource-scope` (`scope_registry.cljc:381`); the whole-db branch of `canonical-spec` and its wrapper (`:342–346`); the ns-docstring section "Whole-db function sugar — the ONE documented explicit alternative" (`:55–71`); the sugar clause in the fn?-check message (`:317–320`).
- Facade: the 2-arity delegate and arglist in `core_resources.cljc:182–184`; `:arglists` and the sugar sentence in `core.cljc:558–575`; the fn-alias docstring `core.cljc:316–325`.
- Authored `:whole-db?` (replaced by the derived value; the key itself survives).
- `spec/016-Resources.md` §Whole-db function sugar (`:192–203`); `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:225,230`; the redundant use-site `:scope` at `routing.cljs:97` and `linearlite/core.cljs:163`.

description:

## Problem

The facade docstring justifies it as protection against a hand-`mapv` "one missed call away from leaking" (`core.cljc:2497-2506`) — a docstring guarding nobody.
- `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:redact-fn f}})` — a fourth, function-shaped projection door: `re-frame.epoch.assembly/apply-redact-fn` (`assembly.cljc:94-122`), invoked only at `tool_pair.cljc:2072`, its state in `epoch/state.cljc:40-43, :60, :78-88, :119-124`, its own warning category `:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception` (`capture.cljc:74-79`; `spec/API.md:674`; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2132`). Installers outside tests: **0** (all `tools/` and `docs/` hits are prose; `skills/…/privacy-and-elision.md:258` already lists "an epoch-history `:redact-fn` storage hook" under "not part of the API"). It is `comp` wearing a `configure!` key: a forwarder that wants an extra scrub writes `(-> r (rf/projected-record opts) scrub)`.

## Evidence

Counts at tip (`git grep -c`, re-measure): `projected-history` — 17 files non-test, of which code: `core.cljc` 3, `core_epoch.cljc` 3, `late_bind/directory.cljc` 1, `epoch.cljc` 5, `epoch/state.cljc` 1, `tool_pair.cljc` 5, `epoch_egress.cljs` 1 (docstring); test files 9. `apply-redact-fn` — `assembly.cljc:12, :94`, `capture.cljc:75`, `tool_pair.cljc:2072`, `implementation/scripts/check-elision.cjs:314-320`, `epoch_jvm_prod_gate_test.clj:358, :382`. `epoch-redact-fn-exception` — 15 files (6 test/probe). `:redact-fn` code sites: `epoch.cljc:84-109, :242, :721`, `assembly.cljc:12, :94-122, :222, :335-337`, `state.cljc` (above), `tool_pair.cljc:1405, :1924, :1966, :2024, :2072`, `core_epoch.cljc:246-249`, `late_bind/directory.cljc:861`, `test_support.cljc:445`, `privacy.cljc:231`. (The `redact-fn` locals in `cofx.cljc:611-627`, `spec.cljc:248-277` and `resources/classification.cljc:629-640` are the schema validation-tag redactor — a different hook, NOT in scope.)

## Target API

```clojure
;; whole ring — before                      ;; after (ordinary composition)
(rf/projected-history f opts)                (mapv #(rf/projected-record % opts) (rf/epoch-history f))

;; post-hoc scrub — before
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:redact-fn scrub}})   ; global, runs inside projected-record, own warning category
;; after — at the forwarder / sink
(-> r (rf/projected-record opts) scrub)
```

`:epoch-history` keeps `:depth` and `:trace-events-keep`; an `:redact-fn` key is UNKNOWN (per the `configure!` unknown-key posture the boot/adapter area is ruling on; until then it is silently dropped like any other unknown sub-key — say so in the PR). `projected-record` (the record-level door) is UNCHANGED by this bead; its epoch-side fate belongs to `@trace-epoch.n` and egress.5.

## Corroboration

`projected-history`: two-reviewer — codex `trace-and-epoch-inspection.md` §Compose selection with projection ("a `mapv` over the full history, so it can leave the supported public surface in favor of ordinary composition") and `fable-reread-2.md` ("retire the whole-history convenience from the supported surface"). `:redact-fn`: one-reviewer with codex's qualified support — "defensible given the measured absence of application installers, but ordinary composition is not automatically equivalent to a globally installed post-projection transform. Its current throwing behavior falls back to built-in output. If removed, explicitly update each affected egress boundary and document that policy; do not change raw replay storage." The affected boundary is exactly one (`tool_pair.cljc:2072`); raw storage is untouched by construction.

title: api(egress): one policy vocabulary — closed walker opts, `projected-record` reads `:rf.size/*`, fix teaching
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from egress.md (ref egress.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

On a privacy surface a RECOGNISED policy key can vanish without a signal, in both directions:

1. `rf/elide-wire-value` does not read `:rf.egress/profile` — the key does not occur in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc` (0 hits at tip); only `re-frame.projection/resolve-elision-opts` (`projection.cljc:190-221`) resolves it. Yet three normative teaching sites pass a profile to the walker, where it is silently dropped: `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:223-227` (the walker example carries `:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool`), `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md:189-191` (same example), and `spec/Conventions.md:825` (`(rf/elide-wire-value v {:include-sensitive? false})` — a BARE key the walker does not read either; harmless only because `false` is the default).
2. `rf/projected-record` reads the bare spelling ONLY: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1303-1320` (`egress-opts` destructures `{:keys [include-sensitive? include-large?]}` and re-spells them to `:rf.size/*` at :1319-1320). A caller passing `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true` — the spelling the walker, `project-egress`, `:rf/project-egress-opts`, Conventions §`:rf.size/*` and ~54 sites use — is silently dropped there. Pair-MCP's eval builder chose the bare spelling for exactly that reason (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs:146-149`: `"{:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool :include-sensitive? true}"`).

Census at tip, non-test `implementation/*/src` + `tools/*/src` (`git grep -o`, re-measure): `:rf.egress/profile` 55, `:rf.size/include-sensitive?` 54, bare `include-sensitive?` 46, bare `include-large?` 26, `:rf.size/include-large?` 24, `:rf.size/include-digests?` 18. The MCP wire key `include-sensitive` (no `?`) is a fourth spelling on a different layer with a written reason (`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive.cljc:17-27`) and is NOT in scope.

## Evidence

```clojure

;;    accepted: :frame :path :query-v :as-of-epoch
;;              :rf.size/include-sensitive? :rf.size/include-large?
;;              :rf.size/include-digests?   :rf.size/threshold-bytes
(rf/elide-wire-value v {:frame f :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})
;; => throws {:rf.error/id :rf.error/bad-egress-opts
;;            :recovery    :pass-the-profile-to-project-egress
;;            :extra       {:unknown-keys [:rf.egress/profile] :accepted [...]}}

;; 2. projected-record — one spelling for the two shared axes; opts CLOSED
;;    accepted: :rf.egress/profile
;;              :rf.size/include-sensitive? :rf.size/include-large?
;;              :include-fx-args? :include-runtime-db? :include-event-args?   ; epoch-local knobs, bare (API.md:919-922 discriminator)
(rf/projected-record r {:rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool :rf.size/include-sensitive? true})
(rf/projected-record r {:include-sensitive? true})   ; => throws :rf.error/bad-egress-opts

;; 3. project-egress — opts CLOSED (Spec-Schemas :rf/project-egress-opts {:closed true});
;;    an unknown key reaches the walker after resolve-elision-opts and throws there.
```

The three epoch-only axes stay bare pending egress.5 (which decides the `:rf.egress/include-*?` namespace question); do not rename `:rf.size/*` here (Grok: separable 50+ site churn).

title: api(egress): explicit `:frame nil` fails closed (walker + `project-egress`); delete the 3 dead-frame sentinels
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from egress.md (ref egress.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value` resolves its governing frame with `(or (:frame opts) (rf.frame/resolve-current-frame))` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1128`). An explicit `{:frame nil}` is therefore indistinguishable from "no `:frame` key" and falls through to the AMBIENT frame. For a tool that is projecting the inspected app's value from its own chrome frame (Xray runs in `:rf/xray`), the ambient frame resolves, is live, and has an empty declaration registry, so the value ships RAW under no policy. `re-frame.projection/project-egress` has the same truthiness quirk one layer up (`projection.cljc:570-576`: `(if (and record-frame (not (:frame opts))) (assoc opts :frame record-frame) opts)`), so `{:frame nil}` in opts is overridden by the record's frame and a record carrying `:frame nil` seeds nothing and falls to the ambient scope too.

Three consumers independently mint a fake frame identity to force the walker's unresolvable-frame (fail-closed) arm:

- Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs:34-47` — `(def ^:private no-frame (js/Object.))`, substituted at :92-97 whenever the caller passes `:frame` explicitly as nil. Its docstring records two earlier failed attempts (a keyword sentinel that a live frame could be registered under — rf2-7htk7 third pass).
- Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc:106-187` — `fresh-dead-frame-sentinel`, a per-call `(Object.)`, stamped at :253 (`:frame (if reachable? frame-id (fresh-dead-frame-sentinel))`); the docstring at :169-187 and the §No public exit note at :202 exist only to explain the workaround.
- core `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:248-276` — `dead-frame-sentinel`, stamped at :435 (`(assoc opts :frame (if reachable? frame-id dead-frame-sentinel))`); docstring bullet :52-56.

Three fixes for one leak. The framework should make the request expressible: an explicit nil means "no governing frame" and fails closed.

## Evidence

- `elision.cljc:1128` (frame resolution), :1134 (`live-frame?`), :1144-1145 (the `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true` opt-out walks under `::no-frame`), :1151-1152 (fail-closed arm returning `rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel`).
- `projection.cljc:570-576` (record-frame seeding by truthiness).
- The three sentinel sites above. Xray tests that exercise them: `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render_cljs_test.cljc`, `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/events_cljs_test.cljs`, `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_cljs_test.cljs`, `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/derivation_graph_redaction_cljs_test.cljc`; core: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/elision_test.clj`, `implementation/core/test/re_frame/projection_cljs_test.cljc` (`fails-closed-with-no-frame`), `implementation/derivation-conformance/test/re_frame/derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc` (re-measure — the list is from a grep for `no-frame|dead-frame-sentinel|egress-value`).
- Conformance: `spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-project-egress-fails-closed-no-frame.edn` pins the ABSENT-key case only; the Mode-B runner (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:1128-1139`) forwards `:frame` when `(contains? call :frame)` and otherwise binds `*current-frame*` to nil. There is no fixture for the explicit-nil-under-a-live-ambient-frame case, which is the leak.

## Target API (presence-aware frame ownership; codex's formulation)

Precedence, in both layers: (1) an explicit `:frame` key in opts wins, INCLUDING nil; (2) else a recognised record's own `:frame` slot, INCLUDING an explicitly frameless record (`:frame nil` present); (3) else the carried scope (`rf.frame/resolve-current-frame`), bare values only. An unknown or destroyed explicit frame keeps failing closed (today's `live-frame?` check). The `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true` opt-out arm is unchanged (a caller that waived redaction still gets the identity walk).

```clojure
;; elision.cljc — before
frame-id (or (:frame opts) (rf.frame/resolve-current-frame))
;; after
frame-id (if (contains? opts :frame) (:frame opts) (rf.frame/resolve-current-frame))

;; projection.cljc — before
(if (and record-frame (not (:frame opts))) (assoc opts :frame record-frame) opts)
;; after — seed only when opts carry no :frame key and the input is a recognised record
(cond (contains? opts :frame)                                   opts
      (and (map? r) (recognised-kind? (:kind r)) (contains? r :frame)) (assoc opts :frame (:frame r))
      :else                                                     opts)
```

Seed only from a recognised `:rf.observe/*` record (today any map with a truthy `:frame` key seeds, so a bare app-db value that happens to carry a `:frame` key is projected under that key — fail-closed today, but hidden context). Do NOT recognise records by a loose shape test (codex).

Consumers after the change:

```clojure
;; Xray egress.cljs — the :frame key is forwarded verbatim; no sentinel
(cond-> {...} (contains? opts :frame) (assoc :frame (:frame opts)))
;; Xray local_render.cljc:253 and core derivation/egress.cljc:435
:frame frame-id            ; nil or a dead id both fail closed by contract
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area, but this slice is two-reviewer: codex (`egress-and-redaction.md` §Codex Thoughts) names it "the most actionable defect" and specifies the presence-aware precedence above, adding "an unknown or destroyed explicit owner must not borrow another frame" and "preserve deliberate raw opt-in". Grok's slice (1) is the same fix.

## Deletion list

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs:34-47` `no-frame` + the `(or (:frame opts) no-frame)` substitution at :92-97 + the ns docstring paragraphs that explain it (:27-31, :70-80).
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/local_render.cljc:106-187` `fresh-dead-frame-sentinel`, the `reachable?` probe at :251 (the walker validates liveness itself), the §No public exit note at :202, docstring lines :243-250.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc:248-276` `dead-frame-sentinel`, the `reachable?` branch at :435, docstring bullet :52-56.

## Consumers to migrate

Framework-internal walker callers that pass `{:frame f}` and would now fail closed on a nil `f` instead of borrowing the ambient scope — audit each, and pin the ones whose `f` can be nil: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/classification.cljc:755, :779`; `error_emit.cljc:556` and `event_emit.cljc:140` (always-on substrates; a frameless error record such as the SSR pre-frame `:frame nil` sub-path named at `spec/API.md:587` now redacts its `:event` slot rather than walking it under the ambient frame — the fail-closed posture 009 L2821 already states); `reply.cljc:661`; `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/sub_egress.cljc:125`; `projection.cljc:240, :458`; `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc:1303-1320` (`egress-opts` stamps `:frame (:frame record)` — a frameless epoch record's slots now fail closed). Framework `project-egress` callers: `observability.cljc:184`, `resources/classification.cljc:446, :481`, `ssr/hydrate.cljc:205`, `ssr/payload_policy.cljc:323, :404`, `tool_pair.cljc:1335, :1893`. Tool-side: Story `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:406-416` and `error.cljc:102-126` already guard nil before calling (unchanged); pair preload `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:476, :3102-3108` pass `{:frame frame-id}` (nil now fails closed — safer, no code change); story-mcp `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/egress.cljc:209-211, :332-337` (unchanged). Counts are for the worker to re-measure: `git grep -n -E "elide-wire-value|project-egress" -- implementation/*/src tools/*/src skills` with `:!*test*`.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- Spec (hot-zone, one-toucher): `spec/API.md:685` (walker row — the `:frame` opt sentence) and `:697` (`project-egress` row — "when `opts` omit `:frame`, the record's own top-level `:frame` is seeded" → presence rule); `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:3662-3688` (`:rf/project-egress-opts` — the bullet "a kindless / frameless input (or a `:frame nil` record) seeds nothing" becomes "an explicit `:frame nil`, in opts or on a recognised record, means no frame and fails closed"); `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2821` (Carried-frame paragraph: add the explicit-nil sentence).

- Docs: `docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:304` ("Omit the frame and the projection fails closed" — add "or pass `:frame nil`").

title: api(boot): init! throws :rf.error/adapter-already-installed when a different adapter is already seated
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from boot.md (ref boot.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`rf/init!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2660-2697`) seats an adapter only when none is seated — line 2682: `(when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter) (rf.substrate.adapter/install-adapter! adapter-map))`. A second `init!` with a DIFFERENT adapter — `(rf/init! reagent/adapter)` then `(rf/init! uix/adapter)` — returns `nil`, leaves the first adapter seated and emits nothing. That is the shape `spec/Conventions.md:1149-1160` §No silent swallow forbids: a recognised input the runtime cannot honour MUST signal. The owning-namespace `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` (`substrate/adapter.cljc:124-175`) already throws `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` on any second call; the facade's front door hides it.

## Evidence (tip 3fbd3a9ede)

- `core.cljc:2682` — the `when-not (current-adapter)` guard; no identity or kind check.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/boot_test.clj:74-97` `init-is-idempotent` asserts the SAME map twice (`identical?` on `current-adapter-spec`); `:99-125` `install-adapter-rejects-double-install` covers the owning fn only; `:423` covers `destroy-adapter!` → `init!` with a different adapter. No test covers `init!` → `init!` with a different adapter.
- `substrate/adapter.cljc:728` `same-adapter?` — the discriminator already exists and is public: two maps carrying the same canonical `:rf.adapter/*` `:kind` are the same adapter even across a copy / `assoc` / re-evaluation (stable token, rf2-dkl5z1); otherwise object identity, so two custom adapters are never conflated; nil-safe. Used by `route-hook!` and by test-react's mount guard (`adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:457`).
- Hot reload decides the discriminator. Every adapter Var is a plain `def` (`adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:185`, `reagent_slim.cljs:108`, `uix.cljs:228`, `hicasso/substrate.cljs:137`, `core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc:145`, `ssr/substrate.cljc:68`), so a reload re-evaluates the map with fresh fn identities — and 30 of the 40 files under `examples/` + `tools/template` that call `(rf/init! …)` call it from a `^:dev/after-load` fn. An `identical?` / `=` rule would throw on every reload; `same-adapter?` does not.

## Target API

```clojure
;; before — core.cljc:2682
(when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter)
  (rf.substrate.adapter/install-adapter! adapter-map))

;; after — one line; the throw stays in the owner and is never duplicated in the facade
(when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/same-adapter? adapter-map
                                               (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter-spec))
  (rf.substrate.adapter/install-adapter! adapter-map))
```

Semantics: nothing seated → install. Seated and `same-adapter?` (same canonical kind, or the identical custom map) → idempotent no-op exactly as today. Seated and different → `install-adapter!` throws `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` (`:where 'rf/init!`, `:extra {:installed <seated> :attempted <arg>}`, `:recovery :no-recovery`) and the seated adapter is untouched. Update the reason string at `adapter.cljc:155` so it also names this path ("a second `init!` / `install-adapter!` with a different adapter and no intervening `(rf/destroy-adapter!)` …"). The three registrar re-seeds (`:2687-2696`) run as before. `init!`'s docstring (`:2661`) gains the rule and the hot-reload sentence from Risks.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area (fable boot doc), but codex's cross-check independently endorses this slice: "really does ignore a different adapter map once one is installed. Correcting that is worthwhile independently of name pruning. Define idempotence against the installed adapter specification — not merely `:kind` … decide explicitly what hot reload means … Keep the actual seating, generation and rollback logic in the existing adapter owner; do not duplicate it in the facade." `same-adapter?` is that definition (canonical-kind token, identity fallback), hot reload of a canonical adapter is the same-adapter no-op, and the throw stays in `adapter.cljc`.

## Deletion list

None.

## Consumers to migrate

None change. All 34 example boots, both template scaffolds (`tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:38`, `_uix/core.cljs:40`) and the ssr-ring host call `init!` with one canonical adapter per process; the after-load re-calls are same-adapter no-ops. `skills/reagent-migration/tests/fixture/test/reagent_migration/mig23_cold_start_test.cljs:78-100` re-inits a different adapter only after `destroy-adapter!` — unaffected.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` (HOT-ZONE): §Adapter selection at boot `:2066` — state the `init!` rule beside the `install-adapter!` sentence; `:2242` "Re-installing after frames exist is an error" — add "or `init!` with a different adapter".
- `spec/API.md` (HOT-ZONE): `:866` `init!` row — "idempotent boot" → "idempotent for the seated adapter (same canonical `:kind`, or the identical custom map); a different adapter raises `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` — `destroy-adapter!` first to swap".
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (HOT-ZONE): `:2250` `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` row — add the `init!` path; while there, fix its stale `dispose-adapter!` (the public verb is `destroy-adapter!`, `Conventions.md:1390`).
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:748-764` `init!` entry (hand-written page, not generated).
- `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md:224` scenario — add the `init!`-with-a-different-adapter variant (optional, not hot-zone).
- Tests — `boot_test.clj`, new `init-rejects-a-different-adapter` beside `init-is-idempotent`: (1) `init!` plain-atom, then `init!` a distinct map with a different kind (e.g. `(assoc rf.substrate.plain-atom/adapter :kind ::other)`) → throws with `:rf.error/id :rf.error/adapter-already-installed`, `:installed` identical to the seated map, seated identity unchanged after the throw; (2) hot-reload CONTROL: a structural copy of the seated canonical map (`(assoc rf.substrate.plain-atom/adapter :doc "reloaded")`) → no throw, seated identity unchanged; (3) two distinct kind-less custom maps → throws (identity fallback). `same-adapter?` is `.cljc` and already exercised on CLJS by `react_shared_suite`; a CLJS mirror is optional.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: no row change; run the drift check anyway (`cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check`).
- Migration README: no v1-era name changes. Conformance corpus / mcp-conformance: not affected (no boot fixtures).

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches `API.md`, `006`, `009` → serialise with @boot.2 (`API.md`, `009`), @boot.3 (all three) and any open bead on those files. @boot.4's implementation bead 1 (delete facade `install-adapter!`) is BLOCKED BY this bead: the facade must throw on a different adapter before the throwing door is removed. Related: rf2-uimu (lifecycle-verb roster has no `install-*`) — unaffected here.

## Risks

Low. The only behaviour change a production app can meet converts a silent misconfiguration into the error the runtime already owns. One honest cost: a CUSTOM adapter whose `:kind` is not under `:rf.adapter/*` (or has none) falls to the identity comparison, so re-evaluating its Var on hot reload and re-calling `init!` throws — the remedy is `defonce` on the custom adapter Var, or `destroy-adapter!` in the after-load fn; write that sentence into 006 §Adapter selection at boot and the `init!` docstring. Every shipped adapter carries a canonical kind and is unaffected.

Local dossier: ai/findings/API-review/fable/boot-adapter-and-features.md (local-only pointer)

- `cd implementation/core && clojure -M:test -n re-frame.boot-test` green with the new `init-rejects-a-different-adapter`: different-adapter arm throws the right id with `:installed` / `:attempted`; structural-copy arm is a no-op; seated identity unchanged in both; `init-is-idempotent` passes unchanged.
- Control discipline: with `core.cljc:2682` temporarily reverted to the `current-adapter` guard, the new test FAILS (state the run in the PR body).
- `git grep -n "when-not (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter)" implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` returns nothing.
- `npm run test:cljs` from `implementation/` green (react_shared_suite, hicasso and uix boots exercise re-init).
- 006 `:2066`/`:2242`, API.md `:866`, 009 `:2250` and `docs/api/re-frame.core.md` updated; `mkdocs build --strict` and `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` green; api-manifest `--check` green.

title: api(egress+epoch) 3/4: stamp :kind :rf/epoch-record; projector behind project-egress; retire projected-record
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 18:27:26 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.9 ruling (option A, delegated by Mike; ruled by the dossier agent). **Ruling needed: NONE.** Stage 3 of 4 of the one-`project-egress`-door ruling. Parent epic rf2-kuky. Line numbers measured at tip `2b6e8a44cf` (2026-09-06 18:1x AUSEST); re-measure at dispatch. The full dossier and the ruling note are on rf2-kuky.9's notes._

**Filed ONCE; coordinated with rf2-kuky.55's epoch-door bead rf2-kuky.82.** This bead owns `projected-record`'s retirement (facade row, home fn, late-bind hook, core manifest row, docs). rf2-kuky.82 (blocked on rf2-kuky.20) owns the SEVEN duplicate `re-frame.epoch` manifest rows — the epoch `projected-record` row (`spec/api-manifest.edn:194` / `api-manifest-metadata.edn:2027`) among them — and re-tiers the five home-only doors. This bead is BLOCKED BY .82 so the two never edit `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`, `epoch.cljc` and the two `docs/api` pages in flight together; .82's "consumer-facing spellings afterwards" list names `(rf/projected-record r opts)` — this bead supersedes that one line, and .82's worker need not act on it. If .82 has landed, the epoch row is already gone and you delete only what remains.

## Problem

Two record doors dispatch on DIFFERENT discriminators. `rf/project-egress` dispatches on `:kind` (`:rf.observe/*`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:482-497`); `rf/projected-record` (`core.cljc:2550` → `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc:192-254` `defwrapper`, `:on-absent :nil` → late-bind `:epoch/projected-record` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:846-849`; published at `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:808` inside the `late-bind/set-fns!` map at `:748`) → `epoch.cljc:701-731` → `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc` (opts re-spelling `:1316-1319`, the projector body after `:2025`)) dispatches on the epoch record's SLOT SET (`:db-*`, `:frame-state-*`, `:trigger-event`, `:trace-events`, `:sub-runs`, `:effects`). `re-frame.epoch.assembly` stamps NO `:kind` (0 hits; `build-record` at `assembly.cljc:262`, the map literal at `:341`) and `EpochRecord` (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4427-4440`) carries `:epoch-id` and `:frame` only. That is exactly why the public door is UNSAFE to hand an epoch record today: `project-egress` would seed `:frame` from the record and walk the whole map from `:path []`, so app-db declarations keyed `[:auth :token]` never match `[:db-after :auth :token]` — the slot ships RAW (reasoned from `elision.cljc:1062-1066` and `projection.cljc:482-497`; not executed). Nothing but the reader's knowledge prevents that call. The epoch door's only non-test caller anywhere in `tools/` is pair-MCP's epoch export, which had to invent the BARE `:include-sensitive?` spelling to use it (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs:146-149`, spliced into the rendered strings at `:193` and `:245`). The spec's own sentence — `project-egress` "names the boundary, not a record kind" (`projection.cljc:24-27`, `spec/API.md:692`) — says epoch slot knowledge belongs BEHIND the door as dispatch data. Codex's objection that "feeding today's record to `project-egress` is not equivalent" is correct, and it is an argument for stamping a discriminator first, not for a second door.

## Target

One door. An epoch record carries a STAMPED discriminator; the door dispatches it to the EXISTING `tool_pair/projected-record` body registered as a late-bound per-kind projector (the pattern `elision.cljc:1121-1127` already uses for `:routing/route-sub-egress-path`); `rf/projected-record` retires. Codex's two guards are RULED: recognition is by the stamped `:kind`, never a loose `:epoch-id` shape test; a recognised kind whose projector is absent THROWS, never falls back to a bare walk. All of `projected-record`'s slot knowledge is preserved, in one private projector.

## Changes

1. `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:262-341`: stamp `:kind :rf/epoch-record` on the assembled record. HOT-ZONE `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4427-4440`: `EpochRecord` gains the `:kind` slot (fixed value `:rf/epoch-record`). Raw replay STORAGE is otherwise unchanged — change what is stamped, not what is stored (codex: "do not change raw replay storage"). Check every equality pin on assembled records in `implementation/epoch/test/**` (a `(= expected record)` pin now needs the slot).
2. `late_bind/directory.cljc:846-849`: replace the `:epoch/projected-record` entry with `:epoch/project-record` (the per-kind projector; `late_bind_drift_test.clj` pins the roster against the in-tree `set-fns!` publications — both move together); `epoch.cljc:808` publishes `tool_pair/projected-record` under it; `projection.cljc:482-497` dispatches `:kind :rf/epoch-record` through `late-bind/require-fn!` (`late_bind.cljc:226`, which already throws the canonical `:rf.error/<artefact>-artefact-missing` shape). ABSENT ⇒ throw `:rf.error/epoch-artefact-missing` naming the kind — NEVER the kindless walk.
3. **Policy axes preserved** (codex, RULED). The epoch projector resolves the profile ONCE, overlays only the keys the caller actually supplied, and hands each internal helper only its applicable keys. The epoch-only axes (`include-fx-args?`, `include-runtime-db?`, `include-event-args?` — `tool_pair.cljc` around `:1358, :1957, :2015`) stay independent of sensitive/large; pair-MCP's `off-box-tool` + sensitive override is a deliberate combination (NOT `local-raw`: large, runtime, effect and event payloads stay independently controlled) and must keep meaning what it means. NEVER forward the whole opts map into the closed walker map (.6 closes it; an epoch-only key reaching the walker would throw `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts` on a path that used to work). Until stage 4 the overlay spelling is `:rf.size/include-sensitive?` etc. (as .6 makes `projected-record` read) — stage 4 renames; do not pre-empt it here. `:path`, routing's `:query-v` reseed and the epoch handle context (`:as-of-epoch`) pass through as today.

title: api(boot) 3/4: add rf/current-config, the read twin of configure!; strike describe-config from Conventions
description:

Slice 3 of 4; parent epic rf2-kuky. Evidence: rf2-kuky.4's description and its DOSSIER ATTACHMENT notes. rf2-kuky.55's item C1 is conditional on this bead._

## Problem

`rf/configure!` (`core.cljc:2554`) is the one process-config write door. `spec/Conventions.md:1283-1293` promises its read twin "on every facade" (`describe-config` / `current-config`) and the facade ships neither. The one tool that reads a knob back — the pair preload, `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:3858` — does `(resolve 're-frame.epoch/current-config)` by symbol: the epoch reader itself is public (codex is right that "private-API access" overstates it), but it lives in an OPTIONAL artefact, and there is no facade door that handles optional availability. rf2-kuky.55 item C1 (delete `re-frame.epoch/current-config` and `re-frame.elision/current-config`, migrate ~10 consumer files to the facade) is conditional on this var — net −2 public vars on the back of this +1. This is the one item of the ruling that ADDS surface, and its demand is the named consumer above plus C1.

## Target

```clojure
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 100}})
(rf/current-config)   ; → {:epoch-history {…} :trace-buffer {…} :elision {…}}
                      ;   the write map's own nested shape; PROCESS values only; a subsystem key is ABSENT
                      ;   when its artefact / tooling sibling is not loaded — never fabricated
(get-in (rf/current-config) [:epoch-history :depth])   ; absent artefact → nil, same as the symbol-resolve today
```

Modest by design (codex): no per-frame effective values; no transactional snapshot; no promise of wire-serialisable output (epoch config can carry `:redact-fn`); namespaced pass-through keys are NOT reflected back. `describe-config` is STRUCK from Conventions — no consumer, no implementation, no proposal, and a second unfulfilled promise is worse than none.

## Code

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc` — `current-config` beside `configure!` (`:2554`), tier `:advanced`, arity 0.
- `:epoch-history` via a NEW `:epoch/current-config` late-bind hook: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:851` has `:epoch/configure!` but no reader; the reader already exists at `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:114-118` over `epoch/state.cljc:154-160` — bind it. Do NOT delete the epoch/elision owning-ns readers here; that is rf2-kuky.55 C1's bead.
- `:trace-buffer` — a reader over the PRIVATE `process-events-retained` atom at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:140` (the process default, NOT a frame ring); publish it through a hook (`:trace.tooling/current-trace-buffer-config`) or the same path `configure!` uses to reach `configure-trace-buffer!` — match the existing wiring rather than inventing a second one.
- `:elision` from `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:73` `current-config`.
- Consumer: pair preload `runtime.cljs:3858` → `(get-in (rf/current-config) [:epoch-history :depth])`; `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md:214` prose.

## Tests

- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/configure_test.clj` — write-then-read round trip per key; an absent-artefact arm proving the key is ABSENT, not fabricated (a JVM run without `re-frame.epoch` on the classpath, or the CLJS bundle-isolation counter that already pins the epoch artefact absent — `TESTING.md` names it); a namespaced carve-out key written through `configure!` is not reflected back.
