title: api(boot) 2/4: delete feature-loaded? and require-feature!; (rf/features) is the one inventory
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 17:24:31 AUSEST by the rf2-kuky.4 ruling (option A — full prune, item (e); delegated by Mike, ruled by the dossier agent). Slice 2 of 4; parent epic rf2-kuky. Evidence: rf2-kuky.4's description and its DOSSIER ATTACHMENT notes._

## Problem

`rf/feature-loaded?` (`core.cljc:2860` → `features.cljc:113`) and `rf/require-feature!` (`core.cljc:2869` → `features.cljc:160`) have zero non-test code consumers after 34 example boots, four tools, two scaffolds and a Ring host — only skill prose (`skills/re-frame2/patterns/resources.md:17`, `resources-mutations.md:7`) and the cheatsheet (`:191-192`). `feature-loaded?` is `(some? (late-bind/get-fn probe-key))` ≡ `(get-in (rf/features) [k :loaded?])`; `require-feature!` throws the same Maven coordinate every late-bound facade fn already throws on first call (`late_bind.cljc:228`, `API.md:891`). `features` is the one inventory and STAYS (data before magic).

## Target

```clojure
(rf/features)                              ; → {:epoch {:maven … :require … :spec … :loaded? true} …} — shape unchanged
(get-in (rf/features) [:epoch :loaded?])   ; the boolean. An UNKNOWN key reads nil here where feature-loaded? read
                                           ; false — teach the lookup; do not claim identical return contracts.

;; The early production guard, for an app that wants boot-time failure rather than first-call failure.
;; One line, no framework verb, NOT an assert (asserts are elidable):
(when-not (get-in (rf/features) [:epoch :loaded?])
  (throw (ex-info "re-frame.epoch is not on the classpath" (get (rf/features) :epoch))))
```

Codex's caution is honoured, not waved away: `require-feature!` gave an EARLY, structured preflight error that first-operation failure does not replace. The replacement is the explicit check above, taught in the skill examples and in `spec/API.md` §Feature inspection, and it carries the same coordinate data because the inventory entry is the throw's data.

## Code

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2855-2875` — the two defs. (The seven-vs-eight features docstring drift on the `features` entry is rf2-kuky.3's — coordinate; whichever lands second rebases.)

title: api(machines): delete the :system-id family and the phantom :child-machine; the address is the id (kuky.15 A)
description:
_Filed 2026-09-06 from the rf2-kuky.15 ruling (option A, delegated by Mike, ruled by the dossier agent); parent epic rf2-kuky. Line numbers measured at tip `13884f326f` (= origin/main, 2026-09-06 17:18 AUSEST) unless marked "dossier tip" (`6d513ba07f`, single-digit drift). Grep by NAME before editing — lines drift._

## Problem

A spawned actor is an event handler whose id is its address (005 §Spawning). Every real parent and child in the tree holds that id (`:rf/spawned` on the parent, `:rf/self-id` / `:rf/parent-id` on the child) and sends with the one verb `[:dispatch [id ev]]` — `examples/patterns/websocket/connection.cljs:99-108`, `messages.cljs:342-344`, `examples/patterns/long_running_work/worker.cljs:56,143`. Beside that, 005 teaches a second addressing mode and heads its example "the common case" (005:2708): a per-frame reverse index `[:rf.runtime/machines :system-ids <name>] → <actor-id>` written at spawn (`spawn.cljc` ~:574), released on every teardown path (D8, 005:3205), read by `re-frame.machines/machine-by-system-id` and sent to by `[:rf.machine/dispatch-to-system [sid ev]]`, with two traces, one error, a conformance axis and a runtime-db slot. Consumers in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/*/src`: **0**, through two independent counts eight weeks apart (July wave 2, September wave 3); the only hits are machines-viz's closed spawn-key vocabulary and Xray's diff-panel row for the SLOT. `dispatch-to-system-fx` is a silent no-op on an unbound name (`machines.cljc` ~:282; `docs/machines/actors.md:217` teaches that as a feature) — Principles §No silent swallow, verbatim. And the one behaviour that distinguishes `:system-id` from `:fixed-actor-id` — a collision REBINDS the name to the new actor while the old one lives on unnamed (005:2905) — is not XState's: `system._set` THROWS on a duplicate systemId (verified on `main`, 2026-09-06). So the rebind is a divergence kept in parity's name.

`:child-machine` is a spec key with no implementation (API.md:952; 005:4595-4602, :4637) whose own reconsideration trigger — repeated hand-rolled entry/exit spawn boilerplate — has never fired: the tree has 0 hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn]` sites, and the sugar it describes already shipped as `:spawn` (005:4049).

**Ruling A (rf2-kuky.15): delete both.** The address is the id; `:fixed-actor-id` is the one stable-name mechanism. No shim, no deprecation, no park, no "retired key" diagnostic.

## Target — replacement teaching (write it; do not only delete)

1. **Flip 005:2708.** Declarative `:spawn` leads (it IS the common case: 4 declarative sites vs 0 hand-emitted); the hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn]` fx is presented as the desugar target and the only non-state-bound lifetime. The example loses `:system-id`; the :2719 `dispatch-to-system` sentence goes.
2. **Write the rebind difference into 005** (§Declarative `:spawn` or the `:fixed-actor-id` row) as plain sentences, so nobody re-adds a registry to "restore parity": *The name is the address. A re-entered `:fixed-actor-id` child is a new incarnation at the SAME address (`spawn.cljc` ~:1184 — attempts reuse the id; `actor-generation` is 1 for them); the join and lifecycle machinery tells incarnations apart via the `:work-generation` stamp (~:313), but an ordinary application dispatch to `:x` reaches whichever incarnation currently owns `:x`. Two children in one `:spawn-all` batch resolving to one literal are rejected (`:rf.error/machine-spawn-all-duplicate-id`, `spawn-all-address-collisions`). XState's actor system throws on a duplicate systemId; re-frame2 has no separate registry — the id is the only name.*
3. **Complete the imperative-spawn recipe** (Codex; verified at tip: only DECLARATIVE spawns carry a reducer-stamped `:rf/spawned-id`, `spawn.cljc:49-62` — a hand-emitted fx with only `:id-prefix` allocates at fx time and delivers nothing back to the author's snapshot): *An action that hand-emits `[:rf.machine/spawn …]` and must keep the child's id chooses a fresh explicit keyword address from an event value or a recorded coeffect, stores it in ordinary `:data`, and passes it as `:fixed-actor-id`. An app that needs a fresh actor while an older one lingers allocates that way and destroys the old one explicitly.* Pin it with ONE unit test (spawn with an explicit `:fixed-actor-id` taken from the event, dispatch to it, destroy it explicitly) — not a new example directory. NO second spawn-result channel.
4. **Do NOT claim frame-wide `:fixed-actor-id` uniqueness.** Codex (source-path analysis, not an executed reproduction): `spawn-all-address-collisions` is a within-batch guard; the ordinary `spawn-fx*` path installs at a supplied fixed address with no general occupied-address rejection. Characterise cross-invocation reuse of an OCCUPIED fixed address with one test that documents current behaviour; if it silently replaces a live actor, file a follow-up bug (`discovered-from` this bead) rather than widening this PR.
5. **Delete the `:child-machine` row, section and bullet outright.** If 005 keeps a dated Disposition list, one line there; no "retired" prose elsewhere.

title: RULING api(epoch): re-frame.epoch's parallel doors, facade projection twins, and the Tool-Pair DCE tier rule
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from trace-epoch.md (ref trace-epoch.5); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The epoch ring and the trace ring are the same kind of thing — a per-frame, dev-only, bounded ring with a read, a clear, a listener and a retention knob — and the code spells them under two grammars. The trace ring is reached through the facade (`rf/trace-buffer`, `rf/clear-trace-buffer!`, `rf/register-listener! :trace`, `(rf/configure! {:trace-buffer …})`) with `re-frame.trace.tooling` as an un-rostered home. The epoch ring is reached through the facade for reads and writes (`rf/epoch-history`, `rf/restore-epoch!`, `rf/replay-epoch!`, `rf/replace-frame-state!`, `rf/projected-record`, `rf/epoch-silence-current?`, `rf/register-listener! :epoch`, `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history …})`) AND through a second, manifest-rostered public namespace `re-frame.epoch` (14 rows, `spec/api-manifest.edn:190-203`) that duplicates the seven and adds five doors of its own: `configure!` (`epoch.cljc:57`), `current-config` (`:114`), `clear-history!` (`:135`), `register-epoch-listener!` / `unregister-epoch-listener!` (`:151`, `:168`), `clear-epoch-listeners!` (`:214`), plus `settle!` (`:293`, tier `implementation`, correctly). Every tool reads the epoch ring through the facade (Xray `spine.cljs`, `epoch.cljs`; Story `artifact.cljc`, `assertions.cljc`, `runtime.cljc`; pair preload `runtime.cljs:1274-1374`; pair-mcp via `rt-call 'epoch-history`); the home-namespace doors have between zero and one tool-code consumer each (measured below). Whether to keep that second grammar is a design call, not a defect.

This bead carries the ruling-dependent remainder after @trace-epoch.1–.4 (fence lift, third-door deletion, dead-var deletion, policy-preserving clear), which are dispatchable regardless of how this is ruled.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b; consumer counts exclude `ai/`)

- **A. `re-frame.epoch/clear-history!`** (`epoch.cljc:135-143`: drops every frame's history AND in-flight capture buffers). Tool-code consumers: 0. 33 files total: `re-frame.test-support` reaches it via the `:epoch/clear-history!` hook (`test_support.cljc:469`), 25 framework/tool test files, `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md:30-41`, `spec/008-Testing.md` (1). Grammar today: trace ring clears as `(clear-trace-buffer! f)` / `(clear-trace-buffer!)` (after @trace-epoch.4); epoch ring clears as `(clear-history!)` — all frames only, fixture-grade.
- **B. `re-frame.epoch/configure!`** (`:57-112`, body `(state/merge-config! opts)`). The documented door is `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history …})` (`Tool-Pair.md:88`, `API.md:895-909`), which reaches `state/merge-config!` via the `:epoch/configure!` hook (`core.cljc:2598`, `directory.cljc:855`). Direct consumers of the home door: 2 sites in one Story test (`tools/story/test/re_frame/story/play/runner_events_cljs_test.cljc:989,1026`); docs `re-frame.epoch.md:227-246`; `implementation/SECURITY.md:188` mention; manifest row `:192`. rf2-f8wu's live-ring prune landed in `state/merge-config!` (`4f5993de17`), so either door carries it.
- **C. `re-frame.epoch/current-config`** (`:114-118`) and `re-frame.elision/current-config` (`elision.cljc:73`): two per-subsystem readers beside the one merged writer; no `rf/current-config` exists. Consumers of the epoch reader: `epoch_test.clj` (15), `epoch_redact_fn_test.clj` (11), `epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc` (2), `epoch_privacy_test.clj` (1), `core/test/.../elision_probe.cljs` (1), pair preload `runtime.cljs` (1 — `(resolve 're-frame.epoch/current-config)` by symbol, because the facade has no read door), `skills/re-frame2-pair/references/ops.md` (1), `tools/mcp-conformance/test/live-re-frame2-pair-*.cjs` (3 eval strings), `docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md:249-260`. Elision reader: `configure_test.clj` (3), `elision_test.clj` (5). The trace ring's retention has NO reader at all. **`rf/current-config` is `@boot.n`'s** (its cross-check: "the one new var three docs want … Own it here"); this item is only what happens to the two per-subsystem readers once it lands.
- **D. `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` / `unregister-epoch-listener!`** as public doors, and the Tool-Pair §"Facade vs home-namespace verb — the DCE tier rule" (`Tool-Pair.md:635-639`): "canonical devtools attach via the per-stream home-namespace verbs … because a tool preload MUST NOT require `re-frame.core` into a production build". Premise false at tip, three ways: the rule's exemplar `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:13` requires `re-frame.core` (used at `:79-80`); its app-side exemplar ("the re-frame2 project template registers its default error sink via `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`") describes nothing — `git grep -i -E 'sink|listener' -- tools/template/resources` → 0 files; and `trace.cljc:49` requires the tooling registry unconditionally on both platforms, so the only DCE lever is the `goog.DEBUG` gate around the call site, which both spellings need equally. What keeps Xray and the pair preload out of production is `:devtools/preloads`, not the verb. Tool-code consumers of the epoch home verb: 1 (`install.cljs:67`); Story chose the facade on purpose (`Tool-Pair.md:639`, `invariants.cljc:395`) for optional-artefact degradation; the pair preload straddles (`runtime.cljs:1272` facade `:epoch`, `:1422` home `:trace`). Manifest rows `:160`, `:180`, `:198`, `:203` cite the rule as their justification. `@observability.n` measured the same premise (its problem item 3) and owns the cross-stream verb collapse; this bead carries the epoch half and the Tool-Pair text only.
- **E. Facade `rf/group-by-event` / `rf/domino-bucket`** (`core.cljc:2319`, `:2345`) re-exporting `re-frame.trace.projection` (`:291`, `:78`). Code consumers via the facade: 0 (docs 1, spec 1); via the projection ns: Xray `self_noise.cljc:152` + 15 tool prose refs, 15 + 19 framework-test sites. Manifest rows `:124`, `:110` justify the facade placement by "the producing home … carries no manifest rows … Conventions forbids inventing one to tidy the column" — while `Conventions.md:762` already names `group-by-event` as "the `re-frame.trace.projection` grouping fn".
- **F.** The seven duplicate `re-frame.epoch` manifest rows for fns the facade re-exports (`epoch-history`, `restore-epoch!`, `replay-epoch!`, `replace-frame-state!`, `projected-record`, `epoch-silence-current?`, plus `projected-history` until @trace-epoch.3).

## Options

**A — epoch clear grammar.** A1 leave `clear-history!` as is (fixture op, hook-reached by test-support, no user-facing consumer). **Status:** Medium–High (tool-tier only — `examples/` has zero consumers — but the spec's canonical spelling `(rf/trace-buffer …)` does not exist on CLJS, the same six trace fns answer to three namespaces, the two rings clear under different grammars, and four shipped vars have zero consumers; wave 3, 2026-09-05 09:17:17 AUSEST, tip 7d7ec09bd7)
**Surfaces:** `rf/trace-buffer` · `rf/clear-trace-buffer!` · `re-frame.trace.tooling/{trace-buffer,clear-trace-buffer!,clear-trace-rings!,configure-trace-buffer!,register-listener!,unregister-listener!,clear-listeners!}` · the six `re-frame.trace/…` aliases · `rf/group-by-event` · `rf/group-by-event-with-events` · `rf/domino-bucket` (and their `re-frame.trace.projection` homes) · `rf/emit-trace-event!` vs `re-frame.trace/emit!` · `rf/sensitive?` · `(rf/configure! {:trace-buffer …} {:epoch-history …})` · the seven `re-frame.core` epoch re-exports vs `re-frame.epoch`'s fourteen exports (`configure!`, `current-config`, `register-epoch-listener!`, `unregister-epoch-listener!`, `clear-epoch-listeners!`, `clear-history!`, `settle!` beside the seven)

Three structural facts make this worse than an ordinary re-export dual:

1. **The trace-ring facade is fenced by platform.** `rf/trace-buffer` and `rf/clear-trace-buffer!` are defined inside `#?(:clj (do …))` (core.cljc:2195) with the docstring "JVM-only alias — CLJS callers use `re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer` directly" (:2213–2215). The spec does not know this: 009 §`trace-buffer` API (009:906–914) tables `(rf/trace-buffer frame-id)` as the API; Tool-Pair §How AI tools attach (Tool-Pair:602) names `(rf/trace-buffer frame-id)` as the surface; `git grep -c 'rf/trace-buffer' -- spec/` → 009:13, Tool-Pair:7, 002:1, Implementor-Checklist:1. Not one is callable from the platform every consumer runs on. The stated reason — production DCE — is not what the code does: core.cljc:52 requires `re-frame.trace` unconditionally; trace.cljc:49 requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally on both platforms and aliases `trace-buffer` there (trace.cljc:955), i.e. an unconditional CLJS alias to the very fn the facade fences. The bundle-isolation gate stays green because Closure removes the unused alias (check-bundle-isolation.cjs:339–352 — whose comment still describes "thin late-bind shells" that rf2-ic1sv, `5b0eb9f9b8`, replaced with static aliases). One more alias in `re-frame.core` is the same shape as the one already in `re-frame.trace`.
2. **`re-frame.trace` is a third door with no consumers.** Its six aliases (trace.cljc:951–957) were "the canonical app-facing names" of rf2-ic1sv pick c; the stream-parameterized facade verb superseded them on 2026-07-08 (rf2-9flalp, `89bb759305`). Non-test code reaching them outside `core.cljc`'s own delegation: zero (two comments — drop_in.cljc:73, install.cljs:27). Tests: 50 files spell `rf.trace/clear-listeners!`.
3. **The manifest rosters one home and not the other.** `re-frame.epoch` carries 14 rows (api-manifest.edn:190–203); `re-frame.trace`, `re-frame.trace.tooling` and `re-frame.trace.projection` carry none (`grep -o ':namespace "[^"]*"' spec/api-manifest.edn | sort | uniq -c`). ## Simpler elegant target

One grammar for two rings; one consumer-facing door; home namespaces are implementation.

```clojure
;; re-frame.core — both platforms, the ONLY consumer-facing spelling
(rf/trace-buffer frame-id)  (rf/trace-buffer frame-id opts)
(rf/clear-trace-buffer!)    (rf/clear-trace-buffer! frame-id)   ; 0-arity = every frame; absorbs clear-trace-rings!
(rf/epoch-history frame-id)
(rf/clear-epoch-history!)   (rf/clear-epoch-history! frame-id)  ; renamed from epoch/clear-history!; same arity grammar
(rf/restore-epoch! f e) (rf/replay-epoch! f e [opts]) (rf/replace-frame-state! f m) (rf/projected-record r [opts]) (rf/epoch-silence-current? tags)
(rf/register-listener! stream id f)  (rf/unregister-listener! stream id)  ; :trace :events :errors :epoch — the one verb
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history … :trace-buffer … :elision …})
(rf/current-config)         ; → the same nested map configure! accepts — the one reader; testing tier
(rf/emit-trace-event! op-type operation tags)

;; homes — reached by the framework's late-bind hooks and re-frame.test-support only
re-frame.trace.tooling        ; ring + listener registry — tier implementation, ^:no-doc publics
re-frame.trace.projection     ; group-by-event, domino-bucket — the only place they live; two `tooling` manifest rows
re-frame.epoch                ; settle!, capture, hook targets — tier implementation; the seven re-exported fns stay as hook targets, ^:no-doc
```

## Why this is better (ethos)

- **Regularity over cleverness** (Principles:18–22 — "there is one obvious way to do a thing"). Today "read the recent past" is spelled by platform, and "clear the ring" by which ring. After: the two rings read as `trace-buffer` / `epoch-history` and clear as `clear-trace-buffer!` / `clear-epoch-history!`, with the same optional frame-id arity, on both platforms.
- **Public query surfaces** (Principles:52–56 — "tooling and agents are first-class clients of these surfaces"). The contract is the spec, and the spec spells `rf/trace-buffer`. A spelling the spec teaches and CLJS refuses is a tax on generated code — the exact AI-first cost the principle exists to remove; rf2-66xy8 is it happening.
- **Facade policy** (Conventions:1199–1220): tooling surfaces default behind a door "unless a deliberate single-import re-export is justified". The justification is already on file for the epoch seven and half on file for the trace ring (JVM). A re-export that exists on one platform is neither front porch nor door; it is a trap. Make the trace-ring re-export whole (its consumers are the same tools that read `rf/epoch-history` through the facade) or remove it — not both by platform.
- **Clojure: namespaces follow dependency shape, not tiers** (Conventions:1211 says exactly this). `re-frame.trace` re-exporting `re-frame.trace.tooling` re-exporting into `re-frame.core` is three names for one var — the "option soup wearing a uniform" the review's bar names. And Clojure's answer to "one frame or all frames" is arity, not a second verb.
- **The demand bar** (Principles:124): `group-by-event-with-events`, `projected-history`, the six `re-frame.trace` aliases and the facade projection re-exports had the whole tool corpus — Xray, Story, two MCP servers, a preload — as their audience and drew zero calls. Pre-alpha deletes.
- **Honest costs.** *(a) Bundle DCE* is the one real reason for a home form. The evidence says it does not bind here: trace.cljc:955 already aliases the ring on CLJS and the `trace-tooling` sentinel stays absent; the epoch re-exports are late-bind shells and the gate pins the artefact absent from the counter bundle (check-bundle-isolation.cjs:205–218). A `:require`-only rule ("a dev preload never requires `re-frame.core`") is not what the exemplars do (install.cljs:13) and not what protects them (`:devtools/preloads`). The proof after lifting the fence is one run of `npm run test:bundle-isolation` — not run here (read-only review). *(b) Optional-artefact absence*: `rf/register-listener! :epoch` degrades to `nil`; the home verb fails at require. Story chose the facade for exactly that reason (Tool-Pair:639) — collapsing to the facade loses nothing and keeps the degradation-friendly form. *(c) The `re-frame.epoch` require as a classpath anchor* (preload.cljs:46–48) stays; requiring a namespace to load its hooks is not calling its vars. *(d) `rf/current-config` is one new var* — offered because the write side is already merged on the facade and three readers exist below it; the minimal alternative is recorded above.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes. The spec's canonical `(rf/trace-buffer f)` does not exist on CLJS, which is the platform every consumer runs on. The same tools read the epoch ring through the facade and the trace ring through a home ns, in the same files. That is an AI-first tax with an open bead (rf2-66xy8) attached. `group-by-event-with-events` and `projected-history` have zero non-test callers; `re-frame.trace`'s six aliases have none outside comments.

**Diagnosis.** Correct on the fence, the third door, and the "same tools, two rings, two namespaces" observation. Two places the target over-unifies, and Codex caught both:

1. `clear-trace-rings!` is not a 0-arity of `clear-trace-buffer!`. It also resets `process-events-retained` to the default and drops the dedup table. Xray's clear/scrub button calls it. A user-facing "clear the rings" that quietly undoes retention policy is a different operation from per-frame data clear (which already preserves `:override?`).
2. `epoch/clear-history!` also drops in-flight capture buffers. Do not invent a per-frame epoch-clear or relabel the full reset as the symmetric twin of `clear-trace-buffer!` just to complete a table. There is no user-facing epoch-clear consumer.

**Options.** Minimal: lift the `#?(:clj` fence so `rf/trace-buffer` / `rf/clear-trace-buffer!` are platform-complete, delete the `re-frame.trace` aliases, delete `group-by-event-with-events` and `projected-history`. Maximal: the doc's full grammar (one listener verb, one `current-config`, epoch clear renamed onto the facade). The minimal set is the finding; the rest is shared with `observability-doors.md` and `boot-adapter-and-features.md`.

**Recommendation.**

- Lift the fence. One documented reader on both platforms. Migrate Xray / pair preload off `rf.trace.tooling/trace-buffer`. Run `npm run test:bundle-isolation` — a require graph is not a DCE measurement.
- Per-frame `clear-trace-buffer!` stays. Add an all-frame *data* clear that preserves retention and override flags. Keep `clear-trace-rings!` (or a test-support reset) as the fixture operation that also resets policy. Point Xray's button at data clear, and keep its extra privacy/cache cleanup.
- Delete facade `group-by-event` / `domino-bucket` / `group-by-event-with-events` (the last is a poorer round-trip than `(trace-buffer f)` which already carries `:trace-events`). Keep `group-by-event` in `re-frame.trace.projection` for Xray's flat-stream case.
- Delete `projected-history`. Pair pages first, then `projected-record`. That deletion is owned here as a consumer fact; the projector itself is `egress-and-redaction.md`'s.
- Collapse listener registration onto `rf/register-listener!` (see observability). The home epoch verb stays a `^:no-doc` hook target. Story's facade choice is the right one for an optional artefact.
- `rf/current-config` is the right read twin of `configure!`, but it is one new var for three docs. Put it in the boot/config bead, not this one.

**Implement.** Fence lift + alias deletion + `projected-history` / `group-by-event-with-events` deletion in one PR (nine tool call sites, large test rename). Policy-preserving all-frame clear as a deliberate behaviour change in the same PR or the next — do not silently reuse `clear-trace-rings!`. Manifest check and bundle-isolation are the gates. No app consumers.

## Codex Thoughts

The missing CLJS spelling taught by the specification is worth correcting; the third trace namespace and unconsumed projection conveniences are also credible cleanup. But the proposed package combines naming repair with new configuration and clearing APIs. Split those decisions. Tool ergonomics improve when documentation names a callable, supported surface; they do not require every tool operation to move into `re-frame.core`.

Two portable outcomes are viable: make `rf/trace-buffer` callable on both platforms, or standardise on the existing `re-frame.trace.tooling` door and retire the JVM convenience aliases. The latter has the smallest consumer migration because actual CLJS tools already use it. Prefer that minimal option unless the project explicitly chooses facade-first tooling. Either way, retire the unused third-door aliases and align the spec, manifest, docs, and generated eval recipes. Existing source reachability is evidence that a portable facade may be safe, **not** a substitute for a fresh advanced-bundle isolation check. The [bundle gate](../../../../implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs) checks particular production artifacts, not every possible custom preload topology.


The clearing proposal contains a substantive non-equivalence. [`clear-trace-buffer!`](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc) preserves retention and per-frame overrides; `clear-trace-rings!` drops every ring, resets the process default, and clears dedup state. [`epoch/clear-history!`](../../../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc) also drops in-flight capture buffers. These are not merely alternate arities of the same data clear. Keep fixture reset internal and separate from consumer clearing. [Xray's `retroactive-scrub!`](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_collector.cljs) currently invokes the fixture-style trace reset from its clear/privacy-narrowing path: that is actionable evidence for a policy-preserving all-frame data clear. Preserve retention configuration deliberately while ensuring scrubbed data disappears; choose the data-clear treatment of dedup state separately from a fixture reset. Do not casually reset capture state during a live event. There is no demonstrated need for a new public per-frame epoch clear.

Likewise, `group-by-event-with-events` transforms an arbitrary supplied stream; `trace-buffer` reads a retained live ring. They do not substitute for one another when processing imported, filtered, frameless, or cross-frame events. Retiring the unused richer projection is reasonable demand pruning, but state that limitation. Keep pure `group-by-event` and its `[frame dispatch-id]` identity rule. `projected-history` is a better removal candidate: the real off-box consumer pages first and already applies `projected-record` to the chosen values. Preserve that projection-before-egress requirement.

Do not add `rf/current-config` or facade clear operations just for symmetry. Existing testing readers can remain testing-tier until a concrete consumer needs a unified snapshot. Coordinate listener policy with the historical listener finding, preserving optional-epoch behavior.

Implement portable naming/documentation first, policy-preserving trace clearing second, and independently justified dead-surface removal last. Verify retention overrides survive clearing, Xray privacy scrub removes retained records, fixture reset still resets policy, epoch capture remains correct, cross-frame grouping remains separate, optional artifacts stay optional, and production tooling still elides.

# Census of spellings per surface name across the tracked corpus.
# Usage: sh census.sh <name> [<name> ...]
cd /c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2 || exit 1
classify() {
  case "$1" in

    tools/*/test/*|tools/*/tests/*) echo tool-test ;;
    tools/*) echo tool ;;
    testbeds/*) echo testbed ;;
    docs/*) echo docs ;;
    skills/*) echo skills ;;

    implementation/scripts/*) echo fw-scripts ;;
    implementation/*) echo framework ;;

    *) echo other ;;
  esac
}
for name in "$@"; do
  esc=$(printf '%s' "$name" | sed -e 's/[?!.]/\\&/g')

    done
done | sort | uniq -c | sort -k2,2 -k3,3 -k1,1nr | awk '{c=$1; $1=""; sub(/^ /,""); printf "%6d  %s\n", c, $0}'

## The problem

re-frame2 has two dev-only, per-frame, bounded rings — the trace ring and the epoch ring — and each has a read, a clear, a listener and a retention knob. The trace ring is reached through the facade. ## Codex Recommendation

The public spelling cleanup is worthwhile; the proposed removal of the `install.cljs` require is not behavior preserving for manual startup. This review read the full primary bead description, acceptance criteria and 54,121-character notes. Source inspection began at `13884f326f63b7afc3606d9f1cd4ca5b7863c2f7`; material cited-file drift was checked against `2b6e8a44cf204db18a752b40a34028f5aeba3901` at `2026-09-06T18:15:33+10:00`. Intervening core/spec changes concern SSR, not these epoch paths. The primary bead remains open.

The real problem is contradictory guidance about an already coherent consumer workflow. [The attachment table](../../spec/Tool-Pair.md#how-ai-tools-attach) teaches facade listeners, history and configuration, while its later rule tells tool authors to change namespaces. [Xray installation](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs) already requires `re-frame.core` and dispatches through it inside the epoch callback; [Story's invariant scope](../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/invariants.cljc) uses the facade for both registration and teardown. The facade's [epoch wrappers](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc) resolve the same producers that [the epoch namespace](../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc) publishes. A second supported spelling contributes little here. The benefit is less guessing for tool authors and generated code, not faster SPA execution or a measured bundle reduction.

However, the dossier conflates dependency availability with namespace loading. [Xray's manual facade](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs) requires `install`, deliberately does not require `preload`, and calls the installation helpers from `init!`. The only actual `re-frame.epoch` requires found in Xray source are in `install.cljs` and `preload.cljs`; the searched framework production sources supply no substitute. [The dependency declaration](../../tools/xray/deps.edn) makes epoch available, but [late binding](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc) merely looks in an atom populated when the producer loads. Deleting the shared install require can therefore leave manual startup with a silent no-op registration and an idempotency flag already set. This is a source-derived regression prediction, not an executed reproduction. Change the call to `(rf/register-listener! :epoch ...)`, but retain bare `[re-frame.epoch]` in `install.cljs`. It serves both startup paths without invoking Xray's preload boot block. The replacement specification should say a mandatory epoch consumer declares the dependency **and loads its producer namespace**; optional consumers may rely on the facade's absent-hook result.

The strongest case for keeping both public forms is idiomatic Clojure: an independently packaged library can reasonably expose its own namespace, and a direct require makes dependency intent visible. The historical Story revert, commit `037f7d999e6d9819c9893e08ab4bf85663c40831`, explicitly retained the Xray ruling; it was not blanket approval to remove home verbs. Nevertheless, a bare producer require preserves that concrete benefit while the facade supplies one callable grammar. This justifies reopening the rule without claiming all home namespaces are undesirable. C retains the teaching contradiction. B is a poor final state because it reclassifies a live Xray dependency as implementation while leaving the tool and documentation teaching it. A true temporary alternative would correct the explanation while keeping classifications honest until migration.

Keep pure trace projection in its existing namespace and remove the unused facade aliases. [Xray's self-noise helper](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/self_noise.cljc) already consumes `group-by-event` there; [the implementation](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/projection.cljc) transforms supplied events independently of a live ring. That dependency shape makes a small, documented tooling namespace useful. Preserve `domino-bucket`, ordering and `[frame dispatch-id]` identity, which [existing tests](../../implementation/core/test/re_frame/trace/projection_cljs_test.cljc) exercise. Do not replace arbitrary-stream grouping with a ring read. No extra public clearing operation is justified: epoch fixture clearing also destroys in-flight capture buffers. Likewise, migrate the [Pair runtime's configuration read](../../skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs) only after .4 supplies its approved replacement; preserve the producer needed by any new configuration hook.

Resolve the egress overlap explicitly. The .9 primary bead proposes retiring `projected-record`, whereas this dossier calls keeping it settled. Independent inspection of [epoch projection](../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc), [generic projection](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc) and [Pair's generated exporter](../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs) confirms that today's specialized projection is necessary: it handles separate payload slots that today's generic kindless walk does not recognize. Keep it callable throughout this cleanup. If .9's explicit epoch-kind integration is approved, migrate those exporters and retire the door once, under that joint change. Removing duplicate namespace rows here must not preempt that decision.

Correct the implementation accounting too. [The manifest generator](../../implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj) excludes `^:no-doc` vars from `public-vars-of`; adding that metadata and retaining implementation-tier rows for those same vars are incompatible instructions. Choose the existing unrowed hook-target convention and regenerate consistently. Conversely, [API documentation coverage](../../implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/doc_api_check.clj) explicitly excludes `:tooling`, so a projection page is sensible documentation, not the claimed mandatory consequence of that gate. These are small corrections to A, not reasons for another governance mechanism.

Acceptance should exercise registration, replacement and teardown through the facade; preserve Story's absent-epoch behavior; and verify Xray receives epoch records through both startup paths. Use a fresh manual-only entry point: [the existing decoupling test](../../tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload_decoupling_cljs_test.cljs) itself imports `preload`, so it cannot establish producer loading in a genuinely manual-only build. Retain the projection tests, regenerate/check manifest and docs, and run the existing bundle-isolation gate with its positive control. Check the result against the actual changed build; the counter bundle alone does not prove manual startup. Coordinate the Tool-Pair paragraph with .22 and neighboring deletions with .53. This review changed only this recommendation, ran no builds or runtime tests, and does not certify the dossier's exhaustive consumer counts or hypothetical bundle-size savings.

title: api(ssr): RULING — re-frame.ssr as the only SSR query door: drop the rf/ copies + hooks, one (head f ?opts)
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from ssr.md (ref ssr.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

One job, two spellings, and the spec has written the second down as deliberate. Seven SSR query fns are defined at home and copied onto `re-frame.core` through late-bind wrappers: `render-to-string`, `render-tree-hash`, `project-error` (home `re-frame.ssr`, `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:48,59,83`) and `render-head`, `active-head`, `head-model->html`, `head-snapshot` (home `re-frame.ssr.head`, `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc:39-45` — NOT `re-frame.ssr`, which carries no head def). The copies live at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:823-869` → `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_ssr.cljc` (whole file, 122 lines) → seven hooks `:ssr/render-to-string`, `:ssr/render-tree-hash`, `:ssr/project-error` (`ssr.cljc:416-419`), `:ssr/render-head`, `:ssr/active-head`, `:ssr/head-snapshot`, `:ssr/head-model-html` (`head.cljc:61-69`) → seven directory rows (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:734-739,747-749,766-781`). The copy's stated purpose is single-import ergonomics plus a guided `:rf.error/ssr-artefact-missing` when the artefact is absent (`spec/Conventions.md:1730-1742`, `spec/API.md:327`).

The premise fails by construction for SSR: `:rf/hydrate`, the `:rf.ssr/check-*` fx, the seven `:rf.server/*` fx and the `:rf.server/request` cofx are registered as a side effect of LOADING `re-frame.ssr` (`ssr.cljc:4-6,229-290`), so every SSR program requires the artefact ns at boot, and every measured call site of a façade copy sits in a file that already has that require. In addition the head fns carry a keyword-or-map second argument (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:199-203`) — a placeful dispatch on type — and three reads (`render-head`, `active-head`, `head-snapshot`) answer one question for one frame.

## Evidence (verified at tip 6445d0611b, 2026-09-05; `git grep` over tracked files)

Façade-spelling call sites outside `implementation/core` and `implementation/ssr/test`, code only:

| fn | `rf/` files | real calls | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render-to-string` | 12 | 5 — `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:307`, `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:379`, `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/url_strategy_test.clj:89`, `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/runtime_cljs_test.cljs:347`, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_test.clj:157` | rest are prose in four `index.html`, a `:where` symbol (`implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:342`), docstrings (`ssr/emit.cljc:884`, `ssr/substrate.cljc:55`); plus `implementation/core/test`: `boot_test.clj:521,607` (`:where` labels), `examples_test.clj` ×3, `smoke_test.clj` ×3 — core's TEST classpath carries ssr as a local dep (`implementation/core/deps.edn:97,207`) |
| `render-tree-hash` | 5 | 5 — `ssr/core.cljc:312`, `resources_ssr/core.cljc:380`, `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ssr.cljc:72`, `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj:268,295` | `examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr_streaming/core.cljc:234` spells the same fn `rf.ssr/render-tree-hash` |
| `project-error` | 0 | 0 | |
| `render-head` | 1 | 0 (`registry.cljc:149`, a `:where` symbol) | |
| `active-head` | 3 | 4 — `lifecycle.clj:178`, `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj:2724,2815,2866` | + `pipeline.clj:605` comment |
| `head-model->html` | 2 | 2 — `lifecycle.clj:179`, `ring_test.clj:2725` | |
| `head-snapshot` | 0 | 0 | deleted by @ssr.2 |

Every one of those app files already requires the artefact: `examples/capabilities/ssr/{ssr,resources_ssr,ssr_streaming}/core.cljc:68,73,36`, `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:53`, `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:47`, all three `testbeds/ssr_*/core.cljs`. The ring adapter's `lifecycle.clj` uses `rf/active-head` + `rf/head-model->html` because `re-frame.ssr` never carried them, while `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn:19` declares `day8/re-frame2-ssr` statically and `pipeline.clj:368,478,581` already calls `ssr/render-to-string` — one artefact, both spellings.

Inside `implementation/ssr/test`: `rf/render-to-string` 23 lines, `rf/head-model->html` 31, `rf/render-head` 14, `rf/render-tree-hash` 9, `rf/active-head` 5, `rf/project-error` 4; plus `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj:41-86,121-` (tests the copies' artefact-missing throw). `tools/`: zero consumers of any of the seven (Xray hits are its `-xray-render-header` protocol method; Story hits are tier-name prose).

Docs/skills carrying the `rf/` spelling: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1445-1507` (the façade SSR section), `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:16,264,282,388,691,729`, `docs/ssr/head.md:14,55-56,76,81`, `docs/ssr/coming-from-nextjs.md:66`, `docs/ssr/tutorial.md:71`, `docs/resources/tutorial/05-test-and-ship.md`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:128-135`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:47,56,61,66-67,163-164`, examples' `README.md` / `index.html` prose, `spec/011-SSR.md:234,1259,1269,1276`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (one `rf/active-head`, one `rf/head-model->html`), `spec/008-Testing.md`, `spec/Construction-Prompts.md` ×2, `spec/Conventions.md:1764,1854,1884`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:1314,1511`, `spec/API.md:26,29,325-342,373,375`.

Tier record vs teaching: `spec/api-manifest.edn:385` rows `hydrate!` `:implementation`; `spec/API.md:373` calls it host-adapter plumbing "(the supported client path is the `:rf/hydrate` event plus the `re-frame.ssr.ring` host adapter)"; yet `spec/011-SSR.md:422-451` ships `hydrate!` as THE client boot, every example calls `rf.ssr/hydrate!` (`ssr/core.cljc:458`, `resources_ssr/core.cljc:488`, `ssr_streaming/core.cljc:428`, `login/core.cljs:296`) and no example dispatches `:rf/hydrate` by hand (the two testbeds that split are `testbeds/ssr_basic/core.cljs:222` and `testbeds/ssr_hydration_mismatch/core.cljs:207`).

## Options

**A. Keep as is** (the 2026-09-04 sweep's position). Seven façade rows stay `:keep`; only the doc drift is fixed (@ssr.2 carries it). Cost: a wrapper ns, seven hooks, seven directory rows, a drift test and two "documented façade exception" sentences that deliver single-import ergonomics to zero measured people; the head surface keeps three reads and a placeful arity.

**B. One door (recommended).** `re-frame.ssr` owns every SSR QUERY; `re-frame.core` keeps only the two REGISTRARS (`reg-head`, `reg-error-projector` — the Convention-A pair every `reg-*` has; keep `-reg-head` / `-reg-error-projector` in `core_ssr.cljc` and the hooks `:ssr/reg-head`, `:ssr/reg-error-projector`).

```clojure
;; re-frame.ssr — the only SSR query door
(render-to-string tree)  (render-to-string tree {:doctype? b :render-hash h})   ; 1-arity home via @ssr.1
(render-tree-hash tree)
(project-error frame-id trace-event)
(head frame-id)                           ; = today's active-head: route :head → model, else default-head
(head frame-id {:head-id id :route r})    ; = today's render-head; opts map only, no keyword dispatch
(head-model->html model ?{:wrap? b})      ; lifted onto re-frame.ssr from re-frame.ssr.head
(hydrate! {:frame … :render-tree-fn …})   ; unchanged; tier :implementation → :advanced, rowed in API.md

;; re-frame.core keeps
(rf/reg-head id ?meta head-fn)   (rf/reg-error-projector id ?meta f)
```

`head` preserves: default-head fallback when the route declares no `:head`; `:rf.error/no-such-head` when a named or route-declared head is unregistered; the difference between an absent `:route` (read the frame's runtime-db route slice) and an explicit `:route nil` (`registry.cljc:150-152` uses `contains?`); `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on a nil frame. `default-head` stays public; `render-head*` stays private.

**C. Partial.** Delete only the three `re-frame.ssr`-homed copies (`render-to-string`, `render-tree-hash`, `project-error` — each has a rowed `re-frame.ssr` peer today, `spec/api-manifest.edn:391,395,396`) and leave the four head copies until `re-frame.ssr` grows a head surface. Cheapest; leaves the ring adapter on two spellings and the head arity as is.

## Recommendation

B. Regularity over cleverness (`spec/Principles.md:18`): the façade re-export pattern is right where `rf/reg-flow` IS the whole surface; SSR is the one feature whose consumer must name the artefact ns anyway. Name over place (`:30`): `render-head`'s keyword-or-map second argument is the placeful signature the principle asks to retire. Public query surfaces (`:52`) are for what the runtime knows and the caller does not; `(rf/registrations :head)` stays and is what the MCP tool uses. Clojure ethos: small namespaces with one meaning each, a fn you can `(doc …)` in the namespace that owns it, no indirection unless it removes a dependency — and here it removes none.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer (fable README lists "the SSR re-exports and head surface" under one-reviewer; codex "explicitly did not verify them and calls them larger design decisions"). Codex's cross-check on this doc, after reading source: consolidating in `re-frame.ssr` "is reasonable: the measured consumers already load that artifact, and namespace-local discovery is more useful than maintaining late-bound spelling aliases"; keep the registrar convention rather than redesigning `reg-head`; the head proposal "is sound" with the snapshot-shape correction (carried in @ssr.2); a single `head` "can replace the overlapping reads while preserving default-head fallback, explicit missing-head failure, and the difference between absent `:route` and explicit `nil`"; verify "byte-identical HTML and hash stamping, route-default head behavior, SSR-before-adapter and adapter-before-SSR boot, destroy/re-init, client-only boot". Codex's general caution (`ai/findings/API-review/codex/intermediate/fable-synthesis.md` §Remaining Fable themes): one documented home per operation "does not, by itself, justify removing every facade export" — the case here rests on the require-graph fact above, not on the rule.

**One door: `re-frame.ssr` owns every SSR query; `re-frame.core` keeps only the two registrars.**

```clojure
(render-to-string tree)                 ; NEW 1-arity moves home
(render-to-string tree {:doctype? bool :render-hash h})   ; :emit-hash? deleted

(rf/reg-head id ?meta head-fn)          ; registrars stay on the facade: one registration grammar
(rf/reg-error-projector id ?meta f)
```

## Why this is better (ethos)

**Regularity over cleverness (Principles:18).** The facade re-export pattern (Conventions:1732) is right for flows, routing and machines, where `rf/reg-flow` *is* the whole surface and a consumer has no other reason to name the artefact namespace. SSR is the one feature where that premise fails by construction: `:rf/hydrate`, the seven `:rf.server/*` fx and the `:rf.server/request` cofx are registered as a *side effect of loading* `re-frame.ssr` (`ssr.cljc:240-362`), so every SSR program requires it at boot, and every measured call site of a facade copy sits in a file that already has the require. The copy turns a compile-time "no such var" into a runtime `:rf.error/ssr-artefact-missing`, adds a wrapper ns, seven hooks, seven directory rows, a drift test and two documented "façade exception" sentences — and delivers single-import ergonomics to zero people. `API.md:327` calls this "one of the two documented façade exceptions"; a written-down exception that nobody exercises is option soup with a citation.

**Name over place (Principles:30).** `render-head`'s second argument means "frame" if it is a keyword and "opts" if it is a map. The framework-wide shape is `(id {:frame …})`; a positional dispatch on type is exactly the placeful signature the principle asks to retire. One fn, one opts map.

**Data before magic, and trust the programmer.** The head model is a pure value `(fn [db route] model)` returns. `head-snapshot` bolts a side-channel atom onto that pure read so a *different* caller can ask what the last caller got — a hidden register nobody reads. The value is already in the caller's hands; a masterpiece hands it back and stops there.

**Public query surfaces (Principles:52)** are for what the runtime knows that the caller does not — registrations, frames, topology. `(rf/registrations :head)` stays and is what the MCP tool actually uses. The four head reads were rowed as query surfaces "for tools (Xray, MCP)"; the tools never came, and the 200-plus-opportunity rule in the fable README applies.

**Clojure ethos.** Small namespaces with one meaning each; a function you can `(doc …)` in the namespace that owns it; no indirection unless it removes a dependency — and here it removes none. The late-bind seam is *simple* for the packaging problem it solves and *complected* when it is also used as a naming convenience.

**Honest costs.** `rf/` head spellings appear 59× in `implementation/ssr/test`, 4× in ring tests, and ring tests `with-redefs` the facade var (`ring_test.clj:2815,2866`) — those retarget to `ssr/head`. Docs and skills carry ~25 `rf/<ssr-fn>` mentions to rename. `render-to-string` gains an arity and loses an opt, so the two example servers change four lines each. The `:emit-hash?` deletion removes a "just stamp it" convenience whose only users also computed the hash separately.

## Codex Thoughts

The strongest findings are the redundant namespace doors, the misleading `hydrate!` tier/documentation, and the unconsumed head snapshot. Consolidating SSR operations in `re-frame.ssr` is reasonable: the measured consumers already load that artifact, and namespace-local discovery is more useful than maintaining late-bound spelling aliases. Move the useful one-argument `render-to-string` convenience home before removing its facade copy. Keep the common registration convention rather than redesigning `reg-head` alongside query cleanup.

The head proposal is sound with one factual correction. [The snapshot implementation](../../../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc) returns `{head-id -> last-model}`, potentially containing several previously rendered heads, **not** the same map as the last `head` return. Its removal is justified by the absence of a consumer for that historical side channel, not value equivalence. A single `head` operation with explicit frame and optional head/route selection can replace the overlapping reads while preserving default-head fallback, explicit missing-head failure, and the difference between absent `:route` and explicit `nil`. Snapshot tests should become tests of required rendering behavior, not mechanically compare differently shaped values.

Do not classify `hydrate-page!` as merely N calls to `hydrate!`. [Its source](../../../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc) also wraps each host `:mount-fn`, reports failures, returns ordered per-root outcomes, and allows healthy roots sharing a frame to continue. That is real composition with different failure behavior. Viable choices are to retain it as an advanced multi-root helper, demote it to host implementation support, or retire it if multi-root orchestration is explicitly outside the supported authoring surface. Prefer **demotion/retention pending a named multi-root host**, rather than deleting the isolation tests as alias cleanup. Per-root isolation and hydration-claim correctness remain framework obligations even if the convenience name disappears.

Removing the unused streaming publication hooks is sensible after checking all consumers, because Ring calls the implementation directly. The emitter's other installation paths are not automatically redundant: [the durable emitter publication](../../../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc) explicitly repairs both load-order reversal and adapter destroy/re-init. Keep that behavior. Removing the unused custom-adapter installation helper is a separate demand decision, with the direct setter recipe documented for custom adapters if it remains supported.

Prefer a single supplied `:render-hash` in hosts that need both stamped HTML and a payload hash; fix the examples' duplicate computation first. Deleting `:emit-hash?` is a modest optional cleanup, not the central value. Keep HTML emission and structural hashing separate rather than inventing a combined renderer protocol.


Implement in small groups: namespace/tier cleanup, head-query consolidation, then independently justified dead hooks/helpers. Verify byte-identical HTML and hash stamping, route-default head behavior, SSR-before-adapter and adapter-before-SSR boot, destroy/re-init, client-only boot, and multi-root failure isolation. Do not delete unrelated request/error side-channel teardown with the head snapshot.

**Cost.** The ongoing one: a 122-line wrapper ns, seven hooks, seven directory rows, four artefact-missing tests and two spec sentences maintained for a benefit no measured program can receive; a keyword-or-map dispatch on a documented surface; two spellings in the Ring adapter and in the example set (`ssr_streaming/core.cljc:234` spells the same hash `rf.ssr/render-tree-hash` that `ssr/core.cljc:312` spells `rf/render-tree-hash`). **What it buys.** Consistency with the sweep of 2026-09-04 and with `Conventions.md` as written; zero migration; no `spec/API.md` / `spec/Conventions.md` / migration-README touch.

**Who has weighed in.** The sweep (rf2-2hpxo, PR #9217) — with the quoted justification. Neither wave-3 reviewer supports it.

## Recommendation

**A.** The posture is elegance and one obvious way, and *Regularity over cleverness* (`spec/Principles.md:18`) says that when a feature admits two shapes for one job, one is canonical and the other needs a stated use case — the façade copy's stated use case is a guided failure for an app that has not loaded `re-frame.ssr`, and no SSR app can be that app, because loading `re-frame.ssr` is what installs `:rf/hydrate` and the `:rf.server/*` fx. The convention is right where it applies and wrong here by construction, and the Ring adapter — the framework's own consumer — already shows what "one artefact, two spellings" looks like on adjacent lines. *Name over place* (`:30`) retires `render-head`'s keyword-or-map second argument on its own. *Public query surfaces* (`:52`) are for what the runtime knows and the caller does not; `(rf/registrations :head)` stays and is what tooling uses, while the four head reads were rowed "for tools (Xray, MCP)" that never came. The registrars stay on the façade because they *are* the whole registration grammar, which is the case the convention was written for. Pre-alpha: delete, no deprecation. **Fallback if Mike wants the façade convention left as written:** B — it fixes the head surface without reopening the sweep. Under C, file only the `hydrate!` tier fix.

## Codex Recommendation

Choose **A — one documented SSR query namespace**, with a contained namespace fix before introducing `ssr/head`. Keep `rf/reg-head` and `rf/reg-error-projector`, move the useful rendering arities home, and expose `(ssr/head frame-id)` plus `(ssr/head frame-id {:head-id id :route route})`. Keep `head-model->html` separate: evaluating application state into a model and serialising that model are useful composable operations. The gain is a coherent authoring contract: a host can discover rendering, head evaluation, hashing and hydration together, while ordinary registration keeps the familiar `rf/reg-*` grammar.
The consumer evidence supports that choice, but the dossier's “population of zero” argument is too strong. [Ring lifecycle](../../implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj) and [RealWorld's payload helper](../../examples/real-apps/realworld_http/ssr.cljc) actually benefit from using core names while another namespace loads SSR. A library can similarly compile optional SSR branches against core without statically requiring SSR. Also, [the head namespace](../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc) publishes its own hooks independently; head evaluation does not intrinsically need every server effect. Missing-artifact guidance therefore has real value during incomplete setup. Removing it trades that value for explicit dependencies; neither a missing namespace nor a missing Var is automatically a better diagnostic.

Nevertheless, the measured consumers already depend on the SSR artifact, and [the main namespace](../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc) already provides the broader operations those hosts use. Adding one explicit require to a helper is a reasonable pre-alpha cost. [The cheatsheet](../../skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md) and [authoring guide](../../skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md) currently teach a different namespace for head queries from the rest of that workflow. Correcting that ownership is more persuasive than counting deleted names. Searches of examples, testbeds and tools found no additional application head-query consumer; [MCP's handler metadata tool](../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs) recognises the `:head` registry kind, which remains available.

**The proposed alias has a ClojureScript collision.** A Var `re-frame.ssr/head` occupies the JavaScript name `re_frame.ssr.head`, already used by the namespace and its `.registry` / `.emit` children. The [ClojureScript analyzer](https://github.com/clojure/clojurescript/blob/master/src/main/clojure/cljs/analyzer.cljc) explicitly detects this `ns-name + "." + var-name` collision; [compiler options](https://clojurescript.org/reference/compiler-options#warnings) document `:ns-var-clash`. This is a source-backed implementation constraint, not an executed reproduction here. Relocate only the existing three-namespace head implementation subtree to a noncolliding prefix such as `re-frame.ssr-head`, including its require and reload references. Then publish `head` and `head-model->html` from `re-frame.ssr`. Renaming only the outer file while leaving `re-frame.ssr.head.registry` would retain the conflicting parent. This needs no new abstraction or broad namespace redesign.

Give the unified head query one consistent selection rule. Resolve the effective route once: an absent `:route` reads runtime-db; explicit `:route nil` means no route. A supplied head id selects that registration; otherwise select the effective route's registered `:head`, falling back to the default only when no head is selected. Pass that same effective route to the head function. This makes `(ssr/head f {:route hypothetical-route})` coherent and avoids selecting from the current route while evaluating another. Preserve required frame targeting and missing-registration errors from [the registry implementation](../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc). Keep the return value as the model; no format discriminator, implicit HTML mode, cache or historical snapshot is needed.

The strongest alternative is **C, keep as designed**, with consistent documentation: centrally loading an optional feature and calling its core exports is a legitimate convenience, and the existing wrappers are already factored through `defwrapper`. The [facade metadata](../../spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn) deliberately records `:keep`. History places that SSR classification in `960d7a1a928a99c8c2a4754d8cabb322c8156679` / PR #9187; rf2-2hpxo's later PR #9217 corrected epoch rationales. Choosing A supersedes a design choice, rather than repairing a proven wrapper defect. B preserves that convenience while regularising head selection, but spends most of the migration effort while retaining two authoring namespaces. For this pre-alpha API, A's clearer ownership is worth the modest consumer change.

Implement after rf2-kuky.42 and .43 actually land. Their latest notes describe completed worker changes, but both remain `in_progress`, and the reviewed mayor still contains the snapshot and old emitter surface. Keep the namespace/tier change and head consolidation as bounded slices; the latter includes the collision fix. Promote `hydrate!` to `:advanced` as [Spec 011's taught client boot](../../spec/011-SSR.md#client-side-hydration-boot-helper), retaining the documented split path and `hydrate-page!` isolation helper. Delete query wrappers and hooks, retaining the registrar wrappers and moving [feature detection](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/features.cljc) to `:ssr/reg-error-projector`; `core-ssr` therefore survives.

Focused acceptance should cover CLJS compilation and an actual head call after namespace load/reload, named/default/overridden-route head results, absent versus nil route, frame errors, and Ring's unchanged head HTML and separate model hash. Retarget both dynamic lookups in [SSR conformance](../../implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj) to the supported exports and ensure missing Vars fail the relevant checks. Retarget Ring's `with-redefs`, check feature detection with SSR absent/present, and regenerate the manifest and affected teaching. Preserve conformance capability ids and unrelated teardown hooks.

title: api(resources): RULING — reduce :scope policy to two shapes (:rf.scope/global | {:from-db id}) and make clear-scope take a concrete scope
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from resources.md (ref resources.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`reg-resource`'s `:scope` policy gate admits FIVE shapes (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc:75–112` `valid-scope-policy?`; resolution arms `:796–870` `resolve-scope-for-event`), a route entry admits a sixth (`route.cljc:507–560`, the anonymous `(fn [route ctx] …)` tier), and `:rf.resource/clear-scope` admits two payload forms (`events.cljc:2144–2214`). The corpus uses two policy shapes across all 13 `reg-resource` registrations in 4 apps + 1 testbed (`:rf.scope/global` ×5, `{:from-db <id>}` ×8) and one clear-scope form (a concrete scope pre-resolved with `resolve-resource-scope`). The other shapes exist only in tests, spec and docs, and two of them carry dedicated diagnostic subsystems that exist for no other reason.

| Shape | Lowers to | app / tool / testbed | tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| B3 `:scope :rf.scope/from-caller` | "every ensure/refetch/sub MUST pass `:scope`" + `:rf.error/resource-scope-required-from-caller` (`registry.cljc:846–855`) + the dev heuristic `:rf.warning/resource-sub-scope-mismatch` (`subs.cljc:121–272`, ~150 lines; the ONLY policy it fires for, `:229–240`) | 0 | 35 lines / 16 files |
| B4 `:scope (fn [] …)` fn-of-nothing | `(policy)` at `registry.cljc:864–866` (arm 3d) | 0 | 1 (`resources_skeleton_cljs_test.cljs:277`) |
| B5 `:scope <literal EDN>` at registration | `canonicalize-scope` of a constant (`:867–868`, arm 3e) | 0 | 0 |
| B6 route entry `:scope (fn [route ctx] …)` | anonymous per-entry resolver (`route.cljc:544–546`); 016 `:239` already reserves `[:runtime path]` inputs as its NAMED replacement | 0 | 7 (`resources_route_cljs_test.cljc:591,675,2086`; `resource_algebra_view_cljs_test.cljc:163`; `routing/test/…/route_algebra_view_test.clj:178,210`; `tools/xray/test/…/resources_helpers_cljs_test.cljc:85`) |

## Options

**O1 — fable (full reduction).** `:scope` is data with two shapes: `:rf.scope/global` (the explicit claim) | `{:from-db <id>}` (a name). Route entries, sub queries and event payloads INHERIT the registration policy; a use-site `:scope` is an OVERRIDE (a concrete scope or a `{:from-db …}`), retained for the admin-reads-tenant-X case, never required. Delete B3 with its error id and the whole `resource-sub-scope-mismatch` heuristic; delete B4, B5, B6; `clear-scope` takes a concrete scope only (delete the `{:from-db …}` arm and `:rf.warning/resource-clear-scope-unresolved`); move E to `:rf.resource.internal/*` beside `succeeded` / `failed` / `stale-fired` / `gc-fired` (11 internal ids already exist). Fable's answer to the counter: every principal in a re-frame2 app already lives in app-db — that is what app-db is for — so "known only at the caller" is "not yet named"; the fail-closed nil of a named resolver refuses to guess exactly as `from-caller` did, without a second mechanism; and a genuinely per-call resource passes a concrete `:scope` override on each ensure and sub — the same obligation `from-caller` imposed, minus the policy keyword.

**O2 — codex (keep the policies; teach).** "The proposed two-policy restriction is not yet justified. A literal tenant/sandbox scope is ordinary useful data, not a redundant resolver language. `:rf.scope/from-caller` says 'there is no default'; replacing it with global-plus-overrides loses that fail-closed requirement. A named resolver reading an otherwise unnecessary db slot also adds friction and state. 'Every principal lives in app-db' is not a demonstrated universal constraint: a multi-tenant inspector or reusable per-call resource can legitimately receive its subject as an argument. Retain concrete and caller-required policies. The anonymous function cases are more plausible pruning candidates, but deserve a separate decision about route-context information that db-only resolvers cannot currently express." On D2: "clear-scope's reference form means resolve against the clearing event's world; a concrete scope means act on a previously selected identity. Logout needs the latter … That timing difference is a teaching obligation, not proof that the former has no valid use. Preserve both unless intentionally narrowing the contract." On E: "demote planner-owned events without inventing a new public lifecycle" (concurs).

**O3 — Grok's middle (sequence, then rule).** D and E now (mechanical; D2's only claimed use has zero consumers and its tests exercise an ordering the headline case cannot produce — "the helper exists because of that time-travel bug; keeping the descriptor form so programmers can select a tenant does not fix the logout case, which is the only app consumer"). B4/B5/B6 with D (zero consumers, anonymous places → named things; the route-entry `:scope` SLOT stays as a data override, so codex's explicit tenant selection is preserved as data rather than as a fn). B3 last, after `@resources.1` / `@resources.2` land: "decide whether `:rf.scope/from-caller` is still a policy or just a way of saying 'override required'. I would delete it — every principal already lives in app-db."

## Recommendation

O1, sequenced as O3: rule all of (a)–(e) but file (d)+(e) and (b)+(c) as the first implementation beads and (a) as the last, so the `from-caller` deletion lands on a tree where the default-plus-override teaching (from `@resources.2`) is already written. The corpus argument is strong on every row: zero consumers after 13 registrations, 8 route plans and every sub in five apps had the opportunity; B3 is the anti-name ("someone else will say") and the sole reason a ~150-line heuristic and a use-time error exist; B6 is a place where 016 already reserves a name; D2 asks the NEXT event to look at a world that no longer exists. Codex's counter is carried honestly: if Mike wants a spelling for "there is no default", the fallback is to keep ONLY `:rf.scope/from-caller` (with its error and the heuristic that exists for it) and still delete (b)–(e). A per-call resource under O1 is modelled as a resolver reading a db slot the caller sets first, or as a concrete `:scope` override on every ensure and sub.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes. The only app that revalidates on focus/reconnect has a 12-line comment explaining that `install-revalidation-listeners!` must run *after* the `frame-root` render that created the frame, never before. Routing already folded the identical shape into `:url-bound? true` (rf2-g8pbwg, no shim). That is not taste — it is a boot-order obligation the library should own. The 2-arity `reg-resource-scope` sugar also shifts the callback's first argument from an inputs map to `db`; zero app consumers, and spec 016 itself brands it "a marked convenience, not a peer."

**Diagnosis.** A, C, D are correctly diagnosed. B (delete `:rf.scope/from-caller`, fn-of-nothing, and registration-time literals) is a policy ruling dressed as a census. The corpus uses two shapes, yes. `from-caller` still names a real idea: "scope is a call-site argument, fail if omitted." The admin-reads-tenant-X *override* the target keeps is essentially that idea without the policy keyword. Deleting the keyword and keeping the override is a coherent end state, but it is not the same kind of change as folding a listener pair into a frame key.

D is sharper than Codex allowed: `[:rf.resource/clear-scope {:scope {:from-db id}}]` from a logout handler's `:fx` resolves against the *next* event's db, after the user is gone, and no-ops. The helper `resolve-resource-scope` exists because of that time-travel bug. Keeping the descriptor form "so programmers can select a tenant" does not fix the logout case, which is the only app consumer.

**Recommendation.**

- **A. Do it.** `(make-frame {:revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}})` / the same key on `frame-root`. Generalise `fire-frame-registered-hook!` from one hardwired key to a roster (`:routing/on-frame-registered!` then `:resources/on-frame-registered!`). No key means no listeners (relinquish, like `:url-bound? false`). JVM/SSR stay no-ops. Delete the install/remove pair and their late-bind keys.
- **C. Do it.** One `reg-resource-scope` arity; `:inputs` required; callback always receives the inputs map. Whole-db is `{:inputs {:db [:db []]}}`.
- **D. Do it.** `clear-scope` takes a concrete scope. `resolve-resource-scope` is how you get one from a named resolver against *this* handler's db. Delete the `{:from-db …}` arm and `:rf.warning/resource-clear-scope-unresolved`.
- **B. Sequence, then rule.** After A/C/D: registration policy is the default; use-site `:scope` is an override (concrete or `{:from-db …}`). Then decide whether `:rf.scope/from-caller` is still a policy or just a way of saying "override required." I would delete it — every principal already lives in app-db — but that needs the ruling the doc asks for, not a bundle with A.
- **E. Yes**, move planner-only `adopt-owner` / `release-owner-identities` to `:rf.resource.internal/*`.

**Implement.** A is independent (frame.cljc roster + resources hook) and can land first. C and D share `scope_registry.cljc` / `events.cljc` — one bead. B is a third. No SSR/hydration surface moves. The one RealWorld call site loses its 12-line comment.

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: adopt frame-owned revalidation and one explicit resolver callback contract; do not remove useful scope policies simply because the examples have not exercised them.** [The RealWorld boot sequence](../../../../examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/core.cljs) contains real ordering knowledge just to install listeners after a frame exists. [The listener implementation](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/revalidate_listeners.cljc) already owns replacement and destruction, so putting the opt-in on the frame removes application coordination rather than merely renaming functions.

`:revalidate-on #{:focus :reconnect}` is a reasonable target. Keep this as a small resource lifecycle integration, not a general-purpose lifecycle plugin bus. Extend the existing post-registration hook path, add early configuration validation, and reconcile listeners when the frame's effective configuration changes. Preserve the existing distinction between **which host events enter a frame** and **which resources refetch for those events**; resource-level stale/owner/refetch policy still makes the latter decision. Focus means both window focus and document visibility becoming visible, not two separate public settings. JVM and non-DOM hosts remain inert.

The implementation must actually support the selected subset—the current installer always installs all three browser listeners—and handle removal, deliberate reconfiguration and destruction without stacking. Verify those behaviors against two frames, including a destroyed/recreated same-id frame, while leaving ordinary repeated `frame-root` renders free of listener churn. Do not promise that merely omitting a key during an incidental ensure call is a configuration update; use the constructor's existing reconfiguration semantics.

The resolver simplification is also sound, with one important correction: [whole-db sugar](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc) is selected whenever metadata lacks `:inputs`, including a three-argument form carrying only `:doc`. Deleting the two-argument arity alone leaves the argument-shape exception alive. Require the explicit input map and always deliver that map; whole-db readers write `{:inputs {:db [:db []]}}`. Derive whole-db tooling information from the declaration instead of maintaining a second authored mode. Keep this separate from broader scope-policy decisions.

**The proposed two-policy restriction is not yet justified.** [Scope resolution](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc) distinguishes a concrete constant, a named db-derived value and a caller-required value. A literal tenant/sandbox scope is ordinary useful data, not a redundant resolver language. `:rf.scope/from-caller` says “there is no default”; replacing it with global-plus-overrides loses that fail-closed requirement. A named resolver reading an otherwise unnecessary db slot also adds friction and state. “Every principal lives in app-db” is not a demonstrated universal constraint: a multi-tenant inspector or reusable per-call resource can legitimately receive its subject as an argument. Retain concrete and caller-required policies. The anonymous function cases are more plausible pruning candidates, but deserve a separate decision about route-context information that db-only resolvers cannot currently express.


Similarly, [clear-scope's reference form](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc) means resolve against the clearing event's world; a concrete scope means act on a previously selected identity. Logout needs the latter, as the example correctly shows. That timing difference is a teaching obligation, not proof that the former has no valid use. Preserve both unless intentionally narrowing the contract. Keep the old-scope capture example prominent, remove genuinely repeated defaults from teaching, and demote planner-owned events without inventing a new public lifecycle. The high-value work is boot ownership and stable callback arguments; the policy deletions can wait.
