title: api(egress): RULING — one `project-egress` door, closed `:rf.egress/*` opts; retire walker export, epoch doors
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from egress.md (ref egress.5); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## The question

After egress.1-3 land, "project this value or record under the owning frame's classification before it leaves" is still spelled three ways on the facade — `rf/elide-wire-value` (bare values; `core.cljc:2247` → `elision.cljc:1068-1152`), `rf/project-egress` (records by `:kind`, and bare values through the same walker; `core.cljc:2262` → `projection.cljc:499-578`), `rf/projected-record` (epoch records; `core.cljc:2493` → `core_epoch.cljc:192-254` → `epoch.cljc:701-731` → `tool_pair.cljc:2029-2072`) — with the policy booleans under `:rf.size/*` (a privacy flag under the size namespace) plus three bare epoch-only knobs, and a pure-data MIRROR of the profile table in `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/egress.cljc:45-108` pinned byte-equal to `projection.cljc:124-163` by `tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/egress_profile_test.clj`. Should this collapse to ONE public door?

## Evidence at tip (2026-09-05, `3fbd3a9ede`)

- Applications never project: `examples/` has 56 `:sensitive [[…]]` declarations and 0 calls to any door. The users are ~10 framework namespaces and 5 tools (pair-MCP, story-mcp, Story, Xray, the pair preload), plus agents reading the skills.
- The written discriminator ("sinks / tools should rarely call [the walker] directly", `spec/015:229`; "layered over", `spec/API.md:693`) is not respected: 11 of 14 tool-side projection calls go through the walker (pair-MCP eval builders `get_path.cljs:51-58`, `snapshot.cljs:167, :177`, `read_sub.cljs:117`, `list_subscriptions.cljs:109-114`, `dispatch_dry_run.cljs:222`; story-mcp `egress.cljc:209`; Story `assertions.cljc:414`, `error.cljc:124` via the HOME namespace `re-frame.elision` — requires at :74 and :68; preload `runtime.cljs:476, :3108`; Xray `egress.cljs:87`), and `project-egress`'s kindless path IS the walker verbatim (`projection.cljc:492-497`).
- The two record doors dispatch on different discriminators: `project-egress` on `:kind` (`:rf.observe/*`, `projection.cljc:476-497`); `projected-record` on the epoch record's slot set (`tool_pair.cljc:2029-2072`: `:frame-state-*`, `:db-*`, `:trigger-event`, `:trace-events`, `:sub-runs`, `:effects`) — and `re-frame.epoch.assembly` does NOT stamp a `:kind` on the record (codex).
- The mirror table exists only because the Node bundle of pair-MCP cannot load `re-frame.projection` and today must hand the walker BOOLEANS: `elision.cljs:142-200` (`elision-opts-edn`: boolean → profile via `mcp-tool-profile` → booleans via `profile-size-opts` → walker) and `walk-required?` (:102-140). story-mcp (`egress.cljc:157-166`) runs in-process and already calls `rf/project-egress` with a profile at :332-337 for its other value shape. Xray / Story resolve the framework table directly (`xray config.cljc:722`, `story config.cljc:549`).
- `tools/**` requiring `re-frame.elision`: Story `assertions.cljc:74`, `error.cljc:68` (the walker) and `frames.cljc:66` (`classification-effect-defect` / `apply-classification-effects` at :691, :704 — NOT the walker; any lint must be symbol-level, not namespace-level).

## Options

**A. One door (fable recommendation, staged).** `rf/project-egress` is the only facade projection export, with a CLOSED opts map (egress.2 delivers the closure) whose every policy key lives under `:rf.egress/*`: `:rf.egress/profile`, `:frame`, `:path`, `:query-v`, `:as-of-epoch`, and per-axis overrides `:rf.egress/include-sensitive? / include-large? / include-digests? / include-fx-args? / include-runtime-db? / include-event-args?` + `:rf.egress/threshold-bytes`. The walker stays internal (`re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value`, 10 framework callers unchanged); the facade re-export at `core.cljc:2247` and manifest row `api-manifest.edn:111` go; Story's two direct walker calls migrate to `project-egress` with `:frame` / `:path`; a symbol-level residue check (an existing residue script, e.g. the pattern of `scripts/check_retired_composition_vocab.py` — codex: no new lint framework) forbids `re-frame.elision/elide-wire-value` under `tools/**` and `skills/**/preload`. Epoch records are dispatched through the door by a late-bound per-kind projector — the pattern `elision.cljc:1121-1127` already uses for `:routing/route-sub-egress-path` — with codex's two guards: the assembler STAMPS a record discriminator (`:kind :rf/epoch-record`, a record-shape change to `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` §`:rf/epoch-record`, hot-zone) so recognition is never a loose `:epoch-id` shape test, and an absent epoch artefact throws `:rf.error/epoch-artefact-missing` rather than falling back to a bare walk. `rf/projected-record` (+ `re-frame.epoch/projected-record`, the `:epoch/projected-record` late-bind key `directory.cljc:875-878`, manifest rows :141, :197) retires — coordinate with `@trace-epoch.n`, which owns that list. pair-MCP's eval forms name the profile to the app-side door, so `profile->size-opts` / `profile-size-opts` (mcp-base :56-107), `elision-opts-edn`, `walk-required?` and story-mcp `posture->elision-opts` go; mcp-base keeps `profiles` (:45) and `mcp-tool-profile` (:108); the conformance gate keeps the NAME-set pin (`egress_profile_test.clj` first deftest) and drops the table pin, replaced by a pin that pair-MCP's rendered eval source names a profile from `re-frame.projection/profiles`. The `:rf.size/*` → `:rf.egress/*` rename is the LAST stage and a separate bead (Grok; ~54 + 24 + 18 sites; the MCP wire key `include-sensitive` is untouched).

**B. Two typed doors, one normaliser (codex).** Keep `elide-wire-value` public for bare-value direct reads and `projected-record` as the explicit epoch door; share one option normaliser and presence-aware ownership (egress.1-2); migrate the tool direct reads (pair-MCP, story-mcp, Xray, preload) to `project-egress`; then decide whether the remaining epoch door still burdens users. Keep `:rf.size/*`. The mirror table shrinks as the servers pass profiles but is not deleted until its last Node-side consumer is gone.

**C. Status quo after egress.1-4.** Three doors with the written "rarely" discriminator; no facade change.

## Recommendation

**A, in the staged order below, with B's ordering guard adopted verbatim (record discriminator first; never a loose shape test; never a silent bare-walk fallback).** Regularity: the spec's own sentence — `project-egress` "names the boundary, not a record kind" (`projection.cljc:24-27`, `spec/API.md:693`) — already says epoch slot knowledge belongs BEHIND the door. The demand bar has ruled on the duplicates (0 app callers of any door; the tool calls that bypass the door do so because the door lacked the epoch arm and the servers had to render booleans). Every change is fail-closed-neutral or safer; the migration itself is the only thing that could fail open, and the closed map (egress.2) turns a stale spelling into a throw.

**The strongest counter, recorded here:** the mcp-base mirror table is pinned by a conformance gate and cannot drift, so "a copy exists" is not by itself a defect; and the Node bundle genuinely cannot load `re-frame.projection`. The answer is that under A the server no longer needs the TABLE (it names a profile and the app-side door resolves it), only the NAME SET and the boolean→profile mapping — so the pin narrows rather than disappears. If a Node-side consumer of the resolved booleans survives inspection (codex: "inspect remaining Node-side consumers before deleting a zero-framework-dependency module"), keep the table and its pin, and the rest of A still stands.

Second counter: codex's "feeding today's record to `project-egress` is not equivalent" — correct, and it is why the epoch stage stamps a discriminator and registers the EXISTING `tool_pair/projected-record` body as the per-kind projector rather than re-implementing its slot knowledge.

Sequence BEFORE `@observability.n`'s implementation (that design's `:rf.egress/local-raw` opt-in lives on this door); `@observability.n` owns the sinks, this bead owns the door.

## Implementation beads to file when ruled (each self-contained, one worker)

**Status:** Medium–High (three public projection doors + a fourth post-hoc hook for one job; the override booleans have three spellings and one of them is silently ignored by the door the docs pair it with; zero app consumers, so the cost lands on tool authors and AI agents rather than the front porch; every door is fail-closed, so the duplication costs clarity and correctness-of-teaching, not safety. ## The problem

There is one job — *take a value or record, apply the owning frame's `[:rf.runtime/elision …]` registry plus a boundary policy, return something safe to ship* — and a caller can spell it four ways, with three spellings of the policy knobs underneath:

|---|---|---|---|

Spec 015 L223-227, skills `privacy-and-elision.md` L189-191 and Conventions L825 all teach passing a profile (or an unqualified `:include-sensitive?`) to it; the key is silently dropped. |
| `(rf/project-egress v-or-record opts)` | profile → `:rf.size/*` floor (projection.cljc:190-221), then per-kind projector, then **the same walker** for every tree slot (projection.cljc:234-240); a kindless value falls straight through to the walker (:476-497) | `:rf.egress/profile` **and** the `:rf.size/*` booleans (overlay wins) | For a bare value this is `elide-wire-value` plus profile resolution — the two doors are the same function with and without the enum. `nil` profile = "raw-flags path" (:207-210). Opts map is `{:closed false}` (Spec-Schemas.md:3672). |
| `(rf/projected-record rec opts)` / `(rf/projected-history frame opts)` | per-slot → `project-egress` (tool_pair.cljc:1322-1335) → walker; then `:redact-fn` | `:rf.egress/profile` **plus unqualified** `:include-sensitive?` / `:include-large?` (re-spelled to `:rf.size/*` at tool_pair.cljc:1316-1320), `:include-runtime-db?` (:1358), `:include-fx-args?` (:1957), `:include-event-args?` (:2015) | Third spelling of the same boolean. A caller passing `:rf.size/include-sensitive? true` here is silently dropped (destructure at :1316 reads only the bare key). |
| `(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:redact-fn f}})` | `assembly/apply-redact-fn` on the already-projected copy (assembly.cljc:94-122) | a `(fn [record] record)` | A fourth, function-shaped projection door; its own warning category `:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception` (API.md:674). |

## Simpler elegant target

One door, one closed opts map, one namespace, one spelling per boolean:

```clojure
(rf/project-egress v-or-record)        ; ⇒ :rf.egress/off-box-observability, fail-closed
(rf/project-egress v-or-record opts)

;; opts — CLOSED: an unrecognised key raises :rf.error/bad-egress-opts
{:rf.egress/profile            <one of the six>   ; default :rf.egress/off-box-observability
 :frame                        <frame-id>         ; override; else the record's own :frame; else the carried
                                                  ;   scope. An EXPLICIT nil means "no frame" and fails closed.
 :path                         [...]              ; bare-value offset (direct reads)
 :query-v                      [...]              ; route-sub re-seed, as today
 :as-of-epoch                  <id>
 ;; advanced, per-axis overrides — the profile is the floor, an explicit key wins
 :rf.egress/include-sensitive? :rf.egress/include-large? :rf.egress/include-digests?
 :rf.egress/include-fx-args?   :rf.egress/include-runtime-db? :rf.egress/include-event-args?
 :rf.egress/threshold-bytes    <int>}
```


Dispatch stays what it is — a record's `:kind` selects a private projector; a kindless value is walked whole — with one addition: the epoch artefact registers its per-kind projector through the late-bind directory (the pattern elision.cljc:1121-1127 already uses for `:routing/route-sub-egress-path`), so an `:rf/epoch-record` handed to `project-egress` is projected by the code that is today `tool_pair/projected-record`. No record-shape change; `:redact-fn` becomes ordinary composition at the caller.

| Xray clipboard (6) | `(egress-value v {:frame observed})` → hand-rolled floor + `js/Object.` sentinel | `(rf/project-egress v {:frame observed :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-tool})` — `observed` may be nil and fails closed by contract |

## Why this is better (ethos)

- **Regularity over cleverness** (Principles L18-22): "there is one obvious way to do a thing." Today the obvious way depends on the shape in hand — value → walker, observation record → `project-egress`, epoch record → `projected-record` — and the spec itself says `project-egress` "names the boundary, not a record kind" (projection.cljc:24-27). Taking that sentence seriously means the boundary is *one* function and record kinds are dispatch data, epoch records included.
- **Data before magic** (L46-50): the profile is a datum from a closed enum; the booleans are the interpreter's knobs. A single namespace (`:rf.egress/*`) for every knob makes the opts map describable by one Malli schema and readable without knowing that a privacy flag hides under `:rf.size`. EP-0007 rule 3 (one name per fact) is currently violated three times over for `include-sensitive?`.
- **No silent swallow** (L81-85; Conventions §No silent swallow): a walker that ignores `:rf.egress/profile`, an epoch projector that ignores `:rf.size/include-sensitive?`, and an open opts map together mean a *recognised* policy key can vanish without a signal. On a privacy surface the swallowed key so far happened to fall on the safe side; the design should not rely on luck. A closed map plus one spelling is what makes the wrong call impossible rather than merely harmless.
- **Low hidden context** (L87-93): `:frame nil` silently resolving to the ambient frame is hidden context with three documented leaks and three sentinel workarounds. Making explicit nil mean "no frame" removes the ambient fallback from a path a tool can reach.
- **Clojure ethos**: one function over data, with `comp` where the framework currently ships configuration. `:redact-fn` is `comp` wearing a `configure!` key, its own warning category and twelve test files; a forwarder that wants an extra scrub writes `(-> r (project-egress opts) scrub)`. `projected-history` is `mapv`.
- **The demand bar** (README ethos bar): after ~200 opportunities `projected-history` has 0 callers, `:redact-fn` has 0 installers, `rf/sensitive?` has 0 direct tool callers. The bar has ruled.

Honest costs. Security surfaces earn conservatism, so each change is checked for fail-open: removing a walker's silent key does not ship more data (a dropped opt could only ever have *widened* egress); an explicit `:frame nil` fails closed where today it falls to an ambient frame — strictly safer; the default profile `:rf.egress/off-box-observability` is the same all-false floor the 1-arity call already resolves to; deleting `:redact-fn` cannot widen egress (it only ever removed more, and nobody installs it); the fail-closed predicate is stricter than today's `(true? …)`. The one thing that could fail open is the *migration* itself — a tool that keeps calling the internal walker with the old bare keys. The closed opts map turns that into a thrown `:rf.error/bad-egress-opts`, and the `tools/** ↛ re-frame.elision` lint catches the home-namespace bypass (assertions.cljc:74, error.cljc:68). The zero-dep MCP bundle is a real constraint: it keeps one mirror *predicate* (`sensitive-event?`), but no longer needs the mirror *table*, because the server hands the profile to the app-side boundary instead of rendering booleans for the walker.

## Codex Thoughts

### Verdict: consolidate the policy vocabulary; fix ownership before merging every projector

This identifies an important ergonomic problem: callers must know which boundary accepts which flag spelling, and some documented options do nothing. I support making `project-egress` the ordinary application/tool boundary. I do not treat the walker, epoch projector, and custom transformation as interchangeable functions.

The most actionable defect is frame selection. The [walker](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc) uses `(or (:frame opts) (resolve-current-frame))`; [project-egress](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc) also seeds a record frame using truthiness rather than key presence. Consequently explicit `:frame nil` cannot reliably mean “no governing frame.” Xray and [derivation egress](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/derivation/egress.cljc) carry dead-frame objects to express that perfectly reasonable request. Fix both resolution layers using presence-aware precedence: explicit option, including nil; otherwise a recognized record's owner, including an explicitly frameless record; otherwise the carried scope for a bare-value call. An unknown or destroyed explicit owner must not borrow another frame. Preserve deliberate raw opt-in. This removes workarounds by clarifying one existing concept, not by adding a policy framework.

### Diagnosis and viable options

The six profiles describe different boundaries even where their current boolean defaults coincide; retain them. Likewise, MCP's wire `include-sensitive` spelling is a transport convention, not another Clojure API to homogenize. Profile overrides are defaults-plus-explicit-overrides, not an immutable privacy “floor”: an explicit true can widen output.

For ordinary boundary calls, choose one inclusion-key vocabulary and one normalizer, with a documented default profile and loud diagnostics for retired/misspelled policy keys. The proposed `:rf.egress/*` vocabulary is coherent; retaining the current `:rf.size/*` spelling everywhere is also viable and cheaper. Renaming alone is not the benefit: identical interpretation at every boundary is. Keep the internal path/query-aware walker. Migrate external walker calls to the boundary without banning legitimate framework use.

An epoch merge is a separate decision. [Epoch assembly](../../../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc) calls its output an epoch record but does not actually stamp the `:kind` consumed by the generic projector. [projected-record](../../../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc) knows partitions, trigger arguments, effect arguments, and trace/subscription slots. Feeding today's record to `project-egress` is not equivalent. Either retain that explicit typed door while sharing option normalization, or first introduce an unambiguous record discriminator/adapter and preserve all slot-specific behavior behind it. Do not recognize arbitrary user maps by a loose `:epoch-id` shape test, or silently fall back to a bare walk when an optional epoch projector is unavailable. `projected-history`, by contrast, is straightforward `mapv` convenience over raw history and can be retired independently.

### Implementation and acceptance

Start with ownership semantics and option normalization, migrate Pair/Story/Xray direct reads, then decide whether the remaining epoch door still burdens users. Test explicit nil under a different live ambient frame, dead owners, record-owned versus overridden frames, all six profiles, and preservation of `:path`, `:query-v`, and epoch-specific omissions. Compare actual tool outputs, not just facade names.

Removing `:redact-fn` is defensible given the measured absence of application installers, but ordinary composition is not automatically equivalent to a globally installed post-projection transform. Its current throwing behavior falls back to built-in output. If removed, explicitly update each affected egress boundary and document that policy; do not change raw replay storage.

The [MCP mirror](../../../../tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/egress.cljc) can shrink as host-side calls accept profiles directly, but inspect remaining Node-side consumers before deleting a zero-framework-dependency module. No new lint framework is required. The ethos win is one understandable policy contract with explicit ownership, while preserving real projection knowledge behind small composable functions.

**Fail-open risk.** No new one, but the Story catch-returns-raw path is not named by any of .5–.8 and would need its own bead.

**Who holds it.** Codex leans B; nobody argued C except as the free baseline. The demand bar (`Principles.md:124-131`) cuts against C: after ~200 opportunities the epoch door has one caller, and it is a tool that had to invent the bare-key spelling to use it.

## Recommendation

**A**, in the three stages above, filed as three sequential implementation beads under rf2-kuky, with stage 4 filed separately and dispatched only after stage 3 merges. The reasons are the posture's: a redundant spelling is deleted, not kept as the documented alternative, and here the three spellings are not even alternatives — they are one function reached through an enum, through a record shape, and through text rendered by a server that had to reconstruct the enum's meaning to call it. *Regularity over cleverness* says shape belongs in dispatch data; *No silent swallow* (`Principles.md:81-85`) is what .6 delivers and what the Story catch fix protects; *Low hidden context* is why the ambient-frame fallback goes under .5; and *The demand bar* has ruled on the epoch door's public life. The stage-3 table deletion should be **unconditional**: I inspected every Node- and JVM-side consumer of the resolved booleans and found exactly the two renderers A replaces. The Story profile is **`:rf.egress/local-redacted`** (identical floor to today's call; on-box). Stage 4 is **in but last and separable** — its whole value is that the closed map becomes describable by one namespace; striking it loses no safety. If Mike prefers B, stages 2 and 3 are unchanged and stage 1 is the catch fix alone; if C, the only new filing is a bug bead for the Story catches, which should exist under any ruling.

**On ruling A, file:** (1) `api(egress): retire the walker facade export; Story assertions/error through project-egress; residue check` — hot-zone API.md, Tool-Pair.md, 009; (2) `api(egress+epoch): stamp :kind :rf/epoch-record; late-bound epoch projector behind project-egress; retire rf/projected-record` — hot-zone Spec-Schemas, Tool-Pair; owned jointly with rf2-kuky.55 (its option F folds in); (3) `api(egress): servers name the profile; retire the mcp-base mirror table; narrow the wire-vocab pin` — hot-zone Tool-Pair; (4) `api(egress): :rf.size/include-*? → :rf.egress/include-*?` — hot-zone Conventions, API.md, Spec-Schemas, 009, P4, blocked on (3). All four blocked on .5, .6, .7 and sequential among themselves. Close .9 citing their ids.

## What is already settled (no decision needed)

- **rf2-kuky.5** (bug, P2, open): explicit `:frame nil` fails closed in both the walker (`elision.cljc:1128`) and `project-egress`'s truthiness seed (`projection.cljc:574`); the three dead-frame sentinels go (two verified at tip: `xray egress.cljs:34-47`, `local_render.cljc:106-187`). Dispatchable now.
- **rf2-kuky.6** (bug, P2, open): closed walker opts, `projected-record` reads `:rf.size/*`, teaching fixed (`spec/015:218-227`, Conventions). The Story catch hazard above should be appended to it as a note, not a change of scope.
- **rf2-kuky.7** (task, P2, open): `projected-history` (0 callers; `core.cljc:2578`, `directory.cljc:875`) and the `:redact-fn` family deleted.
- **rf2-kuky.8** (chore, P3, open) and **rf2-kuky.10** (chore, P3, open): predicate aliases; doc drift. Land regardless.
- **rf2-kuky.55** (decision, P3, open): the epoch namespace's parallel doors. It does not itself rule on `projected-record`; its option F drops the duplicate manifest rows. Stage 2 here is the one place the record door's retirement is decided; .55 follows.
- **rf2-kuky.22** (decision, P2, open): its `:rf.egress/local-raw` process-default entry lives on `project-egress` and is blocked on **.5**, not on this collapse. This ruling need not wait for .22, and .22 need not wait for it; only the profile name is shared, and it is already in the closed enum.
- Not in scope: the MCP wire key `include-sensitive` (transport convention, `mcp-base sensitive.cljc`); the event-level `strip-sensitive` / `scrub-snapshot` mechanism; the six profiles (each has a live consumer); the framework's 15 internal walker calls.

## Provenance

- Tip `6d513ba07fd3bb021ad3e36c6d1ba1b2ad9ae0b4` == `origin/main`, clean tree, 2026-09-06 16:19:31 AUSEST. 218 commits since the bead's cited tip `3fbd3a9ede`; the facade rows moved (`core.cljc` 2247→2313, 2262→2328, 2493→2559, 2512→2578; manifest 138→137, 141→140, 196-197→194-195; preload 3108→3126) but the walker, projector and epoch bodies read at the lines cited here are the ones the bead describes.
- Read: `bd show --json` for rf2-kuky.9 (description 12.9k, notes 41.8k, acceptance criteria), rf2-kuky, .5, .6, .7, .8, .10, .55, .22 (statuses above; none `in_progress`); `bd dep tree rf2-kuky.9`.
- Source read in full or at the cited ranges: `projection.cljc`, `elision.cljc:1060-1160`, `epoch.cljc:699-739`, `tool_pair.cljc:1268-1345, 2025-2081`, `core_epoch.cljc` hooks, `directory.cljc:871-878`, `assembly.cljc` (grep `:kind`), Xray `egress.cljs`, pair-MCP `elision.cljs`, `epoch_egress.cljs:100-200`, `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, story-mcp `egress.cljc:120-215, 325-340`, Story `assertions.cljc:60-470`, `error.cljc:100-130`, mcp-base `egress.cljc`, `egress_profile_test.clj`, `wire-vocab/deps.edn`, `test.yml:5774-5836, 6556`, `spec/015:212-260`, `Spec-Schemas.md:3675-3705, 4427-4446`, `Tool-Pair.md:881-889`, `009:3014`, `api-manifest.edn` rows, `Principles.md:18-22, 46-50, 81-93, 124-131`.
- Counts: ripgrep-backed search over `tools/`, `skills/`, `implementation/` src (tests excluded), paren-prefixed for calls. `re-frame.elision` requires under `tools/**` src: 3; under `skills/**/preload`: 0. `profile-size-opts` consumers: 4 (two mirror, two framework).
- Not executed, reasoned from source: the kindless-walk fail-open on an unstamped epoch record; the Story catch-returns-raw behaviour under a thrown closed-map error. Not re-verified: the `derivation/egress.cljc` sentinel .5 names (my grep pattern did not match it; .5 owns it); the coverage addendum's page list (carried as the addendum's count, "roughly 45 files").

## Codex Recommendation

Recommend **A, with corrected staging and preservation of each surface's policy**. Include the `:rf.egress/*` policy-key rename as a separate final change; retire the MCP mirror table after its two consumers migrate; use `:rf.egress/local-redacted` for Story; file the epoch integration once, jointly with rf2-kuky.55. This supports the target, but not the proposed sequence verbatim. Independent inspection was against source SHA `87a9d6d571746b37c74cdda000e93ca1cf0fe6f9`, checked again at `2026-09-06T16:38:19.9284515+10:00`. The complete rf2-kuky.9 description and 41,813-character notes were read in chunks. Beads .5–.8, .10, .22 and .55 remain open; the inspected implementations still contain the old behavior.
DOSSIER ATTACHMENT 2026-09-06 18:34:33 AUSEST (ai/decisions/rf2-kuky.9.one-project-egress-door.md, now deleted) -- piece 3 of 3, continued:
The strongest reason to consolidate is concrete caller work. [Pair's direct-read renderer](../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/elision.cljs) converts a permission decision to a profile, resolves that profile through the mirror, then serializes booleans for application-side evaluation. [Story-MCP](../../tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/egress.cljc) performs the same resolution for app-db while already sending a profile to `project-egress` for derived trees. [The generic projector](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc) already delegates an ordinary value to the same path-aware walker. Naming the profile at the application boundary removes real translation and teaching work. The [privacy skill](../../skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md) currently recommends a walker call carrying a profile that the walker ignores. My source search found no projection calls in example Clojure/ClojureScript files: the benefit is primarily reliable tool authoring and agent instructions, with little direct change to SPA application code.

The strongest alternative is the original bead's B: keep an explicit epoch operation with a shared option normalizer. This is stronger than merely retaining the walker export. [Epoch projection](../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc) preserves bookkeeping, roots app-db slots separately, treats runtime-db separately, and independently suppresses trigger arguments, effect arguments and subscription values. A generic tree walk cannot replace those semantics. Retaining B would avoid a record-shape and dispatch change; retaining C would also avoid migration costs, and the [existing conformance test](../../tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/egress_profile_test.clj) demonstrates that the mirror is maintained deliberately. Nevertheless, those distinctions can remain in one private epoch projector. Given the existing record dispatch and the concentrated tool consumers, I judge that one documented boundary earns this bounded consolidation. Counting exports alone would not justify it.

First correct the staging. Stage 1 currently deletes `rf/elide-wire-value`, but stage 3 owns the migration of Pair-MCP, Xray, Story-MCP and the preload that still call it. These intermediate commits would leave tools referring to a removed function. Migrate all direct reads and Story's error handling first; then remove the facade export and enforce the residue check when the final caller is gone, or perform those operations atomically. This is ordinary migration sequencing, not a compatibility alias. Keep the epoch integration separate and serialize shared specification edits. A source search must cover aliases and generated eval strings, not only fully qualified source calls.

Second, distinguish an upgraded core with a missing epoch artefact from an older core. [Current dispatch](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc) treats both absent and unknown kinds as bare values. Therefore even a newly stamped epoch record sent to an older core is not protected by the proposed new missing-projector throw: that branch does not exist there. Require compatible core/epoch/preload/tool versions for the changed epoch exporter and coordinate their migration. Pre-alpha needs no general negotiation system or fallback implementation, but a release note alone is not evidence that a mixed-version export is safe. On the supported runtime, a recognized epoch kind without its projector must throw before returning payload data. [Assembly](../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc) currently stamps no `:kind`; add an explicit discriminator rather than recognizing arbitrary maps by their `:epoch-id`.

Third, preserve policy distinctions. [Pair's epoch exporter](../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/epoch_egress.cljs) deliberately uses `off-box-tool` plus a sensitive override: it does not select `local-raw`, because large, runtime, effect and event payloads remain independently controlled. Keep those axes independent after normalization. Resolve defaults once, overlay only keys actually supplied, and pass each internal helper its applicable options; forwarding every epoch-specific option into a newly closed walker map would introduce errors. Preserve `:path`, routing's `:query-v` reseeding, explicit frame ownership and epoch handle context. Existing epoch code takes the record's frame directly, so the generic door's explicit-frame override also needs a deliberate acceptance case.

For [Xray console/clipboard egress](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/egress.cljs), choose `:rf.egress/off-box-observability` to retain today's false digest setting. The dossier's `off-box-tool` substitution enables digests and changes output and work; that is a separate policy choice. Story's `local-redacted` selection does match its existing flags. Both [assertion](../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc) and [error](../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/error.cljc) catches currently return raw input. Change those failure returns to `:rf/redacted`, preserving the error helper's explicit structural-metadata pre-check. The mirror deletion is an agreed end-state, supported by finding just the two production resolver consumers above; keep the profile-name pin and test rendered calls in Pair's CLJS suite.

Acceptance should compare actual projected outputs: bare slices and route subscriptions; every epoch payload family; independent opt-ins; explicit nil under another live frame; missing projector; Story projection failure; and unchanged raw replay records. Update the existing [epoch orthogonality tests](../../implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_egress_redaction_cljs_test.cljc), and exercise generated Pair forms against the supported runtime rather than checking names alone. Retire old policy spellings without aliases, keeping wire marker and MCP argument vocabulary distinct. This review ran no builds or runtime tests; leak paths and migration effects above are source-derived conclusions, not executed reproductions. It also does not independently certify the dossier's entire prose-file census.
close_reason: RULED: A — one rf/project-egress door with a closed :rf.egress/* opts map; the walker facade export, rf/projected-record and the mcp-base mirror table retire in four sequential stages in codex's corrected order (migrate callers first); Story on-box = :rf.egress/local-redacted, Xray egress-value = :rf.egress/off-box-observability, table deletion unconditional, rename in and last (P4); follow-ups rf2-kuky.88, rf2-kuky.90, rf2-kuky.92, rf2-kuky.93 (rf2-kuky.92 sequenced behind rf2-kuky.82). Closed --force: the .5/.6/.7 blockers gate the work, which the stage beads carry, not the ruling.

title: api(egress): delete the three tool-side `sensitive-event?` aliases; `rf/sensitive?` fails closed
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from egress.md (ref egress.4); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`spec/API.md`'s `sensitive?` row and `spec/Privacy.md:81` say `rf/sensitive?` is "the framework-published predicate every forwarder composes against", replacing per-consumer reimplementations. At tip it has 0 direct tool callers; each tool reaches it through its own one-line alias:

- Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc:789-797` `sensitive-event?` → `(rf.privacy/sensitive? ev)`; sole caller `suppress-sensitive?` at :810.
- Story `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc:666-674` `sensitive-event?` → `(rf.privacy/sensitive? ev)`; sole caller `suppress-sensitive?` at :710.
- pair-MCP `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/sensitive.cljs:21-26` `sensitive-event?` → `(rf.mcp-base.sensitive/sensitive-event? ev)`; callers in the same file at :68 and :95.

The prompt counted four; at tip there are three thin delegations. The fourth candidate, `re-frame.mcp-base.sensitive/sensitive-event?` (`sensitive.cljc:174-187`), is NOT an alias: it is the zero-framework-dependency Node-bundle mirror with fail-closed semantics (truthy non-boolean ⇒ drop + log + `malformed-count`), which the review keeps.

The framework predicate itself (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:38-41`) is `(true? (:sensitive? trace-event))` — a malformed truthy stamp (`"true"`, `:yes`) passes as NON-sensitive, the fail-open reading mcp-base's docstring (`sensitive.cljc:144-172`) explicitly refuses.

## Evidence

Predicate census (`^\(defn-? (sensitive\?|sensitive-event\?|sensitive-stamp\?|include-sensitive\?|suppress-sensitive\?)`, non-test src): `privacy.cljc:38`; mcp-base `sensitive.cljc:144, :174`; pair-MCP `sensitive.cljs:21`; story-mcp `args.cljc:65` (`include-sensitive?` — parses the MCP arg, not a stamp predicate, keep); Story `config.cljc:655, :666, :688`; Xray `config.cljc:781, :789, :799`. Direct callers of `rf/sensitive?` / `rf.privacy/sensitive?` in tools: the two aliases only. `skills/re-frame2/references/tooling/story-recorder.md:46` teaches `(rf/sensitive? trace-event)` — the teaching is right, the code goes round it.

## Target API

```clojure
;; privacy.cljc — fail-closed, one predicate
(defn sensitive? [trace-event]
  (and (map? trace-event)
       (let [s (:sensitive? trace-event)]
         (cond (true? s) true (false? s) false (nil? s) false :else true))))
;; Xray / Story: (rf.privacy/sensitive? ev) inline in suppress-sensitive?; the alias defns go.
;; pair-MCP: call rf.mcp-base.sensitive/sensitive-event? directly at :68 and :95; the alias goes.
```

mcp-base keeps `sensitive-stamp?` / `sensitive-event?` (its bundle cannot load `re-frame.privacy`) and its `malformed-count` / `reset-malformed-count!` counters — those are envelope bookkeeping and out of scope (the fable proposed demoting the counters to private/test; leave them, zero cost).

## Corroboration

One-reviewer (fable §The problem para 4, §Simpler elegant target "Predicate" row). Codex did not comment on the predicate. The fail-closed hardening matches a ruling already made for mcp-base (`sensitive.cljc:144-172` docstring) and can only drop MORE, never less.

## Deletion list

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc:789-797`; `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc:666-674`; `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/sensitive.cljs:21-26` (+ the "Delegates to …" docstring sentences at :85 and :115 that name the alias).

## Consumers to migrate

Xray `config.cljc:810`; Story `config.cljc:710`; pair-MCP `sensitive.cljs:68, :95`. Tests naming the aliases (re-measure with `git grep -n "sensitive-event?" -- tools/*/test`): expect Xray `trace_collector` tests, Story `config` / `recorder` tests, pair-MCP `sensitive_test.cljs` / `strip_sensitive` tests.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/API.md` `sensitive?` row (:728 region) — "replaces per-consumer reimplementations" becomes true; add "fail-closed: a non-boolean truthy stamp counts as sensitive" (hot-zone, one line); `spec/Privacy.md:81` same sentence; `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Privacy (:2809-2846) if it states the `(true? …)` semantics (grep `true?` in that range; hot-zone).
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1155` example — add a malformed-stamp line.
- Skills: `story-recorder.md:46` unchanged.
- Tests to add: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/privacy_test` (or the nearest privacy suite): `(rf/sensitive? {:sensitive? "true"})` ⇒ true, `{:sensitive? :yes}` ⇒ true, `{:sensitive? false}` / `{}` / non-map ⇒ false; Xray and Story `suppress-sensitive?` tests still green.
- `spec/api-manifest.edn`: `re-frame.core/sensitive?` row unchanged; Xray / Story config manifests — if `sensitive-event?` is rowed in a tool manifest (`tools/xray/spec`, `tools/story/spec`), delete the row.
- Migration README: none.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

No hot-zone file beyond one-line touches to `spec/API.md` / `spec/009` — coordinate the line with whichever egress bead holds those files at dispatch time, or land this bead after egress.3. Parallel-safe on the tool sources.

## Risks

Strictly stricter. The only behavioural delta is a malformed stamp now suppressing in Xray / Story panels, matching what the MCP wire already does.

## Simpler elegant target

```clojure
;; Boot — the one front-porch call, now honest about a different adapter.
(rf/init! adapter-map)          ; idempotent for the SAME map; a DIFFERENT map while one is
                                ; seated throws :rf.error/adapter-already-installed
(rf/destroy-adapter!)           ; unchanged: the lifecycle inverse

;; One read, one shape.
(rf/current-adapter)            ; → the installed adapter spec map, or nil
(:kind (rf/current-adapter))    ; → :rf.adapter/reagent … (nil for a kind-less custom map)

;; Platform: host default, overridden per frame. Nothing process-wide.
(rf/make-frame {:id :app :platform :server})

;; Features: one data-shaped query.
(rf/features)                   ; → {:epoch {:maven … :require … :spec … :loaded? true} …}
(get-in (rf/features) [:epoch :loaded?])

;; Config: one write door, one read door, same nested shape; bare typos signal.
(rf/configure! {:epoch-history {:depth 100}})
(rf/current-config)             ; → {:epoch-history {…} :trace-buffer {…} :elision {…}}
(rf/configure! {:epoch-histroy {:depth 100}})   ; → :rf.warning/unknown-configure-key (dev-gated)
(rf/configure! {:myapp/thing 1})                ; → passes silently (namespaced carve-out)
```

## Why this is better (ethos)

- **Regularity over cleverness — "one obvious way".** Boot has one way today and the advanced tier undermines it: `install-adapter!` is documented as the thing `init!` is "higher-level than", yet the only difference a consumer can observe is that it throws where `init!` shrugs. Moving the throw into `init!` for the case that matters (a *different* adapter) makes the one door also the honest one, and the second door has nothing left to say.
- **No silent swallow.** Two contradictions with `spec/Conventions.md:1149`. `(rf/init! uix/adapter)` after `(rf/init! reagent/adapter)` returns `nil` and leaves Reagent seated — a recognised input, not honoured, no signal. And `configure!`'s vocabulary is closed and its keys are BARE, which is exactly the shape the rule says "reads as a typo of a real key and MUST signal"; the `API.md:930` rationale ("wrapped config can pass a composed value straight through") is the case the rule already routes to namespaced keys. `configure_test.clj:221` pins the swallow as a feature; it is a tested violation.
- **Low hidden context.** `init-platform` is ambient process state that a per-frame value overrides — behaviour "determined by visible inputs" is the frame config, and the only production host that sets a platform (`ssr-ring`) sets it there. A preset that expands to a single key is hidden context by another name.

- **The demand bar, applied retroactively.** Six shipped facade names have zero non-test consumers after 34 example boots, four tools, two scaffolds and a Ring host: `install-adapter!`, `adapter-disposed?`, `init-platform`, `:ssr-server`, `feature-loaded?`, `require-feature!`. Principles §The demand bar says a surface ships for a *named* consumer; the README's ethos bar says zero consumers after 200+ opportunities is the bar ruling retroactively. The `spec/api-manifest.edn:88-169` `:keep` justifications for every one of these rows argue from "same sitting, same door" coherence — placement — and never from a caller.
- **Data before magic; public query surfaces.** `features` is the data; the boolean and the guard are one-liners over it. `current-adapter` returning the map is the query surface; `:kind` is a key, not a second fn. Clojure's answer to "I only want one field" is `get`, not a projection Var per field.
- **Honest costs.** (i) `(:kind (rf/current-adapter))` is four characters longer at one Xray site. (ii) A custom adapter without `:kind` now reads `nil` where it read `:custom` — arguably more honest, and every shipped adapter carries `:kind`. (iii) Losing `init-platform` means a JVM test that wants `:client` semantics passes `:platform :client` on its frame — the two test files that use it (`init_platform_test.clj`, `cofx_cljs_test.cljc:917`) become frame-config tests. (iv) `require-feature!` gave a boot-time failure instead of a first-call failure; the app that wants that writes `(assert (get-in (rf/features) [:epoch :loaded?]))` — one line, no framework name.

## Grok Thoughts

**Bother handling?** Yes. The porch is clean (34/34 example boots are `(rf/init! <adapter>/adapter)`). The advanced tier is not. I re-read `init!`: a second call with a *different* adapter is a silent no-op — `when-not (current-adapter) (install-adapter! …)` — and `boot_test.clj` only asserts the same-map case. `configure!`'s own docstring says "Unknown top-level keys silently no-op"; the keys are bare, which is exactly the shape Conventions §No silent swallow says MUST signal. There is no `rf/current-config` even though the lifecycle-verb law promises a read twin on every facade. Pair's preload `resolve`s `re-frame.epoch/current-config` by symbol because of that hole.

**Diagnosis.** Right. `install-adapter!` is documented as the throwing form `init!` is "higher-level than," but `init!` creates no frame either, so every "step between install and first frame" already fits between `init!` and `make-frame`. `current-adapter` vs `current-adapter-spec` is a projection Var for one key. `init-platform` / `:preset :ssr-server` / per-frame `:platform` are three spellings of one fact; the only production host (ssr-ring) sets the frame key. `feature-loaded?` / `require-feature!` restate `features` plus the late-bind throw every facade fn already does on first call.

**Options.** Keep `install-adapter!` as the throwing door vs fold the throw into `init!`. Fold it — one door that is also honest. Keep `require-feature!` as a boot-time assert vs delete. Delete: `(assert (get-in (rf/features) [:epoch :loaded?]))` is one line and names no framework verb.

**Recommendation.**

- `init!` throws `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed` on a *different* map while one is seated. Same map stays idempotent. Tests keep `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` (25/29 already do).

## Codex Thoughts

**Verdict: several useful small reductions, but the package is broader and riskier than “six unused facade functions.”** A caller census establishes which door the examples teach; it does not establish that installation, teardown, introspection and early capability checking are the same operation. The strong finding is that `init!` is the clear application boot door while adjacent advanced exports obscure that fact.

[Current boot](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) really does ignore a different adapter map once one is installed. Correcting that is worthwhile independently of name pruning. Define idempotence against the installed adapter specification—not merely `:kind`, since two adapters can share a kind but have different functions. Also decide explicitly what hot reload means when function values in an adapter map are redefined: such a map is different, and refusing it requires a deliberate destroy/re-init cycle. That behavior should be taught, not discovered through a surprising boot exception. Keep the actual seating, generation and rollback logic in [the existing adapter owner](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc); do not duplicate it in the facade.

One adapter-spec read is enough. The proposed map-returning `current-adapter` is sensible, with kind checks expressed as `(:kind ...)`; retaining `current-adapter-spec` and removing the projection is an equally viable, smaller-semantic-change alternative. Choose one, not both plus a new `adapter-kind`. If repurposing `current-adapter`, sweep all internal and external callers: truthiness checks still work, but keyword comparisons can silently stop working. [Story's substrate boundary](../../../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/substrate_boundary.cljc) provides a real consumer for the function map. Preserve nil during disposal and generation-safe destruction. Demoting facade-only installation and disposed-state helpers is reasonable; their owning implementation seams remain useful.

I support retaining `features` as the one public capability inventory and deriving a boolean with ordinary lookup. However, `require-feature!` is not equivalent to waiting for the first operation: it offers **early** failure, and the inventory supports inspection without executing that operation. This distinction should be acknowledged even if its low observed demand warrants pruning the helper. An `assert` is not necessarily an always-enabled production substitute; applications needing an early production check should make an explicit check. Do not delete the inventory itself just because most examples load their dependencies correctly.

The platform reduction is defensible: one host default plus an explicit frame override covers the observed calls, and a one-key `:ssr-server` preset adds little. Verify both effect/coeffect gating and SSR hydration's platform check, including CLJS-on-Node, before removing the mutable host marker. It is not only two fixture files that consult this fact.

A config readback has an actual tool consumer and can improve ergonomics, but keep it modest: report process configuration in the write map's shape, distinguish absent optional subsystems, and do not fabricate per-frame effective values or a transactional snapshot. A development warning for unknown bare keys is useful feedback; it should reuse existing diagnostic conventions, not grow a configuration policy framework.

Land these as separate changes: boot honesty and export pruning first, map-shaped readback next, platform cleanup last. The goal is an obvious boot sequence with trustworthy inspection, not an ever larger project to make every lifecycle noun perfectly symmetric.

This is an independent source review at `f1660fa43220d36d4cd6a759c627bb9634967935`, timestamped by the clock tool **2026-09-06 07:05:15 UTC**. I read rf2-kuky.4's complete description and notes through `bd show --json`, checked related statuses, and searched implementation, tools, examples, testbeds and skills. Changes since this dossier's tip touch beads and unrelated pattern documents, not the boot code cited here. rf2-kuky.1/.2/.3 and .55 remain open; rf2-323z, rf2-i6kh, rf2-kuky.33 and rf2-2hpxo are closed.

One adapter map serves the actual consumers well. [Story's boundary](../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/substrate_boundary.cljc) reads `:flush-render!` to establish a render-commit capability; [Story-MCP](../../tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/lifecycle.cljc) checks whether variant execution can allocate a frame; [Xray](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs) needs the adapter kind to refuse an incompatible shell renderer. These are different questions with clear expressions over one public map. Preserve the exact installed map, including custom function slots, and return nil during terminal disposal. An installed kindless map remains present even though its `:kind` lookup is nil; presence checks must inspect the map. Retaining `current-adapter-spec` as the survivor is viable, but `current-adapter` names the returned thing more directly.

Installation and initialization are **not identical operations**, even after rf2-kuky.1. [Core's `init!`](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) also reseeds three framework registrations and returns nil; [the owner's `install-adapter!`](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc) returns the map and rejects even a repeated installation of the same adapter. Keep that strict primitive and its generation/rollback machinery internally. Likewise, removing the public `adapter-disposed?` alias must retain the breadcrumb that distinguishes never-installed from destroyed delegation errors. None of this requires an additional application boot door.

The companion rf2-kuky.1 notes identify the missing Story fixture evidence precisely. [Its fixture](../../tools/story/test/re_frame/story/play/substrate_boundary_cljs_test.cljc) destroys only after each test, while `committing-adapter` adds `:flush-render!` to plain-atom without changing its canonical kind. An adapter inherited from another namespace can therefore survive the first `init!` and lack the required capability. Fix setup isolation in that prerequisite and verify the first test independently. Teach rf2-kuky.1's proposed same-kind rule accurately: it preserves the seated map; it does not install changed function slots. Actual adapter replacement requires destroy/re-init. Hook-routing equivalence alone is not evidence that two maps offer identical capabilities.

Keep [the feature inventory](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/features.cljc); remove its two convenience exports. This deliberately loses `require-feature!`'s early, structured preflight error, which first-operation failure does not replace. A caller needing that timing can explicitly inspect the entry and throw using its coordinate data. Do not recommend an elidable assertion as the production substitute. Also, an unknown key's ordinary lookup yields nil, whereas `feature-loaded?` currently yields false. Update the resource skill examples to teach the inventory lookup without claiming identical return contracts.

Add config readback for the [pair preload's health query](../../skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs), with the existing nested write shape and process settings only. The existing [epoch reader](../../implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc) is already explicitly public, so describing its use as private-API access overstates the defect. The improvement is giving tools one supported facade call that handles optional availability. Publish optional readers through late-bind hooks; omit unavailable subsystem keys, and read trace retention from its [process default](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc), not a frame ring. Do not promise atomic snapshot or wire-serializable output: epoch configuration can contain `:redact-fn`. Strike the unearned `describe-config` promise. Deferring this addition and retaining the current public reader is a defensible cheaper alternative; symmetry alone would not justify it.

Platform consolidation is supported by actual hosts: [Hicasso's renderer](../../implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs) already forces `:platform :server` on each request frame, and Ring and the SSR examples supply the same key. Preserve explicit client/server overrides and existing host defaults. Removing the process setter and one-key preset is reasonable, but it changes the defaulting model for untagged frames and deserves its own final slice.

The strongest case for **B or C** is the [written introspection contract](../../spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md#adapter-introspection): a small informational discriminator, a capability map, a lifecycle predicate and an early dependency guard communicate distinct intentions. Keeping them is coherent and avoids silent keyword-comparison migrations. I still prefer A under the pre-alpha posture: the map preserves useful capability access, ordinary lookup keeps branch code readable, and the strict lifecycle distinctions remain in their owner. The [manifest's placement rationale](../../spec/api-manifest.edn) should not substitute for this usability judgment.

Implement the four bounded slices already outlined, after rf2-kuky.1. Focus checks on JVM/CLJS boot idempotence and disposal, Story fixture isolation and commit counts, Xray's incompatible-substrate refusal, production feature inventory and optional-module isolation, config write/read plus absent-module cases, and per-frame fx/cofx gating through Node SSR and browser hydration. Update the API/006 contracts, Xray's embedding specification, manifest and relevant skill examples with each slice. Do not close rf2-uimu by subtraction: `register-listener!` still exists, and its mayor note explicitly preserves the joint ruling with rf2-7nk1.

No implementation, build or runtime test was performed. These conclusions establish source-level behavior and in-repository consumers, not the absence of downstream callers. Only this recommendation was appended in the mayor checkout under the user's explicit exception; implementation verification remains future work.

title: xray: :rf.xray/epoch-recorded floods :rf/xray's own queue under load — 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded in the Story feature-load gate
description:
Found while measuring rf2-avi7 (PR #9312). SEPARATE DEFECT — identical count with and without #9312, so it is neither caused nor fixed by that change, and it is NOT the frame-destroyed category rf2-avi7 is about.

npm run test:story-feature-load emits 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded console errors, all on :frame :rf/xray, all from Xray's own instrumentation loop. Two shapes (captured via a pr-str diagnostic planted in error_emit/report-unowned-error!, restored, blob cf828e0e6c167fd0d421c32de0e3b148f2b8e811 verified):

  {:error :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 101
   :last-event-id :rf.xray/epoch-recorded
   :dropped-event-ids [<101 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded>]
   :tail-event-ids    [<16 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded>]
   :rollback? false :recovery :no-recovery}

  {:error :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded :frame :rf/xray :depth 100 :queue-size 1
   :last-event-id :rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width
   :dropped-event-ids [:rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width]
   :tail-event-ids [<9 x :rf.xray/epoch-recorded> <7 x :rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width>]}

MECHANISM (to confirm): preload/install-epoch-listener! dispatches :rf.xray/epoch-recorded into :rf/xray on EVERY epoch the framework records, on ANY frame. The gate's 20-event load burst produces epochs faster than :rf/xray's drain settles, so the queue passes the depth-100 cap and the router drops events with :recovery :no-recovery. The second shape shows an unrelated Xray chrome event (edn-inspector/clear-width) being the one dropped because the queue was already full of epoch-recorded — i.e. the flood costs Xray its OWN UI events, not just redundant refreshes.

Note the handler is already a cheap conditional re-read ((if (= frame-id target) (assoc db :epoch-history …) db)) — so for every frame that is NOT the target this is a full dispatch round-trip to compute . Coalescing is the obvious direction, and there is precedent in the same namespace: :rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer is deliberately task-coalesced (rf2-wq6gx) for exactly this reason — 'so the sub fires on every push without one dispatch per trace event'. epoch-recorded never got the same treatment.

PROPOSED (not ruled): coalesce :rf.xray/epoch-recorded the way sync-trace-buffer is coalesced, and/or drop the dispatch entirely for a frame-id that is not the current :target-frame (the listener can read the target without entering the queue).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: this is a per-PR gate (test.yml, story_full_gate) and PR #9306 unmasks it by removing the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener. After #9312 lands, the gate's remaining 6 console errors are these 4 plus the 2 on rf2-88f1.
notes:
TYPO CORRECTION (shell backtick substitution ate one word when this bead was created): the sentence "so for every frame that is NOT the target this is a full dispatch round-trip to compute ." should read "...to compute the SAME db value it already had". Nothing else in the description was affected.

CORRECTION, same session, ~20 minutes after the close above: that close reason says the residual acceptance measurement would be supplied by tonight nightly full gate. IT WILL NOT BE. PR #9306 is the change that removes the masking listener, and it is NOT merged — trunk still carries that listener (measured: 8 :errors hits in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs on origin/main, control 26 for defn), so the nightly runs masked and cannot see these errors either way. The fix and its regression tests are on main and that part of the close stands; only the claimed instrument was wrong. The real instrument is a full-gate run on a tree carrying trunk PLUS #9306, and it is recorded as the release condition on rf2-kuky.18.
close_reason:
Merged as PR #9320 (rebased onto main at 816e9b82a2), same rollup and same five-clause verification as rf2-88f1.

:rf.xray/epoch-recorded is now coalesced, following the precedent already in the namespace (:rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer, task-coalesced under rf2-wq6gx for exactly this reason) rather than inventing a mechanism. New regression test epoch_pump_coalescing_cljs_test.cljs (162 lines) pins it.

THE REASON THIS MATTERED IS THE SECOND CAPTURED SHAPE, not the flood itself: an unrelated Xray chrome event (:rf.xray.edn-inspector/clear-width) was the event DROPPED, because the queue was already full of epoch-recorded. The flood cost Xray its OWN UI events, not merely redundant refreshes. A pure "too many dispatches" framing would have justified a cheaper fix that left that alive.

Confirmed separate from rf2-avi7 as the bead said: identical count with and without #9312, so it was neither caused nor fixed by that change.

SAME ACCEPTANCE CAVEAT AS rf2-88f1: the local npm run test:story-feature-load console-error count was never reported — the worker was killed by the session rate limit mid-verification. The 4 :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded this bead owns are 4 of the 6 errors remaining after #9312, and the proof that they are gone now sits with tonight nightly full gate, folded into PR #9306 hold condition.

| Fact | Door (tip) | Frame argument shape today | Returns |

| Flows, all frames | `re-frame.flows/flows-snapshot` (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:49`; facade `flows.cljc:40`) | none — every frame at once | `{frame-id {flow-id flow-map}}` (raw `@flows`) |
| One flow | `re-frame.flows/flow-meta-at` (`registry.cljc:77`; facade `flows.cljc:45`) | trailing `opts-or-frame-target`; `coerce-flow-opts` (`:56`) sniffs keyword vs frame-value vs map | `flow-map` |
| App-db schemas of a frame | `re-frame.schemas/app-schemas` (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:690`; facade `schemas.cljc:53-56`) | trailing `opts-or-frame-id`; `coerce-opts` (`:64-78`) sniffs keyword / frame-value / map | `{path schema}` |
| One schema / its meta | `app-schema-at` (`storage.cljc:649`), `app-schema-meta-at` (`:666`) | same trailing sniff | `schema` / `{path schema frame ns line file …}` |
| Schema metas of a frame | `re-frame.schemas/frame-schema-entries` (`storage.cljc:712`; public `def` `schemas.cljc:56`; manifest tier `:implementation`; `docs/api/re-frame.schemas.md:155`) | sole positional `frame-id` | `{path meta}` — the `{id meta}` grammar shape, under a THIRD arity |
| Schema-set digest | `app-schemas-digest` (`schemas/digest.cljc:138-160`) | same trailing sniff | `"sha256:…"` (a computation — KEPT) |
| Actor by system-id | `re-frame.machines/machine-by-system-id` (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc:197-232`) | 2-arity sniffs opts-map vs frame-value (`(and (map? x) (not (rf.frame/frame-value? x)))`) | spawned-machine id |

Costs, measured: two type-sniffing coercers (`coerce-flow-opts`, `coerce-opts`) and a `frame-value?` guard that exists only because a live frame value is itself a map (`spec/Principles.md` §Name over place predicts exactly this brittleness); Xray's schemas panel rebuilds `{path meta}` by hand from two reads (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/schemas/panel.cljs:295-309`) while `frame-schema-entries` already returns it; two spec/code drifts — `spec/API.md:945` says `machine-by-system-id`'s frame-last positional spelling "is retired to internal / test / tooling plumbing" but the code still accepts it, and `spec/API.md:551` blesses the four schema readers' "bare-frame-id arity" as public, so the two spec lines disagree about whether keyword sugar is public. Who it hurts: app authors nobody (`examples/` and `testbeds/` carry ZERO calls to any of these fns); tool authors and the pair-MCP agent carry the whole cost. Every fn here is `tooling` tier.

RULED OUT by rf2-kuky.32 (do not do): `:flow` / `:app-schema` / `:machine` as kinds of `registrations` / `handler-meta` (fable's ceiling; codex and Grok rejected it; `registrations` keeps meaning ONE storage model); a virtual `:machine` kind (machines stay the `filter` over `:event` that rf2-kuky.31 spells; `spec/005-StateMachines.md:3957-4010` "Why a lens, not a registry kind" stands); any core dispatch seam into the flows / schemas artefacts.

## Target — one frame spelling on the whole lane

```clojure
;; re-frame.flows
(rf.flows/flows {:frame f})                          ; => {flow-id flow-map}      (was (get (flows-snapshot) f))
(rf.flows/flow-meta {:frame f :id id})               ; => flow-map or nil         (was (flow-meta-at id f) / (flow-meta-at id {:frame f}))

;; re-frame.schemas
(rf.schemas/app-schemas {:frame f})                  ; => {path meta}             (was {path schema}; folds frame-schema-entries away)
(rf.schemas/app-schema-meta {:frame f :path p})      ; => meta or nil             (replaces app-schema-at + app-schema-meta-at; the schema is (:schema meta))
(rf.schemas/app-schemas-digest {:frame f})           ; => "sha256:…"              (map only; the keyword / frame-value arity is deleted)

;; re-frame.machines — the 2-arity takes the opts map ONLY (what spec/API.md:945 already says)
(rf.machines/machine-by-system-id system-id {:frame f})

;; the all-frames read composes at its one caller — no library verb
(into {} (map (juxt identity #(rf.flows/flows {:frame %}))) (rf/frame-ids))
```

Rules:
- `:frame` is REQUIRED on every side-table read — no ambient-frame default (the same no-ambient-default rule rf2-kuky.30 sets for `registrations`). A frameless or non-map call throws the EXISTING catalogued `:rf.error/no-frame-context` (`spec/009-Instrumentation.md` catalogue) with a message naming the `{:frame f …}` spelling. No new error id. Never `{}` / nil.
- `:frame` accepts exactly what `(rf/registrations {:frame f})` accepts after .30 — a frame id or a live frame value, resolved through the same helper (`resolve-live-frame-object`, `core.cljc:1632` per .30) — and the side tables, keyed by frame-id, read the resolved id's slot. One resolver, not three.
- `app-schemas` returns the `{path meta}` map (the grammar's `{id meta}` shape). The digest computes over `(update-vals … :schema)` internally; its bytes do not change.
- Nothing about `registrations` / `handler-meta` / the registrar `kinds` roster changes here. `.30` still makes `{:kind :flow}` throw `registrar-kind-not-queryable` — this bead only changes the fn names that message points at.

title: api(registry): RULING — `:flow` / `:app-schema` / `:machine` in the query grammar, + two fable-only slices
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from registry-introspection.md (ref registry-introspection.4); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Decision needed

After @registry-introspection.2 (one query map, `:source :store` XOR `:frame f`) and @registry-introspection.3 (the ten registrar-kind aliases deleted), three facts remain reachable only through bespoke doors with their own frame-argument shapes. Mike rules whether the grammar reaches them. Fable's doc proposes the ceiling; codex explicitly declined it; fable's own cross-check says "delete the registrar-kind aliases and adopt `:source` first (a two-reviewer finding), then decide whether `:flow`, `:app-schema` and `:machine` join the grammar (this doc's alone, and it needs a ruling)".

## The facts and their doors (tip 6445d0611b; unchanged since the dossier's tip by diff)

- Flows: `re-frame.flows/flows-snapshot` (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:49`; `@flows` = `{frame-id {flow-id flow-map}}`, ALL frames) and `flow-meta-at` (`:77`; `(get-in @flows [f id])`, trailing `opts-or-frame`). The registrar `:flow` kind is reserved-EMPTY (`registrar.cljc:98-146`); .2 makes a `:flow` query throw `registrar-kind-not-queryable` naming these doors. Consumers: tools code 1 + 1 (Xray `static/flows/panel.cljs`), tests ~135 lines / 24 files.
- App-db schemas: `re-frame.schemas/app-schemas` (`schemas/storage.cljc:690`; `{path (:schema meta)}` for a frame), `app-schema-at` (`:649`), `app-schema-meta-at` (`:666`; the `{id meta}` value), all with a trailing `opts-or-frame-id` that sniffs keyword-vs-map; `app-schemas-digest` (`digest.cljc:138`, a SHA — a computation, kept by both reviewers). Xray's schemas panel rebuilds the `{path meta}` map by hand from two of them (`static/schemas/panel.cljs:298-304`) — codex names this loop as the one worthwhile follow-on ("expose one frame-schema metadata collection from the existing side-table seam"). Consumers: tools code 1 / 0 / 2, tests ~105 lines / 12 files.
- Machines: an `:event` registration with `:rf/machine? true` carrying its spec under `:rf/machine`. After .3 the read is a `filter` / `(:rf/machine (handler-meta …))`. The pair-MCP wire already presents `machine` as a KIND in the same enum as `event` / `route` / `resource` (`descriptors_data.cljs:1709, 1775`), translated tool-side.
- Five frame-targeting shapes coexist on this lane today (fable §The problem): sole positional target; `{:frame f …}` map; trailing `opts-or-frame-id` with type sniffing (the schemas fns, `flow-meta-at`, and `machine-by-system-id` — `machines.cljc:197-232`, which needs a `frame-value?` test because a frame value is itself a map); no frame form; all-frames-at-once (`flows-snapshot`).

## Options

**A — codex floor + one shape (RECOMMENDED; Grok's third option in the fable doc).** Side tables stay their own doors, but take the SAME map shape as the query grammar: `(rf.flows/flows {:frame f})` → `{flow-id flow-map}` (and `(rf.flows/flow-meta {:frame f :id id})`), `(rf.schemas/app-schemas {:frame f})` → `{path meta}` in one read (Xray's loop goes), `(rf.schemas/app-schema-meta {:frame f :path p})`; the trailing `opts-or-frame-id` sniffing goes; a frameless read of a frame-scoped store throws (the loud answer `(registrations :flow)` never gave); `flows-snapshot`'s all-frames read becomes `(into {} (map (juxt identity #(rf.flows/flows {:frame %}))) (rf/frame-ids))` at the one caller, or stays if Mike wants the whole-registry snapshot as a verb. `machine-by-system-id`'s 2-arity drops the sniffing: opts map only. Machines stay a filter; pair-MCP keeps translating its friendly `machine` category. One documented home per fact; no universal registry.

**B — fable ceiling.** `:flow` and `:app-schema` become FRAME-SCOPED kinds of `registrations` / `handler-meta` (map form with `:frame` only; `:source :store` on them throws), read through the artefacts' existing late-bind seams (`:schemas/frame-schema-entries`, `storage.cljc:712`, returns exactly `{path meta}`; a new `:flows/frame-flows` hook); `:machine` becomes a read-side projection kind (`{:source :store :kind :machine}` = `:event` filtered by `:rf/machine?`, meta = the `:rf/machine` spec); `:frame` leaves `kinds`; the five side-table fns are deleted. Cost fable states honestly: `registrations` grows a kind-dispatch seam to two optional artefacts and "the frame-scoped map read is a store read, not an image resolution, so the docstring must say the map form means 'through frame f' in two senses". Codex's objection (§Follow-on): "flow snapshots and app-schema collections are different stores with meaningful frame behavior … one reliable public way to inspect each fact does not require one universal registry for every fact"; Grok's: a virtual `:machine` kind "will fight 005's 'a machine IS an event handler' commitment the first time someone tries to `clear` or image-resolve it".

**C — stop after .2 and .3.** Leave the five doors and their three frame-arg shapes as they are.

## Two smaller fable-only slices to rule in the same breath

## The problem

Every registrar kind is answered by one grammar: `(registrations kind)` → `{id meta}`, `(handler-meta kind id)` → `meta`, with `{:frame f …}` as the frame-targeted form. Beside it, each artefact grew a `<kind>-ids` / `<kind>-meta` pair. For the registrar kinds those pairs are one-line aliases (routing/registry.cljc:609-613 says so in its own comment: "The `<thing>-ids` + `<thing>-meta` enumerate pair every sibling registry carries"). For the three stores that are *not* registrar slots — flows, app-db schemas, frames — the pairs are the only door, because the generic query answers `{}` for `:flow` and `:frame` while both sit in the closed `kinds` set (registrar.cljc:144-145).

## Simpler elegant target

One grammar, two fns, one frame spelling:

```clojure
(registrations kind)                          ; {id meta} from the process store — never generation-scoped
(registrations kind pred)                     ; filtered
(registrations {:frame f :kind k :pred ?p})   ; {id meta} resolved through frame f (image kinds) or f's own store (frame-scoped kinds)
(handler-meta kind id)                        ; meta or nil
(handler-meta {:frame f :kind k :id id})
```

`kind` is the closed set `#{:event :sub :fx :cofx :interceptor :view :route :head :error-projector :resource :mutation :resource-scope :flow :app-schema :machine}`. `:flow` and `:app-schema` are **frame-scoped kinds**: the positional form throws the existing `:rf.error/registrar-query-needs-frame`, the map form reads the artefact's per-frame store through the late-bind seams that already exist (`:schemas/frame-schema-entries`, storage.cljc:712 — it returns exactly `{path meta}`; a `:flows/frame-flows` hook returning `(get @flows f)`). `:machine` is a **read-side projection** of `:event` filtered by `:rf/machine?` with meta = the `:rf/machine` spec — no new registrar slot, which keeps 005's architectural commitment; it is the kind pair-MCP already presents. `:frame` leaves the `kinds` roster: frames are not `reg-*` registrations, they are live runtime objects, and `frame-ids` / `frame-meta` stay as that lane's verbs. Positional `registrations` always reads the process store; `*generation*` is consulted only by the framework's own resolution paths, so a tool inside a sub build gets what API.md already promises and Xray's `host-registry` namespace is deleted.

(rf.routing/route-ids)  (rf.routing/route-meta id)       ;; before
(keys (rf/registrations :route))  (rf/handler-meta :route id)   ;; after (already what tools do)


(rf/resource-meta id)                                   ;; before
(:rf/resource (rf/handler-meta :resource id))           ;; after

;; 4  machines
(rf.machines/machines)  (rf.machines/machine-meta id)   ;; before
(keys (rf/registrations :machine))  (rf/handler-meta :machine id)   ;; after — one string in pair-MCP's list-form goes away

;; 5  frame-scoped kinds
(rf.flows/flow-meta-at id {:frame f})                   ;; before (or `(flow-meta-at id f)` — same fn, keyword sugar)
(rf/handler-meta {:frame f :kind :flow :id id})         ;; after

(keys (rf.schemas/app-schemas f)) + (app-schema-meta-at path f) per path   ;; before — Xray's by-hand loop
(rf/registrations {:frame f :kind :app-schema})         ;; after — the {path meta} map in one read
(:schema (rf/handler-meta {:frame f :kind :app-schema :id path}))          ;; replaces app-schema-at

;; 6  all frames (Xray static flows panel)

(into {} (map (juxt identity #(rf/registrations {:frame % :kind :flow}))) (rf/frame-ids))   ;; after

;; 3  frame-resolved image read — unchanged

**Kept:** `registrations`, `handler-meta`, `frame-generation`, `generation-diff`, `frame-ids`, `frame-meta`, `app-schemas-digest` (a real computation; its frame arg becomes `{:frame f}` only), `sub-topology` (a derived graph, not a registry read), and the live-state lane — `sub-cache-snapshot`, `resource-state`, `mutation-state`, `machine-by-system-id` (the `frame-or-opts` arity drops the keyword/frame-value sniffing: opts map only).

**Demoted:** the nine `*-algebra-view` fns have exactly one consumer, `re-frame.derivation.graph` resolving them by late-bound symbol (graph.cljc:541-547); Xray reads the composed graph (derivation_graph.cljs:382). They leave the `tooling` tier and the four JVM facade alias blocks (routing.cljc:122, resources.cljc:110, machines.cljc:249, subs.cljc:2535) and become the unrowed contributor seam Derivations.md:728/765/827 already calls "no public accessor".

## Why this is better (ethos)

- **Regularity over cleverness** (Principles.md:18) and Conventions' *One obvious way* (:1554): the question "what is registered?" has one answer shape, `{id meta}`, and one frame spelling. Fifteen names that each encode a kind in their identifier are the "multiple equivalent encodings" the principle names as a tax on tooling and generated code — and the tax was paid: pair-MCP pinned a facade name that then moved.
- **Public query surfaces** (Principles.md:52-56) names `registrations`, `handler-meta`, `frame-ids`, `frame-meta`, `sub-topology` as *the* contract. The per-kind pairs are not in that sentence; they are back-room doors onto the same tables.

[The facade](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) promises a source-store positional read, while [the underlying registrar](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc) intentionally honors the bound generation. Making `{:source :store ...}` versus `{:frame f ...}` explicit resolves that ambiguity without teaching tools private state access.

Implement this distinction at the **public inspection boundary**, not by globally changing `registrar/lookup` or `registrar/registrations`. Those internal functions also resolve event handlers, effects and subscriptions within a frame's image; removing their generation behavior would damage the isolation the tool is trying to inspect. A source-store inspection should deliberately bypass generation resolution, while a frame inspection should enter the selected frame's resolution context. Require exactly one source selector and preserve unknown-frame failure without a global fallback.

The thin route/resource/mutation/scope enumeration wrappers are good candidates for removal from the supported public surface. Keep owning-artefact helpers private where they still make runtime code clearer. Returning descriptors and using ordinary `keys`, `filter` and keyword lookup is enough; there is no need to add a query language. Direct `handler-meta` remains justified beside enumeration because looking up one descriptor need not build the collection.

I favor the narrower alternative already recorded in the cross-check. Machines can remain filtered `:event` descriptors, preserving one metadata shape and the fact that a machine is an event handler. A virtual `:machine` kind is feasible but unnecessary merely because an MCP command has that label. The tool can translate its friendly category. Likewise, flows and app-db schemas are genuinely frame-owned side tables, not sealed-image registrations. Their dedicated collection reads can be improved independently without making `registrations` mean two different storage models. Reject reserved-but-empty query kinds clearly rather than silently returning an apparently authoritative empty catalogue.

[Pair-MCP's emitted machine forms](../../../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs) should be corrected even if the API redesign is deferred. A stale symbol inside generated code is still a real consumer, not evidence of zero demand. Test the generated expression against a runtime namespace, not just its string shape.

The essential regression scenario is an inspector frame and host frame containing different registrations with the same id: store reads, host-frame reads and inspector-frame reads must each return the intended descriptor even inside an inspector subscription. That one test protects the conceptual improvement more effectively than a broad catalogue of naming assertions.
