# Registration inspection: one query grammar over explicit sources

Review date: 2026-09-05. Status: proposal only. Tracking bead: `rf2-snkw`.

## Finding

The implementation exposes generic registration reads and a growing set of feature-specific “list IDs / get metadata” pairs. These mostly project facts already present in the registrar. Their names do not reliably tell the caller which registration source will be inspected.

[Core](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc), at `registrations` and `handler-meta`, supports positional queries and frame-targeted map queries. The map form currently requires `:frame`; it is not a general query map. `registrations` additionally accepts a predicate either positionally or as `:pred` in the frame map.

Meanwhile, these feature queries repeat the enumerate/lookup operation:

| Current names | What their implementations read |
| --- | --- |
| `route-ids`, `route-meta` | [Routing registry](../../../../implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/registry.cljc): IDs and full metadata under `:route`. |
| `resource-ids`, `resource-meta` | [Resource registry](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/registry.cljc): IDs under `:resource`; the metadata getter extracts `:rf/resource`. |
| `mutation-ids`, `mutation-meta` | [Mutation registry](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_registry.cljc): IDs under `:mutation`; extracts `:rf/mutation`. |
| `scope-resolver-ids`, `scope-resolver-meta` | [Scope registry](../../../../implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/scope_registry.cljc): IDs under `:resource-scope`; extracts `:rf/resource-scope`. |
| `machines`, `machine-meta` | [Machines](../../../../implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc): filter `:event` registrations by `:rf/machine?`, then read their `:rf/machine` specs. Machines are not a separate registrar kind. |

These are not all byte-identical aliases: some return an inner specification rather than the outer registration metadata. That distinction should be documented as a data projection, not obscured by calling every result “meta.”

## Known use cases and empirical evidence

| Use case | Evidence | Requirement to retain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enumerate host definitions while an inspector runs in its own frame | [Xray host registry](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/host_registry.cljs) | A reliable source-store read independent of the inspector's bound generation. |
| Inspect exactly the definitions selected by a live frame | Core's frame-targeted reads; [Story frame composition](../../../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc), particularly variant image composition/allocation | Inspect a sealed frame generation, not a merge with whichever definitions happen to be globally registered now. |
| Get source coordinates for navigation and inspection | [Pair handler metadata](../../../../tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs) | Singular lookup, full outer metadata, namespace/image provenance and source information. |
| List machine definitions and get their specs | [Xray machine inspector](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs), `machine-definitions-value`; Pair's machine query forms | Preserve the distinction between a registered machine definition and a live machine instance. |
| Inspect resource and scope-resolver specifications | [Xray resources helpers](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc) | Access both full metadata and the inner `:rf/resource` / `:rf/resource-scope` values. |
| Filter a catalogue or enumerate IDs | The generic predicate arities and feature list helpers | Ordinary map filtering and key projection; no additional query language is necessary. |
| Find a guard/action's definition | Core's `handler-meta :machine-guard` / `:machine-action` handling | Derived source metadata for composite IDs; these are not standalone registrar rows. |
| Inspect materialized flows and frame-local schema collections | [Xray flows panel](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/flows/panel.cljs), [schemas panel](../../../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/schemas/panel.cljs) | These are different state stores/views; generic registration reads must not pretend to replace them. |

The reviewed example applications primarily register and use their own known IDs; I found no direct example-app demand for the feature getter families in the qualified-call searches. Tooling is the concrete consumer driving this finding. That is substantial demand in an AI-first library, not a reason to discard inspection.

## The source ambiguity is already costing a real tool

Core's positional docstrings describe the default process-global source store. However, [registrar](../../../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc) lookup/enumeration honor a bound `*generation*`. Xray's subscriptions run under Xray's own image generation, so its host-registry adapter directly dereferences `kind->id->metadata` to see the host definitions instead of its own.

This is not evidence that frame isolation should be weakened. It is evidence that a public inspection request should explicitly identify the source it means. More `resource-meta`-style helpers would not solve that problem.

## Proposed smaller API

Keep two operations: enumerate a kind, or look up one definition. Give both the same map grammar with exactly one source selector: `:source :store`, or `:frame f`.

```clojure
;; PROPOSED source-store forms; these maps are rejected today.
(rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :route})
(rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :route :id :app/home})

;; Existing frame concept, shared grammar.
(rf/registrations {:frame app-frame :kind :event})
(:rf/resource
  (rf/handler-meta {:frame app-frame :kind :resource :id :articles/list}))

;; Ordinary Clojure projections, not more library operations.
(keys (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :resource}))
(into {}
      (filter (fn [[_ metadata]] (:rf/machine? metadata)))
      (rf/registrations {:frame app-frame :kind :event}))
```

Under this proposal, `:source :store` explicitly bypasses inherited generation bindings. `:frame` keeps the existing precise frame resolution and failure behavior. Supplying both, or neither, is an invalid query, not an invitation to choose an ambient default. Retire positional reads, the generic predicate overloads, and the ten feature-specific public getters above. Preserve efficient singular lookup: a tool should not fetch an entire catalogue just to navigate to one definition.

Machine guard/action source queries can retain their existing derived meaning under the same source-store map grammar; they need not become new registries. Frame-targeted machine definition inspection uses the actual `:event` metadata. Extending frame-targeted derived guard/action inspection is not required to make this reduction useful.

Inner metadata keys become an explicitly supported projection contract. Full descriptors, source coordinates and provenance remain available. Feature internals may keep private helpers, and tools may retain user-friendly commands such as “list machines”; the reduction is in the library vocabulary, not the quality of its tools.

## Counterargument and migration

A named `resource-meta` helper is discoverable and hides the storage layout. Removing it makes a one-off call longer and commits the public model to the documented descriptor projection. That tradeoff is acceptable only if the generic API is genuinely usable: explicit sources, reliable data, concise examples, and stable metadata keys. “Use the private atom” is not the proposed API.

Migrate Xray's source bypass first, then frame-specific inspector queries and Pair's query generation. Preserve ID-set meaning without promising the old helpers' incidental vector order; use `(vec (keys ...))` only where a consumer actually requires a vector. Review every positional call for its intended source rather than globally rewriting it to the store: some currently rely on inherited frame resolution.

Keep frame metadata, live machine lookup, flow snapshots, app-schema collections/digests and runtime resource state separate. Those represent other facts, not alternative getters for the same row.

## Why this is more elegant

The domain has definitions, kinds, IDs, and resolution sources. It does not need a new pair of operations every time a feature defines a new kind. Clojure already supplies selection, filtering and projection over maps.

This follows the project's [public query surfaces and regularity principles](../../../../spec/Principles.md): a programmer or AI learns two operations and a data model, while an inspector can state precisely whose definitions it is observing. Fewer names are valuable here because they eliminate source ambiguity and repeated tool adapters, not merely because an API manifest gets shorter.

## Focused acceptance evidence

Exercise source-store reads from inside an image-isolated Xray subscription; compare two live frames with different selections/replacements; verify singular metadata and source navigation, machine filtering, missing IDs and invalid sources. Migrate the cited resource/machine panels and Pair queries without direct registrar-atom access. Do not redesign image composition or the registrar's storage while doing this.

## Follow-on comparison with Fable

[Fable's registry review](../fable/registry-introspection.md) independently reinforces removing per-kind projections and points to Pair's stale machine-query spellings. Its larger proposal also pulls frame-local flows/app-schemas and virtual machine kinds into the generic query grammar. I would retain the narrower boundary here: machines already have event descriptors, while flow snapshots and app-schema collections are different stores with meaningful frame behavior. The valuable common rule is one reliable public way to inspect each fact, not necessarily one universal registry for every fact.

The second reread found that Fable's later cross-check now adopts this document's explicit store/frame map grammar and keeps composite guard/action lookup derived. Those are converged recommendations; the broader side-table unification remains a separate proposal, not a prerequisite.

After .31 deletes `machines` / `machine-meta`, the read is `(into {} (filter (fn [[_ m]] (:rf/machine? m))) (rf/registrations {:source :store :kind :event}))` and `(:rf/machine (rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :event :id id}))`. pair-MCP presents `machine` as a KIND in the same enum as `event` / `route` (`descriptors_data.cljs:1709`, `:1775`) and translates tool-side: since rf2-kuky.29 closed (commit `6597fe5386`) the `:machine` kind routes through the preload's `machines-list` / `machine-describe` (`skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1139-1165`, `handler_meta.cljs:264-275`), and a frame-targeted `machine` request is refused loudly (`handler_meta.cljs:319-327`). Against widening (B / B′), from the reviewers themselves: codex — "flow snapshots and app-schema collections are different stores with meaningful frame behavior … one reliable public way to inspect each fact does not require one universal registry for every fact"; Grok — a virtual `:machine` kind "will fight 005's 'a machine IS an event handler' commitment the first time someone tries to `clear` or image-resolve it". ## Codex Recommendation

Choose **A — separate side-table reads with a common frame-map spelling — retaining `flows-snapshot`; yes to (b), yes to (c) as API demotion only**. This is worthwhile pre-alpha simplification, but the dossier overstates the equivalence of some deletions and understates actual consumers. The desired result is easier, reliable inspection, not the smallest possible function count.

The main diagnosis holds. [Core's query implementation](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) enters a frame's generation resolution, whereas [flows](../../implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc) and [schemas](../../implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc) read their own frame-keyed stores. The schema collection already contains full metadata internally; [Xray's schema panel](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/schemas/panel.cljs) needlessly reconstructs it through enumeration and repeated singular reads. One metadata collection read removes that loop and, by reading one immutable map, avoids mixing metadata from separate reads during concurrent registration. That latter benefit is an inference from the code, not a reproduced race. Qualified-call searches found no direct example/testbed callers, but these tools are substantial first-class consumers under [Public query surfaces](../../spec/Principles.md#public-query-surfaces).

Adopt A's `flows` / `flow-meta` and `app-schemas` / `app-schema-meta` map forms. Return full schema metadata in the collection and use `:schema` for the value projection. Keep direct singular lookup, including its existing path normalization. [Flow algebra tooling](../../implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/tooling.cljc) uses it at both arities, including its all-frame static projection, in addition to Xray's flows panel. The proposed `frame-ids` plus repeated per-frame reads consults two different registries and changes one atom dereference into several reads. Retaining the existing tiny accessor preserves useful power and avoids an unnecessary broad respelling.

The strongest argument for B is discoverability: an agent learns one request shape and asks for any category without learning artefact namespaces. A read facade can legitimately abstract different stores, and a virtual machine projection does not inherently violate the fact that machines are events. Those are viable designs, not architectural impossibilities. Nevertheless, B makes `:frame` select a sealed definition image for some kinds and mutable owned state for others, adds optional-artefact dispatch, and still cannot replace digest or live-state operations. comm ON TWO jq-PRODUCED ID LISTS REPORTS NO DIFFERENCE EVEN WHEN THE SETS DIFFER — CRLF AGAIN, THROUGH A NEW DOOR, AND IT FAKED AN 'ALL CLOSURES HELD' RESULT (measured 2026-09-06).

WHAT HAPPENED. The §3 closure-revert check compares the previous tick's non-closed bead ids against this tick's:
  jq -r '.[].id' prev.json | sort > a ; jq -r '.[].id' now.json | sort > b ; comm -13 a b
It printed NOTHING for appeared and NOTHING for disappeared — the reassuring answer — while wc -l read 99 and 100. A bead had reopened (rf2-88f1, an audit finding a real defect in merged code) and the check said everything was fine.

THE CAUSE is the already-recorded one reached through a different tool: jq writes CRLF on this box, so every line in both files ends \r. comm then compares 'rf2-88f1\r' against 'rf2-88f1\r' — which should match — but the CR also rides into sort's collation, and the two files' orderings disagreed enough that comm, which requires both inputs sorted in the SAME collation, walked off and emitted nothing for both directions. Two empty answers, no error, exit 0.

THE TELL, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE: the COUNTS. 99 vs 100 with an empty comm output is arithmetically impossible. Always print both line counts beside a set difference, and treat 'no difference' plus 'different totals' as an instrument failure rather than a finding. A set-difference check whose EMPTINESS is the reassuring outcome needs a control that must be non-empty — here, the shared set, which must equal the smaller count (it read exactly 99 after the fix).

THE FIX: strip CR and pin the collation before any set operation.
  tr -d '\r' < a | LC_ALL=C sort > a2   (same for b)   then comm -13 a2 b2
Verified: after stripping, comm correctly reported one appeared id and zero disappeared, and the shared set read 99.

GENERALISE IT: this now bites grep -f (recorded), pattern joins (recorded), and set operations (this). Anywhere jq output is COMPARED rather than merely displayed, strip CR first. And note the failure shape is always the same — not an error, but a clean, plausible, empty answer.

In its words: 'the brief said neither bead names spec/API.md — true, but both name spec/api-manifest*.edn, which is the same fenced holding.'

WHY THEY ARE ONE HOLDING AND NOT THREE FILES: the manifest is GENERATED from the tree by implementation/scripts/api-manifest/gen.clj, and the lint job grades API.md and both sidecars together as one drift-check. A worker that moves a public name must regenerate, which rewrites both EDN files and usually API.md's rows too. So any bead touching one of the three touches all three in practice, and two workers on any of them conflict every time.

THE FILTER THAT IS ACTUALLY RIGHT: match /spec\/API[.]md|api-manifest/ — one alternation, both halves. Matching only the first read 8 of 32 kuky beads as API-free when the true figure was smaller.

THE GENERAL SHAPE, and this is the sixth fence error in one session: a fence is not a filename, it is the SET OF FILES ONE CHANGE MOVES TOGETHER. Generated files travel with their source; a spec row travels with the manifest row it pins; a catalogue row travels with the emitter that raises it (spec/009 + spec/Conventions.md, recorded separately on rf2-kuky.43). Before dispatching a bead as parallel-safe, read its own 'Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests' section and take the UNION of what it names — do not pattern-match one representative filename out of a long description.

A MAYOR NOTE BECOMES THE NEWEST TEXT ON A BEAD, SO A WRONG ONE OVERRIDES A CORRECT DESCRIPTION FOR EVERYONE WHO READS IT NEXT (measured 2026-09-06, rf2-kuky.43).

WHAT HAPPENED. An audit reopened a bead listing four residuals. Three I verified. The fourth — skills/.../ssr-authoring.md:158, described as conflating head and body hashes — my grep could not find, so I read the line myself and concluded it was DELIBERATE v1 documentation of a known limitation rather than stale text. I appended that reading to the bead and instructed the next worker: if it is accurate at tip, record no change needed; do not reword a correct paragraph. The worker checked at source and refuted me. Head has its OWN :rf/head-hash channel (11 occurrences in spec/011; render-head-hash 5 and data-rf-head-hash 6 in implementation/ssr-ring/src, against a control of 0 for the deleted head-snapshot). spec/011 even says folding head and body into one hash WAS REVERTED.

AND IT WAS WRONG IN THE HARMFUL DIRECTION: the stale line said head drift at least SURFACES, misattributed as a body mismatch. It does not — the body channel never sees it and the client never reads :rf/head-hash — so head drift is SILENT. The reader got the opposite of the truth.

WHY THE WRONG READING WAS PLAUSIBLE, AND THIS IS THE REUSABLE PART: the line used the vocabulary that SURVIVED the recent change (:rf/render-hash) and never used the vocabulary the change DELETED (head-snapshot). So it looked untouched by the diff I was auditing. It was — its staleness PREDATED that PR and belonged to a different bead. My grep for the deleted names found nothing, and I read that null as evidence the line was CORRECT rather than as evidence I WAS SEARCHING FOR THE WRONG THING. A null from the wrong query is not a finding.

THE STRUCTURAL HAZARD: bd notes are ordered, and the loop instruction says order a bead's material by the tracker's own timestamps and treat the newest as current. That makes a mayor note MORE authoritative than the description it contradicts, by position alone. Here the DESCRIPTION was right the whole time and the newest text was wrong.

TWO RULES OUT OF IT. (1) When a bead's description and a later note disagree, break the tie by GOING TO SOURCE — never by recency, never by authorship. (2) A mayor note that CONTRADICTS a bead's own description must carry the measurement that justifies it, with a control that discriminates. Mine carried a null result from a query that could not have found the thing either way. Writing 'I could not confirm this' would have been correct and safe; writing 'therefore it is fine, leave it' was neither.

## Problem

Four SSR seams have zero consumers outside their own definition and tests, and one of them carries a false spec sentence.

1. `re-frame.ssr/install-render-to-string!` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:54` → `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:922-933`): a fn that takes a setter and calls it with `render-to-string`. Consumers: none in `examples/`, `testbeds/`, `tools/` or any adapter — only its own def, the façade re-export, one contract test (`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_end_to_end_test.clj:1404-1437`), `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:84-89`, and two Conventions sentences that cite it as an example (`spec/Conventions.md:1728,1854`). Every bundled adapter is armed by the three other paths in `emit.cljc:889-920` (plain-atom direct set, the `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` chain, the durable `:ssr/current-hiccup-emitter` slot that `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` replays at every install).
2. The three `:ssr.streaming/*` late-bind hooks (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:806-808`; directory rows `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:787-801`). The only host adapter, `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming`, requires the ns directly (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:51`) and calls `streaming/render-shell`, `streaming/render-continuation`, `streaming/build-final-payload` at `:199`, `:328`, `:401`. Consumers of the hooks: none — no `late-bind/get-fn :ssr.streaming/…` exists anywhere. `spec/011-SSR.md:1749` says "Host adapters call these three hooks in order … The Ring adapter wires them via `re-frame.ssr.ring.streaming/stream-handler`" — false at tip. The same false claim sits in `streaming.cljc:803-804`, `directory.cljc:788-789` and `ssr.cljc:123-125`.
3. The emitter's `:emit-hash?` opt (`emit.cljc:876-877`): when true and no `:render-hash` is supplied, `render-to-string` computes `render-tree-hash` internally — a second canonical-EDN walk the docstring itself warns about (`:856-866`). The `:render-hash` pass-through (`:873-875`) is the one spelling the ring pipeline uses (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:581-585`), and every direct caller of `{:emit-hash? true}` also calls `render-tree-hash` on the same tree for its payload (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:307-312`, `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:379-380`) — two walks for one hash.
4. `ssr/render-to-string` is 2-arity only (`emit.cljc:867`) while the `rf/` façade copy is 1- and 2-arity (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_ssr.cljc:24-25`): the home spelling has fewer arities than its copy.


title: api(observability): key the dev console fallback on nothing-routed-this-record, not on an empty :errors registry
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The untooled-dev console fallback (rf2-fu75) prints a promoted `:rf.error/*` record only while the corpus-wide `:errors` listener registry is EMPTY — `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:221` `(empty? @listeners)`, rationale at `:121-132` ("Registering ANY `:errors` listener takes corpus-wide OWNERSHIP… even if that listener ignores this category or itself throws"). Two consequences the corpus shows:

1. Story registers `(fn [_record] nil)` purely to claim the stream — `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:1149-1161` (`claim-error-ownership!` / `release-error-ownership!`, rf2-8yyd; the comment block at `:1118-1144` explains that the registration IS the payload). That claim silences the console for EVERY frame on the page, including a host app's frames that Story did not mount and does not read — a registration on a door nobody reads, to change behaviour on a door nobody registered. `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:190-210` §Error-stream ownership documents the claim as the framework's off-switch.
2. Conversely, a frame whose `:observability :errors` policy already delivered the record to a registered sink (the NORMAL production door, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270-300`) still gets a console line, because the sink route is not consulted: `report-unowned-error!` runs before the fan-out and before the sink route at `error_emit.cljc:595` (event-centric) and `:848` (union records), and `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` (`observability.cljc:228-297`, `:299-330`) return nil.

`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/server.cljs:280-283` records the same side effect for its one-render `:errors` window.

## Evidence

- `error_emit.cljc:201-230` `report-unowned-error!` (three gates: `debug-enabled?`, DOM host, empty registry); `:595` and `:848` call sites; `:610` and `:852` the `:observability/route-error` / `:observability/route-error-record` hook lookups that follow.
- `observability.cljc:159-170` `deliver-to-sink!` — a sink id with no registered fn is a no-op; a throwing sink is swallowed.
- Pinning tests today: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs` — `an-attached-listener-suppresses-the-fallback` (:318), `ownership-is-implicit-and-corpus-wide` (:346, a listener that ignores the category or throws still owns), `dropping-the-last-listener-resumes-the-fallback` (:366), plus the rollback cases (:406-591) rf2-xpd8 / rf2-vkn8 added; `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/shell_error_ownership_cljs_test.cljs:40-70` (claim/release/idempotent/host-listener-survives).
- rf2-xpd8's ruling (2026-09-04, PR1 on main as `56cd0aa021` / `4b4b104b16`) reasons in "listener, sink, console" vocabulary and names the fallback as firing "when nothing owns the stream" — its producer feeds all three identically and does not move here.

## Target API

No new API, no knob (rf2-fu75's rejections stand: no per-category ownership, no sink discovery, no suppression setting). Only the ownership PREDICATE changes. A record is OWNED when either:

- (a) at least one corpus-wide `:errors` listener is registered — unchanged, including "ignores the category" and "throws" (`ownership-is-implicit-and-corpus-wide` stays green); or
- (b) the record's owning frame declares an `:observability :errors` policy and at least one of its entries resolved to a REGISTERED sink fn, which was invoked. A policy naming a sink the app has not registered does NOT own the record (it went nowhere — codex's "missing sink" caution); a sink that throws DOES own it (the sink author has it — the same posture as a throwing listener).

The fallback fires iff neither holds. Mechanism constraint for the worker: the console decision needs the sink-route result, and today the console fires first at `:595` / `:848`. Have `route-error!` / `route-error-record!` (and `route-stream!`) return the count of registered sinks invoked, and take the console decision after the route. The relative order of listener fan-out and sink route is not contractual (spec 015/009 say "ALONGSIDE") — verify no test pins it (`observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc`, `non_event_observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc`, `capture_frame_reincarnation_sink_route_cljs_test.cljc`) before reordering, and keep "exactly once per record" (`:590-596` comment).

Story then owns its errors as DATA on the frames it creates: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:811` and `:934` (`rf/make-frame` for variant frames) and `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/artifact.cljc:446` conj `{:sink :rf.story/errors}` onto the config's existing `[:observability :errors]` vector (an author's own entries are kept, never replaced), and the shell registers `(rf/register-observability-sink! :rf.story/errors …)` on mount and `unregister-observability-sink!` on unmount, replacing `claim-error-ownership!` / `release-error-ownership!`. The sink fn may be a no-op with the reason in its docstring (Story's capture path is the trace axis, `shell.cljs:1134-1138`), or feed the assertion strip — worker's call; what matters is that ownership is frame-scoped policy readable off `frame-meta`, and a host app's frames on the same page get their console lines back. Sink resolution happens at delivery time (`deliver-to-sink!`), so mount order between the shell and a variant frame does not matter.

```clojure
;; before (shell.cljs:1153) — page-wide claim through a door nobody reads
(rf/register-listener! :errors ::error-ownership (fn [_record] nil))

;; after — variant frames carry the policy; the shell owns the sink id
(rf/make-frame (-> config-map
                   (assoc :id variant-id)
                   (update-in [:observability :errors] (fnil conj []) {:sink :rf.story/errors})))
(rf/register-observability-sink! :rf.story/errors story-error-sink)   ;; on mount
(rf/unregister-observability-sink! :rf.story/errors)                  ;; on unmount
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer. Fable: "Key the fallback on 'no entry routed this record'… so Story's frames declare policy and own their errors honestly." Grok: "Key the console fallback on 'no policy routed this record.'" Codex: "real but should remain small… Changing that to 'an entry routed' can hide an error when a named sink is missing or throws; Story also suppresses errors outside a single variant frame… define successful handoff precisely before changing it. Do not invent per-category routing, acknowledgements, or a suppression framework." The predicate above is that precise definition; the Story point is exactly what the change removes.

## Deletion list

- `shell.cljs:1118-1161` — the ownership comment block, `error-ownership-listener-id`, `claim-error-ownership!`, `release-error-ownership!` (replaced by the sink pair); the mount/unmount call sites that invoke them.
- `error_emit.cljc:121-132` comment and `:201-215` docstring — rewritten to the two-arm predicate.

## Consumers to migrate

Story only (above). `hicasso/server.cljs:280-283` docstring stays true under arm (a); no change. `frame.cljc:2810/3909` transient listeners: unchanged (arm (a) — they own for their window, as today).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1283` (surface #5 paragraph: "an EMPTY `:errors` listener registry", "registering ANY `:errors` listener takes CORPUS-WIDE ownership… that self-suppression IS the off-switch") → nothing owns it = no `:errors` listener AND no frame-policy sink delivery; keep "attach a listener or wire the frame sink before counting on visibility". HOT-ZONE.
- `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:190-210` §Error-stream ownership → rewritten to the frame-policy form (scoped to Story's frames; host frames untouched by construction, not by id discipline).
- `git grep -nE "registry is empty|fallback goes quiet|corpus-wide ownership|takes ownership" -- docs skills spec tools/*/spec` and update each line found (measured at drafting: 009:1283, Story 003:197-205, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md` does not mention the fallback).
- Tests to add in `error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs`: (i) a frame with an `:errors` policy whose sink is registered — record reaches the sink, console silent; (ii) same policy, sink NOT registered — console prints; (iii) a sibling frame WITHOUT policy on the same page — console prints for it while (i)'s frame stays silent; (iv) a throwing registered sink — console silent; (v) a frameless (`:frame nil`) record with no listener — console prints (unchanged). Keep :318, :346, :366 as they are.
- `shell_error_ownership_cljs_test.cljs:40-70` rewritten: claim = variant frame carries `{:sink :rf.story/errors}` and the sink is registered → a variant-frame refusal prints nothing; release = sink unregistered → prints; a host frame without policy prints while the shell is mounted; a host app's own `:errors` listener is untouched.
- Gate: `npm run test:story-feature-load` (`examples/scripts/run-story-feature-load-tests.cjs`, console errors fatal) must stay at 0 console errors — that run is the evidence the frame-scoped claim covers everything Story emits. If it does not (a Story-originated record with `:frame nil`), record the category as a finding on this bead; do not reinstate the page-wide claim.
- Manifest: no var changes. Conformance: none.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

`spec/009` is one-toucher: rf2-6g6e (PR #9182, 009 frame-destroyed row) and observability.5 also edit it — serialise. rf2-xpd8's code is on main; nothing live to wait for. Independent of observability.1/3/4 and of the ruling (under a Target-A ruling the listener arm (a) keeps working for `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!` — implementation tier — and the sink arm (b) is the public door; under Target B both arms are public).

## Risks

A record whose frame declares a policy naming an unregistered sink still prints — intended (fail-visible). A frame policy that routes to a throwing sink is silent — same as a throwing listener today; the sink author owns it. `error_emit.cljc` docstrings and the console test are files rf2-xpd8 / rf2-vkn8 touched recently; rebase carefully, do not revert their deftests.

## Local dossier

ai/findings/API-review/fable/observability-doors.md (§The problem, fact 5; §Simpler elegant target; §Codex Thoughts "The console issue") — local-only pointer.

title: story: the shell dispatches into Xray's :rf/xray frame directly, and races the seat at boot (residual 2 of rf2-avi7)
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:406 hand-rolls (rf/with-frame :rf/xray (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.xray/set-target-frame now])) — reaching into ANOTHER TOOL'S frame instead of calling Xray's host-facing facade day8.re-frame2-xray.core/set-target-frame!.

Two consequences.

(1) THE MEASURED ONE. rf2-avi7 (PR #9312) seats :rf/xray on substrate-adapter readiness, from the Xray preload's bounded 50ms poll. Measured on one tree carrying both #9312 and #9306, against the same tree with #9312 reverted: 97 :rf.error/frame-destroyed -> 2. The residual 2 fire at t=546.9ms and t=561.9ms on one page — inside the poll window, because Story's boot does rf/init! then mounts the shell and selects a variant before the next tick. Record (captured with a pr-str diagnostic planted in error_emit/report-unowned-error!, restored, blob cf828e0e6c167fd0d421c32de0e3b148f2b8e811 verified):
  {:error :rf.error/frame-destroyed :event :rf/redacted :event-id :rf.xray/set-target-frame :frame :rf/xray :source-coord {:ns day8.re-frame2-xray.epoch :line 108}}
No Xray-side change reaches this: the dispatch is Story's, and by the time the watcher fires rf/init! HAS run — so a facade call would seat successfully and land.

(2) THE STRUCTURAL ONE, which is the real point. A host is not supposed to know that :rf/xray is Xray's frame, nor that its lifecycle is tied to adapter readiness. Story already uses the facade for the sibling gesture (rf.story.xray-preset/on-variant-selected!, wire-cross-host!) and already has the ensure-before-dispatch pattern for its OWN frames (ensure-variant-frame!, rf2-zme7). This one call site is the exception.

PROPOSED (not ruled): (a) Story calls (xray-core/set-target-frame! now) in place of the with-frame + dispatch-sync; (b) Xray's core/set-target-frame! routes through mount/ensure-xray-frame! before dispatching, so the facade is correct at boot instant for EVERY host, not just Story. Both halves are one-liners. (b) alone does not fix Story; (a) alone leaves the facade wrong for the next host.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: npm run test:story-feature-load is a per-PR gate (test.yml, story_full_gate) and PR #9306 turns it red by removing the Story shell's page-wide no-op :errors listener that was masking these. #9312 takes it from 101 console errors to 6; this bead is 2 of the remaining 6. ## Problem

`resolve-entry-scope` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/route.cljc:507–557` at 6d513ba07f; sole call site `:722`) accepts a route `:resources` entry's `:scope` as `{:from-db <id>}` (resolved against the route-entry app-db; nil → planning error) or an anonymous `(fn [route ctx] …)` resolver. Zero app/testbed consumers of the fn form; 7 test lines / 4 files. `spec/016-Resources.md` already rules "no anonymous route-context functions as a second public scope-resolution currency" for any NEW source and reserves `[:runtime <path>]` inputs (`016:239–241`) as the NAMED replacement — the fn tier is grandfathered, not chosen. A route entry's siblings `:params (fn [route] …)` and `:when (fn [route ctx] …)` stay (they are not scope currency).

Codex's correction, verified at HEAD: the `cond`'s `:else nil` arm swallows ANY other present value — `:scope :rf.scope/global` or `[:rf.scope/session {…}]` on a route entry today silently inherits the registration policy. So "a concrete override on a route entry" is NOT already supported; this bead ADDS it, and the silent fall-through must go.

## Target

A route `:resources` entry's `:scope` is one of:

1. ABSENT → inherit the registration policy (unchanged; `resolve-scope-for-event` with no route scope). The absence test keys on `(contains? entry :scope)`, never on "unrecognised value".
2. `{:from-db <id>}` → resolved against the route-entry app-db; nil → the existing planning error (unchanged).
3. A CONCRETE scope value → canonicalised through the SAME `canonicalize-scope` / policy-vs-value guard the payload override uses (`state.cljc`), so a `:from-db`-keyed map is refused by (i)'s rule and an unknown `:rf.scope/*` keyword is refused as a typo; the resulting concrete scope is the route tier of the precedence ladder.
4. Anything else PRESENT (a fn, an unrecognised `:rf.scope/*` keyword, nil) → loud `planning-error` (reuse the existing route planning-error shape and `:recovery :fix-scope`; mint no new id — if one is unavoidable, its `009` row is hot-zone).

`[:runtime <path>]` inputs STAY RESERVED — do not pre-build. UN-PARK TRIGGER (record it in `016:239–241`): the first tenant-in-a-path-segment consumer (any site, route or not) ships `[:runtime path]` inputs for named resolvers; until then tenant-in-path derived scope is inexpressible and that is accepted (zero demand in-repo).

title: post-merge-workflow-sanity dispatches with --ref <sha>, gets HTTP 422, and reports success — the 24h-gap closer has an unproven success path
description:
FOUND BY THE MAYOR 2026-09-05 while chasing rf2-2qa7, which expected the first Windows CI leg to run at merge. It did not run, and this is why.

## What is established, by measurement

Run 33946468214 of `.github/workflows/post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml`, on merge commit `73ac28b7af` (PR #9276, which edited `expensive-tests.yml`). Its runtime output, read with the ANSI command-echo lines filtered OUT (the echo lines are the script's source, not its output — my first read matched those and told me nothing):

    dispatching: expensive-tests.yml
    could not create workflow dispatch event: HTTP 422: No ref found for: 73ac28b7af7fbdce3d8a07cacb3e030cb1aa191f
      (https://api.github.com/repos/day8/re-frame2/actions/workflows/277358356/dispatches)
    WARN: gh workflow run failed for expensive-tests.yml (non-fatal)

**Job conclusion: success.** The run is `completed/success`.

## The mechanism

`post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml:200` is `gh workflow run "$f" --ref "${{ github.sha }}" || { echo "WARN: ..."; }`.

Two independent halves, and both need fixing:

1. **`--ref` takes a REF, not a commit SHA.** The Actions dispatch endpoint resolves `ref` as a branch or tag name; a 40-character commit id is not one, hence 422 "No ref found for". `${{ github.sha }}` is always a commit id, so this argument can never succeed as written.
2. **The failure is swallowed by `||` and the job goes green.** So the workflow whose ENTIRE PURPOSE is to close a 24-hour feedback gap on workflow edits reports success while having dispatched nothing. This is the fail-open shape: a green that means "we tried", read by every reader as "it ran".

## What is NOT established — do not overstate it in the fix

I checked the last TEN sanity runs. Only ONE of them attempted a dispatch at all (the other nine printed no dispatch lines — most pushes change no workflow file). So the measured record is **1 attempt, 1 failure**, not "always broken". `expensive-tests.yml` does have 5 `workflow_dispatch` runs among its last 60, so the endpoint has succeeded at some point — plausibly from manual `gh workflow run` with a branch name. **Establish the real history before writing a claim into the file**: search sanity runs further back for `dispatching: ` lines and report how many attempts there have been and how many succeeded.

## Consequence right now

`expensive-tests.yml` has not run since 2026-09-04T15:25:53Z. PR #9276's `mcp-live-windows` job — the repo's first Windows leg — has therefore **never executed**. Its first opportunity is the scheduled nightly at 15:17 UTC. rf2-2qa7 (read the first two nightly runs) is the live path, and rf2-hhw6's close reason has been corrected to say so.

## The fix, on the merits

The obvious repair is `--ref "${{ github.ref_name }}"` (or literally `main`), which dispatches the workflow at the branch tip. **Note the semantic change and decide it deliberately rather than by accident**: dispatching at the branch tip is not the same as dispatching at the merge commit, and if two workflow-editing merges land close together the second dispatch covers both. For this workflow's purpose — "does the edited workflow still run" — the tip is arguably the RIGHT target, since that is what tonight's nightly will use. Say which you chose and why.

The `||` is the other half. A dispatch that fails is not a non-fatal condition for a workflow that exists to dispatch: at minimum it must fail the step, or set a job-level annotation that is visible without opening the log. Weigh `set -e` semantics against the file's own stated reason for the `||` (read the surrounding comment before removing it — the comment at :35 says none of the excluded workflows declare `workflow_dispatch`, so there may be a case the `||` was protecting). If the `||` is genuinely load-bearing for a case the loop already skips, narrow it rather than deleting it.

## Verification is the hard part and the deliverable

A fix you cannot exercise is a guess. `workflow_dispatch` behaviour cannot be proven from a PR branch, because the workflow that runs is the one on the DEFAULT branch. State plainly what you verified and what you could not:
- You CAN verify the argument shape against the API contract and against a manual `gh workflow run expensive-tests.yml --ref <branch>` from your own checkout — do that and quote the result.
- You CANNOT verify the merged behaviour until a workflow-editing commit lands on main. Say so, and note that THIS PR is itself such a commit, so the next sanity run after it merges is the natural witness — name that as the acceptance check and leave the bead for the mayor to close on the evidence.

## Fence
IN: `.github/workflows/post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml`.
OUT: every other workflow file. `.github/workflows/*` is hot-zone and sequential — no other bead may touch that directory while this is live.
notes:
2026-09-05 — DELIVERY: PR #9287 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9287), branch worker/wfsanity-a. NOT closed; see the acceptance check below.

MEASURED HISTORY (the description asked for this before a claim went into the file; it is worse than 1/1).
256 sanity runs all time (2026-05-28 -> 2026-09-05), EVERY ONE concluded success. 174 executed the dispatch step. 155 have readable logs (the other 19, 2026-05-28 -> 2026-06-05, return HTTP 410 - expired, so unmeasured rather than clean). Of those 155: 26 runs reached a dispatch, 27 attempts, 27 failures, ZERO successes - all with the identical "HTTP 422: No ref found for: <sha>". Targets: expensive-tests.yml x18, freehand-conformance.yml x5, freehand-bench.yml x4. First attempt 2026-06-19, last 2026-09-05 (78 days).
The --ref argument is byte-identical in every revision back to the introducing commit 0e708c17d9, so any attempt the 19 expired runs made failed the same way - a DEDUCTION from unchanged source, not a measurement, and the file's comment says so in those terms.
Instrument control: filtered every line carrying an ESC byte (the ANSI 36;1m source echo) before matching "dispatching: ". Exercised on run 33946468214 - unfiltered 2 hits, filtered 1, survivor is the genuine runtime line.
Corroboration: expensive-tests.yml has 6 lifetime workflow_dispatch runs, all on BRANCH refs (main, worker/*) - manual, none from this canary.

THE FIX. (1) --ref takes github.ref_name, through env: as DISPATCH_REF rather than interpolated into the run body (the rule the sibling step states and _post-merge-sanity-base.test.cjs pins). Chose the TIP over the merge commit deliberately - the merge commit was never dispatchable at all, and the tip is what the next cron tick uses, which is the question this canary asks; concurrency: cancel-in-progress already collapses back-to-back pushes. ref_name over a literal main because the workflow also declares workflow_dispatch, where a literal would be wrong. (2) A failed dispatch now reds the step and raises ::error::, mirroring the fail-loud call the base resolution above already makes; failures counted rather than aborting the loop, plus an explicit "dispatched:" line so a success is provable from the log. (3) A workflow deleted in the same push is now skipped EXPLICITLY - it was already skipped, but only via grep exiting non-zero on an unopenable file, which printed stderr noise and the wrong reason (measured on runs 29638598700 and 31924373964). That was the only case the || could have been protecting; stated, so the swallow protects nothing and goes.

VERIFIED: the argument shape, live, against the real API, starting NO run. Two probes that both 422 (so create nothing) and whose different messages isolate the ref: dispatchable workflow + commit sha -> "No ref found for: 46e197f356..." (ref resolution failed); non-dispatchable workflow test.yml + branch name main -> "Workflow does not have 'workflow_dispatch' trigger" (ref RESOLVED, the API reached the trigger check). gh api .../git/ref/heads/main resolves; .../git/ref/<sha> 404s. Confirmed neither probe created a run. expensive-tests.yml was deliberately NOT spent as a syntax check.

COULD NOT VERIFY: merged behaviour. workflow_dispatch runs the DEFAULT-BRANCH copy, so nothing here is provable from a PR branch.

ACCEPTANCE CHECK - AND A CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF. The brief expected this PR to be its own witness because it is a workflow-editing commit. It is NOT: post-merge-workflow-sanity.yml is on its own EXCLUDE list (# self), so this merge runs the canary and prints "skip (excluded)", dispatching nothing. expensive-tests.yml is the ONLY workflow both dispatchable and not excluded (docs/lint/portability declare workflow_dispatch but are excluded as already running on push). So the witness is THE NEXT MERGE TO main THAT EDITS expensive-tests.yml, whose sanity run must print "dispatching: expensive-tests.yml (ref main)" then "dispatched: expensive-tests.yml (ref main)", with a matching workflow_dispatch run of expensive-tests.yml appearing. Do NOT force the evidence by dispatching expensive-tests.yml by hand - that spends the nightly matrix including the new Windows leg; the scheduled 15:17 UTC run covers it and rf2-2qa7 owns reading it.

GATES (foreground, exit captured on the same command line as the redirect, re-run on the final rebased base e9744f511c): check_workflow_yaml --self-test 0 (5 cases); check_workflow_yaml 0 (11 files); check_workflow_job_timeouts --self-test 0 (4 accept + 5 reject); check_workflow_job_timeouts --verbose 0 (117 jobs / 11 files); check_require_alias_dialect --verbose 0 (2794 files, 10867 edges, 2446 non-canonical, every surface at or under its floor); check_view_lifetime_residue --verbose 0 (zero residue); node --test on the 4 workflow-reading policy tests 0 (384 assertions: changed-surfaces 366, post-merge-sanity-base 9, docs-workflow-policy 5, lint-workflow-policy 4); bash -n on the extracted run: body 0 (control: broken copy exits 2).
Sabotage control: unmatched quote planted on the DISPATCH_REF line after committing -> check_workflow_yaml exit 1 naming line 175 col 14, check_workflow_job_timeouts exit 2 "not well-formed YAML". Fault existed only in this worktree, so a wandering run would have come back green. Restore verified by git BLOB hash 5a95e41b45..., not by reading a diff. `clear-scope-handler` (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2144–2214` at 6d513ba07f) accepts TWO payload forms: a concrete scope, or `{:from-db <id>}` resolved against clear-scope's OWN coeffect db. `[:rf.resource/clear-scope {:scope <concrete scope> :cause …}]` is the ONLY payload form. `clear-scope-handler` collapses onto `clear-scope-handler*` (`events.cljc:2073`) over a canonicalised concrete scope. `rf/resolve-resource-scope` (pure, trace-free — the ruled read/write split, `016:163`, `API.md:466`) is how a handler obtains a concrete scope from a named resolver against ITS db; unchanged.

A map is a valid LITERAL scope value (`registry.cljc:87–89`). title: OPERATOR ACT, NOT A DECISION (Mike runs one command at a session boundary): git gc the mayor checkout — 174,378 loose objects / 63 GiB beside a 1.7 GiB pack; runbook in the RULING note
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 by the mayor. The bead was filed with an EMPTY description and the whole finding living in its title, which is fragile — a title is not a record. Filling it in, and correcting how it has been surfaced.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken with `git count-objects -vH` in the mayor checkout (fast: it reads object-directory metadata rather than walking the tree — a `du -sh .git` on this repository EXCEEDED FIVE MINUTES and was killed, so use count-objects):

  count:            168594        loose objects
  size:             61.92 GiB     loose
  in-pack:          532091
  size-pack:        1.72 GiB      packed
  prune-packable:   64882         loose objects that already exist in a pack
  garbage:          3             (2.72 MiB)

So the packed equivalent of the whole history is 1.72 GiB and the loose overhead is roughly THIRTY-SIX TIMES that. 64,882 of the loose objects are already packed and are pure waste.

THE CAUSE is this project's own workflow rather than anything anomalous: every checkpoint writes a new revision of `.beads/issues.jsonl`, a full-database export, and a checkpoint happens per tick per worktree. Twenty worktrees have existed today alone.

THIS IS NOT A DECISION AND SHOULD STOP BEING SURFACED AS ONE. The remedy is named in the bead's own title — `git gc` — and no product, policy or taste question hangs on it. What it needs is a QUIET WINDOW, which is a scheduling constraint:
  - `git gc` on a repository with linked worktrees must see every worktree's refs, and a worker committing mid-gc is the hazard;
  - at the time of writing there were 20 worktrees and 2 live workers;
  - on 168k loose objects it will not be quick.
So the right moment is with the fleet at zero and no merge in flight, which happens naturally between dispatch waves.

WHAT TO RUN, and the ordering matters: `git worktree prune` first (a stale worktree entry holds refs that keep objects reachable), then `git gc` — NOT `--prune=now`, which discards objects a concurrent process may be mid-write on; the default two-week grace is the safe form and still reclaims the 64,882 prune-packable objects. Verify with `git count-objects -vH` before and after and quote both.

THE ONE REAL RISK worth stating: `git gc` prunes objects unreachable from any ref, and an UNPUSHED worktree commit is reachable only from its own branch ref — which gc does see, so it is safe. But rf2-7ngc records exactly one worktree (ep-corpus-coherence) holding work that is absent from the remote. Confirm that its branch ref still exists before and after, since it is the one piece of work in this repository that a ref accident would actually lose.
notes:
FOUND 2026-09-03 incidentally by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal (operator half), while sizing disk before assembling fresh pilot workspaces. Not a pilot finding; filed because it is adjacent to the disk question rf2-t4jpz already flags to Mike, and because it dwarfs it.

MEASURED, mayor checkout C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2, "git count-objects -vH":

  count:           162409          <- loose objects
  size:            61.06 GiB       <- loose object bytes
  in-pack:         530979
  packs:           77
  size-pack:       1.72 GiB        <- the SAME history, packed
  prune-packable:  63979           <- loose objects that ALREADY exist in a pack
  garbage:         3 (2.72 MiB, stale tmp_obj_* files)

So the repository's real content is about 1.72 GiB, and there is 61 GiB of loose objects sitting beside it -- roughly 35x the packed size. Nearly 64,000 of those loose objects are redundant by definition: they are already inside a pack. For scale, a fresh "git clone" of this repo from GitHub produces a .git of 38 MB (measured twice today while assembling pilot workspaces).

CAUSE, measured rather than assumed. Sampling 300 loose objects with "git cat-file --batch-check":

  blob    count=73   total=410.3 MB   avg=5756 KB
  commit  count=53   total=0.1 MB     avg=1 KB
  tree    count=174  total=0.2 MB     avg=1 KB

Blobs are about a quarter of the objects by count and 99.9% of the bytes, averaging 5.6 MB each. .beads/issues.jsonl is currently 9,658,691 bytes (9.7 MB) and was smaller historically, so 5.6 MB is squarely its size range. Extrapolating the sample: 162,409 objects x ~24% blobs x ~5.6 MB ~= 61 GB, which matches the measured 61.06 GiB.

The mechanism is the one CLAUDE.md already describes for a different reason. .beads/issues.jsonl is a full-database export, and bd rewrites it in EVERY checkout. With a mayor loop checkpointing on a heartbeat and roughly 27 live worker worktrees each running bd, every tick hashes a fresh multi-megabyte, near-identical copy into a new loose blob. Loose objects are zlib-compressed but NOT delta-compressed, so each revision is stored at close to full size. The same blobs delta-compress superbly once packed -- which is exactly why the packed store holds the entire history in 1.72 GiB.

This is therefore normal git behaviour meeting an unusual workload, not corruption and not a bug in bd. Nothing is broken: every gate, clone and checkout in this session behaved correctly, and disk is not tight (376 GiB free of 953 GiB on C:). But it grows monotonically with every checkpoint in every worktree, so it is a slow leak rather than a one-off.

REMEDY, and it is NOT mine to run. "git gc" (or "git gc --prune=now") packs the loose objects and drops the prune-packable duplicates, and should reclaim close to the full 61 GiB. Two cautions for whoever does it:

  1. TIMING. Run it in a quiet moment. At the time of measurement this checkout had roughly 27 linked worktrees and a live mayor loop committing on a heartbeat; gc rewriting the object store underneath concurrent git processes is the kind of thing to do deliberately, not mid-tick. Worktrees share the primary checkout's object store, so this is one gc for all of them.
  2. The 3 "garbage found: .git/objects/*/tmp_obj_*" warnings are stale temporary files from interrupted writes, 2.72 MiB total. gc clears them; they are a symptom of killed git processes, which is expected given how often worker runs are killed, and are not themselves a problem.

NOT filed as a fix and NOT actioned: the rehearsal brief scoped me to measurement and forbade repairs, and a 61 GiB object-store rewrite across 27 live worktrees is an operator action regardless.

WORTH CONSIDERING SEPARATELY, if this recurs after a gc: whether the checkpoint cadence needs to be the thing that changes rather than the cleanup. That is a design question about how often a 9.7 MB full-database export is committed, and it belongs to whoever owns the checkpoint loop -- not to this bead, which is only asking for the space back.
MAYOR NOTE 2026-09-03 06:2x AUSEST — VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, AND THE CAUSE IS MINE. I re-ran git count-objects -vH in the mayor checkout myself rather than taking the report: count 162,409 loose / 61.06 GiB, in-pack 530,979 across 77 packs / 1.72 GiB, prune-packable 63,979, plus 3 stale tmp_obj_ files. So the same history packs to 1.72 GiB and sits beside 61 GiB of loose objects, ~35x, with roughly 64,000 of them redundant by definition. 27 worktrees live.

THIS IS NOT A bd BUG AND NOT CORRUPTION. It is normal git meeting an unusual workload: .beads/issues.jsonl is a full-database export, currently 9,658,691 bytes, and LOOSE OBJECTS ARE ZLIB-COMPRESSED BUT NOT DELTA-COMPRESSED. Near-identical multi-megabyte copies delta beautifully once packed - which is exactly why 77 packs hold everything in 1.72 GiB - and cost ~5.7 MB each while loose. The worker sampling supports it: blobs are a quarter of sampled objects by count and 99.9% of the bytes, averaging 5,756 KB, squarely in issues.jsonl range.

WHERE I DIFFER FROM THE REPORT FRAMING, AND I HAVE NOT PROVEN IT EITHER WAY. It attributes the volume to "a heartbeat checkpoint loop". My checkpoint commits cannot be the bulk: roughly 75 of them this session at ~9.6 MB is ~700 MB, not 61 GiB. The likelier amplifier is that bd AUTO-STAGES .beads/issues.jsonl in EVERY checkout (CLAUDE.md records "bd auto-stages, never commits"), and git add writes a loose blob every time - across 27 worktrees each running many bd calls, that is the right order of magnitude. I checked one live worktree and found .beads clean there, which does not settle it. WHOEVER TAKES THIS SHOULD ESTABLISH WHICH BEFORE CHANGING ANY CADENCE, because the two have completely different remedies: fewer checkpoints, versus bd invocation volume in worktrees.

THE ONE-TIME CLEANUP IS AN OPERATOR ACT AND I AM NOT DOING IT. The worker was right not to. A 61 GiB object-store rewrite underneath 27 live worktrees and a running mayor loop is not something to slip into a tick, and worktrees SHARE the primary object store, so it is one gc for all of them and it must happen in a quiet moment. Flagged to Mike.

WHAT I CAN DO WITHOUT AN OPERATOR ACT, and will: the reap backlog is the multiplier. 27 worktrees is well above what the fleet needs (6), and the hygiene loop has fallen behind eleven merged PRs. Reaping the reap-eligible set does not delete objects, but it stops new worktrees from adding bd traffic against the shared store. That is queued for the next hygiene tick and is now its highest-value item rather than tidiness.

NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the rehearsal verdict is unaffected. The precondition still holds; rf2-lh7b remains the blocker before two blinded pilots.
DOSSIER 2026-09-04 15:45:28 AUSEST (mayor, at Mike's request): decision dossier written at ai/decisions/rf2-ah6r.mayor-checkout-git-gc.md (local-only, lives until the ruling lands; paste-ready pre-flight/run/post-check runbook inside). RECOMMENDATION: at the next moment with zero live worker agents, the mayor loop stopped between ticks, and no git.exe/java.exe running, run plain "git gc" (default two-week prune - NOT --prune=now, NOT --aggressive) from an interactive terminal Mike keeps open, budget up to an hour; FIRST set "git config gc.auto 0" and delete the two stale lock files from 2026-07-11 (.git/gc.pid and the 0-byte .git/objects/maintenance.lock); leave the checkpoint cadence alone; file one follow-up bead for "git maintenance start" (fallback: a weekly scheduled git gc). FACTS THAT CORRECT THIS BEAD: (1) the mayor's "~75 checkpoints/session at ~9.6 MB = ~700 MB, cannot be the bulk" is wrong by two orders of magnitude: main carries 6,544 commits touching .beads/issues.jsonl since Jul 11 and 150-200 per day now (Sep 1: 196 of 411 commits; Sep 3: 200 of 441); at ~5 MB zlib'd each that is ~0.75-1 GiB/day, matching measured growth (+5,886 objects / +0.78 GiB in 33 h). (2) The "bd auto-stages in 27 worktrees" hypothesis is NOT the amplifier now: in a 1/256 sample of the store all 44 large loose blobs are issues.jsonl exports, 19 committed on main and 25 dangling - but EVERY dangling one is dated 2026-06-30..2026-07-29 and every large blob after that (13/13) is a committed version; bd 1.1.2 reports export.auto=false, the installed pre-commit hook carries no bd block, worker worktrees' issues.jsonl mtimes equal their HEAD commit time. By bytes ~60% is the dead June-July mechanism and ~40% committed checkpoints; by growth 100% checkpoint commits. (3) NEW: git's own auto-gc has been silently DISABLED since 2026-07-11 21:09 by a stale .git/objects/maintenance.lock (0 bytes) plus .git/gc.pid - "git maintenance run --auto" (invoked by every commit/fetch/merge/rebase) returns silently when that lock exists. The commit at 21:09:32 that day was 270268ba36; on Windows auto-gc runs in the foreground of the triggering command, so it was killed mid-run (kill reason inferred; files measured). This is also why merely re-enabling gc.auto is the wrong cadence fix - it would run a multi-minute foreground gc inside a mayor tool call roughly daily. MEASURED: 168,295 loose / 61.84 GiB; 80 packs (not 77) / 1.72 GiB; prune-packable 64,882; 27 worktrees including three ~/.grok/worktrees/.../subagent-* outside re-frame2-worktrees/; 377 GB free; git count-objects -vH took 1m47s (a first attempt exceeded 5 min under load). Actual gc duration not measured (estimated 20-60 min).
RULING 2026-09-04 21:11:35 AUSEST (delegated by Mike 2026-09-04, operator-reversible; dossier ai/decisions/rf2-ah6r.mayor-checkout-git-gc.md and its Codex Recommendation section folded here and deleted). Ruled by a delegated agent from the mayor checkout at tip 1ad17a77fe (== origin/main), read-only throughout: no gc, repack, prune, lock deletion, config change or worktree change was made. Re-measured at 21:03-21:05: 169,356 loose / 62.02 GiB; 532,332 in 81 packs / 1.72 GiB; prune-packable 65,069; garbage 3 / 2.72 MiB; count-objects -vH wall 2m11s; 31 registered worktrees; 384 GB free; both Jul 11 lock files still present; no gc.* or maintenance.* config at any scope; no Git Maintenance scheduled task.

THE RULING. Mike runs plain "git gc" (default two-week expiry; cruft packs are on by default in git 2.53) ONCE, from an interactive Git Bash terminal in the mayor checkout, at the next SESSION BOUNDARY: after a mayor session's Session Completion push has landed and before the next session starts, with the fleet reaped and no git.exe alive. Before the run he sets "git config maintenance.auto false" and deletes the one stale lock that matters, .git/objects/maintenance.lock (0 bytes, 2026-07-11 21:09); .git/gc.pid is left for git, which overwrites a gc.pid older than 12 hours and removes it on a clean exit, so its ABSENCE afterwards is a post-check. The checkpoint cadence does not change. One follow-up bead, rf2-fmst (discovered-from this bead, status blocked until this closes), trials "git maintenance start" for recurring background packing with a weekly operator gc as the fallback. This is one act with a runbook, owned by Mike; not a hygiene-loop task, and no longer an open decision.

WHY THESE CHOICES. Session boundary and not a tick: the loop commits every 5-7 minutes (107 checkpoint commits today by 21:00), its tool calls carry timeouts, and a timeout is what killed the 2026-07-11 auto-gc and left the locks; the quiet window the job needs cannot exist inside the loop. Mike and not the hygiene loop: same reason, plus the Windows unlink retry prompt needs a tty, and a session boundary is a moment Mike already owns. Plain git gc and not the maintenance form for this one run: no scheduler exists yet so there is no lock to honour, and "git maintenance run" FAILS OPEN on a stale objects/maintenance.lock (warns, exits 0, does nothing) whereas git gc's exit status means what it says; once rf2-fmst arms a scheduler, later manual runs use "git maintenance run --task=gc", which the git 2.53 manual asks for so they take the same object-database lock as the scheduled runs. maintenance.auto=false and not gc.auto=0: it is the single switch every porcelain command consults before spawning "maintenance run --auto", it is exactly what "git maintenance register/start" sets, so the config end-state is identical whether or not rf2-fmst lands, and one knob is enough. Quiet, operationally: (a) no loop - the mayor session has completed its push and ended, or its /loop is stopped; (b) fleet at zero - every ledger row from the session has REPORTED (the reap test is the report, never a field of the row) and tasklist shows no git.exe and no java.exe; (c) no lock files in .git or any .git/worktrees/*/; (d) tree clean. An idle claude.exe or an editor's node.exe is fine, but an editor with git integration open on any worktree spawns git.exe during the run - close it or expect the retry prompt.

OPTIONS REJECTED.
- --prune=now: discards the only margin that protects an object a concurrent process wrote seconds ago; on a quiet machine it gains a few MB, on a busy one it is the corruption path the git manual names.
- --aggressive: ~25x the delta work over ~11,000 near-identical 10 MB blobs for a somewhat smaller pack nobody needs.
- git repack -a -d && git prune: the two halves of gc without reflog expiry, pack-refs, worktree prune and commit-graph; more typing, no benefit.
- Two-stage gc with gc.pruneExpire=never first, default expiry later (Codex): premised on other worktrees' indexes not being reachability roots, which is false on this tree (REVIEWER POSITIONS 1). It would pack ~50 GB of dead June-July exports into a cruft pack only to delete them on a second pass.
- Re-enabling git's auto-gc alone (delete the lock, leave defaults): on Windows gc --auto cannot detach, so it runs the whole job in the foreground of whichever mayor commit or fetch trips the 6,700-object threshold - roughly daily at current growth - inside a tool call with a timeout; that is the 2026-07-11 failure repeated.
- Running it inside a hygiene tick: repack is safe under the two-week grace, but deleting 81 old packs hits files mapped by concurrent git processes and stalls on the Windows "Should I try again?" prompt, and the tick's timeout kills it.
- Fewer checkpoint commits: cuts growth proportionally but trades away the durability window rf2-51uz1 and rf2-rjqtj were built for; disk is not a reason to reopen that.
- Shrinking the export (bd prune of closed beads, dropping memory rows): deletes normative records to answer a disk question.
- Leaving it: ~6,000 objects and 0.6-1 GiB a day, ~120 GiB by November, every object-enumerating git command in 31 worktrees slowing further.
- A separate "git worktree prune" first (this bead's own text): dry run empty twice today (Codex 20:4x, this ruling 21:0x) and gc runs it itself; the pre-flight keeps the dry run as a check only.

REVIEWER POSITIONS. Both reviewers concur on the diagnosis, on compacting now, on no --prune=now and no --aggressive, on an interactive terminal with no agent timeout, on keeping the checkpoint cadence, and on git maintenance start as the follow-up. They dissent on three points; each was settled by reading the tree, not by preference.

(1) Reachability of other worktrees' index blobs. Codex asserted, citing reachable.c, that git's walk adds other worktrees' HEADs but not their indexes, so blob 36c019fd7dc03c57fbffe048a914e0eeb43938f8 (a 10,174,366-byte issues.jsonl export, loose, mtime 2026-07-25, staged in all three ~/.grok/worktrees/code-re-frame2/subagent-* worktrees and committed nowhere) could be expired by a default gc, and built a two-stage plan plus an owner-disposition step on it. Measured 2026-09-04 21:0x AUSEST with git 2.53.0.windows.2: "git rev-list --objects --indexed-objects --no-walk HEAD" lists that blob at path .beads/issues.jsonl; "git rev-list --objects --single-worktree --indexed-objects --no-walk HEAD" does not; "git rev-list --objects --no-walk HEAD" (HEAD tree only) does not; "git rev-list --objects --all -- .beads/issues.jsonl" does not. The installed git-rev-list manual says it outright: "By default, all working trees will be examined by the following options when there are more than one: --all, --reflog and --indexed-objects." gc, prune and repack use that same machinery (prune's mark_reachable_objects calls add_index_objects_to_pending with single_worktree unset; repack hands --all --reflog --indexed-objects to pack-objects), and the git-gc manual's NOTES promise that objects "referenced by the index" are kept. So the dossier's sentence "objects staged in any worktree's index count as reachable" stands, the safety hole does not exist, and the two-stage plan falls with it. Trap for anyone re-testing: --indexed-objects is applied when parsed, so --single-worktree must come BEFORE it or it has no effect - the reverse order reports the blob under both and looks like a contradiction. What survives of Codex's point, and is in the runbook: enumerate staged state in EVERY worktree (git -C wt diff --cached --name-status), since the mayor's own git status says nothing about the others, and prove afterwards that the blob survived (git cat-file -e). The three .grok worktrees are another tool's leftovers, detached at 0f6fa33cb7 (2026-07-25 20:44), directories untouched since 20:48 that day; their staged export must never be committed (a worker checkout never carries issues.jsonl, and a July export would time-travel the tracker) - that is hygiene for whoever owns them, and gc neither needs nor touches them.

(2) Which lock files to delete and which config to set. Dossier: delete gc.pid and maintenance.lock, set gc.auto 0. Codex: delete only maintenance.lock (git's own stale-pid rule - a gc.pid older than 12 hours or naming a dead pid is overwritten - makes gc.pid inert, and manual deletion of git internals should not be normalised), set maintenance.auto false. Ruled for Codex on both, for the reasons in WHY THESE CHOICES; gc.pid absent after the run becomes a success signal, present means the run was killed.

(3) Command form. Dossier: git gc. Codex: git -c gc.pruneExpire=never maintenance run --no-detach --task=gc now, default-expiry maintenance run later. Ruled: plain git gc for this one run (reachability finding above; fail-open lock behaviour of the maintenance form); the maintenance form for manual runs once a scheduler exists.

Distinct contributions preserved - dossier: the amplifier measurement (6,544 issues.jsonl commits on main since Jul 11, 150-200 a day, ~5 MB zlib'd each, matching measured growth of +5,886 objects / +0.78 GiB in 33 h; in a 1/256 sample every dangling large blob is dated 2026-06-30..07-29 and every later one is a committed version, so the worktree-bd-staging hypothesis is dead - bd 1.1.2 export.auto=false, no bd block in the installed pre-commit hook, worker issues.jsonl mtimes equal to their HEAD commit time - and the growth is 100% mayor checkpoints); the stale-lock finding and its mechanism (maintenance run --auto returns silently while objects/maintenance.lock exists; on Windows auto-gc cannot detach, so the 2026-07-11 21:09 run inside commit 270268ba36 ran in the foreground and was killed - kill reason inferred, files measured); 25 of 44 large loose blobs in the sample dangling and all older than two weeks, so default expiry removes every one; the 20-60 minute estimate with a phase description; interrupt safety by write-then-rename; the Windows unlink-prompt drill; the loose store already taxing plain git (count-objects 1m47s then, 2m11s now). Codex: an independent re-measurement (169,295 loose / 62.00 GiB, 81 packs, 65,069 prune-packable at 20:4x; fan-out a7: 676 objects, 160 blobs = 99.85% of bytes, 30 of 51 large blobs exact reachable issues.jsonl versions); the wording correction that 1.72 GiB is the size of what is ALREADY packed, not a measured packed equivalent of the 62 GiB, so final pack size and duration are both estimates - compare before and after, never promise a byte count; the schedule correction that under the incremental strategy loose-objects and incremental-repack run DAILY not hourly (confirmed in the installed manual), with a 50,000-object batch per run (maintenance.loose-objects.batchSize, 0 = unlimited) and a two-step delete-then-pack design; verify over two daily cycles, not one; the Windows schtasks console-window caveat (a visible console per run unless "Run whether user is logged in or not" is set, which needs a password, so git does not set it; rename customised tasks so start/stop cannot overwrite them); the manual's instruction not to mix git gc with scheduled maintenance runs and to prefer maintenance run --task=gc once a scheduler exists; maintenance.prefetch.enabled false before start; if interrupted, keep the transcript and rerun in a new window rather than treating Ctrl-C as free. Both: no worktree-prune candidates; no Git Maintenance scheduled task; no gc.* or maintenance.* config at any scope.

Corrections to this bead's own text, for the record: the "~75 checkpoints per session, cannot be the bulk" reasoning is wrong by two orders of magnitude (see the amplifier); "git worktree prune first because a stale entry holds refs" is moot; and the rf2-7ngc ep-corpus-coherence risk named in the description is CLOSED - its tip is byte-identical to merged PR #8812, the worktree and local branch were removed 2026-09-04, no ref matching corpus exists - so there is nothing for gc to lose there and the runbook carries no special step for it.

WHAT THIS BEAD NOW IS. An operator act with a paste-ready runbook, owned by Mike, executed once at a session boundary; retitled to name the act; P2 because it is bounded (about an hour, unattended) and gets longer every day it waits while every object-enumerating git command across 31 worktrees pays now. Not a hygiene-loop task. Close it only when the RESULT note (before/after counts, wall time) is on it.
THE RUNBOOK. Git Bash, mayor checkout. Not through an agent tool call; not piped through a filter (a pipe hides git's exit status and, with stderr no longer a tty, its progress meter). Each block runs to completion before the next.

PRE-FLIGHT (every line must hold; if one does not, stop and come back at the next boundary):

    cd /c/Users/miket/code/re-frame2
    date "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z"

    # 1. Quiet: loop stopped, fleet reaped, nothing holding the object store.
    tail -8 ai/worktree-agent-ids.tsv                 # every row from this session has reported
    tasklist | grep -iE '^(git|java)\.exe'            # expect NOTHING (close editors with git integration too)
    ls .git/index.lock .git/HEAD.lock .git/worktrees/*/index.lock 2>/dev/null   # expect nothing
    git log -3 --format='%ci %h %s'                   # last checkpoint minutes old, not seconds

    # 2. Tracker committed, tree clean, refs recorded, staged state known in EVERY worktree.
    git status --short                                # expect empty; if .beads is dirty: sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh
    git rev-parse HEAD origin/main                    # note both
    git worktree prune --dry-run --verbose            # expect no output
    for w in $(git worktree list --porcelain | awk '/^worktree /{print $2}'); do
      s=$(git -C "$w" diff --cached --name-status 2>&1); [ -n "$s" ] && echo "STAGED $w :: $s"; done
    # expect exactly the three ~/.grok subagent worktrees, each "M .beads/issues.jsonl" (blob 36c019fd, protected);
    # anything else staged is a worker mid-flight - not quiet, stop.

    # 3. Before-state.
    mkdir -p ai/findings
    git count-objects -vH   | tee ai/findings/gc-before-count.txt      # ~2 min
    git worktree list       | tee ai/findings/gc-before-worktrees.txt
    df -h /c                                          # 384 GB free on 2026-09-04; the run needs a few GiB

    # 4. Keep gc out of the foreground of future commits; clear the dead maintenance lock.
    git config maintenance.auto false
    ls -l .git/objects/maintenance.lock .git/gc.pid   # expect both, dated Jul 11 21:09
    rm .git/objects/maintenance.lock                  # gc.pid stays: git overwrites a >12 h pid file and removes it on exit

THE ACT (leave the terminal open; it needs no attention unless it asks):

    time git gc
    echo "gc exit=$?"                                 # this line, not the screen, is the verdict

Expect a progress meter through Enumerating / Counting / Compressing / Writing objects (~700k total), then a long quiet delete phase. Phases: pack-refs; reflog expire; repack -d -l --cruft --cruft-expiration=2.weeks.ago into one new pack plus, if any unreachable object is younger than two weeks, one cruft pack; prune --expire=2.weeks.ago of unreachable loose objects older than that (this removes the June-July dangling exports and the three tmp_obj_ garbage files from Jul 12/14/23); rerere gc; commit-graph write; worktree prune. Duration NOT measured - estimate 20-60 min (inflate 62 GiB of zlib, delta ~11,000 near-identical 10 MB blobs over 24 threads, write a pack on the order of 2 GiB, delete ~170k files on NTFS with Defender inspecting each). If Windows prints "Unlink of file ... failed. Should I try again? (y/n)", a process still has that pack mapped: find it (tasklist | grep -i git.exe), close it, answer y; or answer n and rerun later - neither loses anything. Ctrl-C at any point loses no data (every writer here writes a temp file and renames it into place at the end; the worst residue is a tmp_pack_ file in .git/objects/pack or duplicate loose objects, both removed by the rerun) but it does cost a full rerun: keep the transcript, run the post-checks, rerun in the next quiet window. Do not kill it from Task Manager unless Ctrl-C is impossible.

POST-CHECKS:

    git count-objects -vH | tee ai/findings/gc-after-count.txt
    # expect: count in the hundreds at most and size in KiB/MiB (0 if truly quiet), packs 1 or 2 (main + cruft),
    # size-pack on the order of 2 GiB (unmeasured), prune-packable 0, garbage 0

    ls .git/gc.pid .git/objects/maintenance.lock 2>&1 # expect BOTH absent (a surviving gc.pid means the run was killed)
    git rev-parse HEAD origin/main                    # identical to the pre-flight reading
    diff <(sed 's/ *$//' ai/findings/gc-before-worktrees.txt) <(git worktree list | sed 's/ *$//') && echo "worktrees unchanged"

title: beads backup remote has no retention policy — 130 .darc archives, 2.6 GB, two of them multi-GB and live
description:
