So none of this is deletable today and nothing here suggests hand-deleting any of it.

THE POINT IS THE ABSENCE OF A POLICY, NOT THE CURRENT SIZE. The Dolt filesystem backup remote writes on a 15-minute interval and rewrites its manifest each time. rf2-8az0 established the accrual rate for .beads as a whole at roughly +100 MB/day. Nothing in that bead, in .beads/config.yaml or in any bd verb documented there establishes how long an archive stays referenced, when an old one falls out of the manifest, or whether anything ever prunes an unreferenced one. rf2-8az0's own survey found a 2.5 GB orphaned quarantine directory from 2026-08-03 that had sat unreferenced for a month with nothing to notice it — which is the shape of the risk here.

WHAT IS WANTED: establish what the backup remote's retention actually is (read bd's own configuration and the manifest's behaviour over a few rotations rather than inferring it), and decide whether it needs bounding. If archives do fall out of the manifest over time, the follow-on question is whether anything deletes them or whether unreferenced ones simply accumulate as the quarantine directory did.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: deleting any currently-referenced archive; changing the backup interval; anything touching .beads/embeddeddolt. This is a measure-and-decide bead, not a cleanup one.

NOT URGENT. Disk is not tight (348 GB free at filing) and the immediate 2.4 GB has already been recovered. P3.
notes:
NOT WORKER-DISPATCHABLE — established 2026-09-06 22:46:02 AUSEST by the mayor before dispatching it, not after. Recording so the next tick does not re-derive it.

I had this queued as a sixth dispatch (it is conflict-free against every live worker fence, which is what made it attractive) and checked its reachability first. THE SUBJECT OF THIS BEAD DOES NOT EXIST IN A WORKER WORKTREE. Measured:

  mayor checkout      .beads/backup   PRESENT
  worker worktree     .beads/backup   ABSENT
  worker worktree     .beads/embeddeddolt   ABSENT
  a worktree's .beads holds only: README.md, config.yaml, hooks, issues.jsonl, metadata.json

The cause is deliberate and is in .beads/.gitignore at tip: 'embeddeddolt/' (line 3) and 'backup/' (line 57). Only the tracked files propagate into a linked worktree; the Dolt database and the filesystem backup remote live in the primary checkout alone. So a worker dispatched here would find nothing to measure, and the two ways out are both wrong — reaching into the mayor checkout violates the worktree boundary every brief carries, and running bd from a worktree does not reach the backup remote either.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS rf2-ah6r AND rf2-8az0: infrastructure whose subject is the mayor checkout itself. It is mayor or operator work, done at fleet-zero in the primary checkout, and it should be surfaced that way rather than sitting in the ready list looking dispatchable. It is NOT urgent — 418 GB free after the rf2-ah6r gc, and the 2.4 GB this bead's parent recovered is already banked — so the natural moment is the next quiet window, alongside anything else that wants the primary checkout.

ONE SCOPE NOTE FOR WHOEVER DOES RUN IT, learned while closing rf2-8az0: the discriminating control is a grep against .beads/backup/manifest, which is a plain extension-less text file. An earlier attempt searched for *.json/*.yaml/*.manifest and found nothing either way — a zero that proved only that the glob never reached the file. Any retention finding here needs the same one-hit-one-miss control.

title: docs(CLAUDE): distinguish curated API metadata from generated manifest
description:
PR #9324 (merge 88db8d696690673af3af68d8a700353564c53789) correctly puts spec/API.md and both manifest EDN files under one concurrency holding, but the new CLAUDE.md hot-zone bullet incorrectly calls BOTH sidecars generated and says both carry GENERATED / do NOT hand-edit headers. A worker following that rule cannot maintain the metadata that drives regeneration.

At this exact merge, spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:2-9 explicitly calls itself the CURATED, human-curated half: its tier/owner/status classification cannot be derived from code. implementation/scripts/api-manifest/src/re_frame/api_manifest/gen.clj:89-90 separates manifest-file from sidecar-file; read-sidecar at :757-759 reads the metadata; generate! at :1182-1191 builds from that input and spits ONLY manifest-file (api-manifest.edn). It does not regenerate the metadata or spec/API.md. Only api-manifest.edn has the GENERATED / do NOT hand-edit header.

Correct the input/output description in the new CLAUDE.md bullet while preserving the single-holding concurrency rule. Say the metadata is curated input and api-manifest.edn is generated output; maintaining a public name may require editing the metadata/API documentation before regenerating the manifest. No generator or manifest content change is needed.

Dedupe: searched all 1004 current issues, all statuses. rf2-kuky.82 and rf2-kuky.86 are consumers doing epoch/derivation changes, not owners of this CLAUDE.md instruction. The former already says edit metadata then regenerate manifest; the latter repeats the false regeneration premise. No exact existing owner of this instruction was found.

Verify the statement against both file headers and gen.clj read-sidecar/generate!; the fix must not impose a no-hand-edit rule on curated metadata or claim the generator writes all three files.
notes:
PR #9328 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9328), branch worker/claudedoc-a, head f42b8fee36. Bead left OPEN.

VERIFIED AT SOURCE at merge base 13d39b986e, all four claims:

- spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn carries NO such header; its head reads 'Public-API manifest - CURATED metadata sidecar (rf2-3nbl5.2). This file is the human-curated half of the public-API manifest's single-source design.'

Dropped 'the two generated ... sidecars' and the false 'the EDN files carry GENERATED headers regenerated by ...' clause; added one sentence saying one holding is not one kind of file - api-manifest.edn ALONE is generated output, api-manifest-metadata.edn is the CURATED INPUT the generator reads, spec/API.md is curated prose, and maintaining a public name means hand-editing API.md plus the metadata sidecar and THEN regenerating the manifest, with the no-hand-edit rule binding api-manifest.edn and nothing else. The lint.yml justification and the dispatch-filter anecdote are preserved verbatim.

AGENTS.md NOT touched and needed no change: censused three ways (line-oriented, whitespace-flattened, comment-markers-stripped-then-flattened) for 'api-manifest' / 'Hot-zone files' / 'Minimise merge conflicts' - zero on all three against a control needle returning 2. The shared tool-generated BEADS INTEGRATION block (hash:ca08a54f) is AGENTS.md:208-253 and CLAUDE.md:5-50; the edit at CLAUDE.md:100 is outside it in both files.

Out-of-fence files spec/API.md and spec/api-manifest*.edn were READ for verification and NOT edited.

GATES (exit code captured on the same command line as the redirect): check_readme_links.py --ci = 0 (this is the gate for repo-root markdown); check_doc_slugs.py = 0 and --self-test = 0 (both files are outside its 11 roots, so that green is a no-collateral check, not a gate on the change); check-commit-attribution.sh = 0; check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh = 0; check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh = 0; and 13 content ratchets (retired_composition_vocab, view_lifetime_residue, retired_spellings, retired_image_keys, inject_cofx_residue, failure_corpus_residue, allocation_non_claim, thrown_error_messages, ambient_durable_reads, keyword_catalogue_drift, architecture_census, require_alias_dialect, readme_inventories) = 0 each, run BEFORE the edit as well so the green is a comparison rather than an assertion.

WORKTREE PROOF: check_readme_links.py went RED (exit 1) on a fault planted at the edited line, naming CLAUDE.md:100 -> docs/rf2-uv60-planted-fault.md, a target existing only in this worktree; match count read as exactly 1 before the run so a no-op plant could not pass as green, and the restore verified by git blob hash rather than by reading a diff. check_doc_slugs.py affords no in-fence plant (all its roots are out of fence), so it was pinned with an explicit --repo-root and its detector shown to bite by --self-test.

title: spec(009/Spec-Schemas): the :revalidate-on catalogue + schema rows, and the malformed-value preflight rf2-kuky.33 could not land
description:
Filed by the rf2-kuky.33 worker (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9305). Three items the rf2-kuky.33 bead specifies fall in single-toucher spec files that were held by peers during that dispatch, so they were fenced OUT and deliberately not edited. None blocked the fold; all three are follow-on.

1. spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2272 — the :rf.error/resources-artefact-missing catalogue row's PROSE still names `install-revalidation-listeners!` among the resources APIs that raise it. That fn no longer exists. Replace the name with "a frame config declaring :revalidate-on" (the new emitter, added by PR #9305 at the frame-config commit chokepoint in re-frame.frame/upsert-frame!). Stale prose only: the ERROR ID is unchanged and still has emitters, so check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK A and CHECK C are both green today. This is the last remaining `git grep -E "(install|remove)-revalidation-listeners!"` hit that is not a deliberate retirement tombstone.

2. spec/009-Instrumentation.md — a NEW `:rf.error/invalid-revalidate-on` row, plus the MALFORMED-VALUE PREFLIGHT it would license. rf2-kuky.33 specified a fail-loud registration preflight rejecting a non-set value (`[:focus]`) or an unknown member (`#{:focsu}`) with zero residue. It was NOT shipped, and the reason is mechanical rather than a judgement call: check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK A requires every `:rf.error/<id>` literal emitted by implementation source to carry a Spec 009 catalogue row, so minting the id without the row reds a repo-wide gate, and the row could not be written from that worktree. The catalogue's own convention is one id per config key (`:rf.error/unknown-preset` for `:preset`, `:rf.error/invalid-url-strategy` for `:url-strategy`), so there is no existing id to reuse honestly.

   PR #9305 therefore follows the `:url-bound?` precedent for value handling — an unrecognised member selects no listener — and DOES ship the artefact-missing preflight, which needed no new id (`:rf.error/resources-artefact-missing`, the mirror of the :url-strategy-without-routing rule, with a test pinning :where, :frame-id and zero residue).

   The work here is: add the `:rf.error/invalid-revalidate-on` row to Spec 009 (sibling of :rf.error/invalid-url-strategy), then add a `:resources/preflight-frame-config!` seam beside `:routing/preflight-frame-config!` in re-frame.frame/upsert-frame! validating the value is a set whose members are a subset of re-frame.resources.revalidate-listeners/revalidation-triggers, with the failure-atomicity the routing preflight tests assert. Note the value-shape half is genuinely optional under the project stance ("trust the programmer", no nagging diagnostics) — decide it on merit rather than treating it as owed.

3. spec/Spec-Schemas.md FrameMeta — add `[:revalidate-on {:optional true} [:set [:enum :focus :reconnect]]]` beside `:url-bound?`. Documentation only: frame config is pass-through (re-frame.frame/frame-meta merges :config verbatim and core declares no closed key set), so nothing in core needs the key declared for it to work.

Also noted while in the file, NOT actioned and NOT part of this bead's scope: spec/API.md:526 (the `frame-state-value` row of the Registrar-query table) carries 6 columns where its header and separator carry 7. Pre-existing on origin/main, unrelated to revalidation; worth a one-line fix by whoever next holds the spec/API.md slot.
notes:
CROSS-REF 2026-09-06 17:28:46 AUSEST (from the rf2-uimu ruling, delegated by Mike): item 1 of this bead — spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2272 still naming install-revalidation-listeners! in the :rf.error/resources-artefact-missing catalogue row — is confirmed live at tip 13884f326f and confirmed as THIS bead's to fix. rf2-uimu's Conventions PR (lifecycle-verb roster: register-*/install-* rows) is fenced OUT of spec/009 and will not touch it, so there is no second toucher. No scope change here; recorded so the residue is not re-filed.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-06 (PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9329, open, ready-for-review; bead left OPEN pending merge). Items 1 and 3 SHIPPED; item 2 NOT shipped, decided on merit as the description asks. Shipped alongside rf2-uimu in one PR because both deliverables sit wholly inside the spec hot-zone files.

PREMISE CHECKED: rf2-kuky.33 is genuinely CLOSED (merged as PR #9311, rebased onto e43bec83ac, after PR #9305), so the predecessor landed and the follow-on work was still wanted. Item 1's residue was confirmed live at branch point 13d39b986e.

ITEM 1 (spec/009-Instrumentation.md, the :rf.error/resources-artefact-missing row). The row's Trigger prose named install-revalidation-listeners! among the APIs that raise it. Replaced: the API list drops it, and the sentence now reads '...was called, or a frame config declaring :revalidate-on was registered, but the optional day8/re-frame2-resources artefact ... is not on the classpath'. That wording was verified against the real emitter rather than taken from the bead - core.cljc:1013 documents ':revalidate-on without re-frame.resources FAILS LOUD at registration' and frame.cljc:3274-3280 is the frame-config commit chokepoint that raises it. Prose only: the error id, channel, category, recovery and tags columns are untouched, and the row is still 6 columns against a 6-column header and separator (hand-counted). This was the LAST non-tombstone (install|remove)-revalidation-listeners! hit in spec/; the surviving hits in docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1406, docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:325, spec/API.md:472 and spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1032 are all deliberate 'there is no such fn' tombstones or dissolution bookkeeping, and are untouched.

ITEM 3 (spec/Spec-Schemas.md FrameMeta). Added [:revalidate-on {:optional true} [:set [:enum :focus :reconnect]]] beside :url-bound?, with a comment recording frame-lifecycle ownership (creation installs, re-registration reconciles replace-don't-stack, dropping the key relinquishes, destroy removes), the absent-key/empty-set case, and the fail-loud :rf.error/resources-artefact-missing rule. The enum was verified against revalidation-triggers (#{:focus :reconnect}) at resources/revalidate_listeners.cljc:162.

THE HUNK NO GATE INSPECTED, AND HOW IT WAS CHECKED INSTEAD. The FrameMeta edit lands INSIDE a fenced clojure block (fence opens at Spec-Schemas.md:4282). Both link gates share one extractor that strips fences before reading a link, so NEITHER check_doc_slugs.py NOR mkdocs build --strict inspected that hunk at all - their exit 0s are silent about it. Checked by hand instead: the whole FrameMeta form was extracted by brace-balancing and run through the Clojure READER, which parsed it cleanly and read the new entry back as exactly [:revalidate-on {:optional true} [:set [:enum :focus :reconnect]]] across 13 map entries. The two doc links inside the added comment (016-Resources.md, beside the pre-existing 012-Routing.md) were confirmed to exist by hand for the same reason. Also confirmed no runtime consumer reads FrameMeta by name (git grep 'FrameMeta' over implementation returns nothing), and the three JVM suites the surface classifier names as extracting from Spec-Schemas.md all pass (see the gate list on rf2-uimu).

ITEM 2 IS NOT SHIPPED - the :rf.error/invalid-revalidate-on catalogue row and the malformed-value preflight. Two independent reasons, and the description explicitly delegates the call ('decide it on merit rather than treating it as owed').

(a) ON MERIT, AGAINST. The :url-strategy precedent it would follow exists because a malformed strategy blows up LATER at an arbitrary downstream call site with a raw host nil-function / TypeError - that is what spec/009's :rf.error/invalid-url-strategy row says in its own Trigger cell, and why routing pays for a registration-time preflight plus a dev consult tripwire. A malformed :revalidate-on has no such downstream: reconcile-listeners! documents and the suite tests that members outside revalidation-triggers select no listener, so [:focus] or #{:focsu} installs nothing and stops there - bounded, local and inert. Different hazard class, so rejecting the value is the nagging diagnostic the project stance declines, not the mirror of the routing rule.

(b) MECHANICALLY, NOT DELIVERABLE FROM A SPEC-ONLY FENCE. check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK C requires every ACTIVE :rf.error/* catalogue row to have a literal emitter in implementation source (verified by reading the gate, and exercised: renaming the resources-artefact-missing row's id took the gate to exit 1 naming both the now-uncatalogued emitted id and the now-emitterless row). The preflight seam lives in implementation/, outside this dispatch's fence, so the row alone reds a repo-wide always-on gate. Shipping half is strictly worse than shipping neither. This is the mirror image of the constraint that stopped rf2-kuky.33: there the row could not be written from that worktree, here the emitter cannot.

So the recommendation is to CLOSE item 2 as declined rather than re-dispatch it. If the operator disagrees, it must be ONE PR carrying both the Spec 009 row and the :resources/preflight-frame-config! seam, never a spec-only follow-up.

ALSO NOTED, NOT ACTIONED: the description's closing paragraph flags spec/API.md:526 (the frame-state-value row of the Registrar-query table) as 6 columns against a 7-column header. rf2-kuky.33's own close reason says that row was FIXED as part of its item 1 ('spec/API.md's 6-vs-7 column row also fixed (hand-counted: header 7, separator 7, all seven body rows 7)'), so that residue note is already stale and needs no follow-up. Not re-verified here because spec/API.md is outside this dispatch's fence.
MAYOR 2026-09-06 22:48:21 AUSEST, on specconv-a's report (PR #9329): ITEM 2 DECLINE ACCEPTED. Items 1 and 3 shipped in #9329.

The worker declined item 2 (a malformed-value preflight rejecting a bad :revalidate-on) on merit, which this bead explicitly delegates, and I am accepting it rather than overriding. Two independent reasons, both good:

(a) THE :url-strategy PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER. That precedent exists because a malformed strategy detonates LATER, at an arbitrary call site, as a raw host TypeError — the preflight converts an unattributable crash into a named error. A malformed :revalidate-on selects no listener and stops: bounded, inert, and attributable where it sits. Adding a rejection there is the nagging diagnostic the project stance declines, and 'trust the programmer' is the clause that decides it.

(b) IT CANNOT BE DONE AS A CATALOGUE ROW ALONE ANYWAY. check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK C requires every active catalogue row to have an emitter in implementation source, so a row without its preflight seam reds a repo-wide gate. The seam was outside #9329's fence. So the honest options were one PR carrying row AND seam, or decline — not a partial.

IF THIS IS EVER OVERRULED it must land as a single PR carrying both halves; a row-only change is not a smaller version of it, it is a red build.

ALSO STALE ON THIS BEAD, and worth striking rather than leaving to mislead: the closing residue note flags spec/API.md:526 as a 6-versus-7 column mismatch. rf2-kuky.33's own close reason records that row as already fixed. Nothing is owed there.

ITEM 2 DECLINED ON MERIT and accepted by the mayor — the :url-strategy precedent does not transfer (a malformed strategy detonates later as a raw host TypeError at an arbitrary call site; a malformed :revalidate-on selects no listener and stops, so rejecting it is the nag diagnostic the stance declines), and separately check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py CHECK C requires an emitter for every active catalogue row, so a row without its preflight seam is a red build rather than a smaller change. If ever overruled it must land as one PR carrying row AND seam. The closing residue note's spec/API.md:526 column complaint is stale — rf2-kuky.33's close reason records that row as already fixed.

title: spec(conventions): RULED A — Lifecycle-verb roster gains register-* and install-* rows and a scope sentence
description:
RULED 2026-09-06 (delegated by Mike; option A, extend and scope, with the second reviewer's corrected semantics — the ruling, both reviewers' full analyses and the pre-ruling description are in the notes). This description is the implementation brief. Single-worker spec task; the 2026-09-05 hold is lifted.

## The work, in one sentence
One spec-only edit to spec/Conventions.md §Lifecycle-verb law (hot-zone) that gives the closed roster the two setup verbs the tree already uses — `register-*` (paired with the existing `unregister-*` row) and `install-*` (its OWN row, not a pair with `destroy-*`) — narrows `attach!`/`detach!` to host-surface listeners, adds a scope sentence saying what the roster governs, fixes two stale lines in the law's own §Naming section, and clears one manifest justification. Zero runtime code, zero renames on any facade.

## The problem (measured at tip 13884f326f, 2026-09-06)
- The roster (Conventions :1265-1275) names teardown verbs (`clear-*`, `unregister-*`, `destroy-*`, `reset-*`) but never the setup half of the two that most need one: the `unregister-*` row (:1268) cites `unregister-listener!` as its exemplar while `register-*` is unrostered; the `destroy-*` row (:1269) cites `destroy-adapter!` with "lifecycle symmetry with the creating call" while the creating call, `install-adapter!`, is unrostered.
- SELF-CONTRADICTION inside one file: the ladder at :1303 says "Is it a listener add/remove? → `attach!` / `detach!`", while §Naming bucket 2 at :1328-1337 teaches `register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!` as the canonical listener shape. An author following :1303 in good faith coins the first-ever facade `attach-x!` beside ~429 files of `register-`. `attach!`/`detach!` has ZERO facade instances on any facade (spec/api-manifest.edn is the authority); its one live use is Xray's non-facade `keybinding/attach!`/`detach!` (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs:507,530), a window keydown listener — a genuine HOST-surface listener, which is the discriminator worth keeping.
- Two stale lines in the law's own bang section: :1336-1337's examples are 2-arity (`(rf/register-listener! ::audit (fn …))`, `(rf/unregister-listener! ::audit)`) where the fns take `[stream id f]` / `[stream id]` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2201,2236; spec/009 §The listener API agrees) — they cannot be pasted into working code; :1344 lists `install-adapter!, dispose-adapter!` where the public teardown has been `destroy-adapter!` since M-53 (the same file says so at :1396: "There is no `dispose-*` verb on the public surface and no alias").
- Subtraction cannot close this (verified by both reviewers): rf2-kuky.33 (closed) removed the revalidation pair; rf2-kuky.4 item (a) may delete `rf/install-adapter!` from the core facade but keeps `re-frame.substrate.adapter/install-adapter!` and touches none of Story; rf2-kuky.22 shrinks `register-listener!`'s streams but keeps the verb under all three of its options. Story's `install-canonical-vocabulary!` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc:648, 34 non-test files) and `register-substrate!` (story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:198) are facade exports (`:facade? true`) that no open bead touches.
- The manifest carries the deferral: spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1193 (`install-adapter!`) reads "RECORDED UNCERTAINTY (naming, not placement): install-* is not in the closed roster…".

## Exact edits (line numbers at tip 13884f326f — re-anchor by TEXT, they drift with every Conventions PR)
spec/Conventions.md — the ONLY hot-zone file in this PR:
1. Roster table (:1265-1275; 3 columns `Verb | Owns | Mechanism (the discriminator)`):
   a. Turn the `unregister-*` row (:1268) into `register-*` / `unregister-*`. Owns: add or replace, and remove, ONE callback or implementation keyed by id in a runtime hook table. Mechanism: the framework invokes the fn from arbitrary call sites; re-registering the same id REPLACES in place (reload-safe); removal is by id. Exemplars: `register-listener!` / `unregister-listener!`, `register-observability-sink!` / `unregister-observability-sink!`, `re-frame.story/register-substrate!`. Distinct from declarative `reg-*` registrar entries (no bang, §Naming bucket 1) and from `attach!` (host surface). `!` per §Naming bucket 2. Keep the existing row's "where `clear-*` would read as drop the whole registry" sentence.
   b. Add an `install-*` row of its OWN. Owns: wire a runtime capability, or seat the registrations that support it. Mechanism: process-level mutation outside the registrar (§Naming bucket 3 gives the `!`). An installer need NOT expose a destroy twin nor promise single-install semantics — only the adapter carries the generation contract (`install-adapter!` → `destroy-adapter!`; a second install without destroy raises `:rf.error/adapter-already-installed`). Exemplars: `rf/install-adapter!` (owner `re-frame.substrate.adapter`), `re-frame.story/install-canonical-vocabulary!` (facade); and, as owning-namespace instances that are `:facade? false` in the manifest, `re-frame.machines/install-machine-runtime!` (idempotent re-registration) and `re-frame.ssr/install-render-to-string!` (hands a renderer to a setter). `destroy-*` keeps its stronger instance-and-owned-resources meaning in its own row; cross-reference, do not merge.
   c. ## The decision

**Which of the following amends `spec/Conventions.md` §Lifecycle-verb law?**

- **A.** Extend the roster with `install-*`/`destroy-*` and `register-*`/`unregister-*` as named pairs, narrow `attach!`/`detach!` to host-surface listeners, and add one sentence scoping the roster to lifecycle *pairs*. Rule rf2-7nk1 in the same edit (`load-theme!`, no `load-*` row).
- **B.** Keep the roster as written and rename the survivors onto it (`register-listener!` → `attach-listener!` etc.).
- **C.** Keep the roster as written; record `install-*`/`register-*` as standing exceptions in the manifest justifications.
- **D.** Keep the hold until rf2-kuky.4 and rf2-kuky.22 land, then re-derive.

## Codex Recommendation

Choose **A with corrected semantics**: document `register-*` and `install-*`, clarify the roster's scope, and keep the working APIs. The inconsistency merits a small documentation repair. It does not justify a rename sweep, a runtime abstraction, or making every setup operation acquire a teardown twin. The proposed wording would otherwise replace one incomplete rule with another inaccurate one.

Independent inspection confirms the immediate problem. [Conventions](../../spec/Conventions.md) directs listener additions to `attach!`, then explicitly teaches `register-listener!` in its bang section. [Core](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc) implements registration as `[stream id f]`, replacement under the same stream/id, and removal as `[stream id]`; [009's listener contract](../../spec/009-Instrumentation.md#the-listener-api) agrees. Both Conventions examples omit `stream`, including the unregister example. Those examples cannot be copied into working code today.

The useful distinction appears in actual consumers. [Story's invariant runner](../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story/invariants.cljc) registers a temporary epoch observer under a generated key and unregisters that key in `finally`. The [pair skill's runtime](../../skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs) re-registers a stable trace-listener id so reload replaces its callback. In contrast, [Xray keybindings](../../tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/keybinding.cljs) retain the exact function passed to `document.addEventListener` so `detach!` removes that function after reload. These are useful differences in ownership and removal, not a vote decided by how many files contain each word. [Story's Hicasso example](../../tools/story/testbeds/hicasso_counter/core.cljs) also registers a renderer by substrate id; registration extends beyond observation listeners. [The production sink contract](../../spec/015-Data-Classification.md#frame-owned-observability-sink-policy) supplies another named use case: an application's APM integration registers its callback by sink id.

Two corrections materially change the proposed repair. First, the [manifest](../../spec/api-manifest.edn) marks `install-machine-runtime!`, `install-render-to-string!`, and the epoch home listener verbs `:facade? false`; the dossier's second table incorrectly calls them facade exports. Story's canonical installer and substrate registration really are facade exports, so subtraction still cannot remove the whole naming question.

Second, `install-*` does not consistently create an instance with a destruction boundary. [Machine installation](../../implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc) idempotently re-registers captured effects and subscriptions. [SSR installation](../../implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc) passes an existing renderer to a supplied setter. [Story's installer](../../tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc) seeds canonical vocabulary and also runs automatically on first registration. None establishes the adapter's particular generation contract. Even the suggested owning-namespace adapter pair is inaccurate: [the adapter owner](../../implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc) still defines `dispose-adapter!`; `destroy-adapter!` is the core facade name. Cite the actual qualified operations without silently turning this ruling into an internal rename.

I would express the convention as follows:

- `register-*` / `unregister-*` add or replace, and remove, a callback or implementation keyed by id in a runtime hook table. Keep the distinction from declarative `reg-*` registrar entries. `register-substrate!` must fit alongside listeners and sinks.
- `attach!` / `detach!` bind and unbind a listener on a host surface. Retain this useful convention even without a facade export; public API demand is not measured by a naming row's occurrence count.
- `install-*` wires a runtime capability or installs its supporting registrations. Describe its mutation under the existing bang rule. Keep `destroy-*`'s stronger instance-and-owned-resources meaning separate; an installer need not expose a destroy function or promise adapter-style single-install semantics.

Scope the closed choices to the operation families actually described: registration, installation, cleanup, observation, UI lifecycle, visibility, and configuration. They are not an exhaustive dictionary of all facade verbs. In particular, avoid “lifecycle pairs”: `watch-variant` returns its stop function, cache clearing need not have a setup twin, and hiding a panel preserves its lifecycle. State that a roster entry supplies naming guidance, not authority to add a missing inverse or read helper. Other operations choose descriptive names and follow the applicable bang convention. This resolves rf2-7nk1's roster objection without adding `load-*`; its final spelling remains that decision's responsibility.

The strongest alternative is keeping everything as designed and merely recording exceptions. Runtime behavior works, and pre-alpha time could go to larger problems. But the two invalid examples and contradictory naming instructions are cheap to correct and recur in author guidance. Renaming registrations to `attach-*` is viable technically, with no compatibility shim owed, but adds no capability and still leaves installation unspecified. Retaining the hold until boot pruning lands adds no necessary evidence: Story and registration survive. Recommend lifting it for this bounded repair, while coordinating overlapping edits; this review does not itself override the recorded hold.

Implementation should change the roster, naming ladder, examples, and only the affected manifest justifications, regenerating the manifest if its metadata changes. Do not bundle Story decorator renames, stream retirement, config readback, or the Xray implementation. Acceptance is a short classification walkthrough of the concrete operations above, exact example signatures checked against definitions, valid links and table columns, and the manifest generator's consistency check if applicable. No new runtime tests or whole-application rebuild are warranted for prose and rationale changes.

title: api(observability): Tool-Pair DCE tier rule is false at tip — rewrite it; tools attach via rf/register-listener!
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.4); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`spec/Tool-Pair.md:633-639` (anchor `facade-vs-home-verb-the-dce-tier-rule`, landed by rf2-rfid2x `eba72089b0`) rules that "canonical devtools attach via the per-stream home-namespace verbs… because a tool preload MUST NOT require `re-frame.core` into a production build", that "those namespaces do not require `re-frame.core`, so a dev-only tool preload that requires them is dead-code-eliminated out of production bundles wholesale", and that "the re-frame2 project template registers its default error sink via `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`". It then carries Story as "a deliberate exception". The same rule is restated in `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1382-1406` (comment plus the `:status` / `:justification` strings of `re-frame.core/register-listener!` and `unregister-listener!`) and `:2029-2037` (`re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!`), copied into `spec/api-manifest.edn` rows 160, 180, 198.

Measured at HEAD, every premise is false:

- `re-frame.core` requires `re-frame.trace` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:52`), which requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally on both platforms (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:39-49`); the facade's `:trace` arm and the home verb swap the same atom (`trace.cljc:951` → `trace/tooling.cljc:81`). Every bundle with the facade has the registry; the only elision lever is the `goog.DEBUG` gate around the CALL SITE (`trace.cljc:28-34`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1124-1135`), which both spellings need equally.
- The exemplar, `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs`, requires `re-frame.core` at `:13` (for `rf/with-frame` + `rf/dispatch` at `:79-80`) two lines above the comment at `:15-16` saying the home namespace keeps the tooling surface "independently elidable". 7 of the 10 non-test `:trace` home-verb files already require `re-frame.core` (measured: install.cljs, pair `runtime.cljs`, both testbeds, Story `frames.cljc` / `play.cljc` / `runtime.cljc`).
- `:events` / `:errors` are always-on — there is nothing to elide.
- The template's own test lists `register-listener!` among substrings that must NOT appear in any emitted file (`tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_test.clj:68-78`); `git grep -n "register-listener" tools/template` → that test line only.
- What actually keeps tools out of production is `:devtools/preloads` (dev builds only) plus the call-site gate; what kept Story's `:epoch` registration on the facade (Mike's revert `037f7d999e`) is that `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` is a hard classpath dependency — a fact of the REQUIRE line (`install.cljs:18`), not of the verb.

The rule protects nothing and licenses a second spelling; two tools straddle it (`install.cljs:67` home, Story `invariants.cljc:395` / pair `runtime.cljs:1272` / Xray runner `core.cljs:169` facade). A dual whose written discriminator the require graph contradicts is not a legitimate dual (`ai/findings/API-review/fable/README.md` §Ethos bar).

## Target API

No new API. One rule sentence replaces `Tool-Pair.md:633-639`:

> Listeners attach through `rf/register-listener!`, apps and tools alike. A tool stays out of production builds by being a `:devtools/preloads` entry and by gating its registration call site on `goog.DEBUG` ([009 §User-side listener registration]) — not by which namespace the call names: `re-frame.core` requires `re-frame.trace` requires `re-frame.trace.tooling` unconditionally, and both spellings swap the same registry. The home-namespace verbs (`re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!`, `re-frame.error-emit/register-error-listener!`, `re-frame.event-emit/register-event-listener!`, `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!`) are implementation seams — late-bind targets, framework-internal registrations and fixture clears — not a second public spelling. `:epoch` carries the one dependency fact: the facade no-ops when `day8/re-frame2-epoch` is absent; a tool that hard-requires `re-frame.epoch` at boot fails at compile time from the require, whichever verb it then calls.

Keep the anchor id (inbound links: `git grep -n "facade-vs-home-verb"`). The Story "deliberate exception" paragraph goes — Story is no longer an exception to anything.

Tool sites move to the facade (11 sites, 9 files; migrate each site's matching `unregister` too):

```clojure
;; install.cljs:45 — before / after
(rf.trace.tooling/register-listener! :rf.xray/trace-collector trace-collector/collect-trace!)
(rf/register-listener! :trace :rf.xray/trace-collector trace-collector/collect-trace!)

;; install.cljs:67 — before / after (KEEP the [re-frame.epoch] require at :18 — it is the hard dependency)
(rf.epoch/register-epoch-listener! :rf.xray/epoch-collector (fn [record] …))
(rf/register-listener! :epoch :rf.xray/epoch-collector (fn [record] …))
```

## Corroboration

One-reviewer; codex on the July doc: "Prefer… use the facade by default while retaining home operations only for demonstrated dependency needs… Story needs no special folklore if optional-producer tolerance is the stated reason… If a call site changes spelling, migrate its matching unregister operation as well and retain the same stream/id." Codex on this doc: "The DCE criticism usefully invalidates an unsupported blanket teaching rule… Verify any claimed bundle improvement with the existing positive-control build, not source greps alone." Grok: "The DCE sentence in Tool-Pair:633-639 is replaced, not enforced."

## Deletion list

- `Tool-Pair.md:633-639` (rule + Story exception) → the paragraph above.
- `install.cljs:15-16` comment; `:27` prose naming `re-frame.trace/register-listener!`.
- `api-manifest-metadata.edn:1382-1406` comment + the two rows' `:status` / `:justification` strings; `:2029-2037` comment + `register-epoch-listener!` `:status` ("tool-embedding form" wording) — rewritten to the rule above; then regenerate.

## Consumers to migrate (all → `rf/register-listener! <stream> …` / `rf/unregister-listener!`)

- Xray `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/install.cljs:45` (`:trace`), `:67` (`:epoch`).
- Story `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/frames.cljc:225,329`, `play.cljc:202`, `recorder.cljc:1023`, `runtime.cljc:103`, `ui/trace_buffer.cljs:164` (`:trace`). `recorder.cljc` and `ui/trace_buffer.cljs` do not yet require `re-frame.core` — add it (27 of Story's 138 source files already do).
- Pair preload `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1422` (`:trace`).
- Testbeds `testbeds/ssr_basic/core.cljs:94`, `testbeds/ssr_hydration_mismatch/core.cljs:81` (`:trace`).
- NOT migrated (framework-internal, stay on the home verb): `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:404`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:1221`, `frame.cljc:2810,3909` (late-bind hook).
- Do NOT delete or demote `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` here — `@trace-epoch.1` owns that door and its manifest rows; if that bead lands first and has already moved `install.cljs:67`, skip it.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` HOT-ZONE (one paragraph). Attach table `:598-603` already names the facade — unchanged.
- `tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md:606-614` names `re-frame.trace.tooling/register-listener!` for the trace panel → facade spelling; `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md:2777` names the retired `re-frame.core/register-epoch-listener!` → `(rf/register-listener! :epoch …)`.
- Xray spec: `git grep -n "register-listener\|register-epoch-listener\|trace.tooling" tools/xray/spec` → 0 at tip; the PR body states "Xray spec unchanged because no page names the verb".
- Manifest: after editing the sidecar, `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen`, then `--check`, `api-md-check`, `story-spec-check`, `xray-spec-check`, `skills-check`, `doc-api-check` (the `lint.yml` `api-manifest` job runs them).
- Tests: existing Xray install / Story invariants / pair preload suites; Story's `with-invariants` must still no-op without the epoch artefact (existing test); testbed builds are gated by `test.yml` `cljs-examples-compile` — `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` names them.
- Examples: 0 listener registrations. Migration README: no v1-era name. Skills: `skills/re-frame2-pair` preload is code, not prose.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

`Tool-Pair.md` is one-toucher — serialise with any `@egress` / `@trace-epoch` bead that edits it. Otherwise independent of observability.1/2/3/5 and of the ruling (the sentence holds under both targets; under Target A the stream list in it shrinks — observability.6's implementation bead edits it again).

## Risks

None to bundles (measured: the require graph is unchanged by the spelling; `npm run test:bundle-isolation` is the proof, and its `trace-tooling` sentinel must still read 0). A reader who learned the old rule from the manifest strings finds the new one in the same rows.

## Local dossier

ai/findings/API-review/fable/observability-doors.md (§The problem, fact 3; §Empirical use cases 1-2) and ai/findings/API-review/fable/listener-registration.md (history) — local-only pointers.

- `git grep -n "MUST NOT require" spec/Tool-Pair.md` → 0; `git grep -n "project template registers its default error sink"` → 0; `git grep -n "deliberate exception" spec/Tool-Pair.md` → 0; anchor `facade-vs-home-verb-the-dce-tier-rule` still resolves (`python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` exit 0).
- `spec/api-manifest.edn` rows for `re-frame.core/register-listener!`, `unregister-listener!`, `re-frame.epoch/register-epoch-listener!` no longer contain "DCE tier rule" / "tool-embedding form"; `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` exit 0 and every projection check green.
- `tools/xray`, `tools/story`, `skills/re-frame2-pair` suites green; `npm run test:bundle-isolation` green; `mkdocs build --strict` exit 0.
- PR body: one line per migrated site with its unregister counterpart, and "Xray spec unchanged because …".

title: api(subs): `:inputs` metadata slot + always-vector delivery, derived inline-image subs, normative spec pages
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from subscription-inputs.md (ref subscription-inputs.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Per the ruling on `@subscription-inputs.1`: `reg-sub` declares its dependencies positionally (`:<-` chain or a two-fn tail, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:87-170`) and hands a single input to the body as a bare value for `:<-` but as `[v]` for an `input-fn` (`subs.cljc:1284-1309`, `subs/memo.cljc:267-282`, `subs.cljc:2068-2098`). This bead lands the regular grammar and delivery; it does NOT yet delete the old grammar (that is `.6`, after the consumer sweeps `.3`–`.5`).

## Target API

```clojure
(reg-sub id ?metadata computation-fn)
;; metadata :inputs
;;   absent          → :input-kind :db          body (fn [db query-v] …)                      ;; unchanged
;;   [query-vector*] → :input-kind :static      body (fn [inputs query-v] …) — inputs a VECTOR
;;   fn-or-Var       → :input-kind :parametric  same body shape; inputs realized per concrete query-v
;; {:inputs []} → body receives [] (no dependencies); absent → app-db. Distinct by design.

(rf/reg-sub :cart/by-price {:inputs [[:cart/items]]}            (fn [[items] _] (sort-by :price items)))
(rf/reg-sub :cart/visible  {:inputs [[:cart/by-price] [:cart/filter]]} (fn [[items f] _] …))
(rf/reg-sub :article/page  {:doc "…" :inputs (fn [[_ id]] [[:article/by-id id] [:viewer]])} (fn [[a v] q] …))
```

**Parser (`parse-reg-sub-args`)** — `:inputs` is read from the metadata map and LIFTED into the runtime-owned slots `:input-kind` / `:input-signals` / `:input-fn` (one representation; it is not stored a second time on the registration — `handler-meta` keeps returning the slots tools already read). Rules: `vector?` → `:static`, shape-checked NOW by the existing pure `normalize-sub-inputs` (`subs.cljc:395-438`: every element a vector with a keyword head; `[:a :b]`, `:a`, a map, a derefable are rejected) and reported as `:rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args` (registration-time, dev-only — NOT `sub-input-fn-bad-return`, which stays the producer-result error at materialization); `fn?`/`var?` → `:parametric`, never executed at registration; any other value → `reg-sub-bad-args`. `:inputs` combined with a `:<-` chain or with two trailing fns → `reg-sub-bad-args` (over-specified). `:input-kind` / `:input-signals` / `:input-fn` in user metadata remain overridden by the runtime (the hostile-metadata pin in `ep0026_inline_grammar_cljs_test.cljc:128-163` keeps holding).

**Delivery** — every `:inputs`-declared sub (static or parametric) receives a VECTOR in all three paths: reactive `build-and-cache!*` (`subs.cljc:1284-1309`), `validate-and-trace` (`memo.cljc:267-282`), pure `compute-sub*` (`subs.cljc:2068-2098`); `compute-sub`, `subscribe-once` and the reactive path agree. **Transitional (deleted by `.6`):** `:<-` and the two-fn tail keep today's exact behaviour — bare-for-one static, vector parametric — so nothing in examples/tools/tests moves in this PR. Carry the distinction on the existing `vector-inputs?` boolean (`memo.cljc:229,248-254,724`), stamped by the parser (`true` for `:inputs`-declared and parametric, `false` for `:<-`), rather than inventing a second flag. The single-input memo specialisation `make-layer-n-single-input-memoised-body` (`memo.cljc:631-699`) STAYS for its allocation profile and hands `[v0]` when flagged (its parity suite `sub_memo_layer_n_1_test.clj` must keep its memo-hit assertions).

**Registrar metadata** — `reg_meta.cljc:63-71` `known-bare-keys :sub` gains `:inputs` (today it would warn `:rf.warning/unknown-registration-key`).

**Inline images (the layer-2 gain)** — `lower-inline-sub` (`subs.cljc:2466-2514`) reads `:inputs` from the normalized metadata and lowers through the SAME function public `reg-sub` uses (one dependency-normalization fn for both paths — codex's refinement; today 2508-2511 hard-codes `:input-kind :db`). `image.cljc:284-306` `reg-section->kind` is unchanged except its comment at :291 ("the layer-1 db-reader form ONLY") — delete the carve-out. Provenance / `:coordinate` / descriptor shape unchanged.

**Tooling** — untouched by construction: `sub-topology` (`subs/tooling.cljc:57-118`), Xray `level-1?` / `topology-input-sub-ids` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs:376-422`), `derivation_graph.cljs:279`, pair-mcp `list_subscriptions.cljs:33-49`, the `:rf.sub/create` trace tag (`subs.cljc:284-289`) all read the slots. A literal `{:inputs [[:a]]}` therefore reports `{:input-kind :static :inputs [[:a]]}` and a producer reports `:parametric` with no new tool code.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer (codex rf2-snkw proposed the slot and the always-vector rule; fable verified the arms and ran the census); the design decision is on `@subscription-inputs.1`. Codex's two refinements are binding here: one normalization fn for public and inline registrations; absent vs explicit `[]` distinguished.

## Deletion list (this bead)

- `subs.cljc:2508-2511` the `:input-kind :db` forcing in `lower-inline-sub`; `image.cljc:291` "layer-1 db-reader form ONLY".
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:376-396` `SubMeta`'s `:rf/inputs` / `:rf/layer` "runtime-stamped" slots — **spec drift**: zero hits for either keyword in `implementation/` at HEAD; the real runtime-owned slots are `:input-kind` / `:input-signals` / `:input-fn`. Replace with the user key `:inputs` (schema: vector of query vectors, or fn) and name the runtime-owned slots.
- The delivery-shape sentences at 006:1020, 008:485-490, Principles.md:42 (rewritten, see below). Nothing else is deleted here; the `:<-` arms stay until `.6`.

## Consumers to migrate

None in this bead (transitional). Tests that pin the old delivery stay green untouched.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

**Spec (ALL hot-zone one-toucher — this bead is the only toucher until `.6`; mayor serialises):**
- `spec/API.md:113-156` §`reg-sub` input-production modes → §`reg-sub` `:inputs` (the modes table becomes the three-row `:inputs` grammar; the registrars table's `reg-sub` signature becomes `(reg-sub id ?metadata computation-fn)`).
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1014-1067` §Subscription input producers: `:inputs` is the producer; delivery is always a vector; "static `:<-` is exactly a constant input-fn" becomes "a literal `:inputs` vector is exactly a constant producer"; fixed-topology / purity / no-app-db-topology / frame-resolution paragraphs unchanged.
- `spec/008-Testing.md:456-502` §`compute-sub` algorithm: `body-arg` collapses to two arms (`:db` → db; else → vector(values)).
- `spec/Conventions.md:1078-1103` §`reg-sub` input grammar: title and body re-pointed at `:inputs`.
- `spec/Principles.md:42` §Uniform context-map callbacks: keep "a sub computation fn is deliberately not in this family (positional `(fn [inputs query-v] …)`)"; replace the bare-value rationale with the ruling (declared inputs always arrive as a vector; the v1 bare-for-one convention was retired under `@subscription-inputs.1`, dated).
- `spec/002-Frames.md:1552-1562` §Subscriptions composing: the `:pending` example.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:376-396` §SubMeta (drift fix above).
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1985` `:rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args` row: the accepted shape is now the `:inputs` grammar; add "malformed literal `:inputs`" to its triggers. Keyword ids unchanged (`scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` stays green).
- `spec/001-Registration.md:295` `:sub` replace row ("sub body and `:<-` chain" → "and `:inputs`").
- Other `:<-` mentions in spec (139 across 24 pages at HEAD) are `.6`'s; do not sweep them here.

**Docs / skills (teaching pages that define the grammar — the rest is `.5`):** `docs/EP/EP-0004-subscription-inputs.md:236-266` (§Static `:<-` sugar → §Literal `:inputs`) and 457-479 (§Single input: the v2 body no longer changes shape between literal and computed — one rewrite, not two); `docs/EP/EP-0026-*.md:452-461` (inline `:reg-sub` accepts derived subs via `:inputs`); `docs/core/subscriptions.md` (17 `:<-` mentions, 7 registrations; delete the "only wrinkle" paragraph at 185-189); `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:57-73` (§`reg-sub` signature and table); `skills/re-frame2/references/fundamentals/subs.md:8-36`. No docs page is digest-pinned any more (the freehand guide gate is retired; verified: no `check_guide_samples` / `samples_coverage` in scripts or tests).

**api-manifest:** `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:813` `reg-sub` status `"v1 (preserved + extended)"` → a status naming the grammar change (e.g. `"v1 name; grammar changed to :inputs (rf2-<.1 id>)"`), justification updated; regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` with `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/`; `--check` green. `docs/api/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/core/**` are manifest projections scanned by `lint.yml`'s api-manifest job, so that job must be green on the PR.

**Tests to add (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/`, JVM `.clj` unless a reactive path needs CLJS):**
- parser: `:inputs` literal / fn / Var / `[]` accepted; `{:inputs [:a :b]}`, `{:inputs :a}`, `{:inputs {:a [:a]}}`, `:inputs` + `:<-`, `:inputs` + two fns → `:rf.error/reg-sub-bad-args` at registration; no `:rf.warning/unknown-registration-key` for `:inputs`; `handler-meta` shows `:input-kind`/`:input-signals`/`:input-fn` and no duplicate `:inputs`.
- delivery: single literal input → `[v]` in reactive, `subscribe-once` and `compute-sub`; `[]` for explicit empty; N inputs in declaration order; map / vector / nil upstream values; the SAME body registered once under `{:inputs [[:a]]}` and once under `{:inputs (fn [_] [[:a]])}` returns the same value (the codex acceptance).
- memo: single-input specialisation still short-circuits on `=`-equal upstream (extend `sub_memo_layer_n_1_test.clj`, 9 sites) while delivering `[v0]`.
- transitional: existing `:<-` / two-fn suites untouched and green (`sub_parametric_inputs_test.clj:246-252` still passes).
- inline image: one static and one parametric derived sub authored inline (`{:registrations {:reg-sub [[id {:inputs …} body]]}}`) — subscribe resolves in the image's frame, `sub-topology` shows the static edge, re-load/replacement and frame isolation behave as public registrations (extend `ep0026_inline_grammar_cljs_test.cljc` — rewrite `inline-sub-lowers-to-layer-1-db-reader-only` at :128 — and `subs_inline_normalization_cljs_test.cljc`).
- topology: `sub-topology` for a literal `:inputs` = `{:input-kind :static :inputs [[…]]}`; producer = `:parametric` sentinel; `sub_topology_test.clj` gains both.
- conformance: extend `spec/conformance/fixtures/image-inline-grammar.edn` (or add `image-inline-derived-sub.edn`) with a derived inline `:reg-sub` and run it through `conformance_runner.cljc`; `spec/conformance/README.md` row.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Blocked by `@subscription-inputs.1`. Touches hot-zone `spec/API.md`, `spec/006`, `spec/002`, `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`, `spec/009` — one PR, no other toucher of those pages in flight. Unblocks `.3`, `.4`, `.5` in parallel. Worker runs the guard (`sh scripts/assert-worker-worktree.sh`) before editing.

## Risks

- Threading `vector-inputs?` for `:inputs`-declared static subs through the single-input specialisation: get the memo-hit structure right (the layer-n-1 parity tests are the witness).
- Explicit `{:inputs []}`: today the static-zero arm delivers `nil` (`memo.cljc:273-274`, `subs.cljc:2089-2090`); under `:inputs` it must deliver `[]`.
- Spec pages describe only `:inputs` while `:<-` is still accepted until `.6`; state this in the PR body.

description:
Measured 2026-09-06 22:5x AUSEST by the mayor on PR #9330 (worker xrayclaims-a), the first worker PR to meet the PR-body arm that rf2-1ndt landed in #9326.

WHAT HAPPENED. #9330's rollup carried one real failure: the job 'Beads PR boundary (no tracker database in a PR)'. The PR touched NO .beads path at all (31 files, zero under .beads/), so the job NAME is a red herring — since #9326 that step runs a SECOND invocation, scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh over the branch commits AND the PR body. It was the body arm that fired.

AND THE LINE IT FIRED ON WAS THE BODY'S OWN DISCLAIMER. Line 98 read, at column 0:
  No `Co-Authored-By: Claude` and no `Generated with [Claude Code]` trailer, in the commit message or in this description...
i.e. the sentence in which the worker states it COMPLIED is what the guard refuses. Reproduced locally against the live body with a control that discriminates: original body -> exit 1, same body with that one line indented by one space -> exit 0, byte count +1 exactly.

THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF, and that is why it is a P2 rather than a note. Every worker dispatch brief in this project instructs the worker to declare that it declined the trailers, and workers naturally put that declaration in the PR body as well as in their report. So this reds a PR per worker per wave until something changes. Three of the five workers in the current wave carry the same sentence in their reports.

THE GUARD IS ARGUABLY CORRECT AS DESIGNED — it deliberately has an indent hatch ('Only column 0 offends'), it prints that hatch in its own failure text, and a substring rule that exempted the word 'No' in front would be trivially defeatable. So the fix is NOT obviously in the detector. THE OPTIONS, none ruled:
  (a) Fix the BRIEFS: tell workers that a compliance statement in the PR body must be indented one space. Cheapest, zero code, but it is prose discipline against a mechanical gate and will be forgotten.
  (b) Fix the guard so a line that is clearly a NEGATIVE assertion does not trip rule 3. Fragile and defeatable; likely rejected under the stance.
  (c) Drop the instruction to declare compliance in the PR BODY at all — the declaration belongs in the worker's report to the mayor, which no gate reads. The PR already proves compliance by passing the guard, so the sentence is redundant with the gate that it breaks. This is my recommendation.
  (d) Make the job NAME honest, separately from all of the above: 'Beads PR boundary' now grades attribution too, and a worker reading that name will look for a tracker file it never committed. That is the same nominate-by-path-not-by-job-name trap CLAUDE.md already records for the two link gates.

INTERIM: the mayor edited #9330's body (indented the one line) rather than dispatching a fix worker, because CLAUDE.md assigns PR descriptions to the mayor — 'Both arms cover commit MESSAGES only; a PR description is still on you.' Note that a body edit does NOT re-trigger the workflow (no 'edited' type on the pull_request trigger, deliberately per rf2-1ndt), so the failed job must be re-run by hand afterwards.

3. Read the workflow to find out why. test.yml:1335 sources the body as PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}. That is the EVENT PAYLOAD, frozen when the run was created. A re-run replays the same payload, so it re-reads the OLD body forever. No number of re-runs can clear it.

SO THE ONLY REMEDIES ARE THINGS THAT MINT A NEW EVENT. test.yml's pull_request trigger declares no types:, so it takes the default set — opened, synchronize, reopened. That gives two:
  (a) push to the branch (synchronize) — costs a fabricated commit if there is no real change to make;
  (b) close and REOPEN the PR (reopened) — costs nothing in history.
I used (b) on #9330. Both re-run the entire 87-check suite, which is the real cost either way.

WHY THIS RAISES THE STAKES ON THE RULING. Option (a) in my original note — 'fix the briefs' — now has to be read as the ONLY cheap remedy, because once a worker has opened a PR with the sentence in it, the cleanup is a full re-run of every check plus an out-of-band close/reopen that no worker can perform for itself (it is the mayor holding the PR). That asymmetry did not exist when I filed this: I described it as a red PR with a one-space fix, and it is actually a red PR with a one-space fix PLUS an 87-check re-run PLUS a mayor intervention.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS UNCHANGED IN DIRECTION AND STRONGER IN FORCE: option (c), stop asking workers to declare compliance in the PR BODY at all. The declaration belongs in the report to the mayor, which no gate reads; the PR proves compliance by passing the guard. I have already applied this to briefs written after the discovery (the rf2-t6yr dispatch carries it), but the DOCUMENTED instruction has not changed and that is Mike's call.

ONE THING I AM NOT PROPOSING: adding 'edited' to the trigger types so a body edit re-fires the check. It would fix this symptom and make every prose tweak to any PR body re-run the full suite. rf2-1ndt deliberately did not add that type.
REMEDY COST MEASURED — CLOSE/REOPEN CLEARS THE CHECK BUT PERMANENTLY BREAKS THE ROLLUP'S BAND TEST. Measured on PR #9330 immediately after using it.

WHAT THE REOPEN DID. It minted a fresh event payload, and the new run's `Beads PR boundary` job passed — confirmed by reading the two check runs of that name at the SAME head oid 522617c603:
  run 34034417513 (pre-reopen)   FAILURE
  run 34035771516 (post-reopen)  SUCCESS
So the remedy works. The body fix was real and the guard now agrees.

BUT THE ROLLUP KEEPS BOTH GENERATIONS. `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` returned 173 entries across EIGHT workflow runs — a full pre-reopen generation (34034417512/513/525/530 = 8+71+3+5 = 87) and a full post-reopen generation (34035771456/465/485/516 = 3+5+8+70 = 86 and still settling). Restricted to the newest generation alone: 70 checks in the main run, 20 success, 48 skipped, ZERO failures, 2 non-terminal.

WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PR. The merge criterion's clause 1 tests the rollup count against a band measured this tick, and clause 2 requires every check passed-or-skipped. A reopened PR fails BOTH on their literal reading, forever: its total is roughly twice the band, and the superseded generation's FAILURE rows never leave the rollup. So the remedy converts a clearable red into a PR that no longer satisfies the criterion as written, and the merge decision has to be made by deduplicating the rollup by workflow-run generation first — which is not a step the criterion describes.

THE DEDUPLICATION THAT ANSWERS IT, recorded so the next reader does not invent a different one: extract the run id from each entry's detailsUrl, take the newest generation, and apply clauses 2 and 3 to that subset alone. The stale rows are superseded by construction — same head oid, later run, same job names — so they are evidence about a payload that no longer exists rather than about the code.

NOTE WHICH DIRECTION THIS FAILS. Clauses 1 and 2 fail CLOSED here: they block a PR that is actually green, rather than admitting one that is red. That is the safe direction and no change to the criterion is urgent. But somebody will meet this again the next time a PR is reopened for any reason, and the natural reflex — subtract the stale rows by eye — is exactly the kind of by-eye adjustment clause 1 exists to prevent.

THIS STRENGTHENS OPTION (c) FURTHER. The full chain for one unindented sentence is now: red PR, a body edit that cannot clear it, a close/reopen, a second full 87-check CI generation, and a permanently deduplication-requiring rollup. Not writing the sentence costs nothing.

title: api(observability): teach the frame sink first — how-to, observability guide, docs/api, and the discriminator sentence
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.5); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The spec rules the frame `:observability` sink the NORMAL production observation surface and the corpus-wide `:errors` / `:events` streams the ADVANCED hook (`spec/API.md:575,585`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1258-1262`, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270-300`, `spec/Conventions.md:1322-1331`). The teaching corpus disagrees three ways:

1. `docs/core/how-to/report-errors-in-production.md` builds the Sentry bridge on `register-listener! :errors` across §1-§7 (`:19-272`; the first code block is at `:24-32`) and reaches the sink at §8 (`:273`, "Prefer the frame sink…"). `docs/core/observability.md:426-480` introduces the two streams and their record shapes before the sink at `:481`. `docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md:33` says "wire your APM and error monitor here, or — the normal off-box path — declare a frame sink". `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:957-967` shows Datadog and Sentry on the raw streams. `docs/core/errors.md:491` teaches `(rf/register-listener! :errors ::sentry report!)`. `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:514-520` and `:1307` say error observability "moves to the always-on `:errors` stream". The pages that already teach sink-first: `docs/resources/tutorial/05-test-and-ship.md:300-308`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/production-observability.md:1-17`, `observability.md:481-506`, `spec/009:1272-1281`.
2. The stated discriminator — the corpus-wide record "carries the raw `:exception`" (`API.md:585`, `009:1258`, how-to `:275-277`) — is not one: the sink delivers `:exception` too under the default profile; `implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:352-363` drops it only under `:rf.egress/public-error`, and the how-to says so itself at `:298`. The corpus-wide door's only unique carries are (i) FRAMELESS `:frame nil` records, which no frame policy can route (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc:321-325`; how-to `:311` already says this), and (ii) not declaring a policy on every frame (no process-level default exists: `core.cljc:2554-2605` `configure!` has no `:observability` key — observability.6's question).
3. `production-observability.md:77,219` says `:rf.trace/no-emit?` is "framework-internal and not yours to set"; `observability.md:624-668` teaches both opt-out flags to tool authors, which is `009:1005-1046`'s contract.

## Target

The how-to leads with the sink and ends with the advanced door, stating exactly what is unique about it:

- §1 Declare the policy on the frame and register the sink (`make-frame {:observability {:errors [{:sink …}]}}` + `register-observability-sink!`); §2 gate it (unchanged); §3 branch on `(:error record)` (unchanged — the projected record keeps `:error`); §4 the frame-teardown report — under the sink the non-event slots are lifted onto `:tags` (`observability.cljc:299-330`), so the sample reads `(get-in record [:tags :hook-failures])`, not `(:hook-failures record)`; §5 what survives (profiles: the default keeps `:exception`, `:rf.egress/public-error` drops it — `:298` moves up); §6 verify in dev; §7 `:handled-events` as the metrics sibling; §8 "Advanced — the corpus-wide listener": one fan-out per process, unprojected, and its two unique carries (frameless records; no per-frame declaration) — and one sentence that the exception is NOT one of them.
- `observability.md:426-480`: the sink paragraph (`:481-506`) comes first after "What survives"; the stream record shapes follow as the advanced tail.
- `configure-dev-and-prod.md:33`: sink first, streams as the advanced hook; `:140-143` unchanged beyond observability.1's `:opts` drop.
- `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:952-967`: the `:events` / `:errors` examples become neutral capture examples (a test-kit capture, a cross-frame audit tap) — the Datadog / Sentry samples live under `register-observability-sink!` (`:1107-1130`) already.
- `docs/core/errors.md:491`: sink first, listener as the advanced form.
- `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md:514-520,1307`: "observability moves to the frame `:observability` sink (normal) or the always-on `:errors` stream (advanced, corpus-wide)" — one line each. HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/API.md:585` and `spec/009:1258` gain one sentence: "The sink also delivers `:exception` under the default `:rf.egress/off-box-observability` profile (only `:rf.egress/public-error` drops it); what the corpus-wide stream alone carries is a frameless record and a declaration made once per process rather than per frame." HOT-ZONE.
- No-emit prose: reconcile `production-observability.md:77,219` to `009:1005-1046` (the handler and frame opt-outs are documented knobs for tool authors — Xray / Story / pair use them; 57 tool sites) — the doc's reading wins, no API change.

Under a Target-A ruling (observability.6) the advanced tail is deleted; under Target B it stays. The reorder is right either way, so it does not wait on the ruling.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer; codex: "Lead the production how-to with a frame-owned projected sink. State plainly what is projected, what happens to exceptions, and when the advanced corpus-wide listener is appropriate. Reconcile the manifest, tool guidance, and examples around that distinction." Grok: "Rewrite `report-errors-in-production.md` so the sink is the first recipe." Fable (Target B minimum): "reorder the how-to so §8 is §1; add the one sentence the docs currently lack."

## Deletion list

None in code. Prose only.

## Consumers to migrate

None. `docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:519` ("captured at Spec 009's `:events` port") is accurate today — untouched here.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

Files: the seven docs pages above, `spec/API.md:585`, `spec/009:1258` (one sentence each), migration README (two lines), `production-observability.md:77,219`. Examples: 0 (the how-to's samples are prose blocks, not `examples/`). Manifest: no var changes. Tests: none — but `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`'s `doc-api-check` / `doc-guide-check` / `skills-check` scan these pages for var names; run `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` and the projection checks. Gates: `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (docs/, spec/, skills/, migration/ — anchors and repo-relative targets), `mkdocs build --strict` (link resolution in the built site; spec/ and migration/ are staged by `mkdocs_hooks.py`). The how-to's §8 heading anchor (`prefer-the-frame-sink-for-metrics-and-privacy-bound-egress`) may have inbound links — `git grep -n "report-errors-in-production.md#"` and update each. Tables and column counts by hand; say so in the PR body.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

`spec/API.md` (also observability.1), `spec/009` (also observability.2 and rf2-6g6e PR #9182), migration README (also observability.3) — run after those three. Independent of observability.4.

## Risks

None functional. Under a Target-A ruling the advanced section is deleted again — a small second edit, accepted over teaching the wrong order for the interval.

title: docs(xray): RULED B — scope the production-elision guarantee to build placement; rewrite ~18 claim sites
description:
RULED B on 2026-09-06 (RULING note on this bead): Xray is kept out of production by BUILD PLACEMENT, not by construction. This bead is now the prose sweep — one worker, one PR, no code behaviour change. Option A (gate init!/mount on goog.DEBUG + an Xray-rooted elision probe) was DECLINED; its un-park triggers are in the RULING note. The full analysis (both reviewers) is attached in notes as DOSSIER ATTACHMENT; the pre-ruling description is preserved in notes as ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION.

PROBLEM (measured at tip 6d513ba07f, 2026-09-06; re-measure at yours)

Xray has two install paths and one gate. The preload path (day8.re-frame2-xray.preload via shadow-cljs :devtools/preloads) wraps its boot block in (when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...) (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:94-133), which Closure folds away under :advanced + {goog.DEBUG false}. The manual path — require day8.re-frame2-xray.core, (xray/init!), a mount verb — has NO gate: init! (core.cljs:159-184) registers 37 :rf.xray/* handlers, the trace/epoch collectors, six window.day8.re_frame2_xray.* globals and the Ctrl+Shift+C keydown listener unconditionally; open!/open-overlay!/toggle!/popout! are bare def-aliases of mount/*; mount/open! (:929-964) gates only on substrate-adapter presence (:960), which every production app that called rf/init! has. Requiring the facade at all runs load-time registrations: seven register-first-mount-hook! forms at mount.cljs:682-845, nine top-level rf/reg-view forms in shell.cljs (:991-:2565, reaching registrar/register! regardless of goog.DEBUG), and keybinding.cljs:602. No CI gate proves Xray's absence from an optimised bundle: npm run test:elision roots re-frame.* sentinels only; implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs contains zero Xray sentinels.

Yet ~18 sites assert the opposite ("zero bytes", "MUST be gated", "CI verifies via test:elision", "mount never reaches production builds"). PR #9226 (merged 2026-09-04, 726d8bf1df) corrected skills/re-frame2-xray/** only, so the repo now teaches two contradictory models of one safety property.

TARGET WORDING — the skill's three facts, in the same words at every site:
1. The preload is dev-only because :devtools/preloads is dev build configuration; its debug-enabled? block folds under goog.DEBUG=false as a second line of defence for that path only. The trace/epoch collectors gate their own entry points (trace_collector.cljs, drop_in.cljc).
2. The manual init!/mount path carries NO goog.DEBUG gate. Exclusion is the host's job: put the :require AND the calls in a namespace only the dev entry point loads (recipe: skills/re-frame2-xray/references/launch-programmatic.md, section "Keeping the manual path out of production" — link or restate it; a bare "guard the require" is not enough guidance). Guarding only the calls is insufficient because requiring the facade runs load-time registrations.

## The problem

Xray has two install paths and one gate. The **preload** path — `day8.re-frame2-xray.preload` wired into shadow-cljs's `:devtools/preloads` — wraps its whole boot block in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/preload.cljs:94`, block runs to :133). `debug-enabled?` is a `@define` alias of `goog.DEBUG` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs:224`), so under `:advanced` + `{goog.DEBUG false}` Closure constant-folds the block away. That is the only gate on the path. The **manual** path — `(require '[day8.re-frame2-xray.core :as xray])` then `(xray/init!)` and a mount verb — has none:

```clojure
;; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/core.cljs:159-167 — init!'s body, verbatim
([{:keys [target-frame theme density buffer-depths] :as _opts}]
 (registry/register-xray-handlers!)          ; 37 reg-* calls, registry.cljs:434
 (install/register-trace-collector!)
 (install/register-epoch-collector!)
 (install/install-browser-api-exports!)      ; window.day8.re_frame2_xray.*, install.cljs:111-125
 (keybinding/attach!)                        ; global Ctrl+Shift+C keydown listener
 …)

;; core.cljs:71-107 — the mount verbs are bare def-aliases, ungated
(def open! … mount/open!)   (def open-overlay! … mount/open-overlay!)
(def toggle! … mount/toggle!)   (def popout! … mount/popout!)
```

`mount/open!` (`mount.cljs:929-964`) gates only on `(rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter)` at :960 — and every app that called `rf/init!` has an adapter in production exactly as in dev, so adapter presence discriminates nothing. Worse, requiring the facade at all transitively loads `mount.cljs`, whose bottom runs **seven top-level `register-first-mount-hook!` calls** (:682, :720, :756, :791, :804, :820, :845) — a private fn doing `swap!` on a `defonce` atom (:480) — at namespace-load time, before any call of the host's. A host that wraps only the *calls* in `(when ^boolean goog.DEBUG …)` is not protected.

**What a consumer gets today.** Take an ordinary app namespace, compiled `:advanced` with `{goog.DEBUG false}`:

```clojure
(ns my-app.core
  (:require [re-frame.core :as rf]
            [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as reagent]
            [day8.re-frame2-xray.core :as xray]))   ; the documented manual path

(defn ^:export init []
  (rf/init! reagent/adapter)
  (xray/init! {:theme :dark})
  (xray/open!))
```

The release bundle: registers 37 `:rf.xray/*` handlers into the app's registry; installs six `window.day8.re_frame2_xray.*` globals; attaches a document-wide keydown listener; creates `#rf-xray-root` inside `[data-rf-xray-host]` (or logs a missing-host `console.error`) and renders the whole shell — app-db inspector, epoch scrubber, EDN viewer, every panel — reading the live `app-db` of a shipped binary. The trace and epoch *collectors* are the one inert part: `trace_collector.cljs` gates its own entry points (:250, :299, :359, :380), as does `drop_in.cljc` (:299, :347, :393). The retained byte count is unmeasured — nothing in the repo compiles Xray under `goog.DEBUG=false`, which is the second half of this bead.

**The same app under the proposed shape (A).** Nothing in the host changes; the gate moves into Xray, in the form Xray's own `trace_collector.cljs:250` and `drop_in.cljc:299` already use:

```clojure
;; core.cljs — init!'s second arity
([{:keys [target-frame theme density buffer-depths] :as _opts}]
 (when rf.interop/debug-enabled?          ; folds to nothing under goog.DEBUG=false
   (registry/register-xray-handlers!)
   …)
 nil)

;; mount.cljs — inside open! (and open-overlay!, toggle!, popout!); the
;; def-alias in core.cljs is untouched, so (identical? mount/open! core/open!) still holds
(defn open! []
  (when rf.interop/debug-enabled?
    (if-let [state @mount-state] … (when (rf.substrate.adapter/current-adapter) …))))

;; mount.cljs bottom — one gate around the seven load-time registrations
(when rf.interop/debug-enabled?
  (register-first-mount-hook! ::seed-trace-and-target-frame …)
  … ;; six more
  )
```

In the release bundle `xray/init!` and `xray/open!` return nil, no handler, global, listener or DOM root is created, and the panels, shell and registry bodies — referenced only from folded branches — are eliminated. In every dev build (`goog.DEBUG=true`) the code is byte-for-byte the same as today.

**No gate can catch it.** `npm run test:elision` (`implementation/package.json:38`) compiles `re-frame.elision-probe` (844 lines, `run` at :824) twice and greps `check-elision.cjs`'s `DEV_ONLY_SENTINELS`, all drawn from `re-frame.*` namespaces; it roots no Xray namespace. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` (:41) compiles `examples/counter` and friends, none of which require Xray, and `check-bundle-isolation.cjs` (1752 lines) contains **zero** occurrences of `rf-xray`, `rf.xray`, `xray-root` or `re_frame2_xray`. It proves Xray is absent from apps that never asked for it, which is a different claim.

## The decision

**Which sentence does Xray get to make about production builds?** Exactly one of:

- **A. "Xray's side-effects are gated by construction."** Manual `init!` and the externally visible mount verbs no-op under `goog.DEBUG=false`, the load-time hook block folds, and an Xray-rooted probe with a positive control holds it in CI. Every claim site is rewritten to this wording.
- **B. "Xray is kept out of production by build placement."** The preload lives in `:devtools`; a manual install belongs in a namespace only the dev entry point loads; the preload's `debug-enabled?` block is a second line of defence for that path only; no CI gate proves absence. Every claim site is rewritten to *this* wording (the skill already is).
- **C. Do nothing.** Leave code and prose as they stand.

Both A and B correct the same sites; they disagree about what the corrected sentence says and whether code moves. That is why this is one ruling, not two.
