title: api(ssr): delete head-snapshot: the snapshot atom, rf/ copy, :ssr/head-snapshot + head teardown hooks
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from ssr.md (ref ssr.2); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`head-snapshot` is a side-channel register bolted onto a pure read. `render-head` returns the head model AND stashes it in a process-wide atom keyed by frame address (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc:36-51,172`); `head-snapshot` (`:53-59`) reads that atom back; `on-frame-destroyed!` (`:61-67`) clears it through a second late-bind hook, `:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc:71-89`), which `re-frame.ssr.request/on-frame-destroyed!` looks up by key and calls inside a try/catch that emits `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/request.cljc:112-124`). The surface is advertised "for tests, introspection, and tools (Xray, MCP)" (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:862-869`, `spec/API.md:342`). Tools read it nowhere; no production code reads it; the atom exists so two test files can assert on it and two fixtures can reset it. The value a caller wants is already in its hands — it is what `render-head` returned.

## Evidence (verified at tip 6445d0611b, 2026-09-05)

- `git grep -n -F 'head-snapshot'` (outside the head ns) → `core.cljc:862-869`, `core_ssr.cljc:113-122`, `late_bind/directory.cljc:774-777,782-785` (+ `:753` description tail), `ssr.cljc:426-427` (comment), `request.cljc:12,97`; tests `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_head_test.clj:10,174-183,549-604`, `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:48-174`; fixtures `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/test_fixture.clj:11,35,85`, `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring/test_support.clj:58,80`; spec `spec/API.md:26,29,327,342,375`, `spec/011-SSR.md:729`, `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:151,325`; docs `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1503-1507`, `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:16,566,691,729`; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:135`; manifest rows. `tools/`: 0. `examples/`, `testbeds/`: 0.
- `git grep -n -E 'head-on-frame-destroyed|rf\.ssr\.head/cleanup-failed'` → the producer/consumer above, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2025` (catalogue row), tests `ssr_head_test.clj:714-770`, `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:180-221`.
- The 2026-09-04 façade sweep (rf2-2hpxo, PR #9217) classified the `re-frame.core` `head-snapshot` row `:action :keep` (`spec/api-manifest.edn:128`, `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1345-1347`). That classification argued the façade MECHANISM (late-bind re-export vs hard require); it did not find a consumer. This bead deletes the surface at its home too, so the façade question does not arise.

## Target API

None added. `render-head` / `active-head` keep returning the model; that return value is the only way to read a head. (Their consolidation into one `head` fn is @ssr.3's ruling — this bead does not touch their signatures.) `re-frame.ssr/on-frame-destroyed!` keeps clearing `pending-error-traces`, `request-slots`, `response-slots` and releasing the payload claim (`request.cljc:103-111`) — three side channels, not four.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer on this slice: fable proposes the deletion; codex's cross-check adopts it after reading `registry.cljc` — "Its removal is justified by the absence of a consumer for that historical side channel" — with one factual correction to carry into the tests: the snapshot is `{head-id → last-model}` and may hold several heads, so it is NOT value-equal to the last `render-head` return; snapshot tests become tests of required rendering behaviour, not a mechanical comparison of differently shaped values. Codex also: "Do not delete unrelated request/error side-channel teardown with the head snapshot."

## Deletion list

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc`: `head-snapshots` (`:36-41`), `record-head-model!` (`:43-51`), `head-snapshot` (`:53-59`), `on-frame-destroyed!` (`:61-67`), the `record-head-model!` call in `render-head*` (`:172` — return the model directly), docstring lines `:16-19,:30-35,:193-195`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head.cljc`: defs `:45-46` and `:47-51` (the `head-snapshots` re-export); hook `:64`; the whole teardown block `:71-89`; ns-docstring mentions.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/request.cljc`: `:12`, `:95-101` (docstring), `:112-124` (head-cleanup call + `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` emission). Keep `:103-111`.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:425-430`: comment → the head hooks that remain (`:ssr/reg-head`, `:ssr/render-head`, `:ssr/active-head`, `:ssr/head-model-html`).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:862-869` (`head-snapshot` def); `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_ssr.cljc:113-122` (wrapper).
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:774-777` (`:ssr/head-snapshot`), `:782-785` (`:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed`), and the trailing sentence of `:753` ("Also invokes `:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed` …").
- `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn:1345-1347` (the `["re-frame.core" "head-snapshot"]` row with its `:action`/`:justification`); regenerate `spec/api-manifest.edn` (row `:128` goes).
- Tests: `ssr_head_test.clj:549-604` (four deftests: `head-snapshot-cleared-on-frame-destroy`, `head-snapshot-isolated-across-frames`, `rf-head-snapshot-resolves`, `rf-head-snapshot-returns-per-frame-map`) and `:714-770` (hook-throws test) — delete; `:170-183` — re-express as "the second `render-head` call returns the second head's model" (behavioural, per codex); `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:180-221` (`on-frame-destroyed-tolerates-missing-head-hook`) — delete; `:45-91` → "clears all THREE side channels" (drop `:62-77` and `:89-91`); `:97-126`, `:132-174` — drop the snapshot assertions, keep request/response/error-trace ones. Fixtures: `test_fixture.clj:11,35,85`, `test_support.clj:58,80` — drop the `head-snapshots` reset.

## Consumers to migrate

None in app, tool or framework production code. Framework: `request.cljc` (above). Tests/fixtures: above.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- `spec/API.md` (HOT ZONE): row `:342` deleted; `:29` namespace-table entry and `:327` list drop `head-snapshot`; `:375` "via `active-head` / `render-head` / `head-snapshot`" → the two; `:26` if it names it. **Fold the head-surface doc drift here, since the same lines are being edited**: `:327` says "the surfaces below live in `re-frame.ssr`" and `:29` lists `render-head`, `active-head`, `head-model->html` under `re-frame.ssr` — they live in `re-frame.ssr.head` (`head.cljc:39-44`; `ssr.cljc` carries no head def) and reach consumers through `re-frame.core`. Say so in both places.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:2025` (HOT ZONE): delete the `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` catalogue row — its only emitter goes with `request.cljc:115`, and the error-catalogue channel conformance test (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj`) would otherwise pin a row with no emitter.
- `spec/011-SSR.md:729` (teardown list "request, response, pending-error, and head-snapshot" → three); `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:151` ("chains `:ssr.head/on-frame-destroyed`") and `:325` ("head snapshots").
- Docs: `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:1503-1507` (section), `docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md:16` (list), `:566` (teardown description's head clause), `:691`, `:729`; `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:135` (row).
- **Fold one more skills drift line here (same skills tree; no code bead will touch it)**: `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md:158` says "Head rides the same `:rf/render-hash` channel as the body … any mismatch (head or body) emits `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch`". Per `spec/011-SSR.md:1262-1264,1284-1289` the head rides its OWN `:rf/head-hash` channel (rf2-1oxjxk), the body hash is body-only, and the bundled client never compares the head hash — so a head-only divergence is SILENT unless the host recomputes `active-head` and compares; `:rf.ssr/head-mismatch` stays host-suppliable via `:failing-id`. Rewrite the bullet to that. (rf2-ygimu, PR #9004, fixed four other claims in this file on 2026-09-02 and left this one.)
- Examples/testbeds: none reference it. Migration README: untouched (no v1-era name).
- Conformance corpus / mcp-conformance: unaffected — no fixture names `head-snapshot`; `spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-head-emits.edn:38` / `ssr-head-hydration.edn:68` use `:ssr/active-head` as an EXPECT channel key, which stays.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches `spec/API.md` and `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` → one-toucher; serialise behind any in-flight API.md / 009 PR, and @ssr.3's implementation beads (also API.md) go after this one. Shares `late_bind/directory.cljc` with @ssr.1 (different rows; merges cleanly, but not the same worktree). `implementation/ssr-ring/test/.../test_support.clj` is in the tree rf2-9guv edits (`node.clj`, `node_crossing_test.clj`) — different files.

## Risks

Low. The one behavioural edge is teardown: after removing the head clause, `re-frame.ssr/on-frame-destroyed!` MUST still clear `pending-error-traces`, `request-slots`, `response-slots` and release the payload claim — `ssr_teardown_corner_test.clj:45-91` pins that (re-titled to three channels). `ring_test.clj` does not `with-redefs` `head-snapshot` (only `rf/active-head` at `:2815,2866`), so ssr-ring tests are unaffected beyond the fixture reset.

Its one piece of information is the revert's own message: an author deciding the build-count fix was out of that dispatch's naming scope. That decision is now moot too, since the fix landed anyway.

BRANCH 3 — worker/receipts-hic081. THREE commits from 2026-08-11, 381 insertions across 3 files:
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/receipt.cljs             (new)
  implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/receipt_spike_cljs_test.cljs (new)
  implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs           (edited)
Commit subjects: "capability receipts derived from the runtime's own leavings", "the receipt witness, green on the hicasso node lane", "split the projection out of the runtime, as the erasure gate demanded".
THIS ONE IS NOT SUPERSEDED. Both new files are ABSENT from main, and 'receipt' returns just 1 hit across all of implementation/hicasso. Every commit calls itself a SPIKE. So it is genuine unmerged exploratory work, four weeks old, and nothing has replaced it.

WHY I DELETED NOTHING, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Per loops.md §5 the authority for deleting a branch is git cherry patch-equivalence, and only a '-' authorises it. All three branches read '+' on EVERY commit:
  worker/naming-tools-story-20260903      + 0b508e744e
  worker/naming-tools-story-20260903-r1   + 0b508e744e, + ce02cf3cec
  worker/receipts-hic081                  + fece72f80a, + 418312d680, + ae14841ab3
Branch 1 is the instructive case: its END STATE is on main byte-for-byte, and cherry still says '+'. That is not a contradiction — cherry compares PATCHES, and a patch that produces the same line from different context, in a different commit, is not patch-equivalent. So "the outcome is already on main" and "the branch is provably contained in main" are DIFFERENT claims, and only the second licenses deletion. A reader who saw the matching line and deleted on that basis would be discarding a branch on the wrong test, and would be right by luck.

MY RECOMMENDATION, for a one-line answer:
  DROP branch 1 — its outcome is already on main; nothing is lost.
  DROP branch 2 — it contains nothing; its net diff is empty.
  For branch 3, KEEP or FILE-AND-DROP. A branch costs nothing to keep, so the cheap default is keep. If you would rather the roster were clean, the alternative is that I file a bead capturing the receipts idea with these three commit ids in it, and then the branch is droppable without losing the thought.
On your word I will delete whichever you name, using the merge-verified path rather than cherry (which cannot authorise these), i.e. an explicit decision recorded here first.

title: api(views): (rf/view id) answers every substrate's mountable head — Hicasso publishes its alias under :handler-fn; correct the view / reg-view spec lines
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.5); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

`(rf/view id)` is the framework's late-bind view lookup (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:788` → `re-frame.views/view-head`, `views.cljs:771-805`) and the spec's answer to "find a view by its registered id" (`spec/API.md:215`, `spec/Conventions.md` §Render-tree shape vs runtime lookup). It is true on Reagent and UIx and `nil` on Hicasso by design: `h/defview` registers through `registrar/register!` with the minted head under a PRIVATE key `:hicasso/component` and `:executable-key :hicasso/component`, and no `:handler-fn` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/collector.cljs:1203-1230`; docstring at `hicasso.cljc:200-209`). A registrar answer that is true on two substrates and nil on the third is the "private-API spelunking" Principles forbid: Story's `:reagent` substrate reads `rf/view` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:227-236`) while Hicasso needs a second substrate hook; a tool enumerating `:view` must know a second descriptor shape. The stated reason for the bypass — `reg-view*` "consults the `:adapter/wrap-view` hook at registration time, which at namespace load precedes `rf/init!`" (`collector.cljs:1218-1221`) — is stale: `view-head` re-derives lazily against the installed adapter (`views.cljs:777-783`, rf2-oz7wr / rf2-8mkmb). The SHAPE reason is still load-bearing: a Hicasso boundary is a React component, not a hiccup render fn, and `reg-view*` would wrap and componentise it (`views.cljs:433-501`, `spine.cljs:2378-2418`). So the fix is the descriptor, not the pipeline. Alongside: three spec lines a reader trips on today, and an example lineage that spells one in-view read two ways.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- `view-head` returns a `:view` slot this namespace did not build "exactly as stored" — `(not (and (some? entry) (identical? handler-fn (:registered entry)))) handler-fn` (`views.cljs:785,791-794`). So a hand-registered slot with `:handler-fn` = the minted head is returned untouched: no `compose-view`, no wrap, no componentise.
- Executable identity for `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` is read from `(get metadata (get metadata :executable-key :handler-fn))` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc:566`), so a head stored under `:handler-fn` needs no `:executable-key` to make a reload report a real swap.
- Production elision: `publish-view-alias!` is called inside `defview`'s `interop/debug-enabled?` gate (`collector.cljs:1221-1224`) — the registration is dev-only today and stays dev-only; `(rf/view id)` for a Hicasso view is nil in a release build, which is the "retaining debug-only production elision" codex asked to keep. Document it.
- Pins that flip: `implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/view_alias_registry_cljs_test.cljs:18-20,147-163` (asserts `:hicasso/component`, `:executable-key`, NO `:handler-fn`, `rf/view` nil); `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:636-648` `rf-view-still-answers-nil-for-a-hicasso-alias` — its docstring names the hazard: a non-nil head would let Story's `:reagent` substrate splice a Hicasso head as a Reagent component (`[resolved eff-args]`, `multi_substrate.cljs:232-234`), a plain function in head position called with the wrong ABI. That is a Story consumer obligation, listed below.
- Spec drift: `spec/API.md:215` — `view` "→ **render-fn** … returns the registered render-fn, *not* hiccup", which contradicts rf2-oz7wr (`views.cljs:834-841`: the value is the substrate's own COMPONENT HEAD — a MetaFn on Reagent, a marked shell on UIx). `spec/002-Frames.md:1377-1385` §What `reg-view` injects — "binds three names … `frame-id` — the keyword itself"; the macro binds TWO (`dispatch`, `subscribe`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:188-195`). `spec/002-Frames.md:1349` — "Qualified `re-frame.core/dispatch` refers to the global function"; it should say the qualified forms inside a `reg-view` body are not a second supported in-view spelling (they render alike and fork at click time: the injected local carries the frame into a callback, the qualified macro raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` there — 002:1520).
- In-view drift in examples, re-measured: 11 code sites of `@(rf/subscribe [` inside `reg-view` bodies in 5 files — `examples/capabilities/machines/state_machine_walkthrough/views.cljs:42,43,102`, `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs:492,506,507,508`, `article_editor.cljs:583,584`, `profile.cljs:637` (all `:rf.machine/has-tag?` reads from one authoring lineage), `examples/capabilities/ssr/resources_ssr/core.cljc:245` (`:rf/resource` read — verify it sits inside a `reg-view` body before touching it); plus 8 comment/docstring mentions (`article_editor.cljs:17`, `settings.cljs:91`, `tags.cljs:61,62,203,204`, `state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:121`). Skills: `git grep -c '@(rf/subscribe \[' skills` — sweep ONLY sites inside a `reg-view` body; a REPL/test/explicit-`{:frame}` read stays qualified.

## Target API

```clojure
(rf/view id)  ;=> the installed substrate's mountable head for `id`, or nil when nothing is registered
;;   Reagent: [(rf/view :app/root) args]      UIx: ($ (rf/view ::row) props)
;;   Hicasso: the minted boundary — mount it the way h/defview documents (inside a body as [head props]; from outside via h/as-element);
;;            registered in dev builds only (the defview alias is debug-gated), so nil in a release build is the documented answer
```

Change in `publish-view-alias!` (`collector.cljs:1226-1230`): register `(assoc slot :handler-fn head)` — drop `:hicasso/component` and `:executable-key`; keep the debug gate, keep the coords + `:doc` for `handler-meta`. No call to `reg-view*`. Rewrite the docstrings at `collector.cljs:1203-1225` and `hicasso.cljc:200-209` (the "answers nil" paragraph becomes "answers the boundary"). Story: `reagent-render` (`multi_substrate.cljs:227-236`) must not splice a head that is not Reagent-mountable — check the head's substrate marker (Hicasso marks its heads via `codec/mark-boundary!`, `collector.cljs:1191`; UIx sets `uix-component?`) and fall through to the existing inline diagnostic ("… is not registered as a `:reagent` view") rather than `[resolved eff-args]`; Story's own `:hicasso` substrate (`h/as-element`) stays — codex: "do not promise that Story's substrate renderers disappear".

Spec wording: `spec/API.md:215` `view` row → "`(view view-id)` → the installed substrate's mountable head (Reagent: the `:contextType`-carrying render fn, usable as `[(rf/view :id) args]`; UIx: a component type for `$`; Hicasso: the minted boundary, dev builds), or nil". `spec/002-Frames.md:1379-1383` → two locals. `spec/002-Frames.md:1349` → one sentence: qualified `rf/dispatch` / `rf/subscribe` inside a `reg-view` body are not a second in-view spelling; the injected locals are the in-view spelling, the qualified `{:frame …}` forms are the REPL/test/explicit-frame shape.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer (fable README: "`(rf/view id)` returning the mountable head on every substrate"). Codex: "Make `rf/view` return the registered head where registration exists, retaining debug-only production elision … [`view-head`] already returns an externally registered `:handler-fn` unchanged; standardising the descriptor's executable field is a smaller viable option than routing every head through `reg-view*`." and the warning: "do not assume calling `reg-view*` on an already-minted Hicasso head is automatically correct: that path also wraps/components a view. Verify no double wrapping, collector bypass, or change to production registry elision." Grok: "Publish `(rf/view id)` by storing the head under `:handler-fn` WITHOUT calling `reg-view*` — a one-line change … Codex's caution is the gate, not a nit." On the sweep: Grok "sweep the 18 qualified in-view reads onto the injected local"; codex "Prefer injected `subscribe`/`dispatch` in `reg-view` examples and teaching. Do NOT add code-walking, a ban, or a runtime diagnostic against qualified calls." Both: fix the two spec lies regardless.

## Deletion list

- `:hicasso/component` and `:executable-key` slot keys from the `:view` alias entry; the stale bypass rationale in `collector.cljs:1218-1221`; the "answers nil for this entry" contract in `hicasso.cljc:200-209` and wherever the guide repeats it (`git grep -n 'answers nil' docs/core/hicasso implementation/hicasso`).
- The two Story/Hicasso test pins named under Evidence (rewritten, not deleted: pin non-nil, `identical?` to the `def`, `handler-replaced` on a real reload, and the `:reagent` substrate refusing a Hicasso head with the diagnostic).
- The `frame-id` bullet at `spec/002-Frames.md:1383`.
- The 11 qualified in-body reads in examples (rewritten to the injected `subscribe`), with the 8 comment mentions updated to match.

## Consumers to migrate (counts at tip)

- implementation: `collector.cljs` (1 fn), `hicasso.cljc` docstring, `view_alias_registry_cljs_test.cljs`; any Hicasso tool-tier reader of `:hicasso/component` — `git grep -n 'hicasso/component' implementation tools` (at tip: `collector.cljs`, the alias test, `hicasso.cljc` docstring) — re-point to `:handler-fn`.
- tools: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:227-236` (guard), `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:636-648` (re-pin). Xray's Views panel and Pair `ui/read` read the `:view` registrar generically — verify they need no change (`git grep -n ':handler-fn' tools/xray/src skills/re-frame2-pair/preload`).
- examples: 5 files / 11 sites + 8 comments (listed).

- migration README: `rf/view` exists in v1 as a different thing? No — not a v1-era name; no entry. `mcp-conformance`: unaffected (`handler-meta :view` shape gains `:handler-fn` and loses a private key; the Tool-Pair `:view` descriptor never promised the private key — verify against `spec/Tool-Pair.md` and `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` with `git grep -n 'hicasso/component' spec`, which at tip returns nothing).

Not 006. rf2-c5w1 (closed, PR #9200): Hicasso stamps `data-rf-view` / `data-rf2-source-coord` itself — that is the second reason the head must not re-enter core's `compose-view` (double-stamp); this bead does not touch annotation. rf2-2vpm: no overlap (006 only).

title: api(views): Hicasso spells ENSURE/SCOPE in-tree — h/frame-root (full make-frame opts) and h/frame-provider; mount config fails loud
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.3); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

On Reagent and UIx the frame lifecycle is spelled in the tree: `[rf/frame-root {…any make-frame opt…} [app]]` ENSURES (commit-owned two-pass, `spec/002-Frames.md:1674-1703`) and `[rf/frame-provider {:frame f} …]` SCOPES (`:1646`), a ruled dual with a written discriminator (rf2-nyea0r). Hicasso has neither public boundary: `re-frame.hicasso.substrate/frame-provider` is `defn-` (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:108`), and ENSURE lives in `h/mount!`'s config instead (`implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:552-608` → `impl.mount/root!` `:139-162` → `ensure-frame!` `:115-137`). That config is CLOSED at `:frame` / `:initial-events` / `:identifier-prefix`: `root!` reads only the two keys it owns (`:154-155`) and every other key is "ignored without complaint" (`docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md:134`, `07-routing-and-navigation.md:82`, `00-installation.md:440`, `20-migration-from-reagent.md:246`). A No-silent-swallow hit with a real detour in the one app example: `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:229-249,285-289` calls `rf/make-frame` first because `:fx-overrides` cannot ride the mount, then mounts to JOIN — and the README (`examples/substrates/hicasso/login/README.md:76-96`) spends a section explaining why. The migration guide has to warn about the same silent failure, and a second frame on a page is a second `h/mount!` root (`implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:451-458`) because there is no in-tree boundary to nest.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- `impl.mount/root!` `:152-162`: `(ensure-frame! frame-kw (:initial-events opts))`, then `createRoot` with `(root-options (:identifier-prefix opts) nil)`; `opts` is the whole config (`hicasso.cljc:604-608`), so unknown keys reach `root!` and are dropped there.
- `impl.mount/tree` `:54-82`: the ROOT is the frame provider — `(provider (:frame handle) (codec/root-element (:frame handle) hiccup))`; `codec/root-element` (`impl/codec.cljs:1712-1722`) is "the one creator that has to NAME the frame" by binding `intent/*frame*`. So today frame identity enters at the root handle, not in the tree. `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` builds its element through the same `tree` so client and server agree on `useId` tree position (`:68-72`, HS-11).
- Core's shared two-pass core: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs` — `frame-root-fc` `:300`, `frame-root-react-element` `:370` (the per-adapter shells are thin: UIx's `frame-root` is `(boundary/frame-root-react-element props (:children props) 're-frame.adapter.uix/frame-root)`, `uix.cljs:134-138`). The first render of `frame-root` emits NO subtree (`frame_boundary.cljs:41-51`), so under hydration the tree must use `frame-provider` (SCOPE) after `rf.ssr/hydrate!` made the frame — exactly what the Reagent SSR examples do (`examples/capabilities/ssr/ssr/core.cljc:460`).
- Consumers of `h/mount!`'s ENSURE keys: example `login/core.cljs:293-298`, testbeds `hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:884-890` (explicit `make-frame` then `{:frame …}` join), `hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:451-458`, Story test `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:363`, skill `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:294-333`, 10 guide pages (`docs/core/hicasso/`: 00-installation ×15 incl. §"What `h/mount!` creates" :281 and §"A frame that needs more than a seed" :318, 07 ×3, 09, 13, 17, 18-ssr ×11, 20-migration ×5, api-reference ×21 incl. :126-141 and §"not symmetric" :143-181, cookbook ×10, glossary ×5), `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md:125-160`, `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:20-30` ("a Hicasso tree has no frame component in it"). The test kit (`implementation/hicasso/test_kit/src/re_frame/hicasso/test/mounted.cljs`) reaches the root through `impl.mount/root!` (`catching-root!`, `:696-697`), not the facade — its `hm/mount!` config is its own and is not this bead's target.

## Target API

```clojure
;; ENSURE — a hicasso-owned head, like h/portal / h/error-boundary; takes THE make-frame map, not a curated subset
[h/frame-root {:id :rf/default :initial-events [[:app/init]] :fx-overrides {…} :url-bound? true :images […]}
 [root-view]]
;; SCOPE — an existing frame (SSR after rf.ssr/hydrate!, Story hosts, a second root on a page)
[h/frame-provider {:frame :app/main} [root-view]]

;; the root door carries ROOT options only, and a key it does not own fails loud
(h/mount!   el {:identifier-prefix "main"} [h/frame-root {:id :rf/default …} [root-view]])
(h/hydrate! el {:identifier-prefix "main"} [h/frame-provider {:frame :app/main} [root-view]])
(h/mount!   el {:frame :x} …)            ;=> throws — did-you-mean naming h/frame-root / h/frame-provider
(h/mount!   el {:initial-events […]} …)  ;=> throws — same diagnostic
(h/mount!   el {:foo 1} …)               ;=> throws — unknown root option (No-silent-swallow)
```

Contract the two heads MUST satisfy: `h/frame-root` realises 002 §`frame-root`'s shared contract (`:1697-1703`: commit-owned ensure, discard-safe, reuse-without-reseed, StrictMode-safe, no destroy-on-unmount, fail-loud on a mounted `:id`/opts change and on a `:frame` key) on the shared `frame-root-fc` core, exactly as UIx's shell does — do not fork the two-pass. `h/frame-provider` is the SCOPE-only component (`:1646`): requires a live frame, refuses `:id` with the did-you-mean. Both are Hicasso-recognised heads: the codec must lower a boundary's children under the frame the head resolved (codex: "Hicasso must recognise its head and lower children under the right frame") — `codec/root-element` no longer receives the frame from the handle; the frame boundary in the tree becomes the creator that names it. Whatever the client `tree` becomes, `re-frame.hicasso.server/render` builds the same element shape (mount.cljs:68-72, HS-11 obstruction 2) — the server side scopes with the same `h/frame-provider`.

Before / after for the one app example (`examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:285-299`), keeping today's verbs (views.4 changes the verbs):

```clojure
;; before
(rf/make-frame (merge {:id frame-id …} model/frame-config))           ; because :fx-overrides can't ride mount!
(let [config {:frame frame-id :identifier-prefix identifier-prefix}]
  (if (some? payload)
    (do (rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload})
        (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/hydrate! el config [root-view])))
    (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/mount! el config [root-view]))))

;; after
(let [opts {:identifier-prefix identifier-prefix}]
  (if (some? payload)
    (do (rf.ssr/hydrate! {:frame frame-id :payload payload})
        (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/hydrate! el opts [h/frame-provider {:frame frame-id} [root-view]])))
    (reset! !root (rf.hicasso/mount! el opts
                    [h/frame-root (merge {:id frame-id} model/frame-config) [root-view]]))))
```

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer on the shape (ENSURE/SCOPE in the tree with full frame options; root options on the root call). Codex: "Keep frame creation/scoping in the corresponding `frame-root` / `frame-provider` boundary, with normal frame options; React root options belong to the root call. Do not conflate DOM unmount with permission to destroy durable frame state." Codex Thoughts: "A public in-tree boundary cannot simply expose the existing raw React provider, because Hicasso must recognise its head and lower children under the right frame. Keep ENSURE versus SCOPE explicit, especially after SSR payload installation; adoption must never silently seed replacement state." Grok: "ENSURE spelled once. Hicasso gets public `h/frame-root` (full `make-frame` opts) and `h/frame-provider`. That is more important than collapsing `hydrate!`/`render!`." Fable: the closed three-key config, the "ignored without complaint" keys, the `make-frame`-then-join dance and the migration guide's silent-failure paragraph all go.

## Deletion list

- `h/mount!`'s `:frame` and `:initial-events` config keys (become fail-loud misplacements); `impl.mount/ensure-frame!` as the mount-time ensure (its `make-frame`-when-absent logic moves behind the `frame-root` head; the `frame-incarnation-token` guard at `:134` is the same idempotence `frame-root-fc` already owns); the "closed list, ignored without complaint" contract (api-reference :126-141, 00-installation :440, 07 :82, 20-migration :243-252) and the "not symmetric" section (api-reference :143-181, docs/api hicasso.md `hydrate!` paragraph) — the tree now spells the difference (`frame-root` vs `frame-provider`), so there is nothing asymmetric left to explain.
- The `make-frame`-then-join detour in `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs:229-249,287-289` and its README section (:76-96).
- `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:20-30`'s "a Hicasso tree has no frame component in it".

## Consumers to migrate (counts at tip)

- examples: `examples/substrates/hicasso/login/core.cljs` (1 file; 3 call sites + comments) and its README.
- testbeds: `implementation/hicasso/testbed/hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:884-890`, `hicasso_hmr_testbed/core.cljs:451-458` (one `frame-root` per frame instead of one config per root).
- tools: `tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test.cljs:363` (1). Story's canvas already scopes with `[rf/frame-provider …]` and splices Hicasso via `h/as-element` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/multi_substrate.cljs:70-78`) — unchanged.
- implementation tests: every facade `h/mount!` / `h/hydrate!` caller that passes `:frame` / `:initial-events` — re-measure with `git grep -nE '(h|rf\.hicasso)/(mount!|hydrate!)' implementation/hicasso` and separate facade callers from `hm/*` test-kit callers (the kit rides `impl.mount/root!`); `public_root_lifecycle_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `revision_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `login_server_crossing_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `instance_key_payload_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs` are the likely set.
- skills: `skills/reagent-migration/references/catalog-mechanical.md:294-333`.
- docs: the 10 guide pages and `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md` listed under Evidence; `docs/core/hicasso/glossary.md`; add `h/frame-root` / `h/frame-provider` entries to api-reference and docs/api. `docs/design/hicasso/decisions.md:1477` (HD-021) and `docs/design/hicasso/product/naming-ledger.md:48,:55` (rows 13/20) get a dated supersession NOTE naming this bead — never an edit of the ruled text.
- spec (hot-zone): `spec/002-Frames.md:1697` ("each substrate (Reagent / reagent-slim / UIx) ships its own `frame-root`") gains Hicasso; `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` cross-substrate table (:2102-2113) Hicasso scope/ensure cells (views.2 adds the column; this bead fills those two rows); `spec/api-manifest.edn` gains `re-frame.hicasso/frame-root` and `frame-provider` rows — regenerate (`clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen`), lint `api-manifest` drift-check.
- migration README: not a v1-era name — no entry. `mcp-conformance` / conformance corpus: unaffected.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Independent of views.1/views.2 in code; hot-zone `spec/002-Frames.md` and `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` (serialise with views.2, views.4, views.5, rf2-2vpm). BLOCKS views.4. rf2-8urba (deferred) models its scaffold boot on `hicasso_testbed/core.cljs:878-884`, which this bead rewrites — see the AMEND. rf2-c5w1 landed Hicasso's own annotation stamping (PR #9200): the new heads are Hicasso components and must not be routed through core's `reg-view*` / spine `wrap-view` path.

## Risks

Medium — this is the one Hicasso change with real design work (the frame enters the codec from the tree instead of the handle). Two things to MEASURE, not assert: (i) first paint — today `ensure-frame!` runs synchronously before `createRoot` so "the first paint is the seeded one" (`mount.cljs:129-132`); 002 §`frame-root` clause 2 promises the same via the layout-phase flip before paint. Witness it (the hicasso testbed's mount + a seeded read on the first painted frame, and the arm1 bench lane's cold-mount row if it moves) and report the numbers; if two-pass costs a visible flash or a measurable cold-mount regression, STOP and report rather than shipping it. (ii) `useId` parity under hydration — the server tree and the client tree must carry the boundary in the same position (HS-11); the existing SSR DOM witnesses (`server_render_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `instance_key_payload_ssr_dom_cljs_test.cljs`) are the gate. Also verify codex's list: seeded first paint; hot reload preserving DOM and state (`h/render!` still reconciles the same root); hydration followed by a rerender without remount; two roots sharing one frame (`00-installation.md:353`); two roots using different frames (`:382`); a Hicasso story under a Reagent adapter (Story's `hicasso_substrate_dom_cljs_test`).

- rf2-gwoz: I claimed a line-oriented grep for "install-* is not in the closed roster" returns 0. It returns 1; the clause sits on one line. I had run only the flattened pass and asserted what the other would say. What I had actually seen wrapped was bd show's RENDERING of my own note.
- rf2-2zl9 (the views-a rider): I warned the id might be written across a line break and told the worker to run the flattened pass. All three passes agree at 5 hits; it is not line-broken.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A RULE RATHER THAN A SHRUG. A false hazard costs a worker real effort confirming a trap that is not there, and it can be worse than that: when the worker's own measurement disagrees with the brief, the natural first hypothesis is that the FILE changed shape, not that the mayor guessed. That sends the worker looking for a phantom edit. And it debases the warning — a worker who has seen two false ones reads the third, real one as boilerplate.

THE DISTINCTION TO HOLD. The three-pass RULE is generic and belongs in every census brief: run all three passes, because the passes disagree unpredictably. A target-specific CLAIM — "this particular string wraps" — is a measurement, and I must not state it unless I have run the line-oriented pass myself on that file. Predicting one pass from another is precisely what the rule forbids.

THE CHEAP FORM THAT IS ALWAYS SAFE: "run all three passes; I have not measured which of them sees this target." That carries the whole benefit and asserts nothing. Where I HAVE measured, state the numbers and the file, so the worker can tell a measurement from a guess.

AND CREDIT WHERE THE PROCESS WORKED: on the second occasion I did write into the brief that I had over-warned about this exact hazard earlier the same day and that the worker should measure rather than believe either of us. It measured, refuted me, and said so plainly. Telling a worker that a specific warning of mine has a track record of being wrong is worth doing when I cannot be bothered to measure — but measuring is cheaper than either.

title: docs(alias): the ratchet's zeros cover CODE only — 427 bare-leaf alias references remain in PROSE; rule or decline
description:
Filed 2026-09-07 by the mayor from worker alias2-a's report on PR #9341 (rf2-7sx1 slice 2). THE MEASUREMENTS BELOW ARE THAT WORKER'S, NOT MINE — I did not independently reproduce them, and my own probe measured a different thing (require FORMS, where implementation/hicasso reads 11 bare-leaf against 99 canonical). Treat them as a claim and re-derive before acting.

THE FINDING. The require-alias ratchet (rf2-7sx1) reads only tracked .clj/.cljs/.cljc. Its surfaces are now at zero almost everywhere — but that means THE CODE HAS BEEN WALKED, NOT THE DIALECT. Prose is uniformly mixed on the same surfaces:

  implementation/hicasso   372 bare-leaf prose references   vs  40 canonical   (walked to zero in PR #9334)
  implementation/flows      78                              vs   4
  implementation/adapters   67                              vs  11

427 non-code hits were deliberately left across slice 2. Code is uniformly canonical on those surfaces; prose is uniformly mixed. So a roster of zeros on the ratchet is not evidence that the repository teaches one dialect.

WHY IT WAS LEFT, and this is the right call rather than an omission: every prior slice walked code only, and slice 3's prose renames in examples/ were the documented exception because examples/ is a teaching surface where the prose IS the product. Folding a 427-site prose sweep into a floor-lowering slice would have mixed a mechanical, gate-verified rename with an unverifiable one — no gate reads prose, so the two have completely different risk profiles and should not share a PR.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD IS ASKING FOR, and it is a taste call rather than a technical one: is a bare-leaf alias in PROSE wrong? In code it is unambiguous — the ratchet says so and the compiler agrees. In prose, `h/defview` is how a consumer actually writes it after `[re-frame.hicasso :as h]`, and PR #9334's worker made exactly that argument when it REVERTED its own prose edits: docs/core/hicasso/ binds `:as h` at 39 sites, so the prose is teaching the idiom a consumer writes, not carrying stale source. That argument may or may not generalise from the guide tree to the other 427 sites.

SO THE HONEST FRAMING IS THREE OPTIONS, not a task:
  (a) Leave prose alone entirely. The ratchet governs code; prose teaches whatever alias the surrounding sample binds. Cheapest, and consistent with #9334's reverted edits.
  (b) Walk prose only where it contradicts the sample beside it — a real defect, small set, needs a per-site read.
  (c) Walk all 427 to canonical. Largest, unverifiable by any gate, and risks making documentation say something no consumer would write.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (b) IF ANY, AND OTHERWISE (a). The stance rejects gold-plating and says trust the programmer; a reader who sees `h/defview` under a require binding `:as h` is not misled. What WOULD mislead is prose whose alias contradicts its own sample, and that set is almost certainly far smaller than 427.

DO NOT DISPATCH THIS AS A SWEEP without a ruling — the whole value of the bead is that the size figure (427) makes option (c) look like tidy mechanical work when it is the option most likely to damage teaching material. If it is dispatched at all, the first deliverable is the option-(b) census: how many prose sites contradict the require form in their own file or page.

## Problem

With every consumer outside `implementation/` on `:inputs` (`.3`–`.5`), the old grammar and its bare-value arms are dead weight that the transitional `.2` left in place. title: api(views): UIx publishes client-root / render! / unmount!; delete the hand-rolled uix.dom root recipe
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from views.md (ref views.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

Spec 006 §The client root (`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:244-261`) says a browser adapter SHOULD publish a reusable client-root lifecycle — `(client-root)` / `(render! handle tree mount-point [opts])` / `(unmount! handle)` — riding the same Root path and active-root ownership as `render`. The Reagent and reagent-slim adapters do (`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:142/160/179`, `reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:79/86/102`, backed by the ratom spine's `client-root` / `render-client-root!` / `unmount-client-root!` at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3792-3816`). The UIx adapter publishes nothing of the kind: `re-frame.adapter.uix`'s public surface is `set-hiccup-emitter!`, `use-current-frame`, `frame-provider`, `frame-root`, `use-subscribe`, `use-frame`, `flush-views!`, `wrap-view`, `adapter` (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:60-239`), and `make-react-spine` (`spine.cljs:2750`) builds no trio even though its `render` path already owns `createRoot` / `hydrateRoot` and the active-root set (`spine.cljs:1213-1259`). So every UIx app re-invents the recipe the trio was built to delete (rf2-k5r9t): `(defonce react-root (atom nil))` + `when-not @react-root` + `uix-dom/create-root` + `uix-dom/render-root`, and takes a `com.pitch/uix.dom` dependency purely for the mount that the how-to has to warn about (`docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:77-90`). The UIx counter (`examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:81-112`) is the concrete before/after.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b)

- Hand-rolled root recipe, app-authored: `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs:81-112`, `login/core.cljs:117-141`, `dashboard/core.cljs:350-368` (3 files). Tool-authored: `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/core.cljs:15-34` (the scaffold every new UIx project gets) and `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs:44,56`. The template test `tools/template/test/day8/re_frame2_template/template_emission_test.clj:313-331` PINS exactly one `uix-dom/create-root` call in the emitted `:uix` core — it must move with the recipe.
- Reagent apps: 27 example files use `client-root` + `render!` (`grep -rlE '\(rf.adapter.reagent(-slim)?/client-root\)' examples | wc -l` → 27 at the doc's tip; re-measure).
- `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn` already says: shipping source requires only `uix.core`; the shared spine mounts through `react-dom/client`; `uix.dom` is test-only and out of the published pom. So the trio needs NO dependency change — the adapter mounts through the spine, as Reagent does.
- Spine proof of the ratom trio's semantics (the contract the UIx trio must match): `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/adapter_client_root_cljs_test.cljs` (deftests `client-root-does-no-dom-work`, `cold-first-render-creates-once-later-renders-update-the-same-root`, `hydrating-first-render-hydrates-once-later-renders-update`, `unmount-is-idempotent-and-a-later-render-mounts-afresh`, `dispose-adapter-releases-live-handles-once`), `adapter_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (`cold-render-updates-the-same-mounted-node`, `hydrating-render-adopts-the-server-node-then-updates-it`, `destroy-adapter-releases-still-live-handles-once`), and `reagent-slim/test/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim_client_root_cljs_test.cljs`.

## Target API

Published on `re-frame.adapter.uix`, same three names, same shapes and semantics as `re-frame.adapter.reagent` (Spec 006 §The client root: ownership / update / hydration / teardown):

```clojure
(uix-adapter/client-root)                              ;=> inert handle; no DOM work at allocation; defonce-safe, Node-safe
(uix-adapter/render! handle element mount-point)       ;=> nil; first call creates the Root and renders; every later call updates the same Root
(uix-adapter/render! handle element mount-point {:hydrate? true})  ;=> nil; first call hydrates once (Spec 011), later calls update — never a second hydration
(uix-adapter/unmount! handle)                          ;=> nil; idempotent; the Root is in the adapter's active-root set, so rf/destroy-adapter! releases it exactly once and a later render! mounts afresh
```

`element` is a React element built with `uix.core/$` (the spine's `render` slot already refuses CLJS data with `:rf.error/hiccup-on-element-render-slot`, `spine.cljs:1218-1226` — keep that guard on the trio path). `opts` is the same map the spine's `render` takes (`:hydrate?`, and the `:on-recoverable-error` composition rf2-qfz65 installs on the hydrate path, `spine.cljs:1196-1211`); do not invent UIx-only keys.

Before / after (the UIx counter, `examples/substrates/uix/counter/core.cljs`):

```clojure
;; before — :81-112
(defonce react-root (atom nil))
(defn ^:dev/after-load mount! []
  (when-let [el (and (exists? js/document) (js/document.getElementById "app"))]
    (when-not @react-root
      (reset! react-root (uix-dom/create-root el)))
    (uix-dom/render-root
      ($ rf.adapter.uix/frame-root {:id app-frame :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]}
         ($ counter-app))
      @react-root)))

;; after — the same file every Reagent example already has
(defonce app-root (rf.adapter.uix/client-root))
(defn ^:dev/after-load mount! []
  (when-let [el (and (exists? js/document) (js/document.getElementById "app"))]
    (rf.adapter.uix/render! app-root
      ($ rf.adapter.uix/frame-root {:id app-frame :initial-events [[:counter/initialise]]}
         ($ counter-app))
      el)))
```

Implementation shape: lift the ratom spine's `client-root` / `render-client-root!` / `unmount-client-root!` (`spine.cljs:3792-3816`) into a shared helper both spine constructors use, built over each spine's own `mount-root!`-equivalent — for the React spine that is the `render` closure `make-render` returns (`spine.cljs:1213-1259`), which already tracks the Root in `active-roots-cell`. Handle liveness is READ off the active set, never kept in the handle (the rf2-k5r9t rule at `spine.cljs:3786-3791`), so `dispose-adapter!`'s drain releases a live handle's Root once. Expose the three fns from `make-react-spine`'s return map and `def` them on `re-frame.adapter.uix` beside `flush-views!`. Do NOT publish the trio from `re-frame.hicasso.substrate` (also built on `make-react-spine`, `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/substrate.cljs:95`): Hicasso's root goes through its own codec root and gets its handle grammar in views.4.

## Corroboration

Two-reviewer. Codex (`view-adapter-ergonomics.md` §Proposed smaller API): "UIx should provide the handle helper instead of teaching a handwritten atom recipe … Retain the already-common `render!` name rather than renaming it merely to settle vocabulary. The first render creates or hydrates the root; subsequent renders reuse it. Hydration remains an explicit first-render mode with its own implementation." Fable adopted both details (keep `render!`; `{:hydrate? true}`); the fable doc's `mount!` rename is withdrawn. Grok: "UIx publishes the trio first — pure addition, deletes the atom/`create-root` recipe."

## Deletion list

- The hand-rolled root recipe (`defonce … (atom nil)` + `uix-dom/create-root` + `uix-dom/render-root`) in: `examples/substrates/uix/{counter,login,dashboard}/core.cljs`, `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/core.cljs`, `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs`, and the teaching copies in `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:168-182` and `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md:112-138`.
- `com.pitch/uix.dom` as an APP dependency: drop it from `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_uix/deps.edn` and from the deps table + warning at `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md:77-90` and `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md:88-97` / `deps-versions.md:48` / `SKILL.md:102` — IF nothing else in the emitted scaffold needs it (verify by compiling the emitted `:uix` scaffold: `template_emission_test.clj` and rf2-eiev's release-boot test `e40f1e3755` cover this). `implementation/adapters/uix/deps.edn`'s `:test` alias keeps `uix.dom` (tests and the docs-pinned component-test recipe use it).
- Nothing on the adapter's existing public surface is removed by this bead (that is views.2).

## Consumers to migrate (counts at tip)

- examples: 3 files (`examples/substrates/uix/{counter,login,dashboard}/core.cljs`).
- tools: `tools/template/.../_uix/core.cljs` (1), `_uix/deps.edn` (1), `tools/template/test/.../template_emission_test.clj:313-331` (re-pin: exactly one `client-root` call, zero `uix-dom/create-root`).
- implementation: `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` (1) — the adapter smoke `implementation/adapters/uix/testbed/spec.cjs` must stay green on the new recipe.
- skills: `skills/re-frame2-setup/references/entry-namespace.md` (root pattern §"The React root pattern" :47-72 already teaches `defonce` + `client-root` for Reagent — make the UIx block the same shape), `deps-versions.md:48`, `SKILL.md:102`; `skills/re-frame2-setup/tests/setup_drift_test.clj:279-298` pins entry-namespace.md's `uix.dom` version against the template's `_uix/deps.edn` — update or delete the pin with the dependency.

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- **spec (hot-zone):** `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §The client root (:244-261) — the "reference adapters (Reagent and reagent-slim, from the shared ratom spine)" sentence at :254 becomes all three React view adapters; raise SHOULD to MUST for browser view adapters now that the tree honours it (the Hicasso row joins in views.4 — say "the React adapters" here, not "every adapter"); §CLJS reference scope UIx row at :2189 gains the trio in its parenthetical. `spec/API.md` §UIx adapter (:241-253): add three rows (`uix-adapter/client-root`, `render!`, `unmount!`) in the shape of the Reagent rows — grep `client-root` in API.md first: if the Reagent trio has no rows there either, add both sets so the two adapters read alike. `spec/Conventions.md:1821` (`day8/re-frame2-uix` artefact row) gains "the `client-root` / `render!` / `unmount!` root trio". `spec/api-manifest.edn`: three new `re-frame.adapter.uix` rows (`:tier :adapter`, `:owner "006"`) — regenerate with `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen` from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest/` (the file's own header says so), then run the drift-check the `api-manifest` job in `.github/workflows/lint.yml` runs (its surface: `spec/API.md`, both `spec/api-manifest*.edn`, `skills/**`, `docs/core/**`, `docs/api/**`).
- **docs:** `docs/core/how-to/use-uix-or-slim.md` (:77-90 deps, :168-192 Step 4 mount, :241 slim comparison), `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:286` ("UIx apps hold a `uix.dom` root themselves" — no longer true), `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md` (add a §client-root / render! / unmount! section mirroring `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.reagent.md:98`), `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md` (add the boot recipe beside :7-24; rf2-tug6 edits :56-66 of the same file — rebase, don't race). `docs/core/testing/views.md:177-182` mounts through `uix-dom/create-root` inside a TEST recipe that `uix_component_recipe_docs_pin_test.clj` holds byte-for-byte to `uix_component_recipe_dom_cljs_test.cljs`; leave it (uix.dom is a test dep) or switch both halves together — state which in the PR.
- **tests to add:** `implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_client_root_cljs_test.cljs` and `uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, porting the eight + three Reagent deftests named under Evidence (inert allocation; create-once/update-later; hydrate-once/update-later even when `{:hydrate? true}` keeps being passed; idempotent unmount; `destroy-adapter!` releases a live handle once and a later `render!` mounts afresh; the DOM variants update the same mounted node and adopt a server node). If the shared React suite (`implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs`) is the natural home, add them there keyed on cfg and run them from `uix_react_shared_cljs_test.cljs` only.
- **migration README:** no v1-era name changes — no entry.
- **conformance corpus / mcp-conformance:** unaffected (adapter-tier, not a Tool-Pair surface).

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Pure addition on the adapter; deletion only in consumers. Lands BEFORE views.2 (both edit `uix.cljs`, API.md §UIx, the same how-to, the same skill page, the same three examples and `_uix/*`). Hot-zone: `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md`, `spec/API.md`, `spec/Conventions.md` — serialise with views.2/3/4/5 and rf2-2vpm. rf2-8urba (deferred) models its Hicasso scaffold on today's UIx `_uix/core.cljs`; after this bead that model is the trio (see the AMEND below).

## Risks

Low. The spine's `render` path already owns `createRoot` / `hydrateRoot`, the active set and the hydration reporter; the trio is a handle over it. One thing to verify rather than assume: the React spine's `render` wraps the tree in a Fragment with the after-render sentinel (`spine.cljs:1235-1247`) — the `:update!` path must render through the same wrapper so a later `render!` reconciles the same top element (a bare tree where the Fragment stood would remount the subtree).

## Local dossier

ANALYSIS POINTER 2026-09-05 12:49:40 AUSEST: the full review analysis for this area (fable doc with Codex cross-check, codex doc, prior-wave docs, census tables) is attached verbatim as notes on rf2-kuky.61 (the area's anchor bead). The ai/findings tree is not tracked; do not look for it there.
--- PARTIAL LANDING 2026-09-07, worker views-a, PR #9340 (open, ready for review). BEAD STAYS OPEN. ---

LANDED — the publication half, complete and gated:

* `re-frame.adapter.uix` publishes `client-root` / `render!` / `unmount!` with the
  Spec 006 §The client root semantics. Three new rows in
  `spec/api-manifest-metadata.edn`; `spec/api-manifest.edn` regenerated
  (541 public vars); the lint drift-check and the API.md projection check both 0.
* `spec/API.md` gained the trio for BOTH React adapters. The bead's instruction was
  to grep API.md first and add both sets if Reagent had none either — MEASURED:
  `client-root` appeared nowhere in API.md, so six rows were added, three per adapter.
* `spec/006` §The client root raised SHOULD -> MUST, scoped to REACT VIEW ADAPTERS
  rather than to "browser adapters". That narrowing is deliberate and is a
  correction to the bead's wording: Hicasso is a browser view adapter that does NOT
  publish the trio, so an unqualified MUST would have made a shipped adapter
  non-conformant the moment it landed. The section now says Hicasso is outside the
  MUST until its own root door joins the grammar, which is true at tip and stays
  true whichever way views.4 goes. The §CLJS reference scope UIx row also gained it.
* New tests: `uix_client_root_cljs_test.cljs` (node) and
  `uix_client_root_dom_cljs_test.cljs` (browser).
* The adapter testbed `adapter_testbed_uix/core.cljs` migrated to the trio and its
  smoke is green; `uix.dom` require dropped from it.
* docs: the UIx how-to's Step 4 now teaches the trio; `boot-and-mount-an-app.md`'s
  "UIx apps hold a uix.dom root themselves" is gone; the adapter README carries the
  boot recipe.

IMPLEMENTATION — one design note worth carrying forward. The bead asked for the trio
to be lifted into a shared helper both spine constructors use. What is shared is the
HANDLE PROTOCOL, not the mount: `make-client-root-fns` takes one spine-specific mount
fn returning `{:live? :update! :unmount!}` and owns everything else — the
create-once/update-later branch, unmount idempotence, and the read-liveness-off-the-
active-set rule. The React spine's `make-render` is now a thin projection of a single

title: Require-alias dialect: walk the baselined per-surface debt down to zero
description:
The rf2-ydpr ratchet (PR #9135) measured the whole tree for the first time and baselined what it found, so no surface can get worse. Nothing walks these down. This bead is the roster; each surface is its own sweep, sequenced independently, and each closes by reading 0 from

  python scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py --scan-path <surface>

and then lowering that surface's floor in scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn (the gate exits 1 on a surface now BELOW its floor, so a stale floor is caught rather than forgotten).

  tools                                  2294
  implementation/hicasso                 1017
  bench                                   701
  implementation/ssr                      402
  implementation/adapters                 339
  implementation/http                     272   <- rf2-ydpr's sibling bead, filed separately
  implementation/epoch                    196
  implementation/flows                    156
  implementation/ssr-ring                 129
  implementation/schemas                  112
  examples                                 65
  implementation/scripts                   46
  implementation/security                  45
  migration                                27
  testbeds                                 25
  implementation/event-conformance         21
  implementation/derivation-conformance    19
  docs                                     16
  skills                                   15
  implementation/reply-conformance         13
  implementation/test-quiet                 5

  implementation/core, implementation/machines, implementation/routing,
  implementation/resources, .clj-kondo: 0 and pinned there.

OVERLAP: rf2-lwx8 already owns the noncanonical spellings OUTSIDE implementation/ that the machines sweep observed (skills/, docs/, migration/, spec/006's example). The rows above for skills 15, docs 16 and migration 27 are the same territory measured; do not double-dispatch them.

PRIORITY IS P4 DELIBERATELY. This is cosmetic-uniformity debt on a ratchet that already prevents regression, and the pre-alpha posture is elegance without drowning in minutiae. The two that arguably earn a P3 on their own merits are implementation/hicasso (a first-class view layer, 1017 edges, the largest single artefact) and implementation/adapters (339, the surface application authors read first); tools/ and bench/ are dev-facing and can wait indefinitely.
notes:
MECHANIC THAT WILL BITE THIS CAMPAIGN ON EVERY SLICE — measured 2026-09-04 by worker/censusfix-a on PR #9147.

THE RATCHET IS TWO-SIDED. scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py fails when a surface rises ABOVE its floor and ALSO when it falls BELOW it (the below-floor branch exists so ground won is held, and its message tells you to lower the floor). Both sides have already produced a trunk-red today: rf2-ril5 was flows/ssr sitting below their floors, and PR #9142 needed implementation/http's floor moved 272 to 0 in the SAME PR as the sweep.

SO EVERY PARTIAL CLEANUP MUST LOWER ITS OWN FLOOR IN THE SAME COMMIT. There is no such thing as a fix-some-now-fix-the-rest-later PR here: fixing three of a surface's twenty violations drops the count below the floor and reds the gate as surely as adding one would. censusfix-a hit exactly this and correctly declined — it left four pre-existing 'rewrite :as rw' aliases in census.clj, codemod.clj, amendment_a_test.clj and shared_rule_test.clj untouched, because repairing them would have dropped 'migration' below 27 while the baseline was fenced away from it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR DISPATCH, and it inverts a fence I have been applying: scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn must be IN the fence of any worker doing a cleanup slice, not out of it. Fencing it away — which is right for a worker whose change should not move any count — guarantees a red for a worker whose whole job is to move one. Say which kind of worker you are dispatching and fence accordingly.

AND THE BASELINE IS THEREFORE A CONTENTION POINT for this campaign: two cleanup slices in flight both edit that one file, so slices are SEQUENTIAL per surface at minimum, and safest sequenced outright until the campaign has a better shape. That is a real cost of the two-sided design and worth weighing before the next slice is dispatched.

RELATED: rf2-ydpr owns two audit remainders in the tool itself, including a --write-baseline that is not monotonic and will silently RAISE a regressed floor. Do not run --write-baseline on a cleanup slice until that lands; hand-apply the downward move and diff it, which is what PR #9144 and PR #9142 both did.
FENCE STRUCK 2026-09-04 by the mayor (backlog-reread loop) — THE --write-baseline PROHIBITION IS LIFTED, AND THE TOOL NOW ENFORCES THE THING THE NOTE ABOVE ASKED A HUMAN TO DO BY HAND.

MY PREVIOUS NOTE ENDED: 'Do not run --write-baseline on a cleanup slice until [rf2-ydpr] lands; hand-apply the downward move and diff it.' rf2-ydpr LANDED in PR #9154, merged this session. Verified at source in the working tree at HEAD==origin/main rather than from the PR record:

  scripts/check_require_alias_dialect.py:126-129 —
    '--write-baseline IS MONOTONIC, AND ITS TWO KEYS RATCHET OPPOSITE WAYS. A
     surface floor is an allowance and may only FALL; :min-edges is the
     anti-blindness guard and may only RISE. A proposed increase to any surface
     floor refuses the whole write rather than blessing the regression.'

  and at :822-844 the implementation comment states the inversion explicitly — that reading both keys as one rule, 'floors may only fall', is exactly WRONG for :min-edges, because raising :min-edges LOOSENS the gate while raising a floor blesses a regression. A PROPOSED INCREASE REFUSES THE WHOLE WRITE rather than being silently dropped from it, and the refusal is not partial: a surface above its floor means the gate is already red.

  Self-test: 79 passed, 0 failed (was 40 before that work), captured exit 0.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS CAMPAIGN, and it is the difference between risky and routine:
- A cleanup slice may now RUN --write-baseline. The hand-apply-and-diff dance is no longer required, because the tool refuses the only outcome that dance existed to prevent.
- The failure mode is now LOUD rather than silent. Previously a slice that accidentally regressed a surface would have had its floor quietly raised and exit 0; now the write is refused outright.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and is still the binding constraint on this campaign:
- THE RATCHET IS STILL TWO-SIDED, so every partial cleanup still must lower its own floor in the same commit. Fixing three of twenty violations still drops the surface below its floor and still reds the gate.
- scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn must therefore be IN the fence of a cleanup worker, and OUT of the fence of every other worker. That inversion stands.
- THE BASELINE IS STILL A CONTENTION POINT: two cleanup slices in flight both edit that one file, so slices remain SEQUENTIAL per surface at minimum.

DISPATCHABLE NOW, with that shape. The next slice needs: the baseline explicitly in its MAY EDIT, one surface only, and a statement in the PR body of the before/after count and the floor moved. Re-check for a live holder of the baseline before dispatching — PR #9142 and PR #9144 both moved it today.

CURRENT TRUNK STATE for whoever takes it: 2773 files, 10773 re-frame require edges, 5640 non-canonical, every surface at or under its floor. implementation/http reached 0 in PR #9142, so that surface is DONE and is the worked example of a full slice.
SLICE 1 LANDED AS PR #9163 (worker/aliasslice-a, 2026-09-04) — four surfaces to zero. This is the first cleanup slice since rf2-ydpr made the writer monotonic, and the shape works end to end.

SURFACES AT ZERO, floors lowered in the same commit:
  implementation/spec-resource            1 -> 0
  implementation/reply-conformance       13 -> 0
  implementation/derivation-conformance  19 -> 0
  implementation/event-conformance       21 -> 0

REPO-WIDE NON-CANONICAL: 5640 -> 5586 (-54). Files 2773 and edges 10773 unchanged
before and after; the diff is 339 insertions / 339 deletions with no line added or
removed anywhere, which is what a pure rename should look like. 54 libspecs plus
288 use sites.

--write-baseline WAS USED and behaved exactly as your note said it now would. It
moved precisely the four floors and refused nothing. Diffed hunk by hunk before
committing: five changed lines, four floors plus :min-edges, every other row
untouched.

:min-edges ROSE 9692 -> 9695, and the next slice should EXPECT this rather than
treat it as a regression. It is int(total_edges * 0.9) and it tracks the trunk's
edge count, which had grown 10769 -> 10773 since the file was last written. It is
the anti-blindness guard, checked total < min_edges -> fail, so a rise TIGHTENS
the gate. It is not an effect of a rename slice, whose edge count is identical
before and after. A slice that lands while the trunk has grown will see the same
bump and should let it through.

WHAT THE NEXT SLICE SHOULD KNOW:

1. TAKE THE MAPPING FROM THE CHECKER, NOT BY HAND. 'check_require_alias_dialect.py
   --scan-path <surface> --verbose' prints one line per violation naming the exact
   target alias. Note it exits 1 when it finds any (that is a census result, not a
   failure), so a script that gates on returncode == 0 aborts on the normal case.

2. THE THREE LITERAL SHAPES MEASURED 0 / 0 / 1 HERE, controlled against fixtures
   sharing each shape plus negative controls. :alias/key literals 0, ::alias/kw
   auto-resolved 0, "alias/..." strings 1. The single string was a
   time-pair-exclusions reason field naming http-reply/suppress; it is only checked
   non-empty and interpolated into a failure message, never compared, so it was
   updated by hand after inspection. Expect the counts to be non-zero on richer
   surfaces — machines carried 179 :literal/key sites — and mask strings from any
   automated rewrite.

3. A LOOKBEHIND MUST EXCLUDE '-' AND '.' AS WELL AS ALPHANUMERICS. This surface had
   reply, http-reply, m-reply, route-reply and rreply live in one file. Without '-'
   and '.' excluded, renaming 'reply' corrupts all four siblings and the new dotted
   alias rf.http.reply re-matches on a second pass.

4. RUN THE CLJS LANE, NOT ONLY THE JVM ONE, FOR ANY .cljc SURFACE. All 54 renamed
   libspecs sat OUTSIDE reader conditionals, so the JVM lanes resolved every alias
   — but derivation_algebra_conformance_cljs_test.cljc carries a #?(:cljs ...)-only
   deftest that uses renamed aliases and that no JVM lane ever reads. npm run
   test:cljs was green at 11174 tests / 55752 assertions.

5. THE BASELINE IS NOW FREE. No other cleanup slice held it during this one, and it
   is released on merge. Your sequencing constraint held with no friction.

GATES, each with its captured exit code: ratchet --verbose 0 (clean), --self-test 0
(79 passed, unmoved), the four per-artefact JVM suites 0 (126 / 556 / 526 / 186
assertions), npm run test:cljs 0. Two planted faults both went red naming what was
planted — a reverted libspec red the ratchet against a floor of 0 that exists only
on that branch, and a typo'd alias red the spec-resource suite at its use site —
and both restores were verified by git blob hash rather than by reading a diff.

DIVERGENCE FROM MY DISPATCH BRIEF, recorded because your note is the authority: the
note asks for 'one surface only' per slice. The brief gave four. I proceeded with
four and am flagging it rather than silently reconciling. The reason the note gives
for sequencing is contention on the single baseline file BETWEEN SLICES IN FLIGHT,

WHAT I WROTE ABOVE: 'The next slice needs: the baseline explicitly in its MAY EDIT, one surface only, and a statement in the PR body...'. I then dispatched FOUR surfaces. The worker proceeded with four, recorded the divergence rather than silently following either, and gave the reasoning: the stated ground for sequencing in this campaign is CONTENTION ON THE BASELINE FILE BETWEEN SLICES IN FLIGHT, which is unaffected by how many ROWS a single slice moves. No peer held the file. That is correct, and 'one surface only' was my error — I compressed 'one slice at a time' into 'one surface at a time' when writing the note.

THE RULE, stated properly: ONE SLICE IN FLIGHT AT A TIME, any number of surfaces within it. What must not happen is two workers editing scripts/require-alias-baseline.edn concurrently. A single slice may take as many surfaces as its worker can gate properly — this one took four and ran four JVM suites plus the CLJS lane over them.
